children.translated_text: // Commentary on the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> //
Composed by the revered <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya</s> (Madhvācārya)
Bhāṣyadīpikā on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1.0:
That which is to be inquired into, which grants birth, protection, dissolution, regulation, knowledge, the bond of individual ignorance,
and the highest good, which is accessible through scripture, expressible in its primary sense through the statements found in <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture),
accompanied by [the consorts] <s>Bhaiṣmī</s> (Rukmiṇī, daughter of Bhīṣmaka) and <s>Satyā</s> (Satyabhāmā), possessing a body of many virtues, far removed from fear and prior causes of fear,
to be contemplated through devotion, scripture, and the like, whose ultimate destination is worship — I meditate on <s>Veṇu-Kṛṣṇa</s> (Kṛṣṇa with the flute). (1)
Having approached from a mango pillar, having struck down those with copper beaks,
I bow to the humble Lord of the universe — <s>Nṛkesarī</s> (Narasiṃha), who seized the unassailable. (2)
Without having studied the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s>, by whose grace the grammar was mastered,
I worship that <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the sun who dispels the darkness of obstacles. (3)
I salute the teachers of perfect knowledge, the victorious noble ones, the teachers in the lineage of <s>Vyāsa</s>,
the noble teachers in the lineage of <s>Rāmacandra</s>, and also the teachers in the lineage of <s>Lakṣmīkānta</s> (Viṣṇu). (4)
By whom the meaning of <s>Madhva</s> guru's excellent commentary was clarified,
who shattered the assemblies of opponents, who was bound to the ocean of teachers,
who gave both kinds of wealth to students, who adorned the seat of learning —
may that great king of teachers, <s>Śrī Raghunāthatīrtha</s>, purify our intellect. (5)
Following the commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>) composed by the victorious noble one, according to one's understanding,
the <s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> (Lamp on the Commentary) is composed by the ascetic named <s>Jagannātha</s>. (6)
In some places, the meaning of the <s>ṭīkā</s> is examined through the elucidation of the commentary itself,
following the methods stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, the <s>Tātparyacandrikā</s>, and other works. (7)
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is exalted by all virtues and free from all faults,

children.text: jñeyaṃ gamyaṃ gurūṃścāpi natvā sūtrārtha ucyate //
children.translated_text: who is to be known, who is to be attained, and also to the teachers — the meaning of the <s>Sūtras</s> is stated.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 1:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.1:
paramānandādyātmakasya paramātmanaḥ pratibimbatayā svataścidānandādyātmakasya jīvasya anādyavidyākāmakarmādinimittabandhadhvaṃsāya nikhilajīvajaḍātmakāt prapañcāt paramārthato 'tyantabhinnatayā nikhilaguṇodāratayā nirastasamastadoṣatayā paramapuruṣamavagamayituṃ sakalasadāgamānāṃ pravṛttiriti tattvam /
yadāhuḥ -
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 1:
The purpose of all the authoritative scriptures (<s>sadāgamas</s>) is to make known the Supreme Person (<s>paramapuruṣa</s>), who is absolutely different in reality from the entire phenomenal world consisting of sentient beings (<s>jīvas</s>) and insentient matter (<s>jaḍa</s>), who is eminent in all virtues, who is devoid of all faults — for the purpose of destroying the bondage of the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), which is inherently of the nature of consciousness and bliss as a reflection of the Supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) who is of the nature of supreme bliss, a bondage caused by beginningless ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), desire, and action — this is the truth.
As they say —
'Everything other [than suffering] is free from suffering; only the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) are the sufferers;
for the removal of their suffering, this <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) operates.'

children.text:
iti /
'pravartate'; duḥkhaprahāṇasādhanaṃ paramātmānaṃ pratipādayatītyarthaḥ / teṣāṃ cārthanirṇayāya brahmasūtrāṇi cakāra bhagavān bādarāyaṇaḥ / tāni ca paṭalapihitanayanavat yathāvadarthāvettṛbhiḥ avidyākhyapaṭalapihitanayanapadoktasadarthaiḥ anyairanyathāvyākhyātāni
children.translated_text:
Thus.
'Operates' — the meaning is that it teaches the Supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) as the means for the removal of suffering. And for the determination of their meaning, the blessed <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> composed the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>. And those [sūtras], like eyes covered by a film, have been otherwise explained by others — those whose eyes are covered by the film called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — who do not comprehend the meaning as it truly is,

children.text: yathāvadvyācikhyāsurbhagavānānandatīrthācāryaḥ samaṅgalasyaiva saphalatvāt prāripsitabhāṣyasya kaivalyādyakhilaphalasādhanatāsiddhyarthaṃ nirantarāyaparisamāptyādyarthaṃ ca nārāyaṇapraṇāmarūpaṃ maṅgalamācaran śiṣyaśikṣārthaṃ grathayati cikīrṣitaṃ ca pratijānīte - 'nārāyaṇam'; iti / 'sarvairguṇaiḥ udīrṇaṃ'; udāram utkṛṣṭam / 'doṣavarjitaṃ'; doṣarahitam/ 'jñeyaṃ'; parokṣāparokṣākhyobhayavidhajñānaviṣayīkaraṇīyam / 'gamyaṃ'; prāpyam / ubhayatra sadbhiriti śeṣaḥ / nārāyaṇaṃ 'natvā gurūṃśca'; iti cakārārthassamuccayaḥ / tathā ca gurūṃśca natvā sāṣṭāṅgaṃ namaskṛtya 'sūtrārthaḥ'; samastavedatadupabṛṃhaṇetihāsapurāṇādiśabdarāśyarthabhūto nārāyaṇākhyo brahmasūtrārtho mayā 'ucyate'; bhāṣyata iti yojanā/
children.translated_text: wishing to explain them as they truly are, the blessed <s>Ānandatīrtha Ācārya</s> (Madhva), since only an auspicious work bears fruit, performs a benediction (<s>maṅgala</s>) in the form of salutation to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — for the purpose of establishing the efficacy of the intended commentary as a means to <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) and all other results, and for the purpose of its unobstructed completion — and instructs the students, and declares his intention with the word '<s>Nārāyaṇam</s>.' 'Exalted by all virtues' — means eminent, excellent. 'Free from faults' — means devoid of defects. 'To be known' — means to be made the object of both mediate and immediate knowledge. 'To be attained' — means to be reached. In both cases, 'by the good' is to be supplied. Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> 'and to the teachers' — the word 'ca' (and) indicates aggregation. And thus, having bowed to the teachers with full prostration, 'the meaning of the sūtras' — the meaning of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>, which is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and which is the meaning of the entire body of words including the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and their supplements — 'is stated by me' — is commented upon: this is the construction.

children.text: atra guṇairudīrṇam ityanena prathamādhyāyasya, doṣavarjitam ityanena dvitīyādhyāyasya, jñeyam ityanena tṛtīyādhyāyasya, gamyam ityanena caturthādhyāyasya arthaḥ śiṣyahitatayā ādau saṅgṛhīta iti jñātavyam / anenaiva viśeṣaṇacatuṣṭayena viśeṣyavācakanārāyaṇaśabdaḥ na ḍitthādiśabdavatsāṅketikaḥ; kintu arāḥ doṣāḥ tadviruddhāḥ nārāḥ guṇāḥ teṣāmāśraya iti vā, arāṇāmāśrayo na bhavatīti vā, viṣayatayā naraviśeṣasambandhijñānāśraya iti vā, aravidhuramuktāśraya iti vā yogenotkṛṣṭaguṇavācaka ityuktaṃ bhavati / tena nārāyaṇa eva śāstrārtha iti pradarśitam / anenaiva viśeṣaṇacatuṣṭayena vandyatāprayojakāni bahuguṇatva-nirdeṣatva-śāstrajñeyatva-śāstragamyatvāni coktāni /
children.translated_text: Here it should be known that by 'exalted in virtues,' the meaning of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) is summarized; by 'free from faults,' the second; by 'to be known,' the third; by 'to be attained,' the fourth — thus the teacher has summarized the content at the outset for the benefit of students. Through these four qualifiers, the word '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' which denotes the qualified entity is not merely conventional like the word '<s>Ḍittha</s>' (an arbitrary name); rather, it is etymologically significant: '<s>arāḥ</s>' means faults; their opposites, '<s>nārāḥ</s>,' means virtues, and he is their abode; or, he is not the abode of faults; or, he is the substrate of the knowledge connected with a particular person as its object; or, he is the abode of the liberated who are free from faults — thus the word, by etymology, denotes one who possesses supreme virtues. Through this, it is shown that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is the meaning of the scripture. Through these four qualifiers, the reasons for his being worthy of salutation — possession of many virtues, being free from faults, being knowable through scripture, and being attainable through scripture — are also stated.

children.text: yadvā - atra nārāyaṇamityādipadapañcakena samudraśāyitva-sarvavasanotkarṣakrīḍājñānādiguṇairuccatva-samyagdoṣa-karṣaṇa-prakṛṣṭadyutimayatva-jñāninaḥ prati prāptinirodharahitatvākhyanimittapañcakayutena nārāyaṇavāsudevasaṅkarṣaṇapradyumnāniruddhākhyamūrtaya ucyante; tāsāmetacchāstrādhyāyapādeṣu pratipipādayiṣitatvāt / tathā ca 'nārāyaṇaṃ natvā guṇairudīrṇaṃ natvā doṣavarjitaṃ natvā'; ityādikā tattvapradīpikoktayojanā draṣṭavyā /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: Here, by the five words beginning with '<s>Nārāyaṇam</s>,' the five forms — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s> — are denoted, endowed with five causes: sleeping on the ocean, excellence in all ornaments, sport, knowledge and other virtues, eminence, proper elimination of faults, being constituted of supreme radiance, and for the knower, freedom from obstruction of attainment — since these are to be taught in the chapters and sections of this scripture. And thus the construction given in the <s>Tattvapradīpikā</s> should be seen: 'Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, having bowed to the one exalted in virtues, having bowed to the one free from faults,' and so on.

children.text: 'gurornāma na gṛhṇīyācchiṣyo bhāryā paterapi'; iti vacanād gurornāma nāgrahīdācāryaḥ / na ca 'gurūn nārāyaṇaśabdavācyān nārāyaṇapadenaiva gurunāma covāca, āsamantāt viśiṣṭassa eva hi vyāso 'pi'; iti tattvapradīpikāvirodha iti vācyam; gurudevatayorvāstavābhedavivakṣayā tadupapatteḥ / yogarūḍhavyāsakṛṣṇādyasādhāraṇanāmavivakṣayā evamuktatvāt / gurutvanimittaśāstraprabhavatva-śāstrasampradāyapravartakatva-sākṣādupadeśakatvākhyaprakārabāhulyāt gauravādvā bahumānārthaṃ vā bahuvacanaprayogaḥ / yadyapi gururvyāsaḥ, iṣṭadevatāpi sa eveti na tayorbhedaḥ, tathāpi viśeṣānugrahārthaṃ pṛthaṅnatiriti / evaṃ svasya gurudevatayoḥ bhede arucisūcanārtho 'piśabdaḥ / tathā ca - 'api'; tathāpi gurudevatābhedābhāve 'pītyarthaḥ / tattvapradīpakṛttu apiśabdātsūtrakāramapītyāha / tasyāpi viśeṣānugrahārthaṃ pṛthaṅnatirityevābhiprāyaḥ / yadvāpiśabdaḥ viśeṣaṇāntarasamuccayārthaḥ, tadvivaraṇamasyetyādi'; iti sudhoktarītyā guṇapūrṇatvopapādakajagajjanmādikāraṇatvādirūpānuktaviśeṣaṇāntarasamuccayārtho 'piśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the scripture says 'a student should not take the name of the teacher, nor a wife the name of the husband,' the <s>Ācārya</s> did not take the guru's name. And one should not say that there is a contradiction with the <s>Tattvapradīpikā</s> which states 'he spoke the guru's name by the word <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> which denotes the gurus who are <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> themselves, for <s>Vyāsa</s> himself is distinguished in all respects' — because this is justified by the intention of expressing the real non-difference between the guru and the deity. It is spoken thus with the intention of the non-conventional names like <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, etc. which are particular to the etymologically significant usage. Due to the multiplicity of aspects of being a teacher — being the source of scripture, being the propagator of the scriptural tradition, being the direct instructor — or out of respect, or for the sake of honor, the plural is used. Although the guru is <s>Vyāsa</s>, and the chosen deity is also he himself, so there is no difference between them, nevertheless, a separate salutation is made for the purpose of special grace. Thus, the word 'api' (also) indicates the absence of aversion to the difference between one's own guru and deity. And thus 'api' — nevertheless, even though there is no difference between guru and deity — this is the meaning. But the author of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> says from the word 'api' — 'to the sūtra-author also.' His intention too is that a separate salutation is for the purpose of special grace. Or the word 'api' is for the purpose of aggregating other qualifiers, and as explained in the <s>Sudhā</s>, it aggregates unmentioned additional qualifiers like being the cause of the creation of the world, etc., which establish the fullness of virtues.

children.text: anenaiva ślokena śrotṛpravṛttyaṅgabhūtāḥ śāstrādhikāriviṣayaprayojanasambandhāśca śiṣyaśikṣārthaṃ sūcitā bhavanti/
children.translated_text: Through this very verse, the components that motivate the listener's engagement — the qualified student (<s>adhikārin</s>), subject matter (<s>viṣaya</s>), purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), and connection (<s>sambandha</s>) — are also indicated for the instruction of students.

children.text: dvāpare sarvatra jñāne ākulībhūte tannirṇayāya brahmarudrendrādibhirarthito bhagavānnārāyaṇo vyāsatvenāvatatāra /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dvāpara</s> age, when knowledge everywhere had become confused, for the determination of that, having been entreated by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and other gods, the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> descended in the form of <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 2:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.2:
nanu brahmasūtrāṇāṃ prāmāṇye satyeva prekṣāvadupādeyatvam, prāyo 'sya prāmāṇyaprayojyatvāt / satyeva tasmin prātītikārthanirāsena yathāvadvyākhyeyatvaṃ sambhavati / prāmāṇyameva kathamityāśaṅkya āptimūlatvādinaiveti parihāramabhipretya vaktṛśrotṛprasaṅgadoṣābhāvarūpāptimūlatvopapādanāya sūtrāgatikramamāha - 'dvāpare'; ityādinā / dvāveva dharmapādau parāvavaśiṣṭau yasmin yuge, dvābhyāṃ yugābhyāṃ parasminnuttarasmin yuge iti vā, vaivasvatamanvantare mahāyugeṣu prathamadvāparāpekṣayāṣṭāviṃśe dharmapādadvayayutatvāt dvāparākhye yuge / 'sarvatra'; 'manuṣyāṇāṃ ṛṣīṇāṃ devānāṃ ca'; iti tattvapradīpokteḥ 'loka iti sajjano vivakṣitaḥ'; iti prameyadīpokteśca sarveṣāṃ devaṛṣyādīnāṃ satāṃ 'jñāne'; samyagjñāne 'ākulībhūte'; samyagjñānaṃ saguṇatvādijñānaṃ uta nirguṇatvādijñānamiti vipratipattijanyasandehaviṣayatāṃ nirguṇatvādijñānameva na tvanyaditi mithyājñānaviṣayatāṃ ca prāpte sati, tajjñānaviṣayībhūtaṃ saguṇatvādikaṃ tattvamanyadveti sandehe tādṛgviparyaye ca satīti yāvat / 'tannirṇayāya'; tasmin saguṇatvādijñāne tasya samyagjñānatvasya niścayārthe, idameva tattvaṃ nānyaditi viṣaye samyaktvaniścayārthamiti yāvat / 'brahmarudrendrādibhiḥ'; devairiti śeṣaḥ / 'arthitaḥ'; upayācitaḥ / anyapadārthānāṃ devānāṃ brahmarudrendrādibhiriti yadviśeṣaṇaṃ tat prasiddhaprabhāvānāmapi bhagavaditareṣāmaśakyamidaṃ kāryamiti pradarśanārtham / 'bhagavān'; samagraiśvaryavairāgyādiguṇasampanno 'nārāyaṇaḥ'; tannirṇayāya 'vyāsatvena'; vyāsabhāvena 'śubhamarakatavarṇam'; ityuktavyāsarūpeṇa 'avatatāra'; āvirbabhūveti / tannirṇayāyetyasyāvṛtyā yojanā / tannirṇayāyendrādibhirarthito rudraḥ brahmā ca tataḥ taiḥ sarvairupagamyottamādhikāribhiḥ arthito bhagavāniti buddhyā vivekenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 2:
Now, the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> are worthy of being accepted by a discerning person only if their authoritativeness is [first established], since their acceptability mostly depends on their authoritativeness. Only when that is established can they be properly explained, refuting misinterpretations. Anticipating the question 'how is their authoritativeness established?' and intending the answer 'through their origin from a trustworthy source (<s>āpta</s>),' to demonstrate the trustworthiness rooted in the absence of defects in both speaker and listener, he states the context of the origin of the sūtras with the words 'In the Dvāpara age' and so on. In the age called <s>Dvāpara</s>, in which only two feet of <s>Dharma</s> remain — or in the age following the two prior ages — in the twenty-eighth [Dvāpara] of the <s>mahāyugas</s> of the <s>Vaivasvata Manvantara</s>, relative to the first Dvāpara, having two feet of Dharma and hence called Dvāpara. 'Everywhere' — as stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, 'of humans, sages, and gods'; and as stated in the <s>Prameyadīpa</s>, 'world means the virtuous.' Of all the gods, sages, and the good, 'in knowledge' — in right knowledge, 'had become confused' — when right knowledge had come to the state of doubt generated by disagreement — whether right knowledge is the knowledge of the qualified (<s>saguṇa</s>) or of the unqualified (<s>nirguṇa</s>) — and to the state of false knowledge that only the unqualified knowledge is [right], the qualified nature and such truths having become objects of doubt and misunderstanding. 'For the determination of that' — for the purpose of establishing the right nature of that knowledge of the qualified, for determining 'this alone is the truth, not otherwise.' 'By <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and others' — the rest is 'the gods.' 'Entreated' — requested. The qualifying of the gods by '<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and others' is to show that this task is impossible even for those of well-known might, other than the Lord. '<s>Bhagavān</s>' — endowed with complete sovereignty, dispassion, and other qualities. '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' descended 'as <s>Vyāsa</s>' — in the form of <s>Vyāsa</s>, in the form described as 'of auspicious emerald complexion.' The construction connects 'for the determination of that' by repetition. For the determination of that, entreated by <s>Indra</s> and others, <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> [also], and then, approached by all those supreme qualified ones, the Lord was entreated — thus the construction follows by intelligent discernment.

children.text: atheṣṭāniṣṭaprāptiparihārecchūnāṃ tadyogamavijānatāṃ tajjñāpanārthaṃ vedamutsannaṃ vyañjayaṃścaturdhā vyabhajat, caturviṃśatidhaikaśatadhā sahasradhā dvādaśadhā ca /
children.translated_text: Then, for the purpose of teaching those who desire the attainment of the desired and the avoidance of the undesired, but do not know the means to those — he manifested the <s>Veda</s> that had become hidden, and divided it fourfold, and further into twenty-four, a hundred and one, a thousand, and twelvefold.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 3:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.3:
tataḥ kiṃ prakṛte ityata āha - atheti / 'atha'; tasmāt tannirṇayāyāvatīrṇatvāt avatārānantarameva tattvajñānānanukūlavijātīyavyāpāravyavadhānamakṛtveti yāvat, na tu paropadeśamapekṣyeti vā / 'iṣṭāniṣṭaprāptiparihārecchūnām'; iṣṭaprāptiścāniṣṭaparihāraśca tāvicchūnām / tattvapradīparītyā aprāptasukhaprāptiduḥkhaparihārecchāvatāmiti vā / mokṣasya puruṣārthatāsamarthanārthaṃ vādivipratipatteḥ tatsvarūpanirūpaṇārthaṃ caivamuktam / anyathā mumukṣūṇāmityeva brūyāt / naitāvatālam 'ātyantika'; iti copaskartavyam / 'tadyogaṃ'; tayorupāyaviśeṣaṃ nivṛttadharmaparāparatattvajñānarūpaṃ 'avijānatām'; ajānānānāṃ sajjanānāṃ 'tajjñāpanārtham'; iṣṭāniṣṭaprāptiparihāropāyajñāpanārthaṃ/ 'utsannam'; apapāṭhādinā tirohitaṃ 'vedaṃ caturdhā'; - 'vyabhajat'; ityāvartate, 'tataḥ prāgeva vibhaktam'; iti 'punarekaikam'; iti ca śeṣaḥ / tathā ca avāntaravedavibhāgāt prāgeva tataḥ svata eva caturdhā vibhaktāt ṛgādirūpāt mūlavedāt caturdhā vibhaktaṃ vedaṃ ṛṅnigadādirūpamupavedaṃ vyañjayan adhyāpanenābhivyajya tatastasmādekaikasmādekaiko bhāga iti caturdhā vyabhajat / ṛco ṛca uddhṛtyābhivyajya tato ṛgvedaṃ, nigadādyajurvedam, sāmnassāmavedam, ātharvaṇādatharvaṇavedaṃ kṛtavānityarthaḥ / punarekaikaṃ ca vedam ṛgvedādirūpāvāntarabhedaṃ vedam
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 3:
What then follows in the topic at hand? To this he says — 'Then' (<s>atha</s>). 'Then' — from that, since he descended for that determination, immediately after the descent, without making any intervening activity of a dissimilar kind unfavorable to the knowledge of truth; not that he waited for the instruction of others. 'Of those desiring the attainment of the desired and the avoidance of the undesired' — of those who desire the attainment of the desired and the avoidance of the undesired. Or, in the manner of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, of those who desire the attainment of unattained happiness and the removal of suffering. This is said thus for the purpose of establishing <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) as the supreme human goal and for defining its nature, since there is disagreement among disputants. Otherwise, one would simply say 'of those desiring liberation.' This alone is not sufficient — 'absolute' is to be supplied. 'The means to those' — the specific means, in the form of the supreme truth-knowledge that is the highest renunciation. 'Of those who do not know' — of the good people who do not know. 'For the purpose of teaching that' — for the purpose of making known the means of attaining the desired and avoiding the undesired. 'The <s>Veda</s>, which had been hidden' — concealed through corrupt readings and the like, 'fourfold' — 'he divided.' This extends [to what follows]. 'That which had been divided even before that' and 'each one again' — these are to be supplied. And thus, from the root <s>Veda</s> in the form of <s>Ṛk</s> and others, which had been divided fourfold even before that, on its own, he manifested fourfold the secondary <s>Vedas</s> (<s>upavedas</s>) in the form of <s>Ṛṅ</s>, <s>Nigada</s>, and others through teaching, and then from each of those, he divided each part fourfold. Having extracted and manifested the <s>Ṛks</s>, he made the <s>Ṛgveda</s> from them; the <s>Yajurveda</s> from the <s>Nigada</s> and other [portions]; the <s>Sāmaveda</s> from the <s>Sāmans</s>; and the <s>Atharvaveda</s> from the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> [portions] — this is the meaning. And again, each <s>Veda</s> — each sub-division of the <s>Veda</s> in the form of <s>Ṛgveda</s> and so on —

children.text: adhyetṛṇāmalpaśaktiṃ vīkṣya caturviṃśatidhā ekaśatadhā ekottaraśatākhyaprakāreṇa sahasradhā dvādaśadhā ca vyabhajadityarthaḥ / taduktam ṛgbhāṣye -
children.translated_text: Seeing the limited capacity of students, he divided [the Veda] in twenty-four ways, in one hundred ways, by the method known as one-hundred-and-one, in a thousand ways, and in twelve ways — this is the meaning. This is stated in the <s>Ṛgbhāṣya</s> (commentary on the Ṛgveda):

children.text: ṛcaḥ sa ṛca uddhṛtya ṛgvedaṃ kṛtavān prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord, having extracted the <s>Ṛc</s>s (Ṛgvedic verses) from the <s>Ṛc</s>s, made the <s>Ṛgveda</s>;
the <s>Yajus</s> (formulae) from the <s>nigada</s>s (recitation portions), and likewise the <s>Sāman</s>s (chants) from the chanting portions. //

children.text: ityādinā svata eva caturdhā vibhaktāt mūlavedāt ṛgādirūpopavedamuddhṛtyābhivyajya tasmādavāntaram ṛgvedādi kṛtavānityarthaḥ / atra pūrvaṃ dvāparagrahaṇaṃ mahāvedāt uddhṛtasya upavedasya avāntaravedatvena avāntaravedasya ca caturviṃśatyāditvena vibhāgakathanaṃ ca akhilajñānākulībhāvasamarthanārtham / kālato vibhāgātpūrvaṃ tattacchākhāparijñānācca bhavati hyākulībhāvaḥ / taduktaṃ - 'cakre vedataroḥ1'; ityādinā / 'alpamedhasaḥ'; ākulībhūtajñānān, tannivāraṇārthamiti śeṣaḥ / yadyapi -
children.translated_text: Thus, having extracted — that is, having manifested — the subsidiary Veda (<s>upaveda</s>) in the form of <s>Ṛg</s> and the like from the original Veda that was itself divided fourfold, he made the further divisions of <s>Ṛgveda</s> and so on — this is the meaning. Here, the prior mention of <s>Dvāpara</s> [yuga], the statement that the subsidiary Veda extracted from the great Veda has the status of a sub-Veda, and the statement that the sub-Veda has twenty-four [and other] divisions — all this is for the purpose of establishing the confusion of all knowledge. For confusion arises from the temporal division and from the knowledge of the various branches [of the Veda]. This is stated [in the verse] 'He made of the tree of the Veda' and so on. 'Of those of limited intellect' — those whose knowledge had become confused; for the purpose of removing that [confusion] — this is to be supplied. Although —

children.text: eko vedaḥ kṛte hyāsīt tretāyāṃ sa tridhābhavat /
children.translated_text: There was one Veda in the <s>Kṛta</s> (Satya) age; in the <s>Tretā</s> age it became threefold;

children.text: sa eva pañcadhā jāto dvāparaṃ prāpya vai yugam //
children.translated_text: that very [Veda] became fivefold upon reaching the <s>Dvāpara</s> age. //

children.text: utsannassa kaliṃ prāpya vedaḥ prāyeṇa sarvaśaḥ //
children.translated_text: The Veda, having reached the <s>Kali</s> age, was almost entirely lost. //

children.text: ityatharvaṇabhāṣyodāhṛtasmṛtau kṛtayuge vedaikatvasya tretāyāṃ traividhyamātrasya dvāpare pañcavidhatvasya cokteḥ, tathā sarvasyāpi vedasya kalāvevotsādokteḥ, atra tu 'vedamutsannam'; ityanena tretāyuge caturdhā vibhāgasya dvāpara evotsādasya coktervirodho bhāti / tathāpi avyaktamūlarāśyapekṣayā vedaikyokteḥ sambhavāt, tretāyuge prācuryeṇa bhagavadijyāsādhanatvavivakṣayā traividhyoktāvapi vastuta atharvaṇākhyaprakārāntarasattvasya aniṣedhena vidhāntarasyāpi sattvasambhavāt, dvāpare apauruṣeyasya vedasya caturvidhatve 'pi pauruṣeyairitihāsapurāṇādibhiḥ saha pañcavidhatvasyāpi sambhavāt, bāhulyena sarvaiḥ prakārairvedasya kalāvutsāde 'pi vyāsāvatārātpūrvaṃ dvāpare 'pyapapāṭhādirūpotsādasya sambhavāt avirodhaḥ/
children.translated_text: — although in the <s>Smṛti</s> (traditional text) cited in the <s>Atharvaṇa-bhāṣya</s> (commentary on the Atharvaveda) it is stated that in the <s>Kṛta</s> age the Veda was one, in the <s>Tretā</s> only threefold, and in the <s>Dvāpara</s> fivefold, and also that all the Veda was lost in the <s>Kali</s> age — while here [in our text] by the statement 'the Veda having been lost,' the fourfold division is said to be in the <s>Tretā</s> age and the loss in the <s>Dvāpara</s> — there appears to be a contradiction. Nevertheless, there is no contradiction: because the statement of the Veda's oneness can be with reference to the unmanifest original mass; because even though the statement of threefoldness in the <s>Tretā</s> age is made with the intention that [the Veda] predominantly serves as the means of worship of the Lord, in reality it does not negate the existence of another form known as the <s>Atharvaṇa</s>, so another [fourth] division can also exist; because in the <s>Dvāpara</s>, though the non-human Veda is fourfold, it can be fivefold together with the human-authored <s>Itihāsa</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and the like; and because even though the Veda was largely lost in the <s>Kali</s> age in all its forms, prior to the descent of <s>Vyāsa</s>, the loss in the <s>Dvāpara</s> too in the form of faulty recitation and the like is possible.
For determining the meaning of those [Vedas], he composed the <s>Brahmasūtra</s>s.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.4:
evamupodghātamuktvā prakṛtamāha - 'tadarthanirṇayāya'; iti / teṣāṃ sarveṣām arthaḥ tam upakramādiyuktibhirnirṇetumityarthaḥ / 'brahmasūtrāṇi'; brahma vedaḥ, tadarthaḥ parabrahma vā, tasya sūtrāṇi tatsvarūpanirṇāyakānītyarthaḥ/ gītābhāṣye tu 'brahmasūtrāṇi cakāra'; ityantena vakturvyāsasya nārāyaṇāvatāratvoktyā parihṛtatvāt, brahmādīnāmarthitvoktyā ca śrotṛdoṣābhāvasya vaktari tannimittavipralambhābhāvasya coktatvāt, 'jñāna ākulībhūte tannirṇayāya'; ityanena ajñānanirharaṇasya prasaktatvena prasaṅgadoṣābhāvasya tata evānapahāsasya coktatvādāptimūlatā darśitā bhavati/ 'brahmasūtrāṇi'; ityanena brahmaparaśrutivyākhyānarūpatvāt śrutimūlatvaṃ, nyāyavyutpādakatvādyuktimūlatvaṃ ca sūcitam / tathā ca siddhaṃ brahmasūtrāṇāṃ prāmāṇyamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.4: Having stated the introduction thus, he states the main topic — 'for determining the meaning of those.' The meaning of all those [Vedas] is to be determined through reasoning such as introductory passages and the like — this is the meaning. '<s>Brahmasūtra</s>s' — <s>Brahman</s> means the Veda, or the meaning of that is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>; its <s>sūtra</s>s (aphorisms) are those which determine the nature of that — this is the meaning. In the <s>Gītābhāṣya</s> (commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā), by the statement ending with 'he composed the <s>Brahmasūtra</s>s,' the speaker <s>Vyāsa</s>'s identity as an incarnation of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> has been stated, thereby [establishing that] there is no fault in the speaker; by the statement that <s>Brahmā</s> and others are seekers [of this knowledge], the absence of listener-defect and the absence of deception caused by that in the speaker have been stated; and by the statement 'for determining that, when knowledge had become confused,' the relevance of removing ignorance and thereby the absence of the fault of irrelevance and the absence of ridicule have been stated — thus the foundation in a trustworthy source has been shown. By '<s>Brahmasūtra</s>s,' since they are in the form of exposition of <s>śruti</s> (Vedic texts) pertaining to <s>Brahman</s>, their foundation in <s>śruti</s> is indicated, and since they generate systematic reasoning, their foundation in reasoning is also suggested. And thus the authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of the <s>Brahmasūtra</s>s is established — this is the purport.

children.text:
taccoktaṃ skānde -
nārāyaṇād viniṣpannaṃ jñānaṃ kṛtayuge sthitam /
kiñcittadanyathā jātaṃ tretāyāṃ dvāpare 'khilam //
children.translated_text: And that has been stated in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]: 'Knowledge, emanated from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, was established in the <s>Kṛta</s> age; some of it became otherwise in the <s>Tretā</s>, and entirely [so] in the <s>Dvāpara</s>.' //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.5:
uktamevārthaṃ pramāṇena sthāpayati - 'tacca'; iti / 'ca'; śabda evārthe / tathā ca - yadasmābhiḥ 'dvāpare'; ityādinoktaṃ tat skāndapurāṇoktameveti bhāvaḥ / na kevalamasmābhiḥ kintu skānde coktamiti samuccaye vā 'ca'; śabdaḥ / tathoktaṃ tattvapradīpe - 'yadyapyācāryaḥ svoktārthe svayameva pramāṇaṃ, sarvajñatvādavipralambhakatvācca / tathāpi skānde coktamiti prauḍhavādaṃ karoti'; iti / 'na kevalamasmābhiḥ'; iti prameyadīpe 'pi kimuktamityatastatpaṭhati - 'nārāyaṇāt'; iti / tadupadeśādityarthaḥ / 'brahmādidvārā'; iti śeṣaḥ / yadvā - utpattyādyaṣṭake jñānasya praviṣṭatvāt tasya nārāyaṇajanyatvopapattiḥ / 'niṣpannam'; utpannaṃ 'akhilaṃ'; saguṇatvādisarvaviṣayakamityatrāpi sambadhyate / 'jñānaṃ'; samyagjñānaṃ 'sthitaṃ'; yathotpannaṃ tathaiva saṃśayādyanāskanditameva sthitam / 'satsu'; iti śeṣaḥ / jñānaviṣaye saṃśayādikaṃ nābhūditi phalitārthaḥ / 'tretāyāṃ'; yuge 'tat'; jñānaṃ 'kiñcit'; viṣaye 'anyathājātam'; idamado veti pūrvoktasaṃśayaviṣayatām anyadeveti mithyājñānaviṣayatāṃ ca prāptamityarthaḥ / atra dvāparavat tretādirapyaṣṭāviṃśo grāhyaḥ / dvāpare yuge akhilaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ tadanyathā jātamityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.5: He establishes the very meaning stated [above] with authority — 'And that.' The word 'ca' (and) is used in the sense of 'eva' (indeed). And thus: what was stated by us with 'in the <s>Dvāpara</s>' and so on, that is stated in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s> itself — this is the purport. Or the word 'ca' is in the sense of aggregation: not only by us, but also stated in the <s>Skānda</s>. Thus it is stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'Although the <s>Ācārya</s> is himself the authority for what he states, due to omniscience and non-deceptiveness, nevertheless he makes the emphatic statement that it is also stated in the <s>Skānda</s>.' 'Not only by us' — this is also read in the <s>Prameyadīpa</s>; wondering what was said, he reads — '<s>Nārāyaṇāt</s>' (from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>). Through his teaching — this is the meaning. 'Through <s>Brahmā</s> and others' is to be supplied. Or: since knowledge has entered into the eight [forms beginning with] creation and the like, the origin of that from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is justified. '<s>Niṣpannam</s>' (emanated) means 'produced'; '<s>akhilam</s>' (entire) is connected here too as meaning 'concerning all subjects including [knowledge of Brahman's] qualified nature and the like.' '<s>Jñānam</s>' (knowledge) means correct knowledge; '<s>sthitam</s>' (established) means it remained just as it was produced, unassailed by doubt and the like. 'Among [the people of that age]' is to be supplied. The resultant meaning is that there was no doubt or the like regarding the subject of knowledge. 'In the <s>Tretā</s> age,' 'that' knowledge 'in some' subject 'became otherwise' — meaning it attained the status of being a subject of the aforementioned doubt ('is this or is it that?') and the status of being a subject of false knowledge ('it is something else entirely'). Here, like the <s>Dvāpara</s>, the twenty-eighth [cycle] of the <s>Tretā</s> and the like should be understood. In the <s>Dvāpara</s> age, 'the entire [knowledge], concerning all subjects, became otherwise' — this is the construction.

children.text:
gautamasya ṛṣeśśāpājjñāne tvajñānatāṃ gate /
saṅkīrṇabuddhayo devā brahmarudrapurassarāḥ /
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ nārāyaṇamanāmayam //
children.translated_text: Due to the curse of the sage <s>Gautama</s>, when knowledge had gone to the state of ignorance, the gods — with confused intellects, led by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s> — went for refuge to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the worthy refuge, the free from affliction. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.6:
nanu kālaprayuktamanyathātvaṃ cet dvāparayuge bhāgadvayasyaivānyathātvaṃ yuktaṃ, na tu sarvasyetyato viśeṣakāraṇaṃ cāha - 'gotamasya'; iti / 'tu'; śabdaścārthaḥ śāpe viśeṣakāraṇatvasya jñāne vā samyaktvasya dyotakaḥ / tathā ca gautamasya ṛṣeḥ śāpācca jñāne guṇapūrṇatvādisamyagjñāne ajñānatāṃ nedaṃ tattvajñānamiti tattvajñānabhinnatvaprakārakapratītiviṣayatāṃ sandehaviṣayatāṃ ca gate prāpte sati, jñānaviṣaye samyagjñānaviruddhasaṃśayaviparyayaviṣayatāṃ gate satīti yāvat / 'brahmarudrapurassarāḥ'; tadādayo 'devāḥ'; 'saṅkīrṇabuddhayaḥ'; ajñānādimiśrajñāninaḥ yadviṣaye jñānaṃ jātaṃ punastadviṣayagataprakāreṣu ajñānasaṃśayādimantaḥ santaḥ 'śaraṇyaṃ'; tatra sādhuṃ śaraṇeṣu rakṣakeṣu agryam 'anāmayaṃ'; pramāṇalakṣaṇaṭīkoktarītyā atra āmayapadaṃ rogavācakaṃ doṣāntaropalakṣakam / tathā ca nirdeṣaṃ 'nārāyaṇaṃ'; "sarvottamatvavijñānapūrvaṃ tatra manaḥ sadā"ityādyuktaprakāreṇa 'śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ'; śaraṇaṃ gatā ityarthaḥ / taṃ prārthayan svakāryaṃ ca vyajñāpayanniti ca draṣṭavyam / atra brahmādibuddhīnāṃ saṅkīrṇatvaṃ nāma saṅkīrṇabuddhiṣu sajjaneṣu dayāyuktatvameva, na tvitareṣāṃ buddhīnāmivājñānādimiśratvam, ajñānasaṃśayādiviṣayaviṣayakatvaṃ vā / svahatagonirmātṛmātraviṣayakagautamaśāpakālanimittābhibhavapadoktatirodhānayordeveṣvasambhavāt / brahmādidevagonirmātṛvyatiriktalokasya tu gautamahatagonirmātṛtvābhāve 'pi sampradāyapravartakābhāvāt kālataścājñānaprāptiriti draṣṭavyam / gautamaśāpāgamaprakārastu ittham - pūrvaṃ hi dvādaśavārṣikyāṃ anāvṛṣṭau satyāṃ tayā pīḍitā ṛṣayo gautamāśramaṃ annavantam adhyūṣuḥ / tatraiva bahukālaṃ tenādṛtāḥ svasvavihitakarmāṇaḥ samavartanta / atha anāvṛṣṭau śāntāyāṃ teṣāṃ svasvāśramagamanecchā samajani / tadarthaṃ gautamamanujñāṃ yayācire / tathāpi svāśramāśūnyatālobhāt na tadanujñāmalambhiṣata / tasminnevāvasare
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.6: [Objection:] If the change is caused by time, then in the <s>Dvāpara</s> age, only a partial change would be justified, not of everything — therefore he states the specific cause — '<s>Gautamasya</s>' (of <s>Gautama</s>). The word 'tu' (but) is used in the sense of 'ca' (and), to indicate that the curse is a specific cause, or to indicate the correctness of knowledge. And thus, due to the curse of the sage <s>Gautama</s>, when knowledge — the correct knowledge of [Brahman's] being full of qualities and the like — had reached the state of ignorance, that is, had reached the status of being the object of a cognition whose mode is 'this is not true knowledge,' i.e., of being different from true knowledge, and had become the object of doubt — in other words, when correct knowledge regarding the subject of knowledge had reached the status of being the object of doubt and error, which are opposed to correct knowledge. 'Led by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>' — those beginning with them; 'gods' — 'with confused intellects' — having knowledge mixed with ignorance and the like; being possessed of ignorance, doubt, and the like regarding the very subject about which knowledge had arisen — having thus come to have modes of ignorance, doubt, and the like regarding that subject. They went 'for refuge' to the excellent among protectors; 'free from affliction' — here, as stated in the commentary on the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), the word '<s>āmaya</s>' means disease and suggests other defects as well. And thus, to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is free from [all] defects, in the manner described by 'the mind always [fixed on Him] with the prior knowledge of His supreme excellence' and the like, they went for refuge — meaning they went for protection. It should be understood that they implored Him and also made known their purpose. Here, the 'confusion' of the intellects of <s>Brahmā</s> and others means their compassion toward people of confused intellects, not the mixing of their intellects with ignorance and the like as in the case of others, nor their being the objects of subjects of ignorance, doubt, and the like — since concealment, which is described as the suppression [of knowledge] at the time occasioned by the curse of <s>Gautama</s> regarding only the creators of their own [created domains], is impossible for the gods. But for the world other than <s>Brahmā</s> and other divine creators, even without being created by the one cursed by <s>Gautama</s>, ignorance arises due to the passage of time and the absence of propagators of the tradition — this should be understood. The narrative of the curse of <s>Gautama</s> is as follows: Previously, during a twelve-year drought, the sages, afflicted by it, dwelt in the hermitage of <s>Gautama</s> which had food. There, honored by him for a long time, they carried on their respective prescribed duties. Then, when the drought ended, the desire to go to their own hermitages arose in them. For this purpose, they sought <s>Gautama</s>'s permission. But due to his attachment to keeping his hermitage populated, he did not grant them permission.

children.text: haraśirassthasurasaritaṃ sapatnīṃ matvā tāṃ niścikāsayiṣantyā pārvatyā preṣito vināyako brahmacāriveṣeṇa pracchannastānṛṣīnupasasāra, abravīcca - he tatra bhavantaḥ, kimarthamimamāśramamadhivasatha? cirakālamekaparānnāśanena yuṣmattapo vinaṅkṣyati/ tasmāt svaṃsvamāśramaṃ vrajata/ tatra ca mayocyamānamupāyamākarṇayata/ yūyaṃ jñānatapobalāt kāñcana māyāmayīṃ māheyīṃ nirmimīdhvam / tāṃ gautamatapobalākṛṣṭabalāhakāvalīvigalitasalilavardhitasasyādau praveśayata / atha sasyagrāsinīṃ tāṃ apakrāmayituṃ prayatiṣyate gautamaḥ / tataḥ sahasā tatkamaṇḍalūdakasaṃsparśamātreṇa sā nipatiṣyati / tadā brāhmaṇāstaṃ pratibrūta yāvadimāmaśeṣamātaraṃ gāṃ notthāpayiṣyati bhavān tāvanna bhojyānnaḥ / tato haraśirassthadyusaritamavatārya tadvāriṇā abhiṣicya tāmujjīvayatu bhavān ityevamanutāpinaṃ tamabhilapyāpasaratetyuktvā herambo 'mbikāṃ jagāma/ atha te vināyakena praṇigaditaṃ prayāṇopāyamupasṛtya anvatiṣṭhan/ tenaivopāyena prātiṣṭhanta / tatastāvadgautamaḥ tapasā tryambakamārādhya mandākinīṃ anusamānīya tadvāriṇā surabhimabhiṣiṣeca / tataḥ sottasthau munistaddhatyāghāt vimuktaśca / ata eva godāvarīti tasyāḥ saṃjñā samajani / atha vināyakaceṣṭitaṃ pratibudhya ṛṣibhyaścukrodha, aśapacca gautamaḥ yadasmadannanimittajñānabalādete gāṃ niramaṃsta tat jñānamapaitviti /
children.translated_text: At that juncture, <s>Pārvatī</s>, considering the celestial river on <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)'s head as a co-wife and wishing to drive her away, sent <s>Vināyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), disguised in the guise of a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), and he approached those sages and said: 'O revered ones, why do you dwell in this hermitage? Your austerity will be ruined by eating another's food for so long. Therefore, go to your own hermitages. And listen to the stratagem I shall tell you. By the power of your knowledge and austerity, create a magical cow. Bring her into the [field of] grain nurtured by the water dripping from the row of clouds attracted by <s>Gautama</s>'s ascetic power. Then <s>Gautama</s> will try to drive her away as she grazes on the grain. Then, merely upon being touched by the water from his water-pot, she will fall dead. Then you <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s should tell him: As long as you do not revive this cow, the mother of all, so long your food is not fit to be eaten by us. Then let him bring down the celestial river from <s>Hara</s>'s head and revive her by sprinkling with that water. Having thus spoken to him so as to cause him remorse, depart.' Having said this, <s>Heramba</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) went to <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>). Then those [sages], having accepted the stratagem described by <s>Vināyaka</s> as their means of departure, carried it out. They proceeded by that very stratagem. Then <s>Gautama</s>, having propitiated <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) through austerity, brought down the <s>Mandākinī</s> (Ganges) and sprinkled <s>Surabhī</s> (the cow) with its water. Then she rose up, and the sage was freed from the sin of cow-slaughter. Hence the name <s>Godāvarī</s> arose for that [river]. Then, having realized the plot of <s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>Gautama</s> became angry at the sages and cursed them: 'Since these [sages], by the power of knowledge gained through eating my food, caused harm to the cow, let that knowledge depart!'

children.text:
tairvijñāpitakāryastu bhagavānpuruṣottamaḥ /
avatīrṇo mahāyogī satyavatyāṃ parāśarāt /
utsannānbhagavānvedānujjahāra harisvayam /
caturdhā vyabhajattāṃśca caturviṃśatidhā punaḥ /
śatadhā caikadhā caiva tathaiva ca sahasradhā /
kṛṣṇo dvādaśadhā caiva
children.translated_text: When their purpose was made known, the Lord, <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person), the great yogin, descended through <s>Parāśara</s> in <s>Satyavatī</s>. The Lord <s>Hari</s> himself retrieved the lost Vedas, divided them fourfold, and again in twenty-four ways, in a hundred ways and in one way, and likewise in a thousand ways, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [divided them] in twelve ways also —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.7:
devaiḥ prārthito bhagavān kimakarodityata āha - 'taiḥ'; iti / 'tuḥ'; avadhāraṇe / 'mahāyogī'; munirūpaḥ mahāśaktirvā / 'puruṣottamaḥ'; kṣarākṣaracetanābhyāṃ uttamo 'bhagavān'; nārāyaṇaḥ 'taiḥ'; svaśaraṇāgatiṃ prāptaireva devaiḥ 'vijñāpitakāryaḥ'; san vijñāpitaṃ pratipāditam avatārādirūpaṃ kāryaṃ yasya saḥ, rūpeṇa 'mahāyogī'; nāmnā kṛṣṇaḥ 'parāśarāt satyavatyāmavatīrṇaḥ'; ityanvayaḥ / avatārānantarikaprayojanamāha - 'utsannān'; iti / 'svayaṃ'; sākṣāt 'hariḥ'; 'bhagavān'; jñānādiguṇaśālī vyāsaḥ 'utsannān'; apapāṭhādinā tirohitān 'vedān'; 'svayameva'; anyopadeśamantareṇa 'ujjahāra'; uccāraṇena vyaktīcakāra / tāṃśca prāgeva caturdhā vibhaktān vedān punaḥ 'caturdhā vyabhajat'; caturbhāgānakarot / ekaikaṃ ca bhāgaṃ 'punaḥ'; caturviṃśatyādiśākhārūpeṇa ṛgvedaṃ 'caturviṃśatidhā', yajurvedaṃ 'ekaśatadhā'; ekottaraśatākhyaikaprakāreṇa, sāmavedaṃ 'sahasradhā'; atharvaṇavedaṃ 'dvādaśadhā ca'; vyabhajadityarthaḥ / bhagavattvasya mukhyatvajñāpanāya 'bhagavān'; iti punaruktiḥ / 'eva'; śabdāḥ prakārādhikyavyavacchedakāḥ / 'ca'; śabdāḥ prakārāṇāṃ parasparasamuccāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.7: When asked what the Lord, entreated by the gods, did—he says 'by them' (<s>taiḥ</s>). The particle '<s>tu</s>' is for emphasis. '<s>Mahāyogī</s>' means either one in the form of a sage or one of great power. '<s>Puruṣottama</s>' means supreme among beings, superior to both the perishable and imperishable conscious entities—'<s>Bhagavān</s>' <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. 'By them' (<s>taiḥ</s>)—by the very gods who had attained refuge in Him. 'Having been informed of the task' (<s>vijñāpitakāryaḥ</s>)—one whose task, in the form of incarnation and the like, has been communicated and established. In form, '<s>Mahāyogī</s>'; by name, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; 'descended from <s>Parāśara</s> through <s>Satyavatī</s>'—this is the syntactic connection. He states the purpose immediately following the incarnation—'the lost ones' (<s>utsannān</s>). '<s>Svayam</s>' means directly; '<s>Hari</s>,' '<s>Bhagavān</s>'—<s>Vyāsa</s>, endowed with qualities such as knowledge—'the lost ones' (<s>utsannān</s>), meaning the <s>Vedas</s> that had been obscured through corrupt readings and the like. 'By himself' (<s>svayameva</s>)—without instruction from another—'raised up' (<s>ujjahāra</s>), i.e., made manifest through recitation. And those <s>Vedas</s>, which had been previously divided into four, he 'again divided into four' (<s>caturdhā vyabhajat</s>)—made into four portions. And each portion he 'further' divided: the <s>Ṛgveda</s> 'into twenty-four,' the <s>Yajurveda</s> 'into one hundred and one'—in the form of one hundred and one branches, the <s>Sāmaveda</s> 'into one thousand,' and the <s>Atharvaveda</s> 'into twelve'—this is the meaning. The repetition of '<s>Bhagavān</s>' is to indicate the primacy of His divine nature. The particles '<s>eva</s>' serve to exclude additional modes. The particles '<s>ca</s>' serve to aggregate the various modes mutually.
Again, for the understanding of its meaning—

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.8:
prakṛtamāha - 'punaḥ'; iti / pūrveṇaivāsyānvayaḥ / yadvā - uttareṇāpyanvayaḥ / vedavibhāgānantaraṃ ityarthaḥ / 'tasya'; vedasya 'arthavittaye'; arthajñānāya / vedānāṃ bahutve 'pi arthasyaikatvāttadvivakṣayā tān vedāniti bahuvacananirdiṣṭānāmapi vedānāṃ tasyetyekavacanena nirdeśo nānupapannaḥ, tasyetyasya samudāyaikavacanatvāt / nityasāpekṣatvāt 'arthavittaye'; iti samāsassādhuḥ / punaśśabdasyānantaryārthatvaṃ ca 'punaraprathame bhede'; ityamaroktyā 'punareva samabhyaset'; ityatra punaḥ nidrāpagamānantaramiti sudhoktyā 'tṛtīye punareva ca'; ityatra varatrayānantaramiti viśveśatīrthoktyā ca siddham / 'cakāra'; ityatrāpi 'kṛṣṇo vyāsaḥ'; ityanuṣajyate / nanu sūtrāntaraireva vedārthanirṇayasambhavātkiṃ brahmasūtrairiti gatārthatāśaṅkāparihārāyāha - 'yeṣām'; iti/ 'sūtratvaṃ'; sūtraśabdapravṛttinimittaṃ 'añjasā'; mukhyato 'stītyarthaḥ/ asya tāni 'cakāra'; iti pūrveṇa 'evaṃvidhāni'; ityuttareṇa vā anvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.8: He states the topic at hand—'again' (<s>punaḥ</s>). The syntactic connection is with the preceding [verse] itself. Or alternatively, the connection is also with what follows. The meaning is: after the division of the <s>Vedas</s>. 'Of that' (<s>tasya</s>)—of the <s>Veda</s>. 'For the understanding of its meaning' (<s>arthavittaye</s>)—for the knowledge of its meaning. Even though the <s>Vedas</s> are many, since the meaning is one, with the intention of expressing that, the designation in the singular 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>) for the <s>Vedas</s> referred to in the plural is not inappropriate, because '<s>tasya</s>' is a collective singular. The compound '<s>arthavittaye</s>' is correct because of the constant expectancy [between the words]. And the meaning of the word '<s>punaḥ</s>' as 'immediately after' is established by the statement of <s>Amara</s>: '<s>punar</s> [means] not the first, in division,' and by <s>Sudha's</s> statement: '<s>punar</s> [means] immediately after the cessation of sleep' in the [verse] 'again one should study,' and by <s>Viśveśatīrtha's</s> statement: 'immediately after three boons' in '<s>tṛtīye punar eva ca</s>.' In the [verb] 'composed' (<s>cakāra</s>), '<s>Kṛṣṇa Vyāsa</s>' is to be supplied. Now, since the determination of Vedic meaning is possible through other <s>sūtras</s> themselves, to remove the objection 'what is the need for the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>?' he says—'of which' (<s>yeṣām</s>). '<s>Sūtratva</s>' means the ground for the application of the word <s>sūtra</s>. '<s>Añjasā</s>' means primarily—this is the meaning. The syntactic connection of 'these' is either with the preceding 'composed' (<s>cakāra</s>) or with the following 'of such nature' (<s>evaṃvidhāni</s>).

children.text:
alpākṣaramasandigdhaṃ sāravad viśvatomukham /
astobhamanavadyaṃ ca sūtraṃ sūtravido viduḥ /
children.translated_text: Of few syllables, unambiguous, containing the essence, facing all directions, without padding, and faultless—those who know <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms) recognize this as a <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.9:
kiṃ tat sūtratvaṃ yadāñjasyaṃ brahmasūtrāṇāmityata āha - 'alpa'; iti / yāvadakṣaratāṃ vinā śrutyarthābhyāṃ vivakṣitārthasiddhirnāsti tadarthapratipādanāya tāvanmātrākṣaramasati niyāmake tato 'dhikākṣararahitam 'alpākṣaram'; / kecittu - alpākṣarabahvakṣarayuktaparyāyapadayormadhye alpākṣarapadopetatvaṃ alpākṣaratvamityāhuḥ / taṭṭīkānanuguṇam / evaṃ ca bhavitumarhatītyanucyamānārtham 'asandigdham'; / 'asandigdhārthaṃ nirṇītārtham'; iti tattvapradīpokteḥ / ananyalabhyottamārthayuktaṃ 'sāravat'; / bahuśākhāgatapadavākyārthanirṇāyakaṃ 'viśvatomukham'; / tattvapradīpe tu ekaṃ prayojanaṃ pratyapekṣitārthasya kṛtsnasya pratipādikaṃ 'viśvatomukham'; ityuktam / arthajñānamantareṇa gānabhāgapūraṇādiprayojanāntarārthākṣararahitam 'astobham'; / śabdārthadoṣavidhuram 'anavadyam'; / yadetāvadviśeṣaṇayutaṃ tadeva 'sūtram'; iti 'sūtravidaḥ'; sūtralakṣaṇajñāḥ 'viduḥ'; abhyupayantītyarthaḥ / atra bhāṣyanirṇayahetuśūnyavākyaṃ kuśalapuruṣoktalaukikavārtādikaṃ bhagavannāmamantrādikam arthāpratipādakatve 'pi
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.9: What is that <s>sūtratva</s> (nature of a <s>sūtra</s>) which primarily belongs to the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>? To this he says—'of few [syllables]' (<s>alpa</s>). '<s>Alpākṣara</s>' (of few syllables) means: having only as many syllables as are needed for establishing the intended meaning, which cannot be achieved without [those syllables] in terms of both scripture and meaning, without additional syllables beyond that in the absence of a constraining factor. Some, however, say that '<s>alpākṣaratva</s>' means being composed of the shorter of two synonymous words, one with few syllables and one with many. That accords with the sub-commentary. And thus, implying the meaning 'it is fit to be so,' '<s>asandigdha</s>' (unambiguous). As stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'of unambiguous meaning, of determined meaning.' '<s>Sāravat</s>' (containing the essence)—endowed with the highest meaning not obtainable elsewhere. '<s>Viśvatomukha</s>' (facing all directions)—determining the meaning of words and sentences across many branches [of the Veda]. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, it is said that '<s>viśvatomukha</s>' means 'teaching the entirety of the required meaning for a single purpose.' '<s>Astobha</s>' (without padding)—free from syllables serving other purposes such as filling a musical section, apart from knowledge of meaning. '<s>Anavadya</s>' (faultless)—free from defects of word and meaning. That which possesses all these qualifications is a '<s>sūtra</s>' (aphorism)—this is what 'those who know <s>sūtras</s>' (<s>sūtravidaḥ</s>), i.e., those who know the definition of a <s>sūtra</s>, 'recognize' (<s>viduḥ</s>), i.e., accept—this is the meaning. Here, [this definition serves] to exclude: a statement in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> lacking a reason for determination, ordinary conversation uttered by a skilled person, the names and <s>mantras</s> of the Lord which, though not teaching meaning,

children.text: ṛgakṣarāvyāptagānabhāgaparipūrakasāmagatastobhākṣarāṇi apaśabdopetatādṛśavākyaṃ ca vyāvartayituṃ krameṇa viśeṣaṇānīti padaprayojanaṃ tattvapradīpoktamanusandheyam / atra sarvatra dharmikathane 'pi taddvārā sūtrapadapravṛttinimittamapyuktamiti nāsaṅgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: the padding syllables (<s>stobha</s>) of the <s>Sāmaveda</s> that fill musical sections not covered by the <s>Ṛg</s> syllables, and such sentences containing corrupt words—[all these are excluded] by the qualifications in sequence. The purpose of each word is to be understood as stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. And here, everywhere, even though there is discussion of <s>Dharma</s>, since the ground for the application of the word <s>sūtra</s> is also stated through that [discussion], there is no irrelevance.

children.text:
nirviśeṣitasūtratvaṃ brahmasūtrasya cāpyataḥ /
yathā vyāsatvamekasya kṛṣṇasyānye viśeṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: The unqualified <s>sūtra</s>-status of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> is thus [established]; just as the <s>Vyāsa</s>-status of the one <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [is primary], while others [are called <s>Vyāsa</s>] through qualification.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.10:
nanvetatsūtratvaṃ kuto brahmasūtrāṇāmāñjasyenetyata āha - 'nirviśeṣita'; iti / 'brahmasūtrasya'; iti samudāyaikavacanam / co 'vadhāraṇe yata ityarthe ca / 'api'; śabdo mukhyasūtratvasamuccaye / tathā ca yato brahmasūtrāṇāṃ mukhyasūtratvamasti ata eva hi 'nirviśeṣitasūtratvaṃ'; nirgatā viśeṣā yasmāttannirviśeṣaṃ tathākhyātaṃ nirviśeṣitaṃ tādṛśaṃ sūtrapadaṃ yasya tasya bhāvaḥ / yadvā - viśeṣo viśeṣaṇaṃ, tasyābhāvo 'sya sañjātaḥ tādṛśaḥ sūtraśabdo yasya tasya bhāvo nirviśeṣitasūtratvam / viśeṣaṇarahitakevalasūtrapadavācyatvamasti purāṇādāvuktam / anyathā tanna syāt, vyāpakābhāve
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.10: How is this <s>sūtratva</s> primarily that of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>? To this he says—'unqualified' (<s>nirviśeṣita</s>). '<s>Brahmasūtrasya</s>' is a collective singular. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is for emphasis, and also means 'because.' '<s>Api</s>' is for aggregating primary <s>sūtra</s>-status. And thus: because the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> possess primary <s>sūtra</s>-status, therefore indeed '<s>nirviśeṣitasūtratvam</s>'—that from which qualifications have departed is <s>nirviśeṣa</s> (unqualified), that which is so designated is <s>nirviśeṣita</s>, the <s>sūtra</s>-word of which is such, the state of that [is <s>nirviśeṣitasūtratvam</s>]. Or alternatively: <s>viśeṣa</s> means qualifier; the absence of that has arisen in this—such a <s>sūtra</s>-word of which, the state of that is <s>nirviśeṣitasūtratvam</s>—the state of being denotable by the bare word '<s>sūtra</s>' without any qualifier—this exists as stated in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and elsewhere. Otherwise it would not be so, because in the absence of the pervader,

children.text: vyāpyābhāvaniyamādityarthaḥ / atrādyapakṣe tathākhyātamityarthe ṇyantātkarmaṇi ktaḥ, dvitīye taddhitaḥ 'itac'; iti vivekaḥ/ anena brahmasūtrāṇāṃ mukhyasūtratve nirviśeṣitaśabdavācyatvāditi heturukto bhavati / atra hetoraprayojakatvamāśaṅkya vyāptivacanena tāṃ parihartuṃ tatra prathamaṃ yadyannanirviśeṣitaṃ tattanna mukhyamityanvayavyāptimabhipretya tatra dṛṣṭāntamāha - 'yathā'; iti / 'eva'; ityanuvartate / tenaikaśabdārthasya mukhyatvasya vyāpakatā labhyate / tathā ca yathā ekasyaiva sataḥ kṛṣṇasya vedavyāsasya vyāsatvaṃ nirviśeṣitavyāsapadavācyatvamastītyarthaḥ / tathā ca nirviśeṣitatvānmukhyasūtratvaṃ brahmasūtrāṇāmiti vākyaśeṣaḥ / idānīṃ ye amukhyāḥ na te nirviśeṣapadavācyāḥ kintu saviśeṣapadavācyāḥ iti vyatirekavyāptimabhipretya tatra dṛṣṭāntamāha - 'anye'; iti / 'yathā'; ityanuvartate / pūrvamekaśabdaśravaṇādatrāmukhyā iti labhyate / 'vyāsāḥ'; iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - yathā kṛṣṇāt 'anye'; drauṇyādayo ye 'mukhyāste 'viśeṣaṇāt'; eva viśeṣaṇamapekṣyaiva vyāsāḥ na tannairapekṣyeṇa / tṛtīyārthe vā pañcamī, saviśeṣaṇavyāsapadavācyā eveti yojanā /
children.translated_text: there is invariably the absence of the pervaded—this is the meaning. In the first interpretation, <s>kta</s> suffix is in the passive sense from the <s>ṇyanta</s> (causative) for the meaning 'so designated'; in the second, it is a <s>taddhita</s> suffix '<s>itac</s>'—this is the distinction. By this, the reason is stated: because the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> are denotable by the unqualified word [<s>sūtra</s>], therefore they possess primary <s>sūtra</s>-status. Anticipating an objection that this reason is inconclusive, and wishing to remove it through a statement of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), he first states an example for the <s>anvaya</s> (positive) pervasion, intending: whatever is <s>nirviśeṣita</s> (unqualified), that alone is primary—'just as' (<s>yathā</s>). '<s>Eva</s>' is to be carried forward. By that, the pervasiveness of the meaning of the word '<s>eka</s>' (one) for primacy is obtained. And thus: just as <s>Vyāsatva</s> (the status of being <s>Vyāsa</s>), i.e., being denotable by the unqualified word '<s>Vyāsa</s>,' belongs to the one <s>Kṛṣṇa Vedavyāsa</s> alone—this is the meaning. And thus the sentence-remainder is: the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> have primary <s>sūtra</s>-status because of being <s>nirviśeṣita</s>. Now, intending the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative) pervasion—those that are non-primary are not denotable by the unqualified word, but are denotable by the qualified word—he gives an example for that: 'others' (<s>anye</s>). '<s>Yathā</s>' is carried forward. From the earlier hearing of the word '<s>eka</s>' (one), the non-primary status is obtained here. '<s>Vyāsāḥ</s>' is to be supplied. And thus: just as others apart from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—<s>Drauṇi</s> and others—who are non-primary, are [called] <s>Vyāsa</s> 'through qualification' (<s>viśeṣaṇāt</s>) alone, only by depending on a qualifier, not without that dependence. Or the ablative may be in the sense of the instrumental: they are denotable by the <s>Vyāsa</s>-word with a qualifier—this is the construction.
For the knowledgeable recognize the other <s>sūtras</s> as [requiring] qualification.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.11:
nanvastu brahmasūtrāṇāṃ mukhyatvaṃ, tathāpi tadanyeṣāmapyasti, na teṣāmeva, itareṣāmamukhyatve kāraṇābhāvādityāśaṅkya, tatra nirviśeṣitatvahetoḥ samavyāptipareṇa tadarthameva prāguktavyatirekavyāptidṛṣṭāntavacanenopapāditānvayavyāptikamanumānaṃ niyāmakatvenāha - 'saviśeṣaṇa'; iti / 'ataḥ'; ityanuvartate / aparāṇīti cāvartate / 'hi'; śabdo hetvarthe / tathā ca - yataḥ 'aparāṇi'; brahmasūtrebhyo 'nyāni sūtrāṇi 'aparāṇi'; amukhyāni ata eva 'vido'; jñāninaḥ 'aparāṇi'; 'saviśeṣaṇasūtrāṇi'; viśeṣaṇasahitasūtrapadavācyānīti 'viduḥ'; upajānantītyarthaḥ / tathā ca anyasūtrāṇāṃ saviśeṣaṇasūtratvāt amukhyatvameva, na mukhyatvamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.11: Granted that the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> have primary status; still, the others too have it, not those [Brahmasūtras] alone—since there is no reason for the non-primary status of the others—anticipating this objection, and in order to present the inference with the <s>anvaya</s> pervasion established by the statement of <s>samavyāpti</s> (co-extensive pervasion) directed toward it, and by the very <s>vyatireka</s> (negative) pervasion example stated earlier for that purpose, as the determining factor, he says: '<s>saviśeṣaṇa</s>' (with qualification). '<s>Ataḥ</s>' is carried forward. '<s>Aparāṇi</s>' also recurs. The particle '<s>hi</s>' is for indicating reason. And thus: because the 'other' (<s>aparāṇi</s>) <s>sūtras</s>, those other than the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>, are 'other' (<s>aparāṇi</s>), i.e., non-primary, therefore indeed the 'knowledgeable' (<s>vidaḥ</s>) 'recognize' (<s>viduḥ</s>) the 'other' [<s>sūtras</s>] as 'requiring qualified <s>sūtra</s>-designation' (<s>saviśeṣaṇasūtrāṇi</s>), i.e., as denotable by the word <s>sūtra</s> accompanied by a qualifier—this is the meaning. And thus: because the other <s>sūtras</s> possess qualified <s>sūtra</s>-status, they are indeed non-primary, not primary—this is the purport.
The word [<s>sūtra</s>] denotes the primary [work] without qualification; for the others, [it denotes] through qualification.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.12:
nirviśeṣitatvamukhyatvayoḥ saviśeṣaṇatvāmukhyatvayośca dṛṣṭāntamukhenopapāditāṃ vyāptiṃ dṛṣṭānte mukhyatvāmukhyatvayoḥ vedavibhāgagranthavistarakartṛtvatatsādṛśyādirūpānyakāraṇaprayojyatvasambhavādasiddhā vyāptirityāśaṅkāparihārāya pramāṇena sādhayati - 'mukhyasya'; iti / sāvadhāraṇametat / evam 'anyeṣām'; ityapi / tena mukhyatvāmukhyatvayorvyāpakatāsiddhiḥ / vācakatvaṃ ṣaṣṭhyarthaḥ / tathā ca yato mukhyasyaiva 'nirviśeṣeṇa'; viśeṣaṇābhāvena 'vācakaśabdo 'sti'; nirviśeṣitaśabdavācyatvamastīti yāvat / 'anyeṣām'; amukhyānāmeva 'viśeṣato'; viśeṣaṇamapekṣya, viśeṣaṇeneti vā, 'śabdo'; vācakaḥ / saviśeṣaṇapadavācyatvamiti yāvat /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.12: He establishes through a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) that was demonstrated through the example, for the primacy and non-primacy [of <s>sūtra</s>-status], between <s>nirviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being unqualified) and primary status, and between <s>saviśeṣaṇatva</s> (being qualified) and non-primary status—[anticipating the objection that] in the example, the pervasion regarding primacy and non-primacy is unestablished because of the possibility of other causes such as being the author of the Veda-division text and similarity to that. He says: 'of the primary' (<s>mukhyasya</s>). This is with emphasis. Similarly, 'of the others' (<s>anyeṣām</s>) too [is with emphasis]. By that, the pervasiveness of primacy and non-primacy is established. Denotability is the meaning of the genitive. And thus: because for the primary alone, 'without qualification' (<s>nirviśeṣeṇa</s>), i.e., without a qualifier, 'there is a denotative word'—i.e., being denotable by the unqualified word. 'Of the others' (<s>anyeṣām</s>)—of the non-primary alone—'through qualification' (<s>viśeṣataḥ</s>), i.e., depending on a qualifier, or through a qualifier, 'the word' (<s>śabdaḥ</s>) is the denotator—i.e., denotability by the qualified word.
Thus say the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>, those who understand the true meaning of words.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.13:
'iti'; evaṃ prakāreṇa 'śabdatattvārthavedinaḥ'; śabdasya yathābhūtārthajñānino 'vedavido'; vedārthajñāḥ vṛddhāḥ 'prāhuḥ'; vadantītyarthaḥ / asya "ato 'yeṣāṃ sūtratvamañjasā'; 'saviśeṣaṇasūtrāṇi aparāṇi amukhyāni'; ityuktaṃ yuktam"iti vākyaśeṣeṇānvayaḥ / 'viśeṣitaḥ'; iti kvacitpāṭhaḥ / viśeṣaṇaṃ prāpta iti tasyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.13: '<s>Iti</s>'—in this manner. 'Those who understand the true meaning of words' (<s>śabdatattvārthavedinaḥ</s>)—those who know the actual meaning of words. 'Knowers of the <s>Veda</s>' (<s>vedavidaḥ</s>)—those who know the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, the elders, 'say' (<s>prāhuḥ</s>)—this is the meaning. The sentence-completion of this is: 'Therefore, what was said—"of which the <s>sūtratva</s> [exists] primarily" and "the other <s>sūtras</s>, with qualifications, are non-primary"—is fitting.' '<s>Viśeṣitaḥ</s>' is a reading found in some [manuscripts]. Its meaning is: one that has received a qualifier.

children.text: tathā ca mukhyāmukhyayornirviśeṣaṇasaviśeṣaṇaśabdavācyatve vedo vṛddhavyavahāraśca pramāṇamityuktatvānna tayoḥ kāraṇāntaraṃ śaṅkyamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, since the <s>Veda</s> and the established usage of the elders are the <s>pramāṇa</s> (authority) for the denotability of the primary by the unqualified word and the non-primary by the qualified word, no other cause need be suspected for those [distinctions]—this is the purport.
In those <s>sūtras</s> in which all determinations are set forth—

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.14:
astvetatsūtratvamañjasā brahmasūtrāṇām / tathāpi vedārthanirṇayasya sūtrāntaraireva sambhavāt kiṃ brahmasūtrairiti codyasya kathaṃ 'yeṣām'; ityanena parihāra ukta ityatastadvākyoktaṃ vivṛṇoti - 'sūtreṣu'; iti / nimittasaptamī iyam / apiḥ abhivyāptau saṅkocanivartakaḥ / nirṇayasya sarvatvaṃ viṣayadvārā tasya ca śabdadvārā bodhyam / tathā ca yebhyaḥ sūtrebhyaḥ sarve nirṇayāḥ sarvaśākhārthanirṇayāḥ bhāvyatayā samudīritāḥ, yeṣāṃ sarvaśākhānirṇāyakatvamuktaṃ
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.14: Granted that this <s>sūtratva</s> primarily belongs to the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>. Even so, since the determination of Vedic meaning is possible through other <s>sūtras</s> themselves, how is the answer to the objection 'what is the need for the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>?' given by 'of which' (<s>yeṣām</s>)? To that, he elaborates the statement of that sentence: 'in those <s>sūtras</s>' (<s>sūtreṣu</s>). This is a causal locative. The particle '<s>api</s>' serves to extend scope and remove restriction. The 'all-ness' of the determination is to be understood through the domain [of subjects], and that [domain] through the branches [of the Veda]. And thus: from those <s>sūtras</s> through which all determinations—the determinations of the meaning of all branches—have been set forth as requiring elucidation—of which the capacity to determine all branches has been stated.

children.text: pramāṇa ityarthaḥ / yadvā nirṇīyanta iti nirṇayāḥ nirṇetavyārthāḥ / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - 'yeṣām'; iti vākye tāvat brahmasūtrāṇāmevāñjasā sūtratvamityuktam / sati caivaṃ tadantargataṃ sūtradharmatayoktaṃ viśvatoṇukhatvamapi teṣāmevāñjasā bhavati / yadā caivaṃ tadā teṣāmasaṅkucitasarvaśākhānirṇāyakatvamuktaṃ bhavet, katipayaśākhānirṇāyakatve āñjasyānupapatteḥ / yata evamataḥ sarvavedaśākhārthanirṇāyakānāṃ brahmasūtrāṇām asarvanirṇāyakebhyo 'nyasūtrebhyo 'tiśayena nirṇāyakatvāt yuktaṃ 'tasyārthavittaye brahmasūtrāṇi cakāra'; iti / tacchabdaghaṭitaṃ tadvacanaṃ tādarthyena sūtrakaraṇavacanamiti bhavati tena śaṅkāparihāra iti /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: 'in the means of valid knowledge.' Alternatively, 'nirṇayāḥ' means 'the things to be ascertained' — i.e., the objects to be determined. The purport is this: In the sentence beginning with 'yeṣām,' it has been directly stated that the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> alone have the nature of <s>sūtra</s>. And this being so, the quality of being 'directed toward all sides' (<s>viśvatomukhatva</s>), which is stated as a property of <s>sūtras</s> contained therein, also directly belongs to them alone. And when this is so, their unrestricted capacity to determine the meaning of all Vedic branches (<s>śākhās</s>) would be stated, since the direct sense would not apply if they determined only a few branches. Since this is so — since the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>, which ascertain the meaning of all Vedic branches, have a superior determining capacity over other <s>sūtras</s> that do not ascertain all — it is fitting that 'for understanding that meaning, he composed the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>.' The expression formed with the word 'tat' is a statement about the composition of <s>sūtras</s> for that purpose — thus the doubt is resolved.
Of the entire collection of words, which is both the means of knowledge and the determination —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.15:
anyeṣāmapi dvitraśākhānirṇāyakatvāt kathameteṣāmeva sarvaśākhānirṇāyakatvamityucyate? anyathā tadvaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt / tathā ca aṃśe gatārthatetyāśaṅkāparihārāyāñjasyoktyā sūcitamanyaccāha - 'śabdajātasya'; iti/ pūrvamīmāṃsādirūpasyetyarthaḥ / ata evoktaṃ sudhāyām "etanmīmāṃsopajīvinī khalu seti purāṇe paṭhyate śabdajātasyeti"iti / kartari ṣaṣṭhīyaṃ na karmaṇi / ata eva ṭīkāyāṃ śabdasamūhairiti tṛtīyā / kartṛtvaṃ ca karaṇībhūtavedetikartavyatayā / itikartavyatvaṃ ca mīmāṃsādvārā upakārakatvāt bhavati / śabdajātapadaṃ śabdapramāṇamātraparamityāśayena sambandhaṣaṣṭhīyam, sambandhaśca janyajanakabhāvaḥ iti kecit / yatpramāṇaṃ mūlaṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ / 'ca'; śabdassamuccaye, 'samudāhṛtaḥ'; ityasyānukarṣakaśca / itiśabdo 'dhyāhāryaḥ / tathā ca anyeṣāṃ dvitraśākhānirṇāyakatve 'pi bhavatyeva brahmasūtrāṇāmevānanyāpekṣāsaṅkucitasarvaśākhānirṇāyakatvam, anyakartṛkadvitraśākhārthanirṇayasya brahmasūtramūlatvena tajjanyanirṇayopajīvitvena anyeṣāṃ śrutivyākhyānarūpatvāt / yathā śrutimūlakasmṛteravaiyarthyaṃ tadvadavaiyarthyopapattermūlena mūlino vaiyarthyābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.15: To the objection 'how can the determining capacity for all branches belong to these alone, when others also determine two or three branches?' — it is replied: otherwise, there would be the contingency of their purposelessness. And so, to resolve the doubt 'would there not be redundancy in part?' — another point indicated by the direct statement is given: 'śabdajātasya' — meaning 'of that which has the form of the <s>Pūrvamīmāṃsā</s> etc.' Hence it is stated in the <s>Sudhā</s>: 'This [<s>Uttaramīmāṃsā</s>] depends on that [<s>Pūrvamīmāṃsā</s>], as is read in the <s>Purāṇa</s> regarding <s>śabdajātasya</s>.' The genitive here is in the agent sense, not the object sense. Hence in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, the instrumental 'by the collection of words' [is used]. And the agency is through the Veda serving as the instrument of what-is-to-be-done. And the what-is-to-be-done-ness arises from the helping role via <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>. Some hold that the word <s>śabdajāta</s> has its meaning restricted to word-as-evidence alone, and the genitive denotes a relation, which is the relation of product and producer. That whose root (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is that — is so described. The word 'ca' is for aggregation; and it draws forward the word 'samudāhṛtaḥ.' The word 'iti' must be supplied. And so, even though others may determine two or three branches, the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> alone have the unrestricted capacity to determine all branches independently, because the determination of the meaning of two or three branches by other authors has the <s>Brahmasūtras</s> as its root, being dependent on the determinations generated by them, and because the others have the nature of commentaries on <s>śruti</s>. Just as a <s>smṛti</s> based on <s>śruti</s> is not purposeless, similarly the non-purposelessness is justified — since the root-text is not rendered purposeless by the existence of derivative texts — this is the purport.
Having composed such <s>sūtras</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s> of great fame —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.16:
'evaṃvidhāni'; iti / añjasā viśvatomukhatvādyupetānītyarthaḥ / asyopasaṃhārarūpatvānna 'tāni cakāra'; ityanena punaruktiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.16: 'Evaṃvidhāni' — meaning: endowed directly with the quality of being directed toward all sides, etc. Since this is a concluding statement, there is no repetition with 'tāni cakāra' (he composed those).
Among the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, among humans, ancestors, and birds —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.17:
'deveṣu'; ityanena karmajājānajadevadevagandharvā api saṅgṛhītāḥ / manuṣyapadaṃ "nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ"(tai. saṃ. 2-5-11) ityādāviva mananaśīlarṣiparam / pāntīti pāḥ cakravartinaḥ / kṣīti kṣayārthasya kṣeḥ rūpaṃ manuṣyottamavācakam, teṣāmitarāpekṣayā atyalpāyuṣṭvāt / manuṣyagandharvāṇāmapyupalakṣakametat / manuṣyāśca pitaraśca pāśca kṣayaśceti vigrahaḥ / anena 'devarṣipitṛpanarāḥ'; ityuktāḥ pañcavidhā api muktiyogyāḥ saṅgṛhītā bhavanti / pakṣītyasyākhaṇḍatve pakṣiśabdo jaritāryādiyogyatiryakparaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.17: By the word 'deveṣu' (among gods), the <s>karma</s>-born, the knowledge-born, and the gods, celestial musicians (<s>gandharvas</s>) are also included. The word 'manuṣya' refers to sages endowed with the faculty of reflection (<s>manana</s>), as in 'nivītaṃ manuṣyāṇām' (<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.5.11) etc. 'Pā' means 'emperors' (<s>cakravartins</s>) — those who protect. The form of the root <s>kṣi</s> in the sense of 'perish' denotes the best among humans, because they have very short lifespans relative to others. This is also indicative of human <s>gandharvas</s>. The compound analysis is: humans, ancestors, protectors, and the perishable. By this, the five types eligible for liberation — stated as 'gods, divine sages, ancestors, celestial musicians, and humans' — are all included. If the word <s>pakṣi</s> is taken as uncompounded, it refers to animals eligible [for liberation], such as the sage <s>Jaritāri</s> and others.

children.text: jñānaṃ saṃsthāpya bhagavān krīḍate puruṣottamaḥ / ityādi /
children.translated_text: Having established knowledge, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person) plays. Thus and so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.18:
'jñānaṃ'; samyagjñānaṃ viśeṣajñānaṃ 'saṃsthāpya'; utpādya dṛḍhīkṛtveti vā / dṛḍhīkaraṇaṃ nāma jñānaviṣaye saṃśayaviparyayanirāsaḥ / tathā ca puruṣottamo mahāyaśāḥ uttamaśloko bhagavān vyāso yeṣu sūtreṣu sarve nirṇayāḥ samudīritāḥ, yeṣāṃ sarvaśākhānirṇāyakatvamuktam, tathā sarvaiḥ śabdasamūhaiḥ jaiminyādisūtrāntarātmakairnirṇāyakaiḥ smṛtyādibhiśca kriyamāṇo lokakartṛkavedaikadeśāvāntaratātāparyanirṇayo yanmūlako yajjanyasarvavedamahātātparyanirṇayamūlakaḥ tadupajīvī - taṃ vinā avāntaratātparyajñānamātreṇa muktiphalāsiddheriti coktaṃ 'yeṣāṃ'; iti pūrvavākye pramāṇe ca - evaṃvidhāni etādṛkprakārāṇi sūtrāṇi kṛtvā brahmarudrādideveṣu manuṣyapitṛpakṣiṣu jñānaṃ saṃsthāpya krīḍata iti mahāvākyayojanā / 'krīḍate parameśvaraḥ'; iti pāṭhe aiśvaryam evaṃvidhasūtrakaraṇe asāmarthyaśaṅkānirāsakatayoktamiti dhyeyam / atra brahmādiṣu jñānasaṃsthāpanaṃ nāma pūrvaṃ sthitasyaiva jñānasya viśeṣayuktyādibhiḥ dṛḍhīkaraṇaṃ kiñcidaprāptalābhaścocyate1, 'jānanto 'pi viśeṣārthajñānāya sthāpanāya vā'; iti gītātātparyodāhṛtavacanāt / na ca 'evaṃ jñānaṃ punaḥ prāpurdevāśca ṛṣayastathā'; iti bhāratatātparyaniraṇayavirodhaḥ, atra punaśśabdātsarvadevādīnāṃ ajñātavismṛtārthajñānaprāpteruktatvāditi vācyam, tasyāpyuktārthatvāt / viriñcetareṣāṃ tirohitārthajñānalābho vātrocyate, yata āhurgītātātparye ācāryāḥ - "brahmaṇastu prāyo nāpratibhāsitam"iti / 'ityādi'; ityasya 'taccoktam'; ityanenānvayaḥ / luptavibhaktiko 'yaṃ nirdeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.18: 'Jñānam' — right knowledge, specific knowledge. 'Saṃsthāpya' — having produced, or having made firm. Making firm means the removal of doubt and misconception regarding the object of knowledge. And so the great sentence-construction is: <s>Puruṣottama</s>, of great fame, the most praised, <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vyāsa</s> — in whose <s>sūtras</s> all determinations are proclaimed, whose capacity to determine all Vedic branches has been stated, and by all collections of words — i.e., other <s>sūtras</s> such as those of <s>Jaimini</s> etc. which serve as determinants, as well as <s>smṛtis</s> etc. — the determination of subsidiary purports of portions of the Vedas made by worldly authors, which is rooted in [the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>], which depends on the determination of the great purport of all the Vedas generated from them — without which, mere knowledge of subsidiary purports would not yield the fruit of liberation — this is also stated in the preceding sentence 'yeṣām,' and in the evidence — having composed <s>sūtras</s> of such a nature, having established knowledge among gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, among humans, ancestors, and birds — he plays: this is the great sentence-construction. In the reading 'krīḍate parameśvaraḥ' (the Supreme Lord plays), sovereignty is stated to refute the doubt of incapacity in composing such <s>sūtras</s> — this should be noted. Here, the 'establishment of knowledge' among <s>Brahmā</s> and others means the strengthening, through special reasoning etc., of knowledge that already existed — and to some extent the attainment of what was not yet attained — as stated in the <s>Gītā-tātparya</s> citation: 'Even those who know, [receive this teaching] for the sake of specific knowledge or for establishment.' Nor is there contradiction with the <s>Bhārata-tātparya-nirṇaya</s> statement 'Thus the gods and sages again obtained knowledge,' since there the word 'again' indicates the attainment of knowledge by all gods etc. of meanings that were unknown or forgotten — this should be stated, as that too has the stated meaning. Or here what is described is the attainment of knowledge of meanings that were concealed, for beings other than <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), since the preceptors state in the <s>Gītā-tātparya</s>: 'But for <s>Brahmā</s>, there is mostly nothing that is not manifest.' The word 'ityādi' connects with 'taccoktam' (thus it is stated). This citation is given with dropped case-endings.
Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.1 |

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.19:
pramāṇābhāvena jīvacaitanyātiriktabrahmaṇo 'bhāvāt, jīvasya ca svaprakāśatvenāsandigdhatvāt, tathā ca viṣayābhāvāt pratyagrūpe brahmaṇyahamiti pratīyamāne 'pi mokṣānuphalambhena prayojanābhāvāt tata eva tatpratibaddhādhikāryabhāvācca na brahmajijñāsā kartavyeti prāpte siddhāntitaṃ bhagavatā sūtrakāreṇa
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.19: Given the objection that inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> should not be undertaken — because, due to the absence of a means of valid knowledge, <s>Brahman</s> as distinct from the consciousness of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) does not exist; because the <s>jīva</s>, being self-luminous, is not doubtful, and hence there is no object [of inquiry]; because even when '<s>Brahman</s>' in its immediate form is cognized as 'I,' there is no fruit since liberation is not observed; and consequently there is no eligible person whose qualification depends on [a valid] purpose — in response to this, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>) has established:
Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.1 |
Oṃ — thus.
Oṃ.

children.text: idamekaṃ sūtramekamadhikaraṇam / adhikaraṇaṃ nāma viṣayasaṃśayapūrvapakṣasiddhāntaprayojanarūpapañcāṅgasamudāyaḥ / yathātraiva jijñāsādhikaraṇe "tadvijijñāsasva"iti jijñāsābhidhāyakavākyavihitā śravaṇādirūpā jijñāsā viṣayaḥ / kartavyā na veti sandehaḥ / na kartavyeti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ / asmin pakṣe ca śāstrasyānārambhaṇīyatvaniścayaḥ phalam / kartavyeti siddhāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: This one <s>sūtra</s> constitutes one <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic). An <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is an aggregate of five components: <s>viṣaya</s> (subject), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view), <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), and <s>prayojana</s> (purpose). As in this very <s>jijñāsā-adhikaraṇa</s>: the inquiry in the form of hearing etc., enjoined by the sentence 'tadvijijñāsasva' (you should inquire into that), is the subject. Whether it should be undertaken or not — that is the doubt. That it should not be undertaken — that is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view). In this view, the ascertainment that the <s>śāstra</s> need not be commenced is the fruit. That it should be undertaken — that is the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion).

children.text: tatra cārambhaṇīyatvanirṇayaḥ phalaṃ, nyāyānusandhānātmakamīmāṃsārūpajijñāsāyāḥ akartavyatve nyāyagrathanātmakamīmāṃsāśāstrasyānārambhaṇīyatvāvaśyaṃbhāvāt / evamanyatrāpi /
children.translated_text: In that [conclusion], the determination that it should be commenced is the fruit, because if the inquiry — which is the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> in the form of investigation through reasoning — were not to be undertaken, the <s>Mīmāṃsā-śāstra</s> in the form of systematic reasoning would necessarily not need to be commenced. The same applies elsewhere.

children.text: ekasyādhikaraṇasya saṅgatipañcakam / tacca - śāstrasaṅgatiḥ, adhyāyasaṅgatiḥ, pādasaṅgatiḥ, pūrvādhikaraṇasaṅgatiḥ, tadviṣayavākyasaṅgatiścetyevaṃrūpam / saṅgatirapi sāmānyato dvividhā, antarbhāvarūpā ānantaryalakṣaṇā ceti / tatra śāstrādhyāyapādairantarbhāvarūpā saṅgatiḥ / pūrvādhikaraṇatadviṣayavākyābhyāṃ tu ānantaryarūpā / sāpi ākṣepikī ātideśikī aupodghātikī āpavādikī prāsaṅgikī ityādirūpeṇa bahuvidhā / tatra pañcādhikaraṇīparyantaṃ śāstrasaṅgatimātraṃ, nādhyāyapādasaṅgatī / samanvayekṣatyoradhyāyena saṅgatisatve 'pi pādenābhāvātsaṅgatyorabhāvaḥ pañcādhikaraṇīsādhāraṇaḥ / tathā pūrvādhikaraṇatadviṣayasaṅgatī api naitadadhikaraṇasya bhavataḥ, asyaivādyādhikaraṇatvāt śrutivicārasyādyāpyanārabdhatvācca; kintvitareṣāṃ caturṇāmiti dhyeyam /
children.translated_text: Each <s>adhikaraṇa</s> has a fivefold connection (<s>saṅgati</s>). That is: connection with the <s>śāstra</s> [as a whole], connection with the chapter (<s>adhyāya</s>), connection with the quarter (<s>pāda</s>), connection with the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, and connection with the scriptural passage that is its subject — these are the five forms.
