Connection is also of two general kinds: that which takes the form of inclusion, and that characterized by sequence. Of these, the connection with <s>śāstra</s>, chapter, and quarter is of the inclusion type. The connection with the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> and its subject-passage is of the sequence type. And that too is of many kinds: by way of objection (<s>ākṣepikī</s>), by way of extension (<s>ātideśikī</s>), by way of introduction (<s>aupodghātikī</s>), by way of exception (<s>āpavādikī</s>), by way of incidental connection (<s>prāsaṅgikī</s>), etc. Of these, up to the five [initial] <s>adhikaraṇas</s>, there is only connection with the <s>śāstra</s>, not with chapter or quarter. Although the <s>Samanvaya</s> and <s>Īkṣati</s> [sections] have a connection with the chapter, [the first five] do not have a connection with the quarter — this absence of connection is common to [all] five <s>adhikaraṇas</s>. Similarly, the connections with the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> and its subject-passage also do not apply to this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, since it is the very first <s>adhikaraṇa</s> and the examination of <s>śruti</s> has not yet begun. But these do apply to the other four — this should be noted.

children.text: atra sūtre ādyantayoroṅkāraḥ uccāraṇīyaḥ tatrādya eka eva dṛṣṭādṛṣṭobhayārthaḥ ata eva sūtrāvayavaḥ sarvasūtreṣu anuvṛttyarthamasaṃhitatayoccāryate / athavā - ādau oṃkāradvayaṃ adṛṣṭārtho dṛṣṭārthaśceti / ante tu pakṣadvaye 'pi adṛṣṭārtha eka evoṅkāraḥ / adṛṣṭārthatvaṃ nāma kevalaṃ sravaṇaviśaraṇarūpadoṣaparihārārthatvam / dṛṣṭārthatvaṃ tu anvetavyapadārthapratipādakatvam / tatrādisūtrāvayavabhūtaṃ 'oṃ'; ityetat avyayaṃ brahmaśabdaviśeṣaṇaṃ guṇapūrṇatvavāci / brahmaśabdo 'pi vidvadrūḍhyā mahāyogena ca viṣṇuvācī / 'atha'; śabda ānantaryārthaḥ / yogyatayā 'adhikārāt'; iti sambadhyate / kartavyeti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca 'atha'; adhyayanaśamadamādirūpādhikārānantaraṃ 'ataḥ'; svajanmajñānajanyaprasādajanyamokṣākhyaphalayuktatvāt 'oṃ'; guṇapūrṇasya 'brahmaṇo'; viṣṇoḥ 'jijñāsā'; śravaṇādirūpo vicāraḥ kartavya iti sūtrārthaḥ / viṣṇoḥ prasādāditi 'ataḥ'; śabdasyārthāntaram / asya jijñāsādikāryaṃ bhavediti vākyaśeṣeṇānvayaḥ / oṃ brahmaśabdayorubhayoryaugikatve 'pi ekasya rūḍhatvena viśeṣyavācitvaṃ anyasya yaugikatvena viśeṣaṇavācitvamāśrityānvayāṅgīkārānnānyataravaiyarthyam / "omityetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta"tadvijijñāsasva / tadbrahmeti"ityādyanekaviṣayavākyasaṅgrahāya cobhayoḥ prayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this <s>sūtra</s>, the syllable 'Oṃ' is to be pronounced at the beginning and end. Of these, the first one alone serves both a seen and unseen purpose, and hence is a component of the <s>sūtra</s>; it is pronounced without <s>sandhi</s> (phonetic merging) for the sake of continuation across all <s>sūtras</s>. Alternatively: at the beginning there are two 'Oṃ' syllables — one serving an unseen purpose and one serving a seen purpose. At the end, in both views, there is only one 'Oṃ' syllable serving an unseen purpose. The unseen purpose means merely serving to avert the flaw of [incorrect] hearing and arrangement. The seen purpose means conveying a word-meaning to be construed. Of these, the 'Oṃ' which forms a component of the first <s>sūtra</s> is an indeclinable qualifying the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' denoting the fullness of qualities. The word '<s>Brahman</s>' too, by learned convention and by the great etymological derivation, denotes <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The word 'atha' has the meaning of sequence (<s>ānantarya</s>). By [syntactic] fitness it connects with [the word] 'adhikāra' (qualification). The complement is 'kartavyā' (should be done). And thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: 'atha' — after qualifications in the form of study, tranquility, self-control, etc.; 'ataḥ' — because of possessing the fruit called liberation, which is generated by the grace born of knowledge of one's own birth; 'Oṃ' — of the one who is full of qualities; '<s>Brahman</s>' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'jijñāsā' — inquiry in the form of hearing etc. — should be undertaken. An alternative meaning of 'ataḥ' is 'from the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' Its syntactic connection with the sentence-complement is: this [inquiry] would be the result of that [grace]. Though both 'Oṃ' and '<s>Brahman</s>' are etymologically derived, one serves as the qualified (substantive) through conventional usage, and the other as the qualifier through etymological meaning — by accepting this connection, neither is rendered purposeless. And both are employed to encompass the multiple subject-passages such as 'One should meditate on the syllable Oṃ as the <s>Udgītha</s>,' 'You should inquire into that; that is <s>Brahman</s>,' etc.
The word 'atha' has the meaning of auspiciousness and the meaning of sequence after qualification. The word 'ataḥ' has the meaning of reason.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.20:
granthādau maṅgalācaraṇasyāvaśyaṃ kartavyatvena maṅgalaprayojakatayā athaśabdaṃ vyācaṣṭe - 'atha'; iti / maṅgalaṃ vighnotsāraṇāsādhāraṇakāraṇānuṣṭheyaviṣṇusmaraṇāthaśabdoccāraṇarūpamarthaḥ prayojanaṃ yasya, tathā praśastarūpānuṣṭheyamaṅgalātmako viṣṇuḥ tadguṇo vābhidheyo yasya sa tathoktaḥ / athaśabdasya maṅgalaphalakatvaṃ tu -
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.20: Since the performance of an auspicious act at the beginning of a treatise is necessarily to be done, and since the word 'atha' serves the purpose of auspiciousness, he explains it: 'atha.' Auspiciousness — that whose purpose (<s>artha</s>) is auspiciousness — has the form of the remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is to be worshipped as the uncommon cause of the removal of obstacles, and the utterance of the word 'atha.' Or: that whose denotation is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is the auspicious one to be worshipped, of praiseworthy form, or His qualities — is so described. The capacity of the word 'atha' to produce the fruit of auspiciousness is [established by] —
'Oṃ' and 'atha' — these two [syllables] formerly [emerged] from <s>Brahman</s>;
Having burst through the throat, they came forth — therefore both are auspicious. //

children.text: iti manusmṛtisiddham / muktyarthimātrasya brahmajijñāsāyāṃ pravṛttinirasanatātparyeṇāpi prayuktasyākhaṇḍāthaśabdasya vācyamarthamāha - 'adhikāra'; iti / ca śabdo 'nuṣṭheyānanuṣṭheyākṣarārthavivakṣayā samuccaye, na kevalaṃ maṅgalaprayojakaḥ kintvānantaryābhidhāyakaśceti viṣayasamuccaye vā /
children.translated_text: — This is established by the <s>Manusmṛti</s>. He states the denotable meaning of the undivided word 'atha,' which is used with the purport of refuting the notion that only one who desires liberation alone should engage in the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>: 'adhikāra' (qualification). The word 'ca' is for aggregation, with the intention of expressing both the syllable-meaning that is to be practiced and that which is not — [it signifies]: not only is [the word 'atha'] productive of auspiciousness, but it also denotes sequence — or [the word 'ca'] is for aggregation of subject-matters.

children.text: yadvā - avadhāraṇe caśabdaḥ / tenānuṣṭheyamaṅgalārambhapraśnakārtsnyārthanirāsaḥ / tatprakārastu candrikāyāmuktaḥ / tathā cādhikārānantaryamartho 'bhidheyo yasya sa tathoktaḥ / athaśabdasyānantaryamātrārthatve 'pi adhikāretipadasya yogyatayā sambandhāt evamuktiḥ / anenānadhikāriṇo muktyarthimātrasya brahmavicāre pravṛttirnirastā bhavati / brahmajijñāsāyāḥ prayojanakāraṇaśūnyatāśaṅkānivartakatayā ataḥśabdaṃ vyācaṣṭe - 'ataḥ'; iti / 'hetvarthaḥ'; iti / heturliṅgamartho yasya, hetuḥ kāraṇaṃ prasādākhyamartho yasyeti vā, sa tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the particle 'ca' is used in the sense of emphasis (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>). By that, the view that the benediction (<s>maṅgala</s>) at the beginning must be a performed act, or that it is merely for comprehensiveness, is rejected. The manner of this is stated in the <s>Candrikā</s>. And thus, he whose meaning to be expressed is the immediate succession of the topic (<s>adhikāra</s>) is called such. Even if the word 'atha' conveys only the meaning of succession, this expression is due to the connection of the word 'adhikāra' through fitness. By this, the engagement in <s>Brahman</s>-inquiry of one who is not qualified, being merely a seeker of liberation, is rejected. He explains the word 'ataḥ' as removing the suspicion that the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> is devoid of a cause as its purpose — 'ataḥ.' 'Meaning cause' — that whose purpose is the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), or that whose purpose is the cause called grace — is called such.
And it is stated in the <s>Garuḍa Purāṇa</s> —
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 21:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.21:
nanvathātaḥ śabdapūrvakatvaṃ sūtrāṇāṃ kiṃ nimittaṃ vighnanivartakaśabdoccāraṇādeḥ "maṅgalaṃ tataḥ"iti śabdāntaroccāraṇenāpi sambhavādityāśaṅkāṃ purāṇavacanenaiva nirākaroti - 'uktañca'; iti / yadetat "athaśabdaḥ"ityādinoktaṃ tadgāruḍapurāṇe uktamevetyarthaḥ / na kevalamasmābhiḥ, kintu gāruḍe ceti samuccaye vā ca śabdaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 21:
Now, what is the reason for the <s>sūtras</s> being preceded by the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ'? Since it is possible even through the utterance of some other word as the obstacle-removing utterance and 'then the benediction' — anticipating this objection, he removes it by the very statement of the <s>Purāṇa</s>: 'And it is stated.' What has been said through 'the word atha' and so forth — that is indeed stated in the <s>Garuḍa Purāṇa</s>: this is the meaning. Not only by us, but 'in the <s>Garuḍa</s> too' — the word 'ca' is either for aggregation or [emphasis].
'All <s>sūtras</s> without exception begin with the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ' preceding them;
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 22:
they commence by rule alone — what then is the regulating factor here?'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 23:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.22-23:
kimuktamityastatpaṭhati - 'atha'; iti / yādṛcchikatvāparaparyāyāniyatatvaśaṅkāvāraṇāya 'niyatyaiva'; iti / 'nikhilāni'; ityetat 'sūtrāṇi'; ityasya saṅkocavārakaṃ viśeṣaṇam / apirabhivyāptau / evakāro 'niyamavyavṛttyarthaḥ / bhinnakramo vā / tathā ca - he 'vidvan'; ādikave 'brahman'; caturmukha 'nikhilānyapi'; vyāsajaiminyādikṛtāni sarvāṇyapyādisūtrāṇi 'niyatyaiva'; niyamenaiva kalpāntarepi 'athātaśśabdapūrvāṇi'; eva, athātaśśabdau pūrvau prathamaprayojyau yeṣu tathāvidhānyeva 'prārabhante'; sūtrakārāḥ / 'atra'; prathamaprayojyatve niyamena prathamaprayoge kenacinniyāmakena bhāvyaṃ, tanniyāmakaṃ kimiti praśnavākyayojanā /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verses 22-23:
What was said? To this he reads that: 'Atha.' To prevent the suspicion of arbitrariness, which is another name for irregularity, [he says] 'by rule alone.' 'All without exception' — this is a qualifier of 'sūtras' that prevents any restriction. The word 'api' (also) expresses comprehensiveness. The particle 'eva' is for the purpose of excluding other regulations. Or the order may differ. And thus — 'O learned one,' O sage, O '<s>Brahman</s>' (four-faced one), 'all without exception' — all the initial <s>sūtras</s> composed by <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Jaimini</s>, and others, 'by rule alone' — by rule alone, even in other <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles), 'begin preceded by the words atha and ataḥ' — they begin, the <s>sūtra</s>-authors, with those in which the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ' are first and primarily employed. 'Here' — what is the regulating factor (<s>niyāmaka</s>) for the rule of being primarily employed first? — this is the construction of the question.
'What is the meaning of each of those two, O learned one? How is their superiority?'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 24:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.24:
nanvavaśyavaktavyārthatvaṃ svarūpottamattvam arthata ādhikyaṃ vā niyāmakaṃ bhaviṣyatītyāśaṅkyādyapakṣe pṛcchati - 'kaśca'; iti / caḥ praśnasamuccaye, avadhāraṇe vā / dvitīyastuśabdārthaḥ arthasyāvaśyavaktavyatvarūpaviśeṣamāha / tuśabdapāṭhastu svarasaḥ / tathā ca - 'tayoḥ'; athātaḥśabdayoḥ ko 'sāvavaśyavaktavyo 'rthaḥ yena prāthamyamityarthaḥ / dvitīyamākṣipati - 'kathaṃ'; iti / 'uttamatā'; svarūpataścādhikyam / na kathamapītyarthaḥ / evaṃ kathaṃśabdasya praśnaparatvamaṅgīkṛtya tṛtīyapakṣapraśnaparatvenāpi kathamityetadyojanīyam / arthata iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - tayorathātaḥśabdayoḥ arthataḥ uttamatā ādhikyaṃ
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 24:
Anticipating that the regulating factor will be either the quality of having a necessarily-to-be-stated meaning, or superiority in own-form, or superiority in meaning — he asks about the first alternative: 'What.' The particle 'ca' is either for aggregating questions or for emphasis. The second 'tu'-word expresses the particular character of the meaning as necessarily-to-be-stated. The reading of the 'tu'-word is natural. And thus — 'of those two,' the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ,' what is that necessarily-to-be-stated meaning by which they come first? — this is the meaning. He challenges the second [alternative]: 'How.' 'Superiority' — superiority in own-form and in superiority. 'Not in any way' — this is the meaning. Thus, having accepted the interrogative force of the word 'how,' it is to be construed also as a question about the third alternative. 'In meaning' is to be supplied. And thus — 'how' is the superiority, i.e., the excess, of those two words 'atha' and 'ataḥ' in meaning? — this is the meaning. Here, for the first and third alternatives — the necessarily-to-be-stated meaning and the superiority in meaning — since their presence and absence are both observed in the world in other words, there is a genuine question about the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ' due to that doubt, not merely a rhetorical objection. But for the second alternative, since superiority in own-form is not observed in other words, this is indeed an objection: this should be noted. Here, it should also be noted that <s>Oṃkāra</s> is not the subject of question etc., because it is not a component of the initial sūtra of all śāstras, and because through the <s>Śruti</s> 'it flows' and the <s>Smṛti</s> 'of the one desiring to create,' and so on, it is established as being primarily of this <s>śāstra</s> alone.

children.text: kathamityarthaḥ / atra ādyatṛtīyapakṣayoravaśyavaktavyārthatārthādhikyayostadabhāvayośca loke śabdāntareṣu darśanāt athātaśśabdayostatsandehāt praśna eva na tvākṣepaḥ / dvitīyapakṣe tu svarūpādhikyasya śabdāntareṣvadarśanāt ākṣepa eveti dhyeyam / atroṅkārasya praśnādyaviṣayatvaṃ sarvaśāstrādisūtrāvayavatvābhāvāt, 'sravati'; iti śrutyā 'sisṛkṣoḥ'; ityādismṛtyā caitacchāstramātramukhyāditvena siddhatvāccetyavadheyam/
children.translated_text: Here, for the first and third alternatives — the necessarily-to-be-stated meaning and the superiority in meaning — since both their presence and absence are observed in the world in other words, the question about the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ' arises from that doubt and is not merely an objection. But for the second alternative, since superiority in own-form is not observed in other words, this is indeed an objection — this should be noted. Here it should also be noted that <s>Oṃkāra</s> is not the subject of question etc., because it is not a component of the initial <s>sūtra</s> of all <s>śāstras</s>, and because through the <s>Śruti</s> 'it flows' and the <s>Smṛti</s> 'of the one desiring to create' and so on, it is established as being primarily of this <s>śāstra</s> alone.

children.text: etadākhyāhi me brahman yathā jñāsyāmi tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Tell me this, O <s>Brahman</s>, so that I may know it in truth.'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 25:
Thus addressed by <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the best of beings, replied:
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 26:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.25-26:
'etat'; praśnākṣepaviṣayībhūtaṃ niyāmakaṃ 'ahaṃ tattvato'; yāthārthyena 'yathā jñāsyāmi'; tathā 'me'; mahyaṃ 'ākhyāhi'; brūhiti 'evaṃ nāradenoktaḥ'; pṛṣṭaḥ ākṣiptaśca 'sattamaḥ'; sajjīvottamaḥ 'brahmā'; pratyuvācetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verses 25-26:
'This' — the regulating factor that is the subject of question and objection — 'I' — 'in truth,' truly, 'so that I may know' — thus 'tell me.' 'Thus addressed by <s>Nārada</s>' — asked and challenged, 'the best of beings' — the best among good beings, '<s>Brahmā</s>' — replied: this is the meaning.
'For the succession of the topic (<s>adhikāra</s>), for the purpose of benediction (<s>maṅgala</s>), and likewise —'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 27:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.27:
jijñāsādhikārasyāvaśyavaktavyatvena taddhetutāsādhakānantaryasya jijñāsāhetostatkartavyatāhetoścāvaśyavaktavyatvāttadarthakatvāttayoḥ prathamaprayoga iti parihāramabhipretyāvaśyavaktavyārthatvaṃ athātaśśabdayordarśayati - 'ānantarye'; iti / parasparasamuccaye tathā caśabdau / evakāro bhinnakramaḥ; tenābhidheyontaraṃ vyāvartyate / tathā ca - sautrāthaśabdaḥ 'adhikārasyānantarye'; adhikāranirūpitānantaryarūpārthe tadviṣaye tanmātravācakatvābhiprāyeṇaiva sūtrakāraiḥ 'samudīritaḥ'; prayukto na maṅgalādivācakatvenetyarthaḥ / avaśyakartavyaprayojanakatvācca prathamamathaśabdaprayoga iti bhāvenāthaśabdo maṅgalārtha iti svoktārthe pramāṇaṃ darśayati - 'maṅgalārthe'; iti / caturthyarthe saptamīyaṃ, avyayaṃ vā / arthaśabdaḥ prayojanavācī / tathā ca - maṅgalarūpaprayojanārthaṃ ca athaśabdaḥ sūtrakāraissamudīritaḥ prayukto bhavedityarthaḥ/ viṣṇuvācakākāraghaṭitāthaśabdoccāraṇarūpamaṅgalasya tatsādhyatvāditi bhāvaḥ / ānantarya itivat 'maṅgale'; ityanuktvā 'artha'; iti vacanaṃ tadvaiṣamyasūcanārtham / svavākye pramāṇakramātikramastu maṅgalasya prathamamanuṣṭheyatvāt kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 27:
Intending the answer that the word 'atha' has first usage because the succession of the topic of inquiry (<s>jijñāsā-adhikāra</s>) necessarily requires statement, and because the succession — being the cause of the inquiry and the means of that duty — necessarily requires statement and therefore serves that purpose, he shows the necessarily-to-be-stated meaning of the words 'atha' and 'ataḥ': 'For the succession.' The particles 'tathā' and 'ca' are for mutual aggregation. The particle 'eva' has displaced position; through it, another meaning is excluded. And thus — the <s>sūtra</s>-word 'ataḥ' 'for the succession of the topic' — in the meaning of succession defined by the topic, in that domain, with the intention of denoting only that, 'has been employed' by the <s>sūtra</s>-authors, not in the sense of benediction and so on: this is the meaning. And since it has the purpose of necessarily being done, the word 'atha' is used first — with this intention, he shows the authority for his own stated position that the word 'atha' has the purpose of benediction: 'For the purpose of benediction.' The seventh case is used in the sense of the fourth case, or it is an indeclinable. The word 'artha' denotes purpose. And thus — the word 'atha' has been employed by the <s>sūtra</s>-authors for the purpose that has the form of benediction: this is the meaning. Since the benediction in the form of uttering the word 'atha' containing the syllable '<s>a</s>' denoting <s>Viṣṇu</s> is accomplished through that: this is the import. Not saying 'for benediction' as with 'for succession,' but saying 'for purpose' — this is to indicate the difference between them. The transgression of the order of authorities in his own statement is made because benediction is to be performed first.
'The word 'atha' and the word 'ataḥ' are employed in the sense of cause.'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 28:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.28:
evamathaśabdasya avasyavaktavyārthatvarūpaṃ prathamaprayoganiyāmakaṃ pradarśya ataḥśabdasyāpi taddarśayati - 'ataḥśabdastu hetvarthe'; iti / tuśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / heturliṅgaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca sa cāsāvartho 'bhidheyaśca tasmin tadviṣaye tadvācakatayā sūtrakṛdbhiḥ 'samudīritaḥ'; ityarthaḥ / gurvarthadīpikāyāntu "hetvarthe iti svavākye pramāṇe ca 'taddhetutvaṃ vadan'; ityuttaravākyānusārāt bhāvapradhāno nirdeśaḥ"ityuktam / tanniṣphalam / tathā ca vyākhyāsyāmaḥ / hetāvityanuktvā arthaśabdagrahaṇaṃ śabdādhikyādarthādhikyamiti nyāyena prakṛterheturarthaḥ pratyayasya tu hetutvamartha iti prakṛtipratyayobhayārthakathanārtham / yadvā - arthaśabdasyobhayatra śravaṇātsa pūrvatrāpyanuṣañjanīya iti jñāpanāya, tadarthamātraṃ bhinnamiti dhyeyam /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 28:
Having thus shown the quality of having a necessarily-to-be-stated meaning as the regulator for the first usage of the word 'atha,' he shows the same for the word 'ataḥ' as well: 'The word ataḥ [is employed] in the sense of cause.' The particle 'tu' is for distinction. Cause (<s>hetu</s>) means mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>), and it is also the meaning, i.e., what is denoted — in that, in that domain, with the denotative force, 'has been employed' by the <s>sūtra</s>-authors: this is the meaning. In the <s>Gurvarthadīpikā</s>, however, it is said: 'In the sense of cause — in this own-statement which is also the authority, following the subsequent statement "declaring its causal nature," the statement is with predominance of the verbal noun.' That is fruitless. And so we shall explain. Not saying 'for cause' (<s>hetau</s>) but taking the word 'artha' — by the principle that excess of words implies excess of meaning, the root-meaning is the meaning of cause, while the suffix-meaning is causality — this is for the purpose of stating both the root and suffix meanings. Or — since the word 'artha' is heard in both places, it indicates that it should be connected to the former also — for that purpose alone there is a difference: this should be noted.

children.text: parasya brahmaṇo viṣṇoḥ prasādāditi vā bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'Or it may be through the grace of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 29:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.29:
atra ataśśabdasyāvaśyavaktavyamarthāntaraṃ cāha - 'parasya'; iti / vāśabdaḥ samuccaye / uktaṃ hi prameyadīpe "vāśabdaścārthaḥ"iti / uktaṃ hi "yadi vā bhedabhinnayoḥ"iti viṣṇutattvanirṇayaṭīkāyāṃ
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 29:
Here he states another necessarily-to-be-stated meaning of the word 'ataḥ': 'Of the supreme.' The word 'vā' is for aggregation. As stated in the <s>Prameyadīpa</s>: 'The word vā conveys meaning.' As stated: 'Whether or of the two distinct ones' — in the <s>Viṣṇutattvarnirṇaya Ṭīkā</s>

children.text: "vāśabdassamuccayārthaḥ"iti / tathā tattvapradīpe 'pi "suptau mokṣe vā"ityatra "vāśabdassamuccayārthaḥ"iti / anena 'ataḥ'; ityetat 'a'; śabdaprakṛtikaṃ tasilantaṃ padam, prakṛtyartho viṣṇuḥ, 'prasādāt'; iti tu labdhārthakathanaṃ, kāraṇatvaṃ pratyayārtha ityuktaṃ bhavati / aparavyāvṛtyarthaṃ 'parasya'; iti / "a iti brahma"(ai.ā.2-3-8-7) iti śrutiṃ sūcayati parabrahmagrahaṇena / tatsthabrahmaśabdavyākhyānāya parasya brahmaṇa ityanuvādena viṣṇorityuktam / prasādādityanantaraṃ tajjijñāsādirūpaṃ kāryamiti śeṣaḥ / bhavedityasya ityarthe 'pi ataḥśabdaḥ ityanvayaḥ / ataḥśabdaprakṛtyarthasya phalasya yathā jijñāsākartavyatve liṅgatvaṃ, na tathā tadarthaprasādasya, kintu kartavyajijñāsāyāṃ jñānamokṣayorathaśabdārthādhyayanādau ca kāraṇatvenānvaya ityāśayena pṛthaguktiḥ / yadyapi hetvarthe ityanenaivāyamartho labhyeta, hetuśabdasya liṅgakāraṇobhayārthatvāt; tathāpi asādhāraṇāsarvanāmaprakṛtikaśabdena bodhanārtamidamityadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'the word vā has the meaning of aggregation.' And likewise in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, in the passage 'in deep sleep or in liberation,' 'the word vā has the meaning of aggregation.' By this, 'ataḥ' is a word with the root '<s>a</s>' and the <s>tasil</s> suffix; the root meaning is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'through grace' is the statement of the obtained meaning; causality is the suffix-meaning: this is what is said. 'Of the supreme' — for the purpose of excluding others. He indicates the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>a</s> means <s>Brahman</s>' (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 2.3.8.7) through the mention of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. To explain the word '<s>Brahman</s>' occurring therein, by the restatement 'of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,' 'of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' is said. After 'through grace,' 'the activity in the form of inquiry into that' is to be supplied. The construction of 'it may be' is that 'the word ataḥ [conveys] the meaning.' Just as the root-meaning's being a mark pertains to the duty of inquiry, the grace that is the fruit-meaning does not pertain thus, but rather has the connection as a cause for the inquiry that is to be performed, for knowledge and liberation, and for study and the like which are the meaning of the word 'atha' — with this intention, the separate statement. Although this meaning could be obtained through 'in the sense of cause' alone, since the word 'hetu' has both meanings of mark and cause, nevertheless, this separate expression with a word having a non-common, non-pronominal root is for the purpose of making clear — and this is not a fault.
'For He is declared to be the impeller of all mental activities.'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 30:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.30:
nanu jijñāsādyarthaṃ kiṃ bhagavatprasādena yenāsāvavaśyavaktavyārthaḥ syādityata āha - 'sa hi'; iti / 'hi'; yasmāt 'saḥ'; viṣṇuprasādaḥ prasanno viṣṇuriti yāvat 'sarvamanovṛttiprerakaḥ'; sarveṣāṃ adhikāriṇāṃ sarvasmin pūrṇe viṣṇau manovṛtteḥ prerakaḥ prāvaṇyahetuḥ 'samudāhṛtaḥ'; prāmāṇikairityarthaḥ / jijñāsāpi sākṣātpramāṇadvārā vā manovṛtteḥ prāvaṇyameva, "jijñāsāpi saiva"iti sudhokteḥ / evaṃ sarvāsāṃ manovṛttīnāṃ tatprabhedānāṃ ṭīkāsthādipadagṛhītānāṃ jñānādhyayanādīnāṃ manovṛttisādhyamokṣādeśca prerakaḥ sampādakaḥ ityapi vyākhyeyam / asya tasmāttadarthepyataśśabdo bhavediti pūrveṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 30:
Now, for what purpose is the grace of the Lord the necessarily-to-be-stated meaning? To this he says: 'For He.' 'For' — because; 'He' — the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that is, <s>Viṣṇu</s> being gracious: this is the sense; 'the impeller of all mental activities' — the cause of the inclination of the mental activity of all qualified persons toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is complete and full; 'is declared' — by the authorities: this is the meaning. Inquiry too is directly or through the means of <s>pramāṇa</s> merely an inclination of mental activity, as stated in the <s>Sudhā</s>: 'inquiry too is just that.' Thus, he is the impeller, i.e., the accomplisher, of all mental activities, their varieties as mentioned in the <s>ṭīkā</s> and other works — knowledge, study, and the like — and of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) and the like that are accomplished through mental activity: this too should be explained. Therefore, the word 'ataḥ' may be used for that purpose also — this is the connection with the preceding.
'From the supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>, when He desired to create, the two first emerged:' —
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 31:
'<s>Oṃkāra</s> and the word 'atha' — therefore they are first in order.'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 32:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.31-32:
nanu maṅgalācaraṇādeḥ "maṅgalaṃ tataḥ"iti śabdāntareṇāpi sambhavātkimetatprayoganiyatyeti kṛtacodyasya kaḥ parihāra ityato na kevalamavaśyavaktavyārthatvādathātaḥśabdayoḥ prathamaprayogaḥ, kintu svarūpādhikyāccetyāśayena 'kathamuttamatā'; ityasyottaratvena tayoḥ svarūpādhikyamāha - 'sisṛkṣoḥ'; iti / śabdayoṛ samuccaye ādyaḥ caśabdaḥ / nimittasamuccaye dvitīyaḥ / 'svarūpottamau'; iti śeṣaḥ / 'tasmāt'; ityāvartate / tathā ca yasmāt 'sisṛkṣoḥ'; sraṣṭumicchoḥ 'paramāt'; sarvottamāt 'viṣṇoḥ'; tanmukhāt 'prathamaṃ'; svasamānajātīyaśabdāntarotpatteḥ pūrvaṃ oṅkāro 'tha śabdaścetyetau kaṇṭhaṃ bhittvā 'vinissṛtau'; viniryātau, tasmātsvarūpottamau, tasmātsvarūpottamatvādeva 'prāthamikau'; prathamaṃ prayojyāviti yojanā / atrākṣepāviṣayasyāpyoṅkārasya svarūpādhikyoktirbrahmamīmāṃsāśāstramātramukhyāmukhyāditvavivakṣayā pravṛttaṃ 'sarva ete'; iti vakṣyamāṇamanusṛtyeti draṣṭavyam / nanu dvayorekavidhaṃ prāthamikatvaṃ viruddhamityata uktaṃ 'kramāt'; iti / ādimadhyakramādityarthaḥ / tatroṅkārasya mukhyaṃ prāthamikatvaṃ, athaśabdasya dvitīyatayā mukhyamiti dhyeyam /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.31-32: [Objection:] Since the auspicious invocation and the like can be accomplished even by other words such as 'may there be auspiciousness,' what is the answer to the objection 'what is the necessity of using these [particular words]?' — Therefore, not only because they have a meaning that must necessarily be stated is there the initial use of the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s>, but also because of the superiority of their essential nature — with this intention, as an answer to 'how is there superiority,' he states the superiority of the essential nature of those two — '<s>sisṛkṣoḥ</s>' (of one desiring to create). The first 'ca' (and) is in the sense of aggregation of the words. The second is in the sense of aggregation of causes. 'Of superior essential nature' is to be supplied. 'Therefore' recurs. And thus: since from the Supreme — the most excellent — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, from his mouth, 'first' — before the arising of any other word of the same kind — <s>Oṃkāra</s> and the word <s>atha</s> emerged, breaking through the throat — therefore they are of superior essential nature; and therefore, because of their superior essential nature alone, they are 'primary' — to be used first. This is the construction. Here, the statement of the essential superiority of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, even though it is not the object of the objection, should be understood as following what will be stated later as 'all these' — with the intention of discussing the primary and non-primary status with respect to the <s>Brahma-mīmāṃsā</s> treatise alone. [Objection:] The same kind of primacy for two is contradictory — therefore it is said 'in sequence.' The meaning is: in the order of beginning and middle. There, <s>Oṃkāra</s> has primary primacy, while the word <s>atha</s> has primacy as being [positioned] second — this should be noted.
And the third [word] <s>ataḥ</s> is cited as speaking of being the cause of that.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.33:
athaśabdasya oṅkāreṇa saha svarūpādhikayamabhidhāya ataḥśabdasyāpi tadāha - 'tat'; iti / 'taddhetutvaṃ vadan'; iti 'hetvarthe'; ityasyānuvādaḥ / sa coddeśyasamarpakasya ata ityasya śabdaparatvajñāpanadvārā tṛtīyatayoktatvādividhānārthaḥ anyathā svarūpādhikyakathanadaśāsaṅgatiḥ syāt / yadyapi purovādānusārāt 'taddhetutvaṃ vadan'; iti suvacam; tathāpi hetuśabdasya liṅgārthatvapakṣe tatsvarūpaṃ vivarituṃ kāraṇārthatvapakṣe tatkāryaṃ tasipratyayārthaṃ ca pradarśayituṃ 'taddhetutvaṃ vadan'; ityuktam / atrātaḥśabdo 'sakṛdāvartate / tatraikaśśabdaparaḥ, anyo hetau, aparo viṣṇuparaḥ / atra śabdaparasyātaśśabdasya samuccayārthena apiśabdenānvayaḥ / co yata ityarthe / 'tṛtīyaḥ udāhṛtaḥ'; ityanayorāvṛttiḥ / 'prāthamikau'; ityasya vacanavyatyayenānuṣaṅga / tṛtīyaśabdo bhāvapradhānaḥ, vibhaktivyatyayaśca / tathā ca na kevalamoṅkārāthaśabdau, kintu 'taddhetutvaṃ'; tasya prasannasyākāravācyasya viṣṇostatra jijñāsādau kāraṇatvaṃ tasipratyayena vadanprakṛtyaiva tasya jijñāsādermokṣahetutvarūpaṃ liṅgaṃ vā vadan 'ataḥ'; sarvanāmāsarvanāmaprakṛtiko 'taśśabdo 'pi yato viṣṇoḥ 'tṛtīyaḥ'; tṛtīyatayā 'udāhṛtaḥ'; uccāritaḥ ataḥ so 'pi svarūpottamaḥ ; yata evamato 'taśśabdo 'pi tṛtīyatayā prāthamika udāhṛta iti yojanā / tathā ca - maṅgalaśabdena maṅgaloktāvapi tasya svarūpādhikyānukteḥ athātaḥśabdābhyāmivādhikāraprayojanayoranukteśca na tena gatārthatā, adhikāraprayonasūcanārthaṃ tayoravaśyāpekṣitatvāt / ata eva ṭīkāyāṃ "maṅgaloktyādeḥ"ityādiśabdaḥ tataśśabdena hetvānantaryapratiyogyadhikārasūcane 'pi na tasyādisūtre niveśā yuktaḥ, tasya svarūpādhikyānuktereveti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.33: Having stated the superiority of the essential nature of the word <s>atha</s> together with <s>Oṃkāra</s>, he states that of the word <s>ataḥ</s> as well — 'tat' (that). 'Speaking of being the cause of that' is a paraphrase of '[it is used] in the sense of reason.' And it [is stated] to indicate that the word <s>ataḥ</s>, which presents the intended subject, is spoken as third — for the purpose of enjoining; otherwise, there would be incongruity in the context of stating essential superiority. Although 'speaking of being the cause of that' is well-said following the prior discussion, nevertheless 'speaking of being the cause of that' is said in order to elaborate its essential nature when the word <s>hetu</s> (reason) is taken in the sense of a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>), and to show its effect and the meaning of the <s>tasi</s> suffix when taken in the sense of cause. Here the word <s>ataḥ</s> recurs several times. Among them, one refers to <s>śabda</s> (word), another to <s>hetu</s> (reason), and another to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Here, the word <s>ataḥ</s> referring to <s>śabda</s> connects with the word <s>api</s> (also) in the sense of aggregation. 'Ca' is in the sense of 'yataḥ' (because). 'Third' and 'cited' are repeated. 'Primary' is carried forward with a change of number. The word 'third' has <s>bhāva</s> (state) as primary, and there is a change of case-ending. And thus: not only <s>Oṃkāra</s> and <s>atha</s>, but the word <s>ataḥ</s> too — since it 'speaks of being the cause' — that is, speaking through the <s>tasi</s> suffix of the causality of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the gracious one denoted by the phoneme <s>a</s>, in the inquiry and the like, or speaking the logical mark which is the nature of the inquiry and the like being the cause of liberation — 'ataḥ,' the word <s>ataḥ</s> formed from a pronominal base, is also, because it was uttered from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'cited as third'; therefore it too is of superior essential nature. Since the word <s>ataḥ</s> is thus cited as primary in the third position — this is the construction.
The phoneme <s>a</s> is the essence of all speech and the designator of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.34:
na kevalamavaśyavaktavyārthatvāt nāpi svarūpādhikyāt athātaśśabdayoḥ prathamaprayogaḥ, kintvavayavārthataśca / ato 'pi prathamaprayoga iti bhāvena kathamiti tṛtīyapraśnasya prākarāntareṇottaramāha - 'akāraḥ'; iti / tayorityanuvartate / tathā ca - athātaśśabdayossambandhī 'akāro'; yataḥ 'sarvavāgātmā'; 'tasmātsarvaguṇān viṣṇoḥ akāro vakti yatprabhoḥ'; ityaitareyabhāṣyadiśā sarvāsāṃ vācāmartho yatpūrṇatvaṃ tadabhidhāyakaḥ, ataḥ parabrahmābhidhāyakaḥ guṇapūrṇatvadharmiṇa eva parabrahmatvāt, dharmadharmiṇorabhedācceti bhāvaḥ/
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.34: Not only because they have a meaning that must necessarily be stated, nor only because of the superiority of their essential nature, is there the initial use of the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s>, but also because of the meaning of their component parts. Hence 'from this too there is initial use' — with this purport, he states the answer to the third question 'how?' in another way — '<s>akāraḥ</s>' (the phoneme <s>a</s>). 'Of those two' is carried forward. And thus: the phoneme '<s>a</s>,' which is related to the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s>, since it is 'the essence of all speech' — in the direction of the <s>Aitareyabhāṣya</s> [statement] 'therefore the phoneme <s>a</s> speaks all the qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord' — it is the designator of the meaning of all words, which is plenitude; therefore it is 'the designator of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — since the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> is indeed the possessor of the quality of plenitude, and since there is no difference between a quality and its possessor — this is the purport.
Likewise, [the phonemes] <s>tha</s> and <s>ta</s> are said to be of the nature of <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), ordaining pervasion and stability.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.35:
evaṃ tayoḥ 'tathau'; taśca thaśca varṇau 'prāṇātmakau'; prāṇau, doṣātmakaḥ doṣa itivat / viśeṣaṇayoḥ pratyekamanvayaḥ / prāṇaśabdo vāyuviṣṇūbhayavācī / "mahataścaturmukhāt"itivat abhimānyabhimanyamānayoḥ, "ayaṃ vai lokaḥ prathamā mahānāmnī"( ) itivadvācyavācakayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyena aikyavyapadeśaḥ / asya nirūḍhatvajñāpanāya 'ātmaka'; śabdaḥ / proktāviti vācyatvābhimānitvayoḥ prāmāṇikatvamāha / kramabhaṅgastu vargakramānusārāt uccāraṇalāghavācca kṛtaḥ / paramātmavācitvaṃ ca tadguṇadvāretyāha - 'vyāpti'; iti / tasyeti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - tasya akāravācyasya parabrahmaṇo vyāptisthityabhidāyakau ityarthaḥ / tathayoretatkrameṇa yojanīyam / atrākārārtho guṇavyāptiḥ, takārārtho deśakālavyāptiḥ, thakārasya tu avikāreṇa avasthitirartha ityarthabhedo jñātavyaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - 'tathau prāṇātmakaṃ prāptau'; iti pāṭhabhedamaṅgīkṛtya prāṇātmakaṃ prāṇapraṇetāraṃ viṣṇuṃ vācakatvena prāptāviti vyākhyātam / yadyapi sūtre praviṣṭasya sarvanāmaprakṛtikasya ataśśabdasya naivamavayavārthakathanaṃ yujyate, asarvanāmaprakṛtikasya tu 'parasya'; ityanenaiva arthata ādhikyaṃ coktam / tathāpi athaśabdasya arthata ādhikyānukteḥ tadgatavarṇayoḥ asarvanāmaprakṛtikātaśśabdagatavarṇayośca vākyārthāpraviṣṭātiśayitārthāntaroktiriyamityadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.35: Thus 'of those two' — 'likewise' — the phonemes <s>ta</s> and <s>tha</s> are 'of the nature of <s>Prāṇa</s>' — that is, they are <s>Prāṇa</s>, just as one says 'of the nature of fault' means 'fault.' The qualifiers connect with each [phoneme] individually. The word <s>Prāṇa</s> denotes both <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) and <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Just as in 'from the great four-faced one' — the designation of unity through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of the presiding deity and the one presided over, and of the signified and the signifier, as in 'this world is indeed the first <s>Mahānāmnī</s>.' The word '<s>ātmaka</s>' (of the nature of) is to indicate that this [usage] is well-established. That they are 'said' indicates the authoritativeness of both the signified and the presiding [deity] status. The break in sequence is made following the order of phonemic classes and for ease of pronunciation. That they designate the Supreme Self is through His qualities — this he states: '<s>vyāpti</s>' (pervasion). 'Of that' is to be supplied. And thus: they designate the pervasion and stability of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> denoted by the phoneme <s>a</s> — this is the meaning. The 'likewise' connects them in this order. Here, the meaning of the phoneme <s>a</s> is pervasion of qualities; the meaning of <s>ta</s> is pervasion of space and time; and the meaning of <s>tha</s> is stability without transformation — this distinction of meaning should be known.

children.text: ataśca pūrvamuccāryāḥ sarva ete satāṃ matāḥ /
children.translated_text: And therefore all these should be uttered first — this is the view of the good.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.36:
astvevaṃ, tataḥ kimityata āha - 'ataśca'; iti / co 'vadhāraṇe samuccaye ca / tatra athātaśśabdaviṣaye samuccayaḥ, oṅkāraviṣaye tu svarūpata ādhikyādevetyavadhāraṇārthateti dhyeyam / 'ete'; ityasya vivaraṇaṃ 'sarve'; omathātaśśabdā iti / 'ataḥ pūrvaṃ'; etacchāstrādāviti ataśśabdāvṛttyā anvayaḥ / 'kramāt'; ityatrāpi sambadhyate / 'uccāryāḥ'; ityevaṃ 'satāṃ'; janānāṃ sammatā ityarthaḥ / yadvā - 'satāṃ'; mukhyānāṃ brahmasūtrāṇāṃ pūrvaṃ ādisūtre ityarthaḥ / na cātra "sakalasūtrakārairevameva prayuktatvāt"iti sudhāvirodhaḥ, tasyāthātaśśabdamātraviṣayatvāt / ata eva "etau"iti pūrvamuktvā sakalasūtrakārairevamevetyuktam, kramāntaraṃ vihāyāvādāvevetyarthaḥ / athaśabdasya sūtrakṛteti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.36: 'Let it be so, then what follows from it?' — to this he says: 'and therefore.' 'Ca' is in the sense of emphasis and aggregation. There, regarding the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s>, it is aggregation; but regarding <s>Oṃkāra</s>, it is emphasis — meaning 'because of superiority of essential nature alone' — this should be noted. 'These' is explained by 'all' — <s>Om</s>, <s>atha</s>, and <s>ataḥ</s>. 'Therefore first' — at the beginning of this treatise — this is the construction with the recurrence of the word <s>ataḥ</s>. It also connects with 'in sequence.' 'Should be uttered' — thus 'of the good' means 'approved by people.' Alternatively, 'of the good' — before the principal <s>Brahmasūtra</s>s, that is, in the first <s>sūtra</s>. And there is no contradiction with the <s>Sudhā</s> [commentary's statement] 'since all <s>sūtra</s>-composers have used them in exactly this way,' because that relates only to the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s>. Hence, having first said 'these two,' the statement 'used by all <s>sūtra</s>-composers in exactly this way' was made — meaning 'abandoning the other sequence, at the very beginning only.' Of the word <s>atha</s>, 'by the <s>sūtra</s>-composer' is to be supplied.
Having thus truly understood the power of the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s>,
the greatly wise use those very [words] at the beginning of their <s>sūtra</s>s. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.37-38:
tatkimatretyādipraśnottaramupasaṃharati - 'atha'; iti / tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe viśeṣe ca / 'evaṃ'; iti uktaprakāreṇa 'vīryaṃ'; svarūpādhikyādimāhātmyaṃ 'ājñāya'; tattvato vijñāya 'sūtreṣu'; vicāraśāstrādiṣu sarveṣu 'tau'; athātaśśabdāveva natvanyaṃ 'ādau'; prathamameva 'prayuñjate'; prayogaṃ kurvantītyarthaḥ / 'mahāprājñāḥ'; ityanena sūtrakṛtāṃ śabdamārātmyatattvajñāne asāmarthyaṃ nivārayati / evakāraḥ sarvaśāstrādisūtravivakṣayoṅkāravyavacchedakaḥ / ata eva 'ataśca'; iti trayāṇāṃ prakṛtatvepi oṅkāravaiṣamyajñāpanāya athātaśśabdayorevoktiḥ / ata eva athātaśśabdaviṣaye upakramopasaṃhārayoḥ 'nikhilāni sūtrāṇi'; 'sūtreṣu'; iti sarvasūtroktiḥ, oṅkāraviṣaye tu tadanuktiḥ / athaśabdasyoṅkāreṇa saha pāṭhe 'pi na sārvatrikatvaṃ, upakramopasaṃhāravirodhāt / iti śabdasya uktamityanenānvayaḥ //
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.37-38: He concludes the questions and answers beginning with 'then what [is the purpose] here' — '<s>atha</s>.' The word 'tu' is in the sense of emphasis and specification. 'Thus' — in the manner described; 'power' — the greatness of superiority of essential nature and the like; 'having understood' — having truly known; 'in the <s>sūtra</s>s' — in all investigative treatises and the like; 'those' — the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s> alone and not others; 'at the beginning' — at the very first; 'they use' — they employ — this is the meaning. By 'greatly wise,' he removes [the doubt about] the <s>sūtra</s>-composers' incapacity in knowing the true greatness of words. The word 'eva' (alone) excludes <s>Oṃkāra</s> with the intention of [discussing] all treatises and other <s>sūtra</s>s. Hence, even though in 'and therefore' all three are under discussion, the statement is made only about the words <s>atha</s> and <s>ataḥ</s>, to indicate the distinctness of <s>Oṃkāra</s>.
And the qualification [of the student] is stated in the <s>Bhāgavatatantra</s> —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.39:
athaśabdo 'dhikārānantaryaṃ vaktītyuktaṃ; tatra kosāvadhikāro brahmajijñāsāyāṃ, katividhaśca sa ityata āha - 'adhikāraḥ'; iti / caśabdo na kevalamadhikāraḥ kintu tadvibhāgaśca bhāgavatatantrākhyagranthe 'bhihita iti samuccaye / atra pramāṇe adhikārikathane 'pi tadviśeṣaṇatayā devatvādirūpo 'pyadhikāraḥ ukto bhavatīti nāsaṅgatiḥ/
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.39: It was stated that the word <s>atha</s> indicates [the topic following] after the qualification; then, what is that qualification for the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>, and of how many kinds is it? — to this he says: 'the qualification.' The word 'ca' means: not only the qualification but its division too is stated in the text called <s>Bhāgavatatantra</s> — [this is] in the sense of aggregation. Here, even though in the authoritative text the discussion of qualification [is the main topic], since the qualification in the form of being a god and the like is also stated as its qualifier, there is no incongruity.
There are three kinds of qualified [students], by [the distinction of] inferior, middling, and superior.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.40:
kathamityatastadvākyaṃ paṭhati - 'manda'; iti / tvaḥ pratyekaṃ sambadhyate / itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇe tṛtīyā / hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.40: 'How?' — to this, he reads that passage — '<s>manda</s>' (inferior). The suffix '<s>tva</s>' connects with each individually. The third case-ending is in the sense of <s>itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇa</s> (characterization by such nature). The particle '<s>hi</s>' is in the sense of being well-known.

children.text: tatra mandā manuṣyeṣu ya uttamagaṇā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: There, those who are considered the best group among humans are the inferior [qualified students].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.41:
'tatra'; trividheṣu madhye manuṣyeṣu ye uttamagaṇāḥ te mokṣayogyeṣu mandādhikāriṇa ityuddeśyavidheyabhāvo draṣṭavyaḥ / evaṃ uttaratrāpi / gaṇaśabdena puruṣārthanayoktatrividhamanuṣyottamā gṛhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.41: 'There' — among the three kinds, those who are the best group among humans are the inferior qualified students among those eligible for liberation — this subject-predicate relationship should be noted. Similarly in what follows. By the word 'group' (<s>gaṇa</s>), the three [types of] best humans mentioned according to the doctrine of the <s>puruṣārtha</s>s (human goals) are included.
The middling are <s>ṛṣi</s>s (sages) and <s>gandharva</s>s (celestial musicians); the gods are considered the superior among those.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.42:
ṛṣayaśca gandharvāśca 'ṛṣigandharvāḥ'; / bahuvacanamādyarthe / tena pitṛpayorgrahaṇam / 'tatra'; triṣu / punaḥ 'tatra'; ityasya 'evaṃvidhāni'; itivadupasaṃhārarūpatvānna punaruktiḥ / yadvā - prathamasya 'tatra'; ityasya brahmajijñāsāyāmityarthaḥ / ata evoktaṃ ṭīkāyāṃ "brahmajijñāsāyāṃ"iti / tathā ca - 'tatra'; brahmajijñāsāyāmadhikāriṇastrividhāḥ, 'tatra'; trividheṣvityanvayaḥ / athavā "itiśabdaḥ pratyekaṃ abhisambadhyate, ata eva dvirgrahaṇaṃ"iti tatvodyotaṭīkārītyā madhyameṣvanuṣaṅgasūcanāyādyantayostatretyuktiḥ / 'tatra'; teṣāmadhikāriṇām //
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.42: <s>Ṛṣi</s>s and <s>gandharva</s>s are '<s>ṛṣigandharvāḥ</s>.' The plural is in the sense of the first [member of the compound]. By that, <s>pitṛ</s>s (ancestors) and [other] pairs are included. 'There' — among the three. Again, 'there' — this is not repetition since it is in the form of a conclusion, like 'of such kinds.' Alternatively, the first 'there' means 'in the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>.' Hence it is said in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> (sub-commentary) 'in the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>.' And thus: 'there' — in the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>, the qualified students are of three kinds; 'there' — among the three — this is the construction.
Thus the distinction is based on birth (<s>jāti</s>), and there is another based on qualities (<s>guṇa</s>).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.43:
'iti'; evaṃ 'jātikṛto'; manuṣyarṣidevatvādirūpasāmānyanimittakaḥ tattatkulajaninimitto vā 'bhedaḥ'; avāntaravibhāgaḥ anyonyābhāvo vā jñeya ityarthaḥ / anena mokṣayogyatvaṃ vaidikabrahmavidyādhikārisāmānyalakṣaṇamabhipretam / nanvidaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ sacchūdrādau ativyāptam / na ca sacchūdrāderviprādidehāntare brahmavidyādhikāritvānnātivyāptiriti vācyam, dehāntare sato 'pi adhikārasyedānīntanapravṛttyanupayogitvāt, taddehāvacchedena tu anutpannabrahmāparokṣajñānitvenāsyābhāvaniścayāt / tathā ca sacchūdrādāvasyādhikārasya prāyikatvādbāhulakatvāt, ata evaitaddehe 'bhāvāt ata evālakṣyatvāt, asya ca mokṣayogyatvasya svarūpatvenānadhikāraḥ daśāyāmapi sattvādvyāpterdhrauvyādityataḥ prakārāntareṇa adhikāriṇaḥ svarūpamāha - 'tathā'; iti / samuccayārthoyam / 'anyo'; jātikṛtabhedādbheda ityasti 'guṇapūrvako'; bhaktyadhyayanādiśubhadharmanimitto 'stīti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.43: '<s>Iti</s>'—thus. '<s>Jātikṛtaḥ</s>'—caused by birth-class, i.e., the general ground in the form of being human, sage, or divine, or the cause arising from birth in specific families. '<s>Bhedaḥ</s>'—a subordinate division, or mutual absence—this is the meaning. By this, fitness for liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is intended as the general characteristic of those qualified for Vedic <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of Brahman). [Objection:] But this definition is over-extensive, as it applies also to virtuous <s>Śūdras</s> and others. Nor can it be said that there is no over-extension because a virtuous <s>Śūdra</s> has qualification for <s>Brahmavidyā</s> in a subsequent body as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the like—since even though the qualification exists in a future body, it is of no use for current practice; and since, by the delimitation of that [current] body, the absence of this [qualification] is certain because one has not yet attained direct knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. Moreover, since the qualification of a virtuous <s>Śūdra</s> and others in this respect is only probable and frequent, and therefore absent in this [current] body and hence not a defining mark—and since this fitness for liberation, being of the essential nature [of the self], exists even in the state of non-qualification due to [its] pervasiveness and permanence—therefore, he states the essential nature of the qualified person in another way: '<s>tathā</s>' (likewise). This is in the sense of aggregation. 'Another' (<s>anya</s>)—there is a distinction from the birth-based distinction—'preceded by qualities' (<s>guṇapūrvakaḥ</s>), i.e., caused by auspicious qualities such as devotion, study, and the like—this is the remainder.
A person who has devotion to the supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s> and is learned in the [Vedic] study—
the lowest; one endowed with tranquility (<s>śama</s>) and the like is declared the middling.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.44-45:
tameva darśayati - 'bhaktimān'; iti / pūrvamuddeśavākye bahuvacananirdeśepyatra 'naraḥ'; ityādyekavacananirdeśo nānupapannaḥ, asya lakṣaṇavākyatvāt, "pramāṇāni"ityuddeśavākye bahuvacananirdeśe 'pi "pramākaraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ"ityekavacanena lakṣaṇoktivat / atra - avaiṣṇavasya vede 'pi hyadhikāro na vidyate /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.44-45: He shows that very [qualified person]: '<s>bhaktimān</s>' (one who has devotion). Although in the prior introductory sentence the designation was in the plural, here the singular designation '<s>naraḥ</s>' (a person) is not inappropriate, because this is a definitional sentence—just as when in the introductory sentence '<s>pramāṇāni</s>' (means of valid knowledge) the designation is in the plural, the definition is given in the singular '<s>pramākaraṇaṃ pramāṇam</s>' (the instrument of valid cognition is the means of valid knowledge). Here [it is said]: 'Even for one who is not a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, there is no qualification even in the <s>Veda</s>;
nor for one devoid of devotion to the guru, nor for one lacking tranquility (<s>śama</s>) and the like.' //

children.text: ityukteḥ / adhyayanalabdhāpi viṣṇubhaktiḥ śamādikañca abhaktānadhikārikṛtādhyayanaśamādinivṛtyarthaṃ pṛthamuktam / ādiśabdena "śānto dāntaḥ"ityuktānāṃ grahaṇam / sāranityasamuccaye cāpiśabdau / 'iti'; iti śeṣaḥ / 'naro'; bhaktajanaḥ / asya sarvatra sambandhaḥ / tathā ca - yo naraḥ parame viṣṇau bhaktimān adhyayanavāṃśca so 'dhamo 'dhikārīti prāmāṇikaiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ / yaḥ śamādisaṃyukto naraḥ sa madhyama iti proktaḥ //
children.translated_text: —thus it is stated. Even devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> gained through study, and tranquility and the like, are separately stated to exclude [qualification through] study and tranquility gained by a non-devotee who is otherwise unqualified. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like), the inclusion of those stated as 'peaceful, self-controlled' is indicated. The particles '<s>ca</s>' and '<s>api</s>' are for aggregation of essential and constant [qualities]. '<s>Iti</s>' is a remainder. '<s>Naraḥ</s>' means a devoted person. This connects to all [the qualifications]. And thus: the person who has devotion to the supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s> and is learned in study—he is the lowest (<s>adhama</s>) qualified person, as stated by authoritative teachers. The person who is endowed with tranquility (<s>śama</s>) and the like—he is declared the middling. //
[One who knows that] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, [all] is without essence and impermanent—

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.46:
yaḥ 'ābrahmastambaparyantaṃ'; caturmukhamārabhya tṛṇajīvaparyantaṃ jīvajātaṃ 'asāraṃ'; asarvottamaṃ, asārapadaṃ mokṣadavaraparaṃ vā 'anityakaṃ'; anityaṃ brahmādijīvānāṃ dehanāśe 'pi svarūpanāśābhāvāt kapratyayaḥ / parabrahma tu sarvasāraṃ sarvathā nityaṃ ceti /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.46: [The one who knows that] '<s>ābrahmastambaparyantam</s>'—the entire class of living beings, beginning from the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> down to grass-dwelling creatures—is '<s>asāra</s>' (without essence), meaning not the supreme, or devoted to lower [goals] than liberation. '<s>Anityaka</s>'—impermanent; since even upon the destruction of the bodies of living beings beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, there is no destruction of their essential nature, the suffix '<s>ka</s>' [indicates approximation]. But the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> is the essence of all and in every way eternal.
having understood [this], one in whom dispassion has arisen, whose sole refuge is the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>—

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.47:
'vijñāya'; jñānavān san sārāsāranityānityavastuvivekavāniti yāvat / yaśca tato vivekāt 'jātavairāgyaḥ'; iti vijñāya janitavairāgya iti vā / yaśca 'viṣṇupādaikasaṃśrayaḥ'; viṣṇupāda eva eko mukhyaḥ saṃśrayo mama śaraṇamiti jñānaṃ yasya saḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.47: '<s>Vijñāya</s>'—being one who has knowledge, meaning one who possesses discrimination between the essential and the non-essential, the eternal and the non-eternal. And one in whom dispassion has arisen through that discrimination—'<s>jātavairāgyaḥ</s>.' Or: '<s>vijñāya</s>' means 'having known,' and thereby one in whom dispassion has been born. And one whose '<s>viṣṇupādaikasaṃśrayaḥ</s>'—whose sole primary refuge is the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, i.e., one who has the knowledge 'the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone are my chief refuge, my shelter.'
he is the highest qualified person, one who has renounced all actions. // Thus [it is stated]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.48:
yaśca 'sannyastākhilakarmavān'; sannyastaṃ bhagavati samarpitaṃ akhilaṃ yadakāmyaṃ karma tadvān 'saḥ'; naraḥ 'uttamo 'dhikārī'; syāditi yojanā / atra sannyāso nāma bhagavān sarvāṇi karmāṇi karoti sarvakarmāṇi bhagavatpūjārūpāṇīti ca jñātvā bhrāntyā jīvakartṛkatvena jñātānāṃ karmaṇāṃ bhagavati visargaḥ / yathoktaṃ gītābhāṣye - "bhagavāneva sarvāṇi karmāṇi karoti"ityādinā / anena 'bhaktimān parame viṣṇau'; ityādi 'sannyastākhilakarmavān'; ityantavākyena yānyadhikāritrayaviśeṣaṇānyuktāni tānyeva sarvāṇi militvādhikārisāmānyalakṣaṇabhūtānītyuktaṃ bhavati/ na ca militānāṃ trayāṇāṃ pratyekaṃ triṣvabhāvādasambhavaḥ, bhāve vādhamādilakṣaṇasya madhyamādiṣvativyāptyāpattiriti vācyam, uttaravākye pūrvasya pūrvavākye cottarasyānukarṣeṇa sarvatra sarvasya satvābhyupagamenāsambhavābhāvāt / nanvasaṅkīrṇaviśeṣalakṣaṇānuktestraividhyāyoga iti cet - atra kecit "uttaroktāprācuryeṇa"iti ṭīkāvākyasyottarayoradhikāriṇoruktānāṃ guṇānāṃ pūrvasminnadhame 'prācuryeṇetyarthamāśritya pracuratamādhyayanādiguṇatrayavattvamuttamatvaṃ, pracuratarādhyayanādiguṇatrayavattvaṃ madhyamatvaṃ, tadubhayabhinnakevalaguṇatrayavattvaṃ adhamatvaṃ ityasāṅkaryamāhuḥ / ta evottaratra saṅgṛhītāḥ pūrvatrānukṛṣṭāśca guṇā uttaroktāsteṣāṃ tatratatra bhaktimānityādiyathāsthitamūloktaguṇāpekṣayāprācuryeṇeti pakṣāntaramāhuḥ / candrikāyāṃ tu pūrvapūrvasmin uttarottarasminnuktāprācuryeṇeti ṭīkārthamāśritya samānādhikaraṇānāṃ adhyayanaśamadamādisampattiviṣṇupādaikasaṃśrayatvādīnāṃ madhye yaḥ pracurādhyayanavān - itare tvapracure - so 'dhamo 'dhikārī / yaḥ pracurādhyayanaśamādimān - anyadekamevāpracuraṃ - sa madhyamaḥ / yaḥ pracuraviṣṇupādaikasaṃśrayatvādimān - itare tvapracure - sa uttamādhikārīti tallakṣaṇamedāt traividhyopapattiriti uktam / 'iti'; śabdasya 'bhāgavatatantre'; ityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.48: And one who has '<s>sannyastākhilakarmavān</s>'—one who has renounced, i.e., surrendered to the Lord, all actions that are performed without desire—'that' (<s>saḥ</s>) person 'is the highest (<s>uttama</s>) qualified person'—this is the construction. Here, renunciation (<s>sannyāsa</s>) means: knowing that the Lord performs all actions, and that all actions are in the form of worship of the Lord, the relinquishing to the Lord of actions that had been erroneously known as performed by the individual soul. As stated in the commentary on the <s>Gītā</s>: 'The Lord alone performs all actions,' and so on. By this, with the statement beginning 'one who has devotion to the supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>' and ending with 'one who has renounced all actions,' the qualifications stated as distinguishing marks of the three types of qualified persons are, when combined together, the general defining marks of all qualified persons—this is what is stated. Nor is there the impossibility [of combination] due to the absence of each of the three [qualifications] individually in each of the three [types]; nor should it be said that if they are present, there would be the fault of over-extension of the lowest [definition] to the middling and the rest—because by the carrying over of the latter in the earlier statement and of the earlier in the latter, the presence of all [qualifications] everywhere is accepted, and hence there is no impossibility. [Objection:] But without a statement of unmixed specific definitions, a threefold classification is unjustified. To this, some, relying on the commentary sentence 'by the abundance of those stated in the latter,' interpret the meaning as: the qualities of the latter two [higher] qualified persons stated [therein] are present in the earlier [lower] one 'in abundance' (<s>prācurya</s>)—and thus: having the three qualities of study and the like in greatest abundance is the highest status; having them in greater abundance is the middling; having merely those three qualities distinct from both [higher grades] is the lowest—thus there is no confusion. Those very qualities, gathered in the latter and carried over in the earlier, are 'stated in the latter'; the meaning 'in abundance' is relative to the originally stated qualities such as 'one who has devotion' and the like—this is an alternative interpretation. In the <s>Candrikā</s>, however, relying on the commentary's meaning that 'the earlier [qualities] in the later in abundance,' among the co-referent [qualifications]—study, tranquility and self-control and other accomplishments, sole refuge in the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like—one who has abundant study, while the others are not abundant, is the lowest qualified person. One who has abundant study and tranquility, with only one other not abundant, is the middling. One who has abundant sole refuge in the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like, while the others are not abundant, is the highest qualified person—thus the threefold classification is justified by the difference of definition. The word '<s>iti</s>' connects with '<s>Bhāgavatatatantre</s>' (in the <s>Bhāgavata</s> tradition).
"Of one who has mere study. Not due to absence of distinction." (1)
Thus [it is stated] later. (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3-4-12-13.)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.49:
adhyayanaṃ brahmavidyādhikāra ityuktam / tatkutaḥ? udāhṛtapramāṇe brahmavidyāyāmiti kaṇṭhato 'nukteḥ kutaśca tatrādhikāratraividhyamityata āha - 'adhyayana'; iti / mātraśabdaḥ kārtsnyārthaḥ / tathā ca - yathāśaktisarvavedādhyayanavato brahmavidyādhikāriteti sūtrārthaḥ / 'nāviśeṣāt'; ityaparaṃ sūtram / devādīnāṃ brahmavidyādhikāritā aviśeṣātsāmānyānna, kintu tāratamyādevetyarthaḥ / 'upari'; tṛtīye adhikārastāratamyena vakṣyate, sūtrakṛteti śeṣaḥ / tadabhipretasmṛtau 'vedoktabrahmavidyāyām'; ityuktatvāt tatrodāhṛtaśrutau jñānādhikāritraividhyasyāpyuktatvāduktaśaṅkāparihāra iti bhāvaḥ / caśabdaḥ 'adhyayanavān'; iti pramāṇasamuccaye /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.49: Study has been stated as [a ground for] qualification for <s>Brahmavidyā</s>. From what [authority]? Since in the cited authority, that [study qualifies] for <s>Brahmavidyā</s> is not explicitly stated—and whence the threefold classification of qualification therein—to this he says: '<s>adhyayana</s>' (study). The word '<s>mātra</s>' is in the sense of entirety. And thus: the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is that one who has studied all the <s>Vedas</s> according to one's ability has qualification for <s>Brahmavidyā</s>. '<s>Nāviśeṣāt</s>'—this is another <s>sūtra</s>. The qualification of gods and others for <s>Brahmavidyā</s> is not from the general [rule] due to absence of distinction, but rather from [the principle of] gradation—this is the meaning. 'Later'—in the third [book], the gradation of qualification will be stated, by the <s>sūtra</s>-author—this is the remainder. Since in the <s>smṛti</s> (traditional text) intended by him, it is stated 'in the <s>Brahmavidyā</s> prescribed by the <s>Veda</s>,' and since in the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text) cited therein the threefold classification of qualification for knowledge is also stated, the removal of the stated objection [is accomplished]—this is the purport. The particle '<s>ca</s>' serves for the aggregation of the authority [with] 'one who has study.'

children.text: "śānto dānta uparatastitikṣuḥ samāhito bhūtvā ātmanyevātmānaṃ paśyet"(bṛ-u. 6-4-23)
children.translated_text: "Having become peaceful, self-controlled, withdrawn, patient, and concentrated, one should see the Self in the self alone." (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4.23)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.50:
śamādikamapi brahmavidyāyādhikāra ityatra kāṇvaśrutimāha (bṛ-6-4-23) - 'śānta'; iti / atra 'ātmani'; ityuktyā madhyamādhikārī sūcitaḥ, 'ṛṣayo 'ntaḥprakāśāḥ'; iti śruteḥ (caturvedaśikhā) 'madhyamā ṛṣigandharvāḥ'; ityukteśca / 'śānto'; bhagavanniṣṭhabuddhiḥ "śamo manniṣṭhatā buddheḥ"iti bhāgavatokteḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - vaiṣṇavasiddhāntādacalanaṃ śama iti paryavasitamuktam / 'dānto'; nigṛhītamadaḥ, indriyanigrahavāniti yāvat / 'uparato'; viṣayālambuddhimān / bṛhadbhāṣyarītyā - upa samīpe svahṛdayesthe viṣṇau santoṣavāniti vā / 'titikṣuḥ'; śītoṣṇādidvandvasahiṣṇuḥ / 'samāhitaḥ'; same sendire harau cittavṛttimān / yadvā - 'yathāvastu tathā jñānaṃ tatsāmyātsamamīritam'; iti vacanāt samaṃ yathārthamāhitamādhānaṃ manovṛttirūpaṃ jñānaṃ icchā ca yasya sa tathoktaḥ / tathāca yathāvastujñānādimānityarthaḥ/ bhūtvetyasya pratyekaṃ sambandhaḥ / sthitamiti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - pūrvaṃ 'evaṃ'; vicchabdenokto hareḥ saṃsāramocakatvajñānīśāntyādimān 'bhūtvā'; 'ātmani'; svahṛdaye sthitaṃ 'ātmanaṃ'; paramātmānaṃ 'paśyet'; jānīyādityarthaḥ, vicārayediti lākṣaṇikārthaḥ / śāntādirbhūtvātmānaṃ vidyādityanena upanayanasya adhyayanārthatvavat śāntyāderbrahmavidyārthatvamuktaṃ bhavati / yadyapi paśyatīti śrutipāṭhaḥ tathāpi viṣṇutattvanirṇayaṭīkāyāṃ "sa tathā cakāreti kvacitpāṭhaḥ sa sadṛśaśākhāntaragato jñātavyaḥ, evamanyatrāpi"ityuktatvāt tannyāyenāyamapi sadṛśaśākhāntaragato vā paśyatītyasyārthānuvādo vetyadoṣaḥ//
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.50: To [show] that tranquility (<s>śama</s>) and the like too are [grounds for] qualification for <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, he cites the <s>Kāṇva</s> recension of the <s>śruti</s> (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.23): '<s>śānta</s>' (peaceful). Here, by the statement '<s>ātmani</s>' (in the self), the middling qualified person is indicated—because of the <s>śruti</s> 'the sages are inwardly luminous' (<s>Caturvedaśikhā</s>) and the statement 'the middling ones are sages and <s>Gandharvas</s>.' '<s>Śānta</s>' (peaceful)—one whose intellect is fixed on the Lord; as stated in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>: '<s>Śama</s> (tranquility) is the fixedness of the intellect upon Me.' In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, it is said that the final purport is: '<s>śama</s> is non-deviation from the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> doctrine.' '<s>Dānta</s>' (self-controlled)—one whose pride is restrained, meaning one who has control over the senses. '<s>Uparata</s>' (withdrawn)—one whose mind is turned away from sense objects. Or, in the manner of the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s>: '<s>upa</s>' means near, i.e., content with <s>Viṣṇu</s> who abides in one's own heart. '<s>Titikṣuḥ</s>' (patient)—enduring the pairs of opposites such as cold and heat. '<s>Samāhitaḥ</s>' (concentrated)—one whose mental activity is directed toward <s>Hari</s> (the Lord) who is in the same [self]. Or: since it is stated 'knowledge that is in accordance with reality is called <s>sama</s> (equal) because of its equality [with reality]'—one who has knowledge, i.e., mental activity in the form of knowing things as they truly are, and intention [directed accordingly]—he is so described. And thus, one who has knowledge according to reality—this is the meaning. The word '<s>bhūtvā</s>' (having become) connects with each [qualification] individually. '<s>Sthitam</s>' (established) is to be supplied. And thus: one who possesses tranquility and the like—mentioned earlier by the word '<s>evam</s>' (thus)—such as knowledge of <s>Hari</s>'s being the liberator from <s>saṃsāra</s>, '<s>bhūtvā</s>' (having become [such]), '<s>ātmani</s>' (in the self), i.e., in one's own heart, '<s>ātmānam</s>' (the Self), i.e., the Supreme Self established [therein], '<s>paśyet</s>' (should see), meaning should know, or in the secondary sense, should investigate. By [the statement] 'having become peaceful and the like, one should know the Self,' it is stated that just as the purpose of the sacred thread ceremony (<s>upanayana</s>) is study, the purpose of tranquility and the like is <s>Brahmavidyā</s>. Although the reading in the <s>śruti</s> is '<s>paśyati</s>' (sees) [indicative mood], nevertheless, since it is stated in the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirṇaya</s> commentary: 'Where 'he thus did' is a reading found in some [manuscripts], that should be understood as belonging to a similar branch'—by that principle, this too may belong to a similar branch, or this is a restatement of the meaning of '<s>paśyati</s>'—hence there is no fault. //
Having examined the worlds acquired through [ritual] action, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—
should attain dispassion: the uncreated [liberation] does not [come] through the created [action].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.51-52:
sārāsāranityāvivekajanyavairāgyādyapi brahmavidyāyāmeva adhikāra ityatrātharvaṇaśrutimāha (muṃ. 1-2-12) - 'parīkṣya'; iti / 'brāhmaṇo'; brahmajñānayogyaḥ 'lokān'; viṣṇuloketarān 'karmacitān'; kāmyakarmasampāditān tata evāsāratvenānityatvena ca 'parīkṣya'; vivicya tena vivekena 'nirvedaṃ'; kāmyakarmaṇi tatphale ca vairāgyaṃ 'āyāt'; prāpnuyāt / yasmātsvarūpānandāvirbhāvarūpatvāt 'akṛto'; nityapumartharūpo mokṣaḥ 'kṛtena'; utpattināśavatphalatvenāvadhṛtakarmaṇā 'nāsti', kintu jñānena /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp 1,1.1.51-52: To [show] that dispassion born of discrimination between the essential and non-essential, the eternal and the non-eternal, too is a qualification for <s>Brahmavidyā</s> alone, he cites the <s>Ātharvana</s> (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad) <s>śruti</s> (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.2.12): '<s>parīkṣya</s>' (having examined). '<s>Brāhmaṇaḥ</s>'—one fit for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. '<s>Lokān</s>'—the worlds other than the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. '<s>Karmacitān</s>'—acquired through desire-motivated actions. Having examined those—discerning them as without essence and impermanent—through that discrimination, '<s>nirvedam</s>'—dispassion toward desire-motivated action and its fruits—'<s>āyāt</s>'—should attain. Because, being in the nature of the manifestation of the bliss of one's own essential nature, '<s>akṛtaḥ</s>'—liberation, which has the form of an eternal human goal, '<s>kṛtena</s>'—through action characterized by origination and destruction as [its] fruit, '<s>nāsti</s>'—does not [come about]; rather, [it comes] through knowledge.
For the knowledge of that, one should approach a teacher (<s>guru</s>) indeed—
fuel in hand, one who is learned in scripture (<s>śrotriya</s>) and established in <s>Brahman</s>. //
(<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.12)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.53-54:
'tat'; tasmāt 'saḥ'; mokṣāditaratra viraktaḥ 'vijñānārthaṃ'; brahmaṇo viśeṣajñānāya / 'samitpāṇiḥ'; samidyuktau pāṇī yasya / yadvā - samprāptau sampuṭīkṛtau ariktau vā pāṇī yasya / sa evaṃbhūtassan 'śrotriyaṃ'; chandodhyetāraṃ brahmaniṣṭhameva gurum 'abhigacchet'; upasīdedityarthaḥ / gurumeva na tvanyamiti vā evaśabdānvayaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - 'karmacitān'; karmaṇā sañcitān aihikān mandirādīn vināśinaḥ 'parīkṣya'; parito vīkṣya pāralaukikatvena tadviparītānapi karmabhiścitān svargādilokān vināśina eva parīkṣya tebhyo 'nirvedamāyāt'; / 'akṛto'; jñānipriyo bhagavān 'kṛtena'; karmaṇā 'na'; labhyate / tataḥ 'tadvijñānārthaṃ'; tasya jñānipriyasya viṣṇorvijñānārthaṃ 'gurumabhigacchet'; iti śrutyartha uktaḥ / atrāpi vijñānapadena brahmajñāniparabrāhmaṇapadena ca uttamādhikārī sūcitaḥ, 'devādīnāṃ tu tajjñānaṃ vijñānamiti kīrtitam'; iti gītābhāṣyokteḥ, 'naiva devapadaṃ prāptāḥ brahmadarśanavarjitāḥ'; iti tattātparyokteśca /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.53-54: 'Tat' — therefore; 'saḥ' — he who is dispassionate toward everything other than liberation; 'vijñānārtham' — for the purpose of specific knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. 'Samitpāṇiḥ' — one whose hands hold sacrificial fuel; or alternatively, one whose hands are joined together, cupped, or not empty. He, being of such a nature, 'śrotriyam' — a teacher who has studied the Vedas and is devoted to <s>Brahman</s> alone — 'abhigacchet' — should approach, i.e., should sit near. The word 'eva' connects [to mean] 'the teacher alone, not anyone else.' In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: 'karmacitān' — those things accumulated through action, worldly things like houses etc. that are perishable — 'parīkṣya' — having examined thoroughly, and having examined even the worlds like heaven etc. that are accumulated through actions as other-worldly yet equally perishable — from those 'nirvedamāyāt' — he should develop dispassion. 'Akṛtaḥ' — the <s>Bhagavān</s> who is dear to the knowers — 'kṛtena' — through action — 'na' — is not obtainable. Therefore 'tadvijñānārtham' — for the purpose of knowing that <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is dear to the knowers — 'gurumabhigacchet' — one should approach a teacher: thus the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is stated. Here too, through the word <s>vijñāna</s> and the word <s>brāhmaṇa</s> meaning 'knower of <s>Brahman</s>,' the highest qualified person is indicated — as stated in the <s>Gītā-bhāṣya</s>: 'The knowledge of gods etc. regarding that is called <s>vijñāna</s>,' and as stated in the <s>Tattātparya</s>: 'Those devoid of the vision of <s>Brahman</s> have not attained even the status of a god.'
Whom this [Self] chooses, by that one He is attainable —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.55:
viṣṇubhaktirapi brahmavidyāyāmadhikāra ityetatkaṭhaśrutyā darśayati - 'yaṃ'; iti / ātharvaṇepīyaṃ paṭhyate /
(muṃ.3-2-3)
'eṣaḥ'; icchārūpaḥ 'ātmā'; viṣṇuḥ 'yaṃ'; adhikāriṇaṃ 'vṛṇute'; parigṛhṇāti 'tena'; eva 'labhyaḥ'; prāpyaḥ tasya prasanno bhavati /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.55: He shows through the <s>Kaṭha</s> <s>śruti</s> that devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> too constitutes qualification for <s>Brahma-vidyā</s>: 'yam.' This is also read in the <s>Ātharvana</s> [Upaniṣad] (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.3). 'Eṣaḥ' — this <s>Ātman</s> whose nature is will — <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'yam' — whichever qualified person; 'vṛṇute' — accepts, chooses; 'tena' — by that person alone; 'labhyaḥ' — He is attainable; He becomes gracious to that person.
To that one, this <s>Ātman</s> reveals His own form. //
(<s>Kaṭhopaniṣad</s> 2.23)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.56:
tataśca 'tasya'; adhikāriṇaḥ 'eṣaḥ'; prasannaḥ 'ātmā svāṃ tanūṃ'; rupaṃ 'vivṛṇute'; prakāśayatītyarthaḥ/ atra 'bhaktameva ca vṛṇuta iti prasiddhaḥ'; iti prameyadīpoktarītyā vṛṇuta ityanena bhaktatvaṃ sūcitam / tattvapradīpe tu - 'yamevaiṣaḥ'; paramātmā bhaktidānena 'vṛṇute'; svīkaroti 'tena'; prāpyo yatastasyaiva 'svāṃ tanuṃ'; prakāśayatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.56: And then, 'tasya' — to that qualified person; 'eṣaḥ' — this, being gracious; '<s>Ātmā</s>' — [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] 'svāṃ tanūm' — His own form; 'vivṛṇute' — reveals, i.e., makes manifest: this is the meaning. Here, as stated in the <s>Prameyadīpa</s>: 'It is well-known that He chooses the devotee alone' — by the word 'vṛṇute,' devotion is indicated. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: 'yamevaiṣaḥ' — the Supreme Self, through the gift of devotion, 'vṛṇute' — accepts; 'tena' — He is attainable, because He 'svāṃ tanuṃ' — reveals [His own form] to that very person: thus it is stated.

children.text: yasya deve parā bhaktiryathā deve tathā gurau /
children.translated_text: He who has supreme devotion to God, and likewise to the teacher as to God —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.57:
sā ca bhaktiḥ viṣṇau sarvādhikā anyeṣvapi yathāyogyā brahmavidyopayoginītyarthe śvetāśvatarāṇāṃ śrutiṃ (śve. 6-23) darśayati - 'yasya'; iti / 'yathā'; ityāvartate / 'tathā'; iti samuccaye / 'kathitāḥ'; 'akathitāḥ'; iti dvedhā vicchedaḥ / pūrvavedādibhirguruṇeti ca śeṣaḥ / tathāca - 'yasya'; adhikāriṇo 'deve'; dyotanādiguṇe viṣṇau 'parā'; sarvādhikā 'bhaktiḥ'; asti 'tathā'; 'deve'; taditaradeveṣu brahmādiṣu 'yathā'; yathāyogyā bhaktirasti, 'tathā gurau'; anyeṣu svottameṣu ca yathā yogyā bhaktirasti /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.57: And that devotion, being supreme toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> and also appropriately directed toward others, is conducive to <s>Brahma-vidyā</s> — to show this, he cites the <s>śruti</s> of the <s>Śvetāśvataras</s> (<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 6.23): 'yasya.' The word 'yathā' is repeated. 'Tathā' is for aggregation. The division is twofold: 'kathitāḥ' (those that have been told) and 'akathitāḥ' (those that have not been told). The complement is: 'by teachers through the Vedas etc.' And thus — 'yasya' — of that qualified person; 'deve' — in God, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who has qualities such as illumination; 'parā' — supreme, surpassing all; 'bhaktiḥ' — devotion exists; 'tathā' — and; 'deve' — toward other gods, <s>Brahmā</s> and others; 'yathā' — appropriate devotion exists; 'tathā gurau' — and toward the teacher and others superior to oneself, appropriate devotion exists.
To that great soul, these meanings that have been told are illuminated. / (<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 6.23)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.58:
'tasya'; mahātmanaḥ kartari ṣaṣṭhīyam / tenādhikāriṇā pūrvaṃ vedādibhirguruṇā vā 'kathitāḥ'; 'ete'; uktāḥ 'arthāḥ'; parāparatattvarūpāḥ 'prakāśyante'; jñāyanta ityarthaḥ / yadvā - 'ete'; śamādirūpā 'arthāḥ'; guṇāstasmin 'prakāśyante'; dṛśyanta ityarthaḥ / atha vā - 'akathitāḥ'; gurubhiranupadiṣṭāḥ 'arthāḥ'; asya bhaktivaśāt 'prakāśyante'; 'hi'; prasiddhamityarthaḥ / 'prakāśante'; iti pāṭhe tatkartṛkajñānānukūlamānakartāro bhavantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.58: 'Tasya' — the genitive is in the agent sense (of that great soul). By that qualified person, previously, by teachers through the Vedas etc. 'kathitāḥ' — 'ete' — the stated 'arthāḥ' — meanings having the form of the higher and lower realities — 'prakāśyante' — are known: this is the meaning. Alternatively, 'ete' — these 'arthāḥ' — qualities in the form of tranquility etc. — 'prakāśyante' — are seen in him: this is the meaning. Or else — 'akathitāḥ' — meanings not taught by teachers — 'arthāḥ' — are 'prakāśyante' — illuminated for him through the force of devotion — 'hi' — this is well known: this is the meaning. In the reading 'prakāśante,' the meaning is: they become favorable to the production of knowledge initiated by him.
Thus from these and other <s>śrutis</s>. And in the <s>Vyomasaṃhitā</s> —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.59:
'ityādiśrutibhyaśca'; ityasya 'adhikāra uktaḥ'; ityanenānvayaḥ na kevalamuktaśrutibhiḥ, kintu "bhaktyā tvananyayā śakya ahamevaṃ vidhorjuna jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ"(bha.gī. 11-54) ityādismṛtibhyaśceti
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.59: The construction of 'ityādiśrutibhyaśca' connects with 'adhikāra uktaḥ' (qualification has been stated). Not only from the <s>śrutis</s> already cited, but also from <s>smṛtis</s> such as 'But through unswerving devotion alone am I, O <s>Arjuna</s>, able to be known and seen in such a form' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 11.54) etc. —

children.text: caśabdārthaḥ / nanu yadyadhyayanavatāmeva brahmavidyādhikāraḥ tarhi trivarṇetareṣāmadhyayanābhāvenādhikāro na syāt / tataśca teṣāṃ brahmajñānābhāvena mokṣābhāvassyādityāśaṅkāṃ smṛtyā pariharati - 'vyomasaṃhitāyāṃ ca'; iti / prakṛtaśaṅkānirāsapūrvakamiti śeṣaḥ / pūrvagranthasamuccaye caśabdaḥ / asyāpi 'adhikāra uktaḥ'; / ityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the meaning of the word 'ca.' Now, if only those who have completed Vedic study are qualified for <s>Brahma-vidyā</s>, then those outside the three <s>varṇas</s>, lacking Vedic study, would have no qualification. Consequently, in the absence of <s>Brahma-jñāna</s> for them, there would be no liberation — to resolve this doubt, he cites a <s>smṛti</s>: 'Vyomasaṃhitāyāṃ ca.' The complement is: 'with the prior removal of the stated doubt.' The word 'ca' is for aggregation with the preceding text. This too connects with 'adhikāra uktaḥ' (qualification has been stated).
Even <s>antyajas</s> (outcastes) who are devotees are qualified for knowledge through [<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s] names —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.60:
ante bhavāḥ antyāḥ teṣu jātāḥ 'antyajāḥ'; trivarṇabāhyāḥ / ayaṃ cārtho "viṣṇunāmasvādhyāyo 'ntyānāṃ"ityetadavatārikārūpatayā "nāgnirna yajñaḥ śūdrasyetyādestrivarṇabāhyānāṃ"iti nyāyadīpikayā sūcitaḥ / 'bhaktāḥ'; iti bhaktimānityuktabrahmavidyādhikārakathanam / evaṃ 'bhaktimatāṃ'; ityapi/ etaccobhayanvayi / tathā ca - na kevalaṃ traivarṇikāḥ, kintu ye antyajāḥ trivarṇabāhyāḥ śūdrādayaḥ pulkasāntāḥ te yadyapi vaidikabrahmajñānānadhikāriṇaḥ, tathāpi yato bhaktāḥ ato nāmajñānādhikāriṇaḥ viṣṇunāmajñānatatsvādhyāyādhikāriṇaḥ, ataste brahmajñānamuktyadhikāriṇa iti yojanā /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.60: '<s>Antyajas</s>' — those born in the lowest [castes], i.e., outside the three <s>varṇas</s>. This meaning is indicated by the <s>Nyāyadīpikā</s> as the context for '[<s>Viṣṇu</s>]-name study is the <s>svādhyāya</s> of the lowest': 'For those outside the three <s>varṇas</s>, since there is no fire, no sacrifice for the <s>śūdra</s>...' etc. 'Bhaktāḥ' — the statement about qualification for <s>Brahma-vidyā</s> for those described as possessing devotion. Similarly 'bhaktimatām.' This applies to both [groups]. And thus — not only the three <s>varṇas</s>, but even those <s>antyajas</s> outside the three <s>varṇas</s> — <s>śūdras</s> and others up to <s>pulkasas</s> — although they are not qualified for Vedic <s>Brahma-jñāna</s>, nevertheless because they are devotees, they are qualified for knowledge through <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s names and for the study of those names, and therefore they are qualified for <s>Brahma-jñāna</s> and liberation: this is the construction.
Women, <s>śūdras</s>, and <s>brahma-bandhus</s> (brāhmaṇas in name only) have eligibility in <s>tantra</s>-knowledge. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.61:
traivarṇikeṣvapi vedānadhikāriṇāṃ keṣāñcit, antyajeṣvapi keṣāñcidbhaktimatāṃ, uktādanyaccāha - 'strīśūdrabrahmabandhūnām'; iti / striyaśca śūdrāśca brahmabandhavo brāhmaṇābhāsāśca teṣāmiti vigrahaḥ / tantraṃ pañcarātrādi, tajjñāne taduktārthajñāne, tantrotpannabrahmavidyāyāmiti yāvat / apiśabdo 'trāpi sambadhyate / tathāca teṣāṃ tadjñānadvārāpi mokṣopapattiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.61: Stating another [type of eligibility] among the three <s>varṇas</s> — for some who are not qualified for the Vedas, and among the outcastes too — for some devotees, he says: 'strīśūdrabrahmabandūnām.'
