The compound analysis is: women, <s>śūdras</s>, and <s>brahmabandhus</s> (those who are brāhmaṇas in appearance only) — of these. <s>Tantra</s> means <s>Pañcarātra</s> etc.; in knowledge of that — in the knowledge of meanings stated therein — i.e., in <s>Brahma-vidyā</s> as arising from <s>tantra</s>: this is the extent [of their eligibility]. The word 'api' connects here too. And thus, their attainment of liberation through that [tantra] knowledge is the purport.

children.text: ekadeśe parokte tu na tu granthapurassare /
children.translated_text: In a portion [of the tantra], when expounded by another, but not when a text is the primary basis —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.62:
tantre 'pi na sarvatrādhikāraḥ, kintu ekadeśe eva / tatrāpi 'na granthapurassare'; na svaprādhānyena granthārambhe 'dhikāraḥ, kintu 'parokte'; pareṇānyena parārthaṃ prokte ārabdha evetyāha - 'ekadeśa'; iti / avadhāraṇe tuśabdaḥ / tadvyāvartyamāha - 'na tu'; iti / stryādimātrapuraskāreṇa prāpabhyamāṇatantragranbhādau teṣāṃ nādhikāritetyarthaḥ/ anena strīśūdrādimātraṃ puraskṛtya purāṇādigranthapravacanamapi na kāryamityuktaṃ bhavati / dvitīyatuśabdasyottaratrānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.62: Even in <s>tantra</s>, the eligibility is not everywhere, but only in a portion. And even there, 'na granthapurassare' — there is no eligibility in the primary study of a text on one's own; rather, 'parokte' — when expounded by another, for another's sake — only in what has already been commenced: he says 'ekadeśa.' The word 'tu' is for restriction. He states what is excluded: 'na tu.' The meaning is: in a <s>tantra</s> text that is undertaken primarily for women and <s>śūdras</s> alone, they do not have eligibility. By this, it is also stated that the exposition of <s>Purāṇa</s> texts and the like should not be done primarily for women and <s>śūdras</s> alone. The second word 'tu' connects with what follows.
For those of the three <s>varṇas</s>, in that which is stated in the Vedas, for those with proper devotion to <s>Hari</s> —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.63:
tarhi vedotpannabrahmavidyāyāṃ keṣāmadhikāraḥ? pariśeṣāt traivarṇikānāṃ cet - teṣāmapi kiṃ sarveṣāmadhikāraḥ? na, kiṃ tu keṣāñcidityāha - 'traivarṇikānāṃ'; iti / 'vedokteḥ'; vedotpannabrahmajñāne tu 'harau samyagbhaktimatāṃ'; eva 'traivarṇikānāṃ'; uktetarabrahmakṣatriyavaiśyānāṃ adhikāritetyarthaḥ / na kevalaṃ nāmādijñānādhikāra ityarthepi tuśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.63: Then in <s>Brahma-vidyā</s> arising from the Vedas, who is qualified? If by elimination it is the three <s>varṇas</s> — then is it all of them? No, but only some of them: he says 'traivarṇikānām.' 'Vedokteḥ' — in <s>Brahma-jñāna</s> arising from the Vedas; 'harau samyagbhaktimatām' — only those with proper devotion to <s>Hari</s>; 'traivarṇikānām' — of the stated other Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas — have eligibility: this is the meaning. The word 'tu' also has the meaning: not merely eligibility for name-knowledge etc.
They also declare eligibility in Vedic [knowledge] for the highest women —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.64:
"sapatnīṃ me parādhamapatiṃ me kevalaṃ kuru/"(maṃ-pra-16-2) ityādau strīṇāmapi vedādhikāradarśanāt kathaṃ tāsāmanadhikāra ityata uktasyāpavādamāha - 'āhuḥ'; iti / turapyarthe 'pi / 'vaidike'; ityasya vipariṇāmenāvṛttiḥ / 'uttamastrīṇāṃ'; iti tatpuruṣakarmadhārayau / tathāca - na kevalamuttamānāṃ devānāṃ strīṇāṃ nāmādijñāne 'dhikāraḥ kintu vaidike 'pi jñāne vedotpannabrahmavidyāyāmapi vaidikāḥ adhikāramāhuriti yojanā /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.64: Since the eligibility of women in the Vedas is observed in passages like 'Make my co-wife the lowest; make my husband exclusively mine' (<s>Mantra Prāśna</s> 16.2), etc. — how then can they be declared ineligible? To this, he states an exception to what has been said: 'āhuḥ.' The word 'tu' has the meaning of 'api' (also). 'Vaidike' is repeated by inversion. 'Uttamastrīṇām' — this is both a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> and a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound. And thus — not only do the highest women, the wives of gods, have eligibility for name-knowledge etc., but they also have eligibility in Vedic knowledge — i.e., in <s>Brahma-vidyā</s> arising from the Vedas — the Vedic [authorities] declare this eligibility: this is the construction.

children.text: yathorvaśī yamī caiva śacyādyāśca tathāparāḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: Such as <s>Urvaśī</s>, <s>Yamī</s>, and likewise <s>Śacī</s> and others. // Thus. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.65:
tāḥ udāharati - 'yathā'; iti / 'eva'; evaṃ 'yamī'; yamasya bhāryā śyāmalā / caśabda uktasamuccaye / ādyaśabdena umāratyādi gṛhyate / anuktasamuccaye dvitīyaścaḥ, tena manuṣyādikulotpannadevastriyo gṛhyante / tathāśabdaḥ upamāyāṃ uktasamuccaye vā / aparāḥ uttamastrībhyo anyāḥ ṛṇipatnyaḥ / avarā iti vā, uttamadevastryapekṣayā madhyamaṛṣipatnīnāṃ avaratvāditi / 'vyomasaṃhitāyāṃ'; iti itiśabdānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.65: He gives examples: 'yathā.' 'Eva' means 'thus.' '<s>Yamī</s>' — <s>Śyāmalā</s>, the wife of <s>Yama</s>. The word 'ca' is for aggregation of those stated. By the word 'ādi,' <s>Umā</s>, <s>Rati</s>, etc. are included. The second 'ca' is for aggregation of those not stated — by which, divine women born in human lineages etc. are included. The word 'tathā' is either for comparison or for aggregation of those stated. 'Aparāḥ' — others than the highest women, i.e., the wives of sages. Or 'avarāḥ' — 'lower,' because the wives of middle-level sages are lower in comparison to the highest divine women. The word 'iti' connects with 'Vyomasaṃhitāyām' (in the <s>Vyomasaṃhitā</s>).

children.text: yato nārāyaṇaprasādamṛte na mokṣaḥ,na ca jñānaṃ vinātyarthaprasādaḥ/
children.translated_text: Since without the grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> there is no liberation, and without knowledge there is no complete grace —
Therefore the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> should be undertaken. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.66-67:
evaṃ pratijñāpramāṇopanyāsābhyāṃ ānantaryapratiyogyadhikāravivaraṇamukhenāthaśabdaṃ saṃkṣepavistarābhyāṃ vyākhyāya sūtre 'kartavyā'; iti padaṃ ataśśabdaparāmarśanīyasamarpakaṃ 'yataḥ'; ityādikaṃ cādhyāhāryamiti darśayan 'ataśśabdo hetvarthe'; iti saṅkṣepeṇoktamarthaṃ viśadayati - 'yataḥ'; iti / 'yataḥ'; ityāvartate / tathāca - yatassukhameva me syāt duḥkhamīṣadapi mābhūditi sarvābhimato 'mokṣaḥ'; samyañcaṃ 'nārāyaṇaprasādaṃ ṛte'; vinā nāsti, sa ca 'atyarthaprasādaḥ'; atimātraprasādaśca nāparokṣajñānaṃ vinā, tacca na brahmajijñāsāṃ vinā, 'ato brahmajijñāsā kartavyā'; ityarthaḥ / uktaṃ hi śabdādhikaraṇe tattvapradīpe "mokṣasyaiva paramapuruṣārthatvāt tasya ca samīco vinā viṣṇuprasādāt alabhyatvāt tasya ca atimātrasya aparokṣajñānaprasādhyatvāt tasya cāparokṣasya jijñāsāsamāyattattvādviṣṇureva jijñāsya ityuktam"iti/ sāvadhāraṇānvayasyāpyupalakṣakametat / tasyātaśśabdena parāmarśānnānupapattiḥ / anena sūtre yato nārāyaṇaprasādamṛte na mokṣaḥ, kintu prasādenaiva, na ca jñānaṃ vinātyarthaprasādaḥ, kintu jñānenaiva, na ca jijñāsāṃ vinā jñānaṃ, kintu jijñānayaiva, ato brahmajijñāsā kartavyetyanvayapradarśanamukhena ataśśabdasya mokṣasādhanaprasādasādhanajñānasādhanatvāditi heturartha ityetadvivṛtaṃ bhavati / evaṃ yato nārāyaṇaprasādamṛte na jñānaṃ na jijñāsā kintu prasādenaiva iti yojanāyāṃ ataḥśabdasyārthāntaramapi vivṛtaṃ bhavati / nārāyaṇaśabdaprayogeṇa sautrabrahmaśabdo 'pi vyākhyāto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verses 66-67:
Thus, having explained the word 'atha' both briefly and in detail through the presentation of the thesis and proof by way of elucidating the sequence-correlate and the topic (<s>adhikāra</s>), [he turns to the word 'ataḥ']. In the <s>sūtra</s>, 'kartavyā' (should be done) is the word to be supplied; 'yataḥ' (because) and so forth are to be mentally supplied as presenting the word 'ataḥ' for consideration. Showing this, he elucidates the meaning stated briefly as 'the word ataḥ [is used] in the sense of cause' — with 'yataḥ.' 'Yataḥ' recurs. And thus — because (<s>yataḥ</s>) <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is universally desired by all as 'may happiness alone be mine, may not even the slightest suffering befall me,' does not exist 'without the complete grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,' and that 'supreme grace' — grace of the highest degree — does not exist without direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) knowledge, and that [direct knowledge] does not exist without the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> — 'therefore the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> should be undertaken': this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> in the <s>Śabdādhikaraṇa</s>: 'Since <s>mokṣa</s> alone is the supreme human goal, and since the complete [mokṣa] cannot be obtained without <s>Viṣṇu's</s> grace, and since that supreme [grace] is accomplished through direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) knowledge, and since that direct [knowledge] depends on inquiry — therefore <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is to be inquired into: this is what has been said.' This is also illustrative of the construction with emphasis (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>). Since [the content] is referred to by the word 'ataḥ,' there is no logical difficulty. By this, the construction of the <s>sūtra</s> is demonstrated through the chain: because without the grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> there is no <s>mokṣa</s>, but rather through grace alone; and without knowledge there is no supreme grace, but rather through knowledge alone; and without inquiry there is no knowledge, but rather through inquiry alone — therefore the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> should be undertaken — and through this demonstration of the syntactic connection, the meaning of the word 'ataḥ' as 'because it is the means to knowledge which is the means to grace which is the means to liberation' is explained. Likewise, in the construction 'because without the grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> there is no knowledge, no inquiry, but rather through grace alone,' another meaning of the word 'ataḥ' is also explained. By the use of the word '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,' the word '<s>Brahman</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> is also explained.
Where a word finds no scope elsewhere, that word is established in that [sentence]. //
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 68:

children.text: vākyaṃ veti satāṃ nītiḥ sāvakāśe na tadbhavatet //
children.translated_text: Or a sentence — this is the rule of the good; when there is scope [elsewhere], it does not apply. //
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 69:
(Thus in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>.)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.68-69:
nanu sūtre 'kartavyā'; iti padasyaiva adhyāhāraḥ kutaḥ adhyāhārasya niraṅkuśatvena 'na kartavyā'; iti vākyasyaivādhyāhāraḥ kiṃ na syādityata āha - 'yatra'; iti / atra yatreti tatreti padamiti cāvartate, tathā vākyamityapi, vinetyadhyāhriyate / tathā ca - 'yatra'; avāntaravākye yat 'padaṃ'; vinā 'anyatra'; arthāntare 'anavasaraḥ'; aghaṭanā 'tatra'; vākye tadeva 'padaṃ'; 'pratiṣṭhitaṃ'; prāptaṃ bhavet nānyaditi 'satāṃ'; nyāyaḥ, yatra vākye yasmin vākye sāvakāśe arthāntare ghaṭanāvati sati tadeva padaṃ niyamena pratiṣṭhitaṃ prāptaṃ na bhavet / evaṃ yatra mahāvākye yadavāntaravākyaṃ vinānyatrānavasaraḥ tatra mahāvākye tadeva vākyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ, yatra yasmin mahāvākye sāvakāśe sati tadavāntaravākyaṃ niyamena pratiṣṭhitaṃ na bhavedityarthaḥ / yatra vākye yatpadaṃ vākyaṃ vāpekṣitaṃ anyatrānyasyānavasara iti vā / iti bṛhatsaṃhitāyāmuktatvāt 'kartavyā'; iti padamevāvaśyamadhyāhartavyamiti vākyaśeṣeṇāsyānvayaḥ / 'na kartavyā'; ityadhyāhāre athātaśśabdārthādhirārāderatrānvayāyogāditi bhāvaḥ / evaṃ candrikoktarītyā 'yatra'; iti śloko 'yataḥ'; ityādyadhyāhārasamarthanaparatayāpi vyākhyeyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verses 68-69:
Now, the objection arises: why should only 'kartavyā' (should be done) be the word to be supplied in the <s>sūtra</s>? Since supplying is unrestricted, why could not the sentence 'na kartavyā' (should not be done) be supplied instead? To this he says: 'Where.' Here, 'yatra' (where), 'tatra' (there), and 'padaṃ' (word) recur, as does 'vākyam' (sentence); 'vinā' (without) is to be supplied. And thus — 'where,' in a subordinate sentence, a 'word' without which 'elsewhere,' in another meaning, there is 'no scope' — no possibility of application — 'there,' in that sentence, that very 'word' is 'established' — arrived at, and no other: this is the 'rule of the good.' Where, in a sentence in which there is scope — where application in another meaning is possible — then that very word is not necessarily 'established' or arrived at. Likewise, where in a main sentence, a subordinate sentence without which there is no scope elsewhere, there in that main sentence that very sentence is established; where, in a main sentence, when there is scope, that subordinate sentence is not necessarily established: this is the meaning. Since it is stated in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>, only 'kartavyā' must necessarily be supplied — this is its syntactic connection with the remainder of the sentence. The sense is that in the case of supplying 'na kartavyā,' the meanings of the words 'atha,' 'ataḥ,' and so forth would have no scope for syntactic connection here.

children.text:
"tamevaṃ vidvānamṛta iha bhavati, nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyate"
(tai.ā. 3-12.)
children.translated_text:
'One who knows Him thus becomes immortal here; there is no other path for attainment.'
(<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12)
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 70:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.70:
yaduktaṃ 'yato nārāyaṇaprasādaṃ'; ityanena prasādasya mokṣasādhanatvaṃ tatkuta ityatastatra śrutiṃ pramāṇayati - 'taṃ'; iti / 'iha'; adhikārivarge prakṛtapuruṣaśabditaṃ 'taṃ'; paramātmānaṃ 'evaṃ'; sahasraśīrṣatvādyuktaprakāreṇa 'iha'; loke 'vidvān'; parokṣajñānadvārā aparokṣato jānannevānte 'amṛto'; mukto bhavati, yato nārāyaṇāyanāya tatprāptirūpamokṣārthaṃ 'anyaḥ'; paramapuruṣajñānāt 'panthāḥ'; upāyo 'na vidyate'; nāsti ata ityarthaḥ / atra jñānasya mokṣasādhanatvaṃ sākṣāt jñāyate / prasādasya mokṣasādhanatvaṃ tu ṭīkāsudhoktarītyā prasādaṃ vinā vidvatpadalakṣyāparokṣajñānamātreṇa mokṣo na bhavatītyanyathānupapattyaiva, na tu sākṣāt / nimittena naimittikopalakṣaṇāvetyavagantavyam /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 70:
What was stated through 'because without the grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' — namely, that grace is the means to <s>mokṣa</s> — whence is this known? To that end, he cites a <s>Śruti</s> as authority: 'Him.' 'Here,' among the class of qualified persons, 'Him' — the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) denoted by the word 'person' in the context — 'thus,' in the manner described as having a thousand heads and so forth, the one who 'knows' — who, through the medium of mediate knowledge (<s>parokṣa-jñāna</s>), knows directly (<s>aparokṣataḥ</s>) — that one alone ultimately 'becomes immortal,' liberated, 'here' in this world. Because for attaining <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — for <s>mokṣa</s> in the form of reaching Him — 'another' path, a means other than knowledge of the Supreme Person, 'is not found,' does not exist: this is the meaning, 'therefore' (<s>ataḥ</s>). Here, the instrumentality of knowledge as a means to <s>mokṣa</s> is directly known. But the instrumentality of grace as a means to <s>mokṣa</s> is known, as explained in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> and the <s>Sudhā</s>, only through indirect reasoning (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>) — that without grace, <s>mokṣa</s> does not occur through mere direct knowledge indicated by the word 'vidvān' (knower) — not directly. It should be understood that the efficient cause is indicated by the occasioning cause.

children.text:
"priyo hi jñāninotyarthamahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ"/
(bha.gī. 7-17)
children.translated_text:
'For I am exceedingly dear to the knower, and he is dear to Me.'
(<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 7.17)
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 71:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.71:
'na ca jñānaṃ vinā'; iti yadaparokṣajñānasya prasādasādhanatvamuktaṃ tatkuta ityatastatra gītāsmṛtimāha 'priyo hi'; iti / 'ahaṃ jñānino 'tyarthaṃ'; atyantaṃ 'priyaḥ'; / 'hi'; prasiddham / 'sa ca so 'pyaparokṣajñānī mama priyaḥ'; ityarthaḥ/ kṛṣṇavākyametat /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 71:
What was stated — that direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) knowledge is the means to [divine] grace — whence is this known? To that end, he cites the <s>Gītā Smṛti</s>: 'For I am dear.' 'I am exceedingly,' that is, supremely, 'dear to the knower.' 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — this is well-known. 'And he' — that one who possesses direct knowledge — 'is dear to Me': this is the meaning. This is a statement of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text:
"yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ"(kaṭha. 2-23.)
"ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ"
(bṛ.u.6-5-6.)
children.translated_text:
'He is attainable by the one whom He chooses.' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.23)
'The Self indeed is to be seen, to be heard, to be reflected upon, to be meditated upon.' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.5.6)
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 72:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.72:
prasādasya mokṣasādhanatvaṃ na kovalamarthāt jñāyate, kintu śrutyā cetyāśayena tatra kaṭhaśrutimāha 'yaṃ'; iti / atraivakāro bhinnakramaḥ / tathā ca 'eṣaḥ'; paramātmā 'eṣaḥ'; icchārūpaḥ prasannaḥ san 'yaṃ'; adhikāriṇaṃ 'vṛṇute'; anugṛhṇāti 'tena'; eva 'labhyaḥ'; prāpyaḥ, na tvanyena karmaṇetyarthaḥ / ata eva viṣṇutattvanirṇayaṭīkāyām "eṣa paramātmā yaṃ vṛṇute yasya prasīdati tenaiva labhyaḥ / kathaṃ? yatastasya svāṃ tanuṃ vivṛṇute prakāśayati, tataścāsya svāṃ tanuṃ avidyāvṛtasvarūpāṃ vivṛṇute āvirbhāvayati"iti prakṛtānukūlatayā samagravākyārtha uktaḥ / yatpūrvaṃ jijñāsāyāḥ aparokṣajñānasādhanatvamupaskṛtavākyenoktaṃ tatra pramāṇatevana śrutimāha 'ātmā'; iti / vā ara iti viśliṣṭapāṭhaḥ/ 'vā'; śabdo 'vadhāraṇe / 'are'; iti yājñavalkyakartṛkamaitreyīsambodhanam / tathā ca 'are'; maitreyi amṛtatvamiṣyate cettarhi 'ātmā'; paramātmā tvayā 'draṣṭavyo'; darśanena viṣayīkartavya ityarthaḥ / darśanaṃ kena syādityākāṅkṣāyāmāha - 'śrotavyaḥ'; ityādi / darśanārthaṃ nididhyāsitavyaḥ / tadarthaṃ 'śrotavyaḥ'; gurūpadeśamukhena ayamasya vākyasyārtha ityupaniṣadvākyārthagrahaṇarūpaśravaṇena viṣayīkartavyaḥ, tathā 'mantavyaḥ'; yuktyanusandhānarūpamananena viṣayīkartavyaścetyarthaḥ/ anena śravaṇamanananididhyāsanātmakajijñāsāyāḥ
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 72:
The instrumentality of grace as a means to <s>mokṣa</s> is not known merely from reasoning, but also from <s>Śruti</s> — with this intention, he cites the <s>Kaṭha Śruti</s>: 'Whom.' Here the particle 'eva' is in displaced order. And thus — 'this' <s>Paramātman</s>, 'this one' who is gracious in the form of desire, 'whom' — whichever qualified person — He 'chooses,' that is, favors, 'by that one' alone He 'is attainable,' that is, reachable, and not by another through action alone: this is the meaning. Therefore, in the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirṇaya Ṭīkā</s> it is said: 'This <s>Paramātman</s>, whom He chooses, upon whom He is gracious, by that one alone He is attainable. How? Because He reveals His own form to that one, and then He reveals that one's own form — the true nature covered by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)' — thus the complete meaning of the sentence is stated in accordance with the context. What was previously stated — that inquiry is the means to direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) knowledge — for that, by way of the constructed sentence, he cites the <s>Śruti</s> as authority: 'The Self.' 'Vā' and 'are' are read separately. The word 'vā' is for emphasis. 'Are' is <s>Yājñavalkya's</s> form of addressing <s>Maitreyī</s>. And thus — 'are,' O <s>Maitreyī</s>, if immortality is desired, then 'the Self' — the <s>Paramātman</s> — 'is to be seen' by you, that is, is to be made the object of direct vision: this is the meaning. In response to the expectation 'by what means would this seeing occur?' he says: 'to be heard' and so on. For the sake of seeing, He 'is to be meditated upon' (<s>nididhyāsitavya</s>). For that purpose, 'He is to be heard' — He is to be made the object of hearing in the form of grasping the meaning of <s>Upaniṣadic</s> sentences through the teacher's instruction, [understanding] 'this is the meaning of this sentence.' Likewise, 'He is to be reflected upon' — He is to be made the object of reflection (<s>manana</s>) in the form of investigation through reasoning: this is the meaning. By this,

the instrumentality of inquiry — which consists of hearing, reflection, and meditation (<s>śravaṇa</s>, <s>manana</s>, <s>nididhyāsana</s>) as principal and subsidiary components — as a means to knowledge, is stated.
Thus [it is established] from <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> passages such as these.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 73:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.73:
'śrutismṛtibhyaḥ'; iti / śrutayaśca smṛtiśca tābhya iti vigrahaḥ / asya 'yato nārāyaṇa'; itāyādinoktaṃ siddhamityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 73:
'From <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>' — the compound analysis is: <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Smṛtis</s>, from those. The syntactic connection of this is: what has been stated through 'because without [the grace of] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' and so forth is established — this is the construction.
But [the grace produced] by action is declared to be inferior; [the grace produced] by hearing and the like —
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 74:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.74:
nanu 'tatkarma haritoṣaṃ'; 'ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ'; (bha.gī.18-68.) ityādeḥ karmādināpi bhagavatprasādasiddheḥ kiṃ jñānena? prasādasya mokṣasādhanatābodhake "tamevaṃ vidvān"yamevaiṣa vṛṇute"ityādāviva "priyo hi"iti vākye 'nyaniṣedhābhāvādityāśṅkāṃ smṛtyā pariharati - 'karmaṇā'; iti / kāmyākāmyobhayakarmaṇeti yāvat/ tathā ca 'karmaṇā'; janyo yaḥ 'prasādaḥ'; sa 'adhamaḥ'; eva 'proktaḥ'; prāmāṇikaiḥ/ evaṃ 'śravaṇādibhiḥ'; yaḥ prasādo bhavati/
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 74:
Now, since divine grace is accomplished even through action and the like, as [seen from] 'that action which pleases <s>Hari</s>' and 'he who [teaches] this supreme secret' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 18.68) and similar [passages], what is the need for knowledge? [Also,] in the <s>Śruti</s> passages that teach grace as the means to <s>mokṣa</s>, such as 'one who knows Him thus' and 'He is attainable by the one whom He chooses,' there is no negation of other [means], unlike in 'for I am dear' — anticipating this objection, he resolves it through <s>Smṛti</s>: 'By action.' This means: by both <s>kāmya</s> (desire-prompted) and <s>akāmya</s> (desireless) action. And thus, the 'grace' that is produced 'by action' is 'declared' by the authorities to be 'inferior' indeed. Likewise, the grace that arises 'from hearing and the like' —
is middling; but the grace [produced] through the attainment of knowledge is considered supreme. //
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 75:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.75:
sa 'madhyamaḥ'; / 'jñānasampattyā'; aparokṣajñānaparipākena janyo yaḥ 'prasādaḥ'; sa eva 'uttamo mataḥ'; utkṛṣṭatayā pramita ityarthaḥ / avadhāraṇārthakatuśabdasya dvirgrahaṇaṃ triṣvapyanvayasūcanārtham /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 75:
That [grace from hearing] is 'middling.' The 'grace' that is produced 'through the attainment of knowledge' — through the ripening of direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) knowledge — that alone 'is considered supreme,' that is, it is apprehended as the most excellent: this is the meaning. The word 'tu' with its emphatic force is used twice to indicate its connection with all three [grades].
From the inferior grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the heavenly world (<s>svargaloka</s>) is proclaimed.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 76:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.76:
kimato yadyevamityata āha - 'prasādāt'; iti / turviśeṣe / tathāca 'adhamāt viṣṇoḥ prasādāt'; kāmyakarmasādhyāt 'svargalokaḥ'; bhāvyatayā vṛddhaiḥ 'prakīrtitaḥ'; ityarthaḥ / kāmyaphalamātropalakṣakametat "parīkṣya lokān"(mu.u. 1-2-12) iti śruteḥ kāmyakarmaṇāṃ vairāgyajananadvārā mokṣe 'pyupayogo 'stīti jñātavyam / evaṃ akāmyakarmasādhyāt adhamaprasādāt antaḥkaraṇaśuddhyādidvārā mokṣo bhavatītyapi jñātavyam / na ca adhamaprasādaśūnyānāṃ atidveṣiṇāṃ duryodhanādīnāṃ kathaṃ svargaprāptiriti vācyam, bhāgavatācāryarahitānāṃ tadabhāvoktāvapi tadvatāṃ tatsambhavāt / yathoktaṃ gītātātparye -
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.1, verse 76:
What follows if this is so? To this he says: 'From grace.' The particle 'tu' is for specification. And thus, 'from the inferior grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — from that [grace] accomplished through desire-prompted action — 'the heavenly world' is 'proclaimed' by the elders as something to be attained: this is the meaning. This is merely illustrative of all desire-prompted fruits. From the <s>Śruti</s> 'having examined the worlds' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.12), it should be known that desire-prompted actions also have utility for <s>mokṣa</s> through the channel of generating dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). Likewise, it should be known that from the inferior grace accomplished through desireless (<s>akāmya</s>) action, <s>mokṣa</s> occurs through the channel of purification of the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) and the like. And one should not object: 'How can those who are devoid of even inferior grace — extreme haters like <s>Duryodhana</s> and others — attain heaven?' Because even when the absence of [grace] is stated for those who lack <s>Bhāgavata</s> teachers, the possibility [of grace] exists for those who possess such [teachers]. As stated in the <s>Gītātātparya</s> —
by the splendor of the <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers),

children.text: yānti svargaṃ tataḥ kṣipraṃ tamondhaṃ prāpnuvanti ca //
children.translated_text: they go to heaven quickly, and then they attain dense darkness. //
Others do not [reach] even heaven. //

children.text: iti / svargaloka ityuktyā tatraiva "mokṣaḥ sāṅkalpikaḥ svargaḥ bhūtāditvaṃ phalaṃ kramāt"iti vacanokto yo nityasaṃsāribhī rājasarājasai rājasatāmasaiśca prāpya svargapratinidhitvena kalpito daityendralokaḥ sāṅkalpikaḥ svargaḥ sa iha na vivakṣitaḥ, kintu saptalokāntargato rājasasāttvikaiḥ prāpyaḥ svargaloka eveti sūcitam /
children.translated_text: Thus. By saying 'the heavenly world,' it is indicated that what is referred to here is not the so-called 'imagined heaven' (<s>sāṅkalpika svarga</s>) mentioned in the statement there: 'Liberation, imagined heaven, and attainment of the state of elements are the fruits in succession' — that realm of the lords of <s>Daityas</s> which is imagined as a substitute for heaven, attained by those of <s>rājasa</s>-<s>rājasa</s>, <s>rājasa</s>-<s>tāmasa</s> nature who are eternally bound in <s>saṃsāra</s> — but rather, the heavenly world included within the seven worlds, attainable by those of <s>rājasa</s>-<s>sāttvika</s> nature: this is what is indicated.
From the middling [grace], <s>Janaloka</s> and other [worlds]; but the supreme [grace] alone grants liberation. //
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.1, verse 77:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.77:
'janalokādiḥ'; ityatra tu janatyāgena janākhyalokasyaiva pratipattayarthaṃ lokaśabdaprayoga iti jñeyam / janalokādirityatra tatpuruṣo bahuvrīhiśca vivakṣitaḥ / tuśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / tathā ca 'madhyamāt'; viṣṇoḥ prasādāt janalokasyādirmaharlokaḥ janatapolokādireva vā bhavati na muktiḥ / 'muktidastu'; uttamaprasāda eva prakīrtito vṛddhaiḥ, na tvanyāviti yojanā / tathā ca karmādinā bhagavatprasādasiddhāvapi tasyānuttamatvāt jñānasādhyasyaivottamatvāt anuttamena svargādimātrasiddhāvapi mokṣāsiddheḥ tatsādhanaprasādāya jñānamapekṣitamiti bhāvaḥ / na cātra "īyustrīn karmaṇā lokān jñānenaiva taduttarān"iti vākyavirodhaḥ śaṅkyaḥ, tasya maharlokasthākṛtakabhāgaviṣayatvāt, asya ca punarāvartyabhāgaviṣayatvāt, 'sāmānyadarśanāllokāḥ'; iti pramāṇabalena jñānaśabdasya svabimbaviṣayayogyāparokṣavyatiriktasāmānyāvatārādyaparokṣaviṣayatvāt, tasya ca śravaṇādibhirityatra hyādipadena grahaṇādvā; nyāyāmṛtoktarītyā jñānadvāreti śeṣakaraṇādvā;
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.77: In '<s>janalokādi</s>' (beginning with the <s>Janaloka</s>), the word '<s>loka</s>' is used for the understanding of the world called <s>Jana</s> alone, by the dropping of [the compounding with] <s>jana</s>. In '<s>janalokādi</s>,' both a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> and a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound are intended. The word 'tu' is for specification. And thus: through the grace of the middling [category] — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — one attains <s>Maharloka</s>, which is the beginning of <s>Janaloka</s>, or the beginning of <s>Janataparloka</s> and the like — but not liberation. 'But the giver of liberation' — the supreme grace alone is declared by the elders, not the other — this is the construction. And thus: even though the grace of the Lord is attained through <s>karma</s> and the like, since that [grace] is not the highest, and since only what is attained through knowledge is the highest, and since even with the non-highest [grace] only heaven and the like are attained but not liberation — knowledge is required for the grace that is the means of that [liberation]: this is the purport. Nor should the contradiction with the statement 'They went to three worlds through action, and to the ones above through knowledge alone' be suspected here, since that pertains to the non-created portion of <s>Maharloka</s>, while this pertains to the returnable portion; and by the force of the authority 'from the general perspective, the worlds,' the word 'knowledge' here refers to the direct perception of general manifestations and the like, excluding the direct perception that is fit for [perceiving] one's own prototype; and because this is included by the word 'ādi' (and so on) in 'through <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing) and so on'; or because, in the manner stated in the <s>Nyāyāmṛta</s>, 'through knowledge' is made a supplement;
or because the word 'eva' (alone) has the sense of excluding what is not connected — there is no contradiction.

children.text: śravaṇaṃ mananaṃ caiva dhyānaṃ bhaktistathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Śravaṇa</s> (hearing), <s>manana</s> (reflection), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) likewise —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.78:
nanvastūttamaprasādāya jñānāpekṣā, tathāpi "karmaṇā jñānamātanoti"ityādeḥ karmādināpi jñānaṃ bhavatīti na tadarthaṃ jijñāsā kartavyā "ātmā"iti vākye 'nyaniṣedhābhāvādityāśaṅkāṃ prakṛtapramāṇaśeṣeṇa pariharati - 'śravaṇaṃ'; iti / atra evakārasya dvirgrahaṇaṃ sarvatra sambandhajñāpanāya / te ca śravaṇādīnāṃ kāryasādhane anyasāhityanirāsaktāḥ, "naraṃ ca nārāyaṇameva"ityādāviva anabhimatakarmādivyāvartakāśca / dvayordvayossamuccaye 'ca'; śabdau / 'tathā'; śabda upamāyām / 'tathaiva ca'; iti nipātasamudāyo vā / bhaktigrahaṇaṃ prasaṅgāt dṛṣṭāntārthaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.78: [Objection:] Granted that knowledge is required for the supreme grace, nevertheless, from [statements like] 'through <s>karma</s> one extends knowledge,' knowledge arises even through <s>karma</s> and the like, so no inquiry need be undertaken for that purpose — since there is no negation of other [means] in the statement '<s>Ātman</s>' — to this objection he responds with the remainder of the authoritative text under discussion: '<s>śravaṇam</s>' (hearing). Here, the doubling of the word 'eva' is for indicating its connection everywhere. Those [words 'eva'] exclude the assistance of other [means] in accomplishing the effect of <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like, and exclude undesired <s>karma</s> and the like, just as in 'both <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone.' The words 'ca' are for aggregation of pairs. The word 'tathā' is for comparison. 'Tathaiva ca' is a group of particles. The mention of <s>bhakti</s> is incidental, or for the purpose of illustration.
The primary means for the attainment of knowledge is accepted [as these]; no other is prescribed. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.79:
tathā ca 'jñānasampattau'; aparokṣajñānaprāptau yathā bhaktistathā śravaṇādyeva sādhanaṃ, nānyatkarmādītyarthaḥ / kā gatistarhi "karmaṇā jñānamātanoti"ityādivacanasyetyata āha - 'pradhānaṃ'; iti / śravaṇādi pradhānaṃ sādhanaṃ 'anyat'; apradhānamityeva 'iṣyate'; abhyupeyate prāmāṇikaiḥ, na tvanyat sādhanameva neti yojanā / apradhānasādhanaviṣayaṃ karmādivacanamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.79: And thus, 'for the attainment of knowledge' — for obtaining direct knowledge — just as <s>bhakti</s>, so <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing) and the like alone are the means, not anything else like <s>karma</s>: this is the meaning. 'What then is the role of the statement "through <s>karma</s> one extends knowledge"?' — to this he says: 'primary.' <s>Śravaṇa</s> and the like are the primary means; 'other [means]' are accepted by the authoritative [teachers] as merely non-primary — not that other means are not means at all: this is the construction. The statements about <s>karma</s> and the like pertain to the non-primary means: this is the purport.

children.text: na caitāni vinā kaścit jñānamāpa kutaścana // iti nāradīye //
children.translated_text: And without these, no one has ever obtained knowledge from any source whatsoever. // Thus in the <s>Nāradīya</s> [Purāṇa]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.80:
viparītaṃ kiṃ na syādityata āha - 'na ca'; iti / caśabdo 'pyarthaḥ / tathā ca 'etāni'; śravaṇādīni 'vinā kaścit'; api adhikārī 'kutaścana'; karmādessataḥ 'jñānaṃ nāpa'; evametāni śravaṇādīni santicet kutaśca karmādervinā jñānaṃ nāpeti neti yojanā / tathā ca nirapekṣānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ śravaṇādyeva jñāne pradhānaṃ sākṣātsādhanaṃ, karmādi tu tadabhāvāt pāramparyeṇa sādhanamiti na vaiparītyamiti bhāvaḥ / 'nāradīye'; 'yata uktaṃ'; iti śeṣaḥ / asya 'ato "yato nārāyaṇa"ityādinoktaṃ yuktaṃ'; ityupaskṛtavākyenānvayaḥ / 'yato nārāyaṇa'; ityanena jijñāsāyāḥ nirviṣayatvaśaṅkānirāsāya prayuktaḥ sautro brahmaśabdo nārāyaṇapara iti vyākhyātaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.80: 'Could not the reverse be the case?' — to this he says: 'na ca' (and not). The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'api' (even). And thus: 'without these' — without <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like, 'no one' — no qualified student, 'from any source whatsoever' — from <s>karma</s> and the like, 'did not obtain knowledge.' Thus: if these <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like exist, then even without <s>karma</s> and the like, knowledge [is obtained]; but not without [<s>śravaṇa</s> and the like]: this is the construction. And thus: by invariable positive and negative concomitance independently, <s>śravaṇa</s> and the like alone are the primary, direct means of knowledge, while <s>karma</s> and the like, lacking that [direct connection], are means only indirectly — therefore there is no reversal: this is the purport. 'In the <s>Nāradīya</s>' — 'as it is stated' is to be supplied. The connection is with the sentence prepared [earlier] as 'therefore what was stated by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like is justified.' By '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like,' the word <s>Brahman</s> in the <s>sūtra</s>, employed to remove the doubt of the inquiry being objectless, is explained as referring to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
And the word <s>Brahman</s> [applies] to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.81:
nanu nārāyaṇaprasādamṛte na mokṣaścet tarhi tajjijñāsaiva kartavyā na brahmajijñāsā / na ca vācyaṃ nārāyaṇa eva brahmapadena vivakṣitaḥ sūtrakṛteti, brahmaśabdasya bahvarthatvena sūtrakāravivakṣāviśeṣasya durjñeyatvādityata āha - 'brahma'; iti / mukhya iti śeṣaḥ / caḥ 'anekārtho 'pi brahmaśabdaḥ'; iti apyarthe, yata ityarthe ca / tathā ca brahmaśabdasyānekārthatve 'pi yataḥ saḥ viṣṇāveva mukhyaḥ ato mukhyāmukhyayormukhyasyaiva grāhyatvāt sa eva sūtrakāravivakṣito jñāyata iti yojanā / atra śabdāntaraṃ vihāya viṣṇuśabdaprayogeṇa tacchabdagatānāṃ vargapañcamaṣaṣṭhacaturthānāṃ ṇaṣavānāṃ saṅkhyārekhālekhanena sūtrāṇāṃ catuṣṣaṣṭyuttarapañcaśatasaṅkhyoktā bhavati / yadvā -
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.81: [Objection:] If liberation is not possible without the grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, then the inquiry should be into Him, not an inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>. Nor can one say that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is intended by the word <s>Brahman</s> by the <s>sūtra</s>-author, since the word <s>Brahman</s> has many meanings and the specific intention of the <s>sūtra</s>-author is difficult to know — to this he says: '<s>Brahma</s>.' 'Primary' is to be supplied. The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'api' (even though) — [meaning] 'even though the word <s>Brahman</s> has many meanings'; and in the sense of 'yataḥ' (since). And thus: even though the word <s>Brahman</s> has many meanings, since it is primary only in [reference to] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, therefore, since between primary and non-primary [senses] the primary alone is to be adopted, that alone is understood as the intention of the <s>sūtra</s>-author: this is the construction. Here, by the use of the word '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' instead of another word, through writing as numerals the count of the class-fifth, class-sixth, and class-fourth [consonants] — <s>ṇa</s>, <s>ṣa</s>, and <s>va</s> — occurring in that word, the number of <s>sūtra</s>s as five hundred and sixty-four is stated. Alternatively —
In terms of space, time, and qualities, and from plenitude,
the name <s>Brahman</s> is primarily [applicable] to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nowhere else. //

children.text: ityaitareyabhāṣyokteḥ deśakālaguṇāparicchedarūpatrividhapūrtivācakabrahmaśabdavyākhyānāya tādṛśaviṣṇuśabdaprayogaḥ/ ṭīkāyāṃ tu - atra viṣṇugrahaṇena "saviṣṇurāha hi / taṃ brahmetyācakṣate"ityanyonyāvyavahitasūtradvayakaraṇānantarameva brahmamīmāṃsāyāḥ vyāsenārabdhatvādetadavyavahitadevamīmāṃsāntyasūtradvaye brahmatvena nārāyaṇasyaiva prakṛtatvaṃ sūcayatīti prayojanāntaramuktam / tattvapradīpe 'pyetadeva 'yaśca devatāmīmāṃsānte "viṣṇureva hi tat śrutestaṃ brahmetyācakṣate"iti sarvadevottamatvena pratijñāto brahmatvena coktaḥ, sa eva brahmaśabdenottaramīmāṃsāyāṃ vicāryatvenocyate'; iti pāṭhabhedenoktam/
children.translated_text: — since in the <s>Aitareyabhāṣya</s>, the word <s>Brahman</s>, which denotes the threefold plenitude of space, time, and qualities, is explained, the word <s>Viṣṇu</s> of that nature is used for the purpose of explaining it. In the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, however, another purpose is stated: by the use of the word <s>Viṣṇu</s> here, since the <s>Brahma-mīmāṃsā</s> was begun by <s>Vyāsa</s> immediately after composing the two <s>sūtra</s>s '<s>sa Viṣṇu</s>' and 'they call him <s>Brahman</s>' — in the last two <s>sūtra</s>s of the <s>Devamīmāṃsā</s> (theology of deities) immediately preceding [the <s>Brahmasūtra</s>s], he indicates that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is the subject under discussion as <s>Brahman</s>. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> too, this same [point] is stated with a variant reading: 'He who at the end of the <s>Devamīmāṃsā</s> was affirmed as superior to all gods with [the statement] "<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, for so says the <s>śruti</s>; they call him <s>Brahman</s>" and declared as <s>Brahman</s> — He alone is stated as being investigated by the word <s>Brahman</s> in the <s>Uttaramīmāṃsā</s> (Vedānta).'
Whom the sages perceive within the ocean — in that imperishable supreme [being], the creatures [rest].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.82:
brahmaśabdasyānyatrāpi rūḍhatvādrūḍhereva mukhyavṛttitvātkuto 'sau viṣṇāveva mukhya ityata āha - 'yaṃ'; iti/ 'brahmaśabdaśca'; ityādi atrāpi sambadhyate / co yadyapītyādyarthe / hiśabdo yata ityarthe / śrutirāheti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca yadyapi brahmaśabdo 'nyatra rūḍhaḥ, tathāpi 'śrutiḥ'; "yamanta"ityādikā yataḥ kavīnāṃ mate 'tadeva paramaṃ brahma'; ityāhuriti prayogabāhulyarūpāṃ rūḍhimāha, ato brahmaśabdo viṣṇāveva paramamukhya ityarthaḥ / anyatrājñarūḍheḥ vidvadrūḍheratimukhyatvāditi bhāvaḥ / yamantassamudre iti vākyam -
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.82: Since the word <s>Brahman</s> is conventional (<s>rūḍha</s>) elsewhere too, and since a conventional meaning is indeed the primary function — how then is it primary only in [reference to] <s>Viṣṇu</s>? — to this he says: '<s>yam</s>' (whom). '<s>Brahmaśabdaśca</s>' (and the word <s>Brahman</s>) and the rest also connect here. 'Ca' is in the sense of 'yadyapi' (even though). The word 'hi' is in the sense of 'yataḥ' (since). 'The <s>śruti</s> says' is to be supplied. And thus: even though the word <s>Brahman</s> is conventional elsewhere, the <s>śruti</s> — [the passage] beginning with '<s>yamantassamudre</s>' (whom within the ocean) — 'since in the view of the sages, "that alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>"' — declares a conventional usage in the form of abundant application, therefore the word <s>Brahman</s> is primarily of the highest [primary sense] only in [reference to] <s>Viṣṇu</s>: this is the meaning. Since the convention of the ignorant is less primary than the convention of the learned: this is the purport. The passage '<s>yamantassamudre</s>' —

children.text: yadoṣadhībhiḥ puruṣān paśūṃśca viveśa bhūtāni carācarāṇi /
children.translated_text: Who entered beings, both moving and non-moving, humans and animals, along with herbs;

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ nānyadaṇīyasaṃ hi parātparaṃ yanmahato mahāntam //
children.translated_text: beyond whom there is nothing else subtler — who is greater than the great, supreme beyond the supreme. //
Who is one, unmanifest, of infinite form, the universe, ancient, beyond darkness. //

children.text: iti vākyena saha vyākhyātaṃ viṣṇutattvanirṇayaṭīkāyām / tathā hi - 'yamantassamudre'; vibhakttayarthe 'vyayībhāvaḥ samudrasyāntassthitaṃ 'kavayo'; jñāninaḥ 'avayanti'; īṣadeva jānanti, yasmin 'tadakṣare'; avijñeyatvarūpapūrvaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭe prasiddhe vā avināśini 'parame'; prajā adhīnāḥ santi /
children.translated_text: — this passage has been explained in the <s>Viṣṇutattvarnirṇaya Ṭīkā</s> together with the [full] passage. That is: '<s>yamantassamudre</s>' — the indeclinable compound is in the sense of the case-ending; situated within the ocean; 'the sages' — the knowers; 'perceive' — know slightly; 'in that imperishable' [being] — in the well-known one who is indestructible, qualified by the prior qualifier in the form of unknowability, or [simply the well-known one who is] imperishable; 'supreme' — the creatures are dependent [on him].

children.text: yataḥ prasūtā jagataḥ prasūtī toyena jīvānvyasasarja bhūmyām //
children.translated_text: From whom the progenitrix of the world issued forth, who created living beings on earth with water. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.83:
'jagataḥ prasūtī'; prasūtirjanayitrī mūlaprakṛtirlakṣmīḥ 'yato'; yasmāt prasūtā utpannā, sṛṣṭau abhimukhībabhūveti vā, yacca yadvastu 'toyena'; tattajjīvakarmaṇā svavīryeṇa vā, toyaśabdoktāmbūpalakṣitairbhūtairvā 'bhūmyāṃ'; pṛthivyādiṣu lokeṣu 'jīvān vyasasarja'; vividhaṃ sasarja /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.83: 'The progenitrix of the world' — the creator, the mother, the primordial <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s> — 'from whom' — from whom she issued forth, was produced, or became disposed toward creation; and 'with water' — through the <s>karma</s> of the respective living beings, or by His own power, or with the elements indicated by the word 'water' — 'on earth' — in the worlds such as earth and the like — 'he created living beings' — created them in diverse ways.

children.text:
ityādyuktvā "tadevartaṃ tadu satyamāhustadeva brahma paramaṃ kavīnām"
(mahānā. 1.)
children.translated_text: Having said this and more, 'That alone is <s>ṛta</s> (truth), that alone is <s>satya</s> (reality) — they say that alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> of the sages.' (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad 1)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.84-85:
yacca 'oṣadhībhiḥ'; sahitān 'puruṣān paśūṃśca carācarāṇi bhūtāni'; preraṇāya 'viveśa'; / 'carācarāṇi bhūtāni'; ityanenaiva siddhe yajñāṅgatvādinā viśiṣṭānāṃ vrīhyoṣadhīnāṃ grahaṇāya punarvacanam / 'ataḥ'; yasmāt 'paraṃ'; atiśayena 'anyat'; vastu 'aṇīyasaṃ'; aṇīyo nāsti, yacca 'parātparaṃ'; utkṛṣṭādutkṛṣṭaṃ 'mahato'; mahatparimāṇādapi 'mahāntaṃ'; mahat, 'yadekaṃ'; kevalaṃ 'avyaktaṃ'; svaprasādaṃ vinā atīndriyaṃ 'viśvaṃ pūrṇaṃ tamasaḥ'; prakṛterajñānādvā 'parastāt'; atikramya sthitaṃ 'tadevartaṃ'; yathārthajñānarūpaṃ 'tadu'; tadeva 'satyaṃ'; jñānapūrvakriyāvat 'tadeva kavīnāṃ'; mate 'paramaṃ'; mukhyaṃ 'brahma'; ityāhuriti / atra 'tadakṣare'; iti śrutipāṭhaḥ / 'yadakṣare'; iti kvacitpāṭhe yasminnityadhyāhāro na kāryaḥ / 'vyasasarja'; iti prāyikaḥ śrutipāṭhaḥ / 'vyacasarja'; ityapi kvacitpaṭhanti / atra sakārasya cakārādeśaḥ chāndasaḥ / ādyapakṣe 'pi vi ā sasarjetyavayavavibhāgaḥ tatrāṅgo hrasvatvaṃ chāndasaṃ bahulagrahaṇāt / "indrā varuṇa vāmaham"iti śrutau ṇakārātparasyākārasya yathā hrasvatvaṃ tadvaditi nārāyaṇapaṇḍitācāryoktiḥ/ "vyasasarja visasarja bahulagrahaṇāt" iti prameyadīpoktirapi hrasvābhiprāyikaiva / kecittu liṭyaḍāgamaḥ chāndaso bahulagrahaṇāditi prameyadīpārthamāhuḥ / tadāryoktātpakṣāntaram / padmanābhatīrthakṛtatattvanirṇayaṭīkāyāṃ nyāyaratnāvalyāṃ tu 'vayanti'; iti vicchidya 'tadakṣare'; ityeva ca paṭhitvā, "yaṃ puruṣaṃ samudre 'ntaḥ kavayo vayanti vāñchanti tadakṣare yasmin tasmin akṣare nāśavarjite parame prajāstadādhārāḥ tiṣṭhanti, jagataḥ prasūtī jagajjanayitrī prakṛtiḥ yataḥ prasūtā prādurbhūtā satī toyena itaramiśritena jīvān dehavattvena vyasasarja visṛṣṭavatī"ityekānvayena "tadeva tātparyaviṣayībhūtatvādṛtaṃ tadevābādhitarūpatvātsatyaṃ tadeva kavīnāmabhimataṃ paraṃ brahma"ityartha uktaḥ / nārāyaṇapaṇḍitāryakṛtau tattvamañjaryāmapi 'tadakṣare'; iti paṭhitvā "yamavayanti avagacchanti yasmiṃstasmin akṣare prajāḥ santi yataḥ prasūtā parādhīnaviśeṣaṃ prāptā śrīḥ toyena karmaṇā jīvān bhūmyāṃ prakṛtyāṃ vyasasarja"ityanvayena "tadevartaṃ śaśvadekaprakāraṃ satyaṃ sādhu guṇapūrṇaṃ"ityartha uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.84-85: And 'who entered, along with herbs, humans and animals, moving and non-moving beings' — for impelling [them]. 'Moving and non-moving beings' — although this is already established by [the phrase] itself, the re-statement is for the inclusion of rice-plants and the like, distinguished by being accessories of sacrifice. 'Beyond that' — from which there is 'nothing else' — no other thing — 'subtler'; and which is 'greater than the great' — greater even than the great measure; 'great' — [and which is] 'one' — sole; 'unmanifest' — beyond the senses without its own grace; 'the universe' — complete; 'beyond darkness' — having transcended <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) or ignorance — standing [thus]; 'that alone is <s>ṛta</s>' — of the nature of knowledge as it truly is; 'that' — that very [being]; '<s>satya</s>' (reality) — possessing action preceded by knowledge; 'that alone' in the view 'of the sages' — is the primary supreme <s>Brahman</s> — they say. Here '<s>tadakṣare</s>' is the <s>śruti</s> reading. In some readings '<s>yadakṣare</s>' — in which case the supply of '<s>yasmin</s>' is not needed. '<s>Vyasasarja</s>' is the usual <s>śruti</s> reading. Some also read '<s>vyacasarja</s>.' Here, the substitution of <s>ca</s> for <s>sa</s> is Vedic. Even on the first view, the analysis is <s>vi ā sasarja</s>, and the shortening of the <s>aṅga</s> there is Vedic, by the principle of <s>bahula</s> (variable application). Just as in the <s>śruti</s> 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,' the shortening of the <s>ā</s> after <s>ṇa</s> — likewise, according to <s>Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya</s>.

children.text:
iti hi śrutiḥ /
"tanno viṣṇuḥ"
(mahānā. 3-16).
iti vacanāt viṣṇureva hi tatrocyate /
children.translated_text: Thus is the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text). From the statement '<s>tanno Viṣṇuḥ</s>' (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad 3.16), it is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone who is spoken of there.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.86:
nanu 'tadeva'; iti vākye tacchabdena kuto viṣṇuniścayaḥ? samudrasthatvaliṅgāditi cet - na, tasya rudrādāvapi kathañcitsambhavādityato niravakāśaviṣṇuśruterevetyāha - 'tannaḥ'; iti / 'iti vacanādviṣṇureva'; 'tatra'; "tadeva"iti śrutau tacchabdena 'ucyate'; iti niśicīyata ityarthaḥ / hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / atra 'tannaḥ'; ityekadeśagrahaṇena "nārāyaṇāya vidmahe vāsudevāya dhīmahi, tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt"iti samagravākyaṃ gṛhyate / dvitīyārthe caturthyau / tathā ca yasmāt vayaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ 'vidmahe'; jānīmahe yataśca taṃ vāsudevaṃ 'dhīmahi'; dhyāyemahi 'tat'; tasmāt 'naḥ'; asmān 'tat'; śubhaṃ prati 'viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt'; prerayatviti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.86: Now, in the sentence 'that very one,' how is certainty about <s>Viṣṇu</s> established through the word 'tat'? If one says it is from the indicatory mark of being situated in the ocean — no, because that could somehow apply to <s>Rudra</s> and others too. Therefore, it is only from the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-<s>śruti</s> that leaves no room [for others] — thus he says '<s>tannaḥ</s>' etc. The meaning is: from the statement '<s>tannaḥ</s>,' it is determined that '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' is denoted by the word 'tat' in the <s>śruti</s> 'that very one.' The particle 'hi' indicates well-known fact. Here, by citing the partial phrase '<s>tannaḥ</s>,' the complete sentence is taken up: '<s>Nārāyaṇāya vidmahe Vāsudevāya dhīmahi, tanno Viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt</s>' (We know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, we meditate upon <s>Vāsudeva</s>, may that <s>Viṣṇu</s> inspire us). The dative case is used in the sense of the accusative. And thus: since we 'know' (<s>vidmahe</s>) <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and since we 'meditate' (<s>dhīmahi</s>) upon that <s>Vāsudeva</s>, 'therefore' (<s>tat</s>) may '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' 'impel' (<s>pracodayāt</s>) 'us' (<s>naḥ</s>) toward 'that' (<s>tat</s>) which is auspicious — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.
And the status [of being <s>Brahman</s>] is not obtained for the others from words [denoting] them.
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.87:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.87:
yadyuttaravākye viṣṇuśabdaśravaṇādviṣṇurevātroktaṃ brahma, tarhi 'tanno rudraḥ'; ityādītaraśabdaśravaṇāt rudrāderapi mukhyabrahmatā prāptetyata āha - 'na ca'; iti / caśabdaḥ samuccaye / tathā ca 'itaraśabdāt'; rudrādivācakaśabdabalāttasya rudrāderapi tasya mukhyabrahmatvasya 'prāptirna'; ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.87: If, because the word <s>Viṣṇu</s> is heard in the subsequent sentence, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the <s>Brahman</s> taught here, then from hearing words denoting others such as '<s>tanno Rudraḥ</s>' etc., the status of being the primary <s>Brahman</s> would be obtained for <s>Rudra</s> and others too — to address this he says 'na ca' (and not). The word 'ca' is used in the sense of conjunction. And thus: from the force of words denoting others such as <s>Rudra</s> etc., 'there is no obtaining' of that status of being the primary <s>Brahman</s> for <s>Rudra</s> and others — this is the meaning.

children.text: nāmani viśvābhi na santi loke yadāvirāsīdanṛtasya sarvam /
children.translated_text: All names in the world do not primarily denote [others], since everything of the non-eternal [world] has come into being [from Him].
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.88:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.88:
kuta ityatastatprāpakaśabdānāṃ viṣṇāveva mukhyatvāditi hetūpaskārabhipretya tasyāsiddhiparihārāya viṣṇormukhyataḥ sarvanāmavācyatve śrutimāha - 'nāmāni'; iti / 'śruteḥ'; iti kvacitpañcamyantapāṭhaḥ / prathamāntapāṭhe yato 'ta iti śeṣaḥ / asya 'na ca'; ityanenānvayaḥ / 'yat'; yasmāt 'anṛtasya'; ṛtabhinnasya viṣṇvitarasya lokasya jagataḥ 'sarvaṃ'; nāmapravṛttinimittaṃ 'āvirāsīt'; abhūt tasmādutpattimatpravṛttinimittavattvāt 'viśvā'; viśvāni sarvāṇi 'nāmāni'; 'loke'; rudrādijagati 'abhi'; mukhyataḥ vācakatayā 'na santi'; ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.88: Why is this so? Because the words that would establish [<s>Brahman</s>-status for others] are primarily applicable only to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — intending this as the supporting reason, and to remove the objection that this is unestablished, he cites a <s>śruti</s> establishing that all names primarily denote <s>Viṣṇu</s>: '<s>nāmāni</s>' etc. In some readings, '<s>śruteḥ</s>' appears with the ablative ending. In the reading with the nominative ending, 'because' is supplied. This connects with 'na ca' (and not). 'Since' (<s>yat</s>) 'everything' (<s>sarvam</s>) — the cause for the application of names — of 'the non-eternal' (<s>anṛtasya</s>), that is, of the world other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'has come into being' (<s>āvirāsīt</s>), therefore, because the causes of name-application are themselves produced, 'all' (<s>viśvā</s>) 'names' (<s>nāmāni</s>) 'in the world' (<s>loke</s>) — in the realm of <s>Rudra</s> and others — 'do not exist' (<s>na santi</s>) 'primarily' (<s>abhi</s>), that is, as primary denotations — this is the meaning.

children.text: nāmāni sarvāṇi yamāviśanti taṃ vai viṣṇuṃ paramamudāharanti //
children.translated_text: All names enter into whom — Him they declare to be <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Supreme.
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.89:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.89:
tarhi kasmin tāni mukhyānītyata āha 'nāmāni'; iti / vaiśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / paramamiti hetugarbhaviśeṣaṇam /
tathā ca 'sarvāṇi nāmāni'; 'yaṃ'; 'ā'; mukhyato vācakatvena 'viśanti'; 'taṃ paramaṃ'; deśakālābhyāmaparicchinnapravṛttinimittaṃ 'viṣṇuṃ vai'; vadanti vidvāṃsa ityarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - 'viśvā'; viśvāni 'nāmāni loke'; abhito 'na santi'; mukhyato na santi mukhyato na lokavācakāni 'yat'; yasmāt, yataḥ puruṣāt 'anṛtasya'; viṣṇvanyasya jagato janmalayādikaṃ sarvaṃ 'āvirāsīt', yaṃ ca vācakatvena 'nāmāni ā'; samantāt 'viśanti', 'taṃ'; ha 'viṣṇuṃ'; uttamaṃ vadantītyartha uktaḥ / etatpakṣe yacchabdasyāvṛttiḥ / dvitīyādipādatrayasya hetusamarpakatvam / pakṣadvaye 'pi viṣṇuśabdo bhinnakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.89: Then in whom are those [names] primary? To this he says '<s>nāmāni</s>' etc. The particle '<s>vai</s>' is used for emphasis. '<s>Paramam</s>' (Supreme) is a qualifier containing the reason within itself. And thus: 'all names' which 'enter into' (<s>viśanti</s>) 'whom' (<s>yam</s>) 'primarily' (<s>ā</s>) as primary denotations — 'Him,' who is 'supreme' (<s>paramam</s>), whose cause for name-application is unlimited by space and time, 'indeed' (<s>vai</s>) the learned ones declare to be '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' — this is the meaning. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: 'all' (<s>viśvā</s>) 'names' (<s>nāmāni</s>) 'in the world' (<s>loke</s>) 'do not exist' (<s>na santi</s>) primarily — they are not primarily denotative of the world — 'since' (<s>yat</s>), because from that <s>Puruṣa</s>, 'everything' of 'the non-eternal' (<s>anṛtasya</s>) — the creation, dissolution etc. of the world other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'has come into being' (<s>āvirāsīt</s>); and the one whom 'names enter into' (<s>nāmāni ā viśanti</s>) completely as denotations — 'Him' (<s>tam</s>) indeed they declare to be '<s>Viṣṇu</s>,' the Supreme — this is the meaning stated [there]. In this interpretation, the word '<s>yat</s>' occurs twice. The latter three quarters serve to present the reason. In both interpretations, the word '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' appears in different sequential positions.

children.text:
iti bhāllaveyaśrutiḥ /
"yo devānāṃ nāmadhā eva eva taṃ sampraśnaṃ bhuvanā yantyanyā"
(ṛ.saṃ.10-82-3.)
ityevaśabdānnānyeṣāṃ sarvanāmatā /
children.translated_text: Thus is the <s>Bhāllavīya</s> <s>śruti</s>. From the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) in the verse 'He who alone is the name-giver of the gods — unto Him as the object of inquiry do the other worlds go' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.82.3), the status of being denoted by all names does not belong to others.
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.90:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.90:
nanu yathā viṣṇoḥ śrutyantarasiddhasarvanāmatvenātroktaṃ brahmatvaṃ siddhyati tathā rudrādīnāmapi viṣṇvādiśabdavācyatvena atroktaṃ brahmatvaṃ kiṃ na syādityata āha - 'yaḥ'; iti / 'ityevaśabdāt'; iti itivākyasyaivaśabdāt 'anyeṣāṃ'; rudrādīnāṃ 'sarvanāmatā'; viṣṇvādisarvaśabdavācyatvaṃ netyarthaḥ / sarvanāmatetyanantaraṃ - yata evamataḥ 'tanno viṣṇuḥ'; (mahānā.3-16) ityādau nānyeṣāṃ prāptiḥ ata eva na brahmatvaṃ teṣāmiti vākyaśeṣaḥ / 'yo'; bhagavān 'eka eva devānāṃ'; brahmādīnāṃ 'nāmadhāḥ'; - viśvapāśabdavadayaṃ śabdaḥ - nāmadhārakaḥ na tvanye 'pi 'taṃ praśnaṃ'; praṣṭāraṃ 'anyā'; anyāni 'bhuvanā'; bhuvanāni lokāḥ 'saṃyanti'; saṃyānti mokṣe pralaye ceti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.90: Now, just as <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>Brahman</s>-hood taught here is established through His being denoted by all names as proven from another <s>śruti</s>, why should not <s>Rudra</s> and others also have their <s>Brahman</s>-hood taught here by being denoted by words like <s>Viṣṇu</s> etc.? To this he says '<s>yaḥ</s>' etc. From the word '<s>eva</s>' in this verse, '[the status of] being denoted by all names including <s>Viṣṇu</s> etc. does not [belong to] others' — meaning it does not belong to <s>Rudra</s> and others. After 'the status of being denoted by all names' — the remainder of the sentence is: since this is so, in '<s>tanno Viṣṇuḥ</s>' (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad 3.16) etc., the status [of <s>Brahman</s>] is not obtained for the others, and therefore <s>Brahman</s>-hood does not belong to them. 'He who' — the Lord — 'alone' (<s>eka eva</s>) is the 'name-giver' (<s>nāmadhāḥ</s>) 'of the gods' (<s>devānām</s>) — of <s>Brahmā</s> and others — this word, like '<s>viśvapā</s>,' [means] the bearer of names, not others also. Unto 'Him,' the 'object of inquiry' (<s>praśnam</s>), the questioner, 'the other' (<s>anyā</s>) 'worlds' (<s>bhuvanā</s>) 'go' (<s>saṃyānti</s>) — they reach [Him] in <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) and at the time of dissolution — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text:
"ajasya nābhāvadhyekamarpitaṃ yasmin viśvāni bhuvanāni tasthuḥ"/
(ṛ.saṃ.10-82-6.)
iti hi viṣṇorliṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'At the navel of the Unborn, one [thing] was placed, in which all the worlds are established' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.82.6) — this is indeed an indicatory mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.91:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.91:
nanvatrāpi yacchabdena viṣṇuriti kutaḥ? viśvakarmeti śrutibalādasya sūktākhyaprakaraṇasya viśvakarmādyanyaparatayā tadgatayacchabdasyāpi tatparatvaucityādityata āha - 'ajasya'; iti / 'hi'; yasmāt iti vākye 'viṣṇoḥ liṅgaṃ'; padmanābhatvākhyamasādhāraṇo dharmaḥ śrutaḥ tasmādyacchabdodito viṣṇurevetyanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.91: Now, how is it known that the word 'who' (<s>yat</s>) here also refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Because the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) named <s>Viśvakarma</s> could, by the force of the <s>śruti</s>, be about <s>Viśvakarma</s> or some other [deity], and the word '<s>yat</s>' occurring in it could appropriately refer to that [other deity] too — to this he says '<s>ajasya</s>' etc. The connection is: 'since' (<s>hi</s>) in the verse, an 'indicatory mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' (<s>Viṣṇoḥ liṅgam</s>) — namely, the unique attribute of being <s>Padmanābha</s> (lotus-naveled) — is heard, therefore the one denoted by the word '<s>yat</s>' is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text: utsargato liṅgāt śruteḥ prābalye 'pi sāvakāśāyā viśvakarmaśruteḥ niravakāśaliṅgena bādhopapatteriti bhāvaḥ / śrutyarthastu - 'ajasya'; ajanyasya puruṣasya 'nābhau ekaṃ'; vastu 'arpitaṃ'; udbhūtam / 'yasmin viśvāni bhuvanāni'; sarve caturdaśalokāḥ 'adhitasthuḥ'; adhiṣṭhitāḥ iti /
children.translated_text: The purport is: although as a general rule, <s>śruti</s> (direct Vedic statement) is stronger than <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark), here the <s>Viśvakarma</s> <s>śruti</s> has scope [for alternative interpretation], whereas the indicatory mark [pointing to <s>Viṣṇu</s>] leaves no scope [for alternatives], and therefore the overriding [of the general <s>śruti</s> by the indicatory mark] is justified. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is: at the 'navel' (<s>nābhau</s>) of the 'Unborn' (<s>ajasya</s>), the uncreated <s>Puruṣa</s>, 'one' (<s>ekam</s>) entity was 'placed' (<s>arpitam</s>), i.e., manifested, 'in which' (<s>yasmin</s>) 'all the worlds' (<s>viśvāni bhuvanāni</s>) — all the fourteen realms — 'are established' (<s>adhitasthuḥ</s>), i.e., are situated.
And no other meaning is possible without [accepting] the well-known meaning.
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.92:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.92:
nābhyarpitaṃ padmādanyatkiṃ na syādityata āha - 'na ca'; iti / caḥ samuccaye / prasiddhaṃ viṣṇunābhisthatvena prasiddhaṃ padmākhyārthaṃ 'vinānyo 'rtho'; na yujyate, prasiddhibādhādityarthaḥ / viśvakarmaśrutivatpadmanābhatvaliṅgamapyanyasya kiṃ na syādityato vādmaha - 'na ca'; iti / padmanābhatvena prasiddhapadārthaṃ bhagavantaṃ vinā 'anyaḥ'; padmanābho na yujyate prasiddhibādhādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.92: Why could not what was placed at the navel be something other than the lotus? To this he says 'na ca' (and not). The 'ca' is for conjunction. Without the well-known entity — well-known as being situated at <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel — namely the lotus, 'no other meaning is possible,' because it would contradict well-established usage — this is the meaning. Could not the indicatory mark of being lotus-naveled, like the <s>Viśvakarma</s> <s>śruti</s>, also apply to someone else? To this too he says 'na ca': without the Lord who is well-known as having a lotus at His navel, 'no other' lotus-naveled one 'is possible,' because it would contradict well-established usage — this is the meaning.

children.text: ajasya nābhāviti yasya nābherabhūt śruteḥ puṣkaraṃ lokasāram /
children.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s> 'at the navel of the Unborn,' a lotus — the essence of the world — came into being from whose navel.
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.93:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.93:
na kevalaṃ prasiddhibalādevaitacchrutyuktaṃ padmaṃ padmanābhaśca harirityavasīyate, kintu 'ajasya'; iti śrutestadubhayabodhakatvena smṛtyanugṛhītatvāccetyāha - 'ajasya'; iti / iti śruterityanvayaḥ / tathā ca 'ajasya nābhāviti śruteḥ'; sakāśāt 'lokasāraṃ'; lokādhārabhūtaṃ 'puṣkaraṃ'; padmaṃ 'abhūt'; iti jñāyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.93: It is not merely from the force of well-established usage that this lotus mentioned in the <s>śruti</s> and the lotus-naveled one are determined to be <s>Hari</s>, but also because the <s>śruti</s> '<s>ajasya</s>' etc. conveys both these [facts] and is supported by <s>smṛti</s> — thus he says '<s>ajasya</s>' etc. The connection is: 'from the <s>śruti</s> thus.' And so: from the <s>śruti</s> '<s>ajasya nābhāu</s>' (at the navel of the Unborn), it is known that the '<s>puṣkara</s>' (lotus), which is the 'essence of the world' (<s>lokasāram</s>), i.e., the support of the worlds, 'came into being' (<s>abhūt</s>).

children.text: tasmai namo vyastasamastaviśvavibhūtaye viṣṇave lokakartre // iti ca skānde /
children.translated_text: 'Salutations to that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the maker of the world, whose glories are the universe in both its differentiated and undifferentiated forms' — thus [it is said] in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa].
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.94:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.94:
'tasmai vyastasamastaviśvavibhūtaye'; viśvasya jagato vibhūtayaḥ sṛṣṭyādyaṣṭakaṃ jīvādau vyastāḥ vistṛtāḥ jaḍādau samastāḥ saṃkṣiptāḥ viśvavibhūtayo yenāsau vyastasamastaviśvavibhūtistasmai 'lokakartre'; lokasvāmine 'viṣṇave namaḥ'; ityarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - samastaviśvavibhūtayo yena vyastā sa vyastasamastaviśvavibhūtiḥ / atha vā vyastāḥ samastā viśvavibhūtayo yeneti dvedhā vyākhyātam / tatra divitīyaṃ ṭīkāyāṃ vivṛtam / pūrvārdhe viṣṇuvācakaśabdābhāvāduttarārdhodāharaṇam / 'iti ca skānde'; iti caśabdo bhinnakrameṇa 'uktaṃ'; ityadhyāhṛtapadena sambadhyate / yata evamataḥ 'ajasya'; ityuktaṃ padmameva, padmanābhaśca harireveti vākyaśeṣaḥ / na kevalaṃ prasiddhibādhāditi cārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.94: 'To Him whose glories are the universe in both differentiated and undifferentiated forms' — the glories (<s>vibhūtayaḥ</s>) of the universe (<s>viśva</s>), namely the eightfold [powers] beginning with creation, are 'differentiated' (<s>vyastāḥ</s>), i.e., distributed, in the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) etc., and 'undifferentiated' (<s>samastāḥ</s>), i.e., concentrated, in insentient entities etc. He in whom these glories of the universe are both differentiated and undifferentiated is the one 'whose glories are the universe in differentiated and undifferentiated forms.' To that 'maker of the world' (<s>lokakartṛ</s>), the lord of the worlds, 'salutations to <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — this is the meaning. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: He by whom the undifferentiated glories of the universe are differentiated is the one 'whose glories are the universe in differentiated-undifferentiated form.' Alternatively, He in whom the glories of the universe are both differentiated and undifferentiated — thus it is explained in two ways. Of these, the second is elaborated in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>. Because the word <s>Viṣṇu</s> does not appear in the first half [of the verse], the latter half serves as the citation. 'Thus in the <s>Skānda</s>' — the word 'ca' connects with the supplied word 'it is stated' in a different order. Since this is so, the remainder of the sentence is: the lotus stated in '<s>ajasya</s>' is indeed [that lotus], and the lotus-naveled one is indeed <s>Hari</s>. The meaning also includes: [this is established] not merely from the contradiction of well-established usage [if interpreted otherwise].

children.text:
"paro divā para enā pṛthivyā"
(ṛ.saṃ. 10-82-5)
iti samākhyāśrutau /
children.translated_text: 'Beyond heaven, beyond this earth' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.82.5) — in the <s>śruti</s> that bears a corresponding designation (<s>samākhyā</s>).
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.95:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.95:
yadā niravakāśaliṅgamātraṃ śrutibādhakaṃ tadā kimu vācyaṃ samākhyāyuktaṃ taditi bhāvenāha - 'para'; iti/ idaṃ cāvartate, 'viṣṇureva'; ityādikamatrāpi sambadhyate / tathā ca yataḥ viśvakarmasūkte "paro divā para enā pṛthivyā paro devebhirasurairyadasti"iti yā ākhyā uktiḥ tasyāḥ samā samānā 'paro divā'; ityevaṃrūpa 'śrutau'; āmbhṛṇīsūkte asti ato 'pi 'viṣṇureva'; viśvakarmasūktodita ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.95: When even an indicatory mark that leaves no scope [for alternatives] can override the <s>śruti</s>, what more need be said when it is accompanied by a corresponding designation — with this purport he says '<s>paraḥ</s>' etc. And this continues [from above]; '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' etc. connects here as well. And thus: since in the <s>Viśvakarma</s> <s>sūkta</s> the declaration 'beyond heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods and the <s>Asuras</s> is whatever exists' — and in the <s>Āmbhṛṇī</s> <s>sūkta</s> there exists a corresponding (<s>samā</s>, identical) designation (<s>ākhyā</s>) of the form 'beyond heaven' — therefore too, the one spoken of in the <s>Viśvakarma</s> <s>sūkta</s> is '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' — this is the meaning.

children.text:
"yaṃ kāmaye taṃ tamugraṃ kṛṇomi taṃ brahmāṇaṃ tamṛṣiṃ taṃ sumedhām"
(ṛ.saṃ. 10-125-5.) ityuktvā /
children.translated_text: Having said, 'Whomever I desire, him I make mighty; him a <s>Brahmā</s> (creator), him a <s>Ṛṣi</s> (seer), him one of great wisdom' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.125.5) —
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.96:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.96:
nanu samākhyāśrutāvapi viṣṇuḥ kuto vācya ityata āha - 'yaṃ'; iti / itītyanantaraṃ vākyenetyubhayatra śeṣaḥ / 'paro divā'; ityetatsamastamanenāpi yojyam / atra samākhyāśrutāvityekaṃ padam/ tathā ca yasmāt 'paro divā'; iti samākhyāśrutau metyākhyā mākhyā tayā sahitā samākhyā "prakṛtirvāva samāsamā"(mādhyandinaśrutiḥ) iti śrutau samāsamatvokteḥ 'nāmaikadeśe'; iti nyāyena samābhidhāvā, ahamiti prakṛtā lakṣmīḥ "yaṃ"ityādivākyena brahmādīnāṃ svādhīnatvamuktvā "mama yonirapsvantaḥ samudre" iti vākyena "paro divā"ityuktaṃ viṣṇuṃ svakāraṇatvena samudrasthatvena cāha, tasmādviṣṇureva samākhyāśrutipratipādya ityarthaḥ/ uktvetyanena lakṣmīkāraṇaṃ brahmādyanyatamaṃ kiṃ na syāditi śaṅkā vāritā / śrutau 'divā'; ityādi tṛtīyā pañcamyarthe / tathā ca - 'divaḥ'; 'śriyaḥ'; 'paraḥ'; 'enā'; etasyāḥ bhūmyāśca 'paraḥ'; uttamaḥ / 'devebhiḥ'; 'devebhyaḥ'; 'asuraiḥ'; asurebhyaśca 'paraḥ'; uttamaḥ / kiṃ bahunā - 'yadasti'; tasmātsarvasmādapi paraḥ / sa viṣṇuḥ dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ paraḥ / ahaṃ tu 'mahinā'; mahimnā 'etāvatī'; parimitā babhūva / ahametāvatī yathoktaprakārā mahimnā nāto 'dhiketi vā śrutyarthaḥ / ahamiti labdhapadena lakṣmīrucyate, etatsūktapravartikāyāḥ āmbhṛṇyāḥ lakṣmīrūpatvāt / tathā ca - ahaṃ 'yaṃ yaṃ'; rudrapadayogyaṃ jīvaṃ 'ugraṃ'; rudraṃ kartuṃ 'kāmaye'; iccheyaṃ 'taṃ taṃ'; ugraṃ kṛṇomi karomi / evaṃ tattatpadayogyaṃ yaṃ yaṃ 'brahmāṇaṃ'; 'ṛṣiṃ'; 'sumedhāṃ'; sumedhasaṃ vā kartuṃ kāmaye taṃ taṃ tathā karomītyarthaḥ / śiṣṭavākyārthaḥ "patyurasāmañjasyāt"(bra.sū. 2-2-37) ityadhikaraṇe vakṣyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.96: Now, why must <s>Viṣṇu</s> be the referent even in the <s>śruti</s> bearing a corresponding designation? To this he says '<s>yam</s>' etc. After 'thus' (<s>iti</s>), 'by the sentence' is to be supplied in both places. '<s>Paro divā</s>' etc. in its entirety should also be connected with this. Here '<s>samākhyā-śruti</s>' is a single compound. And thus: since in the <s>śruti</s> bearing a corresponding designation, 'beyond heaven' etc. [appears] — <s>samākhyā</s> means: the designation (<s>ākhyā</s>) that is 'equal' (<s>samā</s>), since 'me' (<s>me</s>) gives '<s>mākhyā</s>' and combined with '<s>samā</s>' gives '<s>samākhyā</s>' (the designation connected with 'me,' i.e., with <s>Lakṣmī</s>); from the <s>śruti</s> 'the root nature is indeed equal' (<s>Mādhyandina śruti</s>), the identity of <s>samā</s> is established; by the principle of 'a part of the name,' <s>samā</s> can also mean 'co-designated.' The speaker 'I' (<s>aham</s>) who is the subject here is <s>Lakṣmī</s>. Having declared through the sentence '<s>yam</s>' etc. that <s>Brahmā</s> and others are under her control, she then through the sentence '<s>mama yoniḥ apsu antaḥ samudre</s>' (my origin is in the waters, within the ocean) speaks of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the one described as 'beyond heaven' — as her cause and as the one situated in the ocean. Therefore, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the one taught in the <s>śruti</s> bearing a corresponding designation — this is the meaning. By the word 'having said' (<s>uktvā</s>), the doubt is precluded that the cause of <s>Lakṣmī</s> could be <s>Brahmā</s> or some other [deity]. In the <s>śruti</s>, '<s>divā</s>' etc. — the instrumental case is used in the sense of the ablative. And thus: '<s>paraḥ</s>' means 'beyond,' i.e., superior to 'heaven' (<s>divaḥ</s>) and '<s>Śrī</s>' (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); '<s>enā</s>' — and beyond 'this' earth as well; beyond 'the gods' (<s>devebhyaḥ</s>) and beyond 'the <s>Asuras</s>' (<s>asurebhyaḥ</s>) — superior [to all]. In short: 'whatever exists' (<s>yadasti</s>) — He is beyond all of that. That is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is beyond heaven and earth. 'But I' — 'by my greatness' (<s>mahinā</s>), I became 'this much' (<s>etāvatī</s>), i.e., limited. Or: I am this much, of the manner described, by [His] greatness — not more than this — this too is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. By the word 'I' (<s>aham</s>) that is obtained [as the subject], <s>Lakṣmī</s> is spoken of, since <s>Āmbhṛṇī</s>, the originator of this <s>sūkta</s>, is a form of <s>Lakṣmī</s>. And thus: whomever (<s>yam yam</s>) — a <s>jīva</s> fit for the position of <s>Rudra</s> — I 'desire' (<s>kāmaye</s>) to make 'mighty' (<s>ugram</s>), i.e., <s>Rudra</s>, 'him' (<s>tam tam</s>) I make so. Similarly, whomever fit for each respective position I desire to make a '<s>Brahmā</s>' (creator), a '<s>Ṛṣi</s>' (seer), or one 'of great wisdom' (<s>sumedhām</s>), him I make so — this is the meaning. The meaning of the remaining sentences will be explained in the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section) on '<s>patyurasāmañjasyāt</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 2.2.37).
'My origin is in the waters, within the ocean' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.125.7) — thus she declares.
BBs Bhāṣya 1.1.1.97:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.97:
tathāpi mama na svatantryamityaha - 'mama'; iti / 'mama'; 'yoniḥ'; kāraṇaṃ 'samudre apsu'; apām 'antaḥ'; tiṣṭhati / tasyādhikyaṃ kampasvarārthaḥ / patināma na grāhyamiti bhāvena nārāyaṇa ityanuktvā tadarthabodhanāyaivamuktiḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.97:
Even so, to say 'I have no independence,' he states — 'mama' (my). 'My' '<s>yoni</s>' (source), meaning cause, 'resides within the waters of the ocean.' The emphasis on that [word] is for the sake of the trembling tone. The meaning is that, since the name '<s>pati</s>' (lord) should not be taken [as primary], he does not say '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' directly, but speaks thus precisely to convey that meaning.

'<s>Ugra</s>' (fierce) refers to <s>Rudra</s>, and the one within the ocean is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;
because of the well-known usage and because this meaning is indicated.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.98:
nanvatra samudrastho rudraḥ kiṃ na syāt 'tapyamānāya salile'; iti bhāratokteḥ na ca ramādhīnatoktivirodhaḥ, ugraśabdena kasyacitkrūrasya grahaṇasambhavādityata āha - 'ugra'; iti / bhavedityubhayatra śeṣaḥ / tathā ca atrogra ityukto rudra eva bhavet, tathā samudre 'ntassthito nārāyaṇa eva bhavet, iti pratijñāvākyadvayārthaḥ / tatra hetumāha - 'prasiddhatvāt'; iti / 'asyārthasya'; rudre ugraśabdavācyatvarūpārthasya prasiddhatvāt, "ugraḥ kapardī"ityādikośaprasiddhatvāt, ugraśabdena rudraśabdārthasya krauryasya jñāpitatvāccetyarthaḥ / rudro raudra ugra ityeteṣāmekārthatvāditi bhāvaḥ / evaṃ samudraśāyitvarūpārthasya "mahodadhiśayo 'ntakaḥ"ityādiviṣṇusahasranāmaprasiddhatvāt samudre 'ntaḥsthatvakathanena "āpo nārāḥ"iti smṛtisiddhanāraśabdoditodakāśrayatvarūpanārāyaṇaśabdārthasya 'sūcitatvācca'; ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.98:
Now, could not the one dwelling in the ocean here be <s>Rudra</s>, since the <s>Bhārata</s> says 'performing austerities in the waters'? And there would be no contradiction with the statement of dependence on <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), since the word '<s>ugra</s>' could refer to anyone who is fierce — to this he responds: '<s>ugra</s>.' 'It would be' is to be supplied in both cases. Thus the meaning of the two assertion-sentences is: the one called '<s>ugra</s>' here would be none other than <s>Rudra</s>, and the one dwelling within the ocean would be none other than <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. He states the reason for this: 'because of well-known usage.' 'Of this meaning' — because of the well-known usage of the word '<s>ugra</s>' as denoting <s>Rudra</s>, due to the lexical attestation in passages such as "<s>ugraḥ kapardī</s>" (the fierce one with matted hair), and because the word '<s>ugra</s>' indicates the fierceness that is the meaning of the word '<s>Rudra</s>.' The sense is that '<s>rudra</s>,' '<s>raudra</s>,' and '<s>ugra</s>' are synonymous. Similarly, because the meaning of lying in the ocean is well known from the <s>Viṣṇusahasranāma</s> passage "<s>mahodadhiśayo 'ntakaḥ</s>" (He who reclines in the great ocean, the destroyer), and 'because it is indicated' — by the statement of dwelling within the ocean, the meaning of the word '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' is indicated, which denotes having water as one's abode, as taught by the word '<s>nāra</s>' established in the <s>Smṛti</s> passage "<s>āpo nārāḥ</s>" (waters are called <s>nāra</s>).

children.text:
na cāvirodhe prasiddhaḥ parityajate /
uktanyāyena ca śrutaya etameva vadanti /
children.translated_text:
And when there is no contradiction, the well-established meaning is not abandoned.
And by the reasoning stated, the scriptures declare this very one [<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.99:
nanu prasiddhyādisadbhāve 'pi tatparityāgenānyasvīkāre kiṃ bādhakamityata āha - 'na ca'; iti/ arthasyetyetadvipariṇāmenātra sambadhyate / tathā ca co yato 'yamarthaḥ 'prasiddhaḥ'; ato 'avirodhe'; pramāṇavirodhābhāve 'na parityajyate'; na tyajyata ityarthaḥ, prasiddhārthasya virodhaikāpodyatvāt, anyathā prasiddhibādhāditi bhāvaḥ / "ākāśādeva samutpadyante"(chāṃ. u. 1-9-1.) "janitota viṣṇoḥ"(ṛ.saṃ. 9-97-5.) "nakirindratvaduttaraḥ"(ṛ. 4-30-1.) ityādau vyabhicāravāraṇāyāvirodha iti / nanu virodhābhāvo 'siddhaḥ, yato 'tra yadi rudro lakṣmyadhīnatayograpadenocyate tarhi "viśvādhiko rudraḥ"ityādiśrutivirodhaḥ syāt ato 'tra tatparityāgo yukta ityata āha - 'ukta'; iti / karaṇavyutpattyā nyāyaḥ pramāṇam / tathā ca - yato "nāmāni viśvā"(bhāllaveyaśrutiḥ) ityādyuktāgamena, taduktotpattimatpravṛttinimittavattvādyanumānena, caśabdasamuccitaiḥ "vede rāmāyaṇe caiva"iti vakṣyamāṇapramāṇaiśca sādhakaiḥ 'śrutayo'; "viśvādhiko rudraḥ"(mahānā. 10-3.) ityādyāgamāḥ radrādipadānāṃ viṣṇuvācitvamāśritya vā, viśvo vāyuḥ adhiko yasmādviśvādhika ityarthāśrayaṇena vā 'etameva'; viṣṇumeva 'vadanti'; tātparyataḥ prādhānyena bodhayanti ityavagamyate / ato na "viśvādhikaḥ"ityādiśrutivirodha iti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.99:
Now, even if well-known usage and the like exist, what objection is there to abandoning that and accepting another? To this he says: 'na ca' (and not). 'Of the meaning' — this connects here by inversion. Thus: since this meaning is 'well-established,' therefore 'when there is no contradiction' — when there is no conflict with valid means of knowledge — 'it is not abandoned,' meaning it is not given up, because the only thing that can set aside a well-established meaning is a contradiction; otherwise, the well-known usage itself would be undermined — this is the purport...

children.text: vede rāmāyaṇe caiva purāṇe bhārate tathā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Veda</s>, in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, and likewise in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and the <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.100:
śrutīnāṃ viṣṇvekavācitve smṛtiṃ cāha - 'vede'; iti / viṣṇureva 'vede rāmāyaṇe ca purāṇe tathā bhārate'; /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.100:
To state the <s>Smṛti</s> evidence as well for the proposition that the <s>Śrutis</s> speak of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, he says: 'in the <s>Veda</s>.' <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is [praised] 'in the <s>Veda</s>, in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, and likewise in the <s>Bhārata</s>.'

children.text: ādāvante ca madhye ca viṣṇussarvatra gīyate /
children.translated_text: At the beginning, at the end, and in the middle — <s>Viṣṇu</s> is glorified everywhere.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.101:
kiṃ bahunā 'sarvatra'; sarvagrantheṣu 'gīyate'; pratipādyate / teṣvapi na bhāge, kintvādau madhye ante ca, karmādikāṇḍatraye 'pi, upakramopasaṃhārayoravāntaraprakaraṇeṣu ca, sarvatra prativākyaṃ pratipadaṃ pratyakṣaraṃ ca mukhyataḥ pratipādyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.101:
What more need be said? 'Everywhere' — in all texts — He 'is glorified,' meaning He is expounded. And in them, not merely in a portion, but at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end — in all three divisions of the <s>Karma</s> and other <s>kāṇḍas</s>, in the introductions and conclusions, in the intermediate sections as well — everywhere, in every sentence, in every word, in every syllable, He is primarily expounded. This is the meaning.
Thus in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> texts. And there is no contradiction from other scriptures,

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.102:
'veda'; iti vacanasya khilākhilapārijātākhyaharivaṃśabhāgatrayagatatvasūcanāya 'harivaṃśeṣu'; iti bahuvacanam / harivaṃśeṣvityanantaraṃ 'yaduktaṃ'; iti śeṣaḥ, tasyāto na virodha iti, harivaṃśeṣūktanyāyena uktarītyā iti vānvayaḥ / nanu pramāṇavirodhābhāvo 'siddhaḥ, yataḥ śrutivirodhābhāve 'pyasti pāśupatādiśāstravirodhaḥ, tatra rudrādīnāṃ sarvottamatvasya sarvakāraṇatvasya cokteḥ ityata āha - 'na ca'; iti/ co 'pyarthaḥ na kevalaṃ śrutivirodhābhāvaḥ, apitarhītaravirodho 'pi neti / 'asyārthasya'; iti vartate /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.102:
To indicate that the statement beginning with '<s>Veda</s>' occurs in three parts of the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> known as <s>Khila</s>, <s>Akhila</s>, and <s>Pārijāta</s>, the plural 'in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> texts' is used...
I shall quickly create delusion that will delude the people.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.103:
