kuta ityata teṣāṃ mohārthaṃ kṛtatvāditi hetvadhyāhāramabhipretya tasyāsiddhiṃ pramāṇodāharaṇena nirāha - 'eṣa'; iti / rudraṃ prati viṣṇuvākyametat / muhyate 'nena jana iti 'moho'; naṭanaṃ vañcanaṃ vā / 'moho'; mohakāraṇamanādikarmavāsanārupamiti tattvapradīptokterapyayamevārthaḥ, mohakaśāstramiti vyāsatīrthīyokteḥ / na ca asya 'na mohaśāstrasya vaktā viṣṇurāśaṅkyaḥ, "ajasyāvakracetasaḥ"(ka.u. 5-1.) iti hi śrutiḥ'; iti tattvapradīpavirodhaḥ śaṅkyaḥ asatāmityabhiprāyāt /
vidyamānākārācchādanenāvidyamānākārapradarśanaṃ naṭanam / avidyamānakathanaṃ vañcanam / sṛjāmītyuttamapuruṣaprayogādahamiti kartā labhyate / caśabdaḥ kriyākartṛsamuccaye / 'pūrvaśrutasyaitacchabdasya paścāt śruto yacchabdo viśeṣaṇam'; iti nyāyadīpokteḥ ya eṣa iti yojanā / tathā ca ahaṃ 'mohaṃ sṛjāmi'; karomi / 'ya eṣa'; mohaḥ 'janān mohayiṣyati'; ajñānamithyājñānādikaṃ prāpayiṣyati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.103:
Why so? Intending the implicit reason that those [scriptures] were composed for the purpose of delusion, and proving that by citing authoritative evidence, he refutes [the objection]: '<s>eṣa</s>' (this). This is the statement of <s>Viṣṇu</s> addressed to <s>Rudra</s>...

children.text: tvaṃ ca rudra mahābāho mohaśāstrāṇi kāraya /
children.translated_text: And you, O <s>Rudra</s>, O mighty-armed one, cause deluding scriptures to be composed.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.104:
parabādhakatvāt bāhuḥ prāṇyaṅgaṃ, mahān bāhuryasya saḥ, tasya sambuddhiḥ he 'mahābāho'; śatrubādhakāṅgayukta 'rudra'; 'tvaṃ ca'; mohaṃ sṛja 'mohaśāstrāṇi'; ca 'kāraya'; kuru, dadhīcyādibhiśca kāraya/ he 'mahābhuja'; mahābhakṣaka mahākuṭileti vā he rudra /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.104:
Because it wards off adversaries, '<s>bāhu</s>' (arm) is a limb of a being; he whose arms are great is '<s>mahābāhu</s>' — the vocative of that: O '<s>mahābāho</s>' (mighty-armed one), O '<s>Rudra</s>' possessed of limbs that ward off enemies, 'you too' — create delusion, 'cause deluding scriptures' to be 'composed,' that is, make them, and have them composed by <s>Dadhīci</s> and others as well...
Display untruths and falsehoods, O mighty-armed one.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.105:
teṣviti śeṣaḥ tathā ca - 'teṣu'; mohaśāstreṣu 'atathyāni'; kvāpyavidyamānāni liṅgamūlānveṣaṇādīni 'vitathyāni'; vyadhikaraṇatvena vidyamānāni viṣṇuniṣṭhāni vāyuniṣṭhāni vā rudrādiniṣṭhatayocyamānāni sarvottamatvasarvasvātantryaviṣabhakṣaṇādīni 'darśayasva'; pratipādayeti yāvat /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.105:
'In them' is to be supplied. Thus: 'in those' deluding scriptures, display '<s>atathyāni</s>' — things that exist nowhere, such as searching for the root of the <s>liṅga</s> and the like; and '<s>vitathyāni</s>' — things that exist in a different locus, that is, attributes such as supreme excellence, complete independence, consumption of poison, and so on, which properly belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> or <s>Vāyu</s> but are attributed to <s>Rudra</s> and others — 'display' means expound them.

children.text: prakāśaṃ kuru cātmānamaprakāśaṃ ca māṃ kuru /
children.translated_text: Make yourself manifest, and make me unmanifest.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.106:
'mām ātmānam'; ityuddeśyadvitīyāntam / parasparasamuccaye caśabdau / tathā ca lokeṣu 'ātmānaṃ'; svātmānamuddiśya 'prakāśaṃ'; prasiddhiṃ 'kuru'; / na kevalametāvat, kintu 'mām'; uddiśya 'aprakāśam'; aprasiddhiṃ ca kurvītyarthaḥ / kecittu - prakāśo 'syāstīti prakāśamiti arśaādyajantatvamāśritya uddeśyadvitīyānāśrayaṇena prakāśaṃ prasiddhamiti vyācakṣate /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.106:
'Me' and 'yourself' are accusatives serving as the objects. The two uses of 'ca' (and) indicate mutual conjunction...
Thus from the statement in the <s>Vārāha Purāṇa</s>. And in the <s>Śaiva</s> section of the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s> —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.107:
'vārāhavacanāt'; ityasyetareṣāṃ mohārthaṃ kṛtatvāvagamāditi hetumukhena 'na cetara'; iti pratijñāvākyenānvayaḥ / liṅgamūlānveṣaṇakathā tu - pūrvaṃ jagatkartṛtvaviṣaye viṣṇuviriñcayorvivādo 'bhūt ahameva jagataḥ kartā na matto 'nyaḥ iti / etasminnantare tayorgarvavināśāya tanmadhye kiñcana liṅgamudabhūt / tau tat dṛṣṭvā sarvadevasannidhau parasparaṃ samayaṃ cakratuḥ / tatra brahmā viṣṇumāha - avayormadhye 'sya liṅgasya yo 'ntamādiṃ ca gacchati sa bhavedadhiko loke, lokakartā ca sa prabhuḥ / tasmāddhe viṣṇo tvaṃ liṅgasya mūlagaveṣaṇāyādhastādvraja, ahamantagaveṣaṇāya ūrdhvaṃ gamiṣyāmi iti / evaṃ tau samayaṃ kṛtvā mārgamāṇau nirgatau / tatra viṣṇurvarāharūpeṇādhastādgaveṣituṃ yayau / vāṇījānistu haṃsarūpeṇordhvaṃ yayo / atha punarviṣṇuḥ svasthānaṃ samāgatya sarvadevasannidhau ahaṃ liṅgasyādimadrākṣamiti satyam āha / brahmāpi samāgatya ahamantamadrākṣamiti chadmanā mṛṣā āha / atha liṅgarūpī maheśvaraḥ tayorvacaḥ śrutvā he viṣṇo yatastvaṃ satyamevāvocaḥ ataḥ tava loke matsamā pūjā bhaviṣyati / brahmaṇastu netyuvāca / tato brahmā he rudra mamānṛtoktikṛtāparādhastvayā kṣantavya ityāha / tato rudro na mama vaco mithyā bhaviṣyati / tathāpi tvaṃ mithyoktikṛtadoṣaparihārārthaṃ gandhamādanagiriṃ vraja / tatra kratūn kuruṣva/ tatastava śrautasmārtakarmasveva pūjā bhaviṣyati / na tu devālayādiṣvityuktvāntaradhīyatetyādirūpā skāndapurāṇasthā/ nanu tathāpyasyārthasya skāndabrahmavaivartādipurāṇavirodhassyāt, teṣāṃ śivabrahmādipāramyaviṣayatvādityata āha - 'śaive ca'; iti / caśabdo 'pyarthassamuccaye, yadyapītyādyarthe ca - 'śaive'; śivotkarṣapare 'pīti 'skānde'; vacanādityanuṣaṅgadyotakaśca / evamuttaratrāpi /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.107:
'From the statement in the <s>Vārāha</s>' — the connection is with the assertion-sentence 'nor is there [contradiction] from other [scriptures],' by way of the reason that it is understood that they were composed for the purpose of delusion...
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and the other <s>Suras</s> attain a condition worse than that of a dog-cooker (<s>śvapaca</s>),

children.text: tadaivācyuta yāntyeva yadaiva tvaṃ parāṅmukhaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: O <s>Acyuta</s>, at that very moment when You turn away. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.108-109:
he 'acyuta'; 'yadaiva'; yadi ca tvameva sarvathā 'parāṅmukho'; bhavasi anugrahaṃ ca karoṣi 'tadā'; tarhi 'brahmeśānādayaḥ surāḥ'; śvapacādapi śvānaṃ pacatīti śvapaco nīcaḥ tasmādapi 'kaṣṭatvaṃ'; kleśayuktatvaṃ kaṣṭaṃ vā 'yāntyeva'; ityarthaḥ / asya tarkatvāttasya viparyayaparyavasāne brahmādīnāṃ viṣṇvadhīnatvam atyantatadanugrahapātratvaṃ ca siddhyatīti na pramāṇavirodhaḥ / itiśabdasya 'iti skānde'; ityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.108-109:
O '<s>Acyuta</s>' (Unfallen One), 'whenever' You become completely 'averse' in every way and [withdraw] Your grace, 'then' indeed '<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and the other <s>Suras</s>' attain 'a condition worse than' even a '<s>śvapaca</s>' — one who cooks dogs, that is, an outcaste — meaning they reach 'wretchedness,' a state full of suffering...
And in the <s>Brāhma</s> and <s>Brahmavaivarta Purāṇas</s> —

children.text: nāhaṃ na ca śivo 'nye ca tacchaktyekāṃśabhāginaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither I, nor <s>Śiva</s>, nor others partake of even a single portion of His power.
Just as a child plays with toys, <s>Acyuta</s> plays with us. // Thus.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.110-112:
'brāhme'; brahmaviṣaye / atra 'aham'; iti caturmukha ucyate / 'yadvat'; iti śravaṇāt 'tadvat'; iti labhyate / caśabdau samuccayārthau / 'asmābhiḥ'; ityatra śivaścānye ca ahaṃ ca vayaṃ tairityekaśeṣaḥ / tathā ca yadyapi vayaṃ 'tacchaktyekāṃśabhāginaḥ'; tasyācyutasya yā śaktiḥ sāmarthyaṃ tasyaikāṃśabhāgino na bhavāmaḥ tathāpi 'yadvat'; yathā 'bālaḥ krīḍanakaiḥ'; krīḍāsādhanapadārthaiḥ 'krīḍate'; 'tadvat'; tathā 'acyuto'; harirapi 'asmābhiḥ'; karaṇaiḥ 'krīḍate'; sṛṣṭyādikrīḍāṃ karotītyarthaḥ / punarna cetyuktiḥ tātparyārthā, 'nā'; puruṣa iti vā / itiśabdasya iti brahmavaivarte ityanvayaḥ / 'skānde'; 'brahmavaivarte'; ityanayoḥ 'vacanāt'; itipadadvārā 'na cetaragranthavirodhaḥ'; ityanenānvayaḥ / tathā ca teṣāṃ śaivāditve 'pi na virodhitvam, tatrāpi viṣṇūttamatvāderapyuktyā svavirodhena śivādyutkarṣe 'prāmāṇyāt / na ca viparītaṃ kiṃ na syāditi vācyam, śivādyutkarṣādeḥ śaivādipurāṇeṣvevāsādhāraṇyena prāptatvāt, tatraiva viṣṇūtkarṣoktau tatra prāmāṇyasya śivādyutkarṣādāvaprāmāṇyasya ca niścayena vaiparītyāyogāt / tasmātpāśupatādiparikalpitaśivādyuttamatvaparipāṭī darśanabhāṣayā teṣūpanyasyata iti na tadvirodha iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.110-112: 'Brāhme' — in the subject of <s>Brahmā</s>. Here 'aham' refers to the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>. From hearing 'yadvat' (just as), 'tadvat' (so too) is implied. The words 'ca' are for aggregation. In 'asmābhiḥ' (with us) — '<s>Śiva</s> and others and I = we' — this is an <s>ekaśeṣa</s> formation (single-remainder compound). And thus, although we are 'tacchaktyekāṃśabhāginaḥ' — we do not share even a single portion of that power of <s>Acyuta</s> — nevertheless, 'yadvat' — just as 'bālaḥ' — a child 'krīḍanakaiḥ' — with things that serve as instruments of play — 'krīḍate' — plays, 'tadvat' — so too 'Acyutaḥ' — <s>Hari</s> also 'asmābhiḥ' — with us as instruments — 'krīḍate' — plays, i.e., performs the play of creation etc.: this is the meaning. The repeated 'na ca' (nor) serves the purpose of emphasis. Or 'nā' refers to 'puruṣa' (the cosmic person). The word 'iti' connects with 'iti brahmavaivarte' (thus in the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>). 'Skānde' and 'brahmavaivarte' connect through the word 'vacanāt' (from the statement) with 'na cetaragranthavirodhaḥ' (there is no contradiction with other texts). And thus, even though those [Purāṇas] are of Śaiva orientation etc., there is no contradiction, since even there, through the statement of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s supremacy etc., the glorification of <s>Śiva</s> etc. in self-contradiction is not authoritative. Nor should one say 'why not the reverse?' — because the glorification of <s>Śiva</s> etc. is found exclusively in the Śaiva etc. Purāṇas, and when <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s supremacy is stated even there, the authority [of those Purāṇas] in [the matter of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s supremacy] and their non-authority in [the matter of] <s>Śiva</s>'s supremacy etc. are certain, making a reversal impossible. Therefore, the hierarchy of <s>Śiva</s>'s supremacy fabricated by the <s>Pāśupatas</s> etc. is presented in those [Purāṇas] in the language of [their own] philosophical school — hence there is no contradiction: this is the purport.

children.text: na ca vaiṣṇaveṣu tathā / tacca "eṣa"mohaṃ ityuktam //
children.translated_text: And there is no such [glorification of others over <s>Viṣṇu</s>] in the Vaiṣṇava [texts]. And that has been stated as 'this is for the purpose of delusion.' //
// Thus ends the <s>Jijñāsādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Inquiry). //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.1.113:
tathāpi viṣṇūttamatvarūdrādhamatvayorvaiṣṇavagranthavirodho 'stītyata āha - 'na ca'; iti / samuccaye caśabdaḥ / tathā ca - 'vaiṣṇaveṣu'; viṣṇuviṣayapurāṇādiṣvapi 'tathā'; viṣṇoranyasyottamatvamuktaṃ na, ata eva 'tathā'; śaivavat sarvottamatvādhamatvaviṣaye virodho netyarthaḥ, yena svavirodhena svaviṣaye 'prāmāṇyaṃ syāditi bhāvaḥ / tarhi vaiṣṇaveṣu rāmakṛṣṇādiviṣṇukartṛkaśivastutyādi kathamucyata ityata āha - 'tacca'; iti / castavarthaḥ / vacanādityanuvtate / tadityasyāvṛttiḥ / tathā ca - co yato vaiṣṇaveṣu yacchivastutyādyucyate tattu 'eṣa moham'; iti vacanājjñātena tena mohārthatvena 'uktaṃ'; pratyuktaṃ samāhitaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.1.113: Even so, there might be a contradiction in the Vaiṣṇava texts regarding the supremacy of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the inferiority of <s>Rudra</s> — to this he says: 'na ca.' The word 'ca' is for aggregation. And thus — 'vaiṣṇaveṣu' — in the Purāṇas etc. whose subject is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'tathā' — likewise, the supremacy of anyone other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not stated, and therefore 'tathā' — as in the Śaiva [texts], there is no contradiction regarding the matter of absolute supremacy and inferiority: this is the meaning — since there is no self-contradiction that would cause non-authoritativeness in their own domain: this is the purport. Then how is it that in the Vaiṣṇava [texts], praises of <s>Śiva</s> etc. by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and other forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s> are stated? To this he says: 'tacca.' The word 'ca' is connective. 'Vacanāt' continues. 'Tat' is repeated. And thus — since whatever praise of <s>Śiva</s> etc. is stated in the Vaiṣṇava [texts] is, by the statement 'eṣa moham' (this is for delusion), known to be for the purpose of delusion — 'uktam' — it is countered, resolved,
i.e., stated: this is the meaning. This connects with the supplied [clause] 'ato na tadvirodhaḥ' (therefore there is no contradiction).
// Thus ends the <s>Jijñāsādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Inquiry). //
// 2. <s>Janmādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Origin) //
He states the defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> —
That from which [arise] the origin etc. of this [universe]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.2 |
Creation, sustenance, dissolution, regulation, knowledge, ignorance, bondage, and liberation — from which [these arise].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.2.1:
etadadhikaraṇapratipādyaṃ darśayati - 'brahmaṇaḥ'; iti / nirbādharūḍhibalāt jīva evedaṃ brahma, tasya cāsandhigdhatvānna jijñāsyatvamiti prāptetannirākartuṃ brahmaśabdena jīvagrahaṇe bādhakarūpaṃ śrutyuktaṃ jijñāsyabrahmaṇo lakṣaṇamāha sūtrakāra ityarthaḥ / "śrutyuktaṃ lakṣaṇamāha"iti ṭīkayā "sā viṣṇorbrahmatvavidhātrī taittirīyaśrutiryāni tasya lakṣaṇānyāha tānyanena sūtreṇa bhagavānāha"iti tattvapradīpokteḥ tacchabdādhyāhāreṇa bhāṣyārtha uktaḥ / ata eva lakṣaṇamiti samudāyaikavacanamiti jñātavyam/ anena pūrvatra vivakṣitabrahmajijñāsākṣepeṇeha pūrvapakṣotthānāt pūrvādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / brahmaviṣayatvācchāstrasaṅgatiḥ siddhaiva / yadyapi 'brahmaśabdaśca viṣṇāveva'; ityanena brahmaśabdo viṣṇāveva mukhya ityuktam / tathāpi bhāṣyakārairuktatve 'pi sūtrakṛtānuktatvāt brahma kiṃ jīva uta viṣṇuriti bhavatyeva sandehaḥ / sūtraṃ paṭhati - 'janma'; iti / yata ityuktestadbrahmeti prakṛtaṃ bhavatīti śeṣaḥ/ yadvā - "janmādyasya yata iti sūtre śrutamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ"/ iti sudhokteḥ śrutamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ / janma ādiryasya sṛṣṭyādisamudāyasya tajjanmādīti tadguṇasaṃvijñānabahuvrīhiḥ, tasya samāsārthaikadeśasya janmano guṇatvena viśeṣaṇatvena saṃvijñānāt / tathā ca - 'asya'; pramitasya jagato 'janmādi yato'; bhavati śrutamiti vā tadbrahmeti sūtrārtha ityabhipretya asya jagato janma ādipadokte sthitisaṃhṛtī yatastadbrahmetyādyanyathāpratītivāraṇāya sūtraṃ yathāvadvyācaṣṭe - 'sṛṣṭi'; iti / atra prayojakavyāpāravācisṛṣṭisaṃhāraniyamanaśabdairlakṣaṇayā prapañcaniṣṭhajanmanāśaniyamyatvarūpaprayojyavyāpārāḥ pratipādyante / lakṣaṇāprayojanaṃ brahmaṇa upādānatvābhāvapradarśanamiti candrikoktiḥ / sṛṣṭyādīnāmaṣṭānāṃ ca pratyekaṃ lakṣaṇatvaṃ, na tu samuditaveṣeṇa, ativyāptyādyabhāvāt / etacca lakṣaṇamanantaguṇapūrṇatvasyāpyupalakṣakam / ekenopalakṣaṇasambhave 'pi mumukṣujñeyatvātsārthakamaṣṭānāṃ vacanam / yathoktaṃ śrīmanmahābhāratatātparyanirṇaye -

children.translated_text: Having known creation, protection, destruction, knowledge, regulation, ignorance, bondage,

children.text: mokṣaṃ ca viṣṇutaścaiva jñātvā muktirna cānyathā //
children.translated_text: And liberation to be from <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — [one attains] liberation; not otherwise. //

<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.2.1: He shows what this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> establishes: 'brahmaṇaḥ.' Given the prima facie view that by the irresistible force of conventional usage, the <s>jīva</s> alone is this <s>Brahman</s>, and since the <s>jīva</s> is undoubted, it is not a proper object of inquiry — to refute this, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> states the defining characteristic of the <s>Brahman</s> that is to be inquired into, as stated in <s>śruti</s>, which overrides the identification of <s>Brahman</s> with the <s>jīva</s>: this is the meaning. Through the statement in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> 'he states the characteristic stated in śruti,' and the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> statement 'that <s>Taittirīya</s> <s>śruti</s> which establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>Brahman</s>-hood states whatever are His characteristics — those the <s>Bhagavān</s> states through this <s>sūtra</s>' — by supplying the word 'tat,' the meaning of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is stated. Therefore, the word 'lakṣaṇam' should be understood as a collective singular. By this, since the <s>Brahma-jijñāsā</s> intended earlier is alluded to here, and since the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> arises here through that allusion, the connection of this [topic] with the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> by way of allusion (<s>ākṣepikī saṅgati</s>) is stated. The connection with the <s>śāstra</s>, being about <s>Brahman</s>, is already established. Although it was said that 'the word <s>Brahman</s> is primary only for <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' nevertheless, since the <s>bhāṣyakāras</s> have said this but the <s>sūtrakāra</s> has not [explicitly], the doubt remains: is <s>Brahman</s> the <s>jīva</s> or <s>Viṣṇu</s>? He reads the <s>sūtra</s>: 'janma.' The complement is: because 'yataḥ' is stated, 'that is <s>Brahman</s>' becomes the subject under discussion. Alternatively, as stated in the <s>Sudhā</s>: 'In the <s>sūtra</s> janmādyasya yataḥ, the sentence-complement is: it is heard in <s>śruti</s>.' '<s>Janma</s>' (origin) is the beginning of what (<s>asya</s>) — i.e., of the aggregate of creation etc. — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound with the qualification of the secondary quality of the first term of the compound, since <s>janma</s> is cognized as a qualifier (attribute) of the compound meaning. And thus: 'asya' — of this known universe; 'janmādi yataḥ' — that from which [arise] the origin etc. — 'it is heard in <s>śruti</s>, or that is <s>Brahman</s>': this is the <s>sūtra</s>'s meaning. With the intention of preventing any other understanding — where 'ādi' in 'janmādi' would mean only sustenance and dissolution — he explains the <s>sūtra</s> as it truly is: 'sṛṣṭi.' Here, through the words sṛṣṭi, saṃhāra, niyamana which denote the instigating activity, the instigated activities in the form of the origination, destruction, and controlledness of the phenomenal world are conveyed through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). The purpose of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is to show that <s>Brahman</s> is not the material cause: this is the statement of the <s>Candrikā</s>. And each of the eight [attributes] — creation etc. — individually serves as a defining characteristic, not collectively, since there is no over-extension etc. And this defining characteristic is also indicative of the fullness of infinite qualities. Even though indication through a single [attribute] is possible, the statement of [all] eight is meaningful because it is to be known by the seeker of liberation. As stated in the revered <s>Mahābhārata-tātparya-nirṇaya</s> —

children.text: iti / yata ityanantaraṃ 'śrutāḥ'; 'bhavanti'; iti vā śeṣaḥ / asya tadbrahmetyupaskṛtenānvayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus. After 'yataḥ,' the complement is 'śrutāḥ' (heard) or 'bhavanti' (arise). Its construction is with the supplied 'asya tadbrahma' (of this, that is <s>Brahman</s>). //
Origin, sustenance, and dissolution; regulation, knowledge, and covering;
Bondage and liberation — from the <s>Puruṣa</s> from whom [these arise], He, <s>Hari</s>, is the sole sovereign. //
Thus in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.2.2:
nanu jagajjanmādikartṛtvaṃ yadi viṣṇvekaniṣṭhaṃ bhavettadā brahmaśabdena jīvagrahaṇe bādhakarūpaṃ syāt; tasya viṣṇvekaniṣṭhatvameva kuto jñāyata ityata āha - 'utpatti'; iti / asya jagato 'yasmāt'; puruṣāt 'utpattisthitisaṃhārāḥ'; bhavanti 'niyatiḥ'; niyamanam 'āvṛtiḥ jñānaṃ'; ca yasmādbhavati 'bandhamokṣau ca'; yasmādbhavataḥ 'saḥ ekarāṭ'; svatantro 'hariḥ'; eva ityarthaḥ / viriñcādiṣu ativyāptiparihārārtham 'ekarāṭ'; iti/ 'iti skānde'; ityanantaraṃ 'vacanāt sṛṣṭyādikartā harireva'; iti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.2.2: Now, if the agency of origin etc. of the universe were to reside in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, then it would serve as an overriding factor when <s>Brahman</s> is identified with the <s>jīva</s>; how is it known that it resides in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone? To this he says: 'utpatti.' 'Asya' — of this universe; 'yasmāt' — from which <s>Puruṣa</s>; 'utpattisthitisaṃhārāḥ' — origin, sustenance, and dissolution arise; 'niyatiḥ' — regulation; 'āvṛtiḥ' — covering; 'jñānam' — knowledge — from whom [these] arise; 'bandhamokṣau ca' — bondage and liberation — from whom [these] arise; 'saḥ' — He, 'ekarāṭ' — the sole sovereign, independent; 'hariḥ' — is <s>Hari</s> alone: this is the meaning. 'Ekarāṭ' is to prevent over-extension to <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others. After 'iti skānde,' the sentence-complement is: 'vacanāt sṛṣṭyādikartā harireva' (from the statement [in the <s>Skānda</s>], <s>Hari</s> alone is the creator of creation etc.).

children.text:
"yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante / yena jātāni jīvanti /
yatprayantyabhisaṃviśanti / tadvijijñāsasva tadbrahmeti"//
children.translated_text: 'From which indeed these beings are born; by which, once born, they live; into which, departing, they enter — seek to know that; that is <s>Brahman</s>.' //
(<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.2.3:
jijñāsyaṃ brahma viṣṇureva bhavet janmādikartṛtvāt ityanumāne hetvasiddhiṃ jijñāsyabrahmalakṣaṇasya tatrānupalambhakṛtāsambhavaṃ vā nirākartuṃ jagatkāraṇatvalakṣaṇaṃ jijñāsye brahmaṇi "tadvijijñāsasva"ityataḥ pūrvavākye kathitamityāha - 'yataḥ'; iti / vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / bhūtaśabdaḥ "astitvādbhūtanāmabhyaḥ sarvajīvebhya eva yat"iti gītātātparyanirṇayavacanājjīvavācī tadupalakṣitasarvajagatparaḥ / tathā ca - 'imāni bhūtāni yato jāyante yena jātāni'; utpannāni 'jīvanti'; prāṇaṃ dadhati 'yat'; ca pralaye 'prayanti'; praviśanti yacca 'abhi'; svecchayā samyak 'viśanti'; muktau 'tat'; tadeva 'brahma'; nānyat / mukhyataḥ tajjñānāya vedārthabhūtaṃ 'tadvijijñāsasva'; tadviṣayakavicāraṃ kurvityarthaḥ / itiśabdaḥ śrutistha eva / tasya 'iti varuṇo bhṛgumuvāca'; iti kriyāpadenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.2.3: To refute the non-establishment of the reason in the inference 'the <s>Brahman</s> to be inquired into is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, because of being the agent of origin etc.' — or to refute the impossibility caused by the non-observation of the defining characteristic of the <s>Brahman</s> to be inquired into therein — he states that the characteristic of being the cause of the universe is declared in the sentence preceding 'tadvijijñāsasva' (seek to know that) in the <s>Brahman</s> to be inquired into: 'yataḥ.' The word 'vai' is for establishing [what is well-known]. The word '<s>bhūta</s>' denotes <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), as stated in the <s>Gītā-tātparya-nirṇaya</s>: 'Because it exists (<s>astitvāt</s>), from the word <s>bhūta</s>, which applies to all <s>jīvas</s>' — and is extended to the entire universe indicated thereby. And thus — 'imāni bhūtāni yato jāyante' — from which these beings are born; 'yena jātāni' — by which, once born — 'jīvanti' — they live, sustain breath; 'yat' — and which, at dissolution — 'prayanti' — they enter; and 'abhi' — by His own will, completely — 'viśanti' — they enter in liberation; 'tat' — that alone 'brahma' — is <s>Brahman</s>, not anything else. Primarily for the knowledge of that, being the content of the Vedas — 'tadvijijñāsasva' — undertake inquiry regarding that: this is the meaning. The word 'iti' is found in the <s>śruti</s> itself. It connects with the verb-phrase 'iti varuṇo bhṛgumuvāca' (thus <s>Varuṇa</s> said to <s>Bhṛgu</s>).

children.text: ya u tridhātu pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ eko dādhāra bhuvanāni viśvā //
children.translated_text: He who alone sustains the three-layered earth and the heaven, all the worlds — (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 1.154.4)

children.text:
(ṛ.saṃ. 1-154-4.)
caturbhissākaṃ navatiṃ ca nāmabhiḥ cakraṃ na vṛttaṃ vyatīṃravīvipat //
children.translated_text: With four [forms] together with ninety names, like a wheel turned, He set in motion. // (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 1.155.6)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.2.4:
lakṣaṇasyātivyāptiśaṅkāṃ uktānumānasya vyabhicāraśaṅkāṃ vā parihartuṃ spaṣṭārthatvātprathamaṃ smṛtimupanyasya idānīṃ sṛṣṭyādikartṛtvaṃ pratyekamapi viṣṇvekaniṣṭhaṃ kimu sarvamiti bhāvena sthitikartṛtvasya viṣṇvekaniṣṭhatve śrutimāha - 'yaḥ'; iti / uśabda evārthaḥ, tridhātvityekaṃ padaṃ, utaśabdassamuccaye / tathā ca - 'yo'; viṣṇuḥ 'ekaḥ'; eva 'tridhātu'; prakṛtipuruṣakāladhārakaḥ 'pṛthivīṃ'; bhūmiṃ 'dyāṃ'; śriyaṃ ca 'viśvā'; viśvāni sarvāṇi ca 'bhuvanāni'; 'dādhāra'; dadhāretyarthaḥ / niyamanasyāpi viṣṇvekakartṛtve śrutimāha - 'caturbhiḥ'; iti / sa iti śeṣaḥ, naśabda ivārthaḥ, caśabdo mātrārthaḥ / tathā ca - sa bṛhaccharīro mūlarūpī viṣṇuḥ 'nāmabhiśca'; nāmamātraiḥ svarūpabhedaśūnyaiḥ 'caturbhiḥ'; vāsudevasaṅkarṣaṇapradyumnāniruddhaiḥ 'sākaṃ navatiṃ'; navatisaṅkhyākān 'vyatīn'; - deveṣu yaugiko 'yaṃ śabdaḥ - viśeṣeṇādhikān devān kimutānyān 'vṛttaṃ cakraṃ na'; vartulaṃ rathāṅgamiva yugapat 'avīvipat', viparivartana iti dhātuḥ, paryavartayadityarthaḥ / aṣṭau vasavaḥ ekādaśa rudrāḥ viṣṇuvyatiriktaikādaśādityāḥ hiraṇyagarbheṇa saha daśa prajeśvarāḥ pradhānena pañcāśanmaruta iti navatiḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - prathamaṃ ṭīkoktārthamabhidhāya -
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.2.4: To resolve the suspicion of over-extension of the defining characteristic, or the suspicion of deviation in the stated inference — having first cited a <s>smṛti</s> due to its clear meaning — he now cites a <s>śruti</s> to show that the agency of sustenance also resides exclusively in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, let alone all [eight characteristics]: 'yaḥ.' The word 'u' is a mere expletive. '<s>Tridhātu</s>' is one word. The word 'uta' is for aggregation. And thus — 'yaḥ' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'ekaḥ' — alone; '<s>tridhātu</s>' — the sustainer of <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, and <s>kāla</s>; '<s>pṛthivīm</s>' — the earth; '<s>dyām</s>' — <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī); and 'viśvā' — all 'bhuvanāni' — worlds — 'dādhāra' — He sustained: this is the meaning. He cites a <s>śruti</s> showing that regulation too is exclusively by <s>Viṣṇu</s>: 'caturbhiḥ.' The word 'sa' is to be supplied. The word 'na' has the meaning of 'iva' (like). The word 'ca' means 'only.' And thus — He, the great-bodied <s>Viṣṇu</s> in His root form, 'nāmabhiśca' — with mere names, devoid of essential distinction — 'caturbhiḥ' — the four: <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s> — 'sākaṃ navatim' — ninety in number — 'vyatīn' — this word applies in the derived sense to gods — the specially elevated gods, let alone others — 'vṛttaṃ cakraṃ na' — like a round wheel — 'yugapat' — simultaneously — 'avīvipat' — He set in motion, i.e., He controlled: this is the meaning. The root is 'viparivartana' (to revolve). The ninety are: eight <s>Vasus</s>, eleven <s>Rudras</s>, eleven <s>Ādityas</s> excluding <s>Viṣṇu</s>, ten lords of progeny along with <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and fifty <s>Maruts</s> along with <s>Pradhāna</s> — thus ninety. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however — having first stated the meaning given in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> —
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Vināyaka</s>,
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Nirṛti</s>,
Along with <s>Kubera</s> — these gods are declared to be ninety.

BBsBhDīp_1,1.2.5:
eteṣāṃ lakṣaṇānāmativyāptiṃ viṣṇvekaniṣṭhatvoktyā smṛtyā cārthāt parihṛtāmapi sākṣādanyatra lakṣaṇābhāvaṃ pratipādayantyā śrutyā nirāha - 'paraḥ'; iti / viṣṇāvityākṛṣyate / tattvodyotaṭīkoktarītyā muktā amuktāśceti śeṣaḥ / ata eva ṭīkāyāṃ ka ityuktam / tathā ca - 'tanvā'; svamūrtyaiva na tu kīrtimātreṇa 'vṛdhāna'; aparicchinna he viṣṇo tvaṃ yato 'mātrayā'; miteḥ 'paraḥ'; vilakṣaṇo 'si aparimito 'sīti yāvat / ata evaṃbhūtasya 'te mahitvaṃ'; jagatsṛṣṭyādirūpaṃ mahimānam 'anu'; api ke 'pi muktā amuktāśca 'nāśnuvanti'; na prāpnuvantītyarthaḥ / yadvā - 'nāśnuvanti'; nānubhavantītyarthaḥ / nāśnuvantīti vartamānaniṣedhāt syāduttaratretyata āha - 'na'; iti / prāpnotīti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - he 'viṣṇo'; 'devamahimnaḥ'; ramādimahimnaḥ 'param antaṃ'; sīmānaṃ mahimatāratamyaparāvadhibhūtaṃ 'te mahitvaṃ'; mahimānaṃ 'jāyamāno'; na prāpnoti, jāto 'nāpa'; ityarthaḥ / upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat janiṣyamāṇo na prāpsyatītyapi draṣṭavyam / ata eva tattvapradīpe - "paro mātrayā tanvā vṛdhāna / na te mahitvamanvaśnuvanti / ubhe te vidma rajasī pṛthivyā viṣṇo devatvaṃ paramasya vitse / na te viṣṇo jāyamāno na jāto devamahimnaḥ paramantamāpa / udastabhnā nākamṛṣvaṃ bṛhantaṃ dādhartha prācīṃ kakubhaṃ pṛthivyāḥ"iti ṛgdvayamevameva vyākhyātam / tathā hi - mātrāyāḥ paraḥ parimāṇātītaḥ tanvā vṛdhānaḥ tanvā vardhamānaḥ dehena pūrṇaḥ - itthaṃ bhāve tṛtīyā -
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.2, verse 5:
The over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) of these defining characteristics [of Brahman], though resolved by the statement that they belong exclusively to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and implicitly by <s>Smṛti</s>, is here explicitly refuted through <s>Śruti</s> that demonstrates the absence of the defining characteristic elsewhere: 'paraḥ' (supreme). 'In <s>Viṣṇu</s>' is to be supplied. As stated in the <s>Tattvodyota Ṭīkā</s>, 'both the liberated and the unliberated' is the remainder. Hence indeed the <s>Ṭīkā</s> says 'kaḥ' (who?). And thus — 'by His own form' (<s>tanvā</s>), by His own body alone, not merely by fame, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, You who are 'vṛdhāna' (growing, unbounded), 'paraḥ' (beyond), that is, different from 'mātrā' (measure, from the root 'mi' meaning to measure) — You are immeasurable, unlimited: this is the sense. Therefore, 'Your greatness' (<s>mahitva</s>) — Your majesty in the form of the creation of the world and the like — even some liberated and unliberated [beings] 'do not attain' (<s>nāśnuvanti</s>), do not reach: this is the meaning. Or, 'nāśnuvanti' means 'do not experience': this is the meaning. Since the present-tense negation 'they do not attain' might imply that they will in the future, he says: 'na.' 'Attains' is the remainder. And thus — O '<s>Viṣṇu</s>,' 'of the greatness of the gods' — of the greatness of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) and others — 'the ultimate limit' — the boundary, the absolute upper limit of the hierarchy of greatness — 'Your greatness,' Your majesty, one being born (<s>jāyamāna</s>) 'does not attain,' and one already born 'did not attain' (<s>nāpa</s>): this is the meaning. This is also illustrative — one who will be born will also not attain: this too should be seen. Therefore, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, the pair of <s>Ṛk</s> verses — 'paraḥ mātrayā tanvā vṛdhāna / na te mahitvamanvaśnuvanti / ubhe te vidma rajasī pṛthivyā viṣṇo devatvaṃ paramasya vitse / na te viṣṇo jāyamāno na jāto devamahimnaḥ paramantamāpa / udastabhnā nākamṛṣvaṃ bṛhantaṃ dādhartha prācīṃ kakubhaṃ pṛthivyāḥ' — is explained exactly thus. As follows: 'beyond measure' (<s>mātrāyāḥ paraḥ</s>) means one who has transcended limitation; 'growing by His own form' (<s>tanvā vṛdhānaḥ</s>) means growing by His body, complete in body — the instrumental case here is in the sense of 'thus-being' —

children.text: deharūpeṇa pūrṇa ityarthaḥ / yataścidānandādyātmako viṣṇorabhinnaśca dehaḥ / te mahitvaṃ mahimānaṃ nānubhavanti na prāpnuvanti ca / te tvadīyāyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ prakṛteḥ rajasī rajoguṇakārye ubhe puṇyapāpe vayaṃ vidmaḥ / prakṛteḥ rajasā hi puṇyapāpe sṛjyate / paramasya te mahimānaṃ tvameva vitse / tvameva mahimnaḥ mahimasamudāyasyāntaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śriyo vā mahimānamatiśayito hi viṣṇumahimā anyamahimnāṃ param antaṃ te mahimānaṃ na kañcidāpa / yatrākaṃ nāsti tannākam / ṛṣvaṃ prakāśarūpam / bṛhantaṃ pūrṇaṃ lokam udastabhnāḥ udastabhnaḥ uccairastambhayaḥ / pṛthivyāḥ prathivyātmakasya brahmāṇḍasya prācīṃ kakubhaṃ diśaṃ indrasthāpanena dādhartha dhṛtavānasi / sarvadhāraṇopalakṣaṇametaditi /
children.translated_text: that is, He is complete in the form of body: this is the meaning. Because the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is of the nature of consciousness-bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>) and the like, is non-different [from Him]. 'Your greatness' — Your majesty — they 'do not experience,' and 'do not attain.' 'Of Your <s>Pṛthivī</s>' — of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) — the two <s>rajasī</s> (products of <s>rajas</s>), i.e., the two effects of the quality of <s>rajas</s>, namely merit and demerit — 'we know.' For merit and demerit are created by the <s>rajas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s>. 'Of the supreme one, Your greatness' — You alone know. You alone, being 'the ultimate of greatness' — of the totality of greatness — surpassed [even] the greatness of <s>Brahman</s> (Brahmā) or of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), for the greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is indeed the supreme. The 'ultimate limit' — 'Your greatness' — 'no one has attained' any [limit of]. 'Where there is no sorrow' — that is <s>Nāka</s> (heaven). '<s>Ṛṣva</s>' means 'of the nature of radiance.' '<s>Bṛhanta</s>' means 'complete, full.' 'That world You have propped up' (<s>udastabhnāḥ</s>) — You have elevated high. 'Of the earth' — of the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) which is of the nature of earth — 'the eastern quarter' — the direction — 'You have upheld' (<s>dādhartha</s>) — You have supported, by the installation of <s>Indra</s>. This is illustrative of [His] supporting everything.

jagatkāraṇatvaṃ ca brahmaṇo na vikāritvena, kintu pitṛvannimittattvenaiveti śrutyā darśayati, -
'yaḥ'; iti / 'yaḥ'; eka eva 'naḥ'; asmadādisarveṣāṃ 'janitā'; janayitaiva 'pitā'; na dattaputrapitṛvat pālakapitṛmātram / yadvā - "sa eva pitṛsaṃsthastupātṛtvātpitṛnāmakaḥ"ityaitareyabhāṣyadiśā "pitā pātā"iti tattvapradīpokteḥ 'janitā'; janakaḥ 'pitā'; pātā cetyarthaḥ / 'yo vidhātā'; viśeṣeṇa dhārakaḥ poṣakaḥ, "muktānāṃ poṣaṇaṃ ca jñānamokṣadānena"iti tattvapradīpokteḥ / "vidhātā kartā"iti prameyadīpoktiḥ / tasyā dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoriti bhāvaḥ / yo 'viśvā'; viśvāni sarvāṇi bhuvanāni tadgata 'dhāmāni'; gṛhāṇi jīvādisvarūpāṇi ca 'veda'; jānātītyarthaḥ / 'ityādi'; iti vākyam 'uktārthe pramāṇam'; iti śeṣaḥ / ādiśabdena etajjātīyakaśrutyantaraṃ "dyāvābhūmī janayan"iti ca gṛhyate // 2 //
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.2, verse 6:
And the causality of <s>Brahman</s> with respect to the world is not by way of transformation (<s>vikāra</s>), but rather by way of being the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) alone, like a father — he shows this through <s>Śruti</s>:
'He who' — 'who' alone is the 'progenitor' (<s>janitā</s>), the very begetter, of all of us, the 'father' — not merely a guardian-father like a father of an adopted son. Or, following the direction of the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s> — 'He who is established in the fathers is called by the name Father because of fatherhood' — and the statement of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> — 'pitā means protector (<s>pātā</s>)' — 'progenitor' means the one who begets, and 'father' means the one who protects: this is the meaning. 'He who is the ordainer' (<s>vidhātā</s>) — the one who specially sustains and nourishes; as stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'and the nourishment of the liberated is through the granting of knowledge and liberation.' The statement of the <s>Prameyadīpa</s> is: 'vidhātā means the maker.' Its import is: of sustenance and nourishment. He who 'knows' all 'abodes' (<s>dhāmāni</s>) — dwellings, and the essential natures of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) and the like — situated in all (<s>viśvā</s>) 'beings' (<s>bhuvanāni</s>): this is the meaning. 'And so forth' (<s>ityādi</s>) — this sentence 'is the authority for the stated meaning': this is the remainder. By the word 'ādi,' another <s>Śruti</s> of this type — 'generating heaven and earth' — is also included. // 2 //
// Thus ends the <s>Janmādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of origination). //
// 3. The <s>Śāstrayonitvādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of scripture being the source). //
Others should not be imagined [as the cause of the world] on the basis of inference.
[This is] because [<s>Brahman</s>] has scripture as its source of knowledge. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.3 |

atrādhikaraṇe pūrvoktajagajjanmādikāraṇatvarūpabrahmalakṣaṇasya rudrādiṣvativyāptiparihārāya jagatkāraṇe pramāṇamucyate / siddhāntapratijñāmupaskṛtya darśayati - 'anumānataḥ'; iti / kāraṇatveneti śeṣaḥ/ tathā ca - śivo jagajjanmādikartā sarvajñatvāt vyatirekeṇa yajñadattavat ityādyanumānāt viṣṇoḥ 'anye'; rudrādayo 'pi jagatkāraṇatvena 'na kalpanīyāḥ'; na śaṅkyā ityarthaḥ/ kuta ityatastatra hetvākāṅkṣāyāṃ sūtramupanyasyati - 'śāstrayonitvāt'; iti/ jagatkāraṇasyeti śeṣaḥ / "tannirdhāritayuktirvā"ityanuvyākhyāpade "tannirdhāritetyataḥ paraṃ vyāptiśabdo 'dhyāhāryaḥ"iti sudhokteryathā tatra madhye 'dhyāhāraḥ, yathā vā "sarvendriyavivarjitatvādyartha uktaḥ"iti gītābhāṣyaprameyadīpe ādītyataḥ paraṃ śabdaśabdo 'dhyāhārya ityuktestatra yathā madhye 'dhyāhāraḥ, yathā vā "puruṣādvadhavikārasamūhatenakṛteṣu"iti mahābhāṣyavākye samāsamadhye teneti padādhyāhāraḥ, tathātrāpi śāstraśabdātparamekaśabdo 'dhyāhāryaḥ yoniśabdātprāk jñaptiśabdaśca / tathā ca ṛgādirūpaṃ śāstraṃ ca tadekamasahāyaṃ ca jñaptiyonirjñaptikāraṇaṃ yasya vastunaḥ tattathoktaṃ tasya bhāvastattvaṃ tasmāditisūtrārthaḥ / anena na jagatkāraṇamānumānikaṃ tasya śāstraikasamadhigamyatvāt dharmādivat ityanumānamuktaṃ bhavati / na ca dṛṣṭānte sādhyavaikalyam / na hi dharmādiniścayo 'numānena bhavati / tathā ca - anumānādanyeṣāṃ jagatkāraṇatāsādhanamayuktamiti na teṣu lakṣaṇasyātivyāptiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.3, verse 1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), to resolve the over-extension of the defining characteristic of <s>Brahman</s> stated earlier as being the cause of the world's birth and so forth with respect to <s>Rudra</s> and others, the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) regarding the cause of the world is stated. Prefacing the thesis of the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), he shows: 'From inference.' 'As the cause' is the remainder. And thus — from inference such as '<s>Śiva</s> is the maker of the world's birth and the like, because of being omniscient, by exclusion, like <s>Yajñadatta</s>' and so on, 'others' — <s>Rudra</s> and others too — 'should not be imagined,' should not be suspected, as the cause of the world: this is the meaning. Whence [this conclusion]? In anticipation of the reason, he presents the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Because [Brahman] has scripture as its source.' 'Of the cause of the world' is the remainder. Just as in the <s>Anuvyākhyāna</s> passage 'tannirdhāritayuktir vā,' the <s>Sudhā</s> says 'after tannirdhārita, the word vyāpti must be supplied,' and just as there a word is supplied in the middle; or just as in the <s>Gītā Bhāṣya Prameyadīpa</s> passage 'sarvendriyavivarjitatvādyartha uktaḥ,' the word 'śabda' must be supplied after 'ādi'; or just as in the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> sentence 'puruṣādvadhavikārasamūhatenakṛteṣu,' the word 'tena' is supplied in the middle of the compound — so here too, after the word 'śāstra' the word 'eka' (sole) must be supplied, and before the word 'yoni' (source) the word 'jñapti' (cognition) [must be supplied]. And thus, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: scripture in the form of the <s>Ṛg Veda</s> and others is the sole, unaccompanied source of cognition — the cause of cognition — of that entity whose [cognition] has that [scripture] as its source; the state of being that is the reason: therefore. By this, the inference is stated: the cause of the world is not [known] through inference, because it is knowable through scripture alone, like <s>dharma</s> and the like. Nor is there a deficiency of the property to be proven in the example. For the ascertainment of <s>dharma</s> and the like does not occur through inference. And thus — it is improper to establish the world-causality of others through inference; therefore there is no over-extension of the defining characteristic to them: this is the import.
'One who does not know the <s>Veda</s> does not comprehend that great one, the all-experiencing one, at the time of departure.' (<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.12.9)
'The Person of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>' — and from <s>Śruti</s> passages such as these.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.2:
kāraṇasya śāstraikavedyatvaṃ kuta ityata āha - 'na'; iti / taittirīyavākyamidam / atra hrasvokārapāṭhaḥ/ 'aupaniṣadaḥ'; iti śrutyantaram / atrāṅaḥ praśleṣaḥ kāryaḥ / ādiśabdena "sarve vedā yatpadaṃ"(kaṭha. u. 2-15) "vedāhyevainaṃ"(bhāllaveyaṃ) "taṃ tvaupaniṣadaṃ puruṣaṃ pṛcchāmi"(bṛ. u. 5-9-26) iti vākyaṃ ca gṛhyate / 'taṃ'; pūrvaprakṛtaṃ 'bṛhantaṃ'; pūrṇaṃ 'sarvānubhuṃ'; sarvamanubhavatīti sarvānubhūḥ taṃ sarvajñam / yadvā - sarvamanubhāvayatīti sarvānubhustaṃ ātmānaṃ sarvajagatkartāraṃ sarvasvāminaṃ vā / 'sāmparāye'; samyakparasyāyaḥ prāptiḥ samparāyaḥ sa eva sāmparāyaḥ, tādarthye saptamī, tathā ca mokṣāya 'avedavit'; - viṣṇutattvanirṇayaṭīkoktarītyā atra vedaśabdena sadāgamā gṛhyante / tathā ca sadāgamatadarthājñānī vedaviruddhajñānī vā 'na manute'; na jānāti, vedādanyat jagatkartāraṃ na pramāpayatīti yāvat / kintu vedavideva jānāti veda eva pramāpayatīti prathamaśrutyarthaḥ / puruṣo jagatkartā ā aupaniṣadaḥ upaniṣadekasamadhigamya ityanyaśrutyarthaḥ / gamyatvaṃ grāhyatvaṃ taddhitārthaḥ / ādiśabdopāttaśrutyapekṣayā 'śrutibhyaśca'; iti bahuvacanam/ caśabdo 'dhyāhṛtasādhyasamuccaye, svoktisamuccaye vā / asya śāstrayonitvādityanenānvayaḥ / kāraṇasyeti śeṣaḥ / tathā caivamādiśrutibhyaḥ kāraṇasya śāstraikayonitvāvagamāt nāsiddhiriti bhāvaḥ / nañdvayāṅghaṭitaśrutyudāharaṇena sūtra ekaśabdo 'dhyāhārya iti sūcitam /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.3, verse 2:
Whence is it known that the cause is knowable through scripture alone? To this he says: 'na' (not). This is a <s>Taittirīya</s> passage. Here the short 'u' reading is given. 'Aupaniṣadaḥ' (of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>) is another <s>Śruti</s>. Here the word 'aṅ' should be read with <s>praśleṣa</s> (coalescence). By the word 'ādi,' the passages 'all the <s>Vedas</s> [proclaim] that abode' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.15), 'the <s>Vedas</s> indeed [know] Him' (<s>Bhāllaveyam</s>), and 'I ask you about that Person of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 5.9.26) are also included. 'Him' — the previously mentioned one; 'great' (<s>bṛhantam</s>) — complete, full; 'sarvānubhum' — He who experiences everything, i.e., the all-knowing one. Or, 'sarvānubhu' means He who causes everything to be experienced, i.e., the Self, the maker of the entire world, the lord of all. 'At the time of departure' (<s>sāmparāye</s>) — 'samparāya' means the complete attainment of the supreme, i.e., <s>mokṣa</s>; 'sāmparāya' is the same; the seventh case is in the sense of purpose. And thus, for <s>mokṣa</s>, one who 'does not know the <s>Veda</s>' — following the method stated in the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirṇaya Ṭīkā</s>, by the word '<s>Veda</s>' here, the valid scriptures (<s>sadāgamas</s>) are intended. And thus, one who does not know the valid scriptures and their meanings, or one who knows things contrary to the <s>Vedas</s>, 'does not comprehend' — does not know; that is, does not bring about valid cognition of the maker of the world other [than <s>Viṣṇu</s>]: this is the sense. Rather, only one who knows the <s>Veda</s> knows; only the <s>Veda</s> brings about valid cognition: this is the meaning of the first <s>Śruti</s>. The Person who is the maker of the world is 'aupaniṣada' — knowable through the <s>Upaniṣads</s> alone: this is the meaning of the other <s>Śruti</s>. 'Knowability' — 'graspability' — is the meaning of the <s>taddhita</s> suffix. The plural 'from <s>Śrutis</s>' is with reference to the <s>Śrutis</s> included by the word 'ādi.' The word 'ca' (and) is for aggregating the properties to be proven that are implied, or for aggregating [these authorities] with his own statement. Its syntactic connection is with 'because [Brahman] has scripture as its source.' 'Of the cause' is the remainder. And thus, from <s>Śruti</s> passages such as these, since the sole knowability of the cause through scripture alone is ascertained, there is no failure [of the argument]: this is the import. Through the citation of a <s>Śruti</s> constructed with a double negative (<s>nañdvaya</s>), it is indicated that the word 'eka' (sole) must be supplied in the <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text:
na cānumānasya niyataprāmāṇyam /
śrutisāhāyyarahitamanumānaṃ na kutracit /
niścayātsādhayedarthaṃ pramāṇāntarameva ca //
children.translated_text:
And inference does not have unfailing authority.
'Inference unsupported by <s>Śruti</s> can never
establish a matter with certainty; and another means of knowledge [too cannot].' //
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.3, verse 3:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.3:
aupaniṣadasyāpi kāraṇasyānumānena siddhiḥ kiṃ na syādityata āha - 'na ca'; iti / co 'vadhāraṇe / tathā ca - 'anumānasya'; anumānamātrasya 'prāmāṇyam'; atīndriyārthapramāpakatvaṃ netyarthaḥ / tathā ca - na tenānyasya jagatkartṛtāsādhanaṃ yuktamiti bhāvaḥ / nanu kathametat 'sarvadharmopapatteśca'; (sū. 2-1-38) ityadhikaraṇe svātantryādihetunā viṣṇoḥ pūrṇatvādisiddhyaṅgīkārādityata uktam - 'niyata'; iti / idaṃ ca svātantryārthakaṃ pramāṇarūpaprakṛtyarthaviśeṣaṇam / anumānasyeti hetugarbham / tathā ca - anumānatvādeva na tasya svātantryeṇādṛṣṭārthaniścāyakatvaṃ, pratipakṣādisambhavāt, kintvasvātantryeṇa / svātantryaṃ ca sahāyarāhityam / tacca na svātantryādihetāvasti śrutisāhāyyarahitatvena svatantratvānna pramāṇatvamiti bhāvaḥ / kuto nānumānasya niyataprāmāṇyamityata āha - 'śruti'; iti / smṛterapyupalakṣakametat / atra sahāyaśabdo mūlavācī / tasmātsvārthe ṣyañ / śrutiśca tatsāhāyyaṃ ceti karmadhārayaḥ, tatastena rahitamiti tatpuruṣaḥ / śrutyanugrāhyatvarahitamiti yāvat / caḥ samuccaye / evaśabdo bhinnakramaḥ / tathā ca - 'kutracit'; asmādādyadṛṣṭe śraute 'rthe 'śrutisāhāyyarahitamanumānam'; īśvaro na svatantraḥ cetanatvādityādi liṅgam, tathā yajñahiṃsādharmatvānumānaṃ ca tathā 'pramāṇāntaram'; anumānādanyat rāmakṛṣmādidoṣagrāhi mānuṣatvagrāhi ca pratyakṣaṃ 'niścayāt'; sphuṭamatīndriyārthaṃ 'na sādhayet'; iti yojanā / yadvā - arthaṃ niścayānna sādhayenna sādhayedevetyarthaḥ / uktaṃ hi gītābhāṣye - "sa niścayena yoktavyaḥ yoktavya eva bubhūṣuṇetyarthaḥ"iti uktaṃ hi prameyadīpikāyām "ayogavyavacchede niścayaśabdaḥ"iti /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.3, verse 3:
Could not the cause, even though it is of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, be established through inference as well? To this he says: 'na ca' (and not). The word 'ca' is for emphasis. And thus — 'of inference' — of inference alone — 'the authority,' that is, the capacity to produce valid cognition of supersensory objects, does not exist: this is the meaning. And thus — establishing the world-causality of another through [inference] is not proper: this is the import. But how is this so, since in the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> [beginning with] 'sarvadharmopapatteśca' (<s>Sūtra</s> 2.1.38), the fullness and other qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s> are accepted as established through the reason of independence and the like? To this it is said: 'niyata' (unfailing). This word 'niyata,' having the meaning of independence, qualifies the word '<s>prāmāṇya</s>' (authority) which is of the nature of the primary meaning. 'Of inference' contains the implied reason. And thus — precisely because it is inference, it does not have the capacity to determine independently an unseen object with certainty, because of the possibility of counter-arguments and the like; rather, it has [authority] only dependently. And independence means the absence of auxiliary support. And that [independence] does not exist in the reason of independence and the like, since there is no authority because it is independent — being devoid of the support of <s>Śruti</s>: this is the import. Why does inference not have unfailing authority? To this he says: '<s>Śruti</s>.' This is illustrative of <s>Smṛti</s> as well. Here the word 'sahāya' (auxiliary) has the meaning of 'source.' Therefore, the <s>ṣyañ</s> suffix is in its own sense. '<s>Śruti</s> and its auxiliary support' is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound; 'devoid of that' is a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>. The sense is: devoid of being supported by <s>Śruti</s>. The word 'ca' is for aggregation. The word 'eva' is in displaced order. And thus — 'anywhere,' in any unseen, <s>Śrauta</s> (scriptural) matter, 'inference unsupported by <s>Śruti</s>' — a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) such as 'God is not independent because of being sentient' — and likewise, inference that violence in sacrifice is <s>dharma</s> — and 'another means of knowledge' — perception other than inference, which grasps the faults of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and others, and grasps their humanity — 'would not establish' the matter 'with certainty,' clearly, regarding supersensory objects: this is the construction. Or — it would not establish the matter, that is, would definitely not establish [it]: this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Gītā Bhāṣya</s>: 'sa niścayena yoktavyaḥ — the meaning is: yoktavya eva — he must be yoked, i.e., necessarily.' As stated in the <s>Prameyadīpikā</s>: 'the word niścaya is used for exclusion of non-application.'

children.text:
śrutismṛtisahāyaṃ yat pramāṇāntaramuttamam /
pramāṇapadavīṃ gacchennātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
children.translated_text:
That [inference] which is supported by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> is the supreme means of valid knowledge;
it attains the status of [valid] evidence — there should be no deliberation about this. /
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.3, verse 4:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.4:
tarhi kīdṛśasya pratyakṣāderadṛṣṭārthaniścāyakatvamityata āha 'śruti'; iti / bahuvrīhirayam / tathā ca - śrutismṛtirūpasahakāriyuktaṃ 'yatpramāṇāntaraṃ'; yaśodādipratyakṣaṃ tat 'uttamam'; / ataḥ tat 'pramāṇapadavīm'; anupramāṇasya pramākaraṇatvarūpāṃ paddhatiṃ 'gacchet'; prāpnuyādityanvayaḥ / taditi pāṭhe 'pyevameva yojanā / evaṃ śrutismṛtisahāyo yastarkaḥ viṣṇuḥ svatantraḥ pūrṇatvāditi samavyāptikānumānaṃ so 'pi pramāṇapadavīṃ gacchedityanvayaḥ / 'atra'; asmin viṣaye 'vicāraṇā'; saṃśayo 'na'; kārya ityarthaḥ nātretyanena svoktārthe 'prāmāṇyaśaṅkā nirākṛtā /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.4: Then, what kind of perception and the like has the capacity to ascertain unseen objects? — to this he says: '<s>śruti</s>' (scripture). This is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. And thus: that 'other means of knowledge' — the perception of glory and the like — which is endowed with the auxiliary in the form of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, that is 'the best.' Therefore that [perception] 'would attain the status of a means of valid knowledge' (<s>pramāṇapadavīm</s>) — would reach the course that is the nature of being an instrument of valid cognition: this is the construction. Even in the reading 'tat' (that), the syntactic connection is exactly the same. Thus: that reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) which is assisted by <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> — [i.e.,] <s>Viṣṇu</s> is independent because of [His] fullness — such an inference of universal co-extension also attains the status of a means of valid knowledge: this is the construction. 'In this matter' (<s>atra</s>), 'inquiry' (<s>vicāraṇā</s>) — doubt — 'is not' to be entertained: this is the meaning. By 'not here,' the suspicion of invalidity regarding his own stated position is refuted.
'What meaning is intended here, consistent with what precedes and follows?' —
Such deliberation is <s>tarka</s> (reasoning); but dry reasoning should be avoided. //
Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Mahākūrma</s> [Purāṇa]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.5:
tarkapadasya vyāpyāropeṇetyādyanyathāpratītinirāsāya tarkasvarūpamāha - 'pūrva'; iti / 'atra'; vipratipanne vākye 'ko 'rtho 'bhimataḥ'; tātparyaviṣayo 'bhavedityādyam'; evaṃbhūtavimarśapūrvakaṃ 'pūrvottarāvirodhena'; upakramopasaṃhārāvirodhena tadaikarūpyeṇa-liṅgāntarasyāpyupalakṣaṇametat - tathā ca - upakramāditātparyaliṅgaiḥ atra tātparyaviṣayārtho 'yameva bhavedityādyaṃ yat 'ūhanaṃ'; yatpramājñānaṃ tatsādhanaṃ liṅgaṃ sa eva 'tarkaḥ'; atrābhimataḥ / 'śuṣkatarkaṃ'; śrutismṛtisahāyarahitaṃ tannirapekṣaṃ cetanatvādi tarkaṃ tu varjayet, tenātīndriyārthaniścayo na kārya ityarthaḥ / kecittu ka - ityasyobhayārthatvamāśrisya "kaśchandasām"(ṛ. 10-115-9) iti vākyam 'atra'; ityanena parāmṛśyate / ata eva 'ityādyam'; ityapi yuktamityāhuḥ / 'kaurme'; ityanantaraṃ purāṇe yata uktamiti śeṣaḥ / asya 'na ca'; ityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.5: In order to refute the alternative understanding such as 'through the superimposition of what is pervaded' and the like regarding the word <s>tarka</s>, he states the true nature of <s>tarka</s>: '<s>pūrva</s>' (what precedes). 'Here' — in a statement where there is disagreement, 'what meaning is intended' — what is the subject of the purport — 'such as this and the like' — preceded by such deliberation, 'consistent with what precedes and follows' — consistent with the opening and conclusion — 'by the uniformity of those' — this is an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) of other inferential marks as well. And thus: through the inferential marks of purport such as the opening and the like, that 'deliberation' which [determines] 'this alone would be the intended meaning here' and the like, that 'valid knowledge' — that inferential mark which is the means of that valid cognition — that alone is the '<s>tarka</s>' (reasoning) intended here. 'Dry reasoning' (<s>śuṣkatarka</s>) — reasoning devoid of the assistance of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, independent of them, such as [arguments from] consciousness and the like — should be avoided; by that, the ascertainment of supersensible objects should not be made: this is the meaning. Some, however, relying on the dual meaning of 'ka' — cite the Vedic passage 'who among the meters' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.115.9) as being referred to by the word 'here' (<s>atra</s>). Hence 'such as this and the like' is also appropriate — thus they say. After '<s>kaurme</s>' (in the <s>Kūrma</s> [Purāṇa]), 'since it is stated' is to be supplied. This connects with 'na ca' (and not).
And because inferences can be constructed everywhere.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.6:
na kevalaṃ śrutyādisāhityahīnānumānasya prāmāṇyābhāve sādhaka sadbhāvaḥ, api tu tatprāmāṇyābhyupagame bādhakaṃ cāstītyāha - 'śakyatvāt'; iti / prayoktumiti śeṣaḥ / 'anumānām'; iti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī / caśabdo na kevalamityuktasamuccayārthaḥ / tathā ca - śrutyādisāhityahīnānām 'anumānāṃ'; cetanatvavastutvādirūpakevalahetūnāṃ 'sarvatra'; rudrāderjagatkāraṇatvābhāvādau śaśādeḥ śṛṅgitvādau sādhyo 'pi prayoktuṃ 'śakyatvāt'; nānumānasya niyataprāmāṇyamiti yojanā /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.6: Not only is there evidence for the invalidity of inference devoid of the assistance of <s>Śruti</s> and the like, but there is also an invalidating argument even if its validity is accepted — to this he says: 'because of the possibility' (<s>śakyatvāt</s>). 'To employ' is to be supplied. '<s>Anumānām</s>' — the sixth case-ending is used in the objective sense. The word 'ca' is for the purpose of aggregation as stated by 'not only.' And thus: inferences devoid of the assistance of <s>Śruti</s> and the like — [those based on] mere reasons such as consciousness, substance-hood, and the like — 'everywhere' — in [proving] the absence of <s>Rudra</s> and others being the cause of the world, the possession of horns by a hare and the like — 'because of the possibility' of constructing [such inferences] even for the opposite thesis — inference does not have invariable validity: this is the construction.

children.text:
sarvatra śakyate kartumāgamaṃ hi vinānumā /
tasmānna sā śaktimatī vināgamamudīkṣitum // iti vārāhe /
children.translated_text: Inference can be constructed everywhere, for without scripture, inference [is unreliable]. Therefore it is not capable of revealing [truth] without scripture. // Thus in the <s>Vārāha</s> [Purāṇa]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.7:
atraiva pramāṇamāha - sarvatreti / 'hi'; yasmāt 'āgamaṃ vinā'; taddhīnā 'anumā'; 'sarvatra'; īśvarakāraṇatvābhāvādau 'kartuṃ'; prayoktuṃ 'śakyate'; 'tasmāt'; anumā 'āgamaṃ vinā udīkṣitum'; udīkṣayituṃ jñāpayitum arthamiti śeṣaḥ 'śaktimatī'; sāmarthyayutā netyarthaḥ / 'vārāhe'; ityasyāpi 'kaurme'; itivadanvayaḥ / tasmātkevalānumānasyānirṇāyakatvācchāstreṇaiva kartṛtvaniścaya iti sthitam /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.7: For this very point he cites authority: '<s>sarvatra</s>' (everywhere). 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since 'without scripture' — deprived of it, 'inference' — 'everywhere' — in [matters such as] the absence of God being the cause and the like — 'can be constructed,' that is, employed. 'Therefore' inference, 'without scripture,' is 'not capable' — not endowed with the power — 'to reveal' (<s>udīkṣitum</s>), that is, to make known the object: this is the meaning. The construction of 'in the <s>Vārāha</s>' is like that of 'in the <s>Kūrma</s>.' Therefore, since mere inference is inconclusive, the determination of creatorship is through scripture alone — this is established.

children.text:
reto dhāturvaṭakaṇikā ghṛtadhūmādhivāsanam /
jātismṛtirayaskāntaḥ sūryakānto 'mbubhakṣaṇam /
pretya bhūtāpyayaścaiva devatābhyupayācanam /
mṛte karmanivṛttiśca pramāṇamiti niścayaḥ /
iti mokṣadharmavacanānna nāstikyavādo yujyate //
children.translated_text: Semen, bodily constituents, a banyan seed, the fattening [effect of] ghee, fumigation [of trees], birth-memory, the lodestone, the sun-stone, drinking water, the dissolution of the body after death, the dissolution into elements, supplication to deities, and the cessation of activity in the dead [body] — these are the proofs: this is the determination. // Thus, from the statement in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>, the doctrine of atheism is not tenable. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.8:
nanvatīndriyārthābhāvena pratyakṣetarasyāprāmāṇyātkathaṃ śāstrādīśvarasiddhiriti nāstikyavādaṃ mokṣadharmavacanena nirācaṣṭe - reta iti / reta ityādiprathamaikavacanāntānāṃ padānāṃ pratyekaṃ pramāṇamiti padenānvayaḥ / 'atrārthe'; iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - retodhātvādi 'atrārthe'; atīndriyārthasattve anumānādiprāmāṇye ca pramāṇaṃ pramāpakaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ/ bhāṣyakārīyadvitīyetiśabdasya evaṃ mokṣadharmavacanātpratītairhetubhirnāstikyavādo na yujyata iti yojanā / nāstikā eva nāstikyaṃ, nāstikasamudāyo vā nāstikyam / tathā ca - nāsti paralokaḥ, dharmo nāsti, adharmo nāstīti dhiyā vāda ityarthaḥ / yadvā - nyāyadīpikoktarītyā - āstikyaṃ dharmādāvastyanena prayojanamiti bhāvo buddhiḥ, tatpūrvako vādaḥ, tadanyo nāstikyavāda ityarthaḥ / retodhātvādīnāmanumāpakatvaprakārastvittham - retaśśabditacaramadhātuśarīrayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo na pratyakṣaḥ, kintvanvayavyatirekākhyānumānagamya iti tatprāmāṇyasiddhiḥ / mṛtaśarīre siktasya retasaḥ śarīrākāraṇatvena yadadhiṣṭhite śarīre siktaṃ retaḥ śarīrātmanā pariṇamati tajjīvasiddhiḥ/ vandhyādisarvaśarīre siktasya retasaḥ kāryākaratvena yatpreritaṃ retaḥ kāryakaraṃ tadīśvarādṛṣṭasiddhiḥ / tata eva tatpratipādakāgamaprāmāṇyasiddhiḥ / evaṃ vātapittādidhāturapathyādinā jīvaccharīre kvacideva vikriyate, na mṛtaśarīre, nāpi jīvatsarvaśarīreṣu / tato jīveśvaratadbodhakāgamaprāmāṇyādisiddhiḥ / vaṭakaṇikāpadoktavaṭabījādvaṭa utpadyata iti suprasiddham, na ca bharjitāyāstasyāḥ, nāpyabharjitābhyassarvābhya iti tatprerakeśvādṛṣṭasiddhiḥ / ghṛtena jīvaccharīra eva pīnatā jāyate, na mṛtaśarīre kṣiptena nāpi jāvatsarvaśarīreṣu / 'dhūmādhivāsanaṃ'; nāma puṣpādisampattyarthaḥ dhūmena vṛkṣasya saṃskāraḥ / tenāśuṣkavṛkṣeṣveva puṣpādisampattiḥ, na śuṣke, nāpyaśuṣkeṣu sarveṣu / etābhyāmapi liṅgābhyāṃ jīveśvarādṛṣṭādisiddhiḥ / keṣāñcitsādhanaviśeṣāt 'jātismṛtiḥ'; pūrvajanmasmṛtirbhavati anenaiva puṇyena evaṃ svargo 'nubhūtaḥ, anena pāpenetthaṃ narakamanubhūtamiti / sā ca kasyacideva, na sarvasya, na cetanādyabhāve sā yuktetyato 'pi cetanādṛṣṭādisiddhiḥ / ayaskāntākhyaśilāviśeṣeṇāyo bhramati, na cācetane ceṣṭakatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ, nāpi sarvacetanānāmityetasmādapi tatprerakeśvarādṛṣṭādisiddhiḥ / sūryakāntākhyaśilāviśeṣeṇāgnirjāyate, na cāsau śaktiracetane yuktā / ato 'pi prerakeśvarādṛṣṭādisiddhiḥ / ambubhakṣaṇena jīvaccharīra eva tṛṣṇā nivartate, na ca tanmṛtaśarīre pātrāntare vā nihitaṃ pacyate / nāpi jīvatsarvaśarīreṣu / tasmādapi jīveśvarādisiddhiḥ / pretyetyanantaraṃ sthitasyeti śeṣaḥ / 'pretya'; jīvaṃ vihāya sthitasya dehasya 'bhūtāpyayo'; bhūteṣu laya ityarthaḥ / tathā ca - maraṇena dehasya pṛthivyādipañcabhūteṣu layo bhavati, na jīvato, na cecchayetyato 'pi tanniyāmakeśvarādisiddhiḥ / evaṃ devatābhyupayācanena keṣāñcideva sampadādikaṃ bhavati, evaṃ mṛte dehe ceṣṭānivṛttirbhavati, na purā na svecchayā / ato 'pi jīveśvarādṛṣṭādisiddhiriti /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.8: [Objection:] Since there is no supersensible object, and since what is other than perception is therefore invalid, how can God be established through scripture? — To this, he refutes the atheistic doctrine through a passage from the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>: '<s>reta</s>' (semen). Each of the words ending in the first-case singular '<s>reta</s>' and so on connects individually with the word '<s>pramāṇam</s>' (proof). 'In this matter' is to be supplied. And thus: semen, bodily constituents, and the rest are proofs — that is, they are evidence — 'in this matter,' namely in [establishing] the existence of supersensible objects and the validity of inference and the like: this is the meaning. The construction of the commentator's second particle 'iti' is: thus, from the proofs apprehended through the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> statement, the atheistic doctrine is not tenable. The term '<s>nāstikya</s>' means either the atheists themselves, or the community of atheists, or atheism. And thus: the doctrine 'there is no other world, there is no <s>dharma</s>, there is no <s>adharma</s>' — this is the meaning. Alternatively, in the manner stated in the <s>Nyāyadīpikā</s>: '<s>āstikya</s>' is the conviction that there is purpose in <s>dharma</s> and the like; a doctrine preceded by that [conviction]; what is other than that is the atheistic doctrine: this is the meaning. The manner in which semen and bodily constituents and the like serve as inferential proofs is as follows: The cause-effect relationship between the final bodily constituent designated as semen and the body is not perceptible, but is knowable through inference in the form of positive and negative concomitance — thus the validity of that [inference] is established. Since semen deposited on a dead body does not produce a body, while semen deposited in an inhabited body transforms into bodily form — this establishes the existence of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul). Since semen deposited in every body, including the barren, does not produce an effect, while semen that is impelled [in certain cases] does produce an effect — this establishes the existence of God and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit). From that very fact, the validity of the scripture that teaches these is also established. Similarly, the bodily constituents such as <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and the like undergo transformation through improper food and the like only in a living body, not in a dead body, nor in all living bodies — from this too, the existence of the soul, God, and the validity of the scripture that reveals them is established. It is well known that from a banyan seed a banyan tree arises, but not from a roasted seed, nor from all unroasted seeds — thus the existence of God and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> as the impellers is established. Through ghee, fattening occurs only in a living body, not when applied to a dead body, nor in all living bodies. 'Fumigation' (<s>dhūmādhivāsana</s>) means the treatment of a tree with smoke for the purpose of obtaining flowers and the like. Through that, the abundance of flowers and the like occurs only in non-dried trees, not in dried ones, nor in all non-dried ones. Through these two inferential marks as well, the existence of the soul, God, <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, and the like is established. Through certain special practices, 'birth-memory' — the memory of previous births — arises [in the form]: 'Through this very merit, heaven was experienced thus; through this sin, hell was experienced thus.' And that occurs only for some, not for all, and it would not be possible without the existence of consciousness and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> — hence from this too the existence of consciousness, <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, and the like is established. A particular stone called lodestone causes iron to move, and movement in an insentient thing is not observed [independently], nor do all sentient beings [cause such movement] — hence from this too the existence of God and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> as the impellers is established. A particular stone called sun-stone produces fire, and that power is not possible in an insentient thing — hence from this too the existence of God and <s>adṛṣṭa</s> as the impellers is established. Through drinking water, thirst is quenched only in a living body, and water placed in a dead body or another vessel does not undergo digestion, nor does it [quench thirst] in all living bodies — hence from this too the existence of the soul, God, and the like is established. After '<s>pretya</s>' (having departed), 'of one who remains' is to be supplied. '<s>Pretya</s>' — of the body that remains after the <s>jīva</s> has departed, 'dissolution into elements' (<s>bhūtāpyaya</s>) — dissolution into the elements: this is the meaning. And thus: upon death, the dissolution of the body into the five elements — earth and the like — occurs, but not of a living [body], nor by [its own] will — hence from this too the existence of God and the like as the controller is established. Similarly, through supplication to deities, prosperity and the like occur only for some; similarly, when the body dies, cessation of activity occurs — not before, and not by one's own will. Hence from this too the existence of the soul, God, <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, and the like is established.
And because of the observation of the results of austerity and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.9:
yuktyantareṇāpi nāstikyavādaṃ dūṣayati - darśanācceti / co yuktisamuccaye / ādiśabdena pāpaṃ gṛhyate/ tathā ca svādhyāyabrahmacaryādirūpātyutkaṭatapaādiphalasya tejassvitvādeḥ pratyakṣata eva darśanācca na nāstikyavādo yujyata ityarthaḥ / puṇyapāpākhyātīndriyavastunastatsādhakānumānāgamaprāmāṇyasya cāṅgīkāryatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.9: He refutes the atheistic doctrine through another argument as well: 'because of observation.' The word 'ca' is for aggregation of arguments. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), sin is included. And thus: because of the direct observation of the results of exceedingly intense austerity and the like — such as the study of the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) — namely radiance and the like, the atheistic doctrine is not tenable: this is the meaning. The purport is: because the existence of supersensible things called merit and demerit, and the validity of the inference and scripture that establish them, must be accepted.
<s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, <s>Atharva</s>, the <s>Bhārata</s>, and the <s>Pañcarātra</s>,
and the original <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> — these are declared to be scripture. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.10:
nanu yadyanumānasyāniścāyakatvena śāstrādeva kāraṇatvasiddhiḥ, tarhi pāśupatādiśāstreṇa rudrāderjagatkāraṇatvasiddhiḥ syādityata āha - ṛgiti / akārānto 'yamatharvaśabdaḥ / ṛkca yajuśca sāma cātharvaśceti tathoktāḥ / evaśabdasya ṛgādikameveti sambandhaḥ / 'mūlarāmāyaṇamevetyavāntararāmāyaṇavyudāsaḥ'; iti sudhoktiḥ / caśabdau samuccaye /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.10: [Objection:] If the determination of creatorship is through scripture alone, since inference is inconclusive, then through <s>Pāśupata</s> and other scriptures, the creatorship of the world by <s>Rudra</s> and others would be established — to this he says: '<s>ṛg</s>' (the <s>Ṛgveda</s>). This word '<s>atharva</s>' ends in '<s>a</s>.' '<s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Yajus</s> and <s>Sāma</s> and <s>Atharva</s>' — thus they are mentioned. The word 'eva' (alone) connects as: 'the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the rest alone.' 'The original <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> alone' — this is to exclude the derivative <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>s: thus says the <s>Sudhā</s>. The two words 'ca' are for aggregation.
And whatever is consistent with these — that too is declared to be scripture.

children.text: ato 'nyo granthavistāro naiva śāstraṃ kuvartma tat //
children.translated_text: Any other expanse of texts is not scripture at all — that is a false path. //
Thus in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.11:
tarhi mānavādyaśāstraṃ syādityata āha - yacceti / co 'vadhāraṇe, dvitīyo 'pyarthe / tathā ca 'etasya'; ṛgādeḥ 'yat'; yadeva 'anukūlam'; aviruddhārthapratipādakaṃ mānavādi purāṇādikaṃ vā 'tat'; sarvamapi 'śāstraṃprakīrtitaṃ'; prāmāṇikaiḥ 'ataḥ'; etasmāt vedāt tadanukūlācca 'anyaḥ'; viruddhaḥ udāsīnaśca yo 'granthavistāraḥ'; pāśupatādirūpagranthavistaraḥ 'tannaiva śāstram', kintu 'kuvartma'; kutsitamārgaḥ, mārga iva mārgaḥ, kutsitajñānopāyo 'mānamityarthaḥ/ ṛgādikamevetyevakārastu viruddhādiviṣaya iti bhāvaḥ / skānde purāṇe ityuktamityanvayaḥ / pāśupatādeḥ kuvartmatvamitiśabdārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.11: [Objection:] Then the <s>Mānava</s> [Dharmaśāstra] and others would not be scripture — to this he says: '<s>yat</s>' (whatever). The word 'ca' is for emphasis; the second is in the sense of 'api' (also). And thus: 'of this' — of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the rest, 'whatever' — whatever alone is 'consistent' — the <s>Mānava</s> and other [texts], or <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like, that present non-contradictory meaning — 'all that' too is 'declared as scripture' by the authoritative [teachers]. 'Other than this' — from this <s>Veda</s> and what is consistent with it, whatever 'expanse of texts' — the expanse of texts in the form of <s>Pāśupata</s> and the like — that is 'not scripture at all,' but rather a 'false path' (<s>kuvartma</s>) — a debased course, a path-like path, a debased means of knowledge, that is, a delusion: this is the meaning. The particle 'eva' (alone) pertains to what contradicts [the <s>Veda</s>] and the like: this is the purport. The construction is: [this is] stated in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>. The meaning of the particle 'iti' is: the <s>Pāśupata</s> and the like are a false path.
<s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Pāśupata</s>, and the <s>Vedāraṇyaka</s> —

children.text: ityārabhya vedapañcarātrayoraikyābhiprāyeṇa pañcarātrasyaiva prāmāṇyamuktamitareṣāṃ bhinnamatatvaṃ pradarśya mokṣadharmeṣvapi //
children.translated_text: beginning with this [verse], having demonstrated the difference of doctrine of the others, it is stated that only the <s>Pañcarātra</s> has authority, with the intention of showing the unity of the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Pañcarātra</s> — [this too is stated] in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.12:
ito 'pi pāśupatādikaṃ kuvartmetyāha - sāṅkhyamiti / atraivaṃ yojanā - na kevalaṃ skānde, kintu mokṣadharmeṣvapi / 'sāṅkhyaṃ yogaḥ pāśupataṃ vedāraṇyakameva ca'; 'ityārabhya'; upakramyādhītena
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.12: From this too, the <s>Pāśupata</s> and the like are a false path — he says: '<s>sāṅkhyam</s>' (Sāṅkhya). Here the construction is as follows: not only in the <s>Skānda</s>, but in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> too — '<s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Pāśupata</s>, and the <s>Vedāraṇyaka</s>' — 'beginning with' this [verse], having commenced with [the examination of these systems through] what has been studied,
The speaker of the entire <s>Pañcarātra</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself.
Among all these systems of knowledge, O king of kings, this [<s>Pañcarātra</s>] is especially taught. //

children.text: ityuttaravākyena sāṅkhyādiṣu prakṛteṣvapi tatparityāgena pañcarātrasyaiva prāmāṇyarūpamādhikyamuktaṃ yato 'taḥ pāśupatādikaṃ kuvartma amānameveti / nanvanena pañcarātraprāmāṇyameva bhavennānyāprāmāṇyamityata āha - itareṣāmiti / vedapañcarātrayoranyeṣāṃ sāṅkhyādīnāmityarthaḥ/ 'bhinnamatattvaṃ'; viruddhadarśanatvaṃ 'pradarśya'; jñāpayitvā pratipādyeti yāvat/
children.translated_text: By the subsequent statement, even though <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and others are [also] the subject matter, by setting them aside, the superiority of <s>Pañcarātra</s> alone in the form of authoritativeness is stated. Therefore, the <s>Pāśupata</s> and other [systems] are merely false paths, devoid of validity — thus. Now, by this, only the authoritativeness of <s>Pañcarātra</s> would be established, not the non-authoritativeness of others — to this he says: 'itareṣām' (of the others). Of those other than the Veda and <s>Pañcarātra</s>, i.e., <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and the rest — this is the meaning. 'Bhinnamatattvaṃ' — the nature of having contradictory doctrines; 'pradarśya' — having demonstrated, having made known, i.e., having established.
<s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Pāśupata</s>, and <s>Vedāraṇyaka</s> (Vedas and Upaniṣads) indeed —
These systems of knowledge are mutually different; no deliberation should be undertaken here. //

children.text: iti vākyaśeṣeṇeti śeṣaḥ / pradarśyetyasya pañcarātrasyaiva prāmāṇyamuktamityanenānvayaḥ / parasparaviruddhānāmekaprāmāṇyoktāvanyāprāmāṇyalābhāditi bhāvaḥ / tarhi vedāraṇyakasyāpyaprāmāṇyaṃ syādityata āha - vedeti / 'aikyābhiprāyeṇa'; iti / ekārthatvarūpamūlamūlibhāvābhiprāyeṇetyarthaḥ / tathā ca pañcarātrasya vedasamānārthatvena tatprāmāṇyoktau vedaprāmāṇyamevoktaṃ bhavatīti na tasyāprāmāṇyamiti bhāvaḥ / na caikyābhiprāyaḥ kutaḥ kalpyata iti vācyam, yato 'dṛṣṭaviṣayasya pauruṣeyasya pañcarātrasya nirmūlatve 'prāmāṇyādādhikyakathanamasaṅgataṃ syāt / 'sāṅkhyam'; īśvarāvatārānyakapiloktaṃ śāstram /
children.translated_text: — Thus, by the remainder of the sentence: this is the completion. The construction of 'pradarśya' (having demonstrated) is with 'the authoritativeness of <s>Pañcarātra</s> alone is stated.' Since in declaring the authoritativeness of one among mutually contradictory [systems], the non-authoritativeness of others is obtained — this is the purport. Then the non-authoritativeness of <s>Vedāraṇyaka</s> too would follow — to this he says: 'veda.' 'Aikyābhiprāyeṇa' — with the intention of unity. The meaning is: with the intention of the relationship of root and derivative, in the form of identity of meaning. And thus, since the authoritativeness of <s>Pañcarātra</s> is stated through its identity of meaning with the Veda, the authoritativeness of the Veda itself is thereby stated — hence there is no non-authoritativeness of the Veda: this is the purport. Nor should one say 'from where is this intention of unity assumed?' — because for the humanly-authored <s>Pañcarātra</s>, which concerns supersensory matters, if it were rootless, the statement of its superiority would be inconsistent. '<s>Sāṅkhya</s>' — the <s>śāstra</s> taught by <s>Kapila</s>, [who is] an incarnation of <s>Īśvara</s> [named] <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: kapilo vāsudevākhyaḥ tantraṃ sāṅkhyaṃ jagāda ha /
children.translated_text: The <s>Kapila</s> named <s>Vāsudeva</s> taught the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> system;
And another <s>Kapila</s> taught [a version] contradicting all scriptures. //

children.text: ityuktatvāt / 'yogo'; hi hiraṇyagarbhoktaṃ pātañjalam / 'pāśupataṃ'; paśupatinā proktam / araṇye nirjane deśe adhyetavyatvādāraṇyakamityupaniṣaducyate / vedāścāraṇyakāni ca, teṣāṃ samāhāraḥ vedāraṇyakaṃ, dvandvaikavadbhāvo vā / varṇāśramarājadānadharmādipratipādyadharmabahutvāt mokṣadharmāṇāṃ bhedādvā mokṣadharmeṣviti bahuvacanam / ata eva tattvapradīpe - mokṣadharmeṣviti bahuvacanaṃ dharmabhedādityuktam / mokṣadharme hi -
children.translated_text: — Because it is thus stated. '<s>Yoga</s>' — indeed, the <s>Pātañjala</s> [system] taught by <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. '<s>Pāśupata</s>' — taught by <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva). Because it is to be studied in a solitary, uninhabited place, the <s>Āraṇyaka</s> is called <s>Upaniṣad</s>. The Vedas and the <s>Āraṇyakas</s> — their collective designation is '<s>Vedāraṇyaka</s>,' or it is a <s>dvandva</s> compound treated as a single unit. Due to the multiplicity of <s>dharmas</s> taught — pertaining to <s>varṇa</s>, <s>āśrama</s>, royal duties, charity, and other duties — or due to the varieties of <s>mokṣa-dharmas</s>, the plural 'in the <s>Mokṣadharmas</s>' is used. For this very reason, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'The plural in mokṣadharmeṣu is due to the varieties of dharma' — thus it is stated. For in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> —
<s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Pāśupata</s>, and <s>Vedāraṇyaka</s> indeed —
Are these systems of knowledge different, or not? — let this be stated. //

children.text: iti vaiśampāyanoktaṃ prativacanaṃ cāsti / ime yudhiṣṭhirabhīṣmakartṛke ca / bhagavataḥ jñānāni jñānasādhanāni bhinnāni bhinnamatāni / viruddhanāmapi matānāṃ na sarveṣāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ sambhavati vastuno bahurūpatvābhāvāt, kintvekasyātra prāmāṇyamitareṣāmaprāmāṇyaṃ vācyam / tatra kasya prāmāṇyaṃ kasya vāprāmāṇyamiti punaryudhiṣṭhirajanamejayahārdapraśnottaramāha bhīṣmo vaiśampāyanaśca / "sāṅkhyasya vaktā kapilaḥ"ityārabhya "pañcarātrasya kṛtsnasya"ityanena jñāneṣu jñānasādhaneṣu etatpañcarātram / abhiprāyastu paramāptatamena nārāyaṇena sarvasya pañcarātrasya kṛtatvātprāmāṇyaṃ tāvatsiddham, viruddhānāṃ caikaprāmāṇye anyāprāmāṇyaṃ ca/ etaccādyavākyasthavedāraṇyakapadena vedamūlakapañcarātrasyottaravākyasthapañcarātrapadena ca mūlabhūtavedāraṇyakasyopalakṣaṇāmaṅgīkṛtyobhayorekavākyatāyāmeva sambhavati / anyathā pañcarātrasya pūrvamaprakṛtatvena pūrvottaravākyayorasaṅgatatvāpātaḥ / upalakṣaṇāmaṅgīkṛtyaikavākyatāyāṃ ca svīkṛtāyāṃ vedapañcarātrayoreva prāmāṇayaṃ siddhyati / na tadviruddhapāśupatādīnāmiti teṣāmaprāmāṇyameveti /
children.translated_text: — Thus there is the reply spoken by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>. And these [dialogues] have <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s> as their [respective] interlocutors. 'Of the Lord' — the systems of knowledge, i.e., the means of knowledge, are 'different,' having divergent doctrines. Since among mutually contradictory doctrines, not all can be authoritative — because a single entity cannot have multiple natures — but rather one among them must be authoritative and the others non-authoritative, this must be stated. In that regard, the question of which is authoritative and which is non-authoritative is posed by <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and <s>Janamejaya</s>, expressing the sentiment of [their] hearts, and answered by <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> respectively. Beginning with 'The teacher of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> is <s>Kapila</s>' and [continuing to] 'of the entire <s>Pañcarātra</s>' — by this, among the systems of knowledge, i.e., among the means of knowledge, this <s>Pañcarātra</s> [is supreme]. The purport is: since the entire <s>Pañcarātra</s> was composed by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the most supremely authoritative being, its authoritativeness is thereby established; and since one among contradictory [systems] being authoritative entails the non-authoritativeness of the others. And this is possible only when, accepting that the word '<s>Vedāraṇyaka</s>' in the first statement figuratively denotes <s>Pañcarātra</s> (which is rooted in the Veda), and the word '<s>Pañcarātra</s>' in the subsequent statement figuratively denotes <s>Vedāraṇyaka</s> (the Veda being the root) — [only then] is the syntactic unity of both statements possible. Otherwise, since <s>Pañcarātra</s> was not previously the topic, the inconsistency of the prior and subsequent statements would arise. And when figurative usage is accepted and the syntactic unity is established, the authoritativeness of the Veda and <s>Pañcarātra</s> alone is established — not that of the <s>Pāśupata</s> and other [systems] opposed to them — hence their non-authoritativeness alone [follows].
Scripture is the source — [meaning] the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for this [<s>Brahman</s>] — thus [the compound] '<s>śāstrayoni</s>.' // 3 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.13:
