evaṃ sūtraṃ vyākhyāya yatpareṇoktaṃ śāstrasya yoniriti tadayuktamiti bhāvena svābhimatārthaṃ darśayati - śāstramiti / kāraṇārthakena yoniśabdena yogyatayā jñaptessambandhe pramāṇamiti paryavasyatītyabhiprāyeṇa 'yoniḥ pramāṇam'; iti vyākhyātam / 'asya'; jagatkāraṇasya 'iti śāstrayoni'; ityanantaraṃ tuśabdo 'dhyāhāryaḥ / ata eva gītābhāṣye "iti tu śāstrayonitvam"ityuktam / turevārthaḥ / tathā ca - śāstraṃ yoniḥ pramāṇaṃ yasya tacchāstrayonītyeva śāstrayonipadārtho brahma, na tu śāstrasya yonītyarthaḥ/ paravyākhyānaṃ tūktānupayuktamayuktaṃ ceti ṭīkāyāmeva dūṣitam // 3 //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.3.13:
Having thus interpreted the <s>sūtra</s>, [the commentator shows that] what the opponent stated — 'scripture is the origin [of <s>Brahman</s>]' — is inappropriate, and with this intention presents his own accepted meaning: 'śāstram' (scripture). With the word '<s>yoni</s>' (source) in the sense of cause, since the connection is through the fitness for cognition, the meaning culminates in '<s>pramāṇa</s>' (means of knowledge) — with this intention, [the compound] is interpreted as '<s>yoniḥ pramāṇam</s>' (the source is the means of knowledge). 'Asya' — of this cause of the universe; 'iti śāstrayoni' — after this, the particle 'tu' (but/indeed) is to be supplied. For this very reason, in the <s>Gītā-bhāṣya</s>, it is stated: 'iti tu śāstrayonitvam' (thus indeed [is established its] having scripture as its means of knowledge). The word 'tu' has the meaning of 'eva' (indeed/precisely). And thus — '<s>śāstraṃ yoniḥ pramāṇaṃ yasya</s>' — that for which scripture is the source, i.e., the means of knowledge — that is '<s>śāstrayoni</s>' — this is the meaning of the word '<s>śāstrayoni</s>,' i.e., <s>Brahman</s>; it does not mean 'the origin of scripture.' The opponent's interpretation, however, has been refuted as both inappropriate and inapplicable in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> itself. // 3 //
// Thus ends the <s>Śāstrayonitvādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Having Scripture as the Means of Knowledge). //
// 4. <s>Samanvayādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Coherent Interpretation). //

Even though [<s>Brahman</s>] is cognized [through other means], it is not the case that others [besides <s>Viṣṇu</s>] have scripture as their means of knowledge.
Why?
But that [is established] through coherent interpretation (<s>samanvaya</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.4 |

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.1:
atrādhikaraṇe jagatkāraṇasya śāstrayonitvānna lakṣaṇātivyāptiriti pūrvādhikaraṇaphalākṣepaparihāramukhena tasya lakṣaṇatvasiddhaye viṣṇoreva jagatkāraṇatvena śāstragamyatvaṃ netareṣāmapīti samarthyate / pūrvapakṣasūcanapūrvakaṃ siddhāntamāha - ajñānāmiti // kartari ṣaṣṭhīyam / itareṣāṃ iti sambandhe / samuccayārthasyāperubhayatrānvayaḥ / pratītyā āgamopalakṣaṇā vā / tathā ca - na kevalaṃ pāśupatādyuktam, kintu 'ajñānāṃ'; śrutitātparyārthājñānibhirāpātataḥ jñāyamānamapi na kevalaṃ viṣṇoḥ kintu 'itareṣāṃ'; rudrādīnāmapi śāstrayonitvaṃ, jagatkāraṇatvena śāstragamyatvaṃ netyarthaḥ / nanu pratītyāderajñānamūlatvādikaṃ parikalpyānyeṣāṃ kāraṇatayā śāstrayonitvāgrahaṇe ko heturiti pṛcchati - kuta iti / pratīyamānamapītyanenāsyānvayaḥ / tatra hetukathanāya sūtramupanyasyati - tattviti / yata ityādau grāhyam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), since the cause of the universe has scripture as its means of knowledge, there is no over-extension of the defining characteristic — [thus] through the mode of refuting the objection that would negate the fruit of the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the establishment of that [characteristic] as a valid definition is [demonstrated], and [it is shown that] <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, as the cause of the universe, is knowable through scripture, and not others — this is what is argued. Prefacing with an indication of the prima facie view, he states the established conclusion: 'ajñānām.' This is a sixth case ending in the agentive sense. 'Itareṣām' is in the relational sense. The particle 'api' in the sense of aggregation applies to both [clauses]. 'Pratīti' implies scriptural reference as well. And thus — not only is the <s>Pāśupata</s> etc. position refuted, but also, even though 'ajñānām' — by those who are ignorant of the purport of <s>śruti</s>, [<s>Brahman</s>] is superficially cognized [as applicable to others], not only of <s>Viṣṇu</s> but 'itareṣām' — of <s>Rudra</s> and others too, '<s>śāstrayonitvam</s>' — the status of being knowable through scripture as the cause of the universe — 'na' — [this] is not [the case]: this is the meaning. Now, what is the reason for not accepting the scripture-knowability arising from cognition etc. [pertaining to others]? — he asks: 'kutaḥ.' Its syntactic connection is with 'pratīyamānam api' (even though cognized). To state the reason, he introduces the <s>sūtra</s>: 'tat tu.' The word 'yataḥ' (because) is to be supplied at the beginning.
<s>Anvaya</s> (coherent connection) is the indicator (<s>liṅga</s>) [consisting of] logical reasoning (<s>upapatti</s>) and so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.2:
sūtrākṣarāṇi vyācaṣṭe - anvaya iti / anvīyate svārthena sambadhyate tatparatayā jñāyate śāstraṃ śabdo vānenetyanvayaḥ upapattyāditātparyaliṅgamityarthaḥ / sūtrānusārādekavacanaṃ samudāyābhiprāyam / tena copakramādīnāṃ kvacidavirodhaṃ sūcayati / ādipadaṃ śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāmapi grāhakam / atra śrutyādiṣaṭkaṃ ca grāhyamiti ṭīkokteḥ / atra vākye śrutyādiṣaṭkamapyādipadena grāhyamiti hi tasyārthaḥ / parantu śrutyādīnāmupakramādivattātparyagrāhakatvābhāvādāgamārthamātranirṇāyakatvāt nātra tannidarśakapramāṇoktiḥ / ata evottaratra -
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.2:
He explains the words of the <s>sūtra</s>: 'anvaya.' '<s>Anvaya</s>' — that by which [the meaning] is connected with its own purport, i.e., is known as having that as its import — '<s>anvaya</s>' is the indicator (<s>liṅga</s>) consisting of logical reasoning (<s>upapatti</s>) and so forth, for determining the purport (<s>tātparya</s>): this is the meaning. The singular [in the <s>sūtra</s>], following the <s>sūtra</s>'s usage, is in the collective sense. And by this, he indicates that in some cases there is no conflict among <s>upakrama</s> (commencement) and the other [indicators]. The word 'ādi' (etc.) also includes <s>śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory sign), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), <s>sthāna</s> (position), and <s>samākhyā</s> (designation) as well. And from the <s>Ṭīkā</s>'s statement: 'Here the six [beginning with] <s>śruti</s> are also to be included' — and the statement here is: in the sentence [of the <s>sūtra</s>], the six [beginning with] <s>śruti</s> are also to be included by the word 'ādi' — this is indeed its meaning. However, since <s>śruti</s> etc. do not, like <s>upakrama</s> etc., serve as indicators of purport but only determine the meaning of <s>āgama</s> (traditional teaching), they are not cited here as evidence for [determining purport]. For this very reason, later —

children.text: śrutirliṅgaṃ samākhyā ca vākyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory sign), <s>samākhyā</s> (designation), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), and likewise —
Each preceding one is stronger [than the succeeding] — thus in determining the meaning of scripture. //

children.text: iti tatrāpi pramāṇaṃ vakṣyati / uktaṃ hi pramāṇalakṣaṇaṭīkāyām "upakramādīnāṃ tātparyaliṅgatvameteṣāṃ punarartha eveti viśeṣajñāpanārtho yogavibhāgaḥ"iti / na caivam "atra śrutyādiṣaṭkaṃ ca grāhyam"iti ṭīkāyāṃ tātparyagrāhakeṣvantarbhāvoktirayukteti vācyam, yato 'tretyasya samanvayaśabdārtha ityevārtho na tātparyagrahakeṣviti, 'ākāśastalliṅgāt'; 'śabdādeva pramitaḥ'; (bra.sū. 1-1-22, 7-24) ityādau śrutiliṅgādibhirāgamārthaniraṇayadarśanena teṣāmapi anvīyate śaktirūpasambandhavattayā jñāyate padajātamebhiritivyutpattyā anvayaśabdārthatvaucityāt / na copakramopasaṃhārābhyāsāpūrvatāphalārthavādopapattayaḥ śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyāśca tātparyaliṅgānīti jñānapādīyasudhāvirodha iti vācyam, atra śakterapi saṃyojanāt / ata eva candrikāyāmupakramādipramāṇakaḥ śaktitātparyalakṣaṇassambandhaḥ samanvaya ityuktam / atradipadaṃ śrutyādīnāmapi grāhakam / vyutkrameṇānvayaḥ / anenātra bṛhatsaṃhitāvacanodāharaṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇasya śrutirliṅgamiti vacanasyopalakṣakamiti sūcitam /
children.translated_text: There too he will state the authority. For it has been said in the <s>Pramāṇalakṣaṇa-ṭīkā</s>: 'The fact that <s>upakrama</s> etc. are indicators of purport, while these [<s>śruti</s> etc.] determine meaning alone — this distinction is the purpose of the separate classification.' Nor should one object that, given this, the <s>Ṭīkā</s>'s statement 'here the six [beginning with] <s>śruti</s> are also to be included' — [claiming] their inclusion among the indicators of purport — is inappropriate; because the meaning of 'atra' (here) is 'in the meaning of the word <s>samanvaya</s>,' not 'among the indicators of purport.' Since in [passages like] '<s>ākāśas tal liṅgāt</s>' and '<s>śabdād eva pramitaḥ</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.22, 7-24), the determination of scriptural meaning through <s>śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, etc. is observed, and since through the etymology '<s>anvīyate</s>' — [meaning] 'by these, the collection of words is known through a connection in the form of denotative capacity' — the appropriateness of <s>śruti</s> etc. also being within the meaning of the word '<s>anvaya</s>' [is established]. Nor should one say that [our interpretation] contradicts the <s>Jñānapādīya-sudhā</s>, [which states that] <s>upakrama</s>, <s>upasaṃhāra</s>, <s>abhyāsa</s>, <s>apūrvatā</s>, <s>phala</s>, <s>arthavāda</s>, and <s>upapatti</s> are indicators of purport, while <s>śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, <s>vākya</s>, <s>prakaraṇa</s>, <s>sthāna</s>, and <s>samākhyā</s> are not — because here [the word] '<s>śakti</s>' (denotative power) is also conjoined. For this very reason, in the <s>Candrikā</s> it is stated: 'The connection that is characterized by denotative power and purport, established through <s>upakrama</s> etc. as its means of knowledge, is <s>samanvaya</s>.' The word 'ādi' here also includes <s>śruti</s> etc. The construction is inverted. By this, it is indicated that the citation of a statement from the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s> here is illustrative of the statement '<s>śrutir liṅgam</s>' etc. that will follow.
And it is stated in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s> —
<s>Upakrama</s> (commencement) and <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion), <s>abhyāsa</s> (repetition), <s>apūrvatā</s> (novelty), <s>phala</s> (fruit),
<s>Arthavāda</s> (eulogy) and <s>upapatti</s> (reasoning) — [these are] the indicators for determining the purport. //
Thus.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.3:
kāni tānyupapattyādīni kutra ca liṅgānītyata āha - uktaṃ ceti / upapattyādītyanuṣajyate/ na kevalamupapattyādyuktaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ, kintu tajjñāpyaṃ coktamiti cārthaḥ / asmaduktamupapattyādi liṅgaṃ bṛhatsaṃhitāyāmapyuktamiti vā / kimuktamityatastatpaṭhati - upakrameti / prakaraṇādirupakramaḥ tadanta upasaṃhāraḥ / upakramopasaṃhāraśca tau tathoktau / atropakramopasaṃhāratadaikarūpyābhyāsāpūrvatāphalārthavādāśceti pramāṇalakṣaṇokteḥ pratyekavivakṣayā viśakalitāvupakramopasaṃhārau dvau samudāyavivakṣayā ubhayāvirodhalakṣaṇaṃ ekārthatvalakṣaṇaṃ vā tadaikarūpyamapi pṛthaktātparyagrāhakamanusandheyam / ata eva dvivacanaprayogaḥ / ekaprakārāsakṛduktirabhyāsaḥ / prācuryeṇa pramāṇāntarāsiddhārthabodhakatā apūrvatā / phalavadarthapratipādakaṃ phalam / stutiḥ, nindā, ekakartṛkopākhyānarūpā parakṛtiḥ, anekakartṛkopākhyānarūpaḥ purākalpaśca, arthavādaḥ / upapattiḥ yuktiḥ / 'tātparyanirṇaye'; vākyatātparyaniścaye 'liṅgaṃ'; sādhanamitiyarthaḥ/ yadvā - nirṇetavye tātparye sādhye 'liṅgaṃ'; heturityarthaḥ/ liṅgamityasya upakramādipadaiḥ yathāyogyaṃ pratyekaṃ sambandhaḥ / smṛterupakramāditve 'pi virodhe uttarottaraprābalyasūcanāya bhāṣye upapattyādīti vyatyasyoktiḥ / sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvena upapatterupakramādibhyaḥ pṛthaguktiḥ / yadvā - etaccopakramādi svārthe śabdātmakamapi idametatparam abādhe satyetadupakramatvāt
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.3:
What are those [indicators consisting of] reasoning etc., and where are they stated as indicators? — to this he says: 'uktaṃ ca' (and it is stated). '<s>Upapattyādi</s>' is carried forward [from the previous statement]. Not only is '<s>upapatti</s> etc.' stated, but what is to be inferred from it is also stated — this is the meaning of 'ca.' 'What was stated by us as upapatti etc. as indicator is also stated in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>' — or alternatively [this is the meaning]. What is stated? — to this, he reads [the verse]: '<s>upakrama</s>.' '<s>Upakrama</s>' is the commencement, i.e., the initial section of a topic; its end is the '<s>upasaṃhāra</s>' (conclusion). '<s>Upakrama</s>' and '<s>upasaṃhāra</s>' — these two are stated together. Here, from the statement in the <s>Pramāṇalakṣaṇa</s> that '<s>upakramopasaṃhāra-tadaikarūpya-abhyāsa-apūrvatā-phala-arthavādāḥ</s>,' when analyzed individually with the intention of separate treatment, <s>upakrama</s> and <s>upasaṃhāra</s> are two; when treated collectively, <s>tadaikarūpya</s> (their mutual conformity) — characterized by non-contradiction or identity of meaning — is also separately to be noted as a determinant of purport. Hence the dual number usage. Repetition of the same kind is '<s>abhyāsa</s>.' The capacity to convey meaning largely unestablished by other means of knowledge is '<s>apūrvatā</s>' (novelty). That which conveys a result-bearing meaning is '<s>phala</s>' (fruit). Praise, blame, narrative about a single agent called '<s>parakṛti</s>,' and narrative about multiple agents called '<s>purākalpa</s>' — [all these constitute] '<s>arthavāda</s>' (eulogy). '<s>Upapatti</s>' is reasoning. 'In the determination of purport' — in ascertaining the purport of a passage — '<s>liṅga</s>' means 'instrument,' i.e., evidence: this is the meaning. Alternatively: in the purport that is to be determined, i.e., to be established — '<s>liṅga</s>' means 'reason,' i.e., logical ground: this is the meaning. The word '<s>liṅga</s>' has a separate syntactic connection with each of the words '<s>upakrama</s>' etc. as appropriate. Even though <s>smṛti</s> [also has] the status of [teaching] <s>upakrama</s> etc., to indicate the greater strength of the later [authority] in case of conflict, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> says '<s>upapattyādi</s>' in inverted order. The separate mention of '<s>upapatti</s>' (reasoning) from '<s>upakrama</s>' etc. is due to their relationship of general to particular. Alternatively — this [set of indicators including] <s>upakrama</s> etc., even though verbal in nature with respect to its own [primary] meaning, [becomes] an indicator (<s>liṅga</s>) for the purport of the passage in the form 'this [passage] has this as its import, since it has this as its commencement'

children.text: ityādirūpeṇa vākyatātparye liṅgaṃ ca bhavati / upapattistu yathāgnyādirūpasvarthe tathā tātparye 'pi ayametattātparyaviṣayaḥ upapannatvāt iti prakāreṇa liṅgarūpeti pṛthaguktiḥ /
children.translated_text: and so forth. <s>Upapatti</s> (reasoning), however, [functions as] an indicator for the purport as well — in the form 'this is the subject of this purport, because it is logically coherent' — hence its separate mention.
When properly examined through the indicators of purport such as <s>upakrama</s> (commencement) etc., that alone [i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>] is knowable through scripture.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.4:
sūtraṃ yojayati - upakramādīti / 'śāstre'; iti śeṣaḥ / samityasyārthaḥ samyagiti / sarvasminnityapi draṣṭavyam / 'nirūpyamāṇe'; ityanena saṃśabdārthasya adhyāhṛtakriyayānvayo darśitaḥ / tuśabdasyārtha eveti / 'śāstrayoni'; ityanuṣaktapadasyārthaḥ śāstrāgamyamiti / tathā ca yato 'trānvayapadoktaiḥ śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyopakramādibhiḥ śaktitātparyaliṅgaiḥ 'saṃ samyak'; balābalavimarśapūrvakaṃ 'sarvasmin'; śāstre ṛgādirūpe 'nirūpyamāṇe'; vicāryamāṇe ekārthe śaktitātparyarūpavyāpakadharmavattayā avagamyamāne 'tadeva'; viṣṇvākhyaṃ brahmaiva 'śāstragamyaṃ'; tatpramāṇakaṃ pratīyate, na rudrādi, ato 'jñānāṃ pratīyamānamapi netareṣāṃ śāstrayonitvamiti yojanā / liṅgairiti tṛtīyayā nirūpyamāṇe iti saptamīprayoge ca upakramādikaṃ tātparyahetuḥ / tātparyaṃ ca śāstrapramāṇakatve heturiti sūcitaṃ bhavati / na kevalamupapattyādikaṃ samanvayaśabdārthaḥ, kintu taddhetukaḥ śāstrajanyapramāgocaratvarūpaḥ śāstrayonitve hetubhūtaḥ / "tatparatvasambandho 'pi"iti sudhokteḥ / anena 'samanvayāt'; sāvakāśatvaniravakāśatvādinā balābalaniścayapurassaraṃ anyatarabādhayā vākyārthavimarśarūpasamyagvicāritatvalakṣaṇasamyakttvayuktādupakramā-
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.4.4:
He construes the <s>sūtra</s>: 'upakramādi' (from the opening etc.). 'In the scripture' is the remainder. The meaning of the word 'sam' is 'samyak' (properly). It should also be seen as applying to 'sarvasmin' (in all). By the word 'nirūpyamāṇe' (when being examined), the connection of the meaning of the word 'sam' with a supplied verb is shown. The meaning of the particle 'tu' is 'eva' (indeed). The meaning of the carried-over word 'śāstrayoni' (whose source is scripture) is 'śāstrāgamyam' (knowable through scripture). And thus, since here, through the inferential marks of <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) and <s>tātparya</s> (purport) — namely the <s>Śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory sign), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context), <s>sthāna</s> (position), <s>samākhyā</s> (nomenclature), and <s>upakrama</s> (opening) — stated by the word '<s>anvaya</s>' (concordance), 'sam' — properly, with a prior examination of the relative strength and weakness; 'in all' scripture in the form of the <s>Ṛg Veda</s> and others 'nirūpyamāṇe' — when being examined, when comprehended in a single meaning through the pervading property in the form of denotative power and purport — 'that alone' — <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone 'is knowable through scripture' — is ascertained as having that as its means of valid cognition, not <s>Rudra</s> and others; therefore, even though [<s>Brahman</s>] is apprehended by knowledge, others do not have the status of having scripture as their source: this is the construal. Through the instrumental case in 'by the indicatory marks' and the locative case in 'when being examined,' the <s>upakrama</s> and the like are [shown to be] the reasons for purport. And it is indicated that purport is the reason for having scripture as the means of valid cognition. Not merely consistency (<s>upapatti</s>) and the like is the meaning of the word <s>samanvaya</s>, but rather, what is caused by that — namely the state of being the object of valid cognition arising from scripture — which serves as the reason for having scripture as its source. As stated in the <s>Sudhā</s>: 'The relation of exclusive reference too.' By this, 'samanvayāt' (because of harmony) —

children.text: diśaktitātprayaliṅgasamudāyātmasamanvayāt sarvaśāstrasya bhagavatyeva samyagvacanavṛttyā śaktitātparyākhyasambandhāvagamāt tadviṣṇvākhyaṃ brahmaiva jagatkāraṇatayā śāstrayoni na rudrādīti 'samanvayāt'; ityasyāvṛttyā sūtrayojanā darśitā bhavati /
children.translated_text: through the harmony in the form of the totality of indicatory marks of denotative power and purport such as the opening (<s>upakrama</s>) and the like, preceded by the determination of relative strength and weakness through the [principles of] having scope and not having scope, and by the sublation of the alternative, through proper deliberation characterized by thorough examination of the meaning of sentences — from the comprehension of the relation called denotative power and purport through the proper operation of all scripture as referring to the <s>Bhagavān</s> alone — that <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the cause of the world and has scripture as its source of knowledge, not <s>Rudra</s> and others: thus, through the repetition of 'samanvayāt,' the construal of the <s>sūtra</s> is shown.

children.text:
māṃ vidhatte 'bhidhatte māṃ vikalpyo 'pohyā ityaham /
ityasyā hṛdayaṃ sākṣānnānyo madveda kaścana /
iti bhāgavate
// 4 //

BBsBhDīp_1,1.4.5:
nanu karmavidhānādirūpaśāstrasya kathaṃ brahmaparatetyāśaṅkāṃ bhagavadvākyena pratiṣedhati - māmiti/ yadyapi bhāgavate "ityasyā hṛdayaṃ loke"iti pāṭhaḥ, tathā pūrvottarārdhayorvyutkrameṇa pāṭhaśca dṛśyate/ tathāpyācāryokteranyakalpīyo 'yamityadoṣaḥ / ekādaśaskandhe uddhavaṃ prati kṛṣṇavacanametat / atrāsmacchabdena kṛṣṇa ucyate / tathā ca "vasante vasante" ityādi karmavidhātrī śrutiḥ 'mām'; uddiśyaiva matpūjātvena karmavidhatte / indrādyabhidhātrī 'māmabhidhatte'; madguṇānaiśvaryādīnabhidhatte / 'ahaṃ vikalpyaḥ'; kalpanaṃ vidhānaṃ tathā ca -
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.4.5:
[Objection:] How can a scripture that primarily enjoins ritual actions be regarded as having <s>Brahman</s> as its purport? — He refutes this doubt through a statement of the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'mām' (Me). Although in the <s>Bhāgavata</s> the reading is 'ityasyā hṛdayaṃ loke' ('the heart of this in the world'), and although a transposed reading of the first and second halves is also seen, nevertheless, since this is [based on] the <s>Ācārya</s>'s statement, it belongs to a different recension, hence there is no fault. This is a statement of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to <s>Uddhava</s> in the Eleventh <s>Skandha</s>. Here the word 'me' (asmat) refers to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. And thus: the <s>Śruti</s> that enjoins ritual actions, such as 'in every spring' and the like, 'ordains' 'Me' — enjoins rituals designating them as worship of Me. That which 'describes' the deities <s>Indra</s> and others, 'describes Me' — describes My qualities such as sovereignty and the like. 'I am to be prescribed' (<s>vikalpya</s>) — <s>kalpanam</s> means injunction, and thus —

children.text: catvāri vākparimitā padāni tāni vidurbrāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Speech is measured out in four quarters; those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are wise know them.

children.text: guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṃ vāco manuṣyā vadanti // (ṛ. 1-164-45.)
children.translated_text: Three are deposited in the secret place; they do not move them. Humans speak the fourth [quarter] of speech. // (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 1.164.45)

children.text: iti śrutyā yā vāgvaktṛttvānnimittādvākbdito hariḥ tasyā yāni sthānāpekṣayā 'parimitāni'; paricchinnāni 'catvāri padāni'; vāsudevādirūpāṇi tāni ye manīṣiṇaḥ brāhmaṇāḥ ta eva viduḥ / tatra vāco hṛdayaguhāyāṃ nihitāni vāsudevāditrīṇi rūpāṇi 'manuṣyāḥ'; sādhāraṇāḥ 'neṅgayanti'; na jānanti / 'turīyam'; aniruddhākhyaṃ tu 'vadanti'; jānanatītyevaṃrūpeṇa ahameva catuṣṭvasaṅkhyāviśiṣṭavāsudevādivividharūpatayā bahutvena vidheya ityarthaḥ / 'ahamapohyaḥ'; 'na surāṃ pibet'; (manu. 11-94.) ityādivākyenāpriyāditi śeṣaḥ/ tathā ca "niṣedhabuddhiviṣayamapriyaṃ hi hareḥ smṛtam"iti bhāgavatatātparyokteḥ surāpānādikaṃ madaprītisādhanatvāt niṣidhyate ityapriyadvārā 'na surāṃ pibet'; ityādinā ahameva niṣedhya ityarthaḥ / athavā - ahamapriyādapohyaḥ mamāprītikarātsurāpānaśabditāt "surā harerguṇā me syuḥ"iti cintanāttapadapekṣya apohyo niṣedhya ityarthaḥ / taduktaṃ bhāgavatatātparye - vidhirūpatvena kalpanaṃ vikalpaḥ catvāri vāgityādi / tatra vāgityanuvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the <s>Śruti</s> 'Speech' — <s>Hari</s> is [called] 'Speech' due to being the speaker and on account of [speech as] the material cause — of that [speech], the 'four quarters' which are 'measured out' (delimited) with respect to [its] abodes — having the forms of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and others — those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are wise know them. Among these, the three forms — <s>Vāsudeva</s> and others — 'deposited' in the cave of the heart, 'ordinary humans' 'do not move,' do not know. But 'the fourth' — called <s>Aniruddha</s> — they 'speak,' they know. Thus, in the form of being variously prescribed as the one possessing the fourfold form of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and others, I alone am to be enjoined in manifold ways: this is the meaning. 'I am to be excluded' (<s>apohya</s>) — 'one should not drink liquor' (<s>Manu</s> 11.94) and the like: the remainder is 'from what is displeasing.' And thus, as stated in the <s>Bhāgavata Tātparya</s>: 'What is displeasing to <s>Hari</s> is indeed the object of prohibitive cognition.' Since drinking liquor and the like are means of displeasing Him, they are prohibited; thus through the medium of what is displeasing, by 'one should not drink liquor' and the like, I alone am to be excluded: this is the meaning. Alternatively — I am to be excluded (<s>apohya</s>) from what is displeasing to Me, from that which is designated as liquor-drinking; through the reflection 'the <s>Suras</s> (gods) are the qualities of <s>Hari</s>, may they be mine,' considering the word [<s>surā</s>], [I am] to be excluded, to be prohibited: this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Bhāgavata Tātparya</s>: 'Prescription is the injunction in the form of arranging, the four [quarters] of speech' and so on. There, 'speech' is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>).

children.text:
vidhibhāge hareḥ pūjaivābhidhāne ca tadguṇāḥ /
vikalpe tadbahutvaṃ cāpyapohe tu tadapriyam /
ucyate sarvavedeṣu tacca veda sa eva hi // iti / tathā -
children.translated_text:
In the injunctive portion, it is the worship of <s>Hari</s> alone; in the descriptive [portion], it is His qualities.
In the prescriptive [portion], it is His manifoldness; and in the prohibitive [portion], it is what is displeasing to Him.
All this is spoken of in all the <s>Vedas</s>; and He who knows that — He alone [knows]. // Thus —

children.text:
surā harerguṇāḥ proktāste me syuriti cintanam /
surāpānamiti proktaṃ tanna kuryātkathañcana // iti /
children.translated_text:
The qualities of <s>Hari</s> are called '<s>surā</s>' (gods); 'may they be mine' — this reflection
is called '<s>surāpāna</s>' (drinking of <s>surā</s>/liquor); one should never do that. // Thus.

children.text: tattvapradīpe tu - 'dve vā va brahmaṇo rūpe'; iti vikalpya vividhaṃ kalpayitvā 'tatra yassa ātmā'; (talavakārabrāhmaṇam) iti sadoṣādapohyo nirdeṣatvena vidheyo 'pyahamevetyarthaḥ uktaḥ / atra tattvapradīpapakṣe vikalpyeti lyap / ṭīkākṛtpakṣe tu vikalpyaśabdassamāsāntargato vyasto veti viśeṣaḥ / iyaṃ ca bhagavati
children.translated_text: In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: 'Two indeed are the forms of <s>Brahman</s>' — having been prescribed (<s>vikalpya</s>), that is, having been diversely arranged, 'of this one who is the Self' (<s>Talavakāra Brāhmaṇa</s>) — [I am] to be excluded (<s>apohya</s>) from what is defective, [and] to be pointed out, that is, also to be enjoined — I alone: this is the meaning as stated. Here, in the view of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, '<s>vikalpya</s>' is an absolutive (<s>lyap</s>). In the view of the <s>Ṭīkā</s> author, however, the word '<s>vikalpya</s>' is an adjective contained within the compound: the distinction is that it is split as 'vi.' And this [method of harmonizing] regarding the <s>Bhagavān</s>

children.text: vākyasamanvayarītiḥ - ādyasya itiśabdasya prakārārthasya hṛdayamityanenānvayaḥ / dvitīyasya evaṃbhūtāyā ityarthaḥ / tathā ca hyevaṃbhūtāyā vidhiniṣedhādirūpāyā anyaparatvena pratītāyāścāsyāśśruteriti 'māṃ vidhatte'; ityādyuktaprakāreṇa 'hṛdayaṃ'; tātparyam 'ahameva veda'; jānāmi 'madanyaḥ kaścana'; ko 'pi viśeṣataḥ prāyaḥ na veda na jānātītyarthaḥ / bhāgavata ityanantaraṃ tadeva śāstragamyamityuktatvāt na kathamitiśaṅkāvakāśa iti vākyaśeṣaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: is the method of sentence-harmony: the connection of the first word 'iti' (thus), which has the sense of manner, is with 'hṛdayam' (heart). The second [iti] has the meaning 'of such a nature.' And thus: of this <s>Śruti</s> which is of such a nature — which is in the form of injunction, prohibition, and the like, and which is apprehended as having a different purport — following the method stated as 'He ordains me' and so on, 'the heart' — the purport — 'I alone know.' 'No one other than Me' — no one in particular, for the most part, knows: this is the meaning. After '<s>Bhāgavata</s>,' since 'that alone is knowable through scripture' has been stated, there is no occasion for the doubt 'how [can this be]?': this is the remainder of the sentence. // 4 //
// Thus ends the <s>Samanvayādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of harmony). //
// 5. The <s>Īkṣatyadhikaraṇa</s> (topic of seeing/contemplation). //

children.text:
nanu yato vāco nivartante / aprāpya manasā saha /
(tai.u. 2-4-1.)
children.translated_text:
'From which words return, not reaching [Him], together with the mind.'
(<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.1)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.1:
atrādhikaraṇe saṃśabdoktaṃ vācyatvaṃ kārtsnyaṃ cākṣipya samādhīyate / pūrvapakṣayati - nanviti / 'ityādibhiśśrutibhiḥ'; iti tṛtīyāpañcamyarthe / netyādyāvartate / tathā ca 'tat'; pūrvasūtre tacchabdoktaṃ brahmaśabdagocaraṃ śāstroktaṃ kāraṇaṃ na, kutaḥ? yato na śabdagocaraṃ śāstramukhyārthaḥ na, tadapi kutaḥ? yato na śabdagocaraṃ śabdāvācyaṃ, nacekṣaṇīyatvavirodhaḥ tadasiddheḥ / kutaḥ? yato na tadgocaraṃ jñānaviṣayaḥ na, ajñeyamiti yāvat / na cāvācyatvājñeyatvayorasiddhiḥ / "yato vāco nivartante"ityādi śruteriti yojanā/ 'yato vācaḥ'; iti vākye avācyatvasya 'aprāpya manasā saha'; ityajñeyatvasya ca uktatvāditi bhāvaḥ / "trayī na śrutigocarā"ityatra gocaraśabdasya viśeṣyaliṅgatayā prayogāt 'na tacchabdagocaram'; iti sādhu / sudhāyāṃ tu śabdānāṃ gavāṃ jñānānāṃ caraścaraṇaṃ vṛttiryasmin tacchabdagocaramiti vyadhikaraṇabahuvrīhiṃ caraścaraṇamasyāstīti matvarthīyācpratyayāntatvaṃ cāśritya śabdagocaramityasya sādhutvamuktam / 'yataḥ'; iti taittirīyavākyam / yato 'vāco'; vedā vāgindriyāṇi ca 'manasā'; manorūpendriyeṇa saha 'tamaprāpya'; tadviṣayakavṛttijñānamajānantya eva nivartante / taṃ brahmaṇa ānandaṃ vidvānna bibheti ityarthaḥ / guṇaguṇinorabhedāśrayeṇaitadudāhṛtam /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.5.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the expressibility and completeness stated by the word 'sam' are challenged and then resolved. He presents the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view): 'nanu' (but). 'By <s>Śruti</s> passages such as these' — the third case is used in the sense of the fifth (ablative). 'Na' (not) and the like are carried forward. And thus: 'tat' — that which is the object of scripture stated by the word 'tat' in the previous <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> that is the cause — is not [expressible]; why? Because it is not the object of the word (<s>śabdagocara</s>), not the primary meaning of scripture; and that [is so] for what reason? Because it is not the object of the word, not expressible by words, and there is no contradiction with being an object of contemplation since that [contemplation] is unestablished; and for what reason [is it unestablished]? Because it is not the object of that [cognition], not the subject of knowledge — unknowable, in other words. Nor is there any failure to establish inexpressibility and unknowability: this is the construal from the <s>Śruti</s> 'from which words return' and the like. In the passage 'yato vācaḥ' (from which words [return]), inexpressibility is stated; and by 'aprāpya manasā saha' (not reaching together with the mind), unknowability is stated: this is the purport. From the <s>Bhāgavata Tātparya</s> statement 'trayī na śrutigocarā' (the threefold [Veda] is not within the range of <s>Śruti</s>), since the word 'gocara' (range) is used with the gender agreeing with the qualified noun, 'na tacchabdagocaram' (not within the range of that word) is well-formed. In the <s>Sudhā</s>, however, taking it as a <s>vyadhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi</s> compound — 'that in which the going (<s>cara</s>), the movement, the operation (<s>vṛtti</s>) of words and cognitions [takes place]' — and also relying on the <s>matvarthīya</s> suffix [ending in] '<s>ac</s>' [meaning] 'one who possesses going' — the well-formedness of '<s>śabdagocaram</s>' is stated. 'Yataḥ' — this is a <s>Taittirīya</s> passage. From which [<s>Brahman</s>], 'words' — the <s>Vedas</s> and the speech organs — 'together with the mind' — together with the mind-organ — 'not having reached Him' — without generating cognitive activity (<s>vṛtti</s>) directed at Him, return. 'That <s>Brahman</s>'s bliss — the knower does not fear': this is the meaning. This is cited on the basis of the non-difference of quality and qualified.

'That which is without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable, likewise without taste, eternal, and without smell.'
(<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 3.15)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.2:
'aśabdam'; iti kāṭhakavākyam / atra sarvatra yacchabdo yojyaḥ / na vidyate śabdo guṇaḥ pramāṇaṃ vā yasmiṃstattathoktam / prākṛtaśabdaguṇaśūnyaṃ śabdapramāṇāviṣayaḥ śabdabhinnaṃ cetyarthaḥ / 'asparśaṃ'; sparśaguṇaśūnyaṃ tata eva sparśaliṅgāviṣayaḥ tadbhinnaṃ ca, 'arūpaṃ'; rūparahitam ata eva cakṣuṣapratyakṣāviṣayastadbhinnaṃ ca / 'arasaṃ'; rasaguṇaśūnyaṃ rasabhinnaṃ ca / agandhamityasyāpyupalakṣakametat /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.5.2:
'Aśabdam' — this is a <s>Kāṭhaka</s> passage. Here the word 'yat' (which) should be connected throughout. That which has no sound-quality, no means of cognition [through sound], or is different from sound — thus it is called 'without sound.' '[Without] touch' — devoid of the quality of touch, hence not the object of touch-inference, and different from touch. 'Without form' — devoid of form, hence not the object of visual perception, and different from [form]. 'Without taste' — devoid of the quality of taste, and different from taste. 'Without smell' — this too is indicated by the [word for tastelessness].

children.text: anena pañcamātrāvilakṣaṇatvamapyuktam / 'avyayaṃ nityam'; ityābhāyāṃ svarūpato dehataśca nāśaśūnyatvamucyate / agandhavadityanena gandhavatpṛthivīlakṣaṇatvamuktam / anenopalakṣaṇayā pañcamahābhūtavilakṣaṇatvamapyuktaṃ bhavati / asya 'nicāyya taṃ mṛtyumukhātpramucyate'; ityanenānvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: By this, the distinctness from the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) is also stated. 'Imperishable, eternal' — by these, the absence of destruction both in essential nature and in bodily form is stated. By 'like that which is without smell' (<s>agandhavat</s>), the distinctness from earth which possesses smell is stated. By this, through indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>), the distinctness from the five great elements is also stated. The syntactic connection of this [passage] is with 'having ascertained Him, one is released from the jaws of death.'
'He taught through silence alone.' (<s>Bāṣkala Śruti</s>)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.3:
'avacanena'; ityanyacchrutivākyam / 'avacanena'; vacanavṛttiṃ vinaiva lakṣaṇayā 'provāca brahma guruḥ'; śiṣyāyopadideśeti pararītyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.5.3:
'Avacanena' — this is another <s>Śruti</s> passage. 'Through silence' — without the operation of speech, through indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) alone, 'the teacher taught <s>Brahman</s>' — instructed the disciple: this is the meaning according to the opponent's interpretation.

children.text:
'yadvācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāgabhyudyate ... yacchrotreṇa na śruṇoti yena śrotramidaṃ śrutam'
(ke.1.)
ityādibhiśśrutibhiḥ na tacchabdagocaram /
children.translated_text:
'That which is not uttered by speech, that by which speech is uttered... that which one does not hear by the ear, that by which this ear is heard.'
(<s>Kena Upaniṣad</s> 1)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.4:
'yadvācā'; ityanyattalavakāravākyam / 'vācā'; taduccāryeṇa śabdena yat 'anabhyuditam'; anuktam / yena vāk 'abhyudyate'; ucyate / śrotrendriyeṇa na śṛṇoti puruṣaḥ / yenedaṃ śrotraṃ śrutaṃ tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhītyarthaḥ / atra pūrvapakṣarītyā vacanavṛttiniṣedhaḥ / ādipadenaivaṃjātīyakā śrutirgṛhyate /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.5.4:
'Yadvācā' — this is another <s>Talavakāra</s> passage. 'By speech' — by the word that is pronounced by it, that which is 'not uttered' — not expressed. That by which speech 'is uttered' — is expressed. That which a person 'does not hear' by the ear organ. That by which 'this ear is heard' — know that alone to be <s>Brahman</s>: this is the meaning. Here, according to the opponent's interpretation, there is a negation of the operation of speech. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), <s>Śruti</s> passages of this type are included.
To this he says: 'No' —
[<s>Brahman</s> is] not inexpressible, because of [its being] an object of seeing (contemplation). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.5 |

children.text:
'sa etasmājjīvaghanātparātparaṃ puriśayaṃ puruṣamīkṣate'; (pra.5-5.)
'ātmanyevātmānaṃ paśyet'; (bṛ.6-4-23.)
'vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta'; (bṛ. 6-4-21.)
ityādivacanairīkṣaṇīyatvādvācyameva /
children.translated_text:
'From this living mass, He sees the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is higher than the highest, who dwells in the city [of the body].' (<s>Praśna Upaniṣad</s> 5.5)
'One should see the Self in the Self alone.' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4.23)
'Having known [Him], one should cultivate wisdom.' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4.21)
— Because of such statements declaring [<s>Brahman</s>] to be an object of contemplation, it is indeed expressible.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.5:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - neti // itiśabda āvartate / tathā ca atra sūtrakāraḥ iti pūrvapakṣyuktaṃ śrutitātparyāparijñānaprāptaṃ brahmaṇo 'vācyatvaṃ neti niṣedhatītyarthaḥ / sūtraṃ paṭhati - īkṣateriti / atra tadityanuvartate / tacca ādhyāyaparisamāpteḥ vidheyasamarpakamapīhoddeśyasamarpakam / na vidyate śabdo vācako yasya tadaśabdam / tathā ca 'tat'; brahma 'aśabdaṃ'; śabdāvācyaṃ na, kintu vācyameva / kutaḥ? īkṣateḥ / dhātunirdeśo 'yaṃ, tathaiva sudhokteḥ / tathāpi śabdamātrasyāsādhakatayā tena tadartho lakṣyate / tena prakṛtānukūlatayekṣaṇīyatvaṃ vivakṣyate / tathā ca 'īkṣateḥ'; īkṣaṇīyatvāt jñānaviṣayatvādityarthaḥ ityāśayena sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - sa iti / idaṃ ca ṣaṭpraśnavākyam / atra "yaḥ punaretaṃ trimātreṇaumityanenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ puruṣamabhidhyāyīta sa tejasi sūrye sampanno yathā pādodarastavacā vinirmucyate evaṃ ha vai sa pāpmanā vinirmuktaḥ sa sāmabhirunnīyate brahmalokam"iti pūrvavākye prakṛto yaḥ akārokāramakārākhyāṃśatrayayuktapraṇavoktaprakāreṇa paramātmānamabhidhyāya tamaparokṣīkṛtya ca tejorūpe sūrye sampannatvagvinirmuktasarpavadvidhūtapāpassāmābhimānidevaiḥ satyākhyaṃ brahmalokaṃ prāptaḥ praṇavopāsako jīvaḥ saḥ 'jīvaghanāt'; jīvasārāttacchreṣṭhāt 'etasmāt'; caturmukhāttadupadeśena 'parātparam'; uttamāduttamaṃ 'puriśayaṃ'
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.5: He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that represents the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>): 'na' (not). // The word 'iti' recurs. And thus: here the <s>sūtra</s>-author negates — [saying] 'not' — the inexpressibility of <s>Brahman</s> which was stated by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (opponent) and which arose from incomplete understanding of the purport of <s>Śruti</s>: this is the meaning. He reads the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>īkṣateḥ</s>' (because of seeing). Here the pronoun 'tat' (that) is continued [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>]. And that [pronoun], though capable of conveying the predicate up to the completion of the chapter, here conveys the subject. '<s>Aśabdam</s>' (without word) — that for which no designating word exists. And thus: 'that' <s>Brahman</s> is 'not <s>aśabdam</s>' — not inexpressible by words, but rather is expressible indeed. Why? Because of '<s>īkṣateḥ</s>' (seeing). This is a citation by verbal root, as stated in the <s>Sudhā</s>. Even so, since the mere word [form] is insufficient as proof, through it the meaning is indicated. By that, what is intended is its fitness to be investigated (<s>īkṣaṇīyatva</s>) in conformity with the subject under discussion. And thus: 'because of <s>īkṣateḥ</s>' — because of being fit to be investigated, because of being an object of knowledge: this is the meaning — with this intention he explains the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>sa</s>' (he). And this is the passage of the six questions. Here, in the preceding passage 'He who meditates on the Supreme Person through this very syllable <s>Oṃ</s> consisting of three <s>mātrās</s> — he, having attained [identity with] the radiant Sun, is freed from evil as a snake is freed from its skin; he is led upward by the <s>Sāma</s> [hymns] to <s>Brahmaloka</s>' — the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) who is the <s>Praṇava</s>-worshipper, who, having meditated on the Supreme Self in the manner expressed by the <s>Praṇava</s> consisting of the three parts called <s>a-kāra</s>, <s>u-kāra</s>, and <s>ma-kāra</s>, and having directly realized Him, attained the Sun in the form of radiance, freed from evil like a snake freed from its skin, and who, through the deities presiding over the <s>Sāman</s> hymns, reached <s>Brahmaloka</s> called <s>Satya</s> — that 'he,' 'from the mass of <s>jīvas</s>' (<s>jīvaghanāt</s>) — from the one who is the essence and the best of <s>jīvas</s>, 'from this' (<s>etasmāt</s>) — from the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>], through his instruction, 'the supreme beyond the supreme' (<s>parātparam</s>) — the highest beyond the highest, 'dwelling in the body' (<s>puriśayam</s>) —

children.text: sakaladehāntargataṃ 'puruṣaṃ'; pūrṇaṃ vāsudevaṃ paramātmānaṃ 'īkṣate'; jānātītyarthaḥ / yadyapi ṣaṭpraśnaṭīkāyāṃ "jīvaghanādviriñcāttadupāsanayeti yāvat, īkṣate punarabhivṛddhajñāno bhavati / īkṣitvāca taṃ prāpnoti"ityukterīkṣateraparokṣajñānārthatvaṃ pratīyate / tathāpi mūle jñānasāmānyaviṣayatvarūpekṣaṇīyatvahetorasiddhiparihārāya asyāḥ śruterupanyastatvāt "hiraṇyagarbhopadeśena"iti ṭīkokteśceha prakṛtānuguṇyādīkṣatiḥ parokṣajñānārtho vyākhyeyaḥ/ 'ātmani'; ityaparaṃ kāṇvavākyaṃ jijñāsānaye vyākṛtam / 'vijñāya'; ityanyadvājasaneyavākyam/ 'brāhmaṇo'; brahmaniṣṭho dhīraḥ 'taṃ'; paramātmānamevaṃ śāstreṇācāryādvā 'vijñāya'; parokṣato jñātvā 'prajñāṃ'; prakṛṣṭamapokṣajñānaṃ 'kurvīta'
children.translated_text: situated within all bodies, 'the <s>Puruṣa</s>' — the full one, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Supreme Self — 'perceives' (<s>īkṣate</s>) — knows: this is the meaning. Even though in the <s>Ṣaṭpraśna Ṭīkā</s> (commentary on the six questions) it is stated: 'from the mass of <s>jīvas</s>, from <s>Viriñca</s> [<s>Brahmā</s>], through his worship — this much is implied; <s>īkṣate</s> means one becomes one of augmented knowledge; and having perceived, one attains Him' — from which the meaning of <s>īkṣati</s> as direct (<s>aparokṣa</s>) knowledge is understood; nevertheless, since in the root [text] this <s>Śruti</s> is cited for the purpose of removing the objection of non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>) of the reason in the form of fitness-to-be-investigated as an object of knowledge in general, and since in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> it is said 'through the instruction of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>,' [and] since here, in conformity with the subject under discussion, <s>īkṣati</s> should be explained as meaning mediate (<s>parokṣa</s>) knowledge. '<s>Ātmani</s>' (in the Self) — this is another passage from the <s>Kāṇva</s> [recension], explained in the manner of [the analysis of] inquiry. '<s>Vijñāya</s>' (having known) — this is another passage from the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension]. 'The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — the wise one devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, 'having known Him' (<s>vijñāya</s>) — 'Him,' the Supreme Self, thus, through scripture or from a teacher, 'having known' — having known mediately, 'should cultivate direct knowledge' (<s>prajñāṃ kurvīta</s>) — should accomplish excellent direct knowledge:

children.text: sampādayedityarthaḥ / ityādīti / evamādivākyairityarthaḥ / ādiśabdena "ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ"(bṛ.u. 4-4-5.) "ajaātmā mahān dhruvaḥ"(bṛ.u. 6-4-20.) "tameva dhīro vijñāya"(bṛ.u. 6-4-21.) ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / īkṣaṇīyatvāt / avagamopalakṣakametat / anyathānanvayāt / anenāsiddhiḥ parihṛtā / tadanyathānupapatteriti śeṣaḥ / vācyameveti sautranañdvayalabdhārthoktiḥ / na tvavācyaṃ nāpi lakṣyamiti evaśabdārthaḥ / tadityanenāsyānvayaḥ / aniyamasūcanāya sūtrabhāṣyayoḥ pratijñāhetvorvyutkrameṇoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: this is the meaning. 'And so forth' (<s>ityādi</s>) — the meaning is: through such passages and the like. By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), [the passages] 'The Self indeed is to be seen' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.5), 'The unborn Self, great and eternal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4.20), 'The wise one, having known Him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4.21), and the like are included. 'Because of fitness to be investigated' (<s>īkṣaṇīyatvāt</s>) — this is an indication of comprehension in general. Otherwise there would be no syntactic connection. By this, the objection of non-establishment is resolved. 'The impossibility of it being otherwise' is the remainder. 'Is expressible indeed' — this is a statement of the meaning obtained from the two <s>sūtras</s> [together]. 'Not that it is inexpressible, nor that it is [merely] indicated' — this is the meaning of the word 'eva' (indeed). The pronoun 'tat' (that) connects with this. The inverted order of thesis and reason in the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s> is for the purpose of indicating non-restriction.
Because of being [known through] the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, there is no cognition [of <s>Brahman</s>] without verbal expression.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.6:
nanvastvīkṣaṇīyatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, tathāpi na tadanyathānupapattyā tasya vācyatvaṃ vācyaṃ pratyakṣādināpīkṣaṇīyatvopapatterityata āha - aupaniṣadatvāditi / tadityetadvipariṇamyānuvartate / tathā ca 'tasya'; brahmaṇaḥ 'aupaniṣadatvāt'; upaniṣadekasamadhigamyatvāt 'avacanena'; vacanetarapramāṇena 'īkṣaṇaṃ'; jñānaṃ netyarthaḥ / tathā ca śrutismṛtisāhāyyarahitapratyakṣādyavedyatvaviśiṣṭekṣaṇīyatvānyathānupapattyā brahmaṇo vācyatvaṃ siddhyatyeveti bhāvaḥ / pariśeṣapramāṇaparatayā vā idamāvṛttya vyākhyeyam / yojanā tu brahmaṇaśrutiṣūktaṃ īkṣaṇaṃ pramāṇenaiva hi bhavet / prasaktapramāṇeṣu ca 'nāvacanena'; vacanetarapramāṇenekṣaṇaṃ sambhavati aupaniṣadatvāt vacanenaiva bhavadīkṣaṇaṃ nāvacanena vacanavṛttyanyalakṣaṇādinā sambhavati / kutaḥ? 'avacanena'; bhāvapradhāno bahuvrīhiḥ / avacanatvenāvācyatvena nimittena ataḥ pariśeṣādīkṣaṇaṃ vācyatvameva sādhayatīti /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.6: [Objection:] Granted that <s>Brahman</s> is fit to be investigated; nevertheless, the expressibility of <s>Brahman</s> cannot be stated on the basis of the impossibility [of knowing it] otherwise, since fitness to be investigated is possible even through perception and the like — to this he says: 'because of being [known through] the <s>Upaniṣads</s>' (<s>aupaniṣadatvāt</s>). The pronoun 'tat' (that) continues here in modified form. And thus: 'of that' — of <s>Brahman</s>, 'because of being [known through] the <s>Upaniṣads</s>' — because of being comprehensible through the <s>Upaniṣads</s> alone, 'without verbal expression' (<s>avacanena</s>) — through a means of knowledge other than verbal expression, 'cognition' — knowledge — 'is not [possible]': this is the meaning. And thus: because of the impossibility of <s>Brahman</s> being otherwise [known] — [<s>Brahman</s>] being qualified by unknowability through perception and the like that are devoid of the assistance of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> — [<s>Brahman</s>'s] expressibility is indeed established: this is the purport. Or, this should be explained with a view to the method of elimination (<s>pariśeṣa</s>) as a means of proof. The construction is: the cognition of <s>Brahman</s> stated in the <s>Śrutis</s> must indeed be through a valid means of knowledge. And among the applicable means of knowledge, 'not through non-verbal [means]' — cognition through a means of knowledge other than verbal expression is not possible, because of being [known through] the <s>Upaniṣads</s>; the cognition of <s>Brahman</s> that exists is through verbal expression alone, not through non-verbal means — not through something other than verbal expression such as indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) and the like. Why? 'Without verbal expression' (<s>avacanena</s>) — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound with the abstract noun as primary. Through non-verbal-ness, through inexpressibility as the reason — therefore, by elimination, the cognition [of <s>Brahman</s>] establishes expressibility alone.

children.text:
'sarve vedā yatpadamāmanti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yadvadanti'; /
(kaṭha. 2-15.)
children.translated_text: 'All the <s>Vedas</s> proclaim that abode; all austerities speak of that.' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.15)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.7:
nanu śrutisiddhamavācyatvaṃ kathamīkṣaṇīyatvayuktimātreṇa dūṣyate? 'prābalyamāgamasyaiva'; iti yuktitaḥ śruteḥ prābalyokterityataḥ sautro heturāgamopalakṣaka iti bhāvena vācyatve śrutismṛtī cāha - sarva iti // kaṭhānāmiyaṃ śrutiḥ/ sarve vedā 'yatpadaṃ'; yasya brahmaṇaḥ svarūpam 'āmananti'; mukhyavṛttyā satātparyaṃ pratipādayanti / sarve vedāḥ sarvāṇi tapāṃsi prasiddhāni 'yat'; brahma prati 'vadanti'; yaduddeśena kartavyānīti bodhayantītyarthaḥ / tattvapradīparītyā 'tapāṃsi'; ālocanarūpā yuktaya iti vā / sarvairvedairahameva 'vedyo'; mukhyataḥ pratipādyaḥ / ahaṃ 'vedāntakṛt'; brahmasūtrakṛt 'vedavit'; vedārthajñānī ceti gītāsmṛtyarthaḥ / ādipadāt 'atha kasmāducyate'; 'nāmāni sarvāṇi'; 'vacasāṃ vācyamuttamam'; ityādessaṅgrahaḥ / tathā ca śrutau 'āmananti'; iti sākṣādvācyatvokteḥ, smṛtau ca 'ahameva'; ityavadhāraṇopapattaye mukhyatayā vedyatvasya vivakṣaṇīyatvāt tasya ca vācyatvaṃ vināyogātsarvaśabdalakṣaṇāyāścāsambhavādvācyatvamevābhyāṃ siddhyatīti bhāvaḥ / smṛtibhyaścetyasya vācyamevetyanenānvayaḥ / ādiśabdopāttaśrutismṛtyapekṣayā bahuvacanam / na kevalamīkṣaṇīyatvahetoriti cārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.7: [Objection:] How can the inexpressibility established through <s>Śruti</s> be refuted merely by the reasoning of fitness to be investigated? Since [the principle] 'scripture has greater strength' [means] that <s>Śruti</s> has greater strength than reasoning — therefore the <s>sūtra</s>-reason is indicative of scripture: with this purport, he cites <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> for expressibility: '<s>sarva</s>' (all). // This is a <s>Śruti</s> of the <s>Kaṭha</s> [school]. All the <s>Vedas</s> 'proclaim' — through primary signification, with purport — 'that abode' (<s>yatpadam</s>) — the essential nature of that <s>Brahman</s>. All the well-known austerities 'speak of' — 'that' (<s>yat</s>) — toward <s>Brahman</s>; they convey [the meaning] that they are to be performed for its sake: this is the meaning. Or, in the manner of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: '<s>tapāṃsi</s>' — reasonings in the form of investigation. 'By all the <s>Vedas</s>, I alone am to be known' (<s>vedyaḥ</s>) — to be taught in the primary sense. 'I am the maker of <s>Vedānta</s>' (<s>vedāntakṛt</s>) — the composer of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>; 'and the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>' (<s>vedavit</s>) — the one who knows the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>: this is the meaning of the <s>Gītā Smṛti</s>. By the word 'ādi,' the passages 'Then why is He called [<s>Brahman</s>],' 'all names,' 'the supreme object of speech,' and the like are included. And thus: since in the <s>Śruti</s>, through [the word] 'proclaim' (<s>āmananti</s>), expressibility is directly stated; and since in the <s>Smṛti</s>, through the emphatic particle [in] 'I alone' (<s>ahameva</s>), what is to be stated is the knowability in the primary sense — and since that [knowability] is impossible without expressibility, and since the indication characterized by the word 'all' is also impossible [without expressibility] — expressibility is established through both of these: this is the purport. The syntactic connection of '<s>smṛtibhyaśca</s>' (and from <s>Smṛtis</s>) is with 'expressible indeed.' The plural is with reference to the <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Smṛtis</s> included by the word 'ādi.' And the meaning is: not only because of the reason of fitness to be investigated.
'And by all the <s>Vedas</s>, I alone am to be known; I am the maker of <s>Vedānta</s> and the knower of the <s>Vedas</s> indeed.' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 15.15)
And from <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> passages such as these and the like.
But the inexpressibility and the like [are] because of incomprehensibility.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.8:
nanvevaṃ vācyatvasya yuktyādisiddhatve avācyatvājñeyatvābhidhāyakodāhṛtaśruteḥ 'yato vācaḥ'; ityādirūpāyāḥ kā gatirityata āha - avācyatvādikamiti / ajñeyatvamatarkyatvaṃ ca ādiśabdārthaḥ / tuśabdaḥ śaṅkāvyāvartakaḥ bhinnakrameṇāvadhāraṇe vā / tathā ca 'aprasiddhatvāt'; sākalyena agocaratvānnimittādeva brahmaṇi 'avācyatvādikam'; avācyatvādivyapadeśo yujyata iti na tadvirodha iti bhāvaḥ / anena siddhānte 'aśabdam'; ityāderaprasiddhatvātsākalyena vācakaśabdaśūnyamityādirthaḥ / 'avacanena'; ityasya tu sākalyena vacanamantareṇetyartha ityuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.8: [Objection:] If the expressibility [of <s>Brahman</s>] is thus established through reasoning and the like, what is the interpretation of the cited <s>Śruti</s> passages like 'from which speech [turns back]' that teach inexpressibility, unknowability, and the like? — to this he says: 'inexpressibility and the like.' Unknowability and un-reason-ability are the meaning of the word 'ādi' (and the like). The word 'tu' (but) is for removing the doubt, or for emphatic determination in reverse order. And thus: 'because of incomprehensibility' (<s>aprasiddhatvāt</s>) — because of not being an object [of knowledge] in its totality — for this very reason, the designation of 'inexpressibility and the like' — the attribution of inexpressibility and the like — to <s>Brahman</s> is justified, so there is no contradiction: this is the purport. By this, in the established conclusion, '<s>aśabdam</s>' (without word) and the like [are explained as] meaning 'devoid of a designating word in its totality' — because of incomprehensibility. And the meaning of '<s>avacanena</s>' (without verbal expression) is stated as 'without verbal expression in its totality.'

children.text: na tadīdṛgiti jñeyaṃ na vācyaṃ na ca tarkyate /
children.translated_text: That is not to be known as 'of such a kind'; it is not expressible, nor is it subject to reasoning.

children.text: paśyanto 'pi na paśyanti mero rūpaṃ vipaścitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even the wise, though seeing the form of <s>Meru</s>, do not [fully] see [it]. //
[It is] like this [analogy]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.9:
nanvaprasiddhinimittako 'vācyatvādivyapadeśaḥ kva dṛṣṭa ityata āha - na taditi / yasmāt 'vipaścito'; jñānino mero rūpaṃ paśyanto 'pi 'īdṛgiti'; sākalyena 'na paśyanti'; na jānanti / anenāprasiddhatvahetuḥ sūcitaḥ / tasmānmero rūpaṃ na jñeyaṃ pratyakṣeṇa / na vācyaṃ śabdena / 'na tarkyate'; nānumīyate ca liṅgenetyucyata ityarthaḥ / itivaditi / iti vākya ivetyarthaḥ / asyāvācyatvādikamiti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / tathā ca yathā merurūpe aprasiddhinimittakāvācyatvādivyapadeśastathā brahmaṇyapīti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.9: [Objection:] Where is it seen that the attribution of inexpressibility and the like has incomprehensibility as its reason? — to this he says: 'na tat' (not that). Since 'the wise' — the knowers — 'though seeing' the 'form of <s>Meru</s>,' 'as such a kind' — in totality — 'do not see,' do not know [it completely]. By this, the reason of incomprehensibility is indicated. Therefore the form of <s>Meru</s> is 'not to be known' by perception; 'not expressible' by words; 'and not subject to reasoning' (<s>na tarkyate</s>) — not inferable through inferential marks: thus it is said — this is the meaning. '<s>Itivat</s>' — means: like in this passage. The syntactic connection of this is with the previous [statement] 'inexpressibility and the like.' And thus: just as in the case of the form of <s>Meru</s>, the attribution of inexpressibility and the like has incomprehensibility as its reason, so too in the case of <s>Brahman</s>: this is the purport.
Because of incomprehensibility, that is inexpressible; [yet it is] expressible because of being stated in all scriptures.
It is beyond reasoning [yet] subject to reasoning; unknowable [yet] knowable — thus the Supreme is declared. //
Thus in the <s>Gāruḍa</s> [Purāṇa]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.10:
na kevalaṃ 'paśyantaḥ'; ityuktyanyathānupapattimātreṇaiva aprasiddherajñeyatvātarkyatvāvācyatvavyapadeśa iti vyavasthā siddhā, api tu smṛtisiddhā ceti bhāvenāha - aprasiddheriti / tadbrahma yataḥ 'paraṃ'; pūrṇam atassākalyenāprasiddhatvādavācyamucyate / sarvasadāgamoktatvāttatprasiddhatvādvācyaṃ ca bhavatītyarthaḥ / evamaprasiddhiprasiddhibhyāṃ tat atarkyam anumeyaṃ ca ajñeyaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānipratyakṣagamyaṃ ca 'smṛtaṃ'; smṛtikārairuktamityarthaḥ / gāruḍe ityanantaraṃ uktamiti śeṣaḥ / asyāpyavācyatvādikamityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.10: Not only is the determination — that the attribution of unknowability, un-reason-ability, and inexpressibility has incomprehensibility as its reason — established merely through the impossibility of an alternative explanation by the statement 'those who see' and the like, but it is also established through <s>Smṛti</s>: with this purport he says: 'because of incomprehensibility.' That <s>Brahman</s>, since it is 'supreme' (<s>param</s>) — complete — and therefore incomprehensible in its totality, is said to be inexpressible. Because of being stated in all valid scriptures — because of being known through them — it is also expressible: this is the meaning. Thus, because of incomprehensibility and comprehensibility respectively, it is 'beyond reasoning' and 'subject to reasoning' (inferable), and 'unknowable' and 'knowable' — knowable through the direct perception of the wise — 'is declared' (<s>smṛtam</s>) — is stated by the authors of <s>Smṛti</s>: this is the meaning. After 'in the <s>Gāruḍa</s> [Purāṇa],' 'it is stated' is to be supplied. The syntactic connection of this too is with 'inexpressibility and the like.'
And the word-less-ness [of <s>Brahman</s>] is not established by the other [i.e., <s>Sāṅkhya</s>]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.11:
evaṃ 'yato vācaḥ'; ityādiśrutīnāṃ yuktyādibalādarthāntaropapatterna tadbalācchabdāvācyaṃ brahmeti sūtraṃ vyākhyāyāpavyākhyāṃ pratyākhyāti - na ceti / caśabdaḥ svasiddhamapi netisamuccaye / tathā ca jagatkāraṇaṃ 'aśabdaṃ'; pradhānaṃ na, kutaḥ? aśabdaṃ hi tat / 'aśabdaṃ'; pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ neti vā, kutaḥ? 'īkṣateḥ'; 'tadaikṣata'; iti jagatkāraṇasyekṣaṇakartṛtvaśravaṇātpradhānasya cācetanatvena tadasambhavāditi sāṅkhyamatanirākaraṇaparatayā vyākhyāne prathamapratijñāyāṃ hetūkṛtam 'aśabdatvam'; aśrautatvam
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.11: Having thus explained the <s>sūtra</s> [to mean that] <s>Brahman</s> is not inexpressible by words, through the force of reasoning and the like — since the <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'from which speech [turns back]' are given an alternative interpretation — he refutes the wrong interpretation: 'na ca' (and not). The word 'ca' is for aggregation, [meaning] 'not even what is self-established.' And thus: the 'word-less' (<s>aśabdam</s>) — the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) — is not the cause of the world. Why? Because it is indeed word-less. Or: 'the word-less <s>Pradhāna</s> is not the cause.' Why? 'Because of <s>īkṣateḥ</s>' (seeing) — because in [the <s>Śruti</s> passage] '<s>tadaikṣata</s>' (it saw/willed), the cause of the world is heard as the agent of seeing/willing, and because that is impossible for <s>Pradhāna</s> due to its being insentient — thus, when explained as refuting the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> doctrine, the 'word-less-ness' (<s>aśabdatvam</s>) — the non-Vedic character — adduced as the reason in the first thesis,

children.text: 'itarasiddhaṃ'; svetarasāṅkhyasiddhaṃ na, na kevalametāvat, kintu svasiddhamapi na, sāṅkhyena vaidikatvābhyupagateḥ / sūtrakāreṇa 'ajāmekām'; (tai. ā. 10-10-1.) ityādi śrutyuktatvāṅgīkārāt /
children.translated_text: is 'not established by the other' (<s>itarasiddham</s>) — not established by <s>Sāṅkhya</s> as distinct [from the <s>Veda</s>]. Not only this much, but it is not even self-established, since <s>Sāṅkhya</s> itself claims to be Vedic. Because the <s>sūtra</s>-author acknowledges the Vedic character [of the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> terms] from <s>Śruti</s> passages like '<s>ajām ekām</s>' (the one unborn) (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 10.10.1) and the like.

children.text: yadvā - tattvapradīparītyā māyinā sāṅkhyaṃ prati hetutvenopanyastamaśabdatvaṃ māyītarasya sāṅkhyasya na siddhaṃ nāpi sāṅkhyetaramāyisiddhamuktahetubhyāmeva / tathā cāsiddhiriti na tadvyākhyānaṃ yuktamitibhāvaḥ / evamaśabdatvaṃ śrautatvaṃ brahmaṇassāṅkhyetaramāyisiddhaṃ na, tanmate avācyatvāt / cakārādīkṣitṛtvamapi siddhaṃ na, tasyekṣatisvarūpatvādityapi vyākhyeyam / tathā ca hetudvayamapi svapakṣapratikūlamiti na paravyākhyā yukteti bhāvaḥ tattvapradīpe tu 'naca'; ityādibhāṣyaṃ 'itarasiddhaṃ'; māyisiddhamaśabdatvaṃ na śrutyarthaḥ uktanyāyena brahmaṇo vācyatvāt / evam 'aśabdatvam'; avācyatvaṃ brahmaṇa itarasya māyino 'pi na siddham / brahmaṇi vyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgāt iti dvedhā vyākhyāyaparakṛtavyākhyāpratyākhyānāya paroktahetoṣṭīkārītyāsiddhyuktiparatayāpi vyākhyātam // 5 //
children.translated_text: Or — following the method of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: the property of being undenoted-by-scripture (<s>aśabdatva</s>), presented as a reason against <s>Sāṅkhya</s> by the <s>Māyāvādin</s>, is not established for <s>Sāṅkhya</s> which is different from the <s>Māyāvādin</s>; nor is the [<s>aśabdatva</s>] established by the <s>Māyāvādin</s> established for <s>Sāṅkhya</s> which is other [than him], precisely by the stated reasons. And thus there is non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>) — therefore that interpretation is not proper: this is the import. Likewise, the being-undenoted-by-scripture (<s>aśabdatva</s>) — i.e., the being-scripturally-based (<s>śrautatva</s>) — of <s>Brahman</s> is not established by the <s>Māyāvādin</s> who is other than the <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, because in that [Māyāvāda] view, [Brahman] is inexpressible (<s>avācya</s>). And by the word 'ca,' the being-a-seer (<s>īkṣitṛtva</s>) is also not established [for Sāṅkhya], because in that view [seeing] is of the nature of <s>īkṣati</s> (seeing) itself — this too should be explained. And thus, both reasons are adverse to one's own position — therefore the opponent's interpretation is not proper: this is the import. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [passage] 'na ca' and so on is explained in two ways — 'itarasiddham': the being-undenoted-by-scripture (<s>aśabdatva</s>) established by the <s>Māyāvādin</s> is not the meaning of <s>Śruti</s>, because by the stated reasoning, <s>Brahman</s> is expressible (<s>vācya</s>). Likewise, 'aśabdatvam' — inexpressibility (<s>avācyatva</s>) — is not established for the <s>Māyāvādin</s> either, who is other than [Brahman], because of the unwanted consequence that there would be no transactional usage at all regarding <s>Brahman</s> — and [the Tattvapradīpa] also explains it with the intent of refuting the opponent's interpretation through the statement of non-establishment of the opponent's stated reasons, following the method of the <s>Ṭīkā</s> author. // 5 //
If [it be said that the Self is] secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>), [we say] no, because of the word '<s>ātman</s>' (Self). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.6 |
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 12:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.12:
īkṣaṇīyatvasya hetorvyadhikaraṇāsiddhimākṣipya samādhātuṃ sūtram - 'oṃ gauṇaścennātmaśabdāt'; iti / asyārthaḥ - 'yataḥ ātmanyevātmānaṃ paśyet'; ityādiśrutyukta ātmā 'gauṇaḥ'; sattvādiguṇabaddho jīva evātastadanyathānupapattyā vācyo 'pi sa eva syānna nirguṇaḥ paramātmeti cet - na, kutaḥ? 'ātmānaṃ paśyet'; itīkṣaṇīye tasminnātmaśabdaśravaṇāditi / 'ātmapatasāmānādhikaraṇyāya pulliṅganirdeśaḥ'; //
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 12:
Raising the objection of non-establishment-in-a-different-locus (<s>vyadhikaraṇāsiddhi</s>) against the reason of being-worthy-of-seeing (<s>īkṣaṇīyatva</s>), and intending to resolve it, [he presents] the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Oṃ, if [it be said that the Self is] secondary, [we say] no, because of the word ātman.' Its meaning is: the Self (<s>ātmā</s>) stated in <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'because one should see the Self in the Self alone' — if [the objection be that this] is 'secondary' (<s>gauṇa</s>), that is, the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) bound by the qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) of <s>sattva</s> and the like, and therefore, by the principle of impossibility-otherwise (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>), the one to be denoted and spoken of is that [jīva] alone and not the quality-transcending (<s>nirguṇa</s>) <s>Paramātman</s> — [the answer is] no. Why? Because the word '<s>ātman</s>' is heard in the passage 'one should see the Self' — that is, in the entity worthy of seeing (<s>īkṣaṇīya</s>). 'The masculine gender is used for co-referentiality with the word ātma-pada.'

children.text:
na ca gauṇa ātmā dṛśyo vācyaśca na nirguṇa iti yuktam /
ātmaśabdāt /
children.translated_text:
And it is not proper [to say] that the secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) Self is the one to be seen and denoted, and not the quality-transcending (<s>nirguṇa</s>) one.
Because of the word '<s>ātman</s>'.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 13:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.13:
sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - na ceti / atra yato 'dṛśyaḥ'; īkṣatiśrutau dṛśyatayoktaḥ 'ātmā'; jīvākhyo gauṇa eva atastadanyathānupapattyā vācyo 'pi sa eva syāt 'na nirguṇaḥ'; guṇātīto viṣṇuḥ 'dṛśyaḥ'; īkṣatiśruttyuktaḥ / gauṇagrahaṇe bādhakasyetarajñāpakasya cābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / ato na sa vācyaḥ iti codyaṃ na yuktam / kutaḥ? 'ātmaśabdāt'; 'ātmanyeva'; iti vākye īkṣaṇīye tasmin ātmaśabdaśravaṇāddṛśyo nirguṇa eva, ata evekṣatyā liṅgena vācyo 'pi sa eva bhavediti yojanā / yadyapi sudhāyāṃ gauṇapadaṃ māyāśabalitaiśvaryādidharmayuktasaguṇabrahmaparatayā vyākhyātaṃ tathāpi pūrvapakṣiṇo māyāśabalitaṃ vā guṇabaddhā jīvā vā dṛśyā vācyāśca, na sarvathā nirguṇaṃ brahmetyāśayānna virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 13:
He explains the <s>sūtra</s>: 'na ca' (and not). Here, since the 'Self' — designated as <s>jīva</s> — which 'is to be seen' — stated as to-be-seen in the <s>īkṣati</s> (seeing) <s>Śruti</s> — is 'secondary' (<s>gauṇa</s>), therefore by the principle of impossibility-otherwise, the one to be denoted is that [jīva] alone and 'not the quality-transcending' (<s>nirguṇa</s>) <s>Viṣṇu</s> who 'is to be seen' — stated in the <s>īkṣati Śruti</s> — [when the secondary usage] is accepted, there is no invalidating [reason] or indicator-of-another-meaning: this is the import. Therefore the objection 'He is not the one to be denoted' is not proper. Why? 'Because of the word ātman' — because the word '<s>ātman</s>' is heard in the passage 'in the Self alone' in that [entity] which is worthy of seeing — the one to be seen is the quality-transcending (<s>nirguṇa</s>) one alone, and therefore by the principle of impossibility-otherwise, the one to be denoted is that [nirguṇa Self] alone: this is the construction. Although in the <s>Sudhā</s> the word 'gauṇa' is explained as referring to <s>saguṇa Brahman</s> — qualified <s>Brahman</s> endowed with attributes like <s>māyā</s>-tainted sovereignty — nevertheless, since the prima facie opponent's intent is that the ones to be seen and denoted are either [Brahman] tainted by <s>māyā</s> or <s>jīvas</s> bound by <s>guṇas</s>, and not the absolutely quality-transcending <s>Brahman</s>, there is no contradiction.
He who is devoid of all qualities (<s>guṇas</s>), and who is free from all faults,
who is beyond what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted — He is called the Self (<s>ātman</s>).
He whose nature is other than this is declared by the wise to be the non-Self (<s>anātman</s>).
But the word '<s>ātman</s>' (Self) is applied to the non-Self only figuratively (<s>sopacāra</s>). //
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 14:
Thus in the <s>Vāmana</s> [Purāṇa]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.14:
nanvātmaśabdasadbhāve kuto 'yaṃ nirguṇo na gauṇa ityata āha - ya iti / yaḥ 'sarvataḥ'; prakāreṇa 'guṇaiḥ'; sattvādibhiḥ śūnyaḥ yaśca dukhakhādidoṣarahitaḥ yaśca heyopādeyarahitaḥ / bhāvapradhāno 'yam / heyatvasahitopādeyatvarahita iti / upādeya evetyarthaḥ / tattvapradīparītyā svābhāvikadoṣarahito guṇapūrṇatvenāptakāmatvādupādeyarahita iti vā / tattvodyotaṭīkārītyā doṣābhāvāddhāturabhāvādvā heyatvarahitaḥ, laukikaguṇābhāvādupādāturanyasya svatantrasyābhāvādvā upādeyatvarahitaḥ aniṣṭābhāvāddheyaṃ nāsti, apūrtyabhāvādupādeyamasya nāstīti vā tathoktaḥ / ya evaṃ bhūtassa ātmetyabhidhīyate / ya etadviruddhasvabhāvavān so 'nātmeti satāṃ mataṃ sammatamitythaḥ / kvacit 'hṛdi hyeṣa ātmā'
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 14:
But if the word '<s>ātman</s>' is present [in scripture], why is this [Self] quality-transcending and not secondary? To this he says: 'yaḥ' (He who). He who is 'in every respect' devoid of '<s>guṇas</s>' (qualities) — such as <s>sattva</s> and the like — and who is free from faults such as suffering and the like, and who is beyond what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted — this is a <s>bhāvapradhāna</s> (meaning-predominant) [compound]: devoid of acceptability accompanied by rejectability; i.e., He is to be accepted alone: this is the meaning. Or, following the method of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: free from inherent faults, and because of being full of qualities and thus having all desires fulfilled, He is beyond what is to be accepted. Or, following the method of the <s>Tattvodyota Ṭīkā</s>: because of the absence of faults or because of the absence of a cause for them, He is beyond what is to be rejected; because of the absence of worldly qualities or because of the absence of another independent [entity] to acquire [from], He is beyond what is to be accepted; because of the absence of anything undesirable, there is nothing to be rejected for Him; because of the absence of incompleteness, there is nothing to be accepted by Him — thus He is called so. He who is of such nature — He 'is called the Self.' He whose nature is contrary to this — he is 'the non-Self': this is the accepted view (<s>mata</s>), the consensus, of the wise: this is the meaning. In some places, [where we find] 'for this Self is in the heart' —

children.text:
ityādāvetadanyasvabhāve 'pyātmapadaprayogāt
kathaṃ so 'nātmetyata āha - anātmanīti / 'anātmani'; ātmaśabdamukhyārthabhinne jīve 'ātmaśabdaḥ'; 'sopacāraḥ'; upacāraḥ paramamukhyavṛttyanyamukhyavṛttiḥ tatsahitastadvṛttika ityarthaḥ/ tuśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / 'vāmane'; ityanantaraṃ 'nirguṇaikaniṣṭhatvenoktāt'; iti śeṣaḥ / asya nāyaṃ dṛśyo
children.translated_text: and similar [passages], even though the word '<s>ātman</s>' is applied to that which has a nature other than [the true Self], how can he be 'non-Self'? To this he says: 'anātmani' (in the non-Self). 'In the non-Self' — in the <s>jīva</s> who is different from the primary meaning of the word '<s>ātman</s>' — 'the word ātman' is 'sopacāra' (figurative) — <s>upacāra</s> (figurative usage) is a secondary primary usage other than the absolute primary usage; that which is accompanied by such usage, that which functions in that manner: this is the meaning. The word 'tu' is for specification. After 'in the <s>Vāmana</s> [Purāṇa],' 'because it is stated as pertaining exclusively to the quality-transcending (<s>nirguṇa</s>) one' is the remainder. The syntactic connection of this is with 'this one [who is] to be seen',
'and to be denoted, is not secondary, but rather is the quality-transcending one alone.'

children.text:
'dve vāva brahmaṇo rūpe ātmā caivānātmā ca /
tatra yaḥ sa ātmā sa nityaḥ śuddhaḥ kevalo nirguṇaśca /
atha ha yo 'nīdṛśaḥ so 'nātmā'; iti talavakārabrāhmaṇam /
children.translated_text:
'There are indeed two forms of <s>Brahman</s>: the Self (<s>ātman</s>) and the non-Self (<s>anātman</s>).
Of these, He who is the Self — He is eternal, pure, absolute, and quality-transcending.
But he who is not of this nature — he is the non-Self.' — Thus in the <s>Talavakāra Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 15:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.15:
atraiva pramāṇāntaramāha - dve vāveti / 'brahmaṇaḥ'; parabrahmaṇaḥ rūpaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca rūpe / tatrādyo rūpaśabdaḥ svarūpaparaḥ dvitīyo rūpyate jñāyate brahmākhyamiti vyutpattyā pratimāparaḥ / vāveti nipātasamudāyaḥ prasiddhidyotakaḥ / te rūpe darśayati - ātmeti / ātmaśabdamukhyavācyastadavācyaścetyarthaḥ / 'tatra'; ātmanātnormadhye 'sa yaḥ'; ityanvayaḥ / anyathā paunaruktyāt / tathā ca 'saḥ'; prasiddho 'yaḥ'; ātmā ātmaśabdamukhyārtho viṣṇuḥ 'saḥ nityaḥ'; dehahānyādirahitaḥ 'śuddhaḥ'; karmalepavidhuraḥ 'kevalaḥ'; jaḍāmiśraḥ 'nirguṇaḥ'; sattvādiguṇābaddha ityarthaḥ / co viśeṣaṇasamuccaye / evaṃ prathamoddiṣṭātmaśabdārthaṃ lakṣaṇamukhena pradarśya athānātmānamuktalakṣaṇavyatirekamukhena darśayati - atheti / yasmādātmā evaṃ bhūtaḥ 'atha'; tasmāt 'yo 'nīdṛśaḥ'; nityatvādirahitaḥ ha prasiddhaḥ / 'so 'nātmeti'; satāṃ sammatamityarthaḥ / 'brāhmaṇam'; ityanantaraṃ yato nirguṇasya viṣṇorevātmatvaṃ vaktīti śeṣaḥ / asyāpi 'vāmane'; itivadanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 15:
On this very point, he cites another authority: 'dve vāva' (there are indeed two). 'Of <s>Brahman</s>' — of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>: a form and a form — [these are the] two forms. Of these, the first word 'rūpa' (form) means 'own-form' (essential nature); the second, by the derivation 'that which is known as Brahman-like,' means 'reflection' (image). The particle-cluster 'vāva' indicates that this is well-known. He shows those two forms: 'ātmā' (Self). The meaning is: that which is the primary denotation of the word '<s>ātman</s>,' and that which is not its denotation. 'Of these' — between the Self and the non-Self, 'he who is' — this is the syntactic connection. Otherwise there would be redundancy. And thus: 'He' — the well-known one, 'who' is the Self — the primary meaning of the word '<s>ātman</s>,' <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'He is eternal' — free from the destruction of the body and the like, 'pure' — free from the stain of <s>karma</s>, 'absolute' (<s>kevala</s>) — unmixed with insentient matter, 'and quality-transcending' (<s>nirguṇa</s>) — not bound by the qualities of <s>sattva</s> and the like: this is the meaning. The word 'ca' is for aggregation of qualifiers. Having thus shown the meaning of the word '<s>ātman</s>' mentioned first, through the mode of definition, he then shows the non-Self through the mode of exclusion from the stated definition: 'atha' (now). Since the Self is of such nature, 'atha' — therefore, 'he who is not of this nature' — who is devoid of eternity and the like — he is well-known as 'the non-Self': this is the accepted view of the wise: this is the meaning. After '<s>brāhmaṇam</s>' (in the Brāhmaṇa [text]), 'since it declares that selfhood belongs exclusively to the quality-transcending <s>Viṣṇu</s>' is the remainder. The syntactic connection of this too is like that of 'in the <s>Vāmana</s> [Purāṇa].'
And it is not proper to take the non-primary meaning when the primary meaning is viable.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 16:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.16:
nanūpacāreṇāpyātmaśabdasya gauṇe prayogasadbhāvātsa eva śrutyukto dṛśya ātmā kiṃ na syādityata āha - na ceti / 'mukhye'; ātmapadamukhyārthe nirguṇe dṛśyatayekṣatiśrutipratipādye sambhavati sati amukhyārthagauṇagrahaṇaṃ na yujyata ityarthaḥ / atra satītyanena mukhyasambhavākhyo heturuktaḥ / amukhyaṃ na yujyata ityanena sādhyam / ubhayasamuccaye śaṅkāparihārasamuccaye vā caśabdaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 16:
But since the word '<s>ātman</s>' is used figuratively (<s>upacāra</s>) for the secondary meaning too, why should not that very secondary Self stated in <s>Śruti</s> be the one to be seen? To this he says: 'na ca' (and not). When the primary meaning of the word '<s>ātman</s>' — the quality-transcending one — is viable as being stated as the object of seeing in the <s>īkṣati Śruti</s>, the taking of the non-primary, secondary meaning is not proper: this is the meaning. Here, by the word 'sati' (when viable), the reason called 'viability of the primary meaning' (<s>mukhyasambhava</s>) is stated. 'The non-primary is not proper' — this is the thesis (<s>sādhya</s>). The word 'ca' is for aggregating both [the objection and its refutation], or for aggregating the resolution of the doubt. // 6 //
Because liberation is taught for one who is devoted to That. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.7 |
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 17:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.17:
nanu ātmaśabdo mukhyata eva gauṇātmaparaḥ kiṃ na syāt / na coktaśrutismṛtivirodhaḥ, tatrātmaśabdo nirguṇe viṣṇau mukhyo jīveṣvamukhya ityanukteḥ ātmanātmaśabdayoścetanācetanaviṣayatvasambhavāt / kiñca - ātmānātmaśabdayoḥ prasiddhacetanācetanaparatveśruterārjavaṃ, prasiddhārthāparityāgāt, rūpaśabdasyānekārthākalpanācca / na ca jīve nirdeṣatvādyayogaḥ, duḥkhādidoṣasyaupādhikatvena jīvasyāpi svabhāvato nirdeṣatayā śruteḥ svabhāvaviṣayatvopapatterityāśaṅkāṃ parihartuṃ sūtraṃ paṭhati - oṃ tanniṣṭhasya iti// neti vartate / tathā ca - 'tanniṣṭhasya'; asya ātmajñāninaḥ 'mokṣopadeśāt'; nātmaśabdamukhyavācyo gauṇa iti sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 17:
But could the word '<s>ātman</s>' not be primarily itself referring to the secondary (bound) Self? There is no contradiction with the stated <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>, since it has not been said therein that the word '<s>ātman</s>' is primary for the quality-transcending <s>Viṣṇu</s> and non-primary for <s>jīvas</s>; because it is possible that the word '<s>ātman</s>' and the word '<s>ātmaśabda</s>' pertain to both sentient and insentient [entities]. Moreover — since the word '<s>ātman</s>' and the word '<s>anātman</s>' are well-known as pertaining to sentient and insentient respectively, the <s>Śruti</s> would be straightforward, because the well-known meaning is not abandoned; and because no multiple meanings need be imputed for the word 'rūpa' (form). Nor is it the case that designation and the like are impossible for the <s>jīva</s>, since the <s>Śruti</s> can pertain to the essential nature, because even the <s>jīva</s> is inherently devoid of [faults], suffering and other faults being adventitious — anticipating this objection, he reads the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Oṃ, tanniṣṭhasya' (because liberation is taught for one who is devoted to That). 'Na' (not) is carried forward [from the previous sūtra]. And thus — 'for one who is devoted to That' — for this knower of the Self — 'because of the teaching of liberation' — the primary denotation of the word '<s>ātman</s>' is not the secondary (bound) [self]: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
For liberation does not [belong to] one who is devoted to the secondary Self.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 18:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.18:
tanniṣṭhasya mokṣopadeśe 'pi kuto 'yamātmā na gauṇa ityaprayojakatvamāśaṅkhyāha - na hīti /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 18:
Even when liberation is taught for one devoted to That, why is this Self not secondary? — anticipating the [objection of] irrelevance, he says: 'na hi' (for not). The word 'hi,' occurring in collocation with the words 'secondary,' 'mokṣa' (liberation), and '<s>pada</s>' (word), indicates the reason called 'contradiction' (<s>virodha</s>). And thus — 'hi' — because 'liberation' — in the form of the cessation of the bondage of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) — 'does not' — is not possible — 'for one devoted to the secondary Self,' for a knower of the <s>jīva</s> bound by <s>guṇas</s>, from that knowledge, due to contradiction — 'therefore,' 'na hi' — the objection of irrelevance should not be raised: this is the meaning.

children.text: gauṇamokṣapadasamabhivyāhṛto hiśabdo virodhākhyahetusūcakaḥ / tathā ca - 'hi'; yasmāt 'gauṇātmaniṣṭhasya'; guṇabaddhajīvajñāninaḥ tajjñānādguṇabandhanivṛttirūpo 'mokṣo'; na sambhavati, virodhāt tasmāt 'na hi'; nāprayojakatā śaṅkyetyarthaḥ /
