children.translated_text: The word 'hi,' occurring in collocation with the words '<s>gauṇa</s>' (secondary), '<s>mokṣa</s>' (liberation), and '<s>pada</s>' (word), indicates the reason called 'contradiction.' And thus — 'hi' — because 'for one devoted to the secondary Self' — for a knower of the <s>jīva</s> bound by <s>guṇas</s> — 'liberation' — in the form of the removal of bondage to <s>guṇas</s> — 'is not' possible, due to contradiction — therefore 'na hi' — the objection of irrelevance should not be raised: this is the meaning.

children.text:
yasyānuvittaḥ pratibuddha ātmā asmin sandohe gahane praviṣṭaḥ /
sa viśvakṛtsa hi sarvasya kartā tasya lokaḥ sa u loka eva
(bṛ.u. 6-4-13.)
ityātmaniṣṭhasya mokṣa upadiśyate /
children.translated_text:
'He by whom the Self — awakened, which has entered this uncertain, deep body — is known,
He is the maker of all, for He indeed is the maker of everything; His is the world, and He alone is the world.'
(<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4.13)
— Thus liberation is taught for one who is devoted to the Self.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 19:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.19:
asiddhiśaṅkāṃ parihartuṃ ko 'sāvātmaniṣṭhasya mokṣopadeśa ityatastaṃ darśayati - yasyeti / atra śrutiḥ svaprayuktamuśabdam eveti vyācaṣṭe / 'u'; ekaḥ pradhāna iti vā / tacchabdo viṣṇutajjñāniparaḥ / tathā ca - 'hi'; yasmāt 'saḥ'; viṣṇuḥ 'sarvasya kartā'; tasmādeva 'viśvakṛt'; vāyukartā 'pratibuddhaḥ'; svatassarvajñaḥ 'asmin sandohe'; sanduhyate puruṣārtho aneneti vā kāryakāraṇasaṅkhātarūpatvādvā bhūtasamudāyarūpatvādvā sandohanāmake madhyadehe sthite 'gahane'; gambhīre hṛdayaguhāsthāne 'praviṣṭaḥ'; saḥ 'ātmā'; viṣṇuḥ 'yasya'; yenopāsakena 'anuvittaḥ'; samayagjñātaḥ 'tasya'; adhikāriṇaḥ 'u'; pradhānaḥ tasya viṣṇoryo 'lokaḥ'; sa eva lokaḥ sthānaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ / 'sandoghe'; iti pāṭhe 'pyayayamevārthaḥ 'sandehe'; iti pāṭhe anekārthasaṅkaṭa ityarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - sa viśvakṛt kṛtakṛtyaḥ / kutaḥ? yataḥ sa hi paramātmā prasannaḥ sarvaśaktiḥ sarvamasya jñāninaḥ kāryaṃ karotītyuktam / asmin pakṣe prathamaḥ prathamāntatacchabdo viṣṇujñāniparaḥ, viśvaśabdaḥ kṛtyaparaḥ, sarvaśabdo jñānikāryaparaḥ / ṭīkākṛtpakṣe tu - prathamaḥ prakṛtaviṣṇuparaḥ, viśvaśabdo vāyuparaḥ, sarvaśabdo jagatpara iti bhedaḥ / pakṣadvaye 'pi dvitīyatṛtīyau viṣṇutallokapara/ 'iti'; ityevaṃrūpe bṛhadāraṇyake 'ātmaniṣṭhasya'; tajjñānino 'mokṣa upadiśyate'; / asya yata ityupadiśyate ato 'na gauṇa ātmā'; iti vakṣyamāṇapratijñayānvayaḥ / sūtrasya tu na gauṇa ātmaśabda iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / ātmetyanena sautratacchabdo nātmaśabdaparaḥ, kintvarthataḥ pradhānātmapara ityuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.5, verse 19:
To resolve the objection of non-establishment — 'What is this teaching of liberation for one devoted to the Self?' — he shows it: 'yasya' (he by whom). Here, the <s>Śruti</s> uses its own deployed particle 'u.' 'U' means 'the one' or 'the principal.' The word 'tat' (that) refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and to the knower of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. And thus — 'hi' — because 'He' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is 'the maker of everything,' therefore He is indeed the 'maker of all' (<s>viśvakṛt</s>) — the maker of <s>Vāyu</s>. 'Awakened' (<s>pratibuddha</s>) — inherently omniscient. 'In this body' (<s>sandoha</s>) — that by which human goals are milked, or because of its nature as a collection of cause and effect, or because of its nature as an aggregate of elements — in the body called <s>sandoha</s>, situated in the middle body; 'in the deep' (<s>gahana</s>) — in the deep place of the cave of the heart — 'entered'; that 'Self' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'by whom' — by whichever worshipper — 'is known' (<s>anuvittaḥ</s>) — is properly known; 'of that one' — of that qualified person — 'u' — principally — that world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> becomes his world, his abode: this is the meaning. In the reading '<s>sandogha</s>' too, the meaning is the same. In the reading '<s>sandeha</s>' (doubt), the meaning is: [the body which is] a narrow-passage of multiple meanings. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: 'He is the maker of all (<s>viśvakṛt</s>) — one whose purposes are all fulfilled. Why? Because He, the <s>Paramātman</s>, being gracious, all-powerful, does everything — all that is to be done — for this knower': this is what is said. In this interpretation, the first nominative 'tat' refers to the knower of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the word 'viśva' means 'all duties'; the word 'sarva' means 'all that is to be done for the knower.' In the <s>Ṭīkā</s>-author's interpretation, however, the first [tat] refers to the <s>Viṣṇu</s> under discussion; the word 'viśva' refers to <s>Vāyu</s>; the word 'sarva' refers to the world — this is the difference. In both interpretations, the second and third [uses of tat] refer to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and His world. 'Iti' — in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> of this nature, 'liberation is taught for one devoted to the Self' — for the knower of That. Since it is taught thus, therefore 'the Self is not secondary' — this is the syntactic connection with the thesis to be stated. But the syntactic connection of the <s>sūtra</s> is with the preceding through 'the word ātman is not secondary.' Through the word 'ātman' [in this passage], it is stated that the word 'tat' (that) in the <s>sūtra</s> is not referring to the word '<s>ātman</s>,' but rather in meaning it refers to the principal Self.
'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>.' (<s>Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad</s> 1.2; <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.19)
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.5, verse 20:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.20:
ātmaśabdo viṣṇāveva mukhyaḥ na jīveṣvityatra na kevalaṃ tanniṣṭhasyetyādinoktamanumānaṃ mānam, kintu sūtrakṛdabhipretāḥ spaṣṭaśrutismṛtayaśceti bhāvena tāṃ tāścāha - ayamiti / brahmetyantasya upadiśyata iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / 'ayamātmā'; ramābrahmādiṣu ādānādikartṛtvena sthitaḥ ātmā 'brahma'; viṣṇureveti māṇḍūkaśrutyarthaḥ
"so 'yaṃ viṣṇū ramābrahmarudrānantādigaḥ sadā / ādānādanakartṛtvādātmā"iti māṇḍūkabhāṣyoktaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs <s>Bhāṣya</s> 1,1.5.20:
The word <s>ātman</s> is primary only with reference to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not to the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) — regarding this, the inference stated beginning with "of one devoted to Him" is not the only authority; rather, the intent is that the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras) also has in mind clear <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>smṛti</s> (traditional scripture) passages — with this purport he cites those various passages, beginning with "this." The phrase ending with "<s>Brahman</s>" connects with the preceding "is taught." 'This <s>ātman</s>' — the <s>ātman</s> who abides as the agent of sustaining and other acts among <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), <s>Brahmā</s>, and others — 'is <s>Brahman</s>' — this is the meaning of the <s>Māṇḍūka</s> <s>śruti</s>, that He is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.
"This <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who always pervades <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and others, is the <s>ātman</s> because of being the agent of sustaining and consuming" — thus it is stated in the <s>Māṇḍūka Bhāṣya</s>.
He is called '<s>Brahman</s>,' '<s>Paramātman</s>' (Supreme Self), and '<s>Bhagavān</s>' (the Lord).
<s>Bhāṣya</s> on BBs 1,1.5.21:
[<s>Anasūyā</s> bore] <s>Datta</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s>, and <s>Soma</s>, who were born of <s>Ātman</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Rudra</s>), and <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: cetanastu dvidhā prokto jīva ātmeti ca prabho /
children.translated_text: The conscious being is declared to be of two kinds, O Lord — <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>ātman</s> (the Supreme Self).
<s>Brahmā</s> and others are called <s>jīvas</s>, while <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) alone is the <s>ātman</s>.
In the case of others, the word <s>ātman</s> is used figuratively.
From the knowledge of that <s>ātman</s> who is <s>nirguṇa</s> (free from material qualities), <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is declared.
All others are declared to be <s>saguṇa</s> (possessing material qualities); from knowledge of them, one is never liberated.
For <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person); therefore <s>mokṣa</s> is from Him alone — thus it is declared.
Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Pādma Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.21:
"vadanti tattattvavidastattvaṃ yajjñānamadvayam / brahma"ityaparaṃ bhāgavatavākyam / advayaṃ samādhikaśūnyaṃ jñānasvarūpaṃ yattattvaṃ vadanti jñāninaḥ tat deśakālādiṣu bṛṃhitatvāt sarvāntaryāmitvādyaiśvaryādiguṇavāttvācca nimittāt 'brahmeti paramātmeti bhagavāniti śabdyate'; abhidhīyata ityarthaḥ / asyāpi pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ / tatraiva caturthaskandhe "dattam"ityanyadvākyam / etacca 'anasūyā tathaivātrerjajñe putrānakalmaṣān'; iti pūrvārdhenaivānvetavyam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs <s>Bhāṣya</s> 1,1.5.21:
"The knowers of reality declare that reality which is non-dual knowledge — '<s>Brahman</s>'" — this is another passage from the <s>Bhāgavata</s>. That reality which is non-dual — devoid of anything equal or superior — and whose essential nature is knowledge, the knowers declare it; that, because of being expanded (<s>bṛṃhita</s>) in space, time, and so forth, and because of possessing qualities such as being the inner controller of all (<s>sarvāntaryāmitva</s>) and lordly powers (<s>aiśvarya</s>), is 'called <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Paramātman</s>, and <s>Bhagavān</s>' — meaning: it is so designated. This too connects with the preceding. In the same [<s>Bhāgavata</s>], in the fourth <s>skandha</s>, "<s>Datta</s>" is another passage. And this should be connected with the prior half-verse: '<s>Anasūyā</s>, the wife of <s>Atri</s>, bore sinless sons.'
<s>Sukalā</s>, the wife of <s>Marīci</s> and daughter of <s>Kardama</s>, gave birth to
<s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Pūrṇimān</s>, by whom the world was filled.

children.text: iti prakṛtena samuccayārthastathāśabdaḥ / tathā ca - anasūyākhyā atribhāryā atreḥ sakāśāt 'ātmeśabrahmasambhavān'; ātmā viṣṇurīśorudraḥ brahmā caturmukhaḥ ātmā ceśaśca brahmā ca te tathoktāḥ taissaha bhavantītyātmeśabrahmasambhavāḥ tān 'akalmaṣān'; apāpān yo dattaḥ durvāsāḥ somaścaitān putrān 'jajñe'; janayāmāsetyarthaḥ / yadvā - anasūyā atrerdattādīn janayāmāsa, te ca ātmeśabrahmasambhavā iti vipariṇāmena vyākhyeyam / atra brahmāveśena sahotpanne candre niruktasambhavaśabdo mukhyaḥ / sākṣādviṣṇurudrāṃśatvena tatsambhūtayordattadurvāsasostu chatrinyāyenāmukhya iti draṣṭavyam / yadyapi "atreḥ patnyanasūyā trīn jajñe 'tiyaśasaḥ sutān / dattam"iti bhāgavatapāṭhaḥ, tathāpyanuvyākhyāne evaṃ paṭhitatvāttathaiva sudhāyāṃ vyākhyātatvāttadanyakalpīyaṃ pāṭhāntaraṃ bhaviṣyatītyadoṣaḥ / asyāpītyupadiśyata ityanenānvayaḥ / cetanastviti pāvākyam / 'prabho'; iti kasyacitsambodhanam / tatreti śeṣaḥ / ādyastuśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / dvitīyo 'vadhāraṇe / tathā ca - 'jīvāḥ brahmādayaḥ proktāḥ ātmā tu'; tacchabdamukhyavācyastu 'janārdano'; viṣṇuḥ 'ekaḥ'; eva proktaḥ pramāṇeṣu / 'itareṣu'; brahmādiṣu 'ātmaśabdaḥ sopācāraḥ'; paramamukhyavṛttyapekṣayā hīnavṛttiyukta iti jñānibhirabhidhīyata ityartaḥ / kutastasyaivātmatvaṃ nānyeṣāmityata āha - tasyeti / yataḥ 'tasya'; nirguṇasya ātmano 'jñānānmokṣo'; bhavatīti "yasyānuvittaḥ"(bṛ.u. 6-4-31.) ityādau 'udāhṛtaḥ'; uktaḥ ato 'yamātmā nirguṇo viṣṇureva nānyaḥ / kutaḥ? tasyaiva viṣṇornirguṇasya mokṣadātṛtvasambhavāt, anyeṣāṃ tadasambhavādityarthaḥ / ātmajñānānmokṣopadeśe 'pi kuto netareṣāmātmatvaṃ teṣāmapi mokṣadātṛtvasambhavādityata āha - saguṇā iti / turavadhāraṇe / tathāca - 'apare'; viṣṇoranye brahmādayo yataḥ 'saguṇāḥ'; sattvādiguṇabaddhā eva na svatastadvidhurāḥ ataḥ 'tajjñānānnaiva'; sarvathā 'mucyate'; adhikārītyarthaḥ, guṇabaddhātmavijñānāt guṇabandhanivṛttirūpamokṣāyāgāditi bhāvaḥ / nanu viṣṇāvapi nirguṇatvenāstu mokṣadātṛtvasambhāvanā, tanniścayastu kuta ityata āha - paro hīti / 'hi'; yasmāt 'viṣṇuparaḥ'; svatantraḥ / tattvapradīparītyā sarvottama iti vā, 'puruṣaḥ'; pūrṇaḥ 'tasmānmokṣastato'; viṣṇorbhavedeveti smṛtaḥ smṛtyukta ityarthaḥ/ 'iti pādme'; ityasyāpi ityupadiśyata iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ// 7//
children.translated_text: Thus the word 'tathā' (likewise) has the sense of conjunction with the preceding context. And so — <s>Anasūyā</s>, the wife of <s>Atri</s>, from <s>Atri</s> [bore sons who were] 'born of <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>' — <s>Ātman</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Īśa</s> is <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> is the four-faced one; those called <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> — those born together with them are '<s>ātmeśa-brahma-sambhavāḥ</s>' (born of <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>); those 'sinless' ones — namely <s>Datta</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s>, and <s>Soma</s> — she 'bore,' meaning she gave birth to them. Alternatively, <s>Anasūyā</s> gave birth to <s>Datta</s> and others from <s>Atri</s>, and they are '<s>ātmeśa-brahma-sambhavāḥ</s>' — this should be explained by transposition. Here, regarding <s>Soma</s> (the Moon), who was born along with an incarnation of <s>Brahmā</s>, the word 'sambhava' (birth) is primary. But regarding <s>Datta</s> and <s>Durvāsas</s>, who were directly portions of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, it is secondary by the principle of the umbrella (<s>chatri-nyāya</s>). Although the <s>Bhāgavata</s> reading is "<s>Atri's</s> wife <s>Anasūyā</s> bore three illustrious sons — <s>Datta</s>...," nevertheless, since the <s>Anuvyākhyāna</s> reads it thus and the <s>Sudhā</s> commentary explains it accordingly, the alternate reading must belong to some other recension — there is no fault. This too connects with 'is taught' from the preceding. The verse beginning 'cetanastu' is from the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>. 'O Lord' is an address to someone. 'Therein' is to be supplied. The first 'tu' particle has the sense of distinction; the second is for emphasis. And so — '<s>jīvas</s> are <s>Brahmā</s> and others, while the <s>ātman</s>' — the primary referent of that word — 'is <s>Janārdana</s>' (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) 'alone' — thus declared in the authoritative texts. 'In the case of others' — <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest — 'the word <s>ātman</s> is figurative' — meaning that the learned declare it to be of a lesser designation compared to its supreme primary usage. Why is <s>ātman</s>-hood His alone and not of others? To this he says — 'tasya' (of Him). Since 'of that' <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>ātman</s>, from 'knowledge, <s>mokṣa</s>' results — as 'stated' in passages such as "of whom there is realization" (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4.31) — therefore this <s>ātman</s>, who is <s>nirguṇa</s>, is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not anyone else. Why? Because only that <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> can grant <s>mokṣa</s>, while others cannot — this is the meaning. Even when <s>mokṣa</s> is taught from knowledge of the <s>ātman</s>, why is <s>ātman</s>-hood not of others, since they too might grant <s>mokṣa</s>? To this he says — '<s>saguṇāḥ</s>' (possessing qualities). The 'tu' particle is for emphasis. And so — 'others' — those other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, namely <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest — since they are '<s>saguṇa</s>' — bound by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and so forth, not inherently free from them — therefore 'from knowledge of them, never' — in any way — 'is one liberated' — meaning: the aspirant [is not liberated], the purport being that from knowledge of a self bound by <s>guṇas</s>, liberation in the form of freedom from bondage to <s>guṇas</s> cannot arise. Now, even regarding <s>Viṣṇu</s>, let there be the possibility of granting <s>mokṣa</s> due to being <s>nirguṇa</s> — but whence the certainty of this? To this he says — 'paro hi' (for He is supreme). 'Hi' — because '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is para' — independent; or, according to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, the highest of all — '<s>puruṣa</s>' — the complete one; 'therefore <s>mokṣa</s> is from Him' — from <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone it arises — thus it is 'declared' in <s>smṛti</s>, meaning stated in traditional scripture. 'Thus in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>' — this too connects with 'is taught' from the preceding.
And because there is no statement of [its] <s>heyatva</s> (rejectability). || <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.8 ||

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.22:
yuktyantareṇātmaśabdādito na gauṇa ityāha sūtrakṛt - heyatveti / atra heyatvaṃ nāma mokṣārthaṃ prādhānyena jñeyatvenāvihitatvam / tathā ca - na kevalaṃ tanniṣṭhasya mokṣopadeśāt, kintu "tamevaikam"iti śrutau ātmano heyatvāvacanāt, pratyuta 'jānatha'; ityaheyatvavacanāt, jīvasya ca "anyā vāco vimuñcatha"iti mumukṣubhirheyatvavacanācceti sūtravṛttimabhipretya sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - tamiti / he ṛṣayaḥ 'tam'; ātmānaṃ viṣṇum 'eva ekaṃ'; pradhānaṃ 'jānatha'; jānīdhvam / 'anyāḥ'; jīvādiviṣayiṇīḥ 'vācaḥ vimuñcatha'; tyajata, prādhānyena viṣṇvitarān na jānīdhvamityarthaḥ / 'jānatha ātmānam'; iti viśleṣo viṣṇoḥ sarvato vilakṣaṇatvapradarśanārthaḥ / vikaraṇavyatyayastu chāndasaḥ / amṛtasyetyekavacanaṃ samudāyavivakṣayā / tathā ca - 'amṛtasya'; muktavargasya 'eṣaḥ'; viṣṇuḥ setuḥ'; mukhyāśraya ityarthaḥ / 'iti'; ityevaṃrūpāyāṃ muṇḍakaśrutau 'anyeṣāṃ'; jīvānāṃ 'heyatvavacanāt'; ityanena caśabdasamucceyaṃ darśitam / sautranaño vyatyāsena anvayamabhipretya samucceyāntaramāha - asya viṣṇoraheyatveti / caśabdaḥ samuccaye / sūtre gauṇasūtrādanuvṛttasya "na gauṇa ātmaśabdaḥ"ityasyārthamāha - neti / gauṇa ātmaśabdamukhyavācyo na, kintu nirguṇo viṣṇurevetyarthaḥ/ tathā ca - ātmaśabdādīkṣatiśrutyukto 'pi nirguṇa eveti siddham/ tasyekṣatyanyathānupapattyā vācyatvamiti bhāvaḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text:
<s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs <s>Bhāṣya</s> 1,1.5.22:
The <s>sūtrakāra</s> states by another reasoning that <s>ātman</s> [as denoting <s>Viṣṇu</s>] from the beginning is not secondary — '<s>heyatva</s>' (rejectability). Here '<s>heyatva</s>' means not being prescribed as the primary object of knowledge for the purpose of <s>mokṣa</s>. And so — not only because of the teaching of <s>mokṣa</s> for one devoted to Him, but also because in the <s>śruti</s> "know Him, the one alone," there is no statement of the <s>ātman</s>'s rejectability; on the contrary, 'know' is a statement of non-rejectability; and because of the statement of rejectability of the <s>jīva</s> in "abandon other words" for seekers of liberation — intending this as the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with 'tam' (Him). O sages, 'Him' — the <s>ātman</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'alone, the one' — the principal one — 'know' — know Him! 'Other' — words pertaining to <s>jīvas</s> and such — 'abandon' — relinquish them; meaning: do not primarily seek to know anything other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The separation in 'know the <s>ātman</s>' is for the purpose of showing that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is entirely distinct from all else. The irregular conjugation is Vedic license. The singular in '<s>amṛtasya</s>' (of immortality) is because the group [of liberated souls] is intended collectively. And so — 'of immortality' — of the host of the liberated — 'this' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'is the bridge' — meaning the primary refuge. 'Thus' — in a <s>Muṇḍaka</s> <s>śruti</s> of this form, 'because of the statement of the rejectability of others' — of the <s>jīvas</s> — by this the 'ca' (and) particle in the <s>sūtra</s> indicates conjunction. Intending the connection by transposition of the <s>sūtra</s> elements, he states the other item in the conjunction — 'of this <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the non-rejectability.' The 'ca' particle is for conjunction. He states the meaning of 'the word <s>ātman</s> is not secondary,' which continues from the earlier <s>gauṇa-sūtra</s> — 'na' (not). The primary referent of the word <s>ātman</s> is not secondary; rather, it is the <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — this is the meaning. And so — it is established that the one taught even by the <s>īkṣati</s> <s>śruti</s> (the scripture about 'seeing/willing') through the word <s>ātman</s> is <s>nirguṇa</s> alone. His being the referent [of <s>ātman</s>] is because of the impossibility of explaining '<s>īkṣati</s>' (seeing/willing) otherwise — this is the purport.
Because of <s>svāpyaya</s> (self-dissolution/absorption into oneself). || <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.9 ||
That is full, this is full; from the full, the full arises.
When the full is taken from the full, the full alone remains.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.23:
yuktyantareṇāpi nirguṇasya viṣṇorvācyatvamupapādayatsūtramupanyasyati - svāpyayāditi / sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe pūrṇamiti / 'ado'; mūlarūpaṃ 'pūrṇam'; 'idam'; avatārarūpaṃ ca 'pūrṇam'; / 'pūrṇam'; avatārarūpaṃ sṛṣṭikāle 'pūrṇāt'; mūlarūpāt 'udacyate'; udgacchati / tattvapradīparītyā amuṣmādidaṃ saṅkhyāmātreṇodacyate ekameva bahusaṅkhyaṃ bhavati viśeṣādeveti vā / pralaye mūlarūpaṃ 'pūrṇasya'; svasya 'pūrṇam'; avatārarūpam 'ādāya'; svīkṛtyaikībhūya 'pūrṇameva'; anyatrālīnaṃ sadeva svayam 'avaśiṣyate'; iti bṛhadāraṇyakaśrutyarthaḥ / 'sa'; ityanyāśrutiḥ / tadarthastu - 'sa'; viṣṇuḥ 'ātmanaḥ'; svasmāt mūlarūpāt 'ātmānam'; avatāragataṃ svasvarūpaṃ 'uddhṛtya'; sṛṣṭikāle pṛthagvyaktīkṛtya pralaye 'ātmani'; svasvinneva 'vilāpayati'; ekībhāvayati / 'atha'; anantaraṃ sa viṣṇuḥ 'ātmaiva'; mūlarūpyeva 'bhavati'; avaśiṣyata iti / 'sa devaḥ'; iti skāndasmṛtiḥ śrautatacchabdārthavivaraṇarūpā / 'devo'; dyotanādeḥ 'nirguṇaḥ'; sattvādiguṇebhyo niṣkrāntaḥ tata eva guṇakāryadoṣahīnaḥ 'puruṣottamaḥ'; kṣarākṣaracetanottamaḥ 'ādikṛt'; viśvasyotpattikartā prathamakartā vā 'saḥ'; śvetadvīpago 'hariḥ'; ādisṛṣṭau 'bahudhābhūtvā'; varāhādibahurūpāṇi sṛṣṭvā 'punaḥ'; atha pralaye 'ekībhūya'; mūlarūpeṇa tānyekatāṃ prāpayitvā ahipatau 'śete'; yoganidrāṃ karotītyarthaḥ / itītyasya iti śrutyuktatvāccetyadhyāhāreṇa 'vācyameva tat'; iti paramasādhyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs <s>Bhāṣya</s> 1,1.5.23:
Presenting the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes by yet another reasoning that the <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the referent — '<s>svāpyayāt</s>' (because of self-absorption). He explains the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with '<s>pūrṇam</s>' (full). 'That' — the original form — is 'full'; 'this' — the <s>avatāra</s> (incarnation) form — is also 'full.' The 'full' — the <s>avatāra</s> form — at the time of creation 'arises from' the 'full' — from the original form. According to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, from that, this arises merely in number — that is, the one becomes many in number, but differs [only] in specification. At the time of dissolution, the 'full' — the original form — 'having taken' its own 'full' — the <s>avatāra</s> form — having absorbed it and become one — 'the full alone' — itself, without being dissolved elsewhere — 'remains' — this is the meaning of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> <s>śruti</s>. 'He' — this is another <s>śruti</s> passage. Its meaning is: 'He' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'from Himself' — from His own original form — 'the self' — His own form as <s>avatāra</s> — 'having drawn out' — at the time of creation, having manifested separately — at dissolution, 'into Himself' — into His own self alone — 'dissolves' — unifies. 'Then' — after that, He, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'becomes the Self alone' — remains as the original form alone. 'That <s>deva</s>' — this is a <s>Skānda</s> <s>smṛti</s> passage that elaborates the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. '<s>Deva</s>' — because of radiance and such; '<s>nirguṇa</s>' — transcending the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and others, and therefore free from the defects that are effects of the <s>guṇas</s>; '<s>Puruṣottama</s>' — supreme among the perishable and imperishable conscious beings; '<s>ādikṛt</s>' — the creator of the universe, or the first creator; 'He' — the one who resides in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> — '<s>Hari</s>' — at the primordial creation, 'having become manifold' — having created many forms such as <s>Varāha</s> and others — 'again' — then at dissolution — 'having become one' — having brought them into unity through His original form — 'sleeps' upon the serpent lord (<s>Śeṣa</s>) — meaning He enters <s>yoganidrā</s> (yogic sleep). The word 'iti' (thus) — with the implicit supplement 'because it is stated in <s>śruti</s>' — connects with the ultimate conclusion 'that is indeed the referent.'
Because of the statement of absorption of His own self into His own self.
For there is no dissolution of a designation into a secondary <s>ātman</s>.
