children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.24:
etacchrutyukto 'pi nirguṇaḥ kutaḥ? gauṇa eva kiṃ na syādityastatra sautraṃ hetuṃ sāvadhāraṇasvaśabdāvṛttyā yojayati - svasyaiveti // evakāro bhinnakramaḥ / itiśabda āvṛtto 'trāpi yojyaḥ/ vacanādityāvartate / na gauṇa ityanuvartate / ayamiti śeṣaḥ / svāpyayapadaṃ pūrṇatvasyāpyupalakṣakam / tathā ca pūrṇamiti śrutau svāpyayapadopalakṣitapūrṇatvasya vacanāt svasya svasminnevāpyayavacanācca, sa iti spaṣṭaśrutāvapi ātmanyeva vilāpayīti svasya svasminnevāpyayavacanāt, tasya ca nirguṇahariniṣṭhatāyāḥ smṛtau vacanācca ayaṃ nirguṇa eva na gauṇa iti yojanā / vācyatve svāpyayasya sākṣāddhetutvābhāvāt sūtre bhāṣye ca caśabdābhāvaḥ / yadyapyatropalakṣaṇābhiprāyakaṭīkārītyā pūrṇatvahetusamuccāyakaścaśabdo 'nuvartanīyaḥ / tathāpyasya vācyatve sākṣadahetutvāttatra hetvantarasya jñāpakacaśabdo nānuvartanīyaḥ / na ca
children.translated_text:
<s>Dīpikā</s> on BBs <s>Bhāṣya</s> 1,1.5.24:
Even though taught by this <s>śruti</s>, why is He <s>nirguṇa</s>? Why could He not be merely secondary? — To this, he connects the reason from the <s>sūtra</s> by repeating the word 'sva' (own) with emphasis — 'of His own self alone.' The 'eva' particle is in transposed order. The word 'iti' (thus), being repeated, should be connected here as well. 'Because of the statement' continues [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>]. 'Not secondary' also continues. 'This' is to be supplied. The term '<s>svāpyaya</s>' (self-absorption) also serves as an indicator of fullness (<s>pūrṇatva</s>). And so — in the <s>śruti</s> beginning with '<s>pūrṇam</s>' (full), because of the statement of fullness indicated by the term <s>svāpyaya</s>, and because of the statement of the absorption of one's own self into one's own self; and in the explicit <s>śruti</s> 'He dissolves into the Self alone,' because of the statement of the absorption of His own self into His own self; and because in <s>smṛti</s> there is the statement that this pertains to the <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>Hari</s> — the construction is: this [<s>ātman</s>] is <s>nirguṇa</s> alone, not secondary. Because <s>svāpyaya</s> is not a direct reason for the referent-hood [of <s>ātman</s>], there is no 'ca' (and) particle in the <s>sūtra</s> or the <s>bhāṣya</s>. Although here, according to the commentator's intent regarding indication, a 'ca' particle conjoining the reason of fullness should continue, nevertheless, since <s>svāpyaya</s> is not a direct reason for the referent-hood, the indicative 'ca' particle for another reason need not be continued. And not —

children.text: śrutyuktatvāccetyadhyāhṛtahetau caśabdāvaśyaṃbhāvāt kathaṃ tadabhāva iti vācyam, sūtraśrutahetau caśabdābhāva ityabhiprāyāt / ata eva ṭīkāyāṃ tatretyuktam / tathā cāyaṃ sūtrārthaḥ - na kevalaṃ nirguṇaviṣṇvākhyaṃ brahma īkṣaṇīyatvādvācyam, kintvetacchrutyuktatvācca / śrutyuktaṃ nirguṇameva na gauṇamiti kutaḥ? purṇatvātsvasya svasminnapyayācca, gauṇasyāpūrṇatvāt anyasmin layena svāpyayaśūnyatvācceti / śrutyuktasvāpyayapūrṇatvayorasiddhiparihārāya hetau sādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyopapādanāya ca śrutismṛtyorvacanādityuktaṃ bhāṣye / nanvayaṃ svāpyayavān anyatrālīnaśca gauṇassyāt, nirguṇo 'nyo 'stīti cet - na, yadyayaṃ svāpyayavān gauṇaḥ tarhyayaṃ nirguṇaścobhau pralaye 'nyatra layahīnau tiṣṭhataḥ? uta ekasminnanyasya layo bhavati? nādyaḥ "idaṃ vā agne naiva kiñca nāsīt"(tai.brā. 2-2-9-1.) ityādiśrutivirodhāt, atra pralaye dvitīyamātraniṣedhāt / dvitīye na tāvadgauṇasya nirguṇe layaḥ, tasya svāpyayavattayā avasthānābhyupagamāt / tathā ca nirguṇasya saguṇe layo vācyaḥ / sa ca na sambhavatītyāha - na hīti / 'gauṇātmani'; jīve 'nirdeṣasya'; sattvādiguṇabandharūpadoṣahīnasya nirguṇasya viṣṇorlayo nopapadyata ityarthaḥ / hiśabdena "yatprayanti"(tai.u.3-1.) ityādiśrutivirodhāditi hetuḥ sūcitaḥ / tasmānnirguṇasya svasminneva layo vācya ityato 'yamananyalīno nirguṇa eveti tasyaiva śrutyuktatvādvācyatvaṃ siddhamiti bhāvaḥ / atra naye gauṇādivyapadeśaḥ sattvādiguṇayuktatvatadabhāvarūpadharmāśrayajīvaparamātmaviṣayaka eva, na tu mukhyāsambhave gauṇāśrayaṇādityatreva nirguṇo 'yamityatreva vā mukhyārthaguṇahīnaviṣaya iti sūcanāya nirguṇasyeti vaktavyatve 'pi nirdeṣasyetyuktam /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If the supplied reason is 'because of being stated in <s>Śruti</s>,' since the word 'ca' (and) would be necessarily present in the supplied reason, how can its absence [in the sūtra be explained]? — this is to be answered: because the intention is that the word 'ca' is absent when the reason is as read in the <s>sūtra</s> [itself]. For this very reason, in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, 'there' is stated. And thus, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: not only is <s>Brahman</s> named as <s>nirguṇa</s> (quality-free) <s>Viṣṇu</s> expressible because of being an object of contemplation, but also because of its being stated in this <s>Śruti</s>. Whence [the claim] that what is stated in <s>Śruti</s> is the <s>nirguṇa</s> alone and not the <s>gauṇa</s> (secondary, i.e., the <s>jīva</s>)? Because of [<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s] fullness and because of His dissolution into Himself (<s>svāpyaya</s>), and because the <s>gauṇa</s> is incomplete and, being dissolved into another, lacks self-dissolution. To remove the objection of non-establishment of the <s>Śruti</s>-stated self-dissolution and fullness, and to demonstrate the co-location of the property to be proven in the reason, it is stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'from the statements of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>.' [Objection:] But this one who possesses self-dissolution and is not dissolved elsewhere could be the <s>gauṇa</s>, and there could be another who is <s>nirguṇa</s> — if this is said: No. If this one who possesses self-dissolution is the <s>gauṇa</s>, then do both this one and the <s>nirguṇa</s> remain at the time of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) without being dissolved elsewhere? Or does one dissolve into the other? Not the first [option], because of the contradiction with <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'Before this, O <s>Agni</s>, there was nothing whatsoever' (<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 2.2.9.1) and the like, since in those [passages] the existence of a second [entity] at dissolution is negated. In the second [option], the <s>gauṇa</s> does not dissolve into the <s>nirguṇa</s>, since [the <s>gauṇa</s>'s] continued existence is accepted due to its possessing self-dissolution. And thus, the dissolution of the <s>nirguṇa</s> into the <s>saguṇa</s> (the one with qualities) must be stated. And that is not possible — he says: 'na hi' (for not). 'In the <s>gauṇa</s> self' — in the <s>jīva</s>; 'of the <s>nirdeṣa</s>' — of the <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is free from the defect in the form of bondage to the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like, dissolution is not tenable: this is the meaning. By the particle 'hi,' the reason is indicated: because of the contradiction with <s>Śruti</s> passages such as 'to which [all beings] go' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1). Therefore, since the dissolution of the <s>nirguṇa</s> must be stated as into itself alone, this one who is not dissolved elsewhere is the <s>nirguṇa</s> alone, and its expressibility is established precisely because of its being stated in <s>Śruti</s>: this is the purport. In this interpretive system, the designation '<s>gauṇa</s>' and the like pertains only to the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Paramātman</s> as the substrata of the properties of being endowed with or devoid of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like — not to the resort to secondary meaning when the primary meaning is impossible; to indicate this, even though '<s>nirguṇasya</s>' (of the <s>nirguṇa</s>) should be said, '<s>nirdeṣasya</s>' is said [instead].
And [<s>Brahman</s>] is not spoken of otherwise in any branches [of the <s>Veda</s>]. //
Because of the uniformity of purport. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.10 |

children.text: sarve vedā yuktayaḥ supramāṇā brāhmaṃ jñānaṃ paramaṃ tvekameva /
children.translated_text: All the <s>Vedas</s>, reasonings, and valid means of knowledge — the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is supreme, and it is one alone.

children.text: prakāśayante na virodhaḥ kutaścidvedeṣu sarveṣu tathetihāse //
children.translated_text: They illuminate [it]; there is no contradiction from anywhere — in all the <s>Vedas</s> and likewise in the <s>Itihāsa</s>. //
Thus, from the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s>, the uniformity of the purport — of knowledge — is [established]. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.25:
nanvastu nirguṇasya viṣṇorvācyatvopapattau satyāṃ kāraṇatvena śāstragamyatvam / taccopakramādibalāt prasiddhaśākhāsveva kāraṇatvena pratipādyatvaparyavasitam / aprasiddhaśākhāsu punaranyo 'pi kāraṇatvena ucyatām / na ca tā na santi, tāsāmānantyeneyattāniścayādityata āha - na ceti // co 'pyarthaḥ / tathā ca - 'kāsucit'; aprasiddhaśākhāsu 'anyathā'; anyo nirguṇāt saguṇo 'pi 'anyathā'; akāraṇatvādeḥ kāraṇatvena ātmaśabdamukhyavācyatvena mokṣajanakajñānaviṣayatvena ca, nirguṇo vā 'anyathā'; akāraṇatvādinā 'ucyate'; ucyatāmiti 'na'
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.5.25:
[Objection:] Even if the expressibility of <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> as <s>Brahman</s> is established as reasonable, [His] causality is knowable through scripture. And that, by the force of the opening (<s>upakrama</s>) and the like, has its conclusion in being taught as the cause only in well-known branches [of the <s>Veda</s>]. But in unknown branches, let someone else also be taught as the cause. And it is not the case that such [branches] do not exist, since their number cannot be determined due to [the branches'] infinity — to this he says: 'na ca' (and not). // 'Ca' has the meaning of 'api' (also). And thus: in 'some' unknown branches, 'otherwise' — someone other than the <s>nirguṇa</s>, even a <s>saguṇa</s>, 'otherwise' — as the cause and the like, as the primary denotation of the word <s>Ātman</s>, as the object of knowledge that produces liberation; or the <s>nirguṇa</s> [is spoken of] 'otherwise' — as non-cause and the like — 'is spoken of': let it be spoken — 'not':,

children.text: iti yojanā / 'nānyathā'; ityanena sūtre gauṇasūtrānnetyasyānuvṛttiḥ anyathetyadhyāhāraśca sūcitaḥ / 'tattu sam'; ityuktādanyathā netyarthaḥ / kuto netyatastatra hetutvena sūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - gatīti / uttarasūtrapadākarṣaṇena sarvādhikārisādhāraṇaṃ gatisāmānyasya śrutatvāditi yojanāmabhipretya asiddhiparihārāya tatsūtrasūcitāṃ śrutimāha - sarva iti / vedā ityasya vivaraṇaṃ 'sarve'; iti / tathā ca - 'sarve vedāḥ'; tathā 'supramāṇāḥ'; suṣṭhu pramāṇaṃ pramāṇānantaraṃ mūlabhūtaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ 'yuktayaḥ'; / 'tathetihāse'; iti vakṣyamāṇānurodhādatretihāsā apyupalakṣyāḥ / tathā cetihāsāśca / 'brāhmaṃ'; brahmaikaviṣayam 'ekam'; ekavidhameva ramārthaviṣayakatvāt 'paramam'; uttamaṃ 'jñānaṃ'; 'prakāśyante'; utpādayanti, na punaranekam / ataḥ 'sarveṣu vedeṣu'; tathā yuktiṣu 'tathetihāse'; itihāseṣu 'kutaścit'; kaścidapi viṣayakṛto vā prakārakṛto vā 'virodho na'; ityarthaḥ jñānarūpamekameva brahmasvarūpaṃ
children.translated_text: this is the construal. By 'nānyathā' (not otherwise) in the <s>sūtra</s>, the continuation of 'na' (not) from the <s>gauṇa sūtra</s> and the supplying of 'anyathā' (otherwise) is indicated. The meaning is: not otherwise than what was stated by 'tattu sam' (but that [is known through] harmony). Why not? — To this, having presented the <s>sūtra</s> as the reason, he explains: 'gati' (purport). Intending the construal — 'because of the uniformity of purport being heard [as common] to all who are qualified,' by drawing in the word from the subsequent <s>sūtra</s> — to remove the objection of non-establishment, he cites the <s>Śruti</s> indicated by the <s>sūtra</s>: 'sarve' (all). The word 'all' is an exposition of the word '<s>Vedas</s>.' And thus: 'all the <s>Vedas</s>' and also 'valid means of knowledge' (<s>supramāṇāḥ</s>) — those 'reasonings' (<s>yuktayaḥ</s>) which have good, well-established, foundational means of valid knowledge. By 'likewise in the <s>Itihāsa</s>,' in accordance with what will be stated later, the <s>Itihāsas</s> too are to be included here by indication. And thus: [the <s>Vedas</s> and] the <s>Itihāsas</s> too — 'knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>' — having <s>Brahman</s> alone as its object, 'one' — of one kind alone, because it has the beloved of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) as its object, 'supreme' — the highest 'knowledge' — 'illuminate' — generate; and not manifold [knowledge]. Therefore, 'in all the <s>Vedas</s>' and likewise in the reasonings, 'and in the <s>Itihāsa</s>' — in the <s>Itihāsas</s> — 'from anywhere' — whether pertaining to any subject or any mode — 'there is no contradiction': this is the meaning. [Alternatively:] they cause the knowledge of the one <s>Brahman</s>'s essential nature alone

children.text: jñāpayantīti vā / śruteriti pañcamī tṛtīyārthe / gaterityasya vyākhyā jñānasyeti / sāmānyāditi sautrapade prātipadikārthamāha - sāmyamiti / viṣayaguṇānāmananyathoktyā sāmyamityarthaḥ / "na hyekatra jñānānandādikamuktvānyatrājñānādirūpatvaṃ brahmaṇa ucyate"iti tattvapradīpokteḥ kathyata iti śeṣaḥ / na tu viṣamatvamiti vā svayameva sākṣānna tvanyamukheneti vā evaśabdārthaḥ / tathā ca - 'sarve vedā'; iti śrutyā svayameva sākṣādgateḥ sarvaśākhotpādyajñānasya sāmānyāt ekavidhatvokteḥ na kāsucicchākhāsu anyathocyata iti sūtrārthaḥ / atra bhinnaviṣayaprakārakeṣvapi jñāneṣu jñānatvena sāmyasattvātsāmyādityuktau viṣayaprakāraikyaṃ na siddhyatīti sāmānyāt samānatvāt ekavidhatvāt ityuktaṃ sūtre / bhāṣyapadasyāpyayamevārtha eti dhyeyam // 10 //
children.translated_text: — or thus. 'From the <s>Śruti</s>' — the fifth case is used in the sense of the third (instrumental). The explanation of 'gati' (purport) is 'jñānasya' (of knowledge). Regarding the <s>sūtra</s> word 'sāmānyāt' (from uniformity), he states the <s>prātipadika</s> meaning: 'sāmyam' (sameness). The meaning is: sameness through the non-different expression of the object and qualities. As stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'For it is not the case that having stated knowledge, bliss and the like in one place, the nature of ignorance and the like is attributed to <s>Brahman</s> elsewhere.' 'Is stated' is the remainder. The meaning of the word 'eva' is not 'but not unevenness,' but rather 'directly by itself, not through the medium of another.' And thus: from the <s>Paiṅgi</s> <s>Śruti</s> 'all the <s>Vedas</s>,' because of the uniformity — the one-kind-ness — of knowledge generated by all branches, directly by the [<s>Śruti</s>] itself, [<s>Brahman</s>] is not spoken of otherwise in any branches: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. Here, even though knowledge with different objects and modes has sameness qua being knowledge, since the oneness of object and mode would not be established [merely] from 'sāmyāt' (from sameness), in the <s>sūtra</s> it is said 'sāmānyāt' — from commonality, from one-kind-ness. It should be noted that this alone is the meaning of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> word as well. // 10 //
And because of being heard [in <s>Śruti</s>]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.11 |

children.text:
"eko devassarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā /
karmādhyakṣassarvabhūtādhivāsaḥ sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaśca"/
(śve.6-11)
iti na śabdaḥ śrūyate / na cāprasiddhaṃ kalpyam /
sarvaśabdāvācyasya lakṣaṇāyukteḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text:
'The one God hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings,
the overseer of actions, the abode of all beings, the witness, the conscious one, the absolute, and free from qualities.' /
(<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 6.11)
Thus the word 'na' (not) is heard. Nor should what is unknown be imagined.
Because a secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) is not appropriate for that which is inexpressible by all words. // 5 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.5.26:
itaśca nirguṇaṃ brahma vācyamityāha sūtrakṛt - śrutatvācceti/ co hetusamuccaye / tadaśabdaṃ neti vartate/ tathā ca tadviṣṇvākhyaṃ nirguṇaṃ na kevalamīkṣatyādibhiḥ nāśabdaṃ śabdavācyam / kintu "ekaḥ"iti śvetāśvataraśrutau 'śrutatvācca'; svavācakanāmnā sākṣāduktatvāccetyartha ityāśayena sūtropāttaśrutiṃ paṭhati - eka iti / 'ekaḥ'; pradhānaḥ svasmin bhedaśūnya iti vā 'devo'; dyotanādeḥ 'sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ'; sarvaprāṇiṣu guptatayāvasthitaḥ / na kevalaṃ bhūteṣu sthitaḥ kintu 'sarvavyāpī'; ca deśataḥ kālato guṇataśca sarvaṃ vyāpnotītyarthaḥ / na kevalaṃ sarvabhūteṣu sthitimātraṃ, kintu 'sarvabhūtāntarātmā'; sarvaprāṇināṃ antaḥsthitvā ā samyak tanniyantā ca mātā ceti vā / ādānādikartṛtvādvā tathoktaḥ / 'karmādhyakṣaḥ'; karmādhipatiḥ, "karmopari asyākṣāṇīndriyāṇi vartanta ityadhyakṣaḥ"iti tattvapradīpokteḥ / 'sarvabhūtādhivāsaḥ'; sarvaprāṇināmāśrayaḥ / sarvaṃ sākṣādīkṣate paśyatīti 'sākṣī'; / īkṣaṇaṃ ca na prākṛtaṃ kintu caitanyasvarūpamityāha - 'cetā'; jñānarūpa iti / 'kevalo'; jaḍāmiśraḥ samābhyadhikaśūnya iti vā "kevalaṃ tādṛśābhāvāt"iti dvitīyatātparyokteḥ / kevalaṃ caitanyenekṣaṇamasaṃprajñātasamādhisthasya yogino 'pi bhavatīti tadvyāvartanāyāha 'nirguṇa'; iti sattvādiguṇabandhahīna ityarthaḥ, prākṛtaguṇahīna iti vā / itiśabdasya 'śrutau nirguṇasya'; iti padadvayādhyāhāreṇa śrutatvāditi sūtreṇānvayaḥ / "atra vācyatvaṃ pratipādayatsūtraṃ tadupāttaśrutyudāharaṇapūrvakaṃ paṭhati - eka iti"iti kvacitkaṭīkāpāṭhānusāreṇa bhāṣye kvacit śrutipāṭhānantaraṃ sūtrapāṭho dṛśyate / tatpakṣe tvanvayassulabha eveti dhyeyam / śrutatve 'pyaśabdaḥ kiṃ na syādityaprayojakatvaśaṅkāyāmāha - na hīti / 'hi'; yataḥ 'aśabdaḥ'; avācyaḥ padārtho 'na śrūyate'; na śrutipadenocyata ityarthaḥ / ato nāprayojakatvaṃ hetoriti vākyaśeṣaḥ / virodhādityapi hiśabdārthaḥ / nanu aśabdasyāpi brahmaṇo lakṣaṇayā śrutatvaṃ kiṃ na syādityata āha - na ceti / 'aprasiddham'; avācyasya brahmaṇo lakṣyatvaṃ na kalpyamityarthaḥ / kutaḥ? yato 'vācyasya vastuno lakṣyatvamaprasiddham ata iti vyāptiparatvenāpīdaṃ yojanīyam / nanu kathametat? gaṅgāpadāvācyasyāpi tīrasya tatpadalakṣyatvaprasiddherityata uktaṃ - sarveti / 'sarvaśabdāvācyasya'; brahmaṇo lakṣaṇāyāḥ vedapadalakṣyatvasyāyukteḥ vipratipannaṃ na lakṣyaṃ, kenāpi padenāvācyatvāt vyatirekeṇa tīravaditi yuktiviruddhatvādityarthaḥ / tathā ca - nāsmābhiḥ kevalāvācyatvena lakṣyatvābhāvaḥ sādhyate yena tīrādau vyabhicāraḥ śaṅkayeta, kintu sarvaśabdāvācyatvena / tacca na tīrādigataṃ, tasya tīrādipadavācyatvāt / brahma tu na tathā, tasya sarvaśabdāvācyatayaiva pareṇāṅgīkṛtatvāt / ato na vyabhicāra iti yuktivirodho duṣparihara iti bhāvaḥ / nanu lakṣyatvābhāvavati pravāhādau hetvabhāvādasādhāraṇamiti cet - na, lakṣaṇāyogyasyaiva lakṣyapadārthatve
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.5.26:
For this reason too, <s>nirguṇa</s> <s>Brahman</s> is expressible — the <s>sūtrakāra</s> says: 'śrutatvācca' (and because of being heard). The word 'ca' is for the aggregation of reasons. 'That is not inexpressible' (<s>tad aśabdam na</s>) continues. And thus, that <s>nirguṇa</s> [entity] named <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not merely 'not inexpressible' — i.e., expressible by words — through [passages like] 'one who sees' (<s>īkṣati</s>) and the like; but also, 'because of being heard' in the <s>Śvetāśvatara Śruti</s> 'ekaḥ' (one) — because of being directly stated by a name that denotes Him: this is the intent. With this intent, he reads the <s>Śruti</s> taken up by the <s>sūtra</s>: 'eka' (one). 'One' — the chief, or the one in whom there is no division within Himself; '<s>deva</s>' — because of illumination and the like; 'hidden in all beings' — existing in a concealed manner in all living beings. Not merely situated in beings, but also 'all-pervading' — pervading everything in respect of space, time, and quality: this is the meaning. Not merely situated in all beings, but 'the inner Self of all beings' — having entered within all living beings, He is their thorough controller and nourisher; or He is so called because of being the agent of reception and the like. 'The overseer of actions' (<s>karmādhyakṣa</s>) — the lord of actions; as stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'He over whose senses actions operate is called the overseer.' 'The abode of all beings' — the refuge of all living beings. He who directly sees everything is the 'witness' (<s>sākṣin</s>). And that seeing is not mundane but is of the nature of consciousness — he says: 'the conscious one' (<s>cetā</s>) — of the nature of knowledge. 'The absolute' (<s>kevala</s>) — unmixed with insentient matter, or devoid of equals and superiors; as stated in the <s>Dvitīya Tātparya</s>: '<s>Kevala</s> means the absence of such [equals or superiors].' The seeing through consciousness alone also occurs for a <s>yogin</s> in the state of <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s> — to exclude that, he says: '<s>nirguṇa</s>' — free from bondage to the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like: this is the meaning; or free from material qualities. The word 'iti' connects with 'śrutatvāt' (because of being heard) through the supplying of the two words 'śrutau nirguṇasya' (in the <s>Śruti</s>, of the <s>nirguṇa</s>). 'Following the reading of some manuscripts of the <s>Ṭīkā</s> where it says: he reads the <s>Śruti</s> example taken up by the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes expressibility, preceded by: eka iti' — in some [editions of the] <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the reading of the <s>sūtra</s> is seen after the reading of the <s>Śruti</s>. In that case, the syntactic connection is easily [understood] — this should be noted. Even though [<s>Brahman</s>] is heard [in <s>Śruti</s>], could it not be inexpressible? — To the suspicion of purposelessness, he says: 'na hi' (for not). 'Hi' — since 'aśabdaḥ' — an inexpressible entity — 'na śrūyate' — is not stated by a <s>Śruti</s> word: this is the meaning. Therefore, there is no purposelessness of the reason: this is the remainder of the sentence. 'Because of contradiction' is also the meaning of the particle 'hi.' [Objection:] But could not <s>Brahman</s>, even though inexpressible, be heard [in <s>Śruti</s>] through secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>)? — To this he says: 'na ca' (and not). What 'is unknown' — the <s>lakṣya</s>-hood (being the object of secondary indication) of inexpressible <s>Brahman</s> — 'should not be imagined': this is the meaning. Why? Because 'the <s>lakṣya</s>-hood of an expressible entity is unknown — therefore' — this too should be construed as referring to the <s>vyāpti</s> (universal concomitance). [Objection:] But how is this so? For even the bank, which is not directly denoted by the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>,' is well-known as the <s>lakṣya</s> (indicated referent) of that word — to this it is said: 'sarva' (all). 'Of that which is inexpressible by all words' — because a secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) for <s>Brahman</s>, being the <s>lakṣya</s> of a Vedic word, is inappropriate — [since] what is disputed is not a <s>lakṣya</s>, because it is not expressible by any word at all — through the <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), like the bank: because it contradicts reasoning, this is the meaning. And thus: it is not the case that we establish the absence of <s>lakṣya</s>-hood merely through inexpressibility, so that one might suspect deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in the case of the bank and the like; rather, [we establish it] through inexpressibility by all words. And that [universal inexpressibility] does not apply to the bank and the like, since that [bank] is expressible by the word 'bank' and the like. But <s>Brahman</s> is not like that, since its inexpressibility by all words is accepted by the opponent himself. Therefore there is no deviation, and the contradiction with reasoning is difficult to resolve: this is the purport. [Objection:] If there is absence of the reason (<s>hetu</s>) in a stream and the like which lack <s>lakṣya</s>-hood, [then the reason] would be uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) — if this is said: No. If being the referent of a secondary meaning applies only to that which is ineligible for secondary indication,

then since all referents are ineligible for the secondary indication of some word, the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proven) in the form of the absence of that [<s>lakṣya</s>-hood] would be absent everywhere, and hence the <s>sapakṣa</s> (positive example) itself would be absent. // 11 //
// Thus ends the <s>Īkṣatyadhikaraṇa</s> (topic of seeing/contemplation). //
// 6. The <s>Ānandamayādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the one consisting of bliss). //

children.text: tameva samasvayaṃ prakaṭayati 'ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt'; ityādinā samastenādhyāyena prāyeṇa /
children.translated_text: That very [<s>Brahman</s>] which has been concisely stated, he makes manifest through 'the one consisting of bliss, because of repetition' (<s>ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s>) and the like — through almost the entire chapter.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.1:
athādhyāyapādayorupodghātatvena pīṭharūpāyāmasyāṃ pañcādhikaraṇyaṃ brahmasvarūpanarūpaṇe anavaśeṣātkimadhyāyātmakaśeṣagranthenetyata āha - tameveti // tathāpītyādau yojyam / samanvayaśabdaśca vipariṇāmenāvartanīyaḥ / tathā ca - tathāpi prakaṭanaṃ vinādhyāyākhyaśeṣagranthasya kṛtyāntarābhāve 'pi 'tameva'; "tattu samanvayāt"ityanena hetutayā sāmānyataḥ siddhavadupanyastameva samanvayāt 'samanvayam'; upakramādiliṅgajñāpyaṃ samyagvacanavṛttyā sarvaśāstrīyavacanānāṃ harau nirūpaṇaṃ tatparatvaṃ 'prakaṭayati'; prativākyagrahaṇena taddhetūpanyāsādinā prapañcayati "ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt"ityādinā anena prathamenādhyāyena sūtrakāra ityarthaḥ / anyathā pratijñāmātrasya "tadeva śāstrayoni, samanvayāt"iti siddhavadupanyāsamātrasya sādhakatve "viṣṇoranyadeva śāstrayoni, kutaḥ? samanvayāt samyaktātparyaviṣayatvāt, tathā anyadeva tātparyaviṣayaḥ, kutaḥ? upakramādiliṅgāt"ityapi prativādī brūyāditi bhāvaḥ / yathopakramādikaṃ tajjñāpyaṃ tātparyaṃ ca samanvayaśabdārthaḥ tathā bhāṣyaṃ yojitam adhastāt / yadyapyatra sūtrasya pratīkatvena uttaratra udāhariṣyamāṇatvānnātrāpyudāhartavyatā / tathāpi sūtrānudāharaṇe ānandamayākhyaviṣayāparijñānāttasya viṣṇutvasamarthane kā pūrvasaṅgatirityevaṃ śaṅkānudayāt tanmūlapraśnānudayāt ānandamayāparijñāne brahmaṇastadavayavatvapratītimukhenākṣeparūpaśaṅkānudayācca etadākṣeparūpasaṅgatipradarśanāya
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.1:
Now, since in these five <s>adhikaraṇas</s> (topics) — which serve as a preamble to the <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) and <s>pāda</s> (section) in the manner of a foundation — the nature of <s>Brahman</s> is fully delineated, what [need] is there for the remaining text constituting the [rest of the] chapter? — to this he says: 'tam eva' (that very). 'Tathāpi' (even so) should be supplied at the beginning. And the word '<s>samanvaya</s>' (coherent interpretation) is to be carried over in inverted form. And thus — even so, without explicit demonstration, although the remaining text called 'chapter' has no other purpose, 'tam eva' — that very [<s>samanvaya</s>] which was presented as if established in a general way as a reason through the [<s>sūtra</s>] 'tat tu samanvayāt' (but that, through coherent interpretation) — 'samanvayam' — the coherent interpretation, i.e., the determination that all scriptural statements pertain to <s>Hari</s>, which is to be known through the indicators [of purport] such as <s>upakrama</s> (commencement) etc. through the proper operation of [scriptural] words — '[the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] demonstrates' — elaborates through the specific analysis of each sentence, through the presentation of the reasons for each, and so forth — beginning with '<s>ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s>' (the one consisting of bliss, because of repetition) — through this first <s>adhyāya</s>: this is the meaning. Otherwise, if a mere assertion — the mere presentation as if established of 'that alone is <s>śāstrayoni</s>, because of <s>samanvaya</s>' — were to serve as proof, the opponent too could say: 'Something other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> is <s>śāstrayoni</s>; why? Because of <s>samanvaya</s>, because of being the proper subject of purport; likewise, something else is the subject of purport; why? Because of the indicators such as <s>upakrama</s> etc.' — this is the purport. Just as <s>upakrama</s> etc., the purport indicated by them, and [the concept of] <s>samanvaya</s> are the meaning of the word '<s>samanvaya</s>' — in accordance with this, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is interpreted below. Although here the <s>sūtra</s> need not be cited [again] since it will be cited later as an introductory passage — nevertheless, if the <s>sūtra</s> were not cited, then without knowledge of the topic called <s>Ānandamaya</s>, the question 'what is the prior connection for establishing its <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood?' would not arise, nor would the question based on that arise, nor would the objection-form doubt arise through the impression of <s>Brahman</s>'s being a part of that [<s>Ānandamaya</s>] when the <s>Ānandamaya</s> is not [properly] known — therefore, to demonstrate the connection in the form of objection,

children.text: ca adhikaraṇasaṅgativiṣayakaśaṅkotthāpanāya atrāpi sūtrodāharaṇaṃ, uttaratra tu pratīkatveneti draṣṭavyam / adhyāyāntaravyāvṛttyarthamānandamayetyādi / prathamenetyanukttvā evaṃvacanena etadadhikaraṇamārabhyādhyāyārambhaḥ, pañcādhikaraṇyāstu nādhyāyāntarbhāva ityapi sūcitam / samanvayādhikaraṇamārabhyaivādhyāyārambhaḥ tasyaitatprapañcatvāditi pakṣe adhyāyena adhyāyaśeṣeṇetyartha ityavirodhaḥ / caturthapāde na samanvayaḥ kriyata iti paramatanirāsāya 'samastena'; samagreṇetyuktam / devatāpaśūdrādhikaraṇayoḥ samanvayākaraṇāt samastenetyanupapannamityāśaṅkānirākaraṇāya 'prāyeṇa'; prācuryeṇeti / prāya iti sakārāntāvyayaparyāyo 'yamakārāntaḥ prāyaśabdaḥ / tasmātprakṛtyāditvāttṛtīyāyāṃ prāyeṇeti bhavati / ata eva viṣṇutattvanirṇayaṭīkāyāṃ bhūmārthe 'prāyaḥ'; ityavyayamapyasti ityapiśabdaḥ prāyoji / prameyadīpe 'pi sāntasyaivāvyayatvamuktam /
children.translated_text: and to raise the doubt pertaining to the connection between <s>adhikaraṇas</s> (topics), the <s>sūtra</s> is cited here too; but later, it is [cited] as an introductory passage — this should be understood. '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' etc. is for distinguishing from the other chapters. By saying 'evaṃ' (thus) with 'first' instead of [explicitly saying] 'by the first [chapter],' it is also indicated that the chapter begins from this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> onward, while the five [preceding] topics are not included within the chapter. In the view that the chapter begins from the <s>Samanvayādhikaraṇa</s> itself — since this [<s>Ānandamaya</s> topic] is an elaboration of that — 'by the chapter' means 'by the remainder of the chapter': thus there is no contradiction. Since in the fourth <s>pāda</s>, <s>samanvaya</s> (coherent interpretation) is not performed, to refute the opposing view, 'samastena' (by the entire [chapter]) — meaning 'by the whole' — is stated. To counter the objection that 'samastena' (by the entire [chapter]) is inappropriate because <s>samanvaya</s> is not performed in the <s>Devatā</s> and <s>Śūdra</s> topics — 'prāyeṇa' (predominantly) is stated. The word 'prāya' here is an a-ending indeclinable synonymous with the sa-ending form '<s>prāyas</s>.' Therefore, being an original form and the like, in the instrumental case it becomes '<s>prāyeṇa</s>.' For this very reason, in the commentary on the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirnaya</s>, the word 'api' with '<s>prāyaḥ</s>' is used in the sense of 'most/majority' — the word 'api' is an expletive. In the <s>Prameyadīpa</s> too, the indeclinable status of the sa-ending [form] alone is stated.

children.text: prāyeṇānyatraprasiddhānāṃ śabdānāṃ paramātmani samanvayaḥ pradarśyate 'smin pāde / nānyathā tadadṛṣṭe /
children.translated_text: Predominantly, the coherent interpretation (<s>samanvaya</s>) of words that are well-known elsewhere [as denoting other entities] in the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is demonstrated in this <s>pāda</s> (section). Not otherwise, [because] that is not observed [otherwise].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.2:
tarhi adhyāyasyaikārthatvāt pādabhedaḥ kiṃ nibandhana ityataḥ samanvetavyabhedāt samanvaye 'pyavāntarabheda iti bhāvena prathamādhyāprathamapādapratipādyaṃ darśayati - prāyeṇeti // 'asmin'; prathame pāde 'prāyeṇa'; bāhulyena 'anyatra'; viṣṇoranyatra 'prasiddhānāṃ'; śrutyādito lokato vādmapātato rūḍhatvena pratīyamānānāṃ nāmātmakānāṃ 'śabdānāṃ'; 'paramātmani'; viṣṇau niruktaḥ 'samanvayaḥ'; 'pradarśyate'; prapañcyata ityarthaḥ / atrāpi antaradhikaraṇe antaḥsthatvaliṅgasamanvayapratipādanāt avyāptinirāsāya - prāyeṇeti / tattvapradīpe tu eka eva bhāṣye prāyeṇeti śabdaḥ / tasyaivottaratrāpi sambandha ityāśayena "prāyeṇānyatra prasiddhānāṃ śabdānāmiti ca sambandhaḥ"ityuktam / tathā - ānandamayādhikaraṇe liṅgavicārattadapi prāyeṇeti vyāvartyamiti coktam / yadvā - ṭīkāyāmapyāvṛttyabhiprāyeṇaikasyaiva punaruttaratrāpi anvayapradarśanāya pratīkagrahaṇaṃ kṛtamiti na granthavairūpyaṃ kalpyam / ata eva tattvapradīpānusāreṇa "ānandamayanāmnaḥ iti ṭīkāyāmānandamayanāmaśbadaḥ ānandādināmaparo vā yojyaḥ"ityuktaṃ candrikāyām / atha paroktaṃ pādārthaṃ dūṣayati - neti / 'anyathā'; prathame spaṣṭabrahmaliṅgānāṃ śabdānāṃ dvitīyatṛtīyayoraspaṣṭabrahmaliṅgānāṃ samanvayaḥ pratipādyate / tayostu saviśeṣanirviśeṣaviṣayatayā bhedaḥ / caturthapāde tu pradhānasyāśābdatvoktirityevaṃ rūpo 'smaduktādanyaprakāreṇa pādārtho na vācyaḥ ityarthaḥ / kuto netyata āha - taditi / 'tasya'; paroktapādārthaniyamasya 'adṛṣṭeḥ'; etadadhyāyagatapādeṣvadarśanādityarthaḥ / sarvasāṅkaryāditi bhāvaḥ / tacca ṭīkādāvuktam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.2:
Then, since the chapter has a single subject matter, what is the basis for the division into <s>pādas</s> (sections)? — to this, with the purport that even within <s>samanvaya</s> there is a sub-division due to the difference in what is to be coherently interpreted, he shows what the first <s>pāda</s> of the first chapter teaches: '<s>prāyeṇa</s>.' 'In this' — in the first <s>pāda</s>; 'predominantly' — for the most part; 'of words well-known elsewhere' — of words that are nominal in nature, known through <s>Śruti</s> etc., or from common usage, or by superficial impression, as conventionally (<s>rūḍha</s>) denoting [entities] other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'in the <s>Paramātman</s>' — in <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the specific 'coherent interpretation' (<s>samanvaya</s>) 'is demonstrated' — is elaborated: this is the meaning. Here too, since in certain inner topics the <s>samanvaya</s> of the indicator of being-interior (<s>antaḥsthatva</s>) is taught, to remove under-extension — '<s>prāyeṇa</s>' [is stated]. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however — there is only a single occurrence of the word '<s>prāyeṇa</s>' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>; with the intention that it connects to what follows as well — it is stated: 'the connection is with prāyeṇānyatra prasiddhānāṃ śabdānām (predominantly, of words well-known elsewhere).' Likewise — it is also stated: 'In the <s>Ānandamaya</s> topic, since there is consideration of the indicator (<s>liṅga</s>), that too is excluded by prāyeṇa.' Alternatively — in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> too, with the intention of repetition, the same [word <s>prāyeṇa</s>] is taken up again for showing its application later as well — thus no textual inconsistency should be assumed. For this very reason, following the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, in the <s>Candrikā</s> it is stated: 'The word <s>ānandamayanāma</s> in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> should be construed with [the word] <s>ānandādi</s> or another [term].' Now, he refutes the opponent's statement of the purpose of the <s>pāda</s>: 'na' (not). 'Otherwise' — [the opponent says:] in the first [<s>pāda</s>], the <s>samanvaya</s> of words that are clear indicators of <s>Brahman</s> is taught; in the second and third, of words that are unclear indicators of <s>Brahman</s>; and the difference between those two is regarding qualified (<s>saviśeṣa</s>) and unqualified (<s>nirviśeṣa</s>) [<s>Brahman</s>]; in the fourth <s>pāda</s>, the non-Vedic character of <s>Pradhāna</s> is stated — in this manner, i.e., in a way different from what we have stated, the purpose of the <s>pāda</s> should not be stated: this is the meaning. Why not? — to this he says: 'tat' (that). 'Of that' — of the restriction of the <s>pāda</s>'s purpose stated by the opponent; 'because of non-observation' — because it is not observed in the <s>pādas</s> belonging to this chapter: this is the meaning. Because of the complete intermixing [of topics]: this is the purport. And that has been stated in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> etc.

It was stated that inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> is to be undertaken.
And that [<s>Brahman</s>] is [described as]: '<s>Brahman</s> is the tail, the support.'
(<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.2)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.3:
nanvānandamayādhikaraṇamārabhya sarveṣāmadhikaraṇānāmavaśyavaktavye saṅgatipañcake asminnadhikaraṇe lokato 'nyatraprasiddhānandamayaśabdopalakṣitaguṇivāciśabdānāmānandādiguṇavāciśabdānāṃ ca brahmaṇi samanvayakaraṇāt
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.3:
Now, since for all the <s>adhikaraṇas</s> (topics) beginning from the <s>Ānandamaya</s> topic, among the five types of connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) that must necessarily be stated, in this topic — since the <s>samanvaya</s> (coherent interpretation) of words denoting the possessor of qualities indicated by the word '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' (well-known elsewhere in common usage) and of words denoting qualities such as <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) etc. is performed in <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: asyāstu śāstre 'dhyāye pāde cāntarbhāvarūpā saṅgatiḥ / tathāpi ānandamayasya viṣṇutvasamarthane kā pūrvasaṅgatirityato 'vyavahitapūrvādhikaraṇenaiva saṅgatirvaktavyeti niyamābhāvāt
children.translated_text: the connection of this [topic] with the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), the <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter), and the <s>pāda</s> (section) is in the form of inclusion. Even so, for establishing the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the <s>Ānandamaya</s>, what is the prior connection? — since there is no rule that the connection must be stated only with the immediately preceding topic,

children.text: vyavahitapūrveṇa jijñāsādhikaraṇena tadviṣayeṇa ca asyānantaryalakṣaṇalakṣitāmākṣepikīṃ saṅgatiṃ tāvaddarśayati - brahmeti // uktaṃ jijñāsādhikaraṇe iti śeṣaḥ / 'tacceti'; / yajjijñāsyatayā pratijñātaṃ brahma tadevetyarthaḥ / yadvā - prakṛtānusandhānārthaścaśabdaḥ / itītyanantaraṃ 'śrutau'; iti śeṣaḥ / 'ānandamayāvayavarūpamiti'; ānandamayākhyasya kasyacitpucchākhyāvayavabhūtaṃ pratīyata ityarthaḥ/ nanu brahmaṇo 'vayavatvoktāvapi kimarthamānandamayasya viṣṇutvasamarthanamityata āha - na hīti/ hiśabdo hetau/ 'ata'; ityāvartate / 'tacca'; ityādi 'ityata āha'; ityantaṃ saṅgatiprayojanobhayaparatayā vyākhyeyam / na hītyetattadupapādakam / yojanā tu - yato 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā'; iti śrutau jijñāsyatayoktaṃ brahma ānandamayākhyasya kasyacidavayavarūpaṃ 'pratīyate'; ucyate yataśca anyāṅgatayā jijñāsyatve 'pi 'avayavinam'; ānandamayaṃ vinā 'avayavamātrasya'; avayavasyaiva kevalasya brahmaṇo na pṛthak 'jñeyatā'; jijñāsyatā sambhavati / amukhyatvāt / nāpi jijñāsāyā eva tyāgo yujyate / "tadvijijñāsasva"(tai. u. 3-1.) iti śrutivihitatvādityevaṃ śaṅkā prāptā / ataḥ śaṅkārūpasaṅgatisadbhāvāt atrānandamayasya viṣṇvanyatvapakṣe brahmajijñāsākṣepāt viṣṇutvapakṣe ca tatsamādhānāt evaṃ ca pūrvapakṣasiddhāntayoḥ phalasadbhāvācca 'ato'; brahmajijñāsāsiddhyartham 'ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt'; ityānandamayasya viṣṇutvam 'āha'; samarthayati sūtrakāra iti /
children.translated_text: he first shows the connection — characterized by immediate sequence and in the form of objection (<s>ākṣepikī</s>) — with the <s>Jijñāsādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Inquiry), which is a non-adjacent predecessor and which pertains to the same subject: 'brahma.' The remainder is: 'it was stated in the <s>Jijñāsādhikaraṇa</s>.' 'Tat ca' — and that which was asserted as <s>Brahman</s> to be inquired into — is the meaning of 'that very.' Alternatively, the word 'ca' is for resuming the topic under discussion. After 'iti,' 'in <s>Śruti</s>' is the remainder. 'As having the form of a part of the <s>Ānandamaya</s>' — meaning: that which bears the name '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' appears to be a part called '<s>puccha</s>' (tail). Now, even when the part-hood of <s>Brahman</s> is stated, what is the purpose of establishing the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the <s>Ānandamaya</s>? — to this he says: 'na hi' (for not). The word 'hi' indicates the reason. 'Ataḥ' (from this) is carried forward. 'Tat ca' etc. up to 'ityata āha' should be interpreted as pertaining to both the connection and its purpose. 'Na hi' is the substantiation of that. The construction is: since 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' (Brahman is the tail, the support) — in the <s>Śruti</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> stated as to-be-inquired-into 'appears' — is stated — 'as having the form of a part of something called <s>Ānandamaya</s>'; and since, even though it is an object of inquiry as a subordinate part, 'without the whole' — without the <s>Ānandamaya</s> — 'of the mere part alone' — of <s>Brahman</s> which is merely a part — there is no separate 'knowability' — fitness for inquiry — because of its non-primary status; nor is the abandonment of inquiry itself appropriate, because it is enjoined by <s>Śruti</s> in '<s>tad vijijñāsasva</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 3.1) (seek to know that) — thus the objection arises. Therefore, since such an objection-form connection exists, in this [topic], in the view that the <s>Ānandamaya</s> is other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, there arises an objection against the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>; and in the view that [the <s>Ānandamaya</s>] is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that [objection] is resolved. And thus, since both the prima facie view and the established conclusion yield a result — 'therefore' (<s>ataḥ</s>), for the establishment of the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> 'establishes' — argues for — the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the <s>Ānandamaya</s> through '<s>ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s>' (the one consisting of bliss, because of repetition).

children.text: "tasmādvā etasmādvijñānamayāt / anyo 'ntara ātmānandamayaḥ / tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ / sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva / tasya puruṣavidhatām / anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ / tasya priyameva śiraḥ / modo dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ / pramoda uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ / ānanda ātmā / brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā"(tai.u. 2-5-2.) iti taittirīyavākyasyāyamarthaḥ / 'tasmāt'; ātmapadoditāt 'etasmāt'; jīvaśarīragatāt vijñānapūrṇatvāt vijñānamayaśabdavācyāt viṣṇoḥ ananyo 'pyanyaśabdoktaḥ 'ānandamayaḥ'; ānandapūrṇatvādānandamayaśabdavācyaḥ 'ātmā'; nārāyaṇaḥ 'antaro'; vijñānamayasyāntaḥsthitaḥ 'tena'; ānandamayena 'eṣaḥ'; vijñānamayaśabdavācyo vāsudevaḥ 'pūrṇaḥ'; niśchidratvena pūritaḥ / vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / 'sa eṣa'; ānandamayaḥ 'puruṣavidha eva'; puruṣākāra eva / 'tasya'; ānandamayasya śarīrasthānīyasya puruṣākāratām 'anu'; anusṛtya 'ayaṃ'; vijñānamayaḥ śarīrasthānīyaḥ 'puruṣavidhaḥ'; tasmātprādurbhūtaḥ,
children.translated_text: 'From that very one — from this <s>vijñānamaya</s> (the one consisting of knowledge) — there is another, an inner Self consisting of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>). By that, this one is filled. That one indeed is of human form. Following his human form, this one [too] is of human form. Of that, <s>priya</s> (delight) alone is the head; <s>moda</s> (joy) is the right wing; <s>pramoda</s> (ecstasy) is the left wing; <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) is the self; <s>Brahman</s> is the tail, the support.' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.2) — This is the meaning of the <s>Taittirīya</s> passage: 'From that' — from the one spoken of by the word '<s>ātman</s>' (Self); 'from this' — from the one present in the <s>jīva</s>'s body, who is called '<s>vijñānamaya</s>' because of being full of knowledge; though non-different from [that <s>Viṣṇu</s>], He is spoken of with the word 'other' (<s>anya</s>); the '<s>ānandamaya</s>' — called '<s>ānandamaya</s>' because of being full of bliss; the 'inner Self' — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, situated within the <s>vijñānamaya</s>; 'by that' — by the <s>ānandamaya</s>; 'this' — <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who is denoted by the word '<s>vijñānamaya</s>'; 'is filled' — is made complete without any gap. The particle 'vai' indicates well-known [fact]. 'That' — this <s>ānandamaya</s> — 'is of human form indeed' — is of human shape. 'Of that' — of the <s>ānandamaya</s>, who occupies the position of the body; 'following' (<s>anu</s>) his 'human form'; 'this' — the <s>vijñānamaya</s>, who occupies the position of the body [within]; 'is of human form' — has arisen from that,
The prior [sheaths] are filled by the later ones, without any gap, in every respect;
All are of human form, and the prior arises from the later. //

children.text: iti taittirīyabhāṣyokteḥ / 'tasya'; ānandamayasya viṣṇoḥ avayavabhūtaṃ 'pareyaṃ priyanāmakam'; iti bhāṣyokteḥ / parairuttamaiḥ devaiḥ prāpyatvātpriyaśabdavācyaṃ yatsukhaṃ tattasya 'śiraḥ'; tadevānandamayākhyasya jīvaśarīrasya parairanyairupakartṛbhiḥ prāpyatvāt priyanāmakamupakārajanyavaiṣayikasukhākhyaṃ yacchiraḥ tatsthaṃ ca / evamānandamayākhyasya viṣṇoḥ ye dakṣiṇottarabāhumadhyadehāḥ modapramodakāritvānandatvanimittairmoda-
children.translated_text: — Thus, from the statement in the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s>. 'Of that' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called <s>ānandamaya</s> — 'this, which is a part, is named <s>priya</s> (delight)': thus from the statement in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. The happiness that is denoted by the word '<s>priya</s>' because of being attainable by the supreme, excellent gods — that is His 'head' (<s>śiras</s>). That very [happiness] — because in the <s>jīva</s>-body called <s>ānandamaya</s>, it is named '<s>priya</s>' due to its being attainable by superior beings — the happiness arising from benefaction, known as experiential pleasure — which is the head — is situated there. Likewise, of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called <s>ānandamaya</s>, the right and left arms and middle body — which are the causes of <s>moda</s> (joy), <s>pramoda</s> (ecstasy), and <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) respectively, and have those names due to those reasons —

children.text: pramodānandanāmānaḥ te ānandamayākhyajīvaśarīrasya dakṣiṇottarapakṣātmanāmāno dakṣiṇasavyabāhumadhyadehāḥ/ 'modo'; bhoganimittakaḥ 'pramodaḥ'; "tadviśeṣotthaḥ"ityaitareyabhāṣyokteḥ /
children.translated_text: named <s>moda</s>, <s>pramoda</s>, and <s>ānanda</s>, [these] are the right and left wings and the self of the <s>jīva</s>-body called <s>ānandamaya</s>, i.e., the right and left arms and the middle body. '<s>Moda</s>' — caused by enjoyment; '<s>pramoda</s>' — from the statement in the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s>: 'arising from a special [form of enjoyment]';
That which arises from sense objects is called '<s>mud</s>'; that [which arises] from an excellent object is '<s>pramud</s>';
The happiness that is of the nature of one's own essential being is called '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss). //

children.text: iti bṛhadbhāṣyokteśca / apakṛṣṭaviṣayodbhūtatvaprakṛṣṭaviṣayotthatvajīvasvarūpānandatvanimittairmodapramodānandanāmānasteṣu sthitāśca / evamānandamayākhyasya viṣṇoḥ 'pucchaṃ'; pratiṣṭhati gacchati loka ābhyāmiti vyutpattyā pratiṣṭhāpadokto yaḥ pādākhyo 'vayavaḥ tadbrahma 'brahmasṛṣṭyā tu bṛṃhayet'; iti taittirīyabhāṣyoktarītyā sṛṣṭyādikriyayā viśvaguṇavṛddhikaratvādbrahmaśabdavācyaḥ sa evānandamayākhyajīvaśarīrasya yat pucchaṃ yaḥ pādākhyo 'vayavaḥ tatsthite brahmākhye pradhānavāyau sthitaḥ / anena kośāvayavasya brahmaśabdavācyatvaṃ brahmaśabdavācyapradhānavāyvadhiṣṭhānatvanimittaṃ, pradhānavāyorbrahmaśabdavācyatvaṃ tu parabrahmādhiṣṭhānatvādityuktaṃ bhavati / anenānandamayādiśabdavācyasya viṣṇoravayava-
children.translated_text: — thus, because of the statement in the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> as well. And those named <s>moda</s> (delight), <s>pramoda</s> (extreme delight), and <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) are situated in them [the sheaths], because of being produced from an inferior object, because of arising from a superior object, and because of being the inherent bliss of the <s>jīva</s> respectively. Thus, of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called <s>Ānandamaya</s>, 'the tail' (<s>puccham</s>) — by the etymological derivation '<s>pratiṣṭhati</s>' (it rests), '<s>gacchati</s>' (it goes), 'the world [proceeds] from these two' — that which is called a 'foot' (<s>pāda</s>), a constituent part, as mentioned by the word '<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>' (foundation) — that is <s>Brahman</s>. By the method stated in the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s> — 'but one should augment (<s>bṛṃhayet</s>) <s>Brahman</s> through creation' — because of increasing the qualities of the universe through the activity of creation and the like, [that entity] is expressible by the word <s>Brahman</s>. That very one — whatever is the 'tail,' the constituent called 'foot,' of the body of the <s>jīva</s> called <s>Ānandamaya</s> — is situated in the chief <s>Vāyu</s> called <s>Brahman</s>, which abides [as the foundation]. By this, it is stated that the expressibility of a sheath-constituent by the word <s>Brahman</s> has its cause in being presided over by the chief <s>Vāyu</s> who is expressible by the word <s>Brahman</s>; while the expressibility of the chief <s>Vāyu</s> by the word <s>Brahman</s> is because of being presided over by the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. By this, of <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is expressible by words such as <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the like, the parts —

children.text: bhūtāḥ ye priyādayaḥ te viṣṇvabhinnāḥ ye cānandamayādijīvakośāvayavāḥ priyādayaste pratiśarīraṃ bhinnā iti dvividhāḥ priyādaya ityuktaṃ bhavati / yathoktaṃ candrikāyām - ye jīvābhimanyamānānandamayādikośāvayavāḥ priyādayaste pratiśarīraṃ bhinnāḥ, na te ānandamayādyākhyasya viṣṇoravayavāḥ / ye ca bhagavato 'vayavāḥ priyādayo na te pratiśarīraṃ bhinnā kintvabhinnā iti jīvasvarūpasyānandasya hṛdayākhyamadhyagatatvātkośamadhyadehatvaṃ svarūpadehasya jaḍāvayavatvaṃ cāmukhyaṃ yujyate / yadyapi bhāṣye 'śiro nārāyaṇaḥ'; ityudāhariṣyamāṇavacanaparyālocanayādmanandamayākhyo nārāyaṇaḥ punarnārāyaṇādirūpeṇa pañcadhā bhinnaḥ śiraḥprabhṛtyavayavātmanā tiṣṭhatīti pratīyate / taittirīyabhāṣye tu - priyādīnāmanandamayāvayavatvam / tathāpi priyādisukhaviśeṣadehasthitabrahmākhyapradhānavāyugatānāṃ nārāyaṇādirūpāṇāmeva ānandamayākhyaviṣṇvavayavatvasambhavātteṣāmeva /
children.translated_text: those [parts] such as <s>priya</s> (the dear) and the like that are [parts] of <s>Viṣṇu</s> are non-different from <s>Viṣṇu</s>; while those <s>priya</s> and the like that are the sheath-constituents of the <s>jīva</s> [called] <s>Ānandamaya</s> and so on differ from body to body — thus the <s>priya</s> and the like are of two kinds: this is stated. As said in the <s>Candrikā</s>: those sheath-constituents, <s>priya</s> and the like, belonging to [the sheath] <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the like, which are claimed by the <s>jīvas</s>, differ from body to body — they are not the parts of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the like. And those <s>priya</s> and the like that are the parts of the Lord do not differ from body to body, but are rather non-different. Since the bliss that is the inherent nature of the <s>jīva</s> is situated in the middle [of the body] called the heart, the being-in-the-middle-of-the-sheath-body [is possible]; and the having-insentient-parts of the essential body is figurative — [both] are justified. Even though in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, by considering the statement 'the head is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' which will be cited [later], it is understood that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> called <s>Ānandamaya</s> is again divided fivefold in the form of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and others, abiding as the parts beginning with the head; nevertheless, in the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s>, the <s>priya</s> and the like are said to be the parts of <s>Ānandamaya</s>. Even so, since the being-parts-of-<s>Viṣṇu</s>-called-<s>Ānandamaya</s> is possible only for those in the forms of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like, which have reached the chief <s>Vāyu</s> called <s>Brahman</s> situated in the body where the particular bliss called <s>priya</s> and the like [resides] — of those alone,
the supreme one is called by the name <s>priya</s> (the dear).
Those called <s>moda</s> (delight) and <s>pramoda</s> (extreme delight) — because of delighting and because of extremely delighting.

children.text: dehasthavāyusaṃsthaṃ ca brahma sṛṣṭyā tu bṛṃhayet // iti /
children.translated_text: And [the form of] <s>Brahman</s> situated in the <s>Vāyu</s> dwelling in the body should be augmented through creation. // Thus [in the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s>]. //

children.text: taittirīyabhāṣyoktarītyā priyādiśabdavācyatvasyāpi sambhavānna virodhaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - priyaśirastvādinaye "śravaṇotthaṃ priyaṃ, darśanottho modaḥ, bhogotthaḥ pramodaḥ"iti padatrayasyārthāntaramuktam / tathā tatraiva "'abhāvaṃ bādariḥ'; iti sūtreṇa 'priyāpriye'; (chāṃ. 8-12-1.) iti śrutisthapriyaśabdena 'pareyaṃ priyanāmakam'; iti taittirīyachāndogyabhāṣyayoruktatvātparaprāpyasukhasāmānyavācakena prākṛtaṃ sukhaṃ grāhyamiti sūcitam"iti coktam / idaṃ tvavadhayam - paridṛśyamānamannamayaṃ śarīram / tadantaḥ prāṇamayo dehaḥ tadantarmanomayo dehaḥ / tadantarvijñānamayo dehaḥ / tadantarānandamayo 'sti / eteṣu pañcasu dehākhyakośeṣu tattacchabdavācyāni puruṣākārāṇi aniruddhapradyumnasaṅkarṣaṇavāsudevanārāyaṇarūpāṇi dehadehibhāvena vartanta iti /
children.translated_text: — in the manner stated in the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s>, since the expressibility of the <s>priya</s> and the like by their respective names is also possible, there is no contradiction. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, according to the view that <s>priya</s> is the head [of <s>Ānandamaya</s>] and so forth, another meaning is stated for the three words [<s>priya</s>, <s>moda</s>, <s>pramoda</s>]: '<s>priya</s> arises from hearing, <s>moda</s> from seeing, <s>pramoda</s> from enjoyment.' Likewise, in the same [<s>Tattvapradīpa</s>], it is said: 'By the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>abhāvaṃ Bādariḥ</s>" (absence, [says] <s>Bādari</s>), through the word <s>priya</s> occurring in the <s>Śruti</s> "<s>priyāpriye</s>" (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.12.1), since in both the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Chāndogya Bhāṣya</s> it is said "the supreme one is called by the name <s>priya</s>," [the word <s>priya</s>] being a general designator of the bliss attainable through the supreme, the material bliss is to be included — this is indicated.' But this should be noted: the outwardly visible body is the <s>Annamaya</s> (food-made) [sheath]. Within that is the <s>Prāṇamaya</s> (breath-made) body; within that is the <s>Manomaya</s> (mind-made) body; within that is the <s>Vijñānamaya</s> (knowledge-made) body; within that exists the <s>Ānandamaya</s> (bliss-made). In these five sheaths called bodies, the person-shaped [forms] expressible by their respective names — in the forms of <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — exist in the relationship of body and embodied [soul].
Thus the form of the constituents of <s>Ānandamaya</s> is understood.

children.text: na hyavayavinaṃ vinā avayavamātrasya jñeyatetyata āha // -
children.translated_text: For, without the whole (<s>avayavin</s>), the mere parts (<s>avayava</s>) cannot be known — therefore he says: //
<s>Ānandamaya</s> (the bliss-made one), because of repetition. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.12 |
<s>Ānandamaya</s> is either the group [of beings] beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, or <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), or <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.4:
evaṃ saṅgatiṃ phalaṃ coktvā viṣayasaṃśayau darśayati - ānandamaya iti // ānandamaya ityupalakṣakapadena viṣayo darśitaḥ / brahmādirityatra brahmā ādiryasya jīvasaṅghasyeti vigrahaḥ / brahmā caturmukhaḥ, ādiśabdena rudrendrabṛhaspatimukhā devāstattaddehāgatajīvāśca gṛhyante / prakṛtiśabdena citprakṛtiḥ / 'iti saṃśaya'; iti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.4: Having thus stated the connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) and the result (<s>phala</s>), he shows the subject (<s>viṣaya</s>) and the doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>): '<s>Ānandamaya</s>.' // By the word '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' as an indicative term, the subject is shown. In '<s>brahmādiḥ</s>' (beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>), the compound analysis is: <s>Brahmā</s> is the first of which — of that group of <s>jīvas</s>. <s>Brahmā</s> is the four-faced one; by the word 'ādi' (and the like), the gods headed by <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, as well as the <s>jīvas</s> entering their respective bodies, are included. The word '<s>Prakṛti</s>' means the sentient <s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>cit-prakṛti</s>). 'Thus is the doubt' (<s>iti saṃśaya</s>) is the remainder.
From the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' [the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s>] accrues to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>; and because of the name '<s>Śatānanda</s>' (having a hundred blisses).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.5:
atra sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣānāha - brahmaśabdāditi // ānandamayamadhikṛtyadāhṛte 'asti brahmeti cedveda'; (tai.u. 2-6-1.) ityādau śrutādbrahmaśabdādityarthaḥ / brahmaśabdasya anyatrāpi vṛtteḥ kathaṃ tena caturmukhasyānandamayatvaniśca ityato yuktyantaramāha - śateti / co 'pyarthe samuccaye / "te ye śataṃ prajāpaterānandāḥ, sa eko brahmaṇa ānandaḥ"(tai.u. 2-8-4.) iti vākyādarthātsūcitena śatānandanāmnetyarthaḥ / yadvā - ānandamayaśabdasamānārthakena hiraṇyagarbhe vidyamānena śatānandanāmnetyarthaḥ/ 'prāptiḥ'; ānandamayatvasyeti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - hiraṇyagarbhasya ānandamayatvasya prāptirityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.5: Here he states the prima facie views (<s>pūrvapakṣas</s>) with reasons: 'from the word <s>Brahman</s>.' // The meaning is: from the word <s>Brahman</s> heard in the passage '<s>asti brahma iti cedveda</s>' (if one knows that <s>Brahman</s> exists) (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.6.1) and the like, which are cited in the context of <s>Ānandamaya</s>. Since the word <s>Brahman</s> is used elsewhere as well, how does it establish the <s>Ānandamaya</s> status of the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>]? Hence he gives another reason: '<s>śata</s>' (<s>Śatānanda</s>). The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'api' (also), for aggregation. And thus: from the meaning conveyed by the passage 'Those hundred [blisses] that belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>, that is one bliss of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.8.4), [accrual is] through the name <s>Śatānanda</s> that is thereby indicated: this is the meaning. Or: through the name <s>Śatānanda</s> — which exists in <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and is synonymous with the word <s>Ānandamaya</s>: this is the meaning. '<s>Prāptiḥ</s>' (accrual) — 'of the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s>' is the remainder. And thus: the accrual of the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> [belongs] to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — this is the construction.
Because of having eight forms (<s>aṣṭamūrtitva</s>), and because of being stated in the Sun, [the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> accrues] to <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.6:
evamekaṃ pūrvapakṣamabhidhāya anyamāha - aṣṭamūrtitvāditi // caśabdo rudrasya ceti sambadhyate / prāptirityasyānukarṣaṇārtho vā tathā ca - rudrasya cānandamayatvaprāptiḥ kutaḥ? sūrye proktatvāt / 'yaścāsāvāditye'; (tai.u. 2-8-5.) ityānandamayasya sūrye sthiteḥ uktatvādrudrasya ca sūryādyaṣṭaśarīratvādityarthaḥ / tathā ca - rūdraliṅgasya ānandamaye śrutatvāt ānandamayo rudra evepi bhāvaḥ / rudrasya sūryādyaṣṭapratimatvaṃ ca -
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.6: Having thus stated one prima facie view, he states another: 'because of having eight forms.' The word 'ca' connects with 'of <s>Rudra</s> also.' Or it is for the purpose of carrying forward '<s>prāptiḥ</s>' (accrual). And thus: the accrual of the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> also to <s>Rudra</s> — whence? 'Because of being stated in the Sun.' Since the <s>Ānandamaya</s> is stated as situated in the Sun in [the passage] 'and he who is in the Sun' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.8.5), and because <s>Rudra</s> has the Sun and the like as eight bodies: this is the meaning. And thus: since a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>Rudra</s> is heard in the <s>Ānandamaya</s> [context], the purport is that the <s>Ānandamaya</s> is <s>Rudra</s> alone. And <s>Rudra</s>'s having the Sun and the like as eight forms —

children.text: sūryo jalaṃ mahī vahnirvāyurākāśa eva ca /
children.translated_text: the Sun, water, earth, fire, wind, space,
the initiated one, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and <s>Soma</s> — these are [his] bodies in order. //
— this is established from the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> passage.
Likewise for others as well.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.7:
pūrvapakṣāntaraṃ darśayati - evamiti // uktābhyām 'anyeṣām'; indrabṛhaspatyādīnāmapi 'evam'; uktaprakāreṇa svāvarasūryādyadhiṣṭhātṛtvādinā ānandamayatvaprāptirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.7: He shows yet another prima facie view: 'likewise' (<s>evam</s>). // 'For others' — for <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and the like, who are different from those mentioned — 'likewise' — in the manner stated, the accrual of the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> [is possible] because of their presiding over lower entities such as the Sun and the like: this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: 'My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 14.3) — from this word '<s>Brahman</s>,' and because of the [capacity for] becoming-many, [the status accrues] to <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.8:
sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣāntaramāha - mameti / yojanā tu citprakṛtervānandamayatvaprāptiḥ / kutaḥ? brahmaśabdāt/ ānandamaye śrutasya brahmaśabdasya 'mama yonirmahadbrahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmyaham'; iti gītāyāṃ citprakṛtau prayogāditi/ smṛtau - mahat brahmeti bhinne pade / tathā ca mahat brahmaśabdavācyā lakṣmīḥ mama yoniḥ garbhādhānārthaṃ bhāryā / tasmin brahmaṇi prakṛtau ahaṃ garbhaṃ dadhāmi dadha ityarthaḥ / arjunaṃ prati kṛṣṇavākyametat / kathaṃ sāvakāśena brahmaśabdena prakṛterānandamayatvaniścaya ityato hetvantaramāha - 'bahubhāvāt'; bahurūpatvācceti / co hetusamuccaye / tathā ca 'so 'kāmayata / bahu syām'; (tai.u. 2-6-2.) ityānandamayasya 'bahubhāvāt'; bahubhāvaśravaṇāt tadabhimānitvāccitprakṛteḥ svābhimanyamānavikārijaḍadvārā bahubhāvasambhavādityarthaḥ / evaṃ prakṛterityasya jaḍaprakṛterityarthāśrayeṇa pūrvapakṣāntaramapi draṣṭavyam / yojanā tu jaḍaprakṛtervānandamayatvaprāptiḥ / kutaḥ? abhimānitvena vinā sākṣādbahubhāvādeveti /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.8: He states yet another prima facie view with reason: '<s>mama</s>' (my). The construction is: or the accrual of the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> to <s>cit-Prakṛti</s> (sentient <s>Prakṛti</s>). Whence? From the word '<s>Brahman</s>.' Because of the usage of the word <s>Brahman</s>, heard in the <s>Ānandamaya</s> [context], in reference to <s>cit-Prakṛti</s> in the <s>Gītā</s>: 'My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>; in that I place the seed' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 14.3). In the <s>Smṛti</s>, '<s>mahat brahma</s>' is two separate words. And thus: she who is expressible by the words '<s>mahat brahma</s>' — <s>Lakṣmī</s> — is 'my womb' — my wife for the purpose of bearing the embryo. 'In that <s>Brahman</s>' — in <s>Prakṛti</s> — 'I place the seed' — I deposit [it]: this is the meaning. This is the speech of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> addressed to <s>Arjuna</s>. How can the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s> be ascertained through the word <s>Brahman</s> which has alternative referents? Hence he gives another reason: 'because of becoming-many' (<s>bahubhāvāt</s>) — because of having many forms. The word 'ca' is for aggregation of reasons. And thus: since the <s>Ānandamaya</s> is heard as 'becoming many' in 'He desired: may I become many' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.6.2), and since <s>cit-Prakṛti</s>, through the channel of the insentient [matter] that it presides over and transforms, is capable of becoming many — this is the meaning. Thus, with the meaning of <s>jaḍa-Prakṛti</s> (insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>) as the basis [for the word <s>Prakṛti</s>], yet another prima facie view should be seen. The construction is: or the accrual of the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> to insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>. Whence? Because of directly becoming many without the mediation of a presiding [deity].

Since the root <s>bṛh</s> is used in [the senses of] class (<s>jāti</s>), <s>jīva</s>, <s>Kamalāsana</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), and [other] groups of words — from the word <s>Brahman</s> itself, [the status accrues] to all <s>jīvas</s>; and because of being <s>Annamaya</s> (food-made) and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.9:
sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣāntaramāha - bṛha jātīti / tattaddehagatasarvajīvānāṃ vā ānandamayatvaprāptiḥ / kutaḥ? jīvānāṃ brahmaśabdāt / jīvavācibrahmaśabdādityarthaḥ / na tatra pṛthaghgheturgaveṣaṇīya ityevaśabdārthaḥ / kuto brahmaśabdasya jīvavācitvamityata uktam - bṛha jātīti / bṛhadhātuḥ jātyādiṣu vartata ityarthaḥ / itītyanantaraṃ dhātuvyākhyānāditi śeṣaḥ / brahmaśabdasya sādhāraṇatvādaniścāyakatvamityata āha - annamayatvādeśceti / idaṃ cāvartate, tatra dvitīyo vipariṇamyate / ādiśabdo bhinnakramaḥ / tena prāṇādikaṃ gṛhyate / yathākramaśca caśabda uktānuktahetusamuccaye / tathā ca - na kevalaṃ brahmaśabdāt, kintu, yato jīvānām 'annarasamayaḥ'; 'prāṇamayaḥ'; ityuktānnādimayatvāt annādivikāradehādyabhimānitvādannamayatvādi prāptam atastatprāyapaṭhitatvāccānandamayatvaprāptiriti yojanā / atra hiraṇyagarbhādīnāṃ jīvatve 'pi devatvavivakṣayā pṛthaguktiḥ / ata eva tattvapradīpe - "brahmādiryasya devatāsaṅghasya"ityapi brahmādirityasya vigraho darśitaḥ / tatrāpi hiraṇyagarbharudrayoratiprasiddhatvādvakṣyamāṇakrameṇa pṛthaguktiḥ / atha indrādīnāṃ "brahmā śivaḥ sureśādyāḥ"iti vacanoktakrameṇa kṣaradevoktyanantaramakṣarāyāḥ prakṛteruktiḥ / atha atyalpapratibhānatvāt dṛśyamānadehābhimānijīvānāmiti dhyeyam /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.9: He states yet another prima facie view with reason: '<s>bṛh</s> in class' (<s>bṛha jāti</s>). // Or the accrual of the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> to all <s>jīvas</s> entering their respective bodies. Whence? From the word <s>Brahman</s> being applicable to <s>jīvas</s>. The meaning of the word 'eva' is: no separate reason need be sought for this. Why is the word <s>Brahman</s> applicable to <s>jīvas</s>? Hence it is said: '<s>bṛha jāti</s>' — the root <s>bṛh</s> operates in the sense of class and the like: this is the meaning. After 'iti,' 'from the explanation of the verbal root' is the remainder. Since the word <s>Brahman</s> is thus common [to many referents], it is inconclusive — hence he says: 'and because of being <s>Annamaya</s> and the like.' And this [word 'ca'] recurs; therein the second one is modified. The word 'ādi' has a different sequential order — by that, <s>Prāṇamaya</s> and the like are included. The word 'ca' is respectively for aggregating stated and unstated reasons in sequence. And thus: not only from the word <s>Brahman</s>, but since <s>jīvas</s> have the attribute of being <s>Annamaya</s>, <s>Prāṇamaya</s>, and the like, as stated in '<s>annarasamayaḥ</s>' (made of the essence of food) and '<s>prāṇamayaḥ</s>' (made of breath), and since [<s>jīvas</s>] have the attribute of presiding over the bodies that are transformations of food and the like — therefore, since the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> is accrued because of [their status] being mostly read along with these, and because of being <s>Annamaya</s> and the like: this is the construction. Here, even though <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and the others are <s>jīvas</s>, they are mentioned separately with the intention of discussing their divinity. Hence in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> too, the compound analysis of '<s>brahmādiḥ</s>' is shown as 'of which group of deities <s>Brahmā</s> is the first.' There too, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and <s>Rudra</s> are mentioned separately because of their extreme prominence, in the order that will be stated. Then, <s>Indra</s> and the others [are mentioned] in the sequence of the statement '<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the lord of gods, and the rest.' After the mention of the perishable gods, the mention of the imperishable <s>Prakṛti</s> follows. Then, because of exceedingly meager capacity, the <s>jīvas</s> who preside over the visible bodies [are mentioned] — this should be noted.

BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.10:
siddhāntayati - tathāpīti // yadyapyevamanyeṣāṃ prāptiḥ, tathāpi atra ye ānandamayaśabdenocyante na te hiraṇyagarbhādaya ityarthaḥ / kastarhītyāśaṅkate - kintviti / uttaramāha - viṣṇureveti / ya ucyate sa viṣṇurevetyanvayaḥ / anenodāhṛtānandamaya iti sūtrapratijñābhāgasya saṅgatyarthamanvayārthaṃ samanvayasūtrodāhṛto vidheyasamarpakaḥ 'tattu'; iti pratijñābhāgo vyākhyāto bhavati / kuta ānandamayo viṣṇurevetyataḥ pravṛttaṃ sautraṃ hetuṃ vyācaṣṭe - tadeveti / ityādiṣu vākyeṣu tasminviṣṇāveva prasiddhasya mukhyārthatvenoktasya brahmaśabdasya tasminnānandamaye ānandamayaṃ pratyudāhṛte 'asanneva'; iti śloke 'abhyāsāt'; asakṛcchravaṇādityarthaḥ / abhyāsādityanantaraṃ 'viṣṇau tātparyāvagamāt'; iti śeṣaḥ / aprayojakatvaśaṅkāvāraṇāya brahmaśabdasyānyatra niravakāśatvajñāpanāya tasmin prasiddheti eveti coktam/ ādiśabdena 'paramaṃ yo mahadbrahma'; 'vāsudevātparaḥ
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.10: He gives the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>): 'even so' (<s>tathāpi</s>). // Even though the accrual [of <s>Ānandamaya</s> status] to others is thus [possible], 'even so,' 'they' — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and the rest — 'are not' those who 'are denoted by the word <s>Ānandamaya</s>' here: this is the meaning. 'Then who?' — anticipating [this question], he says: 'but rather' (<s>kintu</s>). He answers: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' He who is denoted is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone: this is the construction. By this, the thesis-portion of the <s>sūtra</s> cited as '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' is explained for the purpose of coherence (<s>saṅgati</s>). [Also,] the thesis-portion 'tattu' (but that) cited in the <s>Samanvaya</s>-<s>sūtra</s>, which conveys the predicate, is explained. Why is the <s>Ānandamaya</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone? — to this, he explains the <s>sūtra</s>-reason that has been introduced: '<s>tadeva</s>' (that alone). In passages such as these, because of the repeated hearing (<s>abhyāsa</s>) of the word <s>Brahman</s> — which is well-known and stated in its primary meaning as referring to that <s>Viṣṇu</s> — in reference to that <s>Ānandamaya</s>, [and] in the verse '<s>asanneva</s>' cited with reference to <s>Ānandamaya</s>: this is the meaning. After '<s>abhyāsāt</s>' (because of repetition), 'because of the ascertainment of purport in <s>Viṣṇu</s>' is the remainder. To ward off the suspicion of purposelessness, and to make known that the word <s>Brahman</s> has no scope elsewhere, it is said 'well-known in Him' and 'eva' (alone). By the word 'ādi,' [the passages] 'the Supreme, the great <s>Brahman</s>' and '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is the highest'

BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.11:
'brahmaśabdaḥ'; iti smṛtau 'pare'; pūrṇe iti hetugarbhaviśeṣaṇam / vāśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / tathā ca yato viṣṇuḥ paraḥ, ataḥ 'pare'; viṣṇāveva brahmaśabdo mukhyatayā 'iṣyate'; aṅgīkriyate prāmāṇikaiḥ / na tu viṣṇoḥ 'anyatra'; hiraṇyagarbhādiṣvapītyarthaḥ / kuta ityatasteṣāṃ brahmaśabdamukhyārthatvābhāve hetumāha - 'pare'; anye yasmādasampūrṇā iti / tarhi 'tasmādetadbrahma nāma rūpamannaṃ ca jāyate'; (mu. 1-1-9.) 'dve brahmaṇī veditavye'; (maitri.u. 6-22.) 'brahmāṇi jīvāḥ sarve 'pi'; ityādau brahmaśabdasteṣu kathamiṣyata ityata āha - kvacidanyatreṣṭo 'pi brahmaśabdaḥ 'upacāreṇa'; paramamukhyavṛttyanyamukhyavṛttyaiva bhavediti / 'brahma'; iti bhāgavatasmṛtyarthaḥ / prāgevoktaḥ / madhye ātmapadopetasādhāraṇasmṛtyupādānanimittaṃ tu abhyāsādityasya 'anyontara ātmā'; (tai. u. 2-2-1.) ityādau brahmavācakātmaśabdābhyāsādityapyartho varṇanīya iti jñāpanamityuktaṃ candrikāyām / 'vāsudevātmakam'; iti vyāsasmṛtivākyaṃ tu 'buddhyāvihiṃsan puṣpairvā praṇavena samarcayet'; iti pūrvavākyena saha yojanīyam / atra hi vāsudevātmakaṃ brahmetyāderbhagavān brahmeti pratīyate iti nyāyadīpokteḥ / 'yatiḥ'; 'vāsudevātmakaṃ'; kṛṣṇākhyaṃ brahma 'buddhyā'; manasā samarcayedityanena yatīnāṃ mānasapūjocyate puṣpādyairvā samarcayet ityanena kāyikapūjā / 'avihiṃsan'; kasyāpi hiṃsāṃ hānimakurvanniti teṣāṃ sāmānyadharmoktiḥ / anena yatīnāṃ vaiṣṇavatvaprayuktāt
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 11:
'The word Brahman' — in this <s>Smṛti</s> [passage], 'in the supreme' (<s>pare</s>) — meaning 'in the complete one' — is a qualifier containing the implied reason. The word 'vā' is for emphasis. And thus, since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is supreme, therefore the word '<s>Brahman</s>' 'is accepted' — is acknowledged by the authoritative [teachers] — as primarily [referring to] <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. 'Not anywhere else' — not even in <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (Brahmā) and the like: this is the meaning. Why? — to this, he states the reason for their not being the primary referent of the word '<s>Brahman</s>': 'because the others are incomplete' compared to the supreme one. Then, [the question arises:] in [passages like] 'from this <s>Brahman</s>, name, form, and food are born' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 1.1.9), 'two <s>Brahmans</s> are to be known' (<s>Maitrī Upaniṣad</s> 6.22), 'all <s>jīvas</s> are [called] <s>Brahmans</s>' and the like — how is the word '<s>Brahman</s>' accepted for them? To this he says: even when the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is accepted for others elsewhere, it would be 'only figuratively' (<s>upacāreṇa</s>) — only by a secondary primary usage other than the absolute primary usage. 'Brahma' — the meaning of the <s>Bhāgavata Smṛti</s> has been stated earlier. The reason for the inclusion of the common <s>Smṛti</s> containing the word '<s>ātmapada</s>' in the middle, however, is the repetition — as stated in the <s>Candrikā</s>: the meaning 'because of the repetition of the word ātman which denotes <s>Brahman</s>' in passages like 'the Self within the other' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.2.1) and the like is also to be explained — this is what is indicated. The <s>Vyāsa Smṛti</s> passage '<s>Vāsudevātmakam</s>' (whose essence is <s>Vāsudeva</s>) should be construed with the preceding sentence 'with the mind, without causing harm, with flowers or with <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), the renunciant should worship.' For here, from '<s>Brahman</s> whose essence is <s>Vāsudeva</s>' and the like, it is understood that '<s>Bhagavān</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — as stated in the <s>Nyāyadīpa</s>. 'The renunciant' (<s>yatiḥ</s>) should worship '<s>Brahman</s> whose essence is <s>Vāsudeva</s>' — called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — 'with the mind' (<s>buddhyā</s>) — by this, the mental worship of renunciants is stated; 'or with flowers and the like, he should worship' — by this, bodily worship [is stated]. 'Without causing harm' (<s>avihiṃsan</s>) — not causing injury or loss to anyone — by this, a general <s>dharma</s> (duty) of renunciants is stated. By this,

Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 12:
Having raised the [previously] stated [objection], and intending to resolve it, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> and explains the objection-portion: 'vikāra' (modification). Here the word 'ca' is for aggregation of reasons. By the word '<s>prakṛti</s>' (nature), both sentient and insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> are intended. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) are intended. '<s>Prakṛti</s> and the like' is thus construed. The negative particle 'na' carries forward. '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' [occurs], but rather <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the word 'ca' [indicates]. The word 'tu' (but) is for specification and for emphasis. And thus — '<s>ānandamaya</s>' is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but rather <s>Prakṛti</s> and the like alone. Why? Because the '<s>vikāraśabda</s>' (modification-word) — the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix with the meaning of modification — 'is appropriate,' is used [here]. And it 'is appropriate' — functions — only because of the two reasons: being-of-the-nature-of-modification and identification-with-modification. Therefore it is appropriate only for <s>Prakṛti</s> and the like. Why? Because insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> is of the nature of modification, and because sentient <s>Prakṛti</s> and the like have identification with modification. 'But not for the <s>Paramātman</s>' — because of His being free from modification and free from identification with modification: this is the construction. He explains the portion [corresponding to] 'iti cet na' (if so, [we say] no): 'let it not be [thought].' 'A doubt' is the remainder. Why? — to this he explains the reason stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'pracura' (abundant). 'He is called <s>ānandamaya</s>' is the remainder. The word 'hi' is causal. The word 'tu' is for emphasis. And thus — 'hi' — because the entity [denoted by] '<s>ānandamaya</s>' is called [so] precisely because of '<s>pracurānandatva</s>' (being of abundant bliss) — because of being of complete bliss — and only because of this reason alone, by the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>,' 'not because of being a modification of that' [bliss] — not because of being a transformation of bliss — therefore let the doubt not arise: this is the construction. The import is: because the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix functions in view of another meaning in the form of abundance, there is no contradiction with that. And the three-fold meaning of the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix — 'the <s>mayaṭ</s> [functions] in three ways: in the sense of identity, in the sense of modification, and in the sense of abundance' — is established from this statement: this too is the reason. Although for stating the meaning of the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' — the <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivative) occurring in <s>Śruti</s> and <s>sūtra</s> — the compound should be formed as '<s>ānandapracura</s>' (abundant in bliss) in conformity with the <s>taddhita</s>-derivation, and not the reverse '<s>pracurānanda</s>' (one whose bliss is abundant) — nevertheless, since in stating the compound-sentence '<s>ānandapracura</s>' conforming to the <s>taddhita</s> derivation, the sense 'abundant in non-bliss' could also be obtained, just as in '<s>brāhmaṇapracuro grāmaḥ</s>' (a village abundant in Brāhmaṇas), to prevent that, the reverse compound '<s>pracurānanda</s>' is formed. Some, however, say: since the <s>sūtra</s> says '<s>prācuryāt</s>' (because of abundance), the genitive 'of bliss' is obtained from the context, and therefore the compound-sentence should be formed as '<s>ānandapracuratvāt</s>' in accordance with this passage; nevertheless, with the intention of the stated purpose, the compound reverse to the <s>sūtra-vyāsa</s> sentence — '<s>pracurānandatvāt</s>' — is formed. That is incorrect, because it contradicts the <s>Ṭīkā</s> [passage]: 'when stated as it stands, <s>ānandapracura</s>.' Even though in stating the compound in accordance with the <s>Śruti</s> and <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ānandamaya</s>' with abundance as the qualifier, the sense of 'non-bliss' is not obtained — just as when it is said '<s>prakāśapracuro raviḥ</s>' (the sun abundant in light), not even a trace of darkness is understood in the sun — and therefore it would be proper to explain as '<s>ānandapracuratvāt</s>' alone, since abundance, even when the qualifier, can be defined through the smallness of a member of the same class in a different substratum. Nevertheless, when abundance is the qualifier, the non-obtainment of the sense of 'non-bliss' is accepted even by opponents; but when it is the qualificand, since it must be defined through the smallness of a dissimilar member in the same substratum, the obtainment of [non-bliss] follows, just as in '<s>brāhmaṇapracuro grāmaḥ</s>' (a village abundant in Brāhmaṇas) and the like — and since [the explanation] must follow the conclusion accepted by both sides, with that intention '<s>pracurānandatvāt</s>' is explained in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: thus it is stated in the <s>Candrikā</s>.
