Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 13:
But this word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' does not denote being-of-abundant-bliss; rather, it means modification alone, because it is read together with the words '<s>annamaya</s>' (made of food) and the like which have the meaning of modification of food and the like — to this he says: 'annādīnāṃ ca' (and for food and the like). 'This' carries forward. 'The <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix' also carries forward. Through that, the word 'ca' connects in the sense of aggregation. There is a statement of non-difference between the signified and the signifier. And thus — not only does the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix [pertain to] bliss, but the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix related to food and the like also states 'abundance alone of food and the like': this is the meaning. The word 'eva' (alone) is for excluding the meaning of modification. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the like are intended. Previously, [it was stated] 'and because of being-of-the-nature-of-food,' and here, because of the inclusion of many by [the phrase] 'of food and the like,' [it is indicated that] the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' — by the principle of <s>ajahatsvārthalakṣaṇā</s> (implication that does not abandon its own meaning) — is indicative of other words of similar derivation: this is indicated. But how is the word '<s>annamaya</s>' here in the sense of abundance of food? — since the abundance of food generated from herbs, though possible in the earthly bodies of beings that subsist on food, is not possible in the non-material body of <s>Hari</s>; and because the statement of food-abundance would reduce [the text] to triviality — to this he says: 'adyate' (it is eaten). 'By the sentence about the word anna (food)' is the remainder. After 'is justified,' '<s>annamayaśabdārthaḥ</s>' (the meaning of the word annamaya) is to be supplied. 'Of the <s>Paramātman</s>' is [present]. 'Not only is there no contradiction with being read together' — this too is the meaning of 'ca.' And thus the construction is as follows: 'the abundance of that' — the abundance of food — as the meaning of the word '<s>annamaya</s>' 'is justified.' How? Because that 'is justified for the <s>Paramātman</s>.' Nor should it be said: 'Since the meaning is trivial and lacks the character of greatness, how is it justified for <s>Hari</s>?' — because here, by the word '<s>anna</s>' (food), following the method of the <s>Sudhā</s>, with the <s>bhāvapradhāna</s> (meaning-predominant) [interpretation], only the two meanings — being the eater of all beings and being that which is eaten — are justified, not the well-known [physical] food. How is this known? 'Because of the explanation (<s>vyākhyāna</s>)' — because the word '<s>anna</s>' is explained by the sentence: 'it is eaten by beings and it eats beings — therefore it is called anna.' Since the well-known food cannot be the eater of beings, the inclusion of that [meaning] is impossible. The meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>, however, is: because 'it is eaten' — depended upon — by beings, by living creatures, and 'it eats beings' — destroys them — therefore that [entity] named <s>Viṣṇu</s> — that <s>Brahman</s> — is called '<s>anna</s>' (food) in the <s>Vedas</s>. Thus, the trivial meaning should be avoided for the words '<s>prāṇa</s>' (vital breath) and '<s>manas</s>' (mind) as well, [taking them] in the sense of being the excellent mover and being of complete understanding, rather than the abundance of [physical] breath, wind, inner faculty, and intellect.

Being-depended-upon (<s>upajīvyatva</s>) is the meaning of 'being eaten' (<s>ādyatva</s>).
'He indeed, this one' — (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.2)
because of the commencement of another [topic].

children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 14:
But even so, how is the abundance of being-eaten-by-beings intended for <s>Brahman</s>, since being-eaten in the sense of being-edible is not possible for It? — to this, he states the meaning of the word 'ādyatva' (being eaten): 'upajīvyatvam' (being depended upon). Here, following the <s>Anuvyākhyāna</s> 'ato adyate' (therefore it is eaten), the division is 'ādyatvam.' And thus, following the method of the <s>Sudhā</s>, by secondary usage (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>), 'being depended upon' alone is the intended meaning of 'being eaten' — not being chewable. And that is not contradictory regarding <s>Brahman</s>: this is the import. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: 'No other [entity] is the food of all beings — i.e., the [primarily] eaten by all — nor is that [<s>Brahman</s>] the primarily eaten of anyone. Rather, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, who pervades that [food], is the primarily eaten because of being the giver of satisfaction and contentment which are the fruits of eating. Therefore, being-depended-upon is the [meaning of] being-eaten.
Because of being the eater of all worlds, <s>Hari</s> is called '<s>anna</s>' (food).
And because He is depended upon by beings, <s>Janārdana</s> is [also called] '<s>anna</s>.' //

children.translated_text: By the statement 'iti ukteḥ' (because it is so stated), it is declared that the primary meaning itself is that of being foundational. And there is no contradiction, because the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> proceeds with the purport of <s>samanvaya</s> (reconciliation) in the manner stated in the <s>Kampanādhikaraṇa</s>. Just as the <s>Sudhā</s> commentary proceeds with the intent of somehow establishing that the text refers to <s>Brahman</s>, as in the case of 'like a thunderbolt' and similar passages. Now, if one objects: how can the word <s>annamaya</s> be justified as meaning abundance of food? Since after stating the well-known food-modification body in 'From herbs comes food, from food comes the person' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1.2), the statement 'This very person is made of the essence of food' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1.3) is a reiteration referring to the person who is a modification of food — because the very same person is referred to as <s>annarasamaya</s> — otherwise there would be contradiction, therefore he says 'sa' (that). The phrase '<s>avirodhaḥ</s>' (non-contradiction) is to be supplied here. And by the sentence beginning with 'tathā ca,' since from that <s>Ātman</s> space and the rest have originated, 'this person' — by the 'commencement' (i.e., reference to) 'another,' meaning the <s>Ātman</s> who is different from the body — there is 'no contradiction,' that is, no contradiction in the reference. To remove the doubt as to why that reference is made, instead of saying 'because of the reference,' he says 'because of the commencement.' Having first stated that the <s>Ātman</s> is the cause of space and the rest, 'for another purpose' — for demonstrating another effect, namely the five forms beginning with <s>annamaya</s> — 'because of the commencement,' meaning because it is being continued — this is the meaning. In the <s>śruti</s> passage 'sa vā' (he indeed), the particle 'vai' is used either for emphasis or for well-known usage. The word <s>anna</s> (food) has its essential nature as primary. <s>Rasatva</s> (essence-ness) means supreme excellence, and that is a qualifier of the food-nature. And thus, from that <s>Ātman</s> characterized by the definitions of truth and the rest, from whom space and the rest have originated — 'saḥ' (he) is the creator of elements and the rest, indicated by the word <s>Ātman</s>; 'eṣaḥ' (this one) means he who has entered the body of the <s>jīva</s>; 'puruṣaḥ' means the Lord who is full of the six attributes and who dwells in the body-city; '<s>annarasamayaḥ</s>' means full of supreme food-essence — this is the meaning. But in the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s>, 'Since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the essence of the <s>annamaya</s> body which has the form of being the consumer of food and so forth,

BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.15:
nanvevaṃ mayaṭchabdasyobhayārthe prayogādatrāpyubhayapakṣe doṣadarśanātpañcānāṃ mayaṭāṃ prācuryamevārtho na vikāritvamityatra kiṃ niyāmakam? kiñcānnamayādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ brahmatābhyupagatau 'ekameva'; (chā.u. 6-2-1.) ityādiśrutivirodhaḥ syāt ityata āha - ye 'nnaṃ brahmeti // atrādiśabdena 'ye prāṇaṃ brahmopāsate'; (tai.u. 2-3-1.)/ 'ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān'; (tai.u. 2-4-1.) 'vijñānaṃ brahma cedveda'; (tai.u. 2-5-1.) 'asti brahmeti cedveda'; (tai.u. 2-6-1.) iti vākyajātaṃ gṛhyate / asti ānandarūpaṃ tadvacca / 'ityādi'; iti luptasaptamīvibhaktikam / 'ślokeṣu'; iti śeṣaḥ / brahmaśabdapadaṃ tacchravaṇopalakṣakam / evaṃ pradarśite hetudvaye 'dhyāhṛtahetudvārānvayayogye krameṇa sādhye āha - na vikāritvamiti / 'mayaṭāmartha iti niścīyate'; iti śeṣaḥ / 'avirodho'; virodhābhāvaḥ / caśabdo 'pyarthaḥ / tathā cetthaṃ yojanā - 'ye 'nnaṃ brahma'; ityādiṣu annamayādīnpratyudāhṛtaślokeṣu annamayādiviṣayatvena 'brahmaśabdāt'; brahmaśabdaśravaṇādanyathāsiddhatatsamabhivyāhārāt ubhayathāpi sambhavatāṃ mayaṭāṃ prācuryamevārthaḥ na vikāritvamiti niścīyate / ato na niyāmakākṣepo yuktaḥ / evamekasyaiva brahmaṇo 'bahurūpatvācca'; śabdādekasyaiva bahurūpatvavacanopapatteḥ 'ekameva'; iti śrutivirodho 'pi neti / pūrvaṃ 'tasminneva prasiddhabrahmaśabdābhyāsāt'; ityuktvā atra brahmaśabdādityetāvanmātrokteḥ prayojanaṃ tu "brahmaśabdasyānandavijñānamayayorivānyeṣvabhyāsābhāvātteṣvasiddhiparihāreṇa brahmaśabdaśravaṇarūpasarvasādhāraṇahetvarthakathanameva"ityuktaṃ candrikāyām /
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1.1.6.15:) Now, if it is objected: since the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix is used in both senses, and since defects are seen in both positions here too, what is the determining factor for concluding that the meaning of the five <s>mayaṭ</s> suffixes is abundance alone and not modification? Moreover, if all five beginning with <s>annamaya</s> are accepted as <s>Brahman</s>, there would be contradiction with <s>śruti</s> passages like 'One alone' (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.2.1) — therefore he says 'ye annaṃ brahma iti.' Here, by the word 'ādi' (etc.), the collection of passages is included: 'Those who worship <s>prāṇa</s> as <s>Brahman</s>' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.3.1), 'The knower of the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.4.1), '<s>Vijñāna</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, if one knows' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.5.1), 'If one knows that <s>Brahman</s> exists' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.6.1). 'Asti' means that which has the form of bliss, and likewise. The word 'ityādi' has an elided seventh-case ending; 'in the verses' is to be supplied. The word '<s>brahmaśabda</s>' (the word Brahman) indicates the hearing of that word. When the two reasons thus demonstrated are suitable for connection through two implied reasons, he states the two conclusions in order — 'na vikāritvam' (not modification-nature). 'The meaning of the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffixes is thus determined' — this is to be supplied. '<s>Avirodhaḥ</s>' means absence of contradiction. The particle 'ca' also has the sense of 'also.' And thus the construction is as follows: In the verses cited regarding <s>annamaya</s> and the rest, such as 'Those who worship food as <s>Brahman</s>,' because of the hearing of the word <s>Brahman</s> — that is, because of the contextual association with it which cannot be otherwise established — the meaning of the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffixes, which are possible in both senses, is determined to be abundance alone and not modification. Therefore the objection regarding the absence of a determining factor is not appropriate. Thus, because of the statement of multiple forms of one and the same <s>Brahman</s>, and because of the word establishing that one alone has many forms, there is also no contradiction with the <s>śruti</s> 'One alone.' Previously, having said 'because of the repetition of the well-known word <s>Brahman</s> in that very context,' here only this much is said — 'because of the word <s>Brahman</s>.' The purpose, however, is stated in the <s>Candrikā</s>: 'Since the word <s>Brahman</s> is not repeated in the others as it is in the <s>ānanda</s> and <s>vijñānamaya</s> sections, the purpose is to state the universally applicable reason in the form of hearing the word <s>Brahman</s>, thereby removing the difficulty regarding those other cases.'

children.text:
na ca pṛthakkalpanā yuktā /
svarūpaṃ ca yujyate pracuraprakāśo raviritivat /
children.translated_text: And a separate supposition is not appropriate. And the usage is fitting even regarding the essential nature, just as one says 'the sun is of abundant light.'

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.16:
atrānyaiḥ ānandamaya eva brahma / tadgatamayaṭa eva prācuryārthatā / annamayādayastu kośāḥ / tadgatānāṃ mayaṭāṃ ca vikārārthatvamityuktam / tadayuktamityāha - na ceti // prāyapaṭitamayaṭāṃ 'pṛthakkalpanā'; arthadvaividhyakalpanā na yuktā / tataścānnamayādīnāṃ madhye ekasyaiva brahmatvakalpanā ca na yuktaiva, prāyapāṭhavirodhena kliṣṭatvādityarthaḥ / yastu vādī annamayādīnāṃ pañcānāmapyabrahmatāṃ brūte, sa tu sūtrakāreṇaiva pūrvapakṣīkṛta iti na tatpakṣaṃ pratyākṣipadbhāṣyakāraḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - na ceti vākyaṃ na ca māyinā pṛthakkalpanā 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma'; (tai.u. 2-1-1.) 'tasmādvā etasmādātmanaḥ'; (tai.u. 2-1-2.) ityatra brahmocyate / annamayādayaḥ pañcakośā mitho bhinnāḥ teṣāṃ brahmaśabdoktatve 'pi abrahmatvam/ antyapucchasyaiva brahmatvam / annamayādyatikramo mokṣaḥ / vakṣyamāṇānāṃ cakṣuśśrotramanovācāṃ nānnamayādiṣvanuvṛttiḥ / 'annaṃ brahmeti vyajānāt'; (tai.u. 3-2.) ityādau pañcamasyānandasya brahmatvam / 'etamānandamayamātmānamupasaṅkramya'; (tai.u. 3-10-5.) ityetasmādbrahmānandamayādyatikramanirguṇavākyātpṛthageva 'imān lokān'; (tai.u. 3-10-5.) ityādiko vākyaśeṣaḥ saguṇavākyaikavākyatāpannaḥ tatphalapratipādaka ityādikā yuktā / uktahetubhiratyantāsaṅgatatvāt ityantyapakṣanirākaraṇaparatayā vyākhyātam / na caivametadvirodhaṣṭīkāyā iti vācyam / bhāṣyakāraḥ savistaraṃ viśiṣya na nirācakhyāviti ṭīkābhiprāyābhyupagamāt / nanu 'na brahmaṇi pracurānandaḥ'; ityādiprayogo yujyate/ tasyānandādisvarūpatvāt 'ghṛtapracura odanaḥ'; ityādau bhedasthala eva tathā prayogādityata āha - svarūpe ceti / caśabdo 'pyarthaḥ / itiśabdaḥ śabdapadārthaḥ / 'raviritivat'; ityanantaraṃ 'vyavahāraḥ'; iti śeṣaḥ / 'svarūpe ca'; ityasyāvṛttiḥ / tathā ca prakāśasvarūpe 'pi sūryabimbe viśeṣabalāt 'pracuraprakāśo raviritivat'; evaṃrūpavyavahāravat ānandādisvarūpe 'pi harau viśeṣeṇa tathā vyavahāro yujyata eveti na tadanupapattirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1.1.6.16:) Here, others have maintained: only <s>ānandamaya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>; the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix in that case alone has the sense of abundance; but <s>annamaya</s> and the rest are sheaths (<s>kośas</s>); and the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffixes in those cases have the sense of modification. He says this is incorrect — 'na ca' (and not). A 'separate supposition' — that is, the supposition of two different meanings — regarding the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffixes that generally occur together, is not appropriate. And therefore, the supposition that only one among <s>annamaya</s> and the rest is <s>Brahman</s> is also not appropriate, because it would be forced, contradicting the general usage — this is the meaning. As for the disputant who says that none of the five beginning with <s>annamaya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, he has already been treated as the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector) by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> himself, and therefore the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) does not refute that position here. But in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: the sentence 'na ca' means — and there is no separate supposition by <s>Māyin</s> (the illusionist, i.e., the Advaitin). In 'Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1.1) and 'From that very <s>Ātman</s>' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1.2), <s>Brahman</s> is spoken of. The five <s>kośas</s> beginning with <s>annamaya</s> are mutually different; even though the word <s>Brahman</s> is applied to them, they are not <s>Brahman</s>. Only the final 'tail' (<s>puccha</s>) is <s>Brahman</s>. Liberation is the transcendence of <s>annamaya</s> and the rest. The eye, ear, mind, and speech that are to be mentioned do not continue in <s>annamaya</s> and the rest. In 'He knew food as <s>Brahman</s>' (Taittirīya 3.2) and similar passages, the fifth, namely <s>ānanda</s>, is <s>Brahman</s>. From the passage 'Having approached this self made of bliss' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 3.10.5) — from this passage about transcending <s>Brahman</s> which is <s>ānandamaya</s>, through the attributeless statement, separately — the remainder of the passage 'these worlds' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 3.10.5) and so forth, being syntactically unified with the passage on the qualified <s>Brahman</s>, teaches its fruit — such an interpretation would be appropriate. This is explained as being intended to refute the last position, because it is utterly inconsistent due to the reasons stated. And it should not be said that this contradicts the <s>Ṭīkā</s> (gloss), because the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> did not refute it in detail and specifically — this is accepted as the intent of the <s>Ṭīkā</s>. Now, if one objects that the usage 'abundant bliss is not in <s>Brahman</s>' is appropriate, since <s>Brahman</s>'s essential nature is bliss itself, and such usage of abundance applies only where there is difference, as in 'rice abundant in ghee' — therefore he says 'svarūpe ca' (and regarding the essential nature). The particle 'ca' has the sense of 'also.' The word 'iti' refers to the word itself. After 'like the sun,' 'the usage' is to be supplied. 'And regarding the essential nature' is repeated. And thus, even regarding the solar disc whose essential nature is light, by virtue of a special emphasis the usage 'the sun is of abundant light' is possible; similarly, even regarding <s>Hari</s> whose essential nature is bliss and the rest, such usage is indeed appropriate by special emphasis — therefore there is no impossibility in this — this is the meaning.
'Because of the declaration of it as the cause' — <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.14.

children.text:
'ko hyevānyātmakaḥ prāṇyāt /
yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt'; (tai. 2-7.) iti /
children.translated_text: 'Who indeed could breathe, who could live, if this bliss were not there in space?' (Taittirīya 2.7) — thus.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.17:
ānandamayamātrasya viṣṇutve, hetvantararūpaṃ prācuryameva mayaḍartha ityatra ca hetuṃ pratipādayatsūtramupanyasyati - taddhetviti // ānandamaya iti tattviti cānuvartate / tadityasyāvṛttiḥ / sa cāsau hetuścetyapi vigrahaḥ / tathā ca na kevalaṃ brahmaśabdābhyāsāt / kintu 'taddhetuvyapadeśāt'; tasminnānandamayaprakaraṇe tasya viṣṇoḥ tasmin anandapūrṇatvenānandamayatve prācuryasyaiva mayaḍarthatve ca taddhetuvyapadeśāt lokaceṣṭakatvākhyahetūkteścānandapūrṇatvenaivānandamayaśabdavācyo viṣṇureveti sūtravṛttimabhipretya tameva hetuvyapadeśaṃ darśayati - kohīti / 'yat'; yadā yadi 'eṣaḥ ākāśaḥ'; āsamantātprakāśamāno viṣṇurānandaḥ pūrṇānando na syāt tadāsau lokaṃ na pravartayediti śeṣaḥ / ānandodrekamantareṇa pravṛtto kāraṇāntarābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / yadyasau na lokaṃ pravartayet / tadā 'ko hyevānyāt'; ko vā janaḥ lokaṃ ceṣṭayet / 'kaśca prāṇyāt'; dharmādau ca kaḥ pravartayet / na ko 'pi / anyasyāsvātantryāditi taittirīyabhāṣyaṭīkārītyā śrutyarthaḥ / sudhāyāṃ tu ṇyarthānandarbhāvena na ko 'pi lokikīṃ vaidikīṃ pravṛttiṃ kuryāditi vyākhyātam / itītyasya iti taddhetuvyapadeśādityanvayaḥ //
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1.1.6.17:) To the effect that <s>ānandamaya</s> alone refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and that the meaning of the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix is abundance alone — presenting the <s>sūtra</s> that teaches an additional reason for this, he cites it — '<s>taddhetu</s>' (because of the declaration of it as the cause). The words '<s>ānandamaya</s>' and 'tat' (that) are carried forward from the previous context. The word 'tat' is repeated for emphasis. The compound analysis is: 'that which is both that and the cause.' And thus, not merely because of the repetition of the word <s>Brahman</s>, but 'because of the declaration of it as the cause' — in that very <s>ānandamaya</s> section, because of the statement of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being the cause, namely the cause called being the activator of the world, and because the meaning of <s>mayaṭ</s> is abundance in the sense that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is full of bliss in his <s>ānandamaya</s> nature — intending this as the purport of the <s>sūtra</s>, he shows that very declaration of causality — 'ko hi' (who indeed). 'Yat' means when or if; 'eṣaḥ ākāśaḥ' means <s>Viṣṇu</s> who illuminates in all directions; '<s>ānandaḥ</s>' means one who is full of bliss — if he were not to exist, then he would not activate the world — this is to be supplied. Without the abundance of bliss, the active one would not engage, because there is no other cause — this is the import. If he were not to activate the world, then 'ko hyeva anyāt' — what person would make the world function? 'And who would breathe' — who would engage in <s>dharma</s> and the rest? No one would, because of the dependence of all others — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> according to the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya Ṭīkā</s>. In the <s>Sudhā</s>, however, it is explained by including the causal sense: no one would engage in either worldly or Vedic activity — thus it is interpreted. The word 'iti' connects with 'thus, because of the declaration of it as the cause.'
'That which is characterized in the <s>mantra</s> words is itself what is sung' — <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.15.

children.text: 'brahmāvidāpnoti param'; iti sūcayitvā 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma'(tai.2-1) iti mantravarṇalakṣitaṃ parameva brahma śabdānusandhānādgīyate /
children.translated_text: Having indicated by '<s>Brahmavid</s> attains the Supreme' (Taittirīya 2.1), what is sung — through the connection of words — is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself, which is characterized in the <s>mantra</s> words 'Truth, Knowledge, Infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (Taittirīya 2.1).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.18:
yaduktaṃ brahmaśabdādānandamayādīnāṃ viṣṇutvamiti na tadyuktam / brahmaśabdasya aparabrahmaṇi jīve 'pyupapatteḥ/ tasya parabrahmaṇi mukhyatve 'pi viṣṇoḥ ānandamayāvayavatvoktyādinā bādhakenāmukhyārthasyaiva grahaṇopapatterityāśaṅkāṃ pariharat ānandamayādiśabdavācyasya viṣṇutve yuktyantaraṃ vadan sūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - māntravarṇikamiti / yata ityādau yojyaṃ, 'na te'; iti pratijñānuvartate / tathā ca yataḥ 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma'; (tai.u. 2-1-1.) iti 'mantravarṇe'; mantrākṣare tadātmakavākyaviśeṣe 'lakṣitaṃ'; lakṣaṇavattayā proktameva parameva brahma nālakṣitaṃ, nāparamityevārthaḥ/ annamayādiśabdaiḥ 'gīyate'; pratipādyate ato 'pyānandamayādayo nāpare / kintu parameva brahmeti yojanā / kuto 'nnamayādiśabdairmantravarṇalakṣitasyaiva pratipādanaṃ jñāyata ityata uktam - śabdānusandhānāditi / 'śabdānāṃ'; satyaṃ jñānamanantam ityevaṃrūpāṇām annamayādiśabdānāṃ ca arthānusandhānāt jātāt 'anusandhānāt'
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1.1.6.18:) The objection was raised: the claim that <s>annamaya</s> and the rest refer to <s>Viṣṇu</s> because of the word <s>Brahman</s> is not appropriate, since the word <s>Brahman</s> can also apply to the lower <s>Brahman</s>, namely the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul). Even if the word <s>Brahman</s> primarily refers to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, because of sublating factors such as the statement that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is a part of <s>ānandamaya</s>, only the secondary meaning could be taken — to remove this doubt, stating another reason for the position that what is denoted by words like <s>ānandamaya</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he cites the <s>sūtra</s> and explains it — '<s>māntravarṇikam</s>' (that which is characterized in the <s>mantra</s> words). 'Yataḥ' (because) and so forth should be construed; 'na te' (not those) — the assertion is carried forward. And thus, because 'Truth, Knowledge, Infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1.1) — that which is 'characterized in the <s>mantra</s> words,' that is, spoken of as having defining characteristics in the specific sentence constituting the syllables of the <s>mantra</s> — it is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone that is 'sung,' that is, taught, by the words <s>annamaya</s> and the rest — not something uncharacterized, not the lower <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. Therefore <s>ānandamaya</s> and the rest are not the lower <s>Brahman</s>, but the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone — this is the construction. How is it known that the words <s>annamaya</s> and the rest teach that which is characterized in the <s>mantra</s> words? To this he says — 'śabdānusandhānāt' (because of the connection of words). 'Of the words' — namely those of the form 'Truth, Knowledge, Infinite' and the words <s>annamaya</s> and the rest — 'because of the investigation of meaning' that arises from them, 'because of the connection'

children.text:
ekārthatvajñānādityarthaḥ / mantravarṇe 'pi brahmetyevoktatvātkathaṃ tadarthānāmapyannamayādiśabdānāṃ parabrahmārthatājñaptirityata āha - brahmaviditi / pravṛtta iti śeṣaḥ / asya buddhyā viviktena mantravarṇapadenānvayaḥ / tathā ca yato 'brahmavidāpnoti param'; (tai.u. 2-1-1.) iti / parabrahmatajjñānatatprāptīḥ sūcayitvā saṅkṣepeṇaktvā tatra prāptaśaṅkāpanodāya pravṛtto mantravarṇaḥ / tato 'tra lakṣitaṃ paraṃ
brahmaiveti jñāyata ityarthaḥ / sūtre
children.translated_text: means because of the knowledge of their having a single referent — this is the meaning. Even in the <s>mantra</s> passage the word <s>Brahman</s> alone is used; so how is it known that the words <s>annamaya</s> and the rest, which share the same meaning, refer to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>? To this he says — '<s>brahmavid</s>' (the knower of <s>Brahman</s>). 'Pravṛttaḥ' (having commenced) is to be supplied. This connects with the <s>mantra</s> passage by means of intellectual discernment. And thus, because '<s>Brahmavid</s> attains the Supreme' (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1.1) — having indicated, that is, having briefly stated, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the knowledge of it, and the attainment of it — the <s>mantra</s> passage has commenced in order to remove doubts that arise there. Therefore it is known that what is characterized here is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone — this is the meaning. In the <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: ānandamayādistattviti cānuvartate / caśabdo yatha ityarthe yuktisayuccaye ca / tathā ca na kevalaṃ brahmaśabdādevānandamayādiviṣṇvākhyaṃ parabrahmaiva nāparabrahmetyavasīyate / kintu yato māntravarṇikaṃ 'satyaṃ jñānam'; iti vedavākyena lakṣaṇavattayā proktaṃ paraṃ brahamaivānnamayādiśabdaiḥ 'gīyate'; pratipādyate ca / atastatsamākhyānādārthikādapīti sūtrārthaḥ / 'brahmavit'; parabrahmajñānī 'paraṃ'; paramaṃ brahmāpnoti / parabrahmaprāptikāmaḥ parabrahma jānīyāt iti śruteḥ phalito 'rthaḥ / kiṃ tadbrahmeti śaṅkāyāṃ satyamityādi pravṛttam / tatra satyaśabdenoktaṃ yat gatijīvananāśaprāpakatvaṃ tadevānnamayaprāṇamayaśabdābhyāmucyate / anantaśabdenoktaṃ deśataḥ kālato vastutaśca aparicchinnatvam / paramātmānantaḥ pūrṇānandatvādityānandamayaśabdenopapādyata iti satyādiśabdānāṃ annamayādiśabdānāṃ cakārthatvam anusandheyam / atra deśānantyaṃ nāma anavadhikaparimāṇatvam / kālānantyaṃ nāma anavacchinnasattākatvam / vastvānantyaṃ nāma aparicchinnasaṅkhyāguṇakarmavigrahavattvam //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ānandamaya</s> and the like is that' — this too carries forward. The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'yathā' (just as) and for aggregation of reasons. And thus — it is determined not merely from the word '<s>Brahman</s>' alone that [the entity denoted by] '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' and the like is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Viṣṇu</s> and not the lower <s>Brahman</s> (Brahmā). Rather, since the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone — which is described with defining characteristics by the Vedic sentence '<s>satyaṃ jñānam</s>' (truth, knowledge) belonging to the <s>Mantra</s> portion — 'is praised,' is taught, by the words '<s>Annamaya</s>' and the like as well. Therefore, from that designation also, being based on reasoning: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s>' — the knower of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — 'attains the Supreme' — the highest <s>Brahman</s>. The resultant meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is: one who desires the attainment of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> should know the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. When the doubt arises 'what is that <s>Brahman</s>?', the passage 'satyam' (truth) and so on begins. There, what is stated by the word 'satya' (truth) — namely, the capacity to bestow movement, life, and dissolution — that very thing is stated by the words '<s>Annamaya</s>' and '<s>Prāṇamaya</s>.' What is stated by the word 'ananta' (infinite) — namely, unlimitedness in respect of space, time, and entity — [is also indicated]. The <s>Paramātman</s> is infinite; because of [His] being of complete bliss — this is established by the word '<s>Ānandamaya</s>': thus the equivalence between the words 'satya' and the like and '<s>Annamaya</s>' and the like should be noted. Here, infinity in space means having immeasurable dimensions. Infinity in time means having uninterrupted existence. Infinity in entity means possessing unlimited number, qualities, actions, and forms.

children.text: na cāvayavatvavirodhaḥ / 'sa śiraḥ, sa dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ, sa uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ, sa ātmā, sa puccham'; iti tasyaivāvayavatvokteścaturvedaśikhāyām /
children.translated_text: Nor is there a contradiction with [<s>Brahman</s>] having parts. 'He is the head, He is the right wing, He is the left wing, He is the body, He is the tail' — because in the <s>Caturveda Śikhā</s>, the having-of-parts is stated for that very one [<s>Viṣṇu</s>].
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.6, verse 19:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.19:
nanu viṣṇorānandamayatvaṃ na yuktaṃ, tasya tadavayavatvāt / na cāsiddhiḥ, brahmapucchamityukteḥ / avayavinaścāvayavatvavirodhādityata āha - na ceti / tasyetyātkṛṣyate / 'tasya'; viṣṇorānandamayatve tadavayavatvoktivirodho netyarthaḥ / avayavatve ca avayavitvasya virodho 'pi neti caśabdārthaḥ / kuta ityato 'vayavina evāvayavatvasyāvayavitvasya ca śrutyuktatvenāvayavyāderavayavādyabhedādityāśayena tāṃ śrutimudāharati - sa iti / 'saḥ'; nārāyaṇaḥ 'śiraḥ'; śīrṣaṃ, śiraḥ sa iti vā / evam uttaratrāpi vyākhyeyam / dvitīyāditacchabdāḥ smṛtyanusārātpradyumnādiparāḥ / 'pakṣo'; bāhuḥ 'uttaraḥ'; savyaḥ 'ātmā'; madhyadehaḥ 'pucchaṃ'; pādau itītyasyaivaṃrūpāyāṃ caturvedaśikhāyāṃ tasyaivāvayavibhūtasyaiva viṣṇoravayavatvokterityanvayaḥ / evaśabdenāvayavāvayavibhedo nivāritaḥ / evaṃ avayavasyāvayavitve na kevalamiyaṃ śrutiḥ, kintu - bhāṣye upalakṣaṇayā gṛhītā 'padaṃ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā vai puruṣaḥ'; iti tattvapradīpodāhṛtaśrutirapi pramāṇatayā grāhyā / asmin pakṣe bhāṣyagatāvayavaśabdaḥ arśaādyajanto 'vayaviparaḥ //
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 19:
But the status of <s>Viṣṇu</s> as <s>Ānandamaya</s> is not proper, because He is a part of that [<s>Ānandamaya</s>]. Nor is there non-establishment [of this objection], since it is said '<s>Brahman</s> is the tail.' And there is a contradiction between being a part and being the whole — to this he says: 'na ca' (nor). 'Of that very one' is to be supplied [from context]. There is no contradiction of the having-of-parts statement with 'that' — <s>Viṣṇu's</s> — being <s>Ānandamaya</s>: this is the meaning. And moreover, even when there is having-of-parts, there is no contradiction with being the whole — this is the meaning of the word 'ca.' Why? — to this, with the intention that since both the having-of-parts of the whole and the having-of-whole of the parts are stated in <s>Śruti</s>, there is no difference between the whole and the parts, he cites that <s>Śruti</s>: 'sa' (He). 'He' — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — 'is the head'; or 'the head is He.' The same should be explained for the subsequent [statements] as well. The second and following 'tat' (that) words, following the <s>Smṛti</s>, refer to <s>Pradyumna</s> and the others. '<s>Pakṣa</s>' (wing) means arm. '<s>Uttara</s>' means left. '<s>Ātmā</s>' means the middle body. '<s>Puccham</s>' (tail) means the feet. Thus, in the <s>Caturveda Śikhā</s> of this form, 'because the having-of-parts is stated for that very one' — for <s>Viṣṇu</s> who has become the whole — this is the syntactic connection. By the word 'eva' (very), the difference between parts and whole is negated. Thus, not only this <s>Śruti</s> [establishes] the having-of-parts of the whole, but also — through indication in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — the <s>Śruti</s> cited in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'the foot, the tail, the support, is the Person' — should also be accepted as an authority. In this interpretation, the word 'avayava' (part) occurring in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is a nominal derivative ending in <s>arśaādi</s> and means 'the whole.'
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.6, verse 20:

children.text: śiro nārāyaṇaḥ pakṣo dakṣiṇassavya eva ca /
children.translated_text: The head is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; the right wing and the left as well
are <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s> respectively; the body (<s>sandoha</s>) is <s>Vāsudeva</s>. //
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is also the body, and <s>Vāsudeva</s> is alternatively the head.

children.text: pucchaṃ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ proktaḥ eka eva tu pañcadhā //
children.translated_text: The tail is declared to be <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>; [He is] one alone yet fivefold. //
As parts and whole, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), sports. //
And because of [His] sovereignty, no contradiction should be conceived regarding that <s>Janārdana</s>.
In what is beyond reasoning, whence reasoning? In what is beyond measure, whence measure? //
Thus in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.20:
avayavina avayavatvaṃ viruddhamityāśaṅkāṃ śrutyā parihṛtyātra smṛtiṃ cāha - śira iti / atra citrādau likhyamānanavanārīrūpe avayavibhūtānāmanekastrīṇāmekadehāvayavatvaṃ tathā nārāyaṇādipañcarūpāṇāṃ ekāvayavatvamucyate/ ādyaścaḥ pakṣasamuccaye / rūpayoḥ parasparasamuccaye dvau / avayavibhūta eva nārāyaṇaḥ śira ityevaśabdānvayaḥ / evamavayavibhūtaḥ pradyumno dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣo bāhuḥ / aniruddhaḥ savyaḥ / vāsudevaḥ 'sandoho'; madhyadeha ityanvayaḥ / apiveti nipātasamudāyaḥ pakṣāntare / pūrvasmin pakṣe nārāyaṇasya
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 20:
Having resolved through <s>Śruti</s> the objection that the having-of-parts of the whole is contradictory, he also cites a <s>Smṛti</s>: 'śiraḥ' (the head). Here, just as in the <s>Navanārī</s> figure drawn in paintings — where multiple women who are parts-become-whole form a single body — so too the five forms of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and others [form] a single [whole with] parts: this is stated. The first 'ca' is for aggregation of the two wings. The two [words 'ca'] regarding the forms are for mutual aggregation of the forms. The very <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who has become the whole is the head — the word 'eva' connects thus. Likewise, <s>Pradyumna</s> who has become a part-of-the-whole is the right wing (arm). <s>Aniruddha</s> is the left. '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is the body (<s>sandoha</s>)' — the middle body: this is the construction. 'Api vā' is a particle-cluster for an alternative view. In the first view, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: śīrṣatvam / vāsudevasya madhyadehatvam / asmin pakṣe tu - tadaṃśe vaiparītyamityupāsanābhedena pakṣabhedoktiḥ/ saṅkarṣaṇastūbhayatra 'pucchaṃ'; pādau prokta ityanvayaḥ / tuśabdena dvirūpatvaṃ suparṇarūpatvaviśeṣo vā jñāyate / tataḥ kimityata āha - eka iti / evaṃ 'puruṣottamaḥ'; kṣarākṣarapuruṣābhyām uttamo bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ 'eka eva'; pañcadhā vibhaktaḥ eka evāyavaiḥ abhinna eva na tu bhinnaḥ / 'aṅgatvena'; avayavatvena 'aṅgitvena'; avayavitvena prakāreṇa tadbhāvaṃ prāptaḥ krīḍata ityarthaḥ / itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇe tṛtīyā / nanvastavevaṃ tāvatā na virodhaparihāro jāta ityata āha - aiśvaryāditi / 'tasmin'; avayavibhāvādyāpanne janārdane 'tasmin'; avayavatvādau tadviṣaye 'virodhaḥ'; sahānavasthānarūpo 'na cintyaḥ'; na kenacitkalpyaḥ / kutaḥ? 'aiśvaryāt'; īśvarasāmarthyāt tayorekatrāvasthānarūpāvirodhopapatteḥ īśvaraśaktiścāghaṭitaghaṭiketi bhāvaḥ / evaṃ 'tasmin'; avayave 'tasmin'; avayavitve na virodhaḥ / kutaḥ? ekaikasyāvayavasya sarveśvaratvādityapi vyākhyeyam / evaṃ na virodha ityetat avayavāvayavinorabhede 'yamavayavī ayam avayava iti bhedavyavahāravirodho 'pi netyapi vyākhyeyam / tatra hetustu viśeṣabalācchaktivyaktibhāvāditi caśabdena sūcitaḥ / ata eva caśabdo 'nuktasamuccayārthaḥ aiśvaryāccetyanveti / kiñca - kiṃ tarkānyapramāṇenāvayavino 'vayavatvamavayavasyāvayavitvaṃ ca viruddham? uta avayavī nāvayavaḥ avayavitvāt / avayavo vā nāvayavī avayavatvāllokavaditi tarkapadoktānumānena? nādyo 'siddhatvāt / na dvitīya ityāha - atarkya iti / 'hi'; yasmādatarkyaḥ tasmāt 'atarkye'; tarkāgocare bhagavati tadviṣaye 'tarkaḥ'; avayavī nāvayavaḥ avayavitvāt ityādirūpo hetuḥ 'kutaḥ'; sādhako bādhako vā netyarthaḥ / kiñca - loke parimitaśaktitva eva virodhadarśanāt viṣṇorvirodhopayogiparimitaśaktiśūnyatvāt tarkyatvāṅgīkāre 'pi na virodha
children.translated_text: is the head; <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the middle body. In this [alternative] view, however — in that respect there is reversal: thus the statement of different views is according to differences in meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>). <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, in both [views], is 'the tail' — the feet: this is declared — this is the construction. By the word 'tu,' the two-fold nature or the specific character of being in the form of a bird (<s>suparṇa</s>) is known. Then what? — to this he says: 'eka' (one). Thus, '<s>Puruṣottama</s>' — the Supreme Person, <s>Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is superior to the perishable and the imperishable — 'one alone,' divided fivefold, is one alone — non-different from His parts, not different [from them]. 'As parts' (<s>aṅgatvena</s>) — as the mode of being parts; 'and as whole' (<s>aṅgitvena</s>) — as the mode of being the whole — having assumed that state, He 'sports': this is the meaning. The instrumental case is in the sense of characterizing the mode-of-being (<s>itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇa</s>). But even if this is so, the contradiction is not thereby resolved — to this he says: 'aiśvaryāt' (because of sovereignty). 'Regarding that' <s>Janārdana</s> who has assumed the state of having parts and the like, 'regarding that' — regarding the having-of-parts and the like, regarding that subject — 'contradiction' — in the form of the impossibility of co-existence — 'should not be conceived' — should not be imagined by anyone. Why? 'Because of sovereignty' — because of the Lord's power, since the non-contradiction of their co-existence in one [being] is logically possible. And the Lord's power is capable of making the impossible possible: this is the import. Thus, 'regarding that' — regarding a part, 'regarding that' — regarding its being the whole, there is no contradiction. Why? Because each individual part is the lord of all: this too should be explained. Thus, 'there is no contradiction' — this should also be explained as meaning: there is no contradiction of the transactional usage 'this is the whole, this is a part' even when the parts and whole are non-different. The reason for that is indicated by the word 'ca' — because of the force of a special [capacity], because of the manifestation of [divine] power. Therefore the word 'ca' is for aggregating the unstated [reason], and connects with 'because of sovereignty.' Moreover — is the having-of-parts of the whole and the having-of-whole of the parts contradictory [as established] by reasoning or by other means of knowledge? Or by inference of the form stated in the reasoning: 'the whole is not a part because of being a whole; or, a part is not the whole because of being a part — just as in the world'? Not the first, because of non-establishment. Not the second either — to this he says: 'atarkye' (in what is beyond reasoning). 'Hi' — since He is beyond reasoning, therefore 'in the beyond-reasoning' — in <s>Bhagavān</s> who is beyond the reach of reasoning, 'regarding that' subject, 'reasoning' — in the form of the reason 'the whole is not a part because of being a whole' and the like — 'whence?' — is neither establishing nor refuting: this is the meaning. Moreover, since contradiction is observed in the world only when there is limited power, and since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is devoid of the limited power that is instrumental for contradiction, even if being-within-reasoning is accepted, there is no contradiction —

children.text: ityāha - aprameya iti / 'aprameye'; deśakālaguṇairaparicchinne bhagavati 'pramā'; etāvadeva sāmarthyaṃ nāto 'dhikamiti śaktiparicchedaḥ 'kutaḥ'; netyarthaḥ / tathā ca paroktatarkasya sopādhikatvenāpramāṇatvānna virodhitvamiti bhāvaḥ / anena 'atarkya'; ityasyāsattarkāgocara ityartha ityuktaṃ bhavati / iti bṛhatsaṃhitāyāmityasya 'tasyaivāvayavatvokteḥ'; ityanuṣaktenānvayaḥ //
children.translated_text: to this he says: 'aprameye' (in the immeasurable). 'In the immeasurable' — in <s>Bhagavān</s> who is unlimited by space, time, and qualities — 'measure' (<s>pramā</s>) — a determination of power [stating] 'only this much capacity, no more' — 'whence?' — does not exist: this is the meaning. And thus, since the reasoning of the opponent is subject to a limiting condition (<s>sopādhikatva</s>), it is not a valid means of knowledge, and therefore is not contradictory: this is the import. By this, it is stated that the meaning of 'atarkye' is that He is not within the reach of false reasoning. The construction of 'thus in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>' connects with 'because the having-of-parts is stated for that very one.'

children.text:
rasaśabdena viśeṣaṇāttattatsārabhūtaṃ cinmātramevocyate /
idamiti ca dṛśyamānasannihitatvāt /
children.translated_text:
By the word '<s>rasa</s>' (essence), since it is a qualifier, what is described is pure consciousness alone (<s>cinmātra</s>), which is the essence of each [sheath].
And [the word] 'this' (<s>idam</s>) is because of the proximity of what is visible and present.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.6, verse 21:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.21:
nanu yaduktaṃ sa vā iti vākye 'sya paramātmana eva parāmarśaḥ na annātpuruṣaḥ ityuktadehasyeti tadayuktam; ātmano dūrasthatvāddehasya sa samāpasthatvātsamīpoktaparityāgena dūrasthaparāmarśāṅgīkāre kāraṇābhāvāt / kiñca - puruṣapadena prakṛtasyaiva puruṣapadenoktatvāt ātmanaśca tena aprakṛtatvātpuruṣapadena parāmarśāyogaḥ / na ca -
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 21:
But what was said — that in the sentence 'sa vā eṣaḥ' (He indeed, this one), the reference is to the <s>Paramātman</s> alone, not to the body stated as 'the person [born] from food' — that is not proper, because the Self (<s>ātman</s>) is distant while the body is close and present. Since, when the nearby referent is available, there is no reason to accept the reference to the distant one by abandoning the nearby one, [the reference should be to the body]. Moreover — since the subject under discussion (<s>prakṛta</s>) is itself stated by the word 'puruṣa' (person), and since the Self is not thus stated by [that word], the reference through the word 'puruṣa' to the Self is inappropriate. And [one should not argue] —
Know both <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Person) to be beginningless.

children.text: puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijān guṇān //
children.translated_text: The Person (<s>puruṣa</s>) situated in <s>Prakṛti</s> enjoys the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) born of <s>Prakṛti</s>. //

children.text: iti vākyadvayasthapuruṣapadena ekavidhenaiva vyavasthāyā paramātmajīvayoruktigrahaṇavadihāpi ekavidhenaiva dviruktena puruṣapadena vyavasthayārthadvayoktyaṅgīkāro 'stviti vācyam / tatra duḥkhānubhavitṛtvarūpabhedakaśrutivatprakṛte bhedakābhāvena annātpuruṣaḥ ityatra dehaḥ, sa vā ityatra ca paramātmaivocyata iti vyavasthāṅgīkārāyogādityata āha - raseti // sa vā eṣaḥ iti vartate /
children.translated_text: — [one should not argue:] just as in these two sentences, by the single-form word 'puruṣa' used twice, the two meanings of <s>Paramātman</s> and <s>jīva</s> are grasped through contextual determination (<s>vyavasthā</s>), so here too let the acceptance of the two meanings by the single-form word 'puruṣa' used twice through contextual determination be [accepted]. [This is not valid] because there, just as with the <s>Śruti</s> that has a differentiating factor in the form of experiencing suffering, in the present [passage], due to the absence of a differentiating factor, 'from food, a person' [refers to] the body, and 'He indeed, this one' [refers to] the <s>Paramātman</s> alone — the acceptance of contextual determination is not possible. To this he says: 'rasa' (essence). 'He indeed, this one' is understood [as continuing].

children.text: tadityāvartate / evamucyata iti ca / anyadvihāyeti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca sa vā iti vākyena cideva cinmātraṃ brahmacaitanyameva ucyate parāmṛśyate na dehaḥ / na ca tasya dūroktivirodhaḥ, puruṣapadenāprakṛtatvavirodhaśceti vācyam / yatastat ātmana ākāśassambhūtaḥ (tai.u. 2-1-2.) ityākāśādipuruṣāntaśabdairuktaṃ tattatsārabhūtam ākāśādipadārthaśreṣṭhabhūtaṃ cinmātraṃ brahmaiva sa vā iti parāmarśavākyenocyate / evaṃ tarhi puruṣapadena dvayorapi prakṛtatvādubhayaparāmarśo 'yamastviti na ca vācyam / yataḥ tatsārabhūtaṃ puruṣasārabhūtaṃ cinmātraṃ brahmaivānyadehādikaṃ vihāya saḥ iti parāmarśavākyenocyate / kuta ityata āha - raseti / rasaśabdaghaṭitānnarasamayaśabdena viśeṣaṇāt sārānnamayatvarūpapuruṣaviśeṣaṇābhidhānādityarthaḥ / jaḍāmiśrajīvavilakṣaṇabrahmabodhārthaṃ mātrapadam / rasaśabdena rasaśabdārthena mukhyatvena viśeṣaṇāt viśeṣitatvāt annatvarūpaviśeṣaṇasyeti vā / tataścātra annaraso 'nnasāro 'nnaśabdārtheṣu mukhyāttṛtvādilakṣaṇastatpracuraḥ iti sudhokteḥ / ṭīkāyāṃ caitanyamātraṃ brahmaivetyanvayaḥ / nanvanuvākāntare annamayaprāṇamayamanomayavijñānamayānandamayā me śuddhyantām (yājñikī. 66.) iti prārthitaśuddhīnāmannamayādikośānāmabhidhānam/ kintu, tattatsārabhūtaṃ tattatkośaniyāmakaṃ tadgataṃ brahmacaitanyameva ucyate / kutaḥ? atra sa vā eṣaḥ (tai.u. 2-1-3.) ityādau raso vai saḥ ityante cānnamayādīnāṃ kośavyāvṛttyarthaṃ tadbhedārthameva rasaśabdena viśeṣaṇāt viśeṣitatvādityarthaḥ / ādau viśeṣitatvaṃ ghaṭitatvam / tathā ca śabdāntaranyāyenānnamayādyapekṣayānnarasamayādīnāṃ bheda iti bhāvaḥ / upalakṣaṇametat / vyavahitākāśādikāraṇātmaparāmarśinā tacchabdena ca viśeṣaṇādityapi draṣṭavyam / nanu yadi paridṛśyamānadeha eva nānnamayaḥ, kintu brahmaiva tasyaiva ca saḥ ityādau parāmarśaḥ, tadā tasyedameva śiraḥ (tai.u. 2-1-3.) iti pratyakṣanirdeśo nopapadyate/ na ca vācyam upaniṣaddraṣṭā munirbrahmāparokṣīkṛtya pratyakṣato nirdiśatīti / tathā sati tenāparokṣīkṛtaprāṇamayādāvapi tathā nirdeśaprasaṅgāt / kiñca - svasyāparokṣato jñātatvena śabdānapekṣaṇāt upadeśyapuruṣāṇāṃ cāparokṣāyogyatvānnirdeśavaiyarthyamityata tadasyetyapi vyākhyeyam / tathā ca asya annamayabhagavacchiraḥpakṣādeḥ dṛśyamānapratyakṣasiddhadehaśiraḥpakṣādau vastravarmāntarvartijānuvīrāvayavavat sannihitatvāt samyaṅniyāmakatvena sthitatvāt lakṣaṇayā brahmaśirasi idamiti nirdeśo yujyata iti yojanā / lakṣaṇābījaṃ śakyasambandhaṃ darśayituṃ - dṛśyamāneti / tathā ca vastraprāvṛte varmāntargate vā jānunīdaṃ jānviti vyavahāravadayamapi vyavahāro yujyata eveti na tadvirodha iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'tat' (that) recurs [from the previous passage]. And it is said 'thus it is stated.' The remainder is 'setting aside everything else.' And thus, by the sentence 'sa vā' (he indeed), what is referred to is <s>cit</s> (consciousness) alone, pure <s>cinmātra</s> (consciousness-only), <s>Brahmacaitanya</s> (Brahman-consciousness) itself — not the body. Nor should one object that there is a contradiction with the distant reference, or a contradiction with the word <s>puruṣa</s> (person) referring to something not under discussion. Because what was stated by the words from <s>ākāśa</s> (space) to <s>puruṣa</s> in 'From that <s>Ātman</s>, <s>ākāśa</s> was born' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.2) — the essence of all those, the supreme among the entities denoted by words such as <s>ākāśa</s>, namely <s>cinmātra Brahman</s> (consciousness-only Brahman) itself — is referred to by the referential sentence 'sa vā' (he indeed). Nor should one say 'since the word <s>puruṣa</s> applies to both [the body and Brahman], let this be a reference to both.' Because, setting aside the body and other things, <s>cinmātra Brahman</s> alone, which is the essence of that <s>puruṣa</s>, is referred to by the referential sentence 'saḥ' (he). To the question 'why?', he answers — with 'rasa' (essence). The meaning is: because of the qualification by the word <s>annarasamaya</s> (consisting of the essence of food), which is formed with the word <s>rasa</s>, the qualification describing the <s>puruṣa</s> as having the nature of being the essence, the <s>annamaya</s> (food-constituted), is stated. The word <s>mātra</s> (only/mere) is for the purpose of conveying knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> as distinct from the insentient, the mixed, and the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul). Or: because of being qualified — being made specific — by the primary meaning of the word <s>rasa</s>, the qualifier having the nature of <s>annatva</s> (being food) [is indicated]. And therefore here, <s>annarasa</s> means the essence of food; among the meanings of the word <s>anna</s> (food), the primary one being characterized by enjoyership etc., 'that which abounds in it' — thus it is well stated. In the <s>Ṭīkā</s> (gloss), the construal is: <s>caitanyamātra</s> (pure consciousness) is <s>Brahman</s> alone. Now, in another <s>anuvāka</s> (section), 'May my <s>annamaya</s>, <s>prāṇamaya</s>, <s>manomaya</s>, <s>vijñānamaya</s>, and <s>ānandamaya</s> [sheaths] be purified' (<s>Yājñikī</s> 66) — this refers to the <s>annamaya</s> and other <s>kośas</s> (sheaths) whose purification is prayed for. However, what is referred to is the <s>Brahmacaitanya</s> (Brahman-consciousness) alone that is the essence of each of those, the controller of each of those sheaths, and present within them. Why? Because at the beginning, in 'sa vā eṣaḥ' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.3) and at the end in 'raso vai saḥ' (he is indeed the essence), the qualification by the word <s>rasa</s> is for the purpose of distinguishing [Brahman] from the <s>annamaya</s> and other <s>kośas</s>, for establishing difference from them — this is the meaning. The qualification at the beginning means 'being formed with [the word rasa].' And thus, by the principle of other words, there is difference between the <s>annarasamaya</s> etc. and the <s>annamaya</s> etc. — this is the purport. This is illustrative [not exhaustive]. One should also see that there is qualification by the word 'tat' (that) which refers back to the intervening cause-self beginning with <s>ākāśa</s>. Now, if the visible body itself is not the <s>annamaya</s>, but rather <s>Brahman</s> alone, and if it is <s>Brahman</s> that is referred to by 'saḥ' (he) etc., then the direct perceptual indication 'this is its head' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.3) would be impossible. Nor should one say that the seer of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>, the sage, having realized <s>Brahman</s> directly, indicates it perceptually — because in that case, the same direct indication would apply to the <s>prāṇamaya</s> etc. that he has also directly realized. Moreover, since what is known directly by oneself does not require words, and since the persons being instructed are incapable of direct realization, the indication would be purposeless. Therefore, 'tad asya' (this of it) should also be explained [differently]. And thus: the head, wings, etc. of this <s>annamaya</s> form of the Lord — since they are situated within the directly visible, perceptually established body-head-wings etc. like a knee or a warrior's limb situated inside clothing or armor, and since [Brahman] stands as the complete controller — by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary indication), the indication 'this' with respect to <s>Brahman</s>'s head is appropriate — this is the interpretation. To show the basis of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, the connection with what is expressible, [he says] 'dṛśyamāna' (visible). And thus, just as one says 'this is the knee' of someone covered by cloth or enclosed in armor, this usage too is appropriate — there is no contradiction in it. This is the purport.
Though non-different, <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s> is spoken of by the word 'other'; likewise, though one, He possesses many forms,
The Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person), is so declared because of [His] <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereign power).
Thus in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.22:
nanvannamayādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ brahmatānupapannā 'tasmādvā etasmādannarasamayāt / anyo 'ntara ātmā prāṇamayaḥ'; (tai.u. 2-2-2.) iti parasparaṃ bhinnatvenoktatvāt / evamekasyaiva brahmaṇo bahurūpatvāt na 'ekameva'; iti śrutivirodhaḥ ityapyayuktamapramitatvādityata āha - ananya iti // apiryadyapītyadyarthe / tathāśabdaḥ samuccaye / tathā ca 'puruṣottamo bhagavānviṣṇuḥ'; 'ananyo 'pi'; abhinno 'pi anyo bhinna iti śabdena procyata / tathā yadyapyekastathāpi bahurūpavān bhavatītyarthaḥ / kathamityata ubhayaghaṭakamāha -
aiśvaryāditi / acintyaśakterityarthaḥ / upalakṣaṇametat / annamayādipañcakośagatānyatvāntaratvādayo dharmāstadgatabhagavadrūpeṣūpacaryanta ityapi draṣṭavyam / ata eva tṛtīye 'sthānabhedādaiśvaryācca'; iti bhāṣye sthānabhedākhyaṃ hetvantaramabhihitam / taittirīyabhāṣye tu - bhedābhāve 'pi saṅkhyāviśeṣayuktatvādanyatvoktirityuktam / brahmāṇḍe purāṇe ityanantaram uktatvānna virodha ityanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: Now, the identity of the five [sheaths] beginning with <s>annamaya</s> with <s>Brahman</s> is untenable, since they are stated as mutually different in 'From this <s>annarasamaya</s> [self], different, inner, is a self that is <s>prāṇamaya</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.2.2). [Objection:] If one and the same <s>Brahman</s> has many forms, then there would be contradiction with the <s>śruti</s> 'it is one alone.' [Reply:] This too is inappropriate because it is not established [as a valid objection]. To this he says — 'ananya' (non-different). The word 'api' is in the sense of 'yadyapi' (even though). The word 'tathā' is for conjunction [indicating addition]. And thus: '<s>Puruṣottama Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s>', 'though non-different (ananyo 'pi)', though undivided, is spoken of by the word 'other' (anya), meaning 'different.' Likewise, even though He is one, He possesses many forms — this is the meaning. To the question 'how is this possible?', he states what reconciles both — 'aiśvaryāt' (because of sovereign power). The meaning is: because of [His] inconceivable power. This is illustrative [not exhaustive]. The properties such as otherness and interiority pertaining to the five <s>kośas</s> (sheaths) beginning with <s>annamaya</s> are figuratively attributed to the forms of the Lord present within them — this should also be understood. For this very reason, in the third [<s>adhyāya</s>], the <s>bhāṣya</s> states 'because of difference of location and because of sovereign power,' presenting another reason called 'difference of location.' In the <s>Taittirīya Bhāṣya</s>, however, it is stated: 'even in the absence of real difference, the statement of otherness is justified because of the propriety of numerical distinction.' After [the citation from] the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>, the construal is: therefore there is no contradiction.
And by the stated implication, it is not <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others who are spoken of.
The other [i.e., one other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>] is not [the <s>Ānandamaya</s>], because it would be impossible. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.16 |

children.text:
na hyanyajñānānmokṣa upapadyate /
'tamevaṃ vidvānamṛta iha bhavati /
nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyate'; (tai. ā. 3-12-7.) iti hyuktam /
children.translated_text: For liberation from the knowledge of another [deity] is impossible. 'One who knows Him thus becomes immortal here; there is no other path for attaining [liberation]' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12.7) — thus it has been declared.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.23:
nanu brahmaśabdasya sādhāraṇatvāt taddhetuvyapadeśasya viṣṇuniṣṭhatayā spaṣṭapratibhānāt mantravarṇasamākhyāyāśca anyaliṅgādibhyo durbalatvena sāvakāśatvāt ananyathāsiddhahetvantarasya cābhāvādānandamayādayo viriñcādaya eva santviti śaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramavatārayati - na ceti // co 'vadhāraṇe / viriñcādaya ityanenānveti / tathā ca 'uktaprāptyā'; brahmaśabdaśatānandatvāṣṭamūrtitvabahubhāvādirūpoktaprāpakenānnamayādiśabdairviriñcādirevocyate / na viṣṇuriti na, kintu, viṣṇureva tairucyate / na viriñcādirityarthaḥ / kuto neti hetvākāṅkṣāyāṃ sūtramupanyasya pratijñāṃśasya na cetyādibhāṣyeṇaiva vyākhyātatvātsautramananyathāsiddhahetumeva vyācaṣṭe - netara iti / hiśabdo hetau / 'anyajñānāt'; viṣṇvanyaviriñcādijñānāt / yadyapyayaṃ netara ityuktasādhye na hetuḥ/ tathāpi tasyānanyathāsiddhatvopapādakatvāddhetutvoktiḥ / asya hetuvākyasya adhyāhṛtahetuvākyadvārā na ceti pratijñayānvayaḥ / anenānandamayādiḥ viṣṇoritaro viriñcādirna, kutaḥ? 'brahmavidāpnoti param (tai.u. 2-1-1.) ... sarvaṃ vai te 'nnamāpnuvanti (tai.u. 2-2-1.).... sarvameva ta āyuryanti'; (tai.u. 2-3-1.) ityādinā ānandamayādermuktihetujñānaviṣayatvokteḥ, tasya cetaratra 'anupapatteḥ'; ayogāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / viṣṇujñānādeva mokṣo netarajñānādityetatkuta ityata āha - tamiti / 'hi'; yasmāt 'tamevam'; iti śrutyā mokṣasya viṣṇujñānādanya upāyo nāstītyuktam / tasmādviṣṇoranyajñānānmokṣo nopapadyata ityarthaḥ / śrutyarthastu prāgevoktaḥ //
children.translated_text: Now, since the word <s>brahman</s> is common [to multiple deities], since the designation of its cause is not clearly evident as pertaining exclusively to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since <s>mantravarṇasamākhyā</s> (designation by the words of mantras) is weaker than other indicators, and since there is no other independently established reason — [one might object:] let <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the rest be <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others. Dispelling this doubt, he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> — 'na ca' (and not). The word 'ca' is for emphasis. It connects with '<s>Viriñca</s> and others.' And thus: 'by the stated implication (uktaprāptyā)' — by the implication conveyed through terms like <s>annamaya</s> etc., which carry the force of descriptions such as being called <s>brahman</s>, having hundredfold bliss, having eight forms, and being manifold — it is <s>Viriñca</s> and others who are spoken of; not <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is not so; rather, it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone who is spoken of by those [terms]. Not <s>Viriñca</s> and others — this is the meaning. When the expectation arises 'why not?', having cited the <s>sūtra</s>, since the thesis-portion has already been explained by the <s>bhāṣya</s> beginning with 'na ca,' he explains the independently established reason stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — 'netara' (not the other). The word 'hi' indicates reason. 'From the knowledge of another (anyajñānāt)' — from knowledge of <s>Viriñca</s> and others who are other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Although this is not strictly a reason for the thesis stated in 'netara,' nevertheless, since it establishes the independent validity [of the thesis], the statement of it as a reason is justified. This reason-sentence connects with the thesis 'na ca' through an implied intermediate reason-sentence. By this [the meaning is]: the <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the rest are not the other, namely <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), who is other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? Because it is stated in 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the Supreme' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.1), 'They indeed obtain all food' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.2.1), 'All their life-span indeed extends' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.3.1) etc. that the <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the rest are the objects of knowledge that is the cause of <s>mukti</s> (liberation), and because this 'does not hold good (anupapatteḥ)' — is impossible — in the case of the other [deities]. Thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated. Liberation comes from knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not from knowledge of others — to the question 'how do we know this?', he says — 'tam' (Him). Because by the <s>śruti</s> 'tam evam' (Him alone thus [knowing]), it is declared that there is no other means of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) besides knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Therefore, liberation is impossible from knowledge of anyone other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the meaning. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> has already been explained earlier.
And because of the declaration of difference. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.17 |

children.text:
'te ye śataṃ prajāpaterānandāḥ'; (tai. 2-8.)
'adṛśye 'nātmye 'nirukte 'nilayane 'bhayaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vindate /
atha so 'bhayaṃ gato bhavati'; (tai. 2-7.) 'sa yaścāyaṃ puruṣe'; (tai. 2-8.)
ityādi bhedavyapadeśāt /
children.translated_text: 'Those which are the hundred blisses of <s>Prajāpati</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.8); 'In the invisible, in that which is without a self [i.e., without the limitations of individual selves], in the inexpressible, in that which has no resting place, one finds fearless stability; then he becomes free from fear' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.7); 'He who is in the person' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.8) — because of such declarations of difference.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.24:
hetvantareṇa brahmādīnāmānandamayatvaṃ parākurvatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - bhedeti / atra pūrvahetusamuccāyakena caśabdenānandamayādirnetara iti pratijñāvākyānuvṛtterapi sūcanāt / tadvihāya sūtroktaṃ bhedavyapadeśaṃ darśayati - te ye śatamiti // ādiśabdaḥ 'ānandāḥ'; ityataḥ paro 'pi yojyaḥ / tatrādyena 'te ye śatam'; ityasya pūrvottarataittirīyavākyāni gṛhyante / dvitīyena 'yato vāco nivartante / aprāpya manasā saha / ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān', (tai.u. 2-4-1.) ityādi / yadvā sakṛcchruta eva sarvasaṅgrāhakaḥ/ anena nānandamaya itaro viriñcaḥ, kutaḥ? bhedavyapadeśāt / viriñcasya 'te ye śatam'; (tai.u. 2-8-4.) ityādinā rudrācchataguṇānandatvokteḥ, ānandamayasya ca 'yato vācaḥ'; ityādināparimitānandatvokteḥ / evaṃ na rudraḥ, tasya hiraṇyagarbhācchatāṃśonānandatvokteḥ / nāpi prakṛtyādayaḥ, 'adṛśyenātmye'; ityādau prakṛtyādyayogyasvātantryādirūpabhedakadharmaśravaṇāt / nāpyānandamayo brahmādijīvasamudāyaḥ, tasya 'sa yaścāyam'; iti apakṛṣṭotkṛṣṭasarvajīsthitirūpabhedakadharmokteḥ jīvasamudāyasya cānevaṃvidhatvāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / ete ca sarve vyapadeśāḥ taittirīyaśrutigatāḥ / tatra 'prajāpatiḥ śivaḥ śepho liṅgamityabhidhīyate'; iti śaivapurāṇavacanāt 'prajāpateḥ'; rudrasya 'ye śataṃ'; śataguṇitā ānandāḥ te 'brahmaṇaḥ'; caturmukhasya eka ānanda iti prathamavākyasyārthaḥ / 'adṛśye'; sākalyenājñeye 'anātmye'; ātmanaḥ ime ātmyāḥ jīvagīṇāḥ na vidyante ātmyāḥ yasmin so 'nātmyaḥ tasmin jīvaguṇavidhure / athavā - ātmanaḥ svāmino 'yamātmyaḥ svāmisambandhī sa netyanātmyaḥ tasmin, svāmirahita iti yāvat / 'anirukte'; sākalyena nirvacanāgocare / 'anilayane'; ananyāśraye ānandamayaśabdavācye viṣṇau tadviṣaye yo 'dhikārī 'abhayaṃ'; yathā bhavati tathā dhyānarūpāṃ 'pratiṣṭhāṃ'; sthitiṃ 'vindate'; prāpnoti, karotīti yāvat / 'atha'; anantaraṃ 'saḥ'; upāsakaḥ 'abhayaṃ'; bhayarahitaṃ bhagavantaṃ 'gataḥ'; prāpto bhavatīti dvitīyabhedavyapadeśasyārthaḥ / 'puruṣe'; puruṣapadopalakṣitāpakṛṣṭajīveṣu 'yaḥ'; ayamānandamayo viṣṇurasti / 'yaścāditye'; ādityapadopalakṣitotkṛṣṭajīveṣvasti 'saḥ'; ubhayatra sthito viṣṇuḥ 'ekaḥ'; abhinna iti tṛtīyabhedavyapadeśasyārthaḥ / 'yato vācaḥ'; ityādistu prāgeva vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: Having cited the <s>sūtra</s> which, by another reason, refutes the <s>Ānandamaya</s>-hood of <s>Brahmā</s> and others, he explains — 'bheda' (difference). Here, since the word 'ca' (and) in the <s>sūtra</s>, which conjoins with the previous reason, also indicates the continuation of the thesis-sentence '<s>Ānandamaya</s> and the rest are not the other,' he sets that aside and shows the declaration of difference stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — 'te ye śatam' (those which are a hundred). The word 'ādi' (etc.) should be connected also with what follows 'ānandāḥ' (blisses). Among these, by the first — 'te ye śatam' — the preceding and following <s>Taittirīya</s> passages are included. By the second — 'From which words return, not reaching it, together with the mind; one who knows the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.1) etc. Or, once heard, [the word 'ādi'] is all-inclusive. By this [the argument is]: the <s>Ānandamaya</s> is not the other, namely <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). Why? Because of the declaration of difference. Because <s>Viriñca</s>'s bliss is declared by 'te ye śatam' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.8.4) etc. as being a hundredfold of <s>Rudra</s>'s bliss, while the <s>Ānandamaya</s>'s bliss is declared by 'yato vācaḥ' etc. as being immeasurable. Likewise, [the <s>Ānandamaya</s>] is not <s>Rudra</s>, because his bliss is declared as one hundredth of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>'s. Nor is it <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest, because in 'adṛśye, anātmye' etc., qualities that differentiate [the <s>Ānandamaya</s>] are heard that are inappropriate for <s>Prakṛti</s> etc., such as independence and the like. Nor is the <s>Ānandamaya</s> the aggregate of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, because by 'sa yaś cāyam' (he who is this), differentiating properties in the form of presence in both inferior and superior <s>jīvas</s> are declared, and an aggregate of <s>jīvas</s> is not of such nature — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated. All these declarations are found in the <s>Taittirīya Śruti</s>. There, since in the <s>Śaiva Purāṇa</s> it is stated '<s>Prajāpati</s> is called <s>Śiva</s>, the generative organ is called <s>liṅga</s>,' the meaning of the first passage is: those blisses which are a hundredfold of <s>Prajāpati</s>, i.e., <s>Rudra</s>'s, constitute one bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, i.e., the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>]. 'Adṛśye' — in that which is wholly unknowable; 'anātmye' — '<s>ātmya</s>' means the qualities of <s>jīvas</s> (those belonging to the self); 'anātmya' means that in which <s>jīva</s>-qualities do not exist, i.e., devoid of <s>jīva</s>-qualities. Alternatively — '<s>ātmya</s>' means 'belonging to the master (<s>svāmin</s>)'; 'anātmya' means 'not thus,' i.e., without a master, meaning self-dependent. 'Anirukte' — in that which is beyond complete verbal description. 'Anilayane' — in that which has no other support; in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is denoted by the word <s>Ānandamaya</s>; with respect to Him, the qualified aspirant 'finds (vindate),' i.e., attains, obtains, a 'stability (pratiṣṭhā)' in the form of meditation such that 'fearlessness (abhayam)' results. 'Atha' — thereafter, 'saḥ' — that worshipper, 'having reached (gataḥ)' the Lord who is 'fearless (abhayam),' free from fear, 'becomes' [liberated] — this is the meaning of the second declaration of difference. 'In the person (puruṣe)' — in the inferior <s>jīvas</s> indicated by the word <s>puruṣa</s>, 'yaḥ' — this <s>Ānandamaya Viṣṇu</s> exists; 'and in the sun (yaś cāditye)' — and He exists in the superior <s>jīvas</s> indicated by the word <s>āditya</s> (sun); 'saḥ' — that <s>Viṣṇu</s> present in both is 'ekaḥ' — undivided — this is the meaning of the third declaration of difference. 'Yato vācaḥ' (from which words [return]) etc. has already been explained earlier.

children.text:
na ca 'tattvamasi'; (chā. 6-8.) 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi'; (bṛ. 3-4-10.)
ityādiśrutivirodhaḥ /
'nāmāni sarvāṇi yamāviśanti'; (bhāllaveyaśruti)
iti tattacchabdavācyatvokteḥ /
children.translated_text: And there is no contradiction with <s>śrutis</s> such as 'You are That (<s>tat tvam asi</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8) and 'I am <s>Brahman</s> (<s>ahaṃ brahmāsmi</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.4.10). Because it is declared [in the <s>Bhāllaveyaśruti</s>] that 'all names enter into Him,' [meaning] He is the one denoted by all such words as 'tat' and 'tvam.'

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.25:
nanvastvānandamayaḥ paraṃ brahma / tathāpi tena kathaṃ brahmādīnāṃ bhedaḥ sambhavati / tadbhedasya 'tattvamasi'; ityādi śrutiviruddhatvādityata āha - na ceti // bhedavyapadeśasyeti śeṣaḥ / caḥ samuccaye / etadvirodhaśaṅkāparihārasamuccitasyaiva bhedavyapadeśasya vivakṣitārthasādhakatvāt / evamanyatrāpi / tvaṃ tadbrahmāsītyadvaitarītyādya-
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.25: [Objection:] Granted that <s>Ānandamaya</s> is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>; even so, how is difference (<s>bheda</s>) between It and <s>Brahmā</s> and the others possible, since such difference would contradict <s>Śruti</s> passages like '<s>tattvamasi</s>' (You are That) and the like? — to this he says: 'na ca' (and not). // 'Of the statement of difference' (<s>bhedavyapadeśasya</s>) is the remainder. The word 'ca' is for aggregation — because the very statement of difference, which has been aggregated with the resolution of this objection of contradiction, has the capacity to establish the intended meaning. Likewise in other [contexts] too. 'You are that <s>Brahman</s>' — this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> according to the <s>Advaita</s> interpretation and the like —

children.text: śrutyarthaḥ / dvatīyasyāstu ahaṃ brahmābhinno 'smīti / ādyam uddālakena śvetaketuṃ pratyupadiṣṭaṃ chandogavākyam / dvitīyaṃ bṛhadāraṇyake vāmadevoktam / atrobhayatrāpi viśiṣṭayoraikyāsambhavāt tattvamahaṃbrahmapadairlakṣitacaitanyayoraikyamucyate / ādiśabdena 'tadyo 'haṃ so 'sau yo 'sau so 'haṃ'; (ai.ā. 2-2-4.) 'yo 'sāvasau puruṣaḥ so 'hamasmi'; (ī. 26.) ityādiśrutirgṛhyate / kuto netyatastatraitacchrutīnāṃ parabrahmārthakatvena advaitārthatvābhāvāditi hetūpaskāramabhipretya teṣāṃ parabrahmārthatve pramāṇamāha - nāmānīti / 'nāmāni'; iti śrutyā tasya brahmaṇaḥ 'tattacchabdaiḥ'; tattvamādipadairvācyatvokterityarthaḥ / tathā ca padasamanvayenaiteṣāṃ brahmaparatvānnaitadvirodha iti bhāvaḥ / tatprakārastu - tatatvāttat / tvampadabodhyajīvāntaryāmitvādabhimukhatvādvā tvam / asanāt jagatsaṃharaṇādasiḥ / aheyatvāt haṃnāmakajīvabhinnatvādvā aham / pūrṇatvādbrahma / asanānminuterasmi / yadvā - sumitatvāt smītyukto jīvaḥ, tadbhinnaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahma asmītyucyata iti / jñānarūpatvāt nitarāṃ yantṛtvācca yaḥ / saraṇātsāratvācca saḥ / amuṣmin amuṣmin sthitatvātparokṣatvācca asāvasauśabdavācyaḥ ityaitareyaśrutyarthaḥ / 'asau'; prāṇe sthitaḥ 'puruṣaḥ'; pūrṇaṣaḍguṇaḥ iti īśāvāsyaśrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the meaning of the second [passage] is: I am non-different from <s>Brahman</s>. The first is the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage taught by <s>Uddālaka</s> to <s>Śvetaketu</s>. The second is spoken by <s>Vāmadeva</s> in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>. Here, in both cases, since the identity of two qualified [entities] is impossible, the identity of the consciousnesses indicated by the words '<s>tat</s>' (That), '<s>tvam</s>' (you), '<s>aham</s>' (I), and '<s>brahma</s>' is stated. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the <s>Śruti</s> passages 'That which I am, he is; that which he is, I am' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.2.4) and 'That Person yonder — I am he' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 26) and the like are included. 'Why not [so]?' — because these <s>Śruti</s>s have the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> as their referent, and therefore do not have the meaning of non-duality: intending this qualification of the reason, he cites authority for their having the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> as referent: '<s>nāmāni</s>' (names). By the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>nāmāni</s>' (names), 'of that <s>Brahman</s>' — 'by those respective words' — by words such as '<s>tat</s>' (That), '<s>tvam</s>' (you), and the like — the expressibility is stated: this is the meaning. And thus, since through word-by-word interpretation (<s>padasamanvaya</s>) these [passages] have <s>Brahman</s> as their referent, there is no contradiction: this is the purport. The method is as follows: Because of being the essence (<s>tattva</s>), [He is called] '<s>tat</s>' (That). Because of being the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) of the <s>jīva</s> cognizable by the word '<s>tvam</s>' (you), or because of being favorably disposed, [He is] '<s>tvam</s>.' Because of destroying (<s>asan</s>) — because of dissolving the world — [He is] '<s>asi</s>' (you are). Because of being irrejectable (<s>aheya</s>), or because of being different from the <s>jīva</s> called '<s>haṃ</s>' — [He is] '<s>aham</s>' (I). Because of fullness (<s>pūrṇatva</s>), [He is] '<s>brahma</s>.' Because of destroying (<s>asan</s>) and measuring out (<s>minoti</s>), [He is] '<s>asmi</s>' (I am). Or: the <s>jīva</s> is called '<s>smī</s>' because of being well-measured (<s>sumita</s>), and the complete <s>Brahman</s> different from it is said [to be denoted by] '<s>asmi</s>' (I am). Because of being of the nature of knowledge (<s>jñānarūpatva</s>) and because of being the supreme controller (<s>yantṛtva</s>) — [He is denoted by] '<s>yaḥ</s>' (who). Because of being the mover (<s>saraṇa</s>) and because of being the essence (<s>sāratva</s>) — [He is] '<s>saḥ</s>' (he). Because of being situated in this and that [entity], and because of being beyond [direct perception] (<s>parokṣatva</s>) — He is expressible by the words '<s>asau</s>' and '<s>asau</s>': this is the meaning of the <s>Aitareya Śruti</s>. 'That' (<s>asau</s>) — situated in <s>Prāṇa</s>; '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — full and possessing the six attributes: this is the meaning of the <s>Īśāvāsya Śruti</s>.

children.text:
idaṃ hi viśvaṃ bhagavānivetaro yato jagatsthānanirodhasambhavaḥ /
asarvaḥ sarva ityapi (turaśrutiḥ) /
children.translated_text: This entire universe is indeed the Lord, and He is other [than it]; from whom are the world's continuance, cessation, and origination. He is the non-all [yet] the all — thus says the <s>Śruti</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.26:
astu vā etacchrutīnāṃ aikyaparatvaṃ vākyānvayarītyā / tathāpi naikyaśrutivirodho bhedaśruteḥ śaṅkanīyaḥ, bhagavataḥ sarvaikyaśruteḥ sarvasvāmitvanimittaikyaparatvādityāśayena tatra pramāṇatvena bhāgavatasmṛtiṃ paṭhati - idaṃ hīti // 'bhagavān'; svayam 'itaro 'pi'; jagato bhinno 'pi san 'idaṃ'; pramitaṃ viśvamivocyate 'tattvamasi'; 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi'; ityādivacaneṣu / yathoktaṃ prathamatātparye - 'itaro 'pi bhagavānviśvamiva'; iti / kutaḥ? 'yataḥ'; kāraṇāt 'jagatsthānanirodhasambhavaḥ'; jagataḥ sthānaṃ sthitiḥ nirodho nāśaḥ sambhavaḥ utpattiḥ te yasmādbhavanti sa tathoktaḥ / yadvā - sthāpayati nirodhayati sambhāvyatyasmāditi tathoktaḥ / athavā - tiṣṭhatyasmāt niruddhyate pralīyate 'smin sambhāvayatīti sa tathoktaḥ / tathā ca jagatsṛṣṭyādikartetyarthaḥ / evambhūtsya jagadbhedaḥ pramāṇasiddha iti jñāpanāya hiśabdaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - bahuvrīhiṃ vinā idaṃ viśvaṃ bhagavāniva; etadadhīnatvāt / sa tvitaraḥ / kaḥ? 'yato'; yasmāt 'jagatsthānanirodhasambhavo'; jagatsṛṣṭyādikamityuktam / atra ṭīkāyāṃ ca bhagavānidaṃ viśvamivetyanvayaḥ / svāmitvenaikyavyapadeśa ityetadevāha - asarva iti / turaśrutiḥ / bhagavān sarvabhinno 'pi sarvasvāmitvāt sarva ityabhedena vedādiṣūcyate ityarthaḥ / ityapīti śrutisthaḥ apiḥ samuccaye / yata iti śeṣaḥ / asya ato 'pi na virodha ityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.26: Or let these <s>Śruti</s> passages have identity as their purport, through the method of sentence-level interpretation. Even so, the contradiction of the unity-<s>Śruti</s>s with the difference-<s>Śruti</s>s should not be suspected, because the Lord's unity-<s>Śruti</s>s have [His] ownership of all as their [intended] purport of identity. With this intention, he cites as authority the <s>Bhāgavata Smṛti</s>: '<s>idaṃ hi</s>' (this indeed). // The '<s>Bhagavān</s>' (Lord), Himself being 'also other' (<s>itara</s>) — different from the world, 'this' known 'universe is [said to be] like' [Him] — this is stated in [passages like] '<s>tattvamasi</s>' (You are That) and '<s>ahaṃ brahmāsmi</s>' (I am <s>Brahman</s>) and the like. As stated in the <s>Prathamatātparya</s>: 'Even though other, the Lord is like the universe.' Whence? 'Because' (<s>yataḥ</s>) 'the world's continuance, cessation, and origination' — the world's continuance (existence), cessation (destruction), and origination (creation) — proceed from Him: [He is] described thus. Or: because He causes [the world] to stand, to cease, and to come into being — [He is] described thus. Or: [He is described thus because] it exists through Him, it is dissolved in Him, and He originates it. And thus, the meaning is: He is the creator and the like of the world. The word 'hi' (indeed) is for making known that the world's difference [from Him] is established through valid means of knowledge, [even though He is spoken of as identical]. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: without a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound], 'this universe is like the Lord' — because it is dependent on Him. But 'He is other.' Who? 'From whom' — from which [entity] 'the world's continuance, cessation, and origination' — the creation and the like of the world [proceed]: thus it is said. And here in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> too, the construction is: the Lord is like this universe. That this identity-designation is because of ownership — this very thing he says: '<s>asarvaḥ</s>' (the non-all). [This is] a <s>Śruti</s> statement. The Lord, though different from all, because of ownership of all, is called 'all' — is spoken of as identical in the <s>Vedas</s> and the like: this is the meaning. 'Ityapi' (thus also) — the word 'api' occurring in the <s>Śruti</s> is for aggregation. 'Yataḥ' (because) is the remainder. The construction of this is: 'therefore from this too there is no contradiction.'
Knowledge is the understanding of difference in the Self. Through the perception of difference and through devotion, and through desireless action —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.27:
nanu bhedajñānasya mithyājñānatvātkathaṃ tadanusāreṇaikyaśrutayo yojyanta ityāśaṅkāṃ bhāgavatavākyena pariharati - vidyeti // idaṃ ca kā vidyetyuddhavapraśnasyottaratvena kṛṣṇenoktaṃ vacanamekādaśaskandhe / 'ātmani'; paramātmani 'bhidābodho'; jīvādbhedajñānaṃ jīve vā yadīśvarādbhedajñānam / saiva vidyetyarthaḥ / na ca bhidāyā abodha iti vyākhyeyam, ajñānasya vidyātvābhāvāt / nanu bhedajñānasya puruṣārthahetutvāt kathaṃ tasya vidyātvamityata āha - bhedeti / idaṃ ca bhāgavate tṛtīyaskandhagataṃ vākyam -
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.27: [Objection:] Since the knowledge of difference is false knowledge, how can the unity-<s>Śruti</s>s be interpreted in accordance with it? — he resolves this doubt through a <s>Bhāgavata</s> passage: '<s>vidyā</s>' (knowledge). // And this is a statement spoken by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as the answer to <s>Uddhava</s>'s question 'What is knowledge?' in the Eleventh Canto [of the <s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s>]. 'In the Self' (<s>ātmani</s>) — in the Supreme Self, '<s>bhidābodhaḥ</s>' (understanding of difference) — the knowledge of difference from the <s>jīva</s>; or the knowledge in the <s>jīva</s> of [its] difference from the Lord. That alone is knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>): this is the meaning. And it should not be interpreted as 'the non-cognition (<s>abodha</s>) of difference,' because non-cognition cannot be knowledge. [Objection:] Since the knowledge of difference is the cause of human goals (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), how can it be [called] knowledge? — to this he says: '<s>bheda</s>' (difference). And this is a passage from the Third Canto of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> —
He who is the first of all moving and non-moving beings, the womb of the <s>Vedas</s>, together with the sages,
with the lords of <s>yoga</s>, with <s>Kumāra</s> and the like, and with the accomplished ones who propagate <s>yoga</s> —
— this should be construed with the preceding verse
Because of [His] agency, [He is] <s>Brahman</s> with qualities, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the best of persons.
Having entered that [<s>Brahman</s>] again, at the [appropriate] time, through time in the form of the Lord —
when the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) occurs, O <s>Prajāpati</s>, as before — //
