children.text: ityuttaravākyena ca saha yojanīyam / tatprakārastu - yaḥ 'sthiracarāṇāṃ'; sthāvarajaṅgamānām 'ādyo'; hiraṇyagarbhaḥ saḥ 'ṛṣibhiḥ'; manuṣyottamamārabhya garuḍaśeṣāntaiḥ jñānibhiryogasiddhaiḥ sanatkumārādyaiḥ saha 'bhedadṛṣṭyā'; jīveśvarādibhedajñānena 'abhimānena'; abhito harermānena parameśvare bahumānena āgraheṇa ca 'niḥsaṅgena karmaṇāpi'; phalābhisandhirahitanivṛttakarmaṇā ca muktassan 'kartṛtvāt'; jagatkartṛtvānnimittāt 'saguṇaṃ'; sārvajñādiguṇasampūrṇaṃ 'puruṣarṣabhaṃ'; kṣarākṣarebhyo varaṃ 'puruṣaṃ'; paramapuruṣākhyaṃ brahma 'kāle'; pralayakāle 'saṅgatya'; praviśya punaḥ 'kālena'; kālākhyena 'īśvaramūrtinā'; mūrtyā 'kāle'; sṛṣṭikāle 'jāte'; utpanne sati 'aguṇavyatikare'; sattvādiguṇavikriyāhīne viṣṇuloke 'yathāpūrvaṃ'; pūrvavat prajāyate sarvamuktādhipatirjāyate iti sudhāyāmuktaḥ / karmanirṇayaṭīkāyāṃ tu - na kevalaṃ saguṇaṃ, kintu, 'brahma'; purṇaṃ 'puruṣamiti'; bhagavato nāmakīrtanam / puruṣatvoktyāsmādādisālakṣaṇyaṃ prāptaṃ, tatparihārāya - puruṣarṣabhamiti / tadupapādanāya kartṛtvātsaguṇaṃ brahmeti viśeṣārtha uktaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - abhimāneneti padaṃ abhito mānena viśeṣajñāneneti vyākhyāya, 'guṇavyatikare'; iti padaṃ chitvā 'sa'; brahmādijīvasaṅghaḥ pralaye jñānaiśvaryādyanantaguṇaṃ brahma 'saṅgatya'; prāpya 'punaḥ kāle'; sṛṣṭikāle 'kālena'; jñānātmanā 'īśvaramūrtinā'; viṣṇurūpeṇa 'guṇavyatikare'; guṇānāṃ sattvādīnāṃ vyatikare vaiṣamye jāte sati yathāpūrvaṃ jñānādiguṇatāratamyaṃ parasparabhedaṃ ca avihāya tadviśiṣṭa eva 'prajāyate'; prakarṣeṇa muktāvabhivyajyate / na tu tadabhinno bhavatīti vyākhyātam/ ayaṃ padacchedaṣṭīkākṛto 'pi sammataḥ / tatpakṣe 'guṇavyatikare kāle'; sṛṣṭikāle ityarthaḥ / ubhayatrāpi yathāpūrvamityasya saṃsāra ivetyartha / pūrvakalpe iveti vā /
children.translated_text: — together with the following verse. The method is as follows: He 'who' is the 'first' — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — of all 'moving and non-moving' beings; that one, together with 'sages' — from the best of humans up to <s>Garuḍa</s> and <s>Śeṣa</s>, the knowers, the <s>yoga</s>-perfected ones, <s>Sanatkumāra</s> and the like — 'through the perception of difference' — through the knowledge of difference between <s>jīva</s> and God and the like, 'through devotion' (<s>abhimāna</s>) — through thorough reverence (<s>māna</s>) for <s>Hari</s>, that is, through great regard for and firm attachment to the Supreme Lord — 'through desireless action' — through actions free from attachment to results — having become liberated, 'because of [His] agency' — because of being the cause of the world, 'entered' (<s>saṅgatya</s>) the <s>Brahman</s> 'with qualities' (<s>saguṇam</s>) — complete with qualities of omniscience and the like, 'the best of persons' (<s>puruṣarṣabham</s>) — superior to the perishable and imperishable [souls], 'the <s>Puruṣa</s>' — the Supreme Person called <s>Brahman</s>; [entered it] 'at the time' — at the time of dissolution; and again, 'through time' (<s>kālena</s>) — through the [entity] called time, 'in the form of the Lord' — through His embodiment, 'at the time' — at the time of creation, 'when the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>' (<s>aguṇavyatikare</s>) — when the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like have ceased their transformation — in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'as before' (<s>yathāpūrvam</s>) — as previously, he is born — that is, becomes manifest as the lord of all the liberated: thus it is stated in the <s>Sudhā</s>. In the <s>Karmanirṇaya Ṭīkā</s>, however: not only 'with qualities,' but rather, '<s>brahma</s>' — the complete one; '<s>puruṣam iti</s>' — this is the chanting of the Lord's name. Since the statement of being <s>Puruṣa</s> gives rise to the [objection of] similarity with us and the like, to refute that — '<s>puruṣarṣabham</s>' (the best of persons). To substantiate that — 'because of agency, <s>Brahman</s> with qualities': this specific meaning is stated. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: explaining the word '<s>abhimānena</s>' as 'through thorough particular knowledge (<s>abhito māna</s>),' and separating the word '<s>guṇavyatikare</s>': 'he' (<s>sa</s>) — the group of <s>jīvas</s> beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> — at the time of dissolution — 'having entered' (<s>saṅgatya</s>) — having reached — the <s>Brahman</s> of infinite qualities such as knowledge and sovereignty — 'again at the time' — at the time of creation, 'through time' (<s>kālena</s>) — through the form of knowledge, 'in the form of the Lord' (<s>īśvaramūrtinā</s>) — in the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'when the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> occurs' — when the imbalance of the <s>guṇas</s>, <s>sattva</s> and the like, occurs — 'as before' — without abandoning the gradation of qualities such as knowledge and the mutual difference as in the previous [creation], being distinguished by those very [qualities] — 'is born' (<s>prajāyate</s>) — becomes excellently manifest in liberation. But does not become identical with that [<s>Brahman</s>]: thus it is explained. This word-division is accepted by the <s>Ṭīkā</s>-author as well. In that reading, 'when the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> [occurs], at the time' — meaning: at the time of creation. In both [interpretations], '<s>yathāpūrvam</s>' (as before) means: as in <s>saṃsāra</s>; or: as in the previous <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle).
'When one sees the other, the Lord who is adored, and His greatness — then one becomes free from sorrow.' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.2)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.28:
atraivārthe atharvaṇavākyaṃ pramāṇayati - juṣṭamiti // juṣṭaṃ sarvasevyam īśaṃ svatantram / ata eva anyaṃ jīvādbhinnaṃ viṣṇum iti tadetatsatyam (mu. 2-1-1-.) ityādinā prāguktaprakāreṇa asya mahimānaṃ ca yadā paśyati / paśyo jīvaḥ tadā vītaśoko mukto bhavatītyarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - juṣṭaṃ devaiḥ asya jīvasya īśam anyaṃ yadā paśyati mahimānaṃ mahimaguṇātmakaṃ tadā tadaiva vītaśoko bhavati na duḥkhaleśamapi spṛśati jīvaḥ / na tu mahimaguṇavihīnam anyamanīśamasevitaṃ paśyan vītaśoko bhavatīti vyākhyātam / yadyapīyaṃ śrutiḥ viśeṣaṇabhedavyapadeśābhyām (bra. sū. 1-2-22.) ityatra ayamanyomārga ityukte prasiddhamārgādanyatvabodhavat anyamīśamityukte īśaśabditasya brahmaṇaḥ prasiddheśādrudrāt anyatvapratīterbrahmaṇo rudrādanyatve pramāṇatvenoktā / na tu brahmaṇo jīvādanyatve, nāpi īśatvamanyatve hetūkṛtam / tathāpi tat vyākhyānānantaramabhipretyeti na tadvirodhaḥ / ata eva dyubhvādinaye bhedavyapadeśāt (bra.sū. 1-3-5.) ityatra jīveśabhede 'pīyaṃ pramāṇatayodāhṛtā /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.28: For this very point, he cites as authority the <s>Atharvaṇa</s> (i.e., <s>Muṇḍaka</s>) passage: '<s>juṣṭam</s>' (adored). // '<s>Juṣṭam</s>' — worshipped by all; '<s>Īśam</s>' — independent. Hence 'the other' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is different from the <s>jīva</s> — as stated by the previously explained passage '<s>tadetatsatyam</s>' (that is the truth) (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.1) and in the manner described earlier — 'and His greatness' — 'when one sees,' the seer — the <s>jīva</s> — at that time becomes 'free from sorrow' — liberated: this is the meaning. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: '<s>juṣṭam</s>' — by the gods; '<s>of this</s>' <s>jīva</s>; '<s>the Lord</s>'; '<s>the other</s>' — when one sees [Him as] consisting of the quality of greatness (<s>mahiman</s>) — at that very moment one becomes free from sorrow; not even a trace of suffering touches the <s>jīva</s>. But one who sees [something] other — devoid of the quality of greatness, non-sovereign, unworshipped — does not become free from sorrow: thus it is explained. Even though this <s>Śruti</s> is cited as authority under [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>viśeṣaṇabhedavyapadeśābhyām</s>' (because of qualification and statement of difference) (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.22), where, just as '<s>ayamanyomārgaḥ</s>' (this is another path) indicates the otherness [of something] from the well-known path, so '<s>anyam īśam</s>' (the other, the Lord) indicates the otherness of <s>Brahman</s>, denoted by the word '<s>Īśa</s>' (Lord), from the well-known Lord <s>Rudra</s> — [that passage] is cited as proof of <s>Brahman</s>'s otherness from <s>Rudra</s>, not as proof of <s>Brahman</s>'s otherness from the <s>jīva</s>, nor is the Lordship made the ground of otherness. Nevertheless, since [the current explanation] is intended as following upon that exposition, there is no contradiction. Hence this [passage] is also cited as authority for the difference between <s>jīva</s> and God under the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> [of the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>bhedavyapadeśāt</s>' (because of the statement of difference) (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.5) in the <s>Dyubhvādi</s> topic.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.29:
evaṃ svāmitvārthatayā parābhimatādvaitaśrutīrvyākhyāya vākyasamanvayāśrayaṇena antaryāmitayāpi tāḥ śrutismṛtibhyāṃ vyācaṣṭe - asarva iti / yadyapi asarvaḥ iti vākyam ātmaśabdasya svāmitvārthatvamupetya svāmitvena nimittenaikyaśrutayaḥ pravṛttā ityatra pramāṇatayodāhṛtam / tathāpi svāmitvenevāntaryāmitayāpyaikyaśrutayaḥ pravṛttā ityubhayatrāpyasya pramāṇatvasambhavādubhayatrāpi pramāṇatayodāharaṇaṃ yuktam / tattvapradīpakṛtāmapi svāmitvenevāntaryāmitayāpyaikyaśrutayaḥ pravṛttā ityubhayatrāpi asarvaḥ iti śrutiḥ pramāṇamityabhiprāyaḥ / na caivaṃ tattadantaryāmitvenāpi tattacchabdavācyatvaṃ viṣṇorastītyāha - sarvāntaryāmikaḥ iti tattvapradīpavirodhaḥ; atra padasamanyavābhiprāyapratīteriti vācyam / antaryāmitvenāpītyuktyā na kevalaṃ nāmāni iti śrutibalāttattacchabdapravṛttinimittatvena tattacchabdavācyatvaṃ viṣṇoḥ, api tu antaryāmitvenāpītyetāvanmātrapratīteḥ atra padasamanvaye tātparyānavagamāt / mahāvākyagatasyaitadādiśabdasyaikaikasya sarvāntaryāmikaḥ iti smṛtibalāt antaryāmitvanimittena viṣṇuvācitve 'pi padāntarāṇānyaparatvena vākyasamanvayasyaiva vaktavyatvāt / yadā nāmāni iti śrutibalāt kriyākārakādisarvārthavācisarvapadasya viṣṇuvācitvābhyupagamaḥ tadaiva padasamanvayaḥ / na tvekaikasya viṣṇuvācitva iti na virodhaḥ tathā cāntaryāmitvanimittena tattvamasyādivākyagatatvamahamādipadānāṃ viṣṇuvācitve tvaṃ tvadantaryāmī tat brahma / ahaṃ madantaryāmī brahmeti vākyānvayo draṣṭavyaḥ / na caivami asi asmi iti kriyāpadānvayāyogaḥ / jīvaviśiṣṭāntaryāmivācakasya tvamādiśabdasya dagdhṛśabdasyāyasīvāntaryāmiṇi mukhyavṛttiḥ / jīvetvamukhyavṛttirityāśrayaṇenāmukhyārthavivakṣayā asi asmītyādipadaprayogopapatteḥ / yadyapi nimittakathanaprakaraṇe vidyātmani bhedadṛṣṭyā juṣṭaṃ yadā iti vākyatrayasyānvayābhāvaḥ / tathāpi svāmitvanimittenaikyavyapadeśa ityatra śrutismṛtyorupanyāne sati tatra prāptaśaṅkāparihārasyāvaśyakatvenāvasarasaṅgatyā tadvākyatrayapravṛtteḥ / ityādeḥ ityasāyatrākarṣaṇena na virodhaḥ ityasyānukarṣaṇena cānvayo draṣṭavyaḥ / śrutyarthastu - viṣṇuḥ asarvo 'pi sarvanātmako 'pi sarva iva sarvātmaka iva sarvātmakatvena īyate / kuta ityatastatrāntaryāmitvaṃ hetutvenābhipretya anantaryāmitvapratītyā tasyāsiddhimāśaṅkyāha - ātmaiveti / ātmaiva antaryāmyeva san anātmeva anantaryāmitvena īyate jñāyate rāmakṛṣṇādirūpeṣu / tathā ca ajñānamūlā anantaryāmitvapratītiriti bhāvaḥ / nanu viṣṇorantaryāmitve pratyaktvaṃ syāt taccānupapannaṃ, parāktvena pratīterityata āha - pratyaṅiti / bhagavān pratyaṅ dehāntargato 'pi parāṅiva bahirmātravṛttitveneyate / tathā ca bahirmātravṛttitvapratītirbhrāntiriti bhāvaḥ/ nanu viṣṇau viruddhānekadharmābhyupagame bhedāpattyā ekameva iti śrutivirodha ityata āha - eka iti / eka eva bahudhā bahurūpeṇeyata ityarthaḥ / tathā caikasyaiva rūpabāhulyāt sarvadharmopapattiriti bhāvaḥ / dvigrahaṇātsarvatra kriyāsambandhaḥ sūcitaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - pratyaṅ parāṅiva abhimukho 'pyanabhimukha iva eka eva bahudheyate jñāyate prāpyate ca ityuktam / antaryāmitvanimittena sarvātmakatvena vyapadiśyamānaḥ kiṃ sarvajñaḥ? kva ca vyapadiśyata? ityata āha - sa puruṣa iti / anena puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam (tai.ā. 3-12.) iti śrutimupādatte / sampūrṇaṣaḍguṇatvāt dehākhyapure śayanādvā puruṣasaṃjña ityarthaḥ / sthalāntaramāha - sa iti / anena sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma (chā. 3-14-1.) iti śrutimupādatte / saḥ sarvātmakatvena vyapadiśyamāno bhagavān brahma sarvatra pūrṇatvādbrahmasaṃjña ityarthaḥ / nanvanyatrādṛṣṭamantargatasya bahirgatatvādikaṃ kathaṃ ghaṭata ityata āha - sa īśvara iti / saḥ hariḥ yataḥ īśvaraḥ acintyaśaktyupetaḥ atastasmin anyatrāghaṭitamapi sarvaṃ ghaṭata iti //
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 29:
Having thus explained the non-duality <s>Śrutis</s> favored by the opponents through the meaning of lordship (<s>svāmitva</s>), he explains them also through the meaning of inner-controllership (<s>antaryāmitva</s>) by resorting to sentence-coherence (<s>vākyasamanvaya</s>), through <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>: 'asarvaḥ' (not-all). Although the passage 'asarvaḥ' has been cited as authority in the context 'the unity-Śrutis have arisen through the cause of lordship,' having accepted the lordship-meaning of the word '<s>ātman</s>,' nevertheless, since it is possible for it to be authority in both contexts — 'through lordship alone, and also through inner-controllership, the unity-Śrutis have arisen' — the citation as authority in both contexts is justified. The intention of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> author too is: the <s>Śruti</s> 'asarvaḥ' is authority in both [contexts] — 'through lordship alone, and also through inner-controllership, the unity-<s>Śrutis</s> have arisen.' And one should not object: 'If so, then since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is denotable by each respective word through being the inner controller of each [entity], the statement of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> "<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the inner controller of all" would be contradicted' — saying: 'the purport is understood here as word-coherence (<s>padasamanvaya</s>).' For from the statement 'also through inner-controllership,' the understanding is merely that much; the purport of word-coherence is not grasped here. Because, even when each individual word of the <s>mahāvākya</s> (great sentence) — beginning with 'this' and the like — denotes <s>Viṣṇu</s> through the cause of inner-controllership, by the force of the <s>Smṛti</s> 'the inner controller of all,' the other words being non-self-referential, sentence-coherence alone must be stated. When the word <s>Viṣṇu</s> is accepted as denotable by every word — denoting all meanings including actions, agents, and the like — by the force of the <s>Śruti</s> 'names,' only then is it word-coherence; not when each individual word denotes <s>Viṣṇu</s> — thus there is no contradiction. And so, when the words 'tat' (that), 'tvam' (you), 'aham' (I), and the like occurring in sentences like '<s>tattvamasi</s>' (you are that) denote <s>Viṣṇu</s> through the cause of inner-controllership, the sentence-construction should be seen as: 'tvam' means 'your inner controller'; 'tat' means '<s>Brahman</s>'; 'aham' means 'my inner controller is <s>Brahman</s>.' And there is no impossibility of connecting the verbal words 'asi' (you are) and 'asmi' (I am) in this way, since the word 'tvam' and the like, which denote the inner controller qualified by the <s>jīva</s>, have primary usage in the inner controller — just as the word 'burner' has [primary usage] in iron [heated by fire]; [and] by resorting to [the principle that] the primary usage is in the <s>jīva</s>, the usage of the words 'asi,' 'asmi,' and the like is justified with the intention of the non-primary meaning. Although in the section on stating causes, there is no syntactic connection of the three sentences 'when it is seen' through the vision of difference regarding the knowledgeable self, nevertheless, when <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> are presented in the context 'the designation of unity is through the cause of lordship,' since the resolution of the objection arising there is necessary, by the connection of occasion the three sentences function [here]. The syntactic connection should be seen by the attraction of 'ityādeḥ' (and so forth) [connecting with the previous] and the carrying forward of 'na virodhaḥ' (there is no contradiction). The meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>, however, is: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, though 'not all' (<s>asarvaḥ</s>) — though not being of the nature of all — yet, being the Self of all, is perceived as if He were all, as if He were the Self of all, through [His] being the Self of all. Why? — to this, intending inner-controllership as the reason, and anticipating the objection of non-establishment through the non-cognition of inner-controllership, he says: 'ātmaiva' (the Self alone). Being the Self alone — being the inner controller — He is perceived 'as if not the Self' — as if not the inner controller — in the forms of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and the like. And thus, the cognition of non-inner-controllership is rooted in ignorance: this is the import. But if <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the inner controller, He would be directly perceived (<s>pratyak</s>), and that is impossible, since He is perceived as external (<s>parāk</s>) — to this he says: 'pratyaṅ' (inward-facing). <s>Bhagavān</s>, though inward-facing — though entered within the body — is perceived as if outward-facing, as if engaged only in external activity. And thus, the perception of being engaged only in external activity is a delusion: this is the import. But if mutually contradictory properties are accepted in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then by the occurrence of difference, there would be a contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> 'one alone' — to this he says: 'ekaḥ' (one). He is 'one alone,' perceived in many forms: this is the meaning. And thus, since that one alone has multiplicity of forms, all properties are justified: this is the import. By the double usage [of 'iyate'], the connection with the verb is indicated everywhere. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, it is said: 'pratyaṅ parāṅiva' — though face-to-face, as if not face-to-face — 'one alone is perceived in many ways' — is known and attained. [The question:] He who is being designated as the Self of all through inner-controllership — is He omniscient? And where is He designated? — to this he says: 'sa puruṣaḥ' (He, the Person). By this, he cites the <s>Śruti</s> 'puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam' (the Person alone is all this) (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12). Because of possessing the complete six qualities, or because of sleeping in the city called the body, He is designated as '<s>Puruṣa</s>': this is the meaning. He states another passage: 'saḥ' (He). By this, he cites the <s>Śruti</s> 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma' (all this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>) (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.14.1). 'He' — <s>Bhagavān</s>, who is being designated as the Self of all — is '<s>Brahman</s>' everywhere, because of being complete — therefore He is designated as <s>Brahman</s>: this is the meaning. But how is it possible that what is not seen elsewhere — the being-external of one who is internal, and the like — is coherent? — to this he says: 'sa īśvaraḥ' (He is the Lord). 'He' — <s>Hari</s> — since He 'is the Lord' — endowed with inconceivable power — 'therefore,' even what is impossible elsewhere is possible regarding Him.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.6, verse 30:
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, being the inner controller of all, is denoted by all names.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.30:
smṛtau kapratyayaḥ sarvadehagatasyāpi viṣṇorajñātatvamāha / yadvā - yāmo niyamanaṃ tatra bhava ityarthe ṭhak, yato viṣṇuḥ sarvāntaryāmikaḥ sarvāntarniyāmakaḥ ata eva eṣa ātmeti hovāca (chā. 8-3-4.) so 'hamasmi (ī. 16.) tattvamasi (chā. 6-8-7.) yo 'sāvasau puruṣaḥ (ī. 16.) iti vākyasthena eṣo 'haṃtvamasāviti sarvanāmnā sarvavācakasarvanāmasaṃṅakaśabdena sarvamiti nāmnā cābhidhīyate / na tu sarvasvarūpatvādityarthaḥ / śreṣṭhavastvaikyārthatayāpi aikyaśrutīḥ smṛtyā vyākhyāti - naitaditi / mokṣadharme hi vaiśampāyanaṃ prati he brahman bhedavākyāt bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ pratipattavyāḥ / aikyavākyaṃ tu pradhānapuruṣaparamiti vā? utāho aikyavākyāt eka eva puruṣaḥ, dvaitavākyaṃ tu vyāvahārikabhedaparamiti? tathā - puruṣabāhulyamupetyaikyavākyasya śreṣṭhaparatvapakṣe 'pi ātmasu kiṃ sarve samāḥ? utaikaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ? dvitīye ko 'sāvatra puruṣeṣu śreṣṭhaḥ? sa kathaṃ hi śreṣṭhaḥ? taṃ tathā ca bhavān vaktumarhatītyāśayena kṛtasya janamejayapraśnasya vaiśampāyanenoktamuttaram -
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 30:
In the <s>Smṛti</s>, the <s>ka</s>-suffix indicates the unknownness of <s>Viṣṇu</s> even though He pervades all bodies. Or: '<s>yāma</s>' means regulation; '<s>ṭhak</s>' is in the sense of 'being therein'; since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is 'the inner controller of all' (<s>sarvāntaryāmikaḥ</s>) — the inner regulator of all — therefore, by the words occurring in the passages 'He is the Self' said [the sage] (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.3.4), 'I am He' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 16), 'You are that' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8.7), 'He who is that Person yonder' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 16) — by the pronoun (<s>sarvanāman</s>) called 'this one,' 'I,' 'you,' 'that one' — the word that denotes all, the pronoun — and by the word 'all' as a name, He is denoted. 'But not because of being of the nature of all': this is the meaning. He explains the unity-<s>Śrutis</s> through <s>Smṛti</s> in the sense of the unity of the best entity as well: 'naitad' (they do not [desire] this). For in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>, in response to <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> — O <s>Brahman</s>, from the duality-passage, multiple Persons are to be understood. But is the unity-passage referring to the foremost Person? Or else, from the unity-passage, there is only one Person, and the duality-passage refers to conventional difference? Also — having accepted the plurality of Persons, even in the interpretation that takes the unity-passage as referring to the foremost, among the Selves are all equal? Or is one the foremost? In the second case, who is this foremost among the Persons? How is He the foremost? With the intention that the venerable one should explain that and how — the answer given by <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> to <s>Janamejaya's</s> question is:
'They do not desire this [view] — that there is a single Person, O scion of the <s>Kuru</s> lineage.
For it is said that of the many Persons, there is one source.
I shall explain to you that Person who is complete and superior in virtues.' //

children.text: iti / asyārthaḥ - etanmataṃ necchanti vidvāṃsaḥ / etaditi kimityatastadvivṛṇoti - puruṣamekamiti / tathā ca vedāḥ ekameva puruṣaṃ vadantītyetanmataṃ jñānino necchantītyarthaḥ / yadvā - etasmin jagati ekaṃ puruṣaṃ necchanti, kintu bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ santīti / tarhyadvaitaśrutivirodha iti na vācyam / yato bahūnāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ eka eva, tatparamaikyavākyam / bahūnāṃ kaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ? sa kathaṃ śreṣṭhaḥ? ityasyottaramāha - bahūnāmiti / he kurukulodvaha eteṣāṃ bahūnāṃ puruṣāṇām ātmānāṃ madhye yā yoniḥ yaḥ kāraṇabhūtaḥ ekā śreṣṭhaḥ yathā ca śreṣṭha ucyate śrutyādau tathā tena prakāreṇa taṃ viśvaṃ pūrṇaṃ guṇādhikaṃ puruṣam ākhyāsyāmi vyākhyāsyāmīti prameyadīpikāvyāsatīrthīyadiśā smṛtyarthaḥ / anena parābhimataikyavākyamuttamavastvaikyaparam / tathā ca sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ yadekaṃ brahmatattvamasi tasmādatyavaro 'si atyavaro 'smīti śrutyartha ukto bhavati / ityādeśca ityasya na ca tattvamasītyādivirodhaḥ ityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: the wise 'do not desire this view.' What view? — to this he explains: 'that there is a single Person.' And thus: the <s>Vedas</s> speak of only one Person — the wise do not desire this view: this is the meaning. Or: in this world they do not desire a single Person; rather, there are many Persons. Then, if there is a contradiction with the non-duality <s>Śruti</s> — that should not be said, because one among the many is the foremost alone, and the unity-passage refers to that [foremost one]. Who is the foremost among the many? How is he the foremost? — the answer to this he gives: 'bahūnām' (of the many). O scion of the <s>Kuru</s> lineage, of these many Persons — Selves — in their midst, the one who is the 'source' (<s>yoni</s>) — the cause — [is] the foremost; and 'just as' He 'is said' to be the foremost in <s>Śruti</s> and the like, 'in that manner' — in that way — I shall explain to you 'that Person' who is 'viśva' (complete) and 'guṇādhika' (superior in virtues): this is the meaning of the <s>Smṛti</s>, following the direction of the <s>Prameyadīpikā</s> and <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>. By this, the unity-passage favored by the opponents refers to the unity of the best entity. And thus, the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is: 'You are that' — that one supreme <s>Brahman</s>; 'therefore you are exceedingly subordinate,' 'I am exceedingly subordinate.' The syntactic connection of 'and from such [passages]' is with 'there is no contradiction with tattvamasi and the like.'

children.text:
uktā ca prāptiḥ /
'brahmaiva san'; (bṛ. 6-4.) ityapi, jīva eva brahmaśabdaḥ /
upapadyate ca virodhe //
children.translated_text:
And the scope [of the objection] has been stated.
Regarding 'being <s>Brahman</s> indeed' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 6.4) also, the word '<s>Brahman</s>' refers to the <s>jīva</s> alone.
