Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.6, verse 31:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.31:
nanvadvaitaśrutyabhāve kathamadvaitaṃ bhedaśrutyādinā niṣidhyate / tasyāpratyakṣatvena śrutiṃ vinā prāptyabhāvāt / aprāptasya ca pratiṣedhāyogāt ityata āha - uktā ceti // caḥ sādhyasamuccaye / co yato na ca tattvamasi ityādinā jīveśvaikyasya prāptiḥ śrutyarthāparijñānanimittā prasaktiruktā / ato na tanniṣedhānupapattirityarthaḥ / nanvetacchrutīnāmavirodhakatve 'pi bhedaśruteḥ brahmaiva san brahmāpyeti iti śrutivirodhastu bhaviṣyati / atra brahmaiveteyavakāreṇa jīvasyābrahmatāniṣedhena tadadhīnatvādinā nimittena abrahmabhūte brahmatvavyavahāra ityuktagaterasambhavādityata āha - brahmaiveti / apiḥ samuccaye / na kevalaṃ tattvamasītyādikamaviruddham / kintu brahmaiva san iti bṛhadāraṇyavākyamapītyarthaḥ / kuta ityata āha - jīve eveti / saptamīyaṃ viṣayārthe / tathā ca yato brahmaiva san iti vākye śruto 'yamādyo brahmaśabdaḥ brahmāṇi jīvāḥ sarve 'pi iti śruterjīva eva, na parabrahmaṇi ata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.6, verse 31:
But if the non-duality <s>Śrutis</s> are absent [i.e., do not teach literal identity], how is non-duality refuted through duality-<s>Śrutis</s> and the like? Since [non-duality], being imperceptible, has no scope without <s>Śruti</s>. And since what has no scope cannot be negated — to this he says: 'uktā ca' (and it has been stated). The word 'ca' is for aggregation of properties to be proven. The word 'ca' [also means] 'since' — since the scope (<s>prāpti</s>) — the applicability arising from incomplete understanding of the meaning of <s>Śruti</s> — of the identity of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> 'through tattvamasi and the like' has been stated. Therefore, the impossibility of its negation does not arise: this is the meaning. But even if these <s>Śrutis</s> do not cause a contradiction, there will be a contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> 'brahmaiva san brahmāpyeti' (being <s>Brahman</s> indeed, he reaches <s>Brahman</s>). Because in this passage, through the particle 'eva' (indeed), the negation of the <s>jīva's</s> non-Brahman-hood, and the transactional usage of <s>Brahman</s>-hood for the non-<s>Brahman</s> through a cause such as dependence — the stated interpretation is not possible — to this he says: 'brahmaiva' (Brahman indeed). The word 'api' is for aggregation. Not only is '<s>tattvamasi</s>' and the like non-contradictory, but even the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> passage 'brahmaiva san' is also [non-contradictory]: this is the meaning. Why? — to this he says: 'jīve eva' (in the <s>jīva</s> alone). This locative is in the sense of the object. And thus, since the first word '<s>Brahman</s>' heard in the passage 'brahmaiva san' refers to the <s>jīva</s> alone, from the <s>Śruti</s> 'brahmāṇi jīvāḥ sarve 'pi' (all <s>jīvas</s> are indeed <s>Brahmans</s>), it does not [refer to] the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>: this is the meaning.

children.text: yadvā - jīva iti prathamāntam / tathā ca iti vākye śrutādyabrahmaśabdokto jīva eva, na parabrahmetyarthaḥ / tathā ca iti vākye śrutādyabrahmaśabdokto jīva eva, na parabrahmetyarthaḥ / tathā ca saḥ muktajīvo brahmaiva san jīva eva san jīvabhāvamavihāyaiva pralaye parabrahmāpnoti / apihitassan praviśatīti śrutyarthopapatteḥ noktabhedavyapadeśasyaitacchrutivarodha iti bhāvaḥ / yathoktaṃ bṛhadbhāṣye -
children.translated_text: Or: '<s>jīvaḥ</s>' (the <s>jīva</s>) is in the nominative case. And thus, the <s>jīva</s> who is stated by the first word '<s>Brahman</s>' heard in the passage is the <s>jīva</s> alone, not the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>: this is the meaning. And thus, that liberated <s>jīva</s> — being '<s>Brahman</s> indeed' — being a <s>jīva</s> alone — without abandoning the state of being a <s>jīva</s>, at the time of dissolution attains the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Since the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> 'having been concealed, he enters' is thus justified, there is no contradiction of the stated duality-designation with this <s>Śruti</s>: this is the import. As stated in the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> —
The <s>jīva</s> too is called by the word '<s>Brahman</s>' because of having many more qualities than insentient [matter]. //

children.text: prāpnoti paramaṃ brahma pralaye pralaye sadā / iti //
children.translated_text: He attains the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> at each dissolution, always. //

children.text: yadyapi muktāvabhede pareṇeyaṃ śrutirāśaṅkitā / tathaiva viṣṇutattvavinirṇayaṭīkokteḥ / tathā ca muktāviti vācyaṃ, na tu pralaya iti / tathāpi sarvajīvasādhāraṇyāya pralaya ityuktiḥ / nanu brahmaśabdasya parabrahmaṇyeva mukhyatvānna jīve 'sau yujyata ityata āha - upapadyata iti / co 'pyarthaḥ / tathā ca brahmaśabdo yadyapi parabrahmaṇi mukhyaḥ, tathāpi virodhe svīyapūrvottaravākyavirodhe prāmāṇāntaravirodhe vā sati jīve 'pyupapadyata ityarthaḥ / prakṛte ca brahmāpyeti ityuttarabhāvisvavākyena paramaṃ sāmyam iti pūrvavākyena bhedagrāhipratyakṣādinā ca virodho 'stīti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the opponent has raised this <s>Śruti</s> as an objection regarding non-difference in liberation — and the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirṇaya Ṭīkā</s> says exactly that — and therefore one should say 'in liberation' and not 'at dissolution' — nevertheless, the statement 'at dissolution' is for the purpose of applicability to all <s>jīvas</s> in general. But since the word '<s>Brahman</s>' has its primary meaning in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone, it is not applicable to the <s>jīva</s> — to this he says: 'upapadyate' (it is justified). The word 'ca' means 'also.' And thus, although the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is primary for the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, nevertheless, 'in the case of contradiction' — when there is contradiction with its own preceding and following sentences, or when there is contradiction with another means of valid knowledge — it 'is justified' even for the <s>jīva</s>: this is the meaning. And in the present context, there is contradiction with the subsequent sentence 'brahmāpyeti' (he attains <s>Brahman</s>) and with the preceding passage 'the supreme equality,' and also with perception and the like that grasp difference: this is the import.
Because bondage is of the nature of delusion, liberation is justified.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.6, verse 32:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.32:
nanu tathāpi bhedavyapadeśasya vimuktaśca vimucyate (kaṭha. 2-5-1.) iti kaṭhaśrutivirodhaḥ / atra saṃsāre 'pi jīvasya muktatvoktyā tadanyathānupapattyā parabrahmatvāvagamāt ityata āha - pramādeti // caśabdo 'pyarthe samuccaye ca / tathā ca api - jīvasya parabrahmatvābhāve 'pi vimuktatvaṃ vimuktatvavacanaṃ ca yujyate / na kevalaṃ brahmaśabda upapadyate iti cārthaḥ / katham? bandhasya svataḥkartṛtvabhoktṛtvābhimānarūpasya jīvagatasaṃsārasya pramādātmakatvāt pramādapadoktājñānamūlatvena tannimittapratītikatvenāsvābhāvikatvāt pramādapadoktājñānamūlatvena tannimittapratītikatvenāsvābhāvikatvāt / asvābhāvike cāvidyamānapadaprayogadarśanādityarthaḥ / ato na tadvirodha iti bhāvaḥ / bandhasyājñānamūlatvaṃ ca -
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.32: [Objection:] Granted [all this]; even so, the statement of difference contradicts the <s>Kaṭha Śruti</s>: 'The liberated one is [further] liberated' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.5.1). Since even in this <s>saṃsāra</s>, the <s>jīva</s>'s liberation is stated, and from the impossibility of otherwise [explaining] that, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>-hood [of the <s>jīva</s>] is understood — to this he says: '<s>pramāda</s>' (inadvertence). // The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'api' (even) and for aggregation. And thus: even without the <s>jīva</s>'s being the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the liberation and the statement of liberation are both justified. Not only is the word <s>Brahman</s> applicable [to the <s>jīva</s>]: this is also the meaning of 'ca.' How? Because bondage — the <s>saṃsāra</s> belonging to the <s>jīva</s>, which is in the form of the false self-identification as agent and enjoyer — is of the nature of inadvertence (<s>pramāda</s>); because it has ignorance as its root, as indicated by the word '<s>pramāda</s>'; because it is a cognition caused by that [ignorance]; and because it is therefore non-inherent (<s>asvābhāvika</s>). And because, with respect to what is non-inherent, the usage of words meaning 'non-existent' is observed: this is the meaning. Therefore there is no contradiction: this is the purport. And that bondage has ignorance as its root —

children.text:
ubhe satye kṣatriyādya pravṛtte
moho mṛtyuḥ saṅgato yaṃ kavīnām /
pramādaṃ vai mṛtyumahaṃ bravīmi
tathāpramādādamṛtatvaṃ bravīmi /
children.translated_text: Both truths — O foremost of <s>kṣatriyas</s> — are active. Death is delusion, associated with which [even] the wise [are bound]. I declare death to be inadvertence; likewise, from non-inadvertence I declare immortality.

children.text: iti tattvapradīpanyāyāmṛtodāhṛtabhāratavacanasiddhaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ prati sanatsujātavākyametat / he kṣatriyādya mṛtyuḥ saṃsāra tadabhāvarūpāmṛtatvaṃ cetyubhe api satye eva pravṛtte / tayormadhye mṛtyuḥ mohaḥ ajñānādhīnastanmūlaḥ / tarhi mithyā syādityato netyāha - pramādaṃ vā iti / ahaṃ mṛtyuṃ saṃsāraṃ pramādaṃ asvābhāvikaṃ bravīmi / amṛtatvaṃ muktatvaṃ tu apramādāt pramādāpāyāt bravīmītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: — this passage, cited in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> and <s>Nyāyāmṛta</s>, is established from the <s>Bhārata</s> — it is the statement of <s>Sanatsujāta</s> addressed to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>. O foremost of <s>kṣatriyas</s>, death — <s>saṃsāra</s> — and immortality, which is the absence of that — both 'truths' are indeed 'active,' operational. Between the two, death is dependent on delusion — ignorance — and has that as its root. 'Then it would be false' — to this he says: '<s>pramādaṃ vai</s>' (inadvertence indeed). I declare death — <s>saṃsāra</s> — to be inadvertence — non-inherent. But I declare immortality — the state of liberation — to arise from non-inadvertence — from the removal of inadvertence: this is the meaning.

children.text:
muktirhitvānyathā rūpaṃ svarūpeṇa vyavasthitiḥ /
iti hi bhāgavate /
children.translated_text: Liberation is the abandonment of the aberrant form and the establishment in one's own nature. // Thus indeed in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.33:
bandhasyāsvābhāvikatvaṃ kutaḥ siddhamityata āha - muktiriti // 'anyathārūpam'; asvābhāvikaṃ rūpaṃ 'hitvā'; tyaktvā 'svarūpeṇa'; nijarūpeṇāvasthitireva muktirityarthaḥ / bhāgavata ityasya pramādātmakatvokterityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.33: Whence is the non-inherent nature of bondage established? — to this he says: '<s>muktiḥ</s>' (liberation). // 'The aberrant form' (<s>anyathārūpam</s>) — the non-inherent form; 'having abandoned' (<s>hitvā</s>) — having discarded; 'in one's own nature' (<s>svarūpeṇa</s>) — in one's inherent form, the establishment [therein] alone is liberation: this is the meaning. The syntactic connection of 'in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>' is with 'because of being of the nature of inadvertence.'
And there is no contradiction with those respective inferences.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.34:
nanu bhedokteḥ śrutivirodhābhāve 'pi jīvo brahmābhinnaḥ cetanatvāt brahmavat / bhedo mithyā bhedatvāt candrabhedavat / vimatāni śarīrāṇi madbhogāyatanāni śarītvāt maccharīravat / ityanumānavirodhastu bhaviṣyatītyata āha - na ceti // co 'virodhasamuccaye / tathā ca na kevalaṃ śrutivirodhābhāvaḥ, kintu tasyāḥ bhedokteḥ tenādvaitaparikalpitānumānena virodho 'pi netyarthaḥ / anena sautraścaśabdo vyākhyātaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.34: [Objection:] Even if there is no contradiction with <s>Śruti</s> for the statement of difference, there will be contradiction with inferences such as: 'The <s>jīva</s> is non-different from <s>Brahman</s>, because of being conscious, like <s>Brahman</s>'; 'Difference is false, because of being difference, like the difference of the moons [seen in diplopia]'; 'The bodies in question are receptacles for my enjoyment, because of being bodies, like my body' — to this he says: 'na ca' (and not). // The word 'ca' is for aggregating the non-contradiction. And thus: not only is there no contradiction with <s>Śruti</s>, but moreover, there is no contradiction of that statement of difference with those inferences devised by the <s>Advaitins</s>: this is the meaning. By this, the 'ca' of the <s>sūtra</s> is explained.
And because of [the possibility of constructing inferences] at will, inference is not relied upon. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.18 |

children.text: yathākāmaṃ hyanumātuṃ śakyate / ato na tattve pṛthaganumānamapekṣyate /
children.translated_text: For inference can be constructed at will. Therefore, separate inference is not relied upon for [ascertaining] truth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.35:
tatra hetvākāṅkṣāyāṃ sūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - kāmāditi // 'hi'; yato 'bhedasādhanāya paropanyastam 'anumānam'; anumānatvena parābhimataṃ 'pṛthak'; pratyakṣādiviruddhaṃ śrutisāhāyyarahitaṃ ca ataḥ 'tattve'; viṣaye jñānopalakṣakametat / tattvajñānārthaṃ 'nāpekṣyate'; tattvajñānakāraṇaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ / na cāprayojakatā / 'hi'; yataḥ 'yathākāmaṃ'; yatheccham īśvaro na svatantraḥ cetanatvāt devadattavat / jaḍa ātmā vastutvādityādirūpeṇa na tattve atattve 'pi anumātuṃ śakyate / ataḥ anena pratyakṣādiviruddhasyāpi pramāṇatve cetanatvavastutvāderapi pramāṇatvaṃ syāt aviśeṣāditi vipakṣe bādhakatarka ukto bhavati / sūtre 'kāmāt'; ityekadeśotkīrtanena yathākāmāditi samagraśabdo lakṣyate jyotiśśabdena jyotiṣṭomaśabdavat ityāśayena yathākāmamityuktam / hītyanena pañcamī vyākhyātā / 'tattve'; ityanenāsminnityasyākarṣo 'dhyāhāro vā jñāpitaḥ / 'anumānam'; ityanena 'nānumā'; iti bhinnapadatvaṃ 'pṛthak'; ityanena naño viruddhārthakatvamāśritya 'nānumā'; ityaikapadyaṃ ca sūcitam / 'nāpekṣyate'; ityanena naśabdaghaṭitasamāsamaṅgīkṛtya 'nāpekṣā'; ityaṃśo vyākhyātaḥ / smṛtyanusāreṇa sūtre bhāṣye ca tattvajñānāsādhanatvaprakaṭanāya parābhimatānumāne sādhanagocarecchāviṣayatvaniṣedhaḥ / tathā cāyaṃ sūtrārthaḥ - 'anumā'; anumānatvena parābhimatamabhedasādhakamanumānam 'asmiṃstattve'; tattvajñānārthaṃ 'nāpekṣā'; na apekṣā yasyāṃ sā tathāktā tattvajñānakāraṇaṃ na bhavati / kuta etat? yataḥ iyamanumā 'nānumā'; pratyakṣādiviruddhānumā / tadviruddhāpi sadanumā kiṃ na syāt? na syāt / kutaḥ? 'yathākāmāt'; asyāḥ / kāma icchā tadanusāripravṛttimattvāt / tathā ca pratyakṣādiviruddhāyā api prāmāṇye uktarītyā atattvaviṣaye pravṛttāyā anumāyā api prāmāṇyaṃ syāt, aviśeṣāditi bhāvaḥ / yata evamato na dvaitaśruteranumānavirodho 'pīti /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.35: When the reason [for the above claim] is sought, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and explains it: '<s>kāmāt</s>' (because of desire). // 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since 'the inference' — what is 'considered by the opponent as inference' for proving non-difference — is 'separate' (<s>pṛthak</s>) — contradicted by perception and the like, and devoid of the assistance of <s>Śruti</s>; therefore, 'for [ascertaining] truth' — the subject; this is indicative of knowledge. 'It is not relied upon' — it does not become a cause of knowledge of truth: this is the meaning. Nor is there purposelessness. 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since 'at will' (<s>yathākāmam</s>) — as one wishes, in the form of 'God is not independent because of being conscious, like <s>Devadatta</s>'; 'the Self is insentient because of being a substance' and the like — 'to infer' — not [only] regarding truth but even regarding untruth — 'is possible.' Therefore, by this [<s>sūtra</s>], an invalidating argument (<s>bādhaka tarka</s>) against the opponent is stated: if the validity even of [inferences] contradicted by perception and the like were accepted, then the validity of [the inferences about] consciousness, substance-hood, and the like would also follow, because there is no distinguishing factor. In the <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>kāmāt</s>' — by citing a part [of the phrase], the full word '<s>yathākāmāt</s>' is indicated, like the word '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' indicating '<s>jyotiṣṭoma</s>': with this intention, '<s>yathākāmam</s>' is said. By 'hi,' the fifth [case-ending, i.e., ablative] is explained. By '<s>tattve</s>' (in truth), either '<s>asmin</s>' (in this) is drawn in, or '<s>jñāna</s>' (knowledge) is supplied. By '<s>anumānam</s>' (inference), the splitting into two words '<s>nānumā</s>' (not an inference) is [shown]; by '<s>pṛthak</s>' (separate), relying on the adversative meaning of the negative particle 'na,' the single-word-nature of '<s>nānumā</s>' is also indicated. By '<s>nāpekṣyate</s>' (is not relied upon), accepting the compound formed with the negative particle, the portion '<s>nāpekṣā</s>' (no reliance) is explained. Following the <s>Smṛti</s>, in both the <s>sūtra</s> and the <s>bhāṣya</s>, for making manifest the non-instrumentality of the opponent's supposed inference for truth-knowledge, the negation of its being an object of desire in the domain of proof-hood is [stated]. And thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: '<s>anumā</s>' — the inference considered by the opponent as proving non-difference; 'in this truth' — for the purpose of truth-knowledge — '<s>nāpekṣā</s>' — that in which there is no reliance, that which is not the cause of truth-knowledge. Whence this? Because this inference is '<s>nānumā</s>' — an inference contradicted by perception and the like. [Objection:] Could not even an inference contradicted by [perception] be a valid inference? It could not. Whence? '<s>Yathākāmāt</s>' — because of this [inference]. <s>Kāma</s> means desire; because it has activity conforming to that [desire]. And thus: if even what is contradicted by perception and the like were valid, then in the stated manner, an inference engaged even in non-truth would also be valid, because there is no distinguishing factor: this is the purport. Since this is so, therefore there is no contradiction of the <s>dvaita</s> (dualist) <s>Śruti</s> even by inference.

children.text:
uktaṃ ca skānde -
yathākāmānumā yasmāttasmātsānapagā śruteḥ /
pūrvāparāvirodhāya ceṣyate nānyathā kvacit // iti /
children.translated_text: And it is said in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa]: 'Since inference is at-will, it is therefore not deviant from <s>Śruti</s>; it is employed for the non-contradiction of what precedes and follows — never otherwise anywhere.' //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.36:
atraiva smṛtisammatimāha - uktaṃ ceti // caḥ samuccaye / na kevalaṃ sūtrakṛtā, skānde 'pyuktamiti / kimuktamityatastatpaṭhati - yatheti / padārthānativṛttyartho 'yaṃ yathāśabdaḥ / liṅgamārṣam / yadvā - nāyamavyayībhāvaḥ, kintvanatikrāntaḥ kāmo yayeti bahuvrīhisamāsaḥ / pravartata iti śeṣaḥ / apavṛttaṃ viruddhaṃ gaṃ gamanaṃ yasyāḥ sā apagā, na apagā anapagā iti vigrahaḥ / tathā ca yasmāt 'anumā'; śrutyādiviruddhaṃ pṛthaganumānaṃ 'yathākāmā'; kāmamanatikramya pravartate / puruṣecchānusāreṇa pravṛttimatīti yāvat/ tasmāt 'śruteranapagā'; śrutyanukūlā tadaviruddhaiva sā 'pūrvāparāvirodhāya'; śruteḥ pūrvottaravākyavirodhaparihārārtham 'iṣyate'; apakṣyate / na kevalamatīndriyārthatattvaniścayāyeti caśabdārthaḥ / kvacidanyathā cet yatra śrutyādyānukūlyaṃ tadavirodhaḥ, pūrvottarāvirodhāya tattvaniścayāya ca kāraṇatayeṣyate / nānyathā nānyā pṛthaganumā kvacidvākye 'pi / kutaḥ? yat sā anumā kevalānumā yathākāmā tasmāditi yojyam / yathākāmānumetyekaṃ padaṃ vā / yathākāmā ca sānumeti vigrahaḥ / tathātve - yasmādeṣānapagā na tasmātsā noktaphalārthamapekṣyate / 'anyathā'; yuktiṃ vinā netyāvṛttyānvayaḥ / ata eva sudhāyāṃ 'yathāyogyākhilajñatā'; ityekaṃ padamityuktam / itiśabdasya skānda ityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.36: For this very point, he cites the agreement of <s>Smṛti</s>: 'and it is said.' // The word 'ca' is for aggregation. Not only by the <s>sūtra</s>-author, but in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa] too it is said. What is said? — to this he reads that: '<s>yathā</s>' (as). This word '<s>yathā</s>' means 'not-exceeding.' The gender [of certain forms] is Vedic. Or: this is not an <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound, but rather a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: that which operates without exceeding desire. 'Operates' is the remainder. '<s>Apagā</s>' means that whose course (<s>gama</s>) is deviant (<s>apavṛtta</s>), that is, contradictory; '<s>anapagā</s>' is: not <s>apagā</s>, that is, not deviant. And thus: since 'inference' — a separate inference contradicted by <s>Śruti</s> and the like — is 'at-will' — operates without exceeding desire, that is, operates conforming to human wish; therefore, it is 'not deviant from <s>Śruti</s>' — it is favorable to <s>Śruti</s>, non-contradictory with it — it 'is employed' — it is accepted — 'for the non-contradiction of what precedes and follows' — for the purpose of resolving the contradiction between the preceding and following passages of <s>Śruti</s>. Not only for the ascertainment of supersensible truth: this is the meaning of the word 'ca.' If somewhere it is otherwise — wherever it is favorable to <s>Śruti</s> and the like, and non-contradictory with them — it is employed as a cause for the non-contradiction of preceding and following passages and for the ascertainment of truth. 'Never otherwise' — no other, separate inference, in any passage whatsoever. Whence? Because that inference — mere inference — is at-will: this should be construed. Or '<s>yathākāmānumā</s>' is a single word. The compound analysis is: that which is at-will and is an inference. In that case: since this is not deviant, therefore it is relied upon for the stated purpose. 'Otherwise' — without reasoning, [it is] not [relied upon]: the construction is with the recurring [negative]. Hence in the <s>Sudhā</s>, '<s>yathāyogyākhilajñatā</s>' (knowledge of all in the appropriate manner) is said to be a single word. The syntactic connection of the word 'iti' is with 'in the <s>Skānda</s>.'
'This understanding is not to be obtained by reasoning.' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.9) — thus also. //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.37:
spaṣṭoktitvātprathamaṃ smṛtimupanyasyātraiva arthe śrutisammatiṃ cāha - naiṣeti / āpaneyetyatra ā apeti vicchedaḥ / viruddhārthayorupasargayoḥ krameṇa sambandhaḥ / tathā ca 'eṣā'; parabrahmaviṣayā 'matiḥ'; śuṣkatarkeṇa 'āneyā'; utpādyā 'apaneyā'; nirākāryā ca na bhavatītyarthaḥ / 'proktānyena sujñānāya preṣṭha'; iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / preṣṭheti naciketasaṃ prati yamasya sambuddhiḥ / 'anyena'; anyatvajñāninā jīveśvarādibhedajñāninā bhagavadbhaktyādimateti yāvat/ ācāryeṇa 'proktā'; tadupadesājjātā 'sujñānāya'; syādityarthaḥ / iti ceti caḥ samuccaye / tathā ca iti kaṭhaśrutau coktamiti sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.37: Because of [its] clear statement, he first cites the <s>Smṛti</s>, and then cites the agreement of <s>Śruti</s> for this very point: '<s>naiṣā</s>' (not this). In '<s>āpaneyā</s>' the division is '<s>ā ape</s>.' The two prefixes of opposite meaning connect in sequence. And thus: 'this' (<s>eṣā</s>) — pertaining to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — 'understanding' (<s>matiḥ</s>) — 'by dry reasoning' — is 'not to be produced' (<s>āneyā</s>) and 'not to be refuted' (<s>apaneyā</s>): this is the meaning. 'When taught by another, for easy understanding, O dearest' — this is the remainder of the sentence. '<s>Preṣṭha</s>' — this is <s>Yama</s>'s address to <s>Naciketas</s>. 'By another' (<s>anyena</s>) — by one who knows the otherness [of <s>Brahman</s>], that is, one who knows the difference between <s>jīva</s>, God, and the like; who is endowed with devotion to the Lord and so forth — in sum, by a teacher. 'When taught' (<s>proktā</s>) — produced from his instruction — 'for easy understanding' (<s>sujñānāya</s>) — it would become [clear]: this is the meaning. 'Iti ca' — the word 'ca' is for aggregation. And thus, the construction is: thus it is said in the <s>Kaṭha Śruti</s> as well.

children.text: asminn asya ca tadyogaṃ śāsti | BBs_1,1.19 |
children.translated_text: In this [<s>Brahman</s>], [<s>Śruti</s>] teaches the connection of this [<s>jīva</s>] with that [<s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.19 |

children.text:
asya jīvasya / yuktisamuccaye caśabdaḥ /
'so 'śnute sarvān kāmān saha brahmaṇā vipaścitā'; (tai. 2-9.)
'anilayane 'bhayaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vindate'; (tai. 2-7.)
'etamānandamayamātmānamupasaṅkrāmati'; (tai. 2-8.) ityādi // 6 //
children.translated_text: 'Of this' — of the <s>jīva</s>. The word 'ca' is for aggregation of reasons. 'He attains all desires together with the omniscient <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.9). 'In the imperishable [<s>Brahman</s>], he finds fearlessness and a foundation' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.7). 'He approaches this <s>Ānandamaya</s> Self' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.8) — and the like. // 6 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.38:
nanvastvānandamayena brahmaṇā hiraṇyagarbhādijīvānāṃ bhedaḥ / tathāpi saḥ vyāvahārikaḥ saṃsāra evāsti, na pāramārthiko muktāvapi / udāhṛtaśrutīnāṃ sāṃsārikabhedaparatvopapatterityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhati - asminniti/ atrāsyeti nānandamayaparāmarśaḥ / kintu netara ityuktajīvasyetyāha - asyeti / asyānyasya ceti pratītinirāsāya caśabdaṃ vyākhyāti yuktīti / astīti śeṣaḥ / kiṃ tadyogaśāsanamityata āha - so 'śnuta iti / kriyāviśeṣaṇametat / luptavibhaktiko vā nirdeśaḥ / tathā ca 'ityādi śāsti'; ityādinā śāstīti vānvayaḥ / anena na kevalaṃ bhedavyapadeśādānandamayena jīvānāṃ bhedaḥ siddhaḥ / kiṃ nāma? yato 'smin prakaraṇe asya jīvasyānenānandamayena saha 'asmiṃśca'; mokṣe 'pi 'yogaṃ'; sambandhaṃ śrutiḥ śāsti ato 'pi / ato na tadaikyaṃ jīvānāṃ nāpi sāṃsārika eva bhedaḥ / na caitāvatā kathaṃ bhedasiddhiḥ / sambandhasya bhedasāpekṣatvāt / yadvā - yasmāt 'asmin'; prakaraṇadvaye 'pi 'asya'; jīvasya 'tadyogaṃ'; tairānandamayādyairyogaṃ sambandhaṃ 'śāsti'; pratipādayati phalatvena śrutiriti śeṣaḥ / tasmādānandamayo na jīvakośādiriti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / 'saḥ'; brahmajñānī 'vipaścitā'; sarvajñena jñātenaiva 'parabrahmaṇā'; caturmukhena ca saha 'sarvān'; svayogyakāmān 'aśnute'; muktau prāpnotīti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.6.38: [Objection:] Granted that the difference of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and other <s>jīvas</s> from the <s>Ānandamaya Brahman</s> exists; even so, that [difference] exists only in <s>saṃsāra</s> as conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>), not as ultimate (<s>pāramārthika</s>) [persisting] even in liberation — since the cited <s>Śruti</s> passages can be interpreted as pertaining to difference only within <s>saṃsāra</s>. Resolving this doubt, he reads the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>asmin</s>' (in this). Here, '<s>asya</s>' does not refer to <s>Ānandamaya</s>; rather, it refers to the <s>jīva</s> who has been said [to be different] by 'na itara' (not the other) — thus he says: '<s>asya</s>' (of this). To refute the understanding 'of this one and of another [too],' he explains the word 'ca': '<s>yukti</s>' (reason). 'There is' is the remainder. What is that teaching of connection? — to this he says: '<s>so 'śnute</s>' (he attains). This is an adverbial qualifier. Or, the citation has a dropped case-ending. And thus, the construction is: 'by the passage and the like, [Śruti] teaches' — or, '<s>śāsti</s>' connects with 'and the like.' By this, not merely from the statement of difference alone is the difference of <s>jīvas</s> from <s>Ānandamaya</s> established; rather, since in this passage, of 'this' <s>jīva</s>, with this <s>Ānandamaya</s>, 'and in this' — even in liberation — the 'connection' (<s>yoga</s>) — relationship — the <s>Śruti</s> 'teaches'; therefore from this too [the difference is established]. Hence the identity of <s>jīvas</s> [with <s>Brahman</s>] is not [true], nor is the difference only within <s>saṃsāra</s>. Nor [should one object:] how can this establish difference? Because relationship presupposes difference. Or: since 'in this' — in both passages, 'of this' <s>jīva</s>, 'the connection' — the relationship — with those — with <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the like — the <s>Śruti</s> 'teaches,' that is, presents as the fruit. Therefore <s>Ānandamaya</s> is not the sheath of the <s>jīva</s> and the like: this meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. 'He' — the knower of <s>Brahman</s> — 'with the omniscient' (<s>vipaścitā</s>) — with the known and omniscient one alone, with the 'Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — and with the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] as well — 'attains all' — all desires suited to himself — 'in liberation': this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>.

children.text: 'adṛśye 'nātmye'; iti vākyaṃ tu prāgeva vyākhyātam / dehādutkrānto jīvaḥ 'etam'; 'āndamayaṃ'; pūrṇānandaṃ paramātmānaṃ 'upasaṅkrāmati'; tatsamīpaṃ prāpnotītyanuvākāntaragatatṛtīyavākyasyārthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The passage '<s>adṛśye anātmye</s>' (in the invisible, in the non-self) has already been explained earlier. The <s>jīva</s> who has departed from the body 'approaches' (<s>upasaṅkrāmati</s>) — reaches the proximity of — 'this <s>Ānandamaya</s>' — the <s>Paramātman</s> of full bliss: this is the meaning of the third passage from another section. //
// Thus ends the <s>Ānandamayādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the bliss-made one). //
// 7. The <s>Antassthatvādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of being situated within). //

children.text:
'adṛśye 'nātmye'; ityuktam /
taccādṛśyatvam 'antaḥpraviṣṭaṃ kartārametam /
antaścandramasi manasā carantam /
sahaiva santaṃ na vijānanti devāḥ'
(tai. ā. 3-11.) ityantaḥsthasya kasyaciducyate /
sa ca 'indro rājā'; ...
(tai. ā. 3-11-6.) 'sapta yuñjanti'; (tai. ā. 3-11-8.) ityādibhiranyaḥ pratīyate /
tasmātsa evānandamaya iti na mantavyam //
children.translated_text: It has been stated '<s>adṛśye</s> (invisible) <s>anātmye</s> (beyond the self).' And that invisibility is spoken of regarding someone dwelling within, as stated: 'The one who has entered within as the maker, the one moving within the moon by mind, the <s>devas</s> (gods) do not know Him even though He dwells together with them' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.11). And that one is understood to be someone other [than <s>Viṣṇu</s>] through statements such as '<s>Indra</s> the king' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.11.6), 'seven yoke' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.11.8), and so forth. Therefore, it should not be thought that he alone is <s>Ānandamaya</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.7.1:
atrādhikaraṇe adhidaivagatānyatraprasiddhendrādināmasamanvasiddhyarthaṃ dehāntasthatvarūpaliṅgasamanvayaḥ kriyata iti śāstrādhyāyapādasaṅgatayaḥ siddhā ityāśayena pūrvādhikaraṇatadviṣayavākyasaṅgatī darśayati - adṛśya iti // pūrvādhikaraṇodāhṛte 'adṛśye anātmye'; iti vākye ānandamayasya kārtsnyenājñeyatvarūpamadṛśyatvamuktamityarthaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - tacceti / caśabda evārthe/ tathā ca yatpūrvoktamadṛśyatvaṃ tadeva 'antaḥpraviṣṭam'; iti vākye na vijānantītyanena kasyacidantasthasyocyate / devājñeyatvātkaimutyena pratipādyata ityarthaḥ / anenāntasthatvamukhenādṛśyatvānandamayatvayoranyaniṣṭhatvākṣepāt pūrvādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / hṛdayaguhāntaḥpraviṣṭaṃ jagatkartāraṃ candramasyantarmanasā svecchayā carantaṃ sahaiva sthitam etaṃ devāstattvābhimāninaḥ kārtsnyena na vijānantīti śrutyarthaḥ / pūrvapakṣe tviyamanyaparā / tatra sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣamāha - sa ceti / caśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / anya ityāvartate / tathā ca so 'ntasstho viṣṇoḥ 'anyaḥ'; anya eva bhavet, kutaḥ? 'indro rājā'; ityādivākyairyato 'nyo 'ntaḥsthatayā pratīyate ata iti yojanā / ādiśabdena
children.translated_text: [<s>Dīpikā</s> on <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.7.1]: With the intention of showing that in this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topical section), the coherence of the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of dwelling within the body is undertaken for the purpose of establishing [the identity of] <s>Indra</s> and others who are well-known elsewhere in the <s>adhidaiva</s> (cosmic) context — and thereby the connections with the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), chapter, and section are established — he shows the connection with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> and the passage pertaining to it, beginning with '<s>adṛśye</s>.' In the passage '<s>adṛśye anātmye</s>' cited in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the invisibility in the form of complete unknowability of <s>Ānandamaya</s> was stated — that is the meaning. Then, what follows from that? To this he says — 'that.' The word 'ca' is used in the sense of 'eva' (indeed). And thus, that very invisibility stated earlier is spoken of regarding someone dwelling within, through the statement 'entered within' and 'they do not know.' Since even the gods cannot know Him, it is established <s>a fortiori</s> (<s>kaimutyena</s>) — that is the meaning. By this, since through the mention of dwelling within, the invisibility and <s>Ānandamaya</s>-nature are objected to as belonging to another, the connection with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> as one of objection is stated. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) is: the <s>devas</s>, who preside over the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), do not fully know Him — the one who has entered into the cave of the heart, the maker of the universe, who moves within the moon by His own will, who dwells together [with them]. In the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view), however, this [passage] refers to another. There he states the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> with reasoning — 'and that one.' The word 'ca' is for emphasis. 'Another' is carried over. And thus, that inner dweller would be 'other' than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, an other indeed — why? Because through passages such as '<s>Indra</s> the king,' another is understood as dwelling within — such is the construction. By the word 'ādi' (etc.),
the leader of the waters, the protector of the world,
<s>Tvaṣṭā</s> (the divine fashioner), the wise one who transforms forms,

children.text: brahmendramagniṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ diva ātmānaṃ savitāraṃ bṛhaspatim /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the foundation of the universe, the self of heaven, <s>Savitā</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
the <s>caturhotā</s> (four-fold offerer), established in every direction, He found the essence of speech through <s>tapas</s> (austerity).

children.text: ityādi varuṇatvaṣṭragnyādiprapakatattacchrutiliṅghaṭitataittirīyavākyāni gṛhyante / pūrvapakṣaphalamāha - tasmāditi / idaṃ cāvartate / prasajyata iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca 'tasmāt'; antasthasya viṣṇvanyatvāt 'saḥ'; adṛśyo 'nya eva prasajyate / tasmādanyasyādṛśyatvāt 'so 'nya eva'; indrādyanyatamaānandamayaḥ prasajyate na viṣṇuriti yojanā / rājā ya indro jagataḥ 'īśe'; īṣṭe jagadīśvaratvena vartata ityarthaḥ / yasmādīśe īṣṭe tasmājjagato rājeti vā / etaduttarasya 'saptahotā'; iti padasya sapta buddhīndriyāṇi viṣayeṣu jīvena juhotīti saptahotā / viṣayānandriyaiḥ jīvena vetyarthaḥ/ 'sapta yuñjanti'; iti vākye ādyārdhasya 'sapta'; chandāṃsi gāyatryādīni
children.translated_text: — and so forth: <s>Taittirīya</s> passages composed of <s>śruti</s> indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) that elaborate on <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭā</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and others are taken [as evidence by the opponent]. He states the conclusion of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> — 'therefore.' And this is carried over: 'it would follow' is the remainder. Thus, 'therefore,' since the inner dweller is other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'he' — the invisible one — would follow to be another indeed. Therefore, since invisibility belongs to another, 'he, another indeed' — it would follow that <s>Ānandamaya</s> is one of <s>Indra</s> and others, not <s>Viṣṇu</s> — such is the construction. The king who is <s>Indra</s>, who 'rules' the universe — 'rules' means he functions as the lord of the universe, that is the meaning. Or, because he rules, therefore he is the king of the universe. Of the subsequent [passage], the word '<s>saptahotā</s>' (seven-fold offerer) means: one who offers the seven cognitive senses (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>) through the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) into their objects — thus <s>saptahotā</s>; that is, the <s>jīva</s> [offers] objects through the senses — that is the meaning. In the passage 'seven yoke,' of the first half, 'seven' — the meters <s>Gāyatrī</s> and others,

children.text: aśvarūpāṇi 'ekacakraṃ'; sūryarathaṃ prati svātmānaṃ yuñjanti rathe yuktāni bhavantītyarthaḥ / saptacchando 'bhimāninā pṛthagvedābhimānī saptacchando nāmā ekaḥ pradhāno 'śvo 'sti / 'chando 'bhimāninā pṛthagvedābhimānī saptacchando nāmā saptasveko 'sti'; iti tattvapradīpokteḥ / ata eva 'sapta yuñjanti .... eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā'; ityanayorna virodhaḥ / sūryarathacakrasya sthitimāha - trinābhīti / trirāvṛttamāsacatuṣṭayātmakanābhitrayopetam 'ajaraṃ'; sadā dṛḍham arvaśabditebhyo vājibhyo dūrasthatvādanarvaṃ cakraṃ sūryarathasyāstītyarthaḥ / cakrasya mānasottaragiriśikharavalayaparivartitvāt arvatāṃ merumānasottaramadhyākāśagāmitvāddūrasthatvaṃ yuktam / yena 'yatra'; cakre 'imā'; imāni viśvāni sarvāṇi bhuvanāni 'tasthuḥ'; sthitāḥ ityuttarārdhasyārthaḥ / jagataḥ 'pratiṣṭhām'; āśrayaṃ 'caturhetāram'; antaḥkaraṇacatuṣṭaye viṣayāṇāṃ hotāraṃ 'pradiśaḥ'; pratidiśam 'anukḷptaṃ'; vyavasthitaṃ 'vācaḥ'; vedasya 'vīryaṃ'; sāraṃ mukhyārtham 'indram agniṃ'; 'divo'; devyāḥ 'ātmānaṃ'; svāminaṃ vāyuṃ 'savitāraṃ bṛhaspatiṃ'; 'brahmā'; hiraṇyagarbhaḥ tapasā 'anvavindat'; labdhavānityarthaḥ / siddhāntayati - itīti //
children.translated_text: in the form of horses, 'yoke' themselves — that is, they become yoked — to the '<s>ekacakra</s>' (one-wheeled) chariot of the sun, joining themselves to it — that is the meaning. The one presided over by the seven meters, who separately presides over the <s>Vedas</s>, is the one principal horse named <s>Saptacchandas</s> (seven-metered). As stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'The one presided over by the meters, who separately presides over the <s>Vedas</s>, named <s>Saptacchandas</s>, is one among the seven.' Therefore there is no contradiction with 'seven yoke... one horse bearing seven names.' He states the position of the wheel of the sun's chariot — '<s>trinābhi</s>' (three-naved): endowed with three naves consisting of four-month periods each thrice-revolving, '<s>ajara</s>' (undecaying) — always firm, and far from the horses denoted by the word '<s>arva</s>,' hence '<s>anarva</s>' (unreachable by horses) — such is the wheel of the sun's chariot, that is the meaning. Since the wheel revolves around the peak-circle of Mount <s>Mānasottara</s>, and the horses travel through the sky between <s>Meru</s> and <s>Mānasottara</s>, the distance is fitting. 'Wherein' — in which wheel — 'these,' all these worlds 'stand' — are established: this is the meaning of the second half. 'The foundation' — support — 'of the universe'; '<s>caturhetā</s>' (four-fold offerer) — the offerer of objects in the four-fold inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>); 'in the directions' — in each direction — 'established'; 'of speech' — of the <s>Veda</s> — 'the essence' — the principal meaning; '<s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>'; 'of heaven' — of the goddess — 'the self' — the lord, <s>Vāyu</s>; '<s>Savitā</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'; '<s>Brahmā</s>' — <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — 'found' through <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — obtained, that is the meaning. He gives the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) — 'thus.'
'<s>Antaḥ</s> (within), because of the teaching of His characteristics' — <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.20.

children.text:
antaḥ śrūyamāṇo viṣṇureva /
'antassamudre manasā carantam /
brahmānvavindaddaśahotāramarṇe'; (tai.u. 3-11-1.) 'samudre antaḥ kavayo vicakṣate marīcīnāṃ padamicchanti vedhasaḥ'; (tai.ā. 3-11-11.)
'yasyāṇḍakośaṃ śuṣmamāhuḥ'; (tai.ā. 3-11-4.) ityāditaddharmopadeśāt /
sa hi kṣīrasamudraśīyī /
children.translated_text: The one heard of as being within is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Because of the teaching of His characteristics in passages such as: 'Within the ocean, moving by [His own] mind, <s>Brahmā</s> found the <s>daśahotā</s> (ten-fold offerer) in the waters' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 3.11.1), 'The sages perceive within the ocean the abode of the <s>Marīcis</s> (rays); the creators seek it' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.11.11), 'Whose potency they call the cosmic egg' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.11.4), and so forth. For He is the one who reclines on the milk ocean.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.7.2]:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.7.2:
kuto na mantavyamityatastatra hetutvena sūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - antariti // sūtre 'ntarityuddeśyabhāge apekṣitaṃ padamadhyāhṛtya darśayati - śrūyamāṇa iti / antassthatvena śrutyocyamāna ityarthaḥ / vidheyasamarpakasyānuvṛttasya tattu, ityasyārthamāha - viṣṇureveti / taittirīyopaniṣadgatabhinnabhinnavākyodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ hetvaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - antariti/ ityādīti / tasya dharmāstaddharmāḥ teṣāmupadeśo vacanaṃ ityādirūpaścāsau taddharmopadeśaśca ityāditaddharmopadeśaḥ tasmādityarthaḥ / yadvā - luptavibhaktiko 'yaṃ nirdeśaḥ / tathā cetyāderupadeśādityarthaḥ / samudāyaikavacanametat / anena 'antaḥpraviṣṭam'; iti vākye 'antaḥśrūyamāṇo'; hṛdayāntassthatvena śrutyukto viṣṇureva, na tvanyaḥ / kutaḥ?
children.translated_text: [<s>Dīpikā</s> on <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.7.2]: Why should it not be so thought? To answer this, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> as the reason and explains — '<s>antaḥ</s>.' In the <s>sūtra</s>, he supplies the expected word that is to be understood in the subject portion '<s>antaḥ</s>' and shows it — 'being heard of.' That is, the one spoken of by <s>śruti</s> as dwelling within — that is the meaning. He states the meaning of the continued predicate-indicating phrase 'tattu' (but that) — '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' He explains the reason-portion with citation of various distinct passages from the <s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> — '<s>antaḥ</s>.' 'And so forth' — His characteristics are <s>taddharma</s> (His qualities), the teaching of those is the statement — and the compound '<s>āditaddharmopadeśa</s>' means: that which is of the form beginning with the teaching of His characteristics, therefore — that is the meaning. Or alternatively, this is a citation with an elided case ending. Thus, 'because of the teaching beginning with such-and-such' is the meaning. This is a collective singular expression. By this, in the passage 'entered within,' the one 'heard of as within' — spoken of by <s>śruti</s> as dwelling within the heart — is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not another. Why?

children.text: tasya viṣṇordharmāṇāṃ kṣīrapralayābdhisthatvabrahmajñeyatvabrahmatapolabhyatvabrahmāṇḍavīyatvādirūpāṇāṃ 'tasmin'; antaḥśrute tenāntarityādinā 'upadeśāt'; uktatvāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / upadeśādityantasya sūtrasya tasmādanya eveti na mantavyamityanenānvayaḥ / 'brahmā'; vartamānacaturmukhaḥ 'samudre'; pralayābdhau kṣīrābdhau ca 'antararṇe'; jale kṣīre ca 'manasā'; svecchayā sañcarantaṃ 'daśahotāraṃ'; jñānakarmākhyadaśendriyeṣu viṣayahotāraṃ tattadviṣayasthāpakaṃ daśendriyāṇi jīvena viṣayeṣu juhvataṃ vā viṣṇum 'anvavindat'; vyajānāt / 'kavayo'; jñāninaḥ 'samudre'; kṣīrapralayābdhyorantaḥsthitaṃ vicakṣate jānanti / 'vedhaso'; bhūtabhaviṣyadbrahmāṇaḥ 'marīcirmitaruktvataḥ'; iti chāndogyabhāṣyokteḥ / pramitaruktvanimittāt marīcipadoktānāṃ jīvānāṃ padam āśrayaṃ viṣṇum icchanti prārthayanti / tattvapradīparītyā 'kavayaḥ'; santaḥ 'vedhaso'; vicakṣate vicakṣaṇāya
children.translated_text: Because the characteristics of that <s>Viṣṇu</s> — in the form of dwelling in the ocean of dissolution, being knowable by <s>Brahmā</s>, being attainable through <s>Brahmā</s>'s austerity, having the cosmic egg as His potency, and so forth — are 'taught' in 'that' [passage] about the one heard of as within, through expressions such as 'within,' etc. — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. The connection of '<s>upadeśāt</s>' (because of the teaching), which ends the <s>sūtra</s>, is with 'therefore it should not be thought to be another.' '<s>Brahmā</s>' — the present four-faced one — 'in the ocean' — in the ocean of dissolution and the milk ocean — 'in the waters' — in water and milk — 'by mind' — by His own will — found the '<s>daśahotā</s>' (ten-fold offerer) — the one who offers in the ten sense-organs of knowledge and action directed toward their objects, the one who establishes each in its respective object, or the one through whom the <s>jīva</s> offers through the ten senses into the objects — [that is,] <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'found' means knew. 'The sages' — the knowers — 'perceive,' that is, know the one dwelling within 'the ocean' — in the milk ocean and ocean of dissolution. 'The creators' — <s>Brahmās</s> past and future — because of the statement in the <s>Chāndogya Bhāṣya</s>: '<s>marīci</s> is from the word <s>mitaruk</s>,' that is, on account of measured brilliance — they 'seek,' that is, pray for <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the abode, the refuge, of the <s>jīvas</s> denoted by the word <s>marīci</s>. According to the method of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'the sages,' being such, 'the creators' perceive — for the sake of perception, that is,

children.text: jñānāya marīcīnāṃ padaṃ viṣṇum icchantītyekānvayo vā / kavayaḥ 'aṇḍakośaṃ'; brahmāṇḍākhyasthānaṃ 'yasya'; viṣṇoḥ 'śuṣmaṃ'; vīryaṃ tadupādānakamāhuriti śrutyarthaḥ / viriñcivākyasyāsya 'prāṇa ulbaṃ tena kḷpto amṛtenāhamasmi'; iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / tasya 'ulbaṃ'; jarāyuḥ 'prāṇaḥ'; antaḥprāvaraṇaṃ yena sahaiva jāyate / 'tena'; amṛtena 'ahaṃ'; kḷpto 'smītyarthastattvapradīpe 'bhihitaḥ / kṣīrasamudrasthatvasya viṣṇuliṅgatvaṃ kuta ityata āha - sa hīti / 'saḥ'; viṣṇuḥ hiśabdena lokaprasiddhatvāditi hetu sūcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: knowledge — they desire <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the abode of the <s>Marīcis</s> — or this is a single syntactic construction. The sages declare the '<s>aṇḍakośa</s>' (cosmic egg) — the abode called <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> — to be the '<s>śuṣma</s>' (potency) — the power — of 'that' <s>Viṣṇu</s>, its material cause: such is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. This passage of <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) has the continuation: '<s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is the membrane; by that [immortal one] I have been fashioned.' Its 'membrane' (<s>ulba</s>) means the afterbirth; '<s>prāṇa</s>' is the inner covering, that with which one is born. 'By that' immortal one, 'I' have been 'fashioned' — this meaning is stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. As to why dwelling in the milk ocean is an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he says — 'for He.' 'He' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>; through the word 'hi' (for), the reason indicated is that it is well-known in popular tradition.

children.text:
tasya ca vīryamaṇḍakośaḥ /
so 'bhidhyāya śarīrātsvātsisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ /
apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryamavāsṛjat /
tadaṇaḍamabhavaddhaimaṃ sahasrāṃśusamaprabham /
yasmin jajñe svayaṃ brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ /
āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ /
ayanaṃ tasya tāḥ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ / iti vyāsasmṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: And His potency is the cosmic egg. 'He, contemplating, desiring to create manifold beings from His own body, first created the waters alone; in them He deposited His potency. That became the golden egg, equal in splendor to the thousand-rayed [sun], in which <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire of all worlds, was born by himself. The waters are called <s>nārāḥ</s>, for the waters are indeed the offspring of <s>Nara</s> (the Cosmic Man); since they were His first abode (<s>ayana</s>), He is therefore known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.' — Thus from the <s>Vyāsa Smṛti</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.7.3]:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.7.3:
astu viṣṇoḥ kṣīrābdhisthatvaṃ liṅgaṃ prasiddhatvāt, tathāpi pralayārṇavasthatvasya brahmāṇḍavīryatvasya ca kuto viṣṇudharmatvamityatastayorviṣṇudharmatve pramāṇaṃ vaktuṃ pratijānīte - tasyeti / 'aṇḍakośo'; brahmāṇḍākhyasthānaṃ 'tasya'; viṣṇorvīryamityarthaḥ / caśabdātsaḥ pralayasamudraśāyīti pratijñā sūcyate / tasyaivetyavadhāraṇe vā caśabdaḥ / tathātve pratijñāntaramupalakṣaṇīyam / ata eva pralayābdhiśāyitve 'āpo nārāḥ'; iti paścātpramāṇopanyāsaḥ śrutāvaṇḍakośaśabdaśravaṇe 'pi pratyayasya svārthikatvāttattyāgenāṇḍakośa ityevānūditam / śrutāvapi tathaiva chedo vā / 'saḥ'; vāsudevāt jāto viṣṇuḥ 'svāt'; svakīyāccharīrāt vividhāḥ prajāḥ 'sisṛkṣuḥ'; sraṣṭumicchuḥ 'abhidhyāya'; vicintya 'ādau'; aṇḍasṛṣṭeḥ pūrvameva 'apaḥ'; tadāvaraṇarūpāḥ sasarja / tāsvapsu vīryam 'avāsṛjat'; nyadhāt māyādvāreti śeṣaḥ / 'haimaṃ'; hiraṇyātmakaṃ 'sahasrāṃśusamaprabhaṃ'; sūryasamaprakāśaṃ 'tat'; vīryaṃ brahmāṇḍākhyamabhavat / 'yasmin'; aṇḍe 'sarvalokapitāmaho'; brahmā caturmukhaḥ 'svayaṃ'; svatantrāt hareḥ sākṣājjajñe ityarthaḥ / yataḥ āpo 'narasūnavaḥ'; narasya viṣṇossūnavaḥ / 'viṣṇurnaro nāśātparo yataḥ'; iti bhāgavatatātparyokteḥ / ato nārāḥ proktāḥ yena kāraṇena 'pūrvaṃ'; pralaye 'tāḥ'; āpaḥ tasya viṣṇoḥ ayanaṃ 'tena saḥ nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ'; tacchabdavācyatvena smṛtyukta ityarthaḥ / yadyapi -
children.translated_text: [<s>Dīpikā</s> on <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.7.3]: Granted that <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s dwelling in the milk ocean is an indicatory mark because it is well-known, but how is dwelling in the ocean of dissolution and the cosmic egg being His potency characteristic of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To answer this, he promises to state the authority for those two being characteristics of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'of that.' The '<s>aṇḍakośa</s>' — the abode called <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> — is the potency 'of that' <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that is the meaning. By the word 'ca' (and), the promise 'He reclines in the ocean of dissolution' is indicated. Or the word 'ca' is for emphasis (of 'His alone'), in which case the other promise is to be understood by implication. Therefore, even though the word '<s>aṇḍakośa</s>' occurs in the <s>śruti</s> with the suffix having its own meaning, it is cited as simply '<s>aṇḍakośa</s>' by dropping the suffix [<s>tat</s>]. Or there is the same word-division in the <s>śruti</s> itself. 'He' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, born from <s>Vāsudeva</s> — 'desiring to create' manifold beings 'from His own' body, 'contemplating,' 'first' — even before the creation of the egg — created 'the waters' — those in the form of coverings — and in those waters 'deposited' His potency — placed it; through <s>Māyā</s> is the remainder. 'Golden' — made of gold; 'equal in splendor to the thousand-rayed one' — equal in radiance to the sun; 'that' potency became the [egg] called <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>. 'In which' egg, 'the grandsire of all worlds,' <s>Brahmā</s>, the four-faced one, was born 'by himself' — directly from the independent <s>Hari</s>, that is the meaning. Since the waters are 'offspring of <s>Nara</s>' — offspring of <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is <s>Nara</s>. As stated in the <s>Bhāgavata Tātparya</s>: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> is <s>Nara</s> because He is beyond destruction.' Therefore they are called <s>nārāḥ</s>; because 'formerly' — at the time of dissolution — 'those' waters were the abode (<s>ayana</s>) of that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'therefore He is known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' — He is stated by <s>smṛti</s> as being denoted by that word, that is the meaning. Although —
When the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Person) first came forth, breaking open the egg,
seeking an abode for Himself, He created the waters, the pure one [creating] the pure,
— thus in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>,

children.text: aṇḍaṃ praviṣṭo yo viṣṇuḥ so 'ṇḍaṃ bhittvā prakāśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Viṣṇu</s> who entered the egg, having broken it, was manifested;
He created the waters, therefore [they are called] <s>nārāḥ</s>...

children.text: iti bhāgavatatātparye cāṇḍasṛṣṭyanantaram apsṛṣṭirucyate / tathāpi sā bahiḥsṛṣṭeranyāntareti na virodhaḥ / itītyasya 'tasya ca vīryamaṇḍakośaḥ, sa hi pralayasamudraśāyī yataḥ'; iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: — thus in the <s>Bhāgavata Tātparya</s> also, the creation of waters is spoken of as following the creation of the egg. Nevertheless, that [creation of waters] is different from the external creation, being an internal one — so there is no contradiction. The word 'thus' connects with the preceding: 'And His potency is the cosmic egg, for He reclines in the ocean of dissolution.'
'I [perceived] that radiance, the rays, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s> born in the beginning.
From <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Supreme Person), <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and the cosmic egg (<s>jagadaṇḍa</s>)' — thus in the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s>. // 20 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.7.4]:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.7.4:
itaśca brahmāṇḍajanakavīryatvaṃ pralayasthatvaṃ ca tasyaiva jñāyata ityāha - ahamiti / 'tripuruṣaṃ māyābījamajāyata'; iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / taditi vyāptivacano 'sarvanāmaśabdaḥ / athavā sarvanāmaśabdaḥ, ata eva ṭīkāyāṃ tadaheyamiti vyutkramaḥ kṛtaḥ / tathā ca tatprasiddhaṃ vyāptaṃ vā 'aham'; aheyaṃ ratiḥ śaṃ ca mitamasyeti raśmirjīvaḥ tamindayati prerayatīti raśmīt jīvaprerakaṃ, inda preraṇe iti dhātoḥ ayaṃ dakārāntaḥ śabdaḥ / anukṛtyadhikaraṇe tu - indhī dīptāviti dhātuvyākhyānāt raśmīt bhagavadapekṣayā raśmirūpāṇām alpānāṃ sūryāditejasāṃ prakāśakamiti vyākhyātam, tatra dhakārānto 'gnīcchabdavadayaṃ śabdo jñātavyaḥ / 'tejaḥ'; jagatprakāśakaṃ 'puruṣaṃ'; pūrṇaṣaḍguṇaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tadākhyaṃ brahma teja iti vā / 'agrataḥ'; pralaye 'jātaṃ'; sthitaṃ tasmānnārāyaṇākhyapuruṣāt 'agrataḥ'; prathamaṃ 'prakṛtiḥ'; cetanā jāyate gacchatīti jagat jīvasamudāyaḥ,
children.translated_text: And from this it is known that the power to generate the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) and the state of existing during dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) belong to Him alone — thus he says 'I' (<s>aham</s>). 'The three-<s>Puruṣa</s> seed of <s>Māyā</s> was born' — this is the remainder of the sentence. 'That' (<s>tat</s>) is a pronoun (<s>sarvanāmaśabda</s>) denoting pervasiveness. Alternatively, it is simply a pronoun, and for this very reason the commentary has made the transposition 'that, imperishable' (<s>tad aheyam</s>). And thus, 'that' means 'well-known' or 'all-pervading,' and 'I' (<s>aham</s>); 'imperishable' (<s>aheya</s>); <s>rati</s> (delight) and <s>śam</s> (bliss); 'measured of him' — thus <s>raśmi</s> means the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>); 'that which impels the <s>raśmi</s>' means the impeller of the <s>jīva</s>, from the root <s>ind</s> meaning 'to impel' — this word ends in the letter 'da.' But in the <s>Anukṛtyadhikaraṇa</s>, because the root is explained as <s>indhī dīptau</s> (to shine), <s>raśmīt</s> is interpreted with reference to the Lord as 'that which illuminates the lesser lights such as the sun, which are of the nature of rays' — there the word should be understood as ending in 'dha,' like the word <s>agni</s>. '<s>Tejas</s>' (radiance) means the illuminator of the universe; '<s>Puruṣa</s>' means <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is full of the six attributes (<s>ṣaḍguṇa</s>) — or <s>Brahman</s> known by that name is called <s>tejas</s>. 'First' (<s>agrataḥ</s>) means 'during dissolution' (<s>pralaye</s>); 'born' (<s>jāta</s>) means 'existed' (<s>sthita</s>); from that <s>Puruṣa</s> known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, 'first' (<s>agrataḥ</s>) means 'primarily'; '<s>Prakṛti</s>' means the conscious entity; the aggregate of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) is called <s>jagat</s> (world), meaning 'that which goes,'

children.text: jātamityasyobhayatra yathāyogyaṃ sambandhaḥ / janiśca yathā yogyā grāhyā / paścāt 'aṇḍaṃ ca'; 'tripuruṣaṃ'; brahmavāyurudrākhyapuruṣatrayayuktaṃ 'māyābījaṃ'; prakṛtyupādānakam ajāyateti tattvapradīpadiśā śrutyarthaḥ / caturvedaśikhāyām ityasya vacanādityadhyāhāreṇa tasyetyanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'born' (<s>jāta</s>) connects with both in the appropriate manner. And the root <s>jan</s> (to be born) should be understood as appropriate to each context. Afterwards, 'the egg' (<s>aṇḍa</s>) also; '<s>tripuruṣa</s>' means endowed with the triad of persons known as <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>; 'the seed of <s>Māyā</s>' (<s>māyābīja</s>) means having <s>Prakṛti</s> as its material cause — thus 'was born' — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> according to the direction of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. The phrase 'in the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s>' connects with 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>) by supplying the word 'statement' (<s>vacana</s>).
'And He is different, because of the declaration of distinction.' | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.21 |

(tai.ā. 3-11.) ityādibhedavyapadeśāt // 21 //
children.translated_text: 'The self of <s>Indra</s> is placed as the five <s>hotṛs</s> (invokers)'; ... 'The wise ones have perceived the self of <s>Vāyu</s>'; ... 'Him who moves by His will within the sun, the heart of the gods — <s>Brahmā</s> discovered' (<s>Tai. Ā.</s> 3-11.) — because of such declarations of distinction. // 21 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.7.5:
yadyevaṃ samudrasthatvādiliṅgādantasstho viṣṇuḥ, tarhi tenāntassthena viṣṇunā indrādīnāmabhedo 'tra vivakṣito 'stu / indrādiprāpakakaśrutyāderapi sadbhāvāt / śrutyādeśca svabhāvato liṅgasya niravakāśatayā balavattvenānyatarabādhenānyatarapakṣanirṇayāyogāt / evaṃ ca pūrvottarapakṣadvaye anyonyaṃ bādhyabādhakabhāvaśūnye sati tadanyathānupapattyā antaḥsthena viṣṇunendrādīnāmabhedaḥ prāpta ityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - bhedeti / taittirīye - 'indrasya'; ityeko bhedavyapadeśaḥ / 'vāyoḥ'; ityanyaḥ / 'antaḥ'; ityaparaḥ / 'devānām'; iti cetaraḥ / ādiśabdena 'amṛtaṃ devānāmāyuḥ prajānāmindraṃ rājānaṃ savitāram'; ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / vyapadeśādityasyānya iti sautrapratijñayānvayaḥ / anena sūtre vidheyasamuccayārthakacaśabdasya bhinnakrameṇa anvayena na kevalamantaśśrūyamāṇo viṣṇuḥ, kintvindrādibhyo 'nyaśca / kutaḥ? tasyendrādyantaryāmitvadantassthatvakathanena tebhyo bhedokteriti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / atra śrutāvindraśabdo 'nyaparaḥ; ṣaṣṭhīśravaṇāt / 'indro rājā'; ityādau tu indrādiśabdāḥ paramamukhyavṛttyā viṣṇuparā eva, bādhakābhāvāt / tathā ca mano vihāya pañcasu jñānendriyeṣu śabdādiviṣayahotā tairviṣayānubhāvakaḥ / indrasyātmā antaryāmī ādānādikartā vā / sarvahṛdayeṣu 'nihitaḥ'; sannihitaḥ 'kavayo'; jñāninaḥ 'vāyorātmānaṃ nicikyuḥ'; dadṛśuḥ āditye 'ntaḥ 'manasā'; svecchayā sañcarantaṃ viṣṇuṃ kavayaḥ anvavindan / 'brahmā'; caturmukhaḥ devānāṃ hṛdyayanāt sthiteḥ pravartanādvā hṛdayaṃ viṣṇum 'anvavindat'; apaśyaditi śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: If this is so — that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the indweller based on indicators such as being situated in the ocean — then let it be intended here that <s>Indra</s> and others are non-different from that indwelling <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since <s>śruti</s> and other means that lead to <s>Indra</s> and others also exist. And since the indicator (<s>liṅga</s>), being by nature stronger than <s>śruti</s> and other means due to their having no independent scope, the determination of either position by sublating the other is not possible. And when thus in both the prior and subsequent positions there is no mutual relation of sublator and sublated, then by the impossibility of explaining it otherwise, the non-difference of <s>Indra</s> and others with the indwelling <s>Viṣṇu</s> would follow — having raised this objection, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> and explains it: 'distinction' (<s>bheda</s>). In the <s>Taittirīya</s>, 'of <s>Indra</s>' — this is one declaration of distinction. 'Of <s>Vāyu</s>' — another. 'Within' (<s>antaḥ</s>) — yet another. 'Of the gods' (<s>devānām</s>) — still another. By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), passages such as 'the immortal one, the life of the gods, the people's <s>Indra</s>, the king, <s>Savitṛ</s>' are included. The word 'from declaration' (<s>vyapadeśāt</s>) connects with 'different' (<s>anya</s>) as the thesis of the <s>sūtra</s>. By the word 'ca' (and) in the <s>sūtra</s>, which has the meaning of cumulative predication, connecting in a different order — not only is <s>Viṣṇu</s> heard as being within, but also He is different from <s>Indra</s> and others. Why? Because there is a declaration of His difference from them through the statement of His being their inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) and indweller — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. Here in the <s>śruti</s>, the word '<s>Indra</s>' refers to another entity, because the genitive case is heard. But in passages like '<s>Indra</s> is the king,' the words <s>Indra</s> etc. refer to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone in their supremely primary sense, since there is no sublating authority. And thus, setting aside the mind, in the five sense organs (<s>jñānendriya</s>), the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker) of objects such as sound is the one who causes experience of objects through them. The self of <s>Indra</s> is the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), or the agent of taking and other actions. 'Placed' (<s>nihita</s>) in the hearts of all means 'closely present'; 'the wise' (<s>kavayaḥ</s>) means the knowers; 'perceived the self of <s>Vāyu</s>' (<s>nicikyuḥ</s>) means 'they saw'; within the sun (<s>āditya</s>), 'moving by mind' (<s>manasā</s>) means by His own will — the wise ones found <s>Viṣṇu</s> who moves thus. '<s>Brahmā</s>' means the four-faced one (<s>Caturmukha</s>); 'discovered' (<s>anvavindat</s>) the heart of the gods, meaning <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is the heart of the gods because He dwells in their hearts (<s>hṛdyayana</s>), or because He directs them — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.
// Thus ends the <s>Antaḥsthatvādhikaraṇa</s> (section on the indweller) // 7 //
// 8. <s>Ākāśādhikaraṇa</s> (section on space) //

children.text:
'ko hyevānyātkaḥ prāṇyāt / yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt'
(tai. 2-7.) iti ākāśasyānandamayatve heturuktaḥ na tu viṣṇoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Who indeed could breathe, who could live, if this <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) were not bliss?' (<s>Tai.</s> 2-7.) — here the reason for the bliss-nature (<s>ānandamayatva</s>) is stated with respect to <s>Ākāśa</s>, not with respect to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.8.1:
atrādhikaraṇe bhagatavi lokato 'nyatraprasiddhākāśapadopalakṣitādhibhautikāśeṣaśabdasamanvayaḥ kriyate / phalakathanena pūrvapakṣaḥ sūcito bhavatītyāśayena pūrvapakṣaphalamāha - ko hīti // itīti / ityānandamayādhikaraṇodāhṛtavākyenetyarthaḥ / tuśabdasyākāśasya tviti sambandhaḥ / tathā ca chandogaśrutyuktākāśābhinnākāśasyaivetyarthaḥ / 'ānandamayatve'; pūrṇānandatvena nimittena ānandamayaśabdavācyatve 'hetuḥ'; lokaceṣṭakatvarūpaḥ / tuśabdārthaivakāravyāvartyamāha - neti / anena viṣṇubhinnabhūtākāśasyaiva chandogaśrutyuktākāśaśabdavācyatvamiti pūrvapakṣe 'ko hi'; iti taittirīyaśrutyukto 'pi sa eveti taduktahetunā tasyaivānandamayatvaṃ sidhyati, na viṣṇoriti phalamuktaṃ bhavati / pūrvasaṅgatistvadhikāśaṅkāṃ kṛtvātra pūrvanyāya evātidiśyata ityātideśikī draṣṭavyā /
children.translated_text: In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section), the coordination (<s>samanvaya</s>) of all the words with the physical space (<s>ādhibhautikākāśa</s>), which is well-known elsewhere in common usage and is indicated by the word <s>ākāśa</s>, is carried out — this is the Lord's intention. The prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) is indicated by stating its consequence — thus he states the consequence of the prior position: 'Who indeed' (<s>ko hi</s>). The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) means 'by the sentence cited in the <s>Ānandamayādhikaraṇa</s>.' The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) connects as 'of <s>Ākāśa</s> indeed' (<s>ākāśasya tu</s>). And thus the meaning is: of that very <s>Ākāśa</s> which is non-different from the <s>Ākāśa</s> mentioned in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s>. 'In being the referent of the word <s>Ānandamaya</s>' (<s>ānandamayatve</s>) — the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is in the form of being the cause of worldly activity, by virtue of being full bliss (<s>pūrṇānanda</s>). He states the meaning of the restrictive particle 'but' (<s>tu</s>) that is to be distinguished: 'not' (<s>na</s>). By this, in the prior position that physical space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>), distinct from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is alone the referent of the word <s>ākāśa</s> used in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s>, and the reason stated in the <s>Taittirīya</s> <s>śruti</s> with 'who indeed' (<s>ko hi</s>) also applies to that same entity alone — by the stated reason, its bliss-nature is established, not of <s>Viṣṇu</s>: this is the stated consequence. The prior connection, however, should be seen as an extension (<s>ātideśa</s>) by which a further objection is raised and the previous principle is extended here.
This should not be thought so. Because —
'<s>Ākāśa</s> (space) [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the indicatory marks of that [<s>Brahman</s>].' | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.22 |

children.text:
'asya lokasya kā gatirityākāśa iti hovāca'; (chā. 1-9.)
ityatra bhūtākāśasya prāptiḥ / na cāsau yujyate, kintu, viṣṇureva /
'sa eṣa parovarīyānudgīthaḥ sa eṣo 'nantaḥ'; (chā. 1-9.)
ityāditalliṅgāt /
children.translated_text: 'What is the goal of this world?' — 'It is <s>Ākāśa</s>,' he said. (<s>Chā.</s> 1-9.) Here, the prima facie interpretation would apply to physical space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>). But that is not fitting; rather, it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. 'He is the supremely greatest <s>Udgītha</s> (chant), He is infinite' (<s>Chā.</s> 1-9.) — because of such indicatory marks of that [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.8.2:
siddhāntayati - itīti // kuto na mantavyamityāśaṅkāyāṃ tatra hetutayā sūtramupādatte / yata iti / idaṃ cāvartate / tatrādyasya 'yataścodeti'; itivat kuta ityarthaḥ / 'yacchabdastu parāmarśe praśnārthe 'pi bhaṇyate'; iti bhāgavatatātparyokteḥ / dvitīyastu na mantavyamiti pratijñāyāṃ sūtrārthasya hetutvadyotakaḥ / viṣayādeḥ pūrvapakṣaphalakathanena sūcane 'pi mukhato 'nukteḥ tadanuvādapūrvakaṃ sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - asyeti / 'ityatra'; vākye pratipādyatvasyeti śeṣaḥ / co 'pyarthaḥ / yadyapi tathāpītyarthe / 'asau'; ākāśo 'tra vācya iti śeṣaḥ/ sūtre 'nuvṛttasya 'tattu'; ityasyārtho viṣṇureveti / ityādīti / luptavibhaktiko nirdeśaḥ ādiśabdāt 'sarvāṇi bhūtāni'; ityādijagatkāraṇatvapratipādakaṃ vākyaṃ gṛhyate / yathoktaṃ tattvapradīpe - "sarvāṇi bhūtāni'; ityādinā udīryamāṇaṃ jagadutpādakatvādikamādiśabdādupādadīta"iti / liṅgapadaṃ śrutyupalakṣakam / tathā cetthaṃ yojanā-yadyapi 'asya lokasya'; iti chandogavākye bhūtākāśasya śrutyādibalādasti pratipādyatvasya prāptiḥ / tathāpi nāsāvatra vākye ākāśapadena vācyo yujyate, kintu - viṣṇureva / kutaḥ? 'sa eṣaḥ'; ityādivākye 'talliṅgāt'; tasya viṣṇorliṅgamasādhāraṇadharmaḥ parovarīyastavādiḥ / tasya tasminnākāśe śravaṇāduktatvāt / yata evaṃ talliṅgāt asau
chandogaśrutyuktākāśo viṣṇureva, tata eva 'ko hi'; iti taittirīyavākye 'pyasāveva pratipādyata iti tasyaivānandamayatve heturukto na tu bhūtasya/ ato bhūtākāśasyānandamayatve heturuktaḥ, na tu viṣṇoriti na mantavyamiti / anena sūtrayojanā darśitā/ asyetyāderayamarthaḥ - 'asya'; pratyakṣasiddhasya
children.translated_text: He establishes the conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>): 'this' (<s>iti</s>). When the question arises 'why should it not be thought so?' — he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> as the reason for that: 'because' (<s>yataḥ</s>). And this recurs. There, of the first [<s>yataḥ</s>], the meaning is 'from what cause,' like 'from which it arises' (<s>yataścodeti</s>). As stated in the <s>Bhāgavatatātparya</s>: 'The word <s>yat</s> is used both in reference and in the sense of a question.' The second 'but' (<s>tu</s>) indicates that the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> serves as the reason for the thesis 'it should not be thought so.' Although the subject matter, prior position, and consequence are indicated by stating the consequence, since they are not explicitly stated, he explains the <s>sūtra</s> preceded by restating them: 'of this' (<s>asya</s>). 'Here' (<s>ityatra</s>) — the remainder is 'of the status of being the thing to be established in the sentence.' 'Ca' has the meaning of 'also' (<s>api</s>). 'Even though' (<s>yadyapi</s>) — in the sense of 'nevertheless' (<s>tathāpi</s>). 'That' (<s>asau</s>) — the remainder is 'the <s>ākāśa</s> that is to be denoted here.' The meaning of '<s>tattu</s>' (but that) continuing in the <s>sūtra</s> is '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' 'Such as' (<s>ityādi</s>) — this is a citation with elided case endings; by the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the passage 'all beings' and other statements establishing the causality of the universe are included. As stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'One should include by the word "etc." the statement establishing the creatorship of the universe beginning with "all beings."' The word <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) is an indicator of <s>śruti</s>. And thus the construction is as follows: even though in the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage 'of this world,' there is a prima facie claim that physical space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>) is what is to be established, based on the strength of <s>śruti</s> and other means, nevertheless that physical space is not fittingly the referent of the word <s>ākāśa</s> in this passage; rather, it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Why? Because in the passage 'He is this,' the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of that <s>Viṣṇu</s> — namely the distinctive attribute of being 'supremely greatest' (<s>parovarīyān</s>) and so forth — is heard as belonging to that <s>Ākāśa</s>, i.e., is stated of it. Since it is thus because of that indicatory mark, the <s>Ākāśa</s> mentioned in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; and therefore in the <s>Taittirīya</s> passage 'who indeed' (<s>ko hi</s>) also, it is He alone who is being taught — thus the reason for His bliss-nature is stated, not of physical space. Therefore, 'the reason for the bliss-nature of physical space is stated, not of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — this should not be thought. By this, the construction of the <s>sūtra</s> is demonstrated. The meaning of 'of this' (<s>asya</s>) and what follows is: 'of this'

children.text: pṛthivīlokasya tadabhimāninaścaturmukhasya 'kā gatiḥ'; āśraya iti śilakena pṛṣṭaḥ pravāhaṇo rājā ādīptatvādākāśanāmako viṣṇuriti pratyuvāca / kathamityākāṅkṣāyāṃ tadupapādanāya tasyākāśasya mahimānamāha - 'sarvāṇi havā imāni bhūtānyākāśādeva samutpadyante ākāśaṃ pratyastaṃ yanti ākāśo hyevaibhyo jyāyānākāśaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa eṣa paro varīyānudgīthaḥ sa eṣo 'nantaḥ'; iti / atra vaiśabdasya prasiddhidyotakasya sannihitasarvabhūtānvaye vā, 'syurevaṃ tu punarvaivetyavadhāraṇavācakāḥ'; ityabhidhānādavadhāraṇārthatvaṃ vā draṣṭavyam / bhūtaśabdo bhūtākāśa evātrocyate iti pūrvapakṣe ākāśavyatiriktabhūtaparaḥ / siddhānte tu sarvabhūtaparaḥ / brahmādisarvajagatparo vā / tathā ca 'sarvāṇīmāni'; pramitāni ākāśādibhūtāni brahmādijagadvā ākāśādeva samutpadyante / 'havai'; prasiddhaṃ hi /
children.translated_text: refers to the earth-world (<s>pṛthivīloka</s>), which is well-established through direct perception, or of <s>Caturmukha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>, the four-faced one) who presides over it — 'what is the goal?' (<s>kā gatiḥ</s>) means 'what is the support?' When <s>Śilaka</s> asked thus, King <s>Pravāhaṇa</s> replied that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is called <s>Ākāśa</s> because of His luminosity (<s>ādīptatva</s>), is the answer. When the question 'how?' arises, to establish that, he declares the greatness of that <s>Ākāśa</s>: 'All these beings indeed arise from <s>Ākāśa</s> alone, they dissolve back into <s>Ākāśa</s>; for <s>Ākāśa</s> is greater than all of them, <s>Ākāśa</s> is the ultimate refuge. He is the supremely greatest <s>Udgītha</s> (chant), He is infinite.' Here, the particle 'vai' either indicates well-known usage connecting with 'all beings' that are proximate, or, since 'the particles <s>su</s>, <s>evam</s>, <s>tu</s>, <s>punar</s>, and <s>vai</s> are declarers of emphasis,' it should be seen as having an emphatic restrictive meaning. The word <s>bhūta</s> (being/element) — in the prior position where it is argued that the word <s>ākāśa</s> refers only to physical space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>) — refers to elements other than <s>ākāśa</s>. But in the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), it refers to all beings. Or it refers to the entire universe beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>. And thus, 'all these' well-known beings — the elements beginning with <s>ākāśa</s>, or the universe beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> — arise from <s>Ākāśa</s> alone. 'Indeed' (<s>havai</s>) means 'as is well known.'

children.text: ākāśaṃ 'pratyastam'; adarśanaṃ 'yanti'; tatraiva pralaye muktau ca līnāḥ bhavanti / kutaḥ? 'hi'; yasmādākāśa eva 'ebhyo'; brahmādibhyo 'jyāyān'; adhikottamaḥ / kuta etat? yata ākāśaḥ 'parāyaṇam'; uttamāśrayaḥ naitasmāduttamaṃ vastvāśaṅkyamiti bhāvenāha - sa iti / 'sa eṣaḥ'; ākāśanāmā bhagavān 'parovarīyān'; atra -
children.translated_text: They 'go to dissolution' (<s>pratyastam</s>), meaning disappearance, 'into <s>Ākāśa</s>' — they become absorbed in Him during dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) and in liberation (<s>mukti</s>). Why? 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — because <s>Ākāśa</s> alone is 'greater' (<s>jyāyān</s>), meaning superior and highest, 'than these' (<s>ebhyaḥ</s>) — than <s>Brahmā</s> and others. How is this known? Because <s>Ākāśa</s> is the 'ultimate refuge' (<s>parāyaṇa</s>), the supreme support — with the sense that nothing higher than this can be conceived, he says: 'He' (<s>sa</s>). 'He, this one' (<s>sa eṣaḥ</s>) — the Lord named <s>Ākāśa</s> — is 'supremely greatest' (<s>parovarīyān</s>). Here —

children.text: parasmāduttamaṃ proktaṃ paro iti tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: That which is higher than the highest is called <s>para</s> (supreme); that which is beyond even that,
is called <s>parovara</s> (supreme of the supreme); that which is even beyond that is declared to be <s>pārovarīyaka</s> (the supremely greatest).

children.text: iti sāmasaṃhitāvacanānusāreṇādau para iti śabdāntarasya madhye varaśabdāntarasya ca āvāpena vṛttivākye subādeśasya sorulopena rutvotvaguṇeṣu samāne pare optaśabdadvayasya lope cottamottamottama ityartho jñātavyaḥ / 'udgīthaḥ'; uccatvena gīta ukto vedena / takārasya thakāro vyatyayāt / 'sa eṣaḥ'; ākāśaḥ 'ananto'; deśakālaguṇairaparicchanna iti / chāndogyabhāṣye tu 'uccatvādgīthatvātsarvasthānasthatvādudgītho bhagavān'; iti vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: Following the statement of the <s>Sāmasaṃhitā</s>, by inserting first the additional word <s>para</s> and in the middle the additional word <s>vara</s> in the derivative expression, with the substitution of case endings (<s>subādeśa</s>), the elision of 'su,' the change of 'ru' to 'u' and the <s>guṇa</s> vowel-strengthening — when these are alike before what follows, and with the elision of the two words ending in the optative, the meaning should be understood as 'the highest of the highest of the highest' (<s>uttamottamottama</s>). '<s>Udgītha</s>' (the chant) means 'praised on high' (<s>uccatvena gīta</s>), that is, declared by the <s>Veda</s>. The letter 'ta' becomes 'tha' by phonetic interchange (<s>vyatyaya</s>). 'He, this one' (<s>sa eṣaḥ</s>) — this <s>Ākāśa</s> — is 'infinite' (<s>ananta</s>), meaning not limited by space, time, or qualities. But in the <s>Chāndogya Bhāṣya</s>, it is explained: 'The Lord is <s>Udgītha</s> because of His exaltedness, because of being praised, and because of being present in all places.'

children.text:
'viṣṇornu kaṃ vīryāṇi pravocaṃ yaḥ pārthivān vimame rajāṃsi'; (ṛ. 1-154-1.)
'paro mātrayā tanvā vṛdhāna'; (ṛ. 7-99-1.)
ityādinā tasyaiva hi talliṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed, who could proclaim the heroic deeds? He who measured out the earthly regions' (<s>Ṛ.</s> 1-154-1.) 'He who grew beyond all measure by His own body' (<s>Ṛ.</s> 7-99-1.) — by such passages, the indicatory marks indeed belong to Him alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.8.3:
'sa eṣo 'nantaḥ'; ityuktānantatvasyāparimitatvasya viṣṇuniṣṭhatvaṃ kuto jñāyata ityata āha-viṣṇoriti/ viṣṇorvīryāṇi 'kaṃ'; ko 'nu ko vā 'pravocam'; prāvocat / sākalyena pravakti na ko 'pi / 'yaḥ'; kaḥ kavirbahmā 'pārthivāni rajāṃsi'; pārthivaparamāṇūn 'vimame'; gaṇayati / so 'pi na pravaktīti śrutyarthaḥ/ 'parovarīyān'; ityuktasarvottamatvasya viṣṇudharmatvaṃ kuta ityata āha - para iti / atra 'na te mahitvamanvaśnuvanti'; iti uttaravākyāduktārtho jñāyate / ata evādiśabda ubhayānvayī / tatrādyo 'viṣṇornu vīryagaṇanāṃ katamo 'rhatīha yaḥ parthivānyapi kavirvimame rajāṃsi'; iti smṛtigrāhī / vyākhyāteyaṃ śrutirjanmanaye / ityādinā vākyeneti śeṣaḥ / yadyapi śrutyanusārātsarvottamatve prathamaṃ pramāṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ na tu anantatve / ata eva ṭīkāyāmādau sarvottamatvaṃ gṛhītam/ tathāpi anantatvasya sāvakāśatvaśaṅkāviṣayatvātprathamaṃ tatra pramāṇopanyāsaḥ / ata eva tatraivottaratra smṛtyā sāvakāśatvaśaṅkāparihāraḥ / 'tasya'; viṣṇoḥ hiśabdo yata ityarthe / 'tat'; anantatvādi 'liṅgaṃ'; dharma ityavagatam/ ato na hetuviśeṣaṇāsiddhiriti vākyaśeṣaḥ / evakārapāṭhe nānaikāntyamiti śeṣaḥ / uttaratrānvayo vā/ yadyapi 'anantaḥ'; iti śrutiḥ; vācakaśabdatvāt / tathāpi tatpadapravṛttinimittasya liṅgatvamapyaviruddham /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.8, verse 3:
Whence is it known that the infinitude (<s>anantatva</s>) — the unlimitedness — stated in 'He is indeed infinite' pertains to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he says: 'viṣṇoḥ' (of <s>Viṣṇu</s>). Of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> heroic deeds, 'who' — who indeed, who at all — 'has proclaimed' them? No one proclaims [them] in their entirety. 'He who' — whichever sage, [even] <s>Brahmā</s>, 'measures' — counts — 'the particles of earth' (<s>pārthivāni rajāṃsi</s>) — the atoms of earth — even he cannot proclaim them: this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>. Whence is it known that the supreme excellence stated in 'parovarīyān' (the exceedingly greater) is an attribute of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he says: 'paraḥ' (supreme). Here, the stated meaning is known from the subsequent passage 'they do not attain Your greatness.' Therefore the word 'ādi' (and the like) connects with both. Of these, the first [ādi] includes the <s>Smṛti</s> 'who indeed is worthy of counting <s>Viṣṇu's</s> heroic deeds here, He who, though a sage, measured the particles of the earth.' 'This <s>Śruti</s> has been explained in the <s>Janma</s> method' — 'by a sentence [beginning] thus' is the remainder. Although, following the <s>Śruti</s>, the authority for supreme excellence should be stated first, not for infinitude — and hence in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, supreme excellence is taken up first — nevertheless, since infinitude is the subject of the suspicion of having scope [in others], the authority is presented there first. Hence, in that same [context], subsequently, the suspicion of having scope is resolved through <s>Smṛti</s>. 'Of that' <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the word 'hi' is in the sense of 'because.' 'That' — infinitude and the like — is understood to be the 'liṅga' (mark), i.e., the attribute. Therefore there is no non-establishment of the qualifier of the reason: this is the remainder of the sentence. In the reading with the word 'eva,' the remainder is: there is no inconclusiveness. Or the connection is with what follows. Although 'anantaḥ' (infinite) is a <s>Śruti</s> — because it is an expressive word — nevertheless, the being a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the ground for the operation of that word is also not contradictory.
