children.translated_text: Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.8, verse 4:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.8.4:
nanvanantatvam 'anantākāśavatpaśyan'; ityākāśasyāpi smaryate, ataḥ sāvakāśatvātkathaṃ viṣṇoreva talliṅgamityataḥ smṛtimāha - ananta iti / ānandeti luptavibhaktiko nirdeśaḥ/ viṣṇurevaiko mukhyatayā procyata iti sambandhaḥ / 'pareṣāṃ'; viṣṇoranyeṣām 'upacārataḥ'; svasvasamīpagataparamātmasambandhādeva vācyateti śeṣaḥ / iti brāhma ityasya tasyaiva talliṅgamityuktamiti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / anenaivakāro liṅgasya niravakāśatvajñāpaka iti sūcitam /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.8, verse 4:
But infinitude is also mentioned for space (<s>ākāśa</s>) in 'seeing like the infinite space' — therefore, since there is scope [for the word 'infinite' to apply to others], how can it be a mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone? To this he cites a <s>Smṛti</s>: 'anantaḥ.' 'Ānanda' is cited with elided case-ending. The connection is: <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is proclaimed primarily. 'Of others' — of those other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'figuratively' — only because of the connection with the <s>Paramātman</s> who is near each one — thus [they are] denotable: this is the remainder. The construction of 'thus in the <s>Brāhma</s>' connects with the preceding: 'that alone is stated to be His mark.' By this, the word 'eva' (alone) is indicated as declaring the exclusive scope of the mark.
'All names enter into Him' (<s>Bhāllaveyam</s>) — and thus it is stated. // 22 //
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.8, verse 5:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.8.5:
nanu śrutyā pūrvapakṣite kathaṃ liṅgena nirṇayaḥ / liṅgasya śrutito durbalatvādityataḥ ākāśaśrutirviṣṇau sāvakāśeti śrutyā darśayati - nāmānīti / 'co'; yato 'nāmāni sarvāṇi'; iti vākyena viṣṇorākāśādisarvaśabdavācyatvamuktam, ato liṅgena śruterbādhayā nirṇayo yukta iti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.8, verse 5:
But when the prima facie view is established through <s>Śruti</s>, how can the determination be through a mark (<s>liṅga</s>)? Since a mark is weaker than <s>Śruti</s> — to this he shows through <s>Śruti</s> that the <s>ākāśa</s>-<s>Śruti</s> [has scope] in <s>Viṣṇu</s>: 'nāmāni' (names). 'Ca' — since, by the passage 'all names [enter into Him],' the denotability of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by all words including <s>ākāśa</s> and the like is stated, therefore the determination through a mark by the sublation of <s>Śruti</s> is justified: this is the construction.
// Thus ends the <s>Ākāśādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of space). // 8 //
// 9. The <s>Prāṇādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the vital breath). //
For the same reason, [He is] <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.23 |
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.9, verse 1:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.9.1:
atrādhikaraṇe lokato 'nyatra prasiddhādhyātmikāśeṣaśabdopalakṣakapraṇaśabdasya brahmaṇi samanvayaḥ kriyate / sarvatrādau sūtraṃ pāṭhyam / paścātsaṅgatyādikaṃ vaktavyamiti sūcayitumatra sūtramādāveva paṭhati - ata eveti /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.9, verse 1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the coherence (<s>samanvaya</s>) of the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' — which is well-known elsewhere than in the [present] scriptural context as indicative of all words pertaining to the individual self (<s>adhyātmika</s>) — in <s>Brahman</s> is established. To indicate that everywhere the <s>sūtra</s> should be read first and thereafter the connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) and the like should be stated, here he reads the <s>sūtra</s> at the very beginning: 'ata eva' (for the same reason).

children.text:
tadvai tvaṃ prāṇo abhavaḥ mahān bhogaḥ prajāpateḥ /
bhujaḥ kariṣyamāṇaḥ yaddevān prāṇayo nava (tai. ā. 3-14.)
iti mahābhogaśabdena paramānandatvaṃ prāṇasyoktam //
children.translated_text:
'That, indeed, You became — the <s>Prāṇa</s>, the great enjoyer of <s>Prajāpati</s>;
the enjoyments that were about to be, whereby You enlivened the nine gods.'
(<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.14)
Thus, by the word 'great enjoyer' (<s>mahābhoga</s>), the supreme blissfulness of <s>Prāṇa</s> is stated.
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.9, verse 2:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.9.2:
viṣayavākyodāharṇapūrvakaṃ pūrvādhikaraṇena saṅgatiṃ viṣayasaṃśayau ca sūcayati - taditi // atra yattadorāvṛttiḥ / bhujyata iti bhogaḥ ānandaḥ / tena tadvānupalakṣyate, dharmādharmiṇorabhedavivakṣā vā / tathā ca he viṣṇo 'yat'; yasmāt 'prajāpateḥ'; hiraṇyagarbhasya tadupakṣitānāṃ sakalajīvānāṃ 'bhujaḥ'; bhogān yogyānandān 'kariṣyamāṇaḥ'; upalakṣaṇametat - kurvāṇo 'kārṣīśca / 'tasmāttvaṃ'; 'mahān bhogaḥ'; pūrṇānandavānabhavaḥ/ svasya mahābhogābhāve parasmai taddānānupapatteḥ / yasmācca pāyuguhyaikyena navendriyābhimānino devān tvaṃ 'prāṇayaḥ'; aceṣṭayaḥ/ idamapyupalakṣaṇaṃ - ceṣṭayasi ceṣṭayiṣyasi ca / tasmāttvaṃ prāṇaḥ prāṇaśabdavācyo 'bhava iti siddhāntarītyā śrutyarthaḥ / pūrvapakṣe tvetatsarvaṃ mukhyaprāṇe yojyam / itīti / 'iti'; taittirīyaśākhāgatavākye 'paramānandatvaṃ'; pūrṇānandatvaparyavasitaṃ 'tadvai tvam'; iti vākye 'mahābhogaśabdena'; 'mahān bhogaḥ'; iti padadvayātmakavākyena ca prāṇasyoktamiti yojanā / anena prāṇākhyo viṣayaḥ / tasya viṣṇvanyatvākṣepamukhenānandamayatvasyāpyanyaniṣṭhatvākṣepādānandamayādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ / saḥ vāyuruta viṣṇuriti saṃśayaśca sūcito bhavati /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.9, verse 2:
Preceding the citation of the subject-passage, he indicates the connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the subject, and the doubt: 'tat' (that). Here the words 'yat' (that) and 'tat' (this) recur. 'That which is enjoyed' — that is '<s>bhoga</s>' (enjoyment), i.e., bliss. By that, the possessor [of bliss] is indicated; or there is an intended non-difference between the attribute and the possessor. And thus — O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'since' — because — 'of <s>Prajāpati</s>' — of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and of all <s>jīvas</s> referred to by him — 'the enjoyments' — the suitable blisses — 'about to be made' — this is indicative: having made them and making them — 'therefore You' became 'the great enjoyer' — possessing complete bliss. Since without having great bliss Himself, the granting of it to another is impossible. And since by the unity of the nose, genitals, and the nine sense-organs' presiding deities, 'You enlivened' — You caused to act. This too is indicative — You cause to act and You will cause to act. Therefore You became the one denoted by the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>': this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> in the established-conclusion mode. In the prima facie view, however, all this should be construed as referring to the chief vital breath (<s>mukhya prāṇa</s>). 'Iti' — 'in this' — in the passage belonging to the <s>Taittirīya</s> branch, 'the supreme blissfulness' — culminating in complete blissfulness — is stated 'by the word mahābhoga' — by the sentence consisting of the two words 'mahān bhogaḥ' (great enjoyer) — 'of <s>Prāṇa</s>,' in the passage 'tadvai tvam': this is the construction. By this, the subject called <s>Prāṇa</s> [is indicated]. Since, by way of the objection that <s>Prāṇa</s> is other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>ānandamayatva</s> (the status of being bliss-made) would also pertain to another — the connection of this [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] with the <s>Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa</s> is by way of objection (<s>ākṣepikī</s>). The doubt — whether He is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) or <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is also indicated.
And that <s>Prāṇa</s>, because of [the word's] well-known usage, prima facie appears to be <s>Vāyu</s> (wind).
Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.9, verse 3:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.9.3:
sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣaṃ darśayati - sa ceti // tacchabda āvartate / caśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / vāyurityanena sambadhyate / ānandamayaśceti samuccaye vā / tathā ca paramānandatvaṃ yasya prāṇasyoktaṃ saḥ 'prāṇaḥ'; tacchabdavācyo mukhyavāyureveti 'āpatati'; prāpnoti / ata evānandamayo 'pi sa evetyāpatati / kutaḥ? prasiddheḥ prāṇaśruteḥ tasyāśca tasminvāyau prasiddhe rūḍhatvāt / prāṇapadapravṛttinimittasya jīvanāḍihetutvasya ca śarīre sati mukhye jīvanādikaṃ sambhavati nāsatītyanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ svaśarīragatavāyuvikāradvārā mukhyavāyāveva prasiddherdarśanāditi yojanā /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.9, verse 3:
He shows the prima facie view with reasoning: 'sa ca' (and that). The word 'tat' (that) carries forward. The word 'ca' is for emphasis. It connects with '<s>vāyuḥ</s>' (wind). Or, the word 'ca' is for aggregation with <s>Ānandamaya</s>. And thus, that '<s>Prāṇa</s>' — the entity denoted by the word 'tat' — whose supreme blissfulness is stated, is the chief <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) alone — 'prima facie appears to be' — is obtained [as the meaning]. Therefore, <s>Ānandamaya</s> too is that [<s>Vāyu</s>] alone — this prima facie appears. Why? Because of well-known usage — because the <s>Śruti</s> [using the word] '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is well-known, i.e., established (<s>rūḍha</s>), as referring to that <s>Vāyu</s>. Since the ground for the operation of the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' — being the cause of the vital functions — is such that when the chief [vital breath] is present in the body, vital functions and the like are possible but not when it is absent — [this is established] through positive and negative concomitance, by observing [the word's] well-known usage as referring to <s>Vāyu</s> — the modification of <s>Vāyu</s> within one's own body: this is the construction.

ahorātre pārśve'; (tai.ā. 3-13.) ityāditalliṅgādeva //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.9.4:
siddhāntayati - na ceti // evaṃ prāṇasya vāyutvaṃ ānandamayatvaṃ ca na yuktamityarthaḥ / kuto
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.9, verse 4:
He gives the established conclusion: 'na ca' (but not so). Thus: it is not proper that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Vāyu</s> and that <s>Ānandamaya</s> is also [<s>Vāyu</s>]: this is the meaning. Why

children.text: naivamityāśaṅkāyāṃ tatra hetutayā sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - yata iti / sūtrārthasya hetutvadyotako 'yaṃ yataśśabdaḥ / sūtre 'nuvṛttasya tattvityasyārtho viṣṇureveti / tathā ca yato 'yaṃ prāṇo viṣṇoreva ato naivamityanvayaḥ / kuto 'yaṃ prāṇo viṣṇurevetyataḥ sautraṃ hetumanūdya vyācaṣṭe - ata eveti / ityādīti / ityādinoktaṃ yadviṣṇuliṅgaṃ tasmādevetyarthaḥ / kathaṃ śrutyā pūrvapakṣite liṅgena nirṇaya ityato liṅgasya niravakāśatvajñāpanāyaivakāraḥ / tathā ca sāvakāśaśruterniravakāśaliṅgena bādha iti bhāvaḥ / he viṣṇo 'te'; tava śrīśca lakṣmīśceti dve patnyau staḥ / vakṣasthalāśritā śrīḥ aṅkasthitā lakṣmīriti sampradāyavidaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - aṅkasthitā śrīḥ vakṣasi lakṣmabhūtā lakṣmīrityuktam/ 'ahorātre'; tadabhimānisūryacandrau 'pārśve'; pārśvasthitāvityarthaḥ / divārātramete pārśvagate iti vā / yadyapīdam 'adbhyaḥ'; iti pūrvānuvākagatam / 'tadvai tvaṃ prāṇaḥ'; ityetacca 'bhartā san bhriyamāṇaḥ'; ityuttarānuvākagatam / tathā ca nānayorliṅgaliṅgibhāvo yujyate / tathāpi 'śrīśca te'; iti yuṣmacchabdenoktasya 'tadvai tvaṃ prāṇaḥ'; ityatrāpi yuṣmacchabdena pratyabhijñānāttadupapattiḥ / niravakāśatvādbhinnānuvākasthasyāpi mukhato grahaṇaṃ yuktam / ādiśabdena 'hariṃ harantamanuyanti devāḥ / viśvasyeśānaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ matīnām'; (tai.ā. 3-15.) iti tattvapradīpodāhṛtamanuvākāntarasthaṃ gṛhyate / sarvabuddhiniyantāraṃ jagatpatiṃ sarvasaṃhartāraṃ hariṃ devāḥ anugacchantītyarthaḥ / candrikāyāṃ tu - 'bhartā san'; ityuttarānuvākagataṃ 'tamevamṛtyumamṛtantamāhustaṃ bhartāraṃ tamugoptāramāhuḥ'; (tai.ā. 3-14.) ityādikamādipadena grāhyamityuktam / yadyapi taittirīyaśākhāyāṃ 'hrīścate'; iti pāṭhaḥ / tathāpi vājasaneyaśākhābhiprāyeṇa evamudāhṛtamiti dhyeyam / sūtrārtastu spaṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: is it 'not so'? — in response to this anticipation, he explains the <s>sūtra</s> as the reason: 'yataḥ' (because). This word 'yataḥ' illuminates the reason-hood of the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. The meaning of 'tat' (that) carried forward in the <s>sūtra</s> is: <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. And thus, because this <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, therefore 'it is not so': this is the syntactic connection. Why is this <s>Prāṇa</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone? — to this, echoing the reason from the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains: 'ata eva' (for the same reason). 'Ityādi' (and the like) — from the mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s> stated by 'and the like' and the preceding: this is the meaning. How is the determination through a mark when the prima facie view is established through <s>Śruti</s>? — to this, the word 'eva' is for the purpose of making known that the mark has exclusive scope. And thus: the <s>Śruti</s> that has scope [elsewhere] is sublated by the mark that has no scope [elsewhere]: this is the import. O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'Your' — <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s> — these two are Your consorts. Those who know the tradition [say]: <s>Śrī</s> is the one residing on the chest; <s>Lakṣmī</s> is the one seated on the lap. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, it is said: '<s>Śrī</s> is the one seated on the lap; <s>Lakṣmī</s> is the one who has become the beauty on the chest.' 'Day and night' — the Sun and Moon, who are the presiding deities of those — are 'the sides,' i.e., positioned at [His] sides: this is the meaning. Or: day and night are on either side of Him. Although this [passage] belongs to the preceding <s>anuvāka</s> [beginning with] 'from the waters,' and 'tadvai tvaṃ prāṇaḥ' belongs to the subsequent <s>anuvāka</s> [beginning with] 'the supporter being supported,' and therefore the mark-and-marked relationship between them is not justified — nevertheless, since the person addressed by the pronoun 'te' (Your) in '<s>Śrī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s> are Yours' is recognized by the pronoun 'tvam' (You) in 'that, indeed, You are <s>Prāṇa</s>' — the justification of that [connection is established]. Because of exclusive scope, the primary acceptance even of what is in a different <s>anuvāka</s> is justified. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the passage cited in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> — situated in another <s>anuvāka</s> — is included: 'The gods follow <s>Hari</s> who carries [all] away; the lord of the universe, the bull among intellects' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.15). The meaning is: the gods follow <s>Hari</s>, who destroys all, who is the lord of the world, the sovereign of all intellects. In the <s>Candrikā</s>, however, it is said: from the subsequent <s>anuvāka</s> [beginning with] 'the supporter being,' the passage 'they call Him death, they call Him immortal, they call Him the supporter, they call Him the protector' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.14) and the like should be included by the word 'ādi.' Although in the <s>Taittirīya</s> branch the reading is 'hrīśca te' (modesty is Yours), nevertheless, it should be understood that this is cited with the intention of the <s>Vājasaneya</s> branch. The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is clear.
// Thus ends the <s>Prāṇādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of vital breath). // 9 //
// 10. The <s>Jyotiradhikaraṇa</s> (topic of light). //

Bhāṣya on Brahmasūtra 1.1.10, verse 1:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.10.1:
atrādhikaraṇe tattatsūktagatāśeṣaśabdopalakṣakasya lokato 'nyatraprasiddhasya jyotirnāmno brahmaṇi samanvayaḥ kriyate / pūrvādhikaraṇatadviṣayasaṅgatī viṣayavākyodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ viṣayasaṃśayau ca darśayati - yo vedeti // tataḥ kimityata āha - tacceti / co 'vadhāraṇe / tathā ca yatpūrvaṃ māntravarṇikapadopāttamantravarṇagatena 'yo veda'; iti vākyena guhānihitaṃ vastūktaṃ tadevānandamayādyākhyamityuktam / tadeva 'vime karṇā'; iti vākye 'jyotiruktaṃ'
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.1.10, verse 1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the coherence (<s>samanvaya</s>) of the name '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) — which is well-known elsewhere than in the [present] context as indicative of all words occurring in the respective hymns, pertaining to the individual self — in <s>Brahman</s> is established. He shows the connections with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> and its subject, the subject-passage with its citation, the subject and the doubt: 'yo veda' (he who knows). Then what? — to this he says: 'tat ca' (and that). The word 'ca' is for emphasis. And thus, what was stated earlier by the <s>Mantra</s>-portion-sourced word in the sentence 'he who knows' as the entity hidden in the cave — that alone has been said to be designated as <s>Ānandamaya</s> and the like. That very thing is stated as '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) in the passage 'vi me karṇā' (my ears fly open) —

children.text: jyotiśśabdenoktamityarthaḥ/ anena vakṣyamāṇapūrvapakṣaparyālocanayā jyotiṣo viṣṇvanyatvasādhanamukhenānandamayatvasyānyaniṣṭhatvākṣepādānandamayādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ sūcitā bhavati / jyotirviṣayaḥ kimagniruta viṣṇuriti sandehaśca sūcito bhavati / 'vi me'; iti ṛṅmantre vītyupasargāṇāṃ kriyāpadenānvayaḥ / tatra
children.translated_text: that is, stated by the word '<s>jyotis</s>': this is the meaning. By this, through the consideration of the forthcoming prima facie view, since through establishing that <s>jyotis</s> is other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the <s>Ānandamayatva</s> would also pertain to another — the connection of this [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] with the <s>Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa</s> is by way of objection (<s>ākṣepikī</s>): this is indicated. The doubt — whether [the light] is fire (<s>agni</s>) or <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is also indicated. In the <s>Ṛg</s> <s>mantra</s> 'vi me,' the prefixes 'vi' connect with the verbal word. Therein

children.text: dhātoreva vicaraṇābhidhāyakatvam / upasargāstu dyotakāḥ na vācakāḥ / ata eva sūtre caraṇābhidhānāt ityevoktam/ bhāṣye tu 'vicaraṇābhidhānāt'; iti spaṣṭārthamuktam / ata eva tattvapradīpe 'spaṣṭatvāya vicaraṇābhidhānāt ityuktam'; ityuktam/ 'me'; ityasmacchabdena mantradraṣṭā ṛṣirucyate / 'dūra ādhīḥ'; ityasya ekapadatve 'pi avagrahadarśanena dvikhaṇḍatvādvibhajyānvayaḥ / āṅ īṣadabhivyāptyubhayārthakaḥ / vartata iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca yato me karṇau jyotiṣo viruddhaṃ patayataḥ patataḥ / svārthe ṇic / cakṣuśca viruddhaṃ patatīti vipariṇāmenānvayaḥ / yathā karṇāderjyotirvidūratvaṃ evaṃ jyotiṣo 'pi karṇādividūratvamityāha - vīdamiti / kampo 'tyantamityarthe / tathā ca yadidaṃ hṛdaye 'āhitam'; ā samantāt sthitaṃ jyotistadatyantaṃ karṇādiviruddhaṃ vartate / evaṃ me manaḥ jyotiṣo dūre vicarati atīva taddarśanaviruddhaṃ vartate / manaścaraṇasya tattvaniṣṭhāvirodhitvaṃ 'cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa'; iti gītāyāmuktam / ataḥ kāraṇāt 'ādhīḥ'; īṣadbuddhirahaṃ vyāptabuddhirapīti vā 'kiṃ svit'; kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi / kimu kiṃ vā nu idānīṃ 'maniṣye'; cintayāmīti mantrārthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - ā samantāddūrasthabuddhirahamityekānvayena vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: The verbal root itself has the capacity to denote wandering (<s>vicaraṇa</s>). The prefixes, however, are illuminators, not denotators. Hence in the <s>sūtra</s>, only '<s>caraṇābhidhānāt</s>' (because of the statement of wandering) is said. In the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, however, '<s>vicaraṇābhidhānāt</s>' (because of the statement of wandering about) is said, making the meaning explicit. Hence in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> too, it is said: 'for the sake of clarity, <s>vicaraṇābhidhānāt</s> is said.' By the word '<s>me</s>' (my) — by this pronoun — the seer of the <s>mantra</s>, the <s>ṛṣi</s>, is denoted. '<s>Dūra ādhīḥ</s>' — even though this is a single word, because of being seen with a hyphen (<s>avagraha</s>), it is in two parts and therefore the syntactic connection is made by splitting [it]. The prefix '<s>ā</s>' has both meanings: slight, and pervasion. 'It occurs' is the remainder. And thus: since my ears 'fall away' (<s>patayataḥ</s>) — fall — in a manner contrary to the light; the causative is reflexive. And my eye also falls in a manner contrary [to the light] — the construction is by transposition. Just as the light is distant from the ears and the like, so the ears and the like are also distant from the light — this he says: '<s>vīdam</s>' (this). '<s>Kampa</s>' (trembling) is in the sense of 'exceedingly.' And thus: this light that is 'placed' (<s>āhitam</s>) — situated on all sides — in the heart, exceedingly operates in a manner contrary to the ears and the like. Similarly, my mind wanders far from the light — it operates exceedingly contrary to the vision of that [light]. That the wandering of the mind is not contradictory to devotion to truth is stated in the <s>Gītā</s>: 'For the mind is restless, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' For this reason, '<s>ādhīḥ</s>' — I who am of slight understanding, or of pervading understanding — 'what indeed' (<s>kiṃ svit</s>) — what shall I say? What indeed or what else shall I 'think' (<s>maniṣye</s>) — shall I contemplate now: this is the meaning of the <s>mantra</s>. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, it is explained in a single construction: 'I whose understanding is situated far on all sides.'
And that light — since [the hymn] is an <s>Agni</s>-hymn, and because of common usage — the prima facie conclusion is that it is fire (<s>Agni</s>) alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.10.2:
atha sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣayati - tacceti / cassamuccaye / taditi cāvartate / agniśabdo bhūtataddevatāparaḥ/ dvitīyacaśabdo bhinnakramaḥ / tathā ca tajjyotirguhānihitaṃ cāgnireva bhavediti prāptaṃ, kutaḥ? 'prasiddheḥ'; jyotiśśrutestasyāśca tasminnagnāveva prasiddheḥ rūḍhatvāt / na kevalaṃ śruterevedaṃ jyotiragniḥ, kintu tasya jyotiṣaḥ 'agnisūktatvāt'; agniprakaraṇagatatvācceti yojanā / ata eva pūrvapakṣopasaṃhāraṭīkāyāṃ śrutiprakaraṇayorbalavatvāditi prasiddhapadalakṣitāyāḥ śruteḥ prathamamuktiḥ / ata eva candrikāyāṃ bhāṣye agnisūktasthatvācceti caśabdaprayogādityuktam / tathā ca śrutiprakaraṇābhyāṃ guhānihitatvaliṅgamātrasya bādhāt agnirevedaṃ jyotirguhānihitaṃ ceti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.10.2: Now he presents the prima facie view with reason: '<s>tat ca</s>' (and that). The word 'ca' is for aggregation. The word 'tat' (that) also recurs. The word '<s>Agni</s>' refers to both the element and its presiding deity. The second 'ca' is in a different sequential order. And thus: that light, and also what is situated in the cave [of the heart] — would be fire alone: this is the prima facie conclusion. Whence? 'Because of common usage' (<s>prasiddheḥ</s>) — because of the <s>Śruti</s> [passage about] light, and because that [<s>Śruti</s>] is well-known (<s>rūḍha</s>) as referring to fire alone. Not only from <s>Śruti</s> is this light fire, but also 'because of being in an <s>Agni</s>-hymn' (<s>agnisūkatvāt</s>) — because of occurring in the context of fire: this is the construction. Hence in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> on the prima facie conclusion, it is said: 'because of the greater strength of <s>Śruti</s> and context.' Therefore the <s>Śruti</s>, indicated by the word '<s>prasiddha</s>' (well-known), is stated first. Hence in the <s>Candrikā</s> it is said: 'In the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, from the use of the word "ca" in "<s>agnisūktatvāt ca</s>"...' And thus: because of the overriding force of <s>Śruti</s> and context over the mere inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of being situated in the cave, this light — and what is situated in the cave — is fire alone: this is the purport.
Therefore he says —
The light — because of the statement of wandering. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.24 |
<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the light, because of the statement of the wandering of the ears and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.10.3:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti // yataḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ prāpto 'taḥ uttaraṃ sūtramāha bhagavānbādarāyaṇa ityarthaḥ / tadeva sūtraṃ paṭhati jyotiriti / sūtre tattvityasya anuvṛttiṃ vipariṇāmaṃ cābhipretya pratijñāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - viṣṇureveti / 'jyotiḥ'; tacchabdavācyo viṣṇureva bhavediti yojanā / kuta ityataḥ prāptaṃ 'caraṇābhidhānāt'; iti hetvaṃśaṃ caraṇaśabdasya vicaraṇārthatvaṃ karṇādīnāmityasya adhyāhāraṃ cābhipretya vyācaṣṭe - karṇādīnāmiti / atra vākye karṇādīnāmetajjyotiḥprati viruddhacaraṇokteḥ karṇādividūratvaliṅgaśravaṇādityarthaḥ / atra karṇādividūratvaṃ nāma tairiyaditi paricchedāyogyavaibhavatvaṃ, na tu karṇādividūratvamātram / tadviṣaye tasyāsambhavāt / abhidhānaparyantadhāvanaṃ hetvasiddhiparihārāyeti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.10.3: He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the conclusion: 'therefore' (<s>ataḥ</s>). // Since the prima facie view has arisen, therefore the venerable <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> states the responsive <s>sūtra</s>: this is the meaning. He reads that very <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' (light). Intending the continuation and modification of the word 'tat' (that) in the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains the thesis-portion: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' 'The light' — the one denoted by the word '<s>tat</s>' (that) is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone: this is the construction. Whence? — intending the reason-portion '<s>caraṇābhidhānāt</s>' (because of the statement of wandering), [and intending] the meaning of the word '<s>caraṇa</s>' as '<s>vicaraṇa</s>' (wandering), and the supplying of 'of the ears and the like' — he explains: 'of the ears and the like.' Here, in this sentence, the meaning is: because of the statement of the contrary wandering of the ears and the like with respect to this light — because of hearing the inferential mark of remoteness from the ears and the like. Here, 'remoteness from the ears and the like' means the magnitude (<s>vaibhava</s>) that cannot be delimited by them; not mere remoteness from the ears and the like, since that [mere remoteness] is impossible regarding [the object] in that [context]. That the [argument] extends all the way to 'statement' (<s>abhidhāna</s>) should be understood as being for the purpose of resolving the non-establishment of the reason.

children.text:
sa hi 'paro mātrayā tanvā vṛdhāna'; (ṛ. 7-99-1.)
ityādinā karṇādividūraḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: For He indeed, 'surpassing [all] in measure, growing through His own body' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 7.99.1) — by such [passages], [He is known to be] remote from the ears and the like. // 10 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.10.4:
nanvastu jyotiṣaḥ karṇādividūratvoktiḥ, tāvatā tasya viṣṇutvaṃ kuta ityataḥ karṇādividūratvasya viṣṇvekaliṅgatve śrutimudāharan tatpratijānīte - sa hīti // evetyanuṣajyate / ādiśabdena 'na te viṣṇo'; ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / tathā ca 'hi'; yasmāt 'saḥ'; viṣṇureva 'paro mātrayā'; ityādivākyena karṇādividūra iti pramitaḥ tasmānnāprayojakatā, na vā hetuviśeṣaṇāsiddhirityadhyāhāreṇa yojanā / anena 'jyotiḥ'; tacchabdavācyaṃ brahmaiva / kutaḥ? atra karṇādīnāmetajjyotiḥ prati sākalyena tadaviṣayīkaraṇarūpaviruddha 'caraṇābhidhānāt'; karṇādividūratvaliṅgaśravaṇāt ittyāvṛttyadhyāhārābhyāṃ sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / māpayati jñāpayati viṣayāniti vā mīyante viṣayā aneneti vā mātrā indriyagaṇaḥ tayā tatastvaṃ 'paro'; dūro 'sīti he viṣṇo anyamahimnaḥ paramantaṃ sīmānaṃ te mahimānaṃ ko 'pi śrotrādinā nāpeti ca prakṛtānuguṇyena śrutirvyākhyeyā / atra tattvapradīpasannyāyaratnāvalīkārayoḥ jyotirityādicatussūcī ekamevāntarbhedādhikaraṇamityabhipretam / agnisūktacchāndogyagataviṣayavākyabhedādanayorbhedaḥ / ṭīkākṛtastujyotissūtramekamadhikaraṇaṃ 'chandaḥ'; ityāditrisūtrī adhikaraṇāntaramiti jñātavyam // 10 //
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.10.4: [Objection:] Let there be a statement of the remoteness of the light from the ears and the like; how does that establish its being <s>Viṣṇu</s>? — therefore, citing a <s>Śruti</s> to show that remoteness from the ears and the like is a mark exclusively of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he asserts that: '<s>sa hi</s>' (for He indeed). // The word 'eva' (alone) is carried forward. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), [the passage] 'na te viṣṇo' (not You, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>) and the like are included. And thus: 'for' (<s>hi</s>) — since 'He' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — is ascertained as 'remote from the ears and the like' by the passage '<s>paro mātrayā</s>' (surpassing in measure) and the like, therefore there is no purposelessness, nor non-establishment of the qualifying mark of the reason: this is the construction with the supplied [words]. By this, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated through recurrence and supplementation: 'the light' — what is denoted by the word 'tat' (that) — is <s>Brahman</s> alone. Whence? Here, because of the statement of the 'wandering' of the ears and the like — in a manner 'contrary' to this light — contrary in the sense of totally not being able to objectify it — [that is,] because of hearing the inferential mark of remoteness from the ears and the like. [The meaning of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> passage:] He measures (<s>māpayati</s>) — makes known — objects; or, objects are measured by Him — [thus] '<s>mātrā</s>' means the group of sense-organs; from those, and therefore you 'are surpassing' (<s>paraḥ</s>) — distant — O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; and no one 'approaches' (<s>ape</s>) — reaches — the ultimate limit (<s>param antam</s>) of your greatness — by any sense-organ: and [the passage] should be explained in conformity with the subject under discussion. Here, in the view of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, <s>Sannyāyaratnāvalī</s>, and the authors, the four <s>sūtras</s> beginning with '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' form a single inner <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic) with internal subdivisions. The difference between these [two views] is because of the difference between the subject-passage in the <s>Agni</s>-hymn and that in the <s>Chāndogya</s>. But it should be known that according to the <s>Ṭīkā</s>-author, the '<s>jyotis</s>'-<s>sūtra</s> forms one <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, while the three <s>sūtras</s> beginning with '<s>chandaḥ</s>' form another <s>adhikaraṇa</s>. // 10 //
// Thus ends the <s>Jyotiradhikaraṇa</s> (topic of light). // 10 //
// 11. The <s>Chandoʼbhidhānādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the designation as meter). //

children.text: chando 'bhidhānān neti cen na tathā ceto'rpaṇanigadāt tathā hi darśanam | BBs_1,1.25 |
children.translated_text: If [the objection be raised:] 'not [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], because of the designation as <s>chandas</s> (meter)' — [the answer is:] no, because of the statement (<s>nigada</s>) [being] for the dedication of the mind (<s>cetoʼrpaṇa</s>); for such is the teaching (<s>darśana</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.25 |

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.1:
atrādhikaraṇe adhivedagatagāyatryādyaśeṣaśabdasamanvayaḥ kriyate / saṅgatyādijijñāsājananāya sūtramevādau paṭhati - chanda iti // atra chanda ityāvartate / tacca vyastaṃ samastaṃ ca / tathā ca 'chando 'bhidhānāt'; 'gāyatrī vā idam'; iti vākyasthagāyatrīśabdena caturviṃśatyakṣaramantraviśeṣātmakachandasaḥ pratipādanāt, tacchabdasya tatra rūḍhatvāt, gāyatrīśabdavācyo na viṣṇuḥ, kintu chanda eva / yato gāyatrī na viṣṇuḥ, api tu chandaḥ, ato jyotirapi na viṣṇuḥ kintu chandaḥ / kutaḥ? 'chando 'bhidhānāt'; chandasā gāyatryā tadaikyābhiprāyeṇa jyotiṣo 'bhidhānāt upakramāditi cet - na, viṣṇureva jyotiḥ / kutaḥ? 'nigadāt'; gāyatrīpadena viṣṇorevābhidhānāt / gāyatryādipadairviṣṇorevābhidhānaṃ ca tadabhedavidhānārthaṃ kintu tathopāsanārthamevetyāha - tatheti / 'tathā'; gāyatryādiśabdārthaguṇasvarūpatvena 'cetaso'; manasaḥ 'arpaṇāya'; brahmaṇyādhānāyopāsanārthameva viṣṇornigadādityarthaḥ / upāsanetyanuktvā
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.1: In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the coherent interpretation (<s>samanvaya</s>) of all the words such as <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the like, belonging to the secondary <s>Veda</s>, is carried out. For the purpose of generating inquiry into the connection and the like, he first reads the <s>sūtra</s> itself: '<s>chandaḥ</s>' (meter). // Here, the word '<s>chandaḥ</s>' recurs. And that [recurrence] is both separately and collectively. And thus: 'because of the designation as <s>chandas</s>' — because, by the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' in the passage '<s>gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvam</s>' (the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this), a specific <s>chandas</s> (meter) consisting of a particular <s>mantra</s> of twenty-four syllables is taught, and because of the well-known usage (<s>rūḍhatva</s>) of the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' in that [meter], what is denoted by the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> but rather <s>chandas</s> (meter) alone. Since <s>Gāyatrī</s> is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> but rather <s>chandas</s>, therefore the light (<s>jyotis</s>) too is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> but rather <s>chandas</s>. Whence? 'Because of the designation as <s>chandas</s>' — because the light is designated by the <s>chandas</s> called <s>Gāyatrī</s>, with the intention of their identity, from the opening [of the passage] — if so, [the answer is:] no, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the light. Whence? 'Because of the statement (<s>nigada</s>)' — because of the designation of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone by the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>.' And the designation of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by words like <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the like is not for the purpose of establishing their non-difference, but rather for the purpose of meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) alone — this he says: '<s>tathā</s>' (thus). 'Thus' — as having the nature of the qualities and essential nature denoted by the words <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the like — 'of the mind' (<s>cetasaḥ</s>) — of the mental faculty — 'for the dedication' (<s>arpaṇāya</s>) — for the placing [of the mind] upon <s>Brahman</s>, that is, for the purpose of meditation alone, is <s>Viṣṇu</s> stated (<s>nigada</s>): this is the meaning. Instead of saying 'meditation' (<s>upāsana</s>),

children.text: cetorpaṇetyuktirupāsanāsvarūpakathanārthā / anena prasiddhagāyatryādipadena viṣṇorabhidhānaṃ vyarthamiti śaṅkā parihṛtā/ nanu bhavedgāyatrīśabdavācyatvena viṣṇorjyotiśśabdavācyatvasādhanam, yadi gāyatrīśabdavācyatvaṃ viṣṇoḥ pramitaṃ syāt / tadeva kuta ityata āha - tathā hīti / 'hi'; yasmāt 'tathā'; gānatrāṇakartṛtvanimittena viṣṇorgāyatrīśabdavācyatvasādhakaṃ 'darśanaṃ'; dṛśyate jñāyate 'rtho yayeti vyupattyā 'gāyati ca trāyati ca'; (śākhāntaram) ityādirūpā śrutirasti tasmāditi sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the expression 'dedication of the mind' (<s>cetoʼrpaṇa</s>) is for the purpose of stating the essential nature of meditation. By this, the doubt that the designation of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by the well-known word <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the like is purposeless is resolved. [Objection:] Let the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> denote <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and let that [fact] establish the denotability of the light by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s>; but only if the denotability of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> is ascertained [first]. Whence is that? — to this he says: '<s>tathā hi</s>' (for such is). 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since 'such' (<s>tathā</s>) — through the cause of His being the singer-and-protector (<s>gāna-trāṇa-kartṛtva</s>) — the '<s>darśana</s>' (teaching) that establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s denotability by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> — by the derivation 'that which sings and protects' — the <s>Śruti</s> in the form of 'it sings and it protects' (from another <s>Śākhā</s>) and the like — exists; therefore: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
'Now, the light that shines beyond heaven' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.13.7) —
of the light thus stated, the commencement is made with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [passage] '<s>gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvam</s>' (the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this) (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.1). //
— [This connects with the following passage.]

children.text:
tasmānna viṣṇuriti cet - na, tathā cetor'paṇārthaṃ hi nigadyate /
agnigāyatryādiśabdārtharūpo 'sāviti cetor'paṇārthaṃ hi nigadyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, if [the objection be:] 'it is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — [the answer is:] no, for [it is] stated (<s>nigadyate</s>) for the purpose of the dedication of the mind. He who has the nature of the meanings of words like <s>Agni</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the like — for the purpose of the dedication of the mind, [He is] indeed stated.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.2:
śrutyādisaṅgativiṣayavākyaviṣayasaṃśayapūrvapakṣatatphalāni sūcayan sūtre pūrvapakṣāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - atheti // uktasyetyāvartyate / tathā ca 'hṛdaya āhitaṃ yat'; iti guhānihitatvena yaduktaṃ tasyaiva 'jyotiṣaḥ'; punaḥ 'atha yadataḥ paro divo jyotirdīpyate viśvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu sarvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu anuttameṣūttameṣu lokeṣu / idaṃ vāva tadyadidamasminnantaḥpuruṣe jyotiḥ'; iti chāndogye 'pyuktasya 'gāyatryā'; itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇe tṛtīyā / gāyatrītvena tadrūpatayā 'samārambhaḥ'; pāṭhaḥ kṛtaḥ / kuto 'yaṃ vijñāyate? yato 'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ vāgvai gāyatrī vāgvā idaṃ sarvam'; iti vākye 'gāyatryā'; gāyatrīśabdena tadaikyatātparyeṇa 'samārambhaḥ'; upakramaḥ kṛtaḥ ata iti yojanā / tataḥ kimityata āha - tasmāditi/ idaṃ cāvartate / jyotirgāyatrīti ca śeṣaḥ / chanda iti cānuṣajyate / tathā ca yasmādgāyatryā samārambhaḥ kṛtaḥ, sa ca yasmādanupasañjātavirodhitvena balavān, tasmādidaṃ jyotirgāyatryeva bhavet / sā ca gāyatrī virṇasamāveśalakṣaṇamantrātmakachanda eva bhavet, na viṣṇuḥ / kutaḥ? tasmāt gāyatrīśabdasya chandasyeva rūḍhatvādvāktvābhidhānācceti yojanā / anena 'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvam'; iti pūrvavākyasthagāyatrīśabdasya viṣṇvanyaparatve tata evottaravākyasthajyotiṣo viṣṇvanyatvāpattyā tata eva agnisūktagatajyotiṣo 'pi tadanyatvameva bhavet / ata evānandamayatvamapi anyasyaiva bhavenna viṣṇoriti pūrvoktākṣepeṇa etadadhikaraṇotthānātpūrveṇāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ / evaṃ gāyatrī viṣayaḥ / kiṃ chandoviśeṣaḥ uta viṣṇuriti sandehaḥ / tathā gāyatrī chandoviśeṣa eva bhavet; tacchabdasya tatra rūḍhatvāditi sayuktikaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ / tathā tasmāt jyotirapi chanda eveti tasyaiva guhānihitatvamāndamayatvaṃ ceti pūrvapakṣaphalaṃ ca sūcitaṃ bhavati / atra pūrvapakṣe gāyatryādiśabdāḥ mantraparāḥ, sarvamapi vākyaṃ tanmāhātmyaparatayā yojanīyam/ siddhānte tu 'atha'; ityāderayamarthaḥ - bhagavanmāhātmyāntarārambhe 'thaśabdaḥ 'yat'; śvetadvīpānantāsanavaikuṇṭhagataṃ nārāyaṇavāsudevavaikuṇṭhākhyaṃ rūpatrayaṃ tat 'ataḥ'; etasmādvivakṣitādbuddhisthāt 'divaḥ paraḥ'; paraṃ tadapekṣayoccasthānasthitamityarthaḥ / 'jyotiḥ'; tejomayaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ tat 'viśvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu'
children.translated_text: BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.2: Indicating the <s>Śruti</s> [passages], connection, subject-passage, subject, doubt, prima facie view, and their results, he explains the prima facie portion of the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>atha</s>' (now). // 'Of what was stated' is carried forward. And thus, of the very [light] that was stated as 'situated in the heart' by [the phrase] 'that which is placed in the heart,' of that very 'light,' again — [it is also described in] the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage 'Now, that light which shines beyond heaven, on the backs of all, on the backs of everything, in the unsurpassed worlds, the highest — this is indeed the same as the light within a person' — of the light thus 'stated,' 'with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>' — the third case is in the sense of <s>itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇa</s> (characterization by such nature) — as <s>Gāyatrī</s>, in that form, the 'commencement' — the reading — 'is made.' Whence is this known? Because in the passage '<s>gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ vāgvai gāyatrī vāgvā idaṃ sarvam</s>' (the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this; speech is indeed <s>Gāyatrī</s>; speech is indeed all this), 'with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>' — by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s>, with the intention of their identity, the 'commencement' — the beginning — is made; therefore: this is the construction. What follows from that? — to this he says: '<s>tasmāt</s>' (therefore). 'This [light]' is carried forward. 'The light is [a] <s>Gāyatrī</s>' is also the remainder. And the word '<s>chandas</s>' also is carried forward. And thus: since the commencement is made with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and since that [commencement] is strong because of being an unopposed [opening], therefore this light would be <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone. And that <s>Gāyatrī</s> would be the <s>chandas</s> alone — consisting of a <s>mantra</s> characterized by the combination of syllables — and not <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Whence? Therefore — because of the well-known usage (<s>rūḍhatva</s>) of the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> in <s>chandas</s> alone, that is, because of designation through speech: this is the construction. By this, since the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> in the preceding passage [refers to something] other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, from that very [precedent], the light in the subsequent passage would also be other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and from that the light in the <s>Agni</s>-hymn too would be other than that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>]. Hence, the <s>Ānandamaya</s>-hood too would belong to another and not to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — since this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> arises through the previously stated objection, its connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) with the preceding is through objection. Thus, <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the subject. [The doubt is:] is it a specific <s>chandas</s> or <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Thus <s>Gāyatrī</s> would be a specific <s>chandas</s> alone, because of the well-known usage of the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> in that: this is the prima facie view with reason. Thus, therefore the light too is <s>chandas</s> alone, and therefore the status of being hidden in the cave and the status of being <s>Ānandamaya</s> also belong to that very [chandas] — this is also indicated as the result of the prima facie view. Here, in the prima facie view, the words <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the like refer to <s>mantras</s>; the entire passage is to be construed as pertaining to their greatness. In the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), however, the meaning of '<s>atha</s>' and the rest is as follows: the word '<s>atha</s>' is at the commencement of another [topic of] the Lord's greatness. 'That which' (<s>yat</s>) — the three forms called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, situated in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, on the throne of <s>Ananta</s>, and in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — that — 'beyond this' (<s>ataḥ</s>) — from this intended [light] established in the mind — 'beyond heaven' (<s>divaḥ paraḥ</s>) — situated in a higher place relative to that: this is the meaning. 'Light' (<s>jyotiḥ</s>) — radiant, of such nature — that — 'on the backs of all' (<s>viśvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu</s>) —
On earth, <s>Brahman's</s> [abode is] on <s>Meru</s>; in the atmosphere, <s>Vaijayanta</s>;

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ satyaloke ca sadanaṃ trividhaṃ matam //
children.translated_text: The third [abode] is in <s>Satyaloka</s> — thus the threefold dwelling is understood.

children.text: iti vacanādantarikṣagavaijayantamerusatyalokagatebhyo brahmasadanebhyaḥ krameṇocceṣu 'sarvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu'; antarikṣapṛthivīsvarātmakalokebhyaḥ krameṇocceṣu 'anuttameṣu'; na vidyate uttamo loko yebhyasteṣu pratyavareṣviti vā / 'uttameṣu'; svayamevottameṣu 'lokeṣu'; śvetadvīpānantāsanavaikuṇṭheṣu 'dīpyate'; prakāśate
children.translated_text: Based on this statement, from the abodes of <s>Brahman</s> situated in the atmosphere at <s>Vaijayanta</s>, on <s>Meru</s>, and in <s>Satyaloka</s>, progressively higher in order — 'in all the highest [abodes]' (<s>sarvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu</s>); in the atmospheric, earthly, and self-sovereign worlds progressively higher — 'in the unsurpassed' (<s>anuttameṣu</s>); meaning those beyond which no higher world exists, or in the lower ones. 'In the highest' (<s>uttameṣu</s>) — in those that are themselves the highest. 'In the worlds' (<s>lokeṣu</s>) — in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, <s>Anantāsana</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>. 'It shines' (<s>dīpyate</s>) — it is luminous.

children.text: 'tat'; dīpyamānaṃ tejaḥ 'idaṃ vāva'; idaṃ khalu/ idaṃ ca kim? 'yadidamasmin puruṣe'; hṛdaye 'antarjyotiḥ'; tacchabditaṃ brahmāsti tattenaikībhūtamityarthaḥ / yo gāyatrīnāmā gāyatrīsaṃsthaḥ strīrūpo hayaśīrṣākhyo bhagavān tadidaṃ prathamaṃ rūpamityāśayena tasya dvitīyaṃ rūpaṃ vaktuṃ gāyatrītyādivākyaṃ pravṛttam / 'yadidaṃ kiñca bhūtaṃ'; pūrṇaṃ matsyādyavatārarūpaṃ yacca 'sarvaṃ'; sarvāntaḥsthitaṃ rūpaṃ tatsarvaṃ 'gāyatrī'; gāyatrīnāmā bhagavāneva / vai prasiddham / tasyaiva tṛtīyaṃ rūpamāha - vāgiti / gāyatrīnāmā bhagavān 'vāgvai'; vāṅnāmako viṣṇureva / kuto 'sya viṣṇutvamityatastallakṣaṇayogādityāha - vāgvā iti / 'idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ'; prāṇijātaṃ 'vāgvai'; vāṅnāmakabhagavadadhīnameva / ataḥ sarvasvāmitvādvāco viṣṇutvamiti / siddhāntasūtrāṃśamanukaroti - neti / nigadyata ityatrāpi sambadhyate / tathā ca jyotiḥśabdena viṣṇureva nigadyata ityarthaḥ / kuta ityato nigadāditi hetuṃ yojayati - hi nigadyata iti / gāyatrīśabdeneti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca 'hi'; yasmādgāyatrīśabdenāpi viṣṇureva 'nigadyate'; abhīdhīyate tasmādityarthaḥ / viṣṇorgāyatryādiśabdairabhidhānaṃ ca na tadabhedavidhānārthaṃ, kintu tathopāsanārthamevetyāha - tatheti / ceto 'rpaṇetyuktiprayojanaṃ pūrvavat / bhāṣyatvajñāpanāya tathetyādisvapadāni tathāśabdārthakathanena vivṛṇoti - agnīti / atra jyotiśśabdopalakṣakāgnipadaṃ jyotissūtrasya bhinnādhikaraṇatvapakṣe anyatra prasiddhasya gāyatrīpadasya viṣṇau prayoge prayojanamatra vadatā sūtrakṛtā pūrvatrottaratra cāgnyādipadasya viṣṇau prayoge prayojanaṃ sūcitamiti darśayitum / na ca gāyatryādipadābhyāmeva gāyatrīpadasamanvayaphalasya pūrvatrottaratra coktasamanvayaphalasya ca sūcanasambhavādagnipadaṃ vyarthamiti vācyam / phalībhūtasamanvayaviṣayatvenāsyāpi avaśyopādeyatvāt / samānaprakaraṇasthavāgādigrāhakatvena ādiśabdasyāpyāvaśyakatvāt / avaśyāpekṣitābhyāmubhābhyāmapyānandamayādyadhikaraṇeṣu uttaratra coktaprayojanasyāpi sūcanasambhavādubhayamapyāvaśyakam / jyotirityādicatuḥsūtryā ekādhikaraṇatvapakṣe tu sākṣātsamanvetavyapaśabdatvenaiva śabdadvayopādānaṃ, na tu phalatvenāgniśabdasyādhikaraṇāntare 'pyetannyāyasūcanaṃ tu ādiśabdenaiva, na tūbhābhyām / bhinnajātīyānekaśabdagrahaṇārthaṃ śabdadvayottarādipadam / ata eva tattvapradīpe ādiśabdasyobhayatrānvayaṃ prathamādiśabdena tejaḥśabdānāṃ dvitīyena chandaśśabdānāṃ ca grahaṇamabhipretya 'agnyāditejaḥśabdānāṃ gāyatryādichandaśśabdānāṃ ca'; ityuktam/ kecittu bhāṣyagatahiśabdo jñānārthamatha dhyānārthamiti pramāṇaprasiddhidyotakaḥ, adhikaraṇāntare 'pyasya nyāyasyānusandheyatvajñāpakaścetyāhuḥ / ceto 'rpaṇārthamiti sāvadhāraṇam / tathā ca 'asau'; bhagavānagnigāyatryādiśabdairagnigāyatryādiśabdārthaguṇasvarūpa iti / tatra 'ceto 'rpaṇārthaṃ'; budhyavatāraṇārtham upāsanārthameva nigadyate, na tadabhedavidhānārthamityarthaḥ / itītyantena tathāśabdārtha uktaḥ/ anenāprasiddhagāyatryādipadena viṣṇorabhidhānasya vaiyarthyaśaṅkā parihṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'That' (<s>tat</s>) — that shining radiance. 'This indeed' (<s>idaṃ vāva</s>) — this verily. And what is this? 'That which is this inner light in this person' (<s>yadidamasmin puruṣe antarjyotiḥ</s>) — in the heart; the meaning is that <s>Brahman</s> denoted by 'that' has become one with it. The <s>Bhagavān</s> who bears the name <s>Gāyatrī</s>, who is established in <s>Gāyatrī</s>, who has a feminine form, known as <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> — with the intention that this is His first form, the passage beginning with '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' proceeds to state His second form. 'Whatever has come into being' (<s>yadidaṃ kiñca bhūtaṃ</s>) — the complete form of incarnations such as <s>Matsya</s> and others, and whatever 'all' (<s>sarvaṃ</s>) — the form dwelling within all — all that is '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' — is indeed <s>Bhagavān</s> bearing the name <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Vai</s> [indicates] this is well-known. He states His third form — '<s>Vāk</s>' (Speech). <s>Bhagavān</s> bearing the name <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed '<s>Vāk</s>' (<s>vāgvai</s>) — <s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself bearing the name <s>Vāk</s>. To the question 'why is He <s>Viṣṇu</s>?' — it is because He possesses the characteristics of that, as stated — '<s>vāgvā</s>.' 'All this that has come into being' (<s>idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ</s>) — the entire community of living beings — is indeed dependent upon '<s>Vāk</s>' (<s>vāgvai</s>) — upon <s>Bhagavān</s> bearing the name <s>Vāk</s>. Therefore, because of His sovereignty over all, <s>Vāk</s> has the nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. He paraphrases the portion of the established-doctrine <s>sūtra</s> — 'na' (not). This connects also with 'is declared' (<s>nigadyate</s>). Thus the meaning is: by the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light), <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is declared. To the question 'why?', he connects the reason 'because it is declared' (<s>nigadāt</s>) — 'indeed it is declared' (<s>hi nigadyate</s>). The completion is: 'by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s>.' And thus, 'because' (<s>hi</s>) — since by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> too, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone 'is declared' (<s>nigadyate</s>) — is denoted, therefore [the conclusion follows]. And the designation of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by words such as <s>Gāyatrī</s> and <s>Agni</s> is not for the purpose of establishing identity with them, but only for the purpose of such meditation — as stated with '<s>tathā</s>' (thus). The purpose of the statement '<s>cetorpaṇa</s>' (directing the mind) is as before. To indicate the <s>bhāṣya</s> nature, he explains his own words beginning with '<s>tathā</s>' by stating the meaning of the word '<s>tathā</s>' — '<s>Agni</s>' etc. Here, the word <s>Agni</s> is indicative of the word <s>jyotis</s>. On the view that the <s>jyotis</s>-<s>sūtra</s> belongs to a separate <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> stating the purpose of applying the well-known word <s>Gāyatrī</s> to <s>Viṣṇu</s> here, he shows that the purpose of applying words like <s>Agni</s> to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in earlier and later contexts is also indicated. And one should not say that the word <s>Agni</s> is purposeless since the result of the syntactic connection of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> word and the indication of the syntactic connection stated earlier and later could be achieved by the <s>Gāyatrī</s>-related words alone — because this [<s>Agni</s> word] too must necessarily be included as pertaining to the subject matter of the resultant syntactic connection. The word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) is also necessary as it encompasses <s>Vāk</s> and other terms within the same context. Since both of these necessarily required [words] can also indicate the purpose stated in later <s>adhikaraṇas</s> such as <s>Ānandamaya</s> and others, both are indeed necessary. On the view that the four <s>sūtras</s> beginning with '<s>jyotis</s>' form a single <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the two words are included precisely because they are words directly to be syntactically connected, not because the <s>Agni</s> word indicates this principle in another <s>adhikaraṇa</s> as a result — rather, the indication of this principle [in other <s>adhikaraṇas</s>] is through the word '<s>ādi</s>' alone, not through both. The word '<s>ādi</s>' following the two words serves to encompass multiple words of different categories. For this very reason, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, intending the connection of the word '<s>ādi</s>' in both places — the first '<s>ādi</s>' encompassing words denoting luminosity (<s>tejas</s>), and the second encompassing meter-words (<s>chandas</s>) — it is stated: 'of <s>Agni</s> and other luminosity-words, and of <s>Gāyatrī</s> and other meter-words.' Some, however, say that the word '<s>hi</s>' in the <s>bhāṣya</s> indicates well-known scriptural authority — whether for the purpose of knowledge or meditation — and also indicates that this principle should be applied in other <s>adhikaraṇas</s> as well. The statement '<s>cetorpaṇārtham</s>' (for the purpose of directing the mind) is emphatic. And thus, 'He' (<s>asau</s>) — <s>Bhagavān</s> has the qualities and essential nature denoted by the words <s>Agni</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, etc. In that context, 'for the purpose of directing the mind' (<s>cetorpaṇārtham</s>) — for the purpose of bringing it into the intellect, for the purpose of meditation alone He is declared, not for establishing identity — that is the meaning. By the word '<s>iti</s>' the meaning of the word '<s>tathā</s>' has been stated. By this, the objection of purposelessness in designating <s>Viṣṇu</s> by non-conventional words like <s>Gāyatrī</s> etc. has been resolved.

children.text: tathā hi darśanaṃ 'gāyati trāyati ca'; (chāṃ. 3-12-1.) ityādi /
children.translated_text: For thus there is the scriptural evidence: '<s>Gāyatrī</s> sings and protects' (<s>gāyati trāyati ca</s>) (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.1) and so on.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.3:
nanu bhavedgāyatryādiśabdavācyatvena viṣṇorjyotiśśabdavācyatāsādhanaṃ yadīyaṃ gāyatrī viṣṇuḥ syāttadeva kuta ityato gānatrāṇakartṛtvaliṅgādityāśayena tasyāsiddhiparihārāya pravṛttaṃ tathāhīti sūtraśeṣam
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.11.3:
Objection: The establishment of <s>Viṣṇu</s> as denoted by the word <s>jyotis</s> through His being denoted by words like <s>Gāyatrī</s> would be valid only if this <s>Gāyatrī</s> were indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>. To the question 'how is that established?' — with the intention that it is through the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of being the agent of singing and protecting, the remainder of the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with '<s>tathā hi</s>' (for thus) is presented to remove the charge of unestablishedness,

children.text: anukṛtya darśanapadoktāṃ śrutiṃ darśayati - tatheti // 'hi'; yasmāt 'ityādi darśanaṃ'; śrutirastītyanvayaḥ / yadyapi 'gāyati trāyate ca'; iti pāṭhaḥ chandogānam, tathāpi śākhāntaramevedamityadoṣaḥ / ādipadena 'yā vai sā gāyatrī iyaṃ vāva sā yeyaṃ pṛthivyasyāṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ pratiṣṭhitametāmeva nātiśīyate'; (chāṃ. 3-12.2.) ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / śrutyarthastu - yato gāyatrīvācyo bhagavān vedān 'gāyati'; mukhānnissārayati prathamo vakteti yāvat / yasmācca 'trāyate'; akhilamiti śeṣaḥ/ ato gāyatrīśabdenocyate / 'yā'; prasiddhā gāyatrī tannāmā viṣṇuḥ 'sā iyaṃ vai'; iyaṃ khalu / kimiyam? 'yeyaṃ pṛthivī'; tannāmā bhagavān / kathaṃ pṛthivī viṣṇurityataḥ tallakṣaṇayogādityāha - asyāṃ hīdamiti / 'asyāṃ'; pṛthivyāṃ 'bhūtaṃ'; prāṇijātamāśritamiti / sudhāyāṃ tu pūrvapakṣānuguṇatayā gāyatrī 'gāyati'; arthaṃ pratipādayati, adhyetṛn 'trāyate'; pālayati pāpāt rakṣatītyartha uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: and having paraphrased [the <s>sūtra</s>], he shows the <s>śruti</s> referred to by the word '<s>darśana</s>' (scriptural evidence) — with '<s>tathā</s>' (thus). 'Because' (<s>hi</s>) — since 'there is the following scriptural evidence' (<s>ityādi darśanaṃ</s>) — the syntactic connection is: because there exists such <s>śruti</s>. Although the reading '<s>gāyati trāyate ca</s>' belongs to the <s>Chandoga</s> [recension], still there is no fault, as this is from another <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic branch). By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the following is encompassed: 'That which is the well-known <s>Gāyatrī</s> — this is verily that, namely this earth; for upon it all this that has come into being is established, and it does not go beyond it' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.2) and so on. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is: Because <s>Bhagavān</s> denoted by <s>Gāyatrī</s> 'sings' (<s>gāyati</s>) — brings forth the <s>Vedas</s> from His mouth, meaning He is the first speaker; and because He 'protects' (<s>trāyate</s>) — the completion being: everything. Therefore He is called by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s>. 'That which' (<s>yā</s>) — the well-known <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> bearing that name — 'this is verily' (<s>sā iyaṃ vai</s>) — this indeed. What is this? 'This earth' (<s>yeyaṃ pṛthivī</s>) — <s>Bhagavān</s> bearing that name. To the question 'how is the earth <s>Viṣṇu</s>?' — it is because He possesses its characteristics, as stated: 'upon it indeed this' (<s>asyāṃ hīdam</s>). 'Upon it' (<s>asyāṃ</s>) — upon the earth, 'beings' (<s>bhūtaṃ</s>) — the community of living creatures is dependent. In the <s>Sudhā</s> [commentary], however, in accordance with the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view), the meaning given is: <s>Gāyatrī</s> 'teaches' (<s>gāyati</s>) the meaning, and 'protects' (<s>trāyate</s>) the students — guards and saves them from sin.
He is indeed designated by [the names of] all meters; He is indeed designated by [the names of] all gods;
He is indeed designated by [the names of] all worlds — and their [designation by those names] is by way of secondary attribution (<s>upacāra</s>) from Him.
Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Vāmana</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.4:
nanu gāyatryādiśabdasya anyatra rūḍhatvātkathaṃ liṅgamātreṇa viṣṇutvaniścaya ityato gāyatryādiśruteḥ sāvakāśatvāditi bhāvena gāyatryagnipṛthivyādiśabdāḥ na kevalaṃ śrutyuktayogena viṣṇau sāvakāśāḥ, api tu paurāṇikarūḍhyā gāyatryāḥ bhagavadadhīnatvādapītyāśayena tatra smṛtimāha - sarveti / 'eṣaḥ'; viṣṇuḥ 'sarvachando 'bhidhaḥ'; sarvachandasām abhidhevābhidhā yasyeti bahuvrīhiḥ / chandovācakagāyatryādisarvaśabdavācyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.11.4:
Objection: Since words like <s>Gāyatrī</s> are conventionally established (<s>rūḍha</s>) elsewhere, how can the determination that [she is] <s>Viṣṇu</s> be made merely through an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>)? To this, with the purport that the <s>Gāyatrī</s>-<s>śruti</s> and similar passages have scope [for application to <s>Viṣṇu</s>] — meaning that the words <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Pṛthivī</s>, etc. are applicable to <s>Viṣṇu</s> not only through the etymological connection stated in <s>śruti</s>, but also through conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, since <s>Gāyatrī</s> and others are dependent on <s>Bhagavān</s> — with this intention, he cites a <s>smṛti</s> passage: '<s>sarva</s>' (all). 'This one' (<s>eṣaḥ</s>) — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is 'designated by all meters' (<s>sarvachandobhidhaḥ</s>); this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: He for whom the designation of all meters is His designation — meaning He is denoted by all words that denote meters, such as <s>Gāyatrī</s> and others.

children.text: 'evamasau'; viṣṇuḥ sarvadevatāvācakāgnyādiśabdavācyaḥ / tathā 'eṣaḥ'; viṣṇuḥ sarvalokavācakapṛthivyādiśabdavācya ityarthaḥ / kuta ityataḥ chanda ādīnāṃ bhagavadadhīnatvāditi pratyekaṃ hetutrayasūcanāya hiśabdatrayaṃ, vedaprasiddhijñāpānāya vā / chandasāṃ lokānāṃ ca pratyakṣatvāt devānāṃ ca parokṣatvādeṣo 'sāviti vicitroktiḥ / kathaṃ tarhyanyatra vyavahāra ityata āha - teṣāmiti / chandodevalokānāmityarthaḥ / 'tat'; tacchabdabodhyatvam 'upacārato'; viṣṇusamīpe caraṇāttadadhīnatvādamukhyata evetyarthaḥ/ vāmana ityasya 'hi'; yato vāmane iti 'darśanaṃ'; pratipādanamastyataḥ śrutermukhyavṛtyā viṣṇāveva sāvakāśatvāt liṅgasyāmukhyato 'pyanyatrānavakāśatvāttena tadbādhopapatterbhavatyeva gānatrāṇakartṛtvaliṅgamātreṇāyaṃ nirṇaya ityupaskareṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise He' (<s>evamasau</s>) — <s>Viṣṇu</s> is denoted by words like <s>Agni</s> etc. that denote all deities. Similarly, 'this one' (<s>eṣaḥ</s>) — <s>Viṣṇu</s> is denoted by words like <s>Pṛthivī</s> etc. that denote all worlds — that is the meaning. To the question 'why?' — the three occurrences of the word '<s>hi</s>' (indeed) serve to indicate a threefold reason: because meters, deities, and worlds are each dependent on <s>Bhagavān</s>; or alternatively, to indicate Vedic authority. Because meters and worlds are perceptible while deities are imperceptible, the varied expression '<s>eṣaḥ</s>' (this one) and '<s>asau</s>' (that one) is used. To the question 'how then is there ordinary usage [of these words] elsewhere?' he says: '<s>teṣām</s>' (of those). The meaning is: of the meters, deities, and worlds. 'That' (<s>tat</s>) — their being understood by those words is 'by way of secondary attribution' (<s>upacārata</s>) — because of their moving near <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>viṣṇusamīpe caraṇāt</s>), i.e., because of their dependence on Him, it is only in a non-primary sense. The syntactic connection of '<s>Vāmana</s>' is with the supplementary [explanation]: 'because' (<s>hi</s>) — since in the <s>Vāmana</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] there is 'evidence' (<s>darśanaṃ</s>) — a teaching [to this effect], therefore, since the <s>śruti</s> in its primary sense applies to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, and since the indicatory mark, even though non-primary, has no scope elsewhere, the overriding of [the conventional meaning] by it is justified — thus even through the indicatory mark alone of singing and protecting, this determination [that <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>] is established.
'And it is so because of the applicability of the designation of quarters (<s>pāda</s>) beginning with beings (<s>bhūta</s>).' — <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.26.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.5:
hetvantareṇāpi gāyatryāḥ viṣṇutvaṃ sādhayatsūtramupanyasya tadgṛhītāṃ śrutimudāharati - bhūtādīti/ itiśabdasya bhūtādītyanenānvayaḥ / sūtre bhūtaṃ viśvamādiḥ prathamoddiṣṭaṃ yeṣu te bhūtādayaḥ, te pādāḥ yasya gāyatrīpadārthasya sa bhūtādipādaḥ, tasya vyapadeśaḥ tatpratipādakaṃ vākyaṃ tasyopapatteḥ yuktatvāditi vigrahaḥ / pādaśabdo bhāvapradhānaḥ / ata eva bhūtādipādatvasyetyuktaṃ ṭīkāyām / evamityasya cobhayatrānvayaḥ / tathā ca 'pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni / tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi'; ityevaṃ gāyatryāḥ
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.11.5:
Presenting the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-nature of <s>Gāyatrī</s> through yet another reason, he cites the <s>śruti</s> drawn upon by that [<s>sūtra</s>] — '<s>bhūtādi</s>' etc. The word '<s>iti</s>' connects with '<s>bhūtādi</s>.' In the <s>sūtra</s>, the analysis is: <s>bhūta</s> (beings) is <s>viśva</s> (the universe); <s>ādi</s> means 'first mentioned among them' — thus <s>bhūtādi</s> means 'those beginning with beings'; those are the quarters (<s>pādāḥ</s>) of the entity denoted by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s>, hence <s>bhūtādipāda</s>; its <s>vyapadeśa</s> (designation) is the statement that teaches it; <s>upapatteḥ</s> means 'because of its being fitting.' The word <s>pāda</s> has the sense of a state or property (<s>bhāvapradhāna</s>). For this very reason, it is said in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>: 'of the quarter-nature beginning with beings.' The word '<s>evam</s>' (thus/so) connects with both [the preceding and following]. And thus, of <s>Gāyatrī</s>

children.text: bhūtādiśabdagṛhītāmṛtākhyāṃśacatuṣṭavattvopadeśāt tasya ca viṣṇāvevopapatteranyatrānupapattereva gāyatrīśabdavācyo viṣṇureva bhavedityarthaḥ / caśabdasya vyapadeśapadenānvaye gāyatryā viṣṇutve sādhye pūrvasūtre darśanapadoktahetoḥ etatsūtroktahetudvayasya ca samuccaye saḥ / yathāśrutānvaye tu bhūtādipādatvasya viṣṇuliṅgatvaṃ na kevalaṃ viṣṇorevopapatteḥ siddham, kintu puruṣasūktoktatvācceti hetusamuccaye sa iti jñeyam / chāndogye hi 'saiṣā catuṣpadā ṣaḍvidhā gāyatrī'; (chā. 3-12-5.) iti vākyena yaiṣā ṣaḍvidhā gāyatrī sā catuṣpadetyevaṃ gāyatrīnāmakasya bhagavataḥ prāguktagāyatrībhūtavākpṛthivīśarīrahṛdayalakṣaṇaṣaḍvidhatvamanūdya aṃśacatuṣṭayavattvarūpaṃ catuṣpādatvaṃ vidhāya svoktārtha eva puruṣasūktamantraḥ samākhyārūpatvenodāhṛto brāhmaṇena 'tadetadṛcābhyanūktam'; (chāṃ. 3-12-5.) iti 'tadetat'; bhagavataścatuṣpādatvaṃ 'ṛcā'; ṛṅmantreṇa 'abhi'; niśśaṅkaṃ spaṣṭam 'anu'; ānukūlyenoktamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: — because of the teaching of possessing four quarters whose portions are designated by the words <s>bhūta</s> (beings) etc. and <s>amṛta</s> (immortal), and because this is fitting only with respect to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and is unfitting with respect to anything else — the meaning is that the entity denoted by the word <s>Gāyatrī</s> must be <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. When the word '<s>ca</s>' connects with the word '<s>vyapadeśa</s>' (designation), in establishing the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-nature of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, it serves as a conjunction (<s>samuccaya</s>) of the reason stated by the word '<s>darśana</s>' in the previous <s>sūtra</s> with the two reasons stated in this <s>sūtra</s>. On the literal syntactic reading, however, it should be understood as a conjunction of reasons: the quarter-nature beginning with beings is established as an indicatory mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s> not only because it is fitting for <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, but also because it is stated in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>. For in the <s>Chāndogya</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>], by the statement 'This <s>Gāyatrī</s> is four-footed and sixfold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.5), the sixfold nature of <s>Bhagavān</s> bearing the name <s>Gāyatrī</s> — characterized by the previously mentioned <s>Gāyatrī</s>, beings, speech, earth, body, and heart — is restated (<s>anūdya</s>), and the four-quartered nature in the form of possessing four portions is enjoined; and a <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> <s>mantra</s> is cited by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> as a name-explanation (<s>samākhyā</s>) for its own stated meaning — with the words 'This has been declared by the <s>Ṛc</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.5): 'this' (<s>tadetat</s>) — the four-quartered nature of <s>Bhagavān</s> — 'by the <s>Ṛc</s>' (<s>ṛcā</s>) — by the <s>Ṛg</s>-<s>mantra</s> — has been declared 'fearlessly' (<s>abhi</s>) — clearly and 'in accordance with' (<s>anu</s>) — favorably — that is the meaning.

children.text:
'tāvānasya mahimā tato jyāyāṃśca puruṣaḥ /
pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi'; (chāṃ. 3-12-6.) iti /
children.translated_text: 'So great is His majesty, and greater still is <s>Puruṣa</s>; one quarter of Him is all beings, three quarters are the immortal in heaven' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.12.6).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.6:
kimuktamityatastanmantraṃ paṭhati - tāvāniti // yadyapi ṛci 'etāvān'; iti 'viśvā'; iti ca pāṭhaḥ / tathāpi śākhāntarapāṭho 'yamityadoṣaḥ / 'asya'; puruṣasya 'puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam'; (tai.ā. 3-12.) ityṛcā yassarveśānatvādirūpaḥ tāvānmahimoktaḥ, na kevalametāvān, kintu, puruṣaḥ 'tataḥ'; pūrvoktadapi mahimno 'jyāyān'; adhikamāhātmyopeta ityarthaḥ / jyāyastvameva darśayati - pādo 'syetyādinā / 'sarvā bhūtāni'; sarvaṃ viśvam 'asya'; viṣṇorekaḥ 'pādaḥ'; pādavatpādo bhinnāṃśaḥ / yadyapi tattvapradīpe - viśvabhūvidhirbhāti / tathāpi ṭīkāyāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyasyaikaḥ pāda iti pādavidhānadarśanāt; candrikāyāṃ 'paśvekatvavat vidheyagatatvātpādaikatvaṃ vivakṣitam'; ityuktatvācca, tattvapradīpo 'pyevameva vyākhyeyaḥ / asya 'amṛtaṃ'; nāśarahitam ata eva svarūpabhūtaṃ 'tripāt'; trayāṇāṃ pādānām aṃśānāṃ samudāyo nārāyaṇavāsudevavaikuṇṭhasaṃjñaṃ triṣu rūḍhyā dyotamānatvācca dyuśabdavācyeṣu śvetadvīpānantāsanavaikuṇṭheṣu tiṣṭhatīti ṛcoktamityarthaḥ / yadyapi bhūtaśabdo 'bhinnapādassarvajīvāḥ'; iti chāndogyabhāṣye jīvaparatayā vyākhyātaḥ / tathāpi 'suvarṇam'; iti śrutyanusāreṇa atra viśvārthatayā vyākhyātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.11.6:
Asking 'what was stated?', he cites that <s>mantra</s> — '<s>tāvān</s>' (so great). Although in the <s>Ṛc</s> the readings are '<s>etāvān</s>' and '<s>viśvā</s>', there is no fault since this is a reading from another <s>śākhā</s> (Vedic recension). 'Of this' <s>Puruṣa</s> — the one who, by the <s>Ṛc</s> '<s>puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam</s>' (<s>Tai. Ā.</s> 3-12), possesses the nature of being the Lord of all — 'so great' is his glory declared. But he is not merely this great; rather, the <s>Puruṣa</s> is 'greater' than even the aforementioned glory — meaning he possesses even greater magnificence. He demonstrates this greatness with '<s>pādo 'sya</s>' etc. 'All beings' — the entire universe — is one '<s>pāda</s>' (portion) of '<s>Viṣṇu</s>', a '<s>pāda</s>' meaning a distinct part, like a foot. Although in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> the injunction regarding 'all beings' appears differently, nevertheless, since in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> the designation of <s>pāda</s> is shown as 'all beings are one <s>pāda</s> of His', and since in the <s>Candrikā</s> it is stated that 'the oneness of the <s>pāda</s> is intended as belonging to the predicate, like the oneness of cattle', the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> too should be explained in the same way. His '<s>amṛta</s>' (immortal) — that which is free from destruction and therefore constitutes His essential nature — is '<s>tripāt</s>' (three-footed), meaning the aggregate of three <s>pādas</s> (portions), which is denoted by the names <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, and which abides in the three realms conventionally indicated by the word '<s>dyu</s>' (heaven) — namely <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, <s>Anantāsana</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — this is the meaning declared by the <s>Ṛc</s>. Although the word '<s>bhūta</s>' (beings) is explained in the <s>Chāndogya Bhāṣya</s> as referring to <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), as in 'the distinct <s>pāda</s> is all <s>jīvas</s>', nevertheless, in accordance with the <s>Śruti</s> passage '<s>suvarṇam</s>' (golden), it should be explained here as meaning 'the universe'.

children.text:
suvarṇaṃ kośaṃ rajasā parīvṛtam /
devānāṃ vasudhānīṃ virājam /
amṛtasya pūrṇāṃ tāmu kalāṃ vicakṣate /
pādaṃ ṣaḍḍhoturna kilā vivitse (tai.ā. 3-11.) iti śruteḥ /
pāda iti ekadeśaparimitaṃ caturbhāgabala itivadbhinnaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: '<s>Suvarṇam</s> (golden), the sheath enveloped by <s>rajas</s>, the treasure-holder of the gods, the <s>Virāj</s>, full of the immortal — that portion they perceive as a <s>pāda</s> (foot) of the six-sensed one; it did not indeed attain' (<s>Tai. Ā.</s> 3-11) — thus says the <s>Śruti</s>. The word '<s>pāda</s>' means limited to a part, and distinct — like saying 'having the strength of a fourth'.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.7:
nanu gāyatryāmiva viṣṇāvapi bhūtādipādatvoktiranupapannā / tasya bhūtabhinnatvādityata āha - suvarṇamityādi // 'suvarṇam'; ityārabhya 'bhinnaṃ ca'; ityantamekavākyatayārthakrameṇa vyākhyeyam / yajñadattasya, devadattaḥ, ityucyate, viśvamiti ca śeṣaḥ / pāda iti cāvartate / caśabdaevārthe hetau ca / ekadeśaparimitamiti hetugarbhamāvartanīyam / tathā ca 'co'; yataḥ śrutisthena pāda iti śabdena na bhūtānāmityamṛtapādatrayavatsvarūpāṃśatvamucyate/ yenānupapattiḥ syāt / kintu, yajñadattasya caturbhāgabalo devadatta iti vadbhinnameva viśvam / yataḥ 'parimitam'; viṣṇupādaparimitasāmarthyam ataḥ pāda iti viṣṇupādatvenocyate ityarthaḥ / asyāto viṣṇau bhūtādipādavyapadeśopapatteścaivamiti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / tarhi viśvacatuṣṭayasamo harirityāgatamityato 'pyāha - pāda itīti/ tathā ca yataḥ śrautapāda iti padena caturbhāgabala itivat na viśvaṃ viṣṇusāmarthyasya caturthāṃśaparimitamityucyate / kintu, 'ekadeśaparimitaṃ'; viṣṇusāmarthyaikadeśaparimitamiti ato noktadoṣa ityarthaḥ / kuta etat jñāyata ityata āha - suvarṇaṃ kośamiti / 'śruteḥ'; taittirīyaśruteḥ / śrutau tṛtīyārthe ṣaṣṭhī, samudāyaikavacanaṃ caitat / ata eva 'muktaiḥ pūrṇām'; ityuktaṃ ṭīkāyām / evaṃ ca tattpradīpaṭīkayorekavākyatayā / pādamityāvartate / tatraikaṃ bhāvasādhanam / na kileti dīrghaḥ sāṃhitikaḥ / tathā ca ekasmin kapāle 'suvarṇaṃ'; tanmayaṃ 'rajasā parīvṛtaṃ'; rajoguṇopalakṣitabagnīranabho 'haṃkṛnmahattattvaguṇatrayaiḥ parivṛtaṃ 'virājaṃ'; brahmaṇaḥ śarīraṃ, tattvapradīparītyā viśeṣeṇa rājantamiva 'kośaṃ'; liṅgavyatyayaḥ, brahmāṇḍākhyaṃ yadasti / devānāṃ 'vasudhānīṃ'; dravyanidhānamañjūṣām 'amṛtaiḥ'; muktaiḥ pūrṇāṃ tāṃ 'ṣaḍḍhotuḥ'; ṣaḍindriyeṣu viṣayān juhvataḥ, ṣaḍindriyāṇi viṣayeṣu jīvena juhvato vā, ṣaḍindriyaiḥ sārādanakarturvā, viṣṇoḥ 'kalāmu'; ekadeśaparimitāmeva 'pādaṃ vicakṣate'; pādaśabdenācakṣate vadanti puruṣasūktādyāgamā iti śeṣaḥ / na kila atra pādaśabdenāṅghri vadanti, nāpi caturthāṃśamityevārthaḥ / kutaḥ? yataḥ sā mañjūṣā 'pādaṃ'; pādatvaṃ caturthabhāgasāmyaṃ 'na vivitse'; na lebhe kileti śrutyarthaḥ / sattarkadīpāvalyām - pādaṃ na vivitse iti / pādasāmyaṃ na lebhe ityuktam / atra pakṣadvaye 'pi puruṣavyatyayastulyaḥ / ṭīkākṛtpakṣe lakāravyatyayaśca / yadvā - liṅgavyatyayasya chāndasatvaṃ kośamityasya dvitīyāntatvaṃ copetya strīliṅgapadānāmapi kośaviśeṣaṇatvenaika evānvayaḥ/
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.11.7:
If one objects that just as in the case of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the attribution of <s>pāda</s>-hood (being a portion) through beings and the like to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is also untenable — since He is distinct from beings — to this he responds with '<s>suvarṇam</s>' etc. The passage from '<s>suvarṇam</s>' up to '<s>bhinnaṃ ca</s>' (and distinct) should be explained as a single sentence in order of meaning. [The construction is:] '<s>Yajñadatta</s>'s <s>Devadatta</s>,' it is said, and 'the universe' is to be supplied. And the word '<s>pāda</s>' recurs. The particle '<s>ca</s>' serves both the conjunctive and causal senses. The phrase 'limited to a part' should be understood as containing the reason within the recurrence. And thus, by the word '<s>pāda</s>' established in <s>Śruti</s>, what is stated about beings is not that they constitute an essential portion like the three immortal <s>pādas</s> — which would lead to absurdity. Rather, the universe is distinct, like saying '<s>Devadatta</s> has the strength of a fourth of <s>Yajñadatta</s>.' Because [the universe] is 'limited' — limited to the capacity of one <s>pāda</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — therefore it is called a <s>pāda</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, this is the meaning. Since the attribution of <s>pāda</s>-hood through beings and the like to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is thus established, the connection with the preceding [statement follows]. If one then objects that it would follow that <s>Hari</s> is equal to the fourfold universe, to this too he responds: '<s>pāda iti</s>' (the word <s>pāda</s>). And thus, by the Vedic word '<s>pāda</s>', what is said is not that the universe is limited to a fourth part of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s power — like 'having the strength of a fourth.' Rather, it is 'limited to a part' — limited to one part of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s power — therefore the stated objection does not arise, this is the meaning. Asking 'how is this known?', he says '<s>suvarṇaṃ kośam</s>' etc. 'From <s>Śruti</s>' — from the <s>Taittirīya Śruti</s>. In the <s>Śruti</s>, the genitive is used in the sense of the instrumental, and this is a collective singular. Hence in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> it is stated 'full of the liberated ones.' And thus, with the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> and <s>Ṭīkā</s> forming a single sentence, the word '<s>pādam</s>' recurs. Therein one [derivation] is based on the abstract sense. The long vowel in '<s>na kilā</s>' is a <s>saṃhitā</s> formation. And thus: in one hemisphere, '<s>suvarṇam</s>' — made of gold, '<s>rajasā parīvṛtam</s>' — enveloped by the qualities indicated by <s>rajas</s>, namely fire, water, space, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, <s>mahat-tattva</s>, and the three <s>guṇas</s>; '<s>virājam</s>' — the body of <s>Brahman</s>, or in the manner of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, that which shines distinctly; '<s>kośam</s>' — there is a gender irregularity — the <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) so named. '<s>Vasudhānīm</s>' — a treasure-chest, a receptacle of wealth for the gods; 'full of the <s>amṛta</s>' — full of the liberated souls; '<s>ṣaḍḍhotuḥ</s>' — of the one who offers through six senses into their objects, or of the <s>jīva</s> who offers the six senses into the objects, or of the one who performs worship through six senses — that is, of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; '<s>kalām</s>' — a portion limited to a part; '<s>pādaṃ vicakṣate</s>' — they call it by the word '<s>pāda</s>' — the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> and other <s>āgamas</s> (scriptures) do so, this is to be supplied. The word '<s>pāda</s>' here does not mean 'foot', nor does it mean 'one-fourth' — this is the meaning. Why? Because that cosmic chest '<s>pādam</s>' — the status of being a <s>pāda</s>, the equality with a fourth portion — '<s>na vivitse</s>' — did not attain. '<s>Kila</s>' means 'indeed' — this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>. In the <s>Sattarkadīpāvalī</s> it is stated: '<s>pādaṃ na vivitse</s>' means 'it did not attain equality with a <s>pāda</s>.' Here, in both interpretations, the gender irregularity regarding the <s>puruṣa</s> is the same. In the <s>Ṭīkākṛt</s>'s interpretation, there is also an irregularity of tense. Alternatively, accepting the gender irregularity as a Vedic usage and '<s>kośam</s>' as being in the accusative, the feminine words too, as qualifiers of '<s>kośa</s>', form a single syntactic connection.

children.text:
sa hi puruṣasūktābhidheyaḥ /
'yajñena yajñamayajanta'; (tai.ā. 3-12.) iti yajñaśabdāt /
'yajño viṣṇurdevatā'; (śrutyantaram.) iti hi śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: For He indeed is the subject of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>. From the word '<s>yajña</s>' (sacrifice) in '<s>yajñena yajñam ayajanta</s>' (by sacrifice they worshipped the sacrifice) (<s>Tai. Ā.</s> 3-12). For the <s>Śruti</s> declares: '<s>yajño viṣṇur devatā</s>' (the sacrifice is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the deity).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.8:
syādetadevaṃ yadi 'tāvān'; ityasyāmṛci viṣṇurabhidhīyate ityatra pramāṇaṃ syāt, tadeva nāsti, ato liṅgamanyaniṣṭhaṃ bhaviṣyatītyataḥ sautracaśabdena bhūtādipādatvasya viṣṇuliṅgatve sādhye puruṣasūktoktatvāditi yadanumānaṃ sūcitaṃ tasyāprayojakatvamāśaṅkya pariharati - sa hīti // 'hi'; yasmāt 'saḥ'; viṣṇureva 'puruṣasūktābhidheyaḥ'; tatpratipādyaḥ tasmātsa eva puruṣasūktoktabhūtādipādo 'pīti yojanā / anyathā bhūtādipādatvasya viṣṇudharmatvābhāve puruṣasūktapratipādyatvaṃ na syāditi bhāvaḥ / yadvā - gāyatryā viṣṇutve sādhye sūtre bhinnakrameṇānvitacaśabdasūcitayuktyantaramāha - sa hīti / asya tasmādgāyātrī viṣṇureveti pradhānapratijñāvākyenānvayaḥ / catuṣpadetyuktagāyatrīcatuṣpādatvasya puruṣasūktamantreṇopapādanāt tatpratipādyatve tadupapādyagāyatrīśabdārthatāpi tasyaiva prāpnotīti bhāvaḥ / puruṣasūktoktasya viṣṇutvaṃ kuta ityata āha - yajñeneti / devāḥ 'yajñena'; jñānakarmātmakena rudrākhyapaśunā vā 'yajñaṃ'; viṣṇum 'ayajanta'; apūjayanniti śrutyarthaḥ / iti yajñaśabdāditi / iti vākye yajñaśabdaśravaṇādityarthaḥ / yajñaśabdaḥ kathaṃ viṣṇutvaniścāyaka ityato vidvadrūḍhyetyāha - yajña iti / 'hi'; yataḥ yajña iti padena viṣṇvākhyā devatācyata ityarthaḥ / yadyapi 'yajño vai viṣṇuḥ'; ityadhvaryūṇāṃ śrutiḥ / tathāpi śrutyantaramidamityadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.11.8:
If one objects: 'This would hold only if there were evidence that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is spoken of in the <s>Ṛc</s> '<s>tāvān</s>', but no such evidence exists; therefore the characteristic mark (<s>liṅga</s>) will belong to some other [deity]' — anticipating this objection to the inference suggested by the <s>sūtra</s>'s particle '<s>ca</s>', namely that the <s>pāda</s>-hood of beings and the like is a mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s> because it is stated in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, he refutes it: '<s>sa hi</s>' (for He). '<s>Hi</s>' — because; '<s>saḥ</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is 'the subject of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>' — the one taught therein. Therefore, He alone is also the one whose <s>pāda</s> consists of beings as stated in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> — this is the syntactic connection. Otherwise, if the <s>pāda</s>-hood of beings were not a characteristic of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then His being the subject of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> would not hold — this is the implication. Alternatively, when <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood is to be established for <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he states another reasoning indicated by the particle '<s>ca</s>' connected in a different sequence in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>sa hi</s>.' This connects with the main proposition-sentence: 'therefore <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' Since the four-footedness of <s>Gāyatrī</s> stated as '<s>catuṣpāt</s>' is corroborated by the <s>Puruṣasūkta mantra</s>, and since His being the subject of that [sūkta] is established, the referent of the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>' — that which is corroborated by it — also belongs to Him alone, this is the implication. Asking 'how is the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the one spoken of in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> known?', he says '<s>yajñena</s>' etc. The gods '<s>yajñena</s>' — through sacrifice consisting of knowledge and action, or through the sacrificial animal called <s>Rudra</s> — '<s>yajñam</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — '<s>ayajanta</s>' — they worshipped. This is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>. 'From the word <s>yajña</s>' means: from the occurrence of the word <s>yajña</s> in that statement. How does the word <s>yajña</s> determine <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood? Because it is an established conventional usage among the learned, he says '<s>yajñaḥ</s>' etc. '<s>Hi</s>' — because by the word '<s>yajña</s>', the deity named <s>Viṣṇu</s> is denoted — this is the meaning. Although the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>yajño vai viṣṇuḥ</s>' (sacrifice is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>) belongs to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> tradition, there is no fault in this being from another <s>Śruti</s>.

children.text:
tasmin kāle mahārāja rāma evābhidhīyate /
yathā hi pauruṣe sūkte viṣṇurevābhidhīyate /
iti ca skānde //
children.translated_text: 'In that age, O great king, He was called <s>Rāma</s> alone; just as in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is spoken of' — thus says the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.9:
