nanu puruṣasūktaṃ na viṣṇuprakaraṇaṃ, kintvanyaprakaraṇameva / na ca yajñaśrutivirodhaḥ / paśurūpānyaprakaraṇe tadanyaviṣṇuśruteḥ ayogāditivācyam / tasyāḥ prāsaṅgikatvasambhavāt / na ca tata eva bhūtādipādatvasya viṣṇuliṅgatvaniścayaḥ / tathāpyasiddhiḥ / 'pādo 'sya viśvā bhūtāni'; iti śruterbhūtādipāde yajñaśruterabhāvādtyataḥ puruṣasūktoktasya viṣṇutve smṛtiñcāha - tasminniti // mahārājeti kasyacitsambodhanaṃ rāmaviśeṣaṇaṃ vā / tathātve dīrghassyāt / tathā ca he mahārāja 'tasmin'; tretāyuge sarvaiḥ puruṣanāmabhī rāma evābhidhīyate ityarthaḥ / ata evāṃśādhikaraṇe -
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.11.9:
If one objects: 'The <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> is not a section about <s>Viṣṇu</s> but rather a section about another [deity]. Nor is there a contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> about <s>yajña</s>, since in a section about another [deity] in the form of a sacrificial animal, the <s>Śruti</s> about <s>Viṣṇu</s> being different [from the main subject] would be inapplicable' — this should not be said, because that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>-reference] could be incidental. Nor can the certainty that <s>pāda</s>-hood of beings is a characteristic mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s> be established from that alone. Even so, it remains unproven, because in the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>pādo 'sya viśvā bhūtāni</s>' (all beings are one <s>pāda</s> of His), the word <s>yajña</s> does not occur in the [verse about] the <s>pāda</s> consisting of beings — therefore, to establish the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of what is stated in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, he also cites a <s>Smṛti</s>: '<s>tasmin</s>' etc. '<s>Mahārāja</s>' is either an address to someone or a qualifier of <s>Rāma</s>; in the latter case the vowel would be long. And thus: 'O great king, in that <s>Tretā</s> age, by all the names of <s>Puruṣa</s>, He was called <s>Rāma</s> alone' — this is the meaning. For this very reason, in the <s>Aṃśādhikaraṇa</s> —
The reckoning of stars numbered thirteen thousand,
He made equal to <s>Brahmaloka</s>; the entirety [of that glory] belonged to all at that time.
'<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>' — indeed this became the name of all at that time.
The entire world became pervaded by <s>Rāma</s> when <s>Rāma</s> ruled.

children.text: iti skānde ityuktaṃ tattvapradīpe / atra dṛṣṭāntamāha - yatheti / yathā kṛtsne pauruṣe sūkte viṣṇureva na tvanyaḥ / paśuḥ naraḥ prāsaṅgikatayābhidhīyate ityarthaḥ / anena siddhasyaiva dṛṣṭāntatvātpuruṣasūktasya viṣṇuparatvaṃ siddhamiti bhāvaḥ / skānda ityantaraṃ etaduktamiti śeṣaḥ / asya sa hīti purvavākyenānvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus it is stated in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, as cited in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. Here he gives an illustration: '<s>yathā</s>' (just as). Just as in the entire <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — not another, such as the sacrificial animal (<s>paśu</s>) or man (<s>nara</s>) — is spoken of, [the latter being mentioned] only incidentally. This is the meaning. By this, since what is already established serves as the illustration, the purport of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> being about <s>Viṣṇu</s> is proven — this is the implication. '<s>Skānda</s>' — that this is stated in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa] is to be supplied. This connects with the preceding sentence '<s>sa hi</s>' (for He).

children.text: upadeśabhedān neti cen nobhayasminn apy avirodhāt | BBs_1,1.27 |
children.translated_text: 'If it be said that [<s>Gāyatrī</s> is] not [<s>Brahman</s>] because of difference in teaching — no, because there is no contradiction in either [teaching].' <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.27.

children.text:
'tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi'; (chāṃ. 3-12-6.) iti pūrvopadeśaḥ /
'paro divaḥ'; (chāṃ. 3-13-7.) iti pañcamyantaḥ paścimaḥ /
tasmānnekaṃ vastvatrocyate iti cet - na, trisaptalokāpekṣayā ubhayasminnapyavirodhāt //
children.translated_text: The earlier teaching is: '<s>tripād asyāmṛtaṃ divi</s>' (three-fourths of Him is the immortal in heaven) (<s>Chānd.</s> 3.12.6). The later teaching ends with the fifth case (ablative): '<s>paro divaḥ</s>' (beyond heaven) (<s>Chānd.</s> 3.13.7). If one objects that therefore a single entity is not being taught here — no, because there is no contradiction in either [teaching], considering the [distinction between] the three and seven worlds.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.11.10:
uktamākṣipya samādadhatsūtramupanyasyati - upadeśeti // 'upadeśayoḥ'; saptamīpañcamīyutavākyayoḥ 'upadeśena'; gāyatrījyotiṣoḥ dyusthatvadivaḥparatvarūpaviruddhadharmoktyā 'bhedāt'; virodhāt na dvayorviṣṇvākhyam ekaṃ vastu pratipādyaṃ, kintu bhinnameveti cet - na, kintu 'ubhayasmin'; ubhayatrāpyupadeśe ekameva pratipādyaṃ, katham? avirodhāt / trisaptalokāpekṣayā saptamīpañcamyoḥ ekārthatvena virodhābhāvāditi sūtrayojanāmabhiprayannākṣepāṃśaṃ tāvadvyācaṣṭe - tripāditi / 'pūrvopadeśaḥ'; pūrvoktiḥ / 'paścimaḥ'; paścāttanaḥ uttara upadeśastadbhinno 'stīti śeṣaḥ/ virodhasphoraṇāya pañcamyanta ityādyuktiḥ / upakramagatasya prābalyopapādanāya pūrva ityuktiḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - tasmāditi / yasmādevaṃ bhinnopadeśadvayamasti tasmādatropadeśadvaye gāyatrījyotiśśabdābhyāṃ naikaṃ vastu viṣṇvākhyamucyate / kutaḥ? yato 'tra 'naikam'; anekaṃ vastu dyusthatvadivaḥparatvarūpaṃ dharmadvayamucyate / kintvatra 'naikam'; anekaṃ vastudvayamucyate iti yojanā / siddhāntayatsūtrāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti / nātra vastudvayamucyate ityarthaḥ / kiṃ tvitiśeṣaḥ, ekaṃ vastūcyate iti anuṣajyate / ubhayasminniti sādhyāntargatam / apiśabdo na kevalamekatra, kintūbhayatrāpīti samuccaye / tathā ca kintūbhayasmin apyupadeśe ekameva viṣṇvākhyaṃ vastūcyate iti yojanā / virodhātkathametadyujyate ityata āha - trisaptalokāpekṣayeti / trilokavivakṣayā saptalokavivakṣayā ca 'avirodhāt'; ubhayatrāpyekavastvabhidhāne virodhābhāvādityarthaḥ / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - yadā bhūrbhuvassvariti lokatrayavivakṣā, tadā lakṣayojanocchritāntarikṣākhyabhuva uparitanasya sarvasyāpi dyutvāt śvetadvīpānantasanavaikuṇṭhānāṃ cāntarikṣāduparitanatvāttatratyaṃ nārāyaṇavāsudevavaikuṇṭhākhyaṃ tripācchabdoktaṃ rūpatrayaṃ divitiṣṭhatītyucyate iti na saptamyantopadeśavirodhaḥ / na ca
children.translated_text: Dīpikā on BBsBh 1.1.11.10: Having raised an objection to what was stated, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves it — 'upadeśa' etc. 'Of the two teachings (<s>upadeśayoḥ</s>)': of the two sentences, one ending in the locative (seventh case) and the other in the ablative (fifth case); 'by the teaching (<s>upadeśena</s>)': through the statement of contradictory properties regarding <s>Gāyatrī</s> and <s>jyotis</s>, namely being situated in heaven (<s>dyusthatva</s>) and being beyond heaven (<s>divaḥ paratva</s>); 'because of difference (<s>bhedāt</s>)': because of contradiction, the objection is that both cannot have a single referent called <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but rather they must refer to different things — no, rather 'in both (<s>ubhayasmin</s>)': in both teachings the referent is one and the same. How? Because there is no contradiction (<s>avirodhāt</s>) — since with reference to the three-world and seven-world cosmological frameworks, the locative and ablative have the same meaning and there is no contradiction. Intending this construal of the <s>sūtra</s>, he first explains the objection portion — 'tripād' etc. 'The prior teaching (<s>pūrvopadeśaḥ</s>)': the earlier statement. 'The latter (<s>paścimaḥ</s>)': the subsequent, later teaching is different from it — this is the remainder to be supplied. The expression 'ending in the ablative' etc. is to make the contradiction explicit. The word 'prior' is used to establish the greater strength of what appears at the beginning. Then what follows from this? To this he says — 'therefore (<s>tasmāt</s>)' etc. Since there are thus two different teachings, therefore in these two teachings the words <s>Gāyatrī</s> and <s>jyotis</s> do not refer to one entity called <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? Because here 'not one (<s>naikam</s>)': not one entity but rather a pair of properties, namely being situated in heaven and being beyond heaven, is stated. But the construal is: here 'not one (<s>naikam</s>)' — two distinct entities are spoken of. He explains the <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusive) portion of the <s>sūtra</s> — 'na' etc. The meaning is: two distinct entities are not spoken of here. The remainder is 'but rather' — and one should connect: 'one entity is spoken of.' '<s>Ubhayasmin</s>' is included within the thesis to be proved. The particle 'api' indicates a cumulative sense: not merely in one, but in both. And thus the construal is: but in both teachings, one single entity called <s>Viṣṇu</s> is spoken of. How is this consistent given the contradiction? To this he says — 'with reference to the three-world and seven-world frameworks' etc. 'Because of non-contradiction (<s>avirodhāt</s>)': because there is no contradiction in referring to one entity in both cases, with reference to the three-world framework and the seven-world framework — this is the meaning. The purport is as follows: when the three worlds <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s> are intended, then since everything above the atmospheric realm (<s>Bhuvas</s>), which extends one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> high, constitutes heaven (<s>dyu</s>), and since <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, <s>Anantāsana</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> are above the atmosphere, the three forms referred to by the word 'tripād' — namely <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — which are situated there, are said to be 'in heaven (<s>divi</s>),' and thus there is no contradiction with the teaching ending in the locative. And not —
Among all the worlds situated on the earth, the highest is the world consisting of <s>Anantāsana</s>,
and <s>Hari</s> is situated in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, which is above those worlds that are of the nature of the atmosphere.

children.text: ityukteranantāsanasya nāntarikṣāduparitanateti śaṅkyam / tasya pṛthivīsthatve 'pi bahulakṣayojanocchritatvenaikalakṣayojanocchritāntarikṣāduparitanatvopapatteḥ / sarvapṛthivīsthoccatvoktyā tu na pṛthivīsthānyoccatvayogovyāvartyate / kintu pṛthivīsthoccatvāyogaḥ / yadā tu bhūrbhuvassvarmaharjanaspassatyamiti saptalokavivakṣā / tadendrasadanasya dyutvāt taduccasyāpyuparisthitatvena tatsajātīyasyavaikuṇṭhasya divaḥ paratvam /
children.translated_text: — it should not be objected that <s>Anantāsana</s> is not above the atmosphere on the basis of this statement. For even though it is situated on the earth, since it extends many hundreds of thousands of <s>yojanas</s> high, it is reasonable that it is above the atmosphere which extends one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. And the statement that it is the highest among all things situated on the earth does not preclude its being higher than things situated on earth, but rather precludes the impossibility of something on earth being that high. But when the seven worlds — <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>, <s>Janaḥ</s>, <s>Tapaḥ</s>, and <s>Satyam</s> — are intended, then since <s>Indra's</s> abode constitutes heaven (<s>dyu</s>), and since even what is above it stands higher, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, being of the same class as that, is beyond heaven (<s>divaḥ para</s>).
Heaven on earth is great Mount <s>Meru</s>; in the sky is the orb of the sun;

children.text: divīndrasadanaṃ caiva tatpare tu divaḥ pare //
children.translated_text: in heaven is the abode of <s>Indra</s>, and beyond that, beyond heaven —

children.text: iti smṛtermerorapi dyutvāttaduccasya bhūspṛṣṭatvena tatsajātīyasyānantāsanasyāpi divaḥ paratā / evaṃ sūryamaṇḍalasyāpi dyutvāttaduccasyoparisthatvena tatsajātīyasya bhūmeḥ kiñcidantaritasya sarvargasamonnatasya śvetadvīpasyāpi divaḥ paratvamastīti na pañcamyantopadeśavirodho 'pīti / dyuparatvaṃ ca sambhāvitasajātīyadyuparatvamiti na yāvattvayatkiñcittvamukhena dūṣaṇāvakāśaḥ / vaikuṇṭhasya svargalokātparatvenaiva divaḥ paratvasiddhāvapi tasya 'sarvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu'; ityanenaiva uktatvāt svargatyāgenendrasadanasya dyutvoktiḥ / na ca lokatrayavivakṣayaivānantāsanādīnāmapi mervādiparatvena divaḥ paratvasyāpi siddheḥ saptalokavivakṣā vyartheti vācyam / tathā sati vaikuṇṭhasyāpi dyuśabdārthaniviṣṭatvena tasya sarvadyuparatvāsiddhyāpatyā 'dvyātmakebhyaśca sarvebhyo vaikuṇṭhaścocca ucyate'; iti pramāṇavirodhāpātāt / chāndogyabhāṣye tu -
children.translated_text: thus according to this <s>smṛti</s>, since <s>Meru</s> too constitutes heaven (<s>dyu</s>), and since <s>Anantāsana</s>, being of the same class as what is higher than it and touches the earth, is also beyond heaven. Similarly, since the orb of the sun also constitutes heaven, and since <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, being of the same class as what stands above it, slightly separated from the earth, and equal in elevation to all the heavens, is also beyond heaven — thus there is no contradiction with the teaching ending in the ablative either. And 'being beyond heaven' means being beyond a heaven of a plausible similar class, so there is no room for the objection of over-extension to any arbitrary thing. Even though the beyondness of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> from heaven is already established by its being above the heavenly world (<s>svargaloka</s>), since that has already been stated by 'on all the backs (<s>sarvataḥ pṛṣṭheṣu</s>),' the identification of <s>Indra's</s> abode as heaven is stated by setting aside the heavenly world. And it should not be said that the seven-world framework is pointless since the beyondness from heaven of <s>Anantāsana</s> and others could be established even through the three-world framework by their being above <s>Meru</s> and so forth — because in that case, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> too would fall within the scope of the word <s>dyu</s> (heaven), and its being above all heavens would not be established, leading to a conflict with the authority 'and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is said to be higher than all those of twofold nature.' But in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>Bhāṣya</s> —
The couch of <s>Ananta</s> and likewise the seat of <s>Ananta</s> belonging to <s>Hari</s>,
are situated in an eternal <s>vimāna</s> (celestial vehicle) extending many hundreds of thousands of <s>yojanas</s> high;
because it is in the realm of <s>cit-prakṛti</s> (spiritual nature), it is said to be 'in heaven' in the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: iti pramāṇabalena citprakṛtyātmakānantāsanaśvetadvīpavaikuṇṭhākhyasthānatraye saptamyanto dyuśabdo dyotamānatvanimittena yaugikaḥ, svargādau tu rūḍha iti upadeśayoravirodha iti prakārāntareṇa virodhaparihāraḥ kṛtaḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the force of this authority, the word <s>dyu</s> (heaven) in the locative is etymological (<s>yaugika</s>) — based on luminosity (<s>dyotamānatva</s>) — in the three locations called <s>Anantāsana</s>, <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> which are of the nature of <s>cit-prakṛti</s> (spiritual nature), whereas in <s>svarga</s> and such realms it is conventional (<s>rūḍha</s>). Thus the non-contradiction of the two teachings is established, and the contradiction is resolved in an alternative manner. // 11 //
// Thus ends the <s>Chandoabhidhānādhikaraṇa</s> (section on the designation through meter) // 11 //
// 12. <s>Pādāntyaprāṇādhikaraṇa</s> (section on <s>Prāṇa</s> at the end of the quarter) //

children.text:
prāṇo viṣṇurityuktam /
tatra 'tā vā etāḥ śīrṣan chriyaḥ śritāścakṣuḥ śrotraṃ mano vākprāṇaḥ'; (ai.ā. 2-1-4.) ityatra prāṇasya viṣṇutvaṃ na vidyate /
indriyaissahābhidhānāditi / ata āha -
children.translated_text: It has been stated that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. In that regard, in the passage 'These are the glories (<s>śriyaḥ</s>) resting on the head — the eye, the ear, the mind, speech, and <s>Prāṇa</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.4), the identity of <s>Prāṇa</s> as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not established, because it is mentioned alongside the sense organs. Therefore he says —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.1:
atrādhikaraṇe lokato 'nyatra prasiddhaprāṇanāmno viṣṇau samanvayaḥ pratipādyate / śrutyādisaṅgativiṣayavākyaviṣayasaṃśayasayuktikapūrvapakṣān darśayati - prāṇa iti // ādyaprāṇādhikaraṇe 'tadvai tvam'; (tai.ā. 3-14.) iti vākyoktaprāṇo viṣṇurityuktamityarthaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - tatreti / uktamityanuṣajyate / tasyāvṛttivipariṇāmau / evaṃ tatretyapyāvartanīyam / tathā ca 'tatra'; tadvai tvamiti vākye uktasya prāṇasya viṣṇutvaṃ na vidyate na yujyate / kutaḥ? yatastatra 'tadvai tvam'; iti vākyoktaprāṇaviṣaye 'ukte'; śrute 'tā vā etāḥ'; ityaitareyavākye uktasya śrutasya prāṇasya viṣṇutvaṃ na vidyata iti yojanā / kuto na vidyate ityata āha - indriyaissahābhidhānāditi / indriyaissaha paṭhitatvāt indriyagaṇe gaṇitatvāt ityarthaḥ / anenaitareyaprāṇasya viṣṇvanyatvākṣepamukhena prācīnataittirīyoktaprāṇasyāpyanyatvākṣepāttenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / aitareyaprāṇākhyo viṣayaḥ / prāṇo 'nya uta viṣṇuriti saṃśayaśca sūcitaḥ / tathā vāyvādiranya eveti pūrvapakṣaḥ / indriyagaṇe gaṇitatvākhyatatsādhakaliṅgaṃ ca sūcitam / 'tā vā etāḥ'; ityetacca caturmukhaśirasi śiraśśabdapravṛttinimittakathanāya pravṛttam / vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / tathā ca yataḥ 'tā etāḥ'; cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ manovākprāṇa ityetacchabdavācyāstadabhimāninyo devatāḥ / 'śīrṣan'; śīrṣṇi śiraḥsaṃjñikamūrdhni śritāḥ / ata eva śrayaṇācchriya iti siddhānte śrutyarthaḥ / anena cakṣurādibhiḥ śritatvaṃ śiraḥpadapravṛttinimittamityuktaṃ bhavati / pūrvapakṣī tu prāṇaśabdamanyamātraparaṃ manyate / siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti / yataḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ prāptaḥ ata uttaraṃ sūtramāha bhagavān bādarāyaṇa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dīpikā on BBsBh 1.1.12.1: In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section), the coherent interpretation (<s>samanvaya</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the one well known by the name <s>Prāṇa</s> in contexts other than ordinary usage is to be established. He presents the <s>śruti</s> passage, the matter of correlation, the subject matter, the doubt, and the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) with its reasoning — '<s>Prāṇa</s>' etc. The meaning is: in the earlier <s>Prāṇādhikaraṇa</s>, it has been stated that the <s>Prāṇa</s> mentioned in the passage 'That indeed art thou (<s>tad vai tvam</s>)' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.14) is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Then what follows from that? To this he says — 'tatra' etc. 'It has been stated (<s>uktam</s>)' is to be connected. Its repetition and transformation are as follows. Similarly, 'tatra' too is to be carried forward. And thus: 'there (<s>tatra</s>)' — the identity of the <s>Prāṇa</s> spoken of in the passage 'That indeed art thou' as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not established, is not tenable. Why? Because regarding the <s>Prāṇa</s> that is the subject of the passage 'That indeed art thou,' 'as stated (<s>ukte</s>)': as heard — the identity as <s>Viṣṇu</s> of the <s>Prāṇa</s> stated and heard in the <s>Aitareya</s> passage 'These indeed are' is not established — this is the construal. Why is it not established? To this he says — 'because of being mentioned alongside the sense organs (<s>indriyais sahābhidhānāt</s>).' Because it is enumerated together with the sense organs, because it is counted in the group of sense organs — this is the meaning. By this, through the objection that the <s>Prāṇa</s> of the <s>Aitareya</s> is other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, an objection is also raised against the earlier <s>Prāṇa</s> stated in the <s>Taittirīya</s>, and thus the correlation of this section as responding to that objection is stated. The subject matter is the <s>Prāṇa</s> named in the <s>Aitareya</s>. The doubt is indicated: is <s>Prāṇa</s> something else, or is it <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Likewise the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is that it is merely something else such as <s>Vāyu</s>. And the supporting indicator (<s>liṅga</s>) for that — being counted in the group of sense organs — is also indicated. And 'These indeed are (<s>tā vā etāḥ</s>)' etc. is introduced to explain the basis for the application of the word 'head' (<s>śiras</s>) to the head of <s>Caturmukha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). The particle 'vai' indicates well-known usage. And thus: since 'these (<s>tā etāḥ</s>)' — the deities presiding over the eye, ear, mind, speech, and <s>Prāṇa</s>, which are denoted by those words — are 'resting on the head (<s>śīrṣan</s>)': situated on the crown known as the head. Therefore, because of their resting there, the word <s>śriyaḥ</s> (glories) is explained in the <s>siddhānta</s> as derived from the root 'śri' (to rest). By this it is stated that the basis for the application of the word 'head' is that the eye and other faculties rest there. But the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> considers the word <s>Prāṇa</s> to refer merely to something other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>. He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that represents the <s>siddhānta</s> — 'ataḥ' etc. Since the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> has been arrived at, therefore the revered <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> states the answering <s>sūtra</s> — this is the meaning.
<s>Prāṇa</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of such tracking (<s>anugamāt</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.28 |

children.text:
'taṃ devāḥ prāṇayanta'; (ai.ā. 2-1-5.) 'sa eṣo 'suḥ sa eṣa prāṇaḥ'; (ai.ā. 2-1-5.) 'prāṇa ṛca ityeva vidyāt'; (ai.ā.2-2-2.)
'tadayaṃ prāṇo 'dhitiṣṭhati'; (ai.ā. 2-3-8.) ityādyānugamāt /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>devas</s> led him forth as <s>Prāṇa</s> (<s>taṃ devāḥ prāṇayanta</s>)' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.5); 'He is this <s>Asu</s>, He is this <s>Prāṇa</s> (<s>sa eṣo 'suḥ sa eṣa prāṇaḥ</s>)' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.5); '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Ṛk</s> — one should know thus (<s>prāṇa ṛca ityeva vidyāt</s>)' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.2.2); 'This <s>Prāṇa</s> presides over it (<s>tadayaṃ prāṇo 'dhitiṣṭhati</s>)' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.3.8) — because of the tracking of such passages.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.2:
sūtraṃ paṭhitvā tatrānugamāditi hetvaṃśaṃ śrutyudāharaṇena vyācaṣṭe - prāṇa iti // ityādīti / evamādivākyoktānāṃ devatopadeśyatvādiliṅgānāmatrāsmin prakaraṇe bahuṣu sthaleṣu 'anugamāt'; anuvṛtterabhyāsādityarthaḥ / ādipadena 'prāṇo hyevaiṣa ya eṣa tapati'; iti sūryamaṇḍalasthatvapratipādakavākyaṃ gṛhyate / tathā 'sarvāṇi bhūtānyāpipīlikābhyaḥ prāṇena bṛhatyā viṣṭabdhāni'; ityādi vākyaṃ ca gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: Dīpikā on BBsBh 1.1.12.2: Having cited the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains the reasoning portion 'because of tracking (<s>anugamāt</s>)' therein by illustrating with <s>śruti</s> passages — '<s>Prāṇa</s>' etc. 'And so forth (<s>ityādi</s>)': because of the 'tracking (<s>anugamāt</s>)' — that is, the recurrence and repetition — in many places within this very <s>prakaraṇa</s> (section) of indicators such as being the object of worship by the gods, which are stated in such passages as these. By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), the passage '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is this one who blazes [as the sun] (<s>prāṇo hyevaiṣa ya eṣa tapati</s>)' — which teaches his presence in the solar orb — is included. Likewise, the passage 'All beings from the ants onward are sustained by <s>Prāṇa</s> through <s>Bṛhatī</s> (<s>sarvāṇi bhūtānyāpipīlikābhyaḥ prāṇena bṛhatyā viṣṭabdhāni</s>)' and similar passages are also included.
Here too, <s>Prāṇa</s> is none other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.3:
sautraṃ tathāśabdaṃ vyācaṣṭe - atrāpīti // śruta iti śeṣaḥ / na kevalaṃ 'tadvai tvam'; ityatra, kintvaitareye 'pīti samuccaye 'piśabdaḥ / sūtre anuvṛttasya tattvityasyārthamāha - viṣṇureveti / anena yathā
children.translated_text: Dīpikā on BBsBh 1.1.12.3: He explains the word 'tathā' (thus/similarly) from the <s>sūtra</s> — 'here too (<s>atrāpi</s>)' etc. The remainder is: 'as heard (<s>śruta</s>).' The particle 'api' indicates a cumulative sense: not only in the passage 'That indeed art thou (<s>tad vai tvam</s>),' but in the <s>Aitareya</s> as well. He states the meaning of 'tat' (that) which is carried forward in the <s>sūtra</s> — 'none other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>Viṣṇureva</s>).' By this,

children.text: 'tadvaitvam'; iti śrutyuktaprāṇo viṣṇuḥ tathaitareyokto 'pi viṣṇureva, na tvanyaḥ / kutaḥ? viṣṇuliṅgānāṃ devatopadeśyatvādīnāmasmin prakaraṇe 'anugamāt'; anuvṛtterabhyāsāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: just as the <s>Prāṇa</s> spoken of in the <s>śruti</s> passage 'That indeed art thou (<s>tad vai tvam</s>)' is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so too the one spoken of in the <s>Aitareya</s> is none other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? Because of the 'tracking (<s>anugamāt</s>)' — the recurrence and repetition — of indicators of <s>Viṣṇu</s> such as being the object of worship by the gods, within this <s>prakaraṇa</s> (section) — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.

children.text: aitareye 'taṃ devāḥ prāṇayanta'; iti ekakhaṇḍasthavākyam / 'taṃ'; nārāyaṇaṃ vāyuṃ ca devāḥ 'prāṇayanta'; prakarṣeṇa śiṣyapraśiṣyadiṣu nītavantaḥ upadidiśurityarthaḥ / anena viṣṇoḥ sarvadevopāsyatvamuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Aitareya</s>, 'The <s>devas</s> led Him forth as <s>Prāṇa</s> (<s>taṃ devāḥ prāṇayanta</s>)' is a passage from one section. '<s>Tam</s>' refers to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>; the <s>devas</s> 'led Him forth (<s>prāṇayanta</s>)': they conducted Him with distinction to disciples, grand-disciples, and others — meaning they taught Him. By this, it is stated that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is worshipped by all the <s>devas</s>.

children.text: 'sa eṣo 'suḥ sa eṣa prāṇaḥ sa eṣa bhūtiḥ'; ityādyanyakhaṇḍagataṃ vākyam / anena bhūtitvādinā devādyupāsyatvamucyate / 'sa eṣaḥ'; bhagavān duṣṭanirasanādasuḥ prakṛṣṭānandarūpatvātprāṇaḥ devānāṃ bhūtiśabditajñānādyaiśvaryapradatvādasurāṇām ajñānādyanaiśvaryahetutvācca bhūtyabhūtiśabdavācya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is this <s>Asu</s>, He is this <s>Prāṇa</s>, He is this <s>Bhūti</s> (prosperity)' and so forth is a passage from another section. By this, through attributes such as being <s>Bhūti</s>, His being the object of worship by the <s>devas</s> and others is stated. '<s>Sa eṣaḥ</s>' — the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>) is called <s>Asu</s> because He destroys the wicked; He is called <s>Prāṇa</s> because He is of the nature of supreme bliss; He is denoted by the words <s>Bhūti</s> (prosperity) and <s>Abhūti</s> (adversity) because He bestows knowledge and other forms of sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) designated by the word <s>Bhūti</s> upon the <s>devas</s>, and because He is the cause of ignorance and other forms of non-sovereignty for the <s>asuras</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: tatraiva 'tā vā etāḥ sarvā ṛcaḥ sarve vedāḥ sarve ghoṣā ekaiva vyāhṛtiḥ / prāṇa eva prāṇa ṛca ityeva vidyāt'; iti anyadvākyam / atra prāṇasyasarvavedoktatvamucyate / yāstāḥ etāḥ sarvā ṛcastāsāṃ 'ekaiva vyāhṛtiḥ'; ekameva vyāhartavyaṃ pratipādyam / tacca kim? prāṇo viṣṇureva / kiñca ye sarve vedāḥ teṣāmapi prāṇa eva pratipādyaḥ/ api ca ye samudrādighoṣāḥ teṣāmapi, kimu vedānām / tatra ṛcastu viśeṣata indrādināmavato viṣṇorguṇān alpajñānāmapi prakāśayantīti, prāṇe nārāyaṇe tadviṣayā eva 'vidyāt'; tatpratipādikā eveti jānīyādityarthaḥ / aitareyabhāṣye tu - prathamaprāṇapadamapi viṣayasaptamyantatayā vyāhṛtiśabdaṃ ca vyāharaṇaparatayā vyākhyāya ekameva vyāharaṇaṃ nirdeṣaguṇapūrtivācakatvādekaprakārameva nāmetyarthaḥ uktaḥ / tattvapradīpe 'pyayamevoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: In that same context, 'These indeed are all the <s>Ṛk</s> verses, all the <s>Vedas</s>, all the sounds; they have but one <s>vyāhṛti</s> (utterance): <s>Prāṇa</s> alone. One should know <s>Prāṇa</s> as the <s>Ṛk</s>' is another passage. Here, it is stated that <s>Prāṇa</s> is what all the <s>Vedas</s> teach. Of all those <s>Ṛk</s> verses, 'there is but one <s>vyāhṛti</s>': there is but one thing to be uttered, one thing to be taught. And what is that? <s>Prāṇa</s>, who is none other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Moreover, <s>Prāṇa</s> alone is what all the <s>Vedas</s> too teach. Furthermore, even all the sounds such as the roar of the ocean and the like teach Him — how much more so the <s>Vedas</s>! Among these, the <s>Ṛk</s> verses in particular illuminate the qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who descends as <s>Indra</s> and other <s>avatāras</s>, even to those of limited knowledge; therefore, one should know (<s>vidyāt</s>) that they pertain to <s>Prāṇa</s>, who is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — that is, one should understand them as teaching Him alone — this is the meaning. But in the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s>, even the first occurrence of the word <s>Prāṇa</s> is explained as a locative of subject matter, and the word <s>vyāhṛti</s> is explained as meaning 'utterance,' and the meaning given is: there is but one kind of utterance, because it expresses the fullness of the qualities stated — that is, it is of one type only, namely a name. This same interpretation is given in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> as well.

children.text: atha devarathaḥ 'tasya vāguddhiḥ śrotre pakṣasī cakṣuṣī yukte manaḥ saṅgṛhītā tadayaṃ prāṇo 'dhitiṣṭhati'; iti vākyāntaraṃ atra prāṇasya deharathatvamucyate / prameyāntarakathanārambhārtho 'thaśabdaḥ / ucyata iti śeṣaḥ/ tathā ca devasya viṣṇoḥ vāyoḥ adhyātmamadhidaivataṃ ca ratha ucyate ityarthaḥ / tasyādhyātmaṃ dehākhyarathasya 'vāk'; vāgākhyā umā uddhiḥ dhāraṇarajjurūpā adhidaivaṃ viṣṇurathasya prasiddhasyandanasya ca nāgākāromā uddhiḥ 'śrotre'; dakṣavāmapārśvagatacandratadbhārye 'pakṣasī'; pārśvayuktāśvau anyatrāśvarūpau pārśvayoryuktau 'cakṣuṣī'; ubhayapārśvagatasūryatadbhārye ca 'yukte'; agrato niyuktāśvau 'mano'; mano 'bhimānī rudraḥ 'saṅgṛhītā'; sārathiḥ evam adhidaivaṃ prasiddhasyandanasyāpi rudraḥ sārathiḥ / sa cāsāvayaṃ ca tadayamityekaṃ padam / tattvapradīparītyā
children.translated_text: Now, the chariot of the god: 'His speech is the harness-rope, the ears are the wings, the eyes are yoked, the mind is the charioteer — this <s>Prāṇa</s> presides over [it]' — this is another passage. Here the chariot-nature of the body for <s>Prāṇa</s> is stated. The word 'atha' (now) is for the purpose of introducing another topic. 'It is stated' is the remainder. And thus, of the god <s>Viṣṇu</s> and of <s>Vāyu</s>, the chariot is spoken of both in the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) and cosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) senses — that is the meaning. Of that body-chariot in the individual sense: 'speech' — <s>Umā</s>, known as speech, is the 'harness-rope' (<s>uddhi</s>) in the form of a binding cord; in the cosmic sense, of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> chariot, the well-known vehicle, the serpent-shaped rope is the harness. 'The ears' — the moon and his consort situated on the right and left sides; 'the wings' — the horses yoked on the sides, elsewhere in the form of horses, yoked on either side; 'the eyes' — the sun and his consort on both sides; 'yoked' — the horses harnessed in front; 'the mind' — <s>Rudra</s>, the presiding deity of the mind, is 'the charioteer' (<s>saṅgṛhītā</s>); similarly, in the cosmic sense, <s>Rudra</s> is the charioteer of the well-known vehicle as well. 'Sa ca asau ayaṃ ca tadayam' is a single compound word. According to the method of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>,

children.text: bhinnapadatve 'pi taditi rathatayoktaṃ śarīraṃ parāmṛśyate / liṅgavyatyayena taṃ rathamiti vā / ayaṃ prāṇo viṣṇuḥ vāyuścādhitiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ / liṅgena pūrvapakṣite kathaṃ tenaiva siddhānta ityāśaṅkānudayāya liṅgabāhulyoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: even when the words are separate, by 'tat' the body spoken of as a chariot is referred to. Or, by gender transposition (<s>liṅgavyatyaya</s>), 'that chariot' [is meant]. This <s>Prāṇa</s> — <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> — presides over [it]: that is the meaning. [Objection:] When the prima facie view is established through a mark (<s>liṅga</s>), how can the established conclusion be through that very same [mark]? — to prevent this objection from arising, the statement of abundance of marks is made.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.12, verse 4:]
The gods brought <s>Viṣṇu</s> [forward]; they worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> for prosperity.
He alone is proclaimed in all the <s>Vedas</s>; His chariot is called the body.
Thus in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>.

children.translated_text: The strength [of a mark] is twofold: by abundance and by inherent nature.
Of these two, the inherently strong prevails, and it is also the one depended upon.

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.1.12, verse 4:
But an indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) cited by the prima facie advocate is stronger even than the established-conclusion's mark that is strong by abundance. [Why?] Because of its inherent strength through having no scope [elsewhere] (<s>niravakāśatva</s>). Nor is the determination merely without distinction, because even [a mark] that is strong by abundance is surpassed by one that is inherently strong. As they say —

children.text: iti / ataḥ kathaṃ tairviṣṇutvaniścaya ityato devatopadeśyatvādiliṅgānāṃ niravakāśatvamapi smṛtyā sādhayati
children.translated_text: Therefore, how can the determination of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood be through those [marks of abundance]? — to this, he establishes through <s>Smṛti</s> the no-scope-elsewhere nature of the marks such as being the one taught to the gods and the like.

children.text: - viṣṇumiti / devāḥ viṣṇumeva prādhānyena śiṣyādiṣu jñānasampradāyapravartanena 'ānayan'; upādiśan / bhūtimuddiśya viṣṇumevopāsate / bhūtimiti vidheyaviśeṣaṇaṃ vā / tathā ca viṣṇuṃ bhūtiṃ bhūtirjñānādyaiśvaryarūpa ityupāsate ityarthaḥ / 'saḥ'; viṣṇurmukhyavācyatayeti śeṣaḥ, tenaivakāropapattiḥ / 'tadratho'; viṣṇoreva rathaḥ / atraivakārasya dvirgrahaṇātsarvatrānuṣaṅgaḥ sūcitaḥ / tena sarvaliṅgānāmapi niravagakāśatvamuktaṃ bhavati / skānde ityanantaraṃ liṅgānāmananyathāsiddhatvamuktamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ / tathā caikaprakāreṇa prabalātpūrvapakṣiliṅgātprakāradvayenāpi prabalasya saiddhāntikaliṅgasyādhikyena nirṇayopapattiriti bhāvaḥ / abhyupetya cedamuditam / vastustu pūrvapakṣiliṅgasya na niravakāśatvenāpi prābalyamasti, prāṇaiḥ sahagaṇitatvasyāntaryāminiṣṭhatāsambhavāt /
children.translated_text: — '<s>Viṣṇum</s>': the gods brought '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' alone as the chief one — by propagating the tradition of knowledge to disciples and others — they 'brought' [Him]; they taught [Him]. They worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> 'for the sake of prosperity' (<s>bhūti</s>). Or '<s>bhūti</s>' is an adjective of the object; and thus, they worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> [who is] <s>bhūti</s> — prosperity in the form of knowledge and lordship — that is the meaning. 'He' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as the primary denotation, is the remainder; by that, the word 'eva' (alone) is justified. 'His chariot' — the chariot of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Here, the double occurrence of the word 'eva' suggests its carry-over everywhere. By that, the no-scope-elsewhere of all marks is also stated. After 'in the <s>Skānda</s>,' the sentence-remainder is: 'the non-otherwise-establishment of the marks is stated.' And thus, the established-conclusion's mark, being stronger in two ways than the prima facie mark which is stronger in one way, justifies the determination — that is the purport. This is stated by way of concession. But in reality, the prima facie mark has no superiority even through no-scope-elsewhere, because being enumerated together with the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) is incompatible with the status of inner controller.
And because of the recurrence of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahmaśabdānugama</s>). // [<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.28] //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.12, verse 5:]

children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.1.12, verse 5:
When through the two modes — abundance and no-scope-elsewhere — even the weaker mark surpasses the prima facie mark that is stronger in both ways, then what more need be said about [the conclusion being established through] the recurrence of the no-scope-elsewhere word '<s>Brahman</s>' — with this purport, he glosses the word '<s>anugama</s>' (recurrence) in another way: '<s>brahma</s>.' // In this context, 'this is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.1); 'the world of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.3); '<s>Brahman</s> [entered] this person' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.4); 'the belly is called <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.4); 'a is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.3.8) — and so forth: from the recurrence of the no-scope-elsewhere word '<s>Brahman</s>' — that is the meaning. 'This' — this <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s essential nature — is '<s>Brahman</s>,' full of all qualities. 'This <s>jīva</s>' is the abode of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. 'This person' — the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> — attained the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. The place where <s>Vāyu</s> dwells — the belly [meaning] the supporting-place of the vast one, which is praise — what is situated in that is the meaning.

uktamākṣipya samādadhatsūtraṃ paṭhitvākṣepāṃśaṃ tāvadvyācaṣṭe - neti // prāṇa ityanuvartate / tathā ca prāṇo viṣṇuriti na yuktam / kutaḥ? 'prāṇo vā ahamasmyṛṣe'; iti vākyena bṛhatīsahasravakturviśvāmitrasyendreṇa prāṇatayā ātmanaḥ svasyaivopadeśādityarthaḥ / prāṇa indra eveti phaloktiḥ / na tūktahetoḥ sādhyoktiḥ / 'prāṇo vāhamasmyṛṣe'; iti vākyaṃ tu 'tamindra uvāca ṛṣe priyaṃ vai me dhāmopāgāḥ varaṃ te dadāmīti / sa hovāca tvāmeva jānīyāmiti / tamindra uvāca'; iti pūrvavākyena saha vyākhyeyam/ tatprakārastu - 'taṃ'; viśvāmitraṃ 'indraḥ'; tadantaḥstho bhagavānuvāca / kimiti? he ṛṣe me priyaṃ dhāmopāgāḥ prāpnuhi / te varaṃ dadāmīti / vaiśabdo 'vadhāraṇe prasiddhau vā/ evaṃ trivāraṃ śaṃsanena dhāmaśabditasālokyaprāptibhagavatpuraprāptisādhanabhagavatprasādaṃ prāptaḥ 'saḥ'; viśvāmitraḥ indrāviṣṭena hariṇā varaṃ te dadānīti punaruktassan uvāca / kimiti? tvāṃ sāmānyataḥ pūrvam ahaṃ jāne / adhunā kīdṛśastvamiti viśeṣato jānīyāmiti / evamuktaḥ 'indraḥ'; tadantargato hariḥ ṛṣiṃ pratyuvāca / kimiti? he ṛṣe ahaṃ prakṛṣṭānandarūpatvātprāṇaśabdavācyo 'smīti / atra vākyasamanvayapakṣe 'smadādiṣūpapadeṣu vihitānāmasmītyāditiṅantapadānāṃ tadvṛtteḥ sulabhatvāditi tattvanirṇayaṭīkārītyā ahamitīndrāntaḥsthena hariṇā svātmano nirdeśādasmīti uttamapuruṣopapattiḥ / pūrvapakṣirītyā śrutyarthastu spaṣṭaḥ / ahaṃ prāṇo 'smīti padānāṃ aheyatvaprakṛṣṭānandatvasaṃhartṛtvajñātṛtvanimittaiḥ bhagavati samanvayapakṣe tu na tadanupapattiriti dhyeyam / nañadhyāhāreṇa siddāntāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti / anugamādityanuvartate / netyāvartate / hiśabdo yata ityarthe / asyoktamiti śeṣaḥ / tathā cetthaṃ tattvapradīpaṭīkoktā yojanā - nāyaṃ prāṇa indraḥ, kintu viṣṇureva / kutaḥ? 'anugamāt'; prāguktaprabalatamaliṅgādeḥ / tathā satyupadeśavirodha iti
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.1.12, verse 6:
Having raised an objection against what was established, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves it, and first explains the objection portion — 'na' (not so). // The word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' carries forward. And thus: it is not proper [to say] <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? Because of the passage 'O sage, I am indeed <s>Prāṇa</s>' — by this sentence, [<s>Indra</s>] who is the speaker of the thousand <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> — [rather,] by <s>Indra</s>, his own self-identification as <s>Prāṇa</s>: that is the meaning. '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Indra</s> alone' — this is the statement of the conclusion. It is not a statement of the thesis to be proved from the stated reason. The passage 'O sage, I am indeed <s>Prāṇa</s>' should be interpreted together with the preceding passage: 'To him <s>Indra</s> said: O sage, you have come to my dear abode; I grant you a boon.' He (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>) said: 'I would know you.' 'To him <s>Indra</s> said' — the manner thereof is as follows: 'Him' — <s>Viśvāmitra</s> — '<s>Indra</s>' — the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>) dwelling within him — said. What? 'O sage, come to my dear abode — attain it. I grant you a boon.' The word 'vai' is for emphasis or for well-known usage. Thus, having praised three times, by the attainment of the abode designated by the word '<s>dhāma</s>' — the attainment of co-residence [with God] — the attainment of <s>Bhagavān's</s> city — [<s>Viśvāmitra</s>] attained the grace of <s>Bhagavān</s> which is the means thereof. 'He' — <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, upon <s>Hari</s>'s saying through <s>Indra</s> again 'I grant you a boon,' said. What? 'I have known You generally before; now I would know You in particular — what kind are You?' Thus addressed, '<s>Indra</s>' — <s>Hari</s> dwelling within him — said to the sage. What? 'O sage, I am the one denoted by the word <s>Prāṇa</s> because of being of the nature of supreme bliss.' Here, in the sentence-coherence view, since in the case of grammatical persons such as 'I' and others, the conjugational endings like 'asmi' (I am) naturally take their referent — from the easy availability of such usage — according to the method of the <s>Tattvanirṇaya Ṭīkā</s>: by the word 'I,' <s>Hari</s> dwelling within <s>Indra</s> designates His own self, hence the first-person form 'asmi' is appropriate. In the prima facie view, however, the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is plain. The words 'I am <s>Prāṇa</s>' are not to be abandoned, because in the established-conclusion view too, the coherence in <s>Bhagavān</s> [is established] through the grounds of indestructibility, supreme bliss, power of dissolution, and omniscience. But there is no impossibility of this — this should be reflected upon. With the interpolated negative particle, he explains the established-conclusion portion — 'na' (not so). The word 'anugamāt' (from recurrence) carries forward. The word 'na' recurs. The word 'hi' is in the sense of 'because.' 'Of this, it has been stated' is the remainder. And thus the construction according to the <s>Tattvapradīpa Ṭīkā</s> is: this <s>Prāṇa</s> is not <s>Indra</s>, but <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Why? 'From the recurrence' — from the previously stated most powerful mark and so forth. That being so, if there is contradiction with the self-identification —

children.text: cet - na, kutaḥ? yato 'tra prakaraṇe svasthitasyaiva prathamaṃ 'prāṇo vā ahamasmyṛṣe'; iti vākyena paramātmatvamuktamindreṇa / tarhyaikyoktivirodha ityapi na / yato 'tra tasyaiva prāṇākhyaparamātmanaḥ 'prāṇastvaṃ prāṇaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni'; ityevamādivākyena 'bahvadhyātmasambandhaḥ'; indrādijīvarūpabahudehasambandhaḥ sarvagatatvameva ṛṣiṃ prati indreṇoktaṃ 'vidyate'; asti natvaikyamata iti / sūtroktasambandhabāhulyaṃ sambandhini paryavasyatītyāśayena
children.translated_text: [we reply:] no. Why? Because 'here' in the context, to the one standing within Himself, first by the passage 'O sage, I am indeed <s>Prāṇa</s>,' the supreme-self-hood was stated by <s>Indra</s>. Then, is there not contradiction with the statement of identity? — that too is not so. Because of that very <s>Prāṇa</s>-named <s>Paramātman</s>, by the passage 'You are <s>Prāṇa</s>; <s>Prāṇa</s> is all beings' and similar sentences, the 'abundance of relation to the individual self' — the connection with many bodies in the form of <s>Indra</s> and other <s>jīvas</s> — that is, the all-pervasiveness alone — is 'stated' to the sage by <s>Indra</s>; 'it exists,' but not identity: thus. He indicates that the abundance of connection stated in the <s>sūtra</s> resolves into the one possessing the connection —

children.text: bahvityuktam / bhūmaśabdasya bhāvavācitve 'pi bhāvabhavitrorabhedāt bhavitari prayogaḥ / sūtre tu paranipāta ārṣaḥ / athavā - adhikaścāsāvātmā cādhyātmā tasya sambandhaḥ bahuścāsāvadhyātmasambandhaśceti vigrahaḥ / tathā ca 'hi'; yataḥ 'atra'; indre 'bahuḥ'; bahulaḥ paramātmasambandhaḥ sannidhiviśeṣo vidyata ityarthaḥ / vidyata ityanantaraṃ tadapekṣayāyam upadeśo na svāpekṣayeti śeṣaḥ / tathācendre tātkālikeśvarasannidhānaviśeṣābhiprāyā 'prāṇo vā aham'; ityuktiḥ, na svāpekṣayeti nopadeśavirodha iti bhāvaḥ / kuto na svāpekṣayetyataḥ prāṇastavamityādyāha / yojanā tu - hi yasmāt 'prāṇastvam'; ityādi vākyenāsya prāṇasya 'bahvadhyātmasambandhaḥ'; adhyātmatvenāntaryāmitvena indrādirūpabahudehasambandhaḥ sarvagatatvamuktaṃ vidyate na caitadatra jīvaviśeṣendre vidyate yujyate tasmāditi / prathamapakṣe 'yasyātmā śarīram'; (mādhyandina) iti śruterindrādīnāṃ viṣṇudehatvādaikyavyapadeśaḥ śarīraśarīribhāvanibandhana iti jñāpanāyādhyātmetyuktiḥ / anena bṛhatīsahasravakturviśvāmitrasya taṃ pratīndreṇa prāṇatayātmopadeśādayaṃ prāṇo na viṣṇuḥ, kintu indra eveti cet - nendro 'yaṃ prāṇaḥ, kintu viṣṇureva / kutaḥ? anugamāt prāguktabalatamaliṅgādeḥ / na copadeśavirodhaḥ / yato 'yamindragatādhyātmaviṣaya eva / kutaḥ? hi yasmādasmin prakaraṇe 'dhyātmasambandhabhūmā / atrādhyātmasambandhaśabdenātmādhikāre vartamānamiti / adhiścāsau ātmā ceti dehaḥ paramātmā cocyate / tathā ca yasmādadhyātmano viṣṇorindraviśvāmitrādidehasambandha ukto 'sti tasmāt / athavā - hi yasmāt asminnindre adhyātmasambandhabhūmā - adhirīśvare - adhikasyātmanaḥ paramātmanaḥ sambandhasyāveśasya bhūmā bāhulyaṃ vidyate tasmādupadeśasya sannihitaparamātmaviṣayatvopapteriti bhāvaḥ / tadapi kutaḥ? hi yasmāt asmin prakaraṇe 'dhyātmasambandhabhūmoktaḥ tasmāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: 'bahu' (many) is said [in the sūtra]. Even though the word '<s>bhūma</s>' (abundance) denotes a quality, since there is no difference between a quality and its possessor, it is used for the possessor. In the <s>sūtra</s>, the reverse word-order (<s>paranipāta</s>) is archaic (<s>ārṣa</s>). Or alternatively: '<s>adhyātmā</s>' — one who is superior and is the self — is the <s>adhyātma</s>; his connection is the <s>adhyātmasambandha</s>; it is abundant and it is the <s>adhyātmasambandha</s> — thus the compound analysis. And thus, 'hi' — because — 'here' — in <s>Indra</s> — 'abundant' — plentiful — is the connection with the <s>Paramātman</s>, that is, special proximity 'exists': that is the meaning. After 'exists,' the remainder is: with reference to that, this teaching is [given], not with reference to himself. And thus, <s>Indra</s>'s statement 'I am indeed <s>Prāṇa</s>' is with the intention of the special presence of the Lord in <s>Indra</s> at that time, not with reference to himself — hence there is no contradiction with the teaching: that is the purport. Why not with reference to himself? — to this he presents 'You are <s>Prāṇa</s>' and the rest. The construction is: 'hi' — because — by the passage 'You are <s>Prāṇa</s>' and so forth, of this <s>Prāṇa</s>, the 'abundance of relation to the individual self' — the connection with many bodies such as <s>Indra</s> and others as inner controller — the all-pervasiveness is stated; and this does not exist in, nor is fitting for, a particular <s>jīva</s> such as <s>Indra</s>; therefore [the <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. In the first interpretation, [the teaching] 'the self is the body of all' — by this <s>Śruti</s>, since <s>Indra</s> and others are bodies of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the statement of identity is grounded in the body-soul relationship — to make this known, the word '<s>adhyātma</s>' is used. By this, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, the speaker of the thousand <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses, [received] through <s>Indra</s> the self-identification as <s>Prāṇa</s> — if [it be said] that this <s>Prāṇa</s> is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> but <s>Indra</s> alone — [we reply:] this <s>Prāṇa</s> is not <s>Indra</s>, but <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Why? From the recurrence of the previously stated most powerful marks and so forth. And there is no contradiction with the teaching. Because this pertains to the individual self dwelling within <s>Indra</s>. Why? 'Hi' — because — in this context, abundance of relation to the individual self [exists]. Here, by the word '<s>adhyātmasambandha</s>,' [it is indicated that] 'what is current in the topic of the self' — [i.e.,] the self and what is superior is the body, and the <s>Paramātman</s> is also called [thus]. And thus, since the connection of the superior self — the <s>Paramātman</s> — with the bodies of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, and others is stated, therefore. Or alternatively: 'hi' — because — in this <s>Indra</s>, the abundance of the connection of the individual self — '<s>adhi</s>' [meaning] 'in the lord' — the connection, that is, the possession (<s>āveśa</s>), of the superior self, the <s>Paramātman</s>, is abundant — plentiful — 'exists'; therefore, by the fitness of the teaching being about the <s>Paramātman</s> who is proximate: that is the purport. And whence [is that]? 'Hi' — because — in this context, the abundance of the connection of the individual self is 'stated' — therefore, thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
But the teaching is from the standpoint of scripture (<s>śāstradṛṣṭi</s>), like <s>Vāmadeva</s>. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.30 |
Scripture [teaches that He is] the inner controller.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.1.12, verse 7:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.7:
nanu yadi prāṇaśabdenendreṇāpi viṣṇureva svātmādisarvagatatayocyate tarhi mayi prāṇa iti nirdeśaḥ syāt / na tvahamiti / viṣṇāvahamityādirūpopadeśāyogādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhati - śāstreti // turevārtho 'pyarthaḥ, yatha ityarthe smṛtisūcakaśca / yujyata iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca yato 'pi prāṇasya viṣṇutve 'pyupadeśaḥ prāṇo vāham ityevaṃrūpo yujyate, ato na tadanupapattiḥ / kathamayaṃ yujyate? yato 'yamupadeśaḥ 'śāstradṛṣṭyā'; śāsti sarvamiti śāstraṃ antaryāmī bhagavān, taddṛṣṭyā tadapekṣayaiva pravṛtto na tvaikyena / na cāntaryāmiṇi ahamādiprayogādarśanāt tadayogaḥ / yato 'vāmadevavat'; tatkartṛkaprayogavat / yathā vāmadevo nāma ṛṣiḥ antaryāmivivakṣayā 'ahaṃ manurabhavam'; iti svasmin ahaṃmanvādiśabdān prayuyuje / tathā ayamapyupadeśo yujyate ata iti sūtrayojanāmabhiprayan sautraśāstrapadaṃ vyācaṣṭe - śāstramiti / viṣṇuriti śeṣaḥ / tathācāntaryāmī viṣṇariha śāstrapadenokta ityarthaḥ / antaryāmīti prakṛtābhiprāyeṇa / yadvā - śāsti prerayati sarvāniti vyutapattyā antaryāmītyetadeva śāstramityasya vyākhyānaṃ bhavatīti
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.7:
Now, if by the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' too, through <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is said to pervade one's self and all else, then the statement should be 'in me is <s>Prāṇa</s>' — not 'I am [<s>Prāṇa</s>].' Since the teaching in the form 'I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>' and the like is unjustified — anticipating this objection, he reads the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>śāstra</s>' (scripture/ruler). // The word 'tu' too has the meaning of 'api' (also), and is indicative of <s>Smṛti</s> in the sense of 'just as.' 'Is justified' is the remainder. And thus: since, even when <s>Prāṇa</s> is [identified as] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the teaching in the form '<s>Prāṇa</s> — or rather, I — am [that]' is justified, therefore there is no impossibility of that. How is this justified? Because this teaching is 'from the standpoint of the ruler' (<s>śāstradṛṣṭyā</s>); '<s>śāstra</s>' (that which rules all) is the <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), the Lord; from His perspective, with reference to Him alone, [the teaching] has proceeded — not through identity. Nor is there an impropriety because of non-observation of the usage of 'I' and the like with reference to the inner controller. Because 'like <s>Vāmadeva</s>'; like the usage made by him. Just as the <s>ṛṣi</s> named <s>Vāmadeva</s>, intending [to speak of] the inner controller, used the words 'I,' '<s>Manu</s>' and the like with reference to himself [saying] 'I was <s>Manu</s>, I was <s>Sūrya</s>.' Likewise, this teaching too is justified — thus intending the syntactic connection of the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains the word '<s>śāstra</s>' occurring in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>śāstram</s>' (the ruler). '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' is the remainder. And thus, the <s>antaryāmin</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> is here denoted by the word '<s>śāstra</s>': this is the meaning. 'The <s>antaryāmin</s>' is said with the intention of the subject under discussion.

children.text: nāpadārthatvaśaṅkāvakāśaḥ / ata eva bhāgavate dhyeye 'ntaryāmiṇyeva śāstraśabdaprayogaḥ/ aitareyabhāṣye 'śāsturantaryāmiṇaḥ'; iti śāstṛśabdaṃ mūlīkṛtya vyākhyāne 'pi, tadanusāreṇa ca tattvapradīpe śāsturantaryāmiṇo viṣṇoriti vyākhyānepi nāsya tadvirodhaḥ śaṅkyaḥ, yatastatparyāyaśabdavyākhyānenaiva śāstraśabdo vyākhyāto bhavatītyāśayena śāstraśabdaparyāyaśāstṛśabdo vyākhyāyate / yadvā - śāstraśabde śāstṛ a ityavayavavibhāgamabhipretya śāstrityaṃśasyāntaryāmiṇa ityanena aśabdasya viṣṇorityanena ca vyākhyātattvāt, atra tu avayavavibhāgamavivakṣitvā śāstramityakhaṇḍapadasyāntaryāmiti vyākhyānāt tadanukūlatayā 'saṃvicchāstram'; iti vacanopanyāsācca na virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively — by the etymological derivation 'He who rules, impels all' (<s>śāsti prerayati sarvān</s>), the very [meaning] '<s>antaryāmin</s>' becomes the explanation of '<s>śāstra</s>' — so there is no scope for the doubt of irrelevance. For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, the word '<s>śāstra</s>' is used with reference to the <s>antaryāmin</s> who is to be meditated upon. Even when, in the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s>, the explanation is based on the word '<s>śāstṛ</s>' (ruler) — 'of the ruler, the <s>antaryāmin</s>' — and even when, following that, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, the explanation is 'of the ruler, the <s>antaryāmin</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — no contradiction with this [explanation] should be suspected, since the word '<s>śāstra</s>' is explained through the explanation of its synonymous word '<s>śāstṛ</s>': with this intention, the synonymous word '<s>śāstṛ</s>' of the word '<s>śāstra</s>' is explained. Alternatively — intending the morphological analysis of the word '<s>śāstra</s>' as '<s>śāstṛ</s>' + 'a,' the portion '<s>śāstṛ</s>' has been explained by '<s>antaryāmin</s>' and the portion 'a' by '<s>Viṣṇu</s>'; but here, not intending the morphological analysis, since the undivided word '<s>śāstra</s>' is explained as '<s>antaryāmin</s>,' and in conformity with that, because of the citation of the passage '<s>saṃvicchāstram</s>' (consciousness is the ruler) — there is no contradiction.
'Consciousness is the ruler, the supreme abode' (<s>saṃvicchāstraṃ paraṃ padam</s>) — thus indeed [it is stated] in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.8:
antaryāmiṇo viṣṇoḥ śāstrapadavācyatve pramāṇamāha - saṃviditi // prathamaskandhe vyāsaṃ prati nāradavākyamidam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.8:
He cites the authority for the denotability of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by the word '<s>śāstra</s>': '<s>saṃvit</s>' (consciousness). // This is a statement of <s>Nārada</s> addressed to <s>Vyāsa</s> in the first <s>skandha</s> (book).

children.text:
svapno māyāgrahaḥ śayyā jāgradābhāsa ātmanaḥ /
nāmarūpakriyāvṛttiḥ saṃvicchāstraṃ paraṃ padam // iti /
children.translated_text:
'Dream is the impressions (<s>māyā-vāsanā</s>); sleep is the bed; waking is the appearance of the self;
engagement in name, form, and action — consciousness is the ruler, the supreme abode.'

children.text:
asyārthaḥ - ātmano jīvasya māyāvāsanākhyasaṃskāropādānakavastujñānarūpaḥ
svapnaḥ / agrahaḥ jāgratsvapnaviṣayajñānarahitā śayyā suṣuptiḥ nāmarūpakriyāsu śabdārthakarmasu vṛttirvyāvṛttiryanyāḥ sā / ābhāsaḥ pratyayaḥ saṃjñādiviṣayajñānarūpo jāgracca / āhatyaitadavasthātrayaṃ yasmādātmanaḥ parabrahmaṇo bhavati, tatsaṃvit sarvaviṣayaka-
children.translated_text: The meaning of this is: 'Dream' (<s>svapna</s>) of the self, the <s>jīva</s>, is the cognition of objects whose material cause is the latent impressions called <s>māyā-vāsanā</s>. 'Non-apprehension' (<s>agrahaḥ</s>) — the 'bed' (<s>śayyā</s>), that is, deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>), devoid of cognition pertaining to waking and dream states. 'Engagement' (<s>vṛttiḥ</s>) in 'names, forms, and actions' — in words, meanings, and deeds — is that 'disengagement' (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) which is distinct [from the other states]. 'Appearance' (<s>ābhāsa</s>) — cognition in the form of knowledge pertaining to designations and the like — is 'waking' (<s>jāgrat</s>). Taking together this triad of states — since it arises from the self, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — that '<s>saṃvit</s>' (consciousness) is of the nature of complete, all-encompassing

children.text: yathārthajñānarūpaṃ sarvajñaṃ vā / śāstraṃ sarvaniyantṛ, paraṃ uttamaṃ padaṃ sadbhiḥ prāpyaṃ brahma aham acintayamiti / bhāgavata ityanantaraṃ 'prayogāt'; iti śeṣaḥ / asyāntaryāmītyanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: veridical knowledge, or is omniscient. '<s>Śāstra</s>' (ruler) — the controller of all. 'The supreme' (<s>param</s>) — the highest 'abode' (<s>padam</s>) — the <s>Brahman</s> to be attained by the wise — I contemplated: [this is the meaning]. After '<s>bhāgavate</s>' (in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>), 'because of the usage' (<s>prayogāt</s>) is the remainder. Its syntactic connection is with '<s>antaryāmī</s>' (the inner controller).
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is called by each and every name, because of being the ruler of all;
there is nowhere any name whatsoever that exists apart from Him, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>).
Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.9:
nanvantaryāmiṇi ahamādiprayogaḥ kathaṃ sambhavatītyāśaṅkyāṃ tatra tuśabdasūcitāṃ smṛtimevāha - tattaditi/ viṣṇuḥ 'tattannātmā'; anyaparatvena prasiddhāhamādināmnocyate iti / anena tasyāntaryāmiṇi viṣṇau vidvadrūḍhirdarśitā / 'sarvaśāstṛtvahetutaḥ'; sarvaniyantṛtvanimitteneti / anena mahāyogo darśitaḥ / tatra tasya svātantryanimittokteḥ / anena paramata ivāsmanmate 'pi lākṣaṇikatvaṃ parihṛtam 'puruṣottamam'; antaryāmiṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ 'ṛte'; vinā, anyatra 'kvāpi'; jīvādau 'kiṃ cit'; ahamādirūpaṃ 'nāma'; vācakatayā nāstīti / anena harau paramamukhyatā anyatra kevalamukhyatā coktā / anyathā na kvāpīti sāmānyaniṣedhāyogāt / atrāhamādiśabdāḥ pratyagādivācitvena prasiddhāḥ, pratyagādayaśca sarvadā piṇḍībhūtāḥ, tānavivekenājñāḥ kevalajīvādau prayuñjate dahati śabdamiva kāṣṭhe / prājñāstu mukhyāmukhyavivekavanto hyamukhmarthamanādṛtya mukhyārthe harau prayuñjataiti tattvanirṇaṭīkoktamanusandheyam / 'pādme'; ityanantaram 'antaryāmiṇyahamādipadānāṃ mukhyatvokteḥ śāstradṛṣṭyā ahamādyupadeśo yukta eva'; iti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.9:
Now, how can the usage of 'I' and the like be possible with reference to the inner controller? — anticipating this doubt, which is indicated by the word 'tu' [in the <s>sūtra</s>], he cites the very <s>Smṛti</s>: '<s>tattad</s>' (each and every). <s>Viṣṇu</s> is 'called' (<s>ucyate</s>) by 'each and every name' — by names well-known as referring to others, such as 'I' and the like. By this, His <s>vidvadrūḍhi</s> (learned conventional usage) in the <s>antaryāmin</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> is shown. 'Because of being the ruler of all' (<s>sarvaśāstṛtvahetutaḥ</s>) — because of the ground of being the controller of all. By this, the <s>mahāyoga</s> (great metaphorical connection) is shown — since in that [usage], the ground of His independence is stated. By this, the secondary usage (<s>lākṣaṇikatva</s>), as held in the opponent's view, is refuted in our doctrine as well. 'The Supreme Person' (<s>Puruṣottamam</s>) — the <s>antaryāmin</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'apart from' (<s>ṛte</s>) — without, 'anywhere' (<s>kvāpi</s>) elsewhere — in the <s>jīva</s> and the like — 'any' (<s>kiñcit</s>) — [name] in the form of 'I' and the like — 'name' (<s>nāma</s>) — as a denoter, does not exist. By this, the absolutely primary denotation (<s>paramamukhyatā</s>) in <s>Hari</s> and merely primary denotation (<s>kevalamukhyatā</s>) elsewhere are stated. Otherwise, the general negation 'not anywhere' would be unjustified. Here, the words 'I' and the like are well-known as denoting the individual self (<s>pratyak</s>) and the like; and the individual self and the like are always composite entities (<s>piṇḍībhūtāḥ</s>); the ignorant, not discriminating, use [these words] for the <s>jīva</s> and the like alone — like [using] the word 'burns' for firewood. But the wise, possessing the discrimination between primary and non-primary, disregarding the non-primary meaning, use [these words] with reference to <s>Hari</s> as the primary [referent] — this is stated in the <s>Tattvānirṇaya Ṭīkā</s> and should be kept in mind. After 'in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>,' the remainder of the sentence is: 'since the primary denotation of the words "I" and the like is stated with reference to the <s>antaryāmin</s>, the teaching from the standpoint of the ruler is justified indeed.'
'I was <s>Manu</s>, I was <s>Sūrya</s>' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 4.26.1) — like [the usage in] such [passages]. // 30 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.10:
nanvantaryāmiṇi ahamādiprayogādarśanāt tadayoga ityāśaṅkāṃ sūtroktadṛṣṭāntavivaraṇena pariharati - ahamiti // 'ahaṃ'; vāmadevasaṃjñakaṛṣyantaryāmī tattadantaryāmitayā manuḥ sūryaścābhavamiti ṛṅmantrārthaḥ / ādipadena 'ahaṃ kakṣīvānṛṣirasmi vipro 'haṃ kutsam'; (ṛ.4-26-1.) ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / 'ityādivat'; evamādiprayogavadityasya 'śāstradṛṣṭyopadeśaḥ'; ityanenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.10:
Now, since there is non-observation of the usage of 'I' and the like with reference to the <s>antaryāmin</s>, that is unjustified — he resolves this doubt through the elaboration of the example stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>aham</s>' (I). // 'I' — the <s>antaryāmin</s> of the <s>ṛṣi</s> named <s>Vāmadeva</s>, by virtue of being the inner controller of each of those [entities] — 'was <s>Manu</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>' — this is the meaning of the <s>Ṛg</s> <s>mantra</s>. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the passage 'I am the <s>ṛṣi</s> <s>Kakṣīvān</s>, the learned one; I am <s>Kutsa</s>' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 4.26.1) and the like are included. 'Like such [usages]' (<s>ityādivat</s>) — 'like the usage of this kind' — its syntactic connection is with 'the teaching from the standpoint of the ruler' (<s>śāstradṛṣṭyopadeśaḥ</s>).

Raising the objection of repetition, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves it, and first explains the objection-portion: '<s>jīva</s>' (the individual self). 'It is stated' is

children.text: uktamiti ca śeṣaḥ / saṃvādo vivādaḥ kalahaḥ prāṇasya prāṇaissaha saṃvāda iti vigrahaḥ / tathā ca yasmādatra prakaraṇe 'taṃ śataṃ varṣāṇyabhyārcat tasmācchataṃ varṣāṇi puruṣāyuṣo bhavanti'; (ai.ā. 2-2-1.) ityanena yacchatasaṃvatsaraparyantaṃ prāṇasya jīvadehe 'vastānahetukaṃ śatāyuṣṭvarūpaṃ jīvaliṅgamuktaṃ tat 'tāvanti śatasaṃvatsarasyāhnāṃ sahasrāṇi bhavanti'; ityādinā bahuṣu sthaleṣu anusandhīyate / yasmācca 'tā ahiṃsantāhamukthamahamukthamasmi'; (ai.ā. 2-1-4.) iti vākyena prāṇasya prāṇairindriyaiḥ saha saṃvādarūpamukhyaprāṇaliṅgamuktam / yasmāccādipadagṛhītaṃ 'prāṇo vaṃśa iti sthaviraḥ śākalyastadyathā śālāvaṃśe sarve 'nye vaṃśāḥ samāhitāssyuḥ evamasmin prāṇe cakṣuśśrotraṃ mano vāgindriyāṇi śarīraṃ sarva ātmā samāhitaḥ'; (ai.ā. 3-2-1-1.) iti vākyena sarvajīvendriyadehadhārakatvarūpaliṅgaṃ coktamasti tasmādayaṃ prāṇo na viṣṇuḥ, kintu jīvamukhyaprāṇāveveti yojanā / yadyapi 'tasmācchataṃ varṣāṇi puruṣāyuṣo bhavanti'; (ai.ā. 2-2-1.) iti śatāyuṣṭvaliṅgapratipādakavākyamevodāharaṇīyaṃ, na tu 'tāvanti'; iti vākyam / tathāpi liṅgasya bahuṣu sthaleṣu anugamo 'stīti jñāpanāyopaniṣado jīvaliṅge tātparyamastīti jñāpayitum anusandhivākyamevodāhṛtam / siddhānte śrutyarthastu - puruṣāyuṣaḥ śatasaṃvatsarasyāhnāṃ sahasrāṇi śatasaṃvatsarāntaḥpraviṣṭāharniyāmakasūryagatabhagavatpuruṣarūpāṇi tāvanti sahasrāṇi / kiyanti? bṛhatīsahasragatākṣarāṇāṃ vācyāni puṃrūpāṇi yāvanti sahasrāṇi tāvanti / tathā ca tāni ṣaṭtriṃśatsahasrāṇi sampannāni bhavanti / 'tāḥ'; cakṣurādidevatāḥ 'ahiṃsanta'; vivādamakurvan / kinviti? ahamasya caturmukhadehasyoktho 'smi utthāpako 'smīti /
