And thus, since in this context the passage 'he worshipped him for a hundred years, therefore a hundred years is the lifespan of a person' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.2.1) — the mark of the <s>jīva</s> in the form of a hundred-year lifespan, caused by <s>Prāṇa</s>'s dwelling in the body for a hundred years, is stated — and [since] that is 'followed up' (<s>anusandhīyate</s>) in many places by [the passage] 'so many are the thousands of days of a hundred years.' And since by the passage 'they did not quarrel; I am the <s>uktha</s> (hymn), I am the <s>uktha</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.4), the mark of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> in the form of a dispute of <s>Prāṇa</s> with the <s>prāṇas</s> (senses) is stated. And since the mark included by the word 'ādi' — '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the ridge-pole; just as in a house all other beams rest upon the ridge-pole, so in this <s>Prāṇa</s>, the eye, the ear, the mind, speech, the senses, the body — the entire self rests' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.1.1) — the mark in the form of sustaining all <s>jīvas</s>, senses, and bodies is also stated — therefore this <s>Prāṇa</s> is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but rather the <s>jīva</s> and the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> alone: this is the syntactic connection. Even though the passage 'therefore a hundred years is the lifespan of a person' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.2.1) that teaches the mark of a hundred-year lifespan should have been cited as the example, not the passage 'so many' — nevertheless, to convey that the mark is followed up in many places, and to make known that the <s>Upaniṣad</s> has its purport in the mark of the <s>jīva</s>, the follow-up passage itself is cited as the example. In the established conclusion, however, the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is: the thousands of days of a hundred-year lifespan of a person — [these are] the forms of the Lord (<s>Bhagavat-puruṣa</s>) who has entered into the suns that govern the days within the hundred years — so many thousands. How many? As many thousands as the denotata — the forms of the Person — contained in the thousands of syllables of a <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter]. And thus those amount to thirty-six thousand. 'They' (<s>tāḥ</s>) — the deities of the eye and the like — 'quarreled' (<s>ahiṃsanta</s>) — entered into a dispute. About what? 'I am the <s>uktha</s> (hymn) of this four-faced body — I am its uplifter.'
No — [He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>], because [He pervades] internally, externally, and everywhere — and because of the three-fold nature of meditation being resorted to here.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.12:
parihārāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti // prāṇo viṣṇurneti na, kintu viṣṇurevāyaṃ, na jīvādirityarthaḥ / kuto netyatastatra prāguktānugamahetvanuṣaṅgaṃ, na coktajīvamukhyaprāṇaliṅgavirodha ityatastatrahetutvena yataḥ śāstradṛṣṭyā tvayamupadeśaḥ ityasyānuṣaṅgaṃ, kimarthamantaryāmīti praśnasyāntarupāstyarthamiti parihāraṃ cābhipretya na copāsane 'vāntarabhedābhāva iti codyottaratvena pravṛttam 'upāsā'; iti sūtrāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - antariti / gatatvenetyasyāntarbahissarvaśabdaiḥ pratyekaṃ sambandhaḥ / itiśabdaḥ prakārārthaḥ / tathā ca dehāntargatatvena tadbahirgatatvena sarvagatatveneti prakāreṇa 'upāsātraividhyāt'; bhagavadupāsanasya trividhatvādityarthaḥ/ nanu tathāpi kathanaṃ vyarthaṃ vastuta upāsanātraividhyasyehānuktasyāntaryāmikathanāprayojakatvādityataḥ pravṛttam 'āśritatvāt'; ityaṃśaṃ caśabdādhyāhāreṇa vyācaṣṭe - iheti / etatprakaraṇe uktatvādityarthaḥ / upāsātraividhyasyeti vipariṇāmenātrānvīyate / co
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.12:
He explains the resolution-portion: 'na' (no). // [The objection that] '<s>Prāṇa</s> is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — no, rather this is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not the <s>jīva</s> and the like: this is the meaning. Why 'no'? — therefore, carrying forward the previously stated reason of the 'follow-up' [of marks], and [stating] that the stated marks of the <s>jīva</s> and the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> are not contradictory — and therefore carrying forward the reason 'because the teaching is from the standpoint of the ruler' — and intending the question 'for what purpose is [the mention of] the <s>antaryāmin</s>?' along with the resolution 'for the purpose of inner meditation' — and [intending] that the objection-and-reply has proceeded as 'there is no distinction of internal subdivision in meditation' — he explains the <s>sūtra</s>-portion '<s>upāsā</s>' (meditation): '<s>antar</s>' (internally). The word '<s>gatatvena</s>' (by pervading) has a separate connection with each of the words 'internal,' 'external,' and 'all.' The word 'iti' has the meaning of 'in such manner.' And thus: by pervading internally within the body, by pervading externally outside the body, and by pervading everywhere — 'because of the three-fold nature of meditation' — because the worship of the Lord is of three kinds: this is the meaning. Now, even so, the statement is purposeless, since the three-fold nature of meditation, being unstated here, cannot serve as the ground for the mention of the <s>antaryāmin</s> — therefore, with the supply of the word 'ca' (and), he explains the portion 'because of being resorted to' (<s>āśritatvāt</s>): 'here' (<s>iha</s>). Because of being stated in this context: this is the meaning. 'Of the three-fold nature of meditation' is connected here by inversion. 'Ca' (and)

is for the accumulation of the reason and the supporting reason. And thus, since the mention of the <s>antaryāmin</s> for the purpose of the inner meditation — which is one of the three-fold [types] stated here — is justified: this is the import.

children.text:
'sa etameva sīmānaṃ vidāryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata'; (ai.ā. 2-4-3.)
'sa etameva puruṣaṃ brahma tatamamapaśyat'; (ai.ā. 2-4-3.)
'etaddha sma vai tadvidvānāha mahidāsa aitareyaḥ'; (ai.ā.2-1-8.)
ityādinā /

BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.13:
atropāsanātraividhyamucyata ityatrāpi kiṃ liṅgamityata āha - sa iti / 'saḥ'; vāsudevo bhagavān 'etameva sīmānaṃ'; śiromadhyaṃ vidāryaiva 'etayā dvārā'; suṣumnānāḍyā 'prāpadyata'; prāptaḥ / caturmukhahṛdayamiti śeṣaḥ / anena bhagavato dehāntaḥpraveśokteḥ ukteścopāsanārthatvāt antarupāstiruktā bhavati / 'saḥ'; caturmukhadehe prākprapadābhyāmantaḥ praviṣṭo nārāyaṇaḥ 'etameva puruṣaṃ'; vyāsakṛṣṇakapilādirūpamātmānam ātataguṇaṃ svasvarūpabhūtamādānādikartāraṃ vā / tatamaṃ 'lopaḥ samāne'; iti sūtrāttalopaḥ / tamabarthe mapratyayo vā / tathā ca tatamaṃ atiśayena vyāptaṃ niravadhikavyāptimantaṃ 'brahma'
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.12.13: Here, regarding the statement that the threefold nature of worship is being taught, to the question 'what is the indicatory mark?', he says — 'saḥ' etc. 'He,' <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vāsudeva</s>, 'having split open this very boundary,' the crown of the head, 'through this door,' through the <s>suṣumnā</s> <s>nāḍī</s> (central channel), 'reached' — that is, arrived at. The completion is: the heart of <s>Caturmukha</s> (four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>). By this, since the entry of <s>Bhagavān</s> into the interior of the body is stated, and since the statement serves the purpose of worship, internal worship (<s>antarupāsti</s>) is established. 'He,' <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who entered from the toes into the body of <s>Caturmukha</s>, 'this very person' — His own form as <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, etc., the Self endowed with extended qualities, or the agent of taking up, etc. The word <s>tatama</s> — by the <s>sūtra</s> 'there is elision when similar,' the 'ta' is elided. Or the suffix 'ma' is in the sense of the superlative. Thus <s>tatama</s> means supremely pervading, having unlimited pervasion — '<s>Brahman</s>'

children.text: guṇapūrṇam 'apaśyat'; tadguṇakatayā tadrūpaṃ dadarśetyarthaḥ / kecittu - takāra eva vyāptyabhidhāyaka ityāhuḥ / anena sarvagatatvaṃ tathopāsanārthamuktam / 'tadetat'; prakṛtaṃ sarvaṃ 'vidvān'; jānannaitareyaḥ itarāyā apatyaṃ pumān viśālasaṃjñāt ṛṣeḥ utpannaḥ aitareyaḥ / 'mahidāso'; mahino mahātmāno devāḥ dāsabhūtāḥ yasyāsau bhagavānāhetyarthaḥ / hasmavaiśabdāḥ prasiddhidyotakāḥ / atra bahirupāstyarthaṃ mahidāsa āheti bahirupāstiruktā bhavati / na ca vācyamatra svarūpamātramucyate, nopāsanārthamiti / upāsanāṃ vinoktiprayojanābhāvāt / ityādinetyasyetyādināvākyenopāsanātraividhyasyāśritatvādarthāduktatvādityanvayaḥ / ādiśabdena 'taṃ prapadābhyāṃ prāpadyata brahmemaṃ puruṣametasyāmetam'; (ai.ā. 2-1-4.) ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / nanu 'etaddhasmavai tadvidvānāha hiraṇyadanvaidaḥ'; (ai.ā. 2-1-5.) itivanmahidāso 'pi ṛṣitvenocyatāmiti cenna / asyāḥ upaniṣadaḥ aitareyasaṃjñayaivetarāputrasya mahidāsasya ṛṣitvasiddhyā taduktervyarthatvāt /
children.translated_text: endowed with all qualities, 'he saw' — the meaning is: he perceived its form as consisting of those qualities. Some, however, say that the syllable 'ta' itself denotes pervasion. By this, the all-pervasiveness and worship thereof are stated. 'This,' all that is under discussion, 'the knower,' the one who knows — <s>Aitareya</s>, the male offspring of <s>Itarā</s>, born from the sage named <s>Viśāla</s>, is <s>Aitareya</s>. '<s>Mahidāsa</s>' — the great ones (<s>mahina</s>), the exalted gods, became servants (<s>dāsa</s>) of whom — that is, <s>Bhagavān</s> said this. The particles <s>ha</s>, <s>sma</s>, and <s>vai</s> indicate well-known fact. Here, for the purpose of external worship, '<s>Mahidāsa</s> said' — thus external worship (<s>bahirupāsti</s>) is established. And one should not object that only the essential nature is being stated here, not for the purpose of worship — because without worship there would be no purpose in the statement. The construction is: by this and such sentences, the threefold nature of worship has been relied upon and hence stated. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), passages such as 'he reached him through the toes, this <s>Brahman</s>, this person, of this one, this' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.4) are included. Now, if one objects that just as '<s>Hiraṇyadanva</s> who knew this said' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.5), <s>Mahidāsa</s> too should be spoken of as a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) — no, because since the <s>ṛṣi</s>-hood of <s>Mahidāsa</s>, son of <s>Itarā</s>, is already established by this <s>Upaniṣad</s> bearing the name <s>Aitareya</s>, stating it again would be redundant.
The one named <s>Mahidāsa</s> was born from <s>Itarā</s> by the power of her austerities.
He is directly <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, who composed the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> treatise.
Thus in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.14:
tathāpi mahidāsasya viṣṇutvaṃ kuto jñāyata ityata āha - mahidāseti // 'jajñe'; vyakto babhūva / 'sa ca'; mahidāsaḥ -
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.12.14: Even so, to the question 'how is the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-nature of <s>Mahidāsa</s> known?', he says — '<s>Mahidāsa</s>' etc. 'Was born' — became manifest. 'And he,' <s>Mahidāsa</s> —
<s>Mahidāsa</s>, the <s>Aitareya</s>, who appears in the <s>Bahvṛca Upaniṣad</s>,
is directly <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself; there was one sage of that name.

children.text: iti chāndogyabhāṣye anantaroktabhagavadanyaḥ tatsaṃjñaketarāputraḥ ṛṣiratra na vivakṣitaḥ, kintu / yo 'vaiṣṇavaṃ'; viṣṇuviṣayaṃ 'tantraṃ'; granthaṃ 'vyadhāt'; nirmame / yadvā - 'tantraṃ'; pañcarātraṃ vyadhāt nāradādibhyo vyācakhyau / yaśca 'sākṣāt'; svayaṃ 'bhagavān'; pūrṇajñānādimān 'viṣṇuḥ'; tadavatārabhūtaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sa evātra vivakṣita ityāha - sākṣāditi/ brahmāṇḍe purāṇa ityasyāśritatvādityanenānvayaḥ / mahidāsasya viṣṇutvoktiriti tadarthaḥ / tena caśabdānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Chāndogya Bhāṣya</s>. The <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) who is other than <s>Bhagavān</s> mentioned just previously, the son of <s>Itarā</s> bearing that same name, is not intended here; rather, it is he who 'composed the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>' — pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'treatise' — a text — 'composed' — created. Or alternatively, 'treatise' means the <s>Pañcarātra</s>, which he 'composed' — expounded to <s>Nārada</s> and others. And he who is 'directly' — himself — '<s>Bhagavān</s>' — possessing complete knowledge and other attributes — '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' — the previously mentioned one who is an <s>avatāra</s> (incarnation) of that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], he alone is intended here, as stated — 'directly' etc. The construction with the preceding [<s>sūtra</s>] is: because the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> has been relied upon and thus stated. The purport is: the statement of the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-nature of <s>Mahidāsa</s>. And thereby the connection with the particle 'ca' (and).
And because of the fitness of persons for their respective forms of worship.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.15:
nanvekavidhopāsanayā sarveṣāṃ brahmāparokṣasambhavātkimupāsātraividhyena ityataḥ pravṛttaṃ 'tadyogāt'; iti sūtraśeṣaṃ vyācaṣṭe - tattaditi // upāsanetyanena puruṣāṇāmityanena ca tadityasyāvṛttiḥ sūcitā / caḥ samuccaye / tathā ca teṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ manuṣyarṣigandharvadevākhyādhikāriṇāṃ teṣu trividhopāsaneṣu madhye tattadupāsane yathākramaṃ bahirantarvyāptirūpaikaikopāsana eva yogyatayā yogyatvena hetunetyarthaḥ / asyopāsātraividhyādityanenānvayaḥ / tathā cānekavidhopāstiyogyatāvatāmadhikāriṇāṃ naikavidhopāsanayā brahmajñānamiti tattraividhyamāvaśyakamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.12.15: To the objection, 'Since direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> is possible for all through a single form of worship, what is the need for threefold worship?' — in response to this, he explains the remainder of the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tadyogāt</s>' (because of fitness for that) — 'tattad' etc. By the words 'worship' and 'of persons,' the repetition of 'tad' (that) is indicated. The particle 'ca' is for conjunction. Thus the meaning is: because of the fitness, that is, the suitability, of those persons — the qualified practitioners known as humans, sages, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and gods — for each respective form of worship among the three types, namely, one particular worship in the form of external, internal, or all-pervading, in sequence. The construction is with the preceding statement about the threefold nature of worship. The import is that since the qualified practitioners possess fitness for multiple forms of worship, realization of <s>Brahman</s> does not come from a single form of worship alone; hence the threefold nature is necessary.

children.text:
keṣāṃcitsarvagatvena keṣāṃciddhṛdaye hariḥ /
keṣāñcidbahirevāsau upāsyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ /
iti brāhme /
children.translated_text: For some, <s>Hari</s> is to be worshipped as all-pervading; for some, in the heart; and for some, <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person) is to be worshipped only externally. Thus in the <s>Brāhma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.16:
puruṣāṇāmuktānekavidhopāsanayogyatā kuto jñāyata ityataḥ kartṛviśeṣānanupādāya sāmānyataḥ upāsakatraividhyapratipādikāṃ smṛtiṃ paṭhati - keṣāñciditi // 'puruṣottamo'; hariḥ 'keṣāñcit'; devānāṃ devaiḥ sarvagatatvena prakāreṇopāsyaḥ / 'keṣāñcit'; ṛṣigandharvādīnāṃ 'hṛdaye'; svasvahṛdayākāśe upāsyaḥ / 'keṣāñcit'; manuṣyottamānāṃ tu bahirevopāsya ityarthaḥ / prācuryādevamuktiḥ / iti brāhma ityasya tattadupāsanayogyatayā tadviśiṣṭatvena puruṣāṇāmāśritatvāduktatvāditi pūrveṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.12.16: To the question 'how is the stated fitness of persons for multiple forms of worship known?', without specifying particular agents, he cites a <s>smṛti</s> (traditional text) that establishes the threefold nature of worshippers in general — 'keṣāñcit' (for some) etc. '<s>Puruṣottama</s>' (the Supreme Person), <s>Hari</s>, is to be worshipped 'by some' — by gods — through the mode of all-pervasiveness. 'By some' — by sages, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and others — 'in the heart,' in the space within their own hearts. 'By some' — by the best among humans — he is to be worshipped only externally. This is said with reference to the predominant practice. The construction of 'thus in the <s>Brāhma</s>' with the preceding is: because it has been relied upon as stating the fitness for respective forms of worship and the distinction of persons thereby.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is [worshipped] in the fire by those engaged in ritual action; <s>Hari</s> is in the heart of <s>yogins</s>;
in images by those not yet awakened; and everywhere by those who have realized the Self.
Thus also. [End of <s>sūtra</s>] 31.
Thus ends the <s>Prāṇādhikaraṇa</s> at the conclusion of the <s>pāda</s>.
Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) of the commentary on the <s>Brahmasūtra</s> composed by the revered <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda Ācārya</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,1.12.17:
atraivādhikaraṇe kartṛviśeṣapratipādakaṃ viśeṣapramāṇamāha - agnāviti // viṣṇuḥ 'kriyāvatāṃ'
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,1.12.17: In this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), he cites a specific authority that identifies the particular agents — 'agnau' (in the fire) etc. <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be worshipped 'by those engaged in action' —

children.text: yajñādikriyānuṣṭhātṛṇām 'agnau'; gārhapatyādau upāsyaḥ hariḥ / 'yoginām'; ṛṣīṇāṃ hṛdaye upāsyaḥ / 'aprabuddhānāṃ'; mandamatīnāṃ atyalpapratibhānāṃ manuṣyottamānāṃ 'pratimāsu'; kṛṣṇarāmādivigraheṣu upāsyaḥ / 'viditātmanāṃ'; viśeṣato jñātabhagavadrūpāṇām aśrutapratibhānāṃ devānāṃ tu 'sarvatra'; sarvasthāneṣūpāsya ityarthaḥ / atrāgnau pratimāsviti vākyadvayena bahirmātropāsanopalakṣyate / ata eva sthānadvayoktiḥ / yathāśruteḥ sūryādau
children.translated_text: by those who perform sacrifices and other ritual actions — 'in the fire,' in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and other fires, <s>Hari</s> is to be worshipped. 'By <s>yogins</s>' — by sages — in the heart. 'By the unawakened' — by those of dull intellect, of very limited understanding, the best among humans — 'in images,' in the forms of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and other divine figures. 'By those who have realized the Self' — by the gods who have specifically known the form of <s>Bhagavān</s>, who possess unlearned intuitive knowledge — 'everywhere,' in all places, he is to be worshipped. Here, the two statements 'in the fire' and 'in images' indicate worship that is only external. Hence the mention of two locations. According to the literal sense, worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the sun and elsewhere

children.text: viṣṇūpāsterbahirupāstitvaṃ na syāt / yogināmityanenāntarupāstiruktā / 'ṛṣayo 'ntaḥprakāśāḥ'; () iti śruteḥ / sarvatreti sarvagatopāstiriti jñātavyam / na cātra "yeṣāṃ bahirupāsanena mokṣasteṣāmapi hṛdyupāsanaṃ kiñcitkāryameva"iti bṛhadbhāṣyeṇa "bhagavān bimbadarśanenainaṃ mocayati"iti nyāyavivaraṇena ca virodhaśśaṅkyaḥ / agnāviti vākye 'nyaniṣedhābhāvena bimbaśabditasvasvayogyātmāparokṣārthaṃ hṛdyupāsanasyāpi sarvaiḥ kāryatvābhyupagamāt / mocakayogyāparokṣadvārābhūtāvatārādyaparokṣasādhanopāsanāya eva taistaiḥ prācuryeṇa prakaraṇasyāgnāviti vākyena vyavasthayā pratipādanācca / iti ceti / caḥ samuccaye / vacanadvayasyāpyekārthasādhakatvādasyāpi brāhme āśritatvāditi pūrveṇānvayaḥ / tattadupāsanayogyatāvattvena puruṣaviśeṣāṇāmuktatvāditi tadarthaḥ / ato na tadyogāditi hetvasiddhiḥ śaṅkyeti bhāva /
children.translated_text: would not constitute external worship. By the phrase 'of <s>yogins</s>,' internal worship (<s>antarupāsti</s>) is stated. As per the <s>śruti</s> (scripture): 'The sages are inwardly illumined.' 'Everywhere' should be understood as all-pervading worship. And here one should not suspect a contradiction between the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> statement 'for those whose liberation comes through external worship, meditation in the heart also accomplishes something,' and the <s>Nyāyavivaraṇa</s> statement '<s>Bhagavān</s> liberates him through the vision of the image.' Since there is no negation of other [forms of worship] in the verse beginning with 'in the fire,' meditation in the heart must also be performed by all, for the purpose of direct realization of the Self suited to each, which is denoted by the word 'image.' The instruction through the verse 'in the fire' is that each [type of practitioner] predominantly [engages in] the worship that serves as the means for the direct realization of <s>avatāras</s> and other [forms] that constitute the means for the qualified direct realization that leads to liberation. 'Thus also' — the particle 'ca' is for conjunction. Since both statements serve the same purpose, and since this too has been relied upon in the <s>Brāhma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>], the construction is with the preceding. The purport is: the statement of the particular persons possessing fitness for their respective forms of worship. Therefore, the objection of unestablished reason in 'tadyogāt' (because of fitness for that) should not be raised — this is the import.

children.translated_text: [Objection:] The <s>Prāṇa</s> mentioned here is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but rather the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) and the chief vital breath (<s>mukhyaprāṇa</s>). Why? 'Because of the indicatory marks of <s>jīva</s> and <s>mukhyaprāṇa</s>' — since the indicatory mark of <s>jīva</s> in the form of the hundred-year lifespan, and the indicatory mark of <s>mukhyaprāṇa</s> in the form of the dialogue of the vital breaths, are heard here. [Reply:] No, this <s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not the <s>jīva</s> or others. Why? 'Because of concordance' — because of the supporting reason itself, and there is no contradiction with indicatory marks from other <s>śrutis</s>. In the manner already explained, '<s>tadyogāt</s>' — because the applicability of these [marks] to the Inner Controller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>) is justified. Or because this instruction is from the standpoint of scripture. If asked 'what is the purpose of mentioning the Inner Controller here?', we say: for the purpose of internal worship. Nor is there absence of internal distinction in worship. 'Because of the threefold nature of worship' — because worship of <s>Bhagavān</s> is of three kinds, distinguished as internal and so forth. Nor should one say that even so, mentioning it is unjustified because the actual threefold nature, being unstated here, gives no occasion for mention — because in this very context the threefold nature has been relied upon and stated. Nor should one say 'since direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> is possible for all through a single form of worship, what is the need for threefold worship?' — '<s>tadyogāt</s>' — because of the fitness of those persons for that particular worship alone. And since persons possessing fitness for multiple forms of worship cannot attain direct realization through a single form of worship, the threefold nature of worship is necessary due to the difference in fitness — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated. Nor should one suspect a contradiction with the statement 'both <s>Keśava</s> and the lotus-born [<s>Brahmā</s>] remained neutral,' regarding the applicability of the indicatory mark of the disputer to the Inner Controller — because that [statement] pertains to the external form distinct from the Inner Controller. Since the applicability of other indicatory marks to the Inner Controller of their respective [referents] is established, there is no contradiction with that. Therefore, this <s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and likewise the <s>Ānandamaya</s> — thus 'the inquiry into That' is established.
Thus ends the <s>Prāṇādhikaraṇa</s> at the conclusion of the <s>pāda</s>.
Thus, by the revered <s>Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācāryas</s>, who are independent masters of all systems of thought,
the disciple of the revered <s>Raghunāthatīrtha Pūjyapāda</s>,
the revered <s>Jagannāthayati</s>, in the work composed [by him],
in the glorious <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s>,
[ends] the first <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter).
Om.

pūrvottarapādabhedasya svasminnekavākyatāyāśca siddhaye etatpādapratipādyaṃ darśayati - liṅgeti // liṅgānumāpako dharmaḥ / saḥ ātmevātmā pravṛttinimittaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ / 'nimittanimittinorabhedopacārāt'; iti sudhokteḥ / svarūpārtho vā ātmaśabdaḥ / pūrvayojanāyāmātmapratipādake gauṇī vṛttiḥ / dvitīyāyāṃ tu sāmānādhikaraṇyamiti bhedaḥ / svārthe kaḥ / tathā ca vyāpyadharmadvārā dharmibodhakānāmāpātato yaugikānāmityarthaḥ / viṣṇoranyatra prasiddhānāmiti ca saṃyojyam 'śabdānāmiti'; ekaprātipadikarūpāṇāmanekapadasamabhivyāhārarūpāṇāṃ cetyarthaḥ / 'viṣṇau pravṛttiṃ'; prakarṣeṇa vṛttiṃ mahāyogavidvadrūḍhibhyāṃ viṣṇuparatvamiti yāvat / 'pradarśayati'; prakarṣeṇa sādhayati sūtrakāra ityarthaḥ / vaiśvānarādhikaraṇe nāmasamanvayakaraṇādavyāptinirāsāya prādhānyena ityuktam / tathā ca tatrāpi nāmasamanvayamukhena prādhānyena phalato bahuliṅgasamanvayasyaiva karaṇānnāvyāptiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 1:
To establish the distinction between the first and second <s>Pādas</s> and the syntactic unity within its own [<s>Pāda</s>], he shows what this <s>Pāda</s> establishes — '<s>liṅga</s>' (indicatory mark). // A <s>liṅga</s> is a property that serves as an inferential indicator. '[Marks] whose self is [their] self' — that is, those whose ground of operation (<s>pravṛttinimitta</s>) is the essential nature [of the denoted entity] are so called. This is because of the accepted principle (<s>sudhā</s>) that 'there is non-difference between cause and effect by way of figurative identification.' Or the word '<s>ātma</s>' means 'essential nature.' In the first construction, there is secondary usage (<s>gauṇī vṛtti</s>) in what establishes the self; in the second, however, there is co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) — that is the difference. The suffix '<s>ka</s>' is in reflexive sense. And thus, [they are words] that indicate the possessor of properties through the medium of qualifying properties — that is, [words] that are at first glance etymologically derived (<s>yaugika</s>): that is the meaning. 'And this should be connected with: well-known elsewhere than in <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — 'of words': meaning both those of a single stem-form and those in the form of multi-word sentences. '[Their] operation in <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — their predominant application; [this means] their referring to <s>Viṣṇu</s> through the two [means of] great textual authority (<s>mahāyoga</s>) and conventional usage of the learned (<s>vidvadrūḍhi</s>): that is the import. '[The <s>sūtrakāra</s>] demonstrates' — the <s>sūtrakāra</s> thoroughly establishes: that is the meaning. In the <s>Vaiśvānara-adhikaraṇa</s>, it was said 'primarily' in order to remove the charge of under-extension (<s>avyāpti</s>), since the syntactic connection of names is made there. And thus, even there, since the syntactic connection of multiple marks is accomplished primarily through the medium of the syntactic connection of names, there is no under-extension: that is the purport.

yadyapi pūrvapādāntyadhikaraṇenaitatpādādyasya nāvāntarasaṅgatyapakṣeti na sā pradarśanīyā / tathāpi iha tasyāḥ sambhavātphalasyāvaśyavaktavyatvācca sā pradarśyata ityāśayena pūrvādhikaraṇasaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca darśayati brahmeti // iti vākye viṣṇoḥ nivadhikasarvagatatvamuktamityarthaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - tacceti // tadityāvartate, uktamiti ca vartate / tathā ca 'brahma tatamam'; iti yattatamatvamuktaṃ prāṇākhyaviṣṇostattadekadeśabhūtaṃ sarvagatatvāntargataṃ sarvaprāṇihṛdayasthatvaṃ tatraivaitareyake 'etaṃ hyeva bahvṛcāmahatyukte mīmāṃsanta etamagnāvadhvaryava etaṃ mahāvrate chandogāḥ etamasyāmetaṃ divyetaṃ vāyāvetamākāśa etamapsu etamoṣadhīṣvetaṃ vanaspatiṣvetaṃ candramasyetaṃ nakṣatreṣvetaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣvetameva brahmetyācakṣate'; ityādau etamityuttaravākyena uktamityarthaḥ / tato 'pi kimityataḥ sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣamāha - tacceti // co 'vadhāraṇe / ādiśabdena 'sa yaścāyamaśarīraḥ prajñātmā yaścāsāvāditya ekametaditi vidyāt tasmāt puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyādityo bhavati ..... sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca ... etaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu'; (ai. 3-2-3.) ityādivākyaṃ gṛhyate / atra tasyetyāderupanyāsaḥ etamiti parāmaraśanīyasamarpakatayāvaśyakatvātpūrvapakṣayuktipradarśanārthaṃ ca kṛtaḥ / tathā ca yatha etamityuttaravākyenoktaṃ sarvaprāṇihṛdayasthatvaṃ tasyetyādinā pūrvavākyena prakṛtatvāttasyādityasyaiva pratīyate, atastasyaiva tatpūrvoktaṃ tatamatvamapi bhavet / na viṣṇoriti yojanā / atra pūrvapakṣe tatamatvaṃ saṅkucitaṃ sarvabhūtagatatvarūpaṃ vivakṣitam / na caivaṃ siddhāntyabhimataniravadhikasarvagatatvākṣepāprāptiriti vācyam / pūrvapakṣe 'etameva'; iti avadhāraṇena viṣṇoranyatrākṣepāt tenāsyākṣepikīsaṅgatiḥ, viṣayasaṃśayau, viṣṇoranyasyaiva sarvaprāṇigatatvamiti sayuktikapūrvapakṣaśca darśito bhavati / siddhānete śrutyarthastu - 'tasya'; prakṛtasya 'etasya'; saṃvatsaranāmakasya caturmukhasya sarvāditvatatamatvaniyāmakatvanimittairādityanāmā pradyumno rasaḥ sārabhūtaḥ / sa yaścāyaṃ puruṣadehagataḥ prākṛtadehavarjanādaśarīraḥ 'prajñātmā'; jñānarūpo 'niruddhaḥ / yaścāsāvāditye sthitaḥ pradyumna etatsthānadvayagataṃ rūpamekamiti vidyāt / tasmātpuruṣādityagatāniruddhapradyumnayoraikyādādityaḥ 'puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ prati'; pratipuruṣaṃ 'bhavati'; abhimukho bhavati / pratigṛhaṃ kūpa itivatsarvapuruṣagato bhavatīti ceti / 'jagato'; jaṅgamasya 'tasthuṣaḥ'; sthāvarasya 'ātmā'; ādānādikartā 'sūryaḥ'; sūriprāpyo viṣṇurdivaṃ pṛthivīmantarikṣaṃ ca 'āprāḥ'; āsamantādapūrayadityarthaḥ / etamityādīnāṃ saptamyantapadaiḥ pratyekaṃ sambandhaḥ / tathā ca 'bahvṛcāḥ'; ṛgvedinaḥ 'etaṃ hyeva'; etameva puruṣādityagatameva hi viṣṇuṃ 'mahatyukthe'; mahadukthanāmakabṛhatīsahasre taddevatāviṣaye taddevatāmiti yāvat 'mīmāṃsante'; jānanti / 'adhvaryavo'; yajurvedinaḥ 'agnau'; cayanasādhaneṣṭakādevatāviṣaye taddevatāṃ mīmāṃsante / 'chandogāḥ'; sāmavedino 'mahāvrate'; tadākhyastotrasya devatāṃ stotre mīmāṃsante / 'asyāṃ'; pṛthivyāṃ etaṃ 'divi'; antarikṣe vāyvādau caivaṃ etameva 'sarveṣu bhūteṣu'; sarvaprāṇiṣu antaḥ vyāptamācakṣate vidvāṃśa ityarthaḥ / sarveṣvityeva pūrteḥ punarbhūteṣvityuktiratra bhūtavṛttitvamātraṃ pratipādyatayābhipretamiti jñāpayitum / etaṃ sarvabhūtagatameva viṣṇuṃ guṇapūrṇatvādvyāptatvācca etaṃ mukhyato brahmetyācakṣate iti vākyaśeṣārthaḥ / na sthānādhikaraṇaṭīkāyāṃ tu - sarveṣu bhūteṣu cakṣurādisthāneṣu etamekameva brahma guṇapūrṇamācakṣate iti vyākhyātam / pūrvapakṣī tu tasyaitasya prakṛtaprasiddhasaṃvatsarasyāsau prasiddha ādityaḥ sūryo rasaḥ sārabhūto 'dhipatirityarthaṃ manyate /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 2:
Although there is no need for a separate connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) between this <s>Pāda</s>'s first topic and the preceding, since the last topic of the first <s>Pāda</s> [provides it] — nevertheless, since here such [connection] is possible, and since the result must necessarily be stated — with this intention, he shows the connection with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the subject matter, and the rest — '<s>brahma</s>.' // In the passage, the unlimited all-pervasiveness of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is stated: that is the meaning. What follows from that? — to this he says: '<s>tat ca</s>' (and that). // The word 'tat' (that) carries forward, and 'it is stated' (<s>uktam</s>) also continues. And thus, the pervasiveness (<s>tatamattva</s>) stated in '<s>Brahman</s> is the most pervading' — of the <s>Prāṇa</s>-named <s>Viṣṇu</s> — that which is a particular aspect thereof, namely the all-pervasiveness included within [it], that is, the presence in the hearts of all beings — that in the very same <s>Aitareya</s>, [in the passage] 'This [entity], in the <s>Mahatyuktha</s> (great hymn), the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> investigate; this in the fire, the <s>Adhvaryus</s>; this in the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, the <s>Chandogas</s>; this in the self, this in heaven, this in the wind, this in space, this in the waters, this in plants, this in trees, this in the moon, this in the stars, this in all beings — they call this alone <s>Brahman</s>' — and so forth, by the subsequent passage beginning with 'this' (<s>etam</s>), is 'stated': that is the meaning. What further follows from that? — to this he presents the prima facie view with reasoning: '<s>tat ca</s>.' // The word '<s>ca</s>' is for emphasis. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the passage is included: 'He who is this incorporeal, knowing self (<s>prajñātman</s>), and he who is that sun — know these to be one and the same; therefore, the sun faces each person... the sun is the self of the moving and the stationary... this [is present] in all beings' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.3) and so forth. Here, the citation beginning with 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>) is made because it is necessary as the referent for 'this' (<s>etam</s>), and also for demonstrating the prima facie reasoning. And thus, just as the presence in the hearts of all beings stated by the subsequent passage beginning with 'this' (<s>etam</s>) is understood, by the contextual connection of the preceding passage beginning with 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>), as pertaining to that sun alone — therefore the previously mentioned pervasiveness (<s>tatamattva</s>) also belongs to that [sun] alone, not to <s>Viṣṇu</s>: this is the construction. Here, in the prima facie view, a restricted pervasiveness in the form of being present in all beings is intended. Nor should one say that there is no occasion for objecting to the unlimited all-pervasiveness as accepted by the established-conclusion view — because in the prima facie view, by the word 'eva' (alone) in 'this alone' (<s>etameva</s>), what belongs to others [i.e., to <s>Viṣṇu</s>] is negated, and thereby its connection with the <s>Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa</s> by way of objection is [established], and the subject, doubt, and the prima facie view with reasoning — that the all-pervasiveness of all beings pertains to one other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — are shown. In the established conclusion, however, the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is: 'Of that' — of the one under discussion — 'of this' — of the one named <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (year), the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> — by the determiners of all-lordship and pervasiveness, the sun named <s>Pradyumna</s> is the 'essence' (<s>rasa</s>), the essential one, the overlord: that is the meaning. 'He who is this' — present in the human body, 'incorporeal' — because of being free from the material body, the 'knowing self' — <s>Aniruddha</s>, who is of the nature of knowledge. And 'he who is' that one established in the sun — <s>Pradyumna</s>: know these to be one, that the form present in these two locations is one. Therefore, because of the unity of <s>Aniruddha</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s> present in the sun, the sun faces 'each person' — every person — 'becomes' — turns toward [them]. The meaning is: 'Just as there is a well for each house' — so [the sun] is present in every person. 'Of the moving' (<s>jagataḥ</s>) — of mobile beings; 'of the stationary' (<s>tasthuṣaḥ</s>) — of immobile beings; 'the self' (<s>ātmā</s>) — the agent of sustaining and the like; the 'sun' (<s>sūryaḥ</s>) — attainable by the wise; <s>Viṣṇu</s> 'filled' (<s>āprāḥ</s>) — completely filled heaven, earth, and the atmosphere: that is the meaning. The word 'this' (<s>etam</s>) connects individually with each locative-case word. And thus, the '<s>Bahvṛcas</s>' — the <s>Ṛgvedins</s> — 'this alone indeed' (<s>etaṃ hyeva</s>) — this very one present in the person and the sun, that is, <s>Viṣṇu</s> — in the '<s>Mahatyuktha</s>' — in the thousand <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses named <s>Mahad Uktha</s>, regarding the deity thereof — they 'investigate' (<s>mīmāṃsante</s>), that is, they know. The '<s>Adhvaryus</s>' — the <s>Yajurvedins</s> — [investigate this] in 'the fire' (<s>agnau</s>) — regarding the deity of the bricks used in the construction of the fire-altar, they investigate that deity. The '<s>Chandogas</s>' — the <s>Sāmavedins</s> — in 'the <s>Mahāvrata</s>' — investigate the deity of the hymn so named, [they investigate the deity] in the hymn. 'In this' (<s>asyāṃ</s>) — in the earth, 'this' [entity]; 'in heaven' (<s>divi</s>) — in the atmosphere, in <s>Vāyu</s> and the like, similarly 'this' alone; 'in all beings' (<s>sarveṣu bhūteṣu</s>) — in all living creatures — the learned 'call' (<s>ācakṣate</s>) this one who pervades within as <s>Brahman</s>: that is the meaning. Although 'in all' (<s>sarveṣu</s>) already [suffices], the repetition of 'in beings' (<s>bhūteṣu</s>) is to indicate that what is intended to be established here is merely the attribute of being present in beings. 'This' one present in all beings, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because of His fullness of qualities and His pervasiveness — 'this' one primarily 'they call <s>Brahman</s>' — thus the sentence-remainder meaning. However, in the <s>Sthānādhikaraṇa Ṭīkā</s>, it is explained: 'in all beings' — in the locations such as the eye and others — 'this' one alone, <s>Brahman</s> full of qualities, 'they call.' The prima facie advocate, however, understands 'of that' — of the well-known year (<s>saṃvatsara</s>) under discussion — 'this' well-known sun is the essence, the essential one, the overlord.

Therefore he (<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>) spoke —
<s>Oṃ</s> //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 3:]
Because of the teaching [of <s>Brahman</s>] as well-known everywhere. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.1 |

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.3:
atha siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti // iti saṅgatisambhavādākṣepasadbhāvācca atastatparihārāyottaramabravīdbādarāyaṇa ityarthaḥ / tadeva sūtraṃ paṭhati - sarvatreti /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 3:
Now, introducing the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the conclusion, he says — '<s>ataḥ</s>' (therefore). // The meaning is: since there is occasion for connection and since the objection exists, therefore, to resolve it, <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> spoke the answer. He reads that very <s>sūtra</s> — '<s>sarvatra</s>' (everywhere).

children.text:
'sa yaścāyamaśarīraḥ prajñātmā'; (ai.ā. 3-2-4.)
ityādinā sarvatrocyamāno nārāyaṇa eva /
children.translated_text: 'He who is this incorporeal, knowing self' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.4) — the one spoken of everywhere through such [passages] is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 4:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.4:
atra samanvayasūtrāttattvityasyānuvṛttiṃ liṅgavyatyayam 'ucyamānam'; ityadhyāhāraṃ cābhipretya pratijñāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - sa yaśceti // vākyeneti śeṣaḥ / yadyapi 'tasyaitasyāsau'; ityādineti vaktavyam / pūrvavākyatvāt / tathāpi tasya pūrvapakṣayuktipradarśanārthatvenopanyastatvāttadvihāya siddhāntayuktipradarśakavākyajñāpanāya 'sa yaścāyamaśarīraḥ prajñātmā'; ityādinetyevoktam / vastutastu - na 'tasyaitasyāsau'; ityasyeva 'sa yaśca'; ityasya yuktipradarśanamātratātparyeṇopanyāsaḥ, nāpi viṣayamātrapradarśanatātparyeṇa / api tu pūrvaṃ viṣayavākyasya anudāhṛtatvāttadarthatayā tadgataitacchabdaparāmarśanayasamarpaṇārthamananyasādhāraṇasvato 'śarīratvayuktipradarśanārthaṃ ceti dhyeyam / 'sarvatra'; sarvaprāṇihṛdayeṣvantargatatayocyamāno nārāyaṇa eveti / nārāyaṇaśabdaprayegena -

children.translated_text: Whatever there is in all the universe, whether seen or heard,
pervading all that, both within and without, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> abides.

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 4:
Here, intending the continuation of 'tat tu' (but that) from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s>, the gender transposition, and the interpolation of 'the one being spoken of' (<s>ucyamānam</s>), he explains the thesis-portion — '<s>sa yaśca</s>' (he who). // 'By the passage' is the remainder. Although one should say 'beginning with "of that, this"' (<s>tasyaitasyāsau</s>), since that belongs to the preceding passage — nevertheless, since that was cited for the purpose of demonstrating the prima facie reasoning, setting it aside, to indicate the passage that demonstrates the established-conclusion reasoning, he says 'beginning with "he who is this incorporeal knowing self."' But in reality, the citation of 'of that, this' (<s>tasyaitasyāsau</s>) is not merely for the purpose of demonstrating reasoning, nor merely for the purpose of showing the subject matter — but rather, because the subject-passage had not been cited earlier, for the purpose of presenting it, and for supplying the referent of the word 'this' (<s>etat</s>) contained therein, and for demonstrating the unique reasoning of incorporeality: this should be reflected upon. '[The one spoken of] everywhere' (<s>sarvatra</s>) — in the hearts of all beings, the one spoken of as present within is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone. By the use of the word <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> —

children.text: iti vākyamapi saṅgṛhītaṃ bhavati / tena ca sūtre saṅkucitavṛttinā sarvatretyanena sarvabhūtahṛdgatatvasyaivābhipretatvenānyatra bahirneti prāptaśaṅkā nirastā bhavati /
children.translated_text: — this passage too is encompassed. And by that, [the word] '<s>sarvatra</s>' (everywhere) in the <s>sūtra</s>, used in a restricted sense [meaning 'in all beings'], by [its connection with] the word meaning 'all-pervasiveness,' [indicates that] only the presence in the hearts of all beings is intended — and the apprehension that [it means] 'not outside, elsewhere' is dispelled.

'That very <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme among the wise' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 1.6);
'He who [knows] the supreme, great <s>Brahman</s>'
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 5:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.5:
hetvaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - tadeveti // vyākhyātametajjijñāsānayer / iśvarabrahmaṇorabhedabodhanārthaṃ pravṛttasya 'paramaṃ yo mahadbrahma paramaṃ yaḥ parāyaṇam'; iti bhāratavākyasya yaḥ paramaṃ mahadbrahma yaḥ paramaṃ parāyaṇaṃ tasya lokapradhānasya jagannāthasya nāmnāmityuttaravākyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 5:
He explains the reason-portion — '<s>tadeva</s>' (that very). // This has been explained in the <s>Jijñāsā</s> method. To convey the non-difference between <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Bhārata</s> passage 'He who [knows] the supreme, great <s>Brahman</s>, He who [knows] the supreme refuge' is introduced; and 'He who [knows] the supreme, great <s>Brahman</s>, He who [knows] the supreme refuge' — its syntactic connection is with the subsequent passage: 'of that lord of the world, <s>Jagannātha</s>, by the names.'

children.text:
vāsudevātparaḥ ko nu brahmaśabdodito bhavat /
sa hi sarvaguṇaiḥ pūrṇaḥ tadanye tūpacārataḥ // iti /
tasminneva prasiddhabrahmaśabdopadeśāt // 1 //
children.translated_text:
Who could be higher than <s>Vāsudeva</s> to be denoted by the word '<s>Brahman</s>'?
For He alone is full of all qualities; for others, [the word is used] only figuratively. — Thus.
Because of the teaching, in that very [entity], of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' which is well-known [as denoting Him]. // 1 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 6:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.6:
vāsudevādityaparā smṛtiḥ / 'vāsudevāt'; kṛṣṇādanyaḥ ko vā brahmaśabdamukhyavācyo bhavet, na ko 'pi / kintu sa eva mukhyavācyaḥ / kutaḥ? 'hi'; yasmāt 'saḥ'; vāsudevaḥ sarvaguṇaiḥ pūrṇastadanye tvapūrṇāḥ tasmāt / tarhi 'brahmāṇi jīvāḥ sarve 'pi'; ityādi kathamityata āha tadanya iti // vāsudevādanye jīvāḥ 'upacārataḥ'; amukhyata eva brahmaśabdoditāḥ, na tu mukhyata ityarthaḥ / itīti / vākyeṣviti śeṣaḥ / anena sarvatretyasya hetāvapyanvayo darśitaḥ / tathā ca sarvatrodāhṛtavākyeṣu 'tasminneva'; viṣṇāveva 'prasiddhasya'; rūḍhatvenāvagatasya 'brahmaśabdasyopadeśāt'; sarvagate vastuni śravaṇādityarthaḥ / tasminnevetyanena śruterniravakāśatvamuktaṃ bhavati / anena 'sa yaścāyamaśarīraḥ prajñātmā'; (ai.ā. 3-2-3.) ityādinā 'sarveṣu bhūteṣvetameva brahmetyācakṣate'; (ai.ā. 3-2-3.) iti śākhāśeṣeṇa sarvatra sarveṣu bhūteṣu antargatatayocyamāno nārāyaṇa eva na tvādityādiḥ / kutaḥ? 'etameva brahmetyācakṣate'; iti sarvabhūtagate vastuni nārāyaṇaikaniṣṭhatvena śrutyādiprasiddhabrahmaśabdopadeśācchruteriti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 6:
'<s>Vāsudevāt</s>' — this is the other <s>Smṛti</s> [citation]. 'Than <s>Vāsudeva</s>' — than <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — who else could be the primary denotation of the word '<s>Brahman</s>'? No one at all. Rather, He alone is the primary denotation. Why? 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — because 'He' — <s>Vāsudeva</s> — is full of all qualities, while others are not full; therefore. Then how [is the passage] 'all <s>jīvas</s> are also <s>Brahman</s>' and so forth [to be understood]? — to this he says: '<s>tadanya</s>' (others). // Those other than <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the <s>jīvas</s>, are denoted by the word '<s>Brahman</s>' only 'figuratively' (<s>upacārataḥ</s>) — in a non-primary sense: that is the meaning. The word 'iti' [connects with]: 'in the passages' is the remainder. By this, the applicability of '<s>sarvatra</s>' (everywhere) to the reason-portion is also shown. And thus, 'in that very' (<s>tasminneva</s>) — in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — 'of the well-known' (<s>prasiddhasya</s>) — understood through conventional usage (<s>rūḍhatva</s>) — 'word "<s>Brahman</s>"' — 'because of the teaching' (<s>upadeśāt</s>) — because of [its] being heard in what is all-pervading: that is the meaning. By '<s>tasminneva</s>' (in that very one), the no-scope-elsewhere of the <s>Śruti</s> is stated. By this, through [the passage] 'He who is this incorporeal, knowing self' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.3) and the like, [up to] 'they call this alone <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.3) — the branch-conclusion — the one spoken of everywhere, in all beings, as present within, is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone, not <s>Āditya</s> and the like. Why? Because of the teaching of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' — which is well-known through <s>Śruti</s> and the like as exclusively referring to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — regarding what is present in all beings: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
And because of the fitness of the intended qualities. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.2 |
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 7:]
'He who is hereafter unheard of' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.4) — and so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.7:
yuktyantareṇa viṣṇorevātroktasarvagatatvaṃ pratipādayatsūtramupanyasya tadupāttaśrutimevodāharati - vivakṣiteti/ ādipadena 'agato 'mato 'nato 'dṛṣṭo 'vijñāto 'nādiṣṭaḥ / śrotā mantā draṣṭādeṣṭā ghoṣṭā vijñātā prajñātā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmantarapuruṣaḥ sama ātmeti vidyāt'; (ai.ā. 3-2-4.) iti vākyaśeṣo gṛhyate / ityādīti luptatṛtīyavibhaktikaṃ padam / asya vivakṣiteti sūtrapadenānvayaḥ / ata eva sūtrabhāṣyayorekībhāva iti tattvapradīpoktiḥ / anena sūtre śrutyeti śeṣaḥ sūcitaḥ / caḥ pūrvoktahetusamuccaye 'vadhāraṇe ca / yato vaktuṃ yogye vivakṣā bhavati / ato vivakṣitāḥ vaktuṃ yogyāḥ vakṣyamāṇā iti vā / ye tu śrutīnāṃ brahmaguṇeṣu tātparyābhāvaṃ vadanti, tannirāsāya vivakṣitapadamupanibabandha sūtrakṛditi tattvapradīpokteḥ śrutitātparyaviṣayabhūtā iti vā / sarvatretyanuvartate / gate iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca sarvatra gate vivakṣitānāṃ śrutyā sarvatra gataniṣṭhatayā vaktuṃ yogyānāṃ itaḥparaṃ śrutyā sarvagataniṣṭhatayā vakṣyamāṇānāṃ śrutitātparyaviṣayībhūtānāṃ vā guṇānāmupasaṃhāragatāśrutatvādīnāṃ viṣṇoreva yogyatvena tasminnevopapatteḥ anyatrānupapatteśca sarvatrocyamāno nārāyaṇa eva iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / yaḥ prakṛto viṣṇuḥ saḥ 'ataḥ'; deśakālaguṇairvyāptaḥ / ata sātatyagamane iti dhātuvyākhyānāt 'santato hyata ucyate'; iti vacanācca / yadvā - ato 'tistṛtīye 'tiśaye adhika ityarthaḥ / 'aśrutaḥ'; sarvātmanā śrotumaśakyaḥ / svayameva svātmānaṃ svātantryeṇa śṛṇoti / 'narte tvat'; (ṛ. 10-112-9.) iti śruteḥ / 'agataḥ'; aprāptaḥ pūrṇatvātsarvātmanājñāta iti vā / sarvātmanā mananaviṣayo na bhavatītyamataḥ / anato netṛrahitaḥ svatantra iti yāvat / 'adṛṣṭaḥ'; pratyakṣeṇa kenacit, sarvātmanā pūrṇatvāt / ata eva sarvātmanā 'avijñātaḥ'; viśeṣato na jñātaḥ / 'anādiṣṭaḥ'; niyojakaśūnyo 'nyairanājñapta iti vā / yathānyaiḥ svayamaśrutādirna tathānye, sarvātmanā śrutyādyā ityāha - śroteti / 'śrotā'; yugapatsvātantryeṇa śravaṇakartā / 'mantā'; svātantryeṇa sarvamananakartā / svātantryeṇa sarvadraṣṭā / 'ādeṣṭā'; niyojanakartā / 'āghoṣṭā'; samyagvaktā / 'vijñātā'; viśeṣeṇa jñātā / prakarṣeṇa jñātā / 'sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ'; jīvānām 'antaraḥ'; antasthaḥ 'puruṣaḥ'; pūrṇaḥ 'samaḥ'; samānaḥ, sarvarūpeṇa 'ātmā'; ādānādikarteti vidyādityaitareyabhāṣyatattvapradīpaviśveśvaratīrthīyadiśā śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 7:
Having introduced the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes, by another reasoning, that the quality of being spoken of everywhere (<s>sarvagatatva</s>) stated here belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, he cites the very <s>śruti</s> taken up by it — 'vivakṣita' etc. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), the remainder of the passage is understood: 'agato 'mato 'nato 'dṛṣṭo 'vijñāto 'nādiṣṭaḥ / śrotā mantā draṣṭā ādeṣṭā ghoṣṭā vijñātā prajñātā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām antarapuruṣaḥ sama ātmeti vidyāt' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.4). The word 'ityādi' is a form with the third case-ending elided. Its syntactical connection is with the <s>sūtra</s>-word 'vivakṣita'. Hence the statement of <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> that there is a unification of <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s>. By this, the supplement 'śrutyā' (by scripture) in the <s>sūtra</s> is indicated. The particle 'ca' is for accumulating the previously stated reason and for emphasis. Since the desire to speak (<s>vivakṣā</s>) arises regarding what is fit to be spoken, therefore 'vivakṣitāḥ' means 'fit to be spoken' or 'about to be stated'. As for those who say that the <s>śrutis</s> do not have their purport in the qualities of <s>Brahman</s> — to refute that, the <s>sūtrakṛt</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>) employed the word 'vivakṣita', according to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>; or it means 'being the subject of the purport of scripture'. 'Sarvatra' (everywhere) carries over, with 'gate' (spoken of) as the supplement. Thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated as: the qualities such as being unheard (<s>aśrutatva</s>) etc. found in the concluding section, which are intended to be spoken of — i.e., fit to be spoken of by scripture as established everywhere, or which will henceforth be stated by scripture as established everywhere, or which are the subject of scriptural purport — are appropriate only for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since they are fitting only for Him and tenable only in Him, and untenable elsewhere; therefore the one spoken of everywhere is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone. The <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is the subject — He is 'ataḥ' (from this); pervaded by place, time, and qualities. Because the root 'at' is explained as meaning 'continuous going' (<s>sātatyagamana</s>), and because of the statement 'santato hy ata ucyate' (He is called 'ata' because of being continuous). Or — 'ataḥ' with the suffix 'ati' in the third degree, meaning 'surpassing, superior'. 'Aśrutaḥ' — impossible to be heard in His entirety. He Himself hears His own Self independently. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'na ṛte tvat' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.112.9). 'Agataḥ' — unattained; or, because of His fullness (<s>pūrṇatva</s>), unknowable in totality. 'Amataḥ' — He does not become the object of thought in His entirety. 'Anataḥ' — without a ruler, i.e., independent (<s>svatantra</s>). 'Adṛṣṭaḥ' — not seen by anyone through direct perception, because of His total fullness. For this very reason, 'avijñātaḥ' — not known in His entirety, i.e., not known in His particularity. 'Anādiṣṭaḥ' — devoid of a commander, i.e., not commanded by others. Just as He Himself is unheard etc. by others, others are not so — they are entirely objects of hearing etc. — this he states with 'śrotā' etc. 'Śrotā' — the agent of hearing simultaneously and independently. 'Mantā' — the agent of all thinking independently. The seer of all independently. 'Ādeṣṭā' — the agent of commanding. 'Āghoṣṭā' — the one who speaks perfectly. 'Vijñātā' — the one who knows particularly; the one who knows supremely. Of 'sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām' — of all beings, i.e., of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls); 'antaraḥ' — dwelling within; 'puruṣaḥ' — the full one; 'samaḥ' — equal, in all forms; 'ātmā' — the agent of sustaining etc. — thus one should know. This is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> according to the direction of <s>Viśveśvaratīrtha</s>'s <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya Tattvapradīpa</s>.

children.text:
sa hi 'na te viṣṇoḥ jāyamāno na jāto devaḥ'; (ṛ. 7-99-2.)
ityādināśrutatvādiguṇakaḥ /
children.translated_text: For He possesses the qualities of being unheard (<s>aśrutatva</s>) etc., as stated in 'na te viṣṇoḥ jāyamāno na jāto devaḥ' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 7.99.2) and similar passages.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 8:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.8:
nanvetacchrutyuktānām aśrutatvādiguṇānāṃ kuto viṣṇuniṣṭhatvamityata āha - sa hīti // hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / 'saḥ'; viṣṇuḥ 'na te'; ityādinā vākyenāśrutatvādiguṇaḥ tadvattayā prasiddha ityarthaḥ / śrutau 'śrotrādinā'; iti padādhyāhāreṇeti bhāvaḥ / yadyapi śrutāvatatvasya prathamoktatvādatatvādiguṇa iti vaktavyam / tathāpi tasya sarvagatatvarūpatvena viṣṇuniṣṭhatayā sādhyatvāt asiddhatvāt sa viṣṇuratatvādiguṇakaḥ prasiddha iti siddhanirdeśāyogāt aśrutatvādītyuktam / yadvā - viṣṇuratatvādiguṇakaḥ 'na te viṣṇo'; (ṛ. 7-99-2.) ityādiśruteriti prayoge sarvagatatvarūpasyātatvasya sāodhyatvāttasya ca 'na te viṣṇo'; ityādāvanukterhetvananvayādaśrutatvādītyuktam /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 8:
If it be asked: how is it established that the qualities such as being unheard (<s>aśrutatva</s>) etc. stated in the <s>śruti</s> belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? — to this he says 'sa hi' etc. The particle 'hi' denotes what is well-known. 'Saḥ' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is well-known as possessing qualities such as being unheard etc. through the passage 'na te' and similar statements. The import is that the word 'śrotrādinā' (by hearing-faculties etc.) is to be supplied. Although in the <s>śruti</s>, the quality of 'atatva' (pervading) is mentioned first, and therefore one should say 'atatva-etc.-qualities', nevertheless, since that quality — being of the nature of being spoken of everywhere (<s>sarvagatatva</s>) — is what is to be proved as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and since it is therefore unestablished, it would be improper to refer to it as established by saying 'He, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is well-known as possessing the quality of atatva etc.' Therefore, 'aśrutatva etc.' is said instead. Or alternatively — in the formulation '<s>Viṣṇu</s> possesses qualities such as atatva, from the śruti "na te viṣṇo" etc.', since atatva — being of the nature of sarvagatatva — is what is to be proved, and since it is not mentioned in 'na te viṣṇo' etc., there would be a failure of the reason to connect with what is to be proved; therefore 'aśrutatva etc.' is said.

children.text:
'sa savitā sa vāyuḥ sa indraḥ so 'śrutaḥ so 'dṛṣṭo
yo hariryaḥ paramo yo viṣṇuryo 'nantaḥ'; ityādicaturvedaśikhāyām // 2 //
children.translated_text: 'He is <s>Savitṛ</s>, He is <s>Vāyu</s>, He is <s>Indra</s>, He is the unheard, He is the unseen — He who is <s>Hari</s>, who is the Supreme, who is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is the Infinite' — thus in the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s>. || 2 ||
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 9:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.9:
'na te'; ityādiśrutau mukhato 'śrutatvādikaṃ viṣṇorna pratīyate ityato 'traivārthe spaṣṭaśrutiṃ cāha - sa iti / yaḥ 'savitā'; jagadutpādakaḥ sa harireva / yo 'vāyuḥ'; balajñānarūpo devaḥ sa paramaḥ paramātmaiva / yaḥ 'indraḥ'; paramaiśvaryavān sa viṣṇureva, na prasiddhādiḥ / yo 'śruto 'dṛṣṭaḥ so 'nanto 'parimito harireva nānya ityarthaḥ / yadvā - yo haryādiśabdavācyaḥ prasiddhaḥ, sa eva savitṛtvādiguṇavāciśabdavācya ityarthaḥ / ityādīti / yataḥ caturvedaśikhāyāmityādyuktamato 'pi sa evāśrutatvādiguṇa ityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 9:
Since in the <s>śruti</s> 'na te' etc., the qualities of being unheard etc. are not directly understood as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, therefore for this very purpose he also cites a clear <s>śruti</s> — 'sa' etc. He who is 'Savitṛ' — the producer of the world — He is <s>Hari</s> alone. He who is 'Vāyu' — the deity of the nature of strength and knowledge — He is the Supreme (<s>Parama</s>), the <s>Paramātman</s> Himself. He who is 'Indra' — possessing supreme sovereignty — He is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not the well-known deity <s>Indra</s> etc. He who is unheard, unseen — He is the infinite (<s>ananta</s>), the unlimited — He is <s>Hari</s> alone, none other. This is the meaning. Or alternatively — He who is well-known as denoted by the words <s>Hari</s> etc., He alone is denoted by the words denoting qualities such as being Savitṛ etc. This is the meaning. 'Ityādi' — since it is said 'in the Caturvedaśikhā' etc., from this too He alone possesses qualities such as being unheard etc. — this is the syntactical connection.

And it should not be said that the one spoken of everywhere is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) because of the word 'āditya' (sun) and because of having the nature of the eye (<s>cakṣurmayatva</s>) etc.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 10:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.10:
nanu yathā brahmaśabdādaśrutatvādiliṅgaiśca viṣṇuḥ sarvagata ityucyate / tathādityādiśabdātsarvajīvaliṅgāccādityaḥ sarvajīvā vā sarvagatāḥ kiṃ na syurityata āha - na ceti // 'ādityo rasaḥ'; ityādityaśabdāt sarvagatatvaprakaraṇe 'cakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaḥ chandomayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā'; (ai.ā. 3-2-1) iti śrutau jñānakaraṇacakṣurādyātmakadehābhimānitvena jīve prasiddhāccakṣurmayatvādeścetyarthaḥ / hetusamuccaye caśabdaḥ/ 'jīvaḥ'; ityanena sūtragataṃ śārīrapadaṃ vyākhyātam / 'śārīrau tāvubhau proktau jīvaśca paramastathā'; iti smṛteḥ / śarīrābhimānitvācca jīvasya śārītvaṃ yuktam / jīva ityekavacanaṃ samudāyābhiprāyam / jīvaścetyapi caśabdānvayaḥ / tenādityapratijñā samuccīyate / sarvatra gata iti śeṣaḥ / iti na vācyamiti sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 10:
If it be objected: just as from the word <s>Brahman</s> and the indicators such as being unheard etc., <s>Viṣṇu</s> is said to be spoken of everywhere, so too from the word 'āditya' and the indicators pertaining to all <s>jīvas</s>, why should not <s>Āditya</s> or all <s>jīvas</s> be spoken of everywhere? — to this he says 'na ca' etc. From the word 'āditya' in 'ādityo rasaḥ' etc., and in the context of <s>sarvagatatva</s> (being spoken of everywhere), because of the <s>śruti</s> 'cakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaḥ chandomayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.1) — from this the quality of having the nature of the eye etc. is well-known regarding the <s>jīva</s> as the one identified with the body having cognitive organs like the eye etc. This is the meaning. The particle 'ca' is for accumulating reasons. By 'jīvaḥ' (individual soul), the word 'śārīra' (embodied one) occurring in the <s>sūtra</s> is explained. From the <s>smṛti</s>: 'śārīrau tāv ubhau proktau jīvaś ca paramas tathā' (Both are called embodied — the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme alike). And because the <s>jīva</s> identifies with the body, its designation as 'śārīra' (embodied) is appropriate. The singular 'jīvaḥ' is intended in the sense of the collective. The particle 'ca' also connects with 'jīva'. Thereby the claim regarding <s>Āditya</s> is accumulated. 'Sarvatra gata' (spoken of everywhere) is the supplement. 'Iti na vācyam' (thus it should not be said) — this is the connection.
<s>Oṃ</s>.
But it is not the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>), because of the impossibility. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.3 |
<s>Oṃ</s>.
Because of the very impossibility of a single <s>jīva</s> being present in all bodies. || 3 ||
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 11:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.11:
kuto na vācyamityatra hetvākāṅkṣāyāṃ sūtramupanyasya pratijñābhāgasyāvatārikābhāṣyeṇaiva vyākhyātatvāddhetvaṃśameva vyācaṣṭe - anupapatteriti // ekasyaikaikasya jīvasyeti vipariṇāmenānuvartate / sarvaśarīreti / sarvaśarīrasthatvasyānupapatteḥ sarvajīvasya samānabhogaprāptirūpopapattiviruddhatvādevetyarthaḥ / na tvanyaprāpakābhāvāditi hetvantaramanveṣaṇīyamityevaśabdārthaḥ / evetyanena sautratuśabdo vyākhyātaḥ / anupapattistu ṭīkāyāmeva sahetukamupapāditā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 11:
When there is the expectation of a reason for 'why should it not be said?' — having introduced the <s>sūtra</s>, since the assertion-portion has already been explained by the introductory <s>bhāṣya</s> itself, he explains only the reason-portion — 'anupapatteḥ' etc. 'Ekasya' — of each individual <s>jīva</s> — carries over by inversion. 'Sarvaśarīra' etc. — because of the impossibility of being present in all bodies, i.e., because it contradicts the consequence that all <s>jīvas</s> would have identical experiences (<s>samānabhogaprāpti</s>). But the word 'eva' indicates that one should not seek another reason such as the absence of another means of attainment. The word 'eva' explains the <s>sūtra</s>-word 'tu'. The impossibility is demonstrated with its reasoning in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> itself.
<s>Oṃ</s>.
And because of the designation as object and agent of action. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.4 |
<s>Oṃ</s>.
'He declares the Self to another' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.3) and similar passages. || 4 ||
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 12:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.12:
yuktyantareṇa śārīrasya sarvagatatvaṃ nirākurvatsūtramupanyasya tadupāttaśrutimevodāharati - karmeti // bhāvapradhāno 'yaṃ, caḥ samuccaye / 'sarvatroktaḥ śārīraḥ'; iti padatrayaṃ vipariṇāmenānuvartate / tathā ca sarvatroktasya sarvagatasya prakṛtasya 'etamātmānaṃ parasmai śaṃsati'; ityaitareyaśrutau śaṃsanakriyāyāṃ sa etamātmānamiti karmatvena śārīrasya jīvasya ca tasyāmeva kartṛtvena vyapadeśāt ekasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ tayorutsargato bhinnatvaniyamāt apavādakāraṇābhāvācca na sarvatrocyamānaḥ śārīra ityarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - cakārāt 'parasmai'; iti sampradānavyapadeśāccetyabhiprāya ityuktam / yaḥ 'etamātmānaṃ'; cakṣurmayatvādiguṇakaṃ paramātmānam 'anyasmai'; ayogyāya 'śaṃsati'; upadiśati tasya vedāḥ 'dugdhadohāḥ'; phalavidhurā bhavantītyarthaḥ / ityādītyasya pūrvavatsūtreṇānvayaḥ / ādipadena 'ātmānaṃ veda'; iti ṭīkoktaṃ 'yastityāja sacividaṃ sakhāyaṃ na tasya vācyapi bhāgo 'sti'; (ai.ā. 3-2-4.) iti tattvapradīpodāhṛtavākyaṃ ca gṛhyate / 'sacividaṃ'; karmasañcayavettāraṃ prītyā ekadeśasthatvāt sakhāyaṃ hariṃ 'yastityāja'; tatyāja anyathā veda, tasya 'vāci'; vedādhyayanādau tasmāt 'bhāgaḥ'; phalaṃ nāsti narakaṃ ca syādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 12:
Having introduced the <s>sūtra</s> that refutes by another reasoning the <s>sarvagatatva</s> (being spoken of everywhere) of the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>), he cites the very <s>śruti</s> taken up by it — 'karma' etc. This compound is action-predominant (<s>bhāvapradhāna</s>); 'ca' is for accumulation. The three words 'sarvatra uktaḥ śārīraḥ' carry over by inversion. Thus, regarding the one spoken of everywhere, the one who has been established everywhere, the subject <s>Viṣṇu</s> — in the <s>Aitareya</s> <s>śruti</s> passage 'etam ātmānaṃ parasmai śaṃsati' (he declares this Self to another), the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>), i.e., the <s>jīva</s>, is designated as the object (<s>karman</s>) in the act of declaring through 'sa etam ātmānam' (this Self), and another is designated as the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) in that very act. Since in a single action, the two are by default necessarily different, and since there is no ground for exception (<s>apavāda</s>) — therefore the one spoken of everywhere is not the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>). This is the meaning. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, it is said: by the particle 'ca', the intention is also 'because of the designation as recipient (<s>sampradāna</s>) through the word "parasmai" (to another)'. He who declares 'etam ātmānam' — this Self having qualities such as being of the nature of the eye etc., the <s>Paramātman</s> — to 'anyasmai' — to an unworthy person — for him the <s>Vedas</s> become 'dugdhadohāḥ' — bereft of fruit. This is the meaning. The syntactical connection of 'ityādi' with the <s>sūtra</s> is as before. By the word 'ādi', the passage 'ātmānaṃ veda' mentioned in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> and the passage cited in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> — 'yas tityāja sacividaṃ sakhāyaṃ na tasya vācy api bhāgo 'sti' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.4) — are understood. 'Sacividam' — the knower of the accumulation of <s>karmas</s>, a friend due to affectionate co-presence — <s>Hari</s>; 'yas tityāja' — he who abandoned Him, i.e., who knows Him wrongly; for him, in 'vāci' — in the study of the <s>Vedas</s> etc. — there is no 'bhāgaḥ' — no fruit from that; and hell would result. This is the meaning.
<s>Oṃ</s>.
Because of the distinction of the word. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.5 |
<s>Oṃ</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 13:]
'They call this very one <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.3).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.13:
yaduktaṃ brahmaśabdāt viṣṇureva sarvagata iti / tadayuktam, brahmaśabdasya jīve 'pi vṛtteḥ / na cāsau jīve 'mukhya iti tadagrahaḥ / cakṣurmayatvādibādhakabalenāmukhyārthasyāpi grahaṇopapatteḥ / na ca dvitīyasūtroktabādhakānna jīvaḥ 'śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit'; iti gītāyāṃ jīvasyāśrutatvādiśravaṇāt, tṛtīyoktasya ca viṣṇāvapi sāmyāt / nāpi turīyoktacakṣurmayatvādibādhakena, ekasyaiva karmatvakartṛtvayoḥ upapatterityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya tadupāttaśrutimevodāharati - śabdeti // bhāṣyasya sūtreṇānvayaḥ / tathā ca 'etameva brahmetyācakṣate'; iti vākye hetutvena prakṛtabrahmaśabdasya 'viśeṣāt'; sāvadhāraṇatvarūpaviśeṣavattvādityarthaḥ / asya nānena brahmaśabdena śārīra ucyate iti labdhasādhyenānvayaḥ/ anenaivakāro vidheyapadasaṅgataḥ, tacchiraskabrahmaśabdaśca mukhyabrahmatvārthakaḥ/ sa ca jīve na yukta ityuktaṃ bhavati / yadvā - evakāra emityuddeśyavācipadenaiva saṅgato 'nyayogavyavacchedārthakaḥ / na caivaṃ brahmaśabdasya sāvadhāraṇatvāprāptiriti vācyam / evakārārthāvadhāraṇasyānyayogavyavacchedasyānyasmin brahmatvayogavyavaccheda iti vivaraṇe brahmaśabdārthabrahmatvasambandhāt brahmaśabdasya sāvadhāraṇatvaprāpteḥ / yadyapi na śārīra etacchabdārthaḥ / kutaḥ? tasya evakārārthapratiyogivācakabrahmaśabdenaiva viśeṣitatvāditi sūtravṛttissambhavati / tathāpi na sā ṭīkokteti na kairapi pradarśitā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.1, verse 13:
What was said — that from the word <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is spoken of everywhere — that is improper, since the word <s>Brahman</s> is also used for the <s>jīva</s>. Nor can one say that it is not primary (<s>mukhya</s>) when applied to the <s>jīva</s>, and therefore should not be taken in that sense; for even a non-primary meaning can be adopted by the force of the contradicting evidence of having the nature of the eye (<s>cakṣurmayatva</s>) etc. Nor can one say that by the contradictions stated in the second <s>sūtra</s>, it is not the <s>jīva</s> — because in the <s>Gītā</s>, being unheard etc. is heard regarding the <s>jīva</s> too: 'śrutvāpy enaṃ veda na caiva kaścit'; and the argument stated in the third sūtra applies equally to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Nor by the contradiction of <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> etc. stated in the fourth sūtra, since object-hood and agent-hood can belong to one and the same entity — resolving this doubt, having introduced the <s>sūtra</s>, he cites the very <s>śruti</s> taken up by it — 'śabda' etc. The <s>bhāṣya</s> has its syntactical connection with the <s>sūtra</s>. Thus, in the passage 'etam eva brahmetyācakṣate', the word <s>Brahman</s> in the subject of the <s>sūtra</s> functions as a reason because of its 'viśeṣa' (distinction) — i.e., because it possesses the distinguishing feature of being emphatic (<s>sāvadhāraṇatva</s>). This is the meaning. Its syntactical connection is with what has already been established: 'the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>) is not spoken of by this word <s>Brahman</s>.' By this, the particle 'eva' (alone) is connected with the predicate word, and the word <s>Brahman</s> at its head of the sentence conveys the meaning of being the primary <s>Brahman</s>. And that is not appropriate for the <s>jīva</s> — this is what is stated. Or alternatively — the particle 'eva' is connected with the demonstrative word 'etam' (this one) denoting the subject, and has the sense of <s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s> (exclusion from connection with anything else). Nor should it be said that in this case the word <s>Brahman</s> would not have the quality of being emphatic (<s>sāvadhāraṇatva</s>); because when the meaning of the particle 'eva' — namely <s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s> — is elaborated as 'exclusion of Brahman-hood from another', the word <s>Brahman</s> acquires emphatic quality (<s>sāvadhāraṇatva</s>) through its connection with the Brahman-hood that is the meaning of the word <s>Brahman</s>. Although the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>) is not the referent of the word 'etat' — why? — because it is qualified by the word <s>Brahman</s> which denotes the counter-correlate of the meaning of the particle 'eva' — such a <s>sūtra</s>-commentary is possible; nevertheless, since it is not what the <s>Ṭīkā</s> states, it has not been advanced by anyone.
For they do not call the <s>jīva</s> alone <s>Brahman</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.1, verse 14:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.14:
sāvadhāraṇatve 'pi brahmaśabdasya kuto na jīve vṛttirityata āha - na hīti/ hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau hetau ca/ kavaya iti śeṣaḥ / kuta iti cet evakāraśiraskabrahmaśabdavācyatve jīvasya mukhyabrahmatvaṃ syāt, tacca nopapadyate / tasyāmukhyabrahmatvena prasiddhatvāditi bhāvaḥ / evamevakārasyoddeśyasambandhonānyayogavyavacchedakatve 'pi pūrvapakṣe etacchabdārthatvena abhimatajīvādanyasya brahmatvaṃ niṣiddhaṃ syāt / tacca nopapadyate / jīvādanyasya paramātmāno mukhyabrahmaṇo jātyāderamukhyabrahmaṇaśca sattvenānyasya brahmatvasambandhaniṣedhāyogādityapi draṣṭavyam / tattvapradīpe tu - jīvasya brahmatve tasya bhūtatvena bhūteṣvityuktaṃ bhūtasthatvaṃ na yujyata ityuktam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.14:
Even with the restrictive force [of the word 'eva'], why does the word '<s>Brahman</s>' not apply to the <s>jīva</s>? — to this he says: 'na hi' (for not). The word 'hi' is in the sense of well-known usage and reason. 'The wise' (<s>kavayaḥ</s>) is the remainder. Why? — if [it be asked]: if the <s>jīva</s> were denotable by the word '<s>Brahman</s>' headed by the restrictive particle 'eva,' the <s>jīva</s> would have primary <s>Brahman</s>-hood, and that is not tenable — because the <s>jīva</s> is well-known as not being primary <s>Brahman</s>: this is the import. Similarly, even when the particle 'eva' has the function of excluding the connection-with-another of the referent, in the prima facie view, the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of [an entity] other than the <s>jīva</s> intended by the word 'this' (<s>etad</s>) would be negated, and that too is not tenable — because since the <s>Paramātman</s> who is primary <s>Brahman</s>, distinct from the <s>jīva</s>, and [entities] of non-primary <s>Brahman</s> status such as genus and the like exist, the negation of the <s>Brahman</s>-connection of another is unjustified: this too should be noted. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, it is said: if the <s>jīva</s> were <s>Brahman</s>, then its status of being 'among the elements' (<s>bhūtasthatva</s>), as stated by '<s>bhūtatvena bhūteṣu</s>' (as an element among elements), would not be justified.

children.text:
'eṣa u eva brahmaiṣa u evātmaiṣa u eva savitaiṣa u evendra eṣa u
eva harirharati paraḥ parānandaḥ'; iti cendradyumnaśākhāyām // 5 //
children.translated_text:
'This alone is <s>Brahman</s>; this alone is the Self; this alone is <s>Savitṛ</s>; this alone is <s>Indra</s>; this alone
is <s>Hari</s> — He takes away [sins], the supreme, of supreme bliss' — thus [it is stated] in the <s>Indradyumna</s> branch. // 5 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.15:
viṣṇāvapi sāvadhāraṇabrahmaśabdasya vṛttiḥ kuta ityata āha - eṣa iti // u eva / yadvā - uśabdo viṣṇuparaḥ / tathā caiṣa viṣṇureva brahmetyarthaḥ / 'ātmānam'; ityuktamātmatvaṃ 'sa savitā'; ityuktasavitṛtvādikamapi viṣṇorevetyāha - eṣa u evātmetyādinā / ya u yo viṣṇureva hariḥ / tatra nimittamāha - haratīti / yajñagṛheṣviḍopahūtaṃ bhāgaṃ svīkarotītyarthaḥ / yadvā - satāṃ pāpaṃ haratītyarthaḥ / evameṣa eva para uttamaḥ pūrṇānandaśceti yojanā / indradyumnaśākhāyāmityasya 'ya etaṃ sarvabhūtasthaṃ viṣṇumeva brahmetyācakṣate indradyumnāḥ'; ityupaskṛtenānvayaḥ / asya ca hetoravatārikāgatasādhyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.15:
Whence does the word '<s>Brahman</s>' with restrictive force apply to <s>Viṣṇu</s> as well? — to this he says: '<s>eṣa</s>' (this). // 'U eva' [means 'alone']. Alternatively, the word 'u' refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. And thus, 'this <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>Brahman</s>' — this is the meaning. The selfhood stated by '<s>ātmānam</s>' (the Self), the <s>Savitṛ</s>-hood stated by '<s>sa savitā</s>' (He is <s>Savitṛ</s>), and the like also belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — this he says with '<s>eṣa u evātmā</s>' and so forth. 'Ya u' — He who is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is '<s>Hari</s>.' He states the reason for that: '<s>harati</s>' (He takes away). He accepts the share offered through the <s>iḍā</s> oblation in the sacrificial halls: this is the meaning. Alternatively: He takes away the sins of the virtuous: this is the meaning. Thus, this [entity] alone is the supreme, the highest, and of complete bliss: this is the syntactic connection. The phrase 'in the <s>Indradyumna</s> branch' has its syntactic connection with the interpolated [passage]: 'Those who call this <s>Viṣṇu</s> dwelling in all beings as <s>Brahman</s> alone are the <s>Indradyumnas</s>.' And the syntactic connection of this reason is with the thesis to be proved stated in the introduction.
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
And because of <s>Smṛti</s>. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.6 |
'I am the Self, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, dwelling in the hearts of all beings.' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 10.20)
'Having entered the earth, I sustain all beings by My power.' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 15.13)
And so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.16:
smṛtisamākhyayāpi viṣṇoratroktasarvagatatvaṃ sādhayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā tāṃ smṛtimudāharati - smṛteśceti // ityādismṛteśca sarvatrocyamāno nārāyaṇa evetyanvayaḥ / na kevalamuktahetubhya iti cakārārthaḥ / smṛteḥ svavacanatve 'pi paroktānuvādarūpatvāt taduktiryuktā / evamagre 'pi / he 'guḍākeśa'; guḍākā nidrā tadīśastadrahita iti yāvat / guḍavadāsamantātkeśā yasya saḥ ślakṣṇakeśeti vā / ahamantaryāmitayā sarvahṛdayasthita ityarthaḥ 'gāṃ'; bhūmiṃ āviśya tatrāvatīrya 'bhūtāni'; jīvān 'ojasā'; sāmarthyena dhārayāmītyanyavākyasyārthaḥ / ime ca gītāyāmarjunaṃ prati kṛṣṇavākye / pūrvavākye sarvabhūtāśayastho ya ātmā jīvaḥ so 'hamityabhedapratītinirāsāya dvitīyavākyodāharaṇam / tadgatatvenaiva taddhārakatvamabhipretam / ato nāsaṅgatiḥ / ādipadātsmṛtyantarasaṅgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.16:
Having read the <s>sūtra</s> that also establishes through <s>Smṛti</s> the all-pervasiveness of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> stated here, he cites that <s>Smṛti</s>: '<s>smṛteśca</s>' (and because of <s>Smṛti</s>). // 'From <s>Smṛti</s> and the like,' the one being spoken of everywhere is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone — this is the syntactic connection. The word 'ca' (and) means 'not only from the stated reasons.' Even though <s>Smṛti</s> is [the Lord's] own statement, since it has the nature of restatement of what was said by others, the citation of it is justified. Similarly hereafter too. O '<s>Guḍākeśa</s>' — <s>guḍākā</s> means sleep; its lord (<s>īśa</s>), meaning one who is free from it. Or, one whose hair is thick (<s>guḍavat</s>) like a ball on all sides — that is, one with smooth hair. 'I' — as the inner controller — 'dwell in the hearts of all': this is the meaning. '<s>Gām</s>' — the earth — 'having entered' (<s>āviśya</s>) — having descended into it — 'beings' (<s>bhūtāni</s>) — the <s>jīvas</s> — 'by power' (<s>ojasā</s>) — by capacity — 'I sustain': this is the meaning of the other verse. These are the words of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> addressed to <s>Arjuna</s> in the <s>Gītā</s>. The citation of the second verse is for the purpose of dispelling the misconception of non-difference — [the notion that] whoever is the Self dwelling in the hearts of all beings, that <s>jīva</s> is 'I.' The sustaining [of all] is intended as being through pervading them. Hence there is no incoherence. By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), other <s>Smṛti</s> [passages] are included.
And what is without authority should not be imagined. // 6 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.17:
anye tu 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ satyasaṅkalpaḥ'; iti vākye manomayatvādiguṇar iśvara eva, na jīva iti siddhāntite jīveśayoraikyāt kathametadityāśaṅkya asti bhedaḥ / na cāpasiddhāntaḥ, yato 'yaṃ na pāramārthikaḥ, kintu, mithyābhūta eva sūtrakṛtā vivakṣita iti samādhāya bhedamithyātve sūtratātparyaṃ varṇayanti / teṣāṃ matamāśaṅkya dūṣayati - na ceti // castvarthe / nañ ca tadviruddhatadabhāvārthaḥ / tathā ca 'aprāmāṇikaṃ'; bhedamithyātvaṃ 'na kalpyaṃ'; sūtrakṛdvivakṣāviṣayatvena na kalpanīyam / kutaḥ? yatastadaprāmāṇikaṃ pramāṇaśūnyaṃ 'dvā suparṇā'; ityādipramāṇaviruddhaṃ ca ata iti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.17:
Others, however — having established in the passage 'consisting of mind, having <s>Prāṇa</s> as body, of luminous form, of true resolve' that the qualities of consisting of mind and the like belong to <s>Īśvara</s> alone and not the <s>jīva</s> — [and then] raising the objection 'how is this, given the identity of the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>?' — resolve it by [saying] 'there is difference; but it is not a deviation from the doctrine, since this [difference] is not ultimate but is merely false, and the <s>sūtrakāra</s> intended [it as such]' — [and thus] they describe the purport of the <s>sūtra</s> as the falsity of difference. Anticipating and refuting their view, he says: 'na ca' (and not). The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'tu' (but). The negative particle 'na' has the meaning of what is contrary to and what is the absence of that. And thus: 'what is without authority' (<s>aprāmāṇikam</s>) — the falsity of difference — 'should not be imagined' (<s>na kalpyam</s>) — should not be conceived as being within the purview of the <s>sūtrakāra</s>'s intention. Why? Because that is 'without authority' — devoid of valid means of knowledge — and is contradicted by valid means of knowledge such as 'Two birds [of beautiful plumage]' (<s>dvā suparṇā</s>) and the like: this is the syntactic connection.
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //

children.text: arbhakaukastvāttadvyapadeśācca neti cenna nicāyyatvādevaṃ vyomavacca | BBs_1,2.7 |
children.translated_text: If [it be objected:] 'Not [<s>Brahman</s>], because of the smallness of the abode and because of the designation of that [entity] as [the <s>jīva</s>]' — [the answer is:] no, because it is to be meditated upon as such, and like space. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.7 |

children.text: sarveṣu bhūteṣvityalpaukastvāt cakṣurmayatvādinā jīvavyapadeśācca neti cenna /
children.translated_text: 'In all beings' — because of the smallness of the abode, and because of the designation as the <s>jīva</s> through [the expression] 'consisting of the eye' (<s>cakṣurmayatva</s>) and the like — [it is] not [<s>Brahman</s>] — if such [be the objection] — no.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.18:
uktārthamākṣipya samādadhatsūtraṃ paṭhitvākṣepāṃśaṃ tāvadvyācaṣṭe - arbhaketi // vākya iti śeṣaḥ / arbhaketyasya vyākhyālpeti / alpamokaḥ sthānaṃ yasya tasya bhāvastattvaṃ tasmāt / tathācālpasthānasthitatvokterityarthaḥ / sarvajīvahṛdayasuṣirāṇāmalpatvāditi bhāvaḥ / sūtragatatacchabdasya prakāraprakāryubhayārthatvaṃ matvāha - cakṣuriti, jīva iti ca / ādipadena śrotramayatvādi gṛhyate / cakārādādiśabdādvā ādityaśrutirapi gahyate / ata eva jīvapadamādityasādhāraṇaṃ prāyoji / jīvasya vyapadeśo vacanaṃ jīvavyapadeśaḥ 'cakṣurmayaśśrotramayaḥ'; iti śrutāviti śeṣaḥ / co hetusamuccaye / neti / sarvatrocyamāno nārāyaṇa eveti yaduktaṃ tannetyarthaḥ / paramātmapakṣe 'pi jīvapakṣa iva bādhakasadbhāvāditi bhāvaḥ // parihārāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti / uktabādhakādviṣṇoḥ sarvatrocyamānatvābhāvo netyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.18:
Having raised an objection against the established conclusion, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves it, and first explains the objection-portion: '<s>arbhaka</s>' (small).
