'In the passage' is the remainder. The gloss of '<s>arbhaka</s>' is 'alpa' (small). The smallness of the abode (<s>okas</s>), that is, the place — the state of that — from that. And thus, because of the statement of being situated in a small place: this is the meaning. Since the cavities of the hearts of all <s>jīvas</s> are small: this is the import. Understanding the dual meaning — both as qualifier and qualified — of the word 'tat' occurring in the <s>sūtra</s>, he says: '<s>cakṣur</s>' (eye), and '<s>jīva</s>.' By the word 'ādi' (and the like), 'consisting of hearing' (<s>śrotramayatva</s>) and the like are included. By the word 'ca' (and), or by the word 'ādi,' the <s>Āditya</s>-<s>Śruti</s> (passage about the Sun) is also included. Hence the word '<s>jīva</s>' is used as common to <s>Āditya</s> as well. The designation of the <s>jīva</s> — the statement — is the '<s>jīvavyapadeśa</s>' (designation as <s>jīva</s>), in the <s>Śruti</s> 'consisting of the eye, consisting of hearing': this is the remainder. The word 'ca' is for the accumulation of reasons. 'Na' (not) — what was said, namely that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the one spoken of everywhere — that is not so: this is the meaning. Even in the <s>Paramātman</s> view, since there exists an invalidator just as in the <s>jīva</s> view: this is the import. // He explains the resolution-portion: 'na' (not so). The non-existence of [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] being spoken of everywhere, due to the stated invalidator — is not so: this is the meaning.
Because that very <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be meditated upon (<s>nicāyya</s>) through the smallness of the abode and through the form of consisting of the eye and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.19:
kuto netyato 'tra bādhakābhāvāditi hetum arbhakaukastvādīnāṃ ca viṣṇāvevopapannatvenābādhakatvāditi tadupapādakahetuṃ copaskṛtya tarhi viṣṇāvarbhakaukastvādikathanavaiyarthyamityāśaṅkya tatparihāratvenoktamevaṃnicāyyatvādityaṃśaṃ vyākhyāti - arbhakaukastveneti / ādiśabdenmanomayatvena ityāha / anena sautraivaṃśabdaḥ prakārārthatayā vyākhyātaḥ / siddhāntāṃśe 'pi viṣṇvarthakasya vyatyastatacchabdasya sāvadhāraṇasyānvayamabhipretyāha - tasyaiveti / yadvā - pradhānasūtre 'nuvṛttasya tadityasyeha vipariṇatasyāvṛttiṃ matvāha - tasyaiva viṣṇoriti / evakāro 'pyarthaḥ / tathā ca sarvagatasyāpi jīvavilakṣaṇasyāpītyarthaḥ / na tu jīvasya, ityanyaniṣedhārtho vā evakāraḥ / 'nicāyyatvāt'; upāsyatvāt / anenāparichinne alpaukastvoktiḥ jīvavilakṣaṇe cakṣurmayatvādyuktivyartheti śaṅkā nistā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.19:
Why 'not so'? — because here there is absence of an invalidator — this is the reason; and because the smallness of the abode and the like are established as applicable to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone and therefore are not invalidators — this is the supporting reason. Having interpolated [these], he explains, with anticipation of the objection 'then the statement of smallness of the abode and the like with regard to <s>Viṣṇu</s> would be purposeless,' the portion 'evaṃ nicāyyatvāt' (because it is to be meditated upon as such) as the resolution: 'by the smallness of the abode.' By the word 'ādi' (and the like), 'by consisting of mind' (<s>manomayatva</s>) is stated. By this, the word 'evaṃ' in the <s>sūtra</s> is explained as having the meaning of manner. In the established-conclusion portion too, intending the syntactic connection of the word 'tat' (that) in the <s>sūtra</s> — which refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and has the reversed [order] with restrictive force — he says: 'of that very [<s>Viṣṇu</s>].' Alternatively, understanding the recurrence of the word 'tat' from the <s>sūtra</s> in which it [previously appeared] reversed, he says: 'of that very <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' The word 'eva' (alone) too has a meaning. And thus, even of one who pervades all, even of one who is distinct from the <s>jīva</s>: this is the meaning. Not of the <s>jīva</s> — this is the alternative meaning of the word 'eva' as negating others. 'Because it is to be meditated upon' (<s>nicāyyatvāt</s>) — because it is to be worshipped. By this, the objection that the statement of smallness of the abode with regard to the unlimited, and the statement of consisting of the eye and the like with regard to one distinct from the <s>jīva</s>, are purposeless — is resolved.
And even though [He is] all-pervading, the smallness of the abode is justified — like space.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.20:
idānīṃ sarvagatasyālpaukastvamayuktamiti śaṅkānirāsāya sūtragṛhītaṃ dṛṣṭāntāṃśaṃ evamityasya caśabdenāpyanvayaṃ vyatyastatatpadasya āvṛttasya 'yujyate'; iti adhyāhṛtenāpi sambandhamabhipretya vyākhyāti - sarvagatatva iti // apīti dvitīyacaśabdavyākhyānam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.20:
Now, for the purpose of dispelling the objection that the smallness of the abode is unjustified for the all-pervading, he explains the simile-portion adopted in the <s>sūtra</s>, intending the syntactic connection of 'evaṃ' with the word 'ca,' the recurrence of the reversed word 'tat,' and [its connection] with the interpolated 'is justified' (<s>yujyate</s>): 'even though all-pervading.' // The word 'api' (even though) is the gloss of the second 'ca.'
<s>Viṣṇu</s> consists of all the senses and dwells in all living beings;
He is denoted by all names and is proclaimed in all the <s>Vedas</s>. — Thus in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>. // 7 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.21:
yadapi jīvavilakṣaṇasya nityajñānavato jñānakaraṇacakṣurādiprācuryarūpacakṣurmayatvādikathanamayuktamiti codyaṃ, tat caśabdasūcitasmṛtyā nirāha - sarvendriyamaya iti // viṣṇuryataḥ sarvaprāṇiṣu saṃsthitaḥ / prāṇā indriyāṇi tadvantaḥ prāṇinaḥ teṣvindriyaniyāmakatvena sthitaḥ / sarvendriyasvāmīti yāvat / ataḥ sarvendriyamaya ityukta ityarthaḥ/ svāmitvaṃ mayaḍartha iti bhāvaḥ / caśabdaḥ prathamapādārthe dvitīyapādārthaṃ hetumāha / evaṃ dvitīyatṛtīyapādadvayamapi ādityādisarvaprāṇisthitatvādādityādisarvanāmābhidheya iti hetuhetumadbhāvena vyākhyeyam / ata eva caśabdaḥ dvitīyatṛtīyacaśabdavat viśeṣaṇāntarasamuccayepyanveyaḥ / anena prathamapādena 'cakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayo manomayo vāṅmayaḥ'; ityādikaṃ brahmaṇi tatsvāmitvena nimittena prayuktamiti vyākhyātaṃ bhavati / evaṃ dvitīyatṛtīyapādābhyāṃ tattadgatatvenādityāditattannāmavācyatvakathanamukhenādityaśruterīśvaravācitvamuktaṃ bhavati / anenaivāditye 'nuktiyuktivirodhaśca parihṛtaḥ / caturthapādena chandaḥpadoktavedamukhyārthatvācchandomayatvaṃ ca viṣṇoryuktamitiyuktaṃ bhavati / aitareyabhāṣye - 'sampūrṇadarśanaśakteḥ cakṣurmayaḥ sampūrṇaśravaṇaśakteḥ śrotramayaḥ satyakāmatvāt chandomayaḥ sarvamantṛtvānmanomayaḥ sarvavaktṛtvādvāṅmayaḥ pūrṇaphalarūpatvādātmā'; iti / tathā bṛhadbhāṣye - 'mayaṭprāyuryārthaḥ svarūpe ca'; iti pratijñāya -
sarvadraṣṭṛsvarūpatvāccakṣurmaya itīryate /
sarvaśrotṛsvarūpatvātsa śrotramayar iritaḥ // iti /
tathā bhāgavatatātparye -
sarve viṣṇau sthitā yasmādatassarvamayo hyasau /
iti prakārāntareṇa bhagavati cakṣurmayatvādikaṃ vyākhyātam / skānde ityanantaraṃ uktvāditi śeṣaḥ / asya jīvavilakṣaṇasyāpi indriyasvāmitvādinā cakṣurmayatvādi yujyate iti na tadayoga ityupaskṛtasādhyenānvayaḥ /
anena 'sarveṣu bhūteṣu'; ityātrārbhakaukastvokteḥ 'cakṣurmayaḥ'; ityādau ca tasya jīvasya tena cakṣurmayatvādinā prakāreṇoktatvāt ādityavyapadeśācca asmādeva bādhakānna sarvatrokto nārāyaṇa iti cet - na, kutaḥ? atra bādhakābhāvāt, arbhakaukastvādeśca viṣṇāvevopapatteḥ / na cāparicchinnasyārbhakaukastvoktiḥ jīvavilakṣaṇasya cakṣurmayatvādyuktiśca vyartheti vācyam / evaṃ nicāyyatvāt / cāyṛ pūjāniśāmanayoḥ / tasyaiva tasyāparicchinnasyāpi viṣṇoḥ alpaukastvacakṣurmayatvādinā prakāreṇopāsyatvena upāsanārthaṃ taduktisārthakyāt / na cāparicchinne jīvavilakṣaṇe ca brahmāṇi arbhakaukastvādyuktirna yujyata iti vācyam/ yataḥ 'evaṃ ca'; evamapi sarvagatatve 'pi 'vyomavat'; tadalpaukastvaṃ cakṣurmayatvādi yujyate / yathā vyāptasyāpi vyomno 'vyākṛtākāśasya maṭhādyekadeśāvasthitiḥ tathā brahmaṇo bhūtāśayādau sthitiryuktā / yataścaivaṃ viṣṇorjīvavilakṣaṇatve 'pi indriyasvāmitvādinā cakṣurmayatvādyuktiryuktāta iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.1.21): As for the objection that it is improper to describe <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> (being constituted of the eye) and so forth — which denotes abundance of sense-organs like the eye as instruments of knowledge — for one who is distinct from the <s>jīva</s> and possesses eternal knowledge, [<s>Madhva</s>] refutes this by means of the <s>smṛti</s> indicated by the word 'ca': '<s>sarvendriyamaya</s>' (constituted of all senses). Since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established in all living beings — <s>prāṇas</s> are the sense-organs, those possessing them are <s>prāṇins</s> (living beings), and He is established in them as the controller of the senses — the meaning is: He is the lord of all senses. Hence it is said '<s>sarvendriyamaya</s>' — this is the meaning. The purport is that the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix means lordship (<s>svāmitva</s>). The word 'ca' in the first <s>pāda</s> states the second <s>pāda</s>'s meaning as a reason. Similarly, the second and third <s>pādas</s> too should be explained through the relation of reason and result — namely, because He abides in all beings from <s>Āditya</s> onward, He is denoted by all names such as <s>Āditya</s> and so forth. For this very reason, the word 'ca' should be construed, like the 'ca' in the second and third <s>pādas</s>, as aggregating additional qualifications. By this first <s>pāda</s>, it is explained that '<s>cakṣurmayaḥ</s>, <s>śrotramayaḥ</s>, <s>manomayaḥ</s>, <s>vāṅmayaḥ</s>' and so forth are applied to <s>Brahman</s> by reason of His lordship over them. Similarly, by the second and third <s>pādas</s>, it is stated that the <s>Āditya</s>-<s>śruti</s> refers to <s>Īśvara</s>, through the explanation that He is denoted by names like <s>Āditya</s> by virtue of His presence in each of them. By this very means, the contradiction regarding the non-mention and logical inconsistency with respect to <s>Āditya</s> is resolved. By the fourth <s>pāda</s>, it becomes established that <s>chandomayatva</s> (being constituted of the Vedas) is also fitting for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because the Vedas are the primary meaning of the word '<s>chandas</s>' mentioned in the <s>chandaḥ-pada</s>. In the <s>Aitareya-bhāṣya</s>: 'He is <s>cakṣurmayaḥ</s> because of His complete power of seeing, <s>śrotramayaḥ</s> because of His complete power of hearing, <s>chandomayaḥ</s> because of His having true desires, <s>manomayaḥ</s> because He is the thinker of all, <s>vāṅmayaḥ</s> because He is the speaker of all, and <s>ātmā</s> because He is of the nature of complete fruition.' Similarly, in the <s>Bṛhad-bhāṣya</s>, having stated the principle that 'the <s>mayaṭ</s> suffix means lordship (<s>prāyuryā</s>) and also intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpa</s>)': 'Because His intrinsic nature is that of the seer of all, He is called <s>cakṣurmayaḥ</s>; because His intrinsic nature is that of the hearer of all, He is called <s>śrotramayaḥ</s>.' Likewise in the <s>Bhāgavata-tātparya</s>: 'Since all abide in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, therefore He is indeed <s>sarvamayaḥ</s> (constituted of all)' — thus <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> and the rest are explained in the Lord in another manner. After stating 'in the <s>Skānda</s>' — 'having said' is to be supplied. The connection with the established conclusion is: since even for this one who is distinct from the <s>jīva</s>, <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> and the rest are fitting through lordship over the senses and so forth, there is no incongruity of that. As for the objection that — because in 'in all beings' the smallness of stature is stated, and because in '<s>cakṣurmayaḥ</s>' etc. that <s>jīva</s> is described in that manner of <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> etc., and because of the designation as <s>Āditya</s> — therefore from these very obstructing reasons <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is not the one spoken of everywhere — [the reply is] no, because there is no obstruction here, and because smallness of stature and the rest are appropriate only for <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Nor should one say that the statement of smallness for the unlimited one and the reasoning of <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> for one distinct from the <s>jīva</s> are purposeless — because it is to be ascertained thus: '<s>cāyṛ</s>' means worship and settling. The statement of smallness of stature and <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> and the rest for that very unlimited <s>Viṣṇu</s> serves the purpose of meditation upon Him in that manner. Nor should one say that the statement of smallness of stature and the rest is not fitting for the unlimited <s>Brahman</s> distinct from the <s>jīva</s>, because 'thus also' — even with all-pervasiveness, 'like space' — His smallness of stature and <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> etc. are fitting. Just as space, though pervading everywhere, has a delimitation to a particular place such as a hall in its unmanifest form, so too <s>Brahman</s>'s abiding in the inner recesses of beings is fitting. And because thus, even though <s>Viṣṇu</s> is distinct from the <s>jīva</s>, the reasoning of <s>cakṣurmayatva</s> etc. through lordship over the senses is fitting — this is stated as the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
[If it be said] that the attainment of shared experience [would follow], [we say] no, because of the distinction. (<s>BBs</s> 1,2.8)
<s>Oṃ</s>.
[If it be said] that since the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme Lord abide in the same body, the attainment of shared experience [would follow] — [we say] no.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.22:
punaruktamākṣipya samādadhatsūtramupanyasyati - sambhogeti / atra pūrvasūtrādevaṃśabdamanuvartya tadbodhitamāpādakaṃ darśayan pūrvapakṣāṃśaṃ tāvadvyācaṣṭe - jīveti // jīvaparamātmanorityarthaḥ / eketi // viṣṇoḥ sarvaśarīrasthatve jīvena sahaikaśarīrasthatvaprāpteriti bhāvaḥ / saṃśabdasya 'vyavahṛpaṇossamarthayoḥ'; ityatreva samānārthatvamāśrityāha - samāneti / iveśvarapakṣe 'pi bādhakasāmyānnāyaṃ sarvagata iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / parihārāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti/ neśvarasya samānabhogaprāptirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.1.22): Having raised a seeming repetition, [<s>Madhva</s>] presents the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves it — '<s>sambhoga</s>' etc. Here, carrying forward the word 'thus' (<s>evam</s>) from the previous <s>sūtra</s> and showing the enabling condition it indicates, he first explains the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection) portion — '<s>jīva</s>' etc. The meaning is: of the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>Paramātman</s>. '<s>eka</s>' etc. — the purport is: since <s>Viṣṇu</s> abides in all bodies, the situation of abiding in the same body together with the <s>jīva</s> would follow. Relying on the meaning of the prefix 'sam' as 'equal' according to the rule '<s>vyavahṛpaṇos samarthayoḥ</s>,' he says — '<s>samāna</s>' etc. The remainder of the sentence is: even in the <s>Īśvara</s> position, because the obstruction is the same, this one is not all-pervasive. He explains the resolution portion — '<s>na</s>' etc. The meaning is: <s>Īśvara</s> does not attain shared experience.
Because of the distinction in capacity.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.23:
kuto netyastatra hetutvena vaiśeṣyādityaṃśaṃ yojayati - sāmarthyeti // svārthe ṣyañ / viśeṣiṇo bhāva iti vā / tathā ca parasya samānabhogāprāptau jīvādapi sāmarthyavaiśeṣyādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.1.23): [Asking] why not, he connects the portion '<s>vaiśeṣyāt</s>' (because of distinction) as the reason — '<s>sāmarthya</s>' etc. The <s>ṣyañ</s> suffix is in the reflexive sense (<s>svārtha</s>); or it means 'the state of that which is distinguished' (<s>viśeṣiṇo bhāvaḥ</s>). And thus, the meaning is: the Supreme does not attain shared experience because of the distinction in capacity even from the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text:
uktaṃ ca gāruḍe -
sarvajñālpajñatābhedātsarvaśaktyalpaśaktitaḥ /
svātantryapāratantryābhyāṃ sambhogo neśajīvayoḥ // iti ca // 8 //
children.translated_text: And it has been stated in the <s>Gāruḍa Purāṇa</s>: 'Because of the difference between omniscience and limited knowledge, between omnipotence and limited power, and because of [the distinction of] independence and dependence, the experience of <s>Īśvara</s> and the <s>jīva</s> is not shared.' (8)
Thus ends the <s>Sarvagatatvādhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of all-pervasiveness).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.1.24:
kiṃ tatsāmarthyavaiśeṣyaṃ, yena samānabhogāprāptirityata āha - uktamiti // na kevalaṃ sūtre jīveśayorbhogasāmyābhāvaḥ, tatra hetutvena sāmarthyavaiśeṣyaṃ coktam, kintu gāruḍe ceti samuccayārthaścaḥ / kimuktamityatastatpaṭhati - sarvajñeti // sarvajñatvālpajñatvarūpabhedakadharmābhyāmityarthaḥ / prāptasya bādhakasya parihārāya viṣṇoḥ sāmarthye satyapi prathamaṃ prāptistāvatsyādeva agnistambhavato dāhaprāptivat / sāpi bhagavati na sambhavati / tasya sārvajñenaiṣyadbādhakaparihartṛtvasambhavāditi bhāveneha sārvajñoktiḥ, na jīvena sahekaśarīrasthatve 'pi duḥkhaparityāgena sukhamātrabhoge svātantrayaṃ hetuḥ / jīvasya cobhayānubhave pāratantryaṃ heturiti vivektavyam / sambhogaḥ samānabhogaḥ / gāruḍa ityanvayaḥ / 'iti ca'; iti caśabdapāṭhe tatra pūrvoktena samuccayārthaścakāraḥ/ anena yato yathā ekasya jīvasya sarvaśarīrasthatve sarvasamānabhogaprāptiḥ bādhikānupapattiḥ sūtroktāsti / tathā evamīśasya sarvabhūtagatatvamaṅgīkṛtya jīveśvarayorekaśarīrasthatve parasya jīvasamānabhogaprāptirbādhikāsti / ato neśvaraḥ sarvabhūtagata iti cenna, kutaḥ tasya tadaprāptau jīvādapi sāmarthyavaiśeṣyāt agnistambhavato dāhābhāvavaditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati // 1 //
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.1.24): [Asking] what is that distinction in capacity by which there is no attainment of shared experience, he says — '<s>uktam</s>' etc. Not only is the absence of equality of experience between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, along with the distinction in capacity as the reason, but also in the <s>Gāruḍa Purāṇa</s> — the word 'ca' serves an aggregative purpose. [Asking] what is stated, he cites that — '<s>sarvajña</s>' etc. The meaning is: by the distinguishing attributes in the form of omniscience and limited knowledge. To resolve the obstruction that has arisen, even when <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s capacity is granted, the attainment [of shared experience] would first occur — like the attainment of burning for one who possesses the power of fire-arrest (<s>agnistambha</s>). But even that does not apply to the Lord, because through His omniscience He is capable of removing the obstruction — this is the purport of the mention of omniscience here. [The distinction is] not that independence is the reason for the enjoyment of pleasure alone by abandoning suffering even while abiding in the same body with the <s>jīva</s>; rather, it should be understood that dependence is the reason for the <s>jīva</s>'s experience of both [pleasure and suffering]. '<s>Sambhoga</s>' means equal experience. The syntactic connection is with '<s>Gāruḍa</s>.' Regarding the reading '<s>iti ca</s>': the word 'ca' there serves the aggregative purpose with what was stated previously. By this, just as there is the obstructing impossibility that a single <s>jīva</s>'s abiding in all bodies would lead to the attainment of shared experience in all — so too, having accepted <s>Īśvara</s>'s presence in all beings, the attainment of experience shared with the <s>jīva</s> for the Supreme when <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> are in the same body is an obstruction. If [one says] therefore <s>Īśvara</s> is not present in all beings — [we say] no, because for His non-attainment of that [shared experience] there is a distinction in capacity even from the <s>jīva</s>, just as there is absence of burning for one who possesses the power of fire-arrest — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. (1)
Thus ends the <s>Sarvagatatvādhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of all-pervasiveness).
2. <s>Attṛtvādhikaraṇam</s> (the topic of being the eater/consumer).

It was stated: 'From whom is the origin and so forth [of this universe]' (<s>janmādyasya yataḥ</s>). Among those [characteristics], the attribute of being the eater (<s>attṛtva</s>) is understood from <s>Aditi</s> in the passage: 'Whatever He created, that He resolved to eat; He eats everything — that is the <s>Aditi</s>-hood of <s>Aditi</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.5).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.1:
atrādhikaraṇe lokato 'nyatra prasiddhāditiśabdena sahoktāttṛtvaliṅgasya harau samanvayaḥ kriyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiḥ viṣayavākyamudāhṛtya viṣayasaṃśayau sayuktikapūrvapakṣaṃ ca sūcayati - janmeti // janmādisūtre janmādikartṛtvaṃ viṣṇoruktamityarthaḥ / tatreti / uktalakṣaṇeṣu madhya ityarthaḥ / praviṣṭamiti śeṣaḥ / attṛtvamiti //
children.translated_text: (<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.2.1): In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the coordination (<s>samanvaya</s>) of the attribute of being the eater (<s>attṛtva</s>) — which is stated together with the word <s>Aditi</s>, a term well-known elsewhere as referring to someone other than [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] in common usage — with <s>Hari</s> is carried out. [<s>Madhva</s>] indicates the consistency with <s>śruti</s> and so forth, cites the subject-passage, and suggests the subject, doubt, and reasoned <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> — '<s>janma</s>' etc. The meaning is: in the <s>janmādi-sūtra</s>, the creatorship and other [attributes] of <s>Viṣṇu</s> were stated. '<s>Tatra</s>' — the meaning is: 'among those stated characteristics.' '<s>praviṣṭam</s>' (entered) is to be supplied. '<s>Attṛtvam</s>' —

children.text:
sa sargakāle ca karoti sarvaṃ
saṃhārakāle tu tadatti bhūyaḥ /
sraṣṭā pātā tathaivāttā (skānde)
ityādāvadidhātuprakṛtikānekaśabdavācyaṃ saṃhartṛtvāparaparyāyaśabdabodhyaṃ ūrṇanābhyādivadattṛtvaṃ tadityarthaḥ / anena aderbhakṣaṇārthatvādaditerattṛtve 'pi na saṃhartṛtvalakṣaṇasyātivyāptiriti śaṅkā nirastā / prathametiśabdaḥ śrutigataḥ / dvitīyastu bhāṣyakārīyaḥ / aditerityāvartate / tatraikaṃ bhāvapradhānam / tathā ca iti bṛhadāraṇyakavākye yadattṛtvaṃ pratīyate tat aditeḥ devamātureva bhavet / kutaḥ? 'aditeḥ'; aditiśruteḥ / tathā adititvaliṅgācceti yojanā / adititvaṃ ca gotvādivadaditimātradhramo, na viṣṇau sāvakāśam / anena janmādisūtroktalakṣaṇasyātivyāptyasambhavākṣepāttenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ / śrutyuktamattṛtvaṃ viṣayaḥ / viṣṇoranyasya veti sandehaḥ / devamāturaditereveti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ / aditiśrutiradititvayuktiśca sūcitā bhavati / pūrvapakṣe śrutyarthastu - 'saḥ'; aditirdevamātā saṃvatsaranāmnā caturmukhena 'yadyadasṛjata tattadattumadhriyata'; manaḥ / ādacceti śeṣaḥ / kutaḥ sarvāttṛtvamaditeḥ? yasmātsarvātrī sā sarvamattīti yat tadeva hyaditerdevamātuḥ 'adititvam'; aditiśabdavācyatve nimittam, anyathā tanna syāditi / asmin pakṣe 'pi sthalāntarasthāditiśabdasya nirvacanamidam / atra sarvaśabdaḥ sudhārītyā adityadanayogyasarvaparaḥ / ṭīkārītyā saṅkucitasarvaparo vā/ siddhānte śrutyarthastu - 'saḥ'; saṃvatsaranāmakaḥ caturmukho 'yadyadevāsṛjata tattatsarvamattuṃ'; sa mṛtyunāmā janārdano 'dhriyata / ādacca / kutaḥ sarvasaṃhartṛtvaṃ viṣṇoḥ? 'aditeḥ'; aditiśabdāt / aditirhi 'idaṃ sarvaṃ......yadidaṃ kiñca'; (tai.2-6) 'aditirdevatāmayī'; (kaṭha. 4-7) iti śrutyantare brahmaṇyaditiśabdaprayogāditi yāvat / tāvatāpi kutaḥ sarvāttṛtvaṃ viṣṇoḥ? sarvamattīti yattadeva hi 'aditeḥ'; strīliṅgāditiśabdavācyasya 'adititvam'; aditiśabdavācyatvaṃ anyathā sa nirnimittakaḥ syāditi bhāvaḥ / anena viṣṇoḥ sarvāttṛtāyāṃ tannimittakaśrutyantaragatāditiśabdo heturityuktaṃ bhavati / uktaṃ hi candrikāyām / 'tattadattumiti pūrvapratijñātasarvāttṛtāyāṃ śrutyantare brahmaṇi prayuktasya sarvāttṛtvanimittakasyāditiśabdahetūkaraṇe sambhavati'; iti / ata eva ṛgbhāṣye 'atti viśvaṃ tena caivāditiriti viṣṇuḥ'; ityuktam / tatraiva 'guṇataḥ kālataścānantyarūpamakhaṇḍitatvaṃ cāditiśabdapravṛttinimittam'; iti coktam /
children.translated_text: 'At the time of creation He makes everything, and at the time of dissolution He again consumes that' (<s>Skānda</s>); 'The creator, protector, and likewise the consumer' — in such [passages], the <s>attṛtva</s> (being the eater/consumer), which is expressed by multiple words derived from the root <s>ad</s> (to eat) and which is synonymous with <s>saṃhartṛtva</s> (being the destroyer), is like [the activity of] a spider — that is the meaning. By this, the doubt is removed that since the root <s>ad</s> means eating (<s>bhakṣaṇa</s>), even if <s>Aditi</s>'s <s>attṛtva</s> is accepted, there would be no over-extension of the characteristic of being the destroyer. The first word '<s>iti</s>' belongs to the <s>śruti</s>; the second is the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s>'s (commentator's). '<s>Aditeḥ</s>' is carried forward. One of the two [uses of <s>iti</s>] has the abstract noun as primary. And thus: in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> passage, the <s>attṛtva</s> that is understood would belong to <s>Aditi</s>, the mother of the gods, alone. Why? Because of the <s>Aditi</s>-<s>śruti</s> — [the word] '<s>aditeḥ</s>' [in the text]. And also because of the indication of <s>Aditi</s>-hood (<s>adititva-liṅga</s>) — this is the construal. And <s>adititva</s> is, like <s>gotva</s> (cowness) and the like, a property residing only in <s>Aditi</s>, not applicable to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. By this [objection], since the characteristic stated in the <s>janmādi-sūtra</s> faces the charge of over-extension and impossibility, the connection [of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>] is one of objection (<s>ākṣepikī</s>). The subject is the <s>attṛtva</s> stated in <s>śruti</s>. The doubt is: does it belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> or to someone else? The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is: it belongs to <s>Aditi</s>, the mother of the gods, alone. The <s>Aditi</s>-<s>śruti</s> and the reasoning from <s>Aditi</s>-hood are indicated. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> according to the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is: '<s>saḥ</s>' — <s>Aditi</s>, the mother of the gods, [designated] by the name <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (year) as the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>], 'whatever He created, that He resolved to eat' — [this is] the mind's [intention]. '<s>ādacca</s>' (and consumed) is to be supplied. Why is <s>Aditi</s> the consumer of all? Because she consumes all — that she eats everything is indeed the reason for <s>Aditi</s>, the mother of the gods, being called by the word '<s>Aditi</s>'; otherwise that [etymology] would not hold — thus. Even in this position, this is the etymological explanation of the word <s>Aditi</s> found elsewhere. Here the word '<s>sarva</s>' (all) according to the <s>Sudhā</s> commentary means all that is fit to be consumed by <s>Aditi</s>; or according to the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, it refers to a restricted 'all.' The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> according to the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) is: '<s>saḥ</s>' — the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] named <s>Saṃvatsara</s>, 'whatever He created, all that' — <s>Janārdana</s>, named <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), 'resolved to eat.' And consumed. Why is <s>Viṣṇu</s> the universal destroyer? Because of [the word] '<s>aditeḥ</s>' — from the word <s>Aditi</s>. For <s>Aditi</s> [is used] in other <s>śrutis</s> for <s>Brahman</s>: 'This is all that...... whatever there is' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6), '<s>Aditi</s> who is full of divinity' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 4.7) — thus the word <s>Aditi</s> is applied to <s>Brahman</s> in other <s>śrutis</s>. Even so, why is universal <s>attṛtva</s> [attributed to] <s>Viṣṇu</s>? That He eats everything — that indeed is the reason for the one denoted by the feminine word '<s>Aditi</s>' having '<s>Aditi</s>-hood,' that is, being denoted by the word <s>Aditi</s>; otherwise it would be without a cause — this is the purport. By this it is stated that a word '<s>Aditi</s>' occurring in another <s>śruti</s>, which is occasioned by universal <s>attṛtva</s>, is the reason [for applying it to <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. For it has been said in the <s>Candrikā</s>: 'When the word <s>Aditi</s> — which is applied to <s>Brahman</s> in another <s>śruti</s> and is occasioned by universal <s>attṛtva</s> — is taken as the basis, the previously asserted universal <s>attṛtva</s> in "He resolved to eat that" is established.' Therefore, in the <s>Ṛg-bhāṣya</s>, it is stated: 'He eats the universe, and therefore He is called <s>Aditi</s> — this is <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' And there it is also stated: 'Infinity in terms of qualities and time, and indivisibility, are the grounds for the application of the word <s>Aditi</s>.'

children.text:
'sa yadyadevāsṛjata'; iti pulliṅgaṃ ca 'kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate';
(bha.gī. 15-16.) ityādivat //
children.translated_text: And the masculine gender in 'Whatever He created' [is used] just as in '<s>Kūṭasthaḥ</s> (the immutable) is called <s>Akṣara</s> (the imperishable)' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 15.16) and so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.2:
nanvetadattṛtvamaditeścetkathaṃ tarhi tasyāṃ sa iti pulliṅgaṃ yuktaṃ syāt / atastena śrutyādibādha ityata āha - sa iti // iti vākye śrutamityarthaḥ / ityādivadityānantaraṃ adityāṃ yujyata iti śeṣaḥ / castvarthaḥ / ādipadena 'so 'haṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda'; iti chandogavākyaṃ gṛhyate / kūṭamākāśaṃ tadvannirvikāratayā tiṣṭhatīti kūṭasthaḥ / prakṛtiḥ 'akṣaro'; dehato 'vināśitvāducyate iti gītāvākyasyārthaḥ / dikśabditānāṃ pūrvādi caturdigavasthitabhagavadbāhūnāṃ 'vatsaṃ'; tato jātaṃ 'vāyuṃ'; mukhyaprāṇamahaṃ 'veda'; jānāmītyarthaḥ / lakṣmīvākyametat /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.2:
Now, if the status of being the eater belongs to <s>Aditi</s>, then how can the masculine pronoun 'he' (<s>sa</s>) in [the passage about] her be justified? And therefore, through that, there would be an invalidation by <s>Śruti</s> and the like — to this he says: '<s>sa</s>' (he). // 'Is heard' — in the passage: this is the meaning. After 'like such [passages],' the remainder is: 'is justified in [the passage about] <s>Aditi</s>.' The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'tu' (but). By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage 'I know the wind, the calf of the directions' is included. '<s>Kūṭa</s>' is space; like that, one who stands unchangingly is '<s>kūṭastha</s>' (immutable). '<s>Prakṛti</s>' — the 'imperishable' (<s>akṣara</s>) — is said [to be imperishable] because of non-perishing with respect to the body: this is the meaning of the <s>Gītā</s> passage. 'The calf' (<s>vatsam</s>) — born from the arms of the Lord situated in the four directions — east and the like — denoted by the word 'directions' — is '<s>Vāyu</s>' — the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>. 'I know' (<s>veda</s>) — I understand: this is the meaning. This is a statement of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

Here it is said —
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
The eater (<s>attā</s>) — because of the apprehension of the movable and the immovable. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.9 |

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.3:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - atreti // iti codye samādhānamucyate sūtrakṛtā iti śeṣaḥ / anena sūtre 'trocyate iti śeṣo darśitaḥ / tatsūtraṃ paṭhati - atteti / tattvityanuvartate, vipariṇamyate ca / tathā cātra vākye yaḥ 'attā'; saṃhartocyate sa viṣṇureva / kutaḥ? 'sarvaṃ vā atti'; iti 'carācarasya'; cetanācetanarūpasya viśvasyādyatayā saṃhāryatayā 'grahaṇāt'; carācarāttṛtvaliṅgāditi yāvaditi sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.3:
He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the conclusion: 'here' (<s>atra</s>). // The remainder is: 'In response to this objection, the resolution is stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>.' By this, the remainder 'here it is said' is indicated in the <s>sūtra</s>. He reads that <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>attā</s>' (the eater). The word 'tat' (that) carries forward and undergoes modification. And thus, in this passage, he who is called the 'eater' (<s>attā</s>) — the destroyer — is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Whence? Because of the 'apprehension' (<s>grahaṇa</s>) by the passage 'He indeed eats everything' of 'the movable and the immovable' (<s>carācara</s>) — the entire universe consisting of sentient and insentient entities — as that which is to be eaten, that is, to be destroyed — [in other words,] because of the inferential mark of being the eater of the movable and immovable: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
For the status of being the eater of the entire movable and immovable [creation] does not belong to <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.4:
carācarasyādyatayā grahaṇe 'pi kuto nāditestadattṛtvamiti liṅgasya sāvakāśatvaśaṅkāṃ nirāha - na hīti// hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / carācarasyeti sūtrākṣarāṇyanūdya śrutyanusāreṇa sarvasyeti vyākhyānam / na ca sāmānyapadena vyākhyānaṃ vyarthamiti vācyam / sūtrasya śrutivisaṃvādapratītinirāsārthatvāt / 'aditeḥ'; devamātuḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.4:
Even though there is apprehension as eating the movable and immovable, why does the status of being the eater not belong to <s>Aditi</s>? — he dispels this doubt about the mark having scope [elsewhere]: 'na hi' (for not). // The word 'hi' is in the sense of well-known usage. Having echoed the <s>sūtra</s>-words 'of the movable and immovable,' he explains following the <s>Śruti</s> as 'of all' (<s>sarvasya</s>). Nor should it be said that the explanation through a general term is purposeless — because the <s>sūtra</s>'s purpose is to remove the impression of discordance with the <s>Śruti</s>. '<s>Aditeḥ</s>' — of the mother of the gods.

children.text:
sraṣṭā pātā tathaivāttā nikhilasyaika eva tu /
vāsudevaḥ paraḥ puṃsāmitare 'lpasya vā na vā // iti skānde /
children.translated_text:
The creator, the protector, and likewise the eater of the entirety — one alone indeed —
is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, supreme among persons; the others [create and the like] of a small portion, or not at all. — Thus in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.5:
carācarāttṛtvaṃ viṣṇorapi kutaḥ siddhamityata āha - sraṣṭeti // 'puṃsāṃ paraḥ'; tebhyaḥ uttamo 'vāsudevaḥ'; kṛṣṇaḥ 'eka eva'; nikhilajagataḥ ekaḥ svatantraḥ 'sraṣṭā'; sṛṣṭikartā tathā 'pātā'; rakṣitā tuścārthaḥ / atrā ca / 'vasudevetare'; brahmādyāstu 'alpasya'; jagadekadeśasyāsvātantryeṇa sṛṣṭyādi kartāro bhavanti/ svātantryāpekṣayā netyarthaḥ/ iti skānde ityanantaram uktatvāditi vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.5:
Whence is the status of being the eater of the movable and immovable established for <s>Viṣṇu</s> as well? — to this he says: '<s>sraṣṭā</s>' (creator). // 'Supreme among persons' (<s>puṃsāṃ paraḥ</s>) — the highest among them — is '<s>Vāsudeva</s>' — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — 'one alone' (<s>eka eva</s>) — one independent [agent] of the entire universe — is 'the creator' (<s>sraṣṭā</s>) — the maker of creation; likewise 'the protector' (<s>pātā</s>) — the preserver. The word 'tu' is in the sense of 'ca' (and). And also 'the eater' (<s>attā</s>). 'Other than <s>Vāsudeva</s>' — <s>Brahmā</s> and the others — they are creators and the like 'of a small portion' (<s>alpasya</s>) — of a single part of the universe — without independence. In terms of independence, 'not' (<s>na</s>): this is the meaning. After 'in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>,' the sentence-remainder is: 'because of being stated.'

children.text: ekaḥ purastādya idaṃ babhūva yato babhūva bhavanasya gopā /
children.translated_text: The One who existed before this [universe] came to be, from whom the [universe] came into being, the protector of existence,

children.text: yamapyeti bhuvanaṃ sāmparāye sa no harirghṛtamihāyuṣe 'ttudevaḥ / (ghṛtasū.) iti śrutiḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: to whom beings return at the time of departure — may He, <s>Hari</s>, the god, eat [our] oblation here for [the sake of our] life. (<s>Ghṛtasūkta</s>) — Thus the <s>Śruti</s>. // 9 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.6:
spaṣṭārthatvātprathamaṃ smṛtimudāhṛtyātraivārthe śrutimapyāha - eka iti // eka ityasyāvṛttiḥ, idamityasyāpyāvṛttipariṇāmau / tathā ca ya ekaḥ 'idam'; asya jagataḥ 'purastāt'; pralaye babhūva / yataśca sṛṣṭau 'idaṃ'; jagat 'babhūva'; jātam / atha yaścaiko bhavanasya 'gopāḥ'; goptā babhūva / yaṃ ca 'sāmparāye'; muktipralayayoḥ bhuvanaṃ praviśati nigīrṇaudanavat / 'saḥ devo'; hariḥ naḥ 'āyuṣe'; āyurarthe 'iha'; yajñasthāne āgatya 'ghṛtam'; āhutirūpam 'attu'; svīkarotviti taittirīyaśrutyarthaḥ / mantradraṣṭṛṛṣivākyametat / iti śrutyanantaraṃ yata iti śeṣaḥ / asyāto 'pi viṣṇoścarācarāttṛtvaṃ siddhamityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.6:
Since the meaning is clear, having first cited the <s>Smṛti</s>, he also cites a <s>Śruti</s> for this very point: '<s>ekaḥ</s>' (the One). // The word '<s>ekaḥ</s>' (the One) recurs, and the word '<s>idam</s>' (this) also recurs and undergoes modification. And thus, the One who 'before this' (<s>purastāt</s>) — at the time of dissolution — 'this' universe 'came to be' (<s>babhūva</s>) [i.e., existed]. And from whom, at the time of creation, 'this' universe 'came to be' — was born. And furthermore, the One who became the 'protector' (<s>gopāḥ</s>) of 'existence' (<s>bhavana</s>). And to whom, 'at the time of departure' (<s>sāmparāye</s>) — at the time of liberation and dissolution — beings enter, like swallowed food. 'He' — that 'god' (<s>deva</s>) — <s>Hari</s> — may He 'eat' (<s>attu</s>) — accept — 'for [the sake of our] life' (<s>āyuṣe</s>) — for the purpose of longevity — 'here' (<s>iha</s>) — having come to the sacrificial ground — 'the oblation' (<s>ghṛtam</s>) — in the form of the offering: this is the meaning of the <s>Taittirīya Śruti</s>. This is a statement of the seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>) who beheld the <s>mantra</s>. After 'thus the <s>Śruti</s>,' 'because' (<s>yataḥ</s>) is the remainder. The syntactic connection is: from this [passage] too, the status of being the eater of the movable and immovable is established for <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
And because of the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.10 |

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.7:
yadā niravakāśasarvāttṛtvaliṅgamātrātsāvakāśāditiśrutyadititvaliṅgayorbādhena attā viṣṇureveti siddhyati / tadā kimu vācyaṃ niravakāśaprakaraṇasamuccitālliṅgādityarthaṃ pratipādayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - prakaraṇācceti // 'naivehaṃ kiñcana'; (bṛ. 3-2.) iti niravakāśaviṣṇuprakaraṇabalāccāttā viṣṇureveti sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.7:
When the status of being the eater is established as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — through the invalidation of the <s>Aditi</s>-<s>Śruti</s> and the <s>Aditi</s>-mark, which have scope [elsewhere], by the no-scope-elsewhere mark of being the eater of all movable and immovable — then what more need be said [when the argument proceeds] from the mark combined with the no-scope-elsewhere context? With this purport, having read the <s>sūtra</s> and explained it, he says: '<s>prakaraṇāt</s>' (because of the context). // 'Not a thing existed here [before]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2) — because of the force of the no-scope-elsewhere <s>Viṣṇu</s>-context, the eater is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
And because [this passage] belongs to that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>-]context through the creation of waters, [the creation of] <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.8:
prakaraṇasya vaiṣṇavatvāsiddhimāśaṅkyāha - apsaṃvatsarasṛṣṭyādineti // apsṛṣṭiḥ saṃvatsaranāmakacaturmukhasṛṣṭiśca te ādī yasya tat tathoktam / ādipadena saṃvatsarādanodyamādiliṅgaṃ gṛhyate / 'tatprakaraṇatvāt'; viṣṇuprakaraṇatvādityarthaḥ / etatprakaraṇasyeti śeṣaḥ / avagamopalakṣakametat / asyātaḥ prakaraṇādviṣṇureva atrocyate iti prakṛtasādhyenānvayaḥ / co hetusamuccaye / prakaraṇaṃ nāmaikaprameyapratipādakānekavākyāni / bṛhadāraṇyake hi - 'naiveha kiñcanāgra āsīt / mṛtyunaivedamāvṛtamāsīt / aśanāyayāśanāyā hi mṛtyustanmano 'kurutātmanvī syāmiti/ so 'rcannacaratatasyārcata āpo 'jāyanta....tadyadapāṃ śara āsīttatsamahanyata sā pṛthivyabhavat tasyāmaśrāmyat.... so 'kāmayata dvitīyo ma ātmā jāyeteti sa manasā vācā mithunaṃ samabhavadaśanāyā hi mṛtyustadreta āsīttatsaṃvatso 'bhavat .... taṃ jātamabhivyādadātsa bhāṇamakarotsaiva vāgabhavatsa aikṣata yadi ha vā imamabhimaṃsye kanīyo 'nnaṃ kariṣya iti sa tayā vācā tenātmanā idaṃ sarvamasṛjata'; (bṛ. 1-2.) iti viṣṇuviṣayāṇyanekavākyāni śrūyante / 'agre'; pralaye 'iha'; asvatantravarge, gagana iti vā / 'kiñcana'; jīvajaḍarūpaṃ vastu naivāsīditi /
nanu - sarvasaṃhārakaṃ viṣṇuṃ devīṃ jīvāṃstathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Now — '<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the destroyer of all, and the goddess [<s>Lakṣmī</s>], and the <s>jīvas</s>, likewise,
and time, and the equilibrium of the three <s>guṇas</s>, and <s>karmas</s>, and <s>Prāṇa</s>, and the senses,

children.text: saṃskāraṃ caiva vedāṃśca narte kiñcillaye tvabhūt //
children.translated_text: and latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and the <s>Vedas</s> — nothing besides [these] ceased to exist at dissolution.'

BBsBhDīp_1,2.2.8:
Anticipating the objection that the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the context is not established, he says: 'through the creation of waters, <s>Saṃvatsara</s>, and the like.' // The creation of waters and the creation of [<s>Brahmā</s>] named <s>Saṃvatsara</s> — these are the beginning of which — thus it is so called. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the mark of devouring <s>Saṃvatsara</s> and the like is included. 'Because of belonging to that context' (<s>tatprakaraṇatvāt</s>) — because of being a <s>Viṣṇu</s>-context: this is the meaning. 'Of this context' is the remainder. This is representative of [further marks of] understanding. The syntactic connection is with the thesis under discussion: from this context too, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is spoken of here. The word 'ca' is for the accumulation of reasons. A 'context' (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) means multiple sentences conveying a single subject. For in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> — 'Not a thing existed here before. It was enveloped by <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) alone. By hunger — for hunger is death — he formed the intention: "May I become embodied." Worshipping, he moved about; from his worship, waters were born... The froth that was upon those waters was consolidated; that became the earth. Upon that, in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, he reclined... He desired: "May a second self of mine be born." By mind, by speech, he entered into copulation — for hunger is death — what was the seed, that became <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)... Him, when born, he opened his mouth wide to devour. He (<s>Brahmā</s>) made the sound "bhāṇ." That very speech became [the goddess of speech]... He reflected: "If I consume this one, I will make less food for myself." Therefore, with that speech, with that self (<s>Brahmā</s>), he created all this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.2) — thus many sentences pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s> are heard. 'Before' (<s>agre</s>) — at the time of dissolution; 'here' (<s>iha</s>) — among the dependent class [of beings], or in space. 'Not a thing' (<s>kiñcana</s>) — no entity in the form of <s>jīva</s> or insentient matter — existed.

children.text: iti bṛhadbhāṣyodāhṛtavacanānnityānāṃ jīvānāmapi sattvātkathamiyamuktirityata uktaṃ - mṛtyunaiveti / 'idaṃ'; jīvādikaṃ 'mṛtyunā'; tannāmakena janārdanena 'āvṛtam'; ācchāditamāsīt / mṛtyorāvarakatve hetuḥ - aśanāyayeti / aśaṃ jagattannetryetyarthaḥ / mṛtyoraśanāyātvaṃ śrutiprasiddhamityāha - aśanāyā hīti / 'tat'; tasmādekākitvānmṛtyuḥ 'ātmanvī'; jagadrūpaśarīravān syāmityaicchat / evaṃ sa mṛtyuḥ 'arcan'; svātmānaṃ pūjayan sañcacāra tasyārcata āpo 'jāyanta / tā eva tāsāmarcanasādhanamiti bhāvaḥ / tatrāpsu yo 'pāṃ 'śaraḥ'; phenarūpo maṇḍa āsīttaccharaḥ / sa śaro mṛtyunāsvaretasā 'samahanyata'; saṅghātatvaṃ prāpitaḥ / yassaṅghātaḥ sā 'pṛthivī'; brahmāṇḍarūpābhavat 'tasyāṃ'; pṛthivyāṃ śvetadvīpe 'aśrāmyat'; śiśye mṛtyuḥ / sa mṛtyuḥ 'me'; mama 'ātmā'; brahmā dvitīyo vāyvapekṣayā jāyeteti akāmayata / atha 'aśanāyā'; sa mṛtyuḥ 'manasā'; svecchayā 'vācā'; vedābhimāniśriyā 'mithunaṃ'; dvandvībhāvaṃ 'samabhavat'; prāpat / tena mithunībhāvena yadreta āsīt 'tatsaṃvatsaraḥ'; tupādānakadehavān saṃvatsaranāmakaścaturmukho 'bhavat / atha jātaṃ saṃvatsaramabhilakṣya attuṃ 'vyādadāt'; vidadāra svamukhaṃ mṛtyuḥ / sa saṃvatsaro bhayāt viṣṇudīptyānandabodhakabhāṇiti śabdamakarot / yadbhāṇiti vacastadabhimāninī saiva vāṅnāmnī sarasvatyabhavat / sa mṛtyuḥ aikṣata ālocitavān / kimiti? 'yadīmaṃ'; saṃvatsaram 'abhimaṃsye'; līnaṃ kariṣye tattadā me 'kanīyaḥ'; alpamannaṃ kariṣye / tato bahvannaṃ bhavatvityālocya sa mṛtyuḥ 'tayā vācā'; sarasvatyā 'tenātmanā'; caturmukhenedaṃ sarvamasṛjata / janayāmāseti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since, from this passage cited in the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> (great commentary), the <s>jīvas</s> too, being eternal, exist [during dissolution], how is [the above] statement [that 'not a thing existed here'] justified? — to this it is said: 'by <s>Mṛtyu</s>' (by Death). 'This' (<s>idam</s>) — the [world] consisting of <s>jīvas</s> and the like — was 'enveloped' (<s>āvṛtam</s>) — covered — by '<s>Mṛtyu</s>' — by <s>Janārdana</s> bearing that name. The reason for <s>Mṛtyu</s>'s being the enveloper is: '<s>aśanāyayā</s>' (by hunger). '<s>Aśam</s>' — the world — 'He leads' (<s>nayati</s>) — that is the meaning [of '<s>aśanāya</s>']. That <s>Mṛtyu</s>'s hunger-nature is well-known in <s>Śruti</s>, he says: '<s>aśanāyā hi</s>' (for hunger). 'That' (<s>tat</s>) — therefore, being alone, <s>Mṛtyu</s> 'desired' to become 'embodied' (<s>ātmanvī</s>) — to have the world as His body. Thus, that <s>Mṛtyu</s>, 'worshipping' (<s>arcan</s>) — honoring His own self — moved about; from His worship, waters were born — they were indeed the means of that worship: this is the import. Therein, of the waters, what was the 'froth' (<s>śara</s>) — the foam-like cream — was that <s>śara</s>; that froth was 'consolidated' (<s>samahanyata</s>) — brought to a state of compactness — by <s>Mṛtyu</s> through His own seed. That consolidated [mass] — that 'earth' (<s>pṛthivī</s>) — became [the cosmic egg] in the form of the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>. 'Upon that' (<s>tasyām</s>) — upon that earth, in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s> 'reclined' (<s>aśrāmyat</s>). That <s>Mṛtyu</s> [desired]: 'may a second self of mine' (<s>me ātmā</s>) — <s>Brahmā</s>, second with respect to <s>Vāyu</s> — be born. Then '<s>aśanāyā</s>' — that <s>Mṛtyu</s>, 'by mind' (<s>manasā</s>) — by His own will — 'by speech' (<s>vācā</s>) — by <s>Śrī</s>, the presiding deity of the <s>Vedas</s> — 'entered into copulation' (<s>mithunaṃ samabhavat</s>) — attained the state of a pair. By that copulation, what was the seed — 'that became <s>Saṃvatsara</s>' — one who, being the material body, delights (<s>ramayati</s>) those who have properly become calves — thus by etymology the word '<s>Saṃvatsara</s>' is well-known as [referring to] the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>]. Then, having marked the newborn <s>Saṃvatsara</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s> 'opened wide' (<s>vyādadāt</s>) — opened — His mouth to 'eat' (<s>attum</s>) — to devour. That <s>Saṃvatsara</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), out of fear, from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s splendor, made the sound '<s>bhāṇ</s>' — a word indicative of bliss and knowledge. The presiding deity of that word '<s>bhāṇ</s>' — that very <s>Sarasvatī</s> by name — became speech. That <s>Mṛtyu</s> 'reflected' (<s>aikṣata</s>) — considered. What? 'If I consume this one' (<s>imam</s>) — <s>Saṃvatsara</s> — 'I will make him dissolved' (<s>abhimaṃsye</s>), then I will make 'less' (<s>kanīyaḥ</s>) — scant — 'food' for myself. Therefore, may there be abundant food — having thus reflected, that <s>Mṛtyu</s>, 'with that speech' — with <s>Sarasvatī</s> — 'with that self' — with the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] — created all this — caused it to be born: this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>.
Not a thing existed here even in the beginning; <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), who is <s>Hari</s>, was [present] then.
He, <s>Janārdana</s>, created the waters by His own will;
The Lord, reclining in those [waters], fashioned the great cosmic egg.
Therein, the mighty Lord created <s>Brahmā</s> named <s>Saṃvatsara</s>.
He opened His mouth wide to devour him; thereupon, [<s>Brahmā</s>] cried out.
Then, out of compassion, <s>Viṣṇu</s> appointed him to the work of creation.
He, the mighty one, created the entire world — the food for <s>Hari</s>.
Thus in the <s>Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa</s>. // 10 //
// Thus ends the <s>Attṛtvādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the eater). // 2 //
// 3. The <s>Guhādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the cave [of the heart]). //

children.text:
sarvāttaikaḥ para uktaḥ /
ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe /
chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca trināciketāḥ (kaṭha. 1-3-1.)
iti pibantau pratīyate tau kāviti //
children.translated_text: The one who devours all (<s>sarvāttā</s>) has been stated to be the Supreme. In the verse: "The two who drink <s>ṛta</s> (truth/cosmic order) in the world of good deeds, who have entered the cave, in the highest <s>parārdha</s> (supreme half) — those who know <s>Brahman</s>, those who maintain the five fires, and those who have thrice performed the <s>Nāciketa</s> sacrifice, call them shade and sunlight" (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.3.1) — the two who are understood as 'drinking' — who are they?

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.1:
atrādhikaraṇe lokato 'nyatra prasiddhakarmaphalabhoktṛtvaliṅgasya viṣṇau samanvayaḥ pratipādyate / pūrvādhikaraṇaśrutisaṅgatiṃ viṣayavākyodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ viṣayaṃ sūcayati - sarveti // yasmāt 'paraḥ'; paramātmā 'ekaḥ'; ekatvasaṅkhyāyuktaḥ 'sarvāttā'; sarvasaṃhartā ca, tasmātprakṛtipratyayārthayostatra yogāt sarvāttetyādikriyāliṅgabodhakaśabdavācyatvenokta ityarthaḥ / sarvāttetyuktyaiva arthātpātetyapyukta iti bhāvaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - ṛtamiti / tatretyādau saṃyojyam / tathā ca 'tatra'; sarvāttṛtvamadhye praviṣṭaṃ tadviśeṣabhūtaṃ pātṛtvaṃ yatroktaṃ tatra kāṭhake 'ṛtaṃ pibantau'; ityatra 'pibantau'; karmaphalasārabhoktārau dvau pratīyete iti yojanā / dvivacanena dvitvabodhāditi bhāvaḥ / anena yuktamattṛtvaṃ bhagavatastatra prakṛtipratyayārthayorupapatteḥ / iha tu karmabandhavidhure paramātmani prakṛtyarthasya nirbhede pratyayārthasya cāyogānna tasya dvivacanāntapibacchandavācyateti pūrvavaiṣamyeṇa pratyavasthānādvā pūrvamarthāduktasya pātṛtvasyānyamātraniṣṭhatve 'sambhavasyānyasminnapi sattve 'tivyāptervā ākṣepādvā pūrvādhikaraṇenāsya saṅgatiḥ, pātṛtvākhyaviṣayaśca sūcito bhavati / viṣayavākye janyajanakabhāvaḥ ṣaṣṭhyarthaḥ tathā ca 'sukṛtasya loke'; sukṛtanirmite puṇyakārye tattvapradīparītyā sukṛtanimitte śarīre hṛdayaguhāṃ praviṣṭau guhāyāmapi 'parame'; sarvajīvottame ā ṛddha ārdhaḥ parebhyo rudrādibhya ārdhaḥ parārdhaḥ / tasminnatipūrṇe vāyāviti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca tatra praviṣṭau hṛdayaguhāśritavāyvadhiṣṭhānāviti yāvat / 'sa hāyastaḥ piturardhameyāya'; (chāṃ. 5-3-4.) iti tattvapradīpodāhṛtaśruteḥ parabrahmāvāsatvāttadanyajīvābhimanyamānatvātparārdhaṃ śarīramiti vā / ṛtaṃ satyaṃ tathā dharmaḥ sukṛtaṃ cābhidhīyate /
ṛtaṃ tu mānaso dharmaḥ ....... iti gītābhāṣyodāhṛtasmṛteḥ śāstravihitakarmabhirāgataṃ phalamupalakṣaṇayā ṛtamityucyate / tathā ca 'ṛtaṃ pibantau'; bhuñjānau yāvātmāntarātmākhyabhagavadrūpaviśeṣau vartete tau 'brahmavido'; brahmajñāninaḥ 'pañcāgnayo'; devapitṛbhūtamanuṣyabrahmayajñākhyapañcamahāyajñavantaḥ / 'sa eṣa yajñaḥ pañcavidho 'gnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsau cāturmāsyāni paśuḥ somaḥ'; () ityaitareyoktapañcamahāyajñā vā / dyuparjanyadharāpuṃstryākhyapañcāgnividyāniṣṭhā vā / naciketā nāma ṛṣiḥ naciketasa idaṃ nāciketamagnicayanaviśeṣaḥ / trināciketāstrivāramanuṣṭhitanāciketeṣṭakācayanavanto ye vartante viduṣāṃ pāpināṃ ca krameṇa 'chāyātapau'; sukhaduḥkhakāraṇabhūtau vadantītyarthaḥ / sukhaduḥkhahetutvarūpaṃ gauṇaṃ chāyātapatvaṃ ca pratiyogibhedādaviruddham / yathoktaṃ tattvapradīpe amarāṇāmāhlādakāvasurāṇāṃ tāpakāvityartha iti / praśnarūpakāryadvārā tanmūlasandehaprakāraṃ darśayati - 'tau'; śrutyuktapibantāviti / iti vākye pibantau yau pratīyete tau kāvityanvayaḥ / anena pibantau kiṃ jīvaparau uta pararūpe eveti saṃśayaḥ sūcito bhavati / itītyanantaraṃ iti saṃśaye jīvasahitar iśvaraḥ pāteti pūrvapakṣe ca satīti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> 1.2.3.1: In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topical section), the harmonization with <s>Viṣṇu</s> of the characteristic of being the enjoyer of the fruits of action — a characteristic well-known elsewhere in the world — is established. He indicates the connection with the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) of the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, prefacing it with a citation of the subject-verse, beginning with 'sarvā' etc. Since He is 'supreme' (<s>para</s>), the Supreme Self, and 'one' (<s>eka</s>), possessing the numerical attribute of oneness, and '<s>sarvāttā</s>' (the devourer of all), the universal destroyer — therefore, because both the root-meaning and suffix-meaning apply there, He is spoken of as denoted by words indicating action-characteristics such as <s>sarvāttā</s> etc. — this is the meaning. By the very statement '<s>sarvāttā</s>', the meaning 'drinker' (<s>pātā</s>) is also implicitly conveyed — this is the purport. Then, what follows from this? To that he says — '<s>ṛtam</s>' etc. The word 'there' (<s>tatra</s>) etc. should be connected. And thus: 'there' — in the midst of the quality of being the devourer of all, where the specific quality of being a drinker, which has entered into it and constitutes its specification, is stated — there, in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> (Kaṭha Upaniṣad), in the passage '<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>' (the two drinking truth), the word '<s>pibantau</s>' (the two drinking) indicates two enjoyers of the essence of the fruits of action — this is the construction. The dual number conveys duality — this is the purport. By this, the quality of being a devourer is fitting for the Lord, since both root-meaning and suffix-meaning are applicable there. But here, in the case of the Supreme Self who is free from the bondage of <s>karma</s>, since the root-meaning admits of no distinction and the suffix-meaning does not apply, He cannot be denoted by the verbal form ending in dual number expressing 'drinking'; or alternatively, through objection by way of contrast with the previous position — since the quality of being a drinker, previously stated implicitly, cannot be restricted to merely another entity, and since even if it exists in another there would be over-extension — through such objection, the connection of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> with the previous one is established, and the subject-matter, namely the quality of being a drinker, is indicated. In the subject-verse, the genitive case expresses the relation of effect and cause; and thus '<s>sukṛtasya loke</s>' — in the body created by good deeds, in the body that is the occasion for merit in the manner described in <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, the two have entered the cave of the heart; and even within the cave, '<s>parame</s>' — supreme among all <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), <s>ārdha</s> means filled, <s>parārdha</s> means filled beyond <s>Rudra</s> and other deities. In that supremely full <s>Vāyu</s> — this is the remainder. And thus the two who have entered there are situated in <s>Vāyu</s> who presides over the cave of the heart — this is the meaning. From the <s>śruti</s> cited in <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'He went to half of the father' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3.4), since it is the abode of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, and since the <s>jīva</s> identifies with it, the body is called <s>parārdha</s> — or alternatively thus. '<s>Ṛta</s> means truth, likewise <s>dharma</s>, and <s>sukṛta</s> is also so called; <s>ṛta</s> is the <s>dharma</s> of the mind...' — from the <s>smṛti</s> cited in the <s>Gītā Bhāṣya</s>, by metonymy, the fruit obtained through scripturally ordained actions is called <s>ṛta</s>. And thus '<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>' — the two who are enjoying, that is, the two specific forms of the Lord known as <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>antarātman</s> (inner self), exist; them, 'the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>' and 'those who maintain the five fires' — those who perform the five great sacrifices called <s>deva-yajña</s>, <s>pitṛ-yajña</s>, <s>bhūta-yajña</s>, <s>manuṣya-yajña</s>, and <s>brahma-yajña</s>; or the five great sacrifices mentioned in the <s>Aitareya</s>: 'This sacrifice is fivefold — <s>agnihotra</s>, <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, <s>cāturmāsya</s>, <s>paśu</s>, and <s>soma</s>'; or those established in the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s> (doctrine of five fires) consisting of heaven, rain, earth, man, and woman. <s>Naciketas</s> is the name of the <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage); that which belongs to <s>Naciketas</s> is <s>nāciketa</s>, a particular fire-altar arrangement. '<s>Trināciketāḥ</s>' — those who have performed the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire-altar ceremony three times — of the wise and the sinful respectively, they call them 'shade and sunlight' (<s>chāyātapau</s>), meaning the causes of happiness and sorrow — this is the meaning. The figurative quality of being shade and sunlight, in the form of being the cause of happiness and sorrow, is not contradictory due to the difference in counter-correlates. As stated in <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'For the gods they cause delight, for the demons they cause heat' — this is the meaning. Through the question-form as an effect-medium, he shows the manner of doubt rooted in it — 'those two' (<s>tau</s>) refers to the two drinkers mentioned in the <s>śruti</s>. The construction is: the two who are understood as drinking in the verse — who are they? By this, the doubt is indicated: are the two drinkers the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme, or are they both forms of the Supreme alone? After the word 'iti', in the state of doubt, and in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) that God drinks together with the <s>jīva</s> — this is the remainder of the sentence.
It is said — <s>Sūtra</s>: <s>Oṃ</s>.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.3.2:
The two who have entered the cave are indeed the two selves (<s>ātmanau</s>), because of the seeing of that. (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.11)
<s>Oṃ</s>.
The two who have entered the cave, the two drinkers, are indeed two forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.2:
atha siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ucyate iti // sūtrātparata itiśabdo 'dhyāhāryaḥ / guhāṃ praviṣṭāviti hetugarbhaṃ viśeṣaṇam / pibantāvityātmapadavyākhyānam / ṛtamityādāvadhyāhāryam / viṣṇurūpe ityātmānāvityasya vyākhyānāntaram / tathā ca - yāvātmānau ṛtaṃ pibantau tāvātmānau viṣṇurūpe eva / kutaḥ? yato guhāṃ praviṣṭāviti yojanā / evetyanenānuvṛttatuśabdārtha uktaḥ / viṣṇū iti vaktavye viṣṇurūpe evetyuktiḥ dvivacanasya rūpadvayavivakṣayā sāvakāśatoktyarthā /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> 1.2.3.2: Now, introducing the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the <s>siddhānta</s> (settled conclusion), he explains — 'it is said.' The word 'iti' after the <s>sūtra</s> is to be supplied. 'Who have entered the cave' (<s>guhāṃ praviṣṭau</s>) is a qualification containing the reason. '<s>Pibantau</s>' (the two drinkers) is the explanation of the word '<s>ātma</s>' (self). '<s>Ṛtam</s>' etc. is to be supplied at the beginning. '<s>Viṣṇurūpe</s>' (two forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) is an alternative explanation of '<s>ātmānau</s>' (the two selves). And thus — the two selves who drink <s>ṛta</s> (truth), those two selves are indeed two forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? Because they have entered the cave — this is the construction. By the word 'eva' (indeed), the meaning of the word 'tu' (but) carried over from previous context is expressed. The statement 'two forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' instead of simply '<s>Viṣṇū</s>' (two <s>Viṣṇus</s>) is purposeful, to allow scope for the dual number to convey the intention of two forms.

children.text: 'gharmā samantā trivṛtaṃ vyāpatustayorjuṣṭiṃ mātariśvā jagāma'; (ṛ. 10-114-1.) ityādinā taddarśanāt //
children.translated_text: Because of the seeing of that, through passages such as: 'The two radiant ones pervaded the triple creation from all sides; <s>Mātariśvan</s> (Wind) attained their worship' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.114.1) and so forth.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.3.3:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.3:
nanu viṣṇossarvaśarīreṣvekaikarūpeṇaiva praveśātkathaṃ rūpadvayābhiprāyeṇāpi dvivacanopapattirityataḥ taddarśanāditi sūtrāṃśasūcitaśrutimudāharati - gharmeti // bhagavantāviti, kartumiti ca śeṣaḥ / trivṛtamityāvartate / tathā ca 'gharmā'; gharmau dīptau gharṣakau saṅkocakāviti vā / 'gharṣaṇātsarvalokasya nṛsiṃho gharma ucyate'; ityaitareyabhāṣyokteḥ, ghṛṣṭatvena ca mitāviti tattvapradīpokteśca / 'samantā'; samantau vyāptau prakṛtipuruṣakālavyāpinau / deśataḥ kālataḥ śaktitaśca sampūrṇau yau bhagavantau trivṛtaṃ tejobannātmakaṃ śarīraṃ 'vyāpatuḥ'; viśeṣeṇāpatuḥ dehahṛdayaguhāsthānaṃ prāptau / tayoḥ 'juṣṭiṃ'; sevāṃ kartuṃ 'mātariśvā'; mukhyavāyurapi trivṛtaṃ jagāma / 'divo'; devyā vāyupatnyāḥ stanyaṃ 'payoḥ'; 'didhiṣāṇāḥ'; pipāsanto devāḥ dvirūpaṃ tamekam 'aveṣan'; anvaicchan / tam 'arkam'; aram alaṃ kaṃ sukharūpaṃ 'sahasāmānaṃ'; sahavāyuṃ viduriti śrutyarthaḥ / gurvarthadīpikāyāṃ tu samantāditi padacchedaṃ kṛtvā vidyamānāviti cādhyāhṛtya samantādvidyamānau vyāptāviti vyākhyātam/ taccintyam/ ityādineti / vākyeneti śeṣaḥ / ādipadena 'divaspayaḥ'; ityuttarārdhaṃ, tathā -
ekaḥ suparṇaḥ sa samudramāviveśa sa idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vicaṣṭe /
children.translated_text: One bird of beautiful wings entered the ocean; he surveys this entire universe.

children.text: taṃ pākena manasāpaśyamantitastaṃ mātā relhi sa u relhi mātaram //
children.translated_text: Him, with ripened mind, I beheld from nearby; the mother licks him, and he licks the mother.

<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> 1.2.3.3: But since <s>Viṣṇu</s> enters all bodies in one single form in each, how can the dual number be justified even with the intention of two forms? To this, he cites the <s>śruti</s> indicated by the <s>sūtra</s>-portion 'because of the seeing of that' — beginning with '<s>gharma</s>' etc. The words 'the two Lords' and 'to perform' are to be supplied as remainder. The word '<s>trivṛtam</s>' (triple) recurs. And thus: '<s>gharmā</s>' — the two radiant ones, the two scorching ones, the two who cause friction, or the two who cause contraction. From the statement in the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s>: '<s>Nṛsiṃha</s> is called <s>gharma</s> because of His friction with all the worlds,' and from the statement in <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> that the two are measured by being rubbed. '<s>Samantā</s>' — the two who are all-pervading, pervading <s>prakṛti</s> (matter), <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), and <s>kāla</s> (time); the two Lords who are complete in space, time, and power, '<s>vyāpatuḥ</s>' — they specially pervaded, they reached the place of the cave of the heart in the body, which is triple (<s>trivṛt</s>), consisting of fire, water, and food. Of those two, '<s>juṣṭim</s>' — worship, service, to perform that, '<s>Mātariśvā</s>' — even the chief <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind-god) attained the triple. '<s>Divaḥ</s>' — the milk '<s>payaḥ</s>' of the goddess, the consort of <s>Vāyu</s>; '<s>didhiṣāṇāḥ</s>' — the gods, thirsting for it, sought that one who has two forms as a single being; they knew him '<s>arkam</s>' — whose nature is bliss (<s>aram alaṃ kaṃ sukharūpam</s>), '<s>sahasāmānam</s>' — as accompanied by <s>Vāyu</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. In the <s>Gurvarthadīpikā</s>, however, the word-division '<s>samantāt</s>' is made, and supplying 'existing' (<s>vidyamānau</s>), it is explained as 'existing from all sides, pervading' — that is questionable. 'And so forth' (<s>ityādinā</s>) — with the verse, is the remainder. The word 'ādi' refers to the second half '<s>divaḥ payaḥ</s>' etc., and also —

children.text: suparṇaṃ viprāḥ kavayo vacobhirekaṃ santaṃ bahudhā kalpayanti / (ṛ. 10-114-4., 5.)
children.translated_text: The wise seers, the poets, fashion with their words the one bird of beautiful wings, though he is one, into many forms. (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.114.4-5)

children.text: ityādikaṃ ca gṛhyate / 'ekaḥ suparṇaḥ'; suṣṭhu paramānandarūpo bhagavān samudramāviveśa / sa idaṃ sarvaṃ jagat 'vicaṣṭe'; paśyati / 'taṃ'; paramātmānaṃ pakvena manasā ahamapaśyam / 'taṃ mātā'; vyañjakatvādvāk sarasvatī 'relhi'; lihyata iva / sa paramātmā mātaraṃ relhi / tāvanyonyaṃ sambaddhau bhavataḥ / tathā ca - bhagavadvyañjakavāco 'pi taddhyaṅgyatvamiti bhāvaḥ / tameva suparṇamekaṃ santaṃ 'viprāḥ'; viśeṣeṇa prakṛṣṭāḥ kavayo 'vacobhiḥ'; śabdaiḥ 'bahudhā'; keśavādidvādaśadhā sthitaṃ kalpayanti cintayanti ityarthaḥ / taddarśanāditi / tasya viṣṇoḥ dvirūpatayā sarvaśarīrapraveśasya uktatvādityarthaḥ / tathā ca - ekasminnapi viṣṇau yuktaṃ rūpadvayābhiprāyeṇa dvivacanamiti bhāvaḥ / evaṃ taddarśanāt ityetat tattvapradīparītyā uktaviśeṣaṇe nirṇīte viṣṇau dvivacanadarśanāt 'ekaḥ suparṇaḥ'; ityādinā tacchabdenaikavacanena parāmarśadarśanāt tasyaiva samudraniveśino nikhilabhuvanadarśinaḥ 'apaśyamantitaḥ'; iti guhāpraviṣṭatvadarśanādekasyaiva bahunāmarūpadarśanāt ityapi vyākhyeyam //
children.translated_text: And passages such as these are also taken into account. 'One bird of beautiful wings' (<s>ekaḥ suparṇaḥ</s>) — the Lord, whose nature is supreme bliss, entered the ocean. He 'surveys' (<s>vicaṣṭe</s>), that is, sees this entire universe. 'Him' — the Supreme Self, with a ripened mind, I beheld. 'Him the mother' — <s>Vāk</s> (Speech), that is <s>Sarasvatī</s>, because she is the revealer, 'licks' (<s>relhi</s>) as it were; and He, the Supreme Self, licks the mother. The two are mutually connected. And thus the purport is: even the speech that reveals the Lord is itself something to be revealed by Him. That very bird of beautiful wings, though being one, the '<s>viprāḥ</s>' — those who are especially distinguished, the poets, 'with words' (<s>vacobhiḥ</s>), that is, with names, 'fashion' (<s>kalpayanti</s>), that is, contemplate Him as existing 'in many forms' (<s>bahudhā</s>), as abiding in twelve forms such as <s>Keśava</s> and others — this is the meaning. 'Because of the seeing of that' — because the entry of <s>Viṣṇu</s> into all bodies in two forms has been stated — this is the meaning. And thus the purport is: even in the case of the one <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the dual number with the intention of two forms is justified. Thus, when the qualification indicated by 'because of the seeing of that' is ascertained in the manner of <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, it should also be explained as: because of the seeing of the dual number in reference to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; because of the seeing of reference to Him by the singular number through the word 'that' in '<s>ekaḥ suparṇaḥ</s>' (one bird of beautiful wings) and such passages; because of the seeing of His having entered the cave through '<s>apaśyam antikaḥ</s>' (I beheld from nearby) — of that very one who has entered the ocean, who sees all worlds; and because of the seeing of one entity having many names and forms — thus also it should be explained.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.3.4:
<s>Hari</s> alone, known as <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>antarātman</s> (inner self), exists in two forms,

children.text: niviṣṭo hṛdaye nityaṃ rasaṃ pibati karmajam //
children.translated_text: eternally situated in the heart, He drinks the essence (<s>rasa</s>) born of <s>karma</s> (action).
Thus it is in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.4:
nanu viṣṇau rūpadvayavivakṣayā pratyayārthopapattāvapi prātipadikārthakarmaphalabhoktṛtvāyogāt na 'ṛtam'; iti vākyapratipādyatvaṃ tasyetyata āha - ātmeti // eka eva hariḥ dehajīvarūpopādhibhedāt ātmāntarātmeti rūpabhedena 'dvidhā sthito'; dvidhā bhūtaḥ / dehajīvayorhṛdaye niviṣṭaḥ / yaddhā - ṭīkārītyā upādhibhedavivakṣāmantareṇaiva dvirūpatayā dehaniviṣṭaḥ 'karmajaṃ rasaṃ'; phalaṃ 'nityaṃ'; niyamena 'pibati'; bhuṅkte ityarthaḥ / smṛta iti pāṭhe kīrtitaḥ ityarthaḥ / rasaśabdena jīvābhogyaguṇabhoktaiveśvaraḥ, na tu tadbhogyadravyabhokteti prameyaṃ sūcitam / bṛhatsaṃhitāyāmityasya taddarśanādityanuvṛttavākyenānvayaḥ / karmaphalabhogasyoktatvāditi tadarthaḥ / tathā ca - na tadanupapattiriti bhāvaḥ / na kevalaṃ bṛhatsaṃhitāyām / kintu -
śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca /
children.translated_text: The ear, the eye, the sense of touch, the sense of taste, and the sense of smell,
presiding over these and the mind, this one (<s>ayam</s>) enjoys the sense-objects. (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 15.9)
Thus it is in the <s>Gītā</s> as well — this is the meaning.

<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> 1.2.3.4: But even if the suffix-meaning is justified by the intention of two forms in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since the root-meaning of being an enjoyer of the fruits of action does not apply, the word '<s>ṛtam</s>' in the verse cannot refer to Him — to this he says, beginning with '<s>ātmā</s>' etc. The one <s>Hari</s> alone, due to the distinction of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) in the form of body and <s>jīva</s>, is 'established in two forms' (<s>dvidhā sthitaḥ</s>), that is, has become twofold, as <s>ātman</s> and <s>antarātman</s>. He is situated in the heart of the body and the <s>jīva</s>. Or alternatively, according to the interpretation of the <s>Ṭīkā</s> (gloss), without any intention of distinction through limiting adjuncts, He is situated in the body in two forms. '<s>Karmajaṃ rasam</s>' — the fruit born of action — He 'always' (<s>nityam</s>), that is, invariably, 'drinks' (<s>pibati</s>), meaning He enjoys — this is the meaning. In the reading '<s>smṛta</s>' (remembered), the meaning is 'celebrated.' By the word '<s>rasa</s>' (essence), the doctrine is indicated that the Lord is the enjoyer of the qualities that the <s>jīva</s> should enjoy, but not the enjoyer of the material objects of that enjoyment. The phrase 'in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>' is connected with the carried-over sentence 'because of the seeing of that.' Its meaning is: because the enjoyment of the fruits of action has been stated. And thus the purport is: there is no inapplicability of that. Not only in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>, but also —

nanu kimīśvaro duḥkhaṃ pāpakarmaphalaṃ bhuṅkte? puṇyajaṃ sukhaṃ vā? nādyadvitīyau, pūrṇānandatvādityata āha - śubhamiti // 'asau'; sarvaśarīragataprāṇe sthito 'hariḥ'; yajñe havissvīkartā pāpahartā bhagavān 'nityaṃ'; niyamena śubhakarmaphalameva 'pibati'; bhuṅkte / hariḥ aśubhakarmaphalaṃ 'na pibet'; na bhuṅkte ityarthaḥ / 'puṇyamevāmuṃ gacchati (bṛ. 3-5-20.) parame parārdhe'; (kaṭha. 3-1.) iti śruteḥ / pibatīti ṛtapānakartari advitīyatvamabhyupaiti / anenārthena dvitīyapakṣamaṅgīkṛtya ādyapakṣo 'nabhyupagamena parihṛtaḥ / pūrṇānandasya sukhabhogāyoga iti dvitīyaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ pariharati - pūrṇānandamayasyeti / tādātmyārthe mayaṭ / 'tādātmyārthe vikārārthe prācuryārthe mayaṭ tridhā'; iti gītābhāṣyokteḥ / tathā ca - pūrṇānandarūpasyāsya viṣṇoḥ 'ceṣṭā'; aiśvaryaṃ kvacitkāle deśe kenāpi sākalyena 'na jñāyate'; na cintyate ityarthaḥ / tathā ca - aiśvaryabalena pūrṇānandasyāpi sukhabhogo yukta iti bhāvaḥ / yadvā - viṣṇorbhoktṛtvābhyupagame 'anaśnannanyaḥ'; (mu. 3-1-1.) iti śrutivirodha ityata āha - śubhamiti // parādhīnabhogābhāvaviṣayam aśubhabhogābhāvaviṣayaṃ vā tadvākyamiti bhāvaḥ / na ca 'nīcoccataiva duḥkhāderbhoga ityabhidhīyate / nāsau nīcoccatāṃ yāti'; iti vākyavirodhaḥ, sukhabhogasyoccatārūpatvāditi vācyam / viṣṇau jīvasamavete bhoge svīkārāmātrābhyupagamena uccatāsampādakavikriyāviśeṣānabhyupagamāt / uktaṃ hi tattvapradīpe - na ca 'anaśnannanyaḥ'; iti śrutivirodhaḥ / na hi parādhīnatayā bhogo, nāpyapriyabhogo na ca tannimittoccanīcatā viṣṇoḥ, kintu - jīvasamavete bhoge svīkāramātramucyata iti / yadvā - nīcoccatāsampādako bhogaḥ svīyatayā sākṣātkāraḥ, sa cābhimānayuto vivakṣitaḥ, na cāsāvīśvare iti na virodhaḥ / pādma ityanantaraṃ uktatvāditi śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - na śrutiyuktivirodha iti bhāvaḥ /

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.3, verse 5:
Objection: Does the Lord enjoy suffering, the fruit of sinful action? Or does He enjoy happiness born of meritorious action? The first two are not [applicable], because of His being of complete bliss — to this he says: '<s>śubham</s>' (auspicious). // 'He' (<s>asau</s>) — <s>Hari</s>, situated in the <s>Prāṇa</s> dwelling in every body — <s>Bhagavān</s>, the acceptor of oblations at the sacrifice, the remover of sins — 'always' (<s>nityam</s>) — invariably 'drinks' (<s>pibati</s>) — enjoys the fruit of auspicious actions alone. <s>Hari</s> 'does not drink' (<s>na pibet</s>) — does not enjoy the fruit of inauspicious actions: that is the meaning. Because of the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Merit alone goes to Him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.5.20); 'in the supreme, in the highest abode' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.1). By the word 'drinks' (<s>pibati</s>), he accepts the status of being the drinker of <s>ṛta</s> (truth/cosmic order) as non-dual. By this reasoning, accepting the second alternative, the first alternative is disposed of by non-acceptance. He resolves the second objection — that enjoyment of happiness is unfitting for one of complete bliss — with '<s>pūrṇānandamayasya</s>' (of one whose nature is complete bliss). The suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> is in the sense of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). As stated in the <s>Gītā Bhāṣya</s>: 'The suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> has three senses: identity, modification, and abundance.' And thus — of this <s>Viṣṇu</s> whose nature is complete bliss, His 'activity' (<s>ceṣṭā</s>) — lordly power — at some time, in some place, by anyone in its entirety 'is not known' (<s>na jñāyate</s>) — cannot be comprehended: that is the meaning. And thus: by the power of lordship, even for one of complete bliss, the enjoyment of happiness is justified: that is the purport. Or alternatively: if the enjoyership of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is accepted, there would be contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> 'the other not eating' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1) — to this he says: '<s>śubham</s>.' // The purport is: that passage refers to the absence of enjoyment that is dependent on another, or to the absence of enjoyment of the inauspicious. Nor should one say there is contradiction with the passage 'the experience of low and high states alone is called enjoyment; He does not undergo low and high states' — because the enjoyment of happiness has the nature of elevation. In the case of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is conjoined with the <s>jīva</s>, by accepting mere acceptance in enjoyment, without accepting any specific modification that would produce elevation. For it is stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'There is no contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> "the other not eating"; for [His] enjoyment is not dependent on another, nor is there enjoyment of the unpleasant, nor elevation or degradation caused by that in <s>Viṣṇu</s>; rather — mere acceptance in the enjoyment conjoined with the <s>jīva</s> is stated.' Or alternatively: the enjoyment that produces elevation and degradation is direct experience accompanied by self-identification (<s>abhimāna</s>), and that is intended [to be negated]; and that does not exist in the Lord — hence no contradiction. After 'in the <s>Pādma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>],' the remainder is: 'because it has been stated.' And thus: there is no contradiction with <s>Śruti</s> or reason: that is the purport.
