hi yasmāttau hṛdayaguhāṃ praviṣṭau tasmāt / na hi jīve 'pi guhāniviṣṭatvaliṅgaṃ sambhavatīti vācyam / tasya śrutyādyaprasiddhatvāt / tatra prasiddhasyaiva grāhyatvāt / viṣṇostu 'yo veda'; iti śrutyādyaprasiddhatvāditi hiśabdārthaḥ / nanu viṣṇau pibantāviti dvivacanānapapattiḥ / na ca rūpapraveśena dvirūpeṇa praveśasyāsiddhatvādityāśaṅkyāha - taddarśanāditi / tasya harerdvirūpatayā śarīrahṛdayaguhāsthatvasya liṅgasya darśanāt 'gharmā'; iti śrutyuktatvāditi sūtrārthaḥ / atra tattvityasyānuvṛtyā śrautapadānuvṛttyā ca ānandamayastadbrahmetyādivadihāpi pratijñāsiddheḥ ātmānāvityuktiḥ / śrautadvivacanasya gatimāha - ātmeti // smṛtisamākhyāṃ śrautapadānuvṛttiṃ vinā ādeyaṃ mātīti vyutpattyā śubhakarmaphalabhoktṛtvarūpaliṅgaṃ ca vaktum / uktaṃ hi candrikāyām - ādeyaṃ mātīti vyutpattyā ātmaśabdoktaṃ śubhabhoktṛtvaṃ mūlayuktiriti / na caivamṛtapātṛtvasamānādhikaraṇaguhāpraviṣṭatvoktidvārā taduktiriti tadvākyāntaravirodhaḥ śaṅkyaḥ / tasya sūtre avaśyavaktavyaguhāpraviṣṭatvaliṅgāpakadvivacanāntarapadānvayayogyatādṛśaviśeṣyoktimukhenetyarthābhyupagamāt / tathā - yadyapi samanvetavyamṛtapātṛtvaṃ sākṣādeva vaktavyamiti tadvākyāntarasyāpyādeyaṃ mātīti vyutpattimantareṇāntaryāmītivat ṛtaṃ pibantāviti spaṣṭaśabdenaiva vaktavyam / na tvātmaśabdenetyarthāśrayaṇānna virodhaḥ / anyathā uktavākyavirodhāpātāt / evaṃ cātra keṣāñcidanyathā candrikābhiprāyakathanam, tathā teṣāmeva samanvayasūtrāttadityatrāpyanuvartate iti candrikāvirodhoktirapi cintyā / sautradvivacanopapattyartham uddeśyasamarpaṇārthaṃ cāvaśyavaktavyātmānāviti padenaiva vidheyasyāpi bodhanasambhavenetaravyāvartakāvadhāraṇārthakatuśabdamātrasyaivar ikṣatisūtra ivātrānuvṛttyaucityāt / na ca tadityanuktau tuśabdasyānvayaḥ pratyetuṃ śakyate iti samanvayādhikaraṇīyasudhāvirodhaḥ / uddeśyavidheyapadāntarābhāva ityāśayāt /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.3, verse 6:
Objection: How can the determination that the drinker is <s>Viṣṇu</s> be made through the indicatory mark of being hidden in the cave, since that is possible for the <s>jīva</s> as well? — to this he says: '<s>yo veda</s>' (he who knows). And the supplement should be: only the hiddenness-in-the-cave of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be understood here. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the <s>Smṛti</s> passages 'the inner self of the self' (<s>ātmāntarātmā</s>), 'the ear, the eye' (<s>śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ</s>), 'Having become the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire' (<s>ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā</s>) and the like are included. And thus, by 'and the like,' he shows through the word 'hi' that only the well-known hiddenness-in-the-cave of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be understood here — the <s>sūtrakāra</s> indicates this meaning: that is the meaning. And thus — even though mere dwelling in the cave of the heart is possible for the <s>jīva</s>, that is not taken here as the reason. Rather — only the hiddenness-in-the-cave that is well-known through <s>Śruti</s> and the like and that has the nature of knowledge productive of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), primarily [pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. And that has no scope in the <s>jīva</s>: that is the purport.
In the <s>sūtra</s>, only the word 'tu' carries forward from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s>. '<s>Ātmānau</s>' (the two selves) recurs. And thus, 'the two selves' — the one who experiences (<s>māti</s>) what is to be accepted (<s>ādeya</s>), that is, happiness — by the etymology 'one who measures what is to be taken,' the two who enjoy the fruit of auspicious actions as stated by the word '<s>ātma</s>' — are 'the two selves alone' (<s>ātmānau eva</s>) — the two forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called 'the self' and 'the inner self,' not the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord. Why? 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — because those two have entered the cave of the heart; therefore. Nor should one say that the indicatory mark of being hidden in the cave is possible for the <s>jīva</s> as well — because that [<s>jīva</s>'s hiddenness] is not well-known through <s>Śruti</s> and the like. Because only what is well-known there is to be taken. But for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because of the well-known-through-<s>Śruti</s> nature of 'he who knows' and the like — that is the meaning of the word 'hi.' Objection: In [the case of] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the dual number in 'the two drinking' is unjustified. Nor [can one say] that entry in two forms [resolves it], because entry in two forms is not established — anticipating this, he says: '<s>taddarśanāt</s>' (because of the evidence for that). The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: because of the evidence (<s>darśana</s>) — the <s>Śruti</s> — for that mark (<s>liṅga</s>), namely <s>Hari</s>'s dwelling in the cave of the body-heart in two forms, stated as '<s>gharmā</s>' (heat). Here, by the recurrence of 'tat' (that), by the recurrence of the Vedic word, the thesis is established as in '<s>Ānandamaya</s> is that <s>Brahman</s>' and similar — hence the expression 'the two selves.' He states the interpretation of the Vedic dual number: '<s>ātma</s>.' // The <s>Smṛti</s>-based name-explanation, and the indicatory mark of being the enjoyer of the fruit of auspicious action through the etymology 'one who measures what is to be taken' — are stated without the recurrence of the Vedic word. For it is stated in the <s>Candrikā</s>: 'The etymology "one who measures what is to be taken" — the enjoyership of auspicious fruit stated by the word ātma — is the root reasoning.' And one should not suspect contradiction with another passage through the statement of hiddenness-in-the-cave in co-referentiality with the drinker of <s>ṛta</s> — because the meaning accepted is that [hiddenness-in-the-cave] in the <s>sūtra</s> is stated through the medium of the expression of a qualifier that is fit for syntactic connection with another word, for the necessarily-to-be-stated mark of hiddenness-in-the-cave alongside the dual number. Thus — even though the enjoyership of <s>ṛta</s> to be syntactically connected should be stated directly, and even that other passage too, without the etymology 'one who measures what is to be taken' — like 'the inner controller' (<s>antaryāmī</s>) — should be stated by the explicit word '<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>' (the two drinking <s>ṛta</s>). Not by the word '<s>ātma</s>' — because of resorting to the [required] meaning, there is no contradiction. Otherwise, there would be an apparent contradiction with the stated passage. And thus, of some [commentators], the statement of a different opinion attributed to the <s>Candrikā</s> — and similarly their own statement that 'tat' carries forward from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s> — the statement of non-contradiction with the <s>Candrikā</s> is also to be reflected upon. For the justification of the Vedic dual number and for the supply of the intended subject, by the necessarily-to-be-stated word '<s>ātmānau</s>' (the two selves) alone, since the predicate too can be conveyed, the recurrence of only the word 'tu' with restrictive meaning — as in the '<s>Īkṣati</s>-<s>sūtra</s>' — is fitting here. And the objection that without stating 'tat,' the syntactic connection of the word 'tu' cannot be understood — [raised by] the <s>Sudhā</s> of the <s>Samanvaya-adhikaraṇa</s> — is not contradicted, because of the intention that there is no other word for subject and predicate.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
And because of the qualifying attribute (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.12 |

children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.3, verse 7:
Thus, when through the indicatory mark of hiddenness-in-the-cave that has no scope [elsewhere], which is stronger even than the Vedic dual number that does have scope — and because of the possibility of enjoyership of the fruits of <s>Prakṛti</s> for <s>Viṣṇu</s> — it is established that He alone is the drinker; what more need be said about [the conclusion being established] through a <s>Śruti</s> that has no scope [elsewhere]? — with this purport, having read the <s>sūtra</s> that intends [this], he cites the very <s>Śruti</s> intended by it: '<s>viśeṣaṇāt</s>' (because of the qualifying attribute). // 'Iti' connects with '<s>viśeṣaṇāt</s>.' In the <s>sūtra</s>, 'of the two drinkers' carries forward in reversed form. The word 'ca' is for the accumulation of reasoning. And thus, in the <s>Śruti</s> 'He who is the bridge,' because of the qualifying attribute (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) conveying unity through the singular number for the two drinkers, one alone is the drinker. And he, because of the qualifying attributes of being the bridge of the sacrificers, being <s>Brahman</s>, being imperishable, and the like, and because of the qualifying attribute of being supreme over <s>Brahman</s> — is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not the <s>jīva</s>: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. Not only from the indicatory mark, but also from the <s>setu</s>-<s>Śruti</s> and the like: that too is the meaning of 'ca.' 'He who' (<s>yaḥ</s>) — <s>Bhagavān</s> in the two forms called 'the self' and 'the inner self' — 'of the sacrificers' (<s>ijānānām</s>) — of those performing sacrifice directed toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is 'the bridge' (<s>setuḥ</s>) — the refuge; 'that which is the imperishable, supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — [we pray that we] 'may be able' (<s>śakemahi</s>) to state the means to meditate upon Him, to <s>Naciketas</s>: this is the meaning of the <s>Kāṭhaka Śruti</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.3, verse 8:]
His qualities cannot be stated separately because of their limitlessness;
therefore, by the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' the comprehension of all [qualities] is achieved.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.8:
brahmaśabdasya bhagavadekavācitvaṃ smārayati - pṛthagiti // atra yata ityāvartate / tathā ca yataḥ 'tasya'; viṣṇorguṇāḥ 'amitatvataḥ'; asaṅkhyātatvato nimittāt 'pṛthak'; vivicya vaktuṃ na śakyante / jñātavyāśca sarvairadhikāribhiḥ sarve guṇā iti śeṣaḥ / yato brahmaśabdena sarveṣāṃ guṇānāṃ 'grahaṇaṃ'; jñānaṃ bhavet ataḥ sarvaguṇajñānārthaṃ tasmin viṣṇau brahmaśabdaḥ prayujyate iti śeṣaḥ / yato brahmaśabdena sarveṣāṃ guṇānāṃ grahaṇaṃ bhavet / evaṃ ca sarvaguṇavācī brahmaśabdo bhavati, tatra vṛttimantareṇa tajjñānajanakatvāyogāditi bhāvaḥ / yasmādvibhuṃ taṃ viṣṇumṛte anyeṣāṃ jīvānāṃ nāmitā guṇāḥ, kintu - viṣṇoreva pramāṇasiddham, etasmātkāraṇādayaṃ brahmaśabdo viṣṇoreva 'viśeṣaṇaṃ'; mukhyavācako nānyeṣāmityarthaḥ / brāhma ityanantaraṃ brahmaśabdasya bhagavadekavācitvamuktamiti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.3, verse 8:
He recalls through <s>Smṛti</s> that the word '<s>Brahman</s>' exclusively denotes <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>pṛthak</s>' (separately). // Here, '<s>yataḥ</s>' (because) carries forward. And thus, because 'His' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s — qualities, 'because of their limitlessness' (<s>amitatvataḥ</s>) — because of their innumerability — 'cannot be stated separately' (<s>pṛthak vaktuṃ na śakyante</s>). And all qualities must be known by all eligible persons: this is the remainder. Because by the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' the 'comprehension' (<s>grahaṇam</s>) — knowledge — of all qualities 'is achieved,' therefore, for the purpose of knowing all qualities, the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is applied to that <s>Viṣṇu</s>: this is the remainder. Because by the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' the comprehension of all qualities is achieved. And thus the word '<s>Brahman</s>' denotes all qualities; without a convention (<s>vṛtti</s>) in that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], there would be unfitness for producing that knowledge: this is the purport. Because apart from (<s>ṛte</s>) that all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>) Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the qualities of 'others' — <s>jīvas</s> — are not unlimited, but only those of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone are established by valid means of knowledge; for this reason, this word '<s>Brahman</s>' is the 'qualifier' (<s>viśeṣaṇam</s>) — the primary denotation — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not of others: that is the meaning. After 'in the <s>Brāhma</s>,' the remainder is: 'the exclusive denotation of <s>Bhagavān</s> by the word <s>Brahman</s> is stated.'
And the syntactic connection (<s>samanvaya</s>) in the <s>jīva</s> is not being stated [here].
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.3, verse 9:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.9:
atra paraiḥ pibantau buddhijīvāviti pūrvapakṣe prāpte jīveśvarāveveti vyākhyātaṃ, tannirākaroti - na ceti// atreti śeṣaḥ / asminnadhyāye iti tadarthaḥ / hetau, svavyānena saha paravyākhyānanirākaraṇasya samuccaye vā caśabdaḥ tathā cāsaṅgatiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.3, verse 9:
Here, while others have raised the prima facie view 'the two drinking are the intellect and the <s>jīva</s>,' [the bhāṣyakāra] has explained [it as] 'the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord alone'; he refutes that: '<s>na ca</s>' (and not). // 'Here' (<s>atra</s>) is the remainder. 'In this chapter' is its meaning. The word 'ca' is either in the reason [clause], or in the sense of conjunction of the refutation of others' interpretation along with his own explanation — and thus [it indicates] coherence: that is the purport.

children.text:
satya ātmā satyo jīvaḥ satyaṃ bhidā satyaṃ bhidā
satyaṃ bhidā maivāruvaṇyo maivāruvaṇyo maivāruvaṇyaḥ // iti paiṅgiśrutiḥ /
children.translated_text:
The Self is real; the <s>jīva</s> is real; difference is real; difference is real;
difference is real — do not bark [against this]! Do not bark [against this]! Do not bark [against this]! — Thus the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.3, verse 10:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.10:
nanu nātra jīve samanvayakathanamasaṅgatam / jīveśvarabhedasyāsatyatvena tayoraikyāt / jīvasamanvayasyaiva brahmasamanvayarūpatvādityata āha - satya iti / 'satyaṃ'; satyā 'bhidā'; bhedaḥ / yadyapyatrātmajīvayoḥ satyatvavacanenaiva tatsvarūpabhedasyāpi satyatvamuktaṃ bhavati / tathāpi punaḥ 'satyaṃ bhidā'; ityuktirdarśanapratītābhedapratītinirāsatātparyārthā śapathāvṛttiḥ / kecidbhedamasatyamāhuḥ tatkathametadityatasteṣāṃ pakṣe śrutirabhīkṣṇaṃ dūṣaṇamabhidhatte - maiveti / 'āruvaṇyaḥ'; arā doṣāstadvantaḥ, āsamantādaraśīlā vā āravaḥ tairasatyabhedajñānibhiḥ viṣṇuḥ sarvathā vanyo bhajanīyo netyarthaḥ / iti paiṅgiśrutirityanantaraṃ yata iti śeṣaḥ / asya nāsatyo bheda ityuttareṇānvayaḥ evaṃ bhāllaveyaśrutirityasyāpi / atra yadyapi bhāgavatatātparye - 'satyatvaṃ ca bhedasyoktaṃ bhāllaveyaśrutau / sthāṇurheccakrāma sa prajāpatimuvāca ko 'si ke smaḥ kaḥ saḥ iti / sahovāca yo 'smi ye stha yaḥ sa iti / athainamupākrośat satyaṃ bhidā satyaṃ bhidā satyaṃ bhidā'; ityādinā 'satyam'; iti vākyaṃ bhāllaveyaśrutyantargatatayā paṭhyate / bhāṣyapustake 'pi kvacit 'satyam'; iti vākyam 'ātmā hi'; iti vākyaṃ ca bhāllaveyaśrutitvenaiva paṭhyate / na tu śrutidvayasthatvena / tathāpi anayostātparyānusāreṇaikaśrutisthatvaṃ, bahutarapāṭhabalāt 'satya ātmā'; iti paiṅgiśrutiḥ / 'ātmā hi'; iti bhāllaveyaśrutiḥ / tātparyodāhṛtā tu anyā tatsamākhyā rūpā cetyadoṣaḥ / 'sthāṇuḥ'; rudraḥ 'uccakrāma'; ūrdhvaṃ jagāma/ 'saḥ'; rudraḥ 'prajāpatiṃ'; brahmāṇam upākrośaduvāca / kimiti? tvaṃ 'kaḥ'; kīdṛśaḥ / vayaṃ 'ke'; kīdṛśāḥ / saḥ viṣṇuḥ 'kaḥ'; kīdṛśaḥ / kiṃ bhinna utābhinna ityāśayaḥ / krameṇottaramāha - ahaṃ 'yo'; yādṛśo 'gre sarvadā tādṛśo 'smi / yūyaṃ 'ye'; yādṛśāḥ tādṛśāḥ stha / 'saḥ'; viṣṇuryādṛśo mayā bhavadādibhiśca bhinnastādṛśa eveti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.3.10: Now, [one might object:] the statement of correlation (<s>samanvaya</s>) with regard to the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is not fitting here, since the difference between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is unreal, and therefore the two are identical; the correlation with the <s>jīva</s> is itself of the nature of correlation with <s>Brahman</s> — to this he says 'satya' (real). 'Satyam' means real; '<s>bhidā</s>' means difference. Although here by the statement of the reality of the self and the <s>jīva</s>, the reality of their essential difference is also stated, nevertheless the repeated declaration 'the difference is real' is an emphatic assertion (<s>śapathāvṛtti</s>) whose purpose is to negate the apprehension of non-difference that arises from perception. Some say that difference is unreal — how then is this? To this, the <s>Śruti</s> repeatedly states a refutation against their position — with 'maiva' (never so). '<s>Āruvaṇyaḥ</s>' — '<s>arāḥ</s>' means faults, those possessing them, or those habitually creating discord all around are '<s>āravāḥ</s>'; by those who know difference to be unreal, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is in no way to be worshipped — this is the meaning. This is from the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s>, and what follows after is 'yataḥ' — the connection with the subsequent text is 'the difference of this one is not unreal.' The same applies to the <s>Bhāllavya Śruti</s> as well. Here, although in the <s>Bhāgavata Tātparya</s> it is read: 'The reality of difference is stated in the <s>Bhāllavya Śruti</s>: <s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Rudra</s>) went upward and said to <s>Prajāpati</s>: Who are you? Who are we? Who is He? He replied: I am what I am, you are what you are, He is what He is. Then he admonished him: the difference is real, the difference is real, the difference is real' — thus the passage beginning with 'satyam' is read as belonging within the <s>Bhāllavya Śruti</s>. In some manuscripts of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> too, the passage 'satyam' and the passage 'ātmā hi' are read as belonging to the <s>Bhāllavya Śruti</s> alone, not as being in two separate <s>Śrutis</s>. Nevertheless, following their purport, they belong to one <s>Śruti</s>; by the strength of the majority of readings, 'satya ātmā' is from the <s>Paiṅgi Śruti</s>, and 'ātmā hi' is from the <s>Bhāllavya Śruti</s>. What is cited in the <s>Tātparya</s> is another text of the same name — this is not a fault. '<s>Sthāṇuḥ</s>' is <s>Rudra</s>; 'uccakrāma' means he went upward. 'He' — <s>Rudra</s> — admonished <s>Prajāpati</s>, i.e., <s>Brahmā</s>. With what intention? 'You — what (kaḥ) are you like? We — what (ke) are we like? He, <s>Viṣṇu</s> — what (kaḥ) is He like? Are they different or non-different?' — this is the purport. The answer is given in order: 'I am such as (yaḥ) I was before, always such I am. You are such as (ye) you are. He — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is such as He is, different from me and from you and others' — this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>.

children.text: 'ātmā hi paramassvatantro 'dhiguṇo jīvo 'lpaśaktirasvatantro 'varaḥ'; iti ca bhāllaveyaśrutiḥ / (12) yatheśvarasya jīvasya bhedassatyo viniścayāt /
children.translated_text: 'The self (<s>Ātmā</s>) indeed is the supreme, independent, endowed with superior qualities; the <s>jīva</s> is of limited power, dependent, and inferior' — thus says the <s>Bhāllavya Śruti</s>. (12) Just as the difference between <s>Īśvara</s> and the <s>jīva</s> is real, by firm determination,

children.text: evameva hi me vācaṃ satyāṃ kartumihārhasi //
children.translated_text: so indeed you ought to make my words true here.
Just as <s>Īśvara</s> and the <s>jīva</s> are mutually of real difference,
by that truth, may the <s>Devas</s> together with <s>Keśava</s> protect me.
From such statements and others, the difference is not unreal. (12)
Thus ends the <s>Guhādhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of the one in the cave). (3)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.11:
atroktabhedasādhakapramāṇatvena viruddhaguṇopanyāsāya 'ātmā'; iti dvitīyavākyaṃ pravṛttam / 'ātmā'; paramātmā 'paramaḥ'; svatantraḥ / 'adhiguṇaḥ'; pūrṇaśaktiḥ / ata evottaratra paramatvasvatantratvapūrṇaśaktitvaviruddhānāṃ dharmāṇām alpaśaktirityādipadairyutkrameṇābhidhānaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.3.11: Here, the second passage beginning with '<s>ātmā</s>' is introduced to present the contradictory attributes as evidence for the difference stated above. '<s>Ātmā</s>' means the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātmā</s>); '<s>paramaḥ</s>' means independent (<s>svatantraḥ</s>). '<s>Adhiguṇaḥ</s>' means possessed of full power (<s>pūrṇaśakti</s>). For this very reason, in the subsequent text, the attributes contrary to supremacy, independence, and fullness of power are stated in reverse order by the words '<s>alpaśaktiḥ</s>' (of limited power) and so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.3.12:
atraivārthe purāṇavākye paṭhati - yatheti // atra ṣaṣṭhyantaṃ vākyaṃ pādmasthaṃ, prathamāntaṃ skāndagatamiti tattvapradīpokteḥ / 'me mām'; ityābhyāṃ tatprakṛto grāhyaḥ / 'viniścayāt'; evārtho 'yaṃ śabdaḥ / satyabhedāviti bahuvrīhiḥ / yathā satyabhedau tathaiva vidyamānānatikrameṇa jñātena 'satyena'; satyabhedena bhedasatyatvajñānākhyakāraṇeneti yāvat / sahakeśavā ityekaṃ padaṃ, keśavasahitā devāḥ 'trāyantu'; asmān rakṣantvityarthaḥ / ityādervākyānnāsatyo bhedaḥ, kintu - satya eveti jñāyata ityarthaḥ / atra pūrvavākye jīveśabhedasya dṛṣṭāntatvenopādānātprāmāṇikatvaṃ jñāyate, tādṛśasyaiva dṛṣṭāntatvāt / dvitīye tu viṣayānatikrameṇa bhedasatyatvajñānasya trāṇakāraṇatvoktyā bheda satyatvamapi jñāyata iti prakṛtasaṅgatiḥ / ādipadena grāhyavacanāni tattvapradīpe udāhṛtāni / tathāhi - dvau bhūtasargau loke 'smin daiva āsura eva ca /
daivo vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu //
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.3.12: He cites a <s>Purāṇa</s> passage for this very meaning — with 'yathā.' Here, the passage ending in the sixth case is from the <s>Pādma</s> (<s>Purāṇa</s>), and the one ending in the first case is from the <s>Skānda</s> (<s>Purāṇa</s>), as stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. By the words 'me' and 'mām,' the person referred to in the context should be understood. '<s>Viniścayāt</s>' — this word has the sense of 'eva' (indeed). '<s>Satyabhedau</s>' is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound (meaning 'those whose difference is real'). Just as the difference is real, so also by the truth that is known without transgressing what actually exists — 'by that truth' means by the real difference, i.e., by the causal knowledge of the reality of difference. '<s>Sahakeśavāḥ</s>' is one compound word; it means 'the <s>Devas</s> accompanied by <s>Keśava</s> — may they protect us.' From such passages, the difference is not unreal, but rather — it is known to be real indeed. This is the meaning. Here, in the first passage, since the difference between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> is taken as an illustration, its authoritativeness is understood, for only such a thing serves as an illustration. In the second passage, by stating that the knowledge of the reality of difference, in accordance with the actual state of affairs, is the cause of protection, the reality of difference is also understood — this is the relevance to the present topic. The passages to be cited under 'ādi' (etc.) are given in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. Thus: 'There are two types of created beings in this world — the divine and the demoniac. The divine has been described at length; hear from me about the demoniac, O <s>Pārtha</s>.'
'Those cruel haters, lowest of men in the cycles of existence,
I ceaselessly hurl into inauspicious, demoniac wombs.'
'They say this world is unreal, without foundation, without a Lord' — beginning from this,

children.text:
iti bhagavadvacanam (bha.gī. 16-6, 19.)
asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram /
ta āsurāḥ svayaṃ naṣṭāḥ jagataḥ kṣayakāriṇaḥ // iti vyāsasmṛtiḥ /
indrāsomā tapataṃ rakṣa ujjataṃ nyarpayataṃ vṛṣaṇā tamovṛdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>, burn the <s>Rakṣas</s>, cast them down; hurl down, O mighty ones, those who thrive in darkness.
Shatter the strengthless ones, drive them away; slay them, thrust down the devourers, the <s>atriṇaḥ</s> (those without protectors). (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 7.104.1)

children.text:
indrā somā vartayataṃ divasparyagnitaptebhiryuvamaśmahanmabhiḥ /
tapurvadhebhirajarebhiratriṇaḥ ; (ṛ. 7-104-5.) ityādikā śrutiḥ /
yeṣāṃ bhijjagadīśvarajīvānāṃ nāsti te 'triṇaḥ /
svājñānakalpitajagatparameśvarasya jīvasya bhedakaluṣīkṛtabhūmabhāve / iti hi māyino vadanti /
ācchādya vikṣipati saṃsphuradātmattvam /
jīveśvarasya jagadākṛti tanmṛṣaiva / ityādi ca /
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>, hurl them down from heaven, with fire-heated, stone-striking thunderbolts, with blazing weapons, against the undecaying devourers (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 7.104.5) — such is the <s>Śruti</s>. Those for whom the difference between the world, <s>Īśvara</s>, and the <s>jīvas</s> does not exist — they are the '<s>atriṇaḥ</s>' (devourers). 'In the absence of the ground of the defilement of the difference between the Supreme Lord and the <s>jīva</s>, fabricated by one's own ignorance concerning the world' — thus indeed speak the <s>Māyāvādins</s>. 'Concealing and scattering the flashing reality of the self, the world-form of the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> — that is false indeed' — and so forth.

children.text: triryātudhānaḥ prasitiṃ tayetvṛtaṃ yo agne anṛtena hanti / (ṛ. 10-87-11.)
children.translated_text: Thrice let the <s>Yātudhāna</s> (sorcerer) meet his doom, who strikes truth with falsehood, O <s>Agni</s>. (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.87.11)

children.text: vācā stenaṃ śarava ṛcchantu marman viśvasyaitu prasitiṃ yātudhānaḥ / (ṛ. 10-87-15.)
children.translated_text: Let the arrows of speech pierce the thief in his vital parts; let the <s>Yātudhāna</s> meet the doom of all. (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.87.15)

children.text: atha jñānopasargāḥ ityārabhya yecānye mithyātarkairdṛṣṭāntaiḥ kuhakendrajālairvaidikeṣu paristhātumicchanti taiḥ saha na saṃvaset / prakāśyāhyete taskarā asvargyāḥ (maitrī. 7-8.) ityādiśrutiśatairandhaṃ tama eva māyināṃ gatiriti niścīyate / tathā ca skānde -
children.translated_text: Beginning from 'Now, the obstacles to knowledge' — 'those who, by means of false reasoning, examples, and illusions of deceivers, wish to establish themselves among the followers of the <s>Vedas</s> — one should not associate with them; for these are manifestly thieves, unfit for heaven' (<s>Maitrī Upaniṣad</s> 7.8) — from hundreds of such <s>Śruti</s> passages, it is determined that blinding darkness is the destination of the <s>Māyāvādins</s>. And thus in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>:
Those who know everything to be <s>Brahman</s>, those who know the <s>jīva</s> to be <s>Brahman</s>,
those who know <s>Viṣṇu</s> to be equal to others — they are indeed haters of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: sarve yānti tamo ghoraṃ na teṣāṃ utthitiḥ kvacit // iti //
children.translated_text: They all go to terrible darkness; there is no rising for them ever. Thus it is.

Thus is the statement of the Lord (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 16.6, 19). 'They say this world is unreal, without foundation, without a Lord — those <s>Āsuras</s>, themselves ruined, are the destroyers of the world' — thus says the <s>Vyāsa Smṛti</s>.
Thus ends the <s>Guhādhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of the one in the cave). (3)
4. <s>Antarādhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of the inner one).

children.text:
āditye viṣṇurityuktam / 'ya eṣa āditye
puruṣaḥ so 'hamasmi sa evāhamasmi'; (chāṃ. 4-11.) ityādāvagnīnāmevādityādisthatvamucyate /
children.translated_text: It has been stated that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is in the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). In the passage 'The person who is in the sun — I am He, I am indeed He' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.11), it is stated that the fires themselves are situated in the sun and other [luminaries].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.1:
atrādhikaraṇe cakṣurantaḥsthatvaliṅgaṃ brahmaṇi samanvīyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayavākyaṃ viṣayasaṃśayau sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣaṃ ca darśayati - āditya iti // 'yaścāsāvāditye'; ityānandamayādhikaraṇodāhṛtāyāṃ tathā 'antarāditye'; ityantarnayodāhṛtāyāṃ ca śrutāvānandamayo 'ntasstho viṣṇurāditye 'stītyuktamityarthaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - ya iti / tadityādau saṃyojyam / 'so 'haṃ sa evāham'; ityabhyāsopanyāsaḥ pūrvapakṣayuktipradarśanārthaḥ / prathamādipadena athainamanvāhāryapacano 'nuśaśāsa / ya eṣa candramasi puruṣo dṛśyate / so 'hamasmi sa evāhamasmi / athainamāhavanīyo 'nuśaśāsa / ya eṣa vidyuti puruṣo dṛśyate so 'hamasmi sa evāhamasmīti ca vākyadvaṃ gṛhyate / dvitīyādipadena candravidyutsthatvam / yadyapi ādityasthatvasyeva candravidyutsthatvayoragnerakṣisthatvasādhakatvābhāvāttadupādānaṃ na prakṛtopayuktam / tathā agnīnāmiti bahuvacanaṃ cānupayuktam, pūrvapakṣe gārhapatyasyaiva akṣisthatvasādhanena gārhapatyādīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ tasyāsādhanāt / candravidyutorakṣyekavidhatvābhāvena tatsthatvasyākṣisthatvāsādhakatvācca / tathāpi ādiśabdadvayaṃ bahuvacanaṃ ca pūrvapakṣe gārhapatyādibahvagniśrutirūpayuktisūcanārtham / yathā anvāhāryapacanākhyadakṣiṇāgnyāhavanīyayoḥ candravidyutsthatvamucyate, evaṃ gārhaptayasyāpi ādityasthatvamucyate iti dṛṣṭāntārthaṃ gārhapatyādīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ krameṇādityāditritayasthatve prasiddhagārhapatyasyaivādityasthatvamukhenākṣisthatvamāgacchatīti yuktipradarśanārthaṃ vā tadupādānamiti na vaiyarthyamiti dhyeyam/
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.4.1: In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of being situated within the eye is correlated with <s>Brahman</s>. He shows the <s>Śruti</s> connections, the subject-passage, the subject-matter and doubt, and the prior view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) with its reasoning — with 'āditya.' In the <s>Śruti</s> cited in the <s>Ānandamayādhikaraṇa</s> beginning with 'He who is in the sun,' and also in the <s>Śruti</s> cited in the <s>Antarnaya</s> (inner method) topic beginning with 'within the sun,' it was stated that the blissful inner <s>Viṣṇu</s> is in the sun — this is the meaning. Then what follows from this? To this he says: with 'ya.' One should supply 'tat' and so forth. The repetition 'I am He, I am indeed He' is for the purpose of showing the reasoning of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prior view). By the first 'ādi' word, two additional passages are taken: 'Then the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (the southern sacrificial fire) instructed him: The person who is seen in the moon — I am He, I am indeed He. Then the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (the offering fire) instructed him: The person who is seen in lightning — I am He, I am indeed He.' By the second 'ādi' word, the abiding in the moon and lightning is indicated. Although the abiding in the moon and lightning, like the abiding in the sun, does not serve to prove the abiding in the eye, and therefore citing them is not useful to the present topic; and although the plural 'of the fires' is also unnecessary, since in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> only the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire) serves to prove the abiding in the eye, and the triad of <s>Gārhapatya</s> and others does not serve that purpose; and since the moon and lightning are not of the same type as the eye, their abiding there does not prove abiding in the eye — nevertheless, the two 'ādi' words and the plural are for the purpose of indicating the reasoning in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> that involves the <s>Śruti</s> references to the many fires beginning with the <s>Gārhapatya</s>. Just as the abiding in the moon and lightning is stated for the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern fire) and <s>Āhavanīya</s>, so also the abiding in the sun is stated for the <s>Gārhapatya</s> — this is by way of illustration. The abiding in the eye comes through the mention of the well-known <s>Gārhapatya</s>'s abiding in the sun among the sequential abiding of the three fires in the sun and other [luminaries] — or the citation is for the purpose of showing the reasoning. Thus there is no purposelessness — this should be reflected upon.

Therefore, because of the identity of the eye and the sun, in the passage 'The person who is seen within the eye' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.15), it is the fire (<s>Agni</s>) alone that is spoken of.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.2:
tato 'pi kimityata āha - ata iti // asya na sannihitena 'aikyāt'; ityanenānvayaḥ / prakṛtasya ata ityanena parāmṛṣṭāsyādityāntaḥ sthatvasya aikye hetutvāyogāt / kintu vyavahitena 'atrāpyagnirevocyate'; ityanenānvayaḥ / na kevalamādityavākya ityaperarthaḥ / tathā ca - yadānandamayākhyaviṣṇuniṣṭhatayoktamādityasthatvaṃ tacchāndogye 'ya eṣa āditye puruṣaḥ so 'hamasmi'; ityādāvāgnīnāṃ gārhaptayākhyāgnereva 'ucyate'; pratīyate na viṣṇoḥ/ kutaḥ? yato 'tra 'agnīnāṃ'; gārhapatyadakṣiṇāgnyāhavanīyānāṃ trayāṇāṃ krameṇa ādityādisthatvamucyate, ataḥ / tataḥ kim? yato 'tra gārhapatyākhyāgnerevādityasthatvamucyate 'to 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate'; iti vākye 'pyakṣisthatvena gārhapatyāgnirevocyate, na sa viṣṇuḥ / śrutigatāhaṃśabdenāpi sa evocyate iti yojanā / tathā ca pūrvapakṣaśrutigatāhaṃśabdo agnāveva mukhya iti tasyaiva grahaṇamiti bhāvaḥ / nanvagnerādityasthatve 'pi kuto 'kṣisthatvaprāptirityata āha - akṣyādityayoriti / 'ādityaścakṣurbhūtvākṣiṇī prāviśat'; ityaitareyaśruteracetanākṣyādityamaṇḍalayorādityacakṣuḥpadoditaikacetanādhiṣṭhitatvarūpaikadharmeṇaikavidhatvādityarthaḥ / yadvā - 'aśanayodāhṛtādityastrivṛdiva vai cakṣuḥ śuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kanīnikā'; () iti śrutyanusāreṇa tayostrivṛttvadharmeṇaikavidhatvādityarthaḥ / tathā ca - ādityasthatvoktyā arthādakṣisthatvamapi prāptameveti bhāvaḥ / yadyapi 'sayaścāyam'; iti pūrvodāhṛtataittirīyaśrutisthādityaśabdaḥ utkṛṣṭacetanamātropalakṣakatayā vyākhyātaḥ / tathāpi atrādhikaraṇe sūryābhimanyamānādityamaṇḍalaparatvamapyasyāṅgīkṛtya ākṣepaparihārau kṛtau / ata eva ṭīkāyāmakṣyādityayarekavidhatvādyuktam / tattvapradīpe tu - akṣīndriyaprerakādityayorekatvāditi yathāśrutameva vyākhyātam / candrikāyāmapi tattvapradīpānusāreṇa devatāparamevākṣipadam / ata eva bhāṣye sannyāyaratnāvalyāṃ ca akṣyādityayoraikyādityevoktam, na tvekavidhatvāditi / akṣyādityayorekavidhatvāditi ṭīkāpi bhāṣyānusāreṇa prakārabhedaniṣedhamukhena prakāryaikyaparā neyeti pakṣāntaramapyuktam / tathā ca - devatāparatve 'āditye viṣṇurityuktam'; iti bhāṣyaśrutisthākṣyādityapadayośca yathāśruta evārthaḥ / maṇḍalaparatve tadbhāṣyasthādityapadaṃ pūrvodāhṛtataittirīyaśrutisthādityapadaṃ ca maṇḍalaparatayā vyākhyeyamiti vivekaḥ / anena chandogaśrutyuktākṣisthatvasyānyaniṣṭhatvākṣepamukhenānandamayanayodāhṛtāyāṃ taittirīyaśrutāvarthāduktasyāpi tasyānyaniṣṭhatvākṣepādānandamayādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / akṣisthatvaṃ viṣayaḥ / kimagnerviṣṇorveti sandehaḥ / agnīnāmeva akṣisthatvamiti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ / atra ādityasthatvarūpayuktiścoktā bhavati / atra 'ya eṣa āditye puruṣaḥ'; 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi puruṣaḥ'; ityanayorvākyayoḥ 'ādityaścakṣurbhūtvā'; iti vākyadvārā ekārthatvamupapādya tanmukhena 'ya eṣa āditye'; iti vākyena 'yaścāsāvāditye'; iti vākyasya saṅgatiṃ sampādya taddvārārthākṣiptatadarthārthakasya 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi'; iti vākyasyāpi tena saṅgatirityevaṃ vakrasaṅgatyaitadadhikaraṇārambhaḥ ādityasthatvaliṅgasyāpi samanvayasiddhyartham / anyathā 'netaro 'nupapatteḥ'; ityādau viṣṇujñānānmokṣa ityuktam, sa mokṣaḥ 'tadyathā'; iti vākyena 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi'; ityuktākṣisthajñānātpratīyata iti vakṣyamāṇaṛjusaṅgatyaiva adhikaraṇamārambhaṇīyaṃ syāditi dhyeyam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.2:
To the question 'what further follows from that?', he says — 'ata' (therefore). // The syntactical connection of this [word 'ata'] is not with the proximate [phrase] 'aikyāt' (because of identity), because the identity of the being-within-<s>Āditya</s> referred to by 'ata' — which pertains to the topic under discussion — is not logically fit to serve as a reason. Rather, the syntactical connection is with the remote [phrase] 'atrāpyagnirevocyate' (here too, it is <s>Agni</s> alone that is spoken of). The further meaning is: not merely in the passage about <s>Āditya</s>. And thus — the abiding-within-<s>Āditya</s> that was stated as pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s> known as <s>Ānandamaya</s>, that very thing in the <s>Chāndogya</s> [passage] 'ya eṣa āditye puruṣaḥ so'hamasmi' (the person who is in the sun — I am he) and so forth, is understood ('ucyate') as referring to <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire alone among the fires, not to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? Because here, of the fires — the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>, and <s>Āhavanīya</s> — the three are sequentially said to abide in <s>Āditya</s> and other [locations]. What follows from that? Since the abiding-in-<s>Āditya</s> is stated of the fire called <s>Gārhapatya</s> alone, in the statement 'ya eṣo'ntarakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' (the person seen within the eye) also, it is <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire alone that is spoken of as abiding in the eye — not <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The construction is that even through the word 'aham' (I) occurring in the <s>śruti</s>, it is that [fire] alone that is referred to. And thus, the meaning is: the word 'aham' in the <s>śruti</s> of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (objection) is primary only with reference to fire, therefore it is fire alone that is meant. To the question — even if <s>Agni</s> abides in <s>Āditya</s>, how does the abiding in the eye follow? — he says: 'akṣyādityayoḥ' (of the eye and the sun). The meaning is: on the basis of the <s>Aitareya</s> <s>śruti</s> '<s>Āditya</s>, having become the eye, entered the two eyes,' the non-conscious eye and the solar disc are of one kind (ekavidhatva) by virtue of the single property of being presided over by the one conscious entity denoted by the words '<s>āditya</s>' and '<s>cakṣus</s>.' Or alternatively — in accordance with the <s>śruti</s> 'the sun struck by lightning is threefold; indeed the eye [has] white, black, and the pupil,' the meaning is: those two are of one kind by virtue of the property of being threefold. And thus, the purport is: by the statement of abiding in <s>Āditya</s>, abiding in the eye is also implicitly established. Although the word '<s>āditya</s>' in the previously cited <s>Taittirīya</s> <s>śruti</s> 'sa yaścāyam' has been explained as merely indicating the supreme conscious being, nevertheless in this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), accepting that it also refers to the solar disc itself, objection and resolution have been carried out. For this very reason, in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, the statement about the ekavidhatva (being of one kind) of the eye and <s>Āditya</s> is made. But in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, it is explained literally — 'because of the oneness of the eye-sense organ and its impeller, <s>Āditya</s>.' In the <s>Candrikā</s> also, following the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, the word '<s>akṣi</s>' refers to the presiding deity itself. For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and the <s>Nyāyaratnāvalī</s>, it is stated as 'because of the identity of the eye and <s>Āditya</s>,' not as 'because of being of one kind.' There is also an alternative view that even the <s>Ṭīkā</s> [statement] 'because of the ekavidhatva of eye and <s>Āditya</s>' should be interpreted, in accordance with the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, as referring to the identity of the substrate through the negation of difference in mode. And thus — when [<s>Āditya</s> is taken as] referring to the deity, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>śruti</s> words '<s>akṣi</s>' and '<s>āditya</s>' have their literal meaning; when [taken as] referring to the solar disc, the word '<s>āditya</s>' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and the '<s>āditya</s>' in the previously cited <s>Taittirīya</s> <s>śruti</s> should be explained as referring to the disc — this is the discernment. By this, through the objection that the abiding-in-the-eye stated in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s> pertains to another [entity, i.e. <s>Agni</s>], and since the same objection would apply to that [abiding-in-the-eye] which was implicitly stated in the <s>Taittirīya</s> <s>śruti</s> cited in the <s>Ānandamaya</s> topic, the connection of this [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] with the <s>Ānandamayādhikaraṇa</s> through objection is stated. The subject matter is: abiding in the eye. The doubt is: does it pertain to <s>Agni</s> or to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is: the abiding in the eye belongs to the fires alone. Here, the reasoning based on the abiding-in-<s>Āditya</s> is also stated. Here, having established the unity of meaning between the two statements 'ya eṣa āditye puruṣaḥ' (the person in the sun) and 'ya eṣo'ntarakṣiṇi puruṣaḥ' (the person within the eye) through the passage '<s>Āditya</s>, having become the eye,' and through that connecting the statement 'yaścāsāvāditye' (and the one in the sun) with 'ya eṣa āditye,' and thereby also connecting 'ya eṣo'ntarakṣiṇi' (the one within the eye) — whose meaning is implicitly obtained through that — this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is commenced through this indirect connection, for the purpose of establishing the consistent interpretation (samanvaya) of the indicator of abiding-in-<s>Āditya</s> as well. Otherwise, [since] in 'netaro'nupapatteḥ' (not the other, because of impossibility) and so forth, it was stated that liberation comes from knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and that liberation is understood from the passage 'tadyathā' (just as) as arising from knowledge of the being abiding in the eye stated in 'ya eṣo'ntarakṣiṇi' — the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> could have been commenced through that direct connection alone. This should be contemplated.

children.text:
ataḥ 'tadyathā puṣkarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyanta evamevaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyate'; (chāṃ. 4-14.)
ityagnijñānādeva sarvapāpāśleṣānmokṣopapattiriti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the objector says:] 'Just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so sinful action does not cling to one who knows thus' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.14) — thus, liberation is established through freedom from all sin by knowledge of <s>Agni</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.3:
na kevalamakṣisthatvasiddhāvagnerānandamayatvaprāptiḥ / kintu yatpūrvaṃ 'netaraḥ'; ityādau viṣṇujñānānmokṣa ityuktaṃ, tadapi bādhitaṃ syādityata āha - ata iti // 'agnijñānādityetat'; 'sarvapāpāśleṣāt'; ityaneneva 'mokṣaḥ'; ityanenāpi sambadhyate / tathā ca yato 'gnirakṣistho 'tastajjñānādeva mokṣo 'pi bhavet na viṣṇujñānāt / kuta etat? akṣisthāgnijñānātsarvapāpāśleṣāt / na ca tasyāsiddhiḥ / 'tadyathā'; iti tadarthavāde 'gnijñānādeva sarvapāpāśleṣokteḥ / na ca tajjñānātsarvapāpāśleṣamātreṇa kathaṃ mokṣa iti vācyam / yatastajjñānānmokṣaṃ vinā sarvapāpāśleṣāsambhavena tadanyathānupapattyaiva mokṣasyāpyupapattiriti yojanā / evaṃ ca pūrvapakṣe agnerakṣisthatvena 'tadyathā'; ityakṣisthasyoktaṃ muktihetujñānaviṣayatvamapi tasyaiva prāpnotīti 'netaraḥ'; ityuktamayuktamiti bhāvaḥ / anena ṛjusaṅgatirapyasya darśitā bhavati / chāndogyehītthamākhyāyikā - (chāṃ. 4-10-5.) kamalāyanasyāpatyaṃ kāmalāyanaḥ nāmataḥ upakosalaḥ satyakāmākhye gurau brahmacaryamuddiśyovāsa / sa ācāryasyāgnīn gārhapatyādīn dvādaśavarṣaparyantaṃ paryacārīt / satyakāmastvantevāsinaḥ svādhyāyaṃ grāhayan enamekameva nādhyāpayat / punaḥ punaḥ svajāyayokto 'pi anuktvaiva vidyāṃ pravāsāya prātiṣṭhata / tadopakosalo vyādhipīḍito vidyāprāpticintayā svācāryabhāryayā aśānetyukto 'pi nāśnāt / evaṃ brahmacāriṇyanaśnati tūṣṇīṃbhūte sati tadā gārhapatyādyagnayaḥ kāruṇyāviṣṭāḥ trayo 'pi vayamasmai brahmacāriṇo vidyāṃ prabravāmeti pratijñāya militāssanto vidyāmūcuḥ / 'prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma'; ityādi / evaṃ sambhūyopadeśānantaramenaṃ pratyekam agnaya upadidiśuḥ ityucyate vedapuruṣeṇa 'atha hainaṃ gārhapatyo 'nuśaśāsa ...... ya eṣa āditye puruṣo dṛśyate so 'hamasmi sa evāhamasmi'; ityādinā / evaṃ tribhiragnibhiḥ pratyekamupadiṣṭa upakosalaḥ athāsmābhiruktaṃ jñeyameva, nopāsyam, tattu tavadācārya āgatya vakṣyatīti tairukto 'bhūt / evaṃ sthite 'thācāryaḥ satyakāma ājagāma / āgatya copakosaloktaṃ śrutvā pratyuvāca / kimiti? yadagnibhistubhyamupadiṣṭaṃ tattvayā jñeyameva na tūpāsyaṃ, tattvamahamupadekṣye ityevaṃ pratijñāyādarajananāya vakṣyamāṇamastaut 'yathā puṣkarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyanta evamevaṃvidi pāpaṃkarma na śliṣyata'; iti / evaṃ stutvopakosalāya vidyāmupādiśatsatyakāmaḥ / kimiti? 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate eṣa ātmeti hovāca / etadamṛtametadabhayametadbrahmeti'; / atha sambhūyopadeśānantaraṃ enamupakosalaṃ gārhapatyo 'nuśaśāsa / kimiti? pṛthivyagnyannākhyaṃ brahmeti / evaṃ vyāptavidyāmuktvāntaryāmividyāmāha - ya iti / asya so 'hamasmītyasya dvikartukatvādgārhapatyādyantaryāmī bhagavān svasyādityādyantaryāmiṇā gārhapatyādiḥ svāntaryāmiṇaḥ ādityādyantaryāmiṇā aikyamāhetyucyate / tathā ca - aheyatvāt pratyaktvāccāhaṃ madantaryāmī / āditye ca eṣa puruṣaḥ pūrṇaṣaḍguṇo bhagavān dṛśyate divyadṛṣṭyā so 'smītyarthaḥ / ādityasthasya viṣṇormadantaryāmiṇaśca viduradharmādivadabhedamātraṃ na ; kintu viśeṣābhāvaścetyāha - sa eveti / evamupāsakasya phalamāha - 'sa etadevaṃ vidvānupāste 'pahate pāpakṛtyāṃ lokī bhavati sarvamāyureti jyogjīvatīti'; / 'pāpakṛtyāṃ'; pāpakāryaṃ 'lokī'; bhagavallokī bhavati / 'sarvaṃ'; sampūrṇaṃ cāyuḥ prāpnoti / 'jyok'; sarvajñassan jīvatīti / evaṃ 'ya eṣa candramasi'; 'ya eṣa vidyuti'; ityanayoḥ artho 'vagantavyaḥ / 'tat'; tatrārthe vakṣyamāṇadṛṣṭānto yathā 'puṣkarapalāśe'; padmapatre āpo yathā 'na śliṣyante'; na sajjante 'tathevaṃvidi'; vakṣyamāṇākṣisthatvena brahmāparokṣajñānini jñānottaraṃ pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyate ityarthaḥ / ya eṣo 'kṣiṇyantaḥpuruṣo dṛśyate divyadṛṣṭyā eṣa ātmā vāmanākhya iti hovāca upakosalaṃ prati satyakāmaḥ / 'etadamṛtaṃ'; svato mṛtiśūnyaṃ nityamuktaṃ, 'etadabhayaṃ'; svato bhūyaśūnyaṃ 'etadbrahma'; guṇapūrṇamiti sidbhāntarītyā śrutyarthaḥ / pūrvapakṣī tvetatprakaraṇamagniparaṃ manyate /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.3:
Not only does the proof of <s>Agni</s>'s abiding in the eye lead to the attainment of <s>Ānandamayatva</s> for <s>Agni</s>, but also what was previously stated in 'netaraḥ' (not the other) and so forth — that liberation comes from knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — would also be contradicted. Therefore he says — 'ata' (therefore). // The phrase 'agnijñānāt' (from knowledge of fire) is connected also with 'mokṣaḥ' (liberation) through the phrase 'sarvapāpāśleṣāt' (because of non-clinging of all sins). And thus, since <s>Agni</s> abides in the eye, liberation too would follow from knowledge of that [<s>Agni</s>] alone, not from knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. How so? Because of the non-clinging of all sins from knowledge of <s>Agni</s> abiding in the eye. Nor is this unestablished, because in the <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) beginning with 'tadyathā' (just as), the non-clinging of all sins is stated as arising from knowledge of fire alone. Nor should it be said: how can liberation follow merely from the non-clinging of all sins arising from that knowledge? Because the construction is: since non-clinging of all sins is impossible without liberation following from that knowledge, by that very impossibility of any other explanation, liberation too is established. And thus, in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, [the claim is that] what is stated as the object of knowledge that causes liberation in 'tadyathā' — pertaining to the being in the eye — also accrues to <s>Agni</s> alone through his abiding in the eye; therefore what was stated in 'netaraḥ' (not the other) is unjustified — this is the purport. By this, the direct connection of this [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] is also shown. Now, in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, the narrative is as follows — (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.10.5) <s>Upakosala</s>, the son of <s>Kamālāyana</s> (hence called <s>Kāmalāyana</s> by name), dwelt in the service of his teacher named <s>Satyakāma</s> for the purpose of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship). He tended the fires of the teacher — <s>Gārhapatya</s> and others — for twelve years. <s>Satyakāma</s>, while having his other students recite their studies, did not teach this one alone. Even when repeatedly urged by his wife, he departed on a journey without imparting the knowledge. Thereupon <s>Upakosala</s>, afflicted by illness and anxious about obtaining knowledge, did not eat even when told to eat by his teacher's wife. When the <s>brahmacārin</s> thus remained silent without eating, then the three fires — <s>Gārhapatya</s> and others — overcome with compassion, resolved 'we shall teach this <s>brahmacārin</s> the knowledge,' and having gathered together, spoke the knowledge: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>,' and so forth. Thus, after the collective teaching, each fire individually instructed him — so the <s>Vedapuruṣa</s> (Vedic text) states: 'Then the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire taught him... ya eṣa āditye puruṣo dṛśyate so'hamasmi sa evāhamasmi' (the person seen in the sun — I am he, I am indeed he), and so forth. Thus, when <s>Upakosala</s> had been individually instructed by the three fires, they told him: 'What we have told you is to be known, not to be ritually meditated upon; your teacher, when he comes, will tell you that.' When things stood thus, the teacher <s>Satyakāma</s> arrived. Having arrived and heard what <s>Upakosala</s> said, he replied — what? 'What was taught to you by the fires is indeed to be known, not merely for ritual meditation; I shall teach you that.' Having thus promised, and in order to generate reverence, he praised the forthcoming [teaching]: 'Just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so sinful action does not cling to one who knows thus.' Having thus praised, <s>Satyakāma</s> taught the knowledge to <s>Upakosala</s> — what? 'The person seen within the eye — he is the <s>Ātman</s>,' thus <s>Satyakāma</s> said to <s>Upakosala</s>. 'This is the immortal, this is the fearless, this is <s>Brahman</s>.' Now, after the collective teaching, the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire taught <s>Upakosala</s> — what? That earth, fire, and food are <s>Brahman</s>. Having thus spoken the knowledge of all-pervasiveness, he states the knowledge of the inner controller — 'ya' (who). Since this [statement] 'so'hamasmi' (I am he) has two agents, the indwelling Lord of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and other [fires] declares the identity of Himself — the indwelling controller of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and others — with His own inner controller who is the inner controller of <s>Āditya</s> and others. And thus — because of being non-relinquishable and because of being the inner self — 'I [am] my inner controller.' And 'this person in the sun' — the Lord full of the six attributes — is 'seen' through divine vision — the meaning is 'I am he.' Between <s>Viṣṇu</s> abiding in the sun and my inner controller, there is not mere non-difference as between <s>Vidura</s> and <s>Dharma</s>; rather, there is absence of any distinction — thus he says 'sa eva' (he indeed). The fruit for such a worshipper is stated: 'One who knows thus and worships, removes sinful deeds, becomes a possessor of the world, lives the full span of life, lives long.' 'Pāpakṛtyām' means sinful deeds; 'lokī' means one who possesses the world of the Lord; 'sarvam' means one attains the complete lifespan; 'jyok' means one lives as an omniscient being. Similarly, the meaning of 'ya eṣa candramasi' (the one in the moon) and 'ya eṣa vidyuti' (the one in the lightning) should be understood. 'Tat' — in that context, the forthcoming illustration: just as water 'does not cling' to a 'lotus leaf,' so too, for one who has direct knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> as abiding in the eye in the manner to be described, sinful action does not cling after [the arising of] that knowledge — this is the meaning. 'The person seen within the eye' — through divine vision — 'he is the <s>Ātman</s> named <s>Vāmana</s>' — thus <s>Satyakāma</s> said to <s>Upakosala</s>. 'This is the immortal' — by nature free from death, eternally liberated; 'this is the fearless' — by nature free from fear; 'this is <s>Brahman</s>' — full of all attributes — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> according to the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion). The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector), however, considers this passage to refer to fire.

Therefore he states —
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
<s>Antara</s> (the inner one) [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of logical consistency. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.13 |
The one abiding within the eye is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.4:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // iti saṅgatisambhavāt śaṅkāsadbhāvācca / ataḥ tatparihārāya uttaramabravīt sūtrakāra ityarthaḥ / cakṣurantaḥstha ityanena antara ityaṃśo viṣṇurevetyanena anuvṛttastattvityaṃśaśca vyākhyātaḥ / yadyapi anuvyākhyāne śabdavaiyarthyaparihārāya antassthitvā ramaṇakṛditi vyākhyānāt atrāpi tadanusāreṇa ramaṇakṛcceti vaktavyam / tathāpyatra ramaṇakriyābodhakātmaśabdasya hetukaraṇānna tadarthasya pratijñāyāmanvayaḥ sambhavatīti antastha ityevoktam / tatratvātmaśabdārthasya hetutvāvivakṣāṇātsādhyānvayo na yujyata iti ramaṇakṛdityapyuktam / vastutastu - sūtre antarityanuktyā antara ityadhikokteḥ sārthakyāya atrāpi ramaṇakṛccetyapi upalakṣaṇayā vācyam / avayavārthavivakṣāvivakṣābhyām ātmaśabdasya sādhyasamarpakatāhetutvaṃ ca yujyate iti dhyeyam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.4:
Having introduced the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>sūtra</s>, he explains — 'ata' (therefore). // That is, because the connection [with the previous topic] is possible and the doubt exists, therefore the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>) stated the reply for resolving it — this is the meaning. By 'cakṣurantaḥstha' (abiding within the eye), the portion 'antara' (inner) [of the <s>sūtra</s>] is explained, and by 'viṣṇureva' (it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone), the portion 'tattva' (reality) carried over [from a previous <s>sūtra</s>] is explained. Although in the <s>Anuvyākhyāna</s>, to avoid superfluity of words, the explanation is 'having been situated within, one who delights (<s>ramaṇakṛt</s>),' here too, following that, one should say '<s>ramaṇakṛt</s>' (one who delights). Nevertheless, here, because the word '<s>ātman</s>' — which conveys the meaning of delighting — functions as a reason [in the argument], the meaning of that [delight] does not fit into the proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>); therefore it is stated only as 'antastha' (abiding within). There, because the meaning of the word '<s>ātman</s>' is not intended as the reason, its connection with the thesis to be proved is not appropriate — hence '<s>ramaṇakṛt</s>' (one who delights) is also stated [in the <s>Anuvyākhyāna</s>]. In truth, however — since the <s>sūtra</s> says 'antara' with an extra [syllable] rather than merely 'antar,' to justify this fuller form, here too '<s>ramaṇakṛt</s>' should be understood as implied through <s>upalakṣaṇa</s> (indication). That both the intention and non-intention of the component meaning of the word '<s>ātman</s>' are compatible — [the former] with its capacity to convey the thesis to be proved and [the latter] with its functioning as a reason — this should be contemplated.
Because immortality and other [attributes] are logically consistent with Him alone, as stated in 'Three-quarters of Him are immortal in heaven' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 10.90.3) and similar [passages].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.5:
upapatterityetadanekaliṅgaparatayā liṅgānāṃ niravakāśatvoktiparatayā ca vyāṣṭe - tripāditi // ityādinā vākyena uktasyeti śeṣaḥ / tasyeti vipariṇataṃ padamāvartate / amṛtatvādityetadihāpi ṣaṣṭhyantatayā buddhyā viviktaṃ sambadhyate / prathamenādipadena 'abhayaṃ? titīrṣatāṃ pāram'; (kaṭha.u.3-2.) 'amṛtaivaiṣā devatā'; () 'ātmājaro 'mṛto 'bhayo brahma'; (bṛ. 6-4-25.) ityādivākyaṃ dvitīyena abhayatvādikaṃ gṛhyate / tathā ca - tripādityādinā śrutyantaravākyena tasya viṣṇoreva uktasya 'etadamṛtam'; iti vākye 'ntaḥsthaniṣṭhatvenoktasyāmṛtatvādyupapatterliṅgasya tasmin viṣṇāveva upapatteryuktatvādanyatrāyuktatvāditi yojanā / anena liṅgasya niravakāśatvānekatvābhyāṃ prābālyamuktaṃ bhavati / 'amṛtaṃ'; mṛtiharitaṃ 'yadabhayaṃ'; bhayarahitaṃ yacca 'titīrṣatāṃ'; saṃsārataraṇecchūnāṃ 'pāraṃ'; saṃsārasya pārasthaṃ taduttarāvadhibhūte śvetadvīpādau sthitaṃ muktaprāpyaṃ paraṃ brahma tat dhyātuṃ sādhanaṃ vaktuṃ vayaṃ 'śakemahi'; śaktāḥ sma iti kaṭhaśrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.5:
He explains the word '<s>upapatti</s>' (justification) with the intention of [showing it refers to] multiple marks and to the statement of their having no scope elsewhere: '<s>tripād</s>' (three-footed). // 'Of what was stated' — by a passage such as [this] — is the remainder. The word 'tasya' (of that) recurs in modified form. '<s>Amṛtatva</s>' (immortality) and the rest — here too this is intellectually separated and connected in the genitive case. By the first word 'ādi' (and the like), the passages 'The immortal, the fearless, the far shore for those wishing to cross' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 3.2), '<s>Amṛtā</s> (immortal) indeed is this deity,' 'The Self — unaging, immortal, fearless — is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.25) and the like are included; by the second [word 'ādi'], fearlessness and the like are included. And thus the syntactic connection is: by a passage from another <s>Śruti</s> such as '<s>tripād</s>' (three-footed) and the like, of that <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone who was [previously] stated, in the passage '<s>etad amṛtam</s>' (this is the immortal), [the marks of] immortality and the like stated as belonging to one established within the eye — because of the justification of the mark — that is, because the mark is justified as applying to that <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone and is not justified elsewhere — this is the construction. By this, the superiority of the mark is stated through both its having no scope elsewhere and its multiplicity. '<s>Amṛtam</s>' (immortal) — one from whom death has been removed. '<s>Yad abhayam</s>' — that which is free from fear. 'Of those wishing to cross' (<s>titīrṣatām</s>) — of those desiring to cross <s>saṃsāra</s> — 'the far shore' (<s>pāram</s>) — situated on the other side of <s>saṃsāra</s>, established in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> and the like which form the further boundary beyond that — the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> to be attained by the liberated — to meditate on that — 'we are capable' (<s>śakemahi</s>) — we are able to speak of the means: this is the meaning of the <s>Kaṭha Śruti</s>.
And because of the justification of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.6:
yadaivaṃ niravakāśatvānekatvābhyāṃ balavalliṅgabalāccakṣurantaḥsthasya viṣṇutvaniścayaḥ, kimu tadobhayathā svabhāvaniravakāśatvābhyām anekatvācca balavacchrutito 'pīti bhāvena sautramupapatterityaṃśaṃ brahmādiśrutirūpahetvantaraparatayā tasya prābālyopayoginiravakāśatvopapādanaparatayā ca prakārāntareṇa vyācaṣṭe - brahmeti / ādipadenātmaśabdo gṛhyate / brahmātmādīti pāṭhe ādiśabdena puruṣaśabdo grāhyaḥ / atra śrutetyādau saṃyojyam / tasyaivetyanuṣajyate / tathā ca - atrāntasthaprakaraṇe śrutabrahmaśabdādestasya viṣṇorevopapatteranyasyānupapatterityarthaḥ / guṇapūrtivācibrahmaśabdasya viṣṇāveva mukhyatvādātmaśabdasyāpi ādeyamupādeyaṃ sukhaṃ mātyanubhavatīti vyutpattyā tatraiva mukhyatvāditi bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.6:
When through both having no scope elsewhere and multiplicity, the determination that the entity within the eye is <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established from the powerful mark — what more need be said [when it is established] from the <s>Śruti</s> too, which is powerful in both ways — through inherent [no-scope-elsewhere] and through multiplicity? With this purport, he explains the <s>sūtra</s>-portion '<s>upapatteḥ</s>' (because of justification) in another way, as having the intention of [referring to] another reason in the form of <s>Śruti</s> of the words '<s>Brahman</s>' and the like, and to the establishment of its superiority through no-scope-elsewhere: '<s>brahma</s>' (<s>Brahman</s>). // By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self) is included. In the reading '<s>brahmātmādi</s>,' the word '<s>Puruṣa</s>' (Person) should be included by the word 'ādi.' 'Here in the <s>Śruti</s>' and so forth should be connected. 'Of that alone [<s>Viṣṇu</s>]' is carried forward. And thus the meaning is: here, in the context pertaining to the entity within [the eye], the <s>Śruti</s> of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' and the like — because of its justification in that <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, and non-justification in another. The import is: since the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' which denotes fullness of qualities, has its primary meaning in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, and since the word '<s>Ātman</s>' too — by the etymology 'one who takes, accepts, and experiences the bliss that is to be received' — has its primary meaning in that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] alone.

children.text: anena 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi'; iti śrutyukto 'ntaraḥ tattu tattajjīvaprerakatvena tattaccakṣurantassthito viṣṇureva, na tvagniḥ / kutaḥ? upapatteḥ / atra 'etadamṛtamabhayametadbrahmaiṣa ātmā'; ityamṛtatvābhayatvādiliṅgaśravaṇādbrahmādiśabdaśruteśca teṣāṃ viṣṇāvevopapatteḥ, anyatrānupapatteriti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: By this, the entity stated in the <s>Śruti</s> 'he who is within the eye' — the one within — who is the impeller of each <s>jīva</s> and is therefore situated within each eye — is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not <s>Agni</s> (fire). Whence? Because of justification (<s>upapatti</s>). Here, because of hearing the marks of immortality, fearlessness, and the like in 'this is the immortal, the fearless — this is <s>Brahman</s>; this is the Self' — and because of the <s>Śruti</s> of the words '<s>Brahman</s>' and the like — because of their justification in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone and non-justification elsewhere: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated.
'I am He' (<s>so 'ham asmi</s>) — such [expressions], however, are with reference to the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.7:
nanu niravakāśaśrutiliṅgabalādyadi viṣṇureva akṣisthastadādityastho 'pi sa eva syāt / tarhi 'so 'hamasmi sa evāhamasmi'; ityahamādiśruteḥ kā gatirityata āha - so 'hamasmītyādīti / ādipadena gārhapatyādiśabdānāṃ grahaṇam/ tathā ca ityādivākyasthamahamādipadajātamityarthaḥ / apekṣayetyanantaraṃ pravṛttamiti śeṣaḥ/
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.7:
Now, if through the force of the no-scope-elsewhere <s>Śruti</s> and mark, the entity within the eye is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, then the one within the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) would also be the same. In that case, what is the purport of the <s>Śruti</s> [using] 'I' and the like: 'I am He; He indeed am I'? — to this he says: '<s>so 'ham asmi</s> and the like.' By the word 'ādi' (and the like), the words '<s>gārhapatya</s>' (the household fire) and the like are included. And thus, the words 'I' and the like occurring in such passages: this is the meaning. After 'with reference to' (<s>apekṣayā</s>), the remainder is: '[these expressions] have proceeded [with that reference].'

children.text:
antaryāmiṇamīśeśamapekṣyāhaṃ tvamityapi /
sarve śabdāḥ prayujyante sati bhede 'pi vastuṣu /
iti mahākaurme //
children.translated_text:
With reference to the inner controller, the lord of lords — 'I' and 'you' and
all words are used, even when there is difference in the entities.
— Thus in the <s>Mahākūrma Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.8:
antaryāmiṇi ahamādiśabdapravṛttiṃ smārayati - antaryāmiṇamiti // ādyo 'pi samuccaye / dvitīyo yadyapi tathāpītyarther / iśānāṃ brahmādīnārṃ iśamityantaryāmitvopapādakam / tathā ca - 'vastuṣu'; agnyādijīveṣur iśādbhede satyapi tadabhedabodhako 'hamitiśabdaḥ tvamitiśabdaḥ/ kiṃ bahunābhedasādhakāḥ sarve tattacchabdāḥ prayujyante / katham? yato 'ntaryāmiṇamapekṣyaivaite śabdāḥ prayujyante naitāvatā agnyādijīvānārṃ iśābhedaḥ śaṅkyaḥ / yataḥ so 'ntaryāmīr iśeśo brahmādyuttama ityarthaḥ / mahākaurme ityasya uktatvādityadhyāhāreṇa so 'hamiti pūrvavākyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.8:
He reminds of the <s>Smṛti</s> [support] for the usage of the words 'I' and the like with reference to the inner controller: '<s>antaryāmiṇam</s>' (the inner controller). // The first 'api' (also) is for aggregation. The second 'api' is in the sense of 'even so' (<s>yadyapi tathāpi</s>). '<s>Īśeśam</s>' — the lord of lords, i.e., [the lord] of <s>Brahmā</s> and the others — this establishes the justification of being the inner controller. And thus: even when there is difference in the 'entities' — the <s>jīvas</s> such as <s>Agni</s> and the like — from the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), the word 'I' and the word 'you,' which produce the cognition of non-difference — in short, 'all words' that are the means of establishing non-difference — 'are used.' How? Because 'with reference to the inner controller alone' these words are used — hence the difference of <s>Agni</s> and other <s>jīvas</s> from the Lord should not be doubted. Because that inner controller is '<s>Īśeśa</s>' — the one superior to <s>Brahmā</s> and the others: this is the meaning. After 'in the <s>Mahākūrma</s>,' the syntactic connection with the previous sentence is: 'because of being stated,' and [it connects with] '<s>so 'ham</s>' (I am He).
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
And because of the designation of the abode and the like. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.14 |

children.text: 'tadyadasmin sarpirvodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmanī eva gacchati'; (chāṃ. 4-15.) ityādisthānaśaktiḥ / vāmanirbhāmanirityādyātmaśaktiścocyate / tasya hyetalliṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'When one pours clarified butter or water into this [eye], it goes to the channels alone' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15) — such is the power of the abode. And the power of the Self is stated by [the words] '<s>Vāmana</s>,' '<s>Bhāmana</s>,' and the like. For this is His mark.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.9:
yuktyantareṇa viṣṇoścakṣurantaḥsthatvaṃ sādhayatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - sthānādīti / sarpirityataḥ pūrvaṃ 'tadyadasmin'; iti śrutivākyapāṭhaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - 'yadidaṃ cakṣuṣi'; iti pāṭhabhedena pūrvavākyamudāhṛtam / ityādīti luptavibhaktikam / ityādāvityarthaḥ / evamuttaratrāpi / ādipadena 'vartmanī eva gacchati'; ityādergrahaṇam/ sthānaśaktiriti / brahmasthānabhūtayorakṣṇorakṣisthaparamapuruṣasambandhādasaṅgatvākhyaśaktirityarthaḥ ucyata ityatrāpi sambadhyate / anena sautraṃ sthānapadaṃ paramātmasthānaśaktayupalakṣakatayā vyākhyātam / ucyate ityanena asiddhiparihārakavyapadeśaśabdārtho darśitaḥ / ādipadena 'etaṃ saṃyadvāma ityācakṣate / etaṃ hi sarvāṇi vāmānyabhisaṃyanti .... eṣa u eva vāmanireṣa hi sarvāṇi vāmāni nayati / eṣa u eva bhāmanireṣa hi sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti'; iti samagravākyaṃ gṛhyate / ātmaśaktiriti / saṃyadvāmatvarūpātmasāmarthamityarthaḥ / anena sautrādiśabdo hyadhiṣṭhātṛparamātmaparassan tacchaktyupalakṣaka iti vyākhyāto bhavati / co hetusamuccaye śaktisamuccaye cādyo bhinnakramaḥ / ucyate yata iti śeṣaḥ / asyāto 'pi cakṣurantaḥstho viṣṇureva iti pūrvapratijñāvākyenānvayaḥ / yasmādasaṅgo 'yaṃ puruṣo 'kṣiṇi vidyate niyāmakatayā tattasmādyadi 'asmin'; cakṣuṣi 'sarpiḥ'; ghṛtamudakaṃ vā 'siñcati'; siñcetkaścidapi tarhi tadvartmanī ubhayamārgau pratyeva gacchati na cakṣuḥ spṛśatītyarthaḥ / evaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ vāmanākhyaṃ viṣṇuṃ saṃyadvāma ityācakṣate vidvāṃśaḥ / kutaḥ? hi yasmāt etaṃ 'sarvāṇi vāmāni'; strīrūpāṇi abhisaṃyanti prāpnuvanti / anena saṃyanti vāmāni enamiti vigraho darśitaḥ / 'eṣa u'; cakṣurgata eva mukhyato vāmanirityucyate / kutaḥ hi yasmādeṣaḥ 'sarvāṇi vāmāni'; sundararamādistrīrūpāṇi 'nayati'; prerayati / eṣa u eva cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣo 'bhāmaniḥ'; mukhyataḥ tacchabdavācyaḥ / kutaḥ? hi yasmādeva 'sarveṣu lokeṣu'; puruṣeṣu bhāti tadīyatejaḥprakāśakatayā tatra dīpyate ityarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ tattvapradīpe - vāmaṃ saundaryaṃ bhāmaṃ tejaḥ tatpradhānatvāt strīpuruṣā vāmabhāmaśabditāstannetā vāmanirbhāmaniśceti / etalliṅgadvayasadbhāve 'pi kuto 'kṣisthasya viṣṇutvaniścaya ityata āha - tasyeti / 'hi'; yasmāt 'tasya'; viṣṇoḥ 'etat'; svasambandhena akṣṇorasaṅgatvāpādakatvaṃ sarvasaundaryādhiṣṭhānastrīrūpanetṛtvaṃ ca 'liṅgaṃ'; asādhāraṇo dharmaḥ tasmānnāprayojakatvamiti tena viṣṇutvaniścayopapattiriti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.9:
Having presented the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being within the eye through another reasoning, he explains it: '<s>sthānādi</s>' (the abode and the like). // Before '<s>sarpis</s>' (clarified butter), '<s>tadyad asmin</s>' (when one [pours] into this) is the reading of the <s>Śruti</s> passage. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, the preceding passage is cited with the variant reading '<s>yad idaṃ cakṣuṣi</s>' (what is in this eye). '<s>Ityādi</s>' is [used] with dropped case-ending. The meaning is 'in [expressions beginning with] such and the like.' Similarly hereafter too. By the word 'ādi,' the passage 'it goes to the channels alone' and what follows is included. 'Power of the abode' (<s>sthānaśakti</s>) — means the power called non-attachment (<s>asaṅgatva</s>) of the two eyes, which are the abode of <s>Brahman</s>, due to the connection of the Supreme Person situated in the eye [with them]: this is the meaning. '[It] is stated' is also to be connected here. By this, the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>sthāna</s>' (abode) is explained as representative of the power of the Supreme Self's abode. By the word '[it] is stated' (<s>ucyate</s>), the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>vyapadeśa</s>' (designation) as a statement that resolves non-establishment is indicated. By the word 'ādi,' the entire passage is included: 'They call Him <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>; for all beautiful things (<s>vāma</s>) come together to Him... He indeed is <s>Vāmani</s>; for He leads all beautiful things. He indeed is <s>Bhāmani</s>; for He shines in all worlds.' 'Power of the Self' (<s>ātmaśakti</s>) — means the capacity of the Self in the form of the nature of <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>: this is the meaning. By this, the <s>sūtra</s>-word 'ādi' is explained as referring to the <s>Paramātman</s>, the presiding deity, and as representative of His power. The word 'ca' (and) is for the accumulation of both reasons and powers; the first [ca] is in a different order. 'Since [it] is stated' (<s>ucyate yataḥ</s>) is the remainder. The syntactic connection is with the prior thesis-statement: from this too, the entity within the eye is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Since this Person who is unattached exists in the eye in a governing capacity, therefore if someone 'pours' (<s>siñcati</s>) — were to pour — 'into this' (<s>asmin</s>) eye 'clarified butter' (<s>sarpis</s>) — ghee or water — then it 'goes to the channels alone' (<s>vartmanī eva gacchati</s>) — to both channels — it does not touch the eye: this is the meaning. Thus, the one within the eye, called <s>Vāmana</s> and bearing the name <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the wise call Him '<s>Saṃyadvāma</s>.' Why? Because (<s>hi</s>) — since — 'all beautiful things' (<s>sarvāṇi vāmāni</s>) — [all beings] in the form of beautiful women — come together to (<s>abhisaṃyanti</s>) — reach — this one. By this, the analysis 'the beautiful things come together to him' is shown. 'He indeed' — the one within the eye — is called '<s>Vāmani</s>' in the primary sense. Why? Because (<s>hi</s>) — since — this one 'leads' (<s>nayati</s>) — impels — 'all beautiful things' — [all beings] in the form of beautiful women including <s>Ramā</s> and the like. And this person within the eye is '<s>Bhāmani</s>' — primarily denotable by that word. Why? Because (<s>hi</s>) — since — indeed 'in all worlds' — in all persons — 'He shines' (<s>bhāti</s>) — He illumines through the radiance of His effulgence: this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: '<s>Vāma</s>' is beauty; '<s>bhāma</s>' is radiance; because of having these as predominant, women and men are called by the words '<s>vāma</s>' and '<s>bhāma</s>'; He who leads them is <s>Vāmani</s> and <s>Bhāmani</s>. Even though there exist these two marks, how is the determination of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood for the entity within the eye [achieved]? — to this he says: 'tasya' (of that). 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since — 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>) — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'this' (<s>etat</s>) — the ability to confer non-attachment upon the eyes through His own connection, and the leadership of women who are the abodes of all beauty — is 'the mark' (<s>liṅgam</s>) — the exclusive attribute. Therefore there is no non-productivity [of the argument] — hence the justification of the determination of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood: this is the sentence-remainder.

children.text:
'sar iśaḥ so 'sapatnaḥ sa hariḥ saḥ paraḥ sa parovarīyān
yadidaṃ cakṣuṣi sarpirvodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmanī eva gacchati sa vāmanaḥ sa bhāmanaḥ na ānandaḥ so 'cyutaḥ'; iti caturvedaśikhāyām //

BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.10:
kuta etasya talliṅgamiti jñāyate ityata āha - sa iti // liṅgasya viṣṇuniṣṭhatājñāpanāya 'sa hariḥ'; ityādeḥ 'so 'cyutaḥ'; ityaṃśasya coktiḥ / idaṃcakṣuṣīti samastaṃ padam / anyathā sarpirādiviśeṣaṇatvaṃ pratīyate, tataśca pratyakṣasiddhagokaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ na jñāyeta / asmin cakṣuṣītyetatprakaraṇagataśrutivisaṃvādaśca syāt / cettarhyeradhyāhāraḥ / tathā ca - yadyasmātsannihitādhiṣṭhātuḥ yasya sāmarthyāditi yāvat / 'idaṃcakṣuṣi'; asmiṃścakṣuṣi sarpirudakaṃ vā siñcati cetkaścit tarhi tadvartmanī pratyeva gacchati sar iśaḥ 'so 'sapatnaḥ'; śatrurahitaḥ / 'saparaḥ'; lokavilakṣaṇaḥ / parovarīyān / idamekaṃ padam / rudrādeḥ parato vāṇyāḥ parāccaturmukhātparataḥ śrītattvādva uttamaḥ / sa eva vāmanabhāmanānandācyutaśabdavācya ityarthaḥ / vidheyānekatvātsa ityasakṛdāvṛttiḥ / parovarīyānityatrāpi tacchabdo 'nuṣañjanīyaḥ / ekadeśavikṛtasyānanyatvādvāmanibhāmaniśabdārtha eva vāmanabhāmanaśabdayorarthaḥ / caturvedaśikhāyāmityanantaraṃ uktatvāditi śeṣaḥ / asya tasyaitalliṅgamiti jñāyate iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.10:
Whence is it known that this is His mark? — to this he says: '<s>sa</s>' (He). // The citation of '<s>sa Hariḥ</s>' (He is <s>Hari</s>) and the like, up to '<s>so 'cyutaḥ</s>' (He is <s>Acyuta</s>), is for the purpose of making known that the mark belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. '<s>Idaṃcakṣuṣi</s>' (in this eye) is a single compound word. Otherwise, [if taken separately,] a qualifier-relationship with clarified butter and the like would be understood, and then the qualifier-relationship with a cow known through direct perception would not be known. And there would be discordance with the <s>Śruti</s> of the context, [which reads] 'in this eye' (<s>asmin cakṣuṣi</s>). If so, the word 'in' (<s>ere</s>) is to be supplied. And thus: since — because of the capacity of the proximate presiding deity — to the extent of [saying] 'because of His power' — 'in this eye' — when someone pours clarified butter or water 'into this eye,' then it 'goes to the channels alone.' 'He is without rival' (<s>asapatnaḥ</s>) — devoid of enemies. 'He is supreme' (<s>paraḥ</s>) — distinct from the world. '<s>Parovarīyān</s>' — this is a single word. Superior to <s>Rudra</s>, superior to <s>Vāṇī</s> (speech, i.e., <s>Sarasvatī</s>), superior to the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>], or superior to the <s>Śrī</s>-<s>tattva</s> — the highest. He alone is denotable by the words <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Bhāmana</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, and <s>Acyuta</s>: this is the meaning. Because of the multiplicity of predicates, the word 'sa' (He) recurs repeatedly. The word 'tat' (that) should also be carried forward in '<s>parovarīyān</s>.' Since what is modified in one part is not different [from the whole], the meaning of the words '<s>Vāmana</s>' and '<s>Bhāmana</s>' is the same as that of '<s>Vāmani</s>' and '<s>Bhāmani</s>.' After 'in the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s>,' the remainder is: 'because of being stated.' The syntactic connection is with the previous [statement]: 'of that one, this is the mark — thus it is known.'
Because of being the abode of which, this eye is unattached to all objects —

children.text: sa vāmanaḥ paro 'smākaṃ gatirityeva cintayet // iti vāmane // 14 //
children.translated_text: He, <s>Vāmana</s>, is our supreme goal — thus one should contemplate. — Thus in the <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>. // 14 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.11:
liṅgasvarūpasya tasya viṣṇurūpavyaktiviśeṣaniṣṭhatāyāśca śrutāvasphuṭatvāttadarthamatrārthe smṛtiṃ cāha - yaditi // yasya sthānatvādityarthaḥ / asya yacchabdasya sa iti tacchabdenānvayaḥ / 'sarvavastubhiḥ'; sarpirādibhiḥ/ 'vāmanaḥ'; sundarastrīneteti vāmanākhyo viṣṇureva 'asmākaṃ'; bhaktānāṃ 'paraḥ'; parā 'gatiḥ'; prāpya iti cintayedityarthaḥ/ yadvā - vāmana ityanena prāptālpatvaśaṅkāvāraṇāya 'paraḥ'; pūrṇa ityuktam / vāmana iti / vāmanākhyapurāṇa ityarthaḥ / asya caturvedaśikhāyāmitivadanvayaḥ / spaṣṭaḥ sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.11:
Since the nature of the mark and its belonging to a particular manifestation of the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-form is unclear in the <s>Śruti</s>, for that purpose he also cites a <s>Smṛti</s> bearing on this point: '<s>yat</s>' (because of which). // The meaning is: 'because of being the abode of whom' (<s>yasya sthānatvāt</s>). The syntactic connection of the relative pronoun 'yat' (which) is with the correlative 'sa' (He). 'By all objects' (<s>sarvavastubhiḥ</s>) — by clarified butter and the like. '<s>Vāmana</s>' — the one called <s>Vāmana</s>, who is the leader of beautiful women — that <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — is 'our' — of the devotees — 'the supreme' (<s>paraḥ</s>) — the transcendent — 'goal' (<s>gatiḥ</s>) — the one to be attained — thus one should 'contemplate' (<s>cintayet</s>): this is the meaning. Alternatively: by [the word] '<s>Vāmana</s>,' for the purpose of warding off the suspicion of smallness that might arise from the attainment [of a small form], 'supreme' (<s>paraḥ</s>) — complete: thus it is said. 'In the <s>Vāmana</s>' — means in the <s>Purāṇa</s> called <s>Vāmana</s>: this is the meaning. Its syntactic connection is like that of 'in the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s>.' The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is clear.
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
And precisely because of the designation qualified by bliss. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.15 |
'<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Ka</s> (bliss) is <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Kha</s> (space) is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.10) —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.12:
prakaraṇabalāccakṣurantaḥsthatvaṃ viṣṇoḥ pratipādayatsūtramupanyasya tadupāttaśrutimevodāharati - sukheti // 'khaṃ brahmeti'; ityantasya sūtreṇānvayaḥ upakrame prāṇasya śrutatve 'pi naitatprakaraṇasya tatparatvam, pūrvasūtroktaviṣṇuśrutiliṅgādibādhakasadbhāvāditi pratipādayitum uttaratra śrautakarmaśabdena prāṇabrahmaṇostantreṇopādānātsūcanārthaṃ ca 'prāṇo brahma'; ityaṃśodāharaṇam / sūtre caśabdaḥ pūrvoktahetoriha prakaraṇabalāccetyadhyāhṛtahetośca samuccaye / sūtrodāhṛtahetostvadhyāhṛtasādhyenānvayaḥ / viśiṣṭaṃ ca tatsukhaṃ ca sukhaviśiṣṭam / viśeṣaṇasya paranipātaḥ / sukhena viśiṣṭa iti vā, sukheṣu viśiṣṭa iti vā, vigrahaḥ / tatra dvitīye śraiṣṭhyarūpaṃ vaiśiṣṭyamarthātsukhe 'pyanveti / atra prakaraṇe hi mukhyaprāṇobrahmākhilajīvebhyaḥ pūrṇaḥ iti mukhyaprāṇasya pūrṇatvamuktvā 'kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma'; ityanena 'kaṃ'; sukhaṃ 'brahma'; pūrṇaṃ 'khaṃ'; jñānaṃ pūrṇamiti sukhasaṃvidorapi pūrṇatvamucyate / tathā ca na kevalamuktahetubalāccakṣurantaḥstho viṣṇuḥ, kintu - prakaraṇabalācca / na ca prakaraṇasya vaiṣṇavatvāsiddhiḥ / asyopakrame 'sukhaviśiṣṭābhidhānāt'; pūrṇasukhokteriti sūtrārthaḥ / yadaivamupakrame kaṃ brahma iti pūrṇasukhābhidhānādevāsya prakaraṇasya vaiṣṇavatvaṃ siddhyati kimuta tadā 'khaṃ brahma'; iti pūrṇajñānādapīti kaimutyanyāyasūcanāya sūtre evakāraḥ / yadyapi chāndogyabhāṣye 'prāṇo brahma'; balarūpaṃ brahma / 'kaṃ'; pūrṇānandarūpaṃ brahma / 'khaṃ'; pūrṇajñānarūpaṃ 'brahma'; paraṃ brahmeti vyākhyātam / tathāpi tadbrahmaśabdasya parāparayo rūḍhyā vṛttyā vyākhyānāntaramityadoṣaḥ/
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.12:
Having introduced the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being within the eye by the force of context, he cites the very <s>śruti</s> passage employed therein — with 'sukha' etc. // The connection with the <s>sūtra</s> extends up to '<s>khaṃ</s> <s>brahmeti</s>.' Even though <s>prāṇa</s> is mentioned at the beginning, the passage is not about <s>prāṇa</s>, because there exist overriding factors such as the <s>śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, etc. referring to <s>Viṣṇu</s> as stated in the previous <s>sūtra</s>. To establish this, and to indicate the joint adoption of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>Brahman</s> through the <s>Śrauta</s> ritual term later on, the portion '<s>prāṇo brahma</s>' is cited as an example. The word 'ca' in the <s>sūtra</s> combines the previously stated reason with the reason to be supplied here, namely 'by the force of context.' The reason cited in the <s>sūtra</s>, however, is connected with the proposition to be supplied. '<s>Sukhaviśiṣṭam</s>' means 'distinguished by bliss' — the qualifier is placed last. The analysis is either 'distinguished by bliss' or 'distinguished among blisses.' In the second case, the distinction in the form of supremacy implicitly applies to bliss as well.
