For in this context, having stated the fullness of <s>Mukhyaprāṇa</s> — that '<s>Mukhyaprāṇa</s> who is <s>Brahman</s> is fuller than all <s>jīvas</s>' — through '<s>kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma</s>,' it is said that '<s>kam</s>' means bliss, '<s>brahma</s>' means full, '<s>kham</s>' means knowledge is full — thus the fullness of both bliss and consciousness is declared. Accordingly, <s>Viṣṇu</s> who dwells within the eye is [established] not merely by the force of the previously stated reason, but also by the force of context. Nor is the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> character of the context unestablished. At its beginning, 'because of the designation as distinguished by bliss' — the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is 'because of the mention of perfect bliss.' When even by the mention of perfect bliss through '<s>kaṃ brahma</s>' at the beginning the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> nature of this context is established, how much more so through '<s>khaṃ brahma</s>' indicating perfect knowledge — to suggest this <s>kaimutya-nyāya</s> (argument a fortiori), the word 'eva' is used in the <s>sūtra</s>. Although in the <s>Chāndogya</s> commentary it was explained that '<s>prāṇo brahma</s>' means <s>Brahman</s> in the form of strength, '<s>kam</s>' means <s>Brahman</s> in the form of perfect bliss, '<s>kham</s>' means <s>Brahman</s> in the form of perfect knowledge — the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — nevertheless, this is merely an alternative explanation of the word '<s>brahma</s>' through conventional and derivative usage for the higher and lower [<s>Brahman</s>], so there is no fault.

children.text:
'vijñānamānandaṃ brahma'; (bṛ. 5-9-28.) 'ānando brahmeti
vyajānāt'; (tai. 3-6.) ityādestasyaiva hi tallakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vijñānam</s> (knowledge) <s>ānandaṃ</s> (bliss) <s>brahma</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.9.28), '<s>Ānando brahmeti vyajānāt</s>' (He understood that bliss is <s>Brahman</s>) (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.6) — from such passages, these are indeed the defining marks of that very [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.13:
nanu upakrame pūrṇasukhasaṃvidorabhidhāne 'pi kuto 'sya prakaraṇasya vaiṣṇavatvamityāśaṅkya tayosatallakṣaṇatvāt tadrūpatvāt upakrame tadabhidhāne brahmaivopakrāntaṃ syāditi bhāvena pūrṇasukhajñānayorbrahmalakṣaṇatvaṃ śrutyā darśayati - vijñānamiti // vijñānādirūpaṃ brahmetyarthaḥ / atra vijñānādipadaṃ pūrṇajñānādivāci, saṅkoce kāraṇābhāvāditi prakṛtasaṅgatiḥ / idaṃ vājasaneye śrutam / 'ānando brahma'; iti / taittirīyavākyāditi śeṣaḥ / ādiśabdena 'athaiṣa eva parama ānandaḥ'; 'satyaṃ jñānam'; ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / tathā ca ityādervākyāt 'tasya'; brahmaṇaḥ 'tat'; pūrṇānandādikaṃ 'lakṣaṇaṃ'; svalakṣaṇaṃ jñāyata ityarthaḥ / tathā ca - śrutyantare brahmalakṣaṇatvenāvagatayoḥ pūrṇajñānasukhayoratra prakaraṇe 'bhidhānāt asya vaiṣṇavatvasiddhiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.13:
Objection: Even if perfect bliss and knowledge are mentioned at the beginning, how can this context be about <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Anticipating this doubt, and [responding] that because these are the defining marks of that [<s>Brahman</s>] — because they have that nature — when they are mentioned at the beginning, <s>Brahman</s> itself is what is introduced, he shows through <s>śruti</s> that perfect bliss and knowledge are the defining marks of <s>Brahman</s> — with '<s>vijñānam</s>' etc. // The meaning is: <s>Brahman</s> has the nature of <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge) and the rest. Here the words '<s>vijñāna</s>' etc. denote perfect knowledge and so forth, since there is no reason for restriction — this is the connection with the topic at hand. This is heard in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [recension]. '<s>Ānando brahma</s>' — the rest is to be supplied: 'from the <s>Taittirīya</s> statement.' By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), passages such as '<s>athaiṣa eva parama ānandaḥ</s>' (this alone is the supreme bliss) and '<s>satyaṃ jñānam</s>' (truth, knowledge) are included. Accordingly, from such statements, 'of that' — of <s>Brahman</s> — 'that' — perfect bliss and the rest — is the 'defining mark,' i.e., its essential characteristic — this is the meaning. Thus, since perfect knowledge and bliss, which are understood in other <s>śruti</s> passages as the defining marks of <s>Brahman</s>, are mentioned in this context, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> nature [of the passage] is established — this is the purport.

children.text:
lakṣaṇaṃ paramānando viṣṇoreva na saṃśayaḥ /
avyaktāditṛṇāntāstu vipruḍānandabhāginaḥ // iti brahmavaivarte /
children.translated_text:
The defining mark is supreme bliss, which belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — there is no doubt.
From <s>Avyaktā</s> (<s>Śrī</s>) down to the lowliest blade of grass, [all beings] partake of but a drop of [His] bliss. // Thus in the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.14:
nanu sakalacetanānāmapi pūrṇānandatvātkathametadviṣṇulakṣaṇamityata āha - lakṣaṇamiti // svarūpadharmobhayārthako 'yam / 'paramānandaḥ'; niravadhikapūrṇānanda eva lakṣaṇam / iha lakṣaṇatvenābhipretaḥ na pūrṇānandamātram / sa ca viṣṇoreva nānyeṣām / anyeṣāṃ tvāpekṣikameva pūrṇaṃ sukhaṃ na viṣṇuvanniravadhikaṃ pūrṇamityarthaḥ / kuta ityata āha - yataḥ avyaktādīti / avyaktā śrīḥ saivādiryeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ / tṛṇajīvā manuṣyottamā evānte viśeṣārthaḥ / 'vipruḍānandabhāginaḥ'; tāratamyena brahmānandapratibimbatvāpekṣikānandayuktā ityarthaḥ / cetanā iti śeṣaḥ / 'na saṃśayaḥ'; ityasyārthasya sāvadhāraṇatvamāha / brahmavaivarta ityasyoktatvādityadhyāhāreṇa 'tasyaiva tallakṣaṇam'; iti sāvadhāraṇapūrvavākyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.14:
Objection: Since all sentient beings also possess perfect bliss, how can this be the defining mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he responds — with '<s>lakṣaṇam</s>' etc. // This [term] has both meanings: essential nature and distinguishing attribute. '<s>Paramānandaḥ</s>' — supreme, unsurpassable, perfect bliss alone is the defining mark intended here as the characteristic — not mere perfect bliss. And that belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not to others. For others, perfect bliss is only relative, not unsurpassably perfect as <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s is — this is the meaning. How so? To this he says — 'because <s>avyaktādi</s>' etc. '<s>Avyaktā</s>' is <s>Śrī</s>, and she is the foremost among them — they are so called. '<s>Tṛṇa</s>-<s>jīvas</s>' — the specific meaning is up to the best among humans at the end. '<s>Vipruḍānandabhāginaḥ</s>' — sentient beings possessing relative bliss through a graduated hierarchy as reflections of <s>Brahman</s>'s bliss — this is the meaning. The word '<s>cetanāḥ</s>' (sentient beings) is to be supplied. The meaning of '<s>na saṃśayaḥ</s>' (there is no doubt) is stated as emphatic certainty. The connection of '<s>Brahmavaivarte</s>' with the preceding sentence '<s>tasyaiva tallakṣaṇam</s>' (these are the defining marks of that very one) is through supplying 'because it is so stated' — with the emphatic certainty of the earlier statement.
And when the primary [meaning] is possible, the secondary is not appropriate. // 15 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.15:
nanvagyādisukhasyāpekṣikatayāpi pūrṇatvasadbhāvātteṣāṃ pūrṇasukhamidaṃ kiṃ na syāt / tathā teṣāṃ tallakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ na syāt / tathā teṣāmevedaṃ prakaraṇaṃ kiṃ na syāt ityata āha - na ceti // 'mukhye'; niravadhikapūrṇatve 'kaṃ brahma'; iti śrutyarthatayā tallakṣaṇe sambhavati sati 'amukhyam'; āpekṣikamanyādhīnaṃ pūrṇatvaṃ na yujyate ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.15:
Objection: Since fullness exists even in the relative bliss of fire and the rest, why should this not be their perfect bliss? Similarly, why should this not be their defining mark? And why should this context not be about them? To this he responds — with '<s>na ca</s>' etc. // When '<s>mukhye</s>' — when unsurpassable fullness is possible as the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> '<s>kaṃ brahma</s>' and as the defining mark thereof, then '<s>amukhyam</s>' — relative fullness dependent on something else is not appropriate — this is the meaning.
And because of the mention of the path described in the <s>Upaniṣads</s> [as the destination]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.16 |
'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.16:
nanvetadupakrame sukhajñānayorabhidhāne 'pi nākṣisthaprakaraṇasya vaiṣṇavatvaṃ yuktam / chāndogye 'prāṇo brahma kam'; iti vidyāṃ 'ya eṣa āditye puruṣaḥ'; iti vidyāṃ coktvāgnibhirupakosalaṃ prati 'upakosalaiṣā somya te 'smadvidhā cātmavidyā coktā'; ityuktatvena 'kam'; ityādyavidyāyā viṣṇuviṣayatvasya 'ya eṣaḥ'; iti dvitīyāyāścāgniviṣayatvasyaiva yuktatvāt / na ca 'asmadvidyā'; ityuktādityavidyāyā agniviṣayatve 'pi nākṣisthavidyāyāstadyuktamiti vācyam / 'ya eṣontarakṣiṇi'; ityakṣisthavidyāyā ādityavidyayaikārthatvāt / na copakramavirodhaḥ / yathā 'hvayāmyagniṃ prathamaṃ svastaye'; ityatrāgnerupakrame 'pi 'savitāramūtaye'; 'hiraṇyayena savitā rathena'; ityādisavitṛśrutiliṅgādinā tatprakaraṇaṃ sāvitramiti prakaraṇavicchedaḥ, tathātrāpi brahmaṇa upakrame 'pi 'asmadvidyā'; ityagnerasmacchabdenoktatvādagnīnāmevedaṃ prakaraṇaṃ na viṣṇoḥ / na ca 'asmadvidyā'; ityetadantaryāmiparatayā yojyam / tathāsati 'ātmavidyā'; iti pṛthaguktyayogāt / tasmādagniviṣayatvameva cakṣurantaḥsthavidyāyā ityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā tadupāttaśrutimevodāharati - śruteti // itītasya sūtreṇānvayaḥ / atra sūtre śrutetyulakṣaṇaṃ, matadhyātetyapi draṣṭavyam / keti vāyurucyate / 'ko vāyuriti śabditaḥ'; iti abhidhānāt / kaśabdasyāvṛttyā gatirityanenāpi sambandhe kagatiriti parabrahmagatirucyate / 'kaṃ brahma'; iti vākyabodhitaparabrahmaprakaraṇādetadarthaniścayāt / tathā ca - śrutopaniṣadāṃ śrutamatadhyātaitadvidyānāṃ puṃsāṃ kena vāyunā kagateḥ 'kaṃ brahma'; iti vākyabodhitabrahmaprāpteḥ 'sa enān brahma gamayati'; ityupasaṃhāre 'bhidhānāt viṣṇuviṣayaivākṣisthavidyā, na tvagniviṣayeti sūtrārthaḥ / yadvā - śrutopaniṣadamupakosalaṃ pratyagnibhiretadvidyāphalatvena brahmagatyabhidhānādvaiṣṇavamevedaṃ prakaraṇaṃ, natvagniviṣayamityarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - 'sa enān brahma gamayati'; iti śrutopaniṣatkānāṃ śrutopaniṣadgatopāsanānāṃ brahmagatyabhidhānācca āntaro viṣṇureva / asyāmupaniṣīdati brahmetyupaniṣat upāsanā / anayā brahma upaniṣīdatīti vetyuktam / śrutaviṣayiṇī yā upaniṣat matidhyānarūpopāsanā tatkānāṃ tadgataṃ tadviṣayakaṃ dhyānarūpopāsanaṃ tadvatāmityarthaḥ / anena upaniṣacchabdo matidhyānarūpopāsanāparaḥ / brahmetyanena bahuvrīhisamāsāvayavabhūtaḥ kaśabda āvṛtto brahmavācaka ityuktaṃ bhavati / ata evāha ṭīkākṛt - śrutapadaṃ manananididhyāsanayorupalakṣakamityādinā / tattvapradīpapakṣe - upaniṣacchabda upāsanāparaḥ / ṭīkākṛtpakṣe vidyāparaḥ / ṭīkāyāṃ vāśabdaścārthaḥ / yadyapyasya sūtrasya prakaraṇavicchedaśaṅkāparihārāyopasaṃhārasthaliṅgoktiparatvaṃna paramasādhye yuktyantarapratipādakatvābhāvādatra caśabdo na prayojyaḥ / tathāpi 'sa enān brahma'; ityupasaṃhārasthasyaitadvidyāvettṛṇāṃ brahmaprāptirūpaliṅgasya cakṣurantaro viṣṇureveti paramasādhye 'pi sākṣādanvayādasya ca liṅgasya ādyasūtroktāmṛtatvaliṅgāpekṣayottaravākyasthadvitīyasūtroktaliṅgāpekṣayā tṛtīyasūtroktaprakaraṇāpekṣayā yuktyantaratvāttadvivakṣayā sūtre caśabdaprayogopapattiriti kecidāhuḥ / vastutastu - atra prakaraṇavicchedaśaṅkāparihāre 'pi pūrvasūtre 'tra caitatprakaraṇasya vaiṣṇavatvarūpadhyāhṛtāvāntarasādhyasyaikatvenatatrānena yuktyantarābhidhānāccaśabdopapattiḥ / 'atha yadu caivāsmiñchavyaṃ kurvanti yadi canārciṣamevābhisambhavanti / arciṣoharanha āpūryamāṇapakṣaṃ āpūryamāṇapakṣādyān ṣaḍudaṅṅeti māsānstānmāsebhyaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsarādādityamāditiyāccandramasaṃ candramaso vidyutaṃ tatpuruṣo mānavaḥ sa enān brahma gamayati'; iti chandogaśruterayamarthaḥ - athetyarthāntare / 'atha'; avasitakarmaṇi 'asmin'; jñāniviṣaye putrādayo yadi 'śavyaṃ'; śavayogyaṃ dahanādikarma kurvanti / 'yadi ca na'; yadi vā na kurvanti 'tadārciṣam'; arcirnāmakadevalokaṃ sambhavanti prāpnuvantyeveme jñānina iti vipariṇāmenānvayaḥ / saṃviśatītyekavacanāntaviśidhātupāṭhaḥ 'te'; iti pāṭhaśca prameyadīpachandogapāṭhaviruddhaḥ / tato 'harlokaṃ, tata 'āpūryamāṇapakṣaṃ'; śuklapakṣalokaṃ, tataḥ sūryo 'yān'; ṣaṇmāsān udaṅṅeti tanmāsadevalokam uttarāyaṇalokaṃ ca, tataḥ saṃvatsarādādityacandravidyudabhimānilokānkrameṇa prāpnuvanti / tataḥ 'tasyāḥ'; vidyunnāmnyā bhāratyāḥ 'puruṣo'; bhartā 'mānavo'; manusaṃjñasya viṣṇoḥ priyo mukhyavāyustaṃ gacchanti / 'saḥ'; vāyuḥ 'enān'; svamāptān pratīkālambanān caturmukhākhyaṃ kāryaṃ brahmāpratīkālambanāṃstu paraṃ brahma gamayatīti /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.4, verse 16:
Objection: Even though happiness and knowledge are mentioned at the beginning of this [section], the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>-nature of the passage about the one dwelling in the eye is not justified. In the <s>Chāndogya</s>, having stated the <s>vidyā</s> (meditation) '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Ka</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>]' and the <s>vidyā</s> 'He who is this person in the sun,' the fires said to <s>Upakosala</s>: 'O gentle one, our knowledge and the knowledge of the Self have been told to you' — because of this statement, it is justified that the first <s>vidyā</s> beginning with '<s>Ka</s>' pertains to <s>Viṣṇu</s> while the second 'He who is [in the sun]' pertains to <s>Agni</s>. Nor should one say that even though the <s>Āditya</s>-<s>vidyā</s> stated by 'our knowledge' pertains to <s>Agni</s>, this is not justified for the <s>akṣistha</s>-<s>vidyā</s> (meditation on the one in the eye) — because the <s>akṣistha</s>-<s>vidyā</s> stated by 'He who is within the eye' is identical in meaning with the <s>Āditya</s>-<s>vidyā</s>. Nor is there contradiction with the opening — just as in 'I invoke <s>Agni</s> first, for well-being,' even though <s>Agni</s> is at the opening, the passage becomes a <s>Sāvitra</s> passage through the <s>Śruti</s> marks of <s>Savitṛ</s> such as '<s>Savitā</s> for aid' and '<s>Savitā</s> with the golden chariot' — so too here, even though <s>Brahman</s> is at the opening, since <s>Agni</s> is referred to by the word 'our' (<s>asmat</s>) in 'our knowledge,' this passage belongs to the fires alone, not to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Nor should 'our knowledge' be construed as referring to the inner controller — for if so, the separate statement 'knowledge of the Self' would be unjustified. Therefore, the <s>akṣistha</s>-<s>vidyā</s> pertains to <s>Agni</s> alone — having thus dispelled this doubt, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> and cites the very <s>Śruti</s> adopted by it: '<s>śruteḥ</s>' (because of the <s>Śruti</s>). // The word 'iti' connects with the <s>sūtra</s>. Here in the <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>śruteḥ</s>' is indicative — '<s>matadhyāteḥ</s>' (because of reflection and meditation) should also be understood. By '<s>ka</s>,' <s>Vāyu</s> is referred to — because of the lexical statement '<s>Ka</s> is called <s>Vāyu</s>.' And by the recurrence of the word '<s>ka</s>,' '<s>gati</s>' (attainment) connected with it makes '<s>kagati</s>' — which means the attainment of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Because of the ascertainment of this meaning from the context of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> conveyed by the passage '<s>Kaṃ Brahma</s>' (Ka is <s>Brahman</s>). And thus — for persons who have heard, reflected upon, and meditated on the <s>Upaniṣad</s> teaching, through <s>Vāyu</s> denoted by '<s>Ka</s>,' the attainment of the <s>Brahman</s> conveyed by the passage '<s>Ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' is stated in the conclusion 'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' — therefore the <s>akṣistha</s>-<s>vidyā</s> pertains to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not to <s>Agni</s>: this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. Or alternatively: because the fires state to <s>Upakosala</s>, who has heard the <s>Upaniṣad</s>, the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> as the fruit of this <s>vidyā</s>, this passage is <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> alone, not pertaining to <s>Agni</s>: that is the meaning. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: 'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' — because of the statement of attainment of <s>Brahman</s> for those who have heard the <s>Upaniṣad</s>, that is, for those who have the meditation pertaining to the <s>Upaniṣad</s> teaching, the inner [entity] is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. 'In this one sits near' — by this the <s>Upaniṣad</s> means meditation. 'By this one approaches <s>Brahman</s>' — or thus it is said. The <s>Upaniṣad</s> that pertains to what is heard — the meditation in the form of reflection and contemplation — for those who possess that, what pertains to that, the meditation whose object is that — for those who have that: this is the meaning. By this, the word '<s>Upaniṣad</s>' means meditation in the form of reflection and contemplation. '<s>Brahman</s>' — by this, the word '<s>Ka</s>,' which is a component of the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, recurs as denoting <s>Brahman</s>: this is stated. Hence the <s>Ṭīkā</s>-author says: 'The word <s>śruta</s> (heard) is indicative of <s>manana</s> (reflection) and <s>nididhyāsana</s> (meditation)' and so forth. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> reading, the word '<s>Upaniṣad</s>' means meditation. In the <s>Ṭīkā</s>-author's reading, it means knowledge. In the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, the word 'vā' also has a meaning. Although the purport of this <s>sūtra</s> is to state the mark at the conclusion for dispelling the doubt of context-severance — and since there is no presentation of an additional reasoning for the ultimate thesis, the word 'ca' in this [<s>sūtra</s>] should not be employed — nevertheless, some say that since the mark in the form of the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> for the knowers of this <s>vidyā</s>, stated at the conclusion in 'He [leads] them to <s>Brahman</s>,' directly applies to the ultimate thesis that the inner [entity] of the eye is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, and since this mark is an additional reasoning compared to the immortality-mark stated by the first <s>sūtra</s> from the earlier passage, compared to the mark stated by the second <s>sūtra</s> from the subsequent passage, and compared to the context stated by the third <s>sūtra</s> — with the intention of expressing it, the use of the word 'ca' in the <s>sūtra</s> is justified. But in reality — even in the dispelling of the doubt of context-severance, since the establishment of the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>-nature of this passage, which is the interpolated subsidiary thesis in the preceding <s>sūtra</s>, is one [with it], the use of 'ca' is justified because an additional reasoning is stated here by this for that.
For it is not justified that through the knowledge of another [deity], there be the attainment of another [i.e., <s>Brahman</s>].
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.4, verse 17:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.17:
astvetadvidyāyāḥ phalatvena brahmaprāptyabhidhānaṃ, tathāpi kuto nāgniviṣayatvamasyā ityata āha - na hīti // 'hi'; yasmādanyasyāgnervidyayānyagatiranyasya brahmaṇaḥ prāptirna yuktā / yasmāccātra parabrahmaprāptiḥ phalatvenocyate ityarthaḥ / tasmānnānyavidyeyaṃ brahmavidyaiveti vākyaśeṣaḥ / hiśabdena vipakṣe - 'devān devayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi'; iti smṛtivirodhaṃ sūcayati / 'asmadvidyātmavidyā'; iti vacanavirodhastu tayorantaryāmisarvagatarūpadvayaviṣayakatvena pariharaṇīyaḥ / sāvakāśaśruterapi niravakāśaśruteḥ prābalyāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.4, verse 17:
Granted that the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> is stated as the fruit of this <s>vidyā</s>, even so, why can this [<s>vidyā</s>] not pertain to <s>Agni</s>? — to this he says: '<s>na hi</s>' (for not). // 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since through the knowledge of 'another' — <s>Agni</s> — the 'attainment of another' — the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> — is not justified. And since the attainment of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is stated here as the fruit: that is the meaning. Therefore this is not a knowledge of another [deity], but a knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> alone: this is the sentence-remainder. Through the word 'hi,' he hints at the <s>Smṛti</s> contradiction in the opposing view: 'The worshippers of the gods go to the gods; My devotees come to Me' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 9.25). The contradiction with the statement 'our knowledge [and] knowledge of the Self' should be resolved by taking those two as pertaining to the two forms — the inner controller and the all-pervading: that is the purport. Because the no-scope-elsewhere <s>Śruti</s> is stronger even than the <s>Śruti</s> that has scope.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //

Because of the infinite regress resulting from the instability [of the jīva as controller], and because of the impossibility [of its being the controller], [the inner entity is] not the other [i.e., not the jīva]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.17 |
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.4, verse 18:]

Because of the infinite regress (<s>anavasthiti</s>) if the <s>jīva</s> were the controller of another <s>jīva</s>, and because of the impossibility arising from their equal status, [the inner entity is] not the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.18:
evamupapattyādibhirviṣṇorakṣisthatvaṃ pratipādya vipakṣe bādhakenāpi tatsamarthayatsūtraṃ paṭhati - anavasthiteriti / atrāntarastattajjīvaprerakatayā tattaccakṣussthitaḥ 'itaraḥ'; pūrvaprakṛtāt kaśabdoditāt brahmaṇo 'nyo 'gnijīvo na / kutaḥ? yataḥ sa itaro jīva iti hetusādhyayojanāmabhipretya atra vipakṣe 'niṣṭaprasaṅgābhidhāyakatayānavasthiterityaṃśaṃ yojayati - jīvasyeti / 'sāmyāt'; iti sūtre 'dhyāhṛtaṃ padam, idaṃ ca tattvapradīparītyā dehalīdīpanyāyenobhayatra sambadhyate / jīvasya jīvāntaraniyāmakatve ityetadvipariṇatamasambhavādityanenāpi sambadhyate / co hetusamuccaye / itara ityasyāgnirityarthe vācye jīva iti sāmānyenoktiḥ sādhyahetvostantreṇābhidhānārtham / na jīva ityasya āntara ityuddeśyasamarpakānuvṛttapadenānvayaḥ / anena tattajjīvaprerakatayā tattaccakṣurantaro netaraḥ nāgniḥ / kutaḥ? yataḥ sa itaro jīvaḥ jīvatvāditi yāvat / na ca vipakṣe bādhakābhāvaḥ, jīvasya jīvāntaraniyāmakatve prerakatve āntarajīvasyāpi jīvatvasāmyatāttasyāpi niyāmakaṃ jīvāntaraṃ vācyamityanavasthiterasiddhaparamparākalpanarūpānavasthākhyāniṣṭāpatteḥ / abhyupagamya cedamuditam / vastutastu - jīvasya jīvāntaraniyāmakatvāsambhavācca netaro 'gnirantaraḥ / kuto 'sambhavaḥ? agnerjīvasya preryajīvāntareṇa saha paratantrarūpajīvatvasāmyāditi sūtravṛttirdarśitā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.4, verse 18:
Having thus established through fitness and the like that <s>Viṣṇu</s> dwells in the eye, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> that supports this through an invalidator in the opposing view: '<s>anavasthiteḥ</s>' (because of the infinite regress). Here, the 'inner' [entity] — the one who is the impeller of each respective <s>jīva</s>, dwelling in each respective eye — the 'other' (<s>itaraḥ</s>) — one different from the <s>Brahman</s> referred to earlier by the word '<s>Ka</s>' — the <s>Agni</s>-<s>jīva</s> is not [the inner entity]. Why? Because 'he' (<s>sa</s>) — that other — is a <s>jīva</s>: intending the construction of the reason and the thesis, and with the intent of stating the undesirable consequence as invalidating [the prima facie view], he construes the portion '<s>anavasthiteḥ</s>' (because of the infinite regress) — '<s>jīvasya</s>' (of the <s>jīva</s>). '<s>Sāmyāt</s>' (because of the equal status) is a word interpolated in the <s>sūtra</s>, and this, according to the method of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, connects with both [clauses] by the principle of the threshold-lamp. 'Of the <s>jīva</s>, if it were the controller of another <s>jīva</s>' — this, in reversed form, also connects with '<s>asambhavāt</s>' (because of the impossibility). The word 'ca' is for the accumulation of reasons. The statement '<s>itara</s>' (the other), where the meaning should be '<s>Agni</s>,' is stated generally as '<s>jīva</s>' for the purpose of stating both thesis and reason in a single expression. 'Not the <s>jīva</s>' — its syntactic connection is with the recurrent subject-indicating word 'the inner' (<s>āntaraḥ</s>). By this: the one who, as the impeller of each respective <s>jīva</s>, dwells within each respective eye — is not the other, not <s>Agni</s>. Why? Because he is that other, a <s>jīva</s> — that is the import. And there is no absence of an invalidator in the opposing view — for if the <s>jīva</s> were the controller, the impeller, of another <s>jīva</s>, then that inner <s>jīva</s> too, because of the equal status of being a <s>jīva</s>, would require yet another <s>jīva</s> as its controller — and thus because of the infinite regress, the undesirable consequence of imagining an unestablished infinite chain [would arise]. This is stated by way of concession. But in reality: because of the impossibility of the <s>jīva</s>'s being the controller of another <s>jīva</s> — the inner [entity] is not the other, not <s>Agni</s>. Why the impossibility? Because of the equal status of being a <s>jīva</s> — the equal status of being dependent — between the <s>Agni</s>-<s>jīva</s> and the <s>jīva</s> to be impelled: thus the <s>sūtra</s>-commentary is shown.
Because of the absence of a valid means of knowledge for the restriction [that Agni alone is independent]; and because of [the opponent's] not accepting the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). // 17 //
// Thus ends the <s>Antara-adhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the inner [entity]). // 4 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.4, verse 19:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.4.19:
nanu jīvaprerakāgneḥ svātantryābhyupagamānnānavasthā / na caivaṃ jīvāntarasyāpi svātantryaṃ syāt jīvatvasāmyādityuktamiti vācyam / jīvatvasāmye 'pyagnereva svātantryaṃ nānyeṣāmiti niyamābhyupagamādityata āha - niyameti // jīvatvasāmyepyagnereva svātantryaṃ nānyeṣāmiti niyame pramāṇābhāvādityarthaḥ / ato 'gneḥ svātantryāyogātsusthaivānavasthitiriti bhāvaḥ / nanvastvagnerasvātantryaṃ, tathāpi tatprerakasyeśvarasya svātantryasambhavānnānavasthetyata āha - anīśvaretir / iśvaraṃ jagatprerakatvena yo 'pekṣate 'bhyupaiti sar iśvarāpekṣaḥ, sa na bhavatītyanīśvarāpekṣaḥ, tasya bhāvastattvaṃ tasmādityarthaḥ / pūrvavādina iti śeṣaḥ / hetusamuccaye caśabdaḥ / evaṃ vā - nanu paratantratvasāmye 'pi jīvānāṃ jīvāntaraniyāmakatvātkathaṃ tadasambhava ityata āha - anīśvareti / vyākhyānaṃ pūrvavat / tathā ca - yathāsmatpakṣe sati rājñi maṇḍaleśe prajānāṃ rājaśaktyā niyamyaniyāmakabhāvavart iśvaraśaktyā jīvānāṃ jīvāntaraniyāmakatvasambhavaḥ, na tathā parapakṣe sambhavati, pareṇar iśvarānabhyupagamāditi bhāvaḥ / idaṃ ca vākyadvayasya yojanādvayam / ṭīkāyāṃ tattvapradīpoktamevoktam / uktaṃ hi tattvapradīpe - niyamapramāṇābhāvo 'nīśvarāpekṣatvaṃ cetyubhau ubhayatra heturiti / 'ubhayatra'; anavasthityasambhavayorityarthaḥ / // iti antarādhikaraṇam // 4 //
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.4, verse 19:
Objection: There is no infinite regress, because of accepting the independence of <s>Agni</s>, who is the impeller of the <s>jīvas</s>. Nor should one say that if so, the independence of another <s>jīva</s> too would follow because of the equal status of being a <s>jīva</s> — because of accepting the restriction that <s>Agni</s> alone is independent and not others, even though the status of being a <s>jīva</s> is equal. To this he says: '<s>niyama</s>' (restriction). // Even though the status of being a <s>jīva</s> is equal, there is no valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for the restriction that <s>Agni</s> alone is independent and not others: that is the meaning. Therefore, because of the unfitness of <s>Agni</s>'s independence, the infinite regress stands firm: that is the purport. Objection: Let <s>Agni</s> lack independence; even so, since the independence of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) who is <s>Agni</s>'s impeller is possible, there is no infinite regress. To this he says: '<s>anīśvara</s>' (because of not accepting the Lord). One who accepts (<s>apekṣate</s>) — acknowledges — the Lord as the impeller of the universe is '<s>Īśvarāpekṣa</s>' (one who accepts the Lord); he who is not so is '<s>anīśvarāpekṣa</s>'; the state of such [non-acceptance] — therefore: that is the meaning. 'Of the prima facie advocate' is the remainder. The word 'ca' is for the accumulation of reasons. Or alternatively: objection — even though the status of being dependent is equal among the <s>jīvas</s>, since [one] <s>jīva</s> can control another <s>jīva</s>, how is there impossibility? To this he says: '<s>anīśvara</s>.' The explanation is as before. And thus: just as in our view, when there is a king, in his domain, by the king's power, the controlled-controller relationship exists among the subjects — by the power of the Lord, the <s>jīvas</s>' controlling of other <s>jīvas</s> is possible — so it is not possible in the opponent's view, because the opponent does not accept the Lord: that is the purport. This pair of sentences has a twofold construction. In the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, what was stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> alone is stated. For it is said in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'The absence of a valid means of knowledge for the restriction and the non-acceptance of the Lord — both are reasons in both [cases].' 'In both' means: in [the arguments of] infinite regress and impossibility.
// Thus ends the <s>Antara-adhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the inner [entity]). // 4 //
// 5. The <s>Antaryāmi-adhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the inner controller). //

'He who, dwelling in the earth, is within the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who controls the earth from within — He is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal one' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 5.7.3) — and so forth: the inner controller is spoken of.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.5, verse 1:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.1:
atrādhikaraṇe 'ntaḥsthatvarūpabhāvasahitaṃ niyamanakriyātmakaṃ liṅgaṃ brahmaṇi samanvīyate / viṣayavākyodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ viṣayaṃ darśayati - ya iti // ityādīti prathamā saptamyarthe / tṛtīyārthe vā / 'saptasu prathamā'; iti sūtrāt / 'kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ vā'; iti tattvapradīpokteḥ 'ityādinā'; iti pāṭhastadviruddhaḥ / vākye, vākyeneti vā śeṣaḥ/ 'yo 'psu tiṣṭhan'; 'yo bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan'; ityādikamādiśabdena gṛhyate / antaryāmītyanena viṣayo darśitaḥ / bṛhadāraṇyake uddālakaṃ prati yājñyavalkyenoktaṃ idaṃ vākyam / 'yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ'; pṛthuṃ viṣṇumūḍhvā vāti gacchatīti pṛthivī garuḍaḥ tasmin tiṣṭhan 'pṛthivyāḥ'; tadabhimānicetanāt 'antaro'; viviktaḥ / 'yaṃ ca pṛthivī'; tadabhimānī cetano na veda sākalyena / 'yasya ca pṛthivī'; tadvaśatvanimittāt śarīrabhūtā / na kevalaṃ tatra sthitimātraṃ, kintu 'yo 'ntaraḥ'; antaḥsthitvā bāhyaviṣayāpekṣāṃ vinā ramamāṇaḥ / svato nityatṛptaḥ -
bāhyāpekṣāṃ vinā yastu ramate so 'ntarassmṛtaḥ'; //
children.translated_text: In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topical section), the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) consisting of the act of controlling (<s>niyamanakriyā</s>), together with the nature of being situated within, is harmonized with <s>Brahman</s>. He shows the subject matter preceded by a citation of the subject-passage — 'ya' (he who), etc. 'Ityādi' — the nominative is used in the sense of the locative, or in the sense of the instrumental, based on the <s>sūtra</s> 'the nominative stands for the seven [cases],' and because the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> states 'or as a qualifier of the action'; hence the reading 'ityādinā' (by means of such passages) is contradicted by that. The completion is: 'in the passage' or 'by the passage.' The word 'ādi' (etc.) encompasses passages such as 'He who stands in the waters,' 'He who stands in all beings,' and so forth. By the term '<s>antaryāmin</s>' (inner controller) the subject matter is indicated. This passage was spoken by <s>Yājñavalkya</s> to <s>Uddālaka</s> in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> [Upaniṣad]. 'Yaḥ pṛthivyām' — '<s>pṛthivī</s>' means <s>Garuḍa</s>, for he goes (<s>vāti</s>) having spread (<s>ūḍhvā</s>) the broad one (<s>pṛthu</s>), that is, <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'standing in him' — 'from <s>pṛthivī</s>' means from the conscious being who identifies with that; '<s>antara</s>' means distinct. 'Whom <s>pṛthivī</s> [does not know]' — the conscious being who identifies with that does not know [Him] completely. 'Whose <s>pṛthivī</s> [is the body]' — she has become a body due to being under His control. Not only is there mere abiding there, but 'He who is <s>antara</s>' — having been situated within, rejoicing without dependence on external objects, being eternally self-satisfied by nature — 'He who rejoices without dependence on the external is remembered as <s>antara</s> (the inner one).'
Thus states the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> (the great commentary [of <s>Madhva</s>]). Alternatively — 'The innerness (<s>antaratva</s>) of <s>Hari</s> is declared because of His being supremely dear.'

children.text: iti tatraivokteḥ / 'preyaḥ putrāt'; ityādiśrutyā paramapreyorūpatvāt 'antaraḥ'; atipriyaḥ san 'pṛthivīṃ'; garuḍaṃ 'yamayati'; niyamayati / eṣaḥ 'te'; tava 'antaryāmyātmā'; niyāmakaḥ puruṣaḥ 'amṛtaḥ'; nitya iti śrutyarthaḥ / etena antaro vivikta iti ṭīkāyā bṛhadbhāṣyavirodho nirastaḥ / bṛhadbhāṣyasya 'ya ātmānam'; ityatrasthāntaraśabdaviṣayatvāt / ata eva na śrutau paunaruktyam / dvayorbhinnārthatvāt / pūrvapakṣī tvidaṃ vākyamanyaparaṃ manyate /
children.translated_text: Thus is stated in that same [<s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s>]. Because of His nature as the supremely dear, as stated in the <s>śruti</s> 'dearer than a son' and so forth, '<s>antara</s>' means the supremely beloved one who 'controls' (<s>yamayati</s>), that is, governs '<s>pṛthivī</s>' — <s>Garuḍa</s>. 'This is your <s>antaryāmin</s> <s>ātman</s>' — the governing <s>puruṣa</s> (person), '<s>amṛta</s>' — eternal: this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. By this, the contradiction of the <s>ṭīkā</s>'s [interpretation of] '<s>antara</s>' as 'distinct' with the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> is resolved, since the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s>'s [comment] pertains to the word '<s>antara</s>' occurring in the passage 'He who is the <s>ātman</s>.' Therefore there is no redundancy in the <s>śruti</s>, since the two [usages] have different meanings. The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector), however, considers this passage to refer to something else.

children.text:
tatra ca 'etadamṛtam'; (chāṃ. 4-15.1.) ityuktamamṛtatvamucyate /
sa ca 'yasya pṛthivī śarīram'; ityādinā sarvātmakatvāt prakṛtistattajjīvo vā yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: And there, the immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>) that was stated [in the Chāndogya passage] 'this is the immortal' (Chān. 4.15.1) is being declared. And since he is the self of all, as stated by 'whose body is <s>pṛthivī</s>' and so forth, <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) or the individual <s>jīva</s> (soul) of that [<s>pṛthivī</s> etc.] would be appropriate [as the <s>antaryāmin</s>].
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.5.2:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.2:
pūrvādhikaraṇatadviṣayavākyasaṅgatiṃ darśayati - tatreti // iyamatra tattvapradīpoktā yojanā - 'yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan'; ityādivākyeṣvantaryāmyucyate / tatra tadvākyeṣveva tasminnevāntaryāmiṇi 'etadamṛtametadabhayam'; iti pūrvanayodāhṛtachāndogyavākye 'kṣipuruṣasyoktamamṛtatvaṃ 'eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ'; ityanena ucyate iti / anena bṛhadāraṇyakoktāntaryāmiṇi viṣṇvanyatvākṣepamukhena taduktāmṛtatvasyāpyanyaniṣṭhatvaṃ sampādya tasya pūrvādhikaraṇoktākṣisthatvasya viṣṇutvasādhakatvākṣepātpūrveṇākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / tataḥ kimityataḥ sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣayati - sa ceti / caśabdo hetusamuccaye / ādipadena 'yasyāpaḥ śarīram'; ityādeḥ saṅgrahaḥ / tacchabdasya vipariṇāmena hetuvākyena sambandhaḥ / ātmaśabdaḥ svarūpaśarīrobhayārthaḥ / tathā ca so 'ntaryāmī jaḍacetanobhayarūpā prakṛtiḥ pṛthivyāditattajjīvo vā yuktaḥ / kutaḥ? śrautaśarīraśabdasya idaṃ pūrvapakṣaśarīramityādāviva svarūpārthatvāt / jaḍaprakṛteśca sarvopādānatvena sarvātmakatvāt / citprakṛteśca sarvābhimānitvena sarvātmakatvāt pṛthivyādijīvasya pṛthivyādisarvaśarīratvāditi yojanā /
children.translated_text: He shows the connection with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> and the passage that is its subject — 'tatra' (there), etc. Here the interpretation given in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> is as follows: In passages such as 'He who stands in <s>pṛthivī</s>,' the <s>antaryāmin</s> is spoken of. There, in those very passages, the immortality stated of the <s>akṣipuruṣa</s> (the person in the eye) in the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage cited in the previous section — 'this is the immortal, this is the fearless' — is declared by means of 'This is your <s>ātman</s>, the inner controller, the immortal.' By this, having established through the suggestion of the <s>antaryāmin</s> stated in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> being other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> that the immortality stated there also belongs to another, and from the suggestion that the abiding-in-the-eye stated in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> serves to establish [the <s>antaryāmin</s> as] <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the connection with the preceding [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] through suggestion is stated. Then, 'what follows from that?' — he presents the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) with reasoning — 'sa ca' (and he), etc. The particle 'ca' is for the accumulation of reasons. The word 'ādi' (etc.) encompasses passages like 'whose body is the waters' and so forth. The word 'tat' is connected with the reason-statement by transposition. The word '<s>ātman</s>' means both 'own nature' and 'body.' And thus, that <s>antaryāmin</s> is appropriately <s>Prakṛti</s> in the form of both insentient and sentient, or the individual <s>jīva</s> of the respective <s>pṛthivī</s> and so forth. Why? Because the word 'body' (<s>śarīra</s>) found in <s>śruti</s> means 'own nature,' as in the usage '<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>-<s>śarīra</s>' (the body of the objection); and because insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>, being the material cause of all, is the self of all; and because sentient <s>Prakṛti</s>, being the presiding consciousness of all, is the self of all; and because the <s>jīva</s> of <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. has <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. as its entire body — such is the interpretation.
For the embodiment in <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth) and the rest is not accepted in the case of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.5.3:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.3:
nanu yathā prakṛtyādiliṅgena teṣāmantaryāmitvaṃ tathā amṛtatvaliṅgena viṣṇostatkiṃ na syādityata āha - na hīti // pṛthivyādi śarīraṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ, tasya bhāvastattvaṃ tvapratyayāpāṭhe tvanvayaḥ ṛjuḥ / aṅgīkriyate / siddhāntineti śeṣaḥ / tasya pṛthivyādijaḍabhinnaciccharīratvāditi hiśabdābhiprāyaḥ / tathā ca - saiddhāntikaliṅgāpekṣayā pūrvapakṣaliṅgasya niravakāśatayā balavattvādanena tasya bādhānnāntaryāmī viṣṇuriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, just as through the indicatory marks of <s>Prakṛti</s> etc. their status as <s>antaryāmin</s> [is established], so too through the indicatory mark of immortality, why should the same not apply to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he says — 'na hi' (for not), etc. One whose body is <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. is so described; the state of being such is the meaning. Where the suffix 'tva' is not read, the direct construction with 'tu' is straightforward. 'Is accepted' — by the <s>siddhāntin</s> (the proponent of the established view), this is to be supplied. The purport of the word 'hi' (for) is: because [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] has as His body sentient beings distinct from the insentient <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. And thus — since the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> indicatory mark is stronger due to leaving no scope for the <s>siddhānta</s> indicatory mark, and since by this [argument] the latter is overridden, the <s>antaryāmin</s> is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the purport.
Therefore he says — <s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.5.4:

<s>antaryāmyadhidaivādiṣu taddharmavyapadeśāt</s> — [The <s>antaryāmin</s> is <s>Brahman</s>] because in the <s>adhidaiva</s> (cosmic) and other [sections], the characteristics of that [<s>Brahman</s>] are declared. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.18 |
<s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text:
'yaṃ pṛthivī na veda, yaḥ pṛthivyā antaraḥ'; (bṛ. 5-7-3.) ityādinā
adhidaivādiṣu taddharmavyapadeśāt viṣṇurevāntaryāmī /
children.translated_text: By means of passages such as 'whom <s>pṛthivī</s> does not know, who is inner to <s>pṛthivī</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.3), because the characteristics of that [<s>Brahman</s>] are declared in the <s>adhidaiva</s> (cosmic) and other [sections], the <s>antaryāmin</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.4:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // ityādinā vākyena iti śeṣaḥ / tatra yadyapi sautravyapadeśapadena abhipretaṃ 'yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yaḥ pṛthivīmantaro yamayati'; iti vākyamevodāhartavyam / atroktāntaratvasyaiva sautradharmaśabdārthatvāt, na tu 'pṛthivyāmantaraḥ'; iti vākyam / atrātyantaraśabdasya viviktārthatvena taduktārthasyāhetutvāt / tathā ca tadudāharaṇaṃ na prakṛtopayuktam / tathāpi tatpratīkatvenodāhṛtamityadoṣaḥ / ādiśabdena prakaraṇatrayavākyaṃ gṛhyate / adhidaivādiṣu / prakaraṇeṣviti śeṣaḥ / prakaraṇaṃ nāma ekaprameyapratipādakānekavākyāni / tatra 'yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan'; ityadhidaivataprakaraṇam / 'yassarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan'; ityādibhūtaprakaraṇam / 'yaḥ prāṇe tiṣṭhan'; ityadhyātmaprakaraṇam / sūtre bhāṣye cādhidaivetyuktyā pṛthivyādīnāṃ jaḍatvena tadaviditatvaṃ sarvasyāpi sambhavatīti śaṅkā vāritā / atroktānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ adhidaivatvena cetanatvāt 'prāṇe'; iti śrutau prāṇaśabdaḥ prāṇavāyudevatāparaḥ, saiva prameyadīparītyā prāṇendriyadevatā / adhidaivādiṣvityanekaprakaraṇagrahaṇena na kevalamekatra taddharmoktiḥ, kintu - bahuṣu sthaleṣviti sūcitam / anuvṛttasya tattvityasyārthamāha - viṣṇureveti / tadityasya napuṃsakatve 'pi antaryāmītyuddeśyasamarpakasautrapadānusāreṇa viṣṇureveti vyākhyātam / anena 'eṣa ta ātmā'; (bṛ. 5-7-3.) ityuktāntaryāmī sa viṣṇureva / kutaḥ? adhidaivādiṣu prakaraṇeṣu 'taddharmavyapadeśāt'; tasya viṣṇoḥ dharmasya aviditatvāntaratvādeḥ 'yaṃ pṛthivī na veda'; ityādinoktatvāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: Having introduced the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>sūtra</s>, he explains it — 'ataḥ' (therefore), etc. The completion is: 'by the passage beginning with ityādinā.' There, although the passage intended by the <s>sūtra</s>'s word '<s>vyapadeśa</s>' (declaration) is precisely 'whom <s>pṛthivī</s> does not know, who controls <s>pṛthivī</s> from within' — since the <s>antaratva</s> (innerness) stated here is indeed the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>'s word '<s>dharma</s>' (characteristic) — not the passage '<s>pṛthivyām antaraḥ</s>' (inner to <s>pṛthivī</s>), because the word '<s>antara</s>' there has the meaning of 'distinct,' and what it states is not a reason [for the conclusion]. And thus citing that passage is not useful to the topic at hand. Nevertheless, there is no fault since it is cited as a <s>pratīka</s> (lemma) for that [longer passage]. The word 'ādi' (etc.) encompasses the passages of the three sections (<s>prakaraṇatraya</s>). '<s>Adhidaivādiṣu</s>' — the completion is: 'in the sections.' A 'section' (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) means multiple passages establishing a single subject. There, 'He who stands in <s>pṛthivī</s>' is the <s>adhidaivata</s> (cosmic deity) section; 'He who stands in all beings' and so forth is the <s>bhūta</s> (elemental) section; 'He who stands in <s>prāṇa</s>' is the <s>adhyātma</s> (individual self) section. By the use of '<s>adhidaiva</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s>, the doubt that <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. being insentient could mean anyone's not-knowing-them is possible is warded off — since the <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. mentioned here are conscious beings in their <s>adhidaiva</s> (presiding deity) aspect; and in the <s>śruti</s> '<s>prāṇe</s>' (in <s>prāṇa</s>), the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' refers to the deity of <s>prāṇa</s>-wind, and that same [deity] by the method of establishing the subject is the deity of the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>indriya</s> (vital sense). By the inclusion of multiple sections through '<s>adhidaivādiṣu</s>' (in the cosmic and other [sections]), it is indicated that the declaration of His characteristics is not merely in one place, but in many places. He states the meaning of the recurring word 'tat' (that) — '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone,' etc. Although 'tat' is neuter, it is explained as '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' in accordance with the <s>sūtra</s>'s word '<s>antaryāmin</s>' which denotes the subject. By this, the <s>antaryāmin</s> stated in 'This is your <s>ātman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.3) is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Why? Because in the <s>adhidaiva</s> and other sections, 'the characteristics of that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] are declared' — that is, His characteristics such as unknowability and innerness are stated by passages like 'whom <s>pṛthivī</s> does not know' — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.

children.text:
sa hi 'na te viṣṇo jāyamāno na jātaḥ'; (ṛ. 7-99-2.)
'sa yo 'to 'śruto 'gato 'mato 'nato 'dṛṣṭo 'vijñāto 'nādiṣṭaḥ sarveṣāṃ
bhūtānāmantarapuruṣaḥ'; (ai.ā. 3-2-4.) ityādināvidito 'ntaraśca // 18 //
children.translated_text: For He (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is declared to be unknown and inner by passages such as 'Not those, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who are being born nor those who are born [can reach the limit of Your greatness]' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 7.99.2), and 'He who is unheard, unperceived, unthought, uncognized, unseen, unknown, undirected — the inner <s>puruṣa</s> of all beings' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.4), and so forth. // 18 //
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.5.5:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.5:
aviditatvādeḥ kuto viṣṇudharmatvamityata āha - sa hīti // 'saḥ'; viṣṇuḥ / 'ityādinā'; vākyeneti śeṣaḥ / ādipadena 'divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ'; (subāla. 7.) ityupakramya 'yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīmantaraḥ sañcaran yaṃ pṛthivī na veda eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā apahatapāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ'; ityupasaṃhṛtyādhītaṃ śrutyantaraṃ gṛhyate / 'aviditaḥ'; sākalyenājñātaḥ 'antaraḥ'; antassthitvā ramaṇakṛtprasiddha iti śeṣaḥ / ca samuccaye / 'na te'; iti vākyaṃ ca te devamahimnaḥ paramantaṃ mahimānaṃ śrotrādinā nāpa iti prakṛtānuguṇyena sarvatrādhikaraṇe vyākhyātam / 'saḥ'; iti vākyamapi tatraiva vyākṛtam /
children.translated_text: How is unknowability etc. a characteristic of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he says — 'sa hi' (for He), etc. '<s>Saḥ</s>' refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The completion is: 'by the passage beginning with ityādinā.' The word 'ādi' (etc.) encompasses the passage from the <s>Subāla Upaniṣad</s> (7) beginning with 'The divine, the one god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' and concluding with 'whose body is <s>pṛthivī</s>, who moves within <s>pṛthivī</s>, whom <s>pṛthivī</s> does not know — He is the inner <s>ātman</s> of all beings, free from evil, divine, the one god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'; thus a different <s>śruti</s> passage studied [in another recension] is encompassed. '<s>Avidita</s>' means not known completely; '<s>antara</s>' means well-known as the one who, being situated within, causes delight — this is the completion. The particle 'ca' is for accumulation. The passage 'na te' (not those) [means] that the ultimate limit of Your divine greatness cannot be reached by ear and other [senses] — thus it has been explained everywhere in the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> in accordance with the context. The passage beginning with '<s>saḥ</s>' (He) has also been explained in that same place.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.

<s>na ca smārtam ataddharmābhilāpāt</s> — And [the <s>antaryāmin</s>] is not that which is known from <s>Smṛti</s> [i.e., <s>Pradhāna</s>], because its characteristics are not declared [in the passage]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.19 |
<s>Oṃ</s>.

The <s>antaryāmin</s> is not the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) spoken of in <s>Smṛti</s>, because the characteristics of <s>Pradhāna</s> such as possessing the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) are not mentioned [in the passage]. // 19 //
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.5.6:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.6:
evaṃ niravakāśaliṅgena viṣṇorantaryāmitvaṃ samarthya yaduktaṃ pūrvapakṣiṇā prakṛtyāderantaryāmitvaṃ tatprakṛtijīvasādhāraṇaṃ yuktyā nirākurvatsūtramupanyasyati - na ceti // atra 'ataddharmābhilāpāt'; ityetat 'atacchabdāt'; itivadavyayībhāvasamāsarūpam / ata eva avyayamityāśayenāniyamābhiprāyeṇādau hetuvākyaṃ vyākhyāti - triguṇatvādīti / sattvādirūpāstrayo guṇā yasya kāryabhūtāstattriguṇaṃ, tasya bhāvastriguṇatvaṃ tadādiryeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ, pradhānasya prakṛterdharmāḥ, triguṇatvādayaścate pradhānadharmāśca te jaḍatvasaṃsāritvādīnāṃ grahaṇam / pradhānapadaṃ jīvasyāpyupalakṣakam / ādiśabdo vātra saṃyojyaḥ / sādhyadharmapratiyoginirdeśāya pūrvapakṣe yuktisūcanāya ca prayuktaṃ smārtamityedvyācaṣṭe - smṛtyuktamiti / pṛthivyādyātmakatayā kāpilasmṛtipratipāditamityarthaḥ / smṛtyuktamevaitanna śrutyuktamiti jñāpanāyedam / paryavasitārthamāha - pradhānamiti / jīvasyāpyupalakṣakamidam / śārīraśceti vakṣyamāṇasyātrāpyanvayo darśitaḥ / antaryāmiṇo 'nyarūpatvaniṣedhāya pravṛtte sūtre 'pekṣitaṃ sādhyadharmiṇaṃ darśayati - antaryāmīti / antaryāmī na pradhānamiti yojanā / na pradhānamantaryāmītyanena sautracaśabdaḥ antaryāmī viṣṇureva na tu pradhānamiti tuśabdārthaḥ / sa ca na śārīra ityādāviva parapakṣaniṣedhamātraṃ na kriyate, kintu, svapakṣavidhirapīti parapakṣaniṣedhasya svapakṣavidhipūrvakatvarūpaviśeṣārtha iti sūcitaṃ bhavati / anenāntaryāmī viṣṇureva, na tu smārtaṃ pṛthivyādyātmakatayā smṛtau pratipāditaṃ pradhānam / śārīro jīvaḥ / kutaḥ? atra 'ataddharmābhilāpāt'; triguṇatvasaṃsāritvādirūpapradhānajīvadharmoktyabhāvāditi sūtravṛttirdarśitābhavati / tattvapradīpe tu - nañastadviruddhārthatvamāśrityātmatvāmṛtatvādṛṣṭatvadraṣṭṛtvādyataddharmābhilāpācca iti hetuvākyasya vṛttyantaramapi darśitam/
children.translated_text: Having thus established the <s>antaryāmitva</s> (status as inner controller) of <s>Viṣṇu</s> through an indicatory mark that leaves no scope [for alternatives], he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that refutes by reasoning what the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> had stated — namely the <s>antaryāmitva</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s> etc. — [a refutation] common to both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>jīva</s> — 'na ca' (and not), etc. Here, '<s>ataddharmābhilāpāt</s>' has the form of an <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound, just like '<s>atacchabdāt</s>.' Therefore, with the understanding that it is indeclinable, and with the intention of non-restriction, he first explains the reason-statement — '<s>triguṇatvādi</s>' (possession of three <s>guṇas</s> etc.), etc. <s>Triguṇa</s> means that which has as its effects the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the rest; the state of being that is <s>triguṇatva</s>; those beginning with that are so described. The characteristics of <s>Pradhāna</s>, that is, of <s>Prakṛti</s>, are <s>triguṇatva</s> and the rest, and these characteristics of <s>Pradhāna</s> include insentience (<s>jaḍatva</s>), being subject to <s>saṃsāra</s> (<s>saṃsāritva</s>), and so forth. The word '<s>Pradhāna</s>' is also an indicator (<s>upalakṣaka</s>) for the <s>jīva</s>. The word 'ādi' here is to be connected [with <s>Pradhāna</s>-<s>dharmas</s>]. To indicate the counter-correlate of the characteristic to be established and to hint at the reasoning in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, the word '<s>smārta</s>' is used — he explains this as 'stated in <s>Smṛti</s>.' The meaning is: taught in the <s>Kāpila Smṛti</s> (Sāṅkhya texts) as having <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. as its nature. This [use of '<s>smārta</s>'] indicates that this [<s>Pradhāna</s>] is stated only in <s>Smṛti</s>, not in <s>Śruti</s>. He states the concluded meaning — '<s>Pradhāna</s>,' etc. This is also an indicator for the <s>jīva</s>. The connection with the forthcoming [<s>sūtra</s>] '<s>śārīraśca</s>' (and the embodied [soul]) is also shown here. In the <s>sūtra</s> which proceeds to negate the <s>antaryāmin</s>'s being of another nature, he shows the subject whose characteristic is to be established — '<s>antaryāmin</s>,' etc. The interpretation is: the <s>antaryāmin</s> is not <s>Pradhāna</s>. By 'na pradhānam antaryāmī' (the <s>antaryāmin</s> is not <s>Pradhāna</s>), the <s>sūtra</s>'s particle 'ca' [implies] '<s>antaryāmī</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not <s>Pradhāna</s>' — the word 'tu' (but) conveys this meaning. And just as in 'sa ca na śārīraḥ' (and he is not the embodied soul) and so forth, it is not merely a negation of the opponent's position but also an affirmation of one's own position — thus it is indicated that the negation of the opponent's position presupposes the establishment of one's own. By this, the <s>antaryāmin</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, and not the <s>Pradhāna</s> which is taught in <s>Smṛti</s> as having <s>pṛthivī</s> etc. as its nature; nor the embodied <s>jīva</s>. Why? Because here, '<s>ataddharmābhilāpāt</s>' — because characteristics of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>jīva</s> such as <s>triguṇatva</s> (possession of three qualities) and <s>saṃsāritva</s> (subjection to transmigration) are not stated — thus the paraphrase of the <s>sūtra</s> is shown. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, an alternative paraphrase of the reason-statement is also shown: relying on the meaning of the negative particle 'a-' as denoting the opposite, [the characteristics] such as selfhood (<s>ātmatva</s>), immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>), unseenness (<s>adṛṣṭatva</s>), and being a seer (<s>draṣṭṛtva</s>) — which are characteristics not belonging to that [<s>Pradhāna</s>/<s>jīva</s>] — are declared.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.

<s>śārīraś ca ubhaye api hi bhedena enam adhīyate</s> — And [the <s>antaryāmin</s> is] not the embodied [soul] either, for both [<s>śākhās</s>, recensions] read of him as distinct [from the <s>jīva</s>]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.20 |
<s>Oṃ</s>.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.5.7:

children.text:
'ya ātmani tiṣṭhannātmano 'ntaro yamātmāna veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānamantaro yamayatyeṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ';
(bṛ.mādhyandinapāṭhaḥ) 'yo vijñāne tiṣṭhan vijñānādantaro yaṃ vijñānaṃ na veda yasya vijñānaṃ śarīram'; (bṛ. 5-7-22.) ityubhaye 'pi hi śākhino bhedenainaṃ jīvamadhīyate /
children.translated_text:
'He who, abiding in the Self, is different from the Self, whom the Self does not know, whose body is the Self, who controls the Self from within — He is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal'
(<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>, <s>Mādhyandina</s> recension); 'He who, abiding in consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), is different from consciousness, whom consciousness does not know, whose body is consciousness' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.22) — for the followers of both branches study this <s>jīva</s> as different [from the inner controller].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.7:
yajjīvo 'ntaryāmītyuktam / tatsādhakābhāvena nirastamapi punarbādhakākhyaviśeṣayuktyā nirākurvatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - śārīra iti // ityabhidhīyate ityanvayaḥ / ubhaye ityasya viśeṣyapadaṃ darśayati - śākhina iti / kāṇvā mādhyandināścetyarthaḥ / ātmano 'ntara iti mādhyandināḥ vijñānādantara iti kāṇvāḥ / apiśabdaḥ śākhāsamuccaye / antaryāmiṇaḥ iti vipariṇatamatrānuvartate / enamityanūdyajīvamiti vyākhyātam / ato na śārīraścāntaryāmīti śeṣaḥ / tena sautracaśabdo nañaḥ samākarṣakaḥ / na kevalaṃ na smārtaṃ, kintu śārīraśceti samuccaye 'pītyuktaṃ bhavati / tattvapradīpe tu - citprakṛterapyatra pūrvapakṣaviṣayatāmāśritya śrībhūdurgārūpāyāḥ tasyāḥ 'yastejasi tiṣṭhan'; (bṛ. 5-7-14.) 'yastamasi tiṣṭhan'; (bṛ. 5-7-13.) ityādyantaryāmiṇaḥ sakāśādbhedenādhyayanānna sāpyantaryāmīti samuccayārthaścaśabda ityuktam / anena 'hi'; yasmāt 'ubhaye 'pi'; śākhinaḥ 'enaṃ'; jīvamantaryāmiṇaḥ sakāśādbhedena 'adhīyate'; āmananti / tasmādbādhakānnāntaryāmī 'śārīraḥ'; śarīrābhimānī jīva iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / śrutau 'yaḥ pṛthivyāḥ'; iti vākyasyāditve 'pi tadvihāyātmavijñānavākyayoścetanaparatvenobhayaparatvādaikārthyācca te evātrobhayakartṛkabhedādhyayanatayodāhṛte / 'ātmano'; jīvāt 'antaro'; viviktaḥ / evaṃ vijñānaśabdo 'pi 'ya ātmani'; iti śrutisamākhyānājjīvasāmānyaparaḥ / yadyapi bṛhadbhāṣye ātmādiśabdasya caturmukhākhyajīvaparatayā vyākhyātatvādidaṃ sūtraṃ jīvaviśeṣasya yogino 'ntaryāmitvanirāsakamiti / ata eva tattvapradīpe yogino 'ntaryāmitvaṃ nirākarotītyuktam / tathāpi yadā sarvajīvābhimānicaturmukhādapi tanniyāmakatvādinā bhinno 'ntaryāmī tadā kimu tadabhimanyamānasarvajīvāditi kaimutyadyotanāya tatra tathoktiriti candrikāyāmuktatvājjīvasāmānyāntaryāmitvaniṣedhaparatayā pravṛttāyā etatsūtraṭīkāyāḥ bṛhadbhāṣyatattvapradīpavirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.7:
What was stated — that the <s>jīva</s> is the inner controller — though refuted by the absence of supporting evidence, is now refuted again by a specific reasoning in the form of an invalidator. Having presented the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains: '<s>śārīra</s>' (the embodied self). // The syntactic connection is: 'thus it is stated.' He shows the qualified noun for the word 'both' (<s>ubhaye</s>): 'the followers of the branches' (<s>śākhinaḥ</s>). The meaning is: the <s>Kāṇvas</s> and the <s>Mādhyandinas</s>. 'Different from the Self' — thus [read] the <s>Mādhyandinas</s>; 'different from consciousness' — thus [read] the <s>Kāṇvas</s>. The word 'api' (also) is for the accumulation of branches. 'Of the inner controller' carries forward here in modified form. 'This one' (<s>enam</s>) is echoed, and 'the <s>jīva</s>' is the explanation. Therefore, [the remainder is:] 'the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>) is not the inner controller.' Hence the word 'ca' in the <s>sūtra</s> attracts the negative particle. Not only is [it] not [established] through <s>Smṛti</s>, but also the embodied one — even [this negation] in the form of aggregation is stated. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however — taking even <s>citprakṛti</s> (the sentient <s>Prakṛti</s>) as within the scope of the prima facie view, and [noting that] she, in the forms of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Durgā</s>, is also studied as different from the inner controller by the passages 'He who abides in light' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.14), 'He who abides in darkness' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.13) — she too is not the inner controller: thus the word 'ca' is for aggregation: thus it is said. By this: 'for' (<s>hi</s>) — since — 'both' (<s>ubhaye api</s>) — the followers of the branches — 'study' (<s>adhīyate</s>) — recite — 'this' (<s>enam</s>) — the <s>jīva</s> as different from the inner controller. Therefore, because of this invalidator, the inner controller is not the 'embodied one' (<s>śārīra</s>) — the <s>jīva</s> identified with the body: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated. In the <s>Śruti</s>, even though the passage 'He who [abides] in the earth' comes first, setting that aside, the two passages about the Self and consciousness are cited because both pertain to sentient beings, because both recensions [agree on them], and because they have a single import. 'Different from the Self' — different from the <s>jīva</s>; 'antaraḥ' — distinct. Similarly, the word '<s>vijñāna</s>' too refers to the <s>jīva</s> in general, because of the <s>Śruti</s>'s explanatory designation 'He who [abides] in the Self.' Even though in the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> (great commentary), the words 'Self' and the like are explained as referring to a specific <s>jīva</s> — the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] — and therefore this <s>sūtra</s> negates the inner-controller-hood of a particular <s>jīva</s>, the <s>yogin</s> — hence in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> it is said 'it negates the inner-controller-hood of the <s>yogin</s>' — nevertheless, when even from the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] who represents all <s>jīvas</s>, the inner controller is different through being its ruler and the like, how much more so from all <s>jīvas</s> represented by him — to illuminate this <s>kaimutya</s> (a fortiori) argument, it is stated thus there. There is no contradiction of the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> or <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> with this <s>Ṭīkā</s> on the <s>sūtra</s>, which has proceeded with the purport of negating the inner-controller-hood of <s>jīvas</s> in general.
Such a world is always projected from this <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed;

children.text: ramate ca parohyasmin śarīraṃ tasya tajjagat /
children.translated_text: and the Supreme One delights in this [world] — [therefore] the world is His body.
Thus by this statement, there is no contradiction with [the world's] body-hood. // 20 //
// Thus ends the <s>Antaryāmyadhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the inner controller). // 5 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.8:
nanu na viṣṇorantaryāmitvaṃ yuktam / pṛthivyādiśarīratvasya pradhānadharmasyātrokteḥ tasya viṣṇāvasambhavāt / kathaṃ pradhānadharmānuktiḥ pṛthivyādiśarīratvasyaiva taddharmatvādityata āha - śīryata iti // tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / tathā ca 'hi'; yasmārt 'idṛśaṃ'; vartamānajagatsadṛśaṃ kālatrayābādhyaṃ vā 'jagat'; pṛthivyādi asmāt viṣṇoreva 'nityaṃ'; niyataṃ pratikalpaṃ 'śīryate'; naśyati / ātmādicetanānāmapi dehadvārā śīryatā satyaiva / yasmācca 'paraḥ'; paramātmā 'asmin'; jagati sthitassan ramate 'tat'; tasmādeva 'tasya'; viṣṇoḥ 'jagat'; pṛthivyādikaṃ śarīramucyate, na rūḍhyetyarthaḥ / 'na śarīratvāvirodhaḥ'; iti / na pṛthivyādiśarīratvavirodha ityarthaḥ / viṣṇvantaryāmitāyā ataddharmābhilāpokterveti śeṣaḥ / viṣṇoḥ pṛthivyādyātmakatvataccharīratvābhyāṃ pṛthivyādiśarīratvānupapattāvapi śarīraśabdasya pṛthivyādiṣu yogavṛttimāśritya tasmin pṛthivyādiśarīratvavyapadeśopapatteritaratra tadanupapatteriti bhāvaḥ / yattu bṛhadāraṇyabhāṣye -

children.translated_text: The deities such as earth and the like are like a body, because of being under [His] control;
[they] are called the 'body' of that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the great Self.

BBsBhDīp_1,2.5.8:
Now, the inner-controller-hood of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not justified, because the primary attribute of the earth and the like having body-hood is stated here, and that is impossible for <s>Viṣṇu</s>. How is the statement of earth's body-hood the primary attribute? — because the body-hood of the earth and the like is itself that attribute — to this he says: '<s>śīryate</s>' (is projected/dissolved). // The word 'tu' is for emphasis. And thus, 'for' (<s>hi</s>) — since — 'such' (<s>idṛśam</s>) — a world resembling the present one, or one unfalsifiable across the three times — the 'world' (<s>jagat</s>) — the earth and the like — from this <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — 'always' (<s>nityam</s>) — regularly, in every cycle of creation — 'is projected' (<s>śīryate</s>) — dissolves. Even the dissolution of the Self and other sentient beings [occurs] only through the medium of the body. And since the 'Supreme One' (<s>paraḥ</s>) — the <s>Paramātman</s> — 'delights' (<s>ramate</s>) — in 'this' (<s>asmin</s>) world while abiding [in it]; 'therefore' (<s>tat</s>) — for that very reason — the 'world' — the earth and the like — 'is the body' (<s>śarīram</s>) of 'that' (<s>tasya</s>) <s>Viṣṇu</s> — it is called [body], not by conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>): this is the meaning. 'There is no contradiction with body-hood' — there is no contradiction with the body-hood of the earth and the like: this is the meaning. Of [the claim about] <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s inner-controller-hood — because the statement of attributes not belonging to Him [is resolved]: this is the remainder. Even though the impossibility of the earth being <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s body (since <s>Viṣṇu</s> does not have the earth and the like as His nature), and of the earth having body-hood [remains] — the import is: by taking the word '<s>śarīra</s>' (body) as applying to the earth and the like through etymological usage (<s>yogavṛtti</s>), the designation of body-hood for the earth and the like with respect to Him [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] is justified — while elsewhere it is not. But as stated in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Bhāṣya</s> —

children.text: iti pramāṇānusāreṇa pṛthivyāderbrahmaśarīratvaṃ gauṇamityuktam / tatpurāṇādiṣu prapañce brahmakāyatvādyuktisamarthanāyeti na tadvirodhaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: — thus, following the authority [of this passage], the body-hood of the earth and the like with respect to <s>Brahman</s> is secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>): thus it is stated. That [statement is made] for the purpose of supporting the reasoning of body-hood of <s>Brahman</s> and the like in the elaborations found in <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like — hence there is no contradiction. // 5 //
// Thus ends the <s>Antaryāmyadhikaraṇa</s> (topic of the inner controller). // 5 //
// 6. The <s>Adṛśyatvādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of invisibility). //
The attributes of invisibility and the like have been stated as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.1:
atrādhikaraṇe dṛśyatvādyābhāvākhyaliṅgaṃ brahmaṇi samanvīyate / pūrvādhikaraṇatadviṣayasaṅgativiṣayavākyodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ viṣayasaṃśayau sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣaṃ ca sūcayati - adṛśyatvādīti/ 'guṇāḥ'; śubhadharmāḥ / ādipadenānātmyādigrahaṇam / uktā iti / ānandamayasya 'adṛśye'; iti vākyeneti śeṣaḥ / upalakṣaṇametat / antaḥsthasya 'na vijānanti'; (tai.ā. 3-11) ityanena sarvagatasya 'sa yo 'to 'śrutaḥ'; (ai.ā. 3-2-4.) ityanena antaryāmiṇo 'yaṃ pṛthivī na veda'; (bṛ. 5-7-3.) ityavyavahitapūrvādhikaraṇodāhṛtavākyena cetyapi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the mark in the form of the absence of visibility and the like is coordinated (<s>samanvīyate</s>) with <s>Brahman</s>. Indicating the connection with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the subject-passage with its citation, the subject, the doubt, and the reasoned prima facie view, he says: '<s>adṛśyatvādi</s>' (invisibility and the like). // 'Attributes' (<s>guṇāḥ</s>) — auspicious qualities. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), 'non-self-hood' (<s>anātmya</s>) and the like are included. 'Have been stated' (<s>uktāḥ</s>) — the remainder is: of the <s>Ānandamaya</s>, by the passage '<s>adṛśye</s>' (in the invisible). This is representative. By the passage 'they do not know [Him] who is within' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.11) — [this refers to] the one within all. By the passage 'He who is unheard' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.2.4) — [this refers to] the all-pervading one. And by the passage cited in the immediately preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> — 'this earth does not know Him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.3) — [this refers to] the inner controller: this too should be noted.

children.text:
tatra 'yattadadreśyamagrāhyamagotramavarṇamacakṣuḥśrotraṃ tadapāṇipādam /
nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ tadavyayaṃ tadbhūtayoniṃ paripaśyanti
dhīrāḥ'; // (muṃ. 1-1-6.) ityuktvā -
children.translated_text:
There, [in the <s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s>:] 'That which is invisible, ungraspable, without lineage, without color, without eyes or ears,
without hands or feet — eternal, all-pervading, omnipresent, that imperishable,
the source of beings — the wise perceive [it] everywhere.' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.6) — having thus stated —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.2:
uktā ityāvartate / 'uktvā'; ityanantaram āmnāta iti śeṣaḥ / tena ktvāpratyayopapattiḥ / candrikāyāṃ tu - ityuktvā pratīyata iti bhāṣye kriyayoḥ samānakartṛkatvābhāve 'pi ktvāpratyayo 'yadorvaṃśaṃ naraḥ śrutvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate'; itivaddraṣṭavyamityukterapyayamevābhiprāyaḥ / para itītyanantaraṃ vākya iti śeṣaḥ / 'tasmācca'; iti padadvayaṃ bhāṣyakārīyam / tathocetthaṃ yojanā - pūrvaṃ ye adṛśyatvādiguṇā viṣṇoruktāste yatra kasyacidakṣarasyoktāstatrātharvaṇe 'dṛśyatvādiguṇakākṣaraviṣaye 'yattadadreśyamagrāhyam'; ityādyuktvā tathā tatraiva 'yathorṇanābhiḥ'; ityādi 'viśvam'; ityantaṃ vākyaṃ coktvā paṭhitvā anantaramāmnāte -
divyo hyamūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sa bāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Divine, indeed, formless is the Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>); He is both external and internal, unborn;
without <s>Prāṇa</s>, indeed, without mind, pure — He is higher than the highest <s>Akṣara</s> (the imperishable <s>Prakṛti</s>).

BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.2:
'Have been stated' (<s>uktāḥ</s>) carries forward. After 'having stated' (<s>uktvā</s>), 'is taught' is the remainder. By this, the use of the absolutive suffix (<s>ktvā</s>-pratyaya) is justified. In the <s>Candrikā</s>, however, it is said: even though the two actions in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — 'having stated' and 'is perceived' — do not have the same agent, the use of the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix should be understood as in the passage 'having heard the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, a person is freed from all sins' — yet the intention is the same. After 'para' (supreme), the remainder is: 'in the passage.' The two words '<s>tasmāt ca</s>' (and from that) belong to the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>. When thus construed, the syntactic connection is: the attributes of invisibility and the like that were previously stated as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — wherever they are stated as belonging to some <s>Akṣara</s> (imperishable [entity]) — there in the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s>), in the context pertaining to the <s>Akṣara</s> qualified by invisibility and the like, having stated 'That which is invisible, ungraspable' and so forth, and having also stated in the same [text] 'Just as a spider creates and withdraws' and what follows up to 'the universe' — in the subsequent passage that is then taught —

children.text: iti uttaravākye 'tasmādakṣarāt'; prakṛtādakṣarādapi 'paraḥ'; uttamaḥ 'pratīyate'; pratipādyatayā jñāyata iti / anena pūrvoktādṛśyatvasya viṣṇvanyaniṣṭatvākṣepātpūrveṇānandamayādyadhikaraṇena asyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ / adṛśyatvādirūpo viṣayaḥ / kiṃ viṣṇoranyasya veti sandehaḥ / na viṣṇoradṛśyatvādīti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ / adṛśyatvādiviśiṣṭe 'akṣarātsambhavati'; ityakṣaraśabdaśravaṇāttasya ca tatparatvoktyā viṣṇoḥ niravakāśatvāditi pūrvapakṣayuktiśca sūcitā bhavatīti / śrutyarthastu - 'yat'; paravidyāgamyamakṣaraṃ 'tadadreśyaṃ'; dṛśyaśabditacakṣurādijñeyabhinnam / 'agrāhyaṃ'; manogrāhyabhinnam / 'agotraṃ'; na vidyate gotrādikaṃ yasya taddhi tathocyate iti sudhoktervaśiṣṭhādigotrahīnam / 'avarṇaṃ'; prākṛtaśuklādivarṇahīnam / adṛśyatvādiśabdairdṛśyādyanyonyābhāvābhidhīyate iti sudhokteḥ gotravarṇabhinnatvaṃ cārthaḥ / yat 'acakṣuḥśrotraṃ'; prākṛtajñānendriyādiśūnyam / tat 'apāṇipādaṃ'; prākṛtakarmendriyaśūnyaṃ 'nityaṃ'; svarūpanāśarahitaṃ 'vibhuṃ'; samarthaṃ 'sarvagataṃ'; vyāptaṃ 'susukṣmam'; atyantāvyaktaṃ 'yadbhūtayoniṃ'; 'dhīrāḥ'; jñāninaḥ paripaśyanti 'tadakṣaram'; avyayaṃ dehato nāśaśūnyamiti / atra tacchabdasya sarvatrānvayāya trirgrahaṇam / bhūtayonipadaṃ ca sattarkadīpāvalyāṃ bhūtānām ākāśādīnāṃ brahmādicetanānāṃ vā keṣāṃcit strīvyavadhānena vinā svasvadehādevotpādakamiti vyākhyātam / dhīrā ityanenādṛśyatvadṛśyatvayorvirodhaḥ parihṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: — in this subsequent passage, from that <s>Akṣara</s> which is the subject, one who is 'supreme' (<s>paraḥ</s>) — the highest — 'is perceived' — is known as the subject of the teaching. By this, since the invisibility stated earlier is being attributed to an entity other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the connection of this [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] with the <s>Ānandamaya</s> and other preceding <s>adhikaraṇas</s> is by way of objection (<s>ākṣepikī</s>). The subject is the attribute of invisibility and the like. The doubt is: does it belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> or to another? The prima facie view is: the invisibility and the like do not belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. In the [passage] characterized by invisibility and the like, because of hearing the word '<s>Akṣara</s>' (imperishable) in 'from the <s>Akṣara</s> [the universe] arises,' and because of the statement that [the <s>Akṣara</s>] has that as its purport — [therefore,] due to <s>Viṣṇu</s> having no scope [in this passage]: thus the prima facie reasoning is also indicated. The meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>, however, is: 'That which' (<s>yat</s>) — the <s>Akṣara</s> accessible through higher knowledge — is 'invisible' (<s>adreśyam</s>) — different from what is known by the eye and the like, which are denoted by the word 'visible' (<s>dṛśya</s>). 'Ungraspable' (<s>agrāhyam</s>) — different from what is graspable by the mind. 'Without lineage' (<s>agotram</s>) — as the <s>Sudhā</s> commentary states, 'that in which lineage and the like do not exist is thus called' — [meaning] devoid of lineage such as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the like. 'Without color' (<s>avarṇam</s>) — devoid of mundane colors such as white and the like. By the words 'invisibility' and the like, the mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>) of the visible and the like is denoted — as the <s>Sudhā</s> states — hence being different from lineage and color is also the meaning. 'Without eyes or ears' (<s>acakṣuḥśrotram</s>) — devoid of mundane cognitive sense-organs and the like. That [<s>Akṣara</s>] is 'without hands or feet' (<s>apāṇipādam</s>) — devoid of mundane motor organs. 'Eternal' (<s>nityam</s>) — free from destruction of essential nature. 'All-pervading' (<s>vibhum</s>) — capable. 'Omnipresent' (<s>sarvagatam</s>) — pervading [all]. 'Extremely subtle' (<s>susūkṣmam</s>) — utterly unmanifest. 'The source of beings' (<s>bhūtayonim</s>) — the 'wise' (<s>dhīrāḥ</s>) — the knowers — 'perceive everywhere.' 'That <s>Akṣara</s>' is 'imperishable' (<s>avyayam</s>) — devoid of destruction with respect to the body. Here, the word 'tat' (that) is taken three times for connection everywhere. And the word '<s>bhūtayoni</s>' (source of beings) — in the <s>Satarkadīpāvalī</s>, it is explained as: of certain beings — the space-elements (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like, or sentient beings such as <s>Brahmā</s> and the like — one who generates them from His own body directly without the intermediary of a female. By the word '<s>dhīrāḥ</s>' (the wise), the contradiction between invisibility and visibility is resolved.

children.text:
yathorṇanābhissṛjate gṛhṇate ca
yathā pṛthivyāmoṣadhayaḥ sambhavanti /

children.translated_text:
just as hair grows from a living person —
so from the <s>Akṣara</s> (Imperishable), the universe arises here. (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.7)

children.text:
ityuktvā tasmācca 'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ'; (muṃ. 2-1-2.)
iti paraḥ pratīyate -
children.translated_text:
— having thus stated, and [subsequently:] 'from that [<s>Akṣara</s>], He who is higher than the highest'
(<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2) — one who is supreme is perceived —

Just as a spider creates and withdraws,
just as herbs grow from the earth,

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.3:
etadeva dṛṣṭāntoktyā spaṣṭayati - yatheti // 'yathorṇanābhiḥ'; tantuvāyaḥ 'sṛjate'; svopabhuktavastūni tantvātmanā pariṇatāni svadehānniṣkāsayati / 'gṛhṇate'; cakrādyākāratayā bahirniṣkāsitaṃ vastu punarantaḥ svodare gṛhṇāti / tathā viśvaṃ pralaye nigīrṇaṃ sṛṣṭau akṣarātsambhavati / dṛṣṭāntāntaramāha - yatheti / 'oṣadhayaḥ'; aṅkurādayaḥ / dṛṣṭāntāntaramāha - yatheti / 'sato'; jīvavataḥ puruṣāccharīrāt śirasthāḥ keśāḥ, anyāni lomāni tāni / 'iha'; loke 'viśvaṃ'; nānāvidhakāryaṃ 'sambhavati'; jāyate ityarthaḥ / atra brahmaṇo bhūtakāraṇatvaṃ tatkartṛtvarūpaṃ na tūpādānatvamiti vaktumādyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ / aṅkurādijanane pṛthivī bījamiva viśvasṛṣṭau brahma tatkarmāpekṣata iti vaktuṃ dvitīyaḥ / anāyāsena sṛṣṭiriti vaktuṃ tṛtīyaḥ / divya ityādivākyaṃ tu 'divyaḥ'; adbhutaḥ 'amūrto'; niyataparicchinnaparimāṇarahitaḥ / kintu bāhya ābhyantaraśca / aprāṇo hyamanā iti padābhyāṃ ṣoḍaśakalārāhityamucyate / 'śubhraḥ'; śuddhaḥ jaḍāt 'parataḥ akṣarāt'; citprakṛteḥ para iti karmanirṇayaṭīkāyāṃ vyākhyātam/
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.3:
He clarifies this very point through the statement of similes: '<s>yathā</s>' (just as). // 'Just as a spider' (<s>ūrṇanābhi</s>) — the weaver — 'creates' (<s>sṛjate</s>) — ejects from its own body the materials it has consumed, transformed into the form of threads. 'Withdraws' (<s>gṛhṇate</s>) — it takes back into its belly the material that was ejected externally in the form of a web and the like. Likewise, the universe, having been swallowed at dissolution, arises from the <s>Akṣara</s> at creation. He states another simile: '<s>yathā</s>.' '<s>Oṣadhayaḥ</s>' — sprouts and the like. He states yet another simile: '<s>yathā</s>.' 'From a living' (<s>sataḥ</s>) — from a person possessing life — from the body — the 'hair on the head' (<s>keśāḥ</s>) situated on the head, and the other 'body-hair' (<s>lomāni</s>). 'Here' (<s>iha</s>) — in this world, the 'universe' (<s>viśvam</s>) — various types of effects — 'arise' (<s>sambhavati</s>): this is the meaning. Here, the first simile is to state that <s>Brahman</s>'s being the cause of the elements is in the form of being their maker — not as the material cause. The second is to state that, just as earth [requires] a seed for generating sprouts, so <s>Brahman</s> depends on <s>karma</s> for the creation of the universe. The third is to state that creation is effortless. The meaning of the passage 'divine' (<s>divya</s>) and the like, however, is: 'divine' (<s>divyaḥ</s>) — wondrous. 'Formless' (<s>amūrtaḥ</s>) — devoid of fixed, limited dimensions. But He is both external and internal. By the two words 'without <s>Prāṇa</s>' and 'without mind,' the absence of the sixteen <s>kalās</s> (parts) is stated. 'Pure' (<s>śubhraḥ</s>) — untainted. 'Higher than the <s>Akṣara</s>' (<s>parataḥ akṣarāt</s>) — higher than <s>citprakṛti</s> (sentient <s>Prakṛti</s>), the insentient one: thus it is explained in the <s>Karmanirṇaya Ṭīkā</s>.

Therefore he says —
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
The one qualified by the attributes of invisibility and the like — because of the statement of [these] attributes. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.21 |

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.4:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti // itisaṅgatisambhavāt iti śaṅkāsadbhāvācca taduttararūpaṃ sūtramabravīdbādarāyaṇaḥ ityarthaḥ / tatsūtraṃ paṭhati - adṛśyatvādīti //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.4:
He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the conclusion: 'therefore' (<s>ataḥ</s>). // Because the connection [with the previous topic] is possible, and because the doubt exists — therefore, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> stated this <s>sūtra</s> as a reply: this is the meaning. He reads that <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>adṛśyatvādi</s>' (invisibility and the like).

children.text: pṛthivyādidṛṣṭāntamuktvā 'akṣarātsambhavatīha viśvam'; (muṃ. 1-1-7.) ityataḥ paraṃ tatparataḥ parābhidhānāt 'kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate'; (bha.gī. 15-16.) iti smṛteśca prakṛteḥ prāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having stated the illustration of earth and so forth, from the statement 'From the <s>Akṣara</s> (Imperishable), the universe originates here' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.7), and beyond that, due to the designation of one who is supreme beyond that, and from the <s>Smṛti</s> statement 'The immutable one is called <s>Akṣara</s>' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 15.16), there arises the claim for <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.5:
nanvadṛśyatvādikaṃ viṣṇorna cet - tarhi vākyasya nirviṣayatayā aprāmāṇyaṃ syāt ityataḥ pūrvapakṣaṃ viśadayati - pṛthivyādīti // śrutāvūrṇanābhidṛṣṭāntasya prāthamye 'pi tatra sṛjata ityanena kartṛtvamātrapratīteḥ pūrvapakṣānukūlasyopādānatayā jagatkāraṇatvasyāpratīteḥ taṃ parityajya pṛthivyādītyuktam / caḥ samuccaye / tathācetthaṃ yojanā - pṛthivyādidṛṣṭāntamuktvā anantaramuktāt 'akṣarātsaṃbhavatīha viśvam'; ityato vākyāt 'param'; anantaramadhītena 'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ'; iti vākyena 'tatparataḥ'; tasmātkāraṇībhūtādakṣarātparataḥ parasyottamasyoktatvāt, tathā 'kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate'; iti smṛteśca jaḍaprakṛteścitprakṛteścādṛśyatvādiprāptiriti / atrāyaṃ vivekaḥ - yadā jaḍaprakṛteḥ pūrvapakṣaviṣayatā tadākṣaraśabdastatparo hetuḥ tatparataḥ parābhidhānaṃ ca / tasya niravakāśatve akṣarātparata iti ca vyadhikaraṇe pañcamyau / yadā ca citprakṛtestadākṣaraśabdastatparohetuḥ / samānādhikaraṇe pañcamyau / smṛteścetyapi heturiti / smṛtiścātrādhikaraṇe vyākhyātā /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.5:
If the attributes of invisibility and so forth do not belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then the sentence would become authoritative without a referent — with this concern, he elaborates the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) with 'earth and so forth.' Although the spider illustration in the <s>Śruti</s> comes first, since from 'it creates' only mere agency is understood, and since being the material cause of the world — which would favor the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> — is not understood from it, setting that aside, he said 'earth and so forth.' The word 'ca' is used in the sense of conjunction.
