Thus the interpretation is as follows: having stated the illustration of earth and so forth, from the immediately following statement 'From the <s>Akṣara</s>, the universe originates here,' the word 'beyond' refers to the immediately studied statement 'Beyond the <s>Akṣara</s>, there is the Supreme'; 'beyond that' means because the Supreme, the Highest, is declared as beyond that causal <s>Akṣara</s>; and from the <s>Smṛti</s> 'The immutable one is called <s>Akṣara</s>', there arises the claim of invisibility and so forth for both insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> and sentient <s>Prakṛti</s>. Here is the distinction: when the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> concerns insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>, the word <s>akṣara</s> serves as a reason supporting that view, along with the designation of the supreme beyond that; when that reason has no scope, the two ablatives in 'from the <s>akṣara</s>' and 'beyond' are in different grammatical agreement. When it concerns sentient <s>Prakṛti</s>, the word <s>akṣara</s> serves as a reason supporting that view, and the two ablatives are in the same grammatical agreement. 'And from <s>Smṛti</s>' is also a reason. The <s>Smṛti</s> has been explained in this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic).
Due to the word <s>Brahman</s>, and precisely due to the designation of one who is supreme beyond that, the claim belongs to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.6:
pūrvapakṣāntaraṃ vakti - brahmaśabdāditi // 'sa brahmavidyām'; ityādau śrutabrahmaśabdādityarthaḥ / brahmaśabdo viṣṇāveva mukhya iti tasyaiva sādhako netarasyetyato hetvantaramāha - parata iti // vyadhikaraṇe pañcamyau / tathā ca - hiraṇyagarbhākhyādakṣarāt 'parataḥ'; śrītattvātparasya viṣṇorabhidhānādityarthaḥ / evaśabdena hetorniravakāśatvaṃ nātra hetvantaraṃ gaveṣaṇīyamiti sūcayati / hiraṇyagarbhasya prāptirityanvayaḥ / upalakṣaṇametat / 'kartāramīśam'; itīśaśabdaśravaṇāt rudrasya vā adṛśyatvādiprāptiriti vakṣyamāṇamatrāpi draṣṭavyam / asmin pakṣer iśaśabdasya viṣṇau sāvakāśatvaśaṅkāyāmanantaraṃ tatparataḥ parābhidhānādityapi yojyam / atrāpi vyadhikaraṇe pañcamyau /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.6:
He states an alternative <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> with 'due to the word <s>Brahman</s>.' The meaning is: due to the word <s>Brahman</s> heard in passages like 'He, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>...' Since the word <s>Brahman</s> is primarily applicable to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, and therefore establishes only Him and not another, he states an additional reason with 'beyond.' The two ablatives are in different grammatical agreement. Thus: from the <s>Akṣara</s> known as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, 'beyond' — the meaning is that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is supreme beyond <s>Śrī-tattva</s> (the principle of <s>Śrī</s>), is designated. By the word 'eva' (precisely), he indicates that the reason has no scope elsewhere and no other reason need be sought here. The syntactic connection is: the claim belongs to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. This is illustrative. Since the word <s>Īśa</s> (Lord) is heard in 'the maker, the Lord,' there is also the claim of invisibility and so forth for <s>Rudra</s> — this is to be considered here as well, as will be stated later. In this position, when the doubt arises that the word <s>Īśa</s> has scope in referring to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the following phrase 'due to the designation of the supreme beyond that' should also be construed. Here too the two ablatives are in different grammatical agreement.

children.text:
'tamevaṃ vidvānamṛta iha bhavati'; (tai.ā. 3-12-7.) tatkarma haritoṣaṃ yatsā vidyā tanmatiryayā /
atha dve vāva vidye veditavye parācaivāparā ca /
tatra ye vedā yānyaṅgāni yānyupāṅgāni yāni pratyaṅgāni sāparā /
atha parā yayā sa harirveditavyo yo 'sāvadṛśyo nirguṇaḥ paraḥ paramātmā () ityādinā taddharmatvenāvagataparavidyāviṣayatvokterviṣṇurevādṛśyatvādiguṇakaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text:
'One who knows Him thus becomes immortal here' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12.7). That action which pleases <s>Hari</s> is true action; that understanding by which one knows Him is true knowledge.
Now, two kinds of knowledge must be known — the higher and the lower.
Among these, the <s>Vedas</s>, their limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>), sub-limbs (<s>upāṅgas</s>), and auxiliary limbs (<s>pratyaṅgas</s>) constitute the lower knowledge.
The higher knowledge is that by which <s>Hari</s> is to be known — He who is invisible, beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), supreme, the Supreme Self — through such statements declaring Him to be the subject of the higher knowledge by virtue of possessing the attribute of being characterized by invisibility and so forth, it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone who possesses attributes like invisibility. (21)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.7:
evaṃ prāptaṃ pūrvapakṣaṃ pratikṣeptuṃ sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - tamevamiti // 'tamevam'; ityekaṃ śrutivākyam / 'tat'; ityaparaṃ smṛtivākyam / 'atha'; ityanyacchrutivākyam / ādipadena 'tadetadbrahma'; (bṛ.4-5-19.) 'tripādasyāmṛtam'; (ṛ. 10-90-3.) ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / tasya viṣṇordharmastaddharmaḥ tasya bhāvasatattvaṃ teneti vigrahaḥ / prakāre tṛtīyā / avagatatvaṃ prasiddhatvaṃ viṣayatvaviśeṣaṇam / amṛtatvāderupalakṣakametat / atreti śeṣaḥ / sūtre 'nuvṛttasya tattvityasyārtho viṣṇureveti atrādṛśyatvaṃ dṛśyabhinnatvam / tacca svarūpam, na tu gotrādyatyantābhāvavadbrahmabhinnam / tatra tadvattvaṃ brahmasvarūpamiti viśeṣaṃ vaktum adṛśyatvādayo guṇā yasyeti bahuvrīhitvaṃ ca sūcayituṃ śubhadharmārthakaguṇaśabdaprayogaḥ kapratyayaśca / tathācetthaṃ sūtrabhāṣyayojanā - adṛśyatvādiguṇakastattu viṣṇureva / kutaḥ? atra prakaraṇe 'atha parā yayā tadakṣaramadhigamyate'; (muṃ. 1-1-5.) 'tadetadakṣaraṃ brahma'; (muṃ. 2-2-2.) 'puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapobrahma parāmṛtam'; (muṃ. 2-1-10.) iti vākyeṣu tasyādṛśyatvādiguṇakasya paravidyāviṣayatvarūpadharmokteḥ / na ca tasya paravidyāviṣayatvoktāvapi kuto viṣṇutvamiti vācyam / yatastat 'tamevam'; ityādinā taddharmatvenāvagatamiti / atra 'tamevam'; iti śrutau mokṣasādhanajñānaviṣayatvoktyā viṣṇoḥ paravidyāviṣayatvamuktaṃ bhavati / mokṣasādhanavidyāyā eva paravidyātvāt / tatkarmeti smṛtāvapi yaddharituṣṭikaraṃ tadeva karma / yayā 'tanmatiḥ'; hareḥ jñānaṃ bhavati, saiva vidyetyuktatvena tasya paravidyāviṣayatvamucyate / 'dve vidye veditavye'; (muṃ. 1-1-4.) ityatrāpi viṣṇoḥ paravidyāviṣayatvamucyate iti na hetuviśeṣaṇāsiddhiḥ / atheti prakaraṇārambhe / vāvetyavadhāraṇe / cau parasparasamuccaye / tathā ca parā cāparā ca dve vidye jñātavye / 'tatra'; parāparayormadhye 'ye vedāḥ'; ṛgādyāḥ yāni śikṣādiṣaḍaṅgāni 'yānyupāṅgāni'; āyurvedagāndharvādīni / 'yāni pratyaṅgāni'; śiṣṭāḥ kalā vidyāḥ sāparā / athetyarthāntare / yo 'sau 'adṛśyo'; dṛśyādanyo 'nirguṇaḥ'; sattvādihīnaḥ 'paro'; vilakṣaṇaḥ 'paramātmā'; svottamo vyāptaḥ sa hariryayā veditavyaḥ sā ṛgādirūpaiva pareti śrutyarthaḥ / yathaikasya karmaṇaḥ sakāmatvaniṣkāmatvarūpopādhibhedāt pravṛttinivṛttapadoditatvaṃ tathā viṣṇuviṣayakatvakarmādiviṣayakatvarūpopādhibhedādṛgādīnām eva parāparavidyātvopapattiriti bhāvaḥ / na cānuvyākhyāne brahmasūtrasya paravidyātvoktivirodhaḥ / anugrāhyatayā ṛgādīnāmanugrāhakatayā brahmasūtrasya ca paravidyātvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.7:
To refute the established <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, he comments on the <s>sūtra</s> with 'one who knows Him thus.' 'One who knows Him thus' is one <s>Śruti</s> statement. 'That' is another <s>Smṛti</s> statement. 'Now' is yet another <s>Śruti</s> statement. By the word 'and so forth,' passages like 'That is this <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.19) and 'Three-fourths of Him is immortal' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.90.3) are included. The attribute of that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is His essential nature; the compound is analyzed as 'by virtue of that being His nature.' The instrumental case denotes manner. 'Being known' means 'being well-established,' which qualifies 'being the subject.' This is illustrative of immortality and so forth. 'Here' is to be supplied. The meaning of 'tat' (that) connected to the <s>sūtra</s> is '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' Here, 'invisibility' means being different from the visible. That is His essential nature, not something different from <s>Brahman</s> in the way that complete absence of clan-name and such would be. To state the specific point that possessing such attributes constitutes the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s>, and to indicate that it is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound meaning 'one who has attributes like invisibility,' the word <s>guṇa</s> is used in the sense of auspicious attributes, along with the suffix 'ka.' Thus the interpretation of the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s> together is: the one characterized by attributes such as invisibility is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>. How so? Because in this context, in the statements 'The higher knowledge is that by which the imperishable is known' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.5), 'That imperishable is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.2), and '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this — action, austerity, <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme immortal' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.10), there is a declaration of the attribute of being the subject of higher knowledge for the one characterized by invisibility and so forth. Nor should one object: even if being the subject of higher knowledge is stated, how does that establish that He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Because that is known as His attribute from passages like 'One who knows Him thus' and so forth. In the <s>Śruti</s> 'One who knows Him thus,' by declaring Him to be the object of knowledge that is the means to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), the status of <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the subject of higher knowledge is established, since the knowledge that is the means to liberation is indeed the higher knowledge. In the <s>Smṛti</s> too, with 'that action,' whatever action pleases <s>Hari</s> is true action; that understanding by which knowledge of <s>Hari</s> arises is true knowledge — thus His being the subject of higher knowledge is stated. In 'Two kinds of knowledge are to be known' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.4) also, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being the subject of higher knowledge is stated, so there is no failure of the qualifying reason. 'Now' introduces a new topic. 'Indeed' (<s>vāva</s>) is for emphasis. The two instances of 'ca' are for mutual conjunction. Thus both higher and lower knowledge are to be known. Among the higher and the lower, 'the <s>Vedas</s>' means the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and others; the six limbs are <s>Śikṣā</s> and others; 'sub-limbs' are <s>Āyurveda</s>, <s>Gāndharvaveda</s>, and so forth; 'auxiliary limbs' are the remaining arts and sciences — these constitute the lower knowledge. 'Now' introduces another topic. He who is 'invisible' — different from the visible, 'beyond the <s>guṇas</s>' — devoid of <s>sattva</s> and the rest, 'supreme' — of a distinct nature, 'the Supreme Self' — the one who transcends all selves and is all-pervading — that <s>Hari</s>, by which knowledge He is to be known, that knowledge, which is of the form of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and others themselves, is the higher — this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>. Just as a single action becomes the subject of both the <s>pravṛtti</s> (active) and <s>nivṛtti</s> (renunciatory) paths due to the distinction of conditions such as being performed with desire and without desire, similarly the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and others themselves become both higher and lower knowledge due to the distinction of conditions such as having <s>Viṣṇu</s> as their subject versus having ritual actions as their subject — this is the underlying idea. Nor is there any contradiction with the statement in the <s>Anuvyākhyāna</s> that the <s>Brahmasūtra</s> is the higher knowledge, since the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and others are the objects of grace, while the <s>Brahmasūtra</s>'s status as higher knowledge is established through its being the gracious guide.
<s>Sūtra</s> — Oṃ.
Due to the distinguishing attribute and the statement of difference, the other two are not [the referent]. (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.22)
Oṃ.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.8:
taduktaṃ prakṛtiviriñcayoradṛśyatvādiguṇakatvamiti tatsiddhāntahetoḥ parapakṣanirāse 'pi vyāpārāt taddharmokterityanenoktasya paravidyāviṣayatvasya viṣṇoranyatra niravakāśatvānyathānupapattyā nirākṛtamapi viśeṣayuktyā nirākurvatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - viśeṣaṇeti // vyapadeśaśabda ubhayānvayītyāśayenobhayaśrutimāha - ya iti / 'bhedaḥ'; anyatvam / caśabdasya na kevalaṃ dharmokteḥ, arthāt kintu viśeṣaṇabhedavyapadeśābhyām iti samuccayārthatvasya spaṣṭatvānna tasyārtha uktaḥ / prakṛtiḥ viriñca ityanena itarā itaraśceti vigrahāśrayeṇetaraśabdārtho 'bhihitaḥ / ubhayatrādṛśyatvādiguṇaka ityanuṣajyate / prakṛtipakṣe liṅgavipariṇāmaḥ / tathā ca 'yassarvajñaḥ'; iti vākye tasyādṛśyatvādiguṇakasya 'viśeṣaṇāt'; sārvajñyādiviśeṣaṇokterna dṛśyatvādiguṇā jaḍaprakṛtiḥ / evaṃ 'tasmāt'; iti vākye viriñcasya tasmādakṣarājjanyatvarūpabhedakadharmoktyā bhedavyapadeśānnādṛśyatvādiguṇo viriñca iti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.8:
It was stated that the attribute of being characterized by invisibility and so forth belongs to <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). Even though the opposing view has been refuted by the <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusive) reason that the status of being the subject of higher knowledge, stated as His attribute, has no scope in anything other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> and cannot be otherwise explained, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> that refutes it additionally through specific reasoning, and comments with 'distinguishing attribute.' Intending that the word <s>vyapadeśa</s> (designation) connects with both, he cites both <s>Śruti</s> passages with 'who.' '<s>Bheda</s>' means otherness. The word 'ca' does not merely mean 'due to the statement of His attributes'; rather, its conjunctive meaning in 'due to the distinguishing attribute and the statement of difference' being self-evident, its meaning is not separately stated. By '<s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Viriñca</s>,' the meaning of the word <s>itara</s> (other) is explained through the analysis 'one other and the other.' 'The one characterized by invisibility and so forth' is carried forward in both cases. In the case of <s>Prakṛti</s>, there is a change in grammatical gender. Thus, in the statement 'He who is omniscient,' due to the distinguishing attribute of omniscience and the like stated for the one characterized by invisibility, insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> possessing visible attributes is not the referent. Similarly, in the statement 'From that,' due to the statement of difference in the form of the distinguishing property that <s>Viriñca</s> is produced from that <s>Akṣara</s>, <s>Viriñca</s> who is characterized by invisibility and the like is not the referent — this is the interpretation.

children.text: 'yassarvajñassarvavidyasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ'; (muṃ. 1-1-9.) iti viśeṣaṇānna prakṛtiḥ / 'tasmādetadbrahma nāma rūpamannaṃ ca jāyate'; (muṃ. 1-1-9.) iti bhedavyapadeśānna viriñcaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who is omniscient, who knows all, whose austerity is of the nature of knowledge' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9) — due to this distinguishing attribute, it is not <s>Prakṛti</s>. 'From that are born this <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), name, form, and food' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9) — due to this statement of difference, it is not <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.9:
ātharvaṇe 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit'; ityataḥ pūrvavākye 'tapasā cīyate brahma'; (muṃ 1-1-8.) ityatra parabrahmatapasā sambadhyata ityuktam / tat tapaśśabdasyālocanārthatayājñānapratītau tannirāsāya 'yasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ'; iti vākyāntaraṃ pravṛttam / tasya yasya 'tapaḥ'; ālocanakriyā 'jñānamayaṃ'; tadātmakameva na saṃśayādyātmakamityarthaḥ / kutastapasaḥ santāpānyapūrṇayathārthajñānātmakatvamityākāṅkṣāyāṃ tasya sarvajñatvādāptakāmatvāditi hetupradarśanāya 'yassarvajñaḥ'; iti pūrvavākyopanyāsaḥ / tadarthastu - 'yassarvajñaḥ'; sarvaviṣayakasāmānyajñānavān 'sarvavit'; sarvaviṣayakaviśeṣajñānavāṃśca / sarvasya labdhā sarvakāmaḥ sarvotpādakoveti / tattvapradīpe tu - vidasattāyāmiti dhātuvyākhyānāt sarvatra vidyate iti sarvavidityuktam / 'yasya yaḥ'; iti yacchabdadvayasya 'tasmāt'; akṣarāt 'etadbrahma'; caturmukhākhyaṃ 'nāma rūpamannaṃ'; tadabhimānidaivataṃ cotpadyata iti uttaravākyagatatacchabdenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.9:
In the <s>Ātharvana</s> (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s>), in the statement preceding 'He who is omniscient, who knows all,' the word <s>tapas</s> (austerity) in 'By austerity, <s>Brahman</s> is increased' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.8) was connected with the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Since the word <s>tapas</s> has the meaning of contemplation, when the understanding of ignorance would arise, to negate that, the subsequent statement 'whose austerity is of the nature of knowledge' was introduced. The meaning is: His austerity — the act of contemplation — is 'of the nature of knowledge,' that is, it is of the very nature of knowledge itself, not of the nature of doubt and the like. When the question arises as to how austerity, which involves exertion, can be of the nature of complete, accurate knowledge, to demonstrate the reason — namely His omniscience and thus His being one whose desires are fulfilled — the preceding statement 'He who is omniscient' is cited. Its meaning is: 'He who is omniscient' — possessing general knowledge of all objects; 'who knows all' — possessing specific knowledge of all objects as well. He is the obtainer of all, the one of all desires, the originator of all. However, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, since the root 'vid' is explained in the sense of existence, 'all-knowing' is explained as 'He who exists everywhere.' The two relative pronouns 'whose' connect with the subsequent statement: 'From that' <s>Akṣara</s>, 'this <s>Brahman</s>' — known as the four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>) — 'name, form, and food' together with the presiding deities who identify with them, are born.
The lower <s>Akṣara</s> (Imperishable) is that <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) which is of insentient nature;

children.text: śrīḥ parā prakṛtiḥ proktā cetanā viṣṇusaṃśrayā //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (the Goddess of Fortune) is declared to be the higher <s>Prakṛti</s>, sentient and dependent upon <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
They call Her the supreme <s>Akṣara</s>; the <s>Akṣara</s> that is supreme beyond that
Is <s>Hari</s> alone, possessing all attributes — thus three <s>Akṣaras</s> are declared.

children.text: iti skānde tryakṣarābhidhānādakṣarātparataḥ para ityapi viśeṣaṇameva /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, due to the statement of three <s>Akṣaras</s>, 'the Supreme beyond the <s>Akṣara</s>' is also a distinguishing attribute only [establishing <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not <s>Prakṛti</s> or <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.10:
nanu na viṣṇoradṛśyatvādiguṇakatvaṃ, parataḥ parābhidhānenākṣaraśruteḥ tatra niravakāśatvādityato viśeṣaṇabhedavyapadeśāditi sūtrakhaṇḍasyārthāntaramāha - aparamiti // tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / 'akṣaratrayam'; akṣarasya trayarm 'iritam'; akṣaraṃ trividhaṃ proktam iti yāvat / tisro vidhāḥ vyaktinirdeśapūrvakaṃ darśayati - aparamiti / yā yadaparamakṣaraṃ sā jaḍarūpikā prakṛtireva / yā yatparamakṣaraṃ 'proktā'; proktaṃ vṛddhaistāṃ tat yā viṣṇusaṃśrayā parā uttamā cetanā prakṛtiḥ śrīḥ lakṣmīḥ tāṃ prāhuḥ / yatparataḥ paramakṣaramīritaṃ tajjaḍaprakṛteḥ parāchrītattvādakhilaguṇaṃ harimeva prāhuriti smṛtyarthaḥ / iti skānde ityasya 'tryakṣarābhidhānāt'; akṣaratraividhyasyoktatvādityanenānvayaḥ / akṣarātparataḥ para ityapīti / itivākyoktamakṣarātparataḥ paratvaṃ viruddhamiti vācyam / 'aparam'; iti skānde tryakṣarābhidhānāt akṣarāntarātparādasyākṣarasya paratvopapatteriti yojanā / akṣaratrayābhidhānena akṣarātparataḥ para ityatra sāmānādhikaraṇyena vaiyadhikaraṇyena vā anvayo darśitaḥ / prameyadīpe tu - akṣarācchrītatvātparataḥ paro 'tyuttama iti tadbhāṣyadiśā śrutyartha uktaḥ / anenākṣarātparataḥ para ityapi tasyaiva viśeṣaṇaṃ, na tu anyasya / na cākṣarātparataḥ paratvaṃ viruddhamiti vācyam / bhedavyapadeśāt / 'akṣaratrayamīritam'; ityakṣarāṇāmavāntarabhedokteḥ pāṇḍavasyārjunasya svādhamakārtavīryārjunādiva akṣarātparādakṣarāntarādasyākṣarasya paratvopapattiriti sūtrakhaṇḍasyārthāntaramuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.10:
Objection: <s>Viṣṇu</s> does not possess the qualities of invisibility and so forth, because the <s>akṣara</s> (imperishable) in the <s>śruti</s> is described as 'higher than the highest,' leaving no scope [for <s>Viṣṇu</s>] there. Therefore, he states another meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>-section 'due to the statement of difference in the qualifying attributes' — beginning with 'the lower.' The particle 'tu' is used in the sense of emphasis. '<s>Akṣaratrayam</s>' — the threefold nature of <s>akṣara</s> has been 'declared'; that is to say, the imperishable has been spoken of as threefold. He shows the three kinds with specific designation — beginning with 'the lower': That which is the lower <s>akṣara</s> is indeed the insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). That which is the higher <s>akṣara</s>, 'declared' by the elders — that is the supreme, sentient <s>Prakṛti</s> dependent on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, namely <s>Śrī</s> <s>Lakṣmī</s> — thus they call her. That which is the highest imperishable, beyond [even the higher], is said to be <s>Hari</s> himself, possessed of all qualities, being beyond the insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> and the <s>Śrī</s>-principle — this is the meaning of the <s>smṛti</s>. The phrase 'in the <s>Skānda</s>' connects with 'because of the declaration of the three <s>akṣaras</s>'; meaning: because the threefold nature of <s>akṣara</s> has been stated therein. [Objection:] 'Higher than the <s>akṣara</s>' — one might say this statement of being higher than the <s>akṣara</s> is contradictory. [Reply:] 'The lower' — in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, because of the declaration of the three <s>akṣaras</s>, the superiority of this <s>akṣara</s> over another higher <s>akṣara</s> is established — this is the interpretation. Through the declaration of the three <s>akṣaras</s>, the syntactic connection of 'higher than the <s>akṣara</s>' is shown either through co-reference or through reference to different substrata. In the <s>Prameyadīpa</s>, however: 'Higher than <s>akṣara</s>, i.e., the <s>Śrī</s>-principle, the supremely highest' — thus the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is stated following the direction of that <s>bhāṣya</s>. By this, 'higher than the <s>akṣara</s>' is a qualifier of Him alone, not of another. Nor should it be said that being higher than the <s>akṣara</s> is contradictory — because of the statement of difference. Since the sub-distinctions among the <s>akṣaras</s> are stated in '<s>akṣaratrayam</s> has been declared,' just as <s>Arjuna</s> the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> is superior to <s>Kārtavīryārjuna</s> of his own abode, so the superiority of this <s>akṣara</s> over another higher <s>akṣara</s> is established — thus another meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>-section has been stated.

children.text:
'juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśasya mahimānamiti vītaśokaḥ';
(muṃ. 3-1-2.) iti bhedavyapadeśādīśapadaprāpto 'pi na rudraḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: 'When he sees the other, the <s>Īśa</s> (Lord), and His greatness, being well-served, he becomes free from sorrow' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.2) — because of this statement of difference, even though the word '<s>Īśa</s>' might indicate him, <s>Rudra</s> is not [the referent]. (22)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.11:
nanu 'anyam'; itiśabdaśravaṇādadṛśyatvādiguṇako rudraḥ kiṃ na syāditi śaṅkottaratayāpi bhedavyapadeśānnetara iti sūtrāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - juṣṭamiti // yadyapi tathāpītyarthe 'piśabdaḥ / rudro 'pīti samuccaye vā / na kevalaṃ pūrvahetoḥ, kintu bhedavyapadeśādapīti samuccaye vā / rudra itītaraśabdasyārthāntaroktiḥ / na cetaraśabdasya jaḍaprakṛtiviriñcarudraparatve dvivacanānupapattiriti vācyam / viriñcirudrayoścetanatvenaikīkṛtatvāt / tathā ca yadyapīśaśabdādrudro 'pyadṛśyatvādiguṇakatvena 'prāptaḥ'; pratītaḥ tathāpi 'juṣṭam'; iti vākye pravṛttaviṣṇvākhyākṣarasyeśaśabditarudrādanyatvavyapadeśādapi nādṛśyatvādiguṇako rudra iti yojanā / śrutistu - ānandamayādhikaraṇe vyākhyātā /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.11:
Objection: Since the word 'other' is heard, why should <s>Rudra</s>, who possesses the qualities of invisibility and so forth, not be [the referent]? In response to this doubt as well, he explains the <s>sūtra</s>-portion 'not the other, because of the statement of difference' — beginning with 'well-served.' The particle 'api' (even though) is used in the sense of 'nevertheless.' Or, the word 'api' with '<s>Rudra</s>' is in the sense of aggregation. Not only because of the previous reason, but also because of the statement of difference — or it is aggregation. '<s>Rudra</s>' is stated as the meaning of the word '<s>itara</s>' (the other). Nor should it be objected that if the word '<s>itara</s>' refers to the insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), and <s>Rudra</s>, the dual number would be inapplicable — because <s>Viriñca</s> and <s>Rudra</s> are unified as sentient beings. Thus, even though <s>Rudra</s> too is 'understood' through the word '<s>Īśa</s>' as possessing the qualities of invisibility and so forth, nevertheless, because in the sentence 'well-served' there is a statement of the otherness of <s>Rudra</s> (designated by the word '<s>Īśa</s>') from the <s>akṣara</s> called <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is the subject, <s>Rudra</s> who possesses the qualities of invisibility is not [the referent] — this is the interpretation. The <s>śruti</s>, however, has been explained in the <s>Ānandamayādhikaraṇa</s>.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
[<s>Brahman</s> is the referent] because of the description of [its] form. (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.23)
<s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text: 'yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ kartāramīśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim'; (muṃ. 3-1-3.) iti /
children.translated_text: 'When the seer sees the golden-hued one, the maker, the <s>Īśa</s> (Lord), the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person), the source of <s>Brahmā</s>' (<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.1.3).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.12:
yuktyantareṇa viṣṇorevādṛśyatvādiguṇakatvaṃ sādhayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā tadupāttaśrutimevodāharati - rūpopanyāseti // iti rūpopanyāsādityanvayaḥ / sūtre caśabdo yuktisamuccaye / tathā ca - na kevalaṃ dharmokteḥ, kintvadṛśyatvādiguṇakasya 'yadā'; iti śrutau śuddharukmarūpokteścādṛśyatvādiguṇako viṣṇureveti yojanā / atra yadeti vākyasya 'tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaiti'; (muṃ. 3-1-3.) iti vākyaśeṣeṇānvayaḥ / paśyatīti paśyo draṣṭā jīvaḥ / yadā 'rukmavarṇaṃ'; śuddhahemavarṇaṃ 'brahmayoniṃ'; hiraṇyagarabhakāraṇaṃ, ata eva jagataḥ kartāraṃ 'puruṣaṃ'; pūrṇaṣaḍguṇam / 'svasyeśaṃ'; viṣṇuṃ 'paśyate'; paśyati tadāsau 'vidvān'; jīvanmuktaḥ 'puṇyapāpe'; aprārabdhe aniṣṭapuṇyaṃ pāpaṃ ca vidhūya 'nirañjanaḥ'; jñānottaravikarmakṛtāśucitvādidoṣarahitaḥ añjanākhyāvidyārahita iti sudhokterajñānarahito vā 'paramaṃ sāmyaṃ'; pūrṇānandatvādisāmyaṃ nirduḥkhatvādisāmyaṃ vā 'upaiti'; prāpnotīti śrutyarthaḥ / tattvodyotaṭīkāyāṃ tu iyaṃ śrutiḥ muktaparatayā vyākhyātā / paramamityetadabhivyaktamiti ca vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.12:
Having read the <s>sūtra</s> which establishes that the qualities of invisibility and so forth belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone through another reasoning, he cites the <s>śruti</s> employed therein — beginning with '<s>rūpopanyāsa</s>' (description of form). The syntactic connection is: 'because of the description of form.' The word 'ca' (and) in the <s>sūtra</s> is for aggregation of reasons. Thus: not only because of the statement of the attribute, but also because in the <s>śruti</s> beginning with 'when,' the pure golden form is described for the one possessing the qualities of invisibility — therefore the one possessing the qualities of invisibility is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — this is the interpretation. Here the sentence beginning with 'when' has its syntactic connection with the remainder of the sentence: 'then the wise one, shaking off merit and demerit, becomes stainless and attains supreme equality' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.3). 'The seer' — the one who sees, the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>). When [he sees] the one of 'golden hue' — of the color of pure gold; 'the source of <s>Brahmā</s>' — the cause of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and hence the maker of the world; the '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — full of the six attributes; 'his own <s>Īśa</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'sees' — perceives; then that one, being a 'wise one' — one liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>); shaking off 'merit and demerit' — the non-commenced (<s>aprārabdha</s>) undesirable merit and sin; becoming 'stainless' — free from defects such as impurity caused by actions contrary to knowledge after attaining knowledge, or free from ignorance called <s>añjana</s>, or according to <s>Sudha</s>, free from ignorance; attains 'supreme equality' — equality in full bliss and the like, or equality in freedom from suffering and the like — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. In the <s>Tattvodyota</s> commentary, however, this <s>śruti</s> has been explained as pertaining to the liberated state. And 'supreme' has been explained as meaning 'fully manifest.'

children.text:
'eko nārāyaṇa āsīnna brahmā na ca śaṅkaraḥ / sa munirbhūtvā
samacintayat / tata ete vyajāyanta viśvo hiraṇyagarbho 'gniryamo varuṇarudrendrā iti / tasya haitasya paramasya nārāyaṇasya catvāri rūpāṇi śuklaṃ raktaṃ raukmaṃ kṛṣṇamiti / sa etānyetebhyo 'bhyacīkḷpat / vimiśrāṇi vyamiśrayat'; /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone existed; there was no <s>Brahmā</s> nor <s>Śaṅkara</s>. He, becoming a sage, contemplated. From that [contemplation] these were born — <s>Viśva</s> (<s>Vāyu</s>), <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and so on. Of this supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> there are four forms — white, red, golden, and dark. He fashioned these [forms] for these [beings]. He mixed the mixed ones.'

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.6.13:
nanu brahmādīnāmapi rūpasadbhāvātkuto rūpopanyāsenāsya viṣṇutvaniścaya ityata āha - eka iti // 'idamagre'; ityupaskriyate / ata eva nyāyadīpikāyāṃ jagadādāvityuktam / hetyāsvādane / etebhya iti tādarthye caturthī / tathā ca idamasya jagato 'gre pralaye nārāyaṇaḥ 'ekaḥ'; svatantra āsīt / na tadā caturmukhaśaṅkarau, na svasvavyāpārāvāstām / 'saḥ'; viṣṇustadā 'muniḥ'; mananaśīlo maunī vā bhūtvā 'samacintayat'; ete jāyantāmiti dhyānarūpāṃ cintāmakarot / 'tataḥ'; tasya cintanādete vyajāyanta / ke te? yo 'viśvo'; vāyuḥ, yaśca hiraṇyagarbhaḥ, ye 'gnyādaya eta ityarthaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - 'tasya'; śrutyādiprasiddhasya 'etasya'; sarvajīvaśarīragasya 'paramasya'; sarvottamasya nārāyaṇasya 'rūpāṇi'; varṇāścatvāri bhavanti / kāni tāni? śuklādīni / kiñjātaḥ? 'saḥ'; nārāyaṇaḥ pūrvameva 'vimiśrāṇi'; svena miśrīkṛtāni rūpāṇi 'etebhyo'; vāyuprabhṛtyuktadevānāmarthe 'abhyacākḷpat'; kḷptānyakarot / tāni vimiśrāṇi punarapi 'vyamiśrayat'; mānuṣādau viśeṣeṇa miśrīcakāra yadvā - sa etāni rūpāṇi vyamiśrayat, vimiśrāṇi caitebhyo 'bhyacīkḷpadityarthaḥ / śuddhāni rūpāṇi tu svasyaivākaroditi bhāvaḥ / atrādyayojanā tattvapradīpaṭīkayoruktā / dvitīyā tu ṭīkāyāmiti dhyeyam /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.13:
Objection: Since forms exist for <s>Brahmā</s> and others too, how can the identity as <s>Viṣṇu</s> be determined through the description of form? To this he says — beginning with 'alone.' The phrase 'in the beginning of this' is supplied. Hence in the <s>Nyāyadīpikā</s> it is said 'at the beginning of the world.' The root 'he' is in the sense of tasting/enjoying. The fourth case ending in 'for these' is in the sense of purpose. Thus: in the beginning of this world, during dissolution, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> 'alone' — independently — existed. At that time the four-faced (<s>Brahmā</s>) and <s>Śaṅkara</s> did not exist, nor were they engaged in their respective functions. 'He' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — then becoming a 'sage' — one given to reflection, or a silent one — 'contemplated'; he performed contemplation in the form of meditation, [wishing] 'let these be born.' 'From that' — from his contemplation, these were born. Who are they? '<s>Viśva</s>' is <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and <s>Agni</s> and the others — this is the meaning. Then what? He says: 'Of this' — well-known through <s>śruti</s> and so forth; 'this one' — who dwells in the bodies of all living beings; 'the supreme' — the highest of all — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s 'forms' — colors — are four. What are they? White and so on. How did this come about? 'He' — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — previously 'mixed' — forms mixed by himself — he 'fashioned' — made ready — 'for these' — for the purpose of the gods beginning with <s>Vāyu</s> mentioned above. Those mixed ones he further 'intermixed' — particularly mixed in the human realm and so forth. Alternatively: he intermixed these forms, and fashioned the mixed ones for these — this is the meaning. But the pure forms he made for himself alone — this is the import. Here the first interpretation is stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> and the commentary. The second, however, is in the commentary alone — this should be noted.
Therefore, such forms of such kind are described as belonging to Him alone. (23)
Thus ends the <s>Adṛśyatvādhikaraṇa</s> (section on invisibility). (6)

<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.6.14:
Then what [follows]? He says — beginning with 'therefore.' Therefore, because of the mixing, the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is 'of such kind' — pure, of the nature of white and other [pure colors] alone, not mixed like the forms of <s>Vāyu</s> and others — this is the meaning. Although here only the passage beginning with 'of this supreme one' should be cited as the illustration, since it is relevant to the topic at hand, and not the passage beginning with 'One <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,' nevertheless, for establishing the meaning of 'for these,' that portion has been cited as illustration. The word 'iti' [indicates]: 'for' — since by the cited passage, the 'forms' — the pure golden and other forms — are described as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, and not to others, therefore one should not raise the objection of purposelessness — this is the meaning. By this, although the word 'form' in the <s>sūtra</s> is used in a general sense, it refers specifically to the pure form. And that [pure form] does not exist elsewhere. The attribute perceived in connection with <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun) in 'He is to be meditated upon' is also mixed alone — thus the inapplicability of the inferential mark elsewhere has been stated.
Thus ends the <s>Adṛśyatvādhikaraṇa</s> (section on invisibility). (6)
Section 7: <s>Vaiśvānarādhikaraṇa</s> (Section on <s>Vaiśvānara</s>).

children.text: adṛśyatvādiguṇeṣu sarvagatatvaṃ 'yastvetamevaṃ prādeśamātramabhivimānamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaramupāste'; (chāṃ. 5-18-1.) iti vaiśvānarasyoktamiti //
children.translated_text: Among the qualities of invisibility and so forth, the all-pervadingness — 'Whoever meditates on the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, who is a span in measure, the one who is the measure' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.18.1) — thus it has been stated regarding <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.1:
atrādhikaraṇe pācakatvādyanekaliṅgasamanvayasiddhyarthaṃ brahmaṇi vaiśvānaranāmasamanvayaḥ kriyate / pūrvādhikaraṇasaṅagtiṃ viṣayavākyodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ viṣayādikaṃ sūcayati - adṛśyatvādīti // uktamityasyāvṛttiḥ śrutāviti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca - gatādhikaraṇodāhṛtamuṇḍakaśrutyuktādṛśyatvādiguṇeṣu madhye 'nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagatam'; (muṃ. 1-1-6.) ityanena yatsarvagatatvamuktaṃ tacchabdogaśrutau 'yastvetam'; ityanena vaiśvānarasyoktamiti yojanā / anena chandogaśrutisthavaiśvānaraśabdasyānyaniṣṭhatvākṣepamukhena pūrvoktasarvagatatvāderanyaniṣṭhatvākṣepātpūrveṇāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / vaiśvānaro viṣayaḥ, viṣṇuranyo veti sandehaśca sūcitaḥ / śrutyarthastu - 'yastu'; adhikārī 'prādeśamātraṃ'; dehahṛdaye tāvatparimāṇakam / tattvapradīparītyādhikāryapekṣayā prādeśamātramiti vā / 'abhivimānam'; abhito vigataṃ mānaṃ maryādā yasya taṃ, sarvagatam iti yāvat / 'ātmānam'; ātataguṇam 'etaṃ'; śarīrasthaṃ 'vaiśvānaraṃ'; tadākhyaviṣṇum 'evaṃ'; vakṣyamāṇarītyā upāste 'so 'nnamatti'; (chāṃ. 5-18-1.) svayogyabhogyamanubhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section), for the purpose of establishing the consistency of multiple inferential marks such as the quality of being the digestive fire, the name <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is shown to be consistent with <s>Brahman</s>. He indicates the topic, the subject-verse citation, and the subject matter along with the connection to the previous section — beginning with 'the qualities of invisibility.' The repetition of 'stated' is completed with 'in the <s>śruti</s>.' Thus: among the qualities of invisibility and so forth stated in the <s>Muṇḍaka</s> <s>śruti</s> cited in the previous section, the all-pervadingness stated by 'eternal, all-pervading, omnipresent' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.6) — that [all-pervadingness] is stated regarding <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s> by 'whoever thus [meditates on] this one' — this is the interpretation. By this, through the objection that the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s> refers to something other [than <s>Brahman</s>], and thereby the objection that the previously stated all-pervadingness and other [qualities] refer to something other, the objection-based connection with the previous [section] has been stated. The doubt is also indicated: is <s>Vaiśvānara</s> the topic, or is <s>Viṣṇu</s> different [from <s>Vaiśvānara</s>]? The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is: 'whoever' — the qualified practitioner — [meditates on the one who is] 'a span in measure' — of the extent of the heart in the body; or, according to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, 'a span in measure' is relative to the practitioner. '<s>Abhivimāna</s>' — one whose measure (limit) is gone on all sides — meaning all-pervading. '<s>Ātman</s>' — one whose attributes are extended; 'this' — dwelling in the body; '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> bearing that name; 'thus' — in the manner to be described — worships; 'he eats food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.1) — he experiences what is fit to be enjoyed by him.

Therefore he says —
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
<s>Vaiśvānara</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>] because of the specification by a word that is common [to both fire and <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.24)
<s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text: agnāviṣṇvoḥ sādhāraṇasya vaiśvānaraśabdasya viṣṇāveva prasiddhātmaśabdena viśeṣaṇādvaiśvānaro viṣṇureva // 24 //
children.translated_text: The word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>,' which is common to [the sacrificial] fire and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is specified by the well-known word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self) as referring to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; therefore <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. (24)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti // sādhāraṇasyetyanantaramapīti śeṣaḥ / sādhāraṇyaṃ sāmyam / tatra śruternobhayatra prasiddhatvarūpaṃ, vaiśvānaraśabdasyānyatraiva prasiddhatvāt / kintu śruteḥ prasiddhato liṅgena sāmyarūpaṃ, tadapi niravakāśatvena prakāreṇa, vaiśvānaraśruteḥ viṣṇau prasiddhyabhāvena tatra niravakāśatvātpūrvoktasarvagatatvasyāpi viṣṇoranyatra niravakāśatvāt / tathā ca - yadyapi agnāviṣṇvoḥ pratijñāviṣayayoḥ satoḥ pūrvapakṣasādhakavaiśvānaraśabdo niravakāśatvena prakāreṇottarapakṣasādhakaliṅgasādhāraṇaḥ / śrutiliṅgayorniravakāśatvena sāmye 'pi liṅgācchrutiḥ prabalā tasmādagnireveti prāptam / tathāpi sādhāraṇasyāpi vaiśvānaraśabdasya viṣṇvekaniṣṭhatayā śrutyādisiddhena 'ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram'; ityātmaśabdena 'viśeṣaṇāt'; viśeṣitatvādviṣṇuparatvasambhavāt / prasiddhyāderanyathopapannatvena nirṇayakāraṇābhāvācchabdaviśeṣādātmaśabdādvaiśvānaro viṣṇureva, 'na devatābhūtaṃ ca'; ityāvṛttyā sūtrabhāṣyayoryojanā / anena nirṇayenaiva pūrvapakṣaḥ sūcitaḥ / atra pakṣe liṅgaprābalyanirāsāya sādhāraṇyoktiḥ / siddhāntaśruteḥ sāvakāśatvajñāpanāya sādhāraṇyoktiriti kecit / yadvā - bhāṣyaṭīkāsvārasyādanirṇayenaiva pūrvapakṣaḥ / atra pakṣe sādhāraṇyaṃ prati dharmitvaṃ śabdasyaiva, na liṅgasyāpi / naraśabdaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ sambhavadvṛttikaḥ / tathāpi prasiddhamukhena niravakāśatvena liṅgasya sādhāraṇaśca / tataḥ pūrvottarapakṣasādhakayoḥ samabalatvādanirṇayaḥ / tathāpyubhayatra sādhāraṇasyāpi vaiśvānaraśabdasyetyādikā yojanā draṣṭavyā /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.2:
He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusion) — with 'ata' (therefore). // After 'sādhāraṇasya' (of what is common), 'api' (also) is to be supplied. <s>Sādhāraṇya</s> (commonality) means equality. In this regard, the commonality is not in the form of being well-known in both [<s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>] based on <s>Śruti</s>, since the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is well-known only elsewhere [i.e., in reference to <s>Agni</s>]. Rather, the commonality is in the form of equality through <s>liṅga</s> (indicative mark) based on the well-known usage in <s>Śruti</s>, and even that is in the manner of having no scope — because the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>Śruti</s> has no well-known application to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, hence having no scope there, and because the previously stated all-pervasiveness also has no scope for <s>Viṣṇu</s> elsewhere. And thus — although the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, which supports the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view), is common with the <s>liṅga</s> supporting the <s>uttarapakṣa</s> (final view) in the manner of having no scope, with both <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> being subjects of the thesis; and although when <s>Śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s> are equal in having no scope, <s>Śruti</s> is stronger than <s>liṅga</s>, hence it would follow that it is <s>Agni</s> alone — nevertheless, because the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, though common, has exclusive reference to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, through the word '<s>Ātman</s>' established by <s>Śruti</s> and other means in '<s>ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram</s>' (the Self as <s>Vaiśvānara</s>), and because 'viśeṣaṇāt' (due to qualification) — since being qualified makes reference to <s>Viṣṇu</s> possible; and because the well-known usage and the rest are explained otherwise, there being no cause for determination [in favor of <s>Agni</s>], from the specific word, namely the word '<s>Ātman</s>', <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — this is the interpretation of the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s> through the repetition of 'na devatābhūtaṃ ca' (and not a deity or element). By this very determination, the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is indicated. In this view, the statement of commonality is for negating the predominance of <s>liṅga</s>. Some say the statement of commonality is for indicating that the <s>Śruti</s> of the <s>siddhānta</s> has scope. Alternatively — based on the natural import of the <s>bhāṣya</s> commentary, the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is through non-determination itself. In this view, the subject-hood with respect to commonality belongs to the word alone, not also to <s>liṅga</s>. The word 'nara' is common and has a possible application. Even so, through the face of well-known usage, <s>liṅga</s> is also common in the manner of having no scope. Therefore, due to the equal strength of what supports the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> and <s>uttarapakṣa</s>, there is non-determination. Even so, the interpretation beginning with 'of the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s> which is common to both' should be examined.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
That which is remembered (<s>smaryamāṇam</s>) would serve as an inferential indicator (<s>anumānam</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.25 |

children.text:
ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ /
(bha.gī. 15-14.) iti smaryamāṇamatrāpi sa evocyate ityasyānumāpakam /
children.translated_text: 'I, having become <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, dwelling in the bodies of living beings' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 15.14) — what is thus remembered (<s>smaryamāṇam</s>) serves as an inferential indicator (<s>anumāpakam</s>) that here too it is He alone [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] who is spoken of.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.3:
nanvātmaśabdasyāgnyādiṣvamukhyatvābhyupagamena sāmānādhikaraṇyāvirodhātteṣāmeva vaiśvānaratvaṃ kiṃ na syādityāśaṅkāṃ parihartuṃ samākhyarūpahetvantareṇa vaiśvānarasya viṣṇutvaṃ niścāyayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - smaryamāṇamiti // sūtrabhāṣyayoḥ 'smaryamāṇam'; 'ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā'; iti gītāsmṛtyuktaṃ viṣṇorvaiśvānaratvam 'atra'; vaiśvānaravidyāyāmapi 'saḥ'; gītokto bhagavāneva vaiśvānarapadena ucyate 'ityasya'; evaṃrūpasyārthasya 'anumānam'; anumāpakaṃ 'syāt'; bhavediti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.3:
Objection: Since the non-primary usage of the word '<s>Ātman</s>' in <s>Agni</s> and others is accepted, and there being no contradiction with co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), why should <s>Vaiśvānaratva</s> (the state of being <s>Vaiśvānara</s>) not belong to them [<s>Agni</s> etc.] alone? — To resolve this doubt, having cited the <s>sūtra</s> which ascertains the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> through another reason in the form of designation (<s>samākhyā</s>), he explains — '<s>smaryamāṇam</s>' (that which is remembered). // The interpretation of the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s> is: '<s>smaryamāṇam</s>' — the <s>Vaiśvānaratva</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s> stated in the <s>Gītā</s> <s>Smṛti</s> as 'ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā' (I, having become <s>Vaiśvānara</s>); 'atra' — in the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>vidyā</s> (meditation) too; 'saḥ' — the very Lord spoken of in the <s>Gītā</s> alone is denoted by the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; 'ityasya' — of this meaning of such form; '<s>anumānam</s>' — an inferential indicator; 'syāt' — would be — this is the interpretation.
Because of the designation (<s>samākhyā</s>). The word 'iti' indicates the designation. // 25 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.4:
nanvahamiti viṣṇunā kṛṣṇenokteḥ smṛtyuktavaiśvānarasya viṣṇutve 'pi atroktavaiśvānarasya kuto viṣṇutvamityata āha - samākhyānāditi // asyāḥ smṛteriti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca gītāsmṛteḥ vaiśvānaravidyāsamānoktirūpatvādasyāstatsamākhyānānniścayo bhavatītyarthaḥ / samākhyāyuktirna sūtroktetyata āha - iti śabda iti / 'pradarśakaḥ'; sūcakaḥ / tathā ca - itismaryamāṇamityasya itisamākhyāyamānamityarthābhyupagamāditiśabdaḥ samānoktirūpasamākhyālakṣaṇaliṅgajñāpaka iti bhāvaḥ / atra sūtresamākhyārūpahetvantaroktāvapi tasyātmaśabdākhyapūrvahetoraniścāyakatvaśaṅkāmukhena tannirāsāya pravṛttatvāccaśabdābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.4:
Objection: Since it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who says 'aham' (I), even though the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> mentioned in <s>Smṛti</s> is established as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, how is the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> mentioned here [in <s>Śruti</s>] also <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he says — '<s>samākhyānāt</s>' (because of designation). // 'Of this <s>Smṛti</s>' is to be supplied. And thus, because the <s>Gītā</s> <s>Smṛti</s> has the form of stating the same teaching as the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>vidyā</s>, from that designation (<s>samākhyāna</s>), certainty arises — this is the meaning. Since the reasoning of designation is not stated in the <s>sūtra</s> [explicitly], he says — 'itiśabdaḥ' (the word 'iti'). // '<s>Pradarśakaḥ</s>' means indicator. And thus — by accepting the meaning of 'iti-<s>smaryamāṇam</s>' as 'iti-<s>samākhyāyamānam</s>' (that which is being designated thus), the word 'iti' conveys the <s>liṅga</s> (indicative mark) in the form of <s>samākhyā</s> (designation) having the form of co-statement — this is the purport. In this <s>sūtra</s>, even though another reason in the form of <s>samākhyā</s> is stated, there is no word 'ca' (and), because this proceeds under the pretext of removing the doubt about the inconclusiveness of the previous reason, namely the word '<s>Ātman</s>'.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //

children.text: śabdādibhyo 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhānānneti cenna tathā dṛṣṭyupadeśādasambhavātpuruṣavidhamapi cainamadhīyate | BBs_1,2.26 |

'mūrdhānam'; iti mantre ṣaṣṭhyarthaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvasambandhaḥ / 'mūrdhatvaṃ viṣṇoraṅgāṅgyabhedāt'; iti tattvapradīpokteḥ mūrdhānamaratimityabhedoktiḥ / ṛtāyeti vedāntare pāṭhādṛci ṛta iti saptamī tādarthye / tathā ca divaḥ kāraṇabhūtamūrdhānaṃ loke gamanenāratidarśanāt rativiruddhagatisādhanatvādgauṇyā vṛttyā 'aramalamatati gacchati yena puruṣaḥ so 'ratiḥ pādaḥ'; iti tattvapradīpokteḥ mukhyayā vṛttyā aratiḥ pādaḥ / ṛgatāvityasmātkaraṇe atipratyaye niṣpanno 'ratiśabdaḥ pāde mukhya evetyapi kecit / tattu tattvapradīpacandrikānuktam / tattvapradīpe araśabdopapadādatateḥ, candrikāyāṃ nañupapadādramerasya niṣpatteruktatvāt / tathā ca - pṛthivyāḥ aratiṃ kāraṇībhūtapādaṃ janānām āṛte samyagjñānāya 'jātam'; abhivyaktaṃ 'kaviṃ'; sarvajñaṃ 'samrājam'; akhaṇḍeśam 'annaṃ tham'; () iti śruteḥthaśabdo 'nnavācī / tṛtīye 'tiśaye / tathā ca 'atithim'; atyannam / pātramityanenāpi janānāmityetatsambadhyate / tathā ca janānāṃ 'pātāraṃ'; rakṣakaṃ 'vaiśvānaraṃ'; viśvajīvāntaratvayogena tacchabdavācyam 'agnim'; aṅganetāraṃ viṣṇuṃ prasiddhaṃ ca devā āsan / avibhaktiko 'yaṃ nirdeśaḥ / āsyaśabdasyāsannādeśaḥ / tathā ca āsan svāsyatayā ājanayanta / aḍabhāvaśchāndasaḥ / āsamantātsarvakarmasvakurvanniti siddhāntarītyā śrutyarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - viśvanarastham ṛte vede 'ā samantājjātaṃ'; vyaktam 'agnim'; aṅganetāraṃ 'saṃrājaṃ'; samyagrājantam 'atithiṃ'; sarvānatiśayya sthitaṃ pātāram agniṃ janānām 'āsan'; āśrayam ājanayanta āsamantājjanayāṃcakruḥ / agnyādidevā iti viśeṣārtha uktaḥ / kecittu - janibādhakāṅyogādājanayanta akurvannityuktamityāhuḥ / tattūdāhṛtatattvapradīpaviruddham / ato 'nekārthatvāddhātūnāṃ viṣṇujanye 'gnau devajanyatvāyogāt janerutpattyarthāyogācca akurvannityuktamiti āṅviśleṣeṇaiva ṭīkā vyākhyeyā / pūrvapakṣī tu śrutigatāgnyādiśabdānprasiddhāgniparāneva manyate /
'vaiśvānare taddhutam'; iti vākyārthastu - 'tasmāduhaivaṃ vidyadyapi caṇḍālayocchiṣṭaṃ prayacchedātmani haivāsya vaiśvānare hutaṃ syāt'; (chāṃ. 5-24-4.) iti chandogasamākhyāvākyādavagantavyaḥ / tadarthastu - yadi 'evaṃvit'; uktarītyā vaiśvānarajñānī ucchiṣṭādyanarhāyāpi caṇḍālāyocchiṣṭaṃ 'prayacchet'; dadyāt / tadā taddattamucchiṣṭaṃ caṇḍālāntaryāmiṇi vaiśvānare hutaṃ syānna pāpakaraṃ bhavati / pratyuta mahāphalameveti / anenāhutisthānatvaliṅagamucyate /
'hṛdayaṃ'; hṛdayastho viṣṇurgārhapatyapadavācya ityarthaḥ / evamuttaratrāpi / 'anvāhāryapacano'; dakṣiṇāgniranvāhārya odano 'tra pacyata iti vyutpatti sambhavāt / pūrvapakṣe tu garhapatyaṃ vaiśvānarasya prasiddhāgnerhṛdayasthānīyamityādirarthaḥ /
'tadyadbhaktam'; iti vākyārthastu - 'tat'; tadā bhojanavelāyāṃ 'yadyadbhaktam'; annaṃ 'prathamamāgacchet'; āsyaṃ prati prāṇāhutirūpeṇa / 'taddhomīyaṃ'; pācakatvenāntaḥsthitasyāgnerhemadravyamiti / anenāgnau hūyamānadravyasyāgniḥ pācaka iti siddhamiti pācakatvākhyaliṅgamuktaṃ bhavati / yadyapi 'yenedam'; iti pūrvavākye 'ayamagniḥ'; iti tatpūrvavākyasāhityāt pācakatvenāntaḥpratiṣṭhānoktāvapi na 'tadyadbhaktam'; iti vākye tatpratīyate / tathāpi 'taddhomīyam'; ityanenāntassthitasya homyamityuktatvāttatpratyāyakatvopapattiḥ /

Thus the <s>Ṛgvedic</s> passage. 'Ityādi' is an appositional compound (<s>karmadhāraya</s>). And thus, the word in the form of 'ityādi' is stated by the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>śabda</s>': that is the meaning. Or alternatively: 'ityādi' — the collection of passages of such and similar kinds — is 'the word' (<s>śabdaḥ</s>) — grasped by the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>śabda</s>': that is the meaning. By the word 'ādi' (and the like), passages of similar kind from other <s>Śrutis</s> are included. 'In <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — this is a passage from another <s>Śruti</s>. 'The heart' and so forth — this is the <s>Chāndogya Śruti</s>. 'And the like — the mark of <s>Agni</s>' — means the mark of <s>Agni</s> stated by passages of such and similar kinds: that is the meaning. By the word 'ādi,' the [marks] stated in passages such as 'the navel of sacrifices, the abode of riches' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 6.7.2) and the like are included. 'Stated by the word ādi' — means stated by the <s>sūtra</s>-word 'ādi' and the like: that is the meaning. 'By which this food is cooked that is eaten' — this too is from the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Śruti</s>, following 'This fire is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, which is within the person' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 7.9). 'That which is cooked' — this is the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage. 'By the passage beginning with ityādi' — 'by the passage' is the remainder. By the <s>Kuru</s>-<s>Pāṇḍava</s> principle, following the <s>Śruti</s> 'all-acting, all-marked,' to convey the action distinctly from the mark stated by the word 'ādi,' the <s>sūtra</s> says '<s>antaḥpratiṣṭhānāt</s>' (because of being established within). Or alternatively — since the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> states 'the being established within by way of cooking is stated separately because it is regarded as the primary mark' — intending that this is stated separately because of being the primary mark, he shows that mark by stating that action: 'by way of cooking.' The third case-ending is in the sense of characterization (<s>itthaṃbhūtalakṣaṇa</s>). By this, it is stated that the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>antaḥpratiṣṭhāna</s>' (being established within) is intended not merely as the dwelling within the respective hearts, but as being accompanied by activity. For this very reason, both <s>Śruti</s> citations — 'by which this food is cooked' and 'that which is cooked' — are exemplified. The word 'ca' is for accumulation. What follows from that? — to this he says: '<s>tasmāt</s>' (therefore). // Since thus, even in the <s>Agni</s>-view, <s>Śruti</s>, marks, and the like exist, while in the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-view, you yourself have stated the word '<s>ātma</s>' (Self) and the name-explanation (<s>samākhyāna</s>) — therefore, because of the equality of <s>Śruti</s> and the like on both sides, the determination that <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is not justified: that is the meaning. Objection: In the passage under examination 'He who indeed this [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>],' since the word '<s>Agni</s>' does not occur in co-reference with the word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>,' how can the word '<s>Agni</s>' occurring in another passage be a ground for doubt? — [Reply:] Not so, because here all <s>Vaiśvānara</s>-<s>vidyās</s> are under examination, and for this very reason, multiple passages are cited. Or alternatively: even in the prima facie view, just as in the established conclusion, to demonstrate the name-explanation, the citation of the respective passages in the form of name-explanation is justified. In the passage [beginning with] '<s>ayam</s>' (this), [the question] 'who is referred to by the word '<s>ayam</s>'?' — to this he says: '<s>yo'yam</s>' (he who is this). And thus — 'he who is this, within the person' — <s>Bhagavān</s> situated within the person — this '<s>Agni</s>' — called by the word '<s>Agni</s>' because of being the leader of the body (<s>aṅga</s>) denoted by that word. He is connected with the qualities of all (<s>viśva</s>), and He leads (<s>narīyate</s>) — thus He is called <s>Vaiśvānara</s>: this is the construction. He states His activity: '<s>yena</s>' (by which). What is 'this' (<s>idam</s>)? — to this he says: '<s>yadidamadyate</s>' (that which is eaten). It is eaten — consumed — by living beings.
In the <s>mantra</s> beginning with '<s>mūrdhānam</s>' (the head), the sixth case (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>) has the meaning of the cause-effect relationship. Because of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> statement 'the headship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is because of the non-difference of parts and whole,' the expression 'the head is <s>arati</s> (the foot)' is a statement of non-difference. From the reading '<s>ṛtāya</s>' in another <s>Veda</s>, in the <s>Ṛc</s>, '<s>ṛta</s>' has the seventh case (<s>saptamī</s>) in the sense of purpose. And thus, '<s>arati</s>' (the foot) — the causally-related head of heaven — is that which, being the means of passage contradicting delight, in the world, because of seeing non-delight in passage — by secondary usage, 'one who goes (<s>atati</s>) by <s>ara</s> (means), by whom the person [goes] — that is <s>arati</s>, the foot' as stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> — but by primary usage, <s>arati</s> is the foot. Some say that the word '<s>arati</s>' is derived from the root '<s>at</s>' (to go) with the instrumental suffix, preceded by '<s>ṛg</s>' (going), and is primary in the sense of foot. But that is not stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> or <s>Candrikā</s>. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, it is derived from '<s>at</s>' preceded by the word '<s>ara</s>'; in the <s>Candrikā</s>, from '<s>ram</s>' preceded by '<s>na</s>' (negative). And thus, 'of the earth' (<s>pṛthivyāḥ</s>) — '<s>aratim</s>' — the causally-related foot — for the people, for the sake of proper knowledge (<s>ṛte</s>) — 'born' (<s>jātam</s>) — manifested — 'the wise one' (<s>kavim</s>) — the omniscient — 'the sovereign' (<s>samrājam</s>) — the undivided lord — 'the food-<s>tha</s>' (<s>annam tham</s>) — from the <s>Śruti</s>, the word '<s>tha</s>' denotes food. The third [case] is in the superlative sense. And thus, '<s>atithim</s>' — the most excellent food [giver]. By '<s>pātāram</s>' (protector), 'of the people' also connects. And thus, 'of the people' — 'the protector' (<s>pātāram</s>) — the guardian — '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — denotable by that word because of being the inner self of all <s>jīvas</s> — '<s>Agni</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the leader of the body, who is well-known — the gods produced. This is a caseless citation. The word '<s>āsya</s>' has the substitute '<s>āsan</s>.' And thus, 'they produced' (<s>āsan</s>) — they generated as their own — in the established-conclusion mode, the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is: producing on all sides and performing all actions. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however: the one situated in all beings (<s>viśvanara</s>), in the <s>Veda</s>, for the sake of proper knowledge — 'born' — manifested — '<s>Agni</s>' — the leader of the body — 'the sovereign' — properly ruling — '<s>atithim</s>' — one who stands surpassing all — the protector of the people — '<s>Agni</s>' — the gods — '<s>āsan</s>' — generated as refuge, produced on all sides and everywhere. The specific meaning '<s>Agni</s> and other gods' has been stated. Some, however, say that because of the connection with the particle 'ā' which prevents [the meaning of] birth, '<s>ājanayanta</s>' means 'they made,' i.e., 'served.' But that contradicts the cited <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. Therefore, since verbal roots have multiple meanings, since in <s>Agni</s> who is produced by <s>Viṣṇu</s> there is unfitness for being produced by the gods, and since the root '<s>jan</s>' is unfit in the sense of origination — [the meaning] 'they made' is stated — the <s>Ṭīkā</s> should be explained only through the separation of the prefix 'ā.' The prima facie advocate, however, considers the words '<s>Agni</s>' and the like occurring in the <s>Śruti</s> to refer only to the well-known physical fire.
The meaning of the passage 'in <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, that [food] is offered' is to be understood from the <s>Chāndogya</s> name-explanation passage: 'Therefore indeed, for one who knows thus, even if he gives leftovers to a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, it would be an oblation offered in his <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.24.4). Its meaning is: if 'one who knows thus' — a knower of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in the manner described — were to 'give' (<s>prayacchet</s>) leftovers even to a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> who is unworthy of leftovers and the like, then that given leftover would be 'offered in <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — in the inner controller <s>Vaiśvānara</s> within the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> — and would not be sinful. On the contrary, it would be greatly fruitful. By this, the mark of being the locus of oblation is stated.
'The heart' — means <s>Viṣṇu</s> dwelling in the heart is denotable by the word '<s>Gārhapatya</s>' (the householder's fire): that is the meaning. Similarly in what follows. '<s>Anvāhāryapacana</s>' — the southern fire (<s>dakṣiṇāgni</s>) — because the derivation '<s>anvāhārya</s>: the cooked rice (<s>odana</s>) that is cooked (<s>pacyate</s>) here' is possible. In the prima facie view, however, the meaning is: the heart is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire-pit] of the well-known fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, and so forth.
The meaning of the passage 'that which is cooked' (<s>tadyadbhaktam</s>) is: 'then' (<s>tat</s>) — at the time of eating — 'whatever food' (<s>yadyadbhaktam</s>) — 'comes first' (<s>prathamamāgacchet</s>) — to the mouth in the form of the <s>Prāṇāhuti</s> (offering to <s>Prāṇa</s>). 'That is the oblation material' (<s>taddhomīyam</s>) — the material for the oblation of <s>Agni</s> who dwells within as the cooker: that is [the meaning]. By this, since it is established that <s>Agni</s> who cooks the material being offered into the fire is the cooker — the mark called cookership is stated. Although in the preceding passage 'by which this [food is cooked],' the [reference to] 'this <s>Agni</s>' is from conjunction with the passage before it, and even when the being-established-within by way of cooking is stated, this is not understood in the passage 'that which is cooked' — nevertheless, since by 'that is the oblation material,' the one established within is said to receive the oblation — the fitness of its conveying [the mark] is justified.

parihārasūtrāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti // tasmānna viṣṇuriti pūrvavākyenāsya nañarthasyānvayaḥ / kuto netyatastatra bhāṣye 'tasmādityuktam'; ityāvṛttyā hetutvena saṃyojyam / sūtretu ata ityākarṣaṇīyam / ātmaśabdādipūrvahetoreveti tadarthaḥ / na cetaratrāpyasti śrutyādikamityanirṇayaḥ / teṣāmanyatra mukhyato yogena viṣṇāveva sāvakāśatvopapatterityadhyāhāraḥ / kuto 'gnyādināmakarmaṇāṃ viṣṇāveva sāvakāśatvaṃ jñāyata ityatastatra hetusamarpakaṃ 'tathādṛṣṭyupadeśāt'; ityaṃśam upadeśapadoktaśrutyudāharaṇapūrvakaṃ vyācaṣṭe - atheti / prakaraṇāntarārambhārtho 'yamathaśabdaḥ/ prathametiśabdo vidhisamāptau / dvitīyasya ityupāsītetyanvayaḥ / tathā ca 'etamātmānam'; ādānādikartāram 'aṇoraṇīyāṃsaṃ'; sūkṣmādapi sūkṣmaṃ 'parato'; mahataḥ paraṃ 'viśvaṃ'; pūrṇaṃ harimupāsītetyarthaḥ / kimitītyataḥ upāsanāprakāramāha - sarveti / itiśabdaḥ pratyekaṃ sambadhyate / tathā ca mukhyataḥ indrādisarvanāmavānityupāsīta / 'sarvakarmā'; 'nar te tvatkriyate'; ityādeḥ svātantryeṇa sarvakriyākartetyupāsīta/ liṅgaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ, vajradharatvādisarvaliṅga ityupāsīta/ jñānānandādisarvaguṇapūrṇa ityupāsīta / etadicchayaiva sarvaṃ bhavatīti sarvakāmaḥ pūrṇakāma ityupāsīta / bhedasaṃyogavibhāgādisarvadharmāstadadhīnā iti vā, sarvajñatvādisarvadharmavatvādvā sarvadharma ityupāsīta / sarvatra rūpamasya iti vā sarvaṃ jagadasya rūpaṃ pratimeti vā sarvarūpa ityupāsīta /
