<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.7, verse 6:
He explains the resolution portion of the <s>sūtra</s> — '<s>na</s>' (no). // The syntactic connection of this negative particle is with the preceding passage 'therefore not <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' Why 'not so'? — for that, in the <s>bhāṣya</s>, 'therefore has been said' recurs and should be connected as the reason. In the <s>sūtra</s>, however, '<s>ataḥ</s>' (therefore) should be drawn [forward]. The meaning is: because of the prior reasoning of the word '<s>ātma</s>' (Self) and the like alone [favoring <s>Viṣṇu</s>]. It is not [the case] that there is indetermination because the <s>Śruti</s> and the like exist on the other side as well — the interpolation is: because the fitness of the scope of those [marks] in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is justified, primarily through etymological derivation. Whence is it known that the names, actions, and the like of <s>Agni</s> and others have scope in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone? — for that, he explains the portion '<s>tathādṛṣṭyupadeśāt</s>' (because of the teaching of such contemplation), which supplies the reason, preceded by citing the <s>Śruti</s> stated by the word '<s>upadeśa</s>' (teaching) — '<s>atha</s>' (now). This word '<s>atha</s>' is for the commencement of another topic. The first '<s>iti</s>' is at the completion of an injunction. The second '<s>iti</s>' connects with 'one should meditate.' And thus: 'this Self' — the agent of sustaining and the like — 'smaller than the small' — subtler than even the subtle — 'greater than the great' — 'all-pervading' (<s>viśvam</s>) — complete — one should meditate upon <s>Hari</s>: that is the meaning. How? — to this he states the mode of meditation: '<s>sarva</s>' (all). // The word '<s>iti</s>' connects with each. And thus: one should meditate [thinking] He primarily bears all names such as <s>Indra</s> and others. 'Of all actions' — from [the <s>Śruti</s>] 'nothing of Yours is done [by another],' one should meditate that He is the independent agent of all actions. '<s>Liṅga</s>' means identifying characteristic — one should meditate that He has all marks such as bearing the thunderbolt and the like. One should meditate that He is full of all qualities such as knowledge, bliss, and the like. One should meditate that He is 'of all desires' (<s>sarvakāmaḥ</s>) — of complete desire — because everything comes into being by His will alone. One should meditate that He is 'of all <s>dharmas</s>' — either because all <s>dharmas</s> such as difference, conjunction, separation, and the like are dependent on Him, or because He possesses all <s>dharmas</s> such as omniscience and the like. One should meditate that He is 'of all forms' — either because His form is everywhere, or because the entire universe is His image (<s>pratimā</s>).

children.text: 'sa ya etamevamātmānaṃ viśvaṃ harimārādaramupāste tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu deveṣu sarveṣu vedeṣu kāmacāro bhavati'; iti tattannāmaliṅgādinā tasyaiva dṛṣṭyupadeśānmahopaniṣadi //
children.translated_text: 'He who meditates upon this all-pervading Self, <s>Hari</s>, near at hand and with devotion — for him there is free movement in all worlds, in all beings, among the gods, and in all the <s>Vedas</s>' — because of the teaching of contemplation of Him alone through such names, marks, and the like, [as stated] in the <s>Mahopaniṣad</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.7, verse 7:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.7:
evamupāsakasya phalamāha - sa iti // 'saḥ'; prasiddhaḥ yo 'dhikārī etamātmānam aṇoraṇīyāṃsaṃ parataḥparameva viśvaṃ harimeva, nānyam, 'ārāt'; samīpe svahṛdaye 'aram'; alaṃ samyagupāste tasyaivamavyāpte vyāptarūpopāsakasya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu 'bhūteṣu'; prāṇiṣu sarveṣu lokeṣu sthiteṣu bhūteṣviti vā / vedeṣu sarveṣu, vedeṣu yatheṣṭasañcāraḥ kāmasañcaraṇasarvapūjyatvasarvajñatvādiḥ syāt ityarthaḥ tattvapradīpe 'bhihitaḥ / 'iti'; mahopaniṣadītyanvayaḥ / sautratathāśabdārthamāha - tattaditi / agnyādināmaliṅgādimattvenetyarthaḥ / ādipadena tattatkarmādergrahaṇam / pradhānasūtre 'bhihitaṃ tattvityetadatrāpi vipariṇāmena saṃyojyamityāśayenāha - tasyaiveti / viṣṇorevetyarthaḥ / na tvagnyāderityevārthaḥ / 'dṛṣṭyupadeśāt'; upāsanopadeśāt / śrutau harimeva upāsta ityavadhāraṇenānyavyāvṛttyavagamāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.2.7, verse 7:
He states the fruit for such a meditator: '<s>sa</s>' (he). // 'He' (<s>saḥ</s>) — the well-known eligible person who [meditates upon] 'this Self' — smaller than the small, greater than the great — 'all-pervading <s>Hari</s> alone' — not another — 'near at hand' (<s>ārāt</s>) — close by, in his own heart — 'properly' (<s>aram</s>) — well — meditates upon Him; for such a meditator whose meditation has not fallen short [of the full scope], in all worlds, in all 'beings' — living creatures — or in all worlds situated among beings — and in all <s>Vedas</s> — there is free movement (<s>kāmacāra</s>) in the form of going wherever desired, being worshipped by all, and omniscience: this is the meaning stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. '<s>Iti</s>' connects with 'in the <s>Mahopaniṣad</s>.' He states the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>tathā</s>' (thus): '<s>tattad</s>' (those various). // The meaning is: by possessing such names of <s>Agni</s> and the like, marks, and the like. By the word 'ādi,' the respective actions and the like are included. Intending that '<s>tat tu</s>' (but that) stated in the primary <s>sūtra</s> should be connected here too in reversed form, he says: 'of that very one' (<s>tasyaiva</s>). // The meaning is: of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. The meaning of '<s>eva</s>' (alone) is: not of <s>Agni</s> and the like. 'Because of the teaching of contemplation' (<s>dṛṣṭyupadeśāt</s>) — because of the teaching of meditation. Because in the <s>Śruti</s>, the restrictive particle '<s>eva</s>' in 'one should meditate upon <s>Hari</s> alone' conveys the exclusion of others: that is the purport.

children.text:
anāttatvādanātmāna ūnatvādguṇarāśitaḥ /
abrahmāṇaḥ pare sarve brahmātmā viṣṇureva hi /
ityādinā, 'ko na ātmā kiṃ brahma'; (chāṃ. 5-11-1.)
ityārambhācca anyeṣāmasambhavāt viṣṇureva vaiśvānaraḥ /
children.translated_text:
Because of not taking [all names and forms], they are not Selves; because of deficiency from the aggregate of qualities,
they are not <s>Brahmans</s> — all others [are so]; <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is truly the Self and <s>Brahman</s>.
— By such [statements], and because of the commencement 'Who is the Self? What is <s>Brahman</s>?' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.11.1), and because of the impossibility of [<s>Vaiśvānara</s> being] the others, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.2.7, verse 8:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.8:
evamanyaśrutiliṅgadīnāṃ viṣṇau sāvakāśatvopapādakatayā tathetyaṃśaṃ vyākhyāya ātmaśabdāderanyatra niravakāśoktiparatayāsambhavādityaṃśaṃ pramāṇodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ vyākhyāti - anāttatvāditi // yojanātu - ityādinā pramāṇena viṣṇoranyeṣām ātmatvabrahmatvāsambhavokteḥ ata eva ātmaśabdāderanyatrāsambhavāditi / yadvā - na kevalamātmaśabdaśrutisamākhyābhyāṃ, kintu prakaraṇabalācca vaiśvānarasya viṣṇutvaniścayo bhavatītyāha - anāttatvāditi / ādiśabdena 'brahmaśabdaḥ pare viṣṇau'; ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / tathācetthaṃ yojanā - 'ko na ātmā kiṃ brahma'; 'ityārambhācca'; ityārabhyādhītātprakaraṇācca viṣṇureva vaiśvānaraḥ / brahmātmaśabdayoretadupakrame śravaṇe 'pi kuto 'syāḥ vaiśvānaravidyāyāḥ viṣṇuprakaraṇatvam? 'anāttatvāt'; ityādinā pramāṇena viṣṇoranyeṣāmātmaśabdārthavyāptatvaguṇapūrṇatvayorasambhavāvagamāditi / anena sūtre ārambhāditi padamadhyāhṛtya tenāpiśabdaḥ saṃyojyaḥ / asambhavāditi hetustu ātmaśabdāderanyatrānavakāśatvasādhakatayobhayatra saṃyojyaḥ ityuktaṃ bhavati / ata eva bhāṣye agniśrutyādīnāṃ viṣṇau sāvakāśatvasādhakatayetyādivyākhyānantaraṃ viṣṇupakṣasādhakātmaśabdāderanyatrānavakāśatvasādhakāsambhavāditi hetau vyākhyātavye 'pi tadvihāyārambhādityadhyāhṛtahetūpanyātrāstyavakāśa iti pratijñāya prakaraṇabalāccetyadhyāhāryahetuṃ ca pradarśya, anantaramātmaśabdaprakaraṇayorniravakāśatvasādhakāsambhavādityaṃśo vyākhyātaḥ / tathādṛṣṭyupadeśādasambhavāditivat nādhyāhṛtahetoravāntarasādhyenānvayaḥ, kintu pradhānenaiveti jñāpanāya viṣṇureva vaiśvānara iti punaruktiḥ / uddeśyavidheyanirdeśasyaicchikatvādvyatyāsaḥ / 'hi'; yasmādviṣṇoḥ 'pare'; anye guṇaiḥ 'anāttatvāt'; avyāptatvāt sarvotkṛṣṭatvena vaidikairasvīkṛtatvādvā 'anātmānaḥ'; anātmaśabdamukhyārthāḥ / yasmācca guṇarāśita ūnatvādabrahmāṇaśca / tasmāt 'brahmātmā'; tacchabdamukhyavācyo viṣṇureva siddha ityarthaḥ / chāndogye hi 'ko na ātmā kiṃ brahma'; iti militvā mīmāṃsamānaiḥ pratyabdayajñakṛttvanimittānmahāśālasaṃjñaiḥ pañcabhirmahāmunibhiḥ uddālakoddiṣṭaistadyuktaiḥ paripṛṣṭo rājāśvapatirvaiśvānaramupadideśa / 'naḥ'; asmākam upāsya ātmā 'kaḥ'; kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ / brahma ca 'kiṃ'; kiṃlakṣaṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> on 1,2.7.8:]
Having thus explained the portion 'tathā' (so) by showing that the marks in other <s>śrutis</s> (Vedic texts) are capable of being accommodated in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he now explains, with the citation of authority, the portion 'since there is no possibility that the word <s>Ātman</s> etc. [could refer] elsewhere, [their usage] being applicable only there' — 'anāttatvā' (because of not being taken):

children.text: 'candramā manaso jātaḥ / cakṣossūryo ajāyata'; (tai.ā. 3-12.) ityādinā yaḥ puruṣākhyo viṣṇubhihitastadvidhamevātra 'mūrdhaiva sutejāścakṣurviśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmā'; (chāṃ. 5-18-2.)
children.translated_text: 'The moon was born from his mind; the sun was born from his eye' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12) — by such [passages], the one designated as <s>Puruṣa</s> is declared to be <s>Viṣṇu</s>. And of this very nature, here too — 'The head is of brilliant radiance, the eye is of universal form, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) moves on a separate path' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.18.2) —
by such [passages], they teach this [being] as <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> on 1,2.7.9:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.9:
śrutisamākhyayā ca vaiśvānarasya viṣṇutvamupapādayituṃ pravṛttaṃ 'puruṣavidhamapyenamadhīyate'; ityaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - candramā iti // atra 'candramāḥ'; iti vākyaṃ pratīkatvena gṛhītam / udāharaṇavākyaṃ tu 'cakṣossūryo ajāyata'; itīti dhyeyam / prathamādipadena 'śīrṣṇodyaussamavartata, prāṇādvāyurajāyata, ... padbhyāṃ bhūmiḥ', (tai.ā. 3-12.) ityādikaṃ dvitīyādipadena 'sandoho bahulo vastireva rayiḥ pṛthivyeva pādau'; (chāṃ. 5-18-2.) ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / etamityasya vyākhyānaṃ - vaiśvānaramiti / tathā ca - yasmātpuruṣasūkte 'śīrṣṇodyaussamavartata, cakṣossūryo ajāyata'; ityādinā śabdena yaḥ puruṣākhyo viṣṇuḥ yadvidho dyubhvādijanakaśīrṣādimānabhihitaḥ, tadvidhameva dyubhvādijanakaśīrṣādimattvaprakāropetamevātra chāndogye 'mūrdhaiva sutejāḥ'; ityādinā vākyenainaṃ vaiśvānaramadhīyate chandogāḥ tasmātpuruṣasūktasamākhyayāpi vaiśvānaro viṣṇureveti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> on 1,2.7.9:]
Having undertaken to establish the identity of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> with <s>Viṣṇu</s> through Vedic designation, he glosses the portion 'they teach this one also as having the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>' — with 'The moon...' etc. Here, the sentence 'the moon' etc. is taken as a citation indicator.
And by the word 'ca' (and), he shows that the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> pertains to <s>Viṣṇu</s> across all <s>Vedic tantras</s> (ritual systems), <s>Purāṇas</s>, and other [texts].
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> on 1,2.7.10:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.10:
nanu puruṣasūktasya viṣṇuparatve bhavettatsamākhyayā etadvidyāyā viṣṇuparatvaṃ, tadeva kuta ityata āha - caśabdeneti // śruterādhikyātprathamaṃ pratijñā / 'puruṣasūktasya'; ityanantaraṃ 'prasiddhamiti'; śeṣaḥ / 'darśayati'; sūcayati sūtrakāra ityarthaḥ / ātmaśabdasmṛtisamākhyāprakaraṇasamuccayasyeva prakaraṇaśrutisamuccayasyāpi apipadenaiva siddhatvānna tatropakṣīṇaścaśabda iti bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text:
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> on 1,2.7.10:]
Now, if the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> pertains to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then through its designation, this <s>vidyā</s> (meditation) would also pertain to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — but how is that itself [established]? To this he says 'by the word ca' etc. Because <s>śruti</s> (Vedic testimony) has greater authority, the declaration is stated first. After 'of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>' —

children.text:
tathā ca brāhme -
yathaiva pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ nityaṃ viṣṇuparāyaṇam /
tathaiva me mano nityaṃ bhūyādviṣṇuparāyaṇam // iti /
children.translated_text:
And thus in the <s>Brāhma</s> [Purāṇa]:
'Just as the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> is eternally devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
so may my mind be eternally devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> on 1,2.7.11:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.11:
kiṃ tadvedādītyataśśruteḥ sākṣātpratijñātārthāsādhakatvātpratijñākramamatikramya sākṣātpratijñātārthasādhakatvādādau purāṇavākyaṃ paṭhati - tathā ceti // sūtre puruṣasūktasya viṣṇuparatvaṃ siddhamiti yathoktaṃ tathā brāhme coktamityarthaḥ / caḥ samuccaye / evam uttaratrāpi 'uktam'; iti padādhyāhāreṇa saptamyantapadānāmanvayo draṣṭavyaḥ / 'nityaṃ'; niyamena 'viṣṇuparāyaṇaṃ'; viṣṇau mahātātparyavat / dvitīyasya nityamityasya sadetyarthaḥ / 'iti brāhma iti'; iti śabdānvayaḥ siddhārthasyaiva dṛṣṭāntatvādanena brāhmavacanena vivakṣitārtho jñāyate //
children.translated_text:
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> on 1,2.7.11:]
What is that [authority] from the <s>Vedas</s> etc.? Since <s>śruti</s> directly establishes what is declared, and because [it] transcends the order of declaration due to its direct effectiveness in establishing the declared meaning, he first cites the <s>Purāṇa</s> passage — 'And thus' etc. In the <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>'s pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: caturvedaśikhāyāṃ ca - sahasraśīrṣā puruṣassahasrākṣassahasrapāt / iti eṣa hyaivācintyaḥ paraḥ paramo harirādiranādirananto 'nantaśīrṣo 'nantākṣo 'nantabāhuranantaguṇo 'nantarūpa iti /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s> (The Crest of the Four <s>Vedas</s>): 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> of a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet' — this is indeed the inconceivable, supreme, ultimate <s>Hari</s>, without beginning, beginningless, endless, of infinite heads, infinite eyes, infinite arms, infinite qualities, infinite forms.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> on 1,2.7.12:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.12:
pratijñātāṃ śrutiṃ darśayituṃ prathamameva tatsthānamāha - caturvedaśikhāyāṃ ceti // atra caturvedaśikhāśrutiḥ 'sahasra'; ityārabhya 'sahasrapāt'; ityantena puruṣasūktamupanyasya 'eṣahyeva'; ityanena 'sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ'; ityukto harireva nānya ityetatsūktaṃ viṣṇuparatayā vyākhyātīti prakṛtasaṅgatiḥ / supa ākāro vaidikaḥ / eṣaḥ ka ityato yaḥ 'paro'; vilakṣaṇaḥ ata eva 'acintyo'; manasā 'paramaḥ'; uttamaḥ 'ādiḥ'; kāraṇabhūtaḥ 'anādiḥ'; utpattiśūnyaḥ 'anantaḥ'; nāśaśūnyaḥ, svarūpato 'paricchinno vā hariḥ sa ityāha / kutaḥ ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sahasraśīrṣā? 'hi'; yasmādanantaśīrṣā / kutaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ? yasmādayamanantākṣaḥ / kutaḥ ayaṃ sahasrapāt? yasmādanantabāhuḥ / anantapādityasyāpyupalakṣakametat / evaṃ pūrvavākye 'pi 'sa bhūmim'; ityuttaravākyepyupapādakamāha - anantaguṇo 'nantarūpo 'nantākāra iti / caturvedaśikhāyāmityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> on 1,2.7.12:]
To present the declared <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text), he first states its source — 'In the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s>' etc. Here, the <s>Caturvedaśikhā śruti</s>, having cited the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> from 'sahasra' (thousand) up to 'sahasrapāt' (thousand-footed), [then says] 'this —'

children.text:
bṛhatsaṃhitāyāṃ ca -
yathā hi pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ viṣṇorevābhidhāyakam /
na tathā sarvavedāśca vedāṅgāni ca nārada // ityādi /
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Bṛhatsaṃhitā</s>:
'Just as the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> is expressive of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone,
so too are not all the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, O <s>Nārada</s>.' — and so forth.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> on 1,2.7.13:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.13:
brāhmavākyasya puruṣasūktasya lakṣaṇayā viṣṇuparatve 'nyaparatve 'pi vā sāvakāśatvānnatatpratijñātārthaniścāyakamityato vyākhyānavyākheyabhāvākhyadvāramantareṇa puruṣasūktaṃ mukhyato viṣṇorevābhidhāyakamiti sākṣātpratijñātārthasādhakaṃ smṛtivākyaṃ tatsthānanirdeśapūrvakaṃ paṭhati - bṛhatsaṃhitāyāṃ ceti / cakāraḥ pūrvasamuccayārthaḥ / 'vedāṅgāni'; śikṣādīni brahmavākyametat / ityādi / bṛhatsaṃhitāyāmuktamityanvayaḥ / ādipadena 'sarvataḥ pauruṣe sūkte guṇā viṣṇorudīritāḥ'; iti brahmatarkādigrahaṇam / 'sarvataḥ'; sarve guṇāḥ / sāmānyeneti śeṣaḥ / sarvasmin, sarvasmāt vedatadaṅgebhyo 'tiśayeneti vā /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> on 1,2.7.13:]
Since the <s>Brāhma</s> passage, through indirect indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), might point to the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>'s pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s> or even to another referent — because it has scope [for both] — it does not definitively establish the declared meaning. Therefore, through the relation of gloss and glossed, without any other door [of interpretation], the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> primarily —
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> on 1,2.7.14:]
Since whatever is born from the limbs of <s>Hari</s> — the world, <s>Vedas</s>, and the rest —
that which is designated by his name is his limb; just as <s>Brahmā</s> and others are [his] face.
By this statement of <s>Nārada</s>, there is no contradiction with the assertion of non-difference. // 26 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.14:
nanu puruṣasūkte dyubhvādijanakaśīrṣādimatvaṃ puruṣasyocyate / vaiśvānaravidyāyāṃ tu vaiśvānarasya tadabheda ucyate / tadubhayorviruddhārthatvānneyaṃ samākhyetyata āha - yasmāditi // 'lokaḥ'; svargādiḥ 'vedaḥ'; ṛgādiḥ / yadyapi nātra chāndogye vedābheda ucyate iti na tadgatirvaktavyā / tathāpi śrutyantaragatābhedavākyārthanirṇayāyāyamaṃśaḥ pravṛttaḥ/ yadvā - vedaśabdena 'ura eva vediḥ'; ityuktā vedirgṛhyate / 'tṛtīyo 'tiśaye'; ityuktatvāt / 'vedyādikam'; iti pāṭhaḥ svarasaḥ / tathā ca yasmādyasmāt hareraṅgāt yadyat lokavedādikaṃ jāyate, yadāśritya tiṣṭhati, yatra līyate ca tajjanakamaṅgaṃ tasmāt 'tannāmavācyaṃ'; tasya lokāderyannāma vācakaśabdaḥ tena mukhyavācyaṃ bhavati / ata eva tadabhinnatvena pratīyate ca / na tāvatā tayorabhedo mantavya ityarthaḥ / atra dṛṣṭāntamāha - yatheti / mukhamityupalakṣaṇam / tathā ca - bhagavanmukhādirbrāhmaṇādijātijanakatvāt brāhmaṇādināmnocyate 'brāhmaṇo 'sya mukhamāsīt'; (tai.ā.3-12.) ityādau / ata eva tadabhinnatvena pratīyate ca sāmānādhikaraṇyāt / tadvadrāpītyarthaḥ / na hyatra puruṣottamamukhādibhirabhedo brāhmaṇādīnāmucyate, 'padbhyāṃ śūdro ajāyata'; (tai.ā. 3-12.) ityuttaravākyavirodhāt / iti vacanādityuktatvādvaiśvānarāṅgānāṃ 'mūrdhaiva'; iti lokādyabhedoktinimitto virodho netyarthaḥ / abhedapratyāyakoktestajjanyajanakabhāvavivakṣāpūrvakatvāditi bhāvaḥ / anena bhagavato mūrdhā sutejastvādiguṇayogātsutejaḥśabditasvargajanakatvāt sutejā ityucyate / evaṃ 'cakṣurviśvarūpaḥ'; sarvaprakāśakatvaguṇayogāt viśvarūpaśabditasūryajanakatvāttacchabdenocyate / 'prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmātmā'; (chāṃ. 5-18-2.) vāyujanakatvāttacchabdita iti śrutyarthassūcitaḥ / ātmaśabdaḥ svarūpārtho madhyadehārtho vā / chāndogyabhāṣye tu - 'mūrdhā viṣṇośśiraḥ svargādhāraṃ dyunāmakam'; atitejasā suptejonāmakaṃ ca / viśvāni rūpāṇi viṣayatvena yasyeti vigrahāśrayeṇa sarvarūpātidarśanāt cakṣurviśvarūpākhyam / evaṃ viṣṇoḥ prāṇo nṛsiṃhākhyo vāyvādiprāṇaśakyaṃ yanna bhavati tasya pṛthagvartmātmā pṛthagvilakṣaṇo mārgo yasya sa cāsāvātmā ceti, iti nimittāntareṇa śrutirvyākhyātā / evaṃ bahularayipṛthivīśabditākāśavārivasundharādevatājanakatvāt sandohavastipādapadoktāni madhyadehakaṭiprapadarūpāṇi bhagavato vaiśvānarasyāṅgāni tattacchabdavācyānītyapi jñātavyam /
anena 'śabdādibhyaḥ'; agnyādiśruteḥ gārhapatyādyaṅgavatvādiliṅgācca pācakatvenāntaḥpratiṣṭhānācca vaiśvānaro viṣṇureveti niścayo na yujyata iti cet - na, anyaśrutiliṅgādīnāṃ viṣṇau sāvakāśatvena ātmaśabdādereva niścayopapatteḥ / kutaḥ sāvakāśatvam? 'tathādṛṣṭyupadeśāt '; agnyādināmaliṅgakarmavatvena viṣṇorupāsanopadeśāt / na cātmaśabdāderanyatrāstyavakāśaḥ, anyatrātmatvāderasambhavāt / na kevalamātmaśabdasmṛtisamākhyānādvaiśvānaro viṣṇureveti niścayaḥ, api tu ārambhācca prakaraṇabalācca/ na ca vaiśvānaravidyāyā viṣṇuprakaraṇatvasiddhiḥ, 'ko na ātmā kiṃ brahma'; iti vicārapūrvakamasyārabhyādhītatvāt/ na cātmatvabrahmatvopakrame 'pi kuto 'sya viṣṇuparatā, ātmatvabrahmatvādīnāmagnyādāvasambhavāt / na kevalaṃ smṛtisamākhyāprakaraṇabalādvaiśvānaro viṣṇureveti niścīyate, kintu yataḥ puruṣasūkte puruṣo yadvidho 'bhihitaḥ tadvidhamevainaṃ viṣṇuṃ 'mūrdhaiva'; ityādinādhīyate chandogāḥ / ataḥ śrutisamākhyānādapi caśabdaḥ puruṣasūktasya viṣṇuparatvaṃ bahupramāṇasiddhamiti dyotayatīti sūtravṛttirdarśitā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.14:
Objection: In the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, it is stated that the <s>Puruṣa</s> possesses a head and other [limbs] that give rise to heaven, earth, and so forth. But in the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>vidyā</s>, identity of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> with those [cosmic entities] is stated. Since the two have contradictory meanings, this designation should be figuratively interpreted — to address this, he says 'yasmāt' (because). // '<s>Loka</s>' means heaven and so forth; '<s>Veda</s>' means the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and so forth. Even though in this <s>Chāndogya</s> [passage] identity with the <s>Vedas</s> is not stated, and hence its purport need not be discussed, still this section is introduced to determine the meaning of identity-statements found in other <s>śrutis</s>. Alternatively, by the word '<s>Veda</s>', the <s>vedi</s> (altar) referred to in 'the chest indeed is the <s>vedi</s>' is taken, because of the rule '<s>tṛtīyo 'tiśaye</s>' (the third [suffix] denotes eminence). The reading '<s>vedyādikam</s>' is natural. And thus, from whichever limb of <s>Hari</s> whichever world, <s>vedi</s>, and so forth is born, upon which it rests, and in which it dissolves — that generating limb is therefore 'denoted by that name'; the name that designates that world and so forth becomes its primary denotation. And precisely for this reason, it is also cognized as non-different from it. But merely from that, identity of the two should not be held — this is the meaning. He gives an illustration for this — 'just as.' 'Face' is used as a representative example. And thus — the Lord's face and other [limbs], being the cause of the birth of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and other castes, are called by the names of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and so forth, as in '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was His face' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12). And precisely for this reason, it is also cognized as non-different due to co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). In the same way here too — this is the meaning. For here, identity of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and others with the face and other [limbs] of the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is not stated, because it would contradict the subsequent statement 'from His feet the <s>Śūdra</s> was born' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12). Since it has been stated 'because of the designation,' the contradiction occasioned by the identity-statement of the limbs of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> with worlds and so forth through 'the head itself [is heaven]' is resolved — this is the meaning. The purport is that the statement that conveys non-difference is preceded by the intention to express the cause-effect relationship. By this, the Lord's head is called '<s>Sutejā</s>' (of excellent brilliance) because of possessing qualities like excellent brilliance and because of being the cause of heaven which is denoted by the word '<s>Sutejā</s>'. Similarly, 'the eye is <s>Viśvarūpa</s>' — because of possessing the quality of illuminating everything, and because of being the cause of the sun which is denoted by the word '<s>Viśvarūpa</s>', it is called by that word. '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>pṛthagvartmā ātmā</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.2) — because of being the cause of <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), it is called by that word — thus the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is indicated. The word '<s>ātman</s>' means either 'own nature' or 'middle of the body.' But in the <s>Chāndogya Bhāṣya</s> — '<s>Viṣṇu's</s> head, which is the support of heaven, is named <s>Dyu</s>' and is called <s>Sutejā</s> because of excellent brilliance. Because all forms are His objects — through this etymological analysis, the eye is called <s>Viśvarūpa</s> since all forms are perceived. Similarly, the <s>Prāṇa</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, called <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, is '<s>pṛthagvartmā ātmā</s>' — one whose path is distinct, meaning whose course is unique, and who is the <s>ātman</s> — thus the <s>śruti</s> is explained by another derivation. Likewise, it should be known that the Lord <s>Vaiśvānara's</s> limbs described as <s>Sandoha</s> (milking), <s>Vasti</s> (bladder), <s>Pāda</s> (feet) and <s>Pada</s> (step) — which are the forms of the middle body, hip, and toes — are denoted by those respective words because of being the cause of the deities of space, water, and earth denoted by the words <s>Bahularayi</s>, <s>Pṛthivī</s>, and the like.
By this, [objection:] the conclusion that <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, based on 'because of words [like <s>Ātman</s>],' the <s>śruti</s> mentioning <s>Agni</s> and the like, the indicatory marks such as having the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and other [fires] as limbs, and being established within as the digestive [fire] — is not justified. [Reply:] No, because the other <s>śrutis</s>, indicatory marks, and so forth have scope in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the conclusion is established through the word <s>ātman</s> and the like alone. How do they have scope? 'Because of the instruction to view thus' — because <s>Agni</s> and others, not being the real referents, serve as [objects through which] <s>Viṣṇu's</s> meditation is instructed. And the word <s>ātman</s> and the like have no scope elsewhere, because <s>ātman</s>-hood and the like are impossible in others. Not only is the conclusion that <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone established from the word <s>ātman</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and designation, but also from the commencement [of the passage] and the force of the context. Nor is the <s>Vaiśvānara vidyā's</s> being a context about <s>Viṣṇu</s> unestablished, because it is studied with the prior inquiry 'Who is our <s>Ātman</s>? What is <s>Brahman</s>?' And even with the commencement speaking of <s>ātman</s>-hood and <s>Brahman</s>-hood, why does it culminate in <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Because <s>ātman</s>-hood, <s>Brahman</s>-hood, and the like are impossible in <s>Agni</s> and others. Not only is <s>Vaiśvānara</s> determined to be <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone from the force of <s>smṛti</s>, designation, and context, but also because the <s>Chāndogya</s> school studies Him through 'the head itself [is heaven]' and so forth as being of the same nature as the <s>Puruṣa</s> described in the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>. Therefore, from the concordance of <s>śruti</s> as well — the word 'ca' (and) indicates that the <s>Puruṣasūkta's</s> having <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its subject is established by many proofs — thus the commentary on the <s>sūtra</s> is shown.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //

children.text: ata eva na devatā bhūtaṃ ca | BBs_1,2.27 |
children.translated_text: Therefore, neither the deity nor the element. // <s>BBs</s> 1,2.27 //

children.text: agnivaiśvānarādiśabdastejasi bhūte agnidevatāyāṃ ca prasiddho 'pyataḥ pūrvoktahetuta evātra na sā taccābhidhīyate // 27 //
children.translated_text: Although the word <s>Agni-Vaiśvānara</s> and the like is well-known in reference to fire as an element and to <s>Agni</s> as a deity, for the very reasons stated before, here neither that [deity] nor that [element] is referred to. // 27 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.15:
nanu vaiśvānaraśabdasya devatābhūtayoḥ prasiddhatvādatrāpyasau tatparaḥ kiṃ na syādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasyati - ata eveti // atra caśabdasya samuccayārthatvaṃ yadyapi tathāpītyarthatvaṃ cāśritya sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - agnīti / samudāyaikavacanametat / ādiśabdena jātaveda ādiśabdo gṛhyate / vidyāntaropalakṣaṇayāgniśabdādiśabdayorgrahaṇam / na cāgnyādītyanenaivopalakṣaṇasambhavātkiṃ śabdadvayagrahaṇeneti vācyam / vaiśvānaraśabdasyeha vicāryatvena atiprasiddhatvādagniśabdasya ca grahaṇopapatteḥ / yadvā - ādiśabdasyobhayatrānvayena agnyādīti ādhibhautikavidyāntarasya vaiśvānarādītyādhyātmikavidyāntarasyopalakṣaṇārthamagnyādivaiśvānarādigrahaṇam / 'tejasi bhūte'; iti sāmānādhikaraṇyam / caḥ samuccaye 'prasiddhaḥ'; ityanena pūrvapakṣe prasiddhatvāditi yuktiḥ sūcitā / sautramataḥśabdamanūdya vyākhyāti - ata iti / pūrvokteti / ātmaśabdāditihetuta ityarthaḥ / na tatra hetvantaraṃ gaveṣaṇīyamityevārthaḥ / 'atra'; vaiśvānaravidyāyāṃ vidyāntare ca 'sā'; agnidevatā 'tat'; tejobhūtaṃ prasiddhiprādhānyābhyāṃ nirdeśavyatyāsaḥ / caśabdaḥ samuccaye / abhidhīyate 'tena'; iti śeṣaḥ / vaiśvānarādiśabdeneti tadarthaḥ / 'atra'; iti pāṭhābhāve tadapyadhyāhāryam /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.15:
Objection: Since the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is well-known for both the deity and the element, why should it not refer to those here as well? — Presenting the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves this doubt, he says 'ata eva' (therefore). // Here, although the word 'ca' (and) has the sense of conjunction, the <s>sūtra</s> is explained taking it also in the sense of 'even so.' This is a single collective statement. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the term '<s>Jātavedas</s>' and similar words are included. The words '<s>Agni</s>' and '<s>ādi</s>' are taken as representative of other <s>vidyās</s> as well. And one should not object 'since representativeness is possible with just <s>agnyādi</s> (fire etc.), why take two separate words?' — because the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, being the one under discussion here, is exceedingly well-known, and the word <s>Agni</s> is also appropriately included. Alternatively, with the word '<s>ādi</s>' applying to both, '<s>agnyādi</s>' represents other <s>vidyās</s> in the physical (<s>ādhibhautika</s>) domain, and '<s>vaiśvānarādi</s>' represents other <s>vidyās</s> in the spiritual (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) domain — thus the inclusion of both '<s>agnyādi</s>' and '<s>vaiśvānarādi</s>' serves as representative indication. 'In fire as an element' — this is co-referentiality. The word 'ca' is for conjunction. 'Well-known' — by this, the reasoning that [it is so] because of well-known usage in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is indicated. Quoting and explaining the word 'ataḥ' from the <s>sūtra</s>, he says — 'ataḥ' means for the reasons stated before. 'Previously stated' means from the reason of the word <s>ātman</s> and the like — this is the meaning. There is no need to search for any other reason — this is the purport. 'Here' — in the <s>Vaiśvānara vidyā</s> and in other <s>vidyās</s>; 'that' — the <s>Agni</s> deity; 'that' — fire as an element. The reversal in the order of reference compared to the <s>sūtra</s> is due to the priority of well-known usage. The word 'ca' is for conjunction. 'By that' is to be supplied. The meaning is: by the word <s>Vaiśvānara</s> and the like. In the absence of the reading 'atra' (here), that too must be supplied.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
Directly also, there is no contradiction, [says] <s>Jaimini</s>. // <s>BBs</s> 1,2.28 //

children.text: nāgnyādayaḥ śabdā agnyādivācakāstathāpi sākṣādevānanyayogena brahmavācakaiśśabdaiḥ vyavahārārthamanabhijñānācca anyatra vyavaharantītyabhyupagame 'virodhaṃ jaiminirvakti /
children.translated_text: The words <s>Agni</s> and the like are not denotors of fire and the like; even so, directly, without any secondary connection, [they denote <s>Brahman</s>]. Because people use [those words] elsewhere [i.e., for fire etc.] for practical purposes due to ignorance [of the primary meaning], and upon accepting this, <s>Jaimini</s> states that there is no contradiction.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.16:
nanu loke vede ca agnyādipadānārm iśādanyatra vyavahāraprasiddhidarśanāt tasya ca kāraṇāntarābhāvāttadanyathānupapattyānyeṣāṃ vāṭcvamaṅgīkāryam / anyathā tadvirodhaḥ syādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - sākṣāditi // atra tathāpītyapiśabdavyākhyānādyadyapīti labhyate / agniśabdaḥ svaparaḥ / agniśabda eva ādiryeṣāṃ te 'gnyādaya iti vigrahaḥ / apiravadhāraṇe 'pītyāśayena sākṣādevetyuktam / arthāntarāvyavadhānenetyarthaḥ / phalitārthamāha - ananyeti // śakyarūpānyasambandhamantareṇa mukhyavṛttyetyarthaḥ / yadvā - tattvapradīparītyānyatra yogavṛttyabhāvena brahmaṇi samyagyogenetyarthaḥ / brahmavācakairapītyapiśabdānvayaḥ / 'tairagnyādiśabdaiḥ'; iti śeṣaḥ / 'vyavahārārthaṃ'; hānādivyavahārasiddhyarthaṃ 'anabhijñānāt'; mukhyavācyajñānābhāvāt / caśabdo na kevalaṃ vyavahārārthaṃ kintvanabhijñānācceti samuccaye / 'anyatra'; agnyādiṣu tān tatra vyavaharanti jñānino 'jñāninaśceti krameṇa śeṣaḥ / 'ityabhyupagame'; iti nimittasaptamī / evamaṅgīkārāt 'avaridhaṃ'; jñānyajñānivyavahāravirodhābhāvaṃ jaiminirācāryo vaktītyarthaḥ / 'yatnānavasaraḥ'; ityuktervaktītyuktam / anenāgnyādiśabdāḥ nāgnyādivācakāḥ, kintu brahmavācakā eva/ tathāpi nānyatra prasiddhivirodhaḥ / na vānyathānupapatyānyeṣāṃ vācyatvaṃ kalpyam / kutaḥ? yato vācyārthadhīvyavahitaṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ vinā sākṣānmukhyavṛttyāpi brahmavācakānagnyādiśabdān mukhyārthajñāninaḥ ajāmilacaramatanaye nārāyaṇaśabdamiva hānādisiddhyarthaṃ tadajñāninastvanabhijñānādeva tān jvalanādiṣu vyavaharantītyabhyupagamenānyatrāvirodhaṃ vyavahāravirodhābhāvaṃ prasiddhivilopābhāvaṃ vaktyasya iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati //
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.16:
Objection: Since in common usage and in the <s>Vedas</s>, the words <s>Agni</s> and the like are seen to be used for entities other than the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), and since there is no other cause [for this usage], their denotation of those other entities must be accepted due to the impossibility of explaining it otherwise. Otherwise there would be a contradiction with that [usage]. — Presenting and explaining the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves this doubt, he says '<s>sākṣāt</s>' (directly). // Here, from the explanation of the word 'api' as 'even so,' the sense 'even though' is obtained. The word '<s>Agni</s>' refers to itself [as a word]. The compound '<s>agnyādayaḥ</s>' is analyzed as 'those of which the word <s>Agni</s> itself is the first.' 'Api' is used in the sense of restriction — with this intention, '<s>sākṣāt</s> eva' (directly alone) is said. The meaning is: without the intervention of another meaning. He states the result — 'ananya' (without other). // The meaning is: through primary denotation, without connection to another potential referent. Alternatively, in the sense of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: through proper connection (<s>samyag yoga</s>) with <s>Brahman</s>, without application elsewhere. 'Api' connects with '<s>brahmavācakaiḥ</s>' (with words denoting <s>Brahman</s>). 'With those very words of <s>Agni</s> and the like' is to be supplied. 'For the purpose of practical usage' — for the accomplishment of practical activities such as abandonment [of what is harmful] and the like. 'Due to ignorance' — due to the absence of knowledge of the primary referent. The word 'ca' is for conjunction in the sense of 'not only for practical usage but also due to ignorance.' 'Elsewhere' — in fire and the like; those who know and those who do not know use [the words] there, respectively — this is to be supplied. 'Upon accepting' — this is a causal locative. Thus, upon this acceptance, <s>Jaimini</s> the teacher states that there is 'no contradiction' — no conflict between the usage of the knowledgeable and the ignorant — this is the meaning. Because it was said 'there is no occasion for effort,' it is said 'he states.' By this: the words <s>Agni</s> and the like do not denote fire and the like, but rather denote <s>Brahman</s> alone. Even so, there is no contradiction with common usage. Nor should their denotation of other entities be postulated due to the impossibility of explaining it otherwise. Why? Because those who know the primary meaning use the words <s>Agni</s> and the like, which are denotors of <s>Brahman</s>, through primary denotation directly, without <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary indication) or other [devices] intervening between the cognition of the denoted meaning — just as [one uses] the word <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> for the last-born son of <s>Ajāmila</s> — for the purpose of accomplishing abandonment [of evil] and the like. But those who do not know the primary meaning use them for fire and the like merely out of ignorance. Upon accepting this, there is no contradiction elsewhere, no conflict with usage, no destruction of well-known convention — this is what he states — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
From the space situated in the mind of <s>Vyāsa</s>, certain delimited [portions]
are taken up and employed by others, like [space delimited by] a house and the like.
Thus, from this statement of the <s>Skānda</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>], there is no mutual contradiction among the views. // 28 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.17:
nanu jaiminyādimatānāṃ bhagavanmatāvirodhitve jaiminyādigrahaṇavaiyarthyāt tadvirodhitve vā kathaṃ viruddharāddhāntena parihāra ityata āha - vyāseti // vyāsacittasthitaṃ matāparaparyāyaṃ jñānākhyamahākāśamapekṣya gṛhādyavacchinnākāśavat 'avacchinnāni'; viviktāni parimitaviṣayāṇi kānicidetāni matānyūrīkṛtya 'anye'; kecana jaiminyādyāḥ vyavaharantītyarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ sattarkadīpāvalyām - ākāśavadvyāptatvātprakāśamānatvācca vyāsacittasthitamatākhyākāśāt 'avacchinnāni'; svasvamatyā viviktāni tāni matāni idaṃ madīyaṃ idaṃ madīyaṃ ityūrīkṛtyānye vyavaharanti / yathā gṛhanagarādibhirākāśapradeśānavacchidyāyaṃ madīyaḥ pradeśo 'yaṃ madīyaḥ pradeśa iti janāḥ vyavaharantīti / matānāmiti bahuvacanaṃ vakṣyamāṇamatavivakṣayā / tathā ca jaiminyādimatānāṃ vyāsamatena parasparaṃ cāvirodha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,2.7.17:
Objection: If the views of <s>Jaimini</s> and others do not contradict the Lord's view, then mentioning <s>Jaimini</s> and others would be pointless; and if they do contradict it, how can there be resolution through mutually contradictory doctrines? — To this he says '<s>Vyāsa</s>.' // With reference to the great space called knowledge, which is another name for the view (<s>mata</s>) situated in the mind of <s>Vyāsa</s>, 'delimited' means distinct, having limited scope — certain of these views are taken up by 'others,' namely <s>Jaimini</s> and the like, and employed — this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Sattarkadīpāvalī</s>: Because of being all-pervading and being illuminating, like space, from the space that is the view called the knowledge situated in the mind of <s>Vyāsa</s>, 'delimited' means distinguished by their own respective understanding — those views, saying 'this is mine, this is mine,' are taken up and employed by others. Just as people delimit portions of space by means of houses, cities, and the like, and conduct affairs saying 'this is my portion, this is my portion.' The plural 'views' is used with the intention of referring to the views to be discussed later. And thus, the views of <s>Jaimini</s> and others do not contradict the view of <s>Vyāsa</s>, nor do they contradict each other — this is the meaning.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
Because of manifestation, says <s>Āśmarathya</s>. // <s>BBs</s> 1,2.29 //

Even though [<s>Brahman</s>] is well-known in fire and the like in their respective contexts, the restriction of <s>Agni</s> and other <s>sūktas</s> [to particular deities] is because of the [special] manifestation of <s>Brahman</s> [in them] — thus says <s>Āśmarathya</s>. // 29 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.18:
nanu laukikaprasiddherajñānādimūlatvenānyathopapattāvapi vaidikāgnyādisūktamantrādiprasiddhyanyathānupapattyāgnyādīnāṃ sūktādigatāgnyādiśabdavācyatvaṃ syāt, tatrājñānādimūlakatvakalpanāyogenānyathopapattyabhāvāt / nāpi vyavahārārthatvena anyathopapattiḥ, anāditvādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhati - abhivyakteriti // atra pūrvasmādapiranuvartanīyaḥ / tacchabdaścānuvṛtto 'nekadhā vipariṇetavya ityāśayena tadvyācaṣṭe - tatreti / 'tatra tatra'; sūktādau tasya brahmaṇa eva 'prasiddhāvapi'; pratipādyatve 'pi agnyādīnāmapratipādyatve 'pītyarthaḥ / agnyādiṣviti sāvadhāraṇam / sūtre avirodhamiti anuṣaktapadatātparyamāha - agnyādīti / ādiśabdaḥ ubhayatra yojyaḥ / yujyata iti vaktīti śeṣaḥ / anenāpi - tattatsūktādau brahmaṇa eva pratipādyatve 'pi agnivāyvādīnāmapratipādyatve 'pi avirodhaḥ / agnyādisūktaniyamaḥ idamagnisūktam idaṃ vāyusūktam iti sūktaniyamaḥ, iyamagnividyā iyaṃ vāyuvidyeti vidyāniyamaśca yujyate / kathaṃ? tairagnyādisūktādibhistasya brahmaṇastasyāmupāstau kṛtāyāṃ tatrāgnyādiṣveva tasya brahmaṇaḥ 'abhi'; svecchayābhivyaktiniyamāttadabhiprāyeṇa tatprasiddherupapatterityevaṃ vaidikāgnyādisūktādiprasiddhyavirodhamāśmarathyācāryo vaktīti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.18:
Now, even though the well-known worldly usage [of the words 'Agni' and the like] can be otherwise explained as having its root in ignorance and the like, the well-known Vedic <s>Agni</s>-hymns, <s>mantras</s>, and the like — since their well-known usage cannot be otherwise explained, the denotability of <s>Agni</s> and the like by the words '<s>Agni</s>' and the like occurring in the hymns would stand, because the hypothesis of its being rooted in ignorance cannot serve as an alternative explanation there. Nor is there an alternative explanation through being for the purpose of worldly transactions, since [the Vedic usage] is beginningless — anticipating this objection, he reads the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>abhivyakteḥ</s>' (because of manifestation). // Here, 'api' (also) from the previous [<s>sūtra</s>] must be carried forward. With the intention that the word 'tat' (that) carried forward must be modified in many ways, he explains: '<s>tatra</s>' (there). 'There, in each [hymn]' — in each hymn and the like — 'even though the well-known usage is of that <s>Brahman</s> alone' — even though [<s>Brahman</s>] alone is the subject taught — [the meaning is:] even though <s>Agni</s> and the like are not the subject taught. '<s>Agnyādiṣu</s>' (in <s>Agni</s> and the like) has restrictive force. Indicating the purport of the supplied word 'non-contradiction' in the <s>sūtra</s>, he says: '<s>agnyādi</s>' (Agni and the like). The word 'ādi' (and the like) should be connected in both places. 'Is justified' — '[the teacher] says': this is the remainder. By this too: even though in each hymn and the like <s>Brahman</s> alone is the subject taught, and even though <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the like are not the subject taught, there is no contradiction. The regulation of the <s>Agni</s>-hymn and the like — 'this is an <s>Agni</s>-hymn, this is a <s>Vāyu</s>-hymn' — this regulation of hymns, and 'this is the <s>Agni</s>-meditation, this is the <s>Vāyu</s>-meditation' — this regulation of meditations — is justified. How? By those <s>Agni</s>-hymns and the like, when the meditation of that <s>Brahman</s> has been performed, there, in <s>Agni</s> and the like alone, of that <s>Brahman</s> — 'abhi' — the regulation of manifestation by His own will — with that intention, the justification of the well-known usage — thus, the teacher <s>Āśmarathya</s> says that there is no contradiction with the well-known Vedic usage of <s>Agni</s>-hymns and the like: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated.
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
Because of being meditated upon (<s>anusmṛti</s>) — [thus holds] <s>Bādari</s>. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.30 |
Because <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is taught in each [hymn], is to be meditated upon in <s>Agni</s> and the like, that regulation [of hymns] is [justified] — thus [holds] <s>Bādari</s>. // 30 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.19:
prakārāntareṇa sūktādiniyamasyānyathopapattiṃ kathayatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - anusmṛteriti // atra pūrvavadadhyāhārādiḥ / 'tatra tatra'; agnyādividyāsu / sūtre 'virodhamityanuṣaktapadatātparyamāha - tanniyama iti // anenāpi - viṣṇoreva agnyādividyāpratipādyatve 'pi yatastasyāgnyādividyāsu uktasya viṣṇostaistattatsūktādyupāsakaistatrāgnyādiṣveva 'anusmṛteḥ'; anusmartavyatvāt pratipattavyatvāt avirodhastanniyamaḥ agnyādisūktādivyavasthā yujyate / ato naitadanyathānupapattyānyeṣāṃ vācyatvaṃ kalpyamiti sūktādiprasiddhyavirodhaṃ 'bādariḥ'; bādarātmajaḥ śukācāryo vaktīti sūtravṛttirdarśitā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.19:
Having presented the <s>sūtra</s> that states the alternative explanation of the regulation of hymns and the like in another way, he explains: '<s>anusmṛteḥ</s>' (because of being meditated upon). // Here, the same supplied [words] as before [apply]. 'There, in each' — in the <s>Agni</s> and other meditations. Indicating the purport of the supplied word 'non-contradiction' in the <s>sūtra</s>, he says: '<s>tanniyama</s>' (that regulation). // By this too: even though <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the subject taught in the <s>Agni</s> and other meditations, since that <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is taught in each of those hymns and the like is 'to be meditated upon' (<s>anusmṛteḥ</s>) — to be remembered, to be apprehended — by the worshippers of those respective hymns in <s>Agni</s> and the like alone — there is no contradiction: that regulation — the arrangement of <s>Agni</s>-hymns and the like — is justified. Therefore, since this [teaching about <s>Brahman</s> in each hymn] cannot be otherwise established, the denotability of others [by these words] should not be hypothesized — the teacher <s>Bādari</s>, son of <s>Badara</s>, the teacher <s>Śuka</s>, says this is the non-contradiction with the well-known usage of hymns and the like: thus the purport of the <s>sūtra</s> has been shown.
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
Because of attainment (<s>sampatti</s>) — [thus holds] <s>Jaimini</s>; for thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.31 |
Even speaking directly of non-contradiction, <s>Jaimini</s> considers the regulation of hymns and the like [to be justified] by the attainment of <s>Agni</s> and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.20:
rītyantareṇa sūktādiniyamasyānyathopapattiṃ kathayatsūtramupanyasyati - sampatteriti // jaiminimatasya pūrvamupanyastatvātkimarthaṃ punarvacanamiti mandāśaṅkānirāsāya ubhayānvayīti śabdaparāmṛṣṭapūrvoktānuvādena viṣayabhedaṃ darśayan sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - sākṣāditi // agnyādiśabdānāṃ mukhyato brahmavācakatve 'pi 'avirodhaṃ'; laukikavyavahāravirodhābhāvaṃ vadannityarthaḥ / atrāpyanuvṛttasya avirodhamityasyārthamāha - sūktādīti // niyamo vyavasthā / saṃprāptyā nimittabhūtayeti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.20:
Having presented the <s>sūtra</s> that states the alternative explanation of the regulation of hymns and the like in yet another way, he says: '<s>sampatteḥ</s>' (because of attainment). // Since <s>Jaimini</s>'s view was presented earlier, what is the purpose of repeating it? — to dispel this frivolous doubt, showing the difference in subject matter through the restatement of what was mentioned before as referred to by the word 'ubhayānvayī' (applicable in both ways), he explains the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>sākṣāt</s>' (directly). // Even when the words '<s>Agni</s>' and the like have their primary denotation in <s>Brahman</s>, 'non-contradiction' (<s>avirodham</s>) — meaning the absence of contradiction with worldly usage: this is the meaning. Here too, he states the meaning of the supplied word 'non-contradiction': '<s>sūktādi</s>' (hymns and the like). // '<s>Niyama</s>' means regulation. 'By the attainment' (<s>saṃprāptyā</s>) — 'which has become the occasion': this is the remainder.

children.text: 'taṃ tathā yathopāsate tadeva bhavati'; iti darśayati // 31 //
children.translated_text: 'He becomes just as he meditates upon Him' — thus [the <s>Śruti</s>] shows. // 31 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.21:
nanvagnyādiṣu bhagavadupāstau agnyādiprāptirbhavatītyetatkuta ityataḥ sūtrasūcitāṃ śrutimudāharati - tamiti // 'taṃ'; paramātmānaṃ yena yena prakāreṇa upāsate adhikāriṇaḥ tena prakāreṇa tadeva rūpaṃ 'bhavati'; prāpnuvantītyarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe 'pi 'yādṛśo bhāvitastvīśastādṛśo jīva ābhavet'; iti tṛtīyatātparyokteḥ 'tadeva bhavati'; tathaiva bhavati / yatprakāreṇopāste tatprakāreṇa bhavatītyayamevārtha uktaḥ / tattvapradīpakārapakṣe upāsate ityekavacanaṃ dhātvantarametat / anena yato 'gnyādisūktādiṣu mukhyataḥ parabrahmaṇa eva pratipādyatve 'pyavirodhaḥ, sūktādiniyamo yujyate / ataḥ na tadanyathānupapattyānyeṣāṃ vācyatvaṃ mantavyam / kathamidaṃ yujyate? tairagnyādiṣu bhagavadupāsakānām agnyādisampatteḥ prāpteḥ / na ca tadasiddhiḥ / 'hi'; yasmāttamiti prasiddhā śrutiḥ / 'tathā'; agnyādyadhikaraṇakopāstyā agnyādiprāptirbhavatīti 'darśayati'; pratipādayati / sākṣāditi laukikavyavahāre 'virodhaṃ vadan jaiminiḥ sūtreṣu 'avirodham'; aniyamākhyavirodhābhāvaṃ niyamaṃ 'manyate'; varṇayatīti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / yadyapyuttarasūtradvaye sādhakavyāpārokteralpākṣaratvācca dṛṣṭeriti vācyam, na tvabhivyakteriti, tasyār iśvaravyāpāratvāt / tathāpyabhivyaktiṃ vinā dṛṣṭerayogāttadgrahaṇenobhayalābhātprādhānyādīśvaravyāpāra evoktaḥ / yadyapyanusmṛtiśabditopāstyanantaramabhivyakteḥ tadanantaraṃ tatsampatteḥ prathamamanusmṛteriti vaktavyam / tathāpyabhivyaktisampatyubhayānantaramapyupāstiḥ kāryeti darśayitumanusmṛtermadhye niveśa iti draṣṭavyam / yadyapi ṛgbhāṣye - pṛthagrūpāṇi viṣṇostu devātāntaragāṇi tu /
agnyādiśabdavācyāni nāmnā sūktabhidā bhavet //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.21:
Now, when the worship of the Lord is performed in <s>Agni</s> and the like, the attainment of <s>Agni</s> and the like [by the worshipper] occurs — whence is this known? Therefore he cites the <s>Śruti</s> indicated by the <s>sūtra</s>: '<s>tam</s>' (Him). // 'Him' (<s>tam</s>) — the <s>Paramātman</s>; in whatever manner the qualified [aspirants] 'meditate upon' [Him] — in that very manner, 'He becomes' — [they] attain that very form: this is the meaning. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> too — 'As the Lord is contemplated, so does the <s>jīva</s> come to be' — from this statement of the third purport, 'He becomes just that' means 'He becomes exactly so.' 'In whatever manner he meditates, in that manner he becomes' — this very meaning is stated. According to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>-author's view, 'meditates upon' is in the singular [and represents] a different verbal root. By this: since even though in <s>Agni</s> and other hymns the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is the primary subject taught, there is no contradiction. The regulation of hymns and the like is justified. Therefore, since this cannot be otherwise established, the denotability of others [by these words] should not be held. How is this justified? Because for the worshippers of the Lord in <s>Agni</s> and the like, the attainment of <s>Agni</s> and the like occurs. And this is not unestablished. 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — because the <s>Śruti</s> 'Him' (<s>tam</s>) is well-known. 'Thus' (<s>tathā</s>) — [the <s>Śruti</s>] 'shows' (<s>darśayati</s>) — teaches — that through meditation with <s>Agni</s> and the like as the locus, the attainment of <s>Agni</s> and the like occurs. Directly — speaking of non-contradiction in worldly usage — <s>Jaimini</s> in the <s>sūtras</s> 'considers' (<s>manyate</s>) — explains — 'non-contradiction' (<s>avirodham</s>) — the absence of the contradiction called non-regulation, [that is,] the regulation: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated. Even though in the two subsequent <s>sūtras</s>, because of the statement of the practitioner's activity, and because of having fewer syllables, the word '<s>dṛṣṭeḥ</s>' (from seeing) should be used rather than '<s>abhivyakteḥ</s>' (from manifestation) — since the latter pertains to the Lord's activity — nevertheless, since '<s>dṛṣṭi</s>' (seeing) is impossible without manifestation, and since by adopting that [term] both are obtained, the Lord's activity is stated as primary. Even though the meditation denoted by the word '<s>anusmṛti</s>' should come first, followed by manifestation, and then the attainment — nevertheless, to show that meditation is required even after both manifestation and attainment, the positioning of '<s>anusmṛti</s>' in the middle should be understood. Even though in the <s>Ṛg Bhāṣya</s> —

children.text: ityagnyādyantargataviṣṇuvācakāgnyādiśabdayogaḥ sūktasya vyavasthāpaka uktaḥ / tathā cāgnyādiśabdāstattatsūktāni ca agnyādigatabrahmarūpeṣveva mukhyāni / evaṃ bahirgatarūpeṣu ca atītānāgatavartamānāgnyādisūktopāsakairagnyādigatatvena anusmartavyatvaṃ vā saṃprāptirvā tattatsūktavyavasthāpakamityanuṣṭhānaviśeṣopayogitayā saurasāvitravāmanaviṣṇvādisūktādivyavasthārthaṃ ca vyavasthāpakāntaramuktamityavirodhaḥ / laukikavaidikavyavahārayoragnyādāvupacaritatvabījaṃ tu tayostatra mukhyatvāṅgīkāre 'tathā dṛṣṭyupadeśāt'; ityanena sūcita 'sarvanāma'; ityādiśrutivirodhādirūpaprāguktānupapattiriti ṭīkāyāmevoktam /
children.translated_text:
'The separate forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s> that dwell within the other deities —
those are denotable by the words "<s>Agni</s>" and the like; by that name, the distinction of hymns arises'

— thus the connection of the words '<s>Agni</s>' and the like, which denote <s>Viṣṇu</s> dwelling within <s>Agni</s> and the like, is stated as the determinant of the hymn. And thus the words '<s>Agni</s>' and the like, and the respective hymns, have their primary [meaning] in the <s>Brahman</s>-forms dwelling within <s>Agni</s> and the like. Similarly, for the external forms too, the fact that past, future, and present worshippers of <s>Agni</s> and other hymns must meditate [on <s>Brahman</s>] as dwelling within <s>Agni</s> and the like, or the attainment [of <s>Agni</s> and the like] — is the determinant of the respective hymns. For the purpose of practical application, and also for the purpose of determining <s>Sūrya</s>-hymns, <s>Savitṛ</s>-hymns, <s>Vāmana</s>-hymns, <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hymns, and the like — another determinant is also stated: hence there is no contradiction. However, the basis for the secondary usage in both worldly and Vedic transactions with regard to <s>Agni</s> and the like — [the question of] when the primary meaning is accepted for those [words referring to <s>Brahman</s>] — [has been answered by the <s>sūtra</s>] 'because of the instruction to view thus' (<s>tathā dṛṣṭyupadeśāt</s>) [as a hint]. The previously stated impossibility in the form of contradiction with the <s>Śruti</s> 'He is [called by] all names' (<s>sarvanāma</s>) and the like has been stated in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> itself.

children.text:
na hyanyopāsako 'nyaṃ prāpnuta iti yujyata ityata āha -
sū - oṃ//
children.translated_text:
Now, since a worshipper of one [deity] does not attain another — it is not justified — therefore he says —
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
And [the <s>Śrutis</s>] teach this [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] in this [<s>Agni</s> and the like]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.32 |
'This' (<s>enam</s>) — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'in this' (<s>asmin</s>) — in <s>Agni</s> and the like — [the <s>Śrutis</s>] 'teach' (<s>āmananti</s>).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.22:
yaduktamagnyādisūktādibhiḥ brahmopāsakasyāgnyādiprāptirbhavatīti tacchrutyuktamapi na yuktam / 'madbhaktā yānti māmapi'; ityāderanyopāsakasyānyaprāpterayogāt / 'śrutopaniṣatkagatyabhidhānāt'; ityādau tadanabhyupagamācceti bhāvenāśaṅkya tatparihāratayā sūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - na hīti // ṭīkāyāmāśaṅkyāvatāryetyanvayaḥ / śaṅkārūpasūtrāvatārikāṃ pradarśyetyarthaḥ / 'hi'; yasmādanyopāsako 'nyaṃ prāpnuta ityetatpramāṇavirodhānna yujyate / tasmāduktamayuktamityarthaḥ / enamityanuvādena viṣṇumiti vyākṛtam / asminnityasya vyākhyānamagnyādāviti / 'āmananti'; pratipādayanti śrutaya iti śeṣaḥ / caśabdaḥ viṣṇūpāsakasyāgnyādiprāptirayukteti pūrvapakṣiśaṅkāvyāvartakaḥ / tena siddhāntipratijñā, agnyādiprāptipadena tadantargatabhagavatprāptereva vivakṣitatvāditi sākṣāddhetuśca sūcitaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - na kevalamekatraivāmananti paṭhanti vājasaneyāḥ, kintvanyatra 'sa yaścāyamasmin'; ityādau, evamanye āmananti 'ya eṣa etasmin'; ityādau, anye cāmananti 'etasyām'; ityādau, anye ca 'tatsṛṣṭvā'; / tadevānuprāviśat ityādau / smaranti ca smṛtikartāraḥ 'yaccandramasi yaccāgnau'; ityādīni / samuccayārthaścaśabda ityuktam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,2.7.22:
What was said — that through <s>Agni</s> and other hymns, the worshipper of <s>Brahman</s> attains <s>Agni</s> and the like — even though stated in <s>Śruti</s>, that is not justified, because from passages such as 'My devotees come to Me alone' and the like, a worshipper of one [deity] cannot attain another. And because in '<s>śrutopaniṣatkagatyabhidhānāt</s>' (because of the statement of the path heard in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>) and the like, that [attainment of other deities] is not accepted — raising this objection, and as a resolution of it, having introduced the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains: 'na hi' (for not). // In the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, the connection is: 'having raised the doubt, [he] introduces [the <s>sūtra</s>].' The meaning is: having shown the <s>sūtra</s>-introduction in the form of the objection. 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — since — 'a worshipper of one [deity] attains another' — this is not justified due to contradiction with authority. Therefore, what was said is unjustified: this is the meaning. 'This' (<s>enam</s>) is echoed, and '<s>Viṣṇu</s>' is the explanation. The explanation of 'in this' (<s>asmin</s>) is 'in <s>Agni</s> and the like.' 'Teach' (<s>āmananti</s>) — the <s>Śrutis</s> teach: this is the remainder. The word 'ca' (and) dispels the prima facie objector's doubt that the attainment of <s>Agni</s> and the like for a worshipper of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is unjustified. By that, the thesis of the established conclusion is indicated, and the direct reason — since by the term 'attainment of <s>Agni</s> and the like,' the attainment of the Lord dwelling within them is what is intended — is also indicated. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however — not only do the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> teach [this] in one place, but also elsewhere in 'He who is in this' and the like; likewise others teach [it] in 'He who is in this' and the like; and others in 'in this' and the like; and others in 'Having created that, He entered into it' and the like. And the <s>Smṛti</s> authors also remember [it] in 'that which is in the moon, that which is in fire' and the like. The word 'ca' is for aggregation: thus it is said.

children.text: 'yo 'gnau tiṣṭhan'; (bṛ. 5-7-5.) 'ya eṣa etasminnagnau tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣaḥ'; (bṛ. 4-5-3.) ityādinā // 32 //
children.translated_text: 'He who abides in fire' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.5); 'He who is this Person in fire, full of light, full of immortality' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.3) — by such [passages]. // 32 //
// Thus ends the <s>Vaiśvānarādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>). // 7 //

children.text:
iti śrīmadānandatīrthabhagavatpādācāryaviracite
brahmasūtrabhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya
dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ // om //
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> composed by the revered <s>Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya</s>,
the second <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) [concludes]. // Oṃ //
the venerable <s>Jagannātha Yati</s>, who was the student of the revered Pūjyapāda
among the <s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryas</s>, the independent masters of all systems —

in the <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣyadīpikā</s>,
the second <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) [concludes]. // Oṃ //
Thus, in the [commentary] composed by the disciple of the revered <s>Raghunāthatīrtha</s>,
// Now the third <s>pāda</s> (quarter). //
// 1. The <s>Dyubhvādhikaraṇa</s> (topic of heaven and earth). //

children.text: tatra cānyatra ca prasiddhānāṃ śabdānāṃ viṣṇau samanvayaṃ prāyeṇāsmin pāde darśayati / viṣṇoḥ paravidyāviṣayatvamuktam /
children.translated_text: In this <s>pāda</s>, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] generally shows the coordination (<s>samanvaya</s>) in <s>Viṣṇu</s> of words that are well-known there [in specific contexts] and elsewhere. The fact that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the subject of higher knowledge (<s>paravidyā</s>) has been stated.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.1:
etatpādapratipādyaṃ darśayati - tatreti // anyonyasamuccaye caśabdau / devatādhikaraṇāpaśūdrādhikaraṇayoḥ samanvayākaraṇāttadvyāvṛttyarthaṃ - 'prāyeṇa'; prācuryeṇeti / tathā ca prāyeṇāsmin tṛtīye pāde 'tatra'; harau tasmāt 'anyatra'; rudraprakṛtyādau ca śrutiliṅgādibhiḥ prasiddhānāṃ nāmaliṅgātmakaśabdānāṃ viṣṇau 'samanvayaṃ'; paramamukhyayā vṛttyā tātparyaprabalahetubhiḥ 'darśayati'; pratipādayati sūtrakṛdityarthaḥ / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayavākyamudāhṛtya viṣayasaṃśayasayuktikapūrvapakṣān darśayati - viṣṇoriti /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.1:
He shows what is to be established in this <s>pāda</s>: '<s>tatra</s>' (there). // The two words 'ca' are for mutual aggregation. Since in the <s>Devatādhikaraṇa</s> and the <s>Apaśūdrādhikaraṇa</s> the coordination is not performed, for the purpose of excluding those — 'generally' (<s>prāyeṇa</s>) — for the most part. And thus, generally in this third <s>pāda</s>, 'there' (<s>tatra</s>) — in <s>Hari</s>; therefore 'elsewhere' (<s>anyatra</s>) — in <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the like — the coordination (<s>samanvaya</s>) of words that are well-known through <s>Śruti</s>, marks (<s>liṅga</s>), and the like — words consisting of names and marks — 'in <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — through the absolutely primary usage (<s>paramamukhyā vṛtti</s>), by reasons that are more powerful in establishing the purport — the <s>sūtrakāra</s> 'shows' (<s>darśayati</s>) — demonstrates: this is the meaning. Indicating the <s>Śruti</s> connection and the like, and citing the subject-passage, he shows the subject, doubt, and reasoned prima facie view: '<s>Viṣṇoḥ</s>' (of <s>Viṣṇu</s>).

children.text:
tatra 'yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣamotaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiśca sarvaiḥ tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam'; (muṃ. 2-2-5.) ityatra /
'prāṇānāṃ granthirasi rudro mā'viśāntakaḥ'; (mahānā-35.)
'prāṇeśvaraḥ kṛttivāsāḥ pinākī'; (ghṛtasū) ityādinā rudrasya
prāṇādhāratvapratīteḥ /
'sa eṣo 'ntaraścarate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ'; (muṃ. 2-2-6.)
iti jīvaliṅgācca tayoḥ prāptiriti //
children.translated_text: There, in the passage 'In whom heaven, earth, and the intermediate space are woven, along with the mind together with all the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) — know Him alone as the <s>Ātman</s> (Self)' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.5), because of the understanding that <s>Rudra</s> is the support of the <s>prāṇas</s> from passages such as 'You are the knot of the <s>prāṇas</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, do not enter me, O destroyer' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 35), and 'The lord of the <s>prāṇas</s>, clad in hides, bearing the <s>Pināka</s>' (<s>Ghṛtasūkta</s>), and because of the indicatory mark of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) in 'That very one moves within, being born in many ways' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.6), there arises the possibility of both [<s>Rudra</s> and the <s>jīva</s>].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.2:
uktamityāvartate / tatretyavyayaṃ tadityarthe 'pi / atretyapyāvartate / ādiśabda ubhayānvayī / rudrasyeti śeṣe ṣaṣṭī / tayorityetat pradhānavāyvorapyupalakṣakam / tathā ca adṛśyatvādiguṇakākṣarasya viṣṇoḥ paravidyāviṣayatvaṃ yatroktaṃ tatraivātharvaṇe tatparavidyāviṣayatvaṃ
yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣamotaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiśca sarvaiḥ /
children.translated_text: In whom heaven, earth, and the intermediate space are woven, along with the mind together with all the <s>prāṇas</s>;
Know Him alone as the <s>Ātman</s>; abandon all other speech. (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.5)

children.text:
'amṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ'; ityatra iti vākye tatra dyubhvādyāśraye uktamityekā yojanā / tatra dyubhvādyāyatanatve 'tayoḥ'; rudrajīvayoḥ prāptiḥ / kutaḥ? atravākye dyubhvādyāyatane prāṇādhāratvapratīteḥ śravaṇāt / tathā sa eṣa iti jīvaliṅgaśravaṇācca / na ca prāṇādhāratvaśravaṇe 'pi kuto 'tra rudrasya prāptiriti vācyam / 'prāṇānāṃ granthirasi rudromāviśāntakastenānnenāpyāyasva'; (mahānā. 35.) iti taittirīyavākyena, tathā -
yo brahmā brahmaṇa ujjabhāra prāṇeśvaraḥ kṛttivāsāḥ pinākīr /
iśāno devassa na āyurdadhātu (ghṛtasūktam.)
ityādikhilasaṃhitāvākyena ca rudrasya prāṇādhāratvapratīteḥ ityaparā yojanā / yadvā - asminneva pakṣe tayorityetatsaptamyantamāśritya liṅgaliṅgirūpadharmadvayaparatayā vyākhyeyam / tathātve ādiśabdo 'rudro vāva lokādhāraḥ'; iti vākyagrāhī / evaṃ tatra tayoḥ prāptiriti dūrānvayena 'tatra'; paravidyāviṣayatve tayo rudrajīvayoḥ prāptirityanyā yojanā / tatra ādyayojanāyāṃ dyubhvādyāyatanatvasya viṣṇvanyatvākṣepamukhena 'tamevam'; ityādinā 'amṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ'; (muṃ. 2-2-5.) iti vākyaśeṣabalātpratītasya mokṣajanakajñānajanakavidyāviṣayatvarūpasya tattvapradīparītyānanyayogena prādhānyena jñeyatvarūpasya vā paravidyāviṣayatvasya pūrvoktasya viṣṇoritaratvākṣepāt adṛśyatvādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / tathā dyubhvādyāyatanatvarūpo viṣayaḥ darśitaḥ / dvividhadvitīyayojanāyāṃ sayuktikapūrvapakṣo darśitaḥ / tṛtīyāyāṃ tu pūrvapakṣaphalaṃ darśitamiti draṣṭavyam / 'yasmin'; paramātmani dvyādilokāḥ 'manaḥ'; tadabhimānī 'sarvaiḥ prāṇaiḥ'; indriyaistadabhimānibhiśca saha 'taṃ'; praviṣṭaṃ paramātmānam 'ekaṃ'; pradhānaṃ 'jānatha'; jānīdhvam iti śrutyarthaḥ /
rudra u mā āviśa iti padacchedaḥ / u ityavyayaṃ sambuddhidyotako nipātaḥ / mā ityavyayaṃ, nāsmadādeśaḥ māśabdaḥ / yadvā metyanenāsmadādeśo māśabdaścetyubhau tantreṇopāttau / sa ca niṣedhārthaḥ / tathā ca - he rudra tvaṃ 'prāṇānām'; indriyāṇāṃ grathyate 'sminniti 'granthiḥ'; āśrayaḥ 'antakaḥ'; saṃhartā cāsi / sa tvaṃ 'mā'; mām 'āviśa'; praviśa mayi sannidhiṃ kurvityarthaḥ / yadvā - he rudra antakastvaṃ māṃ mā praviśetyarthaḥ / 'tena'; āhutirūpeṇa dattena 'annena'; mām 'āpyāyasva'; sukhaya /
yo 'brahmaṇe'; caturmukhāya 'brahma'; vedān 'ujjabhāra'; ujjahāra, sa 'prāṇeśvaraḥ'; indriyeśaḥ 'kṛttivāsāḥ'; kṛttiścarma vasanaṃ yasyāsau, 'pinākīr'; iśāno na āyuḥ 'dadhātu'; puṣṇātviti śrutyantarārthaḥ / siddhānte tu rudrādiśabdāḥ viṣṇuparāḥ / ya eṣa jīvo 'bahudhā'; bahuśarīreṇotpadyamānaḥ śarīrāntaḥsañcārītyātharvaṇaśrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
In the statement 'This is the bridge of immortality' — there, regarding the support of heaven, earth, etc., one interpretation is that '<s>uktam</s>' (it is stated) [connects thus]. There, regarding the abode-nature of heaven, earth, etc., both <s>Rudra</s> and the <s>jīva</s> are possible. Why? Because in that passage there is the hearing of the understanding that the abode of heaven, earth, etc. is the support of the <s>prāṇas</s>. And also because of hearing the indicatory mark of the <s>jīva</s> in 'That very one.' Nor should it be objected 'Even though there is hearing of being the support of the <s>prāṇas</s>, how is <s>Rudra</s> possible here?' — because <s>Rudra</s>'s being the support of the <s>prāṇas</s> is understood from the <s>Taittirīya</s> passage 'You are the knot of the <s>prāṇas</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, do not enter me, O destroyer; nourish yourself with that food' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 35), and also from the <s>Khilasaṃhitā</s> passage 'He who brought forth the <s>Vedas</s> for <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of the <s>prāṇas</s>, clad in hides, bearing the <s>Pināka</s> — may that lord grant us long life' (<s>Ghṛtasūkta</s>) — this is another interpretation. Alternatively, in this very view, taking '<s>tayoḥ</s>' as a locative, it should be explained as referring to two attributes in the form of the indicatory mark and that which bears the mark. In that case, the word '<s>ādi</s>' includes the passage '<s>Rudra</s> indeed is the support of the worlds.' Thus, 'there, of the two, the possibility' — by distant connection, 'there' [means] regarding the status as subject of <s>paravidyā</s>, the possibility of both <s>Rudra</s> and the <s>jīva</s> — this is yet another interpretation. In the first interpretation, the status of being the abode of heaven, earth, etc. — which is understood through the force of the remainder of the passage 'Know Him alone' ... 'This is the bridge of immortality' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.5), namely the status of being the subject of <s>paravidyā</s> in the form of being the subject of knowledge that generates liberation-producing cognition, as explained in <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, or primarily in the form of being the object to be known — since this has been stated previously of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the objection is that it could belong to someone other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the connection with the <s>Adṛśyatva-adhikaraṇa</s> is stated as being one of objection. Likewise, the subject matter in the form of being the abode of heaven, earth, etc. has been shown. In the twofold second interpretation, the prima facie view with reasoning has been shown. In the third interpretation, the result of the prima facie view has been shown — thus it should be understood. 'In whom' — in the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), the worlds beginning with heaven; '<s>manaḥ</s>' — the presiding deity of mind; 'with all <s>prāṇas</s>' — with the senses and their presiding deities; 'Him' — the <s>Paramātman</s> who has entered [all]; 'the one' — the principal; 'know' — know Him — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.
The word-division is: '<s>rudra u mā āviśa</s>.' '<s>U</s>' is an indeclinable particle indicating the vocative. '<s>Mā</s>' is an indeclinable, not a substitute for <s>asmad</s> (first person). Alternatively, both the first-person substitute '<s>mā</s>' and the indeclinable '<s>mā</s>' are comprehended together by implication through '<s>me</s>.' And it has the sense of prohibition. Thus: O <s>Rudra</s>, you are the '<s>granthi</s>' (knot), i.e., the support of the <s>prāṇas</s> (senses), and the '<s>antaka</s>' (destroyer). You — '<s>mā</s>' — me, '<s>āviśa</s>' — enter, i.e., be present near me — this is the meaning. Alternatively: O <s>Rudra</s>, you who are the destroyer, do not enter me — this is the meaning. 'With that' — with food given in the form of oblation — 'nourish yourself,' i.e., be satisfied.
'He who' — for '<s>Brahmā</s>' (<s>Caturmukha</s>, the four-faced one) — '<s>brahma</s>' — the <s>Vedas</s> — '<s>ujjabhāra</s>' — brought forth; he is the '<s>prāṇeśvara</s>' — lord of the senses; '<s>kṛttivāsāḥ</s>' — one whose garment is hide; '<s>Pinākin</s>'; may the lord '<s>dadhātu</s>' — grant, i.e., nourish our lifespan — this is the meaning of the other <s>śruti</s>. But in the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), words like <s>Rudra</s> refer to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The <s>jīva</s> that is 'born in many ways' — being produced in many bodies and moving within bodies — this is the meaning of the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> <s>śruti</s>.

<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.1.2:
The word '<s>uktam</s>' (stated) recurs. The indeclinable '<s>tatra</s>' is also used in the sense of '<s>tad</s>' (that). '<s>Atra</s>' (here) also recurs. The word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) connects with both [citations]. '<s>Rudrasya</s>' is a genitive in the predicate. '<s>Tayoḥ</s>' (of the two) is indicative also of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>Vāyu</s>. And thus, the status of being the subject of <s>paravidyā</s> (higher knowledge) — where it was stated that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the imperishable one possessing qualities such as invisibility, is the subject of <s>paravidyā</s> — in that very <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> [Upaniṣad], that status as subject of <s>paravidyā</s>,

Therefore it is said —
<s>Sūtra</s>: <s>Oṃ</s>
The abode of heaven, earth, etc. [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of its own characteristic word. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.1 |
'Know Him alone as the <s>Ātman</s>' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.5) — because of the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self),
the support of heaven, earth, etc. is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.
Words such as <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, and others, apart from the imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
cannot apply [to anyone else], since fullness of qualities is never attained by them.
Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s> [Purāṇa]. // 1 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.3:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // sautrasvaśabdasya svaśabdaparyāyātmaśabdāditi viṣṇutattvanirṇayokteḥ, svetiśabdaḥ svaśabda iti vyutpattyā svaśabdaparyāyātmaśabdagrāhitvaṃ viṣṇoḥ svarūpasyaiva sākṣādvācako hyayamātmaśabda iti tattvapradīpokteḥ, svasya viṣṇoreva vācakaḥ śabdaḥ svaśabda iti vigrahāśrayeṇa ca ātmaśabdaparāmarśitvamāśritya svaśabdādityetadātmaśabdāditi vyākhyātam / tathā ca 'ityātmaśabdāt'; ityatrātmaśabdaśravaṇādityarthaḥ / dyubhvādyāśraya ityanenāyatanaśabdo vyākhyātaḥ / kvacidāyatanaśabdasyaiva pāṭhaḥ / viṣṇurevetyanena samanvayasūtrānuvṛttaṃ tattvityetat śrutyanusārālliṅgavipariṇāmena vyākhyātam / anena - 'svaśabdāt'; viṣṇuvācisvaśabdaparyāyātmaśabdāt svaśabdāt 'dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ'; svargabhūmyādisarvāśrayaḥ 'tattu'; viṣṇureveti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
ātmāśabdādapi kuto 'yaṃ viṣṇurityata āha - ātmeti // yasmāt 'taiḥ'; viṣṇoritaraiścaturmukhādijīvaiḥ guṇapūrṇatā 'naivāptā'; na sarvathā prāptā / tasmādātmabrahmādayaḥ śabdāḥ 'avyayaṃ'; nityaniratiśayapravṛttinimittavantaṃ viṣṇum 'ṛte'; vinā tadanyaṃ 'na sambhavanti'; na mukhyato vācakatvena prāpnuvantītyarthaḥ / anenātmaśabdasyāpi guṇapūrtirartha ityuktaṃ bhavati / brahmavaivarta ityanantaramanyatra niravakāśatayoktāditi śeṣaḥ / tasyātmaśabdādityanenānvayaḥ/
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.1.3:
He introduces the <s>siddhānta</s> <s>sūtra</s> and explains it — 'Therefore.' The word '<s>svaśabda</s>' (own word) in the <s>sūtra</s> is explained as '<s>ātmaśabda</s>' (the word <s>Ātman</s>), which is a synonym of '<s>svaśabda</s>,' as stated in <s>Viṣṇutattvānirṇaya</s>. The word '<s>Ātman</s>' is a synonym of '<s>svaśabda</s>' by the etymology that '<s>sva</s>' (self) means '<s>svaśabda</s>,' as stated in <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> — since the word '<s>Ātman</s>' directly denotes the very essence of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Also, based on the analysis '<s>svaśabda</s>' means 'the word that denotes <s>sva</s> (one's own), i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone,' the reference to the word '<s>Ātman</s>' is adopted, and thus '<s>svaśabdāt</s>' is explained as '<s>ātmaśabdāt</s>' (because of the word <s>Ātman</s>). Accordingly, in 'because of the word <s>Ātman</s>,' the meaning is: because of hearing the word <s>Ātman</s>. The word '<s>āyatana</s>' (abode) is explained by 'the support of heaven, earth, etc.' In some readings, the word '<s>āyatana</s>' itself appears in the <s>sūtra</s>. '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' — by this, the word '<s>tattva</s>' (reality) carried over from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s> is explained by transforming the <s>liṅga</s> (gender) in accordance with the <s>śruti</s>. By this, the <s>sūtra</s> meaning is stated as: because of '<s>svaśabda</s>' — because of the word <s>Ātman</s>, which is a synonym of '<s>svaśabda</s>' denoting <s>Viṣṇu</s> — '<s>dyubhvādyāyatana</s>' — the support of heaven, earth, and all else — '<s>tat tu</s>' — is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.
As to why even from the word <s>Ātman</s> it must be <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he says: '<s>Ātma</s>.' Since 'by them' — by those other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, namely <s>Caturmukha</s> and other <s>jīvas</s> — 'fullness of qualities is never attained' — is never fully reached — therefore words such as <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, etc., apart from the 'imperishable' — one who possesses eternally unsurpassed grounds for application — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'cannot apply' — cannot attain the status of primary denotation — this is the meaning. By this, it is stated that the word <s>Ātman</s> also has fullness of qualities as its [denoted] meaning. After '<s>Brahmavaivarta</s>' [the word] '<s>niravakāśatayā uktāt</s>' (stated as having no other scope) is to be supplied. Its syntactic connection is with 'because of the word <s>Ātman</s>.'
<s>Sūtra</s>: <s>Oṃ</s>.
[<s>Brahman</s> is the abode of heaven, earth, etc.] because of the description of being approachable by the liberated. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.2 |
'This is the bridge of immortality' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.5) — thus.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.4:
nanu viṣṇau mukhyo 'pyātmaśabdo jāyamānatvarūpajīvaliṅgabalādamukhyārthaḥ kiṃ na syāt / tathā ca na tato viṣṇordyubhvādyāyatanatvanirṇaya ityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya tadupāttaśrutimevādāharati - mukteti // iti muktāprāpyatvavyapadeśādityanvayaḥ / sūtre dyubhvādyāyatanasyeti vipariṇāmena anuvartanīyam / muktopasṛpyeti bhāvanirdeśaḥ/ upasṛpyatvaṃ ceha śrautasetuśabdabalātprāpyāntararahitatve sati prāpyatvaṃ vivakṣitam / nanvarcirādivatprāpyatvamātram / tathā ca - dyubhvādyāyatanasya 'amṛtasya'; iti muktopasṛpyatvokterviṣṇutvaniścayānnātmaśabdasyāmukhyārthatvamāśritya viṣṇoranyat dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ kalpyamiti / 'muktānām'; iti smaraṇādamṛtasyeti jātāvekavacanam / tathā ca 'amṛtasya'; muktajātasya 'eṣaḥ'; paramātmā 'setuḥ'; seturiva seturmukhyāśraya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.1.4:
But [one might object]: even though the word <s>Ātman</s> is primary with respect to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, could it not become secondary in meaning due to the force of the indicatory mark of the <s>jīva</s> in the form of 'being born in many ways'? And thus, the determination that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the abode of heaven, earth, etc. would not follow — anticipating this objection, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and cites the very <s>śruti</s> employed therein: '<s>Mukta</s>.' The syntactic connection is: because of the description of being approachable by the liberated, i.e., attainable by the liberated. In the <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>dyubhvādyāyatanasya</s>' (of the abode of heaven, earth, etc.) is to be carried over by grammatical transformation. '<s>Muktopasṛpya</s>' is a statement of the nature [of the entity]. The 'approachability' intended here, by the force of the scriptural word '<s>setu</s>' (bridge), means being the goal that is attainable without intermediary. [Objection:] But is it not merely attainability like that through the <s>arcirādi</s> (path of light)? [Reply:] Thus: because of the statement in '<s>amṛtasya</s>' (of the immortal) that the abode of heaven, earth, etc. is approachable by the liberated, the certainty that it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> [is established], and therefore, resorting to a secondary meaning of the word <s>Ātman</s>, one should not posit something other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the abode of heaven, earth, etc. From the <s>smṛti</s> passage '<s>muktānām</s>' (of the liberated), the singular in '<s>amṛtasya</s>' is a class-singular. Thus, '<s>amṛtasya</s>' — of the class of liberated ones — '<s>eṣaḥ</s>' — this <s>Paramātman</s> — '<s>setuḥ</s>' — is like a bridge, i.e., the primary support — this is the meaning.
'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the Supreme' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the great one to be known, the Self of all,
'One approaches this blissful Self' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.8) — from such [statements],
because of the description that He alone is attainable by the liberated.
What is the use of saying much here? As long as one does not reach <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island),
the <s>yogin</s> is not liberated — this is the determination of the scriptures.

Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Ādityapurāṇa</s>. // 2 //
