BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.5:
nanu dyubhvādyāyatanasya muktaprāpyatvaṃ kutaḥ viṣṇutvaniścāyakamityāśaṅkāparihārakatayāpi sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - brahmaviditi // 'ityādinā'; vākyena 'tasya'; viṣṇoḥ evetyanena prāpyatvaṃ prāpyāntararahitatve sati prāptatvam / anena dyubhvādyāyatanasya muktopasṛpyatvavyapadeśāttasya viṣṇoreva muktopasṛtapyatvavyapadeśādityāvṛttyā sūtraṃ vyākhyātam/ pradhānasūtre 'nuvṛttaṃ tattvityetadiha vipariṇāmena anuvartanīyamiti sūcitam / upasṛpyapadaṃ bhāvapradhānaṃ kṛtvā vyākhyātam/ evakāro liṅgasyānyaniṣṭhatvavyavacchedakaḥ / 'brahmavit'; viṣṇujñānī muktassan 'paraṃ'; viṣṇumāpnotīti taittirīyaśrutyarthaḥ / 'nārāyaṇam'; iti taittirīyopaniṣadi mahopaniṣadi ca śrutam / atra 'tadviśvamupajīvati'; ityanuvartate / tathā ca 'tadviśvaṃ'; jagat mahanīyaṃ jñeyaṃ, pūjyajñeyaṃ vā / viśvasvāminaṃ 'parāyaṇaṃ'; muktānāmāśrayamupajīvatīti śrutyarthaḥ/ 'muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ'; iti sahasranāmagatamekaṃ nāma / paramā mukhyā gamyata iti gatirāśrayaḥ / 'etam'; iti taittirīyavākyamānandamayanaye vyākṛtam / ādipadena 'etamānandamayamātmānamupasaṅkramya'; 'paramaṃ yaḥ parāyaṇam'; ityādikaṃ gṛhyate /
nanūdāhṛtavākyairastu viṣṇoḥ muktaprāpyatvaṃ, tathāpyatrānyavyavacchedābhāvādviṣṇuvadanyasya muktaprāpyatvaṃ kiṃ na syāditi liṅgasya sāvakāśatvamāśaṅkya anyatra prāpyatvamātrasambhave 'pi niruktopasṛpyatvaṃ sautramuktaśabditavivakṣitamuktyupetajīvaprāpyatvaṃ vānyatra niravakāśamiti pramāṇenāha - bahuneti // 'atra'; prāpyamokṣatatsādhanaviṣaye 'bahunoktena'; idamidaṃ ceti pratyekaṃ bahunā vacanena 'kiṃ prayojanaṃ'; na kimapi, pratyutoktigauravameveti bhāvaḥ / tarhi kathaṃ nirṇaya ityata āha - yāvacchvetamiti / 'śvetaṃ'; śvetadvīpākhyaṃ viṣṇusthānaṃ 'yāvanna gacchati'; na prāpnoti, tatratyaṃ viṣṇuṃ ca na paśyati 'tāvadyogī'; aparokṣajñānākhyopāyavān mukto na syāt / bhagavadicchārūpāvaraṇānmuktaḥ samyagāvirbhūtajñānānandādimān na bhavediti 'eṣaḥ'; upadeśaḥ 'śāstravinirṇayaḥ'; śāstratattvaviṣayakanirṇayasādhanamityarthaḥ / eṣor'thaḥ 'śāstravinirṇayaḥ'; tajjanyanirṇayaviṣaya iti vā / bhāvabodhe tu - sūtre purāṇe ca muktapadena liṅgabhaṅgavān vivakṣita ityuktam / atra śvetadvīpāganturamuktatvoktyā śvetadvīpaṃ prāptasyaiva muktatvaṃ jñāyate / tathā ca tatsthitasya viṣṇorevetaravyavacchedena muktaprāpyatvaṃ siddhamiti bhāvaḥ / ityādityapurāṇe ityasya tasyaiva muktaprāpyatvavyapadeśādityanenānvayaḥ / anena tasyaivetyevakārasyopayogo jñāpito bhavati / asya hetorna liṅgasya sāvakāśatvaṃ śaṅkyamityadhyāhṛtasādhyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.1.5:
Now, to address the doubt as to how the fact that the substratum of <s>Dyubhvādi</s> (heaven, earth, etc.) is attainable by the liberated (<s>muktaprāpya</s>) establishes its identity as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he explains the <s>sūtra</s> as resolving this very objection — beginning with '<s>brahmavit</s>' (the knower of <s>Brahman</s>). By the statement beginning with 'iti' and the word 'tasya' meaning 'of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone,' attainability (<s>prāpyatva</s>) is established — that is, the state of being reached while being free from any other object of attainment. By this, the <s>sūtra</s> is explained through the repetition: 'because the substratum of <s>Dyubhvādi</s> is described as approachable by the liberated, and because that description of being approachable by the liberated belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' It is indicated that the word 'tat' carried over from the main <s>sūtra</s> is to be continued here in a modified sense. The word <s>upasṛpya</s> (approachable) is explained with the abstract sense predominating. The particle 'eva' (alone) serves to exclude the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) from referring to any other entity. '<s>Brahmavit</s>' — the knower of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, being liberated, attains '<s>param</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>: this is the meaning of the <s>Taittirīya</s> <s>śruti</s>. '<s>Nārāyaṇam</s>' is heard in the <s>Taittirīyopaniṣad</s> and the <s>Mahopaniṣad</s>. Here the passage '<s>tadviśvam upajīvati</s>' (the entire universe depends on Him) continues. And thus '<s>tadviśvam</s>' means the universe that is worthy of reverence and knowledge, or that which is worshipful and knowable. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is: one depends upon '<s>parāyaṇam</s>' — the refuge of the liberated — the Lord of the universe. '<s>Muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ</s>' (the supreme goal of the liberated) is one name found in the <s>Sahasranāma</s>. 'Paramā' means the primary; '<s>gati</s>' means refuge, that which is reached. 'Etam' — this <s>Taittirīya</s> passage was explained in the section on <s>Ānandamaya</s>. By the word 'ādi,' passages such as '<s>etam ānandamayam ātmānam upasaṅkramya</s>' (approaching this self consisting of bliss) and '<s>paramaṃ yaḥ parāyaṇam</s>' (He who is the supreme refuge) are included.
Now, even if <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being the goal of the liberated is established by the cited passages, still, since there is no exclusion of others here, why could not some other entity, like <s>Viṣṇu</s>, also be the goal of the liberated? — anticipating this objection regarding the indicatory mark having scope elsewhere, he states with authority — beginning with '<s>bahunā</s>': even though mere attainability may be possible elsewhere, the specifically described approachability (<s>upasṛpyatva</s>) — that is, the attainability by the liberated soul as intended by the word <s>mukta</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> — has no scope elsewhere. 'Atra' — in the subject matter of the attainable liberation and its means; 'by much that has been said' — what purpose is served by stating each thing individually at such length? None whatsoever; rather, it only creates verbosity — this is the import. Then how is the determination made? To this he says — beginning with '<s>yāvacchvetam</s>': so long as one does not go to '<s>śvetam</s>' — the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island) — does not reach it and does not see <s>Viṣṇu</s> residing there, the <s>yogī</s> — one endowed with the means called direct knowledge (<s>aparokṣajñāna</s>) — cannot be liberated. Due to the veil in the form of the Lord's will, the liberated one would not fully possess manifested knowledge, bliss, and the rest. 'This' is the teaching; '<s>śāstravinirṇayaḥ</s>' means the instrument for determining the truth of scripture — this is the meaning. Or, the meaning of 'eṣa' is: '<s>śāstravinirṇayaḥ</s>' — the subject matter of the determination produced by it. In the <s>Bhāvabodha</s>, however, it is said that in the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>, by the word <s>mukta</s>, one whose indicatory marks are broken is intended. Here, by the statement that one who has not yet reached <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> is not liberated, it is understood that only one who has reached <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> is truly liberated. And thus, the fact that <s>Viṣṇu</s> residing there alone — to the exclusion of others — is the goal of the liberated is established — this is the import. The word 'ityādi' from the <s>Āditya Purāṇa</s> connects with 'because of the description of His alone being the goal of the liberated.' By this, the utility of the particle 'eva' in 'tasyaiva' is made known. Because of this reason, the objection that the indicatory mark has scope elsewhere should not be entertained — this connects with an implied conclusion.

<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>
// <s>Nānumānam atacchabdāt</s> //
[It is] not that which is inferred (<s>anumāna</s>), because of the absence of words denoting it (<s>atacchabdāt</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.3 |
<s>Rudra</s>, who is conceived by scriptures (<s>āgama</s>) whose authority is established merely by inference (<s>anumāna</s>), is not to be spoken of here [as the substratum].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.6:
nanu prāguktarītyā rudraprakṛtyordyubhvāyatanatvaṃ kiṃ na syādityatastatsādhakābhāvānna tayostadityāha sūtrakṛt - nānumānamiti // atra nānumānamiti sādhyāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - nānumānātmaketi / 'anumānaprāptaprāmāṇyāsadāgamo 'numātmakaḥ'; iti tattvapradīpokteḥ anumānātmake anumānasiddhaprāmāṇyake pāśupatādyāgame sarvāśrayatvena kalpito bodhita ityarthaḥ / kecittu - pramāṇatvena anumīyata ityanumānamiti vyācikhyuḥ / etatpakṣe ātmakaśabdavaiyarthyaṃ, tattvapradīpaṭīke viruddhe / rudrapadaṃ pradhānāderupalakṣakam / pradhānasūtrādanuvṛttena dyubhvādyāyatanapadenopasthāpitaṃ nañarthapratiyoginaṃ darśayati - atreti / dyubhvādyāyatanaprakaraṇa ityarthaḥ / 'vācyaḥ'; pratipādyaḥ / sarvāśrayatveneti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.1.6:
Now, by the reasoning stated earlier, why could <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> not be the substratum of <s>Dyubhvādi</s>? To this, because there is no proof establishing that for them, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>) says — '<s>nānumānam</s>.' Here he explains the part to be proved (<s>sādhyāṃśa</s>) — beginning with '<s>nānumānātmaka</s>.' Since the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> states: 'that scripture (<s>āgama</s>) whose authority is not established but is arrived at through inference is called <s>anumānātmaka</s> (having the nature of inference),' [the meaning is:] <s>Rudra</s>, who is taught or presented as the support of all in the <s>Pāśupata</s> and other scriptures whose authority is established only by inference — is not [the referent here]. Some, however, have explained it as: 'that which is inferred as having authority is <s>anumāna</s>.' In this interpretation, the word '<s>ātmaka</s>' becomes redundant, and it contradicts the commentary on the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. The word '<s>Rudra</s>' is an indicator (<s>upalakṣaka</s>) for <s>Pradhāna</s> and others as well. With the word '<s>Dyubhvādyāyatana</s>' brought forward by continuation from the main <s>sūtra</s>, he shows the counter-positive of the negation — with 'atra,' meaning: in the context of the <s>Dyubhvādyāyatana</s> section. '<s>Vācyaḥ</s>' means 'to be taught' [i.e., as the support of all] — this is to be supplied.
Because of the absence of words (<s>śabda</s>) denoting Him — such as 'bearer of ashes' (<s>bhasmadhara</s>), 'fierce' (<s>ugra</s>), and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.7:
evaṃ sūtre pratijñāṃśaṃ vyākhyāya hetvaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - bhasmadhareti // tasya rudrasya śabdastacchabdaḥ / tacchrutiliṅgātmakaḥ / tathā ca bhasmadharogratvādidharmaviśiṣṭadharmibodhakabhasmadharogrādiśabdābhāvādityarthaḥ / atha vā - 'kimucyate bhasmadharogratvādīnāṃ tacchabdatvam'; ityuttaraṭīkābalādbhāvabhavitrorabhedavivakṣayā svārthe tvapratyayaḥ / tatprayogastu liṅgātmakaśabdasyāpi saṅgrahāya / bhāvabodhe tu - bhasmadharetyanena rudravācakanāmātmakaśabdo gṛhyate / ugratvapadena ugratvarūpaliṅgātmakaśabdo gṛhyate / ādipadena nāmaliṅgātmakaśabdāntarāṇi gṛhyante / samākhyāderupalakṣakametat / tathā ca - bhasmadharādirudraśrutīnām ugratvādirūpatalliṅgānāṃ rudraprāpakasamākhyādīnāṃ cābhāvādityartha ityuktam / atra rudraśivāditacchabdābhāvādityanuktvā bhasmadharogratvādīti vacanaṃ 'rudro bhasmadharo nagnaḥ'; iti vacanādviśeṣanāmābhiprāyeṇa / ata evaitadvacanoktāḥ nagnādiśabdā evādipadena grāhyā iti dhyeyam / bhasmadharetyetatpradhānatriguṇatvādirūpaprakṛtiprāpakaśrutiliṅgādyabhāvādityarthāntaropalakṣakatayāpi vyākhyeyam / yadyapi atacchabdādityasya tacchabdābhāvāditi vyākhyāne nañaḥ kriyāsāpekṣatvenāsamarthatvātsamāsānupapattiḥ / tathāpi nirmakṣikamityādāviva 'arthābhāve yadavyayam'; ityavyayībhāvasamāsāśrayaṇānnānupapattiḥ / pañcamītvāt nātrām bhavati / anena sūtre jagatkartṛtvenānumīyate ityanumānaśabdena vā 'ānumānamanumānasambandhi'; iti sattarkadīpāvalyukterānumānamiti padacchedenānumānaśabdena vā anumānasiddhaprāmāṇyakapāśupatādyāgamasiddhaṃ rudrapradhānādhikaṃ gṛhyate / yadvā - pramāṇatvenānumīyata ityanumānaṃ pāśupatādyāgamaḥ / tato matvarthe arśa ādibhyo 'c, tena tatpratipādyamucyate / evamānumānamiti padacchede 'pyaṇantātpunaraṇ kāryaḥ / tatra prathamāṇantarapadenāgama ucyate / dvitīyena pratipādyatvam / tathā ca anumānātmakapāśupatādyāgamapratipādyaṃ rudrādikaṃ na dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ na 'yasmin'; ityādiprakaraṇe sarvāśrayatvena pratipādyaṃ, kutaḥ? 'atacchabdāt'; rudrapradhānādisādhakaśrutiliṅgādyabhāvāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.1.7:
Having thus explained the thesis portion (<s>pratijñāṃśa</s>) of the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains the reason portion (<s>hetvāṃśa</s>) — beginning with '<s>bhasmadhara</s>.' The word denoting <s>Rudra</s> is '<s>tacchabda</s>' (that-word). That consists of <s>śruti</s> (scriptural text) and <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory marks). And thus the meaning is: because of the absence of words like '<s>bhasmadhara</s>' (bearer of ashes), '<s>ugra</s>' (fierce), etc., which convey a substrate qualified by distinctive attributes of <s>Rudra</s>. Alternatively, by the force of the later sub-commentary that asks 'why is it said that bearing ashes, fierceness, and the like constitute <s>tacchabda</s>?' — with the intention of non-difference between <s>bhāva</s> (state) and <s>bhavitr</s> (possessor), the <s>tva</s>-suffix is in the reflexive sense. Its usage, however, is to include words of the indicatory-mark type as well. In the <s>Bhāvabodha</s>, however, it is said: by '<s>bhasmadhara</s>' the word-type consisting of names denoting <s>Rudra</s> is grasped; by '<s>ugratva</s>' the word-type consisting of indicatory marks in the form of fierceness is grasped; by the word 'ādi' (etc.) other words of both name and indicatory-mark types are grasped. This is an indicator for <s>samākhyā</s> (designation) and the rest. And thus the meaning is: because of the absence of <s>śrutis</s> about <s>Rudra</s> such as '<s>bhasmadhara</s>,' because of the absence of indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) in the form of fierceness and the like pertaining to him, and because of the absence of designations (<s>samākhyā</s>) that lead to <s>Rudra</s>. Here, rather than saying 'because of the absence of words denoting <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, etc.,' the specific mention of '<s>bhasmadhara</s>, <s>ugratva</s>, etc.' is based on the intention of special names, following the statement '<s>Rudro bhasmadharo nagnaḥ</s>' (<s>Rudra</s> is the bearer of ashes, the naked one). Therefore, it should be noted that the words like '<s>nagna</s>' (naked) mentioned in that statement are precisely what is to be grasped by the word 'ādi.' '<s>Bhasmadhara</s>' etc. should also be explained as an indicator for the alternative meaning — namely, the absence of <s>śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, etc. that would lead to <s>Prakṛti</s> with its three <s>guṇas</s> and other attributes. Although in the explanation of '<s>atacchabdāt</s>' as '<s>tacchabdābhāvāt</s>' (because of the absence of that-word), the negation particle, being dependent on a verb, creates an incompetence for compounding, nevertheless — just as in '<s>nirmakṣikam</s>' (free from flies) and the like — by resorting to the <s>Avyayībhāva</s> compound based on the rule 'the indeclinable [is used] in the sense of absence of the thing,' there is no impossibility. The fifth case ending does not apply here. By this, in the <s>sūtra</s>, through the word '<s>anumāna</s>' meaning 'that which is inferred as the creator of the world,' or through the word-splitting '<s>ānumānam</s>' and the statement of <s>Sattarkadīpāvalī</s> that '<s>ānumāna</s> means that which is connected with inference' — <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s>, and others established in the <s>Pāśupata</s> and other scriptures whose authority is established by inference are grasped. Or alternatively: '<s>anumāna</s>' means the <s>Pāśupata</s> and other scriptures that are inferred as authoritative. From that, by the <s>matvartha</s> (possessive) suffix '<s>ac</s>' from the rule '<s>arśa-ādibhyaḥ ac</s>,' what is taught by it is denoted. Even in the word-splitting '<s>ānumānam</s>,' the suffix <s>aṇ</s> must be applied again after the <s>aṇ</s>-ending word. In that case, by the first <s>aṇ</s>-ending word, the scripture is denoted; by the second, its being the thing taught. And thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated: <s>Rudra</s> and others, who are taught by the <s>Pāśupata</s> and other scriptures whose authority rests on inference, are not the substratum of <s>Dyubhvādi</s>, nor are they to be taught as the support of all in the section beginning with '<s>yasmin</s>' (in whom) — why? — '<s>atacchabdāt</s>' — because of the absence of <s>śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, etc. that would establish <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s>, and others.

children.text: 'so 'ntakaḥ sa rudraḥ sa prāṇabhṛtsa prāṇanāyakaḥ sar iśo yo hariryo 'nanto yo viṣṇuryaḥ parovarīyān'; ityādinā prāṇagranthirudratvāderviṣṇorevoktatvāt /
children.translated_text: 'He is <s>Antaka</s> (the destroyer), He is <s>Rudra</s>, He is the sustainer of life-breath (<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>), He is the leader of life-breath (<s>prāṇanāyaka</s>), He is the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), He is <s>Hari</s>, He is the Infinite (<s>Ananta</s>), He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, He is the greatest of the great (<s>parovarīyān</s>)' — because by such passages, attributes like being the knot of the life-breath (<s>prāṇagranthi</s>) and being <s>Rudra</s> are stated to belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.8:
nanvātharvaṇe rudrādijñāpakābhāve 'pi atroktaprāṇādhāratvapratipādikāyāṃ 'prāṇānāṃ granthirasi rudra'; (mahānā-16-2.) ityādisamākhyāśrutau rudrādiśabdānām antakatvādiliṅgānāṃ coktatvāttadbalāttatroktaṃ dyubhvādyātanatvaṃ rudrādeḥ kiṃ na syādityata āha - sa iti // yo 'ntakassaṃhartā sa eva tacchabdavācyaḥ śrutaḥ sa viṣṇureva / yo rudraḥ śrutaḥ so 'pi viṣṇureva / yaḥ 'prāṇabhṛt'; prāṇādhāratvabodhakaprāṇagranthiśabdavācyaḥ, so 'pi viṣṇureva / yaḥ 'prāṇanāyakaḥ'; tatsvāmī tata eva prāṇeśa śabditaḥ so 'pi viṣṇureva / yar iśaḥ śrutaḥ so 'pi viṣṇureva / yo 'nantastacchabdavācyaḥ so 'pi trividhaparicchedaśūnyatvādviṣṇureva, na śeṣaḥ / yaḥ parovarīyān so 'pi rudrādeḥ parato vāṇyādeḥ parādviriñcāt parataḥ prakṛteḥ paratvāddharireva nānya iti śrutyarthaḥ /
atrāntarādhikaraṇodāhṛtacaturvedaśikhāvākye ca 'parasmāduttamaṃ proktam'; iti vacanānusāreṇa paraparataravaravaratamānāṃ caturṇāṃ pratyāyanāya vṛttivākye subādeśasya sorutvotvaguṇasamānaśabdalopā jñātavyāḥ / pratyuddeśyaṃ vidheyānvayajñāpanāya bahūnāṃ yattadāṃ prayogaḥ / 'ityādinā'; śrutyantaravākyena 'prāṇagranthirudratvādeḥ'; prāṇagranthitvaliṅgasya rudraśabdavācyatvasya ca tasyaiva viṣṇorevoktatvādityarthaḥ / prāṇeśvarādiśabdavācyatvamantakatvādiliṅgaṃ cādiśabdārthaḥ / prakṛtiśrutiliṅgāderapyupalakṣakametat / na tu rudrāderityevakārārthaḥ / evakāreṇānyatrāmukhyatassattvamanumanyate / uktatvādityasya 'na rudrādiśrutiliṅgavirodhaḥ'; ityadhyāhṛtasādhyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.1.8:
Now, even if in the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (the <s>Atharva Veda</s>) there is an absence of indicators for <s>Rudra</s> and others, still, in the <s>samākhyā-śruti</s> (designation-scripture) '<s>Prāṇānāṃ granthir asi Rudra</s>' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 16.2) — 'You are <s>Rudra</s>, the knot of the vital breaths' — which teaches the being-the-support-of-<s>prāṇa</s> that is stated here, the words '<s>Rudra</s>' and the like, and the indicatory marks such as being the destroyer (<s>Antaka</s>), are present. So why could not, by the force of that, the substratumhood of <s>Dyubhvādi</s> belong to <s>Rudra</s> and others? To this he says — beginning with '<s>sa</s>': He who is '<s>Antaka</s>' — the destroyer — He who is denoted by that word as heard [in scripture], He is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. He who is heard as '<s>Rudra</s>,' He too is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. He who is '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' — denoted by the word '<s>prāṇagranthi</s>' (knot of the vital breaths) as the support of <s>prāṇa</s> — He too is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. He who is '<s>prāṇanāyaka</s>' — the master of the vital breaths — He who is thereby designated as '<s>Prāṇeśa</s>' (Lord of <s>prāṇa</s>), He too is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. He who is heard as '<s>Īśa</s>' (Lord), He too is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. He who is '<s>Ananta</s>' (Infinite) — denoted by that word — He too, because of being devoid of the three kinds of limitation, is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not <s>Śeṣa</s> (the serpent). He who is '<s>parovarīyān</s>' (greater than the great) — He too, being beyond <s>Rudra</s>, beyond <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) and others, beyond <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), and beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> — is <s>Hari</s> alone and none other: this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.
Here, in the passage from the <s>Caturvedaśikhā</s> cited in the <s>Antarādhikaraṇa</s>, following the statement '<s>parasmād uttamaṃ proktam</s>' (it is declared to be the highest beyond the supreme), for conveying the four degrees — <s>para</s> (beyond), <s>paratara</s> (further beyond), <s>vara</s> (excellent), and <s>varatama</s> (most excellent) — the grammatical operations of <s>su</s>-replacement, <s>sor-utu</s> sandhi, <s>otva</s> (o-substitution), <s>guṇa</s>, and elision of identical sounds should be understood in the compound expression. The use of multiple <s>yat-tad</s> (who-he) correlatives is for indicating the predicate-connection with each subject. 'By such passages' — by the statement from another <s>śruti</s> — 'because being the knot of the life-breath (<s>prāṇagranthi</s>) as an indicatory mark and being denoted by the word <s>Rudra</s> are stated to belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' — this is the meaning. Being denoted by words like '<s>Prāṇeśvara</s>' (Lord of <s>prāṇa</s>) and indicatory marks like being the destroyer are the meaning of the word 'ādi' (etc.). This is also an indicator for the <s>śruti</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, etc. pertaining to <s>Prakṛti</s> as well. 'Not of <s>Rudra</s> and others' — this is the meaning of the particle 'eva' (alone). By the particle 'eva,' it is conceded that these terms do apply to others, but not in the primary sense. The phrase 'because of being stated' connects with the implied conclusion: 'there is no contradiction with the <s>śruti</s> and <s>liṅga</s> pertaining to <s>Rudra</s> and others.'
And in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] —
Because He drives away (<s>drāvayate</s>) affliction (<s>rujam</s>), He is called <s>Rudra</s>; therefore [He is] <s>Janārdana</s>.
He is <s>Īśāna</s> (the Ruler) because of [being the source of] <s>Īśāna</s> himself; He is <s>Mahādeva</s> (the Great God) because of His greatness (<s>mahattvataḥ</s>).
Those men who drink the nectar of heaven (<s>nāka</s>), liberated from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence),

children.text: tadādhāro yato viṣṇuḥ pinākīti tataḥ smṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: because <s>Viṣṇu</s> is their support (<s>ādhāra</s>), He is therefore traditionally called <s>Pinākī</s> (bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> bow).
He is <s>Śiva</s> (the auspicious one) because of being of the nature of bliss (<s>sukhātmakatva</s>); He is <s>Śarva</s> because He destroys affliction (<s>śam rodhanāt</s>); He is <s>Hari</s>,
because He pervades (<s>vaste</s>) this body, which is of the nature of action (<s>kṛtyātmaka</s>), setting it into activity —

children.text:
kṛttivāsāstato devo viriñcaśca virecanāt /
bṛṃhaṇādbrahmanāmāsāvaiśvaryādindra ucyate //
children.translated_text:
He is therefore called <s>Kṛttivāsas</s> (clad in hides); and He is the god <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) because of creating (<s>virecanāt</s>);
He bears the name <s>Brahman</s> because of expanding (<s>bṛṃhaṇāt</s>), and is called <s>Indra</s> because of His supreme lordship (<s>aiśvaryāt</s>).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.9:
nanu tathāpi na prāṇādhāratvadyubhvādyāyatanatvabodhakasamākhyāśrutau viṣṇoḥ pratipādyatvaniścayaḥ / tatratyānāṃ rudrādiśabdānāṃ paśupatyādāveva rūḍhatvena viṣṇau tadabhāvāt, bhāve vā punaraniścayāt / viṣṇau yogavṛttisambhave 'pi tasyā rūḍhito durbalatvenāniścāyakatvāt / na hi śrutyantare viṣṇuliṅgādyastītyata āha - brahmāṇḍe ceti / co 'pyarthaḥ samuccaye / uktatvādityanuvartate / tenāsyānvayaḥ / kimuktamityato rudrādiśabdānāṃ mahāyogavidvadrūḍhipratipādakaṃ vākyaṃ paṭhati - rujamiti / 'rujaṃ'; rogam utpattyādikaṃ 'drāvayate'; nirvāpayati nivartayati yasmāttasmādrudra ityucyate / ka ityata stadrūpaviśeṣamāha - janārdana iti / jananamardayatīti vyutpattirḥ / 'iśanārt iśānāṃ'; brahmādīnāṃ ceṣṭakatvādīśāno 'pi sa evetyarthaḥ / mahattvata ityupalakṣaṇam / dyotanādeścetyapi draṣṭavyam / ye 'narāḥ'; janāḥ saṃsārasāgarānmuktāḥ santo 'nākaṃ'; paramasukhaṃ 'pibanti'; bhuñjate te pinākāḥ / viṣṇuryataḥ 'tadādhāraḥ'; teṣāmādhārastataḥ pinākīti 'smṛtaḥ'; abhihitaḥ śrutāviti śeṣaḥ / śruta iti pāṭhaḥ svarasaḥ / 'śaṃrodhanāt'; muktiparyantaṃ svarūpabhūtamapi sukhaṃ rudhvā vartanāt āsurasakhaṃ nirudhya vartanādvā śarva ityarthaḥ / yataḥ 'kṛtyātmakaṃ'; carmamayamimaṃ dehaṃ 'pravartayan'; sṛjan niyamayan vā tena svātmānaṃ jīvaṃ vā 'vaste'; ācchādayati tadantarvartate / yadvā - dehaṃ vaste adhivasatītyataḥ kṛttivāsā ityucyata ityarthaḥ / 'virecanāt'; jagatsarjanādasau viṣṇuḥ bṛṃhaṇādvardhanādvā brahmanāmā / asau paramaiśvaryādindra ityucyate /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 9:
Objection: Even so, there is no certainty that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the one established in the name-explanation <s>Śruti</s> that conveys the status of being the support of <s>Prāṇa</s>, the abode of heaven, earth, and the like — because the words <s>Rudra</s> and the like occurring therein are conventionally established (<s>rūḍha</s>) in <s>Paśupati</s> and the like alone, and there is no such [usage] in <s>Viṣṇu</s>; or even if [such usage] exists, there is still no certainty. Even though etymological derivation (<s>yogavṛtti</s>) in <s>Viṣṇu</s> is possible, it cannot produce certainty because it is weaker than conventional usage. Nor is there any <s>Śruti</s> from another [source] with a mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like [to support this] — to this he says: 'and in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>].' The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'api' (also), [used] for accumulation. 'Because of being stated' carries forward. The syntactic connection is with that. What is stated? — for that, he reads a passage that establishes the <s>mahāyoga</s> (great etymological derivation) and <s>vidvadrūḍhi</s> (conventional usage among the learned) of the words <s>Rudra</s> and the like in <s>Viṣṇu</s> — '<s>rujam</s>' (disease). '<s>Rujam</s>' — disease, birth, and the like — '<s>drāvayate</s>' — He quenches, removes — because of which, therefore He is called <s>Rudra</s>. Who is He? — to this he states His specific form: '<s>Janārdana</s>.' The etymology is: He who torments (<s>ardayati</s>) birth (<s>janana</s>). '<s>Iśānām</s>' — because of being the agent of <s>Brahmā</s> and others, He is <s>Īśāna</s> (the ruler) as well — that is the meaning. 'Because of greatness' — this is indicative. 'Because of illumination' and '<s>Īśa</s>' should also be understood. Those who are '<s>anarāḥ</s>' — people freed from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> — 'drink' (<s>pibanti</s>) — enjoy — '<s>anāka</s>' — supreme happiness — they are <s>pinākās</s>. Since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is 'their support' (<s>tadādhāra</s>) — the support of those — therefore He is 'remembered' (<s>smṛtaḥ</s>) — called — <s>Pinākī</s>; 'in the <s>Śruti</s>' is the remainder. The reading '<s>śruta</s>' (heard) is natural. 'Because of obstructing bliss' (<s>śaṃrodhanāt</s>) — because He withholds even the happiness that is the essential nature [of the <s>jīva</s>] up to liberation, or because He obstructs the companion of the <s>asuras</s> — therefore He is called <s>Śarva</s>: that is the meaning. Because '<s>kṛtyātmakam</s>' — this body made of skin — He 'sets in motion' (<s>pravartayan</s>) — creates or governs — by that, 'He clothes' (<s>vaste</s>) — covers His own self or the <s>jīva</s>, or He dwells within it. Or alternatively: because He 'wears' (<s>vaste</s>) — inhabits — the body, therefore He is called <s>Kṛttivāsā</s> (wearer of skin): that is the meaning. 'Because of emanation' (<s>virecanāt</s>) — because of creating the world, that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because of augmenting (<s>bṛṃhaṇāt</s>) or nourishing (<s>vardhanāt</s>), bears the name <s>Brahman</s>. That one, because of supreme lordship, is called <s>Indra</s>.

children.text:
evaṃ nānāvidhaiśśabdaiḥ eka eva trivikramaḥ /
vedeṣu sapurāṇeṣu gīyate puruṣottamaḥ // iti /
children.translated_text:
Thus, by words of many kinds, the one <s>Trivikrama</s> alone
is praised in the <s>Vedas</s> together with the <s>Purāṇas</s> — <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person). — Thus.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 10:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.10:
evaṃ viṣṇau rudrādiśabdānāṃ mahāyogamuktvā vidvadrūḍhiṃ cāha - evamiti //
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 10:
Having stated the <s>mahāyoga</s> (great etymological derivation) of the words <s>Rudra</s> and the like in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he also states the <s>vidvadrūḍhi</s> (conventional usage among the learned) — '<s>evam</s>' (thus).

children.text: nimittairityadhyāhāryam / tathā ca 'evam'; uktarītyā nānāvidhairnimitaiḥ sapurāṇeṣu vedeṣu gataiḥ etairnānāvidhaiḥ śabdairviṣṇureka eva 'gīyate'; mukhyato 'bhidhīyata ityarthaḥ / kathamanyatrādṛṣṭaṃ sarvaśabdamukhyavācyatvamasyetyataḥ 'puruṣottamastrivikramaḥ'; ityābhyāṃ tatropapādakamuktam / tribhuvanārthaśabdavyāpī hi trivikramaḥ / sarvapuruṣaśabdanimittakasvāmī hi puruṣottamaḥ / tathā cānena viṣṇau rudrādiśabdānāṃ mahāyogavidvadrūḍhikathanāt tayośta rūḍhimātrātprābalyādyuktaḥ samākhyāśrutyantare 'pi viṣṇoḥ pratipādyatvaniścaya iti bhāvaḥ / 'puruṣottama iti'; ityantasya 'brahmāṇḍe'; iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By reasons' (<s>nimittaiḥ</s>) is to be interpolated. And thus, 'thus' — in the manner described — by the various reasons embedded in the <s>Vedas</s> together with the <s>Purāṇas</s> — by these various words, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, 'one alone' (<s>eka eva</s>), 'is praised' (<s>gīyate</s>) — is primarily denoted: that is the meaning. How is this never-before-seen primary denotability by all words [possible] for Him? — for that, '<s>Puruṣottama</s>' and '<s>Trivikrama</s>' — by these two, the justification thereof is stated. For <s>Trivikrama</s> is the one who pervades all the three worlds, denoted by their words. And <s>Puruṣottama</s> is the master of the ground of operation of all person-denoting words. And thus, by this statement that the words <s>Rudra</s> and the like have <s>mahāyoga</s> and <s>vidvadrūḍhi</s> in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since these are stronger than mere conventional usage (<s>rūḍhimātra</s>) [in <s>Rudra</s>] — the certainty that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established [as the referent] even in the name-explanation <s>Śruti</s> from other [sources] is justified: that is the purport. '<s>Puruṣottama</s>' — 'up to this <s>iti</s>' connects with the preceding 'in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>.'

children.text:
vāmane ca -
na tu nārāyaṇādīnāṃ nāmnāmanyatra sambhavaḥ/
anyanāmnāṃ gatirviṣṇuḥ eka eva prakīrtitaḥ // iti /

children.translated_text: [<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 11:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.11:
nanu yadi rudrādiśabdānāṃ viṣṇuparatvamuktvā 'rudro mā'viśāntakaḥ'; ityādiśrutīnāmanirṇāyakatvamucyate, tarhi nārāyaṇādināmnāṃ rudrādiparatvena 'nārāyaṇaṃ mahājñeyam'; (mahānā-11.) ityādiśrutīnāmanirṇāyakatvaṃ ca syādityata āha - vāmane ceti // co 'pyarthe / asyāpyuktatvādavirodhaiti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / kimuktamityatastadvākyaṃ paṭhati - na tviti / turavadhāraṇe / 'nārāyaṇādīnāṃ'; nārāyaṇa ityādīnamanyatra rudrādau sambhavo mukhyavṛttiḥ astīti śeṣaḥ / 'anyanāmnāṃ'; rudrādiśabdānāṃ 'viṣṇureka eva gatiḥ'; mukhyavācyaḥ prakīrtita ityarthaḥ / itiśabdasya vāmana ityanenānvayaḥ / tasya nārāyaṇādināmnāṃ anyatra niravakāśatvokteḥ na tacchrutīnāmanirṇāyakatvamiti vivakṣitasādhyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 11:
Objection: If the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-referentiality of the words <s>Rudra</s> and the like is stated, and if thereby the <s>Śrutis</s> such as '<s>Rudra</s> entered him, the destroyer' and the like are said to be indeterminate — then by the <s>Rudra</s>-referentiality and the like of the names <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like, the <s>Śrutis</s> such as '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is to be known as the great one' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 11) and the like would also be indeterminate. To this he says: 'and in the <s>Vāmana</s>.' // The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'api.' 'Because of being stated, there is no contradiction' connects with the preceding. What is stated? — for that, he reads the passage: '<s>na tu</s>' (but not). The word 'tu' is for emphasis. 'Of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like' — the possibility of primary usage of [names like] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like 'elsewhere' — in <s>Rudra</s> and others — 'exists': this is the remainder. 'Of other names' — of words like <s>Rudra</s> and the like — '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' is proclaimed as 'the goal' — the primary denotation: that is the meaning. The word 'iti' connects 'in the <s>Vāmana</s>.' Because of the statement that the names <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like have no scope elsewhere — the indeterminacy of those <s>Śrutis</s> does not follow: this connects with the intended thesis.

children.text:
skānde ca -
ṛte nārāyaṇādīni nāmāni puruṣottamaḥ /
prādādanyatra bhagavān rājevarte svakaṃ puram // iti /
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Skānda</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] —
Except for [the names] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like, <s>Puruṣottama</s>
gave other names to others — as a king distributes [possessions] except for his own city. — Thus.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 12:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.12:
bhagavannāmatvāviśeṣādrudrādināmavannārāyaṇādināmnāmapi rudrādau vṛttiḥ kiṃ na syādityata āha - skānde ceti // co 'pyarthaḥ samuccaye / asyāpyuktatvāditi pūrveṇānvayaḥ / kimuktamityatastadvākyaṃ paṭhati - ṛta iti //
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 12:
Since all are equally names of <s>Bhagavān</s>, why should the names <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like not have application in <s>Rudra</s> and the like, just as the names <s>Rudra</s> and the like [have application in <s>Viṣṇu</s>]? — to this he says: 'and in the <s>Skānda</s>.' // The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'api' (also), for accumulation. 'Because of being stated, there is no contradiction' connects with the preceding. What is stated? — for that, he reads the passage: '<s>ṛte</s>' (except for).

children.text: vinetyarthaḥ / 'anyatra'; anyebhyo rudrādibhyaḥ anyāni rudrādināmānītiśeṣaḥ / ādiśabdena viṣṇurityādikaṃ gṛhyate/ atra dṛṣṭāntamāha - rājeti // yathā rājā svakaṃ puramṛte 'nyadamātyādibhyo dadāti tadvadityarthaḥ / itītyantasya skānde ityanenānvayaḥ / tasya ca nārāyaṇādināmnāmanyatra vṛttyabhāvasyoktatvānna sāmyamityupaskṛtenānvayaḥ / anena skānde nārāyaṇādināmnāṃ viṣṇorevoktatvānna sāmyamityanvayena pūrvaprayuktaivakārasya kṛtyāntaraṃ sūcitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: The meaning is 'without.' 'Elsewhere' (<s>anyatra</s>) — to others, <s>Rudra</s> and the like — 'other' names, that is, the names of <s>Rudra</s> and the like, is the remainder. By the word 'ādi,' [names such as] <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like are included. Here he gives the illustration: '<s>rājā</s>' (king). Just as a king gives everything to ministers and the like except for his own city — so too: that is the meaning. The word 'iti' up to its end connects with 'in the <s>Skānda</s>.' And because in the <s>Skānda</s>, the absence of the application of the names <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like elsewhere is stated — therefore there is no equality: this connects with the supplemented [thesis]. By this, since in the <s>Skānda</s> [it is stated that] the names <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the like belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — there is no equality: by this syntactic connection, another function of the particle 'eva' previously employed is indicated.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 13:]
'<s>Caturmukha</s>' (four-faced), '<s>Śatānanda</s>' (of hundred-fold bliss), '<s>Padmabhū</s>' (lotus-born) — thus [are the specific names] of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>);

children.text: ugro bhasmadharo nagnaḥ kapālīti śivasya ca /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ugra</s>' (fierce), '<s>Bhasmadhara</s>' (bearer of ashes), '<s>Nagna</s>' (naked), '<s>Kapālī</s>' (skull-bearer) — and thus [are the specific names] of <s>Śiva</s>.
<s>Keśava</s> gave away the specific names, even His own, [to them].
Thus in the <s>Brāhma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]. // 3 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.13:
yadyevaṃ rudrādiśabdāḥ viṣṇvaikaparāḥ tarhi kimucyate bhasmadharogratvādīnāṃ tacchabdatvam / viṣṇudattatvābhiprāyeṇa cet - tarhi rudrādiśabdā api tādṛśā iti kathaṃ tairnirṇayābhāva ityata āha - caturmukha iti // yadyapi svakīyāni, tathāpi 'keśavaḥ'; brahmarudrapravartako viṣṇuḥ 'svakīyāni'; mukhyataḥ svavācakānyeva caturmukhaḥ śatānandaḥ padmabhūriti 'viśeṣanāmāni'; nāmaviśeṣāneva 'brahmaṇo'; brahmaṇe dadāvityarthaḥ / 'nagnaḥ'; digambaraḥ / 'śivasya'; śivāya / castvarthaḥ / brāhma ityasyāpyuktatvāditi pūrveṇānvayaḥ / rudrādau bhasmadharogratvādereva viṣṇossakāśātprāptatveneti tadarthaḥ / tasya ca pūrvoktaṃ yuktamiti sādhyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 13:
If the words <s>Rudra</s> and the like refer exclusively to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then why is it said that [attributes like] bearing ashes, fierceness, and the like belong to those names? If [it is] with the intention of being given by <s>Viṣṇu</s> — then the words <s>Rudra</s> and the like are also of such nature, so why is there no determination through them? — to this he says: '<s>Caturmukha</s>.' // Even though [the names are] His own (<s>svakīyāni</s>), nevertheless '<s>Keśava</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the initiator of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s> — gave His 'own' (<s>svakīyāni</s>) — primarily denoting Himself alone — 'specific names' (<s>viśeṣanāmāni</s>) — particular names only — namely '<s>Caturmukha</s>,' '<s>Śatānanda</s>,' '<s>Padmabhū</s>' — 'to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahmaṇaḥ</s>) — to <s>Brahmā</s>: that is the meaning. '<s>Nagna</s>' — unclothed. 'Of <s>Śiva</s>' (<s>śivasya</s>) — to <s>Śiva</s>. The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'tu' (but). 'In the <s>Brāhma</s>' — 'because of being stated, there is no contradiction': this connects with the preceding. [The status of] bearing ashes, fierceness, and the like in <s>Rudra</s> and the like is because those [attributes] alone were obtained from <s>Viṣṇu</s>: that is the meaning. And therefore, what was stated earlier is justified: this connects with the thesis.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
And [He is] the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> (<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.4 |
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 14:]
By these very reasons, [the entity spoken of is] not the <s>jīva</s> nor <s>Vāyu</s> (wind).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.14:
nanu 'sa eṣo 'ntaścarate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ'; (muṃ. 2-2-6.) iti jīvaliṅgaśravaṇātprāṇitvaprasiddheśca jīvasāmānyasya vā, viṣayabhūtalokādhāratvasya 'vāyunā vai gautama sūtreṇāyaṃ lokaḥ paraśca lokaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃdṛbdhāni bhavanti'; (bṛ. 5-7-2.) iti śrutyantare vāyuniṣṭhatvena prasiddhatvādvāyorvātra prakaraṇe dyubhvādyāśrayatvena pratipādyatā kiṃ na syādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - prāṇabhṛcceti // etairiti / ātmaśabdaḥ muktopasṛpyatvamatacchabdo rudrādiprāpakaśrutīnāṃ viṣṇuparatvamityevaṃrūpaiḥ pūrvoktahetubhirityarthaḥ / nātra hetvantaraṃ vācyamityevaśabdārthaḥ / jīvo vāyurityanena prāṇabhṛcchabdo vyākhyātaḥ / atra vācya ityanuṣajyate / caḥ samuccaye / anena sūtre caśabdaḥ prāguktahetūnāṃ nānumānamityato nañaśca samākarṣakaḥ / na kevalaṃ rudro 'tra na vācyaḥ, kintu jīvo vāyuśceti samuccayārthaścetyuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 14:
Objection: Since the mark of the <s>jīva</s> — 'He moves within, being born in many forms' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.6) — is heard in the <s>Śruti</s>, and since the status of being an animate being (<s>prāṇitva</s>) is well-known [for the <s>jīva</s>], why should [the entity] not be the <s>jīva</s> in general? Or since the status of being the support of the worlds, which is the subject — 'O <s>Gautama</s>, by <s>Vāyu</s> as a thread, this world and the other world and all beings are strung together' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.2) — is well-known in another <s>Śruti</s> as belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>, why should <s>Vāyu</s> not be the one established here in this context as the abode of heaven, earth, and the like? — having raised this doubt, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves it and explains: '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' (bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s>). // '<s>Etaiḥ</s>' (by these) — by the previously stated reasons of the form: the word '<s>ātma</s>' (Self), the status of being approached by the liberated (<s>muktopasṛpyatva</s>), the non-applicability of the word '<s>tat</s>' (that) [to others], and the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-referentiality of the <s>Śrutis</s> that lead to <s>Rudra</s> and the like: that is the meaning. The word '<s>eva</s>' means: no other reason need be stated here. By 'the <s>jīva</s> [and] <s>Vāyu</s>,' the word '<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>' is explained. Here, 'is to be stated' is to be connected. The word 'ca' is for accumulation. By this, the word 'ca' in the <s>sūtra</s> draws forward the negative particle from 'not an inference' (<s>nānumānam</s>) [stated earlier]. It is stated that not only is <s>Rudra</s> not to be stated here, but also neither the <s>jīva</s> nor <s>Vāyu</s> — such is the cumulative meaning.

children.text:
'ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate'; (tai.ā. 3-13-1.)
iti tasyaiva bahudhā janmokteḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: 'Being unborn, He is born in many forms' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.13.1) — because of the very statement of His manifold birth [while being unborn]. // 4 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 15:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.15:
nanu 'vāyunā vai gautama'; ityādiśruterviṣṇuparatvena vāyusādhakatvābhāve 'pi bahudhā janmākhyaliṅgena jīvo 'tra vācyaḥ kiṃ na syādityata āha - ajāyamāna iti // dehataḥ 'ajāyamānaḥ'; avikurvāṇo 'bahudhā'; rāmakṛṣṇādirūpeṇa 'vijāyate'; tatra tatra prādurbhavatītyarthaḥ / itīti / iti puruṣasūktagatavākyenetyarthaḥ / yasya janmāsambhavo 'bhihitaḥ pūrvavādinā tasyaiva viṣmorna jīvasyetyevaśabdārthaḥ / tathā ca liṅgaṃ sāvakāśamiti na tadvirodha iti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 15:
Objection: Even if the <s>Śruti</s> 'O <s>Gautama</s>, by <s>Vāyu</s>' and the like does not establish <s>Vāyu</s> as [the referent] because of its <s>Viṣṇu</s>-referentiality, the <s>jīva</s> should be the referent here because of the mark of manifold birth. To this he says: '<s>ajāyamānaḥ</s>' (being unborn). // 'Being unborn' (<s>ajāyamānaḥ</s>) — not undergoing transformation from the body — 'in many forms' (<s>bahudhā</s>) — in the forms of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and the like — 'is born' (<s>vijāyate</s>) — manifests here and there: that is the meaning. The word 'iti' means: by the passage from the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>: that is the meaning. The word '<s>eva</s>' means: the manifold birth, the impossibility of which was stated by the prima facie advocate, belongs to that very <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not to the <s>jīva</s>. And thus, the mark has scope [in <s>Viṣṇu</s>] — hence there is no contradiction with it: this is the sentence-remainder.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
Because of the statement of difference (<s>bhedavyapadeśa</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.5 |

children.text: na caikyaṃ vācyam / 'juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśamasya mahimānam'; (muṃ. 3-1-2.) iti bhedavyapadeśāt // 5 //
children.translated_text: And oneness is not to be stated [here]. 'When one sees the other, the Lord, and His greatness, being well-served [by <s>Brahmā</s>]' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.2) — because of this statement of difference. // 5 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 16:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.16:
nanu kiṃ jīvaliṅgasya viṣṇugatatvapratipādanāyāsena, liṅgabalājjīvasyaiva dyubhvādyāyatanatvaṃ syāt / na coktātmaśabdādihetuvirodhaḥ / jīveśābhedābhiprāyeṇa jīve 'pyātmaśabdādyuktisambhavādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - bhedeti / naikyaṃ vācyamiti / jīveśvarayoratrābhipretamiti ca śeṣaḥ / anena sūtre nānumānamityato nañanuvartanīyaḥ / sa ca hetugatabhedapratiyoginā saṃyojya ityuktaṃ bhavati / caśabdo jīveśaikyaprayuktātmaśabdavācyataitatprakaraṇabodhyatāpi netisamuccayārthaḥ / kau'sau vyapadeśa ityata āha - juṣṭamiti / iti bhedavyapadeśāditi / iti bhedaśruterityarthaḥ / anena - 'juṣṭam'; iti vākye 'paśyati'; iti darśanakartṛtvena prakṛtajīvasyar iśapadokteścar iśvarādbhedokteḥ na tayoraikyamatrābhipretamiti vācyamiti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / śrutistavānandamayanaye vyākṛtā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 16:
Objection: What is the point of laboring to show the <s>jīva</s>-mark as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? By the force of the mark, the status of being the abode of heaven, earth, and the like could belong to the <s>jīva</s> alone. Nor is there contradiction with the stated reasons such as the word '<s>ātma</s>' and the like — because in the view of non-difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord, the word '<s>ātma</s>' and the like are possible for the <s>jīva</s> as well. Having raised this doubt, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> that resolves it and explains: '<s>bheda</s>' (difference). 'Oneness is not to be stated' — and the remainder is: it is not intended here that the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord [are one]. By this, the negative particle from 'not an inference' (<s>nānumānam</s>) is to be carried forward in the <s>sūtra</s>. And it is stated that [this negative particle] should be connected with the entity opposed to the difference [mentioned] in the reason-portion. The word 'ca' has the cumulative meaning: not only is the status of being the stated referent of this context through the <s>jīva</s>-Lord identity not [valid], but also [the <s>jīva</s>'s] being the referent — that too is not [valid]. What is that statement [of difference]? — to this he says: '<s>juṣṭam</s>' (well-served). 'Because of the statement of difference in <s>Śruti</s>': that is the meaning. By this — in the passage beginning with '<s>juṣṭam</s>,' the <s>jīva</s> under discussion is stated as the agent of seeing (<s>darśana</s>), and because of the statement of his difference from the Lord through the word '<s>Īśa</s>' — oneness of the two is not intended here: this is what is to be stated, and thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. The <s>Śruti</s> has been explained in the <s>Ānandamaya</s> method.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
Because of the context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.6 |
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 17:]
'Two kinds of knowledge are to be known' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.4) — for this is the context of that [<s>Paramātman</s>]. // 6 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.17:
nanvatra jīvasya kasmāccidīśādanyatvamucyate, na paramātmanaḥ, ato na tayorbheda ityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - prakaraṇāditi // itītyanantaram 'ityupakramyādhītam'; iti śeṣaḥ / 'hi'; yataḥ 'etat'; juṣṭamityādivākyajātaṃ yataḥ 'tasyaiva'; paravidyāviṣayasya paramātmana eva 'prakaraṇaṃ'; nānyasyetyevaśabdārthaḥ / anena svaprakaraṇāt 'dve vidye veditavye'; iti paravidyāviṣayavastuno 'trādhītatvena viṣṇuprakaraṇatvātparamātmana eva bhedavyapadeśāvagateḥ na jīvaparamātnorabhedo 'trābhipreta iti vācyamiti sūtrayojanā darśitā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.1, verse 17:
Objection: Why is the otherness stated here said to be of the <s>jīva</s> from some Lord, and not of the <s>Paramātman</s> [from the <s>jīva</s>]? Hence there is no difference [between the two]. Having raised this doubt, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and explains: 'because of the context.' // After the word 'iti,' the remainder is: 'having thus commenced, it has been studied.' 'For' (<s>hi</s>) — because — 'this' (<s>etat</s>) — the collection of passages beginning with '<s>juṣṭam</s>' — because 'this' is 'the context' (<s>prakaraṇam</s>) of 'that very one' (<s>tasyaiva</s>) — of the <s>Paramātman</s> who is the subject of the higher knowledge — 'and not of another': this is the meaning of the word 'eva.' By this, because of its own context — because of the content of the passage 'two kinds of knowledge are to be known' belonging to the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-context due to the entity studied here being the subject of the higher knowledge — the statement of difference is understood as being of the <s>Paramātman</s> alone; the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>Paramātman</s> is not intended here — this is what is to be stated: thus the construction of the <s>sūtra</s> is shown.
<s>Sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
<s>sthityadanābhyāṃ ca</s> — And because of [the distinction of] abiding and eating. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.7 |
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.1, verse 18:]

children.text: dvāsuparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ bṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte /
children.translated_text: Two birds (<s>suparṇau</s>), inseparable companions, cling to the same tree.
Of these two, one eats the sweet <s>pippala</s> fruit, while the other shines forth without eating. // (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1) //
Thus, because of the statement of abiding and eating with respect to <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>jīva</s> [respectively]. // 7 //
// Thus ends the <s>Dyubhvādhikaraṇa</s> // 1 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.1.18:
na kevalaṃ 'juṣṭam'; iti bhedaśruterna jīveśabhedo 'tra prakaraṇe vivakṣita iti jñāyate, kintu liṅgādapītyāha sūtrakṛt - sthitīti // tadasiddhivāraṇāya śrutyudāharaṇena vyācaṣṭe - dvā suparṇeti / anena - 'dvā suparṇā'; ityatra śrutābhyāḥ karmaphalānupajīvanāvasthititadupajīvanābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ ca naivātra jīveśayoraikyaṃ vācyamiti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / caśabdastu hetusamuccāyaka iti spaṣṭatvānna vyākhyātaḥ / śrutāvadanasya prāthamye 'pi sthiterīśasambandhitvenābhyarhitatvādalpākṣaratvācca sūtre tadanusāreṇa bhāṣye ca śrautakramamullaṅghya sthiteḥ prathamamuktiḥ / 'sayujā'; sayujau saṃyuktau upakāryopakārakabhāvavattayā parasparāparihāreṇa vartamānau 'sakhāyā'; sakhāyau prītyā ekadeśasthau 'dvā'; dvau 'suparṇā'; suparṇau / suparṇasarūpau / 'suparṇā sakhāyā'; iti viśeṣaṇasvārasyādasya samajīvamātraviṣayatve suṣṭhuparamānandarūpau jīveśvarau 'samānam'; ekaṃ 'vṛkṣaṃ'; dehākhyam aśvatthaṃ 'pariṣasvajāteḥ'; āliliṅgatuḥ / 'tayoḥ'; suparṇayormadhyer iśvarāt 'anyo'; jīvaḥ 'pippalam'; aśvatthaphalarūpaṃ dehajanitakarmaphalam 'atti'; asvādveva svādutvenaiva aśnāti / jīvāt 'anyarḥ'; iśvarastu 'anaśnan'; jīvādyamevābhuñjānaḥ 'abhi'; abhitaḥ 'cākaśīti'; prakāśate / na tu svasthityai jīvavatkarmaphalamapekṣata iti muṇḍakaśrutyarthaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: (<s>Dīpikā</s> on 1.3.1.18): Not only from the <s>śruti</s> passage 'juṣṭam' indicating difference is it known that the distinction between <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> is intended in this section, but also from inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>) — thus says the <s>sūtrakāra</s> with 'sthiti' etc. To prevent the objection of non-establishment, he explains with a scriptural citation — 'dvā suparṇā' etc. By this, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated: from the two reasons heard in the <s>śruti</s> 'dvā suparṇā' — namely, the state of not subsisting on <s>karma</s>-fruits (abiding) and the subsisting on them (eating) — the unity of <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> is certainly not to be asserted here. The word 'ca' is for accumulation of reasons, and being clear, is not separately explained. Although in the <s>śruti</s> 'eating' comes first, since 'abiding' is more fitting as related to <s>Īśvara</s> and for brevity of syllables, in the <s>sūtra</s> and accordingly in the <s>bhāṣya</s>, transgressing the scriptural order, 'abiding' is mentioned first. 'Sayujā' — joined together, existing in mutual inseparability as supporter and supported; 'sakhāyā' — companions, dwelling in the same place out of affection; 'dvā' — two; 'suparṇā' — two birds, having beautiful wings. From the suggestive force of the qualifiers 'suparṇā sakhāyā', if this pertains only to co-living beings, then [the meaning is]: two who are of the form of excellent supreme bliss — <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> — cling to ('pariṣasvajāte') the 'same' ('samānam'), i.e. one, 'tree' ('vṛkṣam'), namely the body called <s>aśvattha</s>. 'Of those two' ('tayoḥ') birds, 'the other' ('anyaḥ') from <s>Īśvara</s>, the <s>jīva</s>, 'eats' ('atti') the '<s>pippala</s>' — the fruit of <s>karma</s> born of the body in the form of <s>aśvattha</s> fruit — as though sweet, indeed as sweet alone. 'The other' ('anyaḥ') from the <s>jīva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, 'without eating' ('anaśnan'), not partaking of what the <s>jīva</s> and others consume, 'shines forth' ('cākaśīti') on all sides ('abhi'). He does not depend on <s>karma</s>-fruits like the <s>jīva</s> for His own sustenance — this is the meaning of the <s>Muṇḍaka</s> <s>śruti</s>. // 1 //
// Thus ends the <s>Dyubhvādhikaraṇa</s> // 1 //
// 2. <s>Bhūmādhikaraṇa</s> //

children.text:
'prāṇo vā āśayā bhūyān'; ityuktvā 'yo vai bhūmā tatsukham';
(chāṃ. 7-23.) ityuktestasyaiva bhūmatvaprāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having stated '<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed greater than <s>Āśā</s> (hope)', since it is then stated 'That which is <s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite) — that is bliss' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.23), the attainment of <s>Bhūman</s>-hood would belong to that [<s>Prāṇa</s>] itself.
(<s>Bhāṣya</s> on 1.3.2.1):

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.2.1:
atrādhikaraṇe bhūmanāmno viṣṇau samanvayaḥ pratipādyate / bhūmaśabdaśca 'bhūmnaḥ kratuvat'; ityādau kvaciddharmavācako 'pyatra pūrṇarūpadharmivacanaḥ / pūrṇatvaṃ ca guṇata uttamatvamiti dhyeyam / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca sūcayan sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣaṃ darśayati - prāṇa iti // 'chāndogye'; ityādau upaskāryam / 'ityuktvā'; ityupakrametyupalakṣaṇam / taduttamamanuktvetyapi draṣṭavyam / ata eva tasyaiva prāṇasyaivetyevakāro 'nyavyavacchedakaḥ prāyoji / śrutau pūrvapakṣe prāṇaśabdo vāyumātraparaḥ / siddhānte tu bhāṣyarītyā vāyuviṣṇūbhayaparaḥ / nyāyavivaraṇachāndogyabhāṣyarītyā tu vāyumātraparaḥ / na ca vāyuviṣṇūbhayavācitvaṃ vāyumātravācitvamityarthadvayaṃ viruddham / antaryāmivivakṣayā bhāṣyasya tadavivakṣayā vivaraṇādeḥ pravṛttatvāt / yathā 'ātmanaḥ ākāśaḥ'; (tai. 2-1.) ityatra sambhūtaśabdasyānekārthatve 'ntaryāmiviṣṇurapyākāśapadenocyate / tasya janimātrārthatve tu na tena sa ucyate / tathā tattvapradīpe tu 'abhyupagamavādatvāt'; ityādinā ayaṃ prāṇo viṣṇurityabhyupetya vādena bhāṣyaṃ pravṛttam, ityuktam / tathā cādyapakṣe prāṇaḥ 'āśāyāḥ'; bhāratyāḥ 'bhūyān'; guṇato jyeṣṭhaḥ / evaṃ 'prāṇaḥ'; tadantaryāmī viṣṇurantaryāmitvādeva tata āśāyāśca bhūyānityarthaḥ / anena pūrvamānandamayaśabdoktasajātīyotkṛṣṭatvarūpapūrṇatvasyeha vāyāvākṣepādānandamayādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ sūcitā / chāndogaśrutyukto bhūmākhyo viṣayaḥ, kiṃ vāyuruta viṣṇuriti sandehaśca sūcitaḥ / tathā tasyaiva bhūmatvaprāptiriti pūrvapakṣaḥ / tatra prāṇopakramataduttamānuktirūpayuktiśca darśitā bhavati / 'yo vai bhūmā tatsukhaṃ nālpe sukhamasti bhūmaiva sukham'; iti vākye sukhaśabdaḥ pūrṇasukhārthaḥ / 'yatsukhaṃ sa bhūmā'; iti vyāsatīrthīyokteḥ, sarvanāmāni paryāyeṇa tattalliṅgabhāñjītyukteśca nirupapadasukhaśabdamātrasyāpi pūrṇasukhārthatvāt / yadananyādhīnapūrṇānandasukhaṃ sa bhūmā guṇataḥ pūrṇo nārāyaṇa ityuddeśyavidheyayorvyatyayaḥ / ata eva svātantryeṇa sukhasya viśeṣaṇāt na muktajīveṣvanaikāntyamityāśayena tadupapādayati - nālpa iti / 'alpe'; apūrṇe muktajīve tatprasādaṃ vinā yataḥ sukhaṃ nāstītyarthaḥ / nigamayati - bhūmaiva sukhamiti / atrāpi vyatyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>Dīpikā</s> on 1.3.2.1): In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the coordination (<s>samanvaya</s>) of the name '<s>Bhūman</s>' with <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established. The word '<s>bhūma</s>' is sometimes used to denote a quality (<s>dharma</s>) as in '<s>bhūmnaḥ kratuvat</s>' etc., but here it denotes the possessor of the quality of fullness (<s>pūrṇa</s>). And fullness should be understood as supremacy in terms of qualities. Indicating the textual coherence and the subject matter, he presents the prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) with reasoning — '<s>Prāṇa</s>' etc. In '<s>Chāndogya</s>' etc. is to be supplied. 'Having stated' is indicative of the opening [of the passage]. It should also be seen as 'without stating that as the highest'. Therefore the word 'eva' (indeed) in 'of that <s>Prāṇa</s> itself' is used to exclude others. In the <s>śruti</s> according to the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' refers to <s>Vāyu</s> alone. But in the <s>siddhānta</s>, according to the method of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, it refers to both <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>. According to the method of the <s>Nyāyavivaraṇa</s> and the <s>Chāndogya Bhāṣya</s>, it refers to <s>Vāyu</s> alone. And the two meanings — referring to both <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and referring to <s>Vāyu</s> alone — are not contradictory, because the <s>Bhāṣya</s> proceeds with the intention of [<s>Viṣṇu</s> as] the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), while the <s>Vivaraṇa</s> etc. proceed without that intention. Just as in 'From the <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Ākāśa</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1), when the word 'sambhūta' has multiple meanings, the inner-controlling <s>Viṣṇu</s> too is denoted by the word '<s>Ākāśa</s>'; but when it means only origination, He is not denoted by it. Similarly, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, it is stated through the phrase '<s>abhyupagamavādatvāt</s>' (because it is an argument by concession) that the <s>Bhāṣya</s> proceeds by conceding that this <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. And thus, in the first view, '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is 'greater' — superior in qualities — than '<s>Āśā</s>', i.e. <s>Bhāratī</s> (goddess of speech). Similarly, '<s>Prāṇa</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the inner controller of that — is greater than <s>Āśā</s> by virtue of being the inner controller — this is the meaning. By this, the coherence of this [section] with the <s>Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa</s> is indicated through the drawing in of fullness, which is of the nature of superiority among those of the same kind, as stated by the word '<s>Ānandamaya</s>' previously, here with respect to <s>Vāyu</s>. The subject called '<s>Bhūman</s>' stated in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s> — whether it is <s>Vāyu</s> or <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this doubt is indicated. And thus 'the attainment of <s>Bhūman</s>-hood belongs to that itself' is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. Therein, the reasoning in the form of the opening with <s>Prāṇa</s> and the non-statement of anything higher than it is shown. In the sentence 'That which is <s>Bhūman</s> — that is bliss; in the finite there is no bliss; <s>Bhūman</s> alone is bliss', the word '<s>sukha</s>' (bliss) means complete bliss (<s>pūrṇa-sukha</s>). Because of the statement of <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>: 'That which is bliss, that is <s>Bhūman</s>', and because it is said that pronouns take the gender of what they refer to in sequence, even the bare word '<s>sukha</s>' without qualifiers means complete bliss. That which is independently full, unlimited bliss — that is <s>Bhūman</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who is full in qualities — here there is an interchange of subject and predicate. Therefore, with the intention that from the independent qualification of bliss there is no uncertainty regarding liberated <s>jīvas</s>, he establishes this — '<s>nālpe</s>' etc. 'In the finite' — in the incomplete, in the liberated <s>jīva</s>, without His grace there is no bliss — this is the meaning. He concludes — '<s>Bhūman</s> alone is bliss'. Here too there is an interchange [of subject and predicate].
From the indicative mark in '<s>utkrāntaprāṇān</s>' (those from whom <s>Prāṇa</s> has departed) (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.15.3) etc., the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' denotes <s>Vāyu</s>.
(<s>Bhāṣya</s> on 1.3.2.2):

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.2.2:
nanu 'prāṇo vā āśāyā bhūyān'; ityuktaprāṇaśabdasya 'ata eva prāṇaḥ'; ityuktarītyā viṣṇuparatvādviṣṇoreva bhūmatvaprāpteḥ kathaṃ prāṇaśabdabalādvāyorbhūmatvaprāptirityata āha - utkrānteti // ityādīti / luptavibhaktiko nirdeśaḥ / ādiśabdena 'utkrāntaprāṇān śūlena samāsaṃ vyatiṣaṃ dahet nainaṃ brūyuḥ pitṛhāsīti'; samagravākyaṃ gṛhyate / tacca tat liṅgaṃ ca, tasya liṅgamiti ca vigrahaḥ / ayamiti śeṣaḥ / caśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / vāyuvācī ceti bhinnakramaḥ / tathā ca 'ayaṃ'; prāṇaśabdo 'vāyuvācyeva'; na viṣṇuvācī / kutaḥ? 'utkrāntaprāṇān'; ityādau 'talliṅgāt'; tasya prāṇasyotkramaṇādirūpaliṅgaśravaṇāditi yojanā / utkrāntaḥ prāṇo yebhyaste tathoktāḥ / tānmātṛpitrācāryādīn 'samāsaṃ'; sākalyena 'vyatiṣam'; ekadeśena ca śūlena viluṇṭhya yadi dahetputraḥ śiṣyo vā tathā nainaṃ brūyuḥ janāḥ / kimiti? - pitṛhāsīti mātṛhāsīti / mukhyaprāṇasannidhānābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / iti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>Dīpikā</s> on 1.3.2.2): But since the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' in '<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed greater than <s>Āśā</s>' refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s> as stated in 'therefore indeed <s>Prāṇa</s>', and since the attainment of <s>Bhūman</s>-hood would belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself, how can the attainment of <s>Bhūman</s>-hood for <s>Vāyu</s> arise from the force of the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>'? To this he says — '<s>utkrānta</s>' etc. 'Etc.' (ādi) indicates a citation with elided case-endings. By the word 'ādi', the complete sentence is taken: '<s>utkrāntaprāṇān śūlena samāsaṃ vyatiṣaṃ dahet, nainaṃ brūyuḥ pitṛhāsīti</s>' (If one were to burn on a spit those from whom <s>Prāṇa</s> has departed, people would not say 'he is a killer of his father'). 'That is the indicative mark' — the analysis is: it is the mark of that (<s>Prāṇa</s>). 'This' is to be supplied. The word 'ca' is for emphasis. 'And it denotes <s>Vāyu</s>' — the word order is rearranged. Thus, 'this' word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' 'denotes <s>Vāyu</s> alone', not <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? 'Because of hearing the indicative mark' (<s>talliṅgāt</s>) — the mark in the form of departure etc. of that <s>Prāṇa</s> in '<s>utkrāntaprāṇān</s>' etc. — this is the construction. '<s>Utkrāntaprāṇān</s>' — those from whom <s>Prāṇa</s> has departed, they are so called. Those [beings] — father, mother, teacher etc. — if a son or student were to burn them completely ('samāsam') or partially ('vyatiṣam') on a spit, people would not say of him: 'he is a killer of his father' or 'a killer of his mother'. The implication is: because of the absence of the proximity of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> [life-breath]. This is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.
Therefore he states — <s>Sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
(<s>Bhāṣya</s> on 1.3.2.3):

<s>bhūmā saṃprasādādadhyupadeśāt</s> — <s>Bhūman</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of [the teaching of] complete bliss (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), and because of being taught as above [all]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.8 |
'<s>Saṃprasādāt</s>' — because of being of the nature of complete bliss; '<s>adhyupadeśāt</s>' — and because of being taught as above all others — <s>Bhūman</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.2.3:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti // sūtre prasīdatyanena jana iti prasādaḥ sukham, samyakprasādaḥ samprasādaḥ, tasmāditi vigraharḥ / iśvare sukhamiva duḥkhamapi syāditi nāśaṅkyaṃ, pūrṇasukhakāryeṇa samyakprasādena duḥkhābhāvaniścayādityāśayena prayuktaṃ samprasādāditi hetumanūdya vyācaṣṭe - samprasādāditi / uttarasūtrasthacaśabdo 'trākarṣaṇīya ityāśayena 'adhyupadeśāt'; ityetaddhetvantaraparatayānūdya vyākhyāti - adhyupadeśāditi // nāmādīnāṃ sarveṣām 'upari'; taduttamatvena 'upadeśāt'; ukterityarthaḥ / co hetusamuccaye / atrādhītyeva hetuḥ, na tu samagra eko hetuḥ / sa ceśvaravacano bhāvapradhānaḥ, viśeṣānukteḥ akhileśvaratvāditi hetvarthaḥ akhileśatvādityanuvyākhyānasudhokto jñātavyaḥ / asiddhiparihārāyopadeśaparyantaṃ dhāvanam / prāyapāṭhādbhūmno 'khilādhipaprāṇādhipatye akhilādhipatyaṃ siddhyatīti bhāvaḥ / samanvayasūtrādanuvṛttasya tattvitividheyasamarpakasyārthamāha - viṣṇureveti bhūmā viṣṇurevetyanvayaḥ/
children.translated_text: (<s>Dīpikā</s> on 1.3.2.3): He introduces the <s>siddhānta</s> <s>sūtra</s> with 'therefore' (ataḥ). In the <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>prasāda</s>' means bliss, since people are delighted (<s>prasīdati</s>) by it; '<s>samprasāda</s>' is complete bliss; 'from that' (<s>tasmāt</s>) is the analysis. Lest one object that in <s>Īśvara</s> there could be suffering just as there is bliss, with the intention that from the effect of complete bliss, namely complete delight (<s>samprasāda</s>), the absence of suffering is ascertained, he explains the reason '<s>saṃprasādāt</s>' by restating it — '<s>saṃprasādāt</s>' etc. With the intention that the word 'ca' from the following <s>sūtra</s> is to be drawn here, he restates '<s>adhyupadeśāt</s>' as a separate reason and explains — '<s>adhyupadeśāt</s>' etc. 'Above' ('upari') all — names and the rest — 'because of being taught' ('upadeśāt') as supreme over them — this is the meaning. 'Ca' is for accumulation of reasons. Here 'adhi' alone is the reason, not the whole as a single reason. And that is centered on the sense of <s>Īśvara</s>'s word, being primarily about existence [of the quality], since no specific [deity] is mentioned — the meaning of the reason is: because of being the Lord of all (<s>akhileśvaratva</s>) — this should be known as stated in the <s>Anuvyākhyāna-sudhā</s>. The running up to 'upadeśa' is for removing non-establishment. From the predominant reading, through <s>Bhūman</s>'s sovereignty over the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> and lordship over all, complete sovereignty is established — this is the purport. He states the meaning of the word 'tat' (that) which continues from the <s>samanvaya-sūtra</s> and conveys the predicate — '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' etc. The construction is: <s>Bhūman</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.
(<s>Bhāṣya</s> on 1.3.2.4):
'The God with a thousand heads, all-seeing, the benefactor of all,
The all-pervading <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the God, the imperishable, the supreme abode,

children.text: viśvataḥ paramāṃ nityam'; iti hi śrutiḥ (mahānā. 11.) /
children.translated_text: The eternally supreme over all' — thus is the <s>śruti</s> (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 11).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.2.4:
pūrṇasukhatvādikaṃ kuto viṣṇutvaniścāyakamityata āha - sahasreti // iti hīti / 'hi'; yasmāt 'iti'; nārāyaṇānuvākagatā śrutirasti, tasmātsamprasādāt viṣṇutvaniścayo bhavatyevetyarthaḥ / 'sahasraśīrṣaṃ'; sahasrapadopalakṣitāmitamūrdhānaṃ 'devaṃ'; prakāśarūpaṃ viśvato darśanādakṣyasyeti viśvākṣaṃ 'viśvaśambhuvaṃ'; pūrṇasukhāśrayaṃ 'viśvaṃ'; jagatpraviṣṭatvena vartamānaṃ 'nārāyaṇaṃ'; muktasaṅghe vyaktam 'akṣaraṃ'; svarūpato nāśarahitam akṣeṣu ramamāṇaṃ vā / parebhyo brahmādibhyo 'dhikatvena mīyata iti parā mā yasyeti vā paramastaṃ paramaṃ 'padaṃ'; prāpyaṃ viśvataḥ paramaścāsāvaśceti vigrahaḥ, savarṇadīrghaḥ / somapāśabdavadayaṃ śabdaḥ / sudhārītyā ābantatvāśrayeṇa liṅgavyatyayo vā / tathā ca 'viśvataḥparamāṃ'; sarvasmāduttamam akāravācyaṃ sarvottamaṃ vā 'nityaṃ'; dehato nāśarahitaṃ 'viśvaṃ'; guṇaiḥ pūrṇaṃ yajñeṣu haviḥsvīkaraṇāt harivarṇatvācca 'hariṃ'; 'devaṃ'; krīḍādiguṇakaṃ 'nārāyaṇaṃ'; tadākhyaṃ devaṃ tadviśvamupajīvatīti śrutyarthaḥ / yadyapi viśvataḥ paramam iti drāviḍapāṭhaḥ / tathāpyāndhrapāṭhamanusṛtya paramāmityuktam /
children.translated_text: (<s>Dīpikā</s> on 1.3.2.4): How does the nature of complete bliss etc. ascertain <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood? To this he says — '<s>sahasra</s>' etc. 'Iti hi' — 'hi' means 'because'; 'iti' — because there exists such a <s>śruti</s> found in the <s>Nārāyaṇānuvāka</s>, therefore the ascertainment of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood from <s>saṃprasāda</s> indeed follows — this is the meaning. '<s>Sahasraśīrṣam</s>' — having innumerable heads as indicated by the word 'thousand'; '<s>devam</s>' — of the nature of radiance; '<s>viśvākṣam</s>' — all-seeing, because He sees from all sides, hence one whose eyes are everywhere; '<s>viśvaśambhuvam</s>' — the abode of complete bliss; '<s>viśvam</s>' — existing as having entered the universe; '<s>Nārāyaṇam</s>' — manifest in the assembly of the liberated; '<s>akṣaram</s>' — indestructible in His essential nature, or one who delights in the sense organs; surpassing all others — <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest — hence '<s>parama</s>' (supreme), or one whose measure (<s>mā</s>) is supreme (<s>parā</s>); '<s>padam</s>' — the goal to be attained; 'supreme over all' ('viśvataḥ paramām') — and He is both all-pervading and supreme, this is the analysis, with coalescence of similar vowels. This word is like the word '<s>somapā</s>'. Or according to the <s>Sudhā</s> method, there is a change of gender based on the support [of the word]. And thus '<s>viśvataḥ paramām</s>' — supreme over all, denoted by the letter 'a' as the highest of all, or the supreme among all; '<s>nityam</s>' — free from destruction with respect to the body; '<s>viśvam</s>' — full of qualities; '<s>Harim</s>' — because of accepting oblations in sacrifices and because of having a golden complexion; '<s>devam</s>' — possessing qualities such as play; '<s>Nārāyaṇam</s>' — the God known by that name — the universe subsists on Him — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. Although 'viśvataḥ paramam' is the <s>Drāviḍa</s> reading, nevertheless following the <s>Āndhra</s> reading, '<s>paramām</s>' is stated.

From '<s>tamutkrāmantaṃ prāṇo 'nūtkrāmati</s>' (When he departs, <s>Prāṇa</s> departs after him) (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.2) and such [passages], there is no contradiction from the indicative mark of departure etc. either. // 8 //
(<s>Bhāṣya</s> on 1.3.2.5):

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.2.5:
atra prāṇaśabdena viṣṇorvācyatvāṅgīkāre prāguktatkramaṇādiliṅgavirodha ityato netyāha - tamiti // prathamādiśabdena taduttaravākyāni dvitīyena talliṅgāntarāṇi ca gṛhyante / apiśabdaḥ samuccaye, yadyapi tathāpītyarthe ca / tathā ca - na kevalaṃ prāṇaśabdopakramavirodhaḥ, tasya viṣṇuparatvāt, kintu 'api'; atra prāṇaśabdena viṣṇorvācyatvāṅgīkāre utkramaṇādiliṅgavirodho nāsti / kutaḥ? 'api'; tathāpi sarvagate 'pi viṣṇāvutkramaṇādiliṅgasya 'tamutkrāmantam'; ityādinā vājasaneyavākyena siddhatvāditi yojanā / śrutisiddher'the lokadṛṣṭivirodho 'kiñcitkara iti bhāvaḥ / 'tasya haitasya hṛdayasyāgraṃ pradyotate / tena pradyotenaiṣa ātmā niṣkrāmati'; (bṛ. 6-4-2.) iti pūrvavākye prakṛtaḥ paramātmā tacchabdena parāmṛśyate / tathā ca pradyotitahṛdayāgreṇāparokṣajñānidehāt 'utkrāmantaṃ'; nirgacchantaṃ paramātmānamanusṛtya 'prāṇo'; mukhyavāyuḥ 'utkrāmati'; dehānnirgacchatīti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Brahmasūtra-bhāṣya-dīpikā</s> 1.3.2.5:] Here, [anticipating the objection that] if the denotation of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is accepted, there would be contradiction with the indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of departure (<s>utkramaṇa</s>) etc. mentioned earlier — to address this he says 'tam' etc. By the word 'first' etc., the sentences following that are taken; by the second, the other indicatory marks are also included. The word 'api' is for aggregation, and in the sense of 'even though, nevertheless.' And thus — not only is there no contradiction with the opening use of the word '<s>prāṇa</s>', since it refers to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but 'also': when the denotation of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is accepted here, there is no contradiction with the indicatory marks of departure etc. Why? 'Also' — because even though <s>Viṣṇu</s> is all-pervading, the indicatory mark of departure is established by the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> text 'him departing' and so forth — this is the construction. The purport is that a contradiction from worldly perception is of no consequence when the matter is established by scripture. In the preceding passage, 'the tip of this heart becomes luminous; by that luminosity this Self departs' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.2) — the Supreme Self, who is the subject of the preceding passage, is referred to by the word 'that.' And thus, through the luminous tip of the heart, following the Supreme Self who is 'departing' — going out — from the body of the one who has direct knowledge, '<s>prāṇa</s>' — the chief vital air — 'departs' — goes out from the body — this is the meaning of the scripture.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //

aham 'āhanasaṃ'; svābhimanyamānalatādvārā yajñeṣvabhiṣūyamāṇaṃ 'somaṃ'; somalatābhimāninaṃ candraṃ tvaṣṭāraṃ ca 'uta pūṣaṇaṃ'; pūṣaṇaṃ ca bhagaṃ ca 'bibharmi'; dadhāmītyaṃbhraṇīvākyasyārthaḥ / tvaṣṭrādayastu sūryaprabhedāḥ / tattvapradīpasattarkadīpāvalyostu bṛhadbhāṣyānusāreṇa 'somam'; umayā sahitam 'āhanasam'; āsamantāt hantāraṃ saṃhartāraṃ rudraṃ bibharmīti vyākhyātam /

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti // sūtre gahanārthatvātprathamaṃ hetubhāgaṃ vyākariṣyamāṇo 'siddhiparihārāya śrutimudāharati - etasminniti / itītyanantaraṃ 'vākye'; iti śeṣaḥ / anyapadārthaṃ darśayanvigrahaṃ darśayati - ambareti / ambaramākāśaḥ anto yasya sarvasya pṛthivyāderdhārakatvokterityarthaḥ / yadyapi 'etasmin'; iti vākye 'mbaradhṛtirevocyate / na tu tadantarasarvadhṛtiḥ / tathāpi 'yadūrdhvaṃ gārgi divo yadarvākpṛthivyā yadantarā dyāvāpṛthivī...... ākāśa eva tadotaṃ ca protaṃ ca'; (bṛ. 5-8-7.) ityanenākāśasya citprakṛteḥ sarvādhāratvamuktvānantaram 'etasmin'; iti vākye 'kṣarasya tādṛśaprakṛtyādhāratvokteḥ prakṛtidvārākṣarasyāmbarāntasarvādhāratvamatroktameveti na doṣaḥ / etacca sūtre 'mbarāntetyantapadaprayogātsūcitam / sūtre tattvityanuvṛttapadadvayopetapratijñābhāgaṃ vyākhyāti - brahmaiveti / akṣaraṃ brahmaivetyanvayaḥ / anena akṣarasya 'etasmin'; iti prakṛtidvārā'kāśāntasarvādhāratvaśruterakṣaraṃ brahmaiveti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.2:
He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the settled conclusion: '<s>ata</s>' (therefore). // Since the <s>sūtra</s> has a profound meaning, while about to explain the reason-portion first, he cites a <s>Śruti</s> to remove the objection of non-establishment: '<s>etasmin</s>' (in this). The word '<s>iti</s>' is [to be completed with] 'in the sentence' — this is the remainder. Showing the meaning of other words, he shows the analysis: '<s>ambara</s>' (sky). <s>Ambara</s> means <s>ākāśa</s> (space); '<s>anta</s>' means that of which [everything] is the end — the meaning is: because it is stated that [<s>Akṣara</s>] supports everything beginning with earth, etc. Although in the sentence '<s>etasmin</s>' (in this), only the support of space is stated, and not the support of everything within it, nevertheless, after stating in '<s>yadūrdhvaṃ gārgi</s>...' 'that which is above heaven, that which is below earth, that which is between heaven and earth — all that is woven and interwoven in space alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.7) the all-supporting nature of space, i.e., of <s>citprakṛti</s> (conscious <s>Prakṛti</s>), subsequently in the sentence '<s>etasmin</s>', since the support of <s>Akṣara</s> over such <s>Prakṛti</s> is stated, the all-supporting nature of <s>Akṣara</s> up to and including space through the intermediary of <s>Prakṛti</s> is indeed stated here — hence there is no fault. And this is indicated in the <s>sūtra</s> by the use of the word '<s>anta</s>' in '<s>ambarānte</s>'. He explains the assertion-portion of the <s>sūtra</s> equipped with the two continuing words '<s>tat</s>' and '<s>tu</s>': '<s>brahmaiva</s>' (is <s>Brahman</s> alone). The syntactical connection is: <s>Akṣara</s> is <s>Brahman</s> alone. By this, since there is a <s>Śruti</s> statement that <s>Akṣara</s> is the support of everything up to space through the intermediary of <s>Prakṛti</s> in the sentence '<s>etasmin</s>', the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated to be that <s>Akṣara</s> is indeed <s>Brahman</s>.

sarvādhāratvaṃ kuto viṣṇutvaniścāyakamityataḥ tasya viṣṇuliṅgatvena śrutisiddhatvādityāha - ya iti // vyākhyāteyaṃ śrutirjanmanaye /

BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.3:

children.text:
bhartā sanbhriyamāṇo bibharti /
eko devo bahudhā niviṣṭaḥ /
yadā bhāraṃ tandrayate sa bhartum /
parāsya bhāraṃ punarastameti / (tai.ā. 3-14.)

BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.4:
'bhartā san'; iti taittirīyāṇāṃ śrutiḥ / 'devaḥ'; prāṇākhyo bhagavān svayaṃ jagatā jīvena vā hṛdi bhriyamāṇaḥ tat 'bibharti'; dhatte puṣṇāti ca / tarhi jagadīśayoḥ sāmyāpattirityata āha - bhartā sanniti / jagato mūlabhartā sanneva bhriyamāṇaḥ, na svakīyasthityetyarthaḥ / nanvekasyaiva bhagavataḥ bhartā bhriyamāṇo bibhartītyanekavidhavyavahāraviṣayatvaṃ kathamityata āha - eko bahudheti / eko 'pi bhartṛtvādinā 'bahudhā'; bahurūpeṇa ca 'niviṣṭo'; vyāpta ityarthaḥ / tatra praviṣṭa iti vā / 'yadā bhāraṃ tandrayate sa bhartuṃ parāsya bhāraṃ punarastameti'; iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / 'sa'; viṣṇuryadā taṃ jagadbhāraṃ 'parāsya'; adho nidhāya punarbhartuṃ 'tandrayate'; necchati tadā asau bhāraḥ 'astameti'; naśyatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.4:
'<s>Bhartā san</s>' (the sustainer being) — this is a <s>Śruti</s> of the <s>Taittirīyas</s>. '<s>Devaḥ</s>' — the Lord Himself, called <s>Prāṇa</s>, while being sustained (<s>bhriyamāṇaḥ</s>) by the world or by the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) in the heart, 'sustains' (<s>bibharti</s>) — holds and nourishes it. If so, there would be equality between the world and the Lord — to address this, he says: '<s>bhartā san</s>' (being the sustainer). Being the fundamental sustainer of the world, He is sustained — not for the sake of His own existence; this is the meaning. But how can the one Lord alone be the subject of manifold activities such as sustaining and being sustained? To this he says: '<s>eko bahudhā</s>' (one, manifoldly). Although one, by virtue of being the sustainer and the like, He is 'manifoldly' (<s>bahudhā</s>), i.e., in many forms, '<s>niviṣṭaḥ</s>' — pervading; or, entered into it. '<s>Yadā bhāraṃ tandrayate sa bhartuṃ parāsya bhāraṃ punarastameti</s>' — this is the remainder of the sentence. '<s>Sa</s>' — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — when He '<s>tandrayate</s>' — does not wish — to bear that burden of the world again, having '<s>parāsya</s>' — cast down — [the burden], then that burden '<s>astameti</s>' — is destroyed; this is the meaning.
in whom all the <s>Devas</s> are seated. (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 1.2)

'yasmin'; ityapi taittirīye 'nyadvākyam / atra yacchabdasya 'tadeva brahma paramam'; (mahānā. 1-6.) ityuttaravākyasthatacchabdenānvayaḥ / cau prakārasamuccaye / tathā ca - 'yasminnidaṃ'; sarvaṃ jagat 'saṃ'; samyak 'vi'; vividhaṃ 'caidhi'; avardhata / edhaterliṅi chāndasaṃ rūpametat / yadvā - edhivardhate / astīti vārthaḥ / asmin pakṣe asterlaṭi madhyamapuruṣaikavacane chāndasaṃ rūpam / vastuto loṭi madhyamapuruṣaikavacane rūpametat / yasmiṃśca 'viśve'; sarve devāḥ 'adhiniṣeduḥ'; yamadhyagustadeva brahmetyarthaḥ / ityādiśruterityasya ambarāntadhṛterityanenānvayaḥ / brahmaṇyavagatāyā iti śeṣaḥ / tṛtīyārthe pañcamī / ādiśabdena 'yenāvṛtaṃ khaṃ ca divaṃ mahīṃ ca yenādityastapati tejasā bhrājasā ca'; (mahānā. 1-3.) ityādikam, 'tameva mṛtyumamṛtaṃ tamāhustaṃ bhartāraṃ tamu goptāramāhuḥ'; (tai.ā. 3-14.) ityādi ca gṛhyate / tathā ca viṣṇuliṅgatvena śrutisiddhāt sarvādhāraṇāt viṣṇutvaniścayo bhavatyeveti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.5:
'<s>Yasmin</s>' (in whom) — this is another sentence in the <s>Taittirīya</s>. Here, the word '<s>yat</s>' connects with the word '<s>tat</s>' in the subsequent sentence '<s>tadeva brahma paramaṃ</s>' (that alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>) (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 1.6). The two '<s>ca</s>'-s are for aggregation of modes. And thus — '<s>yasmin</s>' — in whom — '<s>idaṃ</s>' — all this world — '<s>saṃ</s>' — fully — '<s>vi</s>' — in various ways — '<s>caidhi</s>' — grew. This is a Vedic (<s>chāndasa</s>) form of the verb <s>edh</s> (to grow) in the optative. Alternatively, <s>edhi</s> means 'grows' or 'exists.' In this alternative reading, it is a <s>chāndasa</s> form of <s>as</s> (to be) in the second person singular present tense; in reality, it is a form in the second person singular imperative. And in whom 'all' (<s>viśve</s>) the <s>Devas</s> '<s>adhiniṣeduḥ</s>' (are seated upon) — that in which they abide is <s>Brahman</s>; this is the meaning. The expression '<s>ityādiśruteḥ</s>' (from such <s>Śruti</s> passages and the like) connects with '<s>ambarāntadhṛteḥ</s>' (the support up to space). The remainder is: [which is] understood to belong to <s>Brahman</s>. The ablative is used in the sense of the instrumental.
