By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like) are included passages such as '<s>yenāvṛtaṃ khaṃ ca divaṃ mahīṃ ca yenādityastapati tejasā bhrājasā ca</s>' (by whom space, heaven, and earth are pervaded, by whose radiance and brilliance the sun shines) (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 1.3), and '<s>tameva mṛtyum amṛtaṃ tam āhuḥ taṃ bhartāraṃ tamu goptāram āhuḥ</s>' (Him they call both death and immortality; Him they call the sustainer and the protector) (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.14), and the like. Thus the purport is: from the all-supporting nature established through <s>Śruti</s> by means of characteristic marks of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the determination that [<s>Akṣara</s>] is <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed follows.

children.text: pṛthivyādi prakṛtyantaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavacca yat /
children.translated_text: Everything from earth up to <s>Prakṛti</s>, whatever has been, will be, and is —
<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone sustains all this; none other than He is capable of [this] support.
— thus [it is stated] in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.6:
viṣṇuvadanyasyāpi sarvādhāratvaṃ kiṃ na syādityata āha - pṛthivyādīti // prakṛtyantapadena sautrāntapadaṃ vyākhyātam / 'bhūtam'; atītaṃ 'bhavyaṃ'; bhaviṣyat 'bhavat'; vartamānaṃ 'yat'; idaṃ viśvaṃ tadviṣṇuḥ 'eka eva'; asahāyo bibharti / tasya dhṛtau tasmādviṣṇoranyaḥ 'kṣamaḥ'; samartho netyarthaḥ / iti skānda ityasya 'uktatvāt'; ityadhyāhāreṇa na sāvakāśatvaṃ liṅgasyeti vākyaśeṣeṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.6:
Why could all-supporting nature not belong to someone other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> as well? To this he says: '<s>pṛthivyādi</s>' (from earth, etc.). // The word '<s>prakṛtyanta</s>' (up to <s>Prakṛti</s>) explains the word in the <s>sūtra</s>. '<s>Bhūtam</s>' — the past; '<s>bhavyam</s>' — the future; '<s>bhavat</s>' — the present; '<s>yat</s>' — whatever this universe is — that, <s>Viṣṇu</s> 'alone' (<s>eka eva</s>) — without any helper — sustains. In that support, none other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> is '<s>kṣamaḥ</s>' — capable; this is the meaning. The [phrase] '<s>iti skānde</s>' (thus in the <s>Skānda</s>) connects with the remainder of the sentence '<s>uktatvāt</s>' (because it is stated) — [meaning] the indicative mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is not left without scope, by supplying the word 'because it is stated.'
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
And that [all-supporting nature is <s>Brahman</s>'s] because of [its] commanding authority (<s>praśāsana</s>). | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.11 |

children.text:
sā ca dhṛtiḥ prasāsanāducyate / 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane
gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ'; (bṛ. 5-8-9.) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: And that support is said [to belong to <s>Akṣara</s>] because of [its] commanding authority. '<s>Etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ</s>' — 'Under the command of this <s>Akṣara</s>, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon are held in their places' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.9) — by such [passages].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.7:
yuktyantareṇa viṣṇorevākṣaratvaṃ pratipādayatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - sā ceti // 'sā ca'; sarvadhṛtirapi ityādinā praśāsanāducyate yato 'to 'pi brahmākṣaramityanvayaḥ / ādiśabdenaivaṃrūpāṇyekaprakaraṇagatānekavākyāni gṛhyante / anena - yadā 'sā'; pūrvoktā sarvadhṛtireva akṣarasya viṣṇutvasādhikā, tadā sutarāṃ, yā tu 'etasya'; iti śrutivākye 'kṣarasya praśāsanādeva asaṅkucitaviṣayānanyāyattaprakṛṣṭājñāmātrādeva sarvadhṛtirucyate seti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.7:
Presenting and explaining the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the <s>Akṣara</s>-nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone through another reasoning: '<s>sā ca</s>' (and that). // 'And that' — even the all-supporting nature — is said [to belong to <s>Akṣara</s>] because of commanding authority (<s>praśāsana</s>), and therefore too <s>Akṣara</s> is <s>Brahman</s> — this is the syntactical connection. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like), many sentences of this type belonging to the same section are included. By this [the meaning is]: when 'that' (<s>sā</s>) — the aforementioned all-supporting nature itself — is the establisher of <s>Akṣara</s>'s <s>Viṣṇu</s>-nature, then all the more so, the all-supporting nature that is stated in the <s>Śruti</s> passage '<s>etasya</s>' (of this) solely because of the commanding authority of <s>Akṣara</s> — an unrestricted, not dependent on another, supreme command alone — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> as stated.
And that commanding authority belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.8:
nanu sarvadhṛtihetupraśāsanena kuto 'kṣarasya viṣṇutvaniścaya ityatastasya viṣṇukartṛkatvādityāha - tacceti/ sarvadhṛtikāraṇaṃ praśāsanaṃ tvityarthaḥ / na kevalaṃ sarvadhṛtiḥ, kintu taddhetupraśāsanaṃ ceti samuccaye vā caśabdaḥ / 'viṣṇoreva'; viṣṇukartṛkameva / na tvanyakartṛkamiti evārthaḥ / evakārasyottaratropayogaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.8:
But how does the commanding authority that causes all-supporting nature establish the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-nature of <s>Akṣara</s>? Because it is performed by <s>Viṣṇu</s> [alone] — thus he says: '<s>tacca</s>' (and that). The meaning is: the commanding authority that is the cause of all-supporting nature. The word '<s>ca</s>' is for aggregation — not only the all-supporting nature, but also the commanding authority that is its cause. '<s>Viṣṇoreva</s>' — belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; the meaning of '<s>eva</s>' is: and not to anyone else. The word '<s>eva</s>' serves a purpose in what follows.

children.text: saptārdhagarbhā bhuvanasya reto viṣṇostiṣṭhanti pradiśā vidharmaṇi / (ṛ. 1-164-36.)
children.translated_text: The seven with enriched wombs, the seeds of the universe, abide in the ordinance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in [His] manifold sustaining. (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 1.164.36)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.9:
kuta etajjñāyata ityatastaccetyanena pratijñātārthe śrutiṃ pramāṇayati - sapteti // ā ṛddhagarbhāḥ ārdhagarbhāḥ / brahmāṇḍākhyātisamṛddhagarbhāḥ / nigaraṇena bhriyanta iti garbhāstadāvaraṇabhūtā iti yāvat / reta iti liṅgavyatyayenaikavacanaṃ prathamābahuvacanārthe / tathā ca - 'bhuvanasya'; lokasya 'retaso'; ratipradāḥ sārabhūtā vā / yadvā - bhūmatvātpūrṇatvādvananīyatvādbhajanīyatvādbhuvanasya viṣṇo retorūpāḥ 'sapta'; mahadahaṅkārapañcamahābhūtākhyāḥ brahmādayo devāḥ / bhavanasya 'reto'; retaso jagadratipradasya viṣṇoḥ 'pradiśā'; ādeśenājñayā 'vidharmaṇi'; vividhaviśvadhāraṇe tiṣṭhantīti ṛṅmantrārthaḥ / viśveśvaratīrthīye tu 'ardhasya'; viṣṇoḥ 'garbhāḥ'; sapta devāḥ bhuvanasya 'retaḥ'; kāraṇam / ete ca viṣṇoḥ pradiśā vidharmaṇi tiṣṭhantītyartha uktaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.9:
How is this known? To that, he adduces <s>Śruti</s> as evidence for what was asserted by '<s>tacca</s>' (and that): '<s>sapta</s>' (seven). // '<s>Ā ṛddhagarbhāḥ</s>' means '<s>ārdhagarbhāḥ</s>' — those whose wombs are enriched, i.e., enriched with the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>); those who are sustained by being contained — they are the wombs, meaning the coverings thereof. '<s>Retaḥ</s>' — the singular is used in the sense of the nominative plural due to gender irregularity (<s>liṅgavyatyaya</s>). And thus — of '<s>bhuvana</s>' (the world), [they are] the '<s>retaḥ</s>' — those that give delight, or the essential ones. Alternatively: because of greatness, fullness, being worthy of praise, and being worthy of worship, [they are] of <s>bhuvana</s>, i.e., of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the '<s>retaḥ</s>'-forms — the seven, namely <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, and the five great elements (<s>pañcamahābhūta</s>), [or] <s>Brahmā</s> and the other <s>Devas</s>. Of '<s>bhavana</s>' — [they are] the '<s>retaḥ</s>' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> who gives delight to the world — by [His] '<s>pradiśā</s>' — command, instruction — they abide in '<s>vidharmaṇi</s>' — in the manifold sustaining of the universe; this is the meaning of the <s>Ṛgvedic</s> mantra. In the [commentary of] <s>Viśveśvaratīrtha</s>, however, the meaning is stated as: the 'seven <s>Devas</s>' are the '<s>garbhāḥ</s>' (embryos) of '<s>ardha</s>' (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), [who are] the '<s>retaḥ</s>' (cause) of '<s>bhuvana</s>' (the world). And these abide in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s '<s>pradiśā</s>' (command), in '<s>vidharmaṇi</s>' (manifold sustaining).

children.text: caturbhissākaṃ navatiṃ ca nāmabhiścakraṃ na vṛttaṃ vyatīravīvipat / (ṛ. 1-155-6.) ityādiśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With ninety-four names together, the wheel did not turn back' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 1.155.6) — from such <s>Śruti</s> passages.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.10:
'caturbhiḥ'; iti vākyaṃ tu janmanaye vyākhyātam / evaṃjātīyakaśrutirādiśabdārthaḥ / śruterityasya jñāyata ityadhyāhāreṇa tacceti pūrvavākyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.10:
The sentence '<s>caturbhiḥ</s>' (with four) has been explained in the <s>Janmanaye</s> [section]. Such types of <s>Śruti</s> passages are the meaning of the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like). The [expression] '<s>śruteḥ</s>' (from <s>Śruti</s>) connects with the previous sentence '<s>tacca</s>' (and that) by supplying the words '<s>jñāyate</s>' (it is known).

children.text:
ekaśśāstā na dvitīyo 'sti śāstā /
yo hṛcchayastamahamiha bravīmi /
children.translated_text:
There is one ruler; there is no second ruler.
He who dwells in the heart — Him I declare here.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.11:
sarvadhṛtihetupraśāsanaṃ viṣṇorivānyasyāpi kiṃ na syādityata āha - eka iti // idaṃ ca bhāratavākyaṃ sabhāparvagam / 'śāstā'; sarvadhṛtihetvājñākartā / 'ekaḥ'; na tu dvitīyo 'sti, sa ca viṣṇurevetyarthaḥ / 'garbhe śayānaṃ puruṣaṃ ko 'sti śāstā'; iti śiṣṭavākyam / 'yo hṛcchayaḥ'; ityanyadvākyamuttaravākyaparyālocanayā prakṛtasaṅgatam / 'yaḥ'; sarvadhṛtihetupraśāsanāya 'hṛcchayaḥ'; sarvahṛdayanivāsī tamahamiha sthāne bravīmītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.11:
Why could the commanding authority that causes all-supporting nature not belong to someone other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> as well? To this he says: '<s>eka</s>' (one). // This is a passage from the <s>Bhārata</s>, from the <s>Sabhāparva</s>. '<s>Śāstā</s>' — the commander, the issuer of commands that cause all-supporting nature. '<s>Ekaḥ</s>' — [there is only] one; there is no second; and that one is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; this is the meaning. The passage following is: '<s>garbhe śayānaṃ puruṣaṃ ko 'sti śāstā</s>' (who is the ruler of the <s>Puruṣa</s> lying in the womb?). '<s>Yo hṛcchayaḥ</s>' (He who dwells in the heart) — this is another sentence, connected with the topic under discussion by consideration of the subsequent sentence. '<s>Yaḥ</s>' — He who, for the purpose of commanding that causes all-supporting nature, is '<s>hṛcchayaḥ</s>' — the dweller in all hearts — Him I declare here, in this context; this is the meaning.

children.text:
na kevalaṃ me bhavataśca rājan /
sa vai balaṃ balināṃ cāpareṣām /
ityādeśca // 11 //
children.translated_text:
'Not only of me and of you, O King,
He is indeed the strength of the strong and of others' —
from such [passages] as well. // 11 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.12:
'na kevalam'; ityādi hiraṇyakaśipuṃ prati prahlādavākyam / he rājan na kevalaṃ me bhavataśca 'saḥ'; bhagavān 'balaṃ'; balaprado dhṛtihetuḥ, kintvanyeṣāṃ balināṃ ca balamityarthaḥ / ityādeścetyasya 'tacca praśāsanaṃ viṣṇoreveti jñāyate'; ityanenānvayaḥ / anena viṣṇorevetyevakārasya kṛtyaṃ sūcitam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.12:
'<s>Na kevalam</s>' (not only) — this and what follows is a statement of <s>Prahlāda</s> addressed to <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>. O King, '<s>saḥ</s>' — the Lord — is not only the '<s>balam</s>' — the bestower of strength, the cause of support — of me and of you, but also of other strong beings; this is the meaning. The [expression] '<s>ityādeśca</s>' (and from such passages) connects with [the statement] '<s>tacca praśāsanaṃ viṣṇoreva iti jñāyate</s>' (and that commanding authority is known to belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone). By this, the function of the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) in '<s>viṣṇoreva</s>' is indicated.
<s>sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
And because of the exclusion of the nature of other [entities]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.12 |

And because of the exclusion by '<s>asthūlam anaṇu</s>' (not gross, not subtle) (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.8) and the like, of the natures of other entities such as the gross, the subtle, and so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.13:
hetvantareṇa viṣṇorevākṣaratvaṃ pratipādayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - anyeti // ādiśabdena 'etadvai tadakṣaraṃ gārgi brāhmaṇā abhivadanti asthūlamanaṇvahrasvamadīrghamalohitamasnehamacchāyamatamo 'vāyvanākāśamasaṅgamarasamagandhamacakṣuṣkamaśrotramavāgamano 'tejaskamapramāṇamamukhamamātramanantaramabrāhmaṃ na tadaśnāti kiñcana na tadaśnāti kaścana'; (bṛ. 5-8-8.) iti samagravākyaṃ gṛhyate / 'sthūlāṇvādīnām'; iti bhāvapradhāno nirdeśaḥ / vyāvṛtterityanantaraṃ 'kathanāt'; iti śeṣaḥ / co hetusamuccaye / asyāpi brahmaivākṣaramiti pūrveṇānvayaḥ /
anena - na kevalaṃ pūrvoktahetubhyāṃ, kintvanyeṣāṃ sakalavastūnāṃ bhāvānāṃ svarūpāṇāṃ sthaulyādidharmāṇāṃ vyāvṛtteḥ ananyāpekṣārāhityasya 'asthūlam'; ityādinākṣare kathanādapyakṣaraṃ brahmaiveti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
śrutyarthastu - 'tat'; ākāśāśrayatvena vakṣyamāṇam 'akṣaraṃ'; na kṣaratītyakṣaraśabdavācyaṃ brahma etallakṣaṇakaṃ 'brāhmaṇāḥ'; jñānino 'bhivadanti vai prasiddham / tatkiṃ lakṣaṇamityata āha - asthūlamiti / sthūlaṃ mahat / svaprabuddhārthāntaraṃ tu - 'etat'; akṣaraṃ brāhmaṇāḥ 'tat'; citprakṛtyākhyamiti vadanti pūrvapakṣayanti tadbrahmetyabhivadanti siddhāntayanti / siddhāntasādhakaṃ hetumevāha - asthūlamityādineti / anena 'prasiddhasthūlasūkṣmādivailakṣaṇyājjanārdanaḥ'; iti bṛhadbhāṣyoktarītyā prasiddhasthūlādivailakṣaṇyamucyate / sthūlāṇvādipadasya bhāvapradhānatve tu lokikasthaulyādirāhityamanenoktaṃ bhavati / 'alohitaṃ'; lohitaśabditaraktādyupalakṣitaprākṛtarūpasāmānyarahitam / 'asnehaṃ'; prākṛtasneharahitam / 'acchāyaṃ'; 'chāyātvavidyā samproktā'; iti vacanādajñānarahitam / jīvadehasyeva chāyārahitaṃ ca / 'atamaḥ'; āvaraṇarahitam / 'avāyu'; pīḍārūpaśvāsocchvāsarahitam / yadvā - vyāsatīrthīyoktarītyā avāyvanākāśamatejaskamityetaistadārabdhaśarīrarahitamityucyate / ata eva 'acchāyamatamo 'vāyvanākāśam'; ityatra sarvātmanā niṣedha ityuktaṃ sudhāṭīkayoḥ/ 'asaṅgaṃ'; sarvagatamapi tatkṛtaleparahitam / arasamagandhamityābhyāmupalakṣaṇayā prākṛtarasagandhādirāhityamucyate / acakṣuṣkamityādinā prākṛtasvabhinnacakṣurādirāhityam / 'atejaskaṃ'; prākṛtavarcorahitam / 'aprāṇam'; uktacakṣurādivyatiriktaprākṛtajñānendriyakarmendriyarahitam / vyāsatīrthīyoktarītyā prāṇavāyurahitamiti vā / 'amukhaṃ'; prākṛtavigraharahitaṃ vā / 'amātraṃ'; parimitiśūnyam / mīyante ebhiriti mātrā indriyāṇīti ṭīkokteḥ amātraṃ cakṣurādīndriyarahitamiti vyāsatīrthīyoktiḥ / sarvātmanā śarīrārambhakapañcamātraśūnyaṃ vā / na vidyate 'ntaraṃ bāhyaṃ ca yasmāttadanantaramabāhyam, idameva sarvasmādantaraṃ bāhyaṃ cetyarthaḥ / 'tat'; brahma 'kiṃ ca na'; annādikaṃ śubhamaśubhaṃ vā sāśanānaśanatvena naradevau yathoditau /
attiṃ vināpyadaurbalyāttathānattirharerbhujiḥ //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.3.13:
Having cited the sūtra that establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s alone being the <s>Akṣara</s> (Imperishable) through another reason, he explains it — beginning with 'anya' (other). By the word 'ādi' (etc.), the entire statement 'This, O <s>Gārgī</s>, is that <s>Akṣara</s> which the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> speak of — neither gross nor subtle, neither short nor long, not red, not moist, without shadow, without darkness, without air, without space, unattached, without taste, without smell, without eyes, without ears, without speech, without mind, without radiance, without measure, without face, without extent, without interior, not <s>Brahman</s>; nothing eats it, nor does anyone eat it' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.8) is taken as the complete statement. The expression '<s>sthūlāṇvādīnām</s>' (of grossness, subtlety, etc.) is a designation with the abstract sense predominating. After '<s>vyāvṛtteḥ</s>' (because of the exclusion), '<s>kathanāt</s>' (because of the statement) is to be supplied. The particle 'ca' is used for the accumulation of reasons. The syntactic connection of this [sūtra] too is with the preceding: '<s>akṣaram</s> is <s>Brahman</s> indeed.'
By this — not only because of the two previously stated reasons, but also because in the <s>Akṣara</s>, through statements beginning with '<s>asthūlam</s>' (not gross), there is the declaration of the exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) of the essential natures (<s>svarūpa</s>) and attributes like grossness of all other entities — the <s>sūtra</s> meaning is stated as: the <s>Akṣara</s> is <s>Brahman</s> alone.
The meaning of the <s>śruti</s>, however, is: 'That' — which is to be described as the support of space — '<s>Akṣara</s>' — <s>Brahman</s>, denotable by the word '<s>Akṣara</s>' meaning that which does not perish — 'the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>' — the knowers — 'speak of' as well-known. What are its characteristics? To this he says — '<s>asthūlam</s>' (not gross). '<s>Sthūla</s>' means great. But in the interpretation intended by himself: '<s>etat</s>' — this <s>Akṣara</s> — the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — '<s>tat</s>' — call '<s>citprakṛti</s>' (the sentient <s>Prakṛti</s>) in the prima facie view, and declare it to be <s>Brahman</s> in the established conclusion. He states the reason that establishes the established conclusion: beginning with '<s>asthūlam</s>' (not gross). By this, in the manner stated in the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> — 'Because of being different from well-known gross, subtle, etc., [it is] <s>Janārdana</s>' — the difference from well-known grossness and the like is stated. When the word '<s>sthūlāṇvādi</s>' has the abstract sense predominating, then by this the absence of ordinary grossness and the like is stated. '<s>Alohitam</s>' (not red) — devoid of the general <s>prākṛta</s> (material) form indicated by the word '<s>lohita</s>' (red), i.e., blood and the like. '<s>Asneham</s>' (without moisture) — devoid of material moisture. '<s>Acchāyam</s>' (without shadow) — because of the statement '<s>chāyā tu vidyā samproktā</s>' (shadow is declared to be knowledge/ignorance), [it means] devoid of ignorance; and also devoid of shadow like the body of a <s>jīva</s>. '<s>Atamaḥ</s>' (without darkness) — devoid of covering/obstruction. '<s>Avāyu</s>' (without wind) — devoid of inhalation and exhalation that are of the nature of affliction. Alternatively, in the manner stated in <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>'s [commentary]: by '<s>avāyu</s>, <s>anākāśam</s>, <s>atejaskam</s>' — it is said that [He is] devoid of a body constituted of those [elements]. Therefore, in '<s>acchāyam atamaḥ avāyu anākāśam</s>' the negation is absolute — thus it is stated in the <s>Sudhā</s> and <s>Ṭīkā</s>. '<s>Asaṅgam</s>' (unattached) — though all-pervading, devoid of contact produced by it. By '<s>arasam agandham</s>' (without taste, without smell), through indication, the absence of material taste, smell, etc. is stated. By '<s>acakṣuṣkam</s>' etc., the absence of material eyes and other sense organs different from His own is stated. '<s>Atejaskam</s>' (without radiance) — devoid of material splendor. '<s>Aprāṇam</s>' (without breath) — devoid of material sense organs of knowledge and action other than the aforementioned eyes etc. Alternatively, in the manner of <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>'s [commentary], devoid of the vital air (<s>prāṇavāyu</s>). '<s>Amukham</s>' (without face) — devoid of a material body. '<s>Amātram</s>' (without measure) — devoid of limitation. Since the <s>Ṭīkā</s> states '<s>mātrā</s> means the senses, since they are that by which things are measured,' <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>'s interpretation is that '<s>amātram</s>' means devoid of senses like the eye. Or, completely devoid of the five subtle elements (<s>pañcamātra</s>) that constitute the body. 'That which has no interior or exterior is <s>anantaram</s> and <s>abāhyam</s>' — meaning this alone is interior to everything and exterior to everything. 'That' — <s>Brahman</s> — 'what' — food and other things, whether auspicious or inauspicious — does not eat, as stated through the pair of eating and not eating, referring to men and gods respectively;
Even without eating, due to the absence of weakness, likewise [His] non-eating; <s>Hari</s>'s arm [is never weakened] —

children.text: iti smṛterupajīvanārthaṃ 'nāśnāti'; nātti / 'kaścana'; ko 'pi samarthaḥ 'tat'; brahma 'nāśnāti'; na saṃharatīti /
children.translated_text: Thus, for the purpose of supporting the <s>smṛti</s>, '<s>nāśnāti</s>' — does not eat. '<s>Kaścana</s>' — anyone capable — '<s>tat</s>' — <s>Brahman</s> — '<s>nāśnāti</s>' — does not consume, i.e., does not destroy.

children.text:
'asthūlo 'naṇuramadhyamo madhyamo 'vyāpako vyāpako yo 'sau harirādiranādiraviśvo viśvaḥ saguṇo nirguṇaḥ'; ityāderviṣṇoreva
te dharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not gross, not subtle, not middling yet middling, not non-pervading yet pervading, who is <s>Hari</s>, beginning-less yet the beginning, not universal yet universal, with qualities yet without qualities' — such attributes belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.3.14:
laukikasthaulyādirāhityaṃ kathaṃ viṣṇutvaniścāyakaṃ, taddharmatvenāniścitatvādityata āha - asthūla iti/ 'asthūlaḥ'; laukikamahattvarahitaḥ, 'anaṇuḥ'; laukikāṇutvarahitaḥ, 'amadhyamaḥ'; laukikamadhyamaparimāṇarahitaḥ / na ca parimāṇādirāhitye viṣṇorasvabhāvatvāpattiriti vācyam / laukikasthaulyādirāhitye 'pyalaukikaparimāṇādisadbhāvādityāha - madhyama ityādinā // na cānena sthūlatvāderanukternacoktaparihāra iti vācyam / 'madhyamo vyāpakaḥ'; ityādyukteḥ sthūlo 'ṇuścetyupalakṣakatvāt / na camadhyamaparimāṇavattve viṣṇoranityatvāpattiriti vācyam / anityatvānāpādakamadhyamaparimāṇābhyupagamāt / tattvapradīpe tu 'amadhyamo'; madhyamaparimāṇaniyativarjitaḥ 'vyāpto 'ṇurmadhyamastathā'; ityukteḥ madhye mīyamānatvānmadhyama iti vyākhyātam / asmin pakṣe niyatamadhyamaparimāṇa- śūnyatvānnānityatvamiti parihāro 'bhipretaḥ / na vidyate 'nyo vyāpako yasyāsāvavyāpakaḥ / lokavilakṣaṇavyāpaka iti vā / 'vyāpakaḥ'; sarvadeśakālavyāpī / ādiḥ kāraṇamanādistacchūnya utpattiśūnya iti vā / na vidyate viśvaḥ pūrṇo yasmādaviśvaḥ / pūrṇatvādviśvaḥ / yadvā - 'aviśvo'; laukikeṣvapraviṣṭaḥ / 'viśvaḥ'; jagaddhṛdayaṃ vā praviṣṭaḥ / 'saguṇo'; jñānānandādiguṇavān / 'nirguṇaḥ'; sattvādiguṇahīna ityarthaḥ / 'ityādeḥ'; itivākyāt / ādiśabdena 'aṇoraṇīyānmahatomahīyān'; (kaṭha. 2-20.) iti kaṭhaśrutirgṛhyate / 'te'; asthūlatvādayaḥ / yata iti niścitā iti śeṣaḥ / asya ataste akṣarasya viṣṇutvaniścāyakā bhavantītyupaskṛtavākyenānvayaḥ / nanu tathāpi te viṣṇoreveti kathaṃ, yasmātte 'prākṛtavigrahe madhyamākṣare 'pi santi / naiṣa doṣaḥ - yataste yatra bhagavadapekṣayaiva santi / anyānapekṣā eva dharmāhyatra hetutvena vivakṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.3.14:
How does the absence of ordinary grossness, etc. establish <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood, given that it has not been ascertained as His attribute? To this he says — beginning with '<s>asthūla</s>.' '<s>Asthūlaḥ</s>' — devoid of ordinary greatness; '<s>anaṇuḥ</s>' — devoid of ordinary subtlety; '<s>amadhyamaḥ</s>' — devoid of ordinary middling measure. Nor should it be objected that in the absence of measure and the like, <s>Viṣṇu</s> would become non-existent — because even in the absence of ordinary grossness and the like, non-ordinary measure and the like do exist — this he states beginning with '<s>madhyama</s>.' Nor should it be objected that since there is no statement of grossness [for <s>Viṣṇu</s>], the previously offered resolution does not apply — because the statement '<s>madhyamo vyāpakaḥ</s>' (middling, pervading) etc. serves as an indicator for grossness and subtlety as well. Nor should it be objected that if <s>Viṣṇu</s> possesses middling measure, He would be impermanent — because He accepts a middling measure that does not entail impermanence. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, '<s>amadhyamaḥ</s>' is explained as 'devoid of the restriction of middling measure,' citing '<s>vyāpto aṇur madhyamas tathā</s>' (pervading, subtle, and middling likewise) — meaning <s>madhyama</s> is so called because it is measured in the middle. In this interpretation, the resolution is that there is no impermanence because of the absence of a fixed middling measure. '<s>Avyāpakaḥ</s>' — one for whom there is no other pervader; or, a pervader different from the world. '<s>Vyāpakaḥ</s>' — pervading all places and times. '<s>Ādi</s>' (beginning) means cause; '<s>anādi</s>' (beginningless) means devoid of that, or devoid of origination. '<s>Aviśvaḥ</s>' — one from whom fullness (<s>viśva</s>) is never absent; '<s>viśvaḥ</s>' — because of being full. Alternatively, '<s>aviśvaḥ</s>' means one who has not entered into worldly things; '<s>viśvaḥ</s>' means one who has entered the heart of the universe. '<s>Saguṇaḥ</s>' — possessing qualities like knowledge and bliss; '<s>nirguṇaḥ</s>' — devoid of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the rest — this is the meaning. '<s>Ityādeḥ</s>' — from this statement. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' the <s>Kaṭha</s> <s>śruti</s> 'Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.20) is included. '<s>Te</s>' — [the attributes] beginning with not being gross. 'Because they are ascertained' — this is to be supplied. The syntactic connection with the supplemented sentence is: these attributes are determiners of the <s>Akṣara</s> being <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Now, even so, how [can one say] 'they belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone,' since these [attributes] are also present in the material body and the intermediate <s>Akṣara</s> (i.e., <s>citprakṛti</s>)? This is not a defect — because these [attributes] exist in them only with reference to the Lord. It is the attributes that do not depend on anything else that are intended here as the reason.
Not gross, yet of the form of the subtle, He is non-universal yet universal indeed;
He whose form consists of contradictory attributes — He is <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person), by [His] sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>).
Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Brāhma</s> [Purāṇa]. // 12 //
// Thus ends the <s>Akṣarādhikaraṇa</s> // 3 //
// 4. <s>Sadadhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of <s>Sat</s>) //
By [the passage] '<s>Sat</s> (Being) alone, O dear one, this [world] was in the beginning' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) and what follows, the creatorship of <s>Sat</s> is stated.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.4.1:
atrādhikaraṇe 'nekaprakaraṇātmakaṃ 'sadeva'; ityādisthānaṃ samanvīyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayavākyamudāhṛsya viṣayādikaṃ ca sūcayati - saditi // 'ityādinā'; chāndogyavākyena / ādiśabdena 'ekamevādvitīyaṃ, (chāṃ. 6-2-1.) tattejo 'sṛjata, (chāṃ. 6-2-3.) sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ, (chāṃ. 6-8-6.) satā somya tadā sampanno bhavati'; (chāṃ. 6-8-1) ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / taccetyataḥ tadityākṛṣyate / tathā ca ityādinā sataḥ 'tat'; janmanayoktaṃ 'sraṣṭṛtvam'; ananyādhīnakāraṇatvam / upalakṣaṇametat / sarvottamatvasarvādhāratvasuptigamyatvādikaṃ ca 'ucyate'; pratipādyate iti yojanā / anena janmādhikaraṇoktakāraṇatvasya viṣṇvanyasmin pradhāne ākṣepāttenāsya ākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / tathā viṣayavākyam, sadākhyo viṣayaścoktaḥ / 'sadeva'; ityuddālakavākyam / he 'somya'; bhaktijñānalakṣaṇasomārha śvetaketho 'idam'; asya jagataḥ 'agre'; tatsṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ pralaye sacchabdoktaṃ brahmaivāsīt svātantryeṇeti śeṣaḥ/ tatsat 'ekamevādvitīyaṃ'; svagatasvāvayavabhedābhedaśūnyaṃ sarvottamam / prajāḥ 'sanmūlāḥ'; sadbrahmaiva mūlaṃ yāsāṃ tāstathoktāḥ / 'tadā'; suptau satā sampanno bhavati supta iti siddhānte śrutyarthaḥ / brahmalakṣaṇābhidhāyakānekavākyasaṅgrahakādiśabdaprayogena siddhānte 'pyatra pradhānasya pratipādyatvābhyupagamenāniṣṭābhāvādadhikaraṇavaiyarthyamiti śaṅkā nirastā bhavati / atra prakaraṇe śrutānāṃ brahmalakṣaṇānāṃ pradhāne 'sambhavena brahmaṇo 'pi pratipādyatvena pradhānamātrasya pratipādyatvānabhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.4.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the passage beginning with '<s>sadeva</s>' (Being alone), which comprises multiple sections, is coordinated. He cites the subject-passage indicating the <s>śruti</s>-connection and suggests the subject matter and the rest — beginning with '<s>sat</s>.' 'By what follows' — by the <s>Chāndogya</s> statement. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), statements such as 'One only without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1), 'That created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3), 'All these [beings], O dear one, have <s>Sat</s> as their root' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.6), and 'O dear one, then [in deep sleep] one is merged with <s>Sat</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1) are included. Since '<s>tat ca</s>' (and that) follows, '<s>tat</s>' is drawn from it. And thus, by 'what follows,' '<s>tat</s>' — the '<s>sraṣṭṛtvam</s>' (creatorship) stated by birth-generation — means being a cause independent of anything else. This is indicative: the supremacy over all, the being the substratum of all, and the being knowable through deep sleep are also '<s>ucyate</s>' — taught — this is the construction. By this, since the causal status stated in the <s>Janmādhikaraṇa</s> was objected to as belonging to <s>Pradhāna</s> rather than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the connection of this [adhikaraṇa] through objection is stated. Likewise, the subject-passage and the subject called <s>Sat</s> are stated. '<s>Sadeva</s>' is the statement of <s>Uddālaka</s>. O '<s>Somya</s>' (dear one) — O <s>Śvetaketu</s>, worthy of <s>Soma</s> by virtue of devotion and knowledge — '<s>idam</s>' — this universe — '<s>agre</s>' — before its creation, in the state of dissolution — was <s>Brahman</s> alone, denoted by the word <s>Sat</s>, independently — this is to be supplied. That <s>Sat</s> is 'one only without a second' — devoid of internal differentiation (<s>svagata</s>), differentiation among parts (<s>svāvayava</s>), and difference-and-identity — supreme over all. The beings 'have <s>Sat</s> as their root' — <s>Brahman</s> denoted by <s>Sat</s> alone is their root — thus they are so described. '<s>Tadā</s>' — in deep sleep, one is merged with <s>Sat</s> — is asleep: this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> in the <s>siddhānta</s>. By using the word '<s>ādi</s>' which gathers multiple statements declaring the characteristics of <s>Brahman</s>, since it is conceded that even in the <s>siddhānta</s> <s>Pradhāna</s> is taught here, the objection of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> being purposeless is refuted — because although the characteristics of <s>Brahman</s> heard in this section are impossible for <s>Pradhāna</s>, and <s>Brahman</s> too is taught as a subject, the mere teaching of <s>Pradhāna</s> alone is not accepted.

children.text: tacca sat 'bahu syāṃ prajāyeya'; (chāṃ. 6-2-3.) iti pariṇāmapratīterna viṣṇuḥ /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Sat</s>, because of the cognition of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) in 'Let me become many, let me be born' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3), is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.4.2:
sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣayati - tacceti // ca śabdaḥ pradhānamiti padākarṣako 'vadhāraṇe ca / tadityāvṛttaṃ vipariṇamyate / tathā ca 'tat'; chāndogye śrutaṃ satpradhānameva bhavet, na tu viṣṇuḥ / kutaḥ ? 'tasya'; sato 'bahu syām'; ityuttaravākyena bahubhāvākhyapariṇāmasya vikārasya pratīteriti yojanā / 'prajāyeya'; prajanayeyaṃ jagatsṛjāni/ tadarthaṃ 'bahu syām'; niyāmakabahurūpī bhaveyamiti / 'bahu syām'; tadarthaṃ prajāyeyeti vā śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.4.2:
He presents the prima facie view with reasoning — beginning with '<s>tat ca</s>' (and that). The particle '<s>ca</s>' draws in the word '<s>pradhānam</s>' (primordial matter) and also has the force of emphasis. '<s>Tat</s>' is repeated and is transformed [in meaning]. And thus '<s>tat</s>' — that <s>Sat</s> heard in the <s>Chāndogya</s> — is <s>Pradhāna</s> alone, not <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Why? Because of the cognition of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) — i.e., modification — called becoming many, through the subsequent statement 'Let me become many' — this is the construction. '<s>Prajāyeya</s>' — let me bring forth, let me create the world. For that purpose, '<s>bahu syām</s>' — let me become many-formed as the controller. Or, the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is: '<s>bahu syām</s>' — for that purpose — '<s>prajāyeya</s>' — let me be born.

children.text:
sa hi 'avikārassadā śuddho nitya ātmā sadā hariḥ';
ityādināvikāra prasiddha iti /
children.translated_text: For He is well-known as unchanging (<s>avikāra</s>) through [the passage] 'Unchanging, ever pure, eternal is the Self, ever is <s>Hari</s>' and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.4.3:
vikāritvapratītāvapi kuto 'yaṃ na viṣṇurityata āha - sa hīti // 'hi'; yasmāt 'saḥ'; viṣṇuḥ 'avikāraḥ sadā'; ityādipramāṇairavikāraḥ 'prasiddhaḥ'; tattvena niścitastasmāt tadasambhavāt pradhāne ca tatsambhavāt atra ca vikārapratīteḥ tatsat na viṣṇuḥ, kintu pradhānameveti yojanā / śrutau dvitīyasya sadāśabdasya sadāvikāra ityanvayaḥ / ādyasya tu sadā 'śuddho'; nirmala iti /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.4.3: Even when modification (<s>vikāritva</s>) is apprehended, [the opponent asks] why this is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> — to this he says 'sa hi' (for He). 'Hi' means 'because'; 'saḥ' means <s>Viṣṇu</s>; 'avikāraḥ sadā' — He is unchanging, established as immutable (<s>avikāra</s>) by such authoritative texts, ascertained in truth. Therefore, since that [immutability] is impossible [for the entity described here], and since such [modification] is possible for <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), and since modification is apprehended here, that <s>Sat</s> (Being) is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> but rather <s>Pradhāna</s> alone — this is the [opponent's] interpretation. In the <s>śruti</s>, the second word 'sadā' construes as 'sadā avikāraḥ' (always unchanging). But the first 'sadā' [means] 'śuddhaḥ' (pure), i.e., untainted.
Therefore he states — <s>sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
<s>Īkṣatikarmavyapadeśāt saḥ</s> — He [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the designation of [Him as] the object/agent of seeing (<s>īkṣati</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.13 |
Because of the designation [in the <s>śruti</s>] 'tadaikṣata' (It saw/willed) as the object/agent of seeing (<s>īkṣati</s>), it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone who is spoken of here.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.4.4:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // sūtroktaṃ vyapadeśaṃ darśayati - taditir / ikṣatīti dhātunirdeśena tadarthekṣaṇakriyā lakṣyater / ikṣatikarmeti sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ tatkartṛtvaparam / tathā ca 'tadaikṣata'; iti śrutāvīkṣaṇākhyavyāpāre kartṛtvokterityarthaḥ/ yadvā karmaśabdena sṛṣṭyādikriyocyate / tathātve vaiyadhikaraṇyarm / ikṣatipūrvakasṛṣṭyādivyapadeśādityarthaḥ / samanvayasūtrāttadityasya anuṣaṅgasambhave 'pi 'eko nārāyaṇa āsītsamunirbhūtvā'; () ityādisamākhyāmapi pramāṇīkartuṃ sa ityuktam / tadanūdya viṣṇuriti vyākhyātam / viṣṇurevetyanvayaḥ / eveti tu śabdārthaḥ / anena samanvayasūtrāttuśabdamātramanuvartanīyamiti sūcitam / sūtre samanvetavyānukterāha - atreti / 'sadeva'; ityādisthāna ityarthaḥ / sacchabdeneti pradhānamiti sādhyavākyārthaḥ / anena atra sadevetyādisthāne sacchabdenocyamānaḥ sa viṣṇureva, na pradhānam / kutarḥ ? 'ikṣatikarmavyapadeśāt saḥ'; tataḥ 'tadaikṣata'; itīkṣaṇākhyakriyākartṛtvaśravaṇādīkṣitṛtvasṛṣṭyādikriyayorvā śravaṇājjaḍaprakṛtau ca tadasambhavāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / sūtre sacchabdeneti śeṣaṃ vinā sa ityasyāvṛttiḥ, tatraikasya pratīkagrahaṇārthatvamiti pakṣer ikṣatikarmavyapadeśāt 'saḥ'; 'so 'kāmayata'; (tai. 2-6.) ityādiprakaraṇapratipādyaḥ sa viṣṇureva bhavet, na pradhānamitayartho 'vaseyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.4.4: He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the <s>siddhānta</s> (settled conclusion) and explains it — with 'ataḥ' (therefore). He shows the designation stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — with 'tad' etc. By the citation of the verbal root '<s>īkṣati</s>' (to see), the action of seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) in that sense is indicated. The co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) in '<s>īkṣatikarma</s>' pertains to the agenthood thereof. Thus, in the <s>śruti</s> statement 'tadaikṣata' (It saw), the meaning is that agenthood in the activity called seeing is stated. Alternatively, by the word 'karma' (action), the activity of creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) etc. is meant; in that case there is a different grammatical relation (<s>vaiyadhikaraṇya</s>) — the meaning being: because of the designation of creation etc. preceded by seeing. Although the word 'tat' (that) could carry over from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s>, the word 'saḥ' (He) is used [in this <s>sūtra</s>] in order to also validate such authoritative statements as '<s>Eko Nārāyaṇa</s> āsīt' (Only <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> existed). Restating that, he explains it as <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The syntactical connection is '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' The word 'eva' (alone) is the meaning of the particle. By this it is indicated that only the particle 'tu' carries over from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s>. Since the <s>sūtra</s> does not mention what is to be harmonized, he says 'atra' (here) — meaning in the passage beginning with 'sadeva' (Being alone). 'By the word sat' — the meaning of the proposition to be established is <s>Pradhāna</s>. By this [the following <s>sūtra</s> meaning is conveyed]: the one referred to by the word <s>Sat</s> in the passage 'sadeva' etc. is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not <s>Pradhāna</s>. Why? Because of '<s>īkṣatikarmavyapadeśāt saḥ</s>' — from hearing the agenthood in the activity called seeing in 'tadaikṣata,' or from hearing [both] the capacity to see and the activity of creation etc., and because these are impossible for insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> (matter) — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. In the <s>sūtra</s>, the repetition of 'saḥ' without the remainder 'by the word sat' is because one of them serves the purpose of quoting the <s>pratīka</s> (citation-word). According to the view [that it reads] '<s>īkṣatikarmavyapadeśāt saḥ</s>' — with ['so 'kāmayata' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6)] etc. — the one taught in that context is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not <s>Pradhāna</s>; thus the meaning should be understood.

children.text:
'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā'; (bṛ. 5-7-23.) 'nānyadato 'sti
draṣṭṛ'; (bṛ. 5-8-11.) ityādinā tasyaiva hi tallakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'There is no other seer than Him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.7.23), 'There is no other seer than Him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.11) — by such [statements], that characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) belongs to Him alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.4.5:
nanvīkṣaṇakartṛtvaṃ viṣṇuvatpradhānasya kiṃ na syādityataścetanasyāpi iha hetutvenābhimataṃ mukhyekṣaṇaṃ na sambhavati, kimu jaḍasyetyāśayena tatra pramāṇamāha - neti // 'ato'; brahmaṇaḥ sakāśāt 'anyaḥ'; svātantryeṇa draṣṭā draṣṭṛ ca nāstīti vājasaneyaprakaraṇadvayagatavākyadvayasyārthaḥ / ādiśabdenaivaṃjātīyakaṃ vākyaṃ gṛhyate / 'tasya'; viṣṇoreva / hi śabdaḥ prasiddhau / svātantryeṇekṣaṇakartṛtvalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgaṃ uktamiti śeṣaḥ / asya tasmānna liṅgasya anyagāmitvaṃ mantavyamityupaskṛtavākyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.4.5: [Objection:] Why could the agenthood of seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) not belong to <s>Pradhāna</s> just as it does to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this, with the intention that even for a sentient being (<s>cetana</s>) accepted here as the cause, primary seeing in the literal sense is not possible — how much less for an insentient entity (<s>jaḍa</s>) — he cites the authority for that: 'na' etc. 'Ataḥ' means 'from <s>Brahman</s>'; 'anyaḥ' means 'independently'; the meaning of the two statements from two passages of the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension] is that there is no seer or seeing capacity independent [of <s>Brahman</s>]. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), statements of similar purport are included. 'Tasya' means 'of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' The word 'hi' indicates [something] well-established. The remainder is: the characteristic mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of agenthood in seeing with independence has been stated. Therefore, this mark should not be regarded as applicable to any other — this is the syntactical connection with the supplied [completion of the] sentence.
And the multiplicity [of forms] is stated as being without any modification (<s>vikāra</s>): 'Unborn, He is born in manifold ways' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.13.1).
Thus ends the <s>Sad-adhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of <s>Sat</s>, Being). 4.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.4.6:
nanu viṣṇoravikāritayā siddhatvena tatra bahubhāvākhyavikārānvayāyogānniravakāśavikāritvaliṅgenātrekṣatirgauṇo vyākhyeyaḥ / 'sattvātsañjāyate jñānam'; iti smaraṇāt jñānopādānatayā siddhe pradhāne tatkartṛtvāsambhavena tatra tasyāmukhyatvādityata āha - bahutvaṃ ceti // castvarthaḥ / 'avikāreṇa'; vikāritvaṃ vinaiva svarūpabahutvenaivetyarthaḥ/ ityādinoktamityanvayaḥ/ tathā ca bahutvasya sāvakāśatvāt na tadbalenar ikṣatergauṇatvaṃ kalpanīyamiti bhāvaḥ/ yadvā - 'bahutvaṃ'; 'bahu syām'; iti bahubhāvavacanaṃ ca 'uktaṃ'; vyākhyātam / tathā ca ityevamādipramāṇavākyena 'bahu syām'; iti bahubhāvavacanam 'avikāreṇa'; vikāraṃ vinaiva niyāmakasvarūpabahutvenaiva mukhyapratipādyenaiva yuktamityuktam iti yojanā / tathā ca - siddhānte 'bahu syām'; ityasya tattanniyāmakasvarūpabahubhāvasaṅkalpor'tha ityuktaṃ bhavati / na caivaṃ niyāmakasvarūpabahubhāvasaṅkalpānantaraṃ niyamyasṛṣṭirayukteti vācyam / gurutvarājatvādeḥ śiṣyabhṛtyasāpekṣatvena tatsaṅkalpānantaraṃ śiṣyādisampādanavat niyāmakatāyā niyamyasāpekṣatvena niyāmakabahubhāvasaṅkalpānantaraṃ tatsāpekṣaniyamyasṛṣṭeryuktatvāt 'ajāyamānaḥ'; avikurvāṇaḥ iti śrutyarthastu dyubhvādinaye 'bhihitaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: <s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.4.6: [Objection:] Since <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s immutability is well-established, the modification called becoming-many (<s>bahubhāva</s>) cannot apply to Him. Therefore, by the force of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of modification which has no other scope, the seeing (<s>īkṣati</s>) here should be explained as secondary (figurative). Because [it is argued that] from the <s>smṛti</s> statement 'From <s>sattva</s> arises knowledge,' <s>Pradhāna</s> is established as the material cause of knowledge, and agenthood [of seeing] being impossible for it, [seeing] would be non-literal for it too — to this he responds: 'bahutvaṃ ca' (and the multiplicity). 'Ca' has the sense of 'tu' (but). 'Avikāreṇa' — without modification, meaning by the multiplicity of His own essential forms (<s>svarūpa-bahutva</s>) alone — this is the meaning. The syntactical connection is: 'stated by such [texts] beginning with' etc. And thus, since the multiplicity [of forms] has [independent] scope, one should not, by force of that, construe the seeing (<s>īkṣati</s>) as figurative — this is the purport. Alternatively: the 'multiplicity' and the statement of becoming-many 'bahu syām' (may I become many) are 'explained.' And thus, by such authoritative scriptural statements, the statement 'bahu syām' (may I become many) is 'avikāreṇa' — without modification, to be literally understood as referring to the multiplicity of His own controlling forms (<s>niyāmaka-svarūpa-bahutva</s>) alone — this is the interpretation. And thus, in the <s>siddhānta</s> (established view), the meaning of 'bahu syām' is stated to be the will to [manifest] the multiplicity of His own controlling forms. Nor can it be objected that creation of the controlled (<s>niyamya</s>) would be unreasonable after the will for multiplicity of controlling forms, because just as teacher-hood and king-ship etc. are dependent on students and subjects respectively, and after willing those, one produces students etc., similarly, since the controlling capacity (<s>niyāmakatā</s>) is dependent on the controlled, creation of the controlled which depends on [that capacity] is reasonable after the will for multiplicity of controlling forms. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> 'ajāyamānaḥ' (unborn) as 'avikurvāṇaḥ' (not undergoing modification) has been explained in the <s>Dyubhvādi-naya</s> (the method concerning heaven, earth, etc.). 4.
Thus ends the <s>Sad-adhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of <s>Sat</s>, Being). 4.
5. <s>Dahara-adhikaraṇa</s> (The Topic of the Small [Space]).

children.text:
candrādityādyādhāratvaṃ viṣṇoruktam / tacca 'atha yadidamasmin
brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminnantara ākāśaḥ ..... kiṃ
tadatra vidyate .....'; (chāṃ. 8-1-2.)
'ubhe asmin dyāvāpṛthivī antareva samāhite ubhāvagniśca vāyuśca
sūryācandramasāvubhau vidyunnakṣatrāṇi'; (chāṃ 8-1-3.)
ityādinā'kāśasya pratīyate /
children.translated_text: The status of being the support (<s>ādhāratva</s>) of the moon, sun, and other [luminaries] has been stated of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. And that is apprehended of the [inner] space (<s>ākāśa</s>) [described] in [the passage]: 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s> there is a small lotus-dwelling; within it is a small space... what is there within it...' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.2), 'In it are contained both heaven and earth, both fire and wind, both sun and moon, lightning and stars' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.3), and so forth.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.1:
atrādhikaraṇe sarvādhāratayānveṣṭavyatayā ca sākṣādvā vyavadhānena vā sāmānyato hṛtpadmasthatvaliṅgasya brahmaṇi samanvayaḥ kriyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayavākyamudāhṛtya viṣayādikaṃ ca sūcayan sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣayati - candreti // 'etasya vā akṣarasya'; (bṛ. 5-8-9.) ityādineti vartate / ādipadena dyāvāpṛthivyādikaṃ gṛhyate / tataḥ kimityata āha - tacceti // tadityāvartate / caḥ samuccaye 'vadhāraṇe ca / tathā ca 'tatra'; chandogaśrutau yadakṣaranayodāhṛtavākyoktaṃ candrādityādhāratvaṃ tadeva tathā tatsamānādhikaraṇaṃ hṛtpadmasthatvaṃ ca ākāśasya 'atha'; ityādinā vākyena pratīyata iti yojanā /
yadyapi bṛhadbhāṣye akṣaranayodāhṛtabṛhadāraṇyakaśrutigatasūryacandrapadayorbrahmarudraparatayā vyākṛtatvādevamanuvādo 'nupapannaḥ / tathāpi tayoḥ prasiddhacandrasūryaparatvasyāpyanumatatvādevamuktiḥ / yadvā - atra bhāṣye 'pi candrādityapade rudrabrahmapare / ata eva tattvapradīpe akṣaranaye 'ahaṃ somam'; (ṛ. 10-125-2.) iti vacane somaśabdo rudraparatayā vyākṛtaḥ / tathā ca na ko 'pi virodhaḥ / anenākṣaranayoktacandrādityādyādhāratvasya sākṣāt hṛtpadmasthākāśaniṣṭhatākṣepāttena asyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / evaṃ sarvādhāratvānveṣṭavyatvasamānādhikaraṇaḥ sākṣādvyavadhānena vā sāmānyato hṛtpadmasthatvarūpo viṣayaśca darśitaḥ / na caivaṃ 'candrāditya'; iti bhāṣyeṇa sa candrādityādyādhāraḥ kiṃ daharākāśaḥ syāt? āhosvittatsthaḥ kaścit? iti tattvapradīpena ca virodha iti vācyam / tayorakṣarādhikaraṇākṣepeṇa atra pūrvapakṣa iti darśayituṃ pravṛttatvena viṣayapradarśanāyāpravṛttatvāt / 'ākāśasya'; ityanena prasiddhabhūtākāśasyaiva sarvādhāratayā sākṣāt hṛtpadmasthatvamiti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ pradarśitaḥ / tathā praśnaprativacanapūrvakaṃ sākṣādākāśasyaivātra sarvādhāratayā hṛtpadmasthatvakathanāditi pūrvapakṣayuktiśca pradarśitā bhavati / atra yadyapi 'atha yadidamasmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ tasmin yadantastadanveṣṭavyaṃ tadvāva vijijñāsitavyamiti / taṃ cadbrūyuḥ...... kiṃ tadatra vidyate yadanveṣṭavyaṃ yadvā va vijijñāsitavyamiti / sa brūyādyāvānvāyamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ / ubhe asmin dyāvāpṛthivī antareva samāhite / ubhāvagniśca vāyuśca sūryācandramasāvubhau / vidyunnakṣatrāṇi'; ityādisamagravākyamudāhartavyam, na tu vicchidya / tathāpi samānajātīyaśrutyantaropasaṅgrahāyaivamudāhṛtamiti dhyeyam / śrutāvathaśabdaḥ prameyāntarārambhārthaḥ / 'brahmapuram'; ityetat brahmaṇaḥ puraṃ nivāsasthānamiti brahmaiva pūrṇatvātpuramiti ca dvedhā vyākhyeyam / 'antarhṛdaye'; iti saptamyantam / 'ākāśaḥ'; iti prathamāntam / tathā ca etasmin brahmapure śarīre yatpuraṃ brahmāsti 'asmin'; tasminbrahmaṇi 'daharaṃ'; dabhramalpaṃ 'puṇḍarīkam'; abjaṃ 'veśma'; tasya sadmarūpamasti asmin 'antardaharaḥ'; alpo bhūtākāśo 'sti / kiṃ cātaḥ? 'tasmin'; ākāśe 'ntaryadvartate 'tadanveṣṭavyaṃ'; jñātavyaṃ mārgitavyaṃ vā / nanu na ghaṭādivadanveṣaṇaṃ yuktam, apratyakṣatvādityatastadeva vivṛṇoti - tadvāveti // vāvetyavadhāraṇe / tathā ca tadeva 'vijijñāsitavyaṃ'; vicāritavyam / iti guruṇokte 'taṃ'; guruṃ prati 'cet'; yadi śiṣyāḥ 'brūyuḥ'; pṛccheyuḥ / kimiti? 'atra'; bhūtākāśe yadanveṣṭavyaṃ yadvāva vijījñāsitavyamityuktaṃ 'tat'; ādheyasvarūpaṃ 'kiṃ'; kiṃmahimaṃ ceti / na ca brahmapure brahmaṇo veśmetyuktyaivākāśasya brahmatvaniścayātpraśnāyoga iti vācyam / anyapure 'pyanyasya veśmasambhavādanyaveśmanyapyanyasyāvasthānasambhavāttadukteraniścāyakatvāt / evaṃ śiṣyaiḥ pṛṣṭe 'saḥ'; gururbrūyāt /
kimiti? hṛdo 'ntaḥ antarhṛt tasminnayate 'stīti vyutpattyā 'antarhṛdaye'; tacchabdabodhye hṛtpadmagatabhūtākāśe dyāvāpṛthivyādyāśrayaḥ 'ākāśaḥ'; tadākhyaḥ paramātmāstīti / nanvaṇau tasmin kathaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyādyavasthitirityatastasya vyāptatvamāha - yāvāniti // 'ayaṃ'; bahiḥsthitaḥ 'ākāśaḥ'; tadākhyo bhagavān guṇataḥ parimāṇataśca yāvān eṣa āntaro 'pi tāvāneva / tathā cāṇāvapi rūper iśaśaktyā mahattvasyāpi sattvādvyāptasya tasyānekādhāratvaṃ yujyata eveti bhāvaḥ /
anyaparityāgenāsyaiva jijñāsyatve ko heturityato 'sya sarvādhāratvākhyaṃ mahimānamāha - ubha ityādinā // asminnantare ye ubhe muktāmukte dyāvāpṛthivyau devyau 'samāhite'; samavasthite / evamubhayavidhau agniśca vāyuścetyetau devau samāśritau / tathā ubhau muktāmuktau sūryācandramasau vidyut nakṣatrāṇi ca samāśritānīti chāndogyabhāṣyarītyā śrutyarthaḥ / nyāyavivaraṇe tadvivaraṇarūpaṭīkāyāṃ - 'tasmin yadantaḥ'; ityatra hṛtpadmasthākāśagataṃ brahmānveṣṭavyamityuktam / na ca padmasthasya brahmatvāsiddhiḥ / śarīrapuṇḍarīkayorbrahma prati puratvaveśmatvoktyaiva anveṣṭavyasya brahmatvasiddheḥ / tathā ca padme brahmāstītyukte 'pi tadbrahma kiṃ prakāramiti bhāvena punaḥ 'kiṃ tadatra vidyate'; iti pṛṣṭe tatprakārajñāpanāya 'yāvān'; ityādyāha guruḥ / anena ca yadbrahmānveṣṭavyatayoktaṃ tadbrahmāntarhṛdaye yāvāneṣa prasiddhākāśastāvān sarvo 'pyākāśo vartate / tasmiṃścākāśe pṛthivyādikaṃ sarvaṃ samāśritam / apahatapāpmatvādiguṇakaṃ ca tadityevamākāśādisarvāśriyatvādapahatapāpmatvādiprakāra ukto bhavatīti prakārāntareṇa vyākhyātam / pūrvapakṣī tu - 'hṛdaya ākāśe'; iti padaṃ saptamyantaṃ kṛtvā daharākāśastho vyāptākāśo 'nveṣṭavya iti vā ākāśaḥ iti prathamāntaṃ kṛtvā prāguktadaharabhūtākāśamanūdya yāvānityanena bāhyākāśatulyatayā taṃ viśiṣya jijñāsyatvena tatra dyāvāpṛthivyādikamucyata ityāha /
children.translated_text:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topical section), the correlation of the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of being situated in the heart-lotus with <s>Brahman</s> is established — either directly or indirectly — by virtue of [<s>Brahman</s>] being the substratum of all and being that which is to be sought, through general reasoning. Having cited the subject-passage while indicating the <s>śruti</s> (scriptural) connection and the subject matter etc., he states the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) with reasoning — beginning with 'the moon' etc. The word 'of this imperishable' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.9) etc. is to be supplied. By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), heaven, earth and so forth are understood. To the question 'what follows from that?', he says — 'that, and' etc. The word 'that' is carried over. The particle 'ca' serves for both conjunction and emphasis. And thus, in the <s>Chāndogya</s> scripture, that very substratum-hood of the moon, sun, etc. which was stated in the passage cited through the <s>Akṣara</s> method (<s>akṣaranaya</s>), and likewise the being-situated-in-the-heart-lotus which shares the same grammatical co-referentiality (<s>samānādhikaraṇya</s>) with it — these are understood through the passage beginning with 'now' etc. This is the construal.
Although in the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> (the larger commentary), since the words 'sun' and 'moon' in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> scripture cited through the <s>Akṣara</s> method have been explained as referring to <s>Brahma</s> (the creator god) and <s>Rudra</s>, such a restatement would be inappropriate; nevertheless, since their reference to the well-known moon and sun is also accepted, such a statement is made. Alternatively, in this <s>Bhāṣya</s> too, the words 'moon' and 'sun' refer to <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>. For this very reason, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, in the <s>Akṣara</s> method, in the statement 'I am <s>Soma</s>' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.125.2), the word <s>Soma</s> is explained as referring to <s>Rudra</s>. And thus there is no contradiction whatsoever. By this, since the substratum-hood of the moon, sun, etc. stated in the <s>Akṣara</s> method directly implies the being-situated-in-the-<s>dahara</s>-space-of-the-heart-lotus, the suggestive connection (<s>ākṣepikī saṅgati</s>) with that is stated. Thus the subject — namely the being-situated-in-the-heart-lotus which shares co-referentiality with being the substratum of all and being that which is to be sought, either directly or through intermediation, in a general way — has been shown. And one should not say there is a contradiction between the <s>Bhāṣya</s>'s statement 'moon, sun' etc. — meaning 'Is this substratum of moon, sun, etc. the <s>dahara ākāśa</s> (small space) itself? Or is it some entity residing in it?' — and the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, because both have undertaken to show that this is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) through the implication of the <s>Akṣara-adhikaraṇa</s>, and have not undertaken merely to display the subject matter. By the phrase 'of space' (<s>ākāśasya</s>), the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is shown: that it is the well-known elemental space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>) itself that, as substratum of all, is directly situated in the heart-lotus. And the reasoning of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> is also shown: that since the scripture directly states the being-situated-in-the-heart-lotus of space itself as the substratum of all, preceded by question and answer. Here, although the entire passage should be cited without breaking it up — 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmapura</s>) there is a small lotus-dwelling (<s>puṇḍarīka veśma</s>); within it is a small space (<s>dahara ākāśa</s>). That which is within it — that is to be sought, that indeed is to be investigated. If they should say to him... what is there that is to be sought, or what indeed is to be investigated? — he should say: As vast as this space is, so vast is this space within the heart. Both heaven and earth are contained within it; both fire and wind, both sun and moon, lightning and stars' etc. — nevertheless, it should be understood that it is cited in this manner for the purpose of incorporating other scriptures of the same class. The word 'now' (<s>atha</s>) that is heard serves to introduce a new topic. The term '<s>brahmapura</s>' (city of <s>Brahman</s>) should be explained in two ways: as the city, i.e., the dwelling-place of <s>Brahman</s>; and as <s>Brahman</s> itself being the city on account of its fullness. 'Within the heart' is a locative ending. '<s>Ākāśa</s>' (space) is a nominative ending. And thus: in this <s>brahmapura</s>, the body, which is a city, there exists <s>Brahman</s>; 'in it' — in that <s>Brahman</s> — there is a 'small' (<s>dahara</s>, meaning minute, little) 'lotus' (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>, meaning a water-born flower), a 'dwelling' (<s>veśma</s>), having the form of an abode; within it there is a 'small interior' (<s>antardahara</s>) — a minute elemental space. What then? 'In that' space, whatever exists within — 'that is to be sought' — to be known or to be searched for. Now, one might object that searching like for a pot etc. is not appropriate since it is imperceptible — therefore he elaborates that very point: '<s>tadvāva</s>' etc. The particle <s>vāva</s> is for emphasis. And thus, that very thing 'is to be investigated' (<s>vijijñāsitavya</s>), to be deliberated upon. When the teacher has said this, 'him' — towards the teacher — 'if' (<s>cet</s>) the students 'should say' — should ask — what? 'Here' — in this elemental space — 'that which is to be sought, or that which is indeed to be investigated' — as was said — 'that' — the nature of the content — 'what' — of what greatness is it? And one should not say that there is no occasion for the question because the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of the space is already established by the statement that it is a dwelling of <s>Brahman</s> in the city of <s>Brahman</s> — because in another's city, another's dwelling is also possible, and in another's dwelling, another's residence is also possible, so that statement is not conclusive. When thus asked by the students, 'he' — the teacher — would say:
What would he say? 'Within the heart' (<s>antarhṛdaya</s>) — etymologically derived as 'that in which it goes within the heart' — in the elemental space located in the heart-lotus, which is denoted by that word, there exists '<s>ākāśa</s>' — the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) designated by that name, who is the substratum of heaven, earth, etc. Now, if that [space] is minute, how can heaven, earth, etc. be situated in it? To this he states its all-pervasiveness: 'as vast as' etc. 'This' external '<s>ākāśa</s>' — the Lord designated by that name — as vast as He is in qualities and magnitude, this interior one too is exactly that vast. And thus, even in a minute form, by the power of the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), since greatness also exists, it is entirely fitting that the all-pervading one is the substratum of many things — this is the purport.
As to what is the reason for this alone being that which is to be investigated, to the exclusion of others — he states its greatness consisting in being the substratum of all: beginning with 'both' etc. In this interior, the 'two' — the liberated and unliberated — 'heaven and earth,' the two goddesses, are 'contained' — established. Similarly, both types of <s>Agni</s> (fire) and <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) — these two deities — are dependent [on it]. Likewise, both the liberated and unliberated <s>Sūrya</s> (sun) and <s>Candramā</s> (moon), lightning and stars are all dependent [on it] — this is the meaning of the <s>Chāndogya</s> scripture according to the <s>Bhāṣya</s>'s method. In the <s>Nyāyavivaraṇa</s>, the sub-commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>) that is an exposition of that commentary — regarding 'that which is within it': it is stated that the <s>Brahman</s> situated in the space of the heart-lotus is to be sought. And the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of what is situated in the lotus is not unestablished, because the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of what is to be sought is established by the very statement of the body and the lotus being a city and a dwelling for <s>Brahman</s>. And thus, even when it is said that <s>Brahman</s> exists in the lotus, with the intention of asking 'of what nature is that <s>Brahman</s>?' — when the question 'what exists there?' is asked again — the teacher says 'as vast as' etc. to convey that nature. And by this, the <s>Brahman</s> that was stated as to-be-sought exists in the interior of the heart as the entire space, as vast as this well-known space; and in that space, earth and all else is dependent; and it possesses qualities such as freedom from evil (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) etc. — thus the nature is stated through being the substratum of space and all else, and through the mode of freedom from evil etc. — this is explained in another manner. But the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector) says: by making the phrase 'in the space of the heart' a locative ending, the all-pervading space situated in the <s>dahara ākāśa</s> is to be sought; or, by making '<s>ākāśa</s>' a nominative ending and restating the aforementioned small elemental space, qualifying it by 'as vast as' as being equal to the external space, and declaring it to be that which is to be investigated — heaven, earth, etc. are predicated of it.

children.text:
sa cākāśo na viṣṇuḥ / 'tasyānte suṣiraṃ sūkṣmaṃ tasmin
sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam'; (mahānā. 11.) iti śruteriti /
children.translated_text: And that space is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Because of the <s>śruti</s> (scripture): 'At its end there is a minute opening; in that, everything is established' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 11) — thus [argues the objector].
<s>Madhva</s>'s <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5.2:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.2:
nanvastvākāśasya sarvādhāratayā hṛtpadmasthatvaṃ tasya cākāśasya 'ākāśastalliṅgāt'; iti nyāyena viṣṇutvena viṣṇoreva hṛtpadmasthvaṃ sidhyatītyata āha - sa ceti // castvarthaḥ, pratijñāsamuccaye vā / tathā ca yassarvādāratayā hṛtpadmasthatvena ca śrutyuktaḥ 'sa cākāśo na viṣṇuḥ'; bhūtameva na tu viṣṇurityarthaḥ / kuto vā na viṣṇurityata āha - tasyānta iti / sa cetyanuṣaktaścaśabdo 'tra buddhyā viviktasuṣirapadenānvīyate 'vadhāraṇe ca ayam / śrutisamānoktyupalakṣakaṃ caitat / tathā ca 'tasyānte'; iti vākye 'suṣirapadaśruteḥ'; suṣiraśabdaśravaṇāt suṣirasya chidrātmakaprasiddhākāśasyaiva śruteḥ sarvādhāratayā hṛtpadmasthatvokteḥ tatsamākhyānādityarthaḥ / 'tasya'; 'padmakośapratīkāśaṃ hṛdayaṃ cāpyadhomukham'; iti pūrvavākye prakṛtasya hṛtpadmakośasya 'ante'; antare tanmadhye sūkṣmaṃ 'suṣiraṃ'; chidramasti, tasmin 'sarvaṃ'; jagatpratiṣṭhitamiti taittirīyaśrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, even if the being-situated-in-the-heart-lotus belongs to space by virtue of its being the substratum of all, and that space, by the principle '<s>ākāśas tal-liṅgāt</s>' (it is space, because of the indicatory marks of that), is established as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so that it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone who is situated in the heart-lotus — anticipating this objection, he says: 'And that' etc. The particle 'ca' is in the sense of 'but' (<s>tu</s>), or for conjunction with the thesis. And thus, he who is spoken of in scripture as being situated in the heart-lotus by virtue of being the substratum of all — 'that space is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — it is merely elemental [space], not <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the meaning. Or why is it not <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he says: 'at its end' etc. The particle 'ca' carried over from 'and that' (<s>sa ca</s>) is here intellectually connected with the word '<s>suṣira</s>' (opening) and serves for emphasis as well. And this is indicative of a statement similar to the scripture. Thus, in the passage 'at its end,' 'because of the hearing of the word <s>suṣira</s> (opening)' — because the word <s>suṣira</s> is heard — since the scripture speaks only of the well-known space whose nature is an opening (<s>chidra</s>), and since the being-situated-in-the-heart-lotus is stated as that of the substratum of all, and since it is described as such — this is the meaning. 'Of that' — of the heart-lotus-calyx which was the subject in the preceding passage, 'The heart is like a lotus-bud, facing downward' — 'at the end,' in its interior, in its middle, there is a minute '<s>suṣira</s>' (opening), a hole; in that, 'everything' — the entire world — is established. This is the meaning of the <s>Taittirīya</s> scripture.

Therefore he says —
<s>Sūtra</s>: Oṃ.
<s>Madhva</s>'s <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5.3:
The small [space refers to <s>Brahman</s>], because of the subsequent [descriptions]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.14 |

children.text:
'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyurviśoko 'vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmassatyasaṅkalpaḥ so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ
sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ'; (chāṃ 8-7-3.) ityādibhya uttarebhyo guṇebhyo dahare viṣṇureva /
children.translated_text: 'He who is the Self, free from evil, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, whose desires are true, whose resolves are true — He is to be sought, He is to be investigated' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.7.3) — because of such subsequent qualities, in the small [space] (<s>dahara</s>), it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone [who is referred to].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.3:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // 'ityādibhyaḥ'; ityādirūpebhyaḥ 'uttarebhyaḥ'; viṣayavākyānantarabhāvibhyaḥ 'śabdebhyaḥ uktebhyaḥ'; iti śeṣaḥ / ityādyuttaravākyebhya iti paryavasitārthaḥ / yadvā 'guṇebhyo'; guṇavacanebhya ityarthaḥ / hetvasiddhiparihārāya śrutyudāharaṇam / ādipadena 'viśoko 'vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṅkalpaḥ so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ'; ityādikaṃ gṛhyate / guṇebhyaḥ ityanenottarapadamuttaratraśrutānekaśabdavācyaguṇopalakṣakamityuktaṃ bhavati / 'dahare'; hṛtpadmagatālpākāśe ityanena sūtre 'dahare'; iti saptapyantaṃ padaṃ, na paramata iva prathamāntamityuktaṃ bhavati / sthito 'nveṣṭavyatayokta iti śeṣaḥ / samanvayasūtrādanuvṛttasya vidheyaparasya tattvityasyārtho viṣṇoreveti / anena - 'yaḥ'; iti daharavākyāduttaravākye śrutebhyo guṇebhyo 'dahare'; vijijñāsyatayoktaḥ 'tattu'; viṣṇureva na bhūtākāśādiriti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / yo hṛtpadmākāśagataḥ paramātmā 'na vadhenāsya hanyate'; (chāṃ. 8-1-5.) iti prāk śarīrasya nāśenāvadhyatvenoktaḥ saḥ 'apahatapāpmā'; nityameva svato 'pahatapāpmā pāpātyantābhāvavāniti yāvat / ata eva na tatkāryaṃ jarādikamasyetyucyate - vijara ityādinā / 'avijighatsaḥ'; bubhukṣārahitaḥ / 'apipāsaḥ'; pānecchārahita iti / 'bubhukṣādinā pīḍābhāva ucyate'; iti jñānapādīyaṭīkokternādanapānecchābhāvobhi'dhīyate, pramāṇabādhitatvāt / kintu tatpīḍābhāvaḥ / atra hetuḥ - satyakāma iti / tasya yadiṣṭaṃ tatsvataḥ eva bhavediti satyakāmaḥ / tatrāpi hetuḥ - 'satyasaṅkalpaḥ'; apratihatasaṅkalpa iti/ ya evaṃ bhūtaḥ so 'nveṣṭavya iti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He introduces the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>sūtra</s> and explains it — 'Therefore' etc. 'Such as these etc.' — from those of such and similar form; 'subsequent' — occurring after the subject-passage; 'from words stated' — this is to be supplied. The settled meaning is: from the subsequent passages beginning with 'etc.' Alternatively, 'from the qualities' (<s>guṇebhyaḥ</s>) means 'from the statements of qualities' — this is the meaning. The citation of scripture is for removing the objection of the unestablished reason (<s>hetvasiddhi</s>). By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the following is understood: 'free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, whose desires are true, whose resolves are true — He is to be sought, He is to be investigated' and so forth. By the word 'from the qualities' (<s>guṇebhyaḥ</s>), it is stated that the subsequent word is indicative of the many qualities expressed by the multiple words heard later [in the text]. By 'in the small [space]' (<s>dahare</s>) — meaning 'in the small space located in the heart-lotus' — it is stated that the word '<s>dahare</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> is a locative ending, not a nominative ending as the opponent holds. The implied completion is: [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] who abides [there] is stated as that which is to be sought. The meaning of '<s>tat tu</s>' (but that), which continues from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s> and refers to the predicate, is '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.' By this, the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated as follows: from the qualities heard in the passages subsequent to the <s>dahara</s>-passage beginning with 'He who,' that which is stated as to-be-investigated 'in the small space' (<s>dahare</s>) is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not elemental space or anything else. The <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) situated in the space of the heart-lotus, who was previously stated as indestructible — 'He is not slain by the slaying of this [body]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5) — being spoken of as not being destroyed by the destruction of the body, He is '<s>apahatapāpmā</s>' (free from evil) — eternally, by His own nature, free from evil, meaning one in whom evil is absolutely absent. Therefore, since the effects of evil such as old age etc. do not belong to Him, it is said — 'free from old age' (<s>vijara</s>) and so forth. '<s>Avijighatsa</s>' means free from hunger. '<s>Apipāsa</s>' means free from desire to drink. Since the sub-commentary on the <s>Jñānapādīya</s> states 'the absence of affliction from hunger etc. is being stated,' what is meant is not the absence of desire for eating and drinking, since that would be contradicted by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), but rather the absence of affliction from them. Here the reason is — '<s>satyakāma</s>' (one whose desires are true): whatever He desires, that comes about of its own accord — thus He is one whose desires are true. The reason for that too is — '<s>satyasaṅkalpa</s>' (one whose resolves are true) — one whose resolve is unobstructed. He who is of such nature — He is to be sought — this is the meaning of the scripture.

children.text:
'yo 'śanāyāpipāse śokaṃ mohaṃ jarāṃ mṛtyumatyeti'; (bṛ. 5-5)
'sa eṣa sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhya uditaḥ'; (chāṃ. 1-6-7.) ityādinā viṣṇoreva hi te guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who transcends hunger and thirst, grief, delusion, old age, and death' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5); 'This one has risen above all sins' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.7) — by such [passages], for those qualities belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.
<s>Madhva</s>'s <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5.4:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.4:
apahatapāpmatvādikaṃ kathaṃ viṣṇutvaniścāyakaṃ, tadgatatvenāsiddhatvādityata āha - ya iti // bṛhadāraṇyakaśrutiriyam / 'aśanāyā'; aśanecchā / 'pipāsā'; pānecchā / te 'atyeti'; atikramya vartate / yaśca 'śokaṃ'; duḥkhaṃ 'mohaṃ'; mūrchāṃ 'jarāṃ'; maraṇaṃ cāpyetītyarthaḥ / atratyasya yacchabdasya 'tamātmānaṃ viditvā'; iti tacchrutisthatacchabdenānvayaḥ / 'sa eṣaḥ'; iti chandogaśrutiḥ / 'sa eṣaḥ'; paramātmā 'pāpmabhyaḥ'; pāpebhyaḥ 'uditaḥ'; nityaṃ svata evodgataḥ pāparahita ityarthaḥ / 'ityādinā'; vākyena ādiśabdena satyakāmatvādiguṇāntarabodhakavākyāni gṛhyante / hi śabdo yata ityarthe / te apahatapāpmatvādirūpottaravākyoktāḥ siddhā iti śeṣaḥ / tasmānna teṣāṃ viṣṇuliṅgatvaniścayaḥ iti vākyaśeṣeṇāsyānvayaḥ / anyatra pāpādyabhāvasya kathañcidyoge 'pi sarvathā satyakāmatvādikaṃ na yujyata iti jñāpanāyādiśabdabahuvacanayoḥ prayogaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 4:
How is the quality of being free from sin (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and the like a determiner of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood, since [the objection is that] it is unestablished as belonging to Him? — to this he says: 'ya' (he who). // This is a <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> <s>Śruti</s>. '<s>Aśanāyā</s>' — the desire to eat. '<s>Pipāsā</s>' — the desire to drink. Those He '<s>atyeti</s>' — He transcends, surpasses. And He who [transcends] '<s>śokam</s>' — sorrow; '<s>moham</s>' — delusion; '<s>jarām</s>' — old age; and death as well — this is the meaning. The relative pronoun 'yat' occurring here has its correlative connection through the pronoun 'tat' in the <s>Śruti</s> 'having known that Self.' '<s>Sa eṣaḥ</s>' — this is a <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>Śruti</s>. '<s>Sa eṣaḥ</s>' — this <s>Paramātman</s>; '<s>pāpmabhyaḥ</s>' — from sins; '<s>uditaḥ</s>' — eternally risen above from His very nature, meaning free from sin. 'By such [passages]' (<s>ityādinā</s>) — by the sentence; by the word '<s>ādi</s>,' sentences conveying other qualities such as having true desires (<s>satyakāmatva</s>) and the like are included. The word '<s>hi</s>' is in the sense of 'because.' 'Those' — [qualities] stated in the subsequent sentences in the form of freedom from sin and the like — 'are established': this is the remainder. 'Therefore there is no certainty of their being marks of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — this connects with the sentence-remainder. The use of the word '<s>ādi</s>' and the plural is for indicating that even if the absence of sin and the like is somehow possible elsewhere, having true desires (<s>satyakāmatva</s>) and the like are never possible [in others] under any circumstance.
<s>Hari</s> alone, by His own nature, has eternally transcended hunger and the like;
Others transcend hunger and the like by His grace alone. — Thus in the <s>Padma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]. //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5, verse 5:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.5:
tathāpi naite guṇā viṣṇoreva, ramādiṣvapi sambhavādityata āha - nityeti // 'svataḥ'; anyānapekṣayā nityaṃ tīrṇā aśanāyādayo yena sa harireka eva, nānyo 'sti / hareranye ramābrahmādayastu 'aśanāyādikān'; aśanapānecchāśokādidoṣān 'tatprasādāt'; tasya hareranugrahādeva 'taranti'; atiyanti, na svata ityarthaḥ / hi śabdaḥ prasiddhau / 'pādme'; uktamiti śeṣaḥ / ato nirapekṣaguṇānāmanyatrābhāvāt viṣṇorevetyuktamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 5:
Even so, these qualities do not belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, since they are possible in <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) and others as well — to this he says: '<s>nitya</s>' (eternally). // 'By His own nature' (<s>svataḥ</s>) — independently of others — He by whom hunger and the like are eternally transcended — that <s>Hari</s> is 'one alone' (<s>eka eva</s>), and there is no other. Others — <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the rest — who are different from <s>Hari</s>, 'transcend' (<s>taranti</s>) — surpass — 'hunger and the like' (<s>aśanāyādikān</s>) — the faults of desire to eat, desire to drink, sorrow, and the like — 'by His grace' (<s>tatprasādāt</s>) — by the grace of that <s>Hari</s> alone, not by their own nature: that is the meaning. The word '<s>hi</s>' is for well-known [fact]. 'In the <s>Padma</s>' — '[it is] stated': this is the remainder. Therefore, because of the absence of independently-possessed qualities in others, it is said '[these qualities belong to] <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone': this is the purport.
And between a dependent and an independent [quality], the independent one is to be accepted [as the mark].
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5, verse 6:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.6:
nanu ramādiṣvapahatapāpmatvādīnāmanyānadhīnānāmabhāve 'pi yathā kathañcitsattvādanyagataistaiḥ kathaṃ viṣṇutvaniścaya ityata āha - sāpekṣeti // 'sāpekṣam'; anyādhīnaṃ 'nirapekṣam'; anyānadhīnaṃ tayormadhye ityarthaḥ / co 'vadhāraṇe, nirapekṣameveti sambadhyate / apahatapāpmatvādikamiti viśeṣyaṃ prakṛtatvāllabhyate / 'svīkartavyaṃ'; liṅgatveneti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca vivakṣitaliṅgasyānyatrābhāvāttena viṣṇutvaniścayo bhavatyeveti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 6:
Objection: Even if in <s>Ramā</s> and others, the freedom from sin (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and the like that are independent of others are absent, still, since they exist in some fashion [in others], how can there be certainty of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood through [qualities] that are also found in others? — to this he says: '<s>sāpekṣa</s>' (dependent). // 'Dependent' (<s>sāpekṣam</s>) — dependent on another; 'independent' (<s>nirapekṣam</s>) — not dependent on another; between the two: that is the meaning. The word 'ca' is for restriction — it connects as: 'the independent one alone.' The qualified term — freedom from sin and the like — is understood from the context. 'Is to be accepted' (<s>svīkartavyam</s>) — 'as a mark': this is the remainder. And thus, because of the absence of the intended mark in others, the certainty of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood through it is indeed established: this is the purport.
There is no one higher than that imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s> who has true desires (<s>satyakāma</s>);
The 'true-desiredness' (<s>satyakāmatva</s>) of others would be a desire for what is desired by Him. — Thus in the <s>Skānda</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]. // 14 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5, verse 7:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.7:
kiṃ ca sāpekṣatvanirapekṣatvādiviśeṣitānāmapahatapāpmatvādīnāmabhāvarūpāṇāmanyatrākāśādau sākṣādvābhimānidvārā vā yathākathañcidvṛttāvapi na kathañcidanyatra satyakāmatvādyastīti yuktastena viṣṇutvaniścaya ityāha - satyakāma iti // 'avyayam'; akṣīṇakāmamamoghakāmaṃ satyakāmaṃ viṣṇum 'ṛte'; vinā 'paro 'nyaḥ'; viṣṇoranyaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṅkalpaśca nāsti / viṣṇau tadbhāvasya tadanyasmin tadabhāvasya ca pratipādanāya vakroktiḥ / viṣṇoranyeṣāṃ ramādīnāṃ kvacidāgame pratīyamānamapi satyakāmatvaṃ 'tatkāmyakāmitā'; viṣṇukāmanāviṣayaviṣayakakāmanāvattvarūpameva bhavenna mukhyamityarthaḥ / tathā cāpahatapāpmatvaṃ svataḥ parādhīnaṃ ceti yathā dvividhaṃ, na tathā satyakāmatvaṃ kiṃ tvekavidhaṃ, tacca mukhyaṃ viṣṇāveva, anyatra tu pāribhāṣikamiti bhāvaḥ / 'skānde'; uktamiti śeṣaḥ/ ataḥ satyakāmatvādivivakṣayā viṣṇoreva hi te guṇā ityuktaṃ yuktamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 7:
Moreover, even though the freedom from sin and the like, when distinguished as dependent or independent, as negative [attributes], may somehow occur elsewhere — in <s>Ākāśa</s> and the like, either directly or through the presiding deity — nevertheless, the [quality of] having true desires (<s>satyakāmatva</s>) and the like does not in any way exist elsewhere. Hence the certainty of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood through it is justified — to this he says: '<s>satyakāma</s>' (one of true desires). // '<s>Avyayam</s>' — of undiminished desires, of unfailing desires — the <s>Viṣṇu</s> who has true desires; 'except for' (<s>ṛte</s>) — without [Him]; 'another' (<s>paraḥ</s>) — [one] other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> who has true desires and true resolve — does not exist. The indirect expression is for conveying [both] the existence of that [quality] in <s>Viṣṇu</s> and its absence in others. Even though the <s>satyakāmatva</s> of <s>Ramā</s> and others that is sometimes perceived in certain scriptures — 'would be' (<s>bhavet</s>) — is only of the nature of 'desire for what is desired by <s>Viṣṇu</s>' (<s>tatkāmyakāmitā</s>) — i.e., desire whose object is the object of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s desire — not primary: that is the meaning. And thus, just as freedom from sin is of two kinds — inherent and dependent on another — <s>satyakāmatva</s> is not similarly [twofold]; rather, it is of one kind only, and that primary [kind] belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, while in others it is merely conventional: this is the purport. 'In the <s>Skānda</s>' — '[it is] stated': this is the remainder. Therefore, with the intended reference to <s>satyakāmatva</s> and the like, what was said — 'for those qualities belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone' — is justified: this is the purport.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //

children.text: gatiśabdābhyāṃ tathā hi dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ ca | BBs_1,3.15 |
children.translated_text: Because of movement (<s>gati</s>) and the word (<s>śabda</s>); for thus is the mark seen. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.15 |
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5, verse 8:]

children.text:
'aharahargacchantya etaṃ brahmalokaṃ na vindanti'; (chāṃ. 8-3-2.)
iti suptasya tadgatirbrahmaśabdaścocyate /
children.translated_text: 'Day after day they go to this <s>Brahmaloka</s> [and yet] do not find [it]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.2) — thus the movement of the sleeping person to that [Brahman] and the word '<s>Brahma</s>' are stated.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.8:
yuktyantareṇa viṣṇorhṛtpadmasthatvaṃ pratipādayatsūtramupanyasyāsiddhiparihārāya śrutyudāharaṇapūrvakaṃ vyācaṣṭe - gatīti // 'imāḥ'; suptāḥ prajāḥ 'aharahaḥ'; pratidinametaṃ 'gacchantyaḥ'; prāpyamāṇāḥ 'etaṃ'; brahmalokaṃ brahmaṇo viṣṇorāvāsasthānabhūtaṃ hṛtpadmaṃ taddvārā tatratyaṃ brahma sākṣāllokapadoktaṃ brahmākhyamāśrayaṃ vā 'na vindanti'; na vijānanti, sa eṣa ātmā hṛdīti śrutyarathaḥ / itīti / iti chandogavākye 'suptasya'; cetanasya 'tadgatiḥ'; aharaho hṛdgataṃ brahmalokaṃ prati gatiḥ prāptiḥ 'ucyate'; vyapadiśyata ityarthaḥ / 'brahmaśabdaḥ'; ityatrāpi taditi padaṃ buddhyā vivicya vipariṇāmena sambadhyate / tathā ca tasmin prāpyamāṇe hṛdgate brahmaloke 'brahmaśabdaḥ'; 'ucyate'; śrūyate ityarthaḥ / ucyate ca ityapi sambandhaḥ / caḥ samuccaye / yata iti śeṣaḥ / asyāto 'pi dahare viṣṇureveti pradhānasādhyenānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 8:
Presenting the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s abidance in the lotus of the heart by another reasoning, and reading the <s>Śruti</s> as a preliminary to resolving the objection of unestablishedness, he explains: '<s>gati</s>' (movement). // 'These' (<s>imāḥ</s>) — the sleeping creatures — 'day after day' (<s>aharahaḥ</s>) — every day — 'going' (<s>gacchantyaḥ</s>) — reaching — 'this' (<s>etam</s>) — <s>Brahmaloka</s>, the lotus of the heart which is the abode of <s>Brahman</s>, i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>; through it, the <s>Brahman</s> directly residing there, or the <s>Brahman</s>-named refuge spoken of by the word '<s>loka</s>' — 'do not find' (<s>na vindanti</s>) — do not know; the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is: 'This Self is in the heart.'
