The word 'iti' [indicates]: in this <s>Chāndogya</s> passage, 'of the sleeping one' (<s>suptasya</s>) — of the conscious being — 'the movement to that' (<s>tadgatiḥ</s>) — the going toward the <s>Brahmaloka</s> situated in the heart, day after day — 'is stated' (<s>ucyate</s>) — is declared: that is the meaning. 'The word <s>Brahma</s>' (<s>brahmaśabdaḥ</s>) — here too the word 'tat' is to be analytically separated and connected in reverse order. And thus, in that <s>Brahmaloka</s> situated in the heart that is being reached, 'the word <s>Brahma</s>' — 'is stated' (<s>ucyate</s>) — is heard: that is the meaning. The connection 'is stated also' is [also possible]; the word 'ca' is for accumulation. 'Because' (<s>yataḥ</s>) is the remainder. The connection of this with the principal thesis is: from this too, in the <s>Dahara</s> [space within the heart], it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
'satā somya tadā sampanno bhavati'; (chāṃ. 6-7-1.)
iti śrutestaṃ hi supto gacchati /
children.translated_text: 'At that time, O dear one, he becomes united with <s>Sat</s> (Being)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.7.1) — because according to this <s>Śruti</s>, the sleeping person goes to Him.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5, verse 9:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.9:
suptaprāpyatvaṃ kuto viṣṇutvaniścāyakamityata āha - sateti // he 'somya'; bhaktijñānārha śvetaketo 'tadā'; suptikāle 'satā'; brahmaṇā 'sampannaḥ'; saṅgato bhavatītyarthaḥ / uddālakavākyametat / śruteriti pañcamī / 'taṃ'; viṣṇum / hi śabdaḥ prasiddhau / 'gacchati'; prāpnoti / iti jñāyate iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca suptaprāpyatvasya viṣṇuliṅgatvena śrutiprasiddhatvāt tena viṣṇutvaniścayo bhavatīti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 9:
How does the approachability by the sleeping person determine <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood? — to this he says: '<s>satā</s>' (with Being). // O '<s>somya</s>' — O <s>Śvetaketu</s>, worthy of devotion and knowledge — 'at that time' (<s>tadā</s>) — during the state of sleep — 'with <s>Sat</s>' (<s>satā</s>) — with <s>Brahman</s> — he 'becomes united' (<s>sampannaḥ</s>): that is the meaning. This is a statement of <s>Uddālaka</s>. 'From the <s>Śruti</s>' is an ablative [of source]. 'Him' (<s>tam</s>) — <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The word '<s>hi</s>' is for well-known [fact]. '[He] goes to' (<s>gacchati</s>) — reaches. 'Thus it is known': this is the remainder. And thus, because the approachability by the sleeping person is well-known through <s>Śruti</s> as a mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the certainty of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood through it is established: this is the purport.

children.text: 'araśca ha vai ṇyaścārṇavau brahmaloke'; (chāṃ 8-5-3.) iti liṅgaṃ ca tathā dṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ara</s> and <s>Ṇya</s> are the two oceans in <s>Brahmaloka</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.5.3) — and thus the mark is seen.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5, verse 10:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.10:
'liṅgaṃ ca tathā hi dṛṣṭam'; iti sūtraśeṣaṃ hetvantaraparatayā vyācaṣṭe - araśceti // ca śabdo hetusamuccaye / yathā suptagamyatvam 'aharahaḥ'; iti śrutau hṛtpadmasthe dṛṣṭam, tathā araṇyanāmāmṛtasamudradvayāśrayalokavattvarūpaṃ liṅgamapi 'araśca'; iti śrutau hṛtpadmasthe dṛṣṭaṃ śrutamiti / upamāyāṃ tathāśabdaḥ / anenāsiddhiḥ parihṛtā / na ca gatiśabdayorivāsya sannidhau hṛtpadmasthasyānukterasiddhyanivṛttiriti vācyam / hṛtpadmasthasya brahmaṇa āvāsatvena nimittena tallokabhūte hṛtpadme 'etaṃ brahmalokam'; iti prayuktasya brahmalokaśabdasyāṇyāśrayaloke 'pi prayogāttanmukhena tādṛśalokavattvarūpaliṅgasya hṛtpadmasthabrahmaniṣṭhatāyā prāptatvāt / dṛṣṭamityanantaraṃ yata iti śeṣaḥ/ asyāto 'pi dahare viṣṇureveti pratijñāvākyenānvayaḥ / śrutau havā iti nipātau prasiddhidyotakau / samudrayoranyonyasamuccaye ca śabdau / tathā ca brahmaṇo viṣṇorloke śvetadvīpe araṇyākhyārṇavau sudhāsamudrau arṇavopame sudhāsarasī vā sta iti śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 10:
He explains the remainder of the <s>sūtra</s> — 'the mark is seen thus' — as conveying another reason: '<s>ara</s> and [<s>ṇya</s>].' // The word 'ca' is for accumulation of reasons. Just as the approachability by the sleeping person — in the <s>Śruti</s> 'day after day' — is seen as belonging to the one situated in the lotus of the heart, so too the mark in the form of being the abode of two nectar-oceans named <s>Araṇya</s> is also 'seen' — heard — in the <s>Śruti</s> '<s>ara</s> and [<s>ṇya</s>]' as belonging to the one situated in the lotus of the heart. The word '<s>tathā</s>' is for comparison. By this, the objection of unestablishedness is resolved. Nor should it be said that because of the absence of explicit mention of the heart-lotus dweller in its proximity — unlike [the case of] movement and the word [<s>Brahma</s>] — the unestablishedness is not resolved. For because the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' — which was used in 'this <s>Brahmaloka</s>' with reference to the heart-lotus as being the abode of <s>Brahman</s> — is also used for the <s>Araṇya</s>-abode realm, through that instrumentality the mark in the form of possessing such a realm is established as belonging to the <s>Brahman</s> situated in the heart-lotus. After 'seen' (<s>dṛṣṭam</s>), 'because' (<s>yataḥ</s>) is the remainder. The connection with the thesis-statement is: from this too, in the <s>Dahara</s> [space], it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. The particles '<s>ha</s>' and '<s>vai</s>' in the <s>Śruti</s> indicate well-known [fact]. The two 'ca' words are for the mutual accumulation of the two oceans. And thus, in the realm of <s>Brahman</s>, i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, there are two nectar-oceans called <s>Araṇya</s>, or two nectar-lakes resembling oceans: this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>.

children.text: araśca vaiṇyaśca sudhāsamudrau tatraiva sarvābhimatapradau dvau /
children.translated_text: <s>Ara</s> and <s>Vaiṇya</s> are the two nectar-oceans there, bestowing all that is desired.
By such [passages], it is said that these very characteristics belong to Him alone. // 15 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.5, verse 11:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.11:
nanu hṛtpadmasthasyāraṇyāśrayalokavattvaliṅgaśravaṇe 'pi kuto 'yaṃ viṣṇurityato 'raṇyāśrayatvasya viṣṇulokaikaliṅgatvena smṛtisiddhatvādityāśayena sautrahiśabdābhipretāṃ smṛtiṃ darśayati - araśceti // vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / caśabdau parasparasamuccaye / 'tatraiva'; kṣīrābdhimadhyasthitaviṣṇuloka eva 'sarvābhimatapradau'; sarveṣṭakarau sta ityarthaḥ / evakāro 'nyatra sattvavyāvartakaḥ / tenāraṇyāśrayalokavattvaliṅgasya viṣṇutvenāvyabhicāraḥ siddhyati / ata eva bhāṣye tasyaivetyevakāraḥ / 'ityādinā'; puruṣottamadhyānacakravākyena 'tasyaiva'; viṣṇoreva 'tat'; sudhārṇavadvayāśrayalokavattvaṃ 'lakṣaṇatvena'; liṅgatvena 'ucyate'; pratipādyate ityarthaḥ / 'hi'; yasmādityarthe / tasmādetalliṅgabalāt viṣṇutvaniśrayo yukta iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / yadvā - brahmalokamiti hṛtpadmasya viṣṇulokatvokteḥ tadantargato viṣṇurityuktaṃ, brahmalokapadaṃ kuto viṣṇulokavācītyata āha - araśceti / brahmalokapadasya viṣṇuloke 'araśca'; iti vākye prayogādatra hṛtpadme prayuktam 'etaṃ brahmalokam'; iti padamapi viṣṇulokaparameva / na ca 'araśca'; iti śrutāvapi brahmalokapadaṃ kuto viṣṇulokaparamiti vācyam / yatastatrāraṇyāśrayatvaliṅgaṃ śrutamityarthaḥ / athāpyaraṇyāśrayatvasya bhagavallokaliṅgatvaṃ kuta ityata āha - araśceti // asmin pakṣe sautraṃ liṅgapadaṃ hṛtpadmasthasya brahmatvarūpapradānasādhye hetutvābhāvātsūtre liṅgaśabdena pṛthaguktiḥ / pūrvavyākhyāne 'pi gatiśabdayorivāsya liṅgasya viṣṇuniṣṭhatāyā upapādanasāpekṣatvena spaṣṭatvābhāvādgatiśabdaliṅgairityanuktvā liṅgaṃ ceti pṛthaguktiryuktā / anena - na kevalamuttarebhyo guṇebhyaḥ, kintu gatiśabdābhyāṃ ca 'aharahaḥ'; iti vākye hṛtpadmasthaniṣṭhatayā śrutābhyāṃ suptaprāpyabrahmaśabdābhyāṃ ca dahare viṣṇureveti jñāyate / na kevalametābhyāmeva, kintu yataḥ 'araśca'; iti śrutau 'tathā'; gatiśabdayoriva 'hi'; viṣṇuliṅgatvena smṛtisiddhamaraṇyāśrayalokavattvarūpaṃ liṅgaṃ hṛtpadmasthe viṣṇuloke prayuktabrahmalokapadasya hṛtpadme prayogāt 'dṛṣṭaṃ'; śrutamato 'pi dahare viṣṇureva / yadvā - kuto 'tra prayuktasya brahmalokapadasya viṣṇulokaparatvam? 'araśca'; iti vākye viṣṇuloke brahmalokapadaprayogāt / atrāpi 'etaṃ brahmalokam'; iti tasyaiva prayogāt / na ca tatrāpi viṣṇulokaparatvaṃ kutaḥ? yato 'raṇyāśrayatvaṃ liṅgaṃ 'dṛṣṭaṃ'; śrutamata iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.5.11:
Now, even when the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of possessing a world that is a forest-dwelling (<s>araṇyāśraya</s>) is heard regarding the one situated in the lotus of the heart, why should this be <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this, the intention is that because the quality of being a forest-dwelling is established through <s>smṛti</s> as an exclusive indicatory mark of the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he shows the <s>smṛti</s> intended by the word '<s>hi</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> — beginning with '<s>araśca</s>.' The word '<s>vai</s>' is used in the sense of well-known. The two '<s>ca</s>' words are for mutual conjunction. 'There itself' — in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> situated in the middle of the ocean of milk itself — 'the two givers of all desires' — the meaning is that the two are the fulfillers of all wishes. The word '<s>eva</s>' excludes existence elsewhere. By this, the invariable concomitance (<s>avyabhicāra</s>) of the indicatory mark of possessing a forest-dwelling world with being <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established. Hence the word '<s>eva</s>' in '<s>tasyaiva</s>' (of Him alone) in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. 'By such statements as' — by the passage on the meditation on <s>Puruṣottama</s> — 'of Him alone' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — 'that' — the quality of possessing a world resting on two oceans of nectar — 'as a characteristic' — as an indicatory mark — 'is stated' — is established, this is the meaning. '<s>Hi</s>' — in the sense of 'because.' Therefore the remainder of the sentence is: it is proper to conclude it is <s>Viṣṇu</s> based on the strength of this indicatory mark. Alternatively — since it is said that the lotus of the heart is the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> by the expression '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' (world of <s>Brahman</s>), and <s>Viṣṇu</s> is contained within it, the question arises: why does the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' denote the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To this he says — beginning with '<s>araśca</s>.' Because the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' is used in the passage '<s>araśca</s>' in reference to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the expression '<s>etaṃ brahmalokam</s>' (this world of <s>Brahman</s>) used here in reference to the lotus of the heart also refers exclusively to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. And one should not object that even in the <s>śruti</s> passage '<s>araśca</s>' the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' cannot refer to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, because there the indicatory mark of forest-dwelling is heard — this is the meaning. If it is asked whence the quality of being a forest-dwelling is an indicatory mark of the Lord's world, to that he says — beginning with '<s>araśca</s>.' In this interpretation, the word '<s>liṅga</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> is mentioned separately because there is no causal relation for establishing the nature of <s>Brahman</s> of the one situated in the lotus of the heart. Even in the previous interpretation, the separate mention 'and the indicatory mark' rather than saying 'by <s>gati</s>, <s>śabda</s>, and <s>liṅga</s>' together is proper, because this indicatory mark, like <s>gati</s> and <s>śabda</s>, requires demonstration of its pertaining to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and is not self-evident. By this — not only from the subsequent qualities, but also from <s>gati</s> and <s>śabda</s> heard as pertaining to the one situated in the lotus of the heart in the passage '<s>aharahaḥ</s>' (day by day), and from the words '<s>supta</s>' (sleeping) and '<s>prāpya</s>' (attaining) and '<s>Brahma</s>' — it is known that in the <s>dahara</s> (small space) is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Not only from these alone, but also because in the <s>śruti</s> '<s>araśca</s>' — just as with <s>gati</s> and <s>śabda</s> — '<s>hi</s>' — the indicatory mark in the form of possessing a forest-dwelling world, established through <s>smṛti</s> as a mark of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is 'seen' — heard in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> expressed by the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' used for the lotus of the heart — therefore also in the <s>dahara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Alternatively — why does the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' used here refer to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Because of the use of the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' in the passage '<s>araśca</s>' in reference to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Here too there is the same usage in '<s>etaṃ brahmalokam</s>.' And whence is it the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> there too? Because the indicatory mark of forest-dwelling is 'seen' — heard — there. Thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
Because of sustaining (<s>dhṛti</s>), and because this greatness (<s>mahiman</s>) is perceived in this [context] | <s>BS</s> 1,3.16 |
Because of the sustaining (<s>dhṛti</s>) [mentioned] in 'This is the bridge, the upholder (<s>vidhṛti</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.1),

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.12:
hetvantareṇa viṣṇorhṛtpadmasthatvaṃ pratipādayatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - dhṛteriti // 'iti dhṛteḥ'; ityasya 'asminnasya'; iti padānuvartanenetyasminvākye 'sya hṛtpadmasthasya dhṛtipadoktasarvādhāratvaśruterityarthaḥ / asya dahare viṣṇureveti pratijñāvākyenānvayaḥ / śrutau vidhṛtiḥ seturityanvayaḥ / tatra vidhṛtirityetatsetutve hetuḥ / tathā ca ya ātmā hṛtpadmasthatvenoktaḥ sa eṣa 'eṣāṃ'; bhūrādilokānām 'asambhedāya'; asāṅkaryāya avidāraṇāyeti, vyāsatīrthīyoktarītyā varṇāśramasāṅkaryābhāvāyeti vā 'vidhṛtiḥ'; dhāraṇapoṣaṇasamartho 'ta eva seturiva 'setuḥ'; āśraya ityarthaḥ / dhārakatvaṃ ca na dhāryādbahiṣṭhatayā, kintvantaḥkṛtajagattvena, 'śritamasmin jagatsarvamiti seturitīritaḥ'; ityukteḥ mukhyārtha eva vā setuśabdaḥ / yadyapi 'sa seturvidhṛtiḥ'; iti chandogaśrutipāṭhaḥ / tathāpi śākhāntarāṇāmapyatropasaṅgrahāyaivamuktiḥ / evamanyatrāpīti sampradāyavidaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.5.12:
Presenting the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s residence in the lotus of the heart through another reason, he explains — beginning with '<s>dhṛteḥ</s>.' The continuation of the words '<s>asmin asya</s>' (in this, of this) with '<s>iti dhṛteḥ</s>' (because of sustaining) means: because of the <s>śruti</s> declaring the quality of being the support of all, as stated by the word '<s>dhṛti</s>' (sustaining), regarding this one situated in the lotus of the heart — this is the meaning. Its syntactic connection is with the thesis statement that in the <s>dahara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. In the <s>śruti</s>, the syntactic connection is '<s>vidhṛtiḥ</s>' (upholder) and '<s>setuḥ</s>' (bridge). There, '<s>vidhṛti</s>' is the reason for being a '<s>setu</s>' (bridge). And thus, this Self who is described as situated in the lotus of the heart — He is '<s>vidhṛtiḥ</s>' — capable of sustaining and nourishing — 'these' <s>Bhūḥ</s> and other worlds — 'for non-confusion' — for preventing intermixture, for non-destruction — or, according to the method stated by <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>, for the absence of intermixture of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> — and therefore, like a bridge, He is the '<s>setu</s>' — the support, this is the meaning. And the sustaining is not by standing outside what is sustained, but by having made the world internal to Himself, as stated in '<s>śritam asmin jagat sarvam iti setur itīritaḥ</s>' (the entire world rests in Him, hence He is called the bridge). Or the word '<s>setu</s>' is used in its primary sense. Although the reading in the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s> is '<s>sa seturvidhṛtiḥ</s>' (He is the bridge, the upholder), nevertheless, this expression is used to incorporate other <s>śākhās</s> (recensions) as well. The same applies in other cases too — so say the knowers of the tradition.
And because this greatness — 'He is the lord of beings, He is the protector of beings' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.21) and so on — is perceived in this [context].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.13:
evaṃ setusamuccāyakasautracaśabdasya yathāśrutānvayena liṅgoktiparatayā dhṛteścetyaṃśaṃ vyākhyāyedānīṃ samagraṃ sūtraṃ samānoktirūpasamākhyāparatayā vyācaṣṭe - eṣa iti // dhṛteritipadamatrānuṣajyate / asmin pakṣe sautracaśbada upalabdheścetyanveti / tathā ca na kevalaṃ dhṛterliṅgāt, kintu 'dhṛteḥ'; dhṛtiyuktāyāstadbodhikāyā upalabdheḥ vāsaneyake 'ya eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśastasmin śete sarvasya vaśī'; (bṛ. 6-4-21.) ityādyuktvā āmnātāyāḥ 'eṣa sarveśvara eṣa bhūtādhipatireṣa bhūtapāla eṣa seturvidharaṇa eṣāṃ lokānāmasambhedāya'; ityukteḥ samānokteśca dahare viṣṇureveti yojanā / samākhyāyāḥ kuto viṣṇuparatvamityata āha - eṣa iti / ityādīti luptatṛtīyāvibhaktiko nirdeśaḥ / ādiśabdena 'eṣa sarvasya vaśī eṣa sarvasyādhipatireṣa sarveśvaraḥ'; (bṛ. 6-4-21.) iti pūrvavākyam 'eṣa seturvidharaṇa eṣāṃ lokānāmasambhedāya'; ityuttaravākyaṃ ca gṛhyate / ata eva madhyasthavākyagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam / asya mahimna iti vyadhikaraṇaṣaṣṭhyau / upalabdherityāvṛttamatrānveti / tathā ca 'asmin'; vājasaneyake 'eṣa bhūtādhipatiḥ'; ityādinā vākyena 'asya'; viṣṇorbhūtādhipatitvādimahimnaḥ 'asmin'; daharākāśagate vastuni 'upalabdheḥ'; uktatvāditi yojanā / ya eṣa sarvasyādhipatiḥ, yaścaiṣa sarveśvaro, yaścaiṣa prasiddho 'bhūtādhipatiḥ'; bhūta evādhipatirnāsyādhipatyamādimat, yaścaiṣa bhūta eva pālako, yaśca 'eṣāṃ'; bhūrādilokānām 'asambhedāya'; amelanāya eṣāṃ 'vidharaṇaḥ'; vidhāraṇasamarthaḥ, na kevalaṃ sāmarthyamātraṃ, kintu ya eṣāṃ lokānāṃ 'setuḥ'; āśrayaśca, tametaṃ bhagavantaṃ brāhmaṇā vividiṣantīti śrutyarthaḥ / anena - na kevalaṃ pūrvoktahetubhyaḥ, kintu vidhṛteścāsmin prakaraṇe 'sa seturvidhṛtiḥ'; iti sarvādhāratvaliṅgaśravaṇādapi daharapadmastho viṣṇureva / na cāsya hṛtpadmasthatvaṃ kuta iti vācyam / 'asya'; hṛtpadmasthasya 'mahimnaḥ'; apahatapāpmatvāderlakṣaṇasya 'asmin'; sarvādhāre 'sarve pāpmāno 'to nivartante'; (chāṃ.8-4-1.) ityanena 'upalabdheḥ'; uktatvāt / na kevalaṃ dhṛterliṅgāt, kintu dhṛterdhṛtiyuktāyā upalabdherukteḥ / 'ya eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśastasmin śete .... eṣa seturvidharaṇaḥ'; iti vājasaneyasamākhyāyāśca dahare viṣṇureva / samākhyāyā api kuto viṣṇuviṣayatvam? 'asmin'; vājasaneyake 'asya'; viṣṇoḥ 'mahimno'; bhūtādhipatitvāderuktatvāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / yadyapi 'asya mahimnaḥ'; ityādyaṃśo bhāṣye dhṛteścetyasya liṅgaparatayā yojanāyāṃ nānvitaḥ / tathāpi ṭīkāyāṃ 'sarve pāpmāno 'taḥ'; iti tallakṣaṇokteścetyuktatvāt liṅgasya hṛtpadmasthatvarūpapakṣadharmopapādakatayāpi yojanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.5.13:
Having thus explained the portion '<s>dhṛteśca</s>' (and because of sustaining) with the word '<s>ca</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> as conjoining the bridge [reference], taking the '<s>liṅga</s>' (indicatory mark) aspect according to the literal reading, he now explains the entire <s>sūtra</s> as referring to a common statement (<s>samānokti</s>) — beginning with '<s>eṣa</s>.' The word '<s>dhṛteḥ</s>' is connected here. In this interpretation, the word '<s>ca</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> connects with '<s>upalabdheśca</s>' (and because of perception). And thus: not only because of the indicatory mark of sustaining, but 'because of sustaining' — because of the perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>) that involves sustaining and reveals it — in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>], after stating 'This space within the heart — in Him all this sleeps; He is the ruler of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.21) and so on, the statement 'He is the lord of all, He is the lord of beings, He is the protector of beings, He is the bridge, the upholder, for the non-confusion of these worlds' — because of that utterance, and because of the common statement (<s>samānokti</s>), in the <s>dahara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — this is the construal. Whence is the common statement about <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To that he says — beginning with '<s>eṣa</s>.' '<s>Ityādi</s>' (and so on) is a reference with an elided third-case ending. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the prior passage 'He is the ruler of all, He is the lord of all, He is the lord of everything' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.21) and the subsequent passage 'He is the bridge, the upholder, for the non-confusion of these worlds' are included. Hence the citation of the middle passage is made. '<s>Asya mahimnaḥ</s>' (of this greatness) has the two words in different case-relations (<s>vyadhikaraṇa-ṣaṣṭhī</s>). The repeated word '<s>upalabdheḥ</s>' connects here. And thus the construal is: 'in this' — in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] — through the passage 'He is the lord of beings' and so on — 'of this' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s — greatness such as lordship over beings — 'in this' — in the entity present in the <s>dahara-ākāśa</s> — 'because of perception' — because it is stated. That which is the lord of all, and which is the lord of everything, and which is the well-known 'lord of beings' — one whose lordship is eternal, not having a beginning — and which is eternally the protector, and which 'for the non-confusion' — for the non-merging — of these <s>Bhūḥ</s> and other worlds is the 'upholder' — capable of upholding — not merely possessing the capability, but which is the 'bridge' — the support — of these worlds: the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know that Lord — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. By this — not only from the previously stated reasons, but also because of sustaining (<s>vidhṛti</s>), and because in this context the indicatory mark of being the support of all is heard in '<s>sa seturvidhṛtiḥ</s>' (He is the bridge, the upholder), the one situated in the <s>dahara</s> lotus is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. And one should not object: whence is His residence in the lotus of the heart? Because 'of this' — of this one situated in the lotus of the heart — 'greatness' — the characteristic of being free from evil (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and the like — 'in this' — in the all-supporting one — 'is perceived' through the passage 'all evils turn away from this' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.1). Not only because of the indicatory mark of sustaining, but because of the perception that involves sustaining, and because of the common statement in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> — 'This space within the heart — in Him all this sleeps... He is the bridge, the upholder' — in the <s>dahara</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Whence is the common statement about <s>Viṣṇu</s>? 'In this' — in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] — because 'of this' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s — 'greatness' — lordship over beings and the like — is stated. Thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is explained. Although the portion '<s>asya mahimnaḥ</s>' (of this greatness) and so on was not construed in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>'s interpretation of '<s>dhṛteśca</s>' as referring to the indicatory mark, nevertheless, since in the sub-commentary (<s>Ṭīkā</s>) it was stated 'and because of the statement of that characteristic in <s>sarve pāpmāno 'taḥ</s>' (all evils from this), it should also be construed as the indicatory mark serving to establish the thesis-property of residence in the lotus of the heart.

'etasmin khalvakṣare gārgyākāśa otaśca'; (bṛ. 5-8-11.)
'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi'; (bṛ. 5-8-9.)
children.translated_text:
'In this imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), O <s>Gārgī</s>, space is woven' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.11),
'Under the command of this imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8.9),

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.14:
yaduktaṃ sarvādhāratvaliṅgaśravaṇāt hṛtpadmastho viṣṇuriti, tatra sarvādhāratvaṃ kuto viṣṇutvaniścāyakaṃ, tatsamānādhikaraṇatvenāsiddhatvādityata āha - etasminniti // 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane'; iti pratīkagrahaṇena 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ, etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi dyāvāpṛthivyau'; ityādibahuvākyāni sūcayati / imānyakṣaranaye vyākṛtāni /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.5.14:
What was said — that because of hearing the indicatory mark of being the support of all, the one situated in the lotus of the heart is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — to the objection that how does being the support of all determine that it is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since it is unestablished as being in the same substratum (<s>samānādhikaraṇya</s>) [with <s>Viṣṇu</s>] — to that he says, beginning with '<s>etasmin</s>.' By citing the indicative passage '<s>etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane</s>' (under the command of this imperishable), he indicates the many passages such as '<s>etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ</s>' (under the command of this imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon stand upheld) and '<s>etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi dyāvāpṛthivyau</s>' (under the command of this imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, heaven and earth...) and so on. These have been explained in the section on <s>Akṣara</s>.

children.text:
'sa hi sarvādhipatiḥ sa hi sarvapālaḥ sar iśaḥ sa
viṣṇuḥ'; 'patiṃ viśvasyātmeśvaram'; (mahānā. 11.) ityādiśrutibhyastasya hyeṣa mahimā /
children.translated_text: 'For He is the lord of all, He is the protector of all, the lord of everything, He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>'; 'The lord of the universe, the ruler of selves' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 11) — from such <s>śruti</s> passages, for this is His greatness.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.15:
nanu samākhyāśrutyuktaḥ sarveśvaratvādimahimā kuto viṣṇoravagata ityata āha - sa hīti // 'sa hi'; ityārabhya 'sa viṣṇuḥ'; ityantamekaṃ vākyaṃ śrutyantaragatam / 'saḥ'; prakṛtaḥ / 'hiḥ'; prasiddhau / 'patiṃ viśvasya'; iti nārāyaṇānuvākasthaṃ vākyam / 'viśvasya'; acetanaprapañcasya patiṃ 'ātmeśvaraṃ'; cetaneśvaraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tadviśvamupajīvatītyarthaḥ/ ityādīti / evamādiśrutivākyebhya ityarthaḥ / ādiśabdenaitajjātīyaṃ gṛhyate / tṛtīyārthe pañcamī/ 'tasya'; viṣṇoḥ 'hiḥ'; prasiddhau hetau vā / 'eṣa sarveśvaraḥ'; (bṛ.6-4-22.) ityādimahimā / avagata iti śeṣaḥ / tasmānnaiteṣāṃ viṣṇutvarūpasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyāsiddhiriti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.5.15:
Now, the question arises: whence is the greatness such as lordship over all, stated in the common statement (<s>samākhyā</s>) from the <s>śruti</s>, known to pertain to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To that he says — beginning with '<s>sa hi</s>.' From '<s>sa hi</s>' (for He) up to '<s>sa Viṣṇuḥ</s>' (He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>) is one sentence from another <s>śruti</s>. '<s>Saḥ</s>' (He) refers to the one under discussion. '<s>Hi</s>' is in the sense of well-known. '<s>Patiṃ viśvasya</s>' (the lord of the universe) is a passage found in the <s>Nārāyaṇānuvāka</s>. '<s>Viśvasya</s>' — of the entire non-sentient creation — the lord, '<s>ātmeśvaram</s>' — the ruler of sentient beings — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>: that entire universe depends on Him — this is the meaning. '<s>Ityādi</s>' — from such <s>śruti</s> passages — this is the meaning. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), passages of this type are included. The fifth case ending is used in the sense of the third (instrumental). '<s>Tasya</s>' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — '<s>hi</s>' — in the sense of well-known or as indicating a reason — this greatness, such as 'He is the lord of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.22) and so on, is known. 'Is known' is to be supplied. Therefore the remainder of the sentence is: hence there is no failure of the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of these [attributes] with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The lord of all is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; there is no other lord of the world.
Thus in the <s>Skānda</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]. 16.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.16:
nanu sarveśvaratvādikaṃ viṣṇuvadanyasyāpi kiṃ na syādityata āha - sarveśa iti // atra sarvajagacchabdau cetanācetanaprapañcaparau / yadvā - jagataḥ patiriti pratiyogitvenaivoktasyānuvādaḥ / athavā - 'patiḥ'; pālakaḥ / tathā ca sarveśvaraḥ sarvapālakaśca viṣṇureka eva nānyo 'stītyarthaḥ / iti skānda ityasya evakāroktapadādhyāhāreṇa tasyahyeṣa mahimeti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / tasmānnaitalliṅgānāmanyatra sāvakāśatvaṃ śaṅkyamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.5.16:
Now, might not the lordship over all and other such attributes belong to someone other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> as well? To that he says — beginning with '<s>sarveśa</s>.' Here the words '<s>sarva</s>' (all) and '<s>jagat</s>' (world) refer to the sentient and non-sentient creation. Alternatively — '<s>jagataḥ patiḥ</s>' (lord of the world) is a restatement of what was already stated as the counter-correlate. Or — '<s>patiḥ</s>' means protector. And thus the meaning is: the lord of all and the protector of all is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, there is no other. The words '<s>iti skānda</s>' (thus in the <s>Skānda</s>), by supplying the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) [from the verse], connect with the previous [<s>Bhāṣya</s> passage] '<s>tasya hy eṣa mahimā</s>' (for this is His greatness). Therefore the remainder of the sentence is: hence one should not suspect that these indicatory marks could apply elsewhere.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
And because of well-known usage (<s>prasiddhi</s>) | <s>BS</s> 1,3.17 |

children.text: 'tatrāpi daharaṃ gaganaṃ viśokastasmin yadantastadupāsitavyam'; (mahānā. 10-7.) iti prasiddheśca //
children.translated_text: And because of the well-known usage in 'There too is the small space (<s>dahara gagana</s>), free from sorrow; what is within it, that is to be meditated upon' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 10.7).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.17:
samākhyāntararūpayuktyantareṇa viṣṇorhṛtpadmagatākāśasthatvaṃ sādhayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - prasiddheśceti // itītyanantaraṃ śrutāviti śeṣaḥ / tasyetyanuvartate / 'tasya'; viṣṇoḥ 'tasya'; hṛtpadmasthasyeti tadarthaḥ / anena - sūtre 'syāsminnitipadadvayaṃ pūrvasūtrādanuvartanīyam / tathā ca na kevalaṃ vājasaneyasamākhyānāt, kintu 'asmin'; tatrāpīti taittirīyaśrutivākye 'asya'; hṛtpadmasthasya viṣṇutvaprasiddheśca tatsamākhyānādapi daharapadmastho viṣṇureveti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / 'divye brahmapure hyeṣa vyomnyātmā sampratiṣṭhitaḥ'; (muṃ. 2-2-7.) ityātharvaṇe prasiddheśca / 'ya eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśastasminnayaṃ puruṣaḥ'; (tai. 1-2-1.) iti taittirīyavākyāntare prasiddheśceti sūtrasya yadvṛttyantaraṃ ṭīkāyāṃ sūcitaṃ, tadbhāṣyasthetiśabdasyādyarthatvamāśrityeti draṣṭavyam / śrutau 'daharaṃ vipāpmaṃ paraveśmabhūtaṃ yatpuṇḍarīkaṃ puramadhyasaṃstham'; (mahānā. 10-7.) iti vākye yat 'daharam'; alpaṃ parasya brahmaṇaḥ sadmabhūtam, ata eva vigatapāpaṃ dehākhyabrahmapuramadhye saṃsthaṃ hṛdayakamalaṃ prakṛtaṃ tattatreti parāmṛśyate / tathā ca 'tatrāpi'; puṇḍarīke 'pi yat 'daharam'; alpaṃ gaganamasti tasmin 'antaḥ'; antare 'viśoko'; viśokaṃ viśokapadopalakṣitaṃ jarādiśūnyaṃ yadbrahma tadupāsitavyamityarthaḥ / viśokaḥ iti liṅgavyatyayaḥ chāndasaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - liṅgavyatyāsastasya puruṣatvajñāpanārthaḥ / 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyurviśokaḥ'; ityādāvuditaguṇānāmadhikaraṇaikyabalena sannidhīyamānānāmanukarṣaṇārthaśceti prayojanamuktam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.5.17:
Having cited the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s abiding in the space within the lotus of the heart (<s>hṛtpadma</s>) through another reasoning in the form of an additional designation (<s>samākhyā</s>), he explains it — beginning with '<s>prasiddheśca</s>' (and because of the well-known-ness). // After 'iti,' the word '<s>śrutau</s>' (in the <s>śruti</s>) is to be supplied. '<s>Tasya</s>' carries over [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>]. '<s>Tasya</s>' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; '<s>tasya</s>' — meaning: of Him who abides in the lotus of the heart. By this — in the <s>sūtra</s>, the two words '<s>asya</s>' and '<s>asmin</s>' are to be carried over from the previous <s>sūtra</s>. And thus, not only because of the <s>Vājasaneya</s> designation, but also because '<s>asmin</s>' — in the <s>Taittirīya śruti</s> passage beginning with '<s>tatrāpi</s>' — '<s>asya</s>' — of Him who abides in the lotus of the heart — the well-known-ness of His being <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and because of that designation too, the <s>sūtra</s> meaning is stated as: the one dwelling in the <s>dahara</s> lotus is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. And because of the well-known-ness in the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> [Upaniṣad]: 'In the divine city of <s>Brahman</s>, this Self is established in the space' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.7). And because of the well-known-ness in the other <s>Taittirīya</s> passage: 'This space within the heart — in that is this <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.2.1) — this alternative explanation of the <s>sūtra</s> indicated in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> should be understood as being based on taking the word 'iti' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> in its primary sense. In the <s>śruti</s>, the passage 'The small, sinless, abode of the Supreme — the lotus situated in the middle of the city [of the body]' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 10.7) — in that passage, the '<s>dahara</s>' (small) lotus of the heart, which is the abode of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> and therefore free from sin, situated in the middle of the city called the body — is referred to by '<s>tatra</s>' (there). And thus, '<s>tatrāpi</s>' — even in the lotus, whatever '<s>dahara</s>' (small) space there is, '<s>antaḥ</s>' — within it, '<s>viśoka</s>' — that <s>Brahman</s> which is free from sorrow and indicated by the word '<s>viśoka</s>,' devoid of old age and the like — that is to be meditated upon: this is the meaning. '<s>Viśokaḥ</s>' — the gender irregularity is Vedic (<s>chāndasa</s>). In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however — the gender irregularity is for the purpose of indicating His masculinity (<s>puruṣatva</s>). The purpose is stated as: for drawing in the attributes of sinlessness, agelessness, deathlessness, sorrowlessness, etc. mentioned in 'The Self free from evil, ageless, deathless, sorrowless' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5) and other passages, by the force of the unity of the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic).

Because of [the <s>śruti</s>] being made with reference to [<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s] abiding within that [lotus], there is no contradiction with the '<s>suṣira</s>-<s>śruti</s>' (the passage mentioning the opening). // 17 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.18:
nanu sākṣāt padmagatasya viṣṇutvābhyupagame suṣiraśrutivirodhaḥ / evaṃ padmagatākāśasyaiva viṣṇutvābhyupagame 'pi suṣiraśrutivirodhaḥ, suṣiraśabdasyākāśavācitvāt / etadvihāya daharapadmasyākāśatvaṃ, viṣṇostvākāśagatatvaṃ, tasyaiva sarvādhāratvamityupagame 'pi suṣiraśrutivirodhaḥ / tatra sākṣātsuṣirasya sarvādhāratvokterityata āha - tadantasstheti // buddhyā viviktasuṣiraśrutipadaṃ ṣaṣṭhyantamatrānvīyate / tathā ca 'suṣiraśruteḥ'; iti suṣirapadaghaṭitaśruteḥ 'tadantassthāpekṣatvāt'; padmagatasuṣirāntassthaparamātmānamapekṣya pravṛttatvāttasya ca sarvādhāratvānna suṣiraśrutivirodho 'smadabhyupagamasyetyarthaḥ / yathā mandirasthamañjūṣāntargatamapi vastu mandirasthamiti saṅgīyate, evamihāpīti bhāvaḥ / tadantassthatveti pāṭhe paramātmanaḥ suṣirāntassthatvamapekṣya śruteḥ pravṛttatvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.5.18:
Now, if <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s directly being in the lotus is accepted, there would be contradiction with the <s>suṣira</s>-<s>śruti</s> (the passage about the opening/cavity). Likewise, even if <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being the space within the lotus is accepted, there would still be contradiction with the <s>suṣira</s>-<s>śruti</s>, since the word '<s>suṣira</s>' denotes space. And even if, setting aside these [options], one accepts that the <s>dahara</s> lotus has the nature of space and <s>Viṣṇu</s> abides within that space and He alone is the support of all — even then there is contradiction with the <s>suṣira</s>-<s>śruti</s>, because in that [passage] the <s>suṣira</s> (opening) itself is directly stated to be the support of all. To this he says — '<s>tadantasstha</s>' (abiding within that). // The word '<s>suṣiraśruti</s>' (the <s>suṣira</s> passage) is to be construed here as ending in the sixth case (genitive), separated analytically. And thus, '<s>suṣiraśruteḥ</s>' — of the <s>śruti</s> passage containing the word '<s>suṣira</s>' — '<s>tadantassthāpekṣatvāt</s>' — because it operates with reference to the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) abiding within the opening of the lotus — and because He is the support of all — there is no contradiction with the <s>suṣira</s>-<s>śruti</s> in our accepted view: this is the meaning. Just as an object inside a casket within a temple is still spoken of as 'in the temple,' so too here — this is the import. In the reading '<s>tadantassthāpekṣatvāt</s>,' the meaning is: because the <s>śruti</s> operates with reference to the <s>Paramātman</s>'s abiding within the opening.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
If [it be said] that [the entity in the <s>dahara</s> is the <s>jīva</s>] because of reference to the other (<s>itara</s>), [we say] no, because of impossibility. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.18 |

children.text:
'paraṃ jyotirupasampadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate,'; (chāṃ. 8-12-3.) 'eṣa ātmeti hovāca'; (chāṃ. 4-15-1.)
iti jīvaparāmarśātsa iti cet -
children.translated_text: 'Approaching the supreme light, [the <s>jīva</s>] manifests in its own form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3); 'This is the Self — thus he said' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.1) — if [it be said that] because of reference to the <s>jīva</s> [the entity in the <s>dahara</s>] is the <s>jīva</s> —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.19:
bhagavato hṛtpadmasthatvamākṣipya samādadhatsūtramupanyasyākṣepāṃśaṃ tāvadvyācaṣṭe - itareti // 'niṣpadyate'; ityanantaramityuktasyeti śeṣaḥ / asya ca samāsapraviṣṭajīvapadenānvayaḥ / anena sūtre asminnasyetyasyānuvṛttiḥ / itarapadaṃ siddhāntyabhimatabrahmapratiyogijīvaparam / ata eva śrutāveṣa iti jīvaparāmarśaḥ / siddhānte śrutyarthastu vakṣyate /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.5.19:
Having raised an objection against the Lord's abiding in the lotus of the heart and then resolving it, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and first explains the objection portion — beginning with '<s>itara</s>' (other). // After '<s>niṣpadyate</s>,' the word '<s>ityuktasya</s>' (of what was stated) is to be supplied. And its syntactic connection is with the word '<s>jīva</s>' embedded in the compound. By this, the continuation of '<s>asmin asya</s>' from the [previous] <s>sūtra</s> [is indicated]. The word '<s>itara</s>' (other) refers to the <s>jīva</s> as the counter-correlate of <s>Brahman</s> intended in the <s>siddhānta</s>. Therefore, '<s>eṣa</s>' in the <s>śruti</s> constitutes a reference to the <s>jīva</s>. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> in the <s>siddhānta</s>, however, will be stated later.
No, because of the impossibility, for that [<s>jīva</s>], of being free from sin and the like by its own [nature]. // 18 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.20:
dhṛtisūtrāt 'asyāsmin upalabdheḥ'; ityasyānuvṛttimabhipretyaparihārāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti // hṛtpadmastho na jīva ityarthaḥ / kuto netyatastatrānuvṛttavākyena 'asmin'; prakaraṇe 'asya'; apahatapāpmatvāderupalabdherityasya hetorlābhāttamanupanyasyoktahetorjīve niravakāśatvoktiparatayāsambhavādityaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - tasyeti // jīvasyetyarthaḥ / muktabhāvamādāya jīve sambhavāt asiddhivārāṇāya - svata iti // svātantryeṇetyarthaḥ / satyakāmatvādikamādiśabdārthaḥ / anena - 'asmin'; 'paraṃ jyotiḥ'; itivākye 'bhivyaktikartṛtvenoktasya prakṛtasyopasampattikarmībhūtādbrahmaṇa itarasyāsya jīvasyātmeti 'ya ātmā'; ityuktahṛtpadmasthātmatvavidhānāya 'eṣaḥ'; ityetacchabdena 'parāmarśāt'; upasthāpanāt / jīvaparāmarśakaitacchabdaśravaṇāditi yāvat / dahare sa jīva eva, na viṣṇuriti cet - na hṛtpadmastho jīvaḥ/ kutaḥ? asminprakaraṇe 'syāpahatapāpmatvāderupalabdheḥ śravaṇāt / asya cāsmin jīve svato 'sambhavāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.5.20:
Intending the continuation from the anchor-<s>sūtra</s> (<s>dhṛtisūtra</s>) '<s>asya asmin upalabdheḥ</s>' (because of the perception of this in this [context]), he explains the rebuttal portion — beginning with '<s>na</s>' (no). // The meaning is: the one abiding in the lotus of the heart is not the <s>jīva</s>. Why not? With the sentence carried over, '<s>asmin</s>' — in this section — '<s>asya</s>' — because of the perception of being free from sin (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and the like — having presented this reason and intending to state the impossibility of the stated reason [applying to] the <s>jīva</s>, he explains the portion '<s>asambhavāt</s>' (because of impossibility) — beginning with '<s>tasya</s>.' // This means: of the <s>jīva</s>. To forestall the objection that the stated attributes are possible in the <s>jīva</s> if one takes him as being in the liberated state, [he adds] — '<s>svataḥ</s>' (by its own nature). // This means: independently. The <s>satyakāmatva</s> (having true desires) and other [attributes] are the meaning of the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.). By this — in the passage '<s>asmin</s>' — '<s>paraṃ jyotiḥ</s>' (supreme light) — the <s>jīva</s> who is the counter-correlate of <s>Brahman</s>, which is the object of attainment (<s>upasampatti</s>) and the subject under discussion stated as the agent of manifestation, is referred to by the word '<s>eṣaḥ</s>' (this) — '<s>parāmarśāt</s>' — because of its being presented [as the <s>Ātman</s>]. That is, because of hearing the word '<s>etat</s>' which refers to the <s>jīva</s>. [The objector says:] In the <s>dahara</s> [space], that is the <s>jīva</s> alone, not <s>Viṣṇu</s> — if so, no: the one abiding in the lotus of the heart is not the <s>jīva</s>. Why? Because in this section, '<s>asya</s>' — of [the entity's] being free from sin and the like — there is perception, hearing. And '<s>asya</s>' — of this [attribute] — '<s>asmin</s>' — in the <s>jīva</s> — '<s>svataḥ asambhavāt</s>' — because of the impossibility [of its existing] by its own nature — this is the <s>sūtra</s> meaning as stated.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
If [it be said that the <s>jīva</s> is meant] because of the subsequent [passage], [we say] it refers to one whose own nature has become manifest. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.19 |

children.text:
'sa tatra paryeti jakṣan krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ'; (chāṃ. 8-12-3.)
ityādyuttaravacanājjīva eveti cet -
children.translated_text: 'There he wanders about, eating, playing, rejoicing' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3) — if [it be said that] because of such subsequent statements, it is the <s>jīva</s> alone —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.21:
jīvasyāpahatapāpmatvādyasambhavamākṣipya samādadhatsūtramupanyasyākṣepāṃśaṃ tāvadvyācaṣṭe - uttarāditi // 'ityādyuttaravacanāt'; evaṃrūpāddaharavākyāpekṣayā parāmarśavākyāpekṣayā vānantarādvacanādityarthaḥ / vacanādityanantaram asyāsminnupalabdherityanuṣajyate / sambhavāditi śeṣaḥ / 'asya'; satyakāmatvasya 'asmin'; jīve pratītestata eva viśokatvādeḥ 'upalabdheḥ'; siddheruktaguṇānāṃ sambhavāditi tadarthaḥ / jīva ityanena pūrvasūtrātsa ityasyānuvṛttiḥ sūcitā/ neśvarā iti evaśabdārthaḥ / hṛtpadmastha iti vartate /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.5.21:
Having raised the objection against the impossibility of being free from sin and the like [applying to the <s>jīva</s>] and then resolving it, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and first explains the objection portion — beginning with '<s>uttarāt</s>' (from the subsequent). // '<s>Ityādy uttaravacanāt</s>' — from such a statement that is subsequent — with reference to the <s>dahara</s> passage, or with reference to the passage of reference [previously cited] — from a statement that comes after: this is the meaning. After '<s>vacanāt</s>' (from the statement), '<s>asya asmin upalabdheḥ</s>' is connected. '<s>Sambhavāt</s>' (because of possibility) is to be supplied. '<s>Asya</s>' — of the <s>satyakāmatva</s> (having true desires) — '<s>asmin</s>' — in the <s>jīva</s> — because of the perception, hence the possibility of the stated attributes — this is the meaning. By '<s>jīva</s>,' the continuation of '<s>sa</s>' (he) from the previous <s>sūtra</s> is indicated. '<s>Na Īśvara</s>' (not the Lord) is the meaning of the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone). '<s>Hṛtpadmastha</s>' (dwelling in the lotus of the heart) carries over.

children.text: na, tatra hi parameśvaraprasādādāvirbhūtasvarūpo mukta ucyate /
children.translated_text: No; for there, it is the liberated one whose own nature has become manifest by the grace of the Supreme Lord who is spoken of.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.22:
nañanuvṛttyā parihārāṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - neti // naitadvākyabalena jīvasya satyakāmatvādiguṇān sambhāvya hṛtpadmasthatvaṃ vācyamityarthaḥ / kuto netyato 'bhihitam 'āvirbhūtasvarūpastu'; ityaṃśaṃ tatreti padādhyāhāreṇa vyācaṣṭe - tatreti // 'sa tatra'; ityuttaravākya ityarthaḥ / tatra 'āvirbhūtasvarūpaḥ'; ucyate iti sambandhaḥ / āvirbhūtasvarūpaḥ ityasya vyākhyānaṃ mukta iti / hiśabdo yata ityarthe / uttaravacanādityatrāpi sambadhyate / tathā ca 'uttaravacanāt'; 'svena rūpeṇa'; iti jaḍadehatyāgottarakālīnasvarūpābhivyaktiśruteḥ / atra muktasyokteḥ hṛtpadmasya ca dehāntaravṛttitayā muktatvāyogāt nāyaṃ jīva iti bhāvaḥ / nanvasya muktaviṣayatve 'pi muktasyāpi jīvatve nāstyeva jīve 'pahatapāpmatvādisambhavaḥ / na ca tasya hṛtpadmasthatvāyogaḥ, yato jīvo bhāvibhāvenāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇaḥ idānīṃ hṛtpadmagatatayocyata ityata āha - parameśvaraprasādāditi / evetyanuvartate / anena tu śabdo vyākhyātaḥ / parameśvaraprasādādityanena uttarādityetaduttamādityapi vyākhyātam / atra mukta iti na sautrapadavyākhyānamātram / kintūddeśyasamarpakaṃ ca / anena āvṛttistuśabdasya yathāśrutānvayaśca sūcitaḥ / tathā ca yo 'tra mukta ucyate sa tu parameśvaraprasādādeva 'āvirbhūtasvarūpaḥ'; āvirbhūto vyaktaḥ svarūpaḥ apahatapāpmatvādiḥ svadharmo yasya sa tathoktaḥ / ato na svato 'pahatapāpmatvādiguṇakaḥ, ato na daharasthaḥ jīva iti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.5.22:
With the negation particle '<s>na</s>' carrying over, he explains the rebuttal portion — beginning with '<s>na</s>' (no). // The meaning is: the <s>jīva</s>'s abiding in the lotus of the heart should not be stated on the strength of this [subsequent] passage by attributing <s>satyakāmatva</s> and other qualities to the <s>jīva</s>. Why not? To this, the portion '<s>āvirbhūtasvarūpastu</s>' (but one whose own nature has become manifest) is explained with the supplement of the word '<s>tatra</s>' (there) — beginning with '<s>tatra</s>.' // '<s>Sa tatra</s>' means: in the subsequent passage — this is the meaning. The syntactic connection is: there, one 'whose own nature has become manifest' (<s>āvirbhūtasvarūpa</s>) is said [to wander about, etc.]. The explanation of '<s>āvirbhūtasvarūpa</s>' is '<s>mukta</s>' (the liberated one). The particle '<s>hi</s>' has the sense of 'because.' It also connects with '<s>uttaravacanāt</s>' (from the subsequent statement). And thus, '<s>uttaravacanāt</s>' — because of the subsequent statement '<s>svena rūpeṇa</s>' (in his own form) — there is the hearing of the manifestation of one's own nature after the abandonment of the material body. Here, because the liberated one is spoken of, and because the lotus of the heart belongs to another body [which the liberated one has left behind] and therefore liberation is not compatible [with still being in it], this is not the <s>jīva</s> — this is the import. Now, even if this passage pertains to the liberated one, since the liberated one too is a <s>jīva</s>, the possibility of being free from sin and the like [existing] in the <s>jīva</s> is not [negated]. Nor is there incompatibility of the <s>jīva</s>'s abiding in the lotus of the heart, since the <s>jīva</s>, possessing qualities like being free from sin in a future state, could be spoken of now as abiding in the lotus of the heart — to this he says: '<s>parameśvaraprasādāt</s>' (by the grace of the Supreme Lord). The word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) carries over. By this, the word '<s>tu</s>' (but) [in the <s>sūtra</s>] is explained. By '<s>parameśvaraprasādāt</s>' (by the grace of the Supreme Lord), '<s>uttarāt</s>' is also explained as '<s>uttamāt</s>' (from the Highest). Here '<s>mukta</s>' (liberated) is not merely an explanation of the <s>sūtra</s> word; it also indicates the entity under discussion. By this, the recurrence of the '<s>tu</s>' particle and its construal as heard is indicated. And thus, he who is spoken of as '<s>mukta</s>' (liberated) here — he, '<s>tu</s>' (but/indeed), is one 'whose own nature has become manifest' (<s>āvirbhūtasvarūpa</s>) — meaning: whose own attributes such as being free from sin have become manifest, i.e., revealed — '<s>parameśvaraprasādāt eva</s>' — by the grace of the Supreme Lord alone. Therefore, [these attributes] do not [exist] in him by his own nature; therefore, the one abiding in the <s>dahara</s> [space] is not the <s>jīva</s> — this is the construction.

children.text: yatprasādātsa mukto bhavati sa bhagavān pūrvoktaḥ// 19 //
children.translated_text: He by whose grace that [<s>jīva</s>] becomes liberated — He is the aforementioned Lord. // 19 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.23:
nanu 'paraṃjyotirupasampadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate'; (chāṃ. 8-3-4.) ityatra muktasyābhivyaktāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇakatvamevocyate, na tu tadguṇānāṃ parameśvarādhīnatvam / atastatsvata evetyata āha - yaditi // asya yacchabdasya dvitīyatacchabdenānvayaḥ / prasādo nāma icchāviśeṣaḥ / 'saḥ'; jīvaḥ / punaḥ sa ityuktyā sūtre 'nuvṛttasya sa ityasyāvṛttiḥ sūcitā / pūrvokta ityanena sūtre uttaratretyasya pratiyogitayā pūrvatretyupaskāryamityuktaṃ bhavati / tatheti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca 'yatprasādāt'; yasyānugrahāt 'saḥ'; jīvo 'muktaḥ'; apahatapāpmatvādiguṇo bhavati / 'saḥ'; guṇapradātā bhagavān, 'pūrvoktaḥ'; 'paraṃjyotirupasampadya'; iti pūrvavākye 'tathā'; guṇapradātṛtayā ukta iti yojanā/ anyathā lyabantapadaṃ vyarthaṃ syāditi bhāvaḥ / ukta ityanantaraṃ yata iti śeṣaḥ / asyātonātra muktaguṇaprāpteḥ parameśvarādhīnatvoktyabhāva ityupaskṛtavākyenānvayaḥ / athavā - nanu jīve 'nyādhīnasya tadguṇajātasya sattvātsa evāpahatapāpmatvādinokto hṛtpadmasthaścāstvityata āha - yaditi / yojanā tu - yatprasādātsa jīvo jaḍadehānmukto bhavati, mukto bhūtvā ca sopahatapāpmatvādiguṇo bhavati, sa bhagavāneva 'pūrvoktaḥ'; 'eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmā'; (chāṃ. 8-1-5.) ityādipūrvavākye tathāpahatapāpmatvādinokto na jīvaḥ / dātṛpratigṛhītrormadhye dātureva mukhyatvānmukhyāmukhyayośca mukhyasyaiva grāhyatvāditi //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.5.23:
Now, in the passage 'Approaching the supreme light, [the <s>jīva</s>] manifests in its own form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.4), it is only the manifestation of the liberated one's attributes such as being free from sin that is stated, not the dependence of those attributes on the Supreme Lord. Therefore, those [attributes exist] in the <s>jīva</s> by its own nature alone — to this he says: '<s>yat</s>' (by whose). // The syntactic connection of this '<s>yat</s>'-word is with the second '<s>tat</s>'-word. '<s>Prasāda</s>' (grace) means a specific act of will. '<s>Saḥ</s>' — the <s>jīva</s>. By the repetition of '<s>sa</s>' (he), the recurrence of '<s>sa</s>' from the [previous] <s>sūtra</s> is indicated. By '<s>pūrvokta</s>' (aforementioned), it is stated that the word '<s>uttaratra</s>' (in the subsequent [passage]) in the <s>sūtra</s> is to be construed with its correlative '<s>pūrvatra</s>' (in the preceding [passage]). '<s>Tathā</s>' (thus) is to be supplied. And thus, '<s>yatprasādāt</s>' — by whose grace — '<s>saḥ</s>' — the <s>jīva</s> — becomes '<s>mukta</s>' — endowed with attributes like being free from sin. '<s>Saḥ</s>' — that grace-bestower — is the Lord, '<s>pūrvoktaḥ</s>' — mentioned in the preceding passage 'Approaching the supreme light' as '<s>tathā</s>' — i.e., as the bestower of those attributes — this is the construction. Otherwise, the absolutive word (<s>lyabanta</s>) would be purposeless — this is the import. After '<s>ukta</s>' (mentioned), '<s>yataḥ</s>' (therefore) is to be supplied. Its syntactic connection with the supplemented sentence is: therefore, there is no absence of the statement of the dependence of the liberated one's attainment of attributes on the Supreme Lord. Alternatively — now, since in the <s>jīva</s> the class of those attributes dependent on another does exist, that very [<s>jīva</s>] is spoken of as endowed with being free from sin and the like and as abiding in the lotus of the heart — to this he says: '<s>yat</s>' (by whose). The construction, then, is: '<s>yatprasādāt</s>' — by whose grace — '<s>saḥ</s>' — the <s>jīva</s> — becomes '<s>mukta</s>' — liberated from the material body; and having become liberated, he becomes endowed with attributes like being free from sin — '<s>saḥ</s>' — He is the Lord alone, '<s>pūrvoktaḥ</s>' — mentioned in the preceding passage as 'This is the Self, free from sin' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5) and the like, with those [attributes] of being free from sin etc. — not the <s>jīva</s>. Because among the bestower and the recipient, the bestower is primary, and between the primary and secondary [referent], the primary alone is to be taken.

children.translated_text: By this — of this <s>jīva</s> who was mentioned in 'This serene one, having risen from this body' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.4), 'from the subsequent' — from the subsequent passage relative to the <s>Dahara</s> passage, or from the immediately following reference-passage — by the statement 'He moves about there' and the like, 'in this' — in the previously discussed <s>jīva</s> — 'of this' — of <s>satyakāmatva</s> (having true desires) — 'because of perception' (<s>upalabdhi</s>) — because of cognition; and because of the establishment of his being free from sorrow and the like from that very [passage]. Therefore, because there is no impossibility of the stated qualities in him, that one situated in the heart-lotus is the <s>jīva</s> alone, not the Lord — if this be argued: No, because in that [passage], by the force of the subsequent statement 'by his own [form],' the one spoken of as liberated is one whose own nature has become manifest. And he, being no longer within the body, would not be situated in the heart-lotus: this is the purport. Nor should it be said that since the <s>jīva</s>, even when liberated, can have co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of freedom from sin and heart-lotus-abidance even at different times, there is still the possibility [of the <s>jīva</s> being the referent]. Because in this passage, the one who is spoken of as liberated has his own nature manifest by the grace of the <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord) who is the subsequent, the highest — not by his own power. Nor should it be said that here only the possession of those qualities by the liberated one is stated, not the dependence of the set of qualities on the Supreme Lord. Because in the preceding passage, 'the supreme light,' the <s>Paramātman</s> by whose grace he becomes liberated is spoken of as the bestower of qualities. Nor should it be said that since the <s>jīva</s> somehow possesses the qualities of freedom from sin and the like, there is still the possibility [of him being the referent]. Because from the subsequent, the highest Lord — by His grace — that liberated one, whose nature has become manifest — whose freedom from sin and other qualities have become evident — He, however, is <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Lord) Himself who was spoken of in the preceding passage 'This Self is free from sin' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5), not the liberated <s>jīva</s>: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. The meaning of the <s>Śruti</s>, however, is: 'This' — <s>jīva</s> — because he is '<s>samprasāda</s>' — fully endowed with <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s grace — therefore, 'from this final body' — 'having risen' — being liberated — 'that supreme' — 'light' — <s>Brahman</s> — 'having reached' — having attained — by his own form — 'manifests' (<s>abhiniṣpadyate</s>) — becomes manifest in his own qualities — 'he is the supreme person' (<s>sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ</s>) — called the supreme light. He describes the manner of the liberated one's engagement with objects: 'sa' (he). 'He' — the liberated one whose inherent bliss has become manifest upon attainment — 'there' — in the place of liberation — by the grace of the <s>Paramātman</s> alone — 'eating' (<s>jakṣan</s>) — consuming what he desires; laughing or with relatives — i.e., with fellow liberated ones, and with non-relatives — i.e., those liberated in previous cosmic cycles — 'sporting' (<s>krīḍan</s>); with women — 'delighting' (<s>ramamāṇaḥ</s>) — experiencing pleasure, enjoying worldly happiness of women and the like — 'moves about' (<s>paryeti</s>) — wanders about in all directions.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
And the reference (<s>parāmarśa</s>) is for the purpose of the other [i.e., <s>Paramātman</s>]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.20 |

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 24:
Objection: Since, having referred to the <s>jīva</s> by the word 'this' (<s>eṣaḥ</s>), the statement 'Self' (<s>ātmā</s>) declares his being the Self situated in the heart-lotus — could not the <s>jīva</s>, even though possessing non-primary freedom from sin and other qualities, be the Self situated in the heart-lotus by the force of the reference with the word 'this' (<s>etat</s>)? Having raised this doubt, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and, obtaining the required sense from the continued previous statement 'the reference to the other — if so, no' and the thesis of the established conclusion, explains the <s>sūtra</s> as a reason for the already-stated conclusion — '<s>anya</s>' (other). // In the <s>Śruti</s>, the neuter reference '<s>paraṃ jyotiḥ</s>' (supreme light) being referred to with the masculine 'yam' (whom) is justified either because gender is not intended to be significant, or because the gender of the qualified noun is intended. By this, in the <s>Śruti</s>, '<s>paraṃ jyotiḥ</s>' is a single compound word. What will be stated — '<s>paraṃjyotiḥ</s>-word denotes the <s>Paramātman</s> alone' — and that, by the conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) in the <s>Purāṇas</s> '<s>paraṃjyotiḥ paraṃ brahma</s>' (the supreme light is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>), it denotes <s>Viṣṇu</s>: thus it is stated. Some [interpret] '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' (light) as radiant form, and '<s>param</s>' as supreme <s>Brahman</s> — as two separate words. In this interpretation, there is contradiction with the stated <s>Bhāṣya</s>. Moreover, there is contradiction with the sub-commentary explaining the 'yam'-word as 'the Lord called <s>paraṃjyotiḥ</s>.' And contradiction with the <s>Viṣṇutattvaniṇaya Ṭīkā</s>'s '<s>paraṃjyotiḥ</s> means the <s>Paramātman</s>.' The meaning of '<s>upasampadya</s>' in the <s>Śruti</s> is 'having attained.' He explains the word '<s>anya</s>' (other) of the <s>sūtra</s> from the perspective of the prima facie view regarding the <s>jīva</s> as the counter-entity — '<s>Paramātman</s>.' // One whose purpose (<s>artha</s>) — i.e., referent — is the <s>Paramātman</s> alone is so described. '<s>Parāmarśa</s>' (reference) — the word '<s>etat</s>' (this). Or alternatively, the <s>Paramātman</s>'s being the Self is the purpose — i.e., the function — of which; such is the reference. In that case, '<s>parāmarśa</s>' means the apprehension through the word '<s>etat</s>': that is the meaning. The word 'ca' in both the <s>sūtra</s> and the <s>Bhāṣya</s> has the cumulative meaning: not only is there the obstacle (<s>bādhaka</s>) in the form of the impossibility of freedom from sin in the <s>jīva</s> view, but also there is the absence of the establishing factor (<s>sādhaka</s>) in the form of the reference — or, [the word 'ca' has] the meaning of 'tu' (but). In the <s>Candrikā</s>, however, since it is stated that not only is there no obstacle-nature of the reference in the Lord-view, but also there is no establishing-force for the <s>jīva</s> view — the reference is explained as having the restrictive meaning: 'for the purpose of the other, i.e., the Lord, alone.' By this — 'the reference to the other' — having referred to the other, i.e., the <s>jīva</s>, by the word 'this' (<s>eṣaḥ</s>), because of the declaration of his being the Self situated in the heart-lotus — that Self situated in the heart-lotus is the <s>jīva</s> alone, not the Lord — if so: No. Why? Because the reference with the word 'this' (<s>eṣaḥ</s>) is 'for the purpose of the other' — for the purpose of the Lord alone, not for the purpose of the <s>jīva</s>. Therefore — or alternatively: not only because of impossibility, but also because the reference too is for the purpose of the other. Or: because of impossibility, the one in the heart-lotus is not the <s>jīva</s>, but the Lord alone. Nor is there thereby inappropriateness of the reference, because the reference — the word '<s>etat</s>' — is for the purpose of the other: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated in three ways. 'Having reached whom' — having attained proximity to whom. By this, the <s>jīva</s>, having reached the <s>Paramātman</s> called '<s>paraṃjyotiḥ</s>' (supreme light), having directly known Him, then having attained proximity — through the removal of ignorance — manifests by his own form of bliss and the like — i.e., his own qualities become manifest. 'Having reached whom, the <s>jīva</s> manifests by his own form, that one is this Self' — who was previously called the Self — 'is the <s>Paramātman</s>,' said [<s>Prajāpati</s>] to <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, '<s>Ramā</s>' — this is the meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> in the established conclusion.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
If [it be objected that it is not <s>Brahman</s>] because of the <s>Śruti</s> of smallness — that has [already] been stated. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.21 |

BBsBhDīp_1,3.5.27:
nanu yuktaṃ vyomnoṃ'śato 'lpaukastvam, aṃśasyāpūrṇatvāt / brahmaṇi tu aṃśo 'pi pūrṇa iti kathaṃ tasyāṃśato 'lpaukastvamityataḥ sūtraśeṣaṃ prakarāntareṇa vyācaṣṭe - eṣa ma iti // ca śabdo yuktisamuccaye / sūtrakṛcchrutyuktisamuccaye vā / 'guṇāḥ śrutāḥ'; iti śrutisamuccaye vā / 'yasmin'; iti smṛtisamuccaye vā / anena 'alpaśruteḥ'; 'daharaḥ'; iti vākye sarvagate vastunyalpasthānasthitiśravaṇāt, tasyāśca viṣṇāvasambhavādanupapatterna dahare viṣṇuḥ, kintu sa jīva eveti cet - na, yataḥ 'taduktaṃ'; tatra nicāyyatvāditi pūrvatra tasya sarvagatasyāpi viṣṇorvyomavattadalpasthānasthitatvam, tasmādupāsanārthaṃ yuktamityuktam / na cāṃśatopi sarvagatatayā tatra tadanupapattiḥ / yatastasyāṃ 'eṣa ma ātmā'; (chāṃ. 3-14-3.) iti chandogaśrutau tena sarvajyāyastvena vṛddhatamatvena vyāptatvenaiva prakāreṇa tasya viṣṇostaddhṛdayasthatvamuktaṃ smṛtyuktaṃ cāta iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / na ca śrutismṛtyuktamapi kathametadaṅgīkārārhaṃ, yuktivirodhāditi vācyam / brahmaṇo 'cintyaśaktitvādupapatteḥ / 'guṇāḥ śrutāḥ'; (sauparṇaśrutiḥ) 'yasminviruddhagatayaḥ'; ityādivacanācca / mama hṛdaye ya 'ātmā'; paramātmāsti / upalakṣaṇametat / sarvahṛdaye ca ya āste eṣaḥ hṛdayasthāṃśarūpo bhagavān 'jyāyān'; vṛddhatamaḥ deśakālaguṇaiḥ pūrṇa iti śrutyarthaḥ / upaniṣaddraṣṭṛṛṣivākyametat / ('viruddhagatayo 'pi'; anyatra bhinnāśrayā apyaṇutvamahattvādayo dharmāḥ yasmin 'patanti'; vartante ca / na kālabhedenetyāha - aniśamiti / muktasādhāraṇyamāśaṅkyāha -vidyādaya iti /
yasmādviṣṇoranyatrāṇutvamahatvādivividhaśaktayo dharmāḥ / vidyā āhiḥ jñaptikāraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ / jñānajñeyā iti yāvat / harau viruddhadharmasattve pramāṇamāha - ānupūrvyeti / 'ānupūrvī śrutirvedastrayī cāmnāya ucyate'; ityabhidhānācchrutyā siddhā ityarthaḥ / yacchabdasya 'tadbrahmāhaṃ prapadye'; iti uttaravākyagatatacchabdenānvayaḥ) // 5 //
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.5, verse 27:
Objection: It is appropriate that space can be small in part, because a part [of space] is not full. But in the case of <s>Brahman</s>, even a part is full — so how can He be small even in part? To this he explains the remainder of the <s>sūtra</s> with another reasoning — '<s>eṣa ma</s>' (this is my [Self]). // The word 'ca' is for the accumulation of reasons. Or [it is] for the accumulation of reason by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (the author of the <s>sūtras</s>) and the <s>Śruti</s>. Or for the accumulation with the <s>Śruti</s> [statement] 'qualities are heard.' Or for the accumulation with the <s>smṛti</s> [statement] 'in whom.' By this — 'because of the <s>Śruti</s> of smallness' — in the passage '<s>daharaḥ</s>,' because of the hearing of abidance in a small locus in an all-pervading entity, and because of the impossibility of that in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the <s>Dahara</s> is not <s>Viṣṇu</s> but the <s>jīva</s> alone — if so: No. Because 'that has been stated' — there [in the earlier <s>sūtra</s>], 'because of being capable of being meditated upon,' it was previously stated that even the all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>, like space, abides in that small locus, and therefore it is appropriate for the purpose of meditation. Nor is there impossibility [of His being there] even in part, due to [His] all-pervasiveness. Because in that very <s>Chāndogya Śruti</s> — 'This is my Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.3) — <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s abidance in that heart is stated in the very manner of being 'greater' (<s>jyāyān</s>) — i.e., the greatest — full in respect of space, time, and qualities, and also stated in the <s>smṛti</s> — therefore the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. The meaning of the <s>Śruti</s> is: the <s>Paramātman</s> who is the '<s>ātmā</s>' (Self) — who abides in 'my heart' — this is a synecdoche — and who abides in the heart of all — 'this' (<s>eṣaḥ</s>) <s>Bhagavān</s> in the form of the portion residing in the heart, is '<s>jyāyān</s>' (the greatest) — the most exalted — full in respect of space, time, and qualities. This is a statement of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>'s seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>). ('Contradictory qualities' — attributes like subtlety and greatness that are of different loci elsewhere — 'in whom' — 'abide' (<s>patanti</s>) — exist. [They exist] not at different times, [so] he says — '<s>aniśam</s>' (constantly). Anticipating [the objection] that this is common to liberated [souls] too, he says — '<s>vidyādayaḥ</s>' (knowledge etc.). Because in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and not elsewhere, the diverse powers (<s>śaktis</s>) in the form of attributes like subtlety and greatness — [the beings are] '<s>vidyāhis</s>' — those for whom knowledge is the snake, i.e., the cause of apprehension — 'so described': i.e., objects of knowledge. He states the <s>pramāṇa</s> (authority) for the existence of contradictory attributes in <s>Hari</s> — '<s>ānupūrvī</s>' (in sequence). '<s>Ānupūrvī</s> is <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Veda</s>, <s>Trayī</s>, and is called <s>Āmnāya</s>' — from this lexicographical statement, [it is] established by the <s>Śruti</s>: that is the meaning. The relative pronoun 'yat' has its correlative connection with the pronoun 'tat' in the subsequent sentence 'To that <s>Brahman</s> I resort.') // 5 //
// Thus ends the <s>Daharādhikaraṇa</s> // 5 //
// 6. <s>Anukṛtyadhikaraṇa</s> (the topic of imitation) //

adṛśyatvādayaḥ parameśvaraguṇā uktāḥ / 'teṣāṃ sukhaṃ
śāśvataṃ netareṣām / tadetaditi manyante 'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham'; (kaṭha. 5-12,14.) ityādinā jñānisukhasyāpyanirdeśyatvamajñeyatvaṃ cocyata iti //
children.translated_text: Invisibility (<s>adṛśyatva</s>) and other qualities of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) have been stated. 'Their happiness is eternal, not of others. The wise consider that to be the indescribable supreme happiness' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.12, 14) — by this, the indescribability and unknowability of even the happiness of the knower (<s>jñānī</s>) are stated. //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.6, verse 1:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.6.1:
atrādhikaraṇe 'kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyām'; iti vākyoktaṃ jñānārthaṃ jñeyaprārthanāviṣayatvaṃ vā 'kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyāṃ kimu bhāti'; iti brahmajñānānukūlābhivyaktyākhyabhānaprārthanāviṣayatvarūpaṃ vā ānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇatvaṃ liṅgaṃ brahmaṇi samanvīyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca sūcayan sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣaṃ darśayati - adṛśyatvāditi/ 'uktāḥ'; ānandamayādhikaraṇe udāhṛtādṛśya iti vākye iti bhāvaḥ / uktā ityanantaraṃ tatra praviṣṭamiti śeṣaḥ / prathamādipadenāniruktatvādeḥ, dvitīyena 'kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyāṃ kimu bhāti na bhāti vā'; (kaṭha. 5-14) iti samanvetavyaliṅgabodhakottarārdhasya ca grahaṇam / na kevalaṃ viṣṇoḥ, kintu jñānisukhasyāpītyaperarthaḥ / evārtho vāpiśabdaḥ ānumānikasūtragatāpipadavat / 'ajñeyatvaṃ'; sākalyenājñeyatvaṃ durjñeyatvamiti yāvat / caśabdaḥ parasparasamuccaye, ānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇatvarūpasamanvetavyaliṅgasamuccaye vā / pūrvaśratyanusārādadṛśyatvādaya iti, etacchrutyanusārādanirdeśyatvamiti vyutkramaḥ/ yadyapi 'tadetaditi'; etadevodāhartavyam / tathāpi pūrvapakṣe tacchabdārthapradarśanāya 'teṣām'; iti pūrvavākyaikadeśopanyāsaḥ / ata eva tattvapradīpe teṣāmiti prastutiḥ pūrvapakṣotthāpiketyuktam / tathācetthaṃ yojanā - pūrvamānandamayādhikaraṇe ye 'dṛśyatvādayo guṇāḥ parameśvarasyoktāḥ / tatra teṣu praviṣṭamanirdeśyatvamajñeyatvaṃ ca 'teṣāṃ sukham'; iti prakṛtyāmnātena 'tadetat'; ityādinā kāṭhakavākyena pūrvapakṣirītyā samīpasthāttacchabdāt parāmṛṣṭasya 'jñānisukhasyāpi'; jñānisukhasyaivocyata iti / pūrvārdhenānirdeśyatvasyottarārdhe ca 'kimu bhāti na bhāti'; ityanena durjñeyatvaparyavasitājñeyatvasya cārthāduktatvāditi bhāvaḥ / ṭīkāyāmadṛśyatvapadasyānirdeśyatvaparatvādanirdeśyatvamiti pāṭhābhyupagamādvā na tadvirodhaḥ / atrānirdeśyatvamajñeyatvaṃ cocyata iti phaloktiḥ, ānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇatvasyaivātra vicāryatvāt / tattu dvitīyādiśabdopāttavākyena caśabdena vā sūcitamiti draṣṭavyam / yata evamataḥ pūrvoktamayuktamiti bhāvaḥ / anenānandamayādhikaraṇoktādṛśyatvājñeyatvarūpasyānirdeśyatvāniruktatvarūpasya ca tatrānyatra ca sattve jñānisukhe 'tivyāptyākṣepāt itaramātraniṣṭhatvetvasambhavākṣepātphalatastenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / tathā caśabdasūcitamānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇatvaṃ viṣayaḥ / viṣṇoranyasya veti sandehaḥ / jñānisukhasyaiveti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ / anirdeśyatvājñeyatve ca tasyaiveti phalaṃ, sukhaśrutiḥ, prakṛtatvādirupayuktiśca sūcitā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.6.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the indicatory mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of being favorably apprehended — in the form of being the object of the desire for knowledge expressed by 'How shall I know that?' or in the form of being the object of the prayer for manifestation favorable to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, as expressed in 'How shall I know that? Does it shine?' — is harmonized (<s>samanvīyate</s>) in <s>Brahman</s>. Indicating the connection with <s>śruti</s> and the like, the subject and so forth, he presents the prima facie view with reasoning — beginning with '<s>adṛśyatva</s>' (invisibility). 'Have been stated' — the purport is: in the passage '<s>adṛśya</s>' (invisible) cited in the <s>Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa</s>. After 'have been stated,' the remainder is: 'included therein.' By the first word 'ādi' (and the like), indescribability (<s>aniruktatva</s>) and the like are included; by the second, the second half of the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> passage 'How shall I know that? Does it shine or does it not shine?' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.14), which conveys the indicatory mark to be harmonized, is also included. 'Api' means 'not only of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but of the bliss of the knower as well.' The particle 'api' has the meaning 'eva' (indeed), like the word 'api' occurring in the <s>Ānumānika-sūtra</s>. 'Unknowability' (<s>ajñeyatva</s>) — unknowability in its entirety, meaning difficulty of knowing. The particle 'ca' is for mutual aggregation, or for the aggregation of the indicatory mark of being favorably apprehended. Because of following the earlier <s>śruti</s>, the order is 'invisibility and the like' (<s>adṛśyatvādayaḥ</s>); because of following this <s>śruti</s>, 'indescribability' (<s>anirdeśyatva</s>) — thus there is a reversal. Although '<s>tadetat</s>' (that, this) alone should be cited, nevertheless, in the prima facie view, to show the meaning of the word 'tat' (that), a portion of the earlier passage '<s>teṣām</s>' (of those) is presented. Therefore, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, it is said that the introduction with '<s>teṣām</s>' is for raising the prima facie view. And thus the construction is as follows: the qualities such as invisibility and the like that were stated of the Supreme Lord in the <s>Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa</s> earlier — among those, the indescribability and unknowability that are included therein are, according to the prima facie view, spoken by the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> passage '<s>tadetat</s>' and the like (which, by the word 'tat' referring to what is nearby, is interpreted as referring to) 'the bliss of the knower as well' — that is, of the bliss of the knower alone. Because indescribability is conveyed by the first half, and unknowability culminating in difficulty-of-knowing is conveyed by implication through 'Does it shine or does it not shine?' in the second half. There is no contradiction with the <s>Ṭīkā</s>'s taking the word '<s>adṛśyatva</s>' as meaning indescribability, or from accepting such a reading. The statement 'indescribability and unknowability are spoken of here' is the result-statement, since only the being-favorably-apprehended is what is to be deliberated here. But that is indicated by the passage included through the second word 'ādi,' or by the particle 'ca' — thus it should be seen. Since this is so, what was stated earlier is improper — this is the purport. By this, since there is the objection that if the invisibility-unknowability and the indescribability-indeterminacy stated in the <s>Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa</s> are present both there and elsewhere in the bliss of the knower, there would be over-extension, and the objection that they cannot belong to another alone — therefore from the result, the connection of this [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] with the former is by way of objection. And the mark of being favorably apprehended, indicated by the particle 'ca,' is the subject. Whether it belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> or to another is the doubt. That it belongs to the bliss of the knower alone is the prima facie view. And the result is that indescribability and unknowability too belong to that alone — the <s>śruti</s> on bliss, the relevance of the topic, and the reasoning are indicated.

Therefore he says —
<s>Sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
Because of imitation, and of that. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.22 |
