'tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvam'; ityanukṛteḥ, 'tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti'; (kaṭha. 5-15.) iti vacanācca paramātmaiva
anirdeśyasukharūpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Following His shining, everything shines after [Him]' — because of [this] imitation; and because of the statement 'By His light, all this shines' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 5.15), it is the <s>Paramātman</s> alone who is of indescribable blissful nature.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.6.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // 'ityanukṛteḥ'; ityanubhānaśruterityarthaḥ / anubhānaṃ nāma tadicchānurodhena bhānaṃ kriyāviśeṣaḥ / sūtre tasyetyasyānukṛterityanenāpi sambandhe tenaivānukaraṇapratisambandhina ānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇasya tatkartuḥ sūryāditejasaśca lābho bhavatīti spaṣṭatvāttadubhayānuktiḥ / yadvā - pūrvasūtrāttadityasya vipariṇatasyehānuvartanādubhayalābho bhavatītyāśayena tadubhayānuktiḥ / na kevalaṃ tasyetyetat samanvetavyānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇatvākhyaliṅgadharmiṇaḥ, sūryāditejasaśca parāmarśakaṃ, kintu śrutipratīkarūpamapi sarvajagatprakāśakatvaparaṃ cetyāśayena taddhetvantaraparatayā vyācaṣṭe - tasyeti / 'iti vacanāt'; ityanena sūtre ityukteriti śeṣo darśitaḥ / yadyapi sūtrabhāṣyayoḥ 'anubhāti'; itiśrutyanusārādanubhānāditi vācyam / tathāpi tāpinī pācinī caiva śoṣiṇī ca prakāśinī /
naiva rājan raveśśaktiḥ śaktirnārāyaṇasya sā //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.6.2:
Having introduced the <s>sūtra</s> that gives the established conclusion, he explains it — beginning with 'therefore.' '<s>Ityanukṛteḥ</s>' — meaning: because of the <s>śruti</s> on imitation (<s>anubhāna</s>). <s>Anubhāna</s> means shining in conformity with His will — a specific kind of activity. In the <s>sūtra</s>, when '<s>tasya</s>' (of that) is also connected with '<s>anukṛteḥ</s>' (because of imitation), the acquisition of both — that which is favorably apprehended and the radiance of the sun and the like that imitates [Him] — is obtained, this being clear, both are left unstated. Alternatively, because the word '<s>tat</s>' from the previous <s>sūtra</s> is carried forward here in a transformed sense, the acquisition of both is achieved — with this intention, both are left unstated. '<s>Tasya</s>' refers not merely to the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) of the mark to be harmonized, namely being favorably apprehended, and to the radiance of the sun and the like, but also serves as a citation of <s>śruti</s> and refers to the illumination of the entire universe — with this intention, he explains it as referring to a second reason, beginning with '<s>tasya</s>.' 'Because of the statement' — by this, the remainder 'because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>' is shown. Although in the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>bhāṣya</s>, because of following the <s>śruti</s> '<s>anubhāti</s>' (shines after), '<s>anubhānāt</s>' (because of shining after) should be said, nevertheless, [the following Padma Purāṇa passage is cited]: 'The heating, burning, drying, and illuminating power is not of the sun, O King; it is the power of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' //

children.text: iti aitareyabhāṣyodāhṛtapādmavacanātsūryādikartṛkapratapanādikamapi paramātmādhīnamiti darśayitumanukṛterityuktam / sūtre tadanusāribhāṣye ca caśabdo dvitīyasūtrasya vakṣyamāṇavyākhyānabhedena sarvajagatprakāśakatvarūpoktahetusamuccaye vā, sūryādyaprakāśyatvarūpānuktahetusamuccaye vā draṣṭavyaḥ / sūtre samanvayasūtrādanuvṛttasya vidheyaparasya tattvityasyārthamāha - paramātmaiveti / na tu jñānisukhamityevaśabdārthaḥ / liṅgasamanvayena bhavatphalaṃ darśayati - anirdeśyeti / anirdeśyaścāsau sukharūpaśca iti vā, anirdeśyaṃ yatsukhaṃ tadrūpa iti vā vigrahaḥ / atra rūpaśabdo bhinnakramaḥ / tathā cānirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ paramātmarūpamityanvayaḥ / eka ityādau pulliṅgena prakṛtasyaitaditi napuṃsakaliṅgena grahaṇāya rūpaśabdaprayogaḥ / upalakṣaṇametat / anugrāhyascetyapi draṣṭavyam / vastutastu - vacanāccetiśabdasya sukharūpaścetyapi sambandhe tenaivānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇākhyaḥ sādhyadharmī sūcita iti dhyeyam / yadyapyanirdeśyatvamajñeyatvaṃ cetyupakramādubhayaṃ grāhyaṃ, na tvekaṃ, sukharūpamiti cādhikam / tathāpi pūrvapakṣyuktasukhaśruteḥ sukharūpe brahmaṇi sāvakāśatvajñāpanāya 'tadetat'; itivākyoktamanirdeśyasukharūpatvameva gṛhītam / ajñeyatvamapi draṣṭavyam / yadyapyatra bhāṣye liṅgadvayasyānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇasya vā anirdeśyasukharūpasya vā viṣṇutve sādhye sākṣāddhetutvaṃ bhāti / ṭīkāyāṃ tu - 'tadetat'; iti śrutisthatacchabdena samīpoktajñānisukhaparityāgena 'cetanaścetanānām'; (kaṭha. 5-13.) iti vyavadhānena prakṛtaparamātmagrahaṇe liṅgadvayaṃ hetutvena yojitam / tathāpi hetudvayena tacchabdena jñānisukhaparityāgena paramātmana eva grahaṇasiddhau tata eva tacchabdagṛhītasya paramātmana evānirdeśyasukharūpatvaṃ paryavasyatītyāśayena bhāṣye liṅgadvayasya prakṛtasādhyahetutvenoktirityavirodhaḥ / kecittu - 'paramātmaivānirdeśyasukharūpaḥ'; iti bhāṣyamevānukṛtisūtre 'ānandamayobhyāsāt'; ityādāviva samanvetavyaśabdāderviṣṇuparatva eva heturnocye, kintvanirdeśyaṃ sukhamityatra samīpoktajñānisukhaparityāge heturucyate ityatra jñāpakaṃ, ṭīkāpi tadanusāriṇītyāhuḥ / tathā cāyaṃ siddhānte śrutyarthaḥ -
eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti /
children.translated_text: The one controller, the inner Self of all beings, who makes one form manifold —
Those wise ones who perceive Him as established in the Self [attain eternal bliss] // (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 5.12) //

— thus, because of the statement from the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> cited in the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s>, to show that even the heating and the like performed by the sun and others are dependent on the <s>Paramātman</s>, '<s>anukṛteḥ</s>' (because of imitation) is stated. In the <s>sūtra</s> and the <s>bhāṣya</s> that follows it, the particle 'ca' may be seen as aggregating the stated reason of illuminating the entire universe through a different explanation of the forthcoming <s>sūtra</s>, or as aggregating the unstated reason that [He is] not illuminable by the sun and the like. He states the meaning of '<s>tat</s>' carried forward from the <s>Samanvaya-sūtra</s> as the predicate indicator — '<s>Paramātman</s> alone.' The meaning of 'eva' (alone) is: not the bliss of the knower. He shows the result obtained through the harmonization of the marks — beginning with 'indescribable.' The compound is either: '<s>anirdeśya</s>' (indescribable) and '<s>sukharūpa</s>' (of blissful nature); or: 'one whose nature is indescribable bliss.' Here the word '<s>rūpa</s>' (nature) is in a different order. And thus the syntactic connection is: the indescribable supreme bliss is the nature of the <s>Paramātman</s>. The word '<s>rūpa</s>' is used to enable the neuter gender '<s>etat</s>' to refer back to the masculine '<s>eka</s>' and the like in the opening [of the passage]. This is indicative; it should also be seen as including 'and the one to be favored.' In reality, however — when the word 'ca' in 'because of the statement' is also connected with '<s>sukharūpa</s>' (of blissful nature), thereby the subject to be established (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>) called 'being favorably apprehended' is indicated — this should be noted. Although both indescribability and unknowability should be taken from the opening [prima facie view], not just one, and 'of blissful nature' is additional — nevertheless, to indicate that the <s>śruti</s> on bliss stated by the prima facie opponent has scope in <s>Brahman</s> which is of blissful nature, only the indescribable-blissful-nature stated by the passage '<s>tadetat</s>' is taken. Unknowability too should be seen [as included]. Although in this <s>bhāṣya</s>, the two marks or the indescribable blissful nature of being favorably apprehended appear to be directly the reason for establishing <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood — in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, however, by the word 'tat' in the <s>śruti</s>, abandoning the bliss of the knower that was nearby, and with the intervening [passage] '<s>cetanaścetanānām</s>' (the conscious one among the conscious) (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.13) taking up the topic of the <s>Paramātman</s> — the two marks are employed as reasons. Nevertheless, when through the two reasons the apprehension of the <s>Paramātman</s> alone by the word 'tat' — abandoning the bliss of the knower — is established, from that very fact the indescribable blissful nature of the <s>Paramātman</s> apprehended by the word 'tat' follows — with this intention, the statement in the <s>bhāṣya</s> of the two marks as reasons for the topic under discussion is not contradictory. Some, however, [say]: the <s>bhāṣya</s> '<s>Paramātman</s> alone is of indescribable blissful nature' is itself, in the <s>Anukṛti-sūtra</s>, just as in '<s>Ānandamayobhyāsāt</s>' and the like, an indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) that the reason stated is for the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the words to be harmonized, and not for the 'indescribable bliss' — but rather, the reason is for abandoning the bliss of the nearby knower — and the <s>Ṭīkā</s> too follows this. And thus, in the established conclusion, the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is:

children.text: iti pūrvavākye 'ya eko'; jñānānandādyabhinnaḥ samābhyadhikaśūnyo vā yaḥ sarvamasya vaśe 'stīti 'sarvavaśī'; yaḥ 'sarvabhūtāntarātmā'; sarvaprāṇināmantarniyāmakaḥ 'ya ekaṃ'; svasvarūpaṃ bahudhā karoti niyamyānantyāt / 'taṃ'; prakṛtam 'ātmasthaṃ'; jīvahṛdayasthitaṃ ye 'dhīrāḥ'; jñāninaḥ anupaśyantīti prakṛtā ye jñāninasteṣāmeva 'śāśvataṃ sukhaṃ'; nityābhivyaktasaukhyaṃ netareṣām / anena brahmasāmarthyamuktaṃ bhavati / evaṃ 'nityo nityānām'; iti vākyamapi brahmamāhātmyaparatayā vyākhyeyam / 'tadetat'; ityādināpi prakṛtabhagavatsvarūpameva viśeṣataḥ pratipādyate iti / manyante ityasyottaratrānvayaḥ / tathā ca 'yato vāco nivartante'; (tai. 2-4-1.) 'eṣo 'sya parama ānandaḥ'; (bṛ. 6-3-32.) ityādau prasiddham anirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyāmiti manyante ityānukūlyena gṛhṇanti / jñānārthaṃ tadbhānaṃ vā prārthayante / 'kimu bhāti na bhāti vā'; iti tasya durjñeyatvaṃ ca vadanti jñāninaḥ / tat brahmaṇo rūpaṃ svarūpabhūtaṃ sukhametadekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karotītiprakṛteśvararūpābhinnamiti manyante jñānina iti / etacchabdasyeśvaraparatve 'pi rūpaśabdasāmānādhikaraṇyāt napuṃsakaliṅgatopapattiḥ / taduktaṃ nyāyavivaraṇe - 'yadbrahmānirdeśyaṃ sukhamiti vadanti tadetatsvarūpamiti manyanta iti'; / kāṭhakabhāṣye tu - tad 'guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam'; ityupakrāntam / 'rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva'; (kaṭha. 5-9.) iti jīvasya pratibimbatvamuktam / rūpaśabdena prakṛtametat 'ekaṃ rūpam'; ityatra prakṛtaṃ ca bhagavadrūpam 'anirdeśyam'; itthamiti sākalyena nirvaktumaśakyaṃ paramaṃ sukhamiti manyante jñānina iti sukharūpatvavidhiparatayā vyākhyātam / bhāṣye 'pyanirdeśyasukharūpa ityetāvanmātragrahaṇena śrutau sukharūpatvaṃ vidheyamiti sūcitam / tadanirdeśyaparamasukhātmakaṃ bhagavadrūpaṃ tatparasādamṛte kimu bhāti na bhāti veti samyagbhāti na bhātīti kathaṃ nvahaṃ jānīyāmiti śiṣṭavākyārthastatraivoktaḥ / vivṛtaṃ caidvyāsatīrthīye - 'tat'; anirdeśyaparamasukhātmakaṃ bhagavadrūpaṃ tatprasādamṛte kimu samyagbhāti? na bhāti vāti? iti praśnottarabhūtam ekaṃ niścitārthaṃ 'kathamahaṃ vijānīyāṃ'; na kenāpi prakāreṇeti / atretiśabda ubhayānvayī / tathā ca kimu bhātīti praśnasyottarabhūtaṃ na bhātītivākyoktamekamajñeyatvarūpamarthamiti yojanā / kecittu - yadevaṃ brahma tatprasādamṛte 'nu'; idānīṃ 'kathamahaṃ vijānīyām'; prārthanīyāṃ liṅ / na kathamapītyarthaḥ / jñānivākyānukaraṇametat / bhagavatprasādādapi kiṃ sākalyena tajjñānaṃ bhavatīti naciketā yamaṃ pṛcchati - kimu bhātīti / uśabdaḥ samyagityarthe / kimvityekaṃ vā / tathātve samyagiti śeṣaḥ / uttaramāha yamaḥ - na bhātīti / vāśabdoṣa'vadhāraṇe / na bhātyeveti vyākhyāti /
children.translated_text: In the preceding passage, 'He who is one' — He who is non-different from knowledge, bliss, and so forth, devoid of any equal or superior — 'the Lord of all' (<s>sarvavaśī</s>), meaning He in whose control everything exists; He who is 'the inner Self of all beings' (<s>sarvabhūtāntarātmā</s>), the inner controller of all living beings; He who 'makes the one' — His own essential nature — 'manifold,' due to the infinity of those He controls. 'Him' — the one under discussion — 'dwelling in the Self' (<s>ātmastham</s>), situated in the heart of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — those who are 'wise' (<s>dhīrāḥ</s>), the knowers, who perceive Him — for those knowers who are the subject of discussion, there is 'eternal happiness' (<s>śāśvataṃ sukham</s>), perpetually manifest bliss, and not for others. By this, the power of <s>Brahman</s> is declared. Likewise, the passage 'the eternal among eternals' (<s>nityo nityānām</s>) should also be interpreted as referring to the greatness of <s>Brahman</s>. Through the words 'that is this' (<s>tadetat</s>) and so forth, the essential nature of the Lord already under discussion is taught in greater detail. The word 'they think' (<s>manyante</s>) connects with what follows. And thus, in passages such as 'from which words turn back' (<s>yato vāco nivartante</s>, Taittirīya 2.4.1) and 'this is his supreme bliss' (<s>eṣo'sya parama ānandaḥ</s>, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 6.3.32), the well-known supreme happiness that is beyond description — 'how indeed shall I know that?' — they grasp this in a favorable sense as 'they think.' They pray for knowledge of it, or for its manifestation. And the knowers say 'does it shine or does it not shine?' (<s>kimu bhāti na bhāti vā</s>), declaring its being difficult to know. That form of <s>Brahman</s>, the bliss that constitutes His essential nature — 'He who makes the one form manifold' — the knowers think that this is non-different from the form of the Lord who is the subject of discussion. Even though the word 'that' (<s>etat</s>) refers to the Lord, the neuter gender is justified because of its co-referentiality with the word 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>). This has been stated in the <s>Nyāyavivaraṇa</s>: 'That <s>Brahman</s> which they call indescribable bliss — the knowers think this is His essential nature.' But in the <s>Kāṭhaka Bhāṣya</s>, the passage begins with 'that secret, eternal <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam</s>). In 'He became a counterpart corresponding to each form' (<s>rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva</s>, Kaṭha 5.9), the reflection-nature of the <s>jīva</s> is stated. By the word 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>), the subject under discussion — 'the one form' — and the form of the Lord that is under discussion — 'indescribable' — meaning impossible to describe fully in its entirety — 'supreme happiness' — thus the knowers think — this is interpreted as having the primary purport of establishing that His nature is bliss. In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> too, by the mere inclusion of the expression 'whose nature is indescribable bliss,' it is indicated that the bliss-nature is what is to be established in the <s>śruti</s>. That form of the Lord whose nature is indescribable supreme bliss — without His grace, 'does it shine or does it not shine?' — meaning 'does it properly shine or not?' — 'how indeed shall I know?' — the meaning of the remaining learned statement is explained right there. And it is elaborated in the <s>Vyāsatīrthīya</s>: 'That' — the form of the Lord whose nature is indescribable supreme bliss — without His grace, 'does it properly shine? Or does it not shine?' — this is in the form of question and answer, with one definite meaning — 'how shall I know it?' — by no means whatsoever. Here the word 'this' (<s>iti</s>) connects with both. And thus the construction is that the statement 'it does not shine' is the answer to the question 'does it shine?', expressing the single meaning of unknowability. But some say: that <s>Brahman</s> being such, without His grace, 'now' (<s>nu</s>) 'how shall I know?' — this is the optative expressing a prayer. The meaning is 'not by any means.' This is a quotation of the words of the knowers. <s>Naciketas</s> asks <s>Yama</s> whether even by the grace of the Lord complete knowledge of Him is possible — 'does it shine?' The particle <s>u</s> means 'properly.' Or <s>kimv</s> is one unit, in which case 'properly' is supplied. <s>Yama</s> gives the answer: 'it does not shine.' The particle <s>vā</s> here has the sense of emphasis (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>). He explains it as 'it certainly does not shine.'

children.text: na hi jñānisukhamanubhāti sarvaṃ, na ca tadbhāsā /
children.translated_text: For neither does the happiness of the knower illuminate everything, nor does everything shine by its light.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.6.3:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.6.3:
nanu 'tameva bhāntam'; iti vākye sūryāditejasāṃ paramātmādhīnaprakāśakartṛtvasya 'tasya bhāsā'; itivākye ca sarvasya jagatastatprabhāprakāśyatvasya ca śravaṇena asiddhiparihāre kutastayorviṣṇutvasādhyenāvyabhicaritatvam, yena talliṅgadvayabalātsamīpoktajñānisukhapāmarśaparityāgaḥ syādityata āha - na hīti // sarvamityubhayānvayī / bhātīti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca 'hi'; yasmāt 'sarvaṃ'; sūryāditejaḥ jñānisukhamanusṛtya 'na bhāti'; na prakāśate / tathā 'tadbhāsā'; tasya jñānisukhasya prakāśena 'sarvaṃ'; jagat 'na bhāti'; na prakāśate cetyarthaḥ / vakṣyamāṇapramāṇavirodhāditi bhāvaḥ / caśabdaḥ samuccaye / ato na liṅgadvayamanyatrāvakāśavaditi vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> 1.3.6.3:
Now, an objection: In the passage 'Him alone shining' (<s>tameva bhāntam</s>), the dependence of the luminosity of the sun and other lights upon the Supreme Self is heard, and in the passage 'by His light' (<s>tasya bhāsā</s>), the illuminability of the entire world by His radiance is heard — so when the impossibility is already refuted, how can their being established in <s>Viṣṇu</s> through those two indicators (<s>liṅga</s>) serve as proof of invariable concomitance, such that by the force of those two indicators the interpretation referring to the happiness of the knower mentioned nearby would be abandoned? To this he says 'na hi' (for neither). The word 'everything' (<s>sarvam</s>) connects with both clauses. 'Shines' (<s>bhāti</s>) is supplied. And thus, 'since' (<s>hi</s>) 'everything' — the light of the sun and so forth — does 'not shine' following the happiness of the knower; likewise, 'by its light' (<s>tadbhāsā</s>) — by the light of the knower's happiness — 'everything' — the world — does 'not shine,' does not become illuminated — this is the meaning. The purport is: because it contradicts the evidence to be stated. The particle <s>ca</s> (and) is used in the sense of aggregation. Therefore, the two indicators do not find scope elsewhere — this is the remainder of the sentence.

children.text: 'ahaṃ tattejo raśmīt'; iti nārāyaṇabhāsā hi sarvaṃ bhāti // 22 //
children.translated_text: 'I am that light, from the rays' — for everything shines by the radiance of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // 22 //
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.6.4:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.6.4:
astvetadubhayaṃ jñānisukhe 'nupapannam / tathāpyanena kutaḥ paramātmano grahaṇaṃ, asya paramātmatvasādhyasāmānādhikaraṇyāniścayādityatastatra dvitīyasūtrasthāpipadena sūcitāṃ śrutimāha - ahamiti // ahamitītyanantaraṃ śruteriti śeṣaḥ / itiśabda ādyārthe / tena 'tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti'; (kaṭha. 5-15.) ityātharvaṇaśrutirapi gṛhyate / nārāyaṇeti / nārāyaṇādhīnabhāsetyarthaḥ / hiśabdo yata ityarthe, prasiddhau ca / 'sarvaṃ'; sūryāditejaḥ 'bhāti'; prakāśate / yadvā - 'nārāyaṇabhāsā'; nārāyaṇīyabhāsā 'sarvaṃ'; jagat 'bhāti'; prakāśasya ityarthaḥ / 'iti jñāyate'; iti śeṣaḥ / śrutau 'raśmīt'; ityanena sūryāditejasāṃ nārāyaṇādhīnaprakāśakartṛtvasya, 'tejaḥ'; ityanena sarvasya jagato nārāyaṇīyaprakāśaprakāśyatvasya coktatvāditi bhāvaḥ / 'aham'; iti, śrutistvantarnaye vyākhyātā / anena - taduktamityataḥ sūtre tadityanuvartate / tasyetyāvartate vipariṇamyate ca / asambhavāditi cānuvartate / tathā ca -

children.translated_text: 'That is this,' they think, 'the indescribable, supreme happiness;
how indeed shall I know that?' (Kaṭha 5.14).

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> 1.3.6.4:
Let it be granted that both are impossible with respect to the knower's happiness. Even so, how does this lead to the apprehension of the Supreme Self, since there is no certainty of co-referentiality with what is to be established as the Supreme Self? To this, he cites the <s>śruti</s> indicated by the word <s>api</s> in the second <s>sūtra</s>: 'I am' (<s>aham</s>). After the word 'I am,' the word '<s>śruti</s>' is supplied. The particle <s>iti</s> has the sense of 'beginning with.' By this, the <s>Ātharvaṇa śruti</s> (Muṇḍaka) passage 'Him alone shining, everything shines after; by His light all this is illumined' (<s>tameva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti</s>, Kaṭha 5.15) is also included. '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' means 'dependent on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s radiance.' The particle <s>hi</s> means 'because' and also indicates well-known fact. 'Everything' — the light of the sun and so forth — 'shines,' i.e., becomes luminous. Alternatively, 'by the radiance of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' (<s>nārāyaṇabhāsā</s>) means by the light belonging to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, 'everything' — the world — 'shines,' i.e., becomes luminous — this is the meaning. 'Thus it is known' is supplied. In the <s>śruti</s>, by the word 'from the rays' (<s>raśmīt</s>), the dependence of the luminosity of the sun and other lights upon <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is stated; by the word 'light' (<s>tejas</s>), the illuminability of the entire world by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s light is stated — this is the purport. The word 'I' (<s>aham</s>) — this <s>śruti</s> has been explained in the <s>Antarnaya</s> section. By this — from 'thus it is stated' (<s>taduktam</s>) — the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) continues in the <s>sūtra</s>. 'Of that' (<s>tasya</s>) recurs and is transformed. 'Because of impossibility' (<s>asambhavāt</s>) also continues. And thus:

children.text: ityānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇaṃ tadetacchabdaparāmṛśyaṃ sukham anirdeśyaṃ sukhaṃ tattu viṣṇurūpameva, na samīpoktajñānisukham / kutaḥ? 'tasya'; sūryāditejasaḥ 'tasya'; ānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇasya sukhasya tasmin 'tameva bhāntam'; iti 'anukṛteḥ'; anubhānaśravaṇāttasyaitadadhīnaprakāśakartṛtvaśravaṇādasyānyatejoniyantṛtvaśravaṇāditi yāvat / tathā tasya sarvasya jagatastasya tatprakāśaprakāśyatvasya 'tasya bhāsā'; (kaṭha. 5-15.) iti śrutāvuktatvāttasya sarvajagatprakāśatvokteriti yāvat / tasya ca liṅgadvayasya 'ahaṃ tattejaḥ'; (caturvedaśikhā.) ityādiśrutyā smṛtyā ca tasminviṣṇāveva niścayenopapatterjñānisukhe ca 'asambhavāt'; anupapatteḥ / tathā tasminnupasaṃhāre tasyānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇasya 'na tatra sūryo bhāti'; iti vākye tasya sūryādyaprakāśyatvasyacokteśceti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: When grasped favorably, the happiness referred to by the words 'that' and 'this' (<s>tad</s> and <s>etat</s>) — the indescribable happiness — is indeed the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not the happiness of the knower mentioned nearby. Why? Because in 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>) — of the light of the sun and so forth — and 'of that' — of the happiness grasped favorably — in that passage 'Him alone shining' (<s>tameva bhāntam</s>), because of 'imitation' (<s>anukṛti</s>, i.e., the shining-after), because of the hearing that things shine after Him, because of the hearing that the luminosity of those lights depends on Him, because of the hearing that He controls all other lights — this is the full import. Likewise, because of the statement of the illuminability of all the world by His light in the <s>śruti</s> passage 'by His light' (<s>tasya bhāsā</s>, Kaṭha 5.15) — that is, because of the declaration that He illumines the entire world. And because those two indicators are established with certainty in <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone through <s>śruti</s> such as 'I am that light' (<s>ahaṃ tattejaḥ</s>, Caturvedaśikhā) and through <s>smṛti</s>, while in the happiness of the knower they are impossible (<s>asambhavāt</s>) — and also because in that concluding passage, the statement 'there the sun does not shine' (<s>na tatra sūryo bhāti</s>) declares His being beyond the illumination of the sun and other lights, when grasped favorably — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
<s>Sūtra</s>: <s>Oṃ</s>.
It is also remembered (<s>api smaryate</s>). <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.23.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.6.5:

children.text:
yadādityagataṃ tejo jagadbhāsayate 'khilam /
yaccandramasi yaccāgnau tattejo viddhi māmakam // (gī. 15-12.) iti /
children.translated_text: 'That light which, residing in the sun, illumines the entire world, which is in the moon, and which is in fire — know that light to be Mine.' (<s>Gītā</s> 15.12)

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.6.5:
yadetalliṅgadvayasya viṣṇuniṣṭhatvam 'aham'; iti śrutyopapāditam / tatsmṛtyāpyupapādayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā tāṃ smṛtimudāharati - apīti // iti smaryata ityanvayaḥ / 'yat'; ādityādiṣu sthitaṃ tejastat 'māmakaṃ'; madadhīnaṃ madīyaṃ ca, matteja evādityādiṣu prerakatvenāsti / tadevākhilaṃ jagat 'bhāsayate'; prakāśayatīti gītāsmṛtyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> 1.3.6.5:
That these two indicators are established in <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been demonstrated through the <s>śruti</s> beginning with 'I' (<s>aham</s>). Now, demonstrating this also through <s>smṛti</s>, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> and then cites that <s>smṛti</s>: 'api' (also). The construction is: 'thus it is remembered' (<s>iti smaryate</s>). 'That' (<s>yat</s>) light situated in the sun and other luminaries — that is 'Mine' (<s>māmakam</s>), dependent on Me and belonging to Me; My light alone exists in the sun and other luminaries as the impelling force. That very light 'illumines' (<s>bhāsayate</s>) the entire world — this is the meaning of the <s>Gītā smṛti</s>.

children.text:
na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ /
yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama // (gī. 15.6.) iti ca // 23 //
children.translated_text: 'Neither the sun illumines that, nor the moon, nor fire; having gone to which they do not return — that is My supreme abode.' (<s>Gītā</s> 15.6) // 23 //
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.6.6:
Thus ends the <s>Anukṛtya-adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Imitation/Shining-after). // 6 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.6.6:
kiṃ ca pāṭhake 'na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yamagniḥ'; ityādyānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇasya sukhasya sūryādyaprakāśyatvamucyate / tacca viṣṇoreva smaryate, ato viṣṇureva 'tadetat'; ityatra pratipādyaḥ, na jñānisukhamiti sūtrasyārthāntaramapipadasya yuktisamuccayārthatvaṃ cābhipretya tāṃ smṛtimudāharati - na taditi // atrāpītiśabdasya smaryata ityanvayaḥ / jñānino 'yadgatvā'; yatprāpya punastasmānnanivartante, tanmama paramaṃ 'dhāma'; svarūpaṃ, tadetaddhāma sūryo 'na bhāsayate'; na prakāśayate, evaṃ 'śaśāṅkaḥ'; candraḥ / yadā caivaṃ tadā kuto 'yamavamo 'gniriti gītāsmṛtyarthaḥ / anena - pūrvavyākhyāne na kevalamanukṛtyādiḥ 'ahaṃ tattejaḥ'; iti śrutyantare 'tamevabhāntamanubhāti'; ityātharvaṇādau viṣṇudharmatvena śrūyate, kintu yadādityeti smaryatepīti śrutisamuccayārthe 'piśabdaḥ / dvitīyavyākhyāne tu 'tameva bhāntamanubhāti'; ityuttaravākyoktānukṛtyādihetoḥ 'na tatra sūryo bhāti'; iti pūrvavākyoktasūryādyaprakāśyatvahetośca samuccaye 'piśabdaḥ / tathā ca na kevalaṃ 'tadetat'; ityatroktānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇasya viṣṇutvarūpapradhānasādhye hetūkṛtamanukṛtyādikam 'ahaṃ tattejo raśmīt'; ityādau śrūyate, kintu yadādityeti smaryate 'pīti vā apiḥ / kiñca - yato na kevalaṃ prathamasūtroktaliṅgadvayaṃ, kintu tato 'nyadapi 'na tatra'; iti kāṭhakavākye tasyānukūlyena gṛhyamāṇasyoktaṃ sūryādyaprakāśyatvarūpaṃ liṅgaṃ tasya viṣṇoḥ sambandhitvenaiva 'na tat'; iti smaryate / atastadetat 'kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyām'; ityatra viṣṇureva pratipādya iti vā sūtrasyārthadvayamuktaṃ bhavati / 'na tatra'; ityāderayamarthaḥ / pūrvaṃ brahma na samyagbhātīti tasya durjñeyatvamuktaṃ, tatkuta ityataḥ idamucyate - yasyaivaṃvidhaṃ sukhaṃ rūpaṃ 'tatra'; brahmaṇi sūryo 'na bhāti'; tanna prakāśayatīti yāvat / candratārakamiti dvandvaikavadbhāvaḥ/ evaṃ tat vidyuto 'pi 'na bhānti'; na bhāsayantīti / 'tameva bhāntam'; ityuttaravākyaṃ tu yadyapi vyāsatīrthakṛtātharvaṇaṭīkāyām - 'etatsamākhyārūpamātharvaṇavākyaṃ'; 'bhāntaṃ'; bhāsayantaṃ paramātmānamanusṛtyaiva sūryādayo 'bhānti'; prakāśate iti vyākhyātam / tathāpi ṭīkānusārāt 'sarvaṃ'; sūryāditejaḥ 'bhāntaṃ'; prakāśamānaṃ bhagavantamanusṛtyaiva 'bhāti'; prakāśate / 'tasya'; bhagavato 'bhāsā'; prakāśena 'idaṃ sarvaṃ'; jagati 'bhāti'; prakāśyata iti vyākhyeyam / vyāsatīrthīyaṃ tu vyākhyānāntaraṃ ṭīkākṛdabhipretaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tadvirodhaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.6.6:
Moreover, in the recitation passage 'There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightning bolts shine — how then this fire?' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.2.15) and the like, the quality of not being illuminable by the sun and others is stated regarding the bliss that is understood in conformity [with this passage]. And that [quality] is remembered as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone; therefore <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is to be taught in the passage 'That is this' — not the bliss of the knower. With the intention of stating another meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> and [showing] that the word '<s>api</s>' (also) serves the purpose of accumulating reasons, he cites that <s>smṛti</s> — beginning with '<s>na tat</s>.' // Here too, the word 'iti' connects with '<s>smaryate</s>' (it is remembered). 'Of the knower' — having attained '<s>yat</s>' (which), i.e., having reached it, they do not return from it — 'that' is My supreme '<s>dhāma</s>' (abode), i.e., My essential nature. This abode, the sun 'does not illuminate' — does not reveal. Likewise '<s>śaśāṅka</s>' — the moon. And when this is so, how then this lowly fire? — this is the meaning of the <s>Gītā smṛti</s> (<s>BG</s> 15.6). By this — in the first interpretation, not only the <s>anukṛtya</s> (imitation) and the like heard in the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> 'I am that radiance' and in other <s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>tam eva bhāntam anubhāti</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.2.15) as attributes of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but also what is remembered in '<s>yad āditya</s>' — [thus] the word '<s>api</s>' is in the sense of accumulating <s>śruti</s> [evidence]. In the second interpretation, however, the word '<s>api</s>' is for the accumulation of the reason of not being illuminable by the sun etc. stated in the prior passage '<s>na tatra sūryo bhāti</s>' and the reason of <s>anukṛtya</s> (imitation) etc. stated in the subsequent passage '<s>tam eva bhāntam anubhāti</s>.' And thus — not only is the <s>anukṛtya</s> (imitation) etc. made a reason for establishing the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-nature, which is the primary object of proof, of what is understood in conformity with the passage 'That is this,' heard in the <s>śruti</s> passage beginning with 'I am that radiance,' but also it is remembered in '<s>yad āditya</s>' — or [alternatively], the word '<s>api</s>' [means]: furthermore, since not only the two indicatory marks stated in the first <s>sūtra</s>, but also another [mark] — in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> passage '<s>na tatra</s>' — the indicatory mark in the form of not being illuminable by the sun etc., which is understood in conformity with that [passage], is remembered as belonging to that <s>Viṣṇu</s> in '<s>na tat</s>.' Therefore, 'That is this' in the passage 'How shall I know that?' — here <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is to be taught. Thus the two meanings of the <s>sūtra</s> are stated. The meaning of the passage '<s>na tatra</s>' etc. is as follows: previously it was said that <s>Brahman</s> does not shine forth properly — i.e., His being difficult to know was stated. As to the question 'why is that?', this is said: He whose bliss-nature is such — '<s>tatra</s>' — in <s>Brahman</s>, the sun 'does not shine' — does not illuminate, that is the meaning. '<s>Candratārakam</s>' — moon and stars: this is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative) compound treated as singular. Likewise, the lightning bolts too 'do not shine' — do not illuminate that. '<s>Tam eva bhāntam</s>' — the subsequent passage, although in the <s>Ātharvaṇa Ṭīkā</s> composed by <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s> it is explained as 'this <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> passage is a designation-type statement' — '<s>bhāntam</s>' — following the <s>Paramātman</s> who illuminates, the sun and others 'shine' — illuminate — nevertheless, in accordance with the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, it should be explained as: 'everything' — the radiance of the sun and others — following the Lord who is '<s>bhāntam</s>' (shining), 'shines.' 'By His' — by the Lord's — '<s>bhāsā</s>' (illumination), 'all this' — the world — 'shines' — is illuminated. The explanation of <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>, however, being an alternative interpretation, would be what the <s>Ṭīkā</s> author intended — hence there is no contradiction. // 6 //
// Thus ends the <s>Anukṛtyadhikaraṇa</s> // 6 //
// 7. <s>Vāmanādhikaraṇa</s> //

BBsBhDīp_1,3.7.1:
atrādhikaraṇer iśānanāmasamanvayaḥ kriyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayasaṃśayau ca sūcayati - viṣṇureveti / jijñāsāsūtre viṣṇurevasarvairmumukṣubhirmokṣārthaṃ jijñāsya ityuktamityarthaḥ / na ca tatra jijñāsyatvāyogavyavaccheda eva kṛtaḥ, na tvanyayogavyavaccheda iti vācyam / anyasyāpi jijñāsyatve tasyāpi mokṣadātṛtvāpattyā 'yato nārāyaṇaprasādamṛte'; ityādivivaraṇānupapatteranyayogavyavacchedasyāpi tatrābhipretatvāt / ato 'traivakāra ubhayānvayitayā vyākhyeyaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - tatreti / idaṃ cāvartate / tatretyavyayaṃ tadityarthe 'pi / tathā ca 'athāto brahmajijñāsā'; iti yatpūrvaṃ viṣṇorjijñāsyatvamuktaṃ 'tatra'; jijñāsyatve 'tatrar'; 'iśāno bhūtabhavyasya'; ityuktvā āmnāte 'ūrdhvam'; iti kāṭhakavākye 'kaścirt'; iśāno dharmitvena pratīyate / katham? yato 'yaṃ 'sarvadevopāsyaḥ'; tairjijñāsyaḥ pratīyate ata iti vākyayojanā / na ca vāyoḥ sarvadevopāsyatve 'pi na viṣṇossarvadevopāsyatvahāniriti vācyam / tāvatāpi sarvairmumukṣubhirviṣṇureva jijñāsya iti niyamasyāsiddheḥ / na ca śrutigataviśvedevaśabdasya gaṇaviśeṣavācitvāt sarvadevopāsya ityuktiranupapanneti vācyam / gaṇaviśeṣaparatve tasya guṇādhikyāsiddhyā sarvadevaparatvāvaśyaṃbhāvāt / anenar - iśānaśabdasyānyaniṣṭhatvākṣepamukhena phalato mumukṣukartṛkajijñāsyatvasyānyaniṣṭhatvākṣepāt jijñāsādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / tatheśānākhyo viṣayaśca sūcitaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.7.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the coordination of the word '<s>Īśāna</s>' (ruler) is carried out. He indicates the <s>śruti</s>-connection, the subject matter, and the doubt — beginning with '<s>Viṣṇureva</s>' (Viṣṇu alone). In the <s>Jijñāsā-sūtra</s> (<s>BS</s> 1.1.1), it was stated that <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is to be inquired into by all those seeking liberation, for the sake of liberation — this is the meaning. Nor should it be objected that in that [sūtra] only the exclusion of the impossibility of being the object of inquiry was made, not the exclusion of [inquiry into] others. For if another were also to be inquired into, the consequence would be that it too would be a bestower of liberation, and then the explanatory statements like 'Without the grace of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' etc. would be inapplicable — hence the exclusion of [inquiry into] others is also intended there. Therefore, the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) here should be explained as applying in both directions. Then what? To this he says — '<s>tatra</s>' (in that context). And the following also recurs: '<s>tatra</s>' — the indeclinable is also used in the sense of '<s>tad</s>' (that). And thus, when the inquiry into <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone was stated previously in '<s>athāto brahmajijñāsā</s>' (now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>) — '<s>tatra</s>' — regarding that inquiry — '<s>tatra</s>' — in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> passage, after stating '<s>Īśāno bhūtabhavyasya</s>' (the ruler of past and future, <s>Kaṭha</s> 4.12), in the passage beginning with '<s>ūrdhvam</s>' (upward), '<s>kaścit</s>' — a certain ruler — is apprehended as the subject. How? Because he 'is worshipped by all gods' — is apprehended as one to be inquired into by them — therefore — this is the sentence construction. Nor should it be objected that even though <s>Vāyu</s> is worshipped by all gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being worshipped by all gods is not negated — because even so, the restrictive statement that <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is to be inquired into by all seekers of liberation remains unestablished. Nor should it be objected that the word '<s>Viśvedeva</s>' (all gods) in the <s>śruti</s> denotes a specific class [of deities] and therefore the statement 'worshipped by all gods' is inapplicable — because if it refers to a specific class, the superiority of attributes cannot be established, and hence the meaning 'all gods' is necessarily intended. By this — through the objection regarding the word '<s>Īśāna</s>' (ruler) as applying to someone other than [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], and consequentially the objection that the inquiry-by-seekers-of-liberation could apply to another, the connection with the <s>Jijñāsādhikaraṇa</s> through objection is stated. Likewise, the subject called '<s>Īśāna</s>' is indicated.

BBsBhDīp 1,3.7.2:
He presents the prima facie view with reasoning — beginning with '<s>sa ca</s>' (and that). // Here the construction is as follows: 'and that' — the <s>Īśāna</s> who is worshipped by all gods — 'could be <s>Vāyu</s> alone, not <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' Why? Because in this context the hearing of the establishment of vital breaths [is present]. Also because of the statement of middling nature, and because of the statement of being worshipped by all gods. Nor is it the case that these cannot be established as belonging to <s>Vāyu</s> alone — because this <s>Vāyu</s>, through the passage '<s>evam eva eṣa prāṇaḥ</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 3.4), '<s>yo ayaṃ madhyamaḥ</s>,' '<s>kuvid aṅga</s>' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 7.91.1) and such passages, is apprehended as possessing the establishment of vital breaths and the like — therefore [he is <s>Vāyu</s>]. For in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> —

children.text: ityanena bhagavato 'ṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ pūrṇaṣaḍguṇatvaṃ dehamadhyasthatvaṃ bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamāneśānatvamityādimāhātmyamabhidhāyeśānapadoktasya tasyaiva 'ūrdhvam'; ityādinā mahimāntaramucyate / tatra madhyaśabdaḥ siddhānte ūrdhvaṃpratyakchabdasamabhivyāhārāt deśaviśeṣavacanaḥ, natvavāntareśvaratvādirūpamadhyamatvārthakaḥ / tathā ca yaḥ prāṇākhyarūpeṇa 'prāṇaṃ'; prāṇākhyavāyumūrdhvam 'unnayati'; udgamayati ūrdhvagatimattayā prerayati / apānarūpī cāpānākhyaṃ vāyuṃ 'pratyak'; adhastādviṇmūtrādiniṣkāsanahetutayā 'asyati'; nirasyati prerayatīti yāvat / taṃ 'dehamadhye'; hṛdaye 'āsīnam'; upaviṣṭaṃ 'vāmanaṃ'; saundaryapradhānāḥ striyo vāmāḥ tāḥ netāraṃ viṣṇuṃ 'viśve devāḥ'; sarve devāḥ 'upāsate'; jijñāsanta iti siddhāntarītyā śrutyarthaḥ / pūrvapakṣī tvidaṃ vāyuparaṃ matvā madhyaśabdo 'yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ'; iti śrutyantarasamākhyānānmadhyameśvaratvavacano na deśaviśeṣavacana ityāha / 'evam'; iti ṣaṭpraśnavākyaṃ ca 'yathā samrāḍevādhikṛtānviniyuṅkte etāngrāmānadhitiṣṭhasveti'; iti dṛṣṭāntavākyena saha vyākhyeyam / tatprakārastu - yathā 'samrāṭ'; sārvabhaumaḥ 'adhikṛtān niyogino 'dhikṛtya viniyuṅkte'; / katham? tvam 'etān'; pāṭalīputrādīn grāmān 'adhitiṣṭhasva'; tadādhipatyena tiṣṭhasveti / 'evamevaiṣaḥ'; 'ātmata eṣa prāṇo jāyate'; (praśna. 3-2.) ityātmajātatvenokto mukhyaprāṇaḥ 'itarān'; bhinnān svajanyatvenopacāreṇātmapravibhāgān prāṇān vāyūn pṛthaksthāneṣu hṛdayādiṣu sthāpayatīti / 'yo 'yam'; ityādibṛhadāraṇyakavākyam / tatra hi pūrvaṃ vāgādīnāṃ mṛtyugrastatvamuktvā 'athainameva nāpnot'; ityanena mukhyaprāṇasya tadanāttatvena tebhyaḥ śraiṣṭhyamabhidhāya 'yo 'yam'; ityanena prāṇaśabdavācyeṣu viṣṇuvāyutaditareṣu cetaneṣu triṣu viṣṇoruttamatvādanyeṣāmadhamatvādvāyormadhyamatvādasmānnimittādvā avāntareśvaratvādvā mukhyaprāṇasya sarvottamatvarūpakāṣṭhātvāvirodhimadhyasthatvamevocyate, na tu madhyadeśasthatvam / tathā tatraiva caturthādhyāye 'ayaṃ vāva śiśuḥ yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ'; (bṛ. 4-2-1.) iti candrikodāhṛte vākye sthūladehākhyavistṛtapradeśagataliṅgaśarīrarūpagṛhe viṣṇurūpāyāṃ sthūṇāyām annākhyena śrīrūpeṇa dāmnā baddho govatsarūpovāyurmadhyamatvenocyate /
kuvidaṅga namasā ye vṛdhāsaḥ purā devā anavadyāsa āsan /
children.translated_text: Did those gods who formerly were blameless by worship
settle for <s>Vāyu</s>, for <s>Manu</s> who was pressed, the <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) along with <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun)?

By this [passage], having described the Lord's greatness — being of thumb-measure, full possession of the six attributes, dwelling in the middle of the body, and lordship over past, present, and future — the further greatness of that very one denoted by the word '<s>Īśāna</s>' is stated by the passage beginning with '<s>ūrdhvam</s>' (upward). There, the word '<s>madhya</s>' (middle) in the <s>siddhānta</s>, being used in conjunction with '<s>ūrdhvam</s>' (upward) and '<s>pratyak</s>' (inward), denotes a specific location, not middling-lordship or such a meaning. And thus, He who, in the form called <s>Prāṇa</s>, 'leads upward' — causes to ascend, impels to upward motion — '<s>prāṇam</s>' — the vital breath called <s>prāṇa</s>; and in the form of <s>apāna</s>, '<s>pratyak</s>' — downward — '<s>asyati</s>' — casts, impels, i.e., drives the <s>apāna</s> breath downward as the cause of the expulsion of feces, urine, etc. Him — seated 'in the middle of the body' — in the heart — '<s>āsīnam</s>' — enthroned — '<s>Vāmanam</s>' — the leader of <s>vāmā</s>s (beautiful women, in whom beauty predominates), i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s> — '<s>viśve devāḥ</s>' — all the gods — '<s>upāsate</s>' — inquire into: this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> according to the <s>siddhānta</s>. The prima facie view, however, considering this passage to refer to <s>Vāyu</s>, says: the word '<s>madhya</s>' (middle), because of the designation in the other <s>śruti</s> '<s>yo ayaṃ madhyamaḥ</s>' (this middling one), denotes middling-lordship, not a specific location. The <s>Praśna</s> passage '<s>evam</s>' (thus) should be explained along with the simile passage 'Just as an emperor assigns his officers — you preside over these villages.' The manner of that [simile] is: just as an 'emperor' — a universal sovereign — 'assigns his officers' — having appointed his officials, 'commands' [them] — 'How? You preside over these villages such as <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>' — stand as their lord. '<s>Evam eva eṣaḥ</s>' — the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> stated as 'born from the self' (<s>Praśna</s> 3.2) — '<s>itarān</s>' — the different [vital breaths], figuratively called his own divisions — places in separate locations such as the heart and so on. '<s>Yo ayam</s>' — this <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> passage [is as follows]: there, having first stated that speech and the other [faculties] were seized by death, by the statement '<s>athainam eva nāpnot</s>' (but him it did not seize), the superiority of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> over them, by virtue of not being seized by death, having been stated, by '<s>yo ayam</s>' — among those denoted by the word <s>prāṇa</s>, namely <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the other sentient beings — the three — because of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s being the highest and the others' being the lowest, <s>Vāyu</s>'s middling nature — whether because of this reason or because of sub-lordship — the middling position that does not contradict <s>Mukhyaprāṇa</s>'s supreme excellence is stated, not middling spatial position. Likewise, in the same [<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>] in the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>, the passage cited in the <s>Candrikā</s> — 'This indeed is a child — this middling <s>Prāṇa</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.2.1) — in the house-form of the subtle body (<s>liṅga-śarīra</s>) which pervades the extensive region called the gross body, <s>Vāyu</s> in the form of a bull-calf, bound with a rope in the form of <s>Śrī</s> called food, to the pillar in the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is spoken of as middling.

children.text:
iti ṛṅmantre 'aṅga'; iti priyasambodhanam / tathā ca ye devāḥ vāyoḥ 'namasā'; namaskāropalakṣitasevādinā 'vṛdhāsaḥ'; vṛddhā jñānādiguṇapūrṇāḥ 'anavadyāsaḥ'; anavadyāḥ ajñānarāgādyavadyavidhurāśca purā sasūryā āsan / te 'kuvit'; kvacidrahasyasthāne sūryeṇa sākaṃ 'manave'; jñānine 'bādhitāyā'; saṃsārakleśavadbhiḥ śaraṇaṃ prāptāya 'vāyave'; vāyumuddiśya 'uṣasam'; uṣa prakāśe, asun, buddhim 'avāsayan'; tadviṣayāmakurvanniti śrutyarthaḥ /
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // 'vāmanaśabdāt'; vāmanaśruteḥ / evakāro vāyuliṅgasadbhāvāt vāyureveśānaḥ kiṃ na syāditi codyaparihārāya liṅgebhyaḥ śruteḥ prābalyamāha / yathoktaṃ sudhāyām - evaśabdavyākhyānaṃ balavaditi 'śabdādeva pramitaḥ'; iti yatheti / samanvayasūtrādanuvṛttasya tadityasyārtho viṣṇuriti / vidheyabhūtaviṣṇutvasyānvayayogyoddeśyadyotanāyetiśabdaprayogaḥ / āvartate cāyam / itiśabdātparamapi evaśabdo yojyaḥ / tenānuvṛttastu śabdo vyākhyātaḥ / tathā car 'iśāno bhūtabhavyasya'; (kaṭha. 4-12.) iti śrutar iśāno viṣṇureva bhavet / kutaḥ? yastatra pramito viṣṇāveva mahāyogavidvadrūḍhibhyāṃ prasiddho 'madhye vāmanam'; itiśruto vāmanaśabdastasmādeveti yojanā / pramitapadaṃ śruterniravakāśatvasūcakam / anena sūtre itiśabdo 'dhyāhārya iti sūcitam / tathā car 'iśāno bhūtabhavyasya'; itiśrutariśānaḥ 'tattu'; viṣṇureva bhavet / kutaḥ? yastatra viṣṇāveva pramito mahāyogavidvadrūḍhibhyāṃ prasiddho 'nyatra niravakāśo 'madhye vāmanamāsīnam'; (kaṭha. 5-3.) itiśruto liṅgātprabalo vāmanaśabdastacchrutistasmāditi sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Ṛg</s>-mantra, '<s>aṅga</s>' is a term of affectionate address. And thus: those <s>devas</s> who, through '<s>namasā</s>' — service characterized by prostration and the like — of <s>Vāyu</s>, are '<s>vṛdhāsaḥ</s>' — grown, i.e., replete with qualities such as knowledge; '<s>anavadyāsaḥ</s>' — faultless, free from defects such as ignorance and passion; they formerly existed together with the sun. They, '<s>kuvit</s>' — at some secret place, together with the sun, for '<s>manave</s>' — the knower, for '<s>bādhitāyā</s>' — one who has taken refuge, afflicted by the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, '<s>vāyave</s>' — directed toward <s>Vāyu</s>, '<s>uṣasam</s>' — '<s>uṣa</s>' means illumination, '<s>asun</s>' means intellect — '<s>avāsayan</s>' — they made it directed toward that. This is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.
Having introduced the <s>sūtra</s> that states the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), he explains it beginning with '<s>ataḥ</s>.' '<s>Vāmanaśabdāt</s>' means: because of the <s>Vāmana</s> <s>śruti</s>. The word '<s>eva</s>' is used to repudiate the objection 'Since there are indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>) for <s>Vāyu</s>, why should <s>Vāyu</s> alone not be <s>Īśāna</s>?' — it declares the superiority of <s>śruti</s> over <s>liṅga</s>. As stated in the <s>Sudhā</s>: 'The explanation of the word <s>eva</s> is <s>balavat</s> (stronger),' thus '<s>śabdādeva pramitaḥ</s>' is to be understood accordingly. The meaning of '<s>tat</s>' continuing from the <s>Samanvaya Sūtra</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The word '<s>iti</s>' is used to illuminate the referent suitable for syntactic connection with <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood, which is the predicate. And this recurs. The word '<s>eva</s>' should be connected even after the word '<s>iti</s>'. By this, the continuing word '<s>śabda</s>' is explained. And thus, from the <s>śruti</s> '<s>īśāno bhūtabhavyasya</s>' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 4.12), <s>Īśāna</s> would be <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Why? Because the word <s>Vāmana</s>, heard as '<s>madhye vāmanam</s>', which is '<s>pramita</s>' — established through conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) among great yogis and the learned as referring only to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — is therefore the <s>Vāmana</s> word; hence the construction. The word '<s>pramita</s>' indicates that the <s>śruti</s> leaves no scope [for alternative interpretation]. By this it is indicated that the word '<s>iti</s>' is to be supplied in the <s>sūtra</s>. And thus, from the <s>śruti</s> '<s>īśāno bhūtabhavyasya</s>', <s>Īśāna</s> — '<s>tat tu</s>' — would be <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Why? Because the word <s>Vāmana</s>, heard as '<s>madhye vāmanam āsīnam</s>' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 5.3), which is '<s>pramita</s>' — established through conventional usage among great yogis and the learned as referring only to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, leaving no scope elsewhere — is a <s>śruti</s> statement stronger than <s>liṅga</s>; therefore, this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
For <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) is not stronger than <s>śruti</s> (direct scriptural statement).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.7.3:
sūtre evakāraprayogena sūcitaṃ śruteḥ prābalyaṃ liṅgasya prābalyaniṣedhamukhena darśayati - na hīti // śruteriti pañcamī / hiśabdo vakṣyamāṇapramāṇavirodhāditi hetusūcakaḥ / tathā ca 'hi'; yasmāt na śruterliṅgaṃ balavat, kintu durbalameva / tasmālliṅagāt prabalāt vāmanaśabdādeveśāno viṣṇurevetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.7.3:
By using the word '<s>eva</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s>, having indicated the superiority of <s>śruti</s>, he shows it through negation of the superiority of <s>liṅga</s> — beginning with '<s>na hi</s>.' The fifth case ending applies to '<s>śruteḥ</s>'. The word '<s>hi</s>' indicates the reason, namely contradiction with the authority about to be stated. And thus, '<s>hi</s>' — since <s>liṅga</s> is not stronger than <s>śruti</s>, but rather is weak indeed — therefore, from the <s>Vāmana</s> word, which is stronger than <s>liṅga</s>, <s>Īśāna</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — this is the meaning.

children.text:
śrutirliṅgaṃ samākhyā ca vākyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ tathā /
pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ balīyaḥ syādevamāgamanirṇayaḥ / iti skānde /
children.translated_text: <s>Śruti</s> (direct statement), <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark), <s>samākhyā</s> (designation), <s>vākya</s> (sentence), and <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context) — each preceding one is stronger than the following; thus is the determination of scripture. — So says the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.7.4:
kuto na śruterliṅgaṃ balavadityatastathāsati śruterliṅgātprābalyavacanavirodhāpatterityāśayena tadvākyaṃ paṭhati - śrutiriti // iti skānda ityanantaraṃ vacanāditi śeṣaḥ / asya na hītyanenānvayaḥ / vācakaśabdaḥśrutiḥ / asādhāraṇadharmo vā, tadbodhakaśabdo vā liṅgam / nirṇītasyānyatra samānoktiḥ samākhyā / sā dvividhā - arthataśśabdato 'pīti / samabhivyāhṛtapadairevākāṅkṣāpūrtau tacchāntyarthaṃ padāntaranirapekṣāṇi padāni vākyam / ekaprameyapratipādakānekavākyāni prakaraṇam / anuktasthānasamuccaye tathetiśabdaḥ / anekaprameyapratipādakamekārthatātparyayuktaṃ vacanaṃ sthānam / atra 'vākyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sthānaṃ samākhyā ca tathāvidhā'; ityanuvyākhyānusāreṇa samākhyāyāḥ sthānānantaryameva grāhyaṃ, na tvatroktakramānusāreṇa vākyādyapekṣayā prāthamyam / atroktakramasyāvivakṣitatvāt / uktaṃ hi pramāṇalakṣaṇaṭīkāyāṃ - samākhyāditvena grahaṇaṃ 'śrutirliṅgaṃ samākhyā ca'; ityavivakṣitakramaṃ vākyamanusṛtyeti / ata eva jaiminiḥ - 'śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ samavāye pāradaurbalyamarthaviprakarṣāt'; iti smṛtyuktādanyathākramamāha - pūrvaṃpūrvamiti / pūrvoddiṣṭamityarthaḥ / ekatra samavetaṃ viruddhamiti ca śeṣaḥ / 'balīyaḥ'; atiśayena svabhāvato balavat yathātraivādhikaraṇe anantaroddiṣṭaliṅgāpekṣayā pūrvoddiṣṭā vāmanaśrutiḥ svataḥ prabalā/ vākyāpekṣayā prabalaṃ liṅgam/ yathā - daharādhikaraṇe daharākāśasya sākṣātsarvādhāratvaprāpakāt 'kiṃ tadatra vidyate ..... ubhe asmin dyāvāpṛthivī'; (chāṃ. 8-1-2,3.) iti vākyātprabalaṃ viṣṇostatprāpakāpahatapāpmatvādikaṃ liṅgam / prakaraṇāpekṣayā prabalaṃ vākyam/ yathā - jyotirdarśanāt ityadhikaraṇe jīvasya 'hṛdyantarjyotiḥ'; (bṛ. 6-3-7.) itivākyabodhyajyotiṣṭvasādhakājjīvaprakaraṇātprabalaṃ viṣṇorjyotiṣṭvaprāpakaṃ 'katama ātmā'; (bṛ. 6-3-7.) iti praśnavākyam / sthānāpekṣayā prabalaṃ prakaraṇam / yathā - samagropaniṣadar iśvaraparatvasādhakāt ṣaṭpraśnarūpasthānāt prabalam 'ātmata eṣa prāṇo jāyate'; (praśna. 3-3.) ityetatkhaṇḍarūpaṃ mukhyaprāṇaprakaraṇam / ata evātrādhikaraṇe ṣaṭpraśnoktaprāṇavyavasthāpakatvādīnāṃ mukhyaprāṇaliṅgatvamupetya śrutyā bādha uktaḥ / samākhyāpekṣayā prabalaṃ sthānam / yathā - annamayādiśabdānāṃ kośaparatvasādhakāt 'annamayaprāṇamayamanomayavijñānamayānandamayā me śudhyantām'; (yājñikī. 66.) iti nārāyaṇānuvākasamākhyāyāḥ prabalaṃ teṣāṃ viṣṇutvasādhakaṃ brahmaparānekaprakaraṇasandarbharūpaṃ sthānam / etānyeva śrutyādinār'thanirṇayasthalāni / ādyayā samākhyayā nirṇetavyaṃ yathā - puruṣasūktasamākhyayā vaiśvānarasya viṣṇutvam / dvitīyayā yathā - ambhraṇīsūktasamākhyayā viśvakarmasūktoktasyājasya viṣṇutvam / astvevaṃ tataḥ kimityata āha - evamiti / viruddhaiteṣāṃ samavāye sati prabalena pūrveṇottarabādhe ca sati 'āgamanirṇayaḥ'; āgamārthasya vipratipannasyaitaiḥ nirṇayo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.7.4:
Why is <s>liṅga</s> not stronger than <s>śruti</s>? Because if it were so, there would be contradiction with the statement declaring the superiority of <s>śruti</s> over <s>liṅga</s> — with this intent, he cites that statement beginning with '<s>śrutiḥ</s>.' After '<s>iti skānde</s>' (thus in the <s>Skānda</s>), '<s>vacanāt</s>' (because of the statement) is to be supplied. This connects with '<s>na hi</s>' (for not). The directly denoting word is <s>śruti</s>. A distinguishing characteristic, or the word conveying it, is <s>liṅga</s>. The statement of what has been determined elsewhere in similar terms is <s>samākhyā</s> (designation). It is of two kinds — by meaning and by word. The words that, through co-occurring words alone, fulfill mutual expectancy without depending on additional words for that purpose, constitute <s>vākya</s> (sentence). Multiple sentences establishing a single subject constitute <s>prakaraṇa</s> (context). The word '<s>tathā</s>' is for the inclusion of the unmentioned category of <s>sthāna</s> (position). A single statement with purposive unity that establishes multiple subjects is <s>sthāna</s>. Here, following the sub-commentary (<s>anuvyākhyāna</s>) which reads '<s>vākyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ sthānaṃ samākhyā ca tathāvidhā</s>', the position of <s>samākhyā</s> should be taken as after <s>sthāna</s>, not as having priority over <s>vākya</s> and the rest according to the order stated here — since the order stated here is not intended. As stated in the <s>Pramāṇalakṣaṇa Ṭīkā</s>: 'The inclusion as <s>samākhyādi</s> follows the verse "<s>śrutir liṅgaṃ samākhyā ca</s>" where the order is not intended.' Therefore <s>Jaimini</s> states a different order from that stated in the <s>smṛti</s>: '<s>śruti-liṅga-vākya-prakaraṇa-sthāna-samākhyānāṃ samavāye pāradaurbalyam arthaviprakarṣāt</s>' — he says '<s>pūrvaṃ pūrvam</s>' meaning 'the one mentioned earlier.' And 'when they are conflicting in the same place' is to be supplied. '<s>Balīyaḥ</s>' — inherently stronger by nature. For example, in this very <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), the <s>Vāmana śruti</s>, mentioned earlier, is inherently stronger than the <s>liṅga</s> mentioned immediately after. <s>Liṅga</s> is stronger than <s>vākya</s> — for example, in the <s>Dahara-adhikaraṇa</s>, the <s>liṅga</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of freedom from sin and the like, which establishes [His nature], is stronger than the <s>vākya</s> 'What is there in that [space]... in it are both heaven and earth' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 8.1.2-3), which directly conveys that the <s>Dahara-ākāśa</s> is the support of all. <s>Vākya</s> is stronger than <s>prakaraṇa</s> — for example, in the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> beginning with '<s>jyotir darśanāt</s>', the question-sentence '<s>katama ātmā</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.7), which conveys <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s nature as light, is stronger than the <s>jīva</s>-context, which proves the <s>jīva</s>'s nature as light through the <s>vākya</s> '<s>hṛdy antarjyotiḥ</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.7). <s>Prakaraṇa</s> is stronger than <s>sthāna</s> — for example, the <s>Mukhya Prāṇa</s> context in the section '<s>ātmata eṣa prāṇo jāyate</s>' (<s>Praśna Upaniṣad</s> 3.3) is stronger than the <s>sthāna</s> in the form of six questions, which establishes the supremacy of <s>Īśvara</s> throughout the entire <s>Upaniṣad</s>. Therefore, in this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, having accepted that the establishment of <s>Prāṇa</s> as stated in the six questions and the like constitutes <s>liṅga</s> for <s>Mukhya Prāṇa</s>, its being overridden by <s>śruti</s> has been stated. <s>Sthāna</s> is stronger than <s>samākhyā</s> — for example, the <s>sthāna</s> in the form of the collection of multiple <s>Brahman</s>-related contexts, which establishes that <s>Annamaya</s> and the rest are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is stronger than the <s>Nārāyaṇānuvāka samākhyā</s> '<s>annamaya-prāṇamaya-manomaya-vijñānamaya-ānandamayā me śudhyantām</s>' (<s>Yājñikī</s> 66), which establishes that the words <s>Annamaya</s> and the rest refer to sheaths (<s>kośa</s>). These alone are the grounds for determining the meaning of <s>śruti</s> and the rest. Through the first kind of <s>samākhyā</s>, what is to be determined — for example, the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> through the designation of the <s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s>. Through the second kind — for example, the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the unborn one mentioned in the <s>Viśvakarma Sūkta</s> through the designation of the <s>Ambhraṇī Sūkta</s>. If so, what follows from this? — to this he says '<s>evam</s>.' When these conflicting [criteria] are present together, and when the stronger preceding one overrides the later, '<s>āgamanirṇayaḥ</s>' — the meaning of scripture that is disputed is determined by these; this is the meaning.

children.text:
tacca liṅgaṃ viṣṇoreva / tasyaiva prāṇatvokteḥ 'tadvai tvaṃ prāṇo
abhavaḥ'; iti // 24 //
children.translated_text: And that <s>liṅga</s> (indicatory mark) belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, because of the statement that He alone is <s>Prāṇa</s>: 'You indeed became <s>Prāṇa</s>' — thus. // 24 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.7.5:
nanvastu śruteḥ svabhāvataḥ prābalyam / tathāpi bāhulyena pūrvapakṣyuktaliṅgānāmapi prābalyātsāmyenānirṇaya evetyata āha - tacceti // castvarthaḥ / liṅgamiti samudāyaikavacanam / tathā ca 'tat'; pūrvavādyuktaṃ liṅgajātaṃ tu viṣṇoreva yuktam, na vāyorityarthaḥ / tathā ca bāhulye 'pi liṅgānāṃ sāvakāśatvāttebhyaḥ śruterekasyā api niravakāśāyāḥ prābalyānnānirṇaya iti bhāvaḥ / nanu na liṅgaṃ viṣṇau sāvakāśaṃ, pūrvapakṣyudāhṛtasamākhyārūpaśrutyantareṇa tasya prāṇaniṣṭhatayaivoktatvādityata āha - tasyaiveti / 'tadvai tvam'; iti śrutau 'tasya'; viṣṇoḥ prāṇatvasya prāṇaśabdavācyatvasyokteruktatvādityarthaḥ / evaṃ 'ata eva'; ityatrādhyātmikāśeṣaśabdasya samanvayaṃ bruvatā tathā - 'śāstradṛṣṭyā'; ityatrāntaryāmiparatvaṃ bruvatā sūtrakāreṇetaravyāvṛttyā tasyaiva prāṇatvokteḥ sādhitatvādityapi vyākhyeyametat / tathā ca śrutyantare prāṇaniṣṭhatayā liṅgasyoktāvapi na tadvirodhaḥ / tasya prāṇasya viṣṇutvābhyupagamāditi bhāvaḥ / nanu tathāpi 'kuvidaṅga'; iti ṛci vāyuniṣṭhatayā liṅgoktestadvirodha ityasyāpīdamevottaram / asmin pakṣe prāṇatvamiti vāyutvamupalakṣyate / tathā cāntarnaye ādhidaivikāśeṣaśabdasamanvayaṃ bruvatā sūtrakāreṇa 'tasyaiva'; viṣṇoreva 'prāṇatvokteḥ'; vāyuśabdavācyatvarūpavāyutsyoktatvādityarthaḥ / tathā ca na tadvirodhopīti bhāvaḥ / na ca siddhānte 'pi sthānāpekṣayā prabalātprakaraṇāt 'evamevaiṣaḥ'; itiśrutyantaragataprāṇaśabdasya, tathā 'yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ'; (bṛ. 3.5-21.) ityasya, tathā 'kuvidaṅga'; iti mantrasthavāyuśabdasya mukhyavāyuparatvaṃ, tatroktaliṅgānāmapi tatparatvamupetya teṣāṃ śrutyā bādhasyoktatvāt kathaṃ śrutyantarasthaprāṇavāyuśabdayoḥ viṣṇuparatvāṅgīkāreṇa samādhānam / ata eva candrikāyām - madhyamaśabdo 'pi 'ūrdhvaṃ prāṇam'; (kaṭha. 2-2-3.) iti prāṇasya sthānāntaranirdeśāttatyāgena madhyamasthānasthabrahmaparaḥ, na tu śrutyantare madhyamaśabdoktaprāṇapara ityuktam / ataḥ 'evamevaiṣaḥ'; (praśna. 3-4.) iti vākyaṃ sthānātprakaraṇasya prābalye udāhṛtamiti vācyam / uktarītyā mukhyataḥ śrutyantaragataprāṇaśabdāderbrahmaparatvena liṅgānāṃ tattadantaryāminiṣṭhatve 'pi samākarṣanyāyenānyaparatvasyāpyaṅgīkārāt / śrutyantaroktaliṅgānāmanyaniṣṭhatve 'pi vā nānupapattiḥ / na caivaṃ kāṭhakoktaliṅgānāmapyanyaniṣṭhatvāpattyā anyeṣāmīśānatvādyāpattiḥ / niravakāśaśrutyā kāṭhakoktaliṅgānāṃ viṣṇuniṣṭhatānirṇayopapatteḥ / nanu tathāpi kathamīśāno viṣṇurbhavecchrutāvīśānasyāṅguṣṭhaparimitatvokteḥ / sarvagate ca harau tadayogāt / na ca vyomavatsarvagatasyāpyaṇutvaṃ yujyata iti pratipāditamiti vācyam / tathāpi 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ'; iti tanmātraparimāṇatvokterayogāt / na ca 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ'; ityatra śrutaḥ parimāṇārthako mātracpratyaya eva, na tvavadhāraṇārthako mātraśabdaḥ / 'dehāṅguṣṭhamito dehe jīvāṅguṣṭhamito hṛdi'; iti smṛtau mita ityanena parimāṇasyaivokteḥ / tathā ca nānupapattiriti vācyam / tathātve 'ṅguṣṭhamātratvābhidhātryām 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ'; (kaṭha. 4-12.) iti śrutau 'madhya ātmani'; ityasya smṛtau hṛdītyasya ca vaiyarthyāpātāt / tanmātraparimitatvoktyarthaṃ hi tatra hṛdayarūpasūkṣmasthānoktiḥ / tasmādavadhāraṇārthakamātraśabda evāyamaṅgīkāryaḥ uktaṃ hi candrikāyām - mātraśabdasyāvadhāraṇārthakatvāditi /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.7.5:
Granted, let <s>śruti</s> be inherently stronger. Even so, since the <s>liṅga</s>s mentioned by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> are numerous, there would be equality and hence indeterminacy — to this he says '<s>tat ca</s>.' '<s>Ca</s>' means '<s>tu</s>' (but). '<s>Liṅgam</s>' is a collective singular. And thus, '<s>tat</s>' — the collection of <s>liṅga</s>s mentioned by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> — is fitting for <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not for <s>Vāyu</s>; this is the meaning. And thus, even though the <s>liṅga</s>s are numerous, since they have alternative scope (<s>sāvakāśa</s>), even a single <s>śruti</s> that has no alternative scope (<s>niravakāśa</s>) is stronger than them; hence there is no indeterminacy — this is the purport. But the <s>liṅga</s> does not have alternative scope in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since it has been stated as pertaining to <s>Prāṇa</s> alone by means of the <s>samākhyā</s>-type <s>śruti</s> cited by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> — to this he says '<s>tasyaiva</s>.' In the <s>śruti</s> '<s>tad vai tvam</s>', because of the statement of <s>Prāṇa</s>-hood — that is, of being denoted by the word <s>Prāṇa</s> — of '<s>tasya</s>' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, this is the meaning. Thus, by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> who, in '<s>ata eva</s>', states the syntactic connection of all spiritual (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) words, and in '<s>śāstradṛṣṭyā</s>', declares the reference to the Inner Controller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>) — by excluding others, the statement of His alone being <s>Prāṇa</s> has been established; thus this should also be explained. And therefore, even when <s>liṅga</s> has been stated as pertaining to <s>Prāṇa</s> in another <s>śruti</s>, there is no contradiction, because it is accepted that that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the purport. But even so, since <s>liṅga</s> has been stated as pertaining to <s>Vāyu</s> in the <s>ṛc</s> '<s>kuvid aṅga</s>', there is contradiction — to this too, this same is the answer. In this interpretation, '<s>Prāṇa</s>-hood' is used as an indicator for '<s>Vāyu</s>-hood.' And thus, by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> who states the syntactic connection of all <s>ādhidaivika</s> (cosmic) words through the internal interpretation (<s>antarnaya</s>), '<s>tasyaiva</s>' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — '<s>prāṇatvokteḥ</s>' — because of the statement of being denoted by the word <s>Vāyu</s>; this is the meaning. And thus there is no contradiction — this is the purport. Nor [can one object that] even in the <s>siddhānta</s>, from the <s>prakaraṇa</s> which is stronger than <s>sthāna</s>, the word <s>Prāṇa</s> occurring in other <s>śruti</s>s like '<s>evam evaiṣaḥ</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 3.4), and similarly '<s>yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.5.21), and the word <s>Vāyu</s> in the mantra '<s>kuvid aṅga</s>', all refer to <s>Mukhya Prāṇa</s>, and the <s>liṅga</s>s stated there also refer to him, and their being overridden by <s>śruti</s> has been stated — so how can the words <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> in other <s>śruti</s>s be reconciled as referring to <s>Viṣṇu</s>? Therefore in the <s>Candrikā</s> it is said: the word '<s>madhyama</s>' too refers to <s>Brahman</s> situated in the middle region, since <s>Prāṇa</s>'s location is indicated elsewhere by '<s>ūrdhvaṃ prāṇam</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.2.3), and by setting that aside, it refers to <s>Brahman</s> in the middle place, not to <s>Prāṇa</s> mentioned by the word '<s>madhyama</s>' in another <s>śruti</s>. Therefore it should be said that '<s>evam evaiṣaḥ</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 3.4) is cited as an example of <s>prakaraṇa</s> being stronger than <s>sthāna</s>. Because, by the method stated, primarily through the words <s>Prāṇa</s> and others in other <s>śruti</s>s referring to <s>Brahman</s>, even though the <s>liṅga</s>s pertain to the respective inner controllers, by the principle of attraction (<s>samākarṣa-nyāya</s>), reference to another is also accepted. Or even if the <s>liṅga</s>s stated in other <s>śruti</s>s pertain to another, there is no impossibility. Nor does this lead to the <s>liṅga</s>s stated in the <s>Kaṭha</s> also pertaining to another, resulting in others being <s>Īśāna</s> — because the determination that the <s>liṅga</s>s stated in the <s>Kaṭha</s> pertain to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established by <s>śruti</s> that has no alternative scope (<s>niravakāśa</s>). But even so, how can <s>Īśāna</s> be <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since the <s>śruti</s> states that <s>Īśāna</s> is of thumb-size? And since <s>Hari</s> is all-pervading, this is unfitting. Nor can one say that, like space, even what is all-pervading can be atomic, as has been established — for even so, there is the unfitness of the statement '<s>aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ</s>' declaring him to be of exactly that measure. And in '<s>aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ</s>', the <s>mātra</s>-suffix heard is indeed in the sense of measurement, not the word <s>mātra</s> in the sense of limitation — because in the <s>smṛti</s> '<s>dehāṅguṣṭhamito dehe jīvāṅguṣṭhamito hṛdi</s>', the word '<s>mita</s>' expresses measurement alone. Nor should one say there is no impossibility — for if it meant 'of exactly thumb-size,' then in the <s>śruti</s> '<s>aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 4.12), the phrases '<s>madhya ātmani</s>' and '<s>hṛdi</s>' in the <s>smṛti</s> would become purposeless. For the mention of the subtle location in the form of the heart is for the purpose of stating limitation to that measure. Therefore the word <s>mātra</s> should be accepted as having the sense of limitation alone. As stated in the <s>Candrikā</s>: 'Because the word <s>mātra</s> has the sense of limitation.'
<s>Sūtra</s> — Oṃ //
But [the thumb-measure is stated] with reference to [<s>Viṣṇu</s> dwelling in] the heart, because the subject matter pertains to human beings. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.25 |
Even though He is all-pervading, His being of thumb-measure (<s>aṅguṣṭhamātratva</s>) is fitting with reference to the space in the heart.

BBsBhDīp_1,3.7.6:
tathā ca sarvagate harāvaṅguṣṭhamātratvoktiranupapanneti nātreśāno viṣṇurityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya tadakṣarāṇi vyācaṣṭe - hṛdīti // sarvagatasyāpītyanena tuśabdo yadyapitathāpītyarthatayā vyākhyātaḥ / hṛdyapekṣayetyanena sūcitahetoranvayayogyaṃ sādhyaṃ darśayati - tasyeti / yojanā tu - yadyapi viṣṇuḥ sarvagatastathāpi 'tasyāṅguṣṭhamātratvam'; aṅguṣṭhamātratvoktiryujyate / katham? yato 'hṛdyavakāśopekṣayā'; hṛdi vidyamāno yo 'yamavakāśo 'ṅguṣṭhaparimitadeśastadapekṣayā tatrābhivyaktatāvatparibhitabhagavanmūrtiviśeṣamapekṣya tasya viṣṇoraṅguṣṭhamātratvam astyata iti/ yadvā - 'hṛdyavakāśāpekṣayā'; hṛdi vidyamānāvakāśamapekṣya tatsambandhāttasyāṅguṣṭhamātratvavacanaṃ yujyata ityāvṛttiṃ vinā yojanā / prathamapakṣe śaktyāparimite 'pi bhagavati mūrtiviśeṣe vyaktyātmanāṅguṣṭhamātratvasya sthānini brahmaṇi tatsambandhādupacāreṇoktiriti bhedaḥ / atra ṭīkāyāṃ hṛdyavakāśāpekṣayeti bhāṣyaṃ sāvadhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā sautratuśabdo 'vadhāraṇatayā vyākhyātaḥ / tena viṣṇoṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ hṛdyapekṣayaiva, na tu lokavatparicchinnatvādityuktaṃ bhavati / tattatsthāneṣu vyaktamūrtiviśeṣāpekṣayā vā upacāreṇa vā tattatparimāṇatvoktyā 'yastvetameva prādeśamātram'; (chāṃ. 5-18-1.) iti chāndogye 'prādeśamātraṃ puruṣam'; ityanyatra 'prādeśaḥ puruṣottamaḥ'; ityaparatra ca hṛdgatasya viṣṇoḥ prādeśaparimitatvokteḥ / 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ṅguṣṭhaṃ ca samāśritaḥ'; (mahānā. 16.3.) iti śrutyantare 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣaḥ'; iti kaṭhavalyāṃ ca 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣaḥ'; ityaparatra cāṅguṣṭhaparimitatvokteḥ 'aṅguṣṭhāgrapramāṇakaḥ'; iti kvacidaṅguṣṭhāgrapramāṇakatvoktervirodha iti codyaṃ parihṛtaṃ bhavati / dehe hṛdayākāśe prādeśaparimitarūpaviśeṣasya hṛdayagatakamalakarṇikāmūlagatākāśe 'ṅguṣṭhāgrapramāṇakarūpāntarasya karṇikāgragatākāśecāṅguṣṭhaparimitarūpāntarasya ca vyaktisambhavāt, tattatsthānadharmasya sthāninyupacaritatvasambhavācca / yathoktaṃ bṛhadāraṇyakabhāṣye -

children.translated_text: In the heart, all-pervading, of a span's measure, <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person),
designated as the abode of the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), eternal at all times.

BBsBhDīp 1,3.7.6:
And thus, resolving the doubt — 'the statement of being thumb-sized regarding <s>Hari</s> who is all-pervading is unjustified, therefore [the entity referred to] in "<s>na atreśānaḥ</s>" is not <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and explains its words beginning with '<s>hṛdi</s>' (in the heart). // By the phrase '<s>sarvagatasyāpi</s>' (even though all-pervading), the word '<s>tu</s>' is explained in the sense of 'even though... nevertheless.' By the phrase '<s>hṛdyapekṣayā</s>' (with reference to the heart), he shows the conclusion that is fit for connection with the reason indicated — with '<s>tasya</s>' (of Him). The construction is thus: even though <s>Viṣṇu</s> is all-pervading, nevertheless '<s>tasyāṅguṣṭhamātratva</s>' — the statement of being thumb-sized — is fitting. How? Because '<s>hṛdyavakāśāpekṣayā</s>' — with reference to the space present in the heart, which is a region limited to the size of a thumb; with reference to that, considering the specific manifest form of the Lord delimited within that [space], the thumb-sizedness of that <s>Viṣṇu</s> exists — thus. Alternatively, '<s>hṛdyavakāśāpekṣayā</s>' — considering the space present in the heart, the statement of His being thumb-sized is fitting due to its connection with that — this is the construction without repetition. In the first interpretation, the difference is that even though the Lord is unlimited in power, the statement is made figuratively (<s>upacāra</s>) regarding <s>Brahman</s> as the possessor of the locus, due to the thumb-sizedness belonging to a specific manifest form. In the <s>Ṭīkā</s> here, taking the <s>Bhāṣya</s> phrase '<s>hṛdyavakāśāpekṣayā</s>' as containing a restrictive sense, the word '<s>tu</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> is explained as expressing restriction. By this it is stated that the thumb-sizedness of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is only with reference to the heart, not due to His being limited as in worldly objects. With reference to the specific manifest forms in their respective locations, either directly or figuratively, through statements of their respective measurements — '<s>yastvetameva prādeśamātram</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.1), in the <s>Chāndogya</s> '<s>prādeśamātraṃ puruṣam</s>' (the <s>Puruṣa</s> of a span's measure), elsewhere '<s>prādeśaḥ puruṣottamaḥ</s>' (<s>Puruṣottama</s> of a span) — [we find] the statement that <s>Viṣṇu</s> dwelling in the heart is of span-measure; '<s>aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ṅguṣṭhaṃ ca samāśritaḥ</s>' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 16.3), in the <s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> '<s>aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣaḥ</s>' (the <s>Puruṣa</s> of thumb-measure), and elsewhere too the statement of thumb-sizedness; and somewhere '<s>aṅguṣṭhāgrapramāṇakaḥ</s>' (of the measure of the tip of the thumb) — the objection of contradiction is resolved. Because it is possible for a specific form of span-measure to manifest in the heart-space within the body, for another form of the measure of the tip of the thumb in the space at the root of the lotus-pericarp of the heart, and for yet another form of thumb-measure in the space at the top of the pericarp; and because it is possible for the property of the location to be figuratively attributed to the possessor of the location. As stated in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Bhāṣya</s> —
Situated at the root of the heart-lotus pericarp, He is of the measure of the tip of a thumb,

children.text: mūleśa iti nāmāsmin sarve jīvāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ //
children.translated_text: named '<s>Mūleśa</s>' (Lord of the Root) — in Him all <s>jīvas</s> are established.
In the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) of thumb-measure, in <s>Hari</s> situated at the top of the pericarp,

children.text: prāviśanti suṣuptau tu prabudhyante tatastathā // iti //
children.translated_text: the [<s>jīvas</s>] enter during deep sleep and awaken from there likewise. // Thus. //

children.text: asmin mūleśavyāpinormadhye 'ṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ ca dehe dehāṅguṣṭhamitatvaṃ jīvahṛdi jīvāṅguṣṭhamitatvamiti vivektavyam / atra 'aṅguṣṭhaṃ ca samāśritaḥ'; ityanena karmendriyādhiṣṭhitatvamucyata iti prameyadīpoktamapi jñātavyam / nanu 'dakṣiṇākṣimukhe viśvo manasyantastu taijasaḥ'; ityādivacanājjāgradādyavasthāprerakaviśvataijasaprājñānāṃ dakṣiṇākṣyādiṣu sattvaṃ tāvatsiddham / yadi caivaṃ tadā jīvo 'pi jāgradavasthāyāṃ dakṣiṇākṣisthaḥ svapne kaṇṭhadeśasthaḥ suptau hṛdayastho bhavati, 'hṛdayasthātparājjīvo dūrastho jāgradeṣyati'; ityukteḥ / dūrastho 'kṣistho jāgrajjāgratvamiti tasyārthaḥ / tathā ca kathaṃ hṛdayavyāptaprādeśaparimitabhagavadrūpasya sarvadā jīvasthānatvam? kathaṃ ca hṛtkarṇikāmūlagatabhagavadrūpe sadā pratiṣṭhito jīvaḥ? suptau hṛtkarṇikāgragate harau praviśatītyuktiriti cet - na, yatassarvadā hṛdi sthitameva jīvasvarūpaṃ jāgaritādāvakṣyādiṣvapi viśeṣasannihitaṃ dīpaprakāśavadityaṅgīkṛtam / yathoktamaitareyabhāṣye - hṛde sthitameva tasya rūpaṃ jāgarite 'pyakṣyādiṣu viśeṣasannihitaṃ bhavatīti / ekasyaiva jīvasya sthāpanadhṛtyākhyapratiṣṭhāpanasuptiprāpaṇākhyaprayojanabhedādekadehe anekadhā sthitānāṃ bhagavanmūrtīnāṃ śaktyā sarvagānāmapi tatra tatra vyaktyātmanā anekālpaparimāṇavattvaṃ ca yujyata iti na kācidanupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Among these — the <s>Mūleśa</s> form and the all-pervading form — the thumb-sizedness should be discriminated thus: in the body, it means being measured by the body's thumb; in the heart of the <s>jīva</s>, it means being measured by the <s>jīva's</s> thumb. Here, by the phrase '<s>aṅguṣṭhaṃ ca samāśritaḥ</s>' (and has resorted to the thumb), it should be known as stated in the <s>Prameya Dīpikā</s> that the superintendence over the organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>) is expressed. Now, [one might object]: from the statement '<s>dakṣiṇākṣimukhe viśvo manasyantastu taijasaḥ</s>' (the <s>Viśva</s> is in the right eye, the <s>Taijasa</s> is within the mind), the existence of <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Prājña</s> — who impel the states of waking and so forth — in the right eye and other locations is indeed established. And if so, the <s>jīva</s> too in the waking state is situated in the right eye, in dream in the throat region, and in deep sleep in the heart, because it is stated: '<s>hṛdayasthātparājjīvo dūrastho jāgradeṣyati</s>' (the <s>jīva</s>, being far from the heart, comes to the waking state at a distance). The meaning of that is: being at a distance [means] being in the eye; one who is awake has the state of waking. And if so, how can the Lord's form of span-measure pervading the heart be at all times the abode of the <s>jīva</s>? And how can the <s>jīva</s> be always established in the Lord's form situated at the root of the heart-lotus pericarp? If it be said that the statement about the <s>jīva</s> entering <s>Hari</s> who is at the top of the heart-pericarp is only during deep sleep — no, because it is accepted that the essential nature of the <s>jīva</s>, while always situated in the heart, is specially present also in the eyes and other [organs] during waking and so forth, like the light of a lamp. As stated in the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s>: 'Its form, while situated in the heart, is specially present in the eyes and other [organs] even during waking.' Since there are different purposes — placement (<s>sthāpana</s>), sustaining (<s>dhṛti</s>), establishing (<s>pratiṣṭhāpana</s>), and conveying to sleep (<s>suptiprāpaṇa</s>) — for the forms of the Lord situated in multiple ways in a single body, and since it is fitting that these forms, though all-pervading by their power, have multiple small measurements in their manifest aspect in those respective locations — there is no impossibility whatsoever.
Even though other living beings lack thumbs, there is no contradiction, because [Vedic meditation] has human beings as its qualified [practitioners]. // 25 //
// Thus ends the <s>Vāmanādhikaraṇa</s> (Section on the Dwarf). // 7 //
