BBsBhDīp_1,3.7.7:
nanu tathāpi nāṅguṣṭhaparimāṇavattvaṃ viṣṇoryuktam / tathā hi kiṃ tattadaṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ vā yatkiñcidaṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ vā / nādyaḥ, paśvādīnāmaṅguṣṭhābhāvena tadantargatasya viṣṇoraṅguṣṭhaparimitatvāyogāt / na dvitīyaḥ, aṅguṣṭhamātratvoktestaistaistathopāsanārthatvena tasya cāṅguṣṭhavyaktiviśeṣanirdhāraṇa vināyogena yatkiñcidaṅguṣṭhamātratvoktervyarthatvāt / pipīlikādihṛdayasthe 'ṅguṣṭhamātratvasābhānyasyāpyasambhavāccetyāśaṅkāṃ pariharan manuṣyādhikāratvāt itisūtraśeṣaṃ tuśabdasya kākākṣinyāyena atrāpyanvayaṃ tasyāpyarthatvaṃ ca abhipretya tatsambandhipradarśanapūrvakaṃ vyācaṣṭe - itareti // paśvādīnāmityarthaḥ / apirāvartate / aṅguṣṭhamātratvamityetat vipariṇāmevānuvartate / 'na virodhaḥ'; iti virodhasūtrādākṛṣṭe pade / tathā ca 'api'; tattadaṅguṣṭhaparimitatvāṅgīkāre 'pītaraprāṇināmaṅguṣṭhābhāve 'pi na viṣṇoraṅguṣṭhamātratvasya virodhenāṅguṣṭhamātratvokterasambhavaḥ / kutaḥ? aṅguṣṭhamātratvokteretadvidyāyā 'manuṣyādhikāratvāt'; manuṣyānadhikṛtya pravṛttatvāt / tadapi kutaḥ? vedavidyopāsanasya 'manuṣyādhikāratvāt'; manuṣyamātrādhikāratvāditi yojanā / sūtre bhāṣye ca manuṣyāṇāmadhikāro yasmin athavā - adhikriyate 'tretyadhikāra upāsanaṃ śāstraṃ vā, manuṣyāṇāmeva adhikāro manuṣyādhikārastasya bhāvasatasmāditi vigrahaḥ / 'manuṣyādhikāritvāt'; itipāṭhe manuṣyā adhikāriṇo yasmin tattathoktam / tathā ca manuṣyādhikārikatvādityarthaḥ / manuṣyapadaṃ ca vakṣyamāṇanyāyena mananādiśīlacetanaparam / tena devānāṃ jaritāryādīnāṃ vakṣyamāṇanyāyena vedavidyādhikāriṇāmetadvidyādhikārasiddhiḥ / tatra jaritāryādīnāṃ svasvāṅguṣṭhaparimitatvena bhagavadupāsanāsambhavāt, teṣāmetadvidyotpannavākyārthajñāna evādhikāro, nopāstāvapi / ata eva ṭīkāyāṃ manuṣyāṇāmeva vedavidyopāsanādhikāritveneti manuṣyatvaṃ vyāpakatvenoktam / na cānadhikāriṇāṃ paśvādīnāṃ dehasthitasya bhagavato 'ṅguṣṭhaparimitatvābhāve parimāṇāntarānukteradravyatvāpattiriti vācyam / paśvādidehagatasya paramātmanaḥ tattadākārayuktatvena tadanusāriparimāṇavattvāt / yathoktamaitareyabhāṣye - saṅkarṣaṇaśca pradyumnastadākārau nṛṣu sthitau /
nārāyaṇāniruddhau tu paśvākārau paśusthitau // iti //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.7.7:
But even so, the possession of thumb-measure by <s>Viṣṇu</s> is not justified. For consider: is it the thumb-measure of each respective [being], or just any arbitrary thumb-measure? Not the first, because animals and others lack thumbs, and hence <s>Viṣṇu</s> situated within them cannot be of thumb-measure. Not the second, because the statement of thumb-measure is for the purpose of meditation upon Him as such by those [practitioners], and without determination of a specific thumb [as reference], a statement of arbitrary thumb-measure would be purposeless; and because even an approximation to thumb-measure is impossible for [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] situated in the hearts of ants and such [tiny creatures]. Resolving this doubt, and intending that the remainder of the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>manuṣyādhikāratvāt</s>' (because of human qualification) applies here too by the <s>kākākṣi-nyāya</s> (the maxim of the crow's eye), and that it has meaning [here as well], he explains by first showing its connection — beginning with '<s>itara</s>' (other). // The meaning is: of animals and others. '<s>Api</s>' (even) recurs [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>]. '<s>Aṅguṣṭhamātratvam</s>' (thumb-sizedness) — this continues in reversed [application]. '<s>Na virodhaḥ</s>' (no contradiction) — this is the phrase drawn from the <s>sūtra</s> on non-contradiction. And thus, '<s>api</s>' — even upon accepting thumb-measure relative to each respective [being's] thumb, even though other living beings lack thumbs, there is no contradiction — that is, no impossibility — regarding <s>Viṣṇu's</s> thumb-sizedness or the statement thereof. Why? Because the statement of thumb-measure — that is, the <s>vidyā</s> (meditation-knowledge) that teaches it — '<s>manuṣyādhikāratvāt</s>' — has proceeded with reference to human beings alone as qualified. And why that? Because '<s>manuṣyādhikāratvāt</s>' — the qualification for Vedic meditation-knowledge (<s>vedavidyopāsana</s>) belongs to humans alone — this is the construction. In the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>Bhāṣya</s>, [the compound means]: that in which humans have qualification, or alternatively — the <s>adhikāra</s> (qualified practice), namely meditation or scripture, [applies to] humans alone; the state of being of human-qualification — from that — this is the analysis. In the reading '<s>manuṣyādhikāritvāt</s>,' humans are the qualified practitioners in which — thus stated. And thus the meaning is: because of being that which has human practitioners. The word '<s>manuṣya</s>' (human), by the principle to be stated [later], refers to conscious beings possessed of the capacity for reflection (<s>manana</s>) and so forth. Thereby, the qualification for this <s>vidyā</s> is established for gods and for <s>Jaritā</s>'s sons and others who are qualified for Vedic knowledge by the principle to be explained. For those like <s>Jaritā</s>'s sons, since meditation upon the Lord as measured by their own respective thumbs is impossible, their qualification is only for the knowledge of the meaning of the sentences arising from this <s>vidyā</s>, not for meditation as well. For this very reason, in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, human-ness is stated as a pervading [general] attribute by saying 'because only humans have qualification for Vedic meditation-knowledge.' Nor should it be objected that for animals and others who lack qualification, the absence of thumb-measure for the Lord situated in their bodies would lead to the absurdity of incorporeality (<s>adravyatva</s>) due to no other measurement being stated — because the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) situated in the bodies of animals and others possesses the form appropriate to each and has measurements corresponding to those [forms]. As stated in the <s>Aitareya Bhāṣya</s>: '<s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s>, having the forms [appropriate to humans], are situated in humans; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s>, having animal forms, are situated in animals.' //

children.text:
anena - sūtre tuśabdo 'pyarthevadhāraṇe ca / tatrāpyarthasyobhayatrānvayaḥ / aṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ yujyata iti śeṣaḥ / taditi pradhānasūtrādanuvṛttasyeha vipariṇāmenānvayaḥ / na virodhaḥ ityasyākarṣaḥ / 'tasya manuṣyādhikāritvāt'; ityāvartate / tathā ca 'tu'; api sarvagatasyāpi 'tasya viṣṇoraṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ'; taduktiryujyate / na ca virodhaḥ / yato 'tra 'hṛdyapekṣayā tu'; hṛdyavakāśāpekṣayaiva aṅguṣṭhamātratvamucyate, na tu paricchinnatvāt / tacca mūrtiviśeṣe tanmātratvasya sattvādupacāreṇa vā yujyate / na ca nāṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ viṣṇoryuktaṃ, yatkiñcidaṅguṣṭhamātratvoktervyarthatvenāsambhavena ca tattadaṅguṣṭhamātratve vācye tasya ca paśvādīnāmaṅguṣṭhābhāvena tadantargataviṣṇāvayogāditi vācyam / yataḥ 'tu'; api itaraprāṇināmaṅguṣṭhābhāve 'pi na viṣṇostattadaṅguṣṭhamātratvasya 'virodhaḥ'; asambhavaḥ / kutaḥ? aṅguṣṭhamātratvavacanasya yadbodhakavidyāyāḥ 'manuṣyādhikāratvāt'; manuṣyānevādhikṛtya pravṛttatvāt / tadapi kutaḥ? 'tasya'; vedavidyopāsanasya 'manuṣyādhikāratvāt'; manuṣyamātre 'dhikāratvāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
// iti vāmanādhikaraṇam // 7 //
children.translated_text:
By this — the word '<s>tu</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> is in the sense of '<s>api</s>' (even/also) and in the sense of restriction (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>) as well. And even in [the sense of] '<s>api</s>,' the connection is in both places. '<s>Aṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ yujyate</s>' (thumb-sizedness is fitting) is to be supplied. '<s>Tat</s>' (that) — what continues from the principal <s>sūtra</s> applies here in reversed form. '<s>Na virodhaḥ</s>' (no contradiction) is drawn [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>]. '<s>Tasya manuṣyādhikāritvāt</s>' (because of its having human qualification) recurs. And thus: '<s>tu</s>' [meaning] 'even' — even though all-pervading, '<s>tasya viṣṇoraṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ</s>' — the statement of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> thumb-sizedness — is fitting. And there is no contradiction. Because here, '<s>hṛdyapekṣayā tu</s>' — with reference to the heart-space alone, thumb-sizedness is stated, not because of [His] being limited. And that is fitting either because of the existence of that measurement in a specific manifest form, or figuratively. Nor should it be said that thumb-sizedness is not justified for <s>Viṣṇu</s> because a statement of arbitrary thumb-measure would be purposeless and impossible, and because when each respective thumb-measure is to be stated, it is unjustified for <s>Viṣṇu</s> situated within animals and others who lack thumbs — because '<s>tu</s>' [meaning] 'even' — even though other living beings lack thumbs, there is no impossibility of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> respective thumb-sizedness being a '<s>virodha</s>' (contradiction). Why? Because '<s>manuṣyādhikāratvāt</s>' — the <s>vidyā</s> whose comprehension yields the statement of thumb-measure has proceeded with reference to humans alone as qualified. And why that? Because '<s>tasya</s>' — of that Vedic meditation-knowledge — '<s>manuṣyādhikāratvāt</s>' — qualification belongs to humans alone — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
// Thus ends the <s>Vāmanādhikaraṇa</s> (Section on the Dwarf). // 7 //
// 8. <s>Devatādhikaraṇa</s> (Section on the Gods). //
It has been stated that only human beings have qualification for Vedic knowledge (<s>vedavidyā</s>).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.1:
asminnadhikaraṇe devānāṃ brahmavidyādhikāraḥ samarthyate / prāsaṅgikatvānnādhyāyapādasaṅgatī mārgaṇīye / śrutyādisaṅgativiṣayasaṃśayatadbījāni darśayati - manuṣyāṇāmiti // 'uktaṃ'; pūrvasūtre / tuśabdārthāvadhāraṇasya samāsapraviṣṭamanuṣyapadenāpi sambandho 'stīti bhāvena manuṣyāṇāmevetyanuvādaḥ / netareṣāmityevaśabdārthaḥ / 'vedavidyādhikāro'; vedavidyopāsanādhikāraḥ / anena - devatādhikārābhāvamukhena 'viśve devā upāsate'; ityādipūrvodāhṛtaśrutyupalakṣitāśeṣaśrutiprāmāṇyasyākṣepātpūrvādhikaraṇenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ vedavidyādhikārākhyo viṣayaścokto bhavati / 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ'; iti śrutimūlāyāḥ 'manuṣyāṇāmeva'; ityukteḥ 'viśve devā upāsate'; (kaṭha.2-2-3.) iti śruteśca koṭidvayopasthāpakatvena sandehabījatvāttaduktyaiva devānāmadhikāro 'sti uta nāstīti saṃśayo, nāstīti pūrvapakṣaśca sūcitaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.8.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section), the qualification of the gods (<s>devas</s>) for knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmavidyā</s>) is established. Since this is incidental (<s>prāsaṅgika</s>), the connection with the chapter and quarter need not be sought. He shows the <s>śruti</s>-based connection, the subject matter, the doubt, and its grounds — beginning with '<s>manuṣyāṇām</s>' (of humans). // '<s>Uktam</s>' (stated) — in the previous <s>sūtra</s>. Since the restrictive sense of the word '<s>tu</s>' has connection also with the word '<s>manuṣya</s>' (human) that has entered the compound — with this understanding, '<s>manuṣyāṇām eva</s>' (of humans alone) is the restatement. '<s>Na itareṣām</s>' (not of others) — this is the meaning of the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone). '<s>Vedavidyādhikāra</s>' means qualification for Vedic meditation-knowledge (<s>vedavidyopāsana</s>). By this — through the denial of the gods' qualification, since the authority of all <s>śrutis</s> indicated by the previously cited <s>śruti</s> '<s>viśve devā upāsate</s>' (all the gods worship) is challenged, the connection of this [section] with the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s> is one of objection (<s>ākṣepikī</s>), and the subject matter called 'qualification for Vedic knowledge' is also stated. Because the statement '<s>manuṣyāṇām eva</s>' (of humans alone), which is rooted in the <s>śruti</s> '<s>aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ</s>' (of thumb-measure), and the <s>śruti</s> '<s>viśve devā upāsate</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.2.3) present two alternatives, thereby serving as the ground for doubt — by that very statement, the doubt 'do the gods have qualification or not?' and the prima facie view 'they do not' are indicated.
The qualification by the term 'human' (<s>manuṣyatva</s>) was stated only with reference to animals and such [lower beings], not with reference to gods and others — thus he says:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.2:
tataḥ kimityatassaṃśayabījaṃ vighaṭayan siddhāntayituṃ sūtramavatārayati - tiryagādīti // viśiṣṭabuddhyādirahitatiryagādivyāvṛttyarthamityarthaḥ / manuṣyatvaviśeṣaṇaṃ sāvadhāraṇatvenābhipretam / manuṣyapadam 'uktaṃ'; prayuktaṃ, tatreta śeṣaḥ / pūrvasūtra iti tadarthaḥ / svaprayuktaivakāravyāvarttyaṃ darśayati - na tviti // 'devādyapekṣayā'; devādivyāvṛttyartham / tuśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / na tu devādyarthamapītyapiśabdārtho vā / 'ityāha'; ityabhipretya sūtrakāro devānāmadhikārabhāvamāhetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 2:
Dispelling the seed of doubt as to 'what follows from that,' he introduces the <s>sūtra</s> for establishing the conclusion — '<s>tiryagādi</s>' (animals and the like). // The meaning is: for the purpose of excluding animals and the like who lack distinguished intellect and the rest. The qualification by 'human' (<s>manuṣyatva</s>) is intended in the restrictive sense. The word 'human' was 'stated' (<s>uktam</s>) — employed — 'therein' is the remainder. 'In the previous <s>sūtra</s>' — this is its meaning. He shows what is to be excluded by the restrictive particle 'eva' employed in his own [<s>sūtra</s>] — '<s>na tu</s>' (but not). // 'With reference to the <s>devas</s> and the like' — for the purpose of excluding <s>devas</s> and the like. The word 'tu' is for specification. Or, the meaning of the word 'api' is: 'but not even for the purpose of <s>devas</s> and the like.' '<s>Ityāha</s>' (thus he says) — meaning: with this intention, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the <s>sūtras</s>) declares the non-qualification of <s>devas</s>.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
Even for those above that [i.e., above the human state], <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds qualification exists], because of possibility. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.26 |
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.8, verse 3:]

children.text: tadupari manuṣyāṇāṃ satāṃ devāditvaprāptyupari / sambhavati hi teṣāṃ viśiṣṭabuddhyādibhāvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Above that' — above the attainment of the status of <s>devas</s> and the like by existing humans. For it is possible for them, because of the presence of distinguished intellect and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.3:
tatsūtraṃ paṭhati - taduparīti // atra taduparīti sādhyadharmisūcakaṃ padamanūdya teṣāṃ tasmāttasyā iti vigrahāśrayeṇa vyācaṣṭe - taduparīti // vedavidyākāra ityanuṣajyate / na kevalaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ satāṃ, kintu taduparyapītyaperarthaḥ / tathā ca 'teṣāṃ'; manuṣyāṇāṃ satāṃ devatāpadayogyānāṃ jīvānāṃ padaprāpteḥ pūrvaṃ manuṣyaśarīraṃ prāptānāṃ satāṃ 'tasmāt'; manuṣyatvāt 'upari'; manuṣyaśarīrāpagamena 'tasyā upari'; devopadevādipadaprāpteruparitanakāle 'pi devabhāvamāpannānāmapi vedavidyādhikāro 'styeveti yojanā / kuta ityatastaddhetutayā sambhavāditi hetuṃ vyācaṣṭe / 'hi'; yataḥ / 'vedavidyādhikāraḥ'; ityatrāpi sambadhyate / 'teṣāṃ'; devānām / adhikārasambhavo 'pi kuta ityato 'trāpi sambhavādityetadevāvṛttya hetutayā yojayati - viśiṣṭeti // teṣāmityatrāpyanvīyate / tathā ca 'teṣāṃ'; yogyamanuṣyāṇāṃ vidyākarmabhyāṃ devāditvaprāptimatāṃ 'sambhavāt'; viśiṣṭabuddhyādibhāvādarthagrahaṇānuṣṭhānopayuktabuddhiviśeṣādisadbhāvādityarthaḥ / arthitvasāmarthye ādipadena grāhye / na cārthitvābhāvaḥ ityatrāpi teṣāṃ sambhavati hītyeva hetuḥ / vidyābhisteṣāṃ mokṣasiddhiḥ sambhavati hīti tadarthaḥ / anena - sūtre tadityāvartate / manuṣyaparāmarśi cedaṃ buddhisthaparāmarśi ca/ apiḥ samuccaye / adhikāra iti buddhyā vivicyātrānveti / anadhikārādhikārābhidhāyakajaiminibādarāyaṇoktirūpavipratipattisūcanāya bādarāyaṇapadam / tattvapradīparītyā tātparyajñāpanārthamadhikārādhikyajñaptidārḍhyārthaṃ ca bādarāyaṇaḥ svayameva vaktītyāha iti vā / sambhavāditi cāvartate / tathā ca yato na kevalaṃ devādipadayogyajīvānāṃ padaprāpteḥ pūrvaṃ bhūmau kiñcitkālaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ satāṃ tasyāṃ daśāyāmeva adhikāraḥ, kintu 'taduparyapi'; tasmānmanuṣyatvādupari tadatyayena tābhyāṃ vidyākarmabhyāṃ tasyāḥ devāditvaprāpteruparitanakāle 'pi devabhāvamāpannānāmapi vedavidyāyāmadhikāro 'styeva / na ca tatkāraṇābhāvaḥ / 'sambhavāt'; adhikāropayogino viśiṣṭabuddhyādesteṣu sambhavāt / na ca devādīnāṃ viśiṣṭabuddhisāmarthyasadbhāve 'pyarthitvābhāvādadhikārābhāva iti vācyam / kutaḥ? 'sambhavāt'; vidyāsādhyajñānamokṣayorarthitvasambhavāditi bhagavān bādarāyaṇo manyata iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 3:
He reads that <s>sūtra</s> — '<s>tadupari</s>' (above that). // Here, having cited '<s>tadupari</s>' as the word in the <s>sūtra</s> that indicates the subject to be established (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>), he explains it through the analytical resolution 'of them, from that, of that' — '<s>tadupari</s>.' // 'Being doers of Vedic knowledge' (<s>vedavidyākāra</s>) is to be connected. Not only of existing humans, but also 'above that' — this is the meaning of 'api.' And thus: 'of them' — of those <s>jīvas</s> who are existing humans eligible for the station of <s>devas</s>, who have attained human bodies prior to reaching [divine] stations — 'from that' — from the human state — 'above' — by the departure from the human body — 'above that' — even at the time above the attainment of the stations of <s>devas</s>, <s>upadevas</s>, and the like — even of those who have attained the state of <s>devas</s>, the qualification for Vedic knowledge exists indeed: this is the construction. Why? — to this, he explains the reason '<s>sambhavāt</s>' (because of possibility) as the reason for that — '<s>hi</s>' (for/because). // 'Because' (<s>yataḥ</s>). This connects also with 'qualification for Vedic knowledge.' 'Of them' — of the <s>devas</s>. Even the possibility of qualification — from where? — to this, he connects the very same '<s>sambhavāt</s>' as the reason by repeating it — '<s>viśiṣṭa</s>' (distinguished). // 'Of them' is also connected here. And thus: 'of them' — of those eligible humans who have attained the status of <s>devas</s> and the like through knowledge and <s>karma</s> — 'because of possibility' — because of the existence of distinguished intellect and the like, i.e., because of the actual presence of special intellect useful for comprehending meaning and performing [practice]: that is the meaning. Desire (<s>arthitva</s>) and capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) are included by the word 'ādi.' Nor is there absence of desire — here too, 'of them, because of possibility indeed' is the very reason. 'Through knowledge, liberation is possible for them indeed' — this is its meaning. By this — in the <s>sūtra</s>, 'tat' (that) carries forward. This refers both to humans and to what is cognized through intellect. 'Api' is for accumulation. 'Qualification' (<s>adhikāra</s>) is to be analytically connected here. The word '<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>' is for indicating the divergence of opinion between <s>Jaimini</s> and <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> — who advocate the absence and presence of qualification respectively — as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. Or, in the manner of the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, for indicating the intended conclusion and for strengthening the assertion of the excess of qualification, <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> himself speaks — thus it is said. And '<s>sambhavāt</s>' also carries forward. And thus: not only do those <s>jīvas</s> eligible for <s>deva</s> stations have qualification while on earth as humans for some time prior to reaching their stations, during that very state, but 'above that too' (<s>taduparyapi</s>) — above that human state, by its passage, at the time above the attainment of <s>deva</s> status through those two — knowledge and <s>karma</s> — even of those who have attained the state of <s>devas</s>, the qualification for Vedic knowledge exists indeed. Nor is there absence of its cause — '<s>sambhavāt</s>' — because of the possibility of distinguished intellect and the like that are conducive to qualification in them. Nor should it be said that even though <s>devas</s> possess distinguished intellect and capacity, there is no qualification because of the absence of desire. Why? '<s>Sambhavāt</s>' — because of the possibility of desire for knowledge and liberation achievable through knowledge — so <s>Bhagavān Bādarāyaṇa</s> holds: thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.

For animals and the like, there is no [qualification] because of the absence of that [distinguished intellect]. But even among those, wherever there is the presence of distinguished intellect and the like, there is no contradiction.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.8, verse 4:]

nanu na devā vedavidyādhikāriṇaḥ, tathā sati sūtre 'manuṣyamātravyāvartakamanuṣyapadaprayogena tiryagādivadamanuṣyatvānna devā vedavidyādhikāriṇa ityanumānasūcanāttadvirodhāpatterityata āha - tiryagādīnāmiti // ādipadena sthāvarāṇi mūḍhamanuṣyā vā gṛhyante / 'tadabhāvāt'; viśiṣṭabuddhyāderabhāvāt 'abhāvaḥ'; tasya vedavidyādhikārasya / anenādhikārābhāve viśiṣṭabuddhyādirāhityasya prayojakatvoktyā paroktāmanuṣyatvahetoḥ sopādhikatvaṃ sādhyavyatirekasādhakopādhivyatirekākhyapratipakṣagrastatvaṃ coktaṃ bhavati / sautramanuṣyapadaṃ ca mananādiśīlaparaṃ sat viśiṣṭabuddhyādirahitameva cetanaṃ vyāvartayati, na tu martyabhinnamātramiti na tadvirodha iti bhāvaḥ / nanu viśiṣṭabuddhyādirāhityamupādhiḥ / tiryakṣu adhikārābhāvarūpasādhyāvyāpakatvāt / ata eva na tadabhāvo 'pi sādhyavyatirekaheturityata āha - teṣāmapīti // apirubhayatrānveti / tatrādyassamuccaye / adhikāra iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca na kevalaṃ devānāṃ, kintu 'teṣāṃ'; tiraścāmapyadhikāre 'pi na virodhaḥ nanu kathamavirodhastiryakṣu sarvatra vedādhikāre mānavirodhāpātādityata āha - teṣāmapīti // tiraścāṃ madhye 'pītyarthaḥ / 'yatra'; yeṣu viśiṣṭabuddhyarthitvākhyarāgādibhāvaḥ tatsattvaṃ tatraivādhikāre 'avirodho'; mānāvirodhaḥ / bādho na sarvatretyarthaḥ / anenāpinā sautro 'piśabdo jaritāryādisamuccāyakaśceti sūcitam / yadāha tattvapradīpikākāraḥ - 'teṣāmapītyādirapipadavyākhyā'; iti / ānandamālākāro 'pi - 'tiryañco 'pi kecidapiśabdagṛhītāḥ'; ityāha / tathā ca manuṣyabhinneṣvapi tiryakṣvadhikārasadbhāvādvyabhicārādadhikārābhāve nāmanuṣyatvaṃ hetuḥ, kintu viśiṣṭabuddhyādirāhityamevāvyabhicārāt / ato bhavatyeva sa upādhiḥ / ata eva sautramanuṣyapadasya vyāvarttyasaṅkoco 'pi yukta iti bhāvaḥ /

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 4:
Objection: <s>Devas</s> are not qualified for Vedic knowledge, because if so, by the use of the word 'human' in the <s>sūtra</s> to exclude only non-humans, just as animals are non-human and hence not qualified, so too would <s>devas</s> be non-human and hence not qualified — leading to the inference of their non-qualification. To this he says: 'for animals and the like.' // By the word 'ādi,' plants or deluded humans are included. 'Because of the absence of that' (<s>tadabhāvāt</s>) — because of the absence of distinguished intellect and the like — 'absence' (<s>abhāvaḥ</s>) — of that qualification for Vedic knowledge. By this — through the statement that the absence of distinguished intellect and the like is the cause (<s>prayojaka</s>) for the absence of qualification — it is stated that the reason of 'non-humanity' adduced by the opponent is qualified [by a further condition] (<s>sopādhikatva</s>), and is vitiated by the counter-argument (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) in the form of deviation from the exclusion of the counter-example (<s>sādhyavyatireka</s>). And the word 'human' in the <s>sūtra</s>, being in the sense of one who is disposed to reflection (<s>manana</s>) and the like, excludes only those conscious beings who lack distinguished intellect and the like, not merely what is different from mortals: thus there is no contradiction — this is the purport. Objection: The absence of distinguished intellect and the like is a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), since in animals, the absence of qualification — the <s>sādhya</s> — does not [always hold]. Therefore, [the absence of distinguished intellect] is not a reason for the counter-example's exclusion from the <s>sādhya</s> either — to this he says: 'of those too' (<s>teṣāmapi</s>). // The word 'api' connects in both places. The first is for accumulation. 'Qualification' is the remainder. And thus: not only of <s>devas</s>, but also 'of those' (<s>teṣām</s>) — of animals — even in their qualification, there is no contradiction. But how is there no contradiction if animals everywhere have qualification for Vedic [knowledge] — [would this not] lead to the contradiction with scriptural authority? To this he says: 'of those too' (<s>teṣāmapi</s>). // 'Among animals' is the meaning. 'Wherever' (<s>yatra</s>) — in whichever [animals] there is the presence of distinguished intellect, desire, and other qualifying factors — 'there alone' in qualification 'there is no contradiction' (<s>avirodhaḥ</s>) — no contradiction with scriptural authority. Meaning: there is no obstruction everywhere. By this, the 'api' word in the <s>sūtra</s> is indicated as aggregating [animals like] <s>Jaritāri</s> and the like. As the author of the <s>Tattvapradīpikā</s> says: 'the explanation of the api-word by <s>teṣāmapi</s> and the like.' The author of the <s>Ānandamālā</s> also says: 'Some animals too are included by the api-word.' And thus, since even among non-human animals there is the presence of qualification, there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), and therefore non-humanity is not the reason for the absence of qualification; rather, the absence of distinguished intellect and the like alone [is the reason], because of non-deviation. Therefore that is indeed the limiting condition. Therefore the restriction of the <s>sūtra</s>-word 'human' to exclude [only a subset] is also justified: this is the purport.
Because of the absence of prohibition. For <s>Jaritāri</s> and the like are seen [to have such qualification]. // 26 //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.8, verse 5:]

Objection: How can there be no contradiction even in the qualification of animals? — because the prohibition of their qualification, or the evidence [against it], would be contradictory. Anticipating [this objection] that the first [alternative holds], he says: '<s>niṣedha</s>' (prohibition). // 'Of them' is also connected here. 'In qualification' and the like are to be conjoined at the beginning. [Anticipating] that the second [alternative holds], he says: 'for they are seen' (<s>dṛśyante hi</s>). // 'As qualified for Vedic [knowledge]' is the remainder. <s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 6:
Having raised an objection against the createdness (<s>sāditva</s>) stated by '<s>tadupari</s>' (above that) for the purpose of establishing the qualification of <s>devas</s> for Vedic knowledge, and then resolving it, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> and first explains the objection-portion — '<s>virodha</s>' (contradiction). // 'Humans alone' — <s>jīvas</s> eligible for <s>deva</s> stations, being first humans on earth for some time, then become <s>devas</s> and the like: that is the meaning. 'Not without the human state' — this is the meaning of the word 'eva.' 'Thus it was stated' — after this, 'that is improper' is the remainder. Why? — for that, he explains the portion '<s>virodha</s>' (contradiction) in the objection together with its reason — 'in that case, if.' // From 'if' up to 'become' is a restatement of the meaning of the previous sentence, for the purpose of showing its capacity to lead [to the objection]. 'In that case' — 'then' is the meaning — is to be connected after 'become.' Or alternatively, 'humans alone become <s>devas</s> and the like' up to this point is a restatement of the meaning of the previous sentence for showing its capacity [to generate the objection]. 'In that case' — 'then' is the meaning — is to be connected after 'become.' Or: 'in that case, in the <s>karma</s> directed to the deity' — this is a co-location. In this interpretation, 'then' is obtained from the hearing of 'if.' After 'become,' 'thus it was stated' exists [implicitly]. In both [interpretations], by the word 'ādi,' <s>upadevas</s> and the like are included. The word '<s>karma</s>' also indicates words (<s>śabda</s>). And thus: if humans, while being [humans], then become <s>devas</s> and the like as was stated, 'prior to that' (<s>tatpūrvam</s>) — prior to their attainment of the <s>deva</s> station — in the state of being aspirants (<s>sādhaka</s>) — 'because of the non-existence of the deity' — because the deity does not yet exist — that <s>karma</s> by which the <s>deva</s> status is to be achieved, as was stated — 'in that' — in that very '<s>karma</s> directed to the deity' — i.e., <s>karma</s> performed in a previous cosmic cycle (<s>kalpa</s>) for the sake of a deity, and in the word (<s>śabda</s>) denoting the deity — 'there would be contradiction' (<s>virodhaḥ</s>) — futility of both: this is the construction. Because the addressee does not exist, and the referent does not exist: this is the purport.

anenataduparītyatroktaṃ devānāṃ sāditvamayuktaṃ, tathā sati yena karmaṇā devāditvaṃ sādhyamityuktam, tatra karmaṇi śabde ca virodhastasya vaiyarthyaṃ syāt tatpūrvaṃ devatābhāvāditi cet - na, yato na pūrvaṃ devatābhāvaḥ / tatkatham? etaddevānāṃ pūrvamabhāve 'pi devāntarasadbhāvāt / na ca tatra mānābhāvaḥ / 'anekapratipatterdarśanāt'; anekeṣāṃ yogyamanuṣyāṇāṃ pūrvapūrvapadaprāpteḥ 'teha nākam'; ityatroktatvāditi sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / śrutau 'yajñena yajñamayajanta devāḥ / tāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan'; iti pūrvavākye prakṛtāḥ devāstacchabdena gṛhyante / haśabdaḥ punararthe prasiddhau vā / tathā ca ye 'devāḥ'; devatvayogyāḥ manuṣyā jñānakarmātmakena 'yajñena'; 'yajñaṃ'; viṣṇum 'ayajanta'; apūjayan / tatastena jñānapūrvakakarmaṇā devapadaṃ prāpya 'prathamāni'; prathamāḥ mukhyāḥ 'dharmāṇi'; dharmāḥ lokadhārakā āsan / 'mahimānaḥ'; mahātmānaḥ mahimaguṇātmakā vā / 'te'; devāḥ 'ha'; punaḥ anantaraṃ svādhikārāvasāne 'nākaṃ'; kaṃ sukhaṃ tadanyat duḥkhamakaṃ, tanneti nākaṃ, nañdvayena pūrṇasukhātmakamiti labhyate / evaṃbhūtaṃ mokṣaṃ 'sacante'; āpnuvan / laṅarthe laṭ / laṅvā, etvāḍabhāvau chāndasau / 'yatra'; mokṣe 'pūrve'; pūrvakalpe muktāḥ 'sādhyāḥ'; bahuvacanamādyarthe /
ṛjavo brahmamukhyā hi suparṇaśśeṣa eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛju</s> (the upright ones), <s>Brahma</s>-chief ones, <s>Suparṇa</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s> indeed,
<s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Suparṇī</s>, and <s>Vāruṇī</s> are called <s>Sādhyas</s>.

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 7:
He explains the refutation portion — 'na' (not). And this [word] recurs [from the previous context]. The construal is: there is no contradiction in the ritual action. Why? Because there was no prior non-existence of the deities. Since they are beginningless in their flow (<s>pravāha</s>), this means that even if particular deities did not exist before [a given time], other deities did exist — this is the purport. And since there is no absence of a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for that, [the objector's] position that the word <s>pratipatti</s> (attainment) is meant in the sense of 'knowledge' is refuted. Showing the related [scriptural authority] first, he explains — 'of many.' In the <s>śruti</s> 'te ha nākam' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12), 'of many' — of innumerable humans qualified for deity-status, grouped individually [in successive classes], the attainment of the station of prior deities through knowledge and ritual action is observed — this is the meaning.
By this, what was stated earlier with 'taduparī' (above that) — that the beginning-ness (<s>sāditva</s>) of the gods is improper, and that if so, the ritual action by which deity-status and so forth is to be achieved as stated — there would be a contradiction in that ritual action and in the [Vedic] word, and it would be purposeless, since there was no prior existence of deities — if [one objects] thus: no, because there was no prior non-existence of deities. How so? Because even in the prior absence of particular deities, other deities existed. And there is no absence of a means of valid knowledge for that. 'Because of the observation of the attainment of many' — because of the attainment by many qualified humans of successive prior stations, as stated in 'te ha nākam' — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated. In the <s>śruti</s>, 'by sacrifice they sacrificed the sacrifice, the gods; those were the first <s>dharmas</s> (laws)' — the gods mentioned in the preceding sentence are referred to by the pronoun 'tat' (those). The particle 'ha' is used in the sense of 'again' or of well-knownness. And thus, those who were 'gods' — humans qualified for deity-status — 'by sacrifice' (<s>yajña</s>), by knowledge-and-action combined — 'worshipped' 'the sacrifice,' <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Then, having attained the station of gods through that knowledge-preceded ritual action, they were 'the first' — the foremost, principal — '<s>dharmas</s>' — sustaining laws, upholders of the world. '<s>Mahimānaḥ</s>' — great souls, or those whose nature consists of the quality of greatness. 'Te' — those gods; 'ha' — again, immediately upon the conclusion of their term of office; '<s>nākam</s>' — '<s>ka</s>' means happiness, '<s>aka</s>' is what is other than that, i.e. suffering, '<s>na</s>' negates that — thus '<s>nāka</s>,' by the double negation, is obtained as that which consists of complete bliss. Such <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), they 'sacante' — attained. The present tense (<s>laṭ</s>) is used in the sense of past (<s>laṅ</s>). Or it is <s>laṅ</s> itself, with the absence of <s>e</s>-augment and <s>āṭ</s>-augment being Vedic irregularities. 'Yatra' — in <s>mokṣa</s>; 'pūrve' — those liberated in the prior world-cycle; '<s>sādhyāḥ</s>' — the plural is used in the sense of a group of beginning ones.

children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sādhyas</s> and other gods who have been mentioned exist — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. And one should not object that since among the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, and <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s> come first, the commentary (<s>ṭīkā</s>) should say '<s>Vasu</s>-and-other gods,' not '<s>Sādhya</s>-and-others.' For this very reason, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> it is said: 'the prior <s>Sādhyas</s> — the <s>Vasu</s>-and-other gods who were previously established, or liberated' — thus [Jayatīrtha] stated, so [one might] argue. [But this is not valid] because the <s>Sādhyas</s>, being named as such, are given priority by skipping the [usual] order. [This is] because the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> follows the order of the <s>Chāndogya śruti</s>. Nor should one object that in this interpretation, in the <s>Puruṣārthādhikaraṇa</s>, the citation of this [passage] as illustrating those who have attained deity-status would be inapplicable. [For] the <s>śruti</s>'s intent is a different purport — that those who attained the station [of gods] and became world-sustainers are the gods who worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s> through sacrifice, and they attained the supreme bliss of liberation — and since this different intent is applicable, the explanation in the <s>ṭīkā</s> (subcommentary) and the grammatical analysis are also justified accordingly.

children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 8:
What was stated [previously] — that the beginning-and-end-ness of the gods was asserted for the purpose of establishing their eligibility — that [objection] is now taken up by the two [sūtras] beginning with 'aneka' (many). Having raised that objection and then resolved it, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> and first explains the objection portion — 'śabda iti' (in the word). 'There is no contradiction in the ritual action because of the observation of many attaining [deity-status]' and so forth should be connected here. If there is indeed such a connection, then the construal is as follows: if it is said that because of the observation of many [humans] attaining the station of prior deities through liberation, there is no contradiction in the ritual action — then in that very <s>śabda</s> (word), the <s>Veda</s> referred to by the word 'darśana' (observation), there would be a contradiction in the form of invalidity (<s>aprāmāṇya</s>). Why? Because of the non-eternality of the gods. Since the non-eternality, i.e. the having-an-end, of the gods has been stated by [the reasoning beginning with] 'aneka' (many). Now, even if the gods are non-eternal, whence comes the invalidity of the <s>Vedas</s>? To this he says — '<s>taduditānām</s>' (of those denoted by them). This is a reason-embedded qualifier. By this, the reason 'because of denoting non-eternal deities' is indicated. Now, even if the gods are non-eternal, the invalidity of the <s>Veda</s> — which denotes them — in the form of lacking a referent does not follow, because the <s>Veda</s>, like the deities [it denotes], is also non-eternal and therefore is never without a referent. To this he says — 'because of the eternality of the <s>Veda</s>.' Whence the eternality of the <s>Veda</s>? To this he says — 'vācā' (by the word). The construction of 'from the <s>śruti</s>' is: 'because of the eternality of the <s>Veda</s>' — this connects with the earlier [statement]. And this is indicative of [both] knowledge [and word]. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), [passages such as] 'eternal, by the eternal' (<s>Pauṣyāyaṇa śruti</s>) and 'the <s>śruti</s> is indeed eternal' are included. Now, the <s>Veda</s> is not eternal. And there is no contradiction with <s>śruti</s>, because the <s>śruti</s> [declaring eternality] can be interpreted figuratively as meaning 'existing for a long time.' To this too he says — in that case, because of the non-eternality of the <s>Veda</s>, the contradiction in the form of invalidity would arise. Now, even if the <s>Veda</s> is non-eternal, its validity is possible because it is rooted in a trustworthy source (<s>āpta</s>). To this he says — 'because of the uncertainty of trustworthiness.' The word 'of the maker of the <s>Veda</s>' should be supplied. And thus, because of the absence of a means of proof for the omniscience and other [qualities] of the maker of the <s>Veda</s>, there is uncertainty about the <s>āpti</s> (trustworthiness) in the form of omniscience, etc. of the <s>Veda</s>'s maker — this is the meaning. Alternatively — let there be certainty of the maker's trustworthiness; even so, there is no certainty that the <s>Veda</s> is rooted in that [trustworthiness]. To this he says — 'because of the uncertainty of trustworthiness.' 'Of the <s>Veda</s>' should be carried over. And thus, because of the uncertainty of the <s>Veda</s>'s being rooted in a trustworthy source — i.e., being composed by a trustworthy person — this is the meaning. Therefore, since in the absence of proof there is uncertainty about trustworthiness and its being the root, and since in the non-eternality of the <s>Veda</s> there would be the consequence of absence of its validity, the figurative interpretation of the <s>śruti</s> declaring [Vedic] eternality should not be asserted — this is the purport. Not only is the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> established from <s>śruti</s>, but also from the inference by elimination — to this he says — 'nityatva' (eternality). Because the root means of valid knowledge requires the eternality [of the <s>Veda</s>], the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> is understood — this is the construction. The purport is this: if the <s>Veda</s> is to be established as composed by a trustworthy person, there must be a root means of valid knowledge, because of the rule that what is personal (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) requires dependence on a root means of proof. Otherwise, since there would be no confidence [in it], and since direct perception and inference — which could serve as the root source for the <s>Veda</s>'s teaching that sacrifice and so forth are means to merit — are impossible, by elimination it must be said that the word (<s>vākya</s>, i.e. Vedic statement) alone [is the root authority]. And having accepted the non-eternality of that [word], in the search for [its] root [authority], there would be the consequence of infinite regress; therefore eternality alone must be asserted. Hence, it is better to accept the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> itself, since it is established by <s>śruti</s>.

Because of the well-established self-validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) [of the <s>Veda</s>], and because of its eternality, [there is no contradiction]; for the gods denoted by that [<s>Veda</s>] are non-eternal.

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 9:
Now, just as in the case of the <s>Veda</s>'s non-eternality, the consequence of absence of validity — due to uncertainty of trustworthiness — serves as a refutation (<s>bādhaka</s>), similarly, even if the <s>Veda</s> is eternal, the consequence of absence of validity — due to the absence of a quality-based origin such as being composed by a trustworthy person — is equally a refutation. To this he says — 'svataḥ' (self-established). 'Of the <s>Veda</s>' continues from the previous [statement]. And thus, the validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of the <s>Veda</s> — in the form of the truth-correspondence (<s>yāthārthya</s>) of the cognition produced by the <s>Veda</s> — is 'self-established' (<s>svataḥ</s>), i.e. from the very general cause of cognition itself; 'because of being well-established' (<s>prasiddheḥ</s>) — because of being proven, i.e. because of being ascertained — this is the meaning. Alternatively, the validity of the <s>Veda</s> — in the form of the <s>Veda</s>'s capacity to produce true cognition, which is the nature of instrumental validity (<s>karaṇaprāmāṇya</s>) — is 'self-established,' i.e. because of being ascertained as identical with the capacity to produce true cognition that is innate (<s>sahaja</s>) to the capacity of being an instrument of cognition — this is the meaning. This too connects with 'because of the possibility of the <s>Veda</s>'s eternality.' And thus, since the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> is established, in [the case of] the non-eternality of the gods denoted by it, there would be the consequence of invalidity in the form of lacking a referent — this is the purport.
If [one says] there is a contradiction in the [Vedic] word because of the rule that [beings] do not become anything other [than what they are] —

children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.8.10:
Objection: In a past <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle), when one particular deity was absent, since other deities still existed, just as there is no contradiction arising from the absence of the intended object in ritual action, so too here, even when one deity perishes, since the origination of another deity is possible, there should be no contradiction called 'lacking a referent' — to this he says: 'because there is no rule guaranteeing the re-origination of another.' The word 'punar' (again) is used in the sense of sequence, meaning 'after the destruction in the previous <s>kalpa</s>,' or in the sense of 'in the subsequent <s>kalpa</s>.' 'Anyabhāva' means the origination of another. The meaning is: because there is no valid means of knowledge establishing a rule for that. But there is valid evidence for the continuity (<s>pravāha</s>) of the deities of past cycles — this is the intended distinction. By this, it is stated that the contradiction of the absence of deities in the future applies equally to ritual action, and hence through the word 'śabda' (Vedic word) in the <s>sūtra</s>, ritual action is also implicitly indicated. And there is no contradiction with the <s>ṭīkā</s> (gloss) in drawing the word 'contradiction' here as well. Because the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with 'tadupari' states the continued application, and its meaning is not merely the contradiction of the absence of deities in the future with respect to the Vedic word, but also with respect to ritual action — this should not be objected to. Relying on the sense that the word 'ākarṣaṇa' (drawing in) means syntactic connection, the connection of the word 'contradiction' is not only in the previous <s>sūtra</s> but also in this <s>sūtra</s> — this is accepted as the meaning of the <s>ṭīkā</s>, and thus both 'api' and 'virodha' are drawn in. Or let it be a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound); even so there is no inconsistency, because by accepting the meaning of 'api' as 'even in the absence of essential eternality,' the sense of cumulative inclusion with ritual action is not accepted. For this very reason the <s>ṭīkā</s> states 'even in the absence of the essential eternality of the gods.' Here, one 'ca' particle is for the cumulative mention of <s>śruti</s> (scripture) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference) which establish eternality. Another is for the cumulative mention of the negation of non-eternality and the absence thereof in establishing eternality. Yet another is for the cumulative mention of non-eternality and the absence of a rule for the origination of another — this is the distinction.
'To Him, the all-pervading one, O <s>Virūpa</s>, with the eternal voice, urge forth a well-crafted hymn of praise to the bountiful one' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 8.64.6) —
the meaning of this <s>Ṛg</s>-<s>Yajur</s> <s>mantra</s> was not explained in the <s>ṭīkā</s> of the <s>vilakṣaṇatva-adhikaraṇa</s> (section on distinctness). There, although it was stated that '<s>Virūpa</s>' is a self-address, and in the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirṇaya</s> <s>ṭīkā</s> it was stated to be an address to the sage named <s>Virūpa</s>, which appears contradictory — nevertheless, understanding it as the sage <s>Virūpa</s>'s address to his own inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), there is no contradiction. For it is said in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'the exhortation "urge forth" by the sage <s>Virūpa</s> is directed toward the inner controller.' Even in the alternative reading where <s>Virūpa</s> is the agent and the address is directed to him, by accepting the <s>ṭīkā</s>'s meaning that it is an address to one's own <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) denoted by 'svātma,' there is no contradiction. In this reading, what is stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> would be an alternative interpretation. And one should not say there is contradiction with the <s>Nyāyaratṇāvalī</s>, the commentary on the <s>Viṣṇutattvanirṇaya</s> by <s>Padmanābhatīrtha</s>, where it is said 'it is stated regarding the sage <s>Virūpa</s> by way of dharma' — because it is possible that the <s>mantra</s> first seen by <s>Yama</s> was subsequently also seen by <s>Virūpa</s>, and thus self-address would be possible at that time, so there is no contradiction. And thus: 'O <s>Virūpa</s>, <s>abhidyu</s>' means 'He whose radiance is on all sides,' i.e., the all-pervading one; 'to Him,' 'vṛṣṇe' means 'to the bestower' or 'to the supremely powerful one.' According to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>'s reading, <s>vṛṣā</s> means 'the best,' and its dative is 'vṛṣṇe.' To that Lord, directing toward Him, 'nūnam' means 'certainly,' 'nityayā' means 'with the beginningless and endless voice characterized as the <s>Veda</s>,' 'suṣṭutim' means 'an excellent hymn of praise,' 'codasva' means 'urge forth, compose' — this is the meaning.
No [such contradiction exists], because [the <s>śruti</s> declares]: '<s>Dhātā</s> (the Creator) fashioned the sun and the moon just as before' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 5.7).
Just as there is a fixed rule regarding time [and its divisions], so too is there a fixed rule regarding the gods (<s>sura</s>) and others;
Therefore, this universe will never at any time be different from this [pattern].

children.text: ityādeḥ, ata eva śabdātteṣāṃ prabhavaniyamāt mahatāṃ pratyakṣāt /
children.translated_text: Because of such [scriptural statements], and precisely because of the Vedic word (<s>śabda</s>) itself [establishing] the regularity of their origination (<s>prabhavaniyama</s>), and because of the direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) of the great [seers] —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.11:
parihārāṃśaṃ vyākhyāti - neti // virodha ityasti / tathā ca vedasya vācyahīnatvaprayuktāprāmāṇyākhyavirodho netyarthaḥ / kuta ityataḥ prāptaṃ prabhavāditi hetuṃ tatsambandhipradarśanapūrvakaṃ pravāhataḥprabhavaniyamaparatayā ca vyācaṣṭe - teṣāṃ prabhavaniyamāditi / 'teṣāṃ'; vedavācyadevānāṃ 'prabhavasya'; pravāhatautpatteḥ 'niyamāt'; pratikalpaṃ niyamenotpatteriti yāvat / tathā ca devānāṃ svarūpeṇa nityatvābhāve 'pi pravāharūpeṇa nityatvānna tadvācakavedāprāmāṇyamiti bhāvaḥ / nanu pramāṇābhāvādasiddho heturityataḥ prāptamataḥśabdamanūdya sāvadhāraṇatvena vyācaṣṭe - ata eva śabdāditi / ko 'sau śabda ityato yasminvirodhaḥ śaṅkitastasmādeva, nānyasmādaprakṛtādityāśayena tadudāharati - sūryetyādinā / śruto 'smin kalpe 'pīti śeṣaḥ / nanūtpādakābhāva ityato 'pyāha - ata eveti / akāravācyāt śrutyuktāddhāturviṣṇoreva, nānyasmādityarthaḥ / asmin pakṣe ataśśabdāditi vyākhyānāntaram / nanvakalpayaditi laṅyogādiyaṃ śrutiratītaviṣayaiva, ato na devaprabhavaniyamaṃ pramāpayatītyato 'pyāha - ata eveti / tathā ca dhātā yathā pūrvakalpe sūryācandramasāvakalpayat tathāsminkalpe 'pīti pratikalpaṃ śrutyā kathane devānāṃ sarvakalpeṣu prajananākhyasadbhāvasiddheradhyāhāraṃ vinā ataevaśabdāt buddhisthāt yathaiveti spaṣṭaśrutyantarācca teṣāṃ sarvakalpeṣu prabhavasiddhernoktacodyāvakāśa iti bhāvaḥ / nanu śrutāvupacāreṇāpyuktiḥ sambhavatīti na tayā devaprabhavaniyamaniścaya ityataḥ prāptaṃ pratyakṣetyaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - mahatāmiti / atītānāgatavidāmityarthaḥ / asyāpi teṣāṃ prabhavaniyamādityanenānvayaḥ / nanu parapratyakṣasyāpratyakṣatvāttadaniścaya ityatopyāha - mahatāṃ pratyakṣāditi /

children.translated_text: Just as in the seasons, the characteristic signs of each season, though of various forms, are seen to recur in each cycle,

children.text: dṛśyante tāni tānyeva tathā bhāvā yugādiṣu //
children.translated_text: so too do the same entities [recur] at the beginning of each <s>yuga</s> (age) and so on.

<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.8.11:
He explains the portion constituting the refutation — with 'na' (no). The word 'virodha' (contradiction) is understood. Thus the meaning is: there is no contradiction in the form of the Veda's lack of authority caused by the absence of referents. To the question 'why?', he presents the reason beginning with 'prabhavāt' (because of origination), preceded by an indication of related matters, and explains it as referring to the regularity of origination in the flow-sense (<s>pravāha</s>) — with 'teṣāṃ prabhavaniyamāt' (because of the regularity of their origination). 'Teṣām' means 'of the deities who are the referents of the <s>Veda</s>'; 'prabhavasya' means 'of origination in the flow-sense'; 'niyamāt' means 'because of the regularity of origination in every <s>kalpa</s>' — this is the purport. Thus, even though the deities lack eternality in their essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), because they possess eternality in the flow-sense (<s>pravāha-rūpeṇa nityatva</s>), the <s>Veda</s> which denotes them does not lose its authority — this is the intent. To the objection that the reason is unestablished due to the absence of a valid means of knowledge, he glosses the word 'ataḥ' by paraphrasing it with emphasis — with 'ata eva śabdāt' (precisely because of the Vedic word). What is that word? With the intention that it is from that very [<s>Veda</s>] regarding which the doubt of contradiction was raised, and not from anything else extraneous, he cites it — beginning with 'sūrya' etc. The remainder is: '[as] heard in this <s>kalpa</s> as well.' To the objection that there is no creator, he also says 'ata eva' — meaning: from <s>Dhātā</s>, i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s> as stated in <s>śruti</s>, denoted by the syllable 'a,' and from no other — this is the meaning. In this reading, there is an alternative interpretation of 'ataḥ śabdāt.' To the further objection that this <s>śruti</s> pertains only to the past because of the past tense 'akalpayat,' and hence does not establish the regularity of the origination of deities, he also says 'ata eva.' Thus, when the <s>śruti</s> narrates '<s>Dhātā</s> fashioned the sun and moon just as in the previous <s>kalpa</s>, so too in this <s>kalpa</s>,' since the existence of deities through procreation in all <s>kalpas</s> is established, from the word 'ata eva' which is understood in the mind without needing to supply anything, and from the clear additional <s>śruti</s> 'just as' — since the origination [of deities] in all <s>kalpas</s> is established, there is no room for the stated objection — this is the intent. To the objection that even in <s>śruti</s>, figurative usage is possible, and hence no certainty of the regularity of divine origination can be established, he explains the portion 'pratyakṣāt' (from direct perception) — with 'mahatām' (of the great ones). The meaning is: of those who know the past and future. This too has syntactic connection with 'teṣāṃ prabhavaniyamāt.' To the further objection that since another's direct perception is not perceptible to us, there can be no certainty from it, he says 'mahatāṃ pratyakṣāt' —

children.text: ityādirūpāt 'mahatāṃ'; bhāratācāryāṇāṃ 'pratyakṣāt'; pratyakṣavacanādityarthaḥ / asmin pakṣe 'pratyakṣāt'; niścitātpratyakṣādityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: From [statements] of this form — 'of the great ones' means of the teachers of the <s>Bhārata</s> [tradition]; 'from direct perception' means from their statements which have the force of direct perception — this is the meaning. In the alternative reading, 'pratyakṣāt' connects as 'from the certain direct perception [of the great seers].'
And from the inference (<s>anumāna</s>) of others [who are not yogins], that just as deities exist now, so too they will exist in the future. // 28 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.12:
nanvayogināṃ śrutipratyakṣayoraviśvāsena teṣāṃ devaprabhavaniścayābhāva ityataḥ prāptamanumānetyaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - yatheti / idānīntanakāle yathā devāssanti tathoparibhāvikāle 'pi devā bhaviṣyantītītareṣāṃ mahadbhyo 'nyevāmayogināmanumānādityarthaḥ / asyāpi prabhavaniyamādityanenānvayaḥ / caśabdaḥ prabhavaniyame, śabdapratyakṣānumānākhyapramāṇatrayasamuccaye vakṣyamāṇayuktyantarasamuccaye ca / anumānākārastu - uparitanakālo devavān apralayakālatvāt idānīntanakālavaditi / anena - devānāmadhikārasiddhyarthaṃ yadyādyantavattvamabhyupagamyate, tarhi pūrvasūtre yadbalātpūrvapūrvadevatāpravāhasyānāditvamuktaṃ, tasmin 'śabde'; 'vācā virūpa nityayā'; ityādiśrutau nityatayā siddhe vede karmaṇi cottarakalpe vācyoddeśyahīnatvarūpāprāmāṇyākhyo virodhaḥ syāditi cet - na, kutaḥ? 'prabhavāt'; devānāṃ sarvakalpeṣu prabhavaniyamānnityamenopapatteḥ / teṣāṃ pravāhato nityatvāditi yāvat / na cotpādakābhāvaḥ / 'ato'; viṣṇoreva prabhavāt / na cāsiddhiḥ / 'ato'; 'dhātā yathāpūrvam'; (mahānā. 5-7.) itiprakṛtācchabdācchruteḥ 'yathā'; iti spaṣṭaśruteśca / tathā mahatāmatītānāgatakālavidāṃ yogināṃ 'pratyakṣāt'; 'yatharturṣu'; iti pratyakṣavacanāt jñāpitāt mahatāmatītānāgatakālayordevaprabhavaniyamagrāhipratyakṣāt / tathā mahadbhyaḥ itareṣāmayogināmanumānācca tatsiddheriti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / 'yathaiva'; iti śrutyarthastu - yathā pūrvayugātyaye kalpātyaye vā punaryugakalpāntarotpattiriti kāle prabhavaniyamaḥ, tathā surāderdevopadevādeḥ pūrvapūrvakalpātyaye punaranyabhāvaniyamo 'sti / yathoktam -

children.translated_text: For He, the most praiseworthy, the all-pervading Lord, creates again and again <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), <s>Purandara</s> (Indra), <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), and other successive [beings] who are the creators of the universe;
He sustains them, destroys them, and leads the devoted ones of pure intellect to His own abode.

<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.8.12:
To the objection that for non-<s>yogins</s>, due to their lack of trust in <s>śruti</s> and direct perception, there would be no certainty of divine origination — he explains the portion regarding inference — with 'yathā.' Just as deities exist in the present time, so too in the future time deities will exist — this is the inference of others, i.e., non-<s>yogins</s>, who are different from the great ones — this is the meaning. This too has syntactic connection with 'prabhavaniyamāt.' The particle 'ca' serves for the cumulative mention of the three means of valid knowledge — Vedic word (<s>śabda</s>), direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), and inference (<s>anumāna</s>) — in establishing the regularity of origination, as well as for the cumulative mention of additional reasoning to be stated. The form of the inference is: the future time will have deities, because it is a non-dissolution period, just like the present time. By this [it is shown]: if for the sake of establishing the qualifications of the deities, their having a beginning and end is conceded, then in the previous <s>sūtra</s>, by the force of which the beginninglessness of the stream of successive deities was stated — in that Vedic word (<s>śabda</s>), which is established as eternal through the <s>śruti</s> 'with the eternal voice, O <s>Virūpa</s>,' and in ritual action as well, there would be a contradiction in the form of lack of authority due to the absence of referents and intended objects in the subsequent <s>kalpa</s> — if this is objected — no, why? Because of origination (<s>prabhavāt</s>), i.e., because of the regularity of the origination of deities in all <s>kalpas</s>, since eternality in the flow-sense is thereby established. That is: because of their eternality in the flow-sense (<s>pravāha</s>). Nor is there absence of a creator — because origination is from <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, as indicated by 'ataḥ.' Nor is there lack of establishment — because of the Vedic word from the contextual passage '<s>Dhātā</s> [fashioned] just as before' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 5.7), and because of the clear <s>śruti</s> 'just as.' Likewise, from the direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) of the great ones who know past and future times — the <s>yogins</s> — from [the verse] 'just as in the seasons,' from the statement having the force of direct perception, which conveys the regularity of the origination of deities in past and future times as grasped by the direct perception of the great ones. And from the inference of others — non-<s>yogins</s> — different from the great ones, that is established — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> 'just as' is: just as after the end of a previous <s>yuga</s> or <s>kalpa</s>, there is re-origination at the beginning of the next <s>yuga</s> or <s>kalpa</s> — this being the regularity in time — so too there is a rule of re-origination of <s>sura</s> (gods), <s>upadeva</s> (demi-gods), and others at the end of each successive <s>kalpa</s>. As stated:

children.text: iti / pratikalpamiti śeṣaḥ / tasmātpūrvakalpa ivottarakalpe 'pi pūrvakalpasadṛśasarvotpattiniyamādeva 'tasmāt'; viṣṇossakāśādetadviśvaṃ 'kvāpi'; kadāpi 'anīdṛśaṃ'; pūrvapūrvavisadṛśaṃ devatāprabhavaśūnyaṃ na bhaviṣyati, kintu tatsadbhāvopetameva bhaviṣyatīti / yadvā - 'etat'; cetanācetanātmakaṃ viśvamanīdṛśaṃ na bhaviṣyati, kintu nāmarūpābhyāmīdṛśameva bhaviṣyatītyarthaḥ / tattvapradīpe tviyaṃ śrutiḥ 'yathaiva kālaniyamaḥ'; iti vyatyāsena paṭhitā /
children.translated_text: Thus [it is established]. The remainder is: 'in every <s>kalpa</s>.' Therefore, just as in the previous <s>kalpa</s>, so too in the subsequent <s>kalpa</s>, because of the very rule that everything originates in a manner similar to the previous <s>kalpa</s> — 'tasmāt' means 'from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'; this universe will 'never' ('kvāpi' — at any time) be 'anīdṛśam' — dissimilar to the previous [creation], devoid of the origination of deities; rather it will be endowed with their existence. Or alternatively: 'etat' — this universe consisting of sentient and insentient beings — will not be 'anīdṛśam' (different from this pattern); rather, it will be just like this in name and form — this is the meaning. In the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, however, this <s>śruti</s> is read with a transposition as 'yathaiva kālaniyamaḥ' (just as there is regularity of time).
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
And precisely because of this, [their] eternality. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.29 |

children.text: ata eva śabdasya nityatvādeva ca devapravāhanityatvaṃ yuktam // 29//
children.translated_text: Precisely because of the eternality of the Vedic word (<s>śabda</s>), the eternality of the deities in the flow-sense (<s>deva-pravāha-nityatva</s>) is also established. // 29 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.13:
yuktyantareṇa devapravāhasya nityatāṃ sādhayatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - ataeveti // ataevetyanuvādaḥ / tasya vyākhyānaṃ - 'śabdasya'; vedasya nityatvādeveti / evakāreṇa na devapravāhanityatve yuktyantaraṃ gaveṣaṇīyaṃ, kintu yatpūrvapakṣiṇā vedanityatvaṃ sapramāṇakamuktaṃ, tata eva tadanyathānupapattyaitatsidhyatīti sūcayati / nityatvādevetyupalakṣaṇaṃ, pramāṇasya sādhitatvenāprāmāṇyābhāvādevetyapi ataḥśabdavyākhyānaṃ draṣṭavyam / anyathā pūrvapakṣī aprāmāṇyenānyathopapattiṃ brūyāt devapravāhasya / yuktamiti ca sūtraśeṣoktiḥ / 'yuktaṃ'; vedanityatvānyathānupapattyākhyayuktisiddham / caśabdastu samuccetavyayuktīnāṃ śabdātpratyakṣādanumānādityanena darśitatvāttatsamuccayārthakatayār'thādvyākhyātaḥ / ataeva pūrvasūtrabhāṣye caśabdaḥ saṃyojitaḥ / atrāpi bhāṣye caśabdena ca tadvācyadevatāsvarūpasyaiva nityatvena anyathopapattiḥ / ataeva 'sūryācandramasau'; (mahānā.5-7.) 'yathaiva'; ityādyudāhṛtaśrutereva 'yamapyeti bhuvanaṃ sāmparāye'; (nṛ.pū.2-5.) 'yatprayantyabhisaṃviśanti'; (tai.3-1.) ityādi bahulaṃ pralayaśruteśca sūryādidevānāmutpattināśāvagamāt, ataeva svarūpanityatvāyogena pravāharūpeṇaiva teṣāṃ nityatvāvaśyaṃbhāvādityādiṭīkoktārthaḥ sarvo 'pi saṅgṛhītaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.8.13:
Having cited the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the eternality of the divine stream (<s>devapravāha</s>) through another reasoning, he explains it — beginning with '<s>ata eva</s>' (for this very reason). // '<s>Ata eva</s>' is a repetition. Its explanation is: '<s>śabdasya</s>' — because of the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> alone. By the particle '<s>eva</s>' (alone), it is indicated that no other reasoning need be sought for the eternality of the divine stream; rather, that which was stated by the prima facie opponent — the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> — along with evidence, from that alone, because of the impossibility of explaining it otherwise, this [eternality of the divine stream] is established. '<s>Nityatvāt eva</s>' is indicative; the explanation of the word '<s>ataḥ</s>' should also be seen as: 'because of the absence of invalidity, since the means of valid knowledge has been established as valid.' Otherwise, the prima facie opponent would state an alternative explanation through invalidity [of the <s>Veda</s>] for the divine stream. '<s>Yuktam</s>' is the conclusion of the <s>sūtra</s>. '<s>Yuktam</s>' — established through the reasoning called the impossibility of explaining [the <s>Veda</s>'s eternality] otherwise without the eternality of the <s>Veda</s>. The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is explained implicitly as having the purpose of accumulating the reasonings that are to be accumulated — namely, word (<s>śabda</s>), perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), etc. — as shown [earlier]. Therefore, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the previous <s>sūtra</s>, the word '<s>ca</s>' was connected. Here too, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, by the word '<s>ca</s>': the impossibility of explaining otherwise is [established] by the eternality of the essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) of the deities denoted by those [Vedic words]. Therefore — from the very <s>śruti</s> cited earlier, namely '<s>sūryācandramasau</s>' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 5.7), '<s>yathaiva</s>' and so on, and also from abundant dissolution-<s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>yam apyeti bhuvanaṃ sāmparāye</s>' (<s>Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīya</s> 2.5) and '<s>yat prayanty abhisaṃviśanti</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.1) — since the origination and destruction of the gods like the sun are understood, and therefore, because their essential-nature-eternality is impossible, and their eternality in the form of a stream is necessarily required — thus the entire meaning stated in the <s>Ṭīkā</s> is also encompassed.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
And because of the sameness of names and forms, even upon [their] return, there is no contradiction — because of <s>darśana</s> (scriptural vision) and <s>smṛti</s> (tradition). | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.30 |

Because of the sameness of names and forms of the gods of past and future [<s>kalpas</s>], who have attained their respective positions,
even upon [their] return through liberation, there is no contradiction.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.14:
nanu na devānāṃ pravāhanityatvenāpi vedaprāmāṇyopapattiḥ / tathā hi - kiṃ pūrvakalpe muktā eva devā uttarakalpe punarāvartante, tadanye vā / nādyaḥ / mukterapunarāvṛttitvāt / na dvitīyaḥ / tathātve dharmibhūtadevānityatvahetukavirodhābhāve 'pi nāmarūpādidharmavaicitryakṛtavirodhaprāpteḥ, vācakavedasya pratikalpaṃ pāṭhabhedābhāvenaikavidhatvāt, anyathā nityatvavyāghātāt / vācyadevānāṃ ca nānāvidhanāmarūpavattvādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - samāneti // atrātītapadaṃ prācīnaparam / anāgatapadaṃ ca tadanyabhaviṣyadvartamānaparam / dharmipratiyogyubhayasamarpakametat / nāma indrādi, rūpam ākṛtiḥ / sūtrānusārādatrāpi caśabdaḥ saṃyojyaḥ / samānadharmakarmavattvācceti tadarthaḥ /
svapadeṣvati śeṣaḥ / muktyā'vṛttāvapītyuktiḥ pūrvapakṣyāśaṅkitavirodhe hetusūcanārthā / yadyapitathāpītyarthe 'piśabdaḥ āvartate / śabda ityasti / tathā cetthaṃ yojanā - 'prāptapadānāṃ'; prācīnānāṃ devānāṃ 'muktyā'; prāptamuktitvena kāraṇena punasteṣāmeva svapadeṣu 'avṛttāvapi'; asattve 'pi tadanyeṣāṃ tatra satve 'pi ca 'avirodhaḥ'; ma tadvācake ekavidhe 'pi śabde vede 'prāmāṇyākhyo virodhaḥ / kutaḥ? vācyānāmapyatītānāgatānāṃ devānāṃ parasparaṃ 'samānanāmarūpatvāt'; samāne ekavidhe nāmarūpe yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ, teṣāṃ bhāvastattvaṃ tasmāditi / candrikāyāṃ tu - sūtre bhāṣye ca tattvapradīpānusārādāvṛttāviti vicchedaṃ bhāṣye muktyāvṛttāvityasyaikapadyaṃ cāśritya ekasya padaprāptāvanyasya muktiḥ, punastasya muktau punaranyasya padaprāptiriti krameṇa mukterāvṛttāvapīti vā, svasvapadasyāvṛttāvapīti veti ṭīkānuktaprakāradvayenāpyāvṛttāvityaṃśo vyākhyātaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.8.14:
Objection: Even with the eternality of the divine stream, the validity of the <s>Veda</s> is not established. For consider: do the gods who were liberated in a previous <s>kalpa</s> return again in the next <s>kalpa</s>, or do different ones [take their places]? Not the first — because liberation is of the nature of non-return. Not the second — because even if there were no contradiction arising from the non-eternality of the gods as substrates, there would arise a contradiction from the diversity of names, forms, and other attributes; for the <s>Veda</s>, which is the expression, being uniform in its recitation across <s>kalpas</s> without variation in reading — otherwise, its eternality would be contradicted — while the expressed gods have diverse names and forms — anticipating this objection, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and explains it — beginning with '<s>samāna</s>' (same). // Here the word '<s>atīta</s>' (past) refers to what is prior. The word '<s>anāgata</s>' (future) refers to the forthcoming and present that are different from the past. This [compound] indicates both — the substrate-entities and their counter-correlates. '<s>Nāma</s>' (name) means [names like] <s>Indra</s> etc.; '<s>rūpa</s>' (form) means appearance. In accordance with the <s>sūtra</s>, the word '<s>ca</s>' should be connected here too. '<s>Samāna-dharma-karmavattvāt ca</s>' — and because of having the same attributes and actions — this is its meaning.
'In their respective positions' is the remainder. The statement '<s>muktyāvṛttāv api</s>' (even upon non-return through liberation) is intended to indicate the reason within the contradiction apprehended by the prima facie opponent. The word '<s>api</s>' has the sense of 'even though.' The word '<s>śabda</s>' (word) is present [from the <s>sūtra</s>]. And thus the construction is: '<s>prāptapadānām</s>' — of the prior gods who have attained their positions — '<s>muktyā</s>' — by their having attained liberation — '<s>avṛttāv api</s>' — even though they themselves are not present in their respective positions, and even though others are present there — '<s>avirodhaḥ</s>' — there is no contradiction called invalidity in the uniform <s>Veda</s>-word. Why? Because of '<s>samāna-nāma-rūpatva</s>' — because past and future gods have the same names and forms — and because of having the same reality (<s>tattva</s>). In the <s>Candrikā</s>, however — based on the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>Bhāṣya</s> following the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, adopting the division '<s>āvṛttau</s>' (upon return) and the single-word-ness of '<s>muktyāvṛttau</s>' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — when one [god] attains a position, another's liberation [occurs], and upon that one's liberation, yet another attains the position — thus, by sequence, even when liberation undergoes '<s>āvṛtti</s>' (recurrence) — or alternatively, even upon the return of their respective positions — the portion '<s>āvṛttau</s>' is explained in two additional ways beyond what the <s>Ṭīkā</s> stated.
Because of the <s>darśana</s> (scriptural vision) in '<s>yathā pūrvam</s>' (as before) (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 5.7).

To this, the portion '<s>darśanāt</s>' (because of the scriptural vision) is explained — beginning with '<s>yathā</s>.' // The meaning is: from the <s>śruti</s> '<s>dhātā yathā pūrvam</s>' (the Creator, as before).

The names of the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) and the visions (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) that are [seen] in the <s>Vedas</s> —

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.16:
nanvetacchrutestattatsvarūpakalpanāniyamaparatvamapi sambhavatīti nānayā samānanāmarūpatvaniścayo bhavati/ kiṃ ca devapravāhasya nityatve teṣāṃ samānanāmarūpatve vā na tadvācitvena nityavedaprāmāṇyopaptiḥ, tadvācitvasyaivāsambhavāt / na hyapauruṣeyasya vedasyaitāvatkālamayaṃ devo mayoktaḥ, ataḥ paramenaṃ vakṣyāmīti vimṛśya vṛttiḥ sambhavatītyataḥ prāptaḥ smṛterityaṃśa ityāśayena tāṃ darśayati - anādīti // nityatvokterupacaritatvavāraṇāya - anādinidhanetyuktam / ato na paunaruktyam / ata eva tattvapradīpe anādinidhanatvena nityā, na tvanidhanatvamātreṇetyuktam / bahukālīnatvena vetspi draṣṭavyam / vedeṣvityanantaramuktā iti śeṣaḥ / nirmame ityasyāvṛttiḥ / tatheti śeṣaḥ / tenāpyevaśabdasyānvayaḥ / tathā ca 'ādau'; sṛṣṭikāle 'svayambhuvā'; svatantreṇa maheśvareṇa viṣṇunā 'anādinidhanā nityā'; ādyantaśūnyatayaiva nityā, na tūpacāreṇa bahukālīnatāmātreṇānidhanatvamātreṇa nityā / yā 'vāk'; vedarūpā 'utsṛṣṭā'; uccāritā / 'tadvedaśabdebhyaḥ'; vedagatebhyaḥ tebhyaḥ śabdebhya eva, nānyebhyaḥ, 'saḥ'; maheśvaro viṣṇuḥ 'ṛṣīṇāṃ'; brahmādivibudhānāṃ 'nāmadheyāni nirmame'; tāneva śabdān teṣu saṅketitavān pratikalpamayaṃ śabdo 'tra śakta iti jñāpitavān / 'yāśca'; ṛṣīṇāṃ devānāṃ vedeṣūktāḥ dṛśyante iti dṛṣṭayo rūpāṇi, tāśca tāni ca tathaiva pūrvakalpīyarūpasādṛśyenaiva nirmame iti smṛtyarthaḥ / caḥ samuccaye / darśanātsmṛterityanayoḥ samānarūpatvādityanenānvayaḥ / āgamopalakṣakaṃ caitat / tathā ca nāsiddhiriti bhāvaḥ / anena - prācīnānāṃ devānāṃ muktyā punaḥ svapadeṣvavṛttāvapi tadanyeṣāṃ tatra vṛttāvapi na tadvācake ekavidhe 'pi śabde 'prāmāṇyākhyo virodhaḥ / kutaḥ? prācīnānāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ cānyonyaṃ 'samānanāmarūpatvāt'; tadyogyakarmadharmavattvācca / na ca hetvasiddhiḥ / 'darśanāt'; 'yathā pūrvam'; iti śruteḥ 'anādinidhanā'; iti smṛteśceti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati / atra tattvapradīpe pralaye kasyāpi devasyābhāvena tadā vedasya vācyahīnatvarūpāprāmāṇyamāśaṅkya bhagavanmātraviṣayatvena tadupapattiriti samādhānamabhipretya 'śabde'; kadāpi vācyahīnatvakṛto virodhaḥ aprāmāṇyam / kutaḥ? mukhyavācyasya viṣṇoḥ sarvadā vidyamānatvāt / kuta etat? 'ata eva'; śabdātteṣāṃ devānāṃ prabhavaniyamādikarturapīśasya sadā sattvāvagamāt/ pratyakṣaścāsau mahatām/ kutaḥ? 'ataeva'; 'puruṣamīhate'; 'kavayo vayanti'; (mahānā.1-3.) ityādiśrutereva itareṣāmanumānācca / yathā yena prakāreṇedānīṃ devā bhavanti tathānyadāpītyanumānācca tadavagamaḥ / evam 'ataeva'; śabdanityatvādeva pravoḍhurnityatvam / tathā viṣṇossamānanāmarūpatvādanyeṣāṃ tadabhāvācca 'avirodhaḥ'; na tasya sarvaśabdavācyatvavirodhaḥ / samānāni sadṛśāni nāmāni yeṣāṃ rūpāṇāṃ tāni tathoktāni, tādṛśāni rūpāṇi yasya sa tathoktaḥ tasya bhāvastasmāt / na hi viṣṇvanyarūpāṇāṃ sadṛśanāmarūpatvaṃ, śabdapravṛttihetuvaikalyāt / na cātra mānābhāvaḥ, 'yathāpūrvam'; iti darśanāt / yathā pūrvaṃ pūrṇajñānaḥ sarvasvatantraḥ sarvanāmarūpasthitastathaiva sa dhātā sūryādīnakalpayaditi śruteḥ / ataḥ sūryādikḷpteḥ prāgapi pralaye śabdaprāmāṇyāvirodha iti siddhamiti / idamevābhipretya ṭīkāyāṃ 'na ca'; ityādinā śaṅkottare darśite / 'atītaviṣayatvasya ca'; iti parihārottaraṃ cābhihitam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.8.16:
Objection: But that <s>śruti</s> could also refer to the restriction of constructing each particular essential nature, and thus the certainty of sameness of names and forms would not follow from it. Moreover, whether the divine stream is eternal or whether their names and forms are the same, the validity of the <s>Veda</s> as denoting them is not established — because the very denotation [of the gods by the <s>Veda</s>] is impossible. For in the authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) <s>Veda</s>, a deliberation such as 'This god has been spoken of by me up to now; henceforth I shall speak of another' cannot possibly occur. Therefore, the portion '<s>smṛteḥ</s>' (because of <s>smṛti</s>) is shown with this intention — beginning with '<s>anādi</s>' (beginningless). // The statement '<s>anādinidhanā</s>' (beginningless and endless) is to prevent the eternality statement from being taken figuratively. Therefore there is no redundancy. For this very reason, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> it is said: eternal in the sense of being beginningless and endless, not merely in the sense of being without end alone. '<s>Bahukālīna</s>' (of long duration) should also be seen [as included] by way of exclusion. After '<s>vedeṣu</s>' (in the <s>Vedas</s>), '<s>uktā</s>' (stated) is to be supplied. '<s>Nirmame</s>' (created) recurs [in construal]. '<s>Tathā</s>' (thus) is to be supplied. Therefore the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) also connects. And thus — 'in the beginning' — at the time of creation — 'by <s>Svayambhū</s>' — by the independent great Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the '<s>vāk</s>' (speech) — in the form of the <s>Veda</s> — that is '<s>anādinidhanā nityā</s>' — eternal in the sense of being without beginning or end, not merely figuratively eternal as being of long duration or endlessness alone — was '<s>utsṛṣṭā</s>' — uttered. 'From those <s>Veda</s>-words' — from those very words in the <s>Veda</s>, and not from others — 'He' — the great Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> — 'created the <s>nāmadheyāni</s>' (names) 'of the <s>ṛṣis</s>' — of <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods — meaning He established the conventional connection (<s>saṅketa</s>) of those very words with them in every <s>kalpa</s>: 'this word has power [to denote] this [entity]' — thus He made it known. 'And the <s>dṛṣṭayaḥ</s>' — the forms of the <s>ṛṣis</s> and gods that are stated and seen in the <s>Vedas</s> — and those too He created in the very same manner, i.e., in resemblance to the forms of the previous <s>kalpa</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>smṛti</s>. The word '<s>ca</s>' is for accumulation. '<s>Darśanāt smṛteḥ</s>' (from scriptural vision and tradition) — their syntactic connection is with '<s>samāna-rūpatvāt</s>' (because of sameness of form). And this is also indicative of <s>āgama</s> (tradition). And thus the meaning is: there is no unestablished-ness [of the reason]. By this — even though the prior gods do not return to their positions due to liberation, and others occupy those positions, there is no contradiction called invalidity in the uniform <s>Veda</s>-word. Why? Because past and future gods have '<s>samāna-nāma-rūpatva</s>' (sameness of names and forms), and also because they possess the same actions and attributes. Nor is the reason unestablished — 'because of the <s>darśana</s>' in '<s>yathā pūrvam</s>' (as before) from the <s>śruti</s>, and because of the '<s>smṛti</s>' '<s>anādinidhanā</s>' (beginningless and endless) — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated. Here, in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>, anticipating the objection that in dissolution no god exists at all, and therefore the <s>Veda</s> at that time, being devoid of anything expressed, would be invalid — [the reply is:] the validity is established because it pertains to <s>Bhagavān</s> alone [as its referent] — with this intention, [the following is stated]: '<s>śabde</s>' — in the word [<s>Veda</s>], the contradiction called invalidity arising from being devoid of anything expressed at any time — why [does it not arise]? Because the primary expressed [entity], <s>Viṣṇu</s>, always exists. Whence is this? '<s>Ata eva</s>' — from the word (<s>śabda</s>) alone — because from it, the existence at all times of the Lord who is the controller of the origination etc. of those gods is understood. And He is directly perceived by the great ones. Whence? '<s>Ata eva</s>' — from the very <s>śruti</s> '<s>puruṣam īhate</s>' (they strive after the <s>Puruṣa</s>), '<s>kavayo vayanti</s>' (the wise ones weave, <s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 1.3) and the like, and from the inference of others. By the inference 'in whatever manner the gods exist now, so also at other times' — this understanding [is obtained]. Thus, '<s>ata eva</s>' — from the eternality of the word (<s>śabda</s>) alone — the eternality of the stream [of deities] [is established]. Likewise, because of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s sameness of names and forms and the absence thereof in others — '<s>avirodhaḥ</s>' — there is no contradiction of His being denoted by all words. '<s>Samānāni</s>' (same) — similar — are the '<s>nāmāni</s>' (names) of whose '<s>rūpāṇi</s>' (forms) — they are so described. Such forms belong to one who is so described — because of the reality of that [sameness]. For the forms of entities other than <s>Viṣṇu</s> do not have sameness of names and forms — because of the deficiency of the cause of the operation of the word. Nor is there absence of evidence here — '<s>darśanāt</s>' (because of the scriptural vision): from the <s>śruti</s> '<s>yathā pūrvam</s>' (as before) — [meaning] just as before, possessed of full knowledge, fully independent, established in all names and forms — in the same way He, the Creator, fashioned the sun and the like. Therefore, even before the creation of the sun and the like, i.e., during dissolution, there is no contradiction with the validity of the word — thus it is established. With this very intention, in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, the objection and its resolution are shown by '<s>na ca</s>' and so on. And the subsequent objection '<s>atītaviṣayatvasya ca</s>' and its resolution are also stated.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //

<s>Jaimini</s> [holds that] there is non-eligibility (<s>anadhikāra</s>) [of gods for <s>madhu-vidyā</s> and the like], because of the impossibility [of the stated fruit] in the case of honey (<s>madhu</s>) and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.31 |
