BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.17:
nanu na devānāṃ vedavidyādhikāro yuktaḥ / tathā hi dvividhā vedavidyāḥ - muktiphalārthāstaditaraphalārthā iti / mokṣetaraphalā api dvividhāḥ / brahmakarmavidyābhedāt / tatrādyā yathā - madhuvidyā / dvitīyā yathā - agniṣṭomavidyā / tatra na tāvaddevānāṃ mokṣetaraphalakadvividhavidyāsvadhikāro yujyate, tatsādhyānāṃ mokṣetaraphalānāṃ madhye keṣāñcidyogyānāṃ prāptatvena ayogyānāṃ ca prāptumaśakyatvena arthitvābhāvāditi jaiminimatāvalambenākṣipatsūtramunyasya vyācaṣṭe - madhvādiṣviti // prathamādipadena śiṣṭavākyaṃ, tathā 'devo bhūtvā devānapyeti'; (bṛ.6-1-2.) iti vājasaneyavākyaṃ, tathā 'sa ūrjamupagacchati'; iti śrutyantaravākyaṃ, dvitīyamadhuvidyāntgataṃ 'rudrāṇāmevaiko bhūtvā'; (chāṃ. 3-7-2.) ityādikaṃ ca gṛhyate / prāpyaphalatvāt aprāpyaphalatvādityubhayathā vicchedaḥ / asyobhayatrānvayaḥ / vasvādipadānāmiti śeṣaḥ / tatrādipadena devarudrādipadānāṃ grahaṇam / yadvā - prāptapadānāmityatratyaṃ padānāmityetadbuddhyā vivicyātra dharmitvena sambadhyate / prāptapadānāmiti bahuvrīhiḥ, karmadhārayaśca / tatrādyo hetugarbhaviśeṣaṇarūpaḥ / dvitīyasyobhayatrānvayaḥ / devānāmiti sūtre adhyāhṛtaṃ padaṃ, prakaraṇalabdhaṃ vā / madhuśabdo 'madhu'; ityupakramyāmnātaprathamadvitīyādyamṛtavidyāparaḥ / atrādiśabdena vasvādipadaphalakakarmavidyā vājasaneyoktavāgādividyāśca gṛhyante / etaccāvartanīyam / asambhavāditi sautro heturatrāpi saṃyojyaḥ / tadupapādakoktyaiva taduktirbhavatīti tasya sākṣādanuktiḥ / yadvā - prāptapadānāmaprāpyaphalatvādityuktyaiva tasyoktatvādasambhavāditi na saṃyojyam / tathā cetthaṃ bhāṣyayojanā - madhvādividyāsu 'asau vā ādityo devamadhu'; iti prastutyāmnātena 'sa etadevāmṛtaṃ veda vasūnāmevaiko bhūtvā agninaiva mukhenaitadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati'; ityādivākye 'padānāṃ'; vasvādipadānāṃ 'prāpyaphalatvāt'; madhvādividyāsūktopāsanāprāpyaphalatvaśravaṇāt 'prāptapadānāṃ ca'; vasvādidevānāṃ prāptasvasvapadatvena 'asambhavāt'; tadarthitvāsambhavāt 'devānāṃ'; devaiḥ prāptapadānāṃ punastaiḥ 'aprāpyaphalatvāt'; aprārthyaphalatvāditi vā / dvitīyavidyādyamṛtavidyāphalānāṃ rudrādipadānāṃ ca vasvādidevānām 'aprāpyaphalatvāt'; prāptumayogyaphalatvāt tatrāpyarthitvāsambhavātteṣāṃ madhvādividyāsu 'anadhikāram anadhikārābhāvaṃ jaiminirmanyata'; iti / jaiminigrahaṇena āptatamena jaimininaivaṃ matatvācca na teṣāmadhikāra iti yuktyantaraṃ sūcyate / anena - 'madhvādiṣu'; 'asau vā ādityo devamadhu'; ityādimadhuvidyāsu devānām 'anadhikāram'; anadhikārābhāvaṃ jaiminirmanyate tasmāddhetoḥ 'asambhavāt'; taistadvidyāsūktaphalānāṃ madhye keṣāñcidyogyānāṃ prāptatvena keṣāñcitprāptumayogyatvena teṣāṃ tatrārthitvāsambhavāditi āptatamo jaiminirmanyata iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
chāndogye hi - 'asau vā ādityaḥ'; ityanena ādityasya viṣṇoḥ paramānandatvena madhutvamuktvā 'sa etat'; ityādinā madhuśabditasya bhagavata ādityamaṇḍalasya pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarordhvaraśmiṣu sthitānāṃ prathamāmṛtādiśabdapañcakavācyavāsudevasaṅkarṣaṇapradyumnāniruddhanārāyaṇākhyapañcarūpāṇāṃ madhye prācyāditattaddiksthataiḥ tattatpadayogyairvasurudrādityamarutsādhyapadoktaṛjurūpapañcagaṇasthairdevaiḥ krameṇa agnivāyvindrasomaviriñcapradhānakaiḥ agnyādimukhenaikaikopāstau kṛtāyāṃ tadaparokṣajñānajanitatatprasādadvārā vasvādipadaprāptistattadgaṇasthānāṃ bhavatītyucyate / tathā ca 'yaḥ'; adhikārī 'etat amṛtaṃ'; vāsudevākhyaṃ rūpam 'evam'; uktaprakāreṇa 'veda'; 'sa ca vasūnāmapyeko bhūtvā'; vasubhogyadeśakālādhipo bhūtvā 'agninā mukhena'; tatprādhānyena tadupadeśeneti yāvat / 'etadevāmṛtaṃ'; vāsudevākhyaṃ 'dṛṣṭvā'; sākṣātkṛtya 'tṛpyati'; mukto bhavatītyarthaḥ / evaṃ 'yo'; devatvayogyo adhikārī vākprāṇacakṣuḥśrotramanohṛdayanāmakaṃ brahmopāste sa devatvamapyeti tato 'devo bhūtvā'; svottamadeveṣu sāyujyaṃ prāpya devān śvetadvīpagatabhagavadrūpaviśeṣān caturmukhabrahmaṇā sahāpyeti / so 'dhikārī 'ūrjam'; annam 'upagacchati'; yatheṣṭaṃ prāpnoti iti śrutyantarārthaḥ /

Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.3.8, verse 17:
Objection: The qualification of devas for Vedic knowledge is not appropriate. For Vedic knowledge-disciplines are of two kinds — those aimed at the fruit of liberation, and those aimed at other fruits. Even the non-liberation-fruit disciplines are of two kinds, due to the distinction between Brahma-vidyā (knowledge-disciplines) and karma-vidyā (action-disciplines). Among them, the first kind is, for example, the Madhuvidyā. The second kind is, for example, the Agniṣṭoma-vidyā. Now, the qualification of devas for the two kinds of disciplines that have non-liberation fruits is not appropriate — because among the non-liberation fruits achievable through them, some eligible fruits have already been attained, and the ineligible ones cannot be attained, hence there is absence of desire — raising this objection relying on Jaimini's view, he explains the sūtra of the other [sage] — 'in Madhuvidyā and the like.' // By the first word 'ādi,' the authorized statements such as 'Having become a deva, he reaches the devas' (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 6.1.2) — a Vājasaneya passage — and 'He approaches vitality (ūrja)' — another śruti passage — and the second, included within the Madhuvidyā: 'Having become one among the Rudras' (Chāndogya 3.7.2) and the like, are included. The analysis can be divided two ways: 'because of attainable-fruit-ness' and 'because of unattainable-fruit-ness.' Both connect in both places. 'Of the stations of Vasu and the like' is the remainder. By the word 'ādi,' the stations of Deva, Rudra, and the like are included. Alternatively, in 'of those who have attained stations,' the word 'stations' (padānām) is analytically separated by intellect and connected here as the dharmin (subject). 'Those who have attained stations' is both a bahuvrīhi compound and a karmadhāraya. Among them, the first is in the form of a reason-bearing qualifier. The second connects in both places. 'Of devas' is either a word to be supplied in the sūtra or obtained from the context. The word 'madhu' refers to the first, second, and subsequent amṛta-vidyās (immortality-disciplines) taught beginning with 'madhu' (honey). By the word 'ādi' here, the karma-vidyās whose fruits are the stations of Vasu and the like, and the Vāk-ādi-vidyās stated in the Vājasaneya, are included. This also recurs. 'Because of impossibility' — the sūtra-reason should be connected here too. Because the statement of the reason is accomplished by the very statement that establishes it, there is no direct statement of it. Alternatively, since it is already stated by the expression 'because of the unattainable-fruit-ness of those who have attained stations,' 'because of impossibility' need not be connected. And thus the bhāṣya construction is as follows: in Madhuvidyā and the like, in the passage 'That sun is the divine honey' — having been introduced by this, 'He who knows this amṛta in this way, having become one among the Vasus, through Agni alone as the means, having seen this amṛta, is satisfied' — in such a passage, 'of the stations' — of the stations of Vasu and the like — 'because of attainable-fruit-ness' — because of the hearing that the fruit of the worship taught in Madhuvidyā and the like is attainable; 'and of those who have attained stations' — of the Vasu and other devas who have already attained their respective stations — 'because of impossibility' — because of the impossibility of desire for that; 'of the devas' — of those who have attained stations through the devas — 'because of unattainable-fruit-ness' — or because of the fruits of the second vidyā — the Dvitīyāmṛta-vidyā — being the stations of Rudra and the like, and of these being unattainable by the Vasu and other devas — 'because of unattainable-fruit-ness' — because of the fruits being of an ineligible kind that cannot be attained — therefore, because of the impossibility of desire there too — their non-qualification in Madhuvidyā and the like — 'Jaimini holds there is absence of qualification.' By citing Jaimini, the additional reason is indicated: since the most authoritative Jaimini too holds this view, there is no qualification for them. By this — 'in Madhuvidyā and the like' — 'That sun is the divine honey' and the like — in the Madhuvidyā, the non-qualification of devas — the absence of qualification — Jaimini holds, for the reason 'because of impossibility' — because of the impossibility of desire for them for the vidyā-taught fruits, since some eligible fruits have already been attained and some are of an ineligible kind that cannot be attained — so the most authoritative Jaimini holds: thus the sūtra meaning is stated.
For in the Chāndogya — having stated that the sun, being Viṣṇu, is honey (madhu) because of being of supreme bliss, by the passage 'That sun [is the divine honey]' — then by 'He who knows this' and the like, among the five forms — Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, and Nārāyaṇa — denoted by the five words beginning with 'first amṛta' (nectar), situated in the eastern and other directional rays and the upward rays of the sun-maṇḍala of Bhagavān denoted by the word 'madhu' — by the devas belonging to the five groups of upright forms, spoken of by the station-words Vasu, Rudra, Āditya, Marut, and Sādhya, who are eligible for the respective stations in the respective directions, and who are headed by Agni, Vāyu, Indra, Soma, and Viriñca respectively — when each one performs worship through Agni and the other means respectively, the attainment of the station of Vasu and the like for the members of each group is stated as occurring through the grace produced by the direct knowledge generated therefrom. And thus: 'He who' — the qualified aspirant — 'this amṛta' — the form called Vāsudeva — 'in this way' — in the manner described — 'knows'; 'and he, having become one among the Vasus' — having become the lord of the Vasu-realm and its pleasures — 'through Agni as the means' — principally through that, i.e., through instruction from Agni. 'This amṛta' — called Vāsudeva — 'having seen' — having directly perceived — 'is satisfied' — becomes liberated: that is the meaning. Similarly, 'he who' — the deva-eligible qualified aspirant — worships the Brahman called Vāk, Prāṇa, Cakṣus, Śrotra, Manas, and Hṛdaya, he attains deva-hood; then 'having become a deva' — having attained union with his own superior devas — he reaches the devas — the specific Bhagavad-rūpas (divine forms) situated in Śvetadvīpa — together with Caturmukha Brahmā. That aspirant 'approaches ūrja (vitality)' — attains food as desired: this is the meaning of another śruti.
Sūtra — Oṃ //
Because of [their already] being in the light (jyotiṣi), and [because of their already] being [omniscient]. | Brahmasūtra 1.3.32 |
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.8, verse 18:]

Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.3.8, verse 18:
Objection: Even if devas do not have qualification for knowledge-disciplines whose fruits are other than liberation, still, there will be qualification for liberation-aimed knowledge-disciplines such as 'Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite' (Taittirīya 2.1.1) and the like, since desire for liberation is possible in them — to this doubt, he reads the sūtra that resolves it and explains: 'jyotiṣi' (in the light). // 'Jyotiṣi' is a citation of the sūtra-word. Its explanation is 'sarvajñatva' (omniscience). Although 'in knowledge' should be the explanation, nevertheless, since knowledge unqualified by its object cannot be ascertained, and since the inclusion of everything as an object is not established when it comes to knowledge of just anything — to convey this, he explained it as 'sarvajñatva' (omniscience). Thereby it is indicated that in the sūtra, the word 'vastūnām' (of things) is to be supplied as a word indicating the inclusion-relation. The word 'ca' is for accumulation. The connection of this reason, through the reason 'because of impossibility' carried forward, is with the preceding: in Madhuvidyā and the like, Jaimini holds there is absence of qualification. By this, through the word 'ādi' in 'in Madhuvidyā and the like,' liberation-aimed knowledge-disciplines are also included. And the word 'jyotiḥ' recurs, as 'jyotiṣi iva jyotiṣi' (in light, as in light). And it is indicated that the seventh case ending (locative), like 'in the intellect of Caitraratha' in 'śāstrārtha' (the meaning of the śāstra), is appropriate — this is indicated. How is there inclusion of things in knowledge? — to this, he explains 'because of being in omniscience' in his own words — 'āditya' (sun). Just as all things are included within the light of the sun — so too, in that knowledge which is the subject — the knowledge produced by the devas — all things are 'included' — have become objects: that is the meaning. He reveals the implication — 'nitya' (eternally). Because of the devas' omniscience, 'of the knowledge-disciplines' — of the knowledge achievable through all Brahma-vidyās and karma-vidyās — 'eternally accomplished' — necessarily already attained: that is the meaning. Alternatively, 'of the knowledge-disciplines' — of the knowledge-producing disciplines — 'eternally, necessarily accomplished' — i.e., already apprehended: that is the meaning. Because the devas are seers of the Vedas: this is the purport. Or alternatively, 'of the knowledge-disciplines' — of the subjects taught in the disciplines that produce knowledge for liberation and other purposes — 'eternally accomplished' — necessarily already known by them: that is the meaning. And thus there is no desire of the devas for the knowledge achievable through both kinds of vidyā: this is the purport. The connection of these two ablative-ending [reasons] is with the preceding as before. Nor should it be said: how can the word 'ca' be appropriate here when this reason establishes the impossibility-reason stated in the previous sūtra? Because what is intended in the preceding is the impossibility of desire from the standpoint of fruit, and here from the standpoint of means — since this reason establishes a second impossibility, there is appropriateness of the word 'ca' due to the generality of impossibility as an establishing factor. Although in the Bhāṣya, the sūtra 'jyotiṣi' appears to convey a defect from the standpoint of means in both alternatives — whether devas have qualification in non-liberation-fruit or liberation-fruit vidyā — in the Ṭīkā, however, it is explained as conveying a defect from the standpoint of means for the second alternative alone: that devas have no qualification even in liberation-aimed vidyā, since even though desire for the fruit exists, there is no desire for the knowledge that constitutes the worship of vidyā, and since vidyā is for the purpose of knowledge, and since knowledge has already been attained. And thus there is a discrepancy. Nevertheless, in the earlier alternative that there is no qualification in non-liberation-fruit vidyās, the defect is not merely that desire is absent for the Vasu-station and the like because they have already been attained; but also, because desire is absent even for the knowledge that is the means to the Vasu-station and the like — this additional establishing factor for the impossibility-defect is stated, and since this is stated in the Ṭīkā, there is no discrepancy. Therefore there is no inappropriateness of the word 'ca' either — because it is appropriate when the earlier alternative is intended. 'He establishes this by another reason' — the Sattarkadīpavalī too proceeds with the intention of the first alternative. Or the word 'ca' is for the accumulation of both kinds of vidyā. By this — not only does Jaimini hold there is no qualification in Madhuvidyā and the like aimed at non-liberation fruits, but also in liberation-aimed vidyā such as 'Satyaṃ jñānam' and the like, included through the word 'ādi' or through the recurrent word 'jyotiḥ.' Why? 'In jyotiḥ, as it were' — just as in the light of the sun — 'in jyotiḥ' — in the all-encompassing knowledge of the deities — of all things — as objects — 'because of being [included]' — because the knowledge that is the means to liberation is already accomplished. Therefore there is no desire even for liberation, since it too is practically accomplished and hence there is impossibility of desire. Not only does Jaimini hold there is no qualification of Vasu and other devas in Madhuvidyā and the like because of the absence of desire for the fruit, but also 'in jyotiḥ' — in the knowledge that is the means to the Vasu-station fruit — too because of the impossibility of desire. Whence even that? 'In jyotiḥ' — in the knowledge of the devas — 'because of being [included]' — because of the inclusion of all things as objects, i.e., because the fruit-producing knowledge is already accomplished: thus also the sūtra meaning is stated.
Sūtra — Oṃ //
But Bādarāyaṇa [holds there is] qualification, for there is indeed [a special fruit]. | Brahmasūtra 1.3.33 |
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.8, verse 19:]

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 19:
Thus, when the position that the <s>devas</s> have no eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) for any <s>vidyās</s> has been established by one following <s>Jaimini</s>'s view — on the grounds that fruits suited to <s>mokṣa</s> and other worthy goals have already been attained by the <s>devas</s>, that unsuitable fruits cannot be attained, and that even <s>mokṣa</s> has been effectively obtained through their being knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, hence there is no desire [for it] — he [<s>Madhva</s>] cites and comments upon the <s>sūtra</s> that re-establishes their eligibility, [explaining the word] '<s>bhāvam</s>' (existence). By the phrase '<s>phalaviśeṣabhāvāt</s>' (because of the existence of a special fruit), the continuation of '<s>pūrvasmāt bhāvāt</s>' (from prior existence) in the <s>sūtra</s> is indicated. '[For those who have] attained their goals (<s>prāptapadānām</s>)' — '<s>pada</s>' means merely the attainable fruit, derived from '<s>padyate</s>' (is attained). By '<s>api</s>' (even/also), a qualifying sense is also [conveyed]. The word '<s>tu</s>' also carries the sense of '<s>api</s>'. And '<s>api ca</s>' is said to mean 'even though, nevertheless.' '<s>Devānām</s>' (of the gods) is a supplementary expression in the <s>sūtra</s>. '<s>Madhvādiṣu</s>' (in the <s>Madhu-vidyā</s> etc.) is a restatement of a carried-over word. Here, by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), all <s>Brahma-vidyās</s> and <s>karmas</s> aimed at fruits other than <s>mokṣa</s> and <s>mokṣa</s> itself are included. '<s>Adhikāram</s>' means '<s>adhikārabhāvam</s>' (the existence of eligibility). By this, the meaning of '<s>bhāvam</s>' is stated. '<s>Manyate</s>' (considers) is a supplementary expression. Since '<s>asti</s>' (there is) requires an agent, he shows it — '<s>prakāśaviśeṣaḥ</s>' (a special illumination), meaning a superior knowledge. The word '<s>hi</s>' is used in the sense of 'because.' And thus the construction is: The venerable <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> considers that the <s>devas</s> have eligibility in all <s>vidyās</s> such as the <s>Madhu-vidyā</s>. Nor is the objection valid that there is no desire [for these] because their fruits are already attained. Even though the <s>devas</s> have attained their goals and, being knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, have accomplished fruits other than <s>mokṣa</s>, and [some] unsuitable fruits cannot be attained — nevertheless, even for the <s>devas</s> who have attained their goals, because of the existence of a special fruit (<s>phalaviśeṣa</s>) — namely, a surplus (<s>atiśaya</s>) in the fruit of <s>mokṣa</s> that is suited to each one individually and cannot be achieved by mere knowledge alone — [which arises] through the performance of the <s>upāsanā</s> and <s>karma</s> prescribed in <s>vidyās</s> such as the <s>Madhu-vidyā</s>, there is the possibility of desire due to [the possibility of] attainment. Nor should it be said that since the surplus in the fruit is already established, and even though desire for it is possible, the <s>vidyās</s> that are the means to it are eternally established, and inquiry into <s>vidyā</s> is for the sake of knowledge, therefore desire for them is impossible — because, since those other than the Lord do not possess non-figurative omniscience, through inquiry into <s>vidyā</s>, a '<s>prakāśaviśeṣaḥ</s>' (special illumination), i.e., a special knowledge, '<s>asti</s>' (exists), i.e., is possible. By this, the commentary on the <s>sūtra</s> is shown. Here, the word '<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>' is used as a term of honor.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.8, verse 20:]
As much as there is devotion to the Supreme Reality, so much is the distinction in bliss;
And because of the possibility of illumination, except for the one Supreme, <s>Hari</s>,
And because of the conjunction of capability for them, worship even of the <s>devas</s>,

BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.20:
nanu tattadvidyoktopāsanakarmakaraṇābhyāṃ tattadvidyoktaphalādanyadapi phalaṃ prakāśaviśeṣaśca devānāṃ bhavatītyetat kuto jñāyate ityāśaṅkāṃ parihartumuktārthe hiśabdasūcitāṃ smṛtiṃ darśayati - yāvaditi // kriyata iti śeṣaḥ / svārthe tal / bhāvabhavitrorabhedavivakṣayā vā / siddhyatyasyeti śeṣaḥ / co hetusamuccaye / yadvā - ādyaścaḥ prakāśasya ceti sambadhyate / phalasamuccāyakaścāyam, asambhavasamuccaye ca / sambhavādityāvartate / tathā ca 'pare tattve'; paramātmasvarūpe 'asau vā ādityaḥ'; (chāṃ.3-1-1.) ityādinokte tadviṣaye 'devānāṃ'; devairvasvādibhiḥ 'yāvat'; yāvadadhikaṃ 'sevā'; 'eṣā sevā'; ityuktā śravaṇādirūpopāsanā kriyate 'tāvat'; tāvadadhikaṃ teṣāṃ 'sukhaviśeṣatā'; svargāpavargādisukhe 'tiśayaḥ svasvayogyo jñānamātreṇa sādhyaḥ siddhyati / yato 'taḥ 'paraṃ'; svatantraṃ harimekamṛte 'nyeṣāṃ 'prakāśasyāsambhavāt'; nirupacaritasārvajñyābhāvāt / ata eva vidyāvicāreṇa sādhyasya prakāśasya jñānaviśeṣasya sambhavāt, ata evārthitvasya sambhavātteṣāṃ devānāṃ 'sāmarthyayogāt'; sāmarthyasambhavācca vidvattāsambhavāccāpi prāptapadānāmapi 'devānāṃ'; devaiḥ 'sarvamupāsanaṃ'; sarvavidyoktopāsanaṃ sarvayajñādikarma ca 'nityaṃ'; niyamena 'vidhīyate'; śrutiṣu kartavyatvena bodhyata iti yojanā / caḥ samuccaye / aprakāśasyeti pāṭhe nirupacaritasārvajñyābhāvasyetyarthaḥ / tadā prakāśasya caśabdena grahaṇam / sambhavādityasya siddhatvāt sattvādityarthadvayam / pāṭhadvaye 'pyanyeṣāmiti śeṣaḥ / ekaśabdo avadhāraṇārtho viriñcasyāpi varjyatvanivārakaḥ skānde uktamiti śeṣaḥ / ataḥ phalaviśeṣabhāvādasti hi prakāśaviśeṣa ityanayornāsiddhiriti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 20:
Now, how is it known that through performing the <s>upāsanā</s> and <s>karma</s> prescribed in each <s>vidyā</s>, a fruit other than the one stated in that <s>vidyā</s> and a special illumination (<s>prakāśaviśeṣa</s>) accrue to the <s>devas</s>? To resolve this doubt, he cites the <s>smṛti</s> indicated by the word '<s>hi</s>' in the established meaning — beginning with '<s>yāvat</s>' (as much as). '<s>Kriyate</s>' (is performed) is the completion of the sentence. The suffix '<s>tal</s>' is in the reflexive sense. Or, by non-distinction between <s>bhāva</s> (being) and <s>bhavitṛ</s> (the agent of being). '<s>Siddhyati asya</s>' (it is accomplished for this one) is the completion. '<s>Ca</s>' is used for causal accumulation. Alternatively, the first '<s>ca</s>' connects with '<s>prakāśasya ca</s>' (and of illumination). And this '<s>ca</s>' is for accumulation of fruits and for accumulation of impossibility. '<s>Sambhavāt</s>' (because of possibility) is carried over. And thus: In the Supreme Reality (<s>pare tattve</s>), i.e., the nature of the Supreme Self, as stated by passages like 'That sun indeed' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.1.1) and others concerning that subject — 'of the <s>devas</s>' means by <s>devas</s> such as <s>Vasu</s> and others — 'as much as' (<s>yāvat</s>), meaning to a greater degree, '<s>sevā</s>' (devotion), i.e., the <s>upāsanā</s> in the form of <s>śravaṇa</s> etc. described as '<s>eṣā sevā</s>' (this is devotion) is performed, 'so much' (<s>tāvat</s>), to that greater degree, 'distinction in bliss' (<s>sukhaviśeṣatā</s>) — a surplus suited to each individual in the bliss of <s>svarga</s>, <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) and the like, achievable by mere knowledge alone, is accomplished. Because, except for the one independent <s>Hari</s>, 'of illumination there is impossibility' (<s>prakāśasya asambhavāt</s>), i.e., due to the absence of non-figurative omniscience for others. For this very reason, because of the possibility of illumination, i.e., special knowledge, achievable through inquiry into <s>vidyā</s>, and for this very reason, because of the possibility of desire, 'because of the conjunction of capability' (<s>sāmarthyayogāt</s>) for those <s>devas</s>, and also because of the possibility of scholarship — even for the <s>devas</s> who have attained their goals, 'all <s>upāsanā</s>' prescribed in all <s>vidyās</s>, and all <s>karma</s> including <s>yajñas</s> and the like, are 'eternally' (<s>nityam</s>), i.e., necessarily, 'enjoined' (<s>vidhīyate</s>), i.e., taught as obligatory in the <s>śrutis</s> — such is the construction. '<s>Ca</s>' is for accumulation. In the reading '<s>aprakāśasya</s>' (of non-illumination), the meaning is 'due to the absence of non-figurative omniscience.' In that case, '<s>prakāśasya</s>' (of illumination) is taken by the word '<s>ca</s>.' '<s>Sambhavāt</s>' being established, the two meanings are '<s>sattvāt</s>' (because of existence). In both readings, 'of others' (<s>anyeṣām</s>) is the completion. The word '<s>eka</s>' (one) is for the purpose of restriction and removes the exclusion of even <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). 'It is said in the <s>Skānda</s>' is the completion. Therefore, '<s>phalaviśeṣabhāvāt</s>' (because of the existence of a special fruit) and '<s>asti hi prakāśaviśeṣaḥ</s>' (for there is a special illumination) — these are not unestablished — such is the remainder of the sentence.
<s>Jaimini</s>'s view amounts only to the non-eligibility for the stated fruit; therefore there is no contradiction with his view.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.8, verse 21:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.21:
nanvastvevamasambhavādityuktayuktiparābhavaḥ / tathāpi devānāmadhikārābhyupagatāvāptatamajaiminimatavirodha ityata āha - ukteti // uktaṃ ca tat phalaṃ ca uktaṃ phalaṃ yasyeti ca vigrahaḥ / tathā ca tattadvidyoktaphalārthaṃ tatphalakaprāgāptajñānārthaṃ ca yo 'yamadhikārastadabhāvamātraṃ 'jaiminimatam'; jaiminyabhimatamityarthaḥ / mātraśabdena phalāntarārthādhikārābhāvo vyāvartyate / kimato yadyevamityata āha - ata iti jaiminyuktasya sūtrakāreṇāpyaṅgīkṛtatvāt, sūtrakṛduktasya ca jaimininā anirastatvānna tayorvirodhaḥ ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 21:
Granted, let it be so — let the refutation by the reasoning stated as '<s>asambhavāt</s>' (due to impossibility) stand. Still, if the eligibility of the <s>devas</s> is accepted, there would be contradiction with the view of <s>Jaimini</s>, who is most authoritative — to this he responds with '<s>ukta</s>' (stated). The compound is analyzed as: '<s>uktam</s>' (stated) and that is the '<s>phalam</s>' (fruit), i.e., '<s>uktaphalam</s>' (the stated fruit) of which — such is the analysis. Thus, what <s>Jaimini</s>'s view amounts to is merely the absence of that eligibility which is for the fruit stated in each <s>vidyā</s> and for the previously attained knowledge that constitutes [the means to] that fruit. By the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely), the absence of eligibility for other fruits is excluded. What follows from this? To this he says '<s>ataḥ</s>' (therefore) — since what <s>Jaimini</s> stated has also been accepted by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>], and since what the <s>sūtrakāra</s> stated has not been rejected by <s>Jaimini</s>, there is no contradiction between them — such is the meaning.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.8, verse 22:]
It is only a partial reflection of the omniscient <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [<s>Dvaipāyana</s>] alone;
The sages, having adopted [a portion], would speak — their views do not contradict [each other].
Thus in the <s>Brāhma Purāṇa</s>. // 33 //
// Thus ends the <s>Devatādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on the eligibility of deities). // 8 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.8.22:
nanu kimanayormatayorviṣayavailakṣaṇyakalpanena virodha eva kiṃ na syādityata āha - sarvajñasyeti // tuśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / evakāro bhinnakramaḥ / tathā ca yasmāt 'munayo'; jaiminyādyāḥ nirupacaritasarvajñasya 'kṛṣṇasya'; dvaipāyanasya 'ekadeśavicintitaṃ'; vicintitārthaikadeśaṃ tanmataikadeśameva svīkṛtya tadeva brūyuḥ, nānyat / tasmāt 'tanmataṃ'; teṣāṃ kṛṣṇamunīnāṃ mataṃ parasparaṃ na viruddhyata ityarthaḥ / brāhma ityanantaraṃ uktamiti śeṣaḥ / ato viṣayavailakṣaṇyameva kalpyaṃna matavirodha iti bhāvaḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.8, verse 22:
But why resort to imagining a difference of subject matter between their two views — why should there not simply be a contradiction? To this he says '<s>sarvajñasya</s>' (of the omniscient). The word '<s>tu</s>' is for specification. The particle '<s>eva</s>' is placed in a different position [from its construed sense]. And thus: Since the sages (<s>munayaḥ</s>) such as <s>Jaimini</s> and others, having adopted only a partial reflection (<s>ekadeśavicintitam</s>) — a portion of the considered view — of the non-figuratively omniscient '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>', i.e., <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, would speak only that and nothing else, therefore 'their view' (<s>tanmatam</s>), i.e., the views of those sages including <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [<s>Dvaipāyana</s>], do not contradict each other — such is the meaning. After '<s>Brāhma</s>' [<s>Purāṇa</s>], 'it is stated' is the completion. Therefore, only a difference of subject matter should be posited, not a contradiction of views — such is the purport. // 8 //
// Thus ends the <s>Devatādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on the eligibility of deities). //
// 9. <s>Apaśūdrādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on the exclusion of <s>Śūdras</s>). //

children.text: manuṣyādhikāratvādityukte 'viśeṣācchūdrasyāpi 'ahaṃ hāretvā śūdra'; (chāṃ.4.2.3.) iti pautrāyaṇokteradhikāra iti /
children.translated_text: When it is said that humans have eligibility [for <s>brahmavidyā</s>], then without distinction, the <s>Śūdra</s> too [would have eligibility] — because of <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>'s statement 'I am indeed, O <s>Śūdra</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.2.3), [there would be] eligibility [for him].
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.9, verse 1:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.1:
atrādhikaraṇe trivarṇetarasya śūdrasya vedoktabrahmavidyādhikāro nirākriyate / prāsaṅgikatvāt nādhyāyādisaṅgatiranveṣaṇīyā / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca sūcayati - manuṣyeti // nimittasaptamīyam / adhikāropayogitayokte manuṣyatve aviśeṣāditi vā / na kevalaṃ dvijātīnāṃ, kintu śūdrasyāpītyaperthaḥ / tathā ca śūdrasyāpi vedavidyādhikāraḥ prāpnoti / kutaḥ? 'manuṣyādhikāratvāt'; ityanena manuṣyāṇāmadhikārasyoktatvāt / adhikāropayogitayokte manuṣyatve ca śūdrasya dvijātibhyaḥ 'aviśeṣāt'; viśeṣābhāvāt / nanu na manuṣyatvaṃ vedavidyādhikāropayogi, kintu viśiṣṭabudhyādimattvamevetyato 'pyāha - aviśeṣāditi / śūdrasya viśiṣṭabuddhyādimattve 'pi anyebhyaḥ 'aviśeṣāt'; viśeṣābhāvādityarthaḥ / evamaviśeṣākhyayuktimabhidhāya śūdrasya vedavidyādhikārādarśanāt, anadhikāra ityato liṅgadarśanamāha pautrāyaṇokteriti // chāndogye pautrāyaṇasya vaidikasaṃvargavidyādhyayanokterdarśanādityarthaḥ / nanu pautrāyaṇākhyapuruṣasya śūdratvameva kuta ityataḥ tajjñāpakamāha - aha hāretvā śūdreti / pautrāyaṇokteriti /
pautrāyaṇaṃ prati raikkoktestatkartṛkasambodhanādevetyarthaḥ / nanvadhikārābhāve 'pi pautrāyaṇo vedavidyāṃ vicārayāmāseti kiṃ na syādityatopyāha - pautrāyaṇokteriti / pautrāyaṇaṃ prati raikkeṇa nispṛheṇa muninā saṃvargavidyopadeśādityarthaḥ / anadhikāriṇaṃ prati munerupadeśāsambhavāt / pautrāyaṇasya arthācchrutāvadhikārokteśceti vā yojanā / adhikāra ityanantaramato virodha ityanukṛṣyate / tasyokta ityanenānvayaḥ / anenoktanyāyena uktārthe śrutyādipramāṇavirodhākṣepāt pūrveṇāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ, vedavidyādhikārākhyo viṣayaḥ, sayuktikapūrvapakṣaśca darśito bhavati /
chāndogye caturthādhyāye saṃvargaprakaraṇe hītthamākhyāyikā - pautrāyaṇo nāma rājā prāsādāgre niśāyāṃ śayāno 'bhūt / tadā prāsādopari haṃsapakṣiṇo 'gaman / uparipatatāṃ parasparaṃ vārtāṃ kurvatāṃ teṣāṃ madhye dvāvagragāmināvāstām / tatraika ekamuvāca / kimiti? are pautrāyaṇīyaṃ tejastvaṃ māgamaḥ / tatsambandhe tadīyaṃ tejastvāṃ dahediti / evamuktaḥ paro haṃsaḥ kamityākṣepavacanena rājānamanādṛtya raikvamunimeva praśaśaṃsa / tacchrutvā paritaptamanā rājā talpādutthitastvarayā svasārathimāhūya raikvagaveṣaṇāyādideśa / sa tatra tatra raikvamanviṣyan nāvidamiti prathamamāgataḥ / punastallakṣaṇoktipūrvakaṃ rājñā tanmārgaṇāyādiṣṭaḥ punaranviyaṣya kvacitpradeśe raikvamavalokya punā rājānaṃ pratyetyāha - raikvamavidamiti yathāvṛttamavadat / tadā rājā svasārathivacanena raikvamunisthānaṃ niścitya tasmāttattvaṃ vividiṣurgurudakṣiṇāṃ gṛhītvā tatsamīpaṃ jagāma / atha dvāri śakaṭasyādhasthāt sthitaṃ raikvaṃ dṛṣṭvā sambodhya dakṣiṇāṃ nivedya mahyaṃ vidyāṃ brūhītyuvāca / tadā taṃ pautrāyaṇaṃ paro lokavilakṣaṇo raikvaḥ pratyācakhyau / kimiti? ahahāretvā śūdretyādi / atra ahetisambodhanaṃ, hāra itveti bhinnapadatve visargalope guṇe hāretveti bhavati / tathā ca he śūdra hāraḥ kaṇṭhamālākhyaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ itvā rathaḥ / tattvapradīparītyā śakaṭo vā / gobhissaha tavāstvityarthaḥ hāretvānāvityekapadatvapakṣe dvivacanasya ekavacanādeśo vā ākārādeśo vā kartavyaḥ / pratyekaṃ ca astu iti kriyāsambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.9, verse 1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the eligibility of the <s>Śūdra</s> — who is other than the three <s>varṇas</s> — for the <s>brahmavidyā</s> taught in the <s>Vedas</s> is refuted. Since it is incidental, the connection (<s>saṅgati</s>) with the beginning of the chapter need not be sought. He indicates the connection through <s>śruti</s> etc., the subject matter and so forth, with '<s>manuṣya</s>' (human). This is an instrumental seventh case-ending [locative of cause]. When humanness, which is useful for eligibility, is stated, 'without distinction' — meaning not only the twice-born, but even the <s>Śūdra</s> — such is the meaning of '<s>api</s>.' And thus the <s>Śūdra</s> too would have eligibility for Vedic <s>vidyā</s>. Why? '<s>Manuṣyādhikāratvāt</s>' — because the eligibility of humans has been stated. And when humanness useful for eligibility is stated, of the <s>Śūdra</s> there is no '<s>aviśeṣāt</s>' (no distinction), i.e., no difference from the twice-born. Now, lest one say it is not humanness that is useful for eligibility in Vedic <s>vidyā</s>, but rather the possession of qualified intellect etc. — to this too he says '<s>aviśeṣāt</s>' (without distinction): even when the <s>Śūdra</s> possesses qualified intellect etc., there is 'no distinction' from others — such is the meaning. Having thus stated the reasoning called 'non-distinction,' he shows the indicative evidence (<s>liṅga</s>) for the <s>Śūdra</s>'s eligibility for Vedic <s>vidyā</s> by saying '<s>Pautrāyaṇokteḥ</s>' — because in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, there is the observation of <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>'s study of the Vedic <s>Saṃvarga-vidyā</s>, such is the meaning. But how is it known that the person named <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> was a <s>Śūdra</s>? To this he cites the indication: '<s>Aha hāretvā śūdra</s>' (Ah, [take your] necklace and chariot, O <s>Śūdra</s>). '<s>Pautrāyaṇokteḥ</s>' means: because of <s>Raikva</s>'s statement addressed to <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>, such is the meaning. But even without eligibility, could it not be that <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> simply inquired into Vedic <s>vidyā</s>? To this too he says '<s>Pautrāyaṇokteḥ</s>' — because the sage <s>Raikva</s>, who was desireless, taught the <s>Saṃvarga-vidyā</s> to <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>, such is the meaning — since a sage would not teach one who is ineligible. Or the construction is: because <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>'s eligibility is implicitly stated in the <s>śruti</s>. After '<s>adhikāra</s>' (eligibility), '<s>ataḥ virodhaḥ</s>' (hence the contradiction) is drawn in [from the previous context]. The connection is with '<s>tasya ukta</s>' (that which was stated). By this stated reasoning, since there is an objection of contradiction with <s>śruti</s> and other authorities to the established meaning, the connection of this [<s>adhikaraṇa</s>] with the preceding one is as an objection-raiser (<s>ākṣepikī saṅgati</s>), the subject matter is the eligibility for Vedic <s>vidyā</s>, and the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) with its reasoning is shown.
In the <s>Chāndogya</s>, in the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>, in the <s>Saṃvarga</s> section, there is this narrative: A king named <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> was sleeping at the top of his palace at night. Then, above the palace, swan-birds came. Among those flying above and conversing with each other, there were two who were leading. One of them said to the other — what? 'Hey, do not approach the brilliance belonging to <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>! That brilliance associated with him would burn you!' The other swan, thus addressed, disregarding the king with a word of contempt, praised the sage <s>Raikva</s> alone. Hearing this, the king, with a pained heart, rose from his bed and hastily summoned his charioteer and directed him to search for <s>Raikva</s>. He, searching here and there for <s>Raikva</s>, came back the first time not having found him. Then, after the king described the identifying marks and directed him to search again, he searched once more and spotted <s>Raikva</s> at a certain place, and returning to the king said 'I have found <s>Raikva</s>' and reported what had happened. Then the king, having determined <s>Raikva</s>'s location from his charioteer's words, desiring to learn the truth from him, took an offering for the teacher and went to his presence. Then, seeing <s>Raikva</s> seated beneath a cart at the door, he addressed him, presented the offering, and said 'Please teach me the <s>vidyā</s>.' Then the extraordinary, world-transcendent <s>Raikva</s> rejected that <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>. Why? With the words '<s>Ahahāretvā śūdra</s>' and so on. Here, '<s>ahe</s>' is a form of address, and when '<s>hāra itvā</s>' is taken as separate words, with the dropping of <s>visarga</s> and application of <s>guṇa sandhi</s>, it becomes '<s>hāretvā</s>.' Thus: 'O <s>Śūdra</s>! Let the <s>hāra</s> (necklace ornament) and <s>itvā</s> (chariot) — or cart, according to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> — together with the cows, be yours' — such is the meaning. In the alternative reading where '<s>hāretvānā</s>' is a single word, either a substitution of singular for dual, or a substitution of <s>ā</s> must be applied. And the verbal connection '<s>astu</s>' (let it be) applies to each individually.

Therefore he [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>] says —
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.9, verse 2:]
The grief (<s>śuk</s>) of this one [is indicated] because of hearing disregard toward him, because of his rushing toward [<s>Raikva</s>]; it is indicated indeed. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.34 |
That <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> is not a <s>Śūdra</s>; the designation '<s>śūdra</s>' is solely due to <s>śuc</s> (grief) and <s>ādravaṇa</s> (rushing toward).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti // aviśeṣākhyayukteḥ śravaṇasūtre nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt, pūrvapakṣyuktaliṅgadarśanasya anyathopapattipradarśanāya pravṛttasya tadādravaṇādityasya anvayayogyārthākāṃkṣotthāpakaṃ sūtrasya phalitārthaṃ darśayati - neti / 'asau'; raikveṇa sambodhitaḥ pautrāyaṇo 'na śūdraḥ'; jātyā śūdro na, kintu kṣatriya ityarthaḥ / tarhi kathamasya śūdreti sambodhitatvaṃ yujyate rūḍhyabhāvādityato yogādevetyāśayena tacchabdapravṛttinimittapradarśakaṃ tadādravaṇāditi sūtrāṃśaṃ sāvadhāraṇaṃ matvā vyācaṣṭe - śuceti / 'śucā'; śokena raikvaṃ kṣattāraṃ vā pratyāśugamanameva 'śūdratvam'; śūdretisambodhane nimittaṃ, na tu jātirityarthaḥ / anena tadādravaṇādityasya sūtre śūdratvamityadhyāhṛtena śūdreti sambodhitatvarūpārthabodhakena padenānvayaḥ sūcitaḥ / tathā ca na sambodhanānupapattiriti nedaṃ śūdrasya vedavidyādhikāre liṅgamityato na śūdrasya vedavidyādhikāra iti nañāvṛttyā anvayaḥ / evetyanena ayaṃ śūdraśabdaḥ śucādravaṇācchūdra iti nairukta eva, na tu 'śucerdaśca'; ityuṇādisūtreṇa rapratyaye dhātoścadīrghe cakārasya dakārādeśe ca niṣpanno rūḍha ityuktaṃ bhavati / pautrāyaṇa ityanena buddhisthaparāmarśakedaṃśabdārthaḥ śucetyanena prāguktavācisautradvitīyatacchabdārthaḥ, tvapratyayena nimittārthakapañcamyarthaśca darśitaḥ / sūtrakārasya sadā sarvajñatvena śugasyetyuktiḥ / bhāṣye 'saḥ'; iti śrutyanusāreṇa asāviti parokṣeṇoktiśca yuktā /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1.3.9.2:
He introduces the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>sūtra</s> with 'ata' (therefore). Since the argument from non-distinction of designation will be refuted in the <s>śravaṇa-sūtra</s> (sūtra on hearing), in order to demonstrate an alternative explanation for the indicatory marks cited by the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector), he shows the resultant meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> — which raises the expectation of a syntactically fitting meaning for 'tadādravaṇāt' (from rushing toward that) — with 'na' (not). 'Asau' (that one) — <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>, who was addressed by <s>Raikva</s>, is 'not a <s>Śūdra</s>' — meaning he is not a <s>Śūdra</s> by <s>jāti</s> (birth-caste), but rather a <s>Kṣatriya</s>. Then how is the address '<s>śūdra</s>' appropriate for him? Since there is no conventional usage [of the word in that sense], with the intention that it is only through etymological derivation, he considers the <s>sūtra</s>-portion 'tadādravaṇāt' as indicating the cause for the application of that word, takes it as emphatic, and explains — 'śucā' (by grief). 'By grief' — the swift rushing toward <s>Raikva</s> or toward the <s>kṣattṛ</s> (charioteer) alone constitutes the '<s>śūdratva</s>' (state of being called <s>śūdra</s>) — meaning it is the reason for the address '<s>śūdra</s>,' not <s>jāti</s> (birth-caste). By this, the syntactic connection of 'tadādravaṇāt' in the <s>sūtra</s> with the supplied word '<s>śūdratvam</s>' — which conveys the meaning of having been addressed as '<s>śūdra</s>' — is indicated. And thus, since there is no impossibility of the address, this is not an indicatory mark for a <s>Śūdra</s>'s eligibility for Vedic knowledge; therefore, through the repetition of the negative particle, the syntactic connection is: a <s>Śūdra</s> does not have eligibility for Vedic knowledge. By the word 'eva' (only), it is stated that this word '<s>śūdra</s>' is only <s>nairukta</s> (etymologically derived) — from '<s>śuc</s>' (grief) and '<s>ādravaṇa</s>' (rushing toward), yielding '<s>śūdra</s>' — and not the conventional form derived through the <s>Uṇādi-sūtra</s> 'śucerdaśca' with the <s>ra</s>-suffix, lengthening of the root vowel, and substitution of <s>da</s> for <s>ca</s>. By '<s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>,' the meaning of the demonstrative pronoun referring to the one present in mind is shown; by 'śucā,' the meaning of the contextual instrumental case of the previously mentioned term is shown; and by the '<s>tva</s>'-suffix, both the causal sense and the ablative sense are indicated. The statement 'śugasya' (of his grief) is due to the <s>sūtrakāra</s>'s (author of the sūtras) constant omniscience. In the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary), the use of 'asau' (that one) in the indirect sense, following the <s>śruti</s>'s 'saḥ' (he), is also appropriate.
'Kam u are, who are you speaking about, calling this good man [thus]?' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.3) — because of hearing such disrespect.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.3:
kasmānnimittādasya śoka ityasyottaratayā pravṛttaṃ śugasya tadanādaraśravaṇāditisūtrakhaṇḍaṃ vyācaṣṭe - kamvara iti // kaṃ u are iti padacchedaḥ / 'are'; haṃsa etadvacanaṃ kamenamuddiśyāttha 'santaṃ'; nirduṣṭaṃ 'sayugvānaṃ'; saśakaṭaṃ raikvamityevetyarthaḥ / u iti nipātaḥ, asya nindārthaḥ / asmin rājñi vaktumananurūpamidam, evaṃ vaktuṃ raikva eva yogya ityarthaḥ / 'etatsantaṃ'; nindyaṃ santamātthetyarthaḥ tattvapradīpe abhihitaḥ / 'etatsantam'; atra santamiti vā / ityanādaraśravaṇāditi / anādaro nindā / tathā ca ityevaṃrūpasya haṃsakṛtānādarabodhakavākyasya haṃsāt svānādaravākyasya vā śravaṇādityarthaḥ / śravaṇādityanantaraṃ prāptayetiśeṣaḥ / asya śucetyanenānvayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1.3.9.3:
He explains the <s>sūtra</s>-portion 'śugasya tadanādaraśravaṇāt' (from his hearing of that disrespect, [arising] from grief), which is introduced as an answer to 'what was the cause of his grief?' — with 'kam u are.' The word-division is: 'kaṃ u are.' 'Are' — the <s>haṃsa</s> (divine swan) spoke this utterance about someone, referring to him: 'santam' means 'faultless,' 'sayugvānam' means 'together with a cart,' meaning <s>Raikva</s> himself — this is the meaning. 'U' is a particle, here having the sense of censure. This [utterance] is not fitting to be said regarding this king; only <s>Raikva</s> is worthy of being spoken of thus — this is the meaning. 'Etatsantam' means 'you speak of [him as] a praiseworthy one in a contemptible manner' — thus explained in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. Or: 'etatsantam' may be read as 'santam' [separately]. 'Ityanādaraśravaṇāt' — <s>anādara</s> means contempt/disrespect. And thus, from hearing such a statement expressing the <s>haṃsa</s>'s disrespect, or from hearing a statement of disrespect toward himself from the <s>haṃsa</s> — this is the meaning. After 'śravaṇāt' (from hearing), one should supply 'prāptayā' (which came about). Its syntactic connection is with 'asya śucā' (by his grief).

children.text: 'sa ha sañjihāna eva kṣattāramuvāca'; (chāṃ.4.1.5.) iti sūcyate hi // 34 //
children.translated_text: 'He (<s>Jānaśruti</s>), while still getting up [from bed], said to the <s>kṣattṛ</s> (charioteer)' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 4.1.5) — for it is indicated [thereby]. 34.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.4:
nanu śrutānādarasyāpi rājñaḥ kuḥ śokotpattiḥ jñāyate / na ca pratyakṣāttanniścayaḥ / anādaraśravaṇarūpaparabuddherapratyakṣatvena tataḥ śokotpatterapratyakṣatvāt / na ca kāraṇānumānāt kāryānumitiḥ / kāraṇasya kāryāvinābhāvābhāvādityataḥ pravṛttaṃ 'sūcyate hi'; iti sūtraśeṣaṃ vyācaṣṭe - saheti / hetyāścarye / 'saḥ'; śrutānādaraḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ 'sañjihāna eva'; śayanīyāduttiṣṭhanneva 'kṣattāraṃ'; sārathiṃ prati raikvagaveṣaṇāyovāceti śrutyarthaḥ / iti sūcyate hīti / ityetadvākyārthānyathānupapattyā jñātena raikve vyāsaktamanaskatvena kāryeṇa tatkāraṇaṃ śugasya 'sūcyate'; jñāyata ityarthaḥ/ kāraṇasya kāryāvinābhāvābhāve 'pi kāryasya kāraṇāvinābhāvasyāvaśyaṃ bhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / asya tadanādarasya śravaṇāt prāptayā śucā'dravaṇameveti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / śokenādravaṇākhyanimittaparijñānaṃ ca raikvamuneḥ sārvajñyādupapadyate / taduktaṃ chāndogyabhāṣye -

children.translated_text: King <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> was addressed as '<s>śūdra</s>' by the sage due to grief,
Having obtained the <s>prāṇavidyā</s> (knowledge of the vital breath) from him, he attained the supreme <s>dharma</s> (righteousness).

BBsBhDīp 1.3.9.4:
Now, even for a king who has heard disrespect, how is the arising of grief known? There is no certainty of it from direct perception, since the cognition of another's mind — which has the form of hearing disrespect — is not directly perceptible, and therefore the arising of grief from it is also not directly perceptible. Nor can the effect be inferred from inferring the cause, since the cause does not necessarily entail the effect. Therefore, he introduces and explains the remainder of the <s>sūtra</s>, 'sūcyate hi' (for it is indicated) — with 'sa ha' (he indeed). 'Hi' expresses wonder. 'Saḥ' — <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>, having heard the disrespect, 'sañjihāna eva' — while still rising from his bed, 'kṣattāram' — said to the <s>kṣattṛ</s> (charioteer) to search for <s>Raikva</s> — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. 'Iti sūcyate hi' — by the impossibility of explaining this passage otherwise, through the effect — namely, the known preoccupation of his mind with <s>Raikva</s> — the cause, namely his grief, 'sūcyate' (is indicated/known). Even though the cause does not necessarily entail the effect, the effect necessarily presupposes its cause — this is the purport. The syntactic connection with the preceding is: from hearing that disrespect, by the grief that arose, the rushing toward [<s>Raikva</s>] alone [constitutes his being called <s>śūdra</s>]. And the knowledge of the specific cause called '<s>ādravaṇa</s>' (rushing toward) due to grief is justified by the omniscience of the sage <s>Raikva</s>. This has been stated in the <s>Chāndogya-bhāṣya</s> —

children.text: 'śokāt'; śokenā'dravaṇādityarthaḥ / athavā - śokaśabdopapadāt āṅapūrvakāt 'atasātatyagamane'; ityasmāt kvipi rūpametat tathātve yata iti śeṣaḥ / nanu sūtre taddravaṇādityetāvatā pūrtau āṅpraśleṣaḥ kimartha iti cet - na, śrutau śūdretivaktavyatve 'pi śokādhikyajñāpanārthaṃ śūdreti ūkārarūpo yo dīrghasvaraḥ śrutaḥ tadarthavyaktavyarthatvāt / na ca śūgdretivaktavye śrutau śūdretyuktiḥ kathamiti vācyam / 'tasmādrugdrāvaṇāt rudraḥ'; iti śrutau gakārasya dakārādeśena yathāprayogastathopapatteḥ / ata eva tattvapradīpe tṛtīyasya tṛtīyo 'tiśayārthatvādityuktam / 'rujaṃ drāvayate'; iti smṛtāvivopapatteśca / anena - śucā 'ādravaṇāt'; raikvaṃ prati śīghragamanādeva nimittādasya pautrāyaṇasya śūdratvaṃ śūdreti sambodhitatvam, na tu varṇāvaratvāt / śukca śokaścāsya tadanādaraśravaṇādāsīt / taditi śrutyuktaparāmarśaḥ/ kriyākartṛbhāvaṣṣaṣṭhyarthaḥ / tathā ca 'tasya anādaraśravaṇāt'; haṃsakṛtānādaraśravaṇāt ityarthaḥ / tattvapradīparītyā tasmāddhaṃsāt svānādaraśravaṇādityarthaḥ / madhyamapadalopī samāsa iti kecit / nanu śrutānādarasyāpi kutaḥ śokotpattirjñāyate, parabuddheḥ śokapadoktaduḥkhānubhavasya apratyakṣatvādityata uktaṃ - sūcyate hīti // 'hi'; yasmāt 'saha'; iti vākyārthānupapatyā jñātena tadvyagramanaskatvākhyakāryeṇa tatkāraṇaṃ śugasya 'sūcyate'; jñāyate / tasmāt ato na śūdreti sambodhanaṃ śūdrasya vedādhikāre liṅgamiti naitadbalācchūdrasya vedavidyādhikāra iti bhāvaḥ iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: 'Śokāt' (from grief) means 'from grief and rushing toward' — this is the meaning. Alternatively, the form is derived from the root 'atasātatyagamane' (to go constantly) with the prefix 'ā,' preceded by the word '<s>śoka</s>' (grief) as an <s>upapada</s> (qualifying term), through the <s>kvip</s> suffix — in that case, supply 'yataḥ' (because of which). Now, if one asks: when 'taddravaṇāt' would suffice in the <s>sūtra</s>, what is the purpose of including the prefix 'ā'? — No, because even though the <s>śruti</s> should have said '<s>śūdra</s>' [simply], the long vowel 'ū' heard in '<s>śūdra</s>' is meant to indicate the intensity of grief, and its purpose needs to be made explicit. Nor should one object: how can the <s>śruti</s> say '<s>śūdra</s>' when it should have said '<s>śūgdra</s>'? Because just as in the <s>śruti</s> passage 'tasmād rugdrāvaṇāt rudraḥ' (therefore from driving away pain, [he is called] <s>Rudra</s>), the substitution of <s>da</s> for <s>ga</s> is attested in actual usage. Hence in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> it is said: 'the third [letter is substituted] for the third, for the sake of intensification.' And because it is also justified as in the <s>smṛti</s> passage 'rujam drāvayate' (he drives away pain). By this — from '<s>śucā ādravaṇāt</s>' (from grief and rushing toward), i.e., solely from the cause of swiftly going toward <s>Raikva</s>, <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>'s <s>śūdratva</s> (being called <s>śūdra</s>) consists in being addressed as '<s>śūdra</s>,' not from being of a lower <s>varṇa</s> (social class). And his grief arose from hearing that disrespect. 'Tat' (that) is a reference to what is mentioned in the <s>śruti</s>. The genitive of the agent-action relation. And thus 'tasya anādaraśravaṇāt' means 'from hearing the disrespect made by the <s>haṃsa</s>.' According to the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>'s reading, it means 'from hearing the disrespect toward himself from that <s>haṃsa</s>.' Some say it is a compound with elision of the middle term. Now, even for one who has heard disrespect, how is the arising of grief known, since the experience of suffering denoted by the word '<s>śoka</s>' — which is another's mental state — is not directly perceptible? To this he says — 'sūcyate hi' (for it is indicated). 'Hi' — because, through the impossibility of otherwise explaining the meaning of the passage 'sa ha' (he indeed), by the effect — namely, the known preoccupation of his mind [with <s>Raikva</s>] — the cause, his grief, 'sūcyate' (is indicated/known). Therefore, the address '<s>śūdra</s>' is not an indicatory mark for a <s>Śūdra</s>'s eligibility for the <s>Veda</s>, and hence by this force a <s>Śūdra</s> does not have eligibility for Vedic knowledge — this is the purport. Thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated.
<s>Sūtra</s>: Om.
And because <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood is ascertained further on, from the indicatory mark of the chariot associated with <s>Citraratha</s>. <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.35.

children.text: 'ayamaśvatarī rathaḥ'; iti citrarathasambandhitvena liṅgena pautrāyaṇasya kṣatriyatvāvagateśca /
children.translated_text: 'This chariot yoked with mules' — and because the <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood of <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> is ascertained through the indicatory mark of his connection with <s>Citraratha</s> (a splendid chariot).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.5:
nanu śūdraśabdo 'yaṃ kuto yaugiko 'ṅgīkriyate, rūḍhārtha eva kiṃ na syāt / yogarūḍhyormadhye rūḍhereva prābalyāt / tathā ca pautrāyaṇanidarśanenaiva śūdrasya vedavidyādhikārasiddhirityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - kṣatriyatveti / atra 'ayam'; ityataḥ prāk 'uttaratra'; iti sautrapadaṃ sambandhanīyam / śruteneti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca uttaratra raikvaṃ prati pautrāyaṇasya ādravaṇāt, uttaratra tatpratipādanānantaram / yadvā - śūdraśabdena sambodhanāt uttaratra 'ayamaśvatarī rathaḥ'; iti śrutenetyarthaḥ / pautrāyaṇena dīyamānasya rathasya anyadīyatvaśaṅkānirāsāya sūtre caitraratheneti bhāvapradhānapadaṃ prayuktam / anyathā citrarathenetyevāvakṣyat / tatra citraścāsau rathaśca citrarathaḥ tasyāyaṃ caitraratha iti vigrahamabhipretya pratyayārthaṃ pradarśayan tadvyācaṣṭe - citrarathasambandhitveneti // svābhāvikacitrarathasambandhitvenetyarthaḥ/ atra rathamātrameva liṅgaṃ, citrapadaṃ tu svarūpakathanārtham / yadvā - apūrvarathayogena kṣatriyatvasambhāvanārthaṃ tatpadam / athavā yadā rathitvenaiva kṣatriyatvasya niścayaḥ, tadā sutarāṃ citrarathitveneti sūcanārthaṃ tatpadam / yadyapi 'ayamaśvatarīrathaḥ'; ityatra citrarathamātraśravaṇe 'pi na tatsambandho 'sya śrūyate / tathāpi tatpūrvavākye 'hāretvā tavaiva'; iti ṣaṣṭhyā itvāśabdārtharathasambandho gamyata iti tasyāśca rathasambandhe śrutirūpatvāt yuktamuktam / citro ratho yasyeti citrarathastasya bhāvaḥ caitrarathasteneti vyākhyānaṃ tu bhāve 'ṇ pratyayasya kalpyatvāt śrutibhāṣyaviruddhatvācca ayuktam/ na ca caitraratheneti sambandhoktimātreṇa kathamanyadīyatvaśaṅkānirāsa iti vācyam / svataḥ prāptatadīyatve bādhakābhāve tadīyatvasyaiva svābhāvikatvasambhave naimittikagrahaṇāyogāt / 'svatvābhāve dhanāyogāt'; ityādinyāyaprāptatvāt / rathena liṅgādityanayossāmānādhikaraṇyāya liṅgāditi pañcamī vyatyayena vyācaṣṭe - liṅganeti / pautrāyaṇasyetyetat asyetyanuvṛttapadasya arthakathanam / kṣatriyatvāvagaterityasya śucā'dravaṇādevāsya śūdratvaṃ na tu rūḍhyeti pūrveṇānvayaḥ / caśabdo liṅgena ceti sambadhyate / tena 'bahudāyī'; ityādivākyaśeṣoktaṃ liṅgaṃ samuccīyate / liṅgasya śrutitaścaramatvena anekatvena ca prābalyasūcanāya vā caśabdaḥ / evaṃ sūtre 'pi caśabdo bhinnakramaḥ uktaprayojanakaśca / evaṃ ca rūḍhereva prābalye 'pyatra śrutānekaliṅgarūpabādhakāt śūdraśabdasya yogavṛttyaṅgīkāra eva yukta iti bhāvaḥ / 'gardabhādaśvāyāṃ jātā aśvataryaḥ'; iti tattvapradīpe / 'gardabhīṣu aśvairjātā asvataryaḥ'; iti vyāsatīrthīye / tadyukto rathaḥ aśvatarīrathaḥ tava dakṣiṇātvena vartate ityarthaḥ / raikvaṃ prati pautrāyaṇavākyametat /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1.3.9.5:
Now, why should this word '<s>śūdra</s>' be accepted as etymologically derived? Why should it not be in its conventional meaning alone? For between etymological derivation and conventional usage, conventional usage alone has greater force. And thus, through the very example of <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>, the eligibility of <s>Śūdras</s> for Vedic knowledge would be established — to counter this objection, he presents and explains the <s>sūtra</s> — 'kṣatriyatva' (Kṣatriya-hood). Here, the contextual word 'uttaratra' (further on) should be connected before 'ayam' (this). Supply 'śrutena' (as heard in the scripture). And thus, 'uttaratra' — further on, from <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>'s rushing toward <s>Raikva</s>, i.e., subsequent to the description thereof. Alternatively — after the address with the word '<s>śūdra</s>,' further on, through what is heard as 'ayam aśvatarī rathaḥ' (this chariot yoked with mules) — this is the meaning. To remove the doubt that the chariot being given by <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> might belong to someone else, the <s>sūtra</s> uses the term 'caitrarathena' (by the one associated with <s>Citraratha</s>), which is a word primarily denoting the state [of having a splendid chariot]. Otherwise, it would have simply said 'citrathena.' Taking the analysis as: '<s>citraḥ</s>' (splendid) '<s>ca asau rathaḥ ca</s>' (and that is a chariot) = '<s>citrarathaḥ</s>' (splendid chariot), '<s>tasya ayam caitrarathaḥ</s>' (this belongs to him, the one with the splendid chariot) — he shows the suffix-meaning and explains it as 'citrarathasambandhitvena' (by connection with a splendid chariot). This means: by natural connection with a splendid chariot. Here, only the chariot itself is the indicatory mark; the word '<s>citra</s>' (splendid) is for describing its nature. Alternatively, that word is for suggesting the possibility of <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood through possession of an extraordinary chariot. Or, when <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood is already certain from mere chariot-ownership, the word serves to indicate that it is all the more certain from owning a splendid chariot. Although in 'ayam aśvatarīrathaḥ' only a mule-chariot is heard and his connection with a splendid chariot is not explicitly heard, nevertheless, in the preceding sentence, through the genitive case in 'hāretvā tavaiva' (having brought, yours alone) and the meaning of the word 'itvā' (having gone), his connection with the chariot is understood — and since that [expression] has the nature of <s>śruti</s> (scriptural statement) regarding chariot-ownership, the statement is justified. The interpretation as '<s>citro ratho yasya</s>' (one whose chariot is splendid) = '<s>citrarathaḥ</s>,' and '<s>tasya bhāvaḥ caitraratham</s>' (the state of that) '<s>tena</s>' (by that) — this interpretation is inappropriate because the <s>aṇ</s> suffix in the sense of abstract state would need to be artificially postulated and because it contradicts the <s>śruti</s> and the <s>bhāṣya</s>. Nor should one say: how does the mere statement of connection with '<s>caitrarathena</s>' remove the doubt of the chariot belonging to someone else? Because when his ownership is naturally obtained and there is no sublating evidence, and when it is possible that the ownership is natural, there is no ground for taking it as externally caused. Because the maxim 'in the absence of ownership, wealth cannot belong [to one]' and similar principles are applicable. For the syntactic coordination of 'rathena' (by chariot) and 'liṅgāt' (from the indicatory mark), the ablative 'liṅgāt' is explained by grammatical interchange as 'liṅgena' (by the indicatory mark). 'Pautrāyaṇasya' is the explanation of the meaning of the resumed word 'asya' (his). The syntactic connection of 'kṣatriyatvāvagateḥ' (from ascertainment of <s>Kṣatriya</s>-hood) with the preceding is: his <s>śūdratva</s> is only from grief and rushing toward, not from conventional usage. The particle 'ca' (and) connects with 'liṅgena ca' (and by the indicatory mark). Thereby, the indicatory marks stated in the continuation of the passage, such as 'bahudāyī' (a great giver), are included. Or the particle 'ca' is for indicating the greater force [of evidence] due to the indicatory marks being final in the scriptural text and being multiple. Thus in the <s>sūtra</s> too, the particle 'ca' has a different placement and serves the stated purpose. And thus, even though conventional usage has greater force [in general], here, due to the sublating evidence in the form of multiple scriptural indicatory marks, acceptance of the etymological derivation of the word '<s>śūdra</s>' alone is justified — this is the purport. 'Mules born from a mare and a donkey are <s>aśvatarīs</s>' — thus in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. 'Those born from horses among female donkeys are <s>aśvatarīs</s>' — thus in the work of <s>Vyāsatīrtha</s>. A chariot yoked with such [mules] is an <s>aśvatarī-ratha</s> (mule-chariot), which serves as your <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual gift) — this is the meaning. This is <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>'s statement to <s>Raikva</s>.
A chariot yoked with mules and splendid is called [a <s>Citraratha</s>]. Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Brāhma</s> [Purāṇa].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.6:
nanu śrutāvaśvatarīrathaśabdaprayogāt sūtre 'pi tathaiva prayoktavye kathaṃ sūtrakṛt citrarathaśabdaṃ prāyuṅtetyāśaṅkya ubhayorarthaikyānna visaṃvāda ityāśayena tatrābhidhānamāha - ratha iti // tuśabdo viśeṣārtho 'vadhāraṇe vā / aśvatarīyukta eveti sambadhyate / atra ratha iti vāstavaviśeṣoktireva, na tu rathatvasyāpi śakyakoṭipraveśaḥ / tathā ca sūtre rathatvaprakārakabodhāya rathaśabdaprayoga iti na tadvaiyarthyamiti dhyeyam iti brāhme uktatvāt na śrutisūtrayorvairūpyamityupaskāreṇānvayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1.3.9.6:
Now, since the <s>śruti</s> uses the term '<s>aśvatarī-ratha</s>' (mule-chariot), the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras) should also have used the same term — so how did the <s>sūtrakṛt</s> come to use the word '<s>citraratha</s>' (splendid chariot)? Anticipating this objection, with the intention that there is no discrepancy since both terms have the same meaning, he states the authority for that — 'rathaḥ' (chariot). The particle 'tu' serves the purpose of specification or emphasis. It connects as 'aśvatarīyukta eva' (yoked with mules alone). Here, 'rathaḥ' (chariot) is a statement of the actual specific thing, not that the chariot-nature itself falls within the range of mere possibility. And thus, in the <s>sūtra</s>, the word 'ratha' (chariot) is used to produce the cognition qualified by chariot-nature, so there is no redundancy in it — this should be noted. Because it is stated in the <s>Brāhma</s> [Purāṇa], there is no discrepancy between the <s>śruti</s> and the <s>sūtra</s> — the syntactic connection is completed with this supplement.

children.text: yatra vedo rathastatra na vedo yatra no rathaḥ / iti brahmavaivarte // 35 //
children.translated_text: Where there is the <s>Veda</s>, there is the chariot; where there is no <s>Veda</s>, there is no chariot. — Thus [it is stated] in the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s> [Purāṇa]. // 35 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.7:
evaṃ sākṣādeva svābhāvikarathena pautrāyaṇasya kṣatriyatvaṃ prasādhitam / svābhāvikarathitve 'sya varṇāvaratvaṃ kiṃ na syādityaprayojakatvamāśaṅkya maivam-āgantukasyāpi rathasya vedaṃ vināyogāt 'vedasya ca saṃskāreti vakṣyamāṇanyāyena śūdre 'yogāt'; rathamātreṇa vedānumānadvārā pautrāyaṇasya śūdratvābhāvasiddherityāśayena rathena vedānumāne vyabhicāraśaṅkāparihārāya āgamenobhayavyāptiṃ darśayati - yatreti / 'tatra'; tatraivetyarthaḥ / tena yatra vahniḥ tatraiva dhūma ityādāviva vedasya vyāpakatālābhaḥ/ ata eva vyatirekapradarśakāṃśe na veda iti vedabhāvasya prathamamuktiḥ/ smṛtau rathaśabdena āgantukasvābhāvikasādhāraṇarathamātrasya vivakṣitatvāt, samavyāptyabhiprāyeṇa vā yatra veda ityuktiḥ / ata eva ṭīkāyāṃ 'rathasya vedāvinābhāvāt'; iti rathasya vyāpyatvamuktvā 'vaidikatvamātre vidyamānaṃ rathitvam'; ityanena tasya vyāpakatvamuktam / vastutastu - yatra rathastatra veda iti yojanāyāṃ nānupapattiḥ / tathā ca anena vyāptiniścayāt na vyabhicāraśaṅketi yādṛśatādṛśarathamātreṇa vedānumānadvārā śūdratvābhāvaniścayānna pautrāyaṇasya vedabāhyavarṇāvaratvaṃ śaṅkyamiti bhāvaḥ / etena pūrvapakṣiṇā śūdre 'pi vedāṅgīkārānna tena śūdratvābhāvasādhanaṃ yuktamitinirastaṃ, tasyottarasūtre nirākariṣyamāṇatvāt / na ca brāhmaṇādisādhāraṇarathitvenāsya vaidikatvaniścaye 'pi taddvārā aśūdratvasiddhāvapi kathaṃ kṣatriyatvaniścaya iti vācyam / rathitvamātrasya vaidikatvavyāptatvoktyā svābhāvikarathitvasya vaidikaviśeṣakṣatriyatvavyāptatvenāpi smṛtyabhipretatvāt / tasya ca kādācitkarathavati brāhmaṇādāvabhāvāttena sākṣādeva kṣatriyatvaniścayopapattiḥ / na ca 'apalāyanaṃ ca śūdrasya'; ityanena prāptayoddhṛtvānyathānupapattyā śūdrasya rathitvapratītestatra vyabhicāra iti vācyam / apalāyanena yoddhṛtvasya padātitayopapattyā rathitvānākṣepakatvāt / brahmavaivarta ityasya uktatvādityadhyāhāreṇa nāsau śūdra ityanenānvayaḥ iti jñāyata iti śeṣaḥ anena - 'ādravaṇāt'; sambodhanādvā 'uttaratra'; 'ayamaśvatarīrathaḥ'; (chāṃ.4.2.2.) itiśrutena 'caitrarathena liṅgāt'; liṅgena svābhāvikarathena liṅgena bahudāyitvādiliṅgena cāsya pautrāyaṇasya kṣatriyatvāvagateḥ / asmāt bādhakāttadādravaṇānnimittādevāsya śūdratvam, na tu jātyāsau śūdraḥ / tathā rathena vedaniścayācca nāsau śūdra iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.9.7:
Thus, the <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood of <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> has been directly established through [his] natural chariot. [Objection:] Would not his having a natural chariot imply belonging to a lower <s>varṇa</s>? Anticipating this pointless objection [and replying] 'not so' — since even an incidental chariot is of no use without the <s>Veda</s>, and since 'the <s>Veda</s> and the <s>saṃskāra</s>' — by the principle to be stated later — is impossible for a <s>Śūdra</s>, therefore, through any chariot whatsoever, via the inference of the <s>Veda</s>, the absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood of <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> is established — with this intention, to remove the suspicion of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in the inference of the <s>Veda</s> from the chariot, he shows the co-extensiveness (<s>vyāpti</s>) in both directions through scripture — beginning with '<s>yatra</s>' (where). // '<s>Tatra</s>' means 'there alone' — this is the meaning. Thereby, just as 'where there is fire there alone is smoke,' the pervading nature (<s>vyāpakatā</s>) of the <s>Veda</s> is obtained. For this very reason, in the portion showing the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), '<s>na vedaḥ</s>' (no <s>Veda</s>) — the absence of the <s>Veda</s> — is stated first. In the <s>smṛti</s>, since the word '<s>ratha</s>' (chariot) intends any chariot whatsoever — whether incidental or natural — or with the intention of co-extensiveness (<s>samavyāpti</s>), the statement '<s>yatra vedaḥ</s>' (where there is the <s>Veda</s>) is made. For this very reason, in the <s>Ṭīkā</s>, having stated '<s>rathasya vedāvinābhāvāt</s>' (because of the chariot's inseparability from the <s>Veda</s>) — i.e., the pervaded-nature (<s>vyāpyatva</s>) of the chariot — by '<s>vaidikatvamātre vidyamānaṃ rathitvam</s>' (chariot-possession exists only where there is Vedic [status]), its pervading nature is stated. In reality, however — in the construal '<s>yatra rathaḥ tatra vedaḥ</s>' (where there is a chariot, there is the <s>Veda</s>), there is no difficulty. And thus, from the certainty of the co-extensiveness through this [statement], there is no suspicion of deviation — therefore, through any chariot whatsoever, via the inference of the <s>Veda</s>, from the certainty of the absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood, the lower-<s>varṇa</s> status outside the <s>Veda</s> should not be suspected for <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> — this is the purport. By this, the prima facie view that 'even the <s>Śūdra</s> has [access to] the <s>Veda</s>, and therefore proving the absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood through it is unjustified' is refuted — because that [objection] will be rejected in the subsequent <s>sūtra</s>. Nor should it be said that even with the certainty of his Vedic status through having a chariot common to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and others, and thereby the proof of his non-<s>Śūdra</s>-hood, how can his <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood specifically be ascertained? — because through the statement that mere chariot-possession is pervaded by Vedic status, the intent of the <s>smṛti</s> is that natural chariot-possession is pervaded by the specific Vedic [<s>varṇa</s> of] <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood. And since that [natural chariot] is absent in <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and others who only occasionally possess chariots, the direct ascertainment of <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood through it is justified. Nor should it be said that from '<s>apalāyanaṃ ca śūdrasya</s>' (and the <s>Śūdra</s>'s not fleeing), the <s>Śūdra</s>'s chariot-possession is understood through the impossibility of explaining his acquired warrior-status otherwise, and therefore there is deviation [of the inference] — because by '<s>apalāyana</s>' (not fleeing), the warrior-status is explicable through being a foot-soldier, and hence does not imply chariot-possession. The phrase '<s>iti brahmavaivarte</s>' connects with '<s>nāsau śūdraḥ</s>' (he is not a <s>Śūdra</s>) by supplying '<s>uktatvāt</s>' (because it is stated) and '<s>iti jñāyate</s>' (thus it is known). By this — 'because of the rushing' (<s>ādravaṇāt</s>), or because of the address, 'subsequently' the <s>śruti</s> '<s>ayam aśvatarī-rathaḥ</s>' (this is a chariot [drawn by] she-mules, <s>Chāndogya</s> 4.2.2) — 'because of the indicatory mark in the form of the <s>Caitraratha</s> [lineage]' — by the indicatory mark of the natural chariot, and by indicatory marks such as generous giving — the <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood of this <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s> is understood. From this overriding reason (<s>bādhaka</s>), and from the cause that was his rushing — his <s>Śūdra</s>-hood was circumstantial, not by birth. And through the chariot, from the certainty of the <s>Veda</s>, he is not a <s>Śūdra</s> — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
Because of the reference to <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration), and because of the statement of its absence [in the <s>Śūdra</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.36 |
Because of the reference to <s>saṃskāra</s> in 'One should initiate (<s>upanayana</s>) a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> at the age of eight and then teach him' — [a reference made] for the purpose of Vedic study.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.8:
yaduktaṃ rathitvaliṅgena pautrāyaṇasya kṣatriyatvāvagamāt, na talliṅgena śūdrasya vedādhikārasiddhiriti / na tadyuktaṃ - śūdrasyāpi rathitvasambhavāt / na ca rathasya vedavyāpyatvācchūdre ca tadabhāvādrathasyāpyabhāva iti vācyam / śūdre 'pi vedādhikārāṅgīkārādityāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasyati - saṃskāreti // atra 'aṣṭavarṣaṃ brāhmaṇamunayīta/ tamadhyāpayīta'; iti śrutau brāhmaṇasyaivādhyayane upanayanāpekṣā, nānyeṣāmityāśaṅkāparihārāya pravṛttaṃ saṃskāraparāmarśādityaṃśaṃ vyācaṣṭe - aṣṭavarṣamiti / upanayīteteyanantaram ityupanayanamuktveti śeṣaḥ / 'tam'; upanītaṃ māṇavakamātma ācāryakaraṇakāmo 'dhyāpayītetyarthaḥ / itiśabdānantaraṃ śrutāviti śeṣaḥ / 'anyārthavacanaṃ parāmarśaḥ'; ityāśayena parāmarśapadaṃ vyācaṣṭe - adhyayanārthamiti // adhyayanāṅgatayetyarthaḥ /
adhyāpanavākyasyāpi 'svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ'; (tai.ā.2.15.1.) iti śrutyanurodhena jīvikārthādhyayanavidhiparatvāditi bhāvaḥ / 'saṃskāraparāmarśāt'; upanayanākhyasaṃskāramātravacanādityarthaḥ / tacchabdeneti śeṣaḥ / na tu brāhmaṇaparāmarśa iti mātraśabdārthaḥ / tathā ca noktaśaṅkāvakāśa iti bhāvaḥ / kecittu - śrutigatabrāhmaṇaśabdo 'tra brahmāṇana yogyatraivarṇikapara ityāhuḥ / taccintyam, śaṅkāsamādhānānanuguṇatvāt / kuta evaṃ kalpyata ityataḥ smṛtāvapyupanayanākhyadvitīyajanmavata eva sāraṇyaka vedādhyayanavidhānādityāśayena sūtre bhāṣye ca 'vedaḥ kṛtsno 'dhigantavyaḥ sarahasyo dvijanmanā'; iti smṛtisamuccayārthakaścaśabdaḥ prāyoji / saḥ parāmarśādityanenānveti / parāmarśāccetyanantaram adhyayanasya saṃskārasāpekṣatvāvagamāditi śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.9.8:
It was stated that from the indicatory mark of chariot-possession, <s>Pautrāyaṇa</s>'s <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood is understood; therefore, the proof of the <s>Śūdra</s>'s Vedic qualification through that indicatory mark is not valid. [Objection:] That is not proper — because the <s>Śūdra</s> too can possess a chariot. Nor should it be said that since the chariot is pervaded by the <s>Veda</s>, and since the <s>Veda</s> is absent in the <s>Śūdra</s>, the chariot too would be absent [for the <s>Śūdra</s>] — because even the <s>Śūdra</s> has Vedic qualification [in the opponent's view]. Resolving this objection, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> — '<s>saṃskāra</s>' (consecration). // Here, in the <s>śruti</s> 'One should initiate a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> at the age of eight and then teach him,' the expectation of <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) for Vedic study pertains to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> alone, not to others — to resolve this apprehension, the portion '<s>saṃskāra-parāmarśāt</s>' (because of the reference to <s>saṃskāra</s>) is explained — beginning with '<s>aṣṭavarṣam</s>' (at eight years). After '<s>upanayīta</s>' (should initiate), the remainder is 'having stated the <s>upanayana</s>.' '<s>Tam</s>' — that initiated student — one who desires to make [the student] his own — '<s>adhyāpayīta</s>' — should teach: this is the meaning. After 'iti,' the remainder is '<s>śrutau</s>' (in the <s>śruti</s>). With the intention that '<s>parāmarśa</s> means a statement for the purpose of something else,' he explains the word '<s>parāmarśa</s>' — '<s>adhyayanārtham</s>' (for the purpose of study). // Meaning: as an auxiliary to study.
Since even the teaching-statement, in accordance with the <s>śruti</s> '<s>svādhyāyo adhyetavyaḥ</s>' (one's own Vedic recitation is to be studied, <s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.15.1), is intended as an injunction for study for the sake of livelihood: this is the purport. '<s>Saṃskāra-parāmarśāt</s>' — merely because of the statement of the <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration) called <s>upanayana</s>: this is the meaning. '<s>Tacchabdena</s>' (by that word) is the remainder. Not because of the reference to '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — this is the meaning of the word '<s>mātra</s>' (merely). And thus, the stated objection has no scope — this is the purport. Some, however, say: the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' in the <s>śruti</s> here refers to all three <s>varṇas</s> eligible for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge. This is questionable — because it does not accord with the objection and resolution. Why is this construed thus? — because even in the <s>smṛti</s>, the injunction for Vedic study is prescribed only for one who has the second birth (<s>dvijanman</s>) called <s>upanayana</s>. With this intention, the word '<s>ca</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> and <s>Bhāṣya</s> is employed for the purpose of accumulating the <s>smṛti</s> '<s>vedaḥ kṛtsno adhigantavyaḥ sarahasyaḥ dvijanmanā</s>' (the entire <s>Veda</s> with its secrets is to be mastered by the twice-born). It connects with '<s>parāmarśāt</s>' (because of the reference). After '<s>parāmarśāt ca</s>,' the remainder is: 'because of the understanding that Vedic study requires <s>saṃskāra</s>.'

children.text:
'nāgnirna yajño na kriyā na saṃskāro na vratāniśūdrasya'; iti
paiṅgiśrutau saṃskārābhāvābhilāpācca /
children.translated_text: 'No fire, no sacrifice, no rite, no <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration), no vows for the <s>Śūdra</s>' — because of the statement of the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> in the <s>Paiṅgi śruti</s>.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.9:
nanvastvadhyayanasya upanayanasaṃskārasāpekṣatvaṃ, tathāpi na śūdrasya vedādhyayanābhāvasiddhiḥ /
śūdrasyāpi saṃskārasambhavādityataḥ pravṛttaṃ 'tadabhāvābhilāpāt'; iti sūtrakhaṇḍaṃ vyācaṣṭe - nāgniriti // abhilāpāt abhidhānāditi / asya sūtre adhyāhṛtena 'na śūdrasya vedādhikāro, na vā tadavinābhūtaṃ rathitvam'; iti sādhyenānvayaḥ / 'agniḥ', śrautaḥsmārtaśca / 'yajñaḥ'; agnihotrādiḥ, daivapitryādiyajño vā / 'kriyā'; sandhyāvandanādirūpā, uttarakriyā vā / saṃskāra upanayanādiḥ / 'vratāni'; kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādīni //
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.9.9:
Objection: Let it be that Vedic study requires the <s>saṃskāra</s> of <s>upanayana</s>; still, the absence of the <s>Śūdra</s>'s Vedic study is not established — because even the <s>Śūdra</s> can have <s>saṃskāra</s>. To this, the <s>sūtra</s>-portion '<s>tadabhāvābhilāpāt</s>' (because of the statement of its absence) is explained — beginning with '<s>nāgniḥ</s>' (no fire). // '<s>Abhilāpāt</s>' means 'because of the statement.' The syntactic connection in the <s>sūtra</s> is with the implied thesis: 'the <s>Śūdra</s> has no Vedic qualification, nor does he possess chariot-possession which is inseparable from [the <s>Veda</s>].' '<s>Agniḥ</s>' — both the <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) and <s>smārta</s> (traditional) [fires]. '<s>Yajña</s>' — sacrifices like the <s>Agnihotra</s>, or sacrifices for <s>devas</s>, <s>pitṛs</s>, and the like. '<s>Kriyā</s>' — rites in the form of <s>sandhyāvandana</s> (twilight worship) and the like, or funeral rites. '<s>Saṃskāra</s>' — <s>upanayana</s> and the like. '<s>Vratāni</s>' — observances such as <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance), <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar fast), and the like.

children.text: uttamastrīṇāṃ tu na śūdravat / 'sapatnīṃ me parādhama'; ityādiṣvadhikāradarśanāt /
children.translated_text: But for superior women (<s>uttamastrī</s>), it is not as with the <s>Śūdra</s> — because of the observation of [their] qualification in passages such as 'Humiliate my rival, O lowest one' and the like.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.10:
nanvevaṃ saṃskārābhāvena vedānadhikāraśceduttamastrīṇāmapi tatprasaṅgaḥ / saṃskārābhāve 'pi tāsāmadhikāre śūdrasyāpi tatprāptirityata āha - uttameti / tuśabdo vedadraṣṭṛtvākhyaviśeṣadyotakaḥ / 'saṃskārābhāvenābhāvaḥ'; ityākṛṣyate / adhikārasyeti śeṣaḥ / uttamānāṃ striya iti vigrahaḥ, karmadhārayo vā / tathā ca śacī yamīūrvaśyādyuttamastrīṇāṃ śūdravanna saṃskārābhāvena vedavidyādhikārasyābhāvo vaktavyaḥ / kutaḥ? 'sapatnīṃ me parādhama'; (mantrapraśna 1.16.) ityādividyāsu tāsāṃ taddraṣṭṛtvena adhikāradarśanāditi yojanā / atra 'sapatnīm'; iti pratīkagrahaṇena 'sapatnīṃ me parādhama'; patiṃ me kevalaṃ kṛdhi, 'uttarāhamuttara uttareduttarābhyaḥ'; iti samagravākyaṃ gṛhyate/ śacīvākyamidam / he bhagavān 'me sapatnīṃ'; madanyāṃ matpatipāṇigṛhītīṃ 'parādhama'; parāṇuda / mama patiṃ 'kevalaṃ'; mayyevāsaktaṃ kuru / 'ahamuttarābhyaḥ'; saundaryeṇotkṛṣṭābhyaḥ madantarābhyo vā strībhyaḥ 'uttarā'; utkṛṣṭā satī 'uttaret'; priyottamaiva 'uttare'; sapatnīkleśāduttareyamiti śrutyarthaḥ / ādipadena 'udatī paśyavaḥ soma ekebhyaḥ parvate, () udasau sūryo agāt'; (ṛ.10.159.1.) ityādi devamātṛyamīpaulomyādidṛṣṭānāṃ grahaṇam /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.9.10:
Objection: If the absence of Vedic qualification follows from the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s>, then even for superior women the same consequence would apply. And if women have qualification even without <s>saṃskāra</s>, the same possibility would extend to the <s>Śūdra</s> as well. To this he says — '<s>uttama</s>' (superior). The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates the distinctive feature of being <s>Veda</s>-seers (<s>vedadraṣṭṛtva</s>). '<s>Saṃskārābhāvena abhāvaḥ</s>' (absence [of qualification] due to absence of <s>saṃskāra</s>) is drawn in. 'Of qualification' is the remainder. '<s>Uttamānāṃ striyaḥ</s>' is the grammatical analysis — the women of the exalted [beings]; or it is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound [meaning exalted women]. And thus — for the superior women such as <s>Śacī</s>, <s>Yamī</s>, <s>Urvaśī</s>, and the like, it should not be stated — as in the case of the <s>Śūdra</s> — that there is absence of Vedic knowledge-qualification due to absence of <s>saṃskāra</s>. Why? Because of the observation of their qualification through being seers (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) in <s>vidyās</s> (meditative hymns) such as '<s>sapatnīṃ me parādhama</s>' (<s>Mantrapraśna</s> 1.16) and the like — this is the construction.
