Here, by the <s>pratīka</s>-citation '<s>sapatnīm</s>,' the complete passage '<s>sapatnīṃ me parādhama</s>, <s>patiṃ me kevalaṃ kṛdhi</s>, <s>uttarāham uttarā uttared uttarābhyaḥ</s>' is taken. This is the speech of <s>Śacī</s>. O Lord, '<s>me sapatnīm</s>' — my co-wife, one married to my husband other than me — '<s>parādhama</s>' — cast away. '<s>Kevalam</s>' — make my husband attached to me alone. '<s>Aham uttarābhyaḥ</s>' — superior to [women] who are superior in beauty or other than me, 'I am <s>uttarā</s>' — exalted — being the most beloved, 'may I cross over' (<s>uttaret</s>) — may I overcome the distress caused by co-wives: this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the hymns seen by <s>Devamātṛ</s>, <s>Yamī</s>, <s>Paulomī</s>, and others, such as '<s>udatī paśya vaḥ soma ekebhyaḥ parvate, udāsau sūryo agāt</s>' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.159.1) and the like, are included.
But the absence [of qualification] due to the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> [is stated] as a general rule.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.11:
tarhi saṃskārābhāvahetoruttamastrīṣu vyabhicārassyādityata āha - saṃskāreti // abhāvo vedādhikārasya / tuśabdaḥ pūrvoktanyāyasya sāmānyatvākhyaviśeṣadyotakaḥ / ukta iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca saṃskārābhāvena hetunā yatsūtre vedādhikārasya abhāva uktaḥ saḥ 'sāmānyena'; sāmānyanyāyena sāpavādaniyamābhiprāyeṇaiva, na tu nirapavādaniyamena / ato nāpavādaviṣaye vyabhicāra ityarthaḥ / sāmānyatvavacanena śūdrapratibandī mocitā / tathā ca saṃskārābhāvena vedādhikārābhāva iti sāmānyavyāpteḥ śacyādiṣu vidyādhikāradarśanākhyāpavādakena bhaṅge 'pi na śūdrādāvapi tasya bhaṅgaḥ kalpyaḥ, tatra vedavidyādhikāre viśeṣapramāṇākhyāpavādakābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp 1,3.9.11:
Then there would be deviation of the reason — absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> — in the case of superior women. To this he says — '<s>saṃskāra</s>.' // '<s>Abhāvaḥ</s>' — of Vedic qualification. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) indicates the distinctive feature that the previously stated principle is a general rule (<s>sāmānya</s>). '<s>Ukta</s>' (stated) is the remainder. And thus — the absence of Vedic qualification stated in the <s>sūtra</s> due to the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> as its reason is '<s>sāmānyena</s>' — by way of a general rule, i.e., with the intention of a rule that admits exceptions — not as an exceptionless rule. Therefore there is no deviation in the domain of the exception — this is the meaning. By the statement of generality, the restriction to the <s>Śūdra</s> is released. And thus — since the general co-extensiveness 'absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> implies absence of Vedic qualification' is broken by the exception of the observation of <s>vidyā</s>-qualification in <s>Śacī</s> and the like, still, for <s>Śūdras</s> and the like, the breaking [of the rule] should not be imagined — because there is no exception-evidence (<s>apavādaka</s>) in the form of special scriptural authority for their Vedic <s>vidyā</s>-qualification: this is the purport.

children.text:
asti ca tāsāṃ saṃskāraḥ -
strīṇāṃ pradānakarmaiva yathopanayanaṃ tathā / iti smṛteḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text:
And there is <s>saṃskāra</s> for those [women] —
'For women, the act of giving [in marriage] is equivalent to <s>upanayana</s> (initiation).' — Because of <s>smṛti</s>. // 36 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.12:
evaṃ strīṇāṃ upanayanābhāve 'pi pūrvoktavyāpteḥ sāmānyatvena apavādasambhavādasti vedādhikāra ityuktam/ athopanayanākhyavidhyabhāve 'pi tatpratinidhisadbhāvācca astyadhikāra ityāha - asticeti / caḥ adhikārasamuccaye / 'tāsāṃ'; strīṇāṃ kuta etadityata āha - strīṇāmiti / puṃsāmiti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca puṃsāṃ yathā upanayanaṃ saṃskāraḥ, tathā strīṇāṃ 'pradānakarmaiva'; vivāhakriyaiva saṃskāra iti vyāsasmṛtyarthaḥ / smṛterityasya tāsāmityanenānvayaḥ / iti jñāyata iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca uttamastrīṣviha hetūkṛtasya vidhipratinidhisādhāraṇasaṃskārasāmānyābhāvasyābhāvāt na vyabhicāra iti bhāvaḥ / na ca saṃskāramātrasya vedādhikāraprayojakatve adhamastrīṇāmapi tadāpattiriti vācyam / niṣedhābhāvasahitasyaiva tasya prayojakatvābhyupagamāt / nanvevamuttamastrīṇāṃ saṃskārayuktatvādeva adhikāritvamiti noktanyāyabhaṅga iti vaktuṃ śakyatvāt, kimarthaṃ tāsu saṃskārābhāvamaṅgīkṛtya uktanyāyasya sāpavādatvavacanamiti cet - na, pradānādiśūnyatiryagādīnāmapi saṅgrahārthatvāt / teṣāmapi 'ayamagne jaritā'; (ṛ.10.142. 1.) ityādividyādhikāradarśanena apavādaviṣayatvāt / anena - 'tamadhyāpayīta'; iti tacchabdena pūrvaprakṛtopanayanākhyasaṃskāramātrasya parāmarśādvedaḥ kṛtsna iti smṛteścāsya śūdrasya tadabhāvābhilāpānnāgniriti śrutau saṃskārābhāvābhidhānāt na tasya vedādhikāra iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.9.12:
Thus it has been stated that even in the absence of <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread ceremony) for women, there is eligibility for the <s>Veda</s>, since the previously stated <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) being general, an exception is possible. Now he says 'asti ca' — even in the absence of the injunction called <s>upanayana</s>, there is eligibility because a substitute for it exists. The word 'ca' is for accumulating [reasons for] eligibility. 'Of those' — of women; whence is this known? To this he says 'strīṇām' (of women). 'Of men' is to be supplied. And thus, just as <s>upanayana</s> is the <s>saṃskāra</s> (purificatory rite) for men, so for women the marriage ceremony alone is the <s>saṃskāra</s> — this is the meaning of <s>Vyāsa</s>'s <s>smṛti</s>. The word 'smṛteḥ' connects with 'tāsām.' 'It is known' is to be supplied. And thus, since there is no absence of the general <s>saṃskāra</s> common to injunctive substitutes — which was made the reason [for eligibility] — in the case of superior women, there is no deviation; this is the purport. Nor should it be said that if mere <s>saṃskāra</s> were sufficient for Vedic eligibility, then even inferior women would have that status, since it is accepted that only <s>saṃskāra</s> accompanied by the absence of prohibition is the enabling factor. If it be objected: since superior women possess <s>saṃskāra</s>, their eligibility follows without breaking the stated principle, so why accept the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> in them and then speak of the stated principle as having exceptions? — No, because it is meant to include animals and others who lack the marriage ceremony and such rites. For them too, eligibility for <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is seen in passages like 'ayam agne jaritā' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.142.1), so they fall within the scope of exceptions. By this — since the word 'tat' in 'tam adhyāpayīta' (one should teach him) refers merely to the <s>saṃskāra</s> called <s>upanayana</s> previously discussed, and since the <s>smṛti</s> states 'the entire <s>Veda</s>' and for this <s>Śūdra</s> the <s>śruti</s> 'na agniḥ' (no fire) declares the absence of that [<s>saṃskāra</s>], therefore the <s>sūtra</s>'s meaning — that the <s>Śūdra</s> has no Vedic eligibility — is stated.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
And because of the undertaking [of <s>upanayana</s>] upon ascertainment of the absence of that [<s>Śūdra</s>-hood]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.37 |

children.text: 'nāhametadveda bho yadgotrohamasmi'; (chāṃ.4.4.) iti satyavacanena satyakāmasya śūdratvābhāvanirdhāraṇe hāridrumatasya 'naitadabrāhmaṇo vivaktumarhati'; (chāṃ.4.5.) iti tatsaṃskāre pravṛtteśca // 37 //
children.translated_text: Because upon the ascertainment of the absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood of <s>Satyakāma</s> through his truthful speech — 'I do not know, sir, what lineage I am' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.4) — <s>Hāridrumata</s> undertook his <s>saṃskāra</s> (initiation), [saying] 'A non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would not be able to speak thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.5). 37.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.13:
nanu śūdre saṃskārābhāvena vedavidyādhikārābhāvoktiranupapannā / 'śūdraṃ nopanayīta'; iti niṣedhābhāvena tasyāpi saṃskārasambhavāt / 'nāgnirna yajñaḥ'; iti śrutau tu śūdrasya saṃskārābhāva evocyate na tu asau na kārya iti niṣidhyate / ato na tadvirodho 'pītyāśaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtraṃ paṭhitvā vyācaṣṭe - tadabhāveti / 'iti satyavacanena'; vāṅmanasayorekarūpayathārthavacanena tajjñāpitenārjaveneti yāvat / 'satyakāmasya'; tadākhyasya ṛṣeḥ etacca pūrvatrottaratra ca sambadhyate / 'satyavacanena satyakāmasya'; ityādinā sūtre tacchabdo vyastaḥ anekavibhaktikaḥ buddhyā vivicyāvartate ityuktaṃ bhavati / śūdratvābhāvanirdhāraṇe cetyasya naitadbrāhmaṇa ityanena sambandhaḥ / co 'vadhāraṇe / śrutāvabrāhmaṇamātrasya anupanayanābhiprāyapratītestadanusāreṇa brāhmaṇatvābhāvetyanuktvā śūdratvābhāveti tadabhāvapadavyākhyānena śrutau brāhmaṇaśabdo brahmāṇanayogyatraivarṇikapara ityuktaṃ bhavati / etadvākyasya yadyayamabrāhmaṇaḥ śūdraḥsyāttarhmetatsatyavacanaṃ ārjavavacanaṃ vāṅmanasayoravairūpyeṇa vacanaṃ vivaktuṃ nārhediti vipakṣe tarkoktirūpatayā, yo 'brāhmaṇaḥ sa evaṃ vaktuṃ nārhati satyavacanahīna iti vyatirekavyāptyuktirūpatayā vā śūdratvābhaāvanirṇāyakatvam / haridrumato 'patyaṃ hāridrumataḥ gautamaḥ / tasya pravṛtteriti / asya na tadabhāva iti adhyāhṛtapadenānvayaḥ / tathā cetthaṃ mahāvākyayojanā - satyakāmasya nāhametadvedeti satyavacanena naitadabrāhmaṇo vivaktumarhatīti vyatirekavyāptijñānena bādhakatarkeṇa ca śūdratvābhāvanirdhāraṇe satyeva tamanumāyaiva tasya satyakāmasyopanayanasaṃskāre 'hāridrumatasya'; gautamasya 'pravṛtteḥ'; pravṛttatvāt na śūdrasya tadabhāvaḥ saṃskāraniṣedhābhāva iti / co hetusamuccaye / anena - sūtre taditi vyastaṃ luptavibhaktikaṃ padaṃ samastaṃ ca tantreṇopāttam / caśabdo 'vadhāraṇe bhinnakrameṇa, na kevalaṃ śūdrasya saṃskārābhāvaḥ śrutimātrāt, kintu saṃskāraniṣedhajñāpakaliṅgācceti samuccaye ca / netyasti / tadabhāva ityanuṣajyate / tathā ca 'tasya'; satyakāmasya 'tena'; satyavacanena manovākkāyakarmaṇāṃ avaiparītyamārjavaṃ tadeva satyatvaṃ tādṛśavacanena tena jñāpitena ṛjutveneti yāvat / naitadabrāhmaṇo vivaktumarhatīti vyatirekavyāptiṃ bādhakatarkaṃ copanyasya 'tadabhāvanirdhāraṇe ca'; tasya śūdratvābhāvanirṇaye satyeva tadabhāvamanumāyaiva 'samidhaṃ somyāharopa tvāneṣye'; (chāṃ. 4.4.5.) iti tasya tasminnupanayanasaṃskāre tasya gautamasya pravṛtterdarśanācca na śūdrasya tadabhāvaḥ saṃskāraniṣedhābhāvaḥ / śūdrasya upanayananiṣedhābhāve kathamayaṃ tadabhāvanirdhāraṇe satyeva pravarteta, te jñāyate niṣedho 'stīti bhāva iti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
chāndogye hītthamākhyāyikā - satyakāmo nāma ṛṣiḥ jabālākhyaṃ mātaramupetyovāca / kimiti? ahaṃ vedādhyayanārtham ācāryamupagaccheyaṃ tatrādhyayanasyopanayanasaṃskārasāpekṣatvāt upanayanaṃ vinā te māṃ nādhyāpayeyuḥ, upanayanaṃ ca gotrādyavacane na kuryuḥ ato 'haṃ kiṃ gotro 'smi tadvadeti / evamuktā jabālā svaputraṃ satyakāmamabravīt - he tāta tvaṃ yadgotro 'sītyetat nāhaṃ vedeti / evamuktaḥ satyakāmo gautamamupetyovāca / kimiti? he bhagavan brahmacaryārthaṃ tvāmupeyamiti / evamukto gautamaḥ he somya tvaṃ kiṃgotro 'si? tadvadetyuvāca / evamuktassatyakāmaḥ punargautamaṃ pratyāha - nāhametadveda bho iti / bho bhagavan pūjya gautama ahaṃ yadgotro 'smītyetat vedyaṃ 'na veda'; na jānāmītyarthaḥ / evaṃ satyakāmasya satyavacanenārjavaṃ jñātvā punastaṃ pratyuvāca / naitadityādi / atra brāhmaṇaśabdo brahmāṇanayogyatraivarṇikaparaḥ / 'ārjavaṃ brāhmaṇe sākṣāt śūdro 'nārjavalakṣaṇaḥ'; itiśrutivyākhyānarūpāyāṃ smṛtau brāhmaṇapratiyogitvena śūdrasyopādānāt / tathā ca 'etat'; ārjavasaṃyuktavacanam 'abrāhmaṇaḥ'; traivarṇiketaraḥśūdro 'vivaktuṃ'; sarvathā vaktuṃ 'nārhati'; na yogyaḥ / atastvamevaṃ vadan brāhmaṇa evāsi, ato he somya samidhamupahara tvāmupaneṣya iti /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.9.13:
Now, an objection arises: the statement that the <s>Śūdra</s> lacks eligibility for Vedic knowledge due to the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> is unjustified, since <s>saṃskāra</s> is possible for him too due to the absence of prohibition — 'one should not initiate a <s>Śūdra</s>' — and in the <s>śruti</s> 'na agniḥ na yajñaḥ' (no fire, no sacrifice), the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> for the <s>Śūdra</s> is merely stated but not prohibited as 'this should not be done.' Hence there is no contradiction either. To resolve this doubt, he reads the <s>sūtra</s> and explains — 'tadabhāva' etc. 'By truthful speech' — by speech that is in accordance with reality, where mind and speech are of one form; through the straightforwardness revealed by it — this is the meaning. 'Of <s>Satyakāma</s>' — of the <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) of that name; and this connects with what precedes and follows. By 'satyavacanena satyakāmasya' etc., it is said that the word 'tat' in the <s>sūtra</s> is distributed across multiple case-endings and is to be discriminated by the intellect. The phrase 'upon ascertainment of the absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood' connects with 'naitad abrāhmaṇaḥ' (a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [would not say this]). The word 'ca' is for emphasis. Since in the <s>śruti</s> only the non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> status — with the intent of non-initiation — is understood, following that, instead of saying 'absence of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood,' the explanation uses 'absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood' through the phrase 'tadabhāva,' thereby indicating that the word <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the <s>śruti</s> refers to members of the three <s>varṇas</s> (classes) who are worthy of <s>Brahman</s>. The ascertainment of the absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood from this statement takes the form of either a counter-positive reasoning — 'if he were a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Śūdra</s>, he would not be qualified to utter this truthful speech, this straightforward speech where mind and speech are not discordant' — or as the statement of a <s>vyatireka-vyāpti</s> (negative concomitance): 'one who is not a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is not qualified to speak thus, being devoid of truthful speech.' <s>Hāridrumata</s> — descendant of <s>Haridrumata</s>, i.e., <s>Gautama</s>. 'Because of the undertaking' — this connects with the supplied phrase 'there is no absence of that.' And thus the construction of the great sentence is: when, through the truthful speech of <s>Satyakāma</s> — 'I do not know this' — through knowledge of the negative concomitance 'a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would not be able to speak thus,' and through the defeating reasoning, the ascertainment of the absence of <s>Śūdra</s>-hood had been made, only after inferring that, <s>Gautama</s> of the <s>Hāridrumata</s> [lineage] undertook the <s>upanayana</s> <s>saṃskāra</s> of that <s>Satyakāma</s>; therefore there is no absence of that [prohibition] for the <s>Śūdra</s>, meaning there is no absence of the prohibition of <s>saṃskāra</s>. The word 'ca' is for accumulating reasons. By this — the distributed word 'tat' in the <s>sūtra</s>, with elided case-endings, is taken up collectively through the method of construing together. The word 'ca' functions in different sequences: for emphasis — not merely from <s>śruti</s> alone is there absence of <s>saṃskāra</s> for the <s>Śūdra</s>, but also from the indicatory mark that reveals the prohibition of <s>saṃskāra</s> — and for accumulation. 'Na' (not) is present. 'Tadabhāva' (absence of that) is carried forward. And thus 'of that <s>Satyakāma</s>,' 'by that' truthful speech — the non-discordance of actions of mind, speech, and body is <s>ārjava</s> (straightforwardness), which itself is truthfulness; by such speech, by the straightforwardness revealed through it — presenting the negative concomitance 'a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would not be able to speak thus' and the defeating reasoning — 'upon ascertainment of the absence of that' — upon the determination of the absence of his <s>Śūdra</s>-hood, having inferred just that absence, because of the observation that <s>Gautama</s> undertook his <s>upanayana</s> <s>saṃskāra</s> with the words 'Bring fuel, dear one, I shall initiate you' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.4.5), therefore there is no absence of that for the <s>Śūdra</s> — that is, there is no absence of prohibition of <s>saṃskāra</s>. If there were no prohibition of <s>upanayana</s> for the <s>Śūdra</s>, how would he have undertaken [the initiation] only upon ascertaining the absence of that [<s>Śūdra</s>-hood]? From this it is known that the prohibition exists — this is the purport; thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is stated.
For in the <s>Chāndogya</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] the narrative is as follows: A sage named <s>Satyakāma</s> approached his mother named <s>Jabālā</s> and said — what? 'I wish to go to a teacher for the purpose of Vedic study. Since study requires the <s>upanayana</s> <s>saṃskāra</s>, without <s>upanayana</s> they will not teach me, and they will not perform <s>upanayana</s> without declaration of lineage and such; therefore tell me what lineage I am.' Thus addressed, <s>Jabālā</s> said to her son <s>Satyakāma</s>: 'O dear one, I do not know what lineage you are.' Thus told, <s>Satyakāma</s> approached <s>Gautama</s> and said — what? 'Revered sir, I come to you for the life of a <s>brahmacārin</s> (student).' Thus addressed, <s>Gautama</s> said: 'O dear one, what lineage are you? Tell me.' Thus asked, <s>Satyakāma</s> replied to <s>Gautama</s>: 'I do not know this, sir' — meaning: 'O revered <s>Gautama</s>, I do not know what lineage I am.' Having thus learned the straightforwardness of <s>Satyakāma</s> through his truthful speech, he replied to him: 'Naitat' etc. Here the word <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> refers to members of the three <s>varṇas</s> who are worthy of <s>Brahman</s>. 'Since in the <s>smṛti</s>, which is an explanation of the <s>śruti</s> — "straightforwardness belongs directly to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; a <s>Śūdra</s> is characterized by non-straightforwardness" — the <s>Śūdra</s> is mentioned as the counterpart of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' And thus: 'this' — speech conjoined with straightforwardness — 'a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — a <s>Śūdra</s>, one other than the three <s>varṇas</s> — 'would not be able to speak' — to utter in any way — 'is not qualified.' Therefore you, speaking thus, are indeed a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; hence, dear one, bring the fuel, I shall initiate you.
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s>.
And because of the prohibition in <s>smṛti</s> against hearing, studying, and [understanding] the meaning [of the <s>Veda</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.38 |

children.text:
'śravaṇe trapujatubhyāṃ śrotraparipūraṇam / adhyayane jihvācchedaḥ /
arthāvadhāraṇe hṛdayavidāraṇam'; (gautamadharma. 12.4..7.) iti pratiṣedhāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the prohibition: 'If [a <s>Śūdra</s>] hears [the <s>Veda</s>], his ears are to be filled with molten tin and lac; if he studies it, his tongue is to be cut off; if he grasps its meaning, his heart is to be split open' (<s>Gautama Dharmasūtra</s> 12.4-7).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.14:
nanvaviśeṣādityuktarītyā śūdrasyāpi viśiṣṭabuddhyādimattvena adhikāraḥ siddhyet / anyathā tena devatādyadhikārasiddhirapi na syāditi śaṅkāṃ pariharatsūtramupanyasya vyācaṣṭe - śravaṇeti / sūtre 'arthāvadhāraṇe'; iti śrutyanusārādarthaśabdaḥ tadavadhāraṇaparaḥ / tathā ca 'śravaṇe trapujatubhyām'; iti śrutau śūdrasya vedaśravaṇādhyayanārthāvadhāraṇānāṃ pratiṣiddhatvādityarthaḥ / asya na tadabhāva ityanuṣaktasādhyenānvayaḥ /
adhyayananiṣedhābhāva iti tadarthaḥ / tathā cāniṣiddhatve sati viśiṣṭabuddhyādimattvasyaiva vedādhikāraprayojakatvenāṅgīkṛtatvāt tasya ca śūdre abhāvānna tasya devaprativandyā vedādhikāro vācya iti bhāvaḥ / śūdreṇa vedaśravaṇe kṛte sati drutābhyāṃ trapujatubhyāṃ vaṅgalākṣābhyāṃ tatkarṇavivaraparipūraṇaṃ rājabhaṭaiḥ kāryamiti śrutyarthaḥ / śiṣṭaḥ sugamaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.9.14:
Now, an objection arises: in the manner stated as 'without distinction,' the <s>Śūdra</s> too could establish eligibility by virtue of possessing distinguished intellect and such qualities. Otherwise, his eligibility for worship of deities and the like would also not be established. To resolve this doubt, he presents the <s>sūtra</s> and explains — 'śravaṇa' etc. In the <s>sūtra</s>, following the <s>śruti</s>'s mention of 'upon grasping the meaning,' the word 'artha' refers to the comprehension of meaning. And thus the meaning is: because in the <s>śruti</s>, hearing, studying, and comprehending the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> are prohibited for the <s>Śūdra</s> by the passage 'upon hearing, with tin and lac.' This connects with the supplied predicate 'there is no absence of that' — meaning there is no absence of the prohibition of study. And thus, since it is accepted that possessing distinguished intellect and such qualities enables Vedic eligibility only when there is no prohibition, and since that [absence of prohibition] does not exist for the <s>Śūdra</s>, his Vedic eligibility — of the kind envied even by the gods — should not be asserted; this is the purport. When a <s>Śūdra</s> hears the <s>Veda</s>, his ear-holes are to be filled by the king's officers with molten tin and lac (<s>vaṅga</s> and <s>lākṣā</s>) — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. The rest is easy to understand.

children.text:
nāgnirna yajñaśśūdrasya tathaivādhyayanaṃ kutaḥ /
kevalaiva tu śuśrūṣā trivarṇānāṃ vidhīyate // iti smṛteśca /
children.translated_text: 'For the <s>Śūdra</s> there is no fire, no sacrifice; likewise, whence could study come? Only service to the three <s>varṇas</s> is ordained [for him].' Thus from <s>smṛti</s> as well.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.9.15:
śrutau śūdreṇa śravaṇe kṛte ityanuktervarṇabāhyaviṣayeyaṃ śrutiḥ kiṃ na syādityāśaṅkānivṛtyarthaṃ sūtre smṛteścetyuktaṃ, tāṃ smṛtimudāharati - neti / yathā 'śūdrasya'; śūdreṇa nāgnissavathā ādhātavyaḥ pañcavidho yajño 'pi nānuṣṭheyaḥ / tathādhyayanaṃ kutaḥ bhavet na kuto 'pi / tarhi tenānuṣṭheyaṃ paralokasādhanaṃ kimiti pṛcchati - tu kintviti / uttaramāha - kevalaiveti / bhṛtirahitetyarthaḥ / trayaśca te varṇāśca trivarṇāḥ, teṣāṃ brahmakṣatriyavaiśyānāmityarthaḥ / 'śuśrūṣā'; paricaryaiveti sambandhaḥ / vidhīyate / kāryatveneti śeṣaḥ / iti smṛterityasya śūdrasyaivādhyayananiṣedhāvagamāt na tadabhāva ityadhyāhṛtenānvayaḥ / tathā ca spaṣṭasmṛtibalāt śruterapi śūdraviṣayatvameveti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>BBsBhDīp</s> 1,3.9.15:
Since the <s>śruti</s> does not explicitly state 'when a <s>Śūdra</s> hears,' could this <s>śruti</s> not pertain to those outside the <s>varṇa</s> system [rather than <s>Śūdras</s>]? To remove this doubt, the <s>sūtra</s> says 'smṛteś ca' (and from <s>smṛti</s>), and he cites that <s>smṛti</s> — 'na' etc. Just as for the <s>Śūdra</s>, the fivefold fire is not to be established, nor is the fivefold sacrifice to be performed, so study — whence could it come? It could come from nowhere. Then what means of attaining the other world should he perform? — To this he asks with 'tu' (but). The answer is given with 'kevalaiva' (only). Meaning: without remuneration. 'The three <s>varṇas</s>' — three, and they are <s>varṇas</s>, hence <s>trivarṇa</s>; of them, meaning of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>Vaiśyas</s>. '<s>Śuśrūṣā</s>' (devoted service) — this connects with 'paricaryā' (attendance) alone. 'Is ordained' — meaning: as a duty; this is to be supplied. The phrase 'iti smṛteḥ' (thus from <s>smṛti</s>) connects with the supplied text 'there is no absence of that,' meaning: since from this <s>smṛti</s> too the prohibition of study for the <s>Śūdra</s> alone is understood. And thus, by the force of explicit <s>smṛti</s>, the <s>śruti</s> too pertains to <s>Śūdras</s> only — this is the purport.
But for <s>Vidura</s> and others, there is some distinction, since knowledge had arisen [in them] spontaneously. 38.
Thus ends the <s>Apaśūdrādhikaraṇa</s> (section on the exclusion of the <s>Śūdra</s>). 9.
// 10. Kampanādhikaraṇa (the topic of trembling) //

children.text: yadidaṃ kiñca jagatsarvaṃ prāṇa ejati nissṛtam /

children.translated_text: [He is] a great fear, a thunderbolt raised aloft. Those who know this become immortal. (Kaṭha 2.3.2)
Thus, liberation is heard [as resulting] from the knowledge of the raised thunderbolt (udyatavajra).
Whatever there is in this entire world — all this, having issued forth from Prāṇa, trembles.
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.10, verse 1:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.10.1:
atrādhikaraṇe vajranāma samanvīyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ sūcayati - yadidamiti // atra traivarṇikānāṃ vedāt brahmajñānaṃ mokṣadamiti pūrvoktamayuktam / yato 'yadidam'; iti śrutau udyatavajrajñānāt mokṣaḥ śrūyata iti vākyopaskāreṇa yojanā / anena pūrvādhikaraṇe traivarṇikānāṃ vedāt brahmajñānaṃ mokṣadamiti yadabhipretaṃ tasya cānandamayādhikaraṇe 'netaraḥ'; ityanenoktasya mokṣajanakajñānaviṣayatvasya viṣṇoranyatrākṣepāt tenāsya ākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / vajraśabdo viṣaya iti sūcitam / vajraśruteḥ kuliśe rūḍhibalāt tathā 'udyatāyudhadordaṇḍāḥ'; ityādismṛtau 'tenendro vajramudayacchat'; () iti śrutau ca āyudhe prasiddhodyatatvaliṅgabalāccendrāyudhamevedaṃ vajramiti sayuktikapūrvapakṣaḥ sūcitaḥ / śrutau prāṇa iti saptamyantaṃ padam / sthitamitiśeṣaḥ / prāṇa ityasya nimittasaptamītvaṃ vā vibhaktivipariṇāmaṃ vā āśritya āvṛttyā nissṛtamityanenāpi sambandhaḥ / yadityasyāvṛttiradhyāhāro vā / yaditiśravaṇāt taditi labhyate / tathā cāyaṃ siddhānte śrutyarthaḥ - 'yatkiñca'; yatkiñcit dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ yatsarvaṃ jagat 'prāṇe'; prāṇanānnimittāt prāṇaśabdavācye harau sthitaṃ prāṇānnissṛtaṃ tato jātaṃ ca taditaṃ sarvaṃ jagat 'yasmādejati'; yatpreraṇayā ceṣṭate tanmahanīyatvāt pūjyatvāt 'mahat'; bhīṣayatīti bhayaṃ duṣṭānāṃ bhayaṅkaram 'udyataṃ'; sarvaprayatnavat 'udyatatvaṃ ca prayatnavattvam'; utpūrvasya yamestadarthatvāt, iti candrikokteḥ / yatīprayatna ityasyedaṃ rūpam, ucchabda utkarṣavācītyapi kecit / 'vajraṃ'; doṣavarjanāt apriyavarjanādvā tacchabdavācyam / etadye 'viduḥ'; aparokṣato jānanti te 'amṛtāḥ'; muktāḥ bhavantīti / yadvā - prāṇa iti prathamāntaṃ padaṃ tathā ca prāṇo mukhyaprāṇaḥ / idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kiñcānyacchrutaṃ sarvaṃ jagacca yasmānnissṛtaṃ yasmādejati ca tadetadvajraṃ ye vidurityarthaḥ / athavā - yadityasyāvṛttistatra prathamasya jagadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ, dvitīyasya mukhyaprāṇaparatvam, tṛtīyasya vajraparatvam / sa iti labhyate / tasya prathamāntaprāṇapadenānvayaḥ / tathā ca yatkiñcijjagatsarvaṃ yadyasmānnissṛtaṃ sa mukhyaprāṇaḥ / yasmādejati tadvajraṃ ye vidurityarthaḥ / atra prathamavyākhyāne mukhyaprāṇasya jagadantargatatvena bhagavatpreryatvaṃ dvitīye jagatsāmyena, tṛtīye tu mukhyaprāṇasyaiva sākṣādbhagavatpreryatvaṃ jagatastu mukhyaprāṇapreryatvamiti bhedaḥ / pūrvapakṣī tu indrāyudhameva vajrapadenoktam / udyatatvamudyamanakarmatvaṃ tasyaiva liṅgamiti manyate //
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.3.10, verse 1:
In this adhikaraṇa, the word 'vajra' (thunderbolt) is coordinated. He indicates the connection with śruti and the like, and the subject matter — 'yat idam' (whatever this is). // Here [the argument runs]: what was stated earlier — that for the three upper varṇas, knowledge of Brahman arising from the Vedas is the bestower of liberation — is improper. Because in the śruti 'whatever this is,' liberation is heard as resulting from the knowledge of the raised thunderbolt — this is the construction with sentence-supplement. By this, the connection of this [adhikaraṇa] with the previous adhikaraṇa through objection is stated — since what was accepted in the previous adhikaraṇa, that knowledge of Brahman arising from the Vedas is the bestower of liberation for the three varṇas, and since the Viṣṇu-referentiality of the subject of liberation-producing knowledge stated in the Ānandamaya-adhikaraṇa by 'not the other' is now challenged as [potentially referring to] someone other than Viṣṇu. The word 'vajra' is indicated as the subject. From the śruti on vajra, because of the conventional force (rūḍhibala) of kuliśa (thunderbolt [of Indra]), and similarly in the smṛti 'with upraised weapon-arms,' and in the śruti 'thereby Indra seized the vajra' — because of the force of the well-known mark of being 'raised' applying to a weapon — this vajra is Indra's weapon alone: thus the reasoned prima facie view is indicated. In the śruti, 'prāṇa' with the seventh case ending (locative) is the word. 'Established' is the remainder. Alternatively, 'prāṇa' has a causal locative, or through case-transformation, a connection with 'nissṛtam' (issued forth) through recurrence. 'Yat' (whatever) is either recurrent or to be supplied. From the hearing of 'yat,' 'tat' (that) is obtained. And thus, the meaning of the śruti in the siddhānta is: 'whatever' — whatever is seen or heard, all the world — 'in Prāṇa' — in Hari who is denoted by the word Prāṇa because of being the cause of sustenance — is established; from Prāṇa it 'issued forth' — was born from him — and all that world — because it 'trembles' (ejati) — functions by his impulsion — because of His venerability and worthiness of worship, [He is] 'great' (mahat); He is 'bhayam' (fear) — terrifying to the wicked — who 'frightens'; 'raised' (udyatam) — being like one with full effort; 'and the state of being raised means being like one who makes effort' — because the verb 'yam' with the prefix 'ut' has that meaning, as stated in the Candrikā. 'Yatī-prayatna' (effort of an ascetic) — this is its form; some say the prefix 'ut' expresses excellence. 'Vajram' — denoted by that word because of the rejection of faults (doṣavarjana), or because of the rejection of the disagreeable (apriyavarjana). Those who 'know' (viduḥ) this — know it directly — they become 'immortal' (amṛtāḥ) — liberated. Alternatively, 'prāṇa' is a word in the nominative case, and thus Prāṇa means Mukhyaprāṇa (the chief vital breath). Whatever world is seen, and whatever else is heard — all the world — from which it 'issued forth,' from which it 'trembles' — those who know that vajra: this is the meaning. Or alternatively, 'yat' recurs, with the first referring to a qualifier of the world, the second referring to Mukhyaprāṇa, and the third referring to vajra. 'Sa' (he) is obtained. Its connection is with 'Prāṇa' in the nominative. And thus: whatever world there is, that from which it issued forth — that is Mukhyaprāṇa. That from which it trembles — that vajra, those who know [it]: this is the meaning. Here, in the first interpretation, Mukhyaprāṇa is within the world and hence is impelled by Bhagavān; in the second, he has the same status as the world; in the third, Mukhyaprāṇa himself is directly impelled by Bhagavān, while the world is impelled by Mukhyaprāṇa — this is the difference. The prima facie view, however, holds: by the word vajra, Indra's weapon alone is spoken of. The state of being 'raised' — having the nature of being the object of the act of raising — is the mark that belongs to that [weapon] alone. //

Therefore he said —
Sūtra — Oṃ //
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.10, verse 2:]
Because of [causing] trembling (kampana). | Brahmasūtra 1.3.39 |
Because of the statement of trembling — 'trembles' (ejati) — the raised vajra is Bhagavān alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.10.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti // 'kampanavacanāt'; ityetadrūpāt sarvajagacceṣṭakatvavacanādityarthaḥ / yadvā - kampanasya mukhyaprāṇasya ejatītikampanavacanācceṣṭakatvokterityarthaḥ / vacanādityanena kampanapadaṃ tadvacanaparamityuktaṃ bhavati / na ca śrutau vākyabhedāṅgīkāre kampakatvaṃ vajre nocyata iti vācyam / kampakatvanimittabhayaṅkaratvasya vajre abhidhānādvākyabhedāyogāt / udyatavajra iti sūtre śeṣoktiḥ samanvayasūtrādanuvṛttasya tadityasyoddeśyavajrapadānusārātprāṇapadānusārādvā bhagavāniti vyākhyānaṃ kṛtam / sāvadhāraṇaṃ caitat / tena tuśabdārtho darśitaḥ / yadyapi vajro bhagavānevetyetāvadeva vaktavyaṃ, na tūdyata iti vajraviśeṣaṇamapi / tathāpi pūrvapakṣyuktodyatatvaliṅgasya prayatnavattvarūpodyatatvārthatayā sāvakāśatvajñāpanāya udyatetyuktam /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.3.10, verse 2:
Having introduced the sūtra that gives the established conclusion, he explains — 'therefore' (ataḥ). // 'Because of the statement of trembling' (kampanavacanāt) — because of the statement of causing the activity of the entire world: that is the meaning. Alternatively, 'of the trembling one' — of Mukhyaprāṇa — because of the statement of trembling, i.e., because of the statement of causing him to function: that is the meaning. By the word 'vacanāt' (because of the statement), it is stated that the word 'kampana' refers to the statement [about it]. Nor should it be said that if one accepts a division of the śruti passage, the causing of trembling is not stated of the vajra — because since the terrifying nature that arises from the causing of trembling is predicated of the vajra, division of the passage is inappropriate. 'Raised vajra' (udyatavajra) — this is the remainder of the sūtra. From 'tat' carried forward from the Samanvaya-sūtra, following the vajra-word as the addressee or following the Prāṇa-word, the explanation 'Bhagavān' is made. And this is with the restrictive sense. By this, the meaning of the word 'tu' is shown. Although what is to be stated is only 'the vajra is Bhagavān alone' — not the qualifier 'raised' (udyata) of the vajra — nevertheless, to indicate that the mark of being 'raised' stated by the prima facie advocate has scope in the sense of 'being like one who makes effort,' 'raised' is stated.

children.text: 'ko hyevānyātkaḥ prāṇyāt / yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt'; (tai.2.7.) iti hi śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Who indeed could breathe, who could live, if this bliss (ānanda) were not in space (ākāśa)?' (Taittirīya 2.7) — for thus is the śruti.
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.10, verse 3:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.10.3:
nanu śrutiliṅgābhyāṃ pūrvapakṣite kathaṃ liṅgamātreṇa nirṇaya ityato liṅgasya niravakāśatvādevetyāśayena śruteḥ prathamadvitīyavyākhyānānusāreṇa vajre śrutasya prāṇataditarasādhāraṇyena sāmānyato jagacceṣṭakatvaliṅgasya viṣṇoranyatraniravakāśatvaṃ śrutyā darśayati - kohīti / hiśabdo hetau yata ityarthe prasiddhau vā / astīti śeṣaḥ / ato liṅgasya nānyatra sāvakāśatvaṃ śaṅkyamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.3.10, verse 3:
Objection: When the prima facie view is raised through both śruti and liṅga, how can there be determination through liṅga alone? — therefore, [to show] that the liṅga has no alternative scope (niravakāśatva), through the śruti he demonstrates, following the first and second interpretations, that the general mark of causing the activity of the world, which is heard as common to Prāṇa and others in the vajra-passage, has no scope elsewhere than in Viṣṇu — 'ko hi' (who indeed). // The word 'hi' is in the sense of a reason, i.e., 'because' (yataḥ), or for well-known fact. 'Exists' (asti) is the remainder. Therefore the mark has no scope for suspicion elsewhere: this is the sentence-remainder.
'The Prāṇa of Prāṇa, and the Eye of the eye' (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 6.4.18) — and [thus says the śruti].
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.10, verse 4:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.10.4:
yadā sāmānyataḥ sarvajagacceṣṭakatvameva viṣṇvekaniṣṭhaṃ tadā kimu vaktavyaṃ śruteḥ tṛtīyavyākhyānarītyā vajre śrutasya sarvajagatpravartakaprāṇaceṣṭakatvaliṅgasya viṣṇvekaniṣṭhatvaṃ jagacceṣṭakatvasya sarvathānyatrāyogāditi bhāvena tatra śrutiṃ darśayati - prāṇasyeti / co yasmādityarthe / pūrvaśrutisamuccaye vā / śrutirityanuṣajyate / uktaliṅgasya anyatra niravakāśatvaṃ jñāpayatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ / yadvā - yat jagatpravartakaprāṇaceṣṭakatvādiliṅgaṃ kampanādityanena abhisaṃhitaṃ, tasya viṣṇuniṣṭhatvāsiddhiparihārāya tatra śrutiṃ pramāṇayati - prāṇasyeti / 'prāṇasya'; sarvaceṣṭakamukhyaprāṇasya 'prāṇaṃ'; prakṛṣṭaceṣṭakatvarūpaprāṇatvapradam 'uta'; tathā 'cakṣuṣaścakṣuḥ'; darśanakaraṇatvarūpacakṣuṣṭvapradaṃ paramātmānaṃ ye viduste brahma 'nicikyuḥ'; prāpnuyuriti vājasaneya śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.3.10, verse 4:
When the causing of the activity of the entire world in general belongs exclusively to Viṣṇu, then what more needs to be said — following the third interpretation of the śruti — that the mark of causing the activity of the world-impelling Prāṇa, which is heard in the vajra-passage, belongs exclusively to Viṣṇu, since the causing of the activity of the world is in no way possible elsewhere? With this intent, he cites the śruti for that — 'prāṇasya' (of Prāṇa). // The word 'ca' is in the sense of 'because' (yasmāt). Or it is for accumulation with the previous śruti. 'Śruti' is to be connected. '[This śruti] indicates that the stated mark has no scope elsewhere': this is the sentence-remainder. Alternatively — the mark in the form of causing the activity of the world-impelling Prāṇa and the like, which is intended by 'kampanāt' and the like — for resolving the unestablishedness of its belonging to Viṣṇu, he authorizes the śruti for that — 'prāṇasya.' 'Of Prāṇa' — of Mukhyaprāṇa who causes the activity of all — 'the Prāṇa' — the one who bestows Prāṇa-hood in the form of being the cause of excellent activity; 'and also' (uta) — likewise — 'of the eye, the Eye' — the one who bestows eye-hood in the form of being the instrument of seeing — [those who know] that Paramātman reach Brahman, 'nicikyuḥ' — they would attain: this is the meaning of the Vājasaneya śruti.

children.text:
nabhasvato 'pi sarvāssyuḥ ceṣṭā bhagavato hareḥ /
kimutānyasya jagato yasya ceṣṭā nabhasvataḥ // iti ca skānde /
children.translated_text:
Even all the activities of Nabhasvat (Vāyu, the wind-god) belong to Bhagavān Hari;
how much more so the activities of the other world, whose activities [themselves come from] Nabhasvat. — Thus in the Skānda [Purāṇa].
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.10, verse 5:]

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.10.5:
śruteḥ prathamavyākhyāyāmapi kaimutyavyaktikaraṇāya śrutyuktaprāṇaceṣṭakatvaṃ hetūkṛtya pravṛttāṃ smṛtimāha - nabhasvata iti // 'api'; jagatprerakasyāpi 'nabhasvato'; vāyoryadā sarvāḥ ceṣṭāḥ 'bhagavato'; jñānādiguṇapūrṇāddharerbhavanti / tadā kimutānyasya preryasya vāyubhinnasya jagataśceṣṭā harerbhavantīti vaktavyam / kuta etat? yato yasya jagataḥ ceṣṭā nabhasvato na bhavantyata iti vacanārthaḥ / skānda ityanantaramuktamiti śeṣaḥ / ato 'pi liṅgasya nānyatrāvakāśa iti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Bhāṣyadīpikā on 1.3.10, verse 5:
Even in the first interpretation of the śruti, for making clear the a fortiori (kaimutya) argument, he cites the smṛti that proceeds by taking the causing of Prāṇa's activity (stated in the śruti) as its basis — 'nabhasvataḥ' (of Vāyu). // 'Even' (api) — even of the world-impelling 'Nabhasvat' — Vāyu — when all activities 'belong to Bhagavān' — who is full of qualities such as knowledge — Hari, then how much more so should it be said that the activities of 'the other' — the impelled, the world different from Vāyu — belong to Hari. Whence is this? Because — 'of that world whose activities belong to Nabhasvat' — whose activities do not come from Nabhasvat independently: this is the meaning of the statement. After 'Skānda,' '[it is] stated' is the remainder. Therefore, from this too, the mark has no scope elsewhere: this is the purport.

children.text:
cakraṃ caṅkramaṇādeṣa varjanādvajramucyate /
khaṇḍanātsvaṅga evaiṣa hetināmā svayaṃ hariḥ / iti brahmāvaivarte // 39 //
children.translated_text:
He is called Vajra because of His discus, His roaming about, and His rejection [of faults];
Because of His own body being the destroyer, this Hari Himself is called Heti (weapon). — Thus in the Brahmāvaivarta [Purāṇa]. // 39 //
[Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya 1.3.10, verse 6:]
// Thus ends the Kampanādhikaraṇa // 10 //
// 11. <s>Jyotir-adhikaraṇa</s> (Section on Light) //

children.text: hṛdaya āhitaṃ jyotiḥ paramātmetyuktam / tatra 'yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu hṛdyantarjotiḥ puruṣaḥ'; (bṛ. 6.3.7.) iti /
children.translated_text: The <s>jyotis</s> (light) established in the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) has been declared to be the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self). In that regard, the <s>śruti</s> states: 'This <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who consists of <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge), who is the inner light (<s>jyotis</s>) in the heart among the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.7).

children.text: atra 'ubhau lokāvanusañcarati'; (bṛ.6.3.7.) iti vacanājjīva iti pratīyate iti /
children.translated_text: Here, because of the statement 'He wanders through both worlds' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.7), it is understood to refer to the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul).

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.11.1:
atrādhikaraṇe ubhayatraprasiddhajyotirnāma samanvīyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca darśayati - hṛdaya iti / yaddhṛdaye 'āhitaṃ'; nihitaṃ jyotiḥ tacchabdavācyaṃ sa paramātmeti jyotirnaye abhihitamityarthaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - tatreti jyotirviṣaya ityarthaḥ / itiśabdātparaṃ śrūyata iti śeṣaḥ / tato 'pi kimityata āha - atreti / etadvākya ityarthaḥ / śrutaṃ jyotirityanuṣajyate / tathā cātra śrutaṃ jyotiḥ tacchabdavācyo jñānātmako jīva eveti pratīyate / kutaḥ? 'sasamānassannubhau lokāvanusañcarati'; itivacanāt ityādijīvaliṅgābhidhāyakavākyaśeṣāditi yojanā / anena 'hṛdyantarjyotiḥ'; iti vājasaneyavākyoktajyotiṣo viṣṇutvākṣepamukhena pūrvoktasyāpi tadākṣepāttenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiḥ uktā bhavati / vājasaneyoktaṃ jyotirviṣayaḥ, jīva evedaṃ jyotiriti pūrvapakṣaśca sūcitaḥ / vājasaneyake hi ayaṃ puruṣaḥ 'kiṃjyotiḥ'; kiṃjñānasādhanaḥ jīvasya jñānasādhanaṃ kimiti janakena pṛṣṭo yājñyavalkyaḥ 'ādityajyotissamrāḍiti hovāca'; (bṛ. 6.3.2.) ityanena he 'samrāṭ'; sārvabhauma janakarāja ādityākhyajñānasādhanako 'yaṃ puruṣa ityuvāca / evaṃkrameṇa praśnottarābhyāṃ jāgraddaśāyāmādityacandrāgnivācāṃ madhye pūrvapūrvāstamaye uttarottarajyotiṣṭvaṃ jīvasyābhidhāya punaḥ suptisvapnayorādityādiṣu caturṣvastamiteṣu 'kiṃjyotirayaṃ puruṣaḥ'; (bṛ.6.3.2.) iti janakena pṛṣṭo yājñavalkyaḥ 'ātmaivāsya jyotirbhavati'; iti tayorjīvasya svaprakāśaparamātmajyotiṣṭvamuktvā punaḥ 'katam ātmā'; (bṛ.6.3.7.) iti jyotiṣṭvenokta ātmā katamaḥ kīdṛśa iti pṛṣṭo 'yo 'yam'; ityanena jīvadehendriyādiviviktaḥ paramātmetyuttaramāhetyuktam / yo 'vijñānamayo'; vijñānapūrṇaḥ 'prāṇeṣu'; indriyeṣu antaḥ hṛdyantaśca niyantṛtvena vartamāno 'jyotiḥ'; jīvasya buddhyādidyotakaḥ 'puruṣaḥ'; pūrṇaṣaḍguṇo'sti / so 'yamātmetyarthaḥ / tasya mahimānamāha - sa iti / 'saḥ'; ātmā paramātmā 'samānaḥ'; avikāraḥ sadaikarūpaḥ san 'ubhau lokau'; bhūlokadyulokau jāgratsuṣuptī vā pratijīvamādāya tamanusañcaratītyarthaḥ / pūrvapakṣī tu, ātmapadaṃ sa iti padaṃ ca jīvaparaṃ ubhayalokasañcaraṇamapi karmādhīnaṃ vivakṣitaṃ, tacca liṅgaṃ karmavaśāttasyaiveti manyate /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.11.1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (section), the name '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) which is well-known in both contexts is harmonized. He presents the connection with <s>śruti</s> and other sources, along with the subject matter — with 'in the heart.' The <s>jyotis</s> (light) that is 'established' — placed — in the heart, denoted by that word, is the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self) — thus it has been stated in the <s>Jyotir-naya</s> (method of light) — this is the meaning. Then what? To this he says — 'there' means 'regarding the subject of light.' After the word 'iti,' the remainder is 'it is heard in scripture.' And what follows from that? To this he says — 'here' means 'in this passage.' It connects with 'the light that is heard.' And thus, the light heard here, denoted by that word, is understood to be the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) itself, whose nature is knowledge. Why? Because of the statement 'Being the same, he wanders through both worlds' — the construction is: from the remainder of the passage that states indicative marks pertaining to the <s>jīva</s>. By this, through the mode of objecting to the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood of the light mentioned in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> (scripture) passage 'the inner light in the heart,' since the previously stated reference is also objected to thereby, the connection through objection is stated. The light mentioned in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> is the subject, and the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) that this light is the <s>jīva</s> alone is indicated. For in the <s>Vājasaneya</s>, when <s>Yājñavalkya</s> was asked by <s>Janaka</s> about this <s>puruṣa</s> — 'What is his light?' meaning 'What is the means of knowledge for the <s>jīva</s>?' — he replied: 'The sun is his light, O sovereign' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.2), meaning 'O <s>Samrāṭ</s> (sovereign), King <s>Janaka</s> of universal sovereignty, this <s>puruṣa</s> has the sun as his means of knowledge.' In this manner, through questions and answers, having stated that in the waking state, among sun, moon, fire, and speech, when each preceding one sets, the next serves as light for the <s>jīva</s>, then again when asked by <s>Janaka</s> regarding sleep and dream states, when all four — sun and the rest — have set, 'What is the light of this <s>puruṣa</s>?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.2), <s>Yājñavalkya</s> replied 'The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) itself becomes his light,' stating that in both states the self-luminous <s>Paramātmā</s> is the light of the <s>jīva</s>. Then again, when asked 'Which <s>Ātman</s>?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.7) — meaning 'What kind is the <s>Ātman</s> spoken of as light?' — he replied with 'this one who,' meaning the <s>Paramātmā</s> who is distinct from the <s>jīva</s>, body, and sense organs. He who 'consists of <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge)' — who is full of knowledge — who exists among the '<s>prāṇas</s>' — the sense organs — as the inner controller within and in the heart, who is the '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) — the illuminator of the intellect and other faculties of the <s>jīva</s> — the '<s>puruṣa</s>' (person) — endowed with the complete six attributes. He is this <s>Ātman</s> — this is the meaning. He states His greatness — with 'He.' 'He' — the <s>Ātman</s>, the <s>Paramātmā</s> — being 'the same' — unchanging, always of one form — 'wanders through both worlds' — the earthly world and the heavenly world, or the waking and deep sleep states, taking each <s>jīva</s> along — this is the meaning. The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector), however, considers that the word '<s>Ātman</s>' and the word 'he' refer to the <s>jīva</s>, that the wandering through both worlds is meant as dependent on <s>karma</s> (action), and that this indicative mark belongs to the <s>jīva</s> alone who is subject to <s>karma</s>.

Therefore it is said —
<s>Sūtra</s>: Oṃ.
<s>Jyotis</s> (light) [refers to <s>Brahman</s>] because of being seen [so described in scripture]. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1,3.40 |

children.text:
'viṣṇureva jyotirviṣṇurevātmā viṣṇureva brahma viṣṇureva
balaṃ viṣṇureva yaśo viṣṇurevānandaḥ'; iti darśanāccaturvedaśikhāyām /
jyotirviṣṇureva /
children.translated_text:
'<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>jyotis</s> (light), <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>bala</s> (strength), <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>yaśas</s> (glory), <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss)' — because of such a declaration in the <s>Caturveda-śikhā</s>,
<s>jyotis</s> (light) is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.11.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya darśanapadoktaśrutyudāharaṇapūrvakaṃ vyācaṣṭe - ata iti / 'viṣṇureva jyotiḥ.... viṣṇurevānandaḥ'; iti caturvedaśikhāyāmiti 'darśanāt'; viṣṇureva mukhyato jyotiśśabdita iti uktatvāt 'jyotiḥ'; tacchabdavācyo viṣṇureva, na jīva ityarthaḥ / viṣṇurevetyanena tattvityanuvṛttasya arthaḥ uktaḥ / śrutyarthastu spaṣṭaḥ / viśeṣastu - balaṃ balapradaḥ / 'sa vai balaṃ balināṃ cāpareṣām'; iti ca bhāgavate / viṣṇureva yaśaḥ 'tasya nāma mahadyaśaḥ'; (mahānā.1.10.) iti śrutiriti tattvapradīpe abhihitam / brahmādiśabdavajjyotiśśabdo 'pi viṣṇvekaniṣṭha iti jñāpanāya samagravākyodāharaṇam / ata eva śrutāvevakāraḥ /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.11.2:
Having introduced the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>sūtra</s>, he explains it preceded by the citation of the <s>śruti</s> indicated by the word '<s>darśana</s>' (seeing/declaration) in the <s>sūtra</s> — with 'therefore.' Because in the <s>Caturveda-śikhā</s> it is 'declared' that '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>jyotis</s>... <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss),' meaning that <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is primarily denoted by the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light), [therefore] the '<s>jyotis</s>' denoted by that word is <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not the <s>jīva</s> — this is the meaning. By '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone,' the meaning of the resumed word 'tat' (that) is stated. The meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is clear. The specific points are: '<s>bala</s>' (strength) means the bestower of strength. As stated in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>: 'He indeed is the strength of the strong and of others.' '<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is <s>yaśas</s> (glory)' — the <s>śruti</s> declares 'His name is of great glory' (<s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s> 1.10) — thus it is stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>. The entire passage is cited to indicate that, like the words <s>Brahman</s> and others, the word <s>jyotis</s> also exclusively denotes <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone. Hence the use of 'eva' (alone) in the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: 'prājñenātmanā anvārūḍha utsarjadyāti'; (bṛ.6.3.35.) iti vacanāt tasyāpi lokasañcaraṇamastyeva // 40 //
children.translated_text: Because of the statement 'Mounted upon by the all-knowing <s>Ātman</s> (<s>Prājña</s>), he departs, releasing [the body]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.35), the wandering through worlds belongs to Him (<s>Paramātmā</s>) as well. // 40 //
// Thus ends the <s>Jyotir-adhikaraṇa</s> (Section on Light) // 11 //
// 12. <s>Ākāśa-adhikaraṇa</s> (Section on Space) //

children.text:
sarvādhāratvaṃ viṣṇoruktam / tacca 'ākāśo vai nāma
nāmarūpayornirvahitā'; (chāṃ.8.14.1.) ityatrākāśasya
pratīyate / vaināmeti prasiddhopadeśāt / prasiddhākāśaścāṅgīkartavya iti /
children.translated_text: The quality of being the support of all has been declared of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. And that is understood to belong to <s>ākāśa</s> (space) in the passage '<s>Ākāśa</s> (space) indeed is the name — it is the bearer of names and forms' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1). Since '<s>vai nāma</s>' indicates a well-known teaching, the well-known <s>ākāśa</s> (physical space) should be accepted — thus [the objection].

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.12.1:
atra ubhayatraprasiddhamākāśanāma brahmāṇi samanvīyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca darśayati - sarvādhāratvamiti / dyubhvādyadhikaraṇa iti śeṣaḥ / tataḥ kimityata āha - tacceti / co 'vadhāraṇe / 'ityatra'; ityevaṃrūpe chandogavākya ityarthaḥ / anenātratyākāśaśabdasya viṣṇvanyatvaparatvoktimukhena pūrvoktasarvādhāratvasyāpi anyaniṣṭhatvākṣepāttenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / chandogaśrutyukta ākāśākhyo viṣayaśca sūcitaḥ / sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣaṃ darśayati - vaināmeti // sa iti śeṣaḥ / co 'vadhāraṇe / tathā ca chandogyaśrutyuktaḥ ākāśaḥ prasiddhaḥ sākṣisiddhaḥ avyākṛtākāśa evāṅgīkāryaḥ / kutaḥ? ākāśapadena vaināmeti nipātadvayadyotitaprasiddhimadarthasyopadeśāt uktatvādityarthaḥ / kecittu - 'sattarkadīpāvalyāṃ prasiddho bhūtākāśa evāṅgīkāryaḥ'; iti vacanāt avakāśasyāpi nāmarūpavattvāditi candrikākṛdabhipretaṃ ṭīkāpāṭhamāśritya ākāśaśabdapravṛttinimittamavakāśatvaṃ bhūte niravadhikamiti sudhokteratrāvakāśaśabditaṃ bhūtameva pūrvapakṣaviṣayaityāhuḥ / śrutau vai nāmeti nipātadvayaṃ prasiddhau / 'nāma'; vācakaśabdaprapañcaḥ rūpapadena prākṛtarūpāntarbhāvitārthaprapañcamātramucyate / tathā ca ākāśo 'nāmarūpayoḥ'; śabdārthaprapañcayoḥ 'nirvahitā'; nirvoḍhā āśrayaḥ kartācetyarthaḥ / 'te'; nirvāhyatayā prakṛte nāmarūpe 'antarā'; bhedena / yaditi nāmarūpaprapañcādbhinnaṃ yadastīti yāvat / yadvā - tacchabdena vācyaprapañcāntarbhūtaṃ nīlādirūpaṃ vācakaṃ nāma ca gṛhyate/ tathā ca 'te'; nāmarūpe 'antarā'; vinā tadrahitamiti yāvat / sākalyena nāmavācyaṃ prākṛtarūparahitaṃ ca yadvartate tadbrahmetyarthaḥ / yadvā - 'te'; nāmirūpiṇām 'antarā'; bhedena yadastītyarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ tattvapradīpe - nāmi ca rūpi ca yannabhavati tadbrahmeti /
children.translated_text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.12.1:
Here, the name '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space), which is well-known in both senses, is harmonized with <s>Brahman</s>. He presents the connection with <s>śruti</s> and other sources, along with the subject matter — with 'the support of all.' The remainder is 'in the <s>Dyubhvādi-adhikaraṇa</s> (section on heaven and earth, etc.).' Then what? To this he says — 'and that.' The particle 'ca' is for emphasis. 'In this passage' means 'in the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage of this form.' By this, through the mode of stating that the word <s>ākāśa</s> here refers to something other than <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since the previously stated quality of being the support of all is also objected to as belonging to another, the connection through objection is stated. The subject, namely <s>ākāśa</s> as mentioned in the <s>Chāndogya</s> scripture, is also indicated. He presents the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) with reasoning — with '<s>vai nāma</s>.' The remainder is 'he' (referring to <s>ākāśa</s>). The particle 'ca' is for emphasis. And thus, the <s>ākāśa</s> mentioned in the <s>Chāndogya</s> scripture is the well-known, directly perceived, unmanifest physical space alone that should be accepted. Why? Because of the teaching of a meaning that possesses the well-known significance indicated by the two particles '<s>vai nāma</s>' — this is the meaning. Some, however, based on the statement in the <s>Sattarkadīpāvalī</s> that 'the well-known elemental <s>ākāśa</s> (physical space) should be accepted,' and since even spatial extension (<s>avakāśa</s>) possesses names and forms — relying on the reading preferred by the author of the <s>Candrikā</s> — say that since the defining characteristic of the word <s>ākāśa</s>, namely providing space (<s>avakāśatva</s>), applies unlimitedly to the physical element, as stated in the <s>Sudhā</s> commentary, the element denoted by '<s>avakāśa</s>' (space) is indeed the subject of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. In the <s>śruti</s>, the two particles '<s>vai nāma</s>' indicate well-knownness. '<s>Nāma</s>' (name) refers to the elaboration of designating words; by the word '<s>rūpa</s>' (form), only the elaboration of meaning including material forms and their subdivisions is expressed. And thus, <s>ākāśa</s> is the '<s>nirvahitā</s>' (bearer) — the sustainer, support, and creator — of 'names and forms' — of the elaboration of words and meanings. 'Those' — the names and forms presented as what is sustained — 'apart from' — as different from. 'That which' — that which exists as different from the elaboration of names and forms — this much is meant. Alternatively, by the word 'tat,' material form such as blue etc. which is included in the elaboration of denotable things, and the designating name, are grasped. And thus, 'those' — names and forms — 'apart from' — without, i.e., devoid of them; that which exists completely devoid of what is denoted by names and devoid of material form is <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. Alternatively, 'those' — 'apart from' those who possess names and forms — as different — 'that which' exists — this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s>: 'That which is neither a named thing nor a formed thing is <s>Brahman</s>.'

Therefore it is said —
<s>Sūtra</s>: Oṃ.
<s>Ākāśa</s> (space) [refers to <s>Brahman</s>] because of the designation as something different, and so on. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1,3.41 |
'That which is between those two is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1) — because of the designation as something different and so on, <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is <s>Hari</s> alone.

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.12.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti / ityarthāntaratvādivyapadeśāditi / sūtre bhāṣye ca padārthatvabodhāyārthaśabdaḥ / śrutyanusārādantaraśabdaḥ / tābhyāmiti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca tābhyāṃ nāmarūpābhyāṃ anyaḥ arthaḥ arthāntaraṃ yadvā tābhyāṃ vilakṣaṇaḥ arthaḥ arthāntaraḥ tasya bhāvastattvam / nāmarūpaprapañcabhinnatvaṃ vā prākṛtanāmarūparāhityaṃ vā / nāmarūparāhityākhyārthāntaratvavyapadeśādityarthaḥ / ādipadena brahmatvaṃ gṛhyate / yadvā - nirapekṣayoreva nāmarūparāhityayorākāśasya brahmatvasādhakatvāt arthāntarapadena rūparāhityaṃ ādipadena nāmarāhityaṃ ca gṛhyate/ tathā ca evaṃrūpārthāntaratvādyukterityarthaḥ / 'ākāśaḥ'; chāndogye śruto 'yamākāśastacchabdavācyaḥ / samanvayasūtrādanuvṛttasya tattvityasyārthamāha - harireveti // anena - ayamākāśo harireva / kutaḥ? asya arthāntaratvādivyapadeśāt 'te yadantarā'; iti nāmarūparāhityākhyavilakṣaṇārthatvokteḥ, brahmatvokteśceti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text: He introduces and explains the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) <s>sūtra</s> — 'ataḥ' (therefore). 'Because of the designation of being <s>arthāntara</s> (different in nature), etc.' — In both the <s>sūtra</s> and the <s>bhāṣya</s>, the word 'artha' is used to convey the sense of 'entity' (<s>padārthatva</s>). The word 'antara' (different) follows the <s>śruti</s>. 'By those two' is to be supplied. And thus, that which is different (arthāntara) from those two — <s>nāma</s> (name) and <s>rūpa</s> (form) — is a different entity; or alternatively, that which is distinct (<s>vilakṣaṇa</s>) from those two is arthāntara, and its state (<s>bhāva</s>) is its reality (<s>tattva</s>). This means either distinctness from the phenomenal expanse of name and form, or the absence of material name and form. The meaning is: because of the designation of being arthāntara, defined as the absence of name and form. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), <s>Brahma</s>-hood is indicated. Alternatively — since the absence of name and the absence of form independently establish the <s>Brahma</s>-hood of <s>ākāśa</s>, by the word 'arthāntara' the absence of form is indicated, and by the word 'ādi' the absence of name is indicated. And thus the meaning is: because of reasoning establishing such arthāntaratva (difference in nature), etc. '<s>Ākāśa</s>' — this <s>ākāśa</s> heard in the <s>Chāndogya</s> is denoted by that word (<s>tacchabda</s>). He states the meaning of 'tat' (that), which continues from the <s>samanvaya-sūtra</s> — '<s>Hari</s> alone.' By this, the <s>sūtra</s>'s meaning is stated thus: this <s>ākāśa</s> is <s>Hari</s> alone. Why? Because of the designation of its being arthāntara, etc. — because of the statement 'te yadantarā' (that which is between them) declaring its distinct nature as absence of name and form, and because of the declaration of <s>Brahma</s>-hood.

From <s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>avarṇam</s>' (without color/appearance) and 'yato vāco nivartante' (from which words turn back) (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.4), for that very characteristic belongs to Him alone.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.12.3:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.12.3:
ākāśe śrutena nāmarūpatvādiliṅgena kuto viṣṇutvaniścaya ityatastasya tanniṣṭhatvāditibhāvena tatra pramāṇatayā ātharvaṇīṃ śrutimāha - avarṇamiti / prākṛtaśuklādivarṇarahitaṃ tadbhinnaṃ vetyarthaḥ / yadvā avarṇaṃ na varṇyaṃ 'nāpivarṇātmakam'; ityarthaḥ 'yataḥ'; iti śrutiḥ / 'yato'; brahmaṇo 'vāco'; nāmāni 'nivartante'; ityanāmatvoktiparatayā vyākhyeyā / ādiśabdāt 'aśabdamasparśamarūpam'; (kaṭha. 1.3.15.) ityādiśrutirgṛhyate / ityādiśruterityasya tasya viṣṇoretadarūpatvādikaṃ lakṣaṇamasādhāraṇadharma iti jñāyate ityadhyāhāreṇānvayaḥ / hi yasmāttasmāt na liṅgasya vyadhikaraṇāsiddhiriti bhāvaḥ / tasyaivetyevakāreṇa vyabhicāraśaṅkāpi nirastā / yadyapi 'yataḥ'; ityanāmatvaśrutireva prathamamudāhartavyā, 'te yadantarā'; iti nāmarāhityasyaiva prathamamuktatvāt / na tu 'avarṇam'; ityarūpaśrutiḥ / tathāpi vācakasya nāmno vācyāpekṣayāprādhānyāt vācyasyaiva pradhānatvādvācyaprapañcāntargatarūparāhityaśrutireva prathamamudāhṛtetyadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the indicators heard in the context of <s>ākāśa</s>, such as being devoid of name and form, establish its <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood, the question arises: how is this certainty of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-hood established? To this, with the sense that those indicators are grounded in Him, he cites the <s>Ātharvaṇī śruti</s> as authoritative evidence — '<s>avarṇam</s>' (colorless). The meaning is: devoid of material colors such as white, etc., or different from them. Alternatively, '<s>avarṇam</s>' means 'not describable,' i.e., 'not constituted by syllables' — this is the meaning. The <s>śruti</s> 'yataḥ' (from which) — 'from <s>Brahman</s>, words (names) turn back' — should be interpreted as declaring His being beyond names (<s>anāmatva</s>). By the word 'ādi' (etc.), <s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>aśabdam asparśam arūpam</s>' (soundless, touchless, formless) (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.15) are included. The construction of 'from such <s>śrutis</s>' is completed by supplying: 'it is known that this characteristic — formlessness, etc. — is the distinguishing attribute (<s>asādhāraṇa dharma</s>) of that <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' The word 'hi' (for/because) conveys the sense: therefore there is no invalidity of the indicator through being in a different locus (<s>vyadhikaraṇa</s>). By the emphatic particle 'eva' in 'of that very one,' even the suspicion of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is dispelled. Although the <s>śruti</s> 'yataḥ' declaring namelessness should have been cited first, since the absence of name was mentioned first in 'te yadantarā,' rather than the <s>śruti</s> '<s>avarṇam</s>' declaring formlessness — nevertheless, since the denoting name is secondary compared to the denoted object, and since the denoted object is primary, there is no fault in citing first the <s>śruti</s> on formlessness, which falls within the scope of the denoted phenomenal world.

He is nameless (<s>anāmā</s>) because of being beyond ordinary knowledge (<s>aprasiddhatva</s>); He is formless (<s>arūpa</s>) because of being beyond material elements (<s>bhūtavarjana</s>) — thus it is stated in the <s>Brāhma</s> [Purāṇa]. // 41 //
// Thus ends the <s>Ākāśādhikaraṇa</s> // 12 //
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.12.4:

An objection arises: the absence of name and form cannot be established for <s>Hari</s>, since He is denoted by all words and since He possesses forms such as golden-hued (<s>rukmavarṇa</s>), etc. Otherwise, there would be a contradiction with what was previously stated in 'because of seeing (<s>īkṣateḥ</s>)' and 'because of the mention of form (<s>rūpopanyāsa</s>).' To this he responds — '<s>anāmā</s>' (nameless). '<s>Saḥ</s>' — <s>Hari</s>. 'Because of <s>aprasiddhatva</s>' (being beyond ordinary cognition) — because His own Self is not completely known through words and other means of knowledge by anyone other than Himself, He is called nameless — this is the meaning. And one should not object that there is a contradiction with the two particles indicating well-knownness in the case of the one denoted by the word <s>ākāśa</s>. For the well-knownness conveyed by the particles, being connected as a predicate with the subject in the manner of the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>'s interpretation, does not attach to <s>ākāśa</s> as the subject. And although the attribute of being the sustainer is not well-known in the world, it is well-known from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'eko dādhāra' (the One who sustains). And it is not prohibited by 'His being beyond cognition' (<s>aprasiddhatva</s>). 'Because of <s>bhūtavarjana</s>' (absence of material elements) — because of being devoid of a body made of material elements, or because of the absence of such material form, He is called formless — this is the meaning. The construction is completed by supplying: since this is stated in the <s>Brāhma</s> [Purāṇa], there is no contradiction with what was previously stated.
// Thus ends the <s>Ākāśādhikaraṇa</s> // 12 //
// 13. <s>Suṣuptyadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic on Deep Sleep) //

children.text: asaṅgatvaṃ paramātmana uktam / tacca 'sa yattatra kiñcitpaśyananvāgatastena bhavatyasaṅgo hyayaṃ puruṣaḥ'; (bṛ.6.3.15.) iti svapnādidraṣṭuḥ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: The non-attachment (<s>asaṅgatva</s>) of <s>Paramātman</s> has been stated. And that is understood from the passage about the seer in dreams, etc.: 'Whatever he sees there, he is not followed by it, for this <s>Puruṣa</s> is unattached (<s>asaṅga</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.15).
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.13.1:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.13.1:
atrādhikaraṇe svapnādidraṣṭṛtvaliṅgaṃ brahmaṇi samanvīyate / śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca sūcayati - asaṅgatvamiti / akṣaranayodāhṛte 'agandhamarasam'; iti vājasaneyavākye paramātmano asaṅgatvamuktamityarthaḥ /
tataḥ kimityata āha - tacceti / co 'vadhāraṇe / itīti evaṃrūpe vājasaneyavākya ityarthaḥ / anena svāpnādidraṣṭṛttvasya anyaniṣṭhatvākṣepamukhena pūrvoktāsaṅgatvasyāpyanyaniṣṭhatvākṣepāt, akṣaranayenāsya ākṣepikī saṅgatissūcitā/ svapnādidraṣṭṛtvākhyo viṣayaśca sūcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the indicator of being the seer in dreams, etc. is shown to be harmonized with <s>Brahman</s>. He indicates the connection with <s>śruti</s>, etc., and the subject matter — '<s>asaṅgatvam</s>' (non-attachment). The meaning is: in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> passage 'without smell, without taste (<s>agandham arasam</s>),' which was cited in the <s>Akṣara</s> section, the non-attachment of <s>Paramātman</s> is stated. To the question 'what follows from that?' he says — 'tacca' (and that). The particle 'ca' is used in the sense of emphasis (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>). 'Iti' means: in the <s>Vājasaneya</s> passage of such form — this is the meaning. By this, through the mode of objecting that the quality of being seer in dreams, etc. belongs to another entity, the previously stated non-attachment is also objected to as belonging to another entity, and thus the connection with the <s>Akṣara</s> section as one of challenge (<s>ākṣepikī saṅgati</s>) is indicated. And the subject matter, namely the quality of being the seer in dreams etc., is also indicated.
And that [seer] is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), because of well-known usage.
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.13.2:

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.13.2:
tataḥ kimityataḥ sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣayati - sa ceti / co 'vadhāraṇe / 'saḥ'; svapnādidraṣṭā / jīva eva bhavet / kutaḥ taddraṣṭṛtvasya loke jīva eva prasiddhatvādityarthaḥ / siddhānte śrutau 'saḥ'; iti tacchabdena 'sa vā eṣa etasmin samprasāde ratvā caritvā dṛṣṭvaiva puṇyaṃ ca pāpaṃ ca punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ prati yonyā dravati svapnāyaiva'; (bṛ. 6.3.15.) iti pūrvavākye prakṛtaḥ paramātmā parāmṛśyate / vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / samyakprasīdati jīvo 'syāmiti samprasādaḥ suptiḥ / tathā ca sa paramātmā 'samprasāde'; suptau 'ratvā'; ramaṇaṃ kṛtvā jīvagataṃ puṇyaṃ ca pāpaṃ ca dṛṣṭvaiva na tvanubhūya 'caritvā'; sañcaritvā 'pratinyāyam'; avasthāntaraṃ pravartanīyamiti nyāyamanusṛtya yadvā tattatkarmanusṛtya 'pratiyoni'; pratidehaṃ sarvadeheṣu yadvā pratiyoni tattanmārgamanusṛtya 'punaḥ'; 'svāpnāyaiva'; jīvasya svapnaprāptaye eva 'ādravati'; kaṇṭhadeśamāgacchati / 'saḥ'; paramātmā 'tatra'; svāpnāvasthāyāṃ yatkiñcidaniṣṭaṃ paśyati 'tena'; tatkṛtapāpaphalena duḥkhena 'ananvāgataḥ'; asaṃspṛṣṭo bhavati / tatra hetuḥ - asaṅga iti / hi yasmādayaṃ puruṣaḥ 'asaṅgaḥ'; tatkṛtapāpaphalasaṃsargaśūnyaḥ pramitaḥ, tasmādityarthaḥ / pūrvapakṣī tu śrautatacchabdena jīvaṃ gṛhītvā sarvaṃ vākyaṃ jīvaparatayā vyākhyāti /
children.translated_text: To the question 'what follows from that?' he presents the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie view) with reasoning — 'sa ca' (and that). The particle 'ca' is in the sense of emphasis. '<s>Saḥ</s>' — the seer in dreams, etc. He would be the <s>jīva</s> alone. Why? Because being the seer of dreams is well-known in the world as belonging to the <s>jīva</s> alone — this is the meaning. In the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), in the <s>śruti</s>, by the word 'saḥ' (he) — that <s>tacchabda</s> (the pronoun 'that') — refers back to <s>Paramātman</s> who is the subject of the preceding passage: 'He, having enjoyed himself in that state of deep sleep, having moved about and having seen good and evil, returns again along the same course, along the same path, to the state of dreams' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.15). The particle 'vai' indicates well-knownness. '<s>Samprasāda</s>' (deep sleep) means: the state in which the <s>jīva</s> becomes fully serene (<s>samyak prasīdati</s>), i.e., <s>supti</s> (sleep). And thus that <s>Paramātman</s>, in the state of deep sleep (<s>samprasāda</s>), 'having enjoyed' — having performed the act of enjoyment, 'having seen' the merit and demerit belonging to the <s>jīva</s> — but not having experienced them Himself — 'having moved about,' 'according to the rule' — following the principle by which transition to another state is to be effected, or alternatively, following the respective <s>karmas</s>, '<s>pratiyoni</s>' — toward each body, in all bodies, or alternatively, following the respective paths of each destination, 'again,' 'for the dream state alone' — for the <s>jīva</s>'s attainment of the dream state, 'rushes' — arrives at the throat region. '<s>Saḥ</s>' — that <s>Paramātman</s>, 'there' — in the dream state, whatever unpleasant thing He sees, 'by that' — by the suffering that is the fruit of the sin committed, 'is not followed' — is untouched. The reason for this is: '<s>asaṅga</s>' (unattached). 'Hi' (for) — because this <s>Puruṣa</s> is known to be '<s>asaṅga</s>' — devoid of contact with the fruits of sins committed, therefore — this is the meaning. The <s>pūrvapakṣin</s>, however, takes the pronoun 'saḥ' in the <s>śruti</s> as referring to the <s>jīva</s> and interprets the entire passage as pertaining to the <s>jīva</s>.

Therefore he states —
<s>Sūtra</s> — Om //
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.13.3:
Because of the distinction [stated] in deep sleep and departure. | <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.42 |

'Embraced by the omniscient Self (<s>prājñena ātmanā</s>), he knows nothing external nor internal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.21); 'Mounted upon by the omniscient Self, he departs, releasing [the body]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.35) — because of the designation of distinction (<s>bheda</s>) [between the two], it is not the <s>jīva</s> [who is the unattached seer]; it is the Supreme (<s>para</s>) alone who is unattached (<s>asaṅga</s>). // 42 //

children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.13.3:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārya vyācaṣṭe - ata iti / 'vakti'; samādhatte / svapnādidraṣṭṛtvaṃ tasyaivetyatrāpi sambadhyate / tena sūtre uddeśyavidheyapratipattyartham anuvṛttāvṛttasya tacchabdasya vipariṇāmassūcitaḥ / tacchabdena gṛhītasyāpi samanvetavyaliṅgasya spaṣṭapratipattyarthaṃ svaśabdena nirdeśaḥ / itiśabdānantaraṃ suṣuptīti sautrapadaṃ saṃyojyam / vyapadeśāditi buddhyā vivicya pūrvasmādanuṣaktaṃ padam / asaṅga ityapi hetusūcanāya sūtre adhyāhṛtaṃ padam / jīvaḥ para ityanena suṣuptyutkrāntipadaṃ tatprakaraṇalakṣakamapi jīvaparamātmaparamapītyuktaṃ bhavati / tathātve suṣuptiśabdaḥ kartari ktinnantaḥ / utkrāntiśabdaḥ dehādutkrāmayitṛparaḥ tathā cetthaṃ yojanā - svapnādidraṣṭṛtvaṃ tasya paramātmana eva bhavet na jīvasya / kutaḥ? yato 'sāvasaṅgaḥ śrutaḥ / na ca svapnādidraṣṭuḥ asaṅgatvaśravaṇe 'pi kuto 'yaṃ viṣṇuriti vācyam / yato 'yamasaṅgaḥ karmābaddhatvāt paraḥ paramātmaiva na jīvaḥ / tathā ca liṅgasya niravakāśatvāt nāprayojakatvaṃ śaṅkyamiti bhāvaḥ / na ca jīve 'pir iśvarabhedena asaṅgatvoktiḥ sambhavatīti vācyam / prājñenetyādisuṣuptyutkrāntiprakaraṇadvayagatavākyayorasaṅgātsvapnādidraṣṭurḥ iśvarājjīvasya bhedavyapadeśāditi/ prājñeneti śrutyudāharaṇena sūtre suṣuptipadaṃ mokṣasyāpi grāhakaṃ, tenāyaṃ bhedo vyāvahārika iti śaṅkānirāso 'pi bhavati/ suṣuptyutkrāntipadena ca tatprakaraṇaṃ lakṣyata ityuktaṃ bhavati / utkrāntipadaṃ ca jīvasya dehādutkramaṇarūpamaraṇavāci / śrutau prājñaśabdaḥ svārthikāṇantaḥ / tathā ca 'prājñena'; sarvajñena paramātmanā 'sampariṣvaktaḥ'; samāśliṣṭaḥ supto muktaśca dehādbāhyamāntaraṃ ca kiñcana viṣayādikaṃ na vedeti prathamavākyārthaḥ / dvitīyārthastu - prāktanādhikaraṇe 'bhihitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He introduces and explains the <s>siddhānta sūtra</s> — 'ataḥ' (therefore). '<s>Vakti</s>' means: he reconciles (<s>samādhatte</s>). The phrase 'the quality of being seer in dreams, etc. belongs to Him alone' also connects here. Thus, for the purpose of understanding the subject and predicate in the <s>sūtra</s>, the reversal of the pronoun 'tat' — whether carried over or newly introduced — is indicated. Even though the indicator to be harmonized has been grasped by the pronoun 'tat,' for clear understanding it is designated by its own word (<s>svaśabda</s>). After the word 'iti,' the <s>sūtra</s>-word '<s>suṣupti</s>' (deep sleep) should be connected. The word '<s>vyapadeśāt</s>' (because of designation) is a term carried over from the previous [<s>sūtra</s>], to be intellectually discerned. The word '<s>asaṅga</s>' (unattached) is also a term to be supplied in the <s>sūtra</s> for indicating the reason. By the words '<s>jīva</s>' and '<s>para</s>' (supreme), it is stated that the word '<s>suṣuptyutkrānti</s>' (deep sleep and departure), though primarily indicating those topics, also pertains to the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Paramātman</s>. In that case, the word '<s>suṣupti</s>' has a <s>ktin</s>-suffix in the agent sense. The word '<s>utkrānti</s>' means 'the one who causes departure from the body.' And thus the construction is: the quality of being the seer in dreams, etc. belongs to that <s>Paramātman</s> alone, not to the <s>jīva</s>. Why? Because He is heard as unattached (<s>asaṅga</s>). And even though non-attachment is heard of the seer in dreams, one should not ask 'why must this be <s>Viṣṇu</s>?' — because this unattached one, being unbound by <s>karma</s>, is the Supreme (<s>para</s>), <s>Paramātman</s> alone, not the <s>jīva</s>. And thus, since the indicator has no other possible locus (<s>niravakāśatva</s>), one cannot suspect it of being purposeless — this is the purport. Nor should one say that non-attachment can be stated of the <s>jīva</s> as well, as distinct from <s>Īśvara</s>. For in the two passages occurring in the contexts of deep sleep and departure beginning with '<s>prājñena</s>' (by the omniscient), because of the designation of the distinction of the <s>jīva</s> from <s>Īśvara</s> as the unattached seer in dreams, etc. By citing the <s>śruti</s> '<s>prājñena</s>,' the word '<s>suṣupti</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> is shown to also encompass <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), and thereby the objection that this distinction is merely empirical (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) is also refuted. And by the word '<s>suṣuptyutkrānti</s>,' the relevant scriptural context is indicated — this is what is stated. The word '<s>utkrānti</s>' refers to death, i.e., the departure of the <s>jīva</s> from the body. In the <s>śruti</s>, the word '<s>prājña</s>' has the <s>svārthika aṇ</s>-suffix (retaining its own meaning). And thus the meaning of the first passage is: 'Embraced by the omniscient (<s>prājña</s>) <s>Paramātman</s>, the sleeping one or the liberated one knows nothing external or internal — no objects, etc.' The meaning of the second passage was explained in the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s>.
And the quality of being the seer in dreams, etc. is appropriate for Him alone, because of His omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>). // 42 //
// Thus ends the <s>Suṣuptyadhikaraṇa</s> // 13 //
<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.13.4:

<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.13, verse 4:
But how can the seeing of dreams and so forth be appropriate for one who is bodiless? To this he says — 'dreams and so forth.' The particle 'ca' is used in the sense of conjunction, or in the sense of 'also.' By the word 'ādi' (etc.), the states pertaining to the <s>jīva</s> are included. And thus, not only is freedom from attachment (<s>asaṅgatva</s>) appropriate for the Supreme alone — because of being unbound by <s>karma</s> — but also the being-the-seer of dreams and so forth belongs 'to Him alone'; it is more properly applicable to <s>Paramātman</s> alone than even to the <s>jīva</s>. Therefore, such statement is appropriate only of Him, not of the <s>jīva</s>. Why? Because 'of His alone' being 'omniscient' (<s>sarvajñatva</s>); the meaning is: because of His true knowledge of all objects, since the reality of dream-objects and of the states pertaining to the <s>jīva</s> will be stated [hereafter]. Nor is the indicatory mark of bodilessness an obstacle, because here the being-the-seer of dreams and so forth is stated of Him alone who has consciousness as His body. Nor should it be objected that [the text] 'having seen both merit and sin' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.3.15) and so forth would not apply; because here the being-the-seer of merit, sin, and so forth — included by the word 'ādi' — and also other indicatory marks, are appropriate for Him alone. This is the interpretation. The reasoning for this should be understood from the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> (the main commentary on <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>). By this — [the sūtra] 'in deep sleep and departure' [and] 'by the wise one' (<s>prājñena</s>) — in the sections dealing with deep sleep and departure: because of being connected with deep sleep, deep sleep pertains to the <s>jīva</s>; because of being the cause of departure, departure pertains to <s>Īśvara</s>; and thus the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> are spoken of 'with distinction,' that is, as being different — since this has been stated, there is no non-difference between them. Therefore, even by non-difference from <s>Īśvara</s>, the statement of freedom from attachment cannot apply to the <s>jīva</s>. Rather, that belongs to Him alone, to <s>Īśvara</s> alone. For this very reason, the being-the-seer of dreams and so forth is appropriate to state of Him alone, not of the <s>jīva</s> — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated.
// Thus ends the <s>Suṣuptyadhikaraṇa</s> (topic on deep sleep). // 13 //
// 14. <s>Brāhmaṇādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, i.e. <s>Brahman</s>). //

children.translated_text: 'This is the eternal greatness of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.22) — thus eternal greatness is understood to belong also to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. And that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, from the word '<s>aja</s>' (unborn) in 'He indeed is this great, unborn Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.24), is prima facie concluded to be <s>Viriñca</s> (four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>). And [in the sūtra] 'above that also,' the attainment of a station through knowledge and ritual action by the gods has been indicated.
