children.text:
BBsBhDīp_1,3.14.1:
atrādhikaraṇe brāhmaṇanāma samanvīyate/ śrutyādisaṅgatiṃ viṣayādikaṃ ca sūcayati - eṣa iti / itīti/ vājasaneyakodāhṛtaṛṅmantra ityarthaḥ / na kevalaṃ viṣṇoḥ api tu kasyacit brāhmaṇasyāpītyaperarthaḥ / idaṃ ca yo janmādyadhikaraṇeṣu viṣṇorananyāpekṣayā jagatsraṣṭṛtvoktyā abhisaṃhito nityamahimā saḥ 'eṣaḥ'; iti vākye brāhmaṇasyāpi pratīyata iti yattacchabdādhyāhāreṇa yojyam / anena pūrvābhisaṃhitanityamahimatvasya viṣṇoranyasyāpyākṣepāt janmādyadhikaraṇaiḥ phalamukhena asyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā bhavati / tathā brāhmaṇākhyaviṣayo 'pi sūcitaḥ / yadvā - devānāmiti vākyaṃ devatādhikaraṇapratipādyānuvādaparatvenāpi vyākhyāya tenāsyākṣepikī saṅgatiruktā draṣṭavyā / tathā hi 'tadupari'; iti sūtreṇa devānāṃ viriñcādyamarāṇāṃ vidyākarmaṇossakāśāt sādhyā yā nityapadaprāptiruktā, sā na yuktā / kutaḥ? yataḥ 'eṣaḥ'; iti vākye brāhmaṇapadoditasya viriñcasya nityamahimā 'pratīyate'; pratipādyata iti vākyayojanā / śrutau brahmaṇā vedenāṇyate 'vagamyate iti vyutpattiḥ / dīrghavyatyāso viṣṇorvedagamyatve jīvādādhikyajñāpakaḥ / tathā ca brāhmaṇasya viṣṇoreṣaḥ pūrvoktamahimā nityaḥ / kuto? yato 'yaṃ 'na karmaṇā vardhate no kanīyān'; (bṛ.6.4.22.) śubhakarmaṇā tatphalena sukhena na vardhate / pāpakarmaṇā tatphalena duḥkhena na hrasate iti śrutyarthaḥ / sayuktikaṃ pūrvapakṣayati - sa iti / vājasaneyaśruta ityarthaḥ / caśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / viriñca eveti sambadhyate / ityajaśabdāditi / ityevaṃ rūpeṣu pūrvottaravākyeṣu śrutājaśabdādityarthaḥ / 'sa eṣaḥ'; paramātmā 'mahān'; aparimitaḥ 'ajo'; janmarahitaśceti śrutyarthaḥ / pūrvapakṣī tu brāhmaṇājaśabdavācyaṃ viriñciṃ manyate / nanu kathaṃ brāhmaṇo viriñco bhavet / taduparīti sūtre devānāṃ vidyākarmabhyāṃ padaprāpteḥ samarthitatvena brāhmaṇe śrutanityamahimatvasya viriñce asambhavāt / sādipadasyānityatvaniyamāt ityata āha - devānāṃ ceti / co 'vadhāraṇe / itītyanantaraṃ sūtra iti śeṣaḥ / tathā ca taduparīti sūtre viriñcetaradevānāmeva vidyākarmaṇoḥ sakāśāt padaprāptiḥ 'sūcitā'; samarthitā / na tu viriñcasyāpi / tasyeśvararūpatvena devakoṭyapraviṣṭatvādato viriñcasya nityamahimattvaṃ yuktameveti yojanā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.14, verse 1:
In this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the word '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' is interpreted. He indicates the coherence from scripture and so forth, the subject matter, and so on — 'This.' The word 'iti' means: this is a <s>Ṛg</s>-verse cited in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>. 'Api' (also) means: not only of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but also of some <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. And this should be construed by supplying 'that': the eternal greatness that was intended as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s> through the statement of His being the creator of the universe without dependence on anything else in the <s>Janmādyadhikaraṇa</s> and other topics — 'this' same greatness is now understood in the [scriptural] sentence as belonging also to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. By this, since the eternal greatness previously intended for <s>Viṣṇu</s> is now challenged as applying to another as well, the connection [of this topic] with the <s>Janmādyadhikaraṇa</s> and other topics through the mode of result-based challenge has been stated. Likewise, the subject matter — one called '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — has also been indicated. Alternatively, the sentence 'of the gods' may be explained as a restatement of what was established in the <s>Devatādhikaraṇa</s>, and by that, the challenge-based connection of this topic should be seen. For indeed, by the <s>sūtra</s> 'above that,' the attainment of an eternal station achieved through knowledge and ritual action by the gods — namely <s>Viriñca</s> and other immortals — was stated, but that is not proper. Why? Because in 'this' sentence, eternal greatness is 'understood' — that is, taught — of <s>Viriñca</s> who is denoted by the word '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' This is the syntactical construal of the sentence. In <s>śruti</s>, the etymology is: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' means one who is known (<s>aṇyate</s>) through <s>Brahman</s>, i.e. the <s>Veda</s>. The lengthening [of the vowel] indicates the superiority of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s knowability through the <s>Veda</s> over that of the <s>jīva</s> and others. And thus, this previously mentioned greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is eternal. Why? Because this one 'does not increase by good action, nor does He become less' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.4.22) — He does not increase by auspicious <s>karma</s> or the happiness that is its fruit; He does not diminish by sinful <s>karma</s> or the suffering that is its fruit — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. He presents the prima facie view with reasoning — 'He.' The meaning is: as heard in the <s>Vājasaneya</s>. The particle 'ca' is used in the sense of emphasis and is connected with '<s>Viriñca</s> alone.' 'From the word <s>aja</s>' means: from the word '<s>aja</s>' heard in such preceding and following sentences. 'He, this' <s>Paramātman</s> is 'great,' unlimited, and '<s>aja</s>,' devoid of birth — this is the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>. But the <s>pūrvapakṣin</s> (objector) considers the one denoted by the words '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' and '<s>aja</s>' to be <s>Viriñca</s>. But how could the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> be <s>Viriñca</s>? Since in the <s>sūtra</s> 'above that,' the attainment of a station by the gods through knowledge and ritual action has been established, the eternal greatness heard in [the passage about] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is impossible for <s>Viriñca</s>, because one who has a beginning is necessarily non-eternal. To this he says — 'of the gods, and.' The particle 'ca' is used in the sense of emphasis. After 'iti,' the word '<s>sūtra</s>' is to be supplied. And thus, in the <s>sūtra</s> 'above that,' the attainment of a station through knowledge and ritual action is 'indicated' — established — only for gods other than <s>Viriñca</s>, not for <s>Viriñca</s> himself; because he, being of the nature of <s>Īśvara</s>, does not fall within the category of [ordinary] gods. Therefore, eternal greatness is indeed proper for <s>Viriñca</s> — this is the construal.

Therefore he [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>] says —
<s>Sūtra</s> — <s>Oṃ</s> //
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.14, verse 2:]

BBsBhDīp_1,3.14.2:
siddhāntayatsūtramavatārayati - ata iti / vājasaneyake sarvavaśitvavāciśabdasyaivāditvātsūtrasya tadvisaṃvādamāśaṅkya tatparihārāya sūtrānukūlatayā sadṛśaśākhāntaragatavākyodāharaṇapūrvakaṃ sūtraṃ vyācaṣṭe - sarvasyeti / 'sarvasya'; brahmarudrādeḥ sakāśāt guṇairadhikaścāsau sarvasya patiḥ pālakaśceti sarvādhipatiḥ / 'sarvasya'; jagatarḥ 'iśānāṃ'; brahmādīnāṃ anaḥ preraka iti sarvasyeśāna iti śrutyantarārthaḥ / sarvavaśiśabdārthastu sarvamasya vaśe yasmāddhariḥ sarvavaśī tata iti bṛhadbhāṣyādavagantavyaḥ / 'sa vā eṣaḥ'; iti vājasaneyaśrutiḥ / 'saḥ'; prāṇaśabdoktaḥ 'eṣaḥ'; samānaśabdābhidheyaḥ 'ātmā'; paramātmā 'iti na'; dṛṣṭavanna 'iti na'; śrutavanna, kintu dṛṣṭaśrutavilakṣaṇa ityarthaḥ / vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhau / kuta ityataḥ 'ātmāgṛhyo na hi gṛhyate 'śīryo na hi śīryate 'saṅgo na hi sajjate 'sito na vyathate na riṣyati.........sa eṣa ātmājaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayaḥ'; (bṛ. 2.4.24.) iti vākyaśeṣaḥ pravṛttaḥ / atrāgṛhya ityādirātmana iti netyuktārthe sākalyena agrāhyatvādirūpahetusamarpakaḥ / na hītyādistu tatra pramāṇābhāvāditi hetusūcakaḥ / yadyapi bṛhadbhāṣye 'itina'; ramāvanna 'itina'; brahmādivanna, baddhavanna, muktavannetyanyathā vyākhyātam / tathāpyatra 'sa yo 'to 'śrutaḥ'; (ai.ā. 3.2.4.) iti samākhyāśrutyanusārādevaṃ vyākhyātamityadoṣaḥ / ityādīti / ityādau śrutāḥ ye sarvādhipatyādivācakāḥ śabdāḥ tebhya ityarthaḥ / ādipadātsarvavaśitvādivāciśabdasaṅgrahaḥ / anena sautrādiśabdo na kevalaṃ śākhāntaroktasarveśānādiśabdagrāhakaḥ, kintu vājasaneyoktasarvavilakṣamatvasarvavaśitvādiśabdagrāhako 'pīti uktaṃ bhavati / evaṃ hetuṃ vyākhyāya sūtre samanvayasūtrāt tattvityanuvartya vipariṇamyamānena tadityanenānvayayogyamuddeśyasamarpakaṃ nityamahimeti padaṃ cādhyāhṛtyāhatya niṣkṛṣṭāṃ pratijñāṃ darśayati - nityamahimeti / idaṃ ca phalakathanarūpam / śabdebhya iti hetvanvayayogyaṃ sādhyaṃ tu brāhmaṇa ityadhyāhṛtaṃ draṣṭavyam / anena - ayaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ tattu viṣṇureva, na viriñcaḥ / kutaḥ? 'patyādiśabdebhyaḥ'; sarvādhipatyādivācisarvādhipatyādiśabdebhyo 'tra śrutebhyaḥ / tathā ca nityamahimāpi sa eveti sūtrārtha ukto bhavati /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.14, verse 2:
He introduces the <s>sūtra</s> that establishes the <s>siddhānta</s> (conclusion) — 'Therefore.' Since in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>, the word denoting lordship over all comes first, anticipating a possible contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>, he explains the <s>sūtra</s> in agreement with it by first citing a passage from a similar branch of scripture — 'Of all.' '[Lord] of all' — one who is superior in qualities to all, including <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others, and who is the protector (<s>pati</s>) of all — thus '<s>sarvādhipati</s>' (lord of all). 'Ruler of all' — the meaning from another <s>śruti</s> is: the impeller (<s>anaḥ</s>, i.e. <s>preraka</s>) of the rulers (<s>īśāna</s>) of all, including <s>Brahmā</s> and others, over the entire universe. But the meaning of the word '<s>sarvavaśin</s>' (one who has all under His control) is: since everything is under His control, <s>Hari</s> is the controller of all — this should be understood from the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s>. 'He indeed is this' — this is a <s>Vājasaneya śruti</s>. 'He' — the one spoken of by the word <s>prāṇa</s>; 'this' — the one denoted by the word 'samāna' (equal/same); 'Self' — the Supreme Self. 'Not this' — not like anything seen; 'not this' — not like anything heard; rather, He is distinct from everything seen and heard — this is the meaning. The particle 'vai' is used in the sense of well-known. From where [is this known]? 'The Self that is ungraspable — for He cannot be grasped; indestructible — for He cannot be destroyed; unattached — for He does not attach; unfettered — He does not suffer, He is not injured... He indeed is the Self — ageless, immortal, deathless, fearless' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.24) — thus the remainder of the passage proceeds. Here, 'ungraspable' and so forth present reasons in their totality for what was stated as '<s>neti</s>' — namely, that He is completely ungraspable and so forth in nature. And 'for He cannot be' and so forth indicates the reason: because there is no means of proof [to apprehend Him thus]. Although in the <s>Bṛhadbhāṣya</s> it is explained differently — 'not this' means not like <s>Ramā</s> (not this); 'not this' means not like <s>Brahmā</s> and others; not like a bound soul; not like a liberated soul — nevertheless, here it is explained thus following the <s>śruti</s> of the <s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 'He who is beyond what is heard' (3.2.4), which provides a designation — this is not a fault. 'From such words as these' — the meaning is: from words that denote lordship over all and so forth, which are heard in these and similar [passages]. By the word 'ādi,' words denoting being the controller of all and so forth are included. By this, it is stated that the word 'ādi' in the <s>sūtra</s> is not merely a reference to words like '<s>sarveśāna</s>' (lord of all) found in other branches, but also comprehends words denoting complete distinctness from everything and control over everything found in the <s>Vājasaneya</s>. Having thus explained the reason, he shows the extracted thesis by carrying forward 'tat' (that) from the <s>samanvaya sūtra</s>, modifying it with 'tad' (that), supplying the statement-qualifying subject 'of eternal greatness,' and presenting [the conclusion] — 'Of eternal greatness.' And this is in the form of stating the result. The word 'from words' is the reason-qualifier, while '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — the object to be proved — should be understood as supplied. By this [the meaning is]: this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not <s>Viriñca</s>. Why? 'From words such as <s>pati</s> (lord) and so forth' — from words denoting lordship over all and so forth, which are heard here. And thus, the one of eternal greatness is also He alone — thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> has been stated.
'And the lord of immortality, who grows through food' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12.)
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.14, verse 3:]

BBsBhDīp_1,3.14.3:
nanu sarvādhipatyādivāciśabdasadbhāve 'pi kuto brāhmaṇasya viṣṇutvaniścaya ityaprayojakatavaśaṅkāvāraṇāya tatra sarvādhipitvasya viṣṇvekaniṣṭhatve tāvacchrutimāha - uteti / idaṃ ca 'puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam'; / 'yadbhūtaṃ yacca bhavyam'; iti pūrvavākyena saha vyākhyeyam / tatprakārastu - 'yadbhūtam'; atītaṃ 'bhavyaṃ'; bhaviṣyat vartamānaṃ ca tatsarvaṃ 'puruṣa eva'; paramapuruṣādhīnameva / kutaḥ? yato yasmāt na kevalamamuktasarvādhipatiḥ puruṣaḥ, kintu 'amṛtatvasyota'; muktasamudāyasyāpir 'iśānaḥ'; adhipatiḥ / 'vicitrā hi taddhitagatiḥ'; iti vacanātsamudāyārthe tvapratyayaḥ / tattvapradīpe tu - bhāvabhavitrorabhedavyapadeśāt bhāve tvapratyayaḥ / 'amṛtatvasya'; mokṣasyar iśāna iti ceti arthāntaraṃ coktam / atra hetumāha - yaditi / tṛtīyā dvitīyārthe / tathā ca 'yat'; yasmāt 'annena'; annaṃ martyaṃ saṃsārisamūham 'atirohati'; atiśete, tasmādityarthaḥ / muktāvanadhīnatve sarvajñasya buddhimataḥ svādhīnasaṃsāribhyo mokṣapradānāyogāditi bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.14, verse 3:
But even if words denoting lordship over all are present, how is there certainty that the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s>? To remove this doubt of purposelessness, he cites a <s>śruti</s> regarding the exclusive applicability of lordship over all to <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone — 'And the lord of.' This should be explained together with the preceding passage: '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this,' 'whatever has been and whatever will be.' The exposition is as follows: 'What has been' — the past; 'what will be' — the future; and the present — all this is 'of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone,' dependent on the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> alone. Why? Because <s>Puruṣa</s> is not merely the lord of all who are unliberated, but 'also (<s>uta</s>) the lord (<s>īśāna</s>) of immortality' — that is, lord even of the aggregate of the liberated. [The suffix <s>tva</s> is used in the sense of] collectivity, by the statement 'For the derivation of <s>taddhita</s> suffixes is varied.' But in the <s>Tattvapradīpa</s> it is said: because of non-distinction between the state and the one in that state, the <s>tva</s>-suffix is used in the sense of the state; and '<s>amṛtatva</s>' means lordship over <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) as well — this is another interpretation stated. Here he states the reason — 'who.' The instrumental case is used in the sense of the accusative. And thus, 'because' (<s>yat</s>) He 'surpasses through food' — '<s>anna</s>' means the mortal, the aggregate of beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> — He 'surpasses,' excels beyond them; therefore [He is the lord of immortality]. The purport is: if He were not the lord over the liberated as well, then for the omniscient and wise one, there would be no possibility of granting liberation to the beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> who are under His control.
[<s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya</s> 1.3.14, verse 4:]

BBsBhDīp_1,3.14.4:
idānīṃ sarvaśabdasambandhikeśānapadoktasarvaprerakatve śrutimāha - sapteti / akṣaranaye vyākhyāteyaṃ śrutiḥ / neti netītyuktadṛṣṭaśrutasarvavilakṣaṇatve 'pi śrutimudāharati - sa iti / iyamapi sarvatrādhikaraṇe vyākhyātā / ityādītyādipadena sarvavaśitvādāvapyevameva śrutyantarāmyudāhartavyānīti sūcayati / 'tasyaiva'; viṣṇoreva nānyasyetyevārthaḥ / 'hi'; yasmātte sarvādhipatyādiśabdāḥ ityavagatāḥ tasmāt nāprayojakatvaṃ śaṅkyamiti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Bhāṣyadīpikā</s> on 1.3.14, verse 4:
Now, he cites a <s>śruti</s> for the fact that [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] is the impeller of all, as stated by the word '<s>īśāna</s>' (ruler) which is connected with [the word] 'all' — 'Seven.' This <s>śruti</s> has been explained in the <s>Akṣaranaya</s> [section]. Regarding the complete distinctness from everything seen and heard as stated by '<s>neti neti</s>,' he cites a <s>śruti</s> — 'He.' This too has been explained in the <s>Sarvatrādhikaraṇa</s>. By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), he indicates that for [establishing] control over all and so forth as well, <s>śrutis</s> from other [branches] should similarly be cited. 'Of Him alone' — of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone, not of anyone else — this is the meaning of 'eva.' 'Hi' (for) — because those words denoting lordship over all and so forth have been ascertained [to refer to <s>Viṣṇu</s>], therefore the doubt of purposelessness should not be entertained — this is the remainder of the sentence.
// Thus ends the <s>Brāhmaṇādhikaraṇa</s> (topic on the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>). // 14 //

children.text:
iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryāṇāṃ sarvatantrasvatantrāṇāṃ
śrīmadraghunāthatīrthapūjyapādānāṃ śiṣyeṇa śrīmajjagannāthayatinā kṛtāyāṃ
śrīmadbrahmasūtrabhāṣyadīpikāyāṃ
prathamādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the <s>Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya Dīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrīmaj Jagannātha Yati</s>,
disciple of the revered <s>Śrīmad Raghunātha Tīrtha Pūjyapāda</s>,
who belongs to the lineage of the most exalted <s>paramahaṃsa parivrājakācāryas</s>, masters of all systems of thought,
the third <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the first <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter).
